reviews.comment: this class is making chem 101 feel like a cake walk right now. its genuinely so upsetting. thats it. dont do this unless you want to feel constantly defeated.

Dr. Rea was disorganized and often late in posting assignments and other announcements, but her exams were very fair and aligned with her lectures, which are always posted. The assignments were straightforward with lots of grace points. Also, a very sweet person and wants you to do well if you schedule meetings with her and show up to reviews.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is such a sweet lady, and she is brilliant. However, teaching is simply not her calling. She spends more time off topic than on in lectures, doesn't give proper (if any) prep materials for exams (which are in total, 73% of our grade), and currently is 5 lessons behind all other classes. Avoid if possible, but don't be too hard on her. She tries

Nice and passionate about biology, but extremely disorganized. Short notice on assignments and posted assignments after ldoc. Went on tangents during lecture and got behind on the material. Exams were full of select all that apply with no partial credit, but she did offer some extra credit on exams. Would NEVER recommend, but not end of the world.
Professor was disorganized and unavailable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Makes simple content hard and doesn't give us some of the slides, so we are writing while she's explaining when she could've just supplied the slides. Also assigns GRQs and warmup assignments for future lessons because we are so behind on lectures. The lessons take 3 classes to cover, and we had our first exam on 1.5 real lessons.

I'm not too sure why she had such low ratings. I thought she was a wonderful professor and the tests themselves were, in my opinion, very fair. As long as you did your readings and attended the lectures the class is easy enough. She did take a very long time to grade the assignments but was one of the best professors I've had at unc.

Professor Rea is a very sweet person and is a very good lecturer, but she does have a tendency to not be very organized so you won't know your grade until the very end. She is very knowledgeable but you need to remember everything she says in class because it will show up on the test. She is a good lecturer but not the most organized professor.
Professor changed up on her word ALL THE TIME

Dr. Rea is very kind and knowledgeable about biology! However, she can be a bit disorganized and our section of BIOL 103 was far behind other sections. It felt like we rushed through the last few chapters since we were behind, and there ended up being some lessons we had to do on our own. Review the lecture slides and quizzes to study for exams!

listen to her lectures over and over again. she tests on what she says. lowk i dont think there are great options for biol 240 at unc so she might be your only option. i didnt buy the textbook, it was $$ and not super useful.

Hardest class of the semester, chemistry is a breeze in comparison. The content is not hard in itself, but Rea expect us to remember a random assortment of facts tangent to the things we actually need to know. Also extremely unorganized, we are several lessons behind other classes at all times. DO NOT RECOMMEND!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She wasn't fair on midterms, and often went on tangents in class that put the entirety of our class behind. She has a PhD in plant biology so if you take her class make sure you know everything about plants. She also told me in office hours that I might have ADHD when I only went to go over test questions, and we didn't go over any questions.

Very nice and passionate about biology. Teaches in an open ended way which is bad for succeeding on the tests where there is only one answer. Willing to help outside of class. Test questions can be tricky because one word could change the answer. Read the textbook, rewrite notes after class, and do practice questions if you want to do well.

Engaging lecturer, but didn't cover much. Exams were insanely hard. Even after going to her office hours and doing what she told me I still got a 58 on a midterm after getting an 86 on the one before. No consistency or organization. She gave us 7 assignments worth 20% and did not grade them until after the final.

Even though I ended with an A in this class, I would NOT recommend Rea for 103. Extremely unorganized and unprofessional. Our class was several lectures behind the other 103 sections all year long. Class was unnecessary stressful.

Professor Rea is inconsiderate, rude, irresponsible, confusing, and honestly unknowledgeable about the content of this course. I do not understand the rationale of her hiring and I do not believe she should be kept as a UNC professor. I have had the absolute worst experiences in her class. EVERYTHING is unclear.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Look, Dr. Rea is genuinely the sweetest most caring professor I have met at UNC - but she cannot teach.  There was clearly just something about her teaching style and my learning that did not line up because I felt like I was grasping at straws studying for her exams.  The exams had biochem on them??? There were also no grades in before the final.

Focuses too much on irrelevant details during the lecture. Behind schedule since FDOC. Lessons skipped or moved asynchronously to "be caught up" (we never caught up). ALWAYS last minute. Unit quizzes due less than 24 hours before the exam. Has assignments due AFTER LDOC. Modules and assignments are not posted in a timely manner.

This was the most dysfunctional class I've ever taken. Did not know half of my grades in the class before the final; her exams were a disaster (there were poorly written questions in every one of them), and she would cancel class at the drop of a hat. I promise you IT'S NOT WORTH IT!!!!!!! Save your sanity!

Extremely disorganized, barely anything was graded until after the final except for exams which were graded 3 weeks after, no resources to actually study for exams that were based off the tiniest things from her tangents. Genuinely worst professor I've ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This course might be the worst part of the human experience. How someone could have a degree in something and know so little is insane. I pray that she remembers even half of it or she'd be better off teaching at the asylum I'll be at.

i think a squirrel is more organized than her. she will spend 50 minutes on a tangent then test you on the tiny details. assignments from the first week of the semester are just now being graded (extremely harshly based on a rubric we weren't given) kept trying to move exams the week before. if you value organization or sanity take with anyone else
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: she literally had no structure to her class. just spent the entire time yapping about random topics. takes forever to grade exams and assignments. the fact that i did not know (and still don't) know my grade going into the final is absolutely insane. take anybody else for this class.

By far the worst class I've ever taken at UNC. The last day of exams was three days ago, and in-class assignments have yet to be graded. It takes over 3 weeks to get exam grades back. Not to mention the in-class assignments are graded SO harshly for absolutely no reason, and we never got a course schedule.

Please take anyone else.  We are just now getting our grades back for assignments we turned in months ago, and the semester and finals are over! We asked about these assignments several times, and she dismissed our concerns as a non-issue.

Genuinely the worst professor AND TAs I've had at UNC. Hasn't graded anything all semester until today and will give you failing grades on those assignments based on a rubric they didn't even give us. I want a refund for this class and I WISH I P/F and was never a BIOL major. To all freshman, change your major and never take a class with this b.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: ain't never called a prof a b before but she's genuinely a b

She was a new professor but I think a squirrel is more organized than her. She would lecture 50 minutes on one slide and say nothing of importance. MC exams took over 2 weeks to grade because there were so many mistakes. Review sheets were posted at 11:50pm the two night before the exams and she tried to move every exam the week before we took it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very kind and clearly enthusiastic about the material. However, the course was incredibly unorganized. Lectures often veered off into completely different topics, we received no feedback on our assignments throughout the semester, thus no one knew their real grade going into the final. Good vibes but def try to take the course with someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I literally had no idea what was going on ever felt like she be making her own biology up at one point as literally what she taught was different from what I was taught in other biology courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: worst professor. always behind on everything since the year started, and by thanksgiving break, we were basically 1 whole unit behind. she "taught" the entire 4th unit through asynch videos. all exams were so tricky - miss reading 1 word, u get the question wrong. u overthink 1 word in a sentence, still get the question wrong. AVOID!

genuinely nobody I've met likes her class, even the ones who are buddy buddy with her. How someone can fumble so hard at teaching is beyond me. Needlessly strict about closing off REVIEW SESSIONS, and overly lax about genuinely everything else. I swear this class is harder than Organic Chem here.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This prof is truly horrible. The final was supposed to not be cumulative, and have a heavy emphasis on the fourth unit. She sent out an email three days before the exam to let us know that the final is going to have a heavy emphasis on the third unit instead. She released the final review sheet TWO days before the final! Truly the worst.

poor grading criteria, genuinely have trouble learning in her class, unclear structure and format, too many errors on exams/during class, constantly receiving conflicting information instead of a clear answer we can rely on (to study, answer questions on test). 3 total grades in. its been a week since ldoc. dr. rea is a sweet person, but im cooked.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is so passionate about what she teaches, but fails actually to teach anything. I've always been good at biology, but her rambles ruined the subject for me. Her last-minute, inconsiderate lesson planning caused me to fall back on studying for the final (where I had to review a whole lesson and learn it) and inevitably flunk the final.

Dr. Rea is very sweet but can be condescending when answering questions. She explains thing at a higher level needed for this class which confuses you as to which information is important. Get good at dissecting important information from lectures and critical thinking for tests. Class is also very disorganized with last minute announcements.

DONT TAKE HER! Nice person, terrible professor. Extremely disorganized, very late in grading tests and assignments, where half of the assignments still aren't graded even after LDOC. No resources except for a review sheet provided two days before the exam, and pollev questions that dont reflect the exam. Exams are based on her tangents in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: There were two aspects of this course that I was very frustrated with. First, Dr. Rea often discussed topics we did not need to know, which I did not find helpful since I don't plan on taking higher-level courses related to this material. Second, she made it very difficult to see what you missed on tests. She was very passionate about the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Rea is nice. Lectures aren't worth going tbh cuz she isn't great @ teaching. also, cuz no LCs. I just studied the presentations for many hours before each exam and managed to do well enough. Tons of EC though that boosts ur grade by a letter! also, i believe we were very behind compared to other sections. also, doesn't release tests to study :(

Dr. Rea is very nice, and obviously loves biology she just isn't meant to teach. I did everything right, attended review sessions, asked questions, and went to every office hours and still found her lectures and exams confusing. Studying is pointless because her questions are more reading comprehension than biology. Take someone else if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: At this point, finding a way to study for this class is a bigger achievement than curing cancer

Dr. Rea is a very nice person, but not meant to be an upper-level biology professor, especially at UNC. Lectures are beyond disorganized, and her "teaching concepts" are random little tangents she goes off into during lecture. There are no assignments outside of 7 "out of class assignments", of which only 1 of have been graded (2 days before final)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I feel bad writing this because she is very nice and obviously cares about course content, but this class has been done very sloppy. Her lectures have little relation to assignments and the exams are weighed super heavy while being cryptic and deliberately tricky. At this point I don't even know what I'm supposed to be learning...
We are a week past LDOC, and there are 2 grades in. She has canceled 8 classes this semester, and no one has any idea what they are supposed to be learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is very nice, but she is very unorganized. Since she is new at UNC, she was behind schedule. Her tests were very difficult, but she gives lots of extra credit! Her final was a lot easier than the midterms. I wouldn't recommend taking bio 103 with her, but if you take it with her, you will survive!

She is so sweet and quirky and a knowledgable but her class and exams are so unpredictable and unorganized. I would give her some grace because it's her first semester at UNC. She is accessible outside of class and really values each and every one of her students. I think she will be better in coming semesters.

Is she nice? Sure, as a person, but as a professor, I would argue that her disorganization makes her mean. She doesn't do GRQs or pre-lecture homework, but she also doesn't have a schedule for when she will cover topics. The textbook would be much more helpful to read if there were a schedule for us to follow. Please don't take her.

felt like she was CONSTANTLY playing in my face. never on schedule with course content, don't even think we finished the course. super condescending in emails, not accommodating at all either. half the class was unnecessary tangents that we were TESTED on... take this class with literally anyone else.

Nice lady but the worst professor I've ever had. Lectures did not have a schedule, so we were constantly behind on content. She only tests on things from lectures, but this includes tangents that aren't always on topic. Most of our assignments still haven't been graded.

I understand it's her first year at UNC, but we often fell behind and had extra work to catch up. Each exam was more difficult than the last and left me more confused. I do not recommend taking her if you care about your GPA and sanity.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: actually awful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great person, not great at teaching. After working through all our assignments and readings, the exams were so unnecessarily complicated that it felt like she thinks you are supposed to know more than what you are supposed to for this class. Lectures were VERY behind schedule, and she always said, "You don't need to know this for this class, but"

Maybe it's just me, but I felt as though the exams weren't testing what we knew on the subject; rather, it felt like she was just trying to trick us with lengthy word questions. Extremely condescending in personal emails. Also no cheat sheet for the test when other teachers do allow it. Take Biol 103, just not with her...
The only thing good about this class was when it ended
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS. Genuinely the worst class ever. Studying for her exams is a huge pain, as she doesn't release her exams, so you never find out what you did wrong. Unhelpful. Never was on pace with the content; fully rushed through unit 4. Her lesson outlines are unhelpful, and you might as well just start teaching yourself from day 1. RUN.

She is sweet and knowledgeable, but the class was so unorganized. Ended up getting so far behind that we had to basically all of the fourth unit asynchronously the same week as the final. Never knew what to study for the exams, she often goes on unrelated tangents in lecture, and tests you about very specific things she briefly mentioned.

She is extremely hilarious and sweet, but avoid taking her class! You have to imply so many things off of what she "teaches". I watched every lecture and took notes on every word she said. I was confident each time I went to take it but always ended with a D. I don't know how to study for this class and what to expect on the exams each time.

EXTREMELY disorganized. no cheat sheets when other classes got them, didn't receive past exams for review, and SO behind. going to lectures made me actually lose braincells. Get ready to basically self study the entire course. consistently contradicts the textbook and makes test nothing like the class. 
Save yourself.
the minute this class ended, life was worth living again. GENUINELY don't know how I survived.
This class made me bald.

How are we supposed to study for her tests when her questions are the most obscure, niche things that she talked about for a whole two seconds?  She would ramble about unrelated things for so long, one of the reasons we were constantly behind and had to be assigned extra work to make up for it. No cheat sheet, but the other sections have it.
She made my gf cry on multiple occasions, and my gf is doing well in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: For our finale (which is tomorrow), every other BIO 103 class gets to use cheat sheets. Dr. Rea expressed that using cheat sheets was unfair and that we wouldn't learn anything from them. I TOTALLY disagree because we wouldn't need the cheat sheets if she would actually teach, instead of going over material that's not relevant for the class/exams

Dr. Rae is a super nice human being, but as a professor, she's TERRIBLE! We spent most of our time in class lecturing on material that's not correspondent to anything on our exams. Tests were very hard, mainly because of how she intends to word questions and trick you. She uses big words while lecturing, ending up making the material more confusing
Always last minute emails, extremely niche questions on exams, incomplete lectures, and whole lessons switched to asynchronous on the dime. What more could you want from an instructor?

Very disorganized and provides few resources to do well. Lectures and slides are unclear. She makes the review sheet last minute and doesn't give practice exams. Her practice questions from class are so easy compared to the actual test questions. I think the professor is pretty sweet, but I am at a loss for how to do well in her class.
Biology two forty
the campus squirrels could teach better

She's nice but also doesn't know how to teach. at all. Its incredibly difficult to tell which random comment is her rambling about something unrelated or if it'll be a trick question on exams. We have been behind since day one, she just graded our exam we took a month ago. Incredibly frustrating class, study for hours and it makes no difference.

I am a junior, and I can confidently say she is the worst professor I have had. The material isn't hard, she unnecessarily makes it hard. LDOC was yesterday, and she has only graded two exams and one assignment (still waiting on third exam and many other assignments). Avoid her at all costs, unless you want a low GPA and mental illness.

Dr. Rea is the worst professor/teacher in general I've ever had. She is highly condescending and teaches as if she's above the curriculum. At least half of the content on tests is ONLY in lecture, and almost all of her questions are worded to trick you. We have been behind since day 1, and she is still assigning work after LDOC. Take ANYONE else.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nice enough, slightly condescending. Very unorganized. She will cancel class at the last minute, rambles, and is somehow overly detailed/convoluted in lecture without actually covering the course content. You have to go out of your way to find any information for her course, would recommend any other professor.

If I ask you to picture the worst professor you can imagine, you are likely thinking of Dr. Rea. Her almost unbelievable lack of ability to teach and disorganization made this class impossible despite the straightforward material. She hasn't graded anything, and it is LDOC. Taking this class was the worst decision of my entire college career, RUN!
Our final exam is in 3 days and she gave us a whole lesson (60 slides) to study by ourselves. If you take her you will literally have a migraine the whole semester and regret all your life decisions.

Hasn't graded most of our written assignments and our third midterm yet and it's almost LDOC. There are very few resources to study for this course. The lecture slides barely have any written notes, and the exams are heavily based on them. I wish there wasn't a character limit because I still have more to say about how horrible this class was.

She is very sweet and upbeat, but often goes on tangents, which makes it difficult to follow lecture material and differentiate between what you do and don't have to know. Her exams, while not difficult content-wise, feel like they're written to trip people up. I often find the wording extremely confusing. Be prepared to struggle.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is very sweet and wants you to learn the material that she cares very much about, and I admire that in a professor. Since it's her first year at UNC, I feel like she's still adjusting to timing for assignments and course content. I feel like she will definitely improve and become a great professor in time; she taught at Cornell in the past!

She is very nice most of the time, though sometimes I feel like she is condescending. We are really behind in the class, and I am so disappointed because it is my first major class at UNC Chapel Hill. We are about 3 lessons behind, and the final is on Saturday, and she canceled class today at 7:14 when the class starts at 8. Don't take her.

She seems sweet and considerate but she really isn't. Her timing is always off, we were consistently about 10 days behind, and she often posted assignments late with very little time to finish them. She assigned four tasks over Thanksgiving break and regularly makes assignments due on wellness days or days off. Overall, not the best Bio professor.
Take 103 with any other professor!

Wish I could cuss. Terrible and overly nuanced; you are expected to devote to her class like a cult if you even dream of doing well. The exams are a toss-up; the mean is always low, and the questions are unrelated to the lessons we are told to pay attention to. The 5 star review is 100% from the few people Rea is actually nice to. Condescending af
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Currently writing over thanksgiving break since we're skipping over three lessons because we are so behind other classes and she couldnt even post the asynchronous lesson she was supposed to post today so now I have a lesson and a wonderful grq/mastering duo to complete over break. So unorganized, test questions are ridiculously specific, A MESS

Never take her. Take anyone else. It's literally been three months and she can't even manage to grade a single homework. Everyone I talk to feels the same way about her, and there's a reason her 240 class still has available seats in her Spring 2026 section.
take anyone else besides her i beg you its for your own good
she's just yapping bro idek anymore i just want this sem to end purely bc of her class

Always makes lots of mistakes when creating tests. When you ask for help, she humiliates you and does not offer helpful advice in the end. Anything she says during lecture is fair game and she stated she makes the tests more difficult on purpose. Would NEVER recommend. Take any other professor if you want to keep your sanity and GPA.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Rea is a great and really caring person, however she is not meant to be a professor. We are 4 whole unit's behind the other bio 103 sections. She goes on tangents about things that are not relevant to the course. Her tests even skip whole lessons we learned about, and instead we are tested on random things. Do not take her if possible.

Too many people give this professor too much hate. Yes, sometimes we fall a little behind, but she actually does a great job at teaching content. She is also very merciful—one time she gave the class a ten points extra credit for one of our midterm tests if we did a reflection. Your lowest midterm grade is also dropped. Best class I have so far.

I can't even explain what this class is about to you. Every lecture is just full of random tangents, her running around answering questions way beyond the scope of the class, and spending over half the class time just talking about logistics, making her rush the content. She loves Biology, but can't teach it.  DO NOT RECOMMEND HER AT ALL.

She's a really really sweet person but cannot teach for her life. Tests are more reading comprehension than anything. She spends the first 40 minutes of class going over stuff we already know and rushes over the hard things in the last 10. Do yourself a favor and do not take this class. I love bio but this class is ruining it for me.

Dr. Rea is super kind, wants everyone to succeed, and a big bio nerd (in a good way). However, she isn't a good professor. We are very far behind and content is very crammed at the end of every unit. Worst of all (BY FAR) imo are the test questions. Some of them are worded poorly with lots of strange nuances. Don't even know how to study anymore.

She's an ok lecturer, and she is a nice person to talk to, but she does go off on tangents when you ask her questions sometimes. Her assignments and her exam papers are like night and day. Her exams are actually hell to do compared to other professors. I would recommend her if her exams were easier and she were better at answering questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Avoid taking her at all costs. This class is ridiculous and it is beyond hard to keep up with her exam papers, let alone what she says in class. She goes on tangents, writes exams that need deciphering, doesn't even proof read her exams - in exam 3, she took two questions out because they were completely irrelevant to the content. Beyond unfair.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I thought I was tripping but it seems we're all on the same page. Lectures not cohesive, reading the textbook kind of helps to narrow things down, but we are not adequately prepared for exams. Very last minute posting exam resources and exam dates are subject to change. Not sure how to be successful in this class anymore and feeling discouraged.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you are a planner, get ready to have major changes w/ exams/quiz on a weekly basis. Posted Unit 3 Quiz (which are pretty important to final grade) on Saturday at 5pm and made it due Sunday 12pm. Because it was my birthday, I missed this email and therefore my grade dropped 3 points. The lectures are very unclear and the slides are unstructured.

Honestly, this exam 3 pretty much solidified the fact that she isn't a good test maker. I spent so long on two questions that didn't even make sense, only to then hear when the test time is almost over that the questions weren't even possible to answer with our course knowledge. also we are so far behind its actually kinda crazy as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: sweet person but made simple lessons much harder in lecture, so expect to self study everything. Exam questions are written with slight nuances that can trick you, rather than actual application of content. LC were used for attendance for a portion of the grade, but stopped mid semester so not sure what makes up the grade as of now.

I've never seen anyone so incompetent to be multiple lessons behind, not proofread exam questions, post quizzes/assignments short notice, and yap every lecture. Exams are purposefully confusing with "select all the following" or "only two of the above are true". Prepare to spend hours of studying because she can't get any learning done herself.

There are 2 weeks left before finals, and we are 4 lessons behind the other sections. 2 questions were cut from the exam today because she worded them so poorly and wanted to stop answering questions. Do not take this professor. I think 24 awful reviews in her first semester here is a pretty good testament to it. She's kind, but not worth it.

Dr. Rea is a sweet person but a difficult professor. The syllabus is fluid and assignments often take multiple hours and are due shortly after assigned. Her tests are lecture-based but her lectures are full of tangents. Not impossible if you are highly self-sufficient and spend multiple hours a day studying from outside sources. USE YOUR SIs & TAs!

Just goes above and beyond for unnecessary things, provides long and confusing explanations and horrible test maker, questions are so confusing. Doesn't give exams back, instead holds exam review sessions where she literally takes pictures of everyone who came (what I mean by above and beyond for useless things)

The lack of consideration for a student's time is comical. Posted unit quiz + study materials at 5pm ON A SATURDAY & made it due at 12PM next day. Had to cancel plans with my parents who flew in from Cali so I could study. This wouldn't have happened if she wasn't so behind that she had to reschedule the exam to catch up (we're still behind).

absolute WORST professor for BIOL103. does not know how to get anything done technology-wise, always behind on lectures, and randomly sets unit quizzes so they are due at noon instead of 11:59 without ANY notice whatsoever. avoid at all costs unless you want a semester long migraine

She's literally the worst professor I have ever had, she is always so behind on everything but still somehow manages to waste time every single class telling us about utter nonsense that barely relates to the content. She's nice but that's it, she's so mean as a professor, her explanations always are extremely complex and I HATE HER SLIDES!!!!

Just got out her test. I studied the lecture slides, the review sheet, the lectures (multiple times), and even watched the review session she posted at 3:30AM the night before the exam. I'm now even more lost, and she still has only graded one homework. Why hasn't she graded the other homework's that she handed out 3 months ago? Don't take her
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: just don't

DO NOT TAKE HER. Just got out of the 3rd exam - even more lost now than I was before. Her lectures are long-winded and confusing, her slideshows barely have any words on them, and anytime you ask a question, she says she already talked about it. She also rewrites test questions during the test because she realizes she messed up.

reviews.comment: we spent all of one class on one homework question and then the pre-exam review lesson was 3 questions. class is 50 minutes long. genuinely what are we doing
genuinely don't even know what this class is about anymore.

reviews.comment: Take anyone else. I don't even know how to study for the exams anymore since they're mostly based on lectures, but she spends most of the lecture going on tangents. I've just given up at this point.

Literally what are we doing? This class is so unorganized and very confusing. Constantly falling behind and lectures serve no purpose. It's gotten to a point where I don't go to lectures anymore bc I don't gain anything from it. I'm sure she's a great person but she needs to get it together.

she's super nice and genuinely cares about her students. she gave extra credit on the first exam because everyone did bad but she is a super sporadic teacher and doesn't organize the course the way it should be. she's always changing things around and either goes way to slow in a lesson or way to fast. she's just quite disorganized.

She is often wrong on exams or things she says in class. Goes on too many tangents that have nothing to do with what we are learning. Trying to figure out what you should know for an exam is like searching for a needle in a haystack.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I am left contemplating my life choices after taking this class. She is the most disorganized professor I've ever had and the tests are about the random PhD level things that she creates in her mind the night before the test. No curves in site and no extra credit. Save your gpa, don't take this class with her
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She has a "syllabus" that she edited multiple times, and is currently *jumping around on*, and her learning objectives are released the day before the exam. She essentially goes off on tangents the entire class. Her tests feel impossible unless you memorize everything she talks about word for word, including random side tangents. Don't take this!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Talks too much to not be saying anything for real. So disorganized from the grading, the test, the in-class assignments. Like what the hell do you mean you wrote the test the night before the test. That's why the questions are so convoluted like did you even have the TA check or take the test before we did. She's really nice but can't teach.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I wish I could turn back time and not register for this class. I wish I never took it-- I hate it. Never take this class, it truly sucks. It's been almost 2.5 months since school has started and only one assignment has been graded.

do not take this class at all. class isn't that hard but she does not care about your time and won't release assignments to turn in until a few hours before it's due. she talks to us as if we've never heard of what a bacteria is, and will give you a zero on an assignment if you talk about things you learned from other classes calling it AI.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's one of those lecturers that speaks a lot but simultaneously goes through no content, she speaks like she's addressing kindergarteners, she's permanently behind schedule, she's constantly having technology problems, and her exams are mostly lecture-based but her lectures are very confusing and she often goes on unnecessary tangents.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's a really nice lady but her lectures are so confusing. I leave class feeling more confused. She goes through the lessons so slow and we're always behind. We end up doing a lot of work right before the midterms because of how slow she goes. Exams are huge portion of grade and the exam questions are worded in a way that it meant to trick you.

nice person but not good lectures. goes on random tangents, adds in unnecessary info, and is condescending. feel like we barely made progress on content in class. frequent amount of work, and test question phrasing can be confusing/riddle-like. she ends up rushing content close to midterms, so need to cram in last-minute content close to exams.

You'll have to study A LOT, which isn't bad until you realize the lectures can get very overwhelming and confusing. She goes on tangents that cause you to zone out. Suddenly, you are in your head trying to remember what came over you when registering for this class. I will say once you understand what's going on, life is worth living again.

Avoid her class if you can. We're still waiting on 90% of our grades to be updated, and the semester is almost over. She doesn't give objectives till 2 days before the test, and she has no GRQs or anything for lecture prep. If you must take her, she bases her tests almost entirely on lecture. Test reviews are not helpful.

great lady, bad professor. course content is pretty easy, but her lectures make it super confusing. understood the content better when i taught it to myself outside of class. we also rarely finished the lectures and fell behind often. dr. rea is a nice person and is willing to help you, but honestly just avoid her class.

Seems nice, but lectures are so unhelpful- leave me more confused than I was before I walked in. She goes on tangents about hypotheticals that don't matter AT ALL. Tests are written like riddles, on small word and the answer is wrong, not bad, but sucks when exams are only 25 questions. Work load is manageable, but midterms are weighted like crazy

Her lectures are terrible to follow. At this point, I don't even know what to study. She goes on tangents in class about things, she gives almost no study material, and all you can study to prep for exams are the lectures themselves. Please avoid her at all costs-- take anything or anyone else. She also does a horrible job at clarifying answers.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Genuinely the WORST bio professor at UNC. Avoid at all costs. Her exams are written like riddles and she is horrifically unorganized. Lectures are impossible to follow, and she does a poor job of clarifying. I have never hated a UNC class more than this one. Choose literally anyone else. It's not hard, but it is absolutely miserable.

She's disorganized but nice—no GRQs or HW for lecture prep. We had to fight for pre-slides, and she rarely includes objectives for lessons. Tests aren't bad, and the focus is heavily on lectures. She gives a lot of grace if a question is bad.

Bad lecturer. Graded by 5 assignments and 4 exams which are both easy with sufficient studying from study guide and research on picked policy topic. TA's were not too harsh on grading and their feedback was helpful.

I feel that some of the negative reviews of Prof. Addo are exaggerated. She is one of the most caring and supportive professors I've had at UNC. She truly wants her students to succeed, is approachable outside of class, and takes the time to explain material when you're confused. If you put in the effort, she will absolutely meet you halfway.

Very nice person and is willing to help you outside of class, but isn't always good at answering questions. We had three midterm exams and one final exam with 5 policy assignments throughout the semester, which felt like a lot, but if you study the lecture content well you're fine. She reads straight off the slides which isn't helpful.

Professor Addo cares a lot and is knowledgable but her lectures were verbatim off the slides. She was not great at answering student questions in lecture either. 4 exams throughout the semester which was a lot but if you study the guide she gives then you should do well on them. Easy class and interesting content but unhelpful lectures.

When she lectures she often does not answer student questions well, or at all. The course was very disorganzied but easy. The TA's are lenient with the grading of the decontructed policy brief. Overall if you go to class and are willing to do some of the readings you are fine.

Dr. Addo seems like a very nice person, but she has very poor lecturing skills. No one in the class listened because she was reading the slides verbatim. This class was also so disorganized. I wouldn't take her if there is another professor avaliable. Her class was still easy, it was the last of my concerns and I did well.

Dr. Addo is a wonderful person and you can tell she has a lot of passion for her field. However, lectures were rather dry and I do not feel I gained a whole lot from the class. Still, assignments weren't too hard, nor were exams. Attendance is technically required but often not enforced.

lectures were boring and pointless since she mostly reads off the slides, the content is also boring, tests are more about memorization with a little application, I didn't pay attention but got >95 on every test and assignment

This class was extremely repetitive with the same content in every single module. Prof. Addo does NOT know how to lecture in any way shape or form. She needs to take a workshop on lecturing. The class itself was boring, tests were fine, just study the review that she posts. Application based. Our assignments were easy 100's. I skipped class a lot.

She is clearly smart but such a bad lecturer. She gets confused by her own slides, mostly just reads off them anyway, and struggles to answer student questions. She also weirdly giggles so much and it makes me so angry. Exams weren't too hard though and out of class assignments were easy 100s

I found her class frustrating. She is condescending and fails to answer questions beyond the content of her lecture slides. The content is manageable, but lectures are poorly organized. My biggest issue with her class was the volume of tests. A policy innovation and analysis course should focus on research and writing, not multiple choice exams.

These reviews over-exaggerate what Dr. Addo's class is like. While she is not an engaging lecturer (she mostly reads off her slides), she is clearly knowledgeable in her field. If you do the few readings assigned and put in a decent amount of effort on the problem sets, you'll be just fine. This class was my last priority and I ended with an A.

I don't think I learned a lot from this class and I found Professor Addo confusing in general (how she explained things), but I didn't feel that this affected my ability to succeed in the course. She was very helpful outside of class and seemed to care a lot about students. Grading didn't feel nitpicky and the workload was relatively light.

Professor Addo is a really nice person, but I think that they need to work on their lecture skills. It is really hard to pay attention. Majority of the time I had no idea what was going on. Available outside of class and just so nice, but the class needs to be restructured and they need to go to a lecture/public speaking workshop.

There were multiple occasions where the teacher or TA could not answer a question posed by a student in the class. Not gonna lie, I didn't even know if the teacher knew what was being taught. The tests aren't terribly hard but they grade hard for no reason. If you could pick another professor for 210 probably would do that. Gonna end with a B.

Probably one of the worst classes I have taken at UNC. The professor and TA's grade super hard for no reason and give no feedback. They don't even seem to understand the material themselves and just take off points randomly. They give you 8th grade level exams and then grade them super harshly for no reason. I might get a B in this class.
She's a robot reading slides and exams are poorly designed and graded. Don't take her if you can avoid it.

She does nothing to engage students while lecturing. While she seems to know a lot about the subject, she does not teach it well at all and you many leave lectures more confused than when you entered. She talks in circles and does not give straight answers. Impossible to reach outside of class and you're better off asking a TA.

Grading is fairly unclear with only very brief notes given, and the rubrics provided are inconsistent.Although she's very kind her lectures are unfocused and she tends to repeat herself or talk around clearly explaining something. It is also fairly difficult to review and follow the slides as they are mostly just terms without explanation.

Do not take her class unless you absolutely need to. She is a very unclear grader and when she explains your grade, she does nothing to explain it well. She is the worst professor I've had at UNC so far. I only gave her 1/5 because I couldn't give 0...

Dr. Addo is a really sweet lady who I believe genuinely does care about her students. However, she is quite simply not a good teacher. Her lectures are quite unclear and unfocused. She communicates quite poorly in general and it's very difficult to learn much from her class.
regret taking his class lmao
The class is a mix of lecture, group work and guests. I enjoyed the class
eh class. don't take it as an elective. not worth it
Boring. not learning much

This class was a bit different from my other classes, but in a good way. His class is combo of lectures, group projects and guests to speak to the class along with the main project. I learned a lot from his class.

There are so many other professors you should take for MEJO 121. Not much structure. Didn't take much from the class. He was the worst professor I've ever had and I had him my first semester sophomore year.
Thoroughly enjoyed this class. Professor Eddy really enjoys teaching. It shows in his lectures. There is some hard work in this class and group projects.

I learned a great deal in Prof Eddy's class. He cared for all his students. There is a ton of group project which makes class fun. There were a few guest speakers from different industries that added to the class. I highly recommend his class.
Class was ok. a bit boring and very technical. Not a formal class since he's not a formal teacher but if you put in a lot of work you might be able to receive an A.

His teaching style was often disorganized and course expectations/grading criteria weren't communicated clearly. Assignments required a significant amount of work, sometimes without sufficient guidance or clarification. Lots of guest speakers. Overall, the instructor did not seem very flexible or understanding when students raised concerns.

Prof Eddy was great, very accessible, and helpful with questions. There is no rubric for any assignments, which made it sometimes difficult to understand feedback and grades. The class is boring because its a prereq, but Prof Eddy did provide good advice about the real world and had educational guest lectures.
Such a sweetheart!! Genuinely loved and cared for all his students, I had to ask for a 24-hour extension a couple of times, and he was willing to give me one for as long as I needed!

I don't go here, because I'm in high school, but this guy is my godfather and I would like to mention that. He's pretty good at being a godfather, I think, but please don't let him wear suits. Otherwise someone might mistake him for Jeff Bezos and that would be bad.

The sweetest man. He really cares about his students and takes the time to reply to every one of our submissions. The class was so easy and I'm sure almost everyone got an A. I loved him and found his content to be interesting. Take his class!

Art was AMAZING. Always gave clear and constructive feedback. Assignments were straight forward and relatively easy but beneficial to learn basic editing and website building. Easy grader, it is not hard to do well in this class. Overall, awesome guy who really cares about his students and what he is teaching

Very easy grader, but I didn't get out of this class what I wanted. There was no clear guidelines for a lot of our assignments, and he taught us all our video-editing/web building skills via LinkedIn Learning. Very nice guy, but I honestly don't feel like I learned much

I loved taking 121 with Art Eddy! He is such a nice guy and makes every class fun and interesting. He always made his expectations for our projects clear and did not grade harshly. I would definitely recommend taking mejo121 with him.

Gem of a professor! He is so sweet and clearly cares so much about students. The class is not too challenging-- perfect for those who have little to no experience with video editing/web design. Highly reccommend!

ENGL 148. Good lecturer and engagement, can tell she has a passion for the literature. There is in class canvas discussions at the beginning that is used for participation and assume she used this in place of a student not actively speaking in class. Did this class more for fun and to retouch on reading outside main major.

Instructor Fowler was a very nice person, just not a great instructor. They would be late to many meetings and these meetings felt unprepared. However, they were very accommodating when it came to due dates and attendance. I felt my tuition was wasted, but if you want an easy class, this is the way go.

Professor Fowler was very inconsistent with grading assignments (providing feedback), and often cancelled class last minute (or was very late). In their defense they had a lot of personal issues going on this semester, so I can't speak for their teaching under normal circumstances, but overall I learned little to nothing from this class.

Professor Fowler is the most compassionate and caring professor you will ever have. Prioritizes student well-being over everything and will work with students no matter their situation. It's hard to lose your A in this class as long as you complete your feeder assignments and give good effort on your unit projects. Couldn't recommend them more.

I actually had her for ENGL120**
Mandy was excellent and caring. She was clear and concise in her feedback when grading and was incredibly accessible outside of class. She was always great at giving advice when I needed it and was very accommodating with deadlines if an extension was needed. She also helped students create networking in the class.

I really enjoyed Professor Fowler and her class, she's one of the most caring professors I've had and is always willing to extend deadlines or work with you if you're struggling for any reason. Assignments can be pretty long, but the feeders truly help you for the unit projects, so I wasn't even mad they were long. Definitely recommend!

Professor Fowler is SUPER caring and genuinely goes out of her way to be there for her students and support them in any way she can. However, the class is disorganized and very busy work heavy, and Professor Fowler's long off-topic tangents do not help. Also, she does not give grades so your final grade is unknown, although she is an easy grader

Professor Fowler is a kind human. She is passionate about what she teaches and deeply cares about her students wellbeing. She's always willing to offer extensions for assignments and projects. The essays aren't fun to write, and at times it felt like a heavy workload, but she's super lenient with due dates and willing to help in office hours.

Although Professor Fowler went off-topic a ton and would keep us after class, she was an AMAZING Professor. She out the student's mental health first and would usually give deadlines if asked properly. She was extremely caring and made her classroom a safe space for everyone. She is very disorganized, but as long as you do your work, you'll pass.

At first I was scared to have her as a professor because of her past reviews but I absolutely adore her as a person and as a teacher. She makes you feel safe and heard in class and is a great teacher. She barely assigns homework and always extends the deadlines of assignments when you ask. She cares more about improvement than number grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Mandy is quite literally the best teacher I've ever had, let alone professor. She is so sweet and understanding! She is also completely upfront about her expectations and her grading system is really forgiving. If you are a freshman you definitely should take her section of Engl-105.

Uses live class time during a mostly asynchronous course to make you watch a live video demonstration on mind mapping and journaling. Makes group breakout sessions for the most mundane tasks. Assignments are spoon-fed ad nauseam.

I liked Mandy a lot during recitations, but her grading did not make a lot of sense to me. She would comment on one thing wrong with a paper and dock 10 points. I just think there could have been some more commentary or a rubric for grading to work on improvements. Overall a really nice and caring TA.

For a basic Gen Ed class, it was a lot of projects and work. You have to make a podcast and create a Wiki entry. You have to watch hours of instruction just to understand how to use the software needed. I spent tons of effort on this class. It seemed like she just gave everything a 90. She was a nice teacher, it definitely could have been worse.

I took English 105 in the online summer format. 50% of your grade depends on three assignments. While the work in this class was not exceptionally difficult; the rubrics were often unclear and Professor Fowler took a long time to grade all major assignments. I would not recommend taking Professor Fowler for this online summer class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely kind and caring. Was willing to be flexible and work with a challenging situation from day one. Would highly recommend ENGL 105 with her!

Fowler is a pretty typical English 105 teacher. She is caring for her students and is accessible outside of class if someone needs any help. She can be pretty funny too-she'll laugh at her own mistakes when she misspells words during class. I'd probably take another class with her if I needed to. She's a fair grader and willing to give feedback.

Dr. Abramowitz was always funny during lectures. Always willing to help. You're graded on 2 midterms, a final, and a few case studies (group assignment). No grade cushioning, but exams are pretty straightforward, mostly factual and not application based. Attendance is not graded but you have to come to class since he puts very little on his slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: TAKE THIS CLASS as a freshman. It's an easy and interesting class with no tests, only short weekly writing assignments, and a group project. You get to learn from a really caring and intelligent professor who makes the class fun. He is very helpful and understanding with deadlines or missing class. He's the best professor I've had so far.

If you are a freshman, TAKE THIS CLASS. It is not overwhelming at all. No final exam or final paper, so you have more time to study for finals for other classes. You have very short (around 200 words) writing assignments each week, and one presentation you do in a group in class. It was so easy, and let me get close to a great professor.

TAKE THIS CLASS: super interesting and great lectures. Some topics were more interesting than others but Abramowitz always made them enjoyable. He is a really cool guy and great teacher. The grade is based on 3 exams and 2 papers. The exams are fair if you take good notes. You can't miss any class though because he doesn't post the full slideshows.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Abramowitz is the best! So knowledgable about psychopathology. Lecture heavy but there's interesting videos and he's a great lecturer. Tests are 75% of your grade but all multiple choice and very straight forward. Easy A and great prof!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: If you need an easy A and don't mind attending lecture every class, TAKE ABNORMAL WITH ABRAMOWITZ. Seriously. Just do it.

The best prof I've had so far. His class is 75% exams and 25% final essay, I was hesitant about that but the tests are extremely easy if you go to class and listen. He doesn't post full lectures so attendance is a must. Super nice guy and I really enjoyed his class even though I hate psych.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Super chill professor. Nice, friendly, easily accessible. Willing to give feedback. Good lectures. Expects participation (part of your grade). Interesting lectures. Would definitely take this professor again.

Dr. Abramowitz is awesome!! He is so passionate about psychology and really wants everyone to do well. As long as you go to class and take notes, you will do fine on the exams. There are just 3 non-cumulative exams and a paper on a movie about a psychological disorder. He is a great lecturer and very kind!!
Very engaging and clearly cares about the success of his students! As long as you come to class and take good lecture notes you will be fine. Each test is 25% and 10 page final paper is also 25%

Professor Abramowitz is a super fun and interesting lecturer. I love that he helps illustrate concepts using stories from his own experience as a clinical psychologist. The class is very easy - the tests only have questions from the lectures, so reading the textbook is completely unneccesary. Besides the three tests, there is just one final paper.

Seriously the best prof I've ever taken at UNC. He's very passionate about the material and his tests reflect the lectures well. The only "complaint" I have is that he doesn't post his full ppts online, so you have to go to class to get all the info. 75% of the grade is tests & 25% final essay, so take that for what you will. 10/10 would take again

Professor Abramowitz clearly loves what he does, and is extremely intelligent.  He enjoys discussion, and encourages it in his class.  Professor Abramowitz specializes in Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, and it was extremely interesting to see the way he tied in his daily work to his class.
One of the best professor's I have had. Extremely clear and helpful, and truly a nice guy. I learned a lot, and he really knows what he is talking about. Highly recommend.

Dr. Abramowitz is one of the most interesting professors I've ever had ~ really witty and funny.  Learned a lot about abnormal psychology.  We did fun activities in class.  He wants you to do well (you have to study, though).  No regrets taking this class.
Made abnormal psychology fun and interesting. He had great "props" and demonstrations to make classes very hands on.

This guy's lectures man...they're actually so fantastic. By far the most engaging history class I've ever taken. He's always asking for participation, but never in a pressured way. It leads to a great learning environment. The content gave an amazing, all-encompassing view of the 1960s.

Every good thing you have heard about him is true. Best lectures I have ever attended and I was always genuinely excited to hear them. He is easily accessible outside of class and loves to get to know his students. Grading and recitations are up to the TAs, but the grading criteria is super clear for both essays and exams.

Wow. Professor Andrews was incredible! Coming from a stem major, I didn't think lectures could be so entertaining. The class is not an easy A. There are 3 papers that are graded harshly. Final was easier than the papers if you studied by the study guide. But class is worth it because of how great Professor Andrews was. Just enroll. You'll be fine.

His reviews say it all: Andrews is an incredible lecturer and a great person during office hours. He offered a full 2% extra credit on final grades, and the final was very fair if you reviewed some Quizlets or took good notes. The TA grading on papers could be tough, but not incredibly unfair.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Such a caring professor who has really interesting lectures!! Coursework was three essays and a final. The essays can be annoying if you have a bad TA, but go to office hours and work with them and you will be fine!! Extra credit opportunities give +2 points to your final grade so an A is very doable. Overall my favorite class this semester!

My favorite history professor at UNC! Dr. Andrews was my academic advisor for an internship as well. In both experiences he was such a caring, brilliant professor. He's well spoken and entertaining and makes his class content extremely relevant and interesting. Highly recommend. TAs grade everything, though, and they can be hit or miss.
Great professor, really cares about the class. Most of your grade is 2 essays and the final. TAs are super strict when grading. They'll always find ways to dock off points.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lectures were very interesting however the final is based on knowing key concepts which are not made clear. Study guide mentions the structure of the exam, not what to study, so you are going into the exam not know what to expect regardless of your notes are. Grade in class is largely based on 3 papers which are graded by TAs who can be tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing professor and great lectures, but the grading is honestly tough and since there are so few grades the final is stressful because you have to do well. Participation didn't matter but I always wanted to attend his class! Just go to your TA's office hours to get tips on how to do well on the essays. Also lots of readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Matt Andrews is a great person, and the lectures were interesting. However, for this class 67% of your grade is based on papers, and if you get a bad TA, as I did, you are SCREWED. I would not recommend taking a class with him if you can not pass fail it since this year he made his class significantly more difficult without the grading contract.
TAKE A CLASS WITH PROFESSOR ANDREWS IN YOUR TIME AT UNC. He is such a capitvating lecturer and the essays are not that difficult. Do it!!!!!! Olympics was so so cool.

Amazing professor and he's truly loved by his students. The course itself is so interesting, especially if you love basketball, and the grading structure is designed for success. Your effort and engagement with the content translates directly to your grade. The final exam is just an essay that you will be well-prepared to write.

I have but two regrets in life thus far: 
1) texting her at 3am
2) not taking Dr. A's classes sooner

Professor Andrews, as noted by many others, runs a fun, interesting class, where it is easy to thrive. Lectures are engaging, and you have two papers and a final, along with participation. He teaches interesting content, I recommend the class.
Goated professor, everyone should take atleast one of his classes.

Just brilliant. Best Professor at UNC by a mile, and the content of this course makes it even better. Great lectures, easy enough assignments, just a great guy. One of the few professors that you want to listen to for 3 hours a week, and would also want to grab a beer with. What a man, what a class.

Best Professor OAT. Attendance isn't mandatory, but you still find yourself looking forward to his classes and actually wanting to go. Lectures are incredibly interesting and well-delivered, and it's very easy to get an A. Knew nothing about Baseball going it, and now I'm an expert on both the game's history and wider American history. 10/10 class.
Matt Andrews is such a good lecturer and clearly enjoys his job. Please take a class with him if you get the chance. Recitations were kind of useless in my opinion but his grading system is very good

Great guy, let me rant about baseball for an hour in his office once. Class is great and lectures are really engaging, I went to class because I actually wanted to (shocker). Only gripe is that his TAs grade everything so it's not super fair when some students get awful TAs and others don't. I'd still take this class though he's incredible.

Dr. Andrews is so entertaining and every lecture in his baseball class felt like I was watching a movie. You should definitely take one of his couses if you enjoy sports. My TA was a little harsh- she caused me to lose my 4.0 because of how she tore apart my essays- but I don't regret taking this class at all.

One of the best classes I have had at UNC. Basketball being my favorite sport made me very excited to go to lectures, and we got to pick our grade as long as we completed the essays and attended recitation. Lots of reading if you want to understand the lectures better, but overall a very fun class for gen ed credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best professor I've ever had. Lectures were great, and I was entertained enough to pay attention at every lecture. Just take a class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Andrews is an amazing professor! He makes every class so interesting and loves when students ask questions! The only downside is TAs grade everything and the one I had was a little bit of a tough grader. Overall I 100% recommend taking this class you won't regret it!!!!

Favorite professor I have had at UNC so far. Super kind, knowledgable, and funny. If you like baseball and need FC credit, take this class! The recitations can be slightly difficult but you will do well if you participate.
Incredible professor, incredible lectures, and incredible ball knowledge.
Literally the best lecturer I've had at my time at UNC. Content was super interesting too, and grading contract was more than fair. 11/10
Please take baseball & american history!! It is not hard to make an A. My favorite class at UNC!! & fav professor.

Dr. Andrews is hands down the best professor I have ever had. Attendance is optional but the lectures were awesome. He clearly knows a lot about what he teaches and has a clear passion for sports history. Guaranteed good grade if you put in an ounce of effort. If you like basketball you have to take this class, it'll be one of your favorites.

I LOVE PROFESSOR ANDREWS. cannot wait to take every class he offers. For HIST 585, there was a grading policy where if you did the minimum assignments you got a B+ and you could "go for the A" by doing other assignments. His lectures are beyond captivating and I genuinely enjoyed them. Race and Basketball is so so cool, take this class!

Dr. Andrews is such a great professor! He keeps students engaged and makes every lecture interesting. There are only readings for bi-weekly discussion groups that are pretty easy. The TAs can be kind of harsh on grading, but the class is still so worth it. You'll love this class even if you don't care about baseball!

Andrews is an excellent professor who gives very interesting lectures. However, if you're hoping for a free A, this course is not for you. None of the coursework is that difficult, but the TAs grade harshly.

I love Professor Andrews teaching style and his classes!! He is so nice and easy to talk to and his classes are interesting. I didn't take this class for anything, I had just heard how good it was and I 100% agree. Take this class, it's awesome!!
Loved the lectures and found myself wanting to come every week.

Easily the best professor I've ever had. My sole complaint is that your TA's determine your grade and all of it is essay based + the final. The Rome 1960 quiz didn't cover the essentials of the book and it's 5% of your grade. I learned so much content in this course and I loved the lectures, I went to class because I wanted to. Def take his course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Absolutely incredible, every lecture is a performance
Amazing lecturer. Even though this was his first semester teaching HIST384, the lectures were great and the expectations were clear in the syllabus. Take a class with him if you can.

Can't say enough good things-- syllabus was abundantly clear, lectures were very interesting, and this course is overall just so helpful to understanding how the 60s impact American life today. Took for the FC-POWER Gen Ed as a STEM major and still really loved the class. Also, all assignments were completion-based, so no stressing about grades.

I LOVE him he is one of the best teachers I've had at UNC. Only complaint is that your grade is based upon 3 papers that your TA rips to shreds. But he gave a lot of extra credit that boosted my grade from an A- to an A. Lectures are not mandatory but I went everyday and took good notes. I still thought the exam tested small details and concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: By far the best professor at UNC. The class was not very hard if you go to lectures (and the lectures are optional, but still always full- shows what a great teacher he is). It can be dependent on your TA, so I'd recommend going into your TA's office hours to clearly understand their guidelines/expectations. I never really did readings and was fine

An awesome guy and I really enjoyed every single one of his lectures. Definitely a good amount of reading and writing, but nothing crazy. Attend class because it is interesting - not mandatory. It is necessary to attend recitations and participate, make sure the TA knows who you are because it is a large part of your grade. GO TO THE EXTRA CREDIT!!

Dr. Andrews is the best. His lectures are so freaking interesting like one time he pranked us that this guy died during the Olympics but he didn't. Im getting a history minor to be with him And hes hot.There are three paper which are graded hard (prob depends on TA too) and then the final you have to study for. Read Rome 1960 it'll help with paper.

I wouldn't say I care a lot about sports, but I genuinely enjoyed this class because Dr. Andrews is so great. His lectures were engaging and easy to follow. Most of your grade is determined by 3 essays (2 with a prompt and 1 research), but they are all are laid out clearly and aren't super time consuming to complete.

This was my second class with Andrews and it was just as good as my first. Lectures are engaging and the assignments give you a lot of creative freedom. I was never stressed about grades in this class, allowing me to come to class each day with enthusiasm. Andrews has a great sense of humor and fosters a comfortable class environment. A must-take.

Hands-down the coolest professor I've had at UNC. Lectures were really interesting and often felt like you were listening to a story. This definitely wasn't a free A class and required a fair amount of reading and writing, but Matt provides a good amount of extra credit opportunities for students to boost their grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Matt Andrews is awesome at lecturing... however this is not a free A or easy gen ed. The course requires some things that are a bit rediculous such as reading a 400 page book that is quizzed on. There are 2 papers around 6 pages long and then a research paper that is 7 pages long throughout the semester that take a lot of research.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Matt continues to be the best. Take this class if you can, the information is both entertaining and very important history to learn.

One of my favorite classes this semester! His lectures are never boring. One book quiz, 8 online quizzes, 2 shorter papers, 1 longer research paper, 2 extra credit movie nights (the points go to your overall letter grade!), and 5 extra credit points on your final. I have learned so much about the Olympics and will never look at them the same way...

Professor Andrews' lectures are always engaging and interesting. Attendance isn't mandatory. Your final grade is heavily determined by 3 papers - all of which are graded by your T.A., so consider that. I would recommend this class again though.
Probably the best professor you'll ever have. Give this man a raise. There are papers and quizzes but if you go to class and turn them in on time, you'll be fine.
One of the best professors at UNC. Engaging lectures, even if attendance is mandatory. Lots of reading, but worth it. Unstuckstudy was a huge help for preparing.

Prof. Andrews is a great lecturer, but an even better guy. He truly loves what he does, and his knowledge on the sports world is unmatched. He's very down-to-earth and is one of the best professors I've had while at UNC. Although the papers are a little tough, the final exam was very fair and allowed for students to recover. Would Recommend.

Hands down my favorite class and favorite professor at UNC. It's the type of class you don't have to attend but still go every time because the lectures are that good. There's a lot of reading for this class, but almost all of it was interesting. You're definitely missing out if you don't take one of Andrews' classes.

Love Matt. ~60% of grade if from three papers which might be difficult if you're not a strong writer. Definitely go to office hours if you need help, Matt's very welcoming. Lectures are enjoyable and quizzes are easy if you attend lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This dudes a legend and easily the most engaging prof I've had. Never cared for baseball but he's inspired me to maybe watch some this year. Caveat is that there are a couple mildly graded essays but even then the class is still way worth it. Gonna try and take another class w him.

I am going to take all of Dr. Andrews classes if I can. Easily the best lecturer at UNC and I really enjoyed some of the personal touch he added to our class. One of the most welcoming and best overall professors here!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Andrews is a great lecturer and frankly it's pretty cool to get credit for learning about awesome sports stories. My only problem with the class is that there aren't many assignments and they're graded by TAs, so getting an A isn't easy despite the class feeling easy.

I would HIGHLY recommend taking any of Matt's classes if you have an interest in sports & can use them for a gen-ed credit. That being said, do not expect a free A out of his class. While the final isn't too hard, the midterm papers are graded (fairly, but) quite hard. Unless you need a perfect GPA, Id say his lectures and personality are worth it.

I absolutely loved Prof. Andrews.  His lectures were extremely engaging and I enjoyed the course content.  Lectures weren't recorded at the beginning of the semester, though, so make sure you attend class.  Quizzes were directly from lectures.  Paper grading depends on your TA so hope you get lucky there.  If you attend class you'll do well.

This is the fourth class I've taken with Dr. Andrews and every one of them is amazing. There is really no reason any UNC student, regardless of major, shouldn't carve out the time in their time at Carolina to take one of his classes. Insanely interesting, well designed, and impactful, you'd be doing yourself a disfavor if you passed up the chance.

The lecturing GOAT, what else is there to say that others haven't said yet. You're graded by a TA; there's 2 essays, recitation participation, and a final where the prompt is given ahead of time. Take this class to get a new insight on the world of American sports.

Matt Andrews was a great professor and great lecturer! Every one of his lectures was very engaging! However, your grade in this class is determined heavily by TAs. My TA was a very hard grader in comparison to other TAs which was disappointing because his ridiculous grading took away from the engagement and great content in this class.

Professor Andrews is a great lecturer, and the content of the course is extremely interesting if you're a sports or history person. Your grade will heavily depend on your TA, as your grade is mostly comprised of essays that are subjectively graded.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You don't have to love sports to love this class. It covers sports but more so its relationship with international relations, politics, gender, drugs, patriotism, finance, etc. Also, all professors have a thing or two to learn from Prof. Andrews. One of the best lecturers and profs I've had at UNC.

Absolutely love Matt Andrews as a professor! His lectures are so engaging. However, beware all your papers are graded by the TA's and I got stuck with a hard-grader and will probably end up with a B like most others with the same TA. Its a luck of a draw if you get an easy grader or not. The class itself it so enjoyable though!

I loved this class so much that I actually went in person even though he posted the lectures online afterward. Dr. Andrews is thoughtful and passionate enough to cover some tough topics really well. There are 3 papers and a lot of readings, but the work is worth it. I got so much out of this class and I would take it again if I could.

I would honestly have gone to this class just to listen to the lectures even if I wasn't in the class, that's how great his lectures are. If you like sports at all, do yourself a favor and take a class with him. The TAs lowkey can suck and they grade harshly, and there is a fair bit of reading, so it's not the easiest A around, but 1000% worth it.

The professor is amazing! But (you must notice this "but" because) you will suffer in this course if you want to achieve a good grade and you unluckily have a harsh TA.
