reviews.comment: I love Bliem! I came from 101 with Pedersen and it helped me so much to have a professor that could actually lecture well. Attendance is REQUIRED because she's such a good lecturer. I never read the textbook but she was amazing at explaining things in class and always welcomed questions. She's an awesome professor, and I would recommend her.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Professor Bliem is one of the best professors I've had at UNC. She's hilarious and really cares about her students. She is always willing to help students outside of class and if you put in the effort, so will she. I would absolutely recommend taking her class for 102. The standardization of the tests sucks, but there's no getting around that.

Prof Bliem is a great professor. She really cares about her students succeeding in her class. She does have a really monotone voice but is hilarious and going to class is fun and interesting. Clicker quizzes every day at the beginning of class, so you really can't skip. All the gen chem tests are standard, so now it's all about teaching style.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof Bliem is VERY inflexible; beware that exams are taken separately from the main class and if you have a conflict, you WILL be forced into the 6:30 AM make up slot for 3 midterms, yes 6 AM in the morning

While Prof. Bliem is a good lecturer and can explain complicated topics, her class is really hard. I took her course over others because she assigns graded homework thinking this would help prepare me for tests, but I still struggled. They're full of trick questions and much more difficult than the practice exams. Luckily hw can bump up your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Bliem is the best! If you go to lecture, office hours, and do all the assigned work you will be fine! I studied all the time for this class, and the tests were still extremely difficult for me. You have to learn how to do the problems quickly. I loved the mentor review sessions as well. I loved this class, and I'm sure you all will too!

Professor Bliem is a good person to take 101 or 102 with. The tests are difficult, but she gives you plenty of practice problems to work in class and out of class that are very beneficial. She's pretty cool too, so that helps

Bliem is a charismatic professor. I looked forward to her lectures, but I may be biased since I enjoy chemistry. She has a great sense of humor that she shows often, and her daily homework and quizzes are great learning aids. They're not busy work, and they help the material stay fresh in your mind.

One of the most enthusiastic professor's I've had. This is not an easy class but if you put in the work you'll get a high grade. She has tons of resources for you and if you really try in the class you will get a good grade.

I personally think Professor Bliem is one of the best Chem professors at UNC. She does had a flipped classroom, which means you will have to get familiar with the material before coming to class. However, I think this is a very effective method. During class, she does a lot of practice problems and goes in depth for the important topics.

Clear lectures and homework, but tests are much more difficult than any other assigned material.  Office hours and homework are a must.  She is very helpful during her office hours, and they are often even more beneficial than the class.  Read the textbook and do the recommended problems.  Fair grader and wonderful teacher, but tests are difficult.

It is totally possible to do well in Bliem's class, but you have to do your readings, homework, and come to class. Her tests are tough, but make you think critically about chemistry. Taking her again for 102 next semester. Avoid is you aren't willing to put in the work to get an A.

Bliem is a super cool person, but she's not the best teacher around. I never went to class, but to get daily points you have to go to class... so go to class. You have homework every day, and she reads straight off the powerpoint during lectures. Her tests are insanely hard, but if you study for two weeks beforehand, you'll be okay. Not the worst

Professor Bliem has a flipped class, but she gives COUNTLESS resources to help. Office hours, extra recommended problems and helpful videos are abundant. FREE ONLINE TEXTBOOK! Homework is minimal, but VERY helpful. I spent 10-45 min MAX on homework. Attendance is mandatory and she has in class quizzes each day (3 ?'s each). Best CHEM101 class.

One of those 'wake up and welcome to college' professors. If you don't take the class seriously, your grade will reflect it. Go into every mid-term prepared and armed to the teeth with every single thing that has been mentioned in lecture and in the readings. Sapling and recommended problems help learning content as well. Don't be afraid to ask.

She's a nice lady but a terrible teacher. If you do not do well in the flipped classroom style of learning, meaning you cannot teach yourself well, do not take her class. Most of what you learn is from teaching yourself problems and homework she assigns outside of class. Her tests are much more difficult than anything she ever teaches in class.

Professor Bliem was very nice, but I felt very confused by a lot of her explanations, and she had a tendency to introduce concepts on the warmup quiz using the exceptions to the concepts; sound confusing? It was. The tests required a fair amount of studying, but sometimes the study materials provided did not align well with the test material.

Dr. Bliem's tests were quite difficult, all free response, but overall fair, just gotta work for it. Her lectures can be a little unorganized and doesn't really follow the textbook, though she doesn't explain things well. Problem sets are hard, but good practice for the exams. Not a lot of practice for exams. Did curve the class to 85  A though.

Professor Bliem is super nice and tries to help you, but it doesn't always work out. She gives you daily homework and assigns practice problems, which you should definitely; however, her tests are ten times harder than the homework she gives, so be prepared for that. I went to her office hours and did all the practice problems and wasn't successful
The averages for her 101 class for the second and third tests were a 68 (after a 10 point curve) and a 62. Expect to work if chemistry doesn't come naturally to you. She is nice but not super helpful

Prof. B is awesome. If you go to her for help she will help you for sure. Like other chem classes, practice problems are a must. But if you don't plan on doing practice problems all of your life, go to mentor review session because they go over problems, sometimes problems from previous exams. Online homework also helps a ton, so take it seriously.

Personally I thought she was a boring lecturer. Tests are more concept based unlike Professor Benton. Look to the mentors for help as Dr. Bliem can't and won't help all the hundreds of students she has.

The class requires some work, but it's not impossible. There is "daily work" you have to do before class everyday, like online warm ups, and there are clickers, so you have to go to class. Most of your grade is determined by the tests. You should go to at least a few TA review sessions because they offer helpful tips and tricks to make life easier.

Bliem was great this semester, although I do believe her teaching style isn't for everyone. You definitely have to learn things on your own, but she gives you the resources to do that.  If thats not for you, Benton is the way to go! I struggled in her class at first but I went and spoke to her and she was very helpful and offered great advice!

I usually love chemistry, but the tests for this class were extremely hard, the lectures were extremely boring, and the homework was extremely long. There are mandatory homework assignments every weekend, including holiday weekends, that you can't do ahead of time. So be prepared to do a lot of work and little reward grade-wise.
First off, I'm a dean's list student. It's a reversed classroom. If you can't teach yourself, do not take with this professor. The tests are tough, typically average about a 78, and she never curves.

Professor Bliem is by far my favorite professor I've had at UNC. Her exams are challenging, and she will find ways to trick you, but she is very good at preparing you for future chemistry classes. She's funny and extremely approachable. She tries to know all of her students by name. 100% would recommend. Go to class for sure.

Bliem was not my favorite. I prefer Krumper as a lecturer, even though their styles are the same. Bliem is very monotonous and dry, even during her office hours. She shows zero interest in her subject, which eventually trickles down to her students and their interest in the class. Overall, not satisfied, and would not recommend this teacher.

One of the best professors I've had at UNC. She is very energetic, charismatic, and funny! Her classes are very enjoyable. The exams are hard however, she does give you a lot of practice and she's always available in person and mostly by email. This is Biophysics people. Don't blame her on being hard, this class is hard with any professor.
Great as a person and very helpful. Answers her emails very fast. Her exams are hard and have few questions that take you forever to answer because of how difficult they are.
I love prof bliem!  She makes chemistry more enjoayble than I thought it would be and her tests are fair for the most part.  She is also really funny, which is needed in a Chem class in my opinion.
Professor Bleim is very approachable and she likes to make corny jokes every once in a while, but her style of teaching is not for everyone.

Professor Bleim is WONDERFUL! She is 100% my favorite professor at Carolina. I can tell that her main priority is making sure that her students actually learn the material. Yes, the tests are hard but that's because it's CHEM 101 at UNC. If you put in the effort, an A-/B+ is definitely attainable.

ATTEND CLASS! There is a daily quiz and problem solving that require a clicker & are a part of your grade. Tests can be difficult but manageable. It consist of multiple choice and open answer. You can drop lowest test. No regular office hours but problem solving hours. She's very nice and will know you by name if you take the effort to meet her.

She is so nice and sometimes funny but her class is difficult simply because it's Chemistry & most people don't get Chemistry without putting in several hours of studying. She gives you the resources you need and makes your homework harder than the test on purpose. You can be successful in this class if you read, practice problems and attend class!

Really nice & wants to know you by name. Attendance is a must because she now has mini quizzes with clickers and problem solving questions which are a part of your grade. She also assigns Mastering Chem (online) which has the same level difficulty as her tests. She follows the flipped classroom method. So lots of studying on your own!
Great Teacher. She teaches clearly and office hours helped a lot.
If one were to read the textbook, do all the mastering chemistry, go to class, and do the majority of the textbook problems, the class is pretty manageable;)

Dr. Bliem is a very sweet lady and a great professor. She teaches in an organized fashion and goes by the book which is helpful in studying. Her class (and tests) are hard but if you put in the effort she is always willing to help by explaining concepts and doing problems. Office hours are extremely helpful and I would highly recommend her.
She does not prepare you for her crazy hard tests.... at all. You have to do a lot of work on your own. And the homework assignments are unnecessarily long and annoyingly repetitive

Professor Bliem is really nice and she is very organized with her lectures. That being said she only uses powerpoint but answers questions and is nice about the face that she is teaching such a hard class. This is not estimation on how hard her tests are. She tells you what you need to know but her wording is extremely tricky!

Professor Bliem is an extremely nice lady. That being said, she teaches to the very lowest level and tests to the very highest level. I made the first B of my life in this course after putting in about 3 hours of studying chemistry a day. The tests in this course are OUT OF THIS WORLD. Also, homework is only available online on the weekends.

I had never taken a chemistry class in my life. I found her class to be incredibly difficult. I never understood what she was teaching in class. She uses power points and does a few practice problems. Unfortunatley the practice problems are way easier than her tests which are ridiculous. I would not reccomend her.

While obviously a sweet lady, her teaching was hindered by the size of the class. She spent the time doing practice problems, which was useful for me personally but may not be for others. The MC assignments are tough but not impossible, and they're easier if you do the tutorials and read the section in the textbook. Office hours are helpful too!
Terrible. Do all you can to avoid her as a professor. She does not care and does not prepare students well for her ridiculous tests.

Nice Lady.  Her powerpoints are long and she relies on working on problems in class.  Her online MasteringChemistry assignments are brutal and assigned over the weekend which makes getting them finished extremely difficult.  Her tests are very difficult, average was a 64 for the last test we took.  You MUST read the book and do problems in the book

Although she has a great personality, her teaching consists of doing practice problems in class. The powerpoints were useless and the MasteringChemistry is ridiculous since u only get to work on it on weekends and the tutoring center is only open on week days. shes very helpful during office hours but not everyone has time to go.

Consider carefully before enrolling in this professor's class. Unless you are considering taking a lot of upper level chemistry classes, this professor might not be for you. Also she wasn't very understanding when I couldn't make an exam due to an emergency room visit. Not easily accessible either.
BEST PROFESSOR EVER!!!! so helpful and nice- actually teaches the concepts and tests are totally fair and manageable if you study and work the book problems! web assigns are super helpful!

BORING!  Her monotone voice can put people with even the highest levels of ADHD into a coma.  Powerpoints were useless resources for the tests.  A huge waste of ink and paper printing all of those slides.  Most help came from the book and doing problems.

Professor Bliem is the best Chemistry professor I've had at UNC or anywhere.  She actually teaches you concepts rather than relying completely on the book or someone else's powerpoints.  For the first time at UNC I felt successful learning science rather than frustrated and confused.  Definitely take her classes if you can.

Lectures are pretty boring, but she is extremely helpful in her office hours.  Webassigns are pretty challenging, but if you do well on the webassigns you should be fine on the tests.  I suggest studying your webassigns before each test.  Tests aren't too bad, but the time constraint makes things a little harder.  Final exam is easier.

This class was fairly painful and I had to spend a ridiculous amount of time studying to pull off an A. She cares and is somewhat helpful during office hours, but she isn't very clear during class and your grade doesn't end up reflecting what you know. You're better off with another teacher.

Very helpful teacher.  People say she is monotone, but really she is pretty interesting and the nicest person ever.  GO TO OFFICE HOURS!!  She's very helpful and if you do poorly on a test and go see her she will everything she can to help you.  Fair grading, tests were challenging but not impossible.  Highly recommend.

Bad professor. Powerpoints were useless, you had to read and work all the problems in the book in order to a) do the webassign, and b) actually pass her test. She's quite a loser too (she makes a lot of lame jokes)

Def thought I was going to fail her class. She drops the lowest grade on tests and webassigns. GO TO OFFICE HOURS. I managed a C but failed like all her exams. THe final was multiple choice which helped ALOT!!

I hate chem but this woman made it as painless as possible. Webassigns are a pain but they're a good study tool and her tests are fair. The final was a piece of cake. She puts all her lectures online before and after she marks them up in class. I'd suggest printing them out before class and writing your notes on them.

She puts all of her powerpoints online with her notes from class on them.  Drops a test grade.  Don't underestimate webassign and don't let it be your learning experience.  Know how to do the chemistry before you do the webassign because it's 10% of your course grade.  It can cost you a letter grade if you aren't careful!
Four tests which can be hard, drop lowest. Online webassigns (homework) each week.
Really helpful if you are confused

obviously intro chem is never going to be a fun class but she was very nice and clear with her teaching style. Her tests were generally straightforward and were never harder than the hardest book problem.

Very montone, ef. read the book for btter understanding.  She is one of the nicest professors I have come in contact with at Carolina.  She really knows what she is talking about but sometimes has a hard time explaining.  If she gets to know your face you'll do better in th class, she favors kids she knows.

She meant well, but overall I would NOT recommend taking her class. She was nice and sincere and wanted you to understand, but material was covered so quickly in class that it had to be learned on the student's own time. The tests were frustrating, however she did give partial credit. Her review sessions were a joke.

she's nice and wants to help, but she relies on powerpoint pictures to teach for her. class is mainly an hour and a half of example problems that never seemed to help, to do well: teach yourself concepts and go to her for practice probs. the tests are hard and she will try to be sneaky with them

i got a b- in the class. it helps if you read what she's going to teach before she goes over it because lecture will either clarify what you've already read, help you figure out whether to ignore her or not based on you're understanding of the reading, or go over your head. class will put you to sleep but go when you can to get random hints.

She has a wonderful personality, and I always enjoyed talking to her.  Not the best teacher though.  Her exams can be very hard.  I never felt like I got a lot out of lecture.  I more or less taught the material to myself.
The monotone voice will put you to sleep. I did better on tests when I didn't go to class and taught myself the tests.
The class really isn't that bad. It's chemistry, it's supposed to be hard.

If you have a solid foundation in mathematics (did decent in anything involving calculus) then her teaching style might be frustrating for you. She tends to spend the entire hour doing sample problem after sample problem and focusing more on the mathematics behind the problems than the chemistry concepts.

She is wonderful about wanting to help her students, but like everyone has said above, her test are very tricky. Sometimes so tricky that she tricks herself. She will put you to sleep in lectures, but she is an incredibly nice lady who is like many other chemists and just isn't that great a teacher. She'll try to help you all day though.
Very helpful outside of class.

Compared to some of the other chem profs, Bleim is one of my favorites.  Tests are kinda tricky, but do like she says and work lots of problems before hand! She's entirely passable, and always available for help (she's great about email too) when you need it.

prof bliem was helpful and seemed to really care about her students. the only problem with her tests is how shes really tricky. also, she takes some of the multiple choice questions directly from the books website, so if you have time, look over those.

This class is hard but if you study, you should do fine. (She has office hours often and is pretty helpful.) The test are hard (mainly tricky, she likes to put trick questions) and often long, so it does take a while to finish.

She's really a nice person.  She is always available to help you when you need it.  The most difficult part is her exams, but you have the option of dropping your lowest one.  To do well on an exam honestly requires more work then its worth, so its really up to the individual.

She's a great chem teacher. Her tests are difficult, but if you make an effort and actually study and go to class (usually about 40% of our lecture class shows up for lecture) you will be ok. Lectures good and detailed.
Her lectures are very boring and her tests a pretty difficult. Wouldn't really recommend her class.
She's very available to help... webassigns were the most difficult part of class.  She's fair though.

Even though her lessons can be kind of boring, she really tries to teach the material, mostly on powerpoint though.  She'll say a lot of "funny" stuff during class, mostly morning humor that no one catches.
Monotone voice made it hard to want to learn or go to class at 8am.  Her tests were nearly impossible and asked a lot for a gen chem class.
No Comments
Ridiculous

I could genuinely listen to Professor Musachio talk for hours. He is knowledgeable and I found his lectures effective at conveying important connections. I found it amusing that he maintains a mysterious air around his background. This was a seminar, so readings and participation were most important, but he also gave several writing assignments.

There was a lot of readings to do outside of class, which weren't always enjoyable to parse, and were mostly philosophical. However, if you enjoy reading, want to improve your critical thinking, and like big class discussions (which could sometimes get off topic), then this is a really good class to take.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Professor Musachio's class. I initially chose the class because I thought it would be easy but it was a lot of reading and required a lot of participation (speaking up in class). However, even as a stem major, it was more enjoyable than I thought. Musachio is so passionate and you can see it in his lectures. Would recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Musachio is a really caring professor who makes discussion interesting and provides multiple opportunities for extra credit! His class was reading-heavy but discussion was easy to follow. Participation is really important. He always replies to emails fast and is always available for office hours.

I loved this class! He is an amazing professor and took the time to connect with each student. There is a lot of reading, but it is worth it. Opportunity for extra credit. Long lectures, but definitely worth it for a clearer understanding of the texts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Musachio is an excellent teacher. He's pretty traditional in his teaching methods, but makes every lecture fun and interesting. His class has A LOT of reading but it can be pretty interesting and its all important things to know. The discussions are based on the readings and he has a few quizzes, a midterm paper, and the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Musachio is overall an extremely caring and passionate professor, and very knowledgeable about many different realms of literature. The class itself wasn't too difficult, although there was a fair amount of reading. Would definitely recommend if you are interested in American literature and/or political science.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Really passionate about the content in the class, very old-timey, a bit silly. A lot of extra work and reading for a seminar, I would only suggest him if you're interested in the topic of the class. Also, grades by only a few quizzes, 2 papers, and participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Recommend everyone to take PSYC230 with Professor Chanon. Her lectures are clear and amazing and her grading is very generous, the grade is mostly determined by HW, participation and cumulative quiz and learning check( which can drop the lowest)

Love love love Dr. Chanon, she is the best!! I enjoyed her class so much, and it's genuinely been one of my favorite classes I've taken. She puts in a lot of effort into making it such a great experience.

I would love to say this is an awful class to get off her waitlists lol, but Dr. Chanon is an amazing professor. She's incredibly kind and personable and learns everyone's name, and her lectures are fun to attend. This class was mainly group project focused with that taking the place of the final, which I really enjoyed. 20/10 reccomend Dr. Chanon.
Dr. Chanon's lectures were really engaging, and she had a lot of demos that made class more fun. She also made the content easy to understand.

I love Vicki down! Super kind and cracked me up all semester. She learns everyone's names and her in-class participation is engaging and solidifies concepts. Exams are pretty straightforward, 2 homework drops, and quizzes that you can take until you get a 100. You can also miss 6 classes which is nice. Very easy class and an excellent prof.

Dr. Chanon is just a great professor. Super kind and enjoyable to be in class with. She has a weird attendance policy with the use of flashcards to answer in class questions and then you turn in the flashcard the same day so you will have to be ok with that. She'll learn everyone's names so that's nice.

One of my favorite professors I've had at UNC! Her lectures are very engaging including fun activities to understand the content. Her exams are very straightforward and she also offers a few extra credit opportunities. Also, one exam is dropped, and you can take the quizzes as many times as you want. I genuinely enjoyed going to her class :)

Dr. Chanon genuinely cares about her students, making an effort to know everyone's name, and she also makes class enjoyable to attend. There are a ton of interesting demonstrations that make lectures fun, and her grading scale is super chill. 3 exams, 1 dropped, weekly homework that will get full credit if completed, and the final.

I absolutely adore Dr. Chanon! She's hilarious and gets to know every student in her class (and our lecture was definitely more than 50 people)! She's really great about posting slideshows and recordings! Number one tip is to fill out the outlines for learning checks! The lowest learning check is dropped! Homeworks are pretty easy too!
Nice professor but the learning checks were hard for me and there was a lot of content on each one

LOVE HER super nice she learned everyone's name in a 100+ lecture, exams were super easy, attendance is mandatory via notecards you write on during class but for completion, lets you review exams in office hours, lectures recorded, hw one a week but rly easy, take her!!

AVOID AT ALL COST! Her teaching style was so confusing and inconsistent and never align with the textbook content order.  I spent most of my time just figuring out where the content she taught on the textbook. Her learning checks were one of the hardest STEM exam I have at UNC without any practice problem sets. DO NOT TAKE. SAVE YOUR GPA.

I loved going to this class because of Dr. Chanon. She is absolutely hilarious and so much fun to listen to. I really enjoyed the activities we did in class, they made the lectures engaging even when the content could be dull. Dr. Chanon, on the other hand, is never, ever dull. Also you get four absences, two homeworks, and one midterm dropped!

The class is super chill—graded based on weekly homework, a few quizzes, and a group project (you get to pick your group). Chanon is awesome. This is my third class with her and I honestly have nothing bad to say. She even says everyone should get an A.

Dr. Chanon was an amazing professor, probably one of the best I've had at UNC. She makes an effort to learn every students name (even in a class of over 100 students), is very understanding, and makes lectures fun. Homework and quizzes are guaranteed 100s, and the midterms and finals are easy. As long as you pay attention and try, you'll be fine.

dr chanon is so sweet, yes this class is kinda difficult, but as long as you put the work into it, you'll def do good, if you study hard for the final, you'll get an A, weekly hws, take home quizzes, 21/25 lectures need to be attended, 1 quiz and learning check is dropped, 2 hws are also dropped, def take it w her.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Chanon is so funny and upbeat! Attendance matters a lot and is mostly done by using notecards and answering questions. She is super knowledgable and honestly this class is very easy and straight forward especially if you prior knowledge of the nervous system and actually come to class.

Dr. Chanon is the Gold-Standard. Her lectures are engaging, grading criteria is clear & fair, & she gives you every opportunity to succeed. She cares about her students & will learn your name in a class of 200 students. I plan to take every class I can with her, and I recommend you do, too! She's the type of professor that changes students' lives.

Chanon is amazing, take her if you can! She genuinely cares about students understanding the material, not just memorizing it. Lots of opportunities to get your grade up and clear grading criteria. Really interesting lectures that are interactive and get you invested in the material.

Dr. Chanon was AMAZING. I was nervous for the class since I didn't think it'd be my strong suit, but she made it easy to learn and ask questions. Lectures are great and she also does a lot of helpful review. Attendance is technically mandatory but you get like 6 free absences. Tests are low-stakes and all multiple choice. Plus she's funny and nice!

Dr. Chanon is amazing. She structures grading so that you have wiggle room. Her lectures are incredibly entertaining with lots of activities. Her review for exams are very helpful. As long as you show up and put in effort you will do great. She's also super nice and hilarious.

Chanon is one of the best professors I have had at UNC. She learned everyone's names in an over 100 person class and made an effort to connect. She gave us countless opportunities to up our grade and class was so engaging. I could not recommend a class more!!!!

Dr. Chanon is an awesome professor! She really cares about you and made an effort to learn my name in a classroom of hundreds of students. Her classes were really engaging and helped you learn the material. The learning checks (midterms) and final were easy. Homework and quizzes are a guaranteed 100.

the content is medium/difficult and the exams are tricky, but she is easy to talk to and is more than willing to meet to help you understand the content. Even though the exams are tricky, there is a lot of flexibility in the grading and many opportunities to improve your grade! She's really engaging and overall a fun person!

Easily one of my favorite professors and classes! She makes an effort to learn your name, even among so many students, and she does a lot of in class activities to keep you engaged. She gives cumulative quizzes in between unit exams that you can take as many times as you want to get a 100, so getting a good grade is really attainable.

This was my third class with Dr. Chanon, and it was the easiest class I have taken of hers.  She made it easy for everyone to get an A (she literally said everyone should get an A in this class).  Half of your grade can easily be a 100 with HW and attendance.  Quizzes have simple questions, and she allows retakes.  Group project was fun too.

Dr. Chanon is the absolute best professor! She is so organized and considerate of students, making it really easy to manage her class. This 490 was on Animal Sensation/Perception which is a new class and it was super interesting. Highly recommend!

Dr. Chanon was one of my favorite professors this semester! The class structure involves attending class, taking notes, weekly quizzes, and 3 exams. You can drop your lowest scores in attendance, quizzes, and exams! She is super engaging and made cognitive psychology fun. The exams were super straightforward and reasonable.
Dr. Chanon is amazing!! I genuinely learned so much and enjoyed doing it. She's pretty lenient in terms of attendance/exam grades so it's not difficult to get a good grade with minimal effort.

This was my 2nd class with Dr. Chanon, but first online class with her over the summer.  Class was organized well, and there was plenty of wiggle room for participation.  Assignments and LCs were same difficulty, maybe a bit easier than her in-person class.  Would recommend any class with Chanon

Dr. Chanon is AMAZING. She tries very hard to make her lectures interactive so that students can relate to the information that she is teaching. Despite the lecture hall being massive, she makes an effort to put a face to every name, and is there for her students to help them. All tests are based entirely on lectures, which are recorded.

Awesome, Awesome, Awesome! This class has a lot of content but she makes learning easier and fun (she is so funny)! There is HW, 2 online quizzes (can retake many times), 3 tests (one dropped), and a final! The exams were not terrible, as long as you take good notes and do the learning objectives/outlines. The final was easier than her tests! DO IT

Awesome Professor! Truly cares about her students. She learned all the names for a 100 or so person class. There are 3 exams and one is dropped! As well, as a final that was somewhat easier than the other exams! This has been one of my favorite classes at UNC, and I feel like I learned a lot!

Dr. Chanon is amazing! Her grading is based off HW assignments, 2 cumulative quizzes (which you can retake to get a 100!), exams, and a final! Her exams were pretty straightforward as long as you took note of important things she says in class and look over the learning objectives. She is also really funny and learned all of our names! Not a hard A

The absolute best professor I've had at UNC! Dr. Chanon is so caring and very accessible, definitely a teacher to the core. She and the TAs provide plenty of review materials, and the homework assignments aren't too demanding. Her grading criteria are also very clear and there's a lot of flexibility. Very funny, highly respected, overall 10/10!

Love Vicki! She is so kind and hilarious in class. The homework and tests are pretty easy. I would recommend buying the book (if you really want it), taking pictures of all the pages, and then returning it for all your money back at the UNC Student Store. Textbook pretty much goes over everything in class - so maybe I'm just extra.

Dr. Chanon is amazing! She's so sweet, and she tries her best to get to know everyone in the class.  Content was fun, and all assignments were chill.  She has a nice grading system; you can drop lowest midterm and 2 HWs.  HW was graded nicely.  The final was easier compared to midterms/LCs.  Make sure to study a bit. We got 1 point EC for final.

I thought it was a tough class content-wise, especially compared to her PSYC 230 class. But, Dr. Chanon still has teaching down to a science and is an engaging lecturer. Her grading system is incredibly reasonable too, just make sure you really put in the work for the exams. The final is easy compared to them!
Every lecture was incredibly engaging and she taught the material really well. They were also recorded and posted if you missed a day. Really fair tests too.

She was such a caring professor and I rly want to take another class with her before I graduate! She learned everyone's names (and our class is over 100 people)!! It's a lot of material, but she makes it manageable for sure!

Dr. Chanon is my favorite professor so far at UNC. She cares so much about her students and responds to emails very quickly. Her grading system is very forgiving. Her exams are very straight forward. Plus, she practically does reviews every day. She also makes the lectures interesting by making what we learned relatable. Highly recommend!!!

Professor Chanon is one of the best professors ever. She learned all her ~100 students' names within the first few weeks of class. Her lectures are well-organized, engaging, and fun. Cognitive Psychology requires lots of memorization, but she makes it durable for her students. I have so many good things to say about her. Highly recommend!

I loved this course! The content was interesting and Dr. Chanon is an amazing lecturer! She really wants all her students to succeed. She was more than fair with all assignments. The workload was manageable. I recommend this class to anybody.

Dr. Chanon is one of the best professors at UNC. She is positive and encouraging toward her students and clearly wants to see everyone succeed. Her tests are pretty straightforward and the posted recorded lectures are great for studying. She was super understanding and flexible with attendance and assignment grading.

Professor Chanon is really kind and caring. The material wasn't that bad, but she teaches it very well. There are 3 exams but 1 is dropped, and they are pretty easy. As long as you pay attention in class and do the assignments, you will get an A.

Dr. Chanon is super sweet and she teaches the material very well. I felt like I actually learned a lot from her class. You have easy homework due every Friday, 3 exams (1 is dropped), and a few quizzes but you can use your notes. The material is a little hard, but she explains in very well. Tests are fair.

I loved Dr. Chanon! She's super passionate about neuroscience and she was always ready to answer our questions. The workload was very manageable and the tests were fair. She cares a lot about her students and consistently updates us about the class. Make sure to keep up with the content! Definitely take this class with Dr. Chanon, she's the best!

One of the best at UNC! The way she set up her class was perfect. I feel like I genuinely learnt a lot from the class- the material stuck all semester. Content is cool and she gives great lectures. The 3 tests are kinda challenging but you drop one and the final is easy in comparison. You can miss up to 6 classes without penalty but should catch up

Professor Chanon is a great professor. Textbook was not required for the course and lectures covered all the material that we were tested on. Chanon made this course very stress free and her learning checks were great preparation for the final. She sets this class up for your success and it is easy to pass if you put in the effort!

Dr. Chanon is so incredible it makes me emotional. In a way, I literally felt like her office was a safe space for me because of how caring and helpful she was. She has kids which I think helps her have even more of a heart for college students & their well-being. Her lectures are amazing, the class is very organized, and she is so accessible!

Dr. Chanon is super sweet. The class was not super difficult so long as you study (especially for the learning checks!) The unique part of this class is the UX BeAM project, which while tedious at times was pretty cool to do. There is pretty regular homework, but you don't necessarily have to read the book. Be sure to study the learning goals!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She was great! It was online and asynchronous, but I still felt very engaged with the class. She also made the material super easy to understand. I have no complaints about her or this class!

Professor Chanon is funny and so relatable. She is also very caring. Her exams are easy and she accommodates her students well. I would without a doubt take more classes with her, she makes the content very interesting and has her students engage in a way that actually helps.The class content is hard at times but her exams are easy and minimal work

Dr. Chanon truly gives students all the guidance and materials we need to succeed in her class. Her class is well organized, you have decent cushioning for your grades, and most importantly, she's a great lecturer and is really good at breaking down concepts in easy to understand language.

I love Dr. Chanon so much I would give her my first born child. The material is not easy but she makes it so understandable and her exams are a direct reflection of what is taught. Amazing professor and incredibly helpful to anyone wanting to get into research. Take her for a class if you can!

Dr. Chanon is an amazing professor. She gives you exactly what information you need to know for the exams. If you miss class, you can still get participation credit and lectures are posted online, so that was very accommodating. She genuinely wants you to learn and has everything structured very well. You will definitely get an A if you study well!
Vicki Chanon is wonderful. This class was a bit of work (studying, the usual) but she is very flexible with having online lectures posted and participation credit.

Fantastic prof. I highly recommend her for Learning. She is a veteran and has teaching down to a science. She is also fun, pleasant, and makes lectures highly interactive. The class was also not challenging, if that's your thing.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Most organized class I have ever taken. 100% take this class if you can and if not take it the semester after. Dr. Chanon is an amazing lecturer and is SO understanding and genuinely cares. Anybody can take this class and do well, she has it structured so amazingly. I always knew my grades and always felt supported.

Dr. Chanon's a fantastic instructor. This course specifically is laid out well and all of the assignments are presented on a very easy-to-grasp schedule. Dr. Chanon teaches with an enthusiasm and clear interest in the material that makes it easy to be interested yourself. Highly recommend taking a class or two with her!

The absolute epitome of what a professor should be! The entire class is structured so that you know exactly what to expect, when assignments are due, how assignments need to be done, what you REALLY need to know for the exams, and all of that is laid out in the least stressful way possible! Dr. Chanon actually cares unlike most professors at UNC.

Dr. Chanon is absolutely amazing! Not only was the content and the demos so interesting but also very accommodating as well. She is very supportive and pushes you to do your very best! If you are stem, consider majoring in neuroscience and take her!!!

Professor Chanon's NSCI 225 class is an example of a remote async class done right. She was accessible all semester, was great with feedback, never blindsided us with exam questions, and had forgiving grading policies. Considering that this is a demo-heavy class, it's probably the toughest type of class to do remotely, but she did incredibly well.

Ive had Dr. Chanon for nsci 222,225 and now 330. I LOVED this class. Well made asynchronous lessons, fair quizzes/learning checks, extra credit and test corrections, and a super fun human centered design project with the makerspaces. Dr. Chanon is a phenomenal teacher and PSYC 330 was an awesome class

I normally don't like async courses but this one (cog sci) was outstanding. Dr. Chanon builds in so many opportunities for active learning into class and was very organized with course content, even making a due date list on Sakai. Really enjoyed the diverse guest speakers, makerspace UX project, group activities and cool readings. Take Dr. Chanon!

Dr. Chanon is awesome! Her lectures are very engaging, and she is an incredibly reasonable grader. The textbook is optional, and you are graded on attendance, weekly homework assignment, non-cumulative quizzes, cumulative quizzes (can take more than once), and the cumulative final. Her class is designed to really help you learn the material!

Knows how to teach in a pandemic and is intentional about assigning easy work that supplements core concepts. Open note tests/quizzes with lax time limits. Easy participation questions and homework assignments. Allows flexibility by letting your drop a certain number of assignments. Very effective teacher who is passionate about her work.

Dr. Channon was the only professor I had who truly understood and respected the fact that we are in a pandemic. Her lectures were all recorded and to get participation credit you had to answer a couple of questions throughout the lectures. Her quizzes and exams were open-note and you could take her quizzes many times to get 100.

Chanon is a GEM! I absolutely love her. She has such a nice personality and she really cares about her students. I wish we weren't online this semester because I would've really enjoyed having her in person. Exams/quizzes are open-note so that takes the pressure off, but the info you learn is very interesting and she makes it easy to understand!
She's simply the most fantastic online instructor I've had at UNC yet, and I'm sure her in person class would be much of the same. Absolutely recommended, take NSCI225 with her!

Dr. Chanon is amazing! She is knowledgable and incredibly caring. Her tests, and her class overall, are incredibly fair. Her online class flows really well and is super easy to keep up with. All assignments build off of each other and are meant to help you solidify the material. 10/10 recommend any class with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I had her before in psyc 330. both classes are super easy and interesting. Her classes do overlap somewhat but that is to be expected with the content. Great lecturer and super engaging. Study a little bit and you'll do great. 10/10

Dr. Chanon is a great professor especially given the circumstances. However, the online class felt like a lot of busy work. Homework was often barely related to the content or seemed silly. The due dates for homework were also a little inconsistent, so make sure you double check due dates. Overall she was super nice and the class was fine.

Dr. Channon is an AMAZING professor and person! She has a kind heart and made my first semester at UNC the best it could be considering COVID. Her online lectures is structured beautifully and I cannot stress how fair of professor she is. I wish I had her for in person to know her more since she is my favorite prof at UNC. I will miss her def :(

I adore Professor Chanon, and I'm trying so hard to get another class with her, but they're all full. Her lectures are really interesting and interactive. She has a very forgiving grading and attendance policy. She also responds quickly to emails, and makes a good effort to get to know students -- even in large lecture halls. Would def recommend.

This was online, but her Sakai site was beautifully done and her lectures were clear, interactive, and accessible. It was obvious that she put a ton of care into making sure that we still got a great learning experience. This is a nerdy thing to say, but the class was... can I even say that it was too easy? I felt like I could have learned more.

Dr. Channon is amazing! Her tests are very fair (+1 is dropped) and her lectures are enjoyable. She was very understanding and organized when we moved to online learning, as she was in the classroom. She makes an effort to know everyones name and encourages participation. 222/225/230 are great classes and I recommend Dr. Channon for them!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Chanon is amazing as a person and a professor. She is very accessible outside of class too, but honestly if you pay attention in lectures and take good notes and study, you should be fine. She never tries to trick you on exams and while there is some homework, they're usually easy while also helping you learn. 10/10 would recommend.
Chanon is an absolute gem!! One of the sweetest professors I've had at UNC. PSYC 230 was an easy A and is so so interesting. 10/10 recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Chanon is amazing!! I had her for NSCI 225 and PSYC 230. Very clear in what is going to be on the exam and easy to follow during lecture with all the demos. She gave homework once a week and does PollEv in class for participation.. As long as you study from the guides she makes and your notes, you should be good for the exams!

Super fun and easy professor! Her PSYC 230 class is super engaging. There are homework assignments every week but theyre easy and it helpful to know for the exam. Participation is required so as long as youre good with that, you can get an A in the class! Exams were fair, just use her study guide that she makes and you will get an A!
Dr. Chanon is amazing. She is very clear with her class and is always helpful with any questions you may. I cannot recommend her enough and she always makes class as enjoyable as possible!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr Chanon was such a great professor. She made the class really fun and enjoyable with her demos throughout the semester. She also gives you all the tools you need to be successful. Highly recommend!

This is the best class I have taken at UNC. Dr. Chanon is an incredible professor who connects concepts from psychology to your daily life, making the class super interesting. I would take as many classes as I could with Dr. Chanon. For tests, studying your notes from class is more than enough. You won't regret taking this class!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Chanon is a really great professor. She is very helpful, and really cares about your success in her class. She is always accessible and holds office hours every weak which are helpful if you dont understand the material. Her tests can be hard, so be prepared to study, but overall I really enjoyed the class.

Dr. Chanon is amazing! I will say if you dont pay attention in class, take notes, & don't study this class can be hard. It may be easier for those people who have a strong neuroscience background (I didnt) I have gone to her office hours & she was always so helpful & caring. Exams can be easy when you study and she is never trying to trick you.

Prof Chanon goes through lectures SO FAST AND IS HORRIBLE AT EXPLAINING CONCEPTS. Then when you go to read through the slides to understand the material better, she has no explanation on the slides. Her tests are way too hard considering there is no explanation anywhere online to learn from. I wish I could put her at half speed during lectures.

Dr. Chanon is the best instructor that I had at UNC I took two of her classes, and she is an excellent instructor. She includes plenty of spaced practice so you don't forget earlier material. Her exams make up a large portion of the grade, but if you pay attention and try you will do well. Her lectures are interesting and she does fun demos.

Easy class if you pay attention in lecture. Dr. Chanon is so sweet and cute! She is kind of shy but warms up after the first few weeks and tries really hard to make the material fun. She's good for 222 and 225!

Dr. Chanon is a GREAT prof. I took learning psychology with her last semester, and now I have her for sensation and perception. She sets up the class to be very lenient towards absences and drops one exam grade plus three homework grades at the end of the year. She is also cute and engaging and seems to really match the mood of her students!

I lOVE Dr. Chanon. The material in the class was somewhat hard to understand at first but I always understood it after she lectured on it. As long as you read most of the assigned textbook readings and pay attention, this class is super interesting and easy to do well in.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I had Sensation and Perception psychology with her. She was a good teacher, but I think the material just happened to be a little dry. She did her best to spice it up though, and there were many interesting activities sprinkled throughout the semester.
I took Dr. Chanon for 225 as well. She's really nice, funny, and helpful, but her exams are pretty difficult. Be ready to study for those.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: He is amazing!!! Super clear and organized on everything!!! Gives practice exams everytime which have very similar problems to the tests. Love to give partial credits.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: amazing professor and lecturer, plus hes pretty cute and has a nice accent

Absolutely incredible teacher with clear guidelines, a student-centered grading policy, and great accessibility outside class. Clearly understands what he's doing and works to make sure you do as well.

He is extremely smart, but kind of goes beyond the course material to explain what can be done in further math classes (which is great for math majors, just not my thing). 2 midterms and a final, final can replace the lowest midterm. A bunch of homework sheets that are way harder than the exam questions. Super nice guy with plenty of office hours.

I love Tom. Amazing lectures that really made the content make sense. Posted notes were neat as a pin. Second midterm and final were hard, but totally worth it to have him as a lecturer. Highly recommend for math majors
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Chandler's a super well-organized prof with amazing lectures, and the content isn't too hard. He's definitely passionate about the class and wants everyone to learn/pass. Homeworks and practice exams aren't too difficult and prepare you well for exams. Strongly recommend taking 383 with him, it'd be a mistake not to. Also take linear algebra first!

British, lively, and efficient at explaining concepts and clearing up confusion. He shares his lecture notes, and practice sets mirror his brief, straightforward exams. Graded by weekly HW, two midterms, and a HARD non-cumulative final that replaces your lowest midterm.
Really enthusiastic and passionate about what he was teaching, made class super interesting and enjoyable. Only graded by weekly problem sets, two midterms and HARD final exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best math class I've ever taken! Classes are extremely structured to really make you understand the concepts, beyond just knowing the right equations/methods. Very smart guy, but explains it clearly. Office hours are extremely helpful. Weekly homeworks and midterms are only 4 questions, very similar to the practice. Definitely take him if you can!

Super engaging professor. I would only recommend you take him if you are a math major. He dives very deep into theory and as a non-math major myself I found it hard to follow. Exams are just four questions and the second one is a lot harder than the first. Very application based as well, which I enjoyed.
I love this maf man!

The GOAT. Pretty funny guy, and tries to make lectures as engaging as possible. You will definitely succeed as long as you put some effort into this class. I would definitely take him again. Tests weren't that hard too and he really goes out of his way to make sure you get the concepts. 10/10

Some of my classmates weren't big fans of Prof Cabrera -- but I liked him! While a little unorganized/inconsistent, Prof Cabrera clearly cared about his students and was a good and understanding grader. He has a great personality and elicits very interesting class discussions.

This class wasn't too bad. He cares about his students and tries his best to implement practices that help students in areas they are struggling. If you do the work and study for test you will be fine.

As someone who hadn't taken Spanish in years but was placed into 203, Cabrera was a great professor who truly cares about the success of his students and was very lenient. He was super chill and we had fun in his class, so definitely try to take a class with him, if available.
He is a great professor and definitely tries to make the class as enjoyable as possible I would highly recommend taking him, participating is so so important and he is funny
Great professor, the classes in span 203 were great and the homework wants too difficult. Make sure to study well for the tests and you will have a great time in the class!

Great guy and really kind. The only class this semester that I actually looked forward to going to. You can tell he really cares about his students, and he always brought a chill energy to class which was really nice. Explained Spanish in a simple way which was easy for me to understand :)
He's great, Spanish at UNC is hard in general but Cabrera is lenient and tries to work with you.
Prof. Cabrera was an awesome professor. He made Spanish more fun and engaging. It is clear he cares about each of his students, and he grades a lot based on your effort in the class.

Chemistry at UNC is extremely challenging, but Shepard finds a way to make it better. He is very kind and helpful in explaining difficult topics. I will say that we often get behind in lectures, but I didn't have too much of a problem with it since you'll have everything in time for exam day. Loved him and his dogs!

Dr. Shepard is passionate about chemistry, and he is very kind. However, his lecture style does NOT help you better understand the material. He will start class by talking about his dogs, and we are always behind in lecture. We typically talk about material from a day or two before. You'd be better off taking 101 with another professor.

Chem 101 is notoriously difficult but standardized, so it has nothing to do with the professor. Dr. Shepard is super kind and always encourages class participation. He's a great teacher and seems like he genuinely cares about students and ULs. Love hearing his dog stories and analogies!
Only went to his GPSS sessions and he's great. Doesn't make you feel bad for not understanding the content

I have taken 420, 425, 525, and 490 with Dr. Roark. He's the best professor I've had in my time at UNC. The QFE is the most valuable experience I've had in the department. I would recommend taking any class with Dr. Roark.
Roark's QFE is the most valuable program in the econ department

Professor Roark is great! I've had him for both 420 & 425. He is generous with curves, accessible, and provides PLENTY of test prep. There are weekly assignments, but he will sometimes extend deadlines. Had an injury I was out for a month for, so he met with me via zoom to keep up. Hard content, but if you do hw will do fine. Take with Roark!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I like this better than 420, and he's genuinely a really nice guy which makes it a lot better. It isn't super easy content, but my complaint is really just that he makes the homework sometimes unnecessarily hard. One question will be completely fine, easy even, and then the next has math so convoluted that a TI-84 can't process it. Just annoying.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I generally liked Roark. The structure of the class was logical, and content built so by the end I still remembered early stuff for the final. It's not a super easy class, but I preferred it to 410 and thought it was a little more intuitive. Lots of graphs, and some math like derivatives and iffy algebra. I did feel like it got harder throughout.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I did not enjoy 420 with Dr. Roark. Lectures are quite boring and there are plenty of mistakes on his slides. We also did't solve a lot of practice questions and mostly focused on theories. Midterms 1 and 2 were fine, but the final exam was extremely difficult and tanked my grade. Homework grading is quite harsh as well.

Roark is a caring professor and the goat grading-wise, but I'm not sure I love his teaching style. He's clearly a macro expert. However, during lectures he often skipped math steps or implicit assumptions about the concepts he was teaching, which made it difficult to follow. I had to become an EconAid warrior and teach myself some concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Roark is a great person; he cares about his students, and it shows throughout his class. However, his lectures are heavily based on the theory of Macro, and he does not explain much of the math behind the theory. The exams are difficult, but his grading scale makes the class easy to pass. Be prepared to teach yourself some of the concepts.

Roark is an expert in this field and I enjoyed this more than 420! I'm in QFE so I'll be taking 525 with him next semester too. Exams are hard and there is only one midterm. He drops one problem set and the last one is graded for completion. Group investment project which is a grade booster but also annoying to deal with if you have bad groupmates.
Slides, problem wording, and grading criteria were super confusing.

Roark is a super nice guy and very helpful. Only gripe is that he spent a lot of time on topics which weren't tested at times which meant some important concepts (like fed policy) were rushed. 

Overall the exams are difficult but doable. You have to be proactive and address uncertainties early or you will fall behind.

This guy is a total beast. Very generous with curves and willing to answer any question. Very available to students and honestly just an expert at macro. Don't know why I got on the final but very easy to do well if you put in some effort

Prof. Roark can be a little bit disorganized and confusing at times, but he is a super nice guy whose humor is often misunderstood. If you are engaged in this class and ask questions when things become unclear you will succeed. Definitely not an easy class, but there is no reason to avoid Roark when signing up. Making friends in class will help.
The only people who liked this class are the ones who do not care about their grades. I actually had a stroke trying to understand all the contradictory points in the materials.
he does a good job of making a bad class ok. he wants everyone to succeed and came to our office hours despite being sick.

IM WRITING THIS AS IM STUDYING FOR MY FINAL EXAM. PLS DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE WITH HIM. Chris is a chill person and hes funny but his lectures are SO UNORGANIZED. I actually studied so hard for the midterm but the materials he gave were super confusing and I got a B. Compared to Chris Handy and MSA, this class was x100000 more unorganized.

Very disorganized class, no clear grading expectations, and very passive aggresive with students. Thinks he's funny (he's not). The class itself is an amalgamation of idiosyncratic economic teaching that is not found anywhere but his lecture hall, so good luck studying outside of class. However, curve is forgiving. Overall just a "meh" class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Many self-contradictory points on the slides...
Was a sleeper class. Not that much work, just study problem sets before exams.

Dr. Roark is a fun professor and an overall good guy. Highly recommend going to office hours regularly (Roark or TA/ULA) to discuss homework questions and exam review material, as 420 can be unintuitive sometimes. Class is curved generously so that the median is a B+. Biweekly assignments + textbook readings not required ⇒ relatively light workload

Professor Roark is the best! He really cares about his students' learning and success– don't be afraid of this class if you take it with him. It's also curved so much and he posts a lot of practice tests and past exams. Super funny.

Dr. Roark's lectures are a little messy and hard to follow and his multiple choice grading is frustrating. But macro is just not intuitive, and I think that's why 420 is so challenging. His curve is generous though, and he is accessible outside of class in office hours and on CampusWire. He answers questions well in class.

Would give 0/5 if I could. Bad lectures, confusing MC questions with the worst grading system for them ever, passive-aggressive, unhelpful TAs and office hours, need I say more? If you have any reason to take this class, take it with another prof if possible. You will save both your GPA and your life.

He is a super personable professor. Really cares about student learning and wants us to succeed. The curve (already in the syllabus) is really generous. Its a hard class but the practice exams he gave were super similar to the actual exams, a lot of it is a matter of reasoning through a problem which was fun

I think some of these reviews, while containing valid criticisms, are a bit harsh. Yeah, he does make a decent amount of mistakes, but he's pretty flexible with deadlines and shifts them around to account for errors on his end. The curve is pretty generous as well, and I personally didn't find this course as taxing as 410. Also a personable dude.
Ngl I think people give him 1 just because they screwed up their exams. Overall a nice and approachable guy with some humor. Helps are available on campuswire and Econ aid center.
It is a difficult class, but Roark and the ULAs and TAs want to help you pass and do well. Just use the practice material, and you will do fine.

grading scale isn't terrible like some other Econ courses, decent guy just comes across as odd sometimes. never went to office hours but am currently passing with an ok grade so not the worst class just do the practice exams he gives they're almost identical to the actual ones. also relearn algebra tricks because its heavy on the exams sometimes.

Funny how as soon as a 1/5 rating appears, it's followed by at least two 5/5s to inflate the overall rating. If it's not obvious enough, those 5/5s are from trolls, or the few people who actually liked this class. 

Pros: Responds to CampusWire questions quickly
Cons: Arrogant, terrible grading system, near useless lectures, mistakes EVERYWHERE

Really hard class, but not impossible. Roark cares about his students, he can get frustrated when people are not understanding concepts, but this is fair since his office hours are usually pretty empty...if you are struggling go get help!!! The econ aid center almost always has someone to help with 420.
This class is not as difficult as people make it seem. It is a lot of work, but it is manageable, and tests are curved if people struggle.
Really kind, cares about his job and his students. It is a hard class, as all econ classes at UNC are, but Roark does a great job being available for students and is always patient and respectful.
AVOID AT ALL COSTS! If you need to take this class, take it over the summer with literally anyone else.

Didn't curve any tests when I had him. Awful wording on HW and test questions. MC system is the worst I have ever seen. Very passive aggressive and will not hesistate to humiliate you in front of the whole class for things you didn't even do.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: didnt like his teaching methods, his "multiple choice" grading is the worst I've ever seen and the lectures and slideshows don't help that much without added notes and teachings on top of it. didn't enjoy the class at all but I managed to pass it, will not retake with roark ever again.

I loved this class and I love Chris, had him for 420 as well and that was much harder for me since it was a lot less intuitive. Graded by 6 homeworks (1dropped, 1 for completion), a midterm, final, and an easy prospectus project.

Roark is a chill guy, he's pretty understanding and fair when it comes to grading, this course is just hard to perform well in for a lot of students. Make sure to do practice problem sets/exams before tests and you should be fine. Go to office hours and go to class!
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I think he gets way too much hate tbh. Had him for 420, and I think the content in that class is just not intuitive hence the ratings... but he was awesome for 425! Super active on CampusWire and made a 3:30 class bearable. While he does make a lot of /mistakes, he's pretty chill about correcting them and willing to help clarify anything confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Difficult exams with a final worth 35% of your grade. The slides are incomprehensible sometimes and Roark would often make mistakes whether it be the answer keys, slide information, or hw question wording. He seems to know what he's talking about but has difficulty relaying the info. He can be extremely passive aggressive when answering questions.

Roark really cares about students engaging with and learning the material. He is very accessible and wants to help. The investment project is super fun and a grade booster. The tests are as to be expected, but if you can do the problem sets then you will be fine, utilize the practice sets. Don't get the textbook it wasn't necessary.
I loved this class! Learned a lot and he really cares about students. Lenient with deadlines and just wanted us to participate. Not easy exams, but to be expected in upper level Econ.

Roark got upset with our lecture for not being enthusiastic enough (mind you - it was during a semester when many students' families were suffering in W. North Carolina). Tests were pretty hard and it took months for homework grades to be returned so you couldn't really use those to study. He lets you drop a couple hw grades though

Don't really get the other reviews. I sat on my phone pretty much every day and learned through the slides and homework. Wound up with mid 90s on just about everything.

I thought he was entertaining and was able to communicate well. His slides and other resources (i.e. previous hws) were everything I needed. Generally don't do well in econ either.

Overall lectures are confusing, problem sets only minimally help solidify concepts taught in lectures, and his responses to questions on campuswire are often vague. Chill guy but not great at helping to understand material which is already difficult. Takes up time trying to be funny at least once every lecture but speeds through difficult concepts.

Very nice and funny guy but something about his teaching style just didn't click with me. I often left class feeling even more confused. Answers questions but, again, answers just didn't usually click, which is dangerous in a class like 420 where the material is hard to wrap your head around. EconAid Center was also unhelpful, unfortunately.
Get ready for Mr. Grumpy.-and by that the most entertaining and quirky professor you'll ever have. Can't believe this guy is so polarizing, his lectures are straight comedy.
I kid you not I've had to copy-paste his slides into ChatGPT with the prompt "Reword to be more clear and easier to understand" at least a hundred times.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Good guy and it's obvious he tries, but his lecture slides are genuinely the worst slides I have ever seen in my entire life. They are border-line indecipherable and are rarely helpful for studying. If you're unlucky enough to miss a lecture, you might as well just not try to understand the material you missed because the slides won't help at all.
Genuinely the worst professor I have ever had. And not a good person either

He has to curve the class by 10-20 points at the end of the semester because everyone performs so poorly. Homeworks are insanely hard and lectures are comprised of bullet point slides that are extremely hard to follow. I recommend just ignoring anything in lecture and teaching yourself. The overall quality of this class is horrendous.

I'm a micro person, so class was kinda hard but not too bad. Lectures weren't helpful, too fast, not recorded, didn't really explain things well. STILL don't know half of my HW grades. Roark was kinda condescending and tried to be relatable but it was just a bit weird. Seems like a fine guy, but teaching style didn't work for me

Roark is an awesome guy, hard to get close to him in a 200 person class, but he's super easy to talk to and is funny/down to earth. Tests aren't too difficult compared to content, averages were in the B range. ECON aid center is super helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are really bad. The slides aren't easy to follow on your own, he moves way too fast, and then will randomly ramble about nothing for 5 minutes. It's honestly easier to just not pay attention in class and try to figure out the homework on your own, vs trying to use what you learned from his lectures to do the homework.

Chris is a great guy, really cares about all his students and their success. Macro was very tough for me, not as easy to conceptualize as micro. I made a 42 on the first exam and finished with a B-. If you put in the work, you can easily make an A.

Dr. Roark is my favorite professor in the econ department. He is super accessible outside of class, curves generously, and his exams reflect the in-class practice problems and homework sets. It is also clear he really cares about his students, and I found him to be generally pretty funny. He made class engaging and worthwhile.

Professor Roark is great. I was really struggling in this course and was failing for first 12 weeks, ended up finishing with a C+. Roark assured me that as long as I did my best, I would pass the class. Very nice professor who wants the best for his students!

Prof Roark does a decent job of explaining things but could be a lot more concise and clear in his explanations. Problem sets were easy enough and tests were very fair and closely resembled problem sets and practice exams.

Roark genuinely cares about his students and wants to see them succeed, he gives helpful and quick responses on Campuswire, all of his exam questions pull from concepts you will have seen on a real/practice problem set, which have useful answers and grading criteria. TA's also give helpful feedback for psets, go to office hours and ask questions!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super smart guy, not the best professor. Can be rude sometimes when you ask questions but he still likes when people engage in lecture. If you are afraid of taking this class like I was, don't be. Dr. Roark curves GENEROUSLY on exams. My best advice would be to complete entire problem sets in TA/ULA office hours!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I found this class to be comparable to 410, its a lot of material that econ majors need to know to succeed. Roark does his best to give lectures and problem sets designed to teach more than we will be tested on so we have the best chance of success. Roark is funny, engaging, and intelligent, I enjoyed his lectures, and found office hours useful.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I've taken 3 courses with Roark (420, 425, 525/493) and he's a good professor. He gives engaging lectures, though sometimes confusing, and he's very personable. He designed a good curriculum for this class that reinforced concepts from 425 and built new skills, such as research and programming. Overall, this is an interesting and useful course.

I don't know if he personally understand what he was talking about. Going to office hour will just make you more confused. He was inconsistent with what he said, which is the key why so many people though this class was hard.

Overall he is a great professor, but sometimes the way he explained was really confusing. I have 17 credits this semester but i spent nearly all my free time with this course. it's hard to get an A, but A- is easy because you got it when overall grade was 86

Professor Roark is a solid professor who I think has gotten a lot better considering the reviews for him the past few semesters. He is a bit all over the place at times and his problem sets can be very tricky and graded a bit harshly. However he makes up for it with the midterms being a lot easier and straightforward (which he himself admits).

He's a definitely qualified professor as in he knows what he's talking about conceptually, but the way he formats and words his slides can give you a massive headache. You'll also have to read through some grammatical errors that can sometimes make learning the material more frustrating.
So far best pf in econ department

Dr. Roark is a little scatterbrained and his lectures move quickly. Yet, he's a great person who cares about his teaching. Homeworks are difficult, yet the tests are relatively easy (he even admits that). He's accessible at office hours which helps. Just work in groups on assignments and he gives a lot of practice problems that help for exams.

Roark is a great guy and a great professor. 420 is hard, but it's clear that he really wants all of his students to succeed. He's super funny and accessible. Just make sure you study a lot for exams and do as many practice problems as you can. You don't really need the textbook because his powerpoints are pretty comprehensive.

Roark cares a lot about his students and has been restructuring his class to make it as fair and manageable as possible. His exams are hard and you will have to study a LOT, but if you have this expectation going into it, you will be okay. Definitely utilize campuswire and your ULA's. Don't fall behind and ask him questions, he wants to help.

Prof. Roark genuinely wants you to do good. He assigns weekly problem sets + there are 2 midterms and a final. You need a very holistic understanding of the material to do good on his exams. If you utilize practice questions, past papers and attend class, you'll do fine. He also answers every Campuswire question he gets, and curves generously.

The second half of this semester is more difficult than the first half, but still doable. I unfortunately was sick for three weeks and fell behind in all my classes.
