There are plenty of practice resources. He tries his best to help you but the class is just too big for only one professor. The ULAs are your best resources.

I second the wholesome sentiment and enjoyed generous curves, but too many mistakes on in-class examples and problem sets for me to feel Roark is an authority. Just teach yourself the content from more thorough sources and hope the content transfers. Encouraging "game theory" on multiple choice is also goofy.

Roark is nice, but class is Hard with a capital H. Go to office hours to compare PS and USE CAMPUSWIRE! He answers so fast basically texting him. Multiple choice grading system SUCKSSSS. Never got above a 33% on an MC section. 54 on first midterm, and ~70% on the others, still ended with a B. Big overall curve. Good luck econ majors stay strong.

For Econ 420 you should review the slides and all relevant practice problems (he gives past problem sets and exams for review prior to each test). Additionally the textbook is helpful if you are confused on a topic and need a more in depth explanation, however he does not completely follow the textbook and to excel in the course it is not required.

He's a caring prof and explains things pretty clearly. The material can be challenging and confusing, but he's always willing to help. The exams can be difficult, and sometimes there are problems that feel unfairly difficult (i.e. we never did such difficult problems in homework), but if everyone does poorly, he curves, so don't stress.

He's a great professor who clearly knows his stuff. He's very funny, very accessible, and kind to everyone. The class is by no means easy, but he offers a generous curve. The workload is relatively light, but it is in your best interest to study throughout the semester.

Roark is the saving grace of UNCs econ department and one of few professor I look forward to taking again. He is good at explaining concepts although he can sometimes make things more complex than they need to be. He is extremely helpful and responsive via email/office hours/campus wire and genuinely wants students to do well. Also pretty funny.

Roark is a genuinely nice guy and cares a lot. I'll be honest though, his natural teaching abilities are pretty horrid. He has extreme difficulties explaining simple concepts, and most of the time comes off as condescending/sarcastic when he isn't even trying to. He makes this class more difficult than it needs to be but that's the whole department

Nice Guy. That being said, on test reviews and during tests there is stuff that wasn't really in the lecture. He tests for a complete understanding of the material. But, homework is not like this. He doesn't teach the understanding of the concepts well. Tests are harder than the reviews and problem sets by a good margin which is hard to study for.

Good guy. Course Material is tough and he was a fairly new professor when I took the class. You can tell he continues to grow and learn the more he teaches the material. ULAs were helpful. Was accommodating and held office hours for assignments. Generous curve at the end of the semester, so don't panic.

Roark is a good professor, and he really does care about his students. Very reasonable grading policies and problem sets, but the class is really hard (especially if you have no experience with the stock market/finance industry). Great guy, difficult class.

This classes' topics build on each other throughout the semester. If you get lost in the first units then the remainder will be more difficult to grasp. Roark cares about seeing you succeed, the class is just difficult for most people. Make sure that if you don't understand something that you take the time to get help or figure it out.

Excellent professor, knowledgeable and caring. The class is simply the hardest I have ever taken. Roark does his best to bring the material to the students. He is funny and wants to cut everyone a break, but at the end of the day it is still Intermediate Macro.

Makes the class way harder than it needs to be. Homeworks are overly complicated and take hours to complete. Constantly makes mistakes in lectures and on answer keys. Can be hard to follow at times during lectures. Also will round some students grades up and not others. Nice guy besides all that though.

The course itself has difficult concepts but as a professor, he is really great and understanding. He always wants to make sure we understand the material which is nice. His HW was harder than the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Honestly, the material itself isn't that hard, but they he teaches it makes it much harder. There were moments where the same info was presented differently during the semester, which seriously confused me on the final. Prof Roark is a decent lecturer, however, I would recommend looking for alternatives for this credit if you want a good grade.

Great guy, one of my favorite professors in the econ department. The content in 425 is interesting although sometimes lectures can get boring and seem overcomplicated. Really straight forward grader though, and the work load is super manageable. Only downside is how long it takes for things to be graded. Overall loved Roark though, nicest guy.

Genuinely the best econ prof. I've ever had, I cannot write a review that does him justice. He's insanely nice, funny, and accessible, and is the first prof. I've had that has actually made sense regarding the material. 8 problem sets (2 lowest are dropped), 2 midterms, and a final. I would literally take every class with him if I could!

You can tell that Chris genuinely cares about the success of his students and I haven't felt this seen by a professor before but I really WISH he would change his multiple choice rule. Some MC questions have multiple answers but you can't get half credit if you get one right and one wrong and it is so absurd

Professor Roark is a very nice and funny guy who has the bad fortune of teaching a very difficult class. Though I feel that he occasionally struggled to explain concepts in class, he is accessible outside of class and easy to ask for help. Above all, I feel that he wants his students to succeed.

Chill dude but moves a bit fast and skips steps in examples, though outside of class he's super accessible and gives great explanations. Main concern was that most of his MC questions have 2 right answers and you have to get both for full credit, and one answer is usually far more convoluted than the other. He's the only prof I've seen do this.

Roark is a good professor and a very reasonable person. He uses Campuswire extensively and will answer messages and questions very quickly online, which is helpful when completing the (very difficult) homeworks or studying for the exams. The lectures can move fast, but you can always ask clarifying questions later.
just took the final and oh my god. Last semester reviews were right that the final will kill you. His personality is the only reason I'm giving him a nice review because that final was not very nice.

Chris genuinely cares about us and he's the most accessible prof I've had so far at UNC. His personality makes even macro bearable to learn
He's a really good prof but the material is still pretty hard you have to spend a fair amount of time out of class to get a good understanding 
My one complaint is the exams are DAMN hard. Very painful. Very.

Chris is the man. The content is hard and sometimes I blame him for making it overcomplicated, but overall hes such a genuinely good guy with a great sense of humor. I'll miss his presence in the classroom. 
Also he makes up for the difficulty of the class with a great curve so I have no complaints.

This class by no means easy. Our first exam was given a 15-point curve this semester, but the second exam was given a 4-point curve because of how the C. Breezy likes to curve the mean of the exams (or sometimes the median) to a 75. The grading scale makes the class passable, but the exams are tough, and the homeworks collaboration.

Roark is a very nice guy and has been one of the most accessible professors outside of class I've ever had. The material is tough, but if you attend every lecture and take notes on what he says instead of copying the slides it's not that bad. Homeworks are tough but you can collaborate and he answers questions on campuswire. Gives curves on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
His explanation of concepts and the lecture slides are difficult to follow and on occasion do not fully elaborate topics being covered. His tests occasionally, without warning, involve more complex math than he teaches.

Granted, he makes an effort to answer questions and presents in a friendly and engaging way.

Gotta self study to pass 420.

This class is just really tough. As someone who got As in Econ 410 and 400 without working that hard, this class really pushed my limits. Roark is overall doing his best with a massive class and hard material. He does really care about wanting all of his students to do well. Go to office hours, get ready to study, and you will be okay. Curves a lot
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I've never had a professor so accessible while at UNC so points for that!! I wont bs this is a really hard class lol but it could be a lot harder...dr Roark does a great job at simplifying concepts during lectures and is always ready to answer questions/listen to feedback to adapt how he's teaching the concept. Don't be scared to take the class
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I sometimes laugh during class because he can be funny but I often cry outside of class because of his lectures and assignments and exams.

He's better than some of the other econ professors and I think he is still finding his footing at UNC but I wish he would be better about returning grades and releasing assignments on a timely manner/sticking to dates he gives himself. Class is much harder than expected and some lectures overcomplicate textbook subjects, but unfortunately it's life
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He was a nice guy, but his teaching was not the best. The material of the class is challenging but it is stuff that you will actually use in the future. Lecture slides are not super descriptive so you have to pay attention in the class. Tests and homeworks are lengthy and challenging.

I took 425 with him and Roark is one of the better Econ professors I've had at UNC. His lectures are long and often not too engaging so it is easy to tune him out but the structure of the class is fair and the content is interesting. His exams are fair and the homework takes a really long time and are tough but really prepare you for the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I'm a neuroscience and econ double major and this is the hardest class I've taken at UNC. Prof is awful. Seems to make the class impossibly hard for no reason. One time Roark quoted "I make the home works and exams super hard so you have to struggle through them which helps you learn." Not a super nice guy either; passive aggressive, snarky, etc.

Roark was an all around terrible professor.  Lecture material was impossibly hard and on top of that he was awful at conveying the information. Homeworks took 8+ hours to complete and know one I knew ever got better than a 70 on them. Kind of class that makes you want to switch majors. Seriously, take class at a community college to avoid Roark

He's a really nice guy, but ECON 420 is just ridiculously hard. It is by far the most difficult course I've taken at UNC. It makes ECON 410 look easy. The test are extremely hard and almost impossible to study for, but they are curved significantly and the final grades are curved in addition to that.
Really nice guy but the class is hard af. I didn't really study much and still got a B because of the massive curve. (Failed the final and one of the midterms and still got a B.

If it's not obvious the 5 star reviews are trolls, this is the hardest class I've taken at UNC by far. Roark is a nice guy but he seemed to make a lot of mistakes in his lectures and just overall didn't prepare us very well for the exams; I ended up teaching myself everything and scored well only because of his very generous curves.

Roark wanted people to do well in his class but he just wasn't a good professor. He often made errors in class and on answer keys for homework and practice problems. Be prepared to spend hours working on homework assignments and studying for exams. The only good thing about this class is that he curves the exams because everyone does so poorly.

All the good reviews on here have to be from the VERY few ppl (i'm talking like at most 6 ppl) that enjoyed his class and MAYBE got higher than a B on the exams. Being completely honest- from someone who has taken all the notoriously hard classes here at UNC and passed with A's, the structure/grading/prof of this class is astonishingly ridiculous.

Def thought 410 and 101 were difficult but not NEARLY as difficult as this class. He was bound to have mistakes on every single thing he put out to the class and the whole "MCQ can have multiple answers but if you choose one wrong, then the entire question is wrong" was BS. I respect all my professors, but the ULAs were the backbone to this class.

Dr. Roark is clearly very smart & kind, but he struggled with lectures and often made mistakes that he didn't correct. The ULAs were the ones who taught a ton of us. 101 and 410 were a breeze for me, but I never knew what was going on in this class. Avg. curved exam grades were in the 70s, so raw scores were often failing. The final was a disaster.
Just show up and you'll be fine. Can't imagine anyone getting below an B+ in this class.  One of the easiest courses taught in Econ/UNC in general

*ECON 425* Nice guy, very knowledgeable but sometimes to the extent he makes things seem more complicated than they are. The problem sets are difficult and lengthy, but very helpful in reviewing for the midterm and final. He did curve the midterm and final course averages. Though the class was challenging, I learned a lot and would take it again.

Pros: Nice guy, test curves were big. Cons: Homeworks took incredibly long to complete, tests were long and very difficult, lectures were fast with lots of information, used weird, confusing notation, he made numerous mistakes during lectures and practice problems. Got an A, but the class was by no means easy as I've seen other reviews indicate.

One time Roark got mad for people talking and said "I can throw this on the hw/exam without teaching it" and a student said "you already do that" and I've never heard something more accurate. Always had an attitude and the teaching was not there. Hw took HOURS and exams were rlly hard and long. He did curve the class (bc ppl did bad bc no teaching)

Dr. Roark is great! Lectures fast-paced (don't take notes on slides b/c they're posted). Office hours essential to understand PS content. Exams are a time crunch. Most intimidating aspect was complicated notation and derivatives he threw at us initially, but we were his first group at UNC and he had a misconception of our calculus fundamentals.

Roark is simply the man. He always pulled up to class in the dopest fits and made every lecture exciting. I honestly don't get all of the negativity on this page, the class isn't that bad and C-Breezy (yes we are on a nickname basis) is always there to answer questions outside of class.

Chris is without a doubt the most intelligent person I have ever met, every time I spoke to him it felt like I was being injected with knowledge. Content wasn't too bad, studied for a couple hours before the tests and managed to get an A. Definitely an easy A if you go to class.

I learned from this class by rewatching his lectures. His lectures and homework are full of mistakes. It's the kind of mistake that confuse students. He also said the wrong things in class multiple times. For example, "Demand curve moves leftward...I mean rightward." MULTIPLE TIMES. It was a very frustrating experience.

*425* Dr. Roark is very nice, but damn this class was brutal. Each lecture is 30 slides of dense material so if you don't understand something initially, it's almost impossible to catch back up. Homeworks took hours to finish and ended up being nothing like the tests, which were somehow even more difficult. My hardest class at UNC by far.

The hardest class I've taken in my five semesters at Carolina. The other reviews say it... lectures are so incredibly dense. Exam averages are awful, but they get a handsome curve. Roark has another ECON class that I will likely be taking, but I wouldn't strongly suggest him. The MC grading system is bad, often multiple answers w/o him stating it.

Prof. Roark is a really cool guy and extremely knowledgable. The content for this course is intense. Part of it is heavy on the math and the other is very dense conceptual work. Simple mistakes are easy to make and he makes plenty. Lecture slides, homework questions, and answer keys always have something wrong. He desperately needs an iPad.

*FOR 425*

Roark is very knowledgeable and has passion. That said, this class was the hardest Ive taken at unc. Psets take hours (get ready for confusing questions), lectures are so dense, and tests are very challenging. He is a tough grader that doesnt award a lot of partial credit. Final was insane and nothing like the homeworks. Good luck.

If you struggled with 410 and are hoping to have a better time with Macro, you're in for a rude awakening. This class makes Econ 410 seem like 6th grade algebra. It's do-able with a VERY significant amount of time and effort but expect it to be the hardest class you've taken in your life. Roark is ok but sometimes hard to follow and a harsh grader
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Roark is a decent professor and is very knowledgable about economics. He also actually cares about the class and will get back to you if you reach out with concerns. In the flip side, his lectures are extremely dense and sometimes unclear. The tests are very hard with the un-curved average being around a D-.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: prof def knows a lot and is a very smart guy but his lectures are extremely dense, with slides often filled with mistakes, making the content just so dull and hard to engage in without extreme focus. material is conceptually hard but if you sit down with it you can grasp it. hard class no matter what. has high expectations.

He really cares about his students and gives us a lot of resources (ULAs, TAs, practice exams, etc), but he goes over SO much content during class and honestly it was much easier to rely on the internet or khan academy to study rather than go through the lecture slides. I usually have no idea how to do the homework. extremely hard class.

He's fr a genuinely great, great person. His lectures are super dense so it's easy to fall behind. If you just rewatch every lecture, you'll understand the material (I got an 80 from doing this and reviewing HW). He doesn't have practice problems which makes teaching yourself super difficult. HWs are hard, but dont let the other reviews scare you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are basically useless. He uses the strangest notation and uses complex terminology to explain stuff. The material is hard and he just makes it harder. HW takes a long time to complete. Midterms are so long
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: "I just kept flipping, and the test just kept going." _ my classmate after the last midterm
Roark is a great prof but hold on for dear life cause if you get lost in this class it's very hard to catch up.

Got a B+ in 410; didn't enjoy it but it was fine. This class is 5x harder than 410. 420 with Roark is an L any way you look at it. He is a brilliant and super nice professor but he explains everything in the most complex ways possible. Lecture is not helpful. Exams are insanely long and hard. Each mc q has multiple answers and he gives no partial c

This class is not it. He knows the material well but isn't the best at explaining it if you don't immediately understand it. He also does not do any example problems in class so the first time you do practice is one the problem sets and puts lots of information in one lecture to the point you can't keep up.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Fall 2025 ARTH 453. Manageable class. Lectures were a bit redundant and was usually confused on what was being taught. Deeply appreciate Prof. Magee's drive in this class though. Grading can be a bit harsh
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Class wasn't graded super hard and she's really nice. But unless you are really interested in the very niche topics, it's hard to feign interest in all semester and there are definitely more useful electives. Super small class so you must be engaged and present at all times, and she grades participation harshly.

Dr. Magee is an expert in her field and her class was rather enjoyable, however her grading scheme is rather unforgiving and many of the grades seem arbitrary. Expectations are laid out clearly but she seemingly doesn't give out grades >95.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This was a really unique interdisciplinary class that combined art history with Feldenkrais movement lessons. Sometimes it was hard to make the link between the readings and lessons, but overall fascinating. She is definitely a tough grader—the more "meta" and detailed you can get with your analysis the better.
tough grader and has her favorites. not much else to say
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Graded things very last minute, didn't know my grade until the end of semester and it was sent to connect Carolina. Many times her rubric is very unclear and she takes off points for no reason very very tough grader. Participation counted a lot and needed and projects. Don't recommend this class to anyone!

I'm rating her for ARTH280 (not listed). Prof. Magee is very kind and enthusiastic about what she teaches, and she explains things well for those that don't know a lot about art. I thoroughly enjoyed the class and would take her again. The class is graded by a lot of different things, so there's no assignments that are particularly heavy.
This was barely a class. She played favorites so much that it wasn't worth talking. She doesn't teach ARTH290 either.

Professor Magee really is a true gem of a teacher. I took her ARTH 290 course as an elective and have absolutely loved my time in the course! One thing I love about her course is how interactive it is compared to other ARTH courses. It's nice to be able to learn skills and senses to help us better utilize them in the art world and you get that

Professor Rovine really is a true gem of a teacher. I took her ARTH 488 course as an elective and have absolutely loved my time in the course! One thing about her though, she is a tough grader but she is fair, she makes all of her lectures available so you can go back cover concepts you arent to good in so its fair I'd say. Anyways, take her class
One of the most useless classes I have ever taken. Still not quite sure what I have learned or was suppose to learn. Literally got our first grade on the very last day of class.

I was super excited about taking this class, but it was not what I had hoped it would be. I am still wondering what the real objective was. Lectures were somewhat boring. Professor Magee is professional and fair. I wish the class had a bit more spice and/or flair to it.

Yes, this class is hard. Yes, she grades hard. If you are looking for an easy road through college then avoid Magee. However, if you are interested in improving your critical thinking and writing skills while learning about something esoteric yet interesting, consider taking this class with Magee. It also satisfies a truckload of Gen Ed requirement

This class was the bane of my existence. Her lectures are extremely dry and hard to follow. She grades EXTREMELY hard. Classes are either lecture or group discussions. Group discussions include forced discussion about boring readings. SHOULD be an interesting class but IS NOT. DO NOT TAKE.

This class was crap. Barely related to art at all and she graded so hard it was next to impossible to get an A, even with extra credit. Lectures were super boring and she was really hateful too. Bottom line, if you take art stay away from Magee!!

I have taken two classes with her and she is amazing. A presentation and some response papers is pretty much all she grades on. Pretty easy material, some reading, but very interesting too. She is the nicest woman also! Very helpful and kind.

I have taken two classes with her and she is amazing. A presentation and some response papers is pretty much all she grades on. Pretty easy material, some reading, but very interesting too. She is the nicest woman also! Very helpful and kind.
Gave me a really low grade although I made A's on all the assignments. Her lectures suck and she is heartless.
No Comments

Good and passionate prof. Attendance is random but you could expect it'll be taken at least once a week. Lots of classwork and projects, and lectures can be super boring, but the class is really easy. You don't design maps until the final month of the semester, and for this all you do is follow her guide and watch videos on how to use GIS software.

Dr.Cardwell is great. You do HAVE to show up to class. Pop quizzes for attendance. She never makes you do the group projects at home only in class, so you have to be there. The assignments are not difficult. If you go to class and do the assignments, you will get an A. Also if you don't get a good grade on the assignments, she lets you redo it.

GEOG 370 is a hard class, and Dr. Cardwell's grading system is kind of weird. Once you understand it, though, it is pretty straightforward. If you don't understand something, Dr. Cardwell and TAs are always available outside of class and able to explain stuff in more depth.

Amazing professor, very open to feedback from students, which makes up for some disorganization. Very accessible in and outside of class, and open to helping you troubleshoot. Class consisted of a test, some labs and a final project, manageable as long as you dedicate some effort.
Great teacher, will be taking another class taught by her in the spring. Also took geog 115 with her and she is funny, passionate and makes sure you do not fall behind.

Dr. Cardwell is fair, clear, and engaging. I saw the world differently after her class, and I enjoyed the combination of thoughtful instruction, collaboration with others, and patience from Dr. Cardwell. I'd highly recommend her class and hope I can take another.

Dr. Beaver is a great teacher during lecture and really breaks down the material in an enthusiastic way. That being said, his exams are very difficult and contain a lot of niche material. I gave him a 3 because he is quite rude and condescending to students who asked him questions on 1 to 1.

I loved Beaver for orgo 2, genuinely wants his students to succeed and get the most out of his class. Orgo 2 is a hard subject theres no workaround, but if you put in the effort it is very doable. Listen to his suggestions on how to study. Attend GPSS and do the ULA worksheets. Sit in the front, ask and answer questions in class.

man he's a good prof but unless you're confident you know the material he's not worth it. his exams are the hardest out of the entire department and the stress is unreal. i got out with an A but then my physical health genuinely declined due to the stress solely from that class. unless you want your entire life to be chem, dont take him.

Beaver is a great guy and probably knows the course content he's teaching better than anyone. Yes the midterms are very challenging but the final is much more fair in my opinion. If you got through orgo 1 with a decent grade, you know what to expect with Beaver. Study hard for the midterms and practice practice practice and you will succeed.

Dr. Beaver is one of my favorite chemistry professors at UNC. He genuinely cares, will listen to student feedback, and is amazing at breaking down difficult concepts. His GPSS is super helpful and his class is very engaging. I highly recommend taking 262 with him.

Dr. Beaver is really nice and truly wants you to succeed. Explains content well during lecture and provides a lot of resources to succeed, but the exams are HARD. You need to do all of the practice material he offers and understand everything fully, but that's probably true regardless of the professor for organic chemistry.

His lectures are great and he's incredibly knowledgeable about the material. He expects lot from students, but also cares about learning if you want to learn. I'd recommend if you truly want an understanding of organic chemistry, take it with him, but if you want the best letter grade you can get, take it with someone else.

I enjoyed 262 with Dr. Beaver. His lectures make sure you will know the content. There's just a lot. Exams always have a few trippy questions, but fair overall. Did amazing on the first 3 and poorly on the final due to other stuff. An A is certainly possible if you spend 1-2 hours a day practicing. He gave some extra credit too so can't complain.

Orgo is just a hard class, and it takes a lot of time to understand and memorize it. Beaver was a good lecturer and 100% cared, but he made his exams SO HARD. You aren't screwed when you take him, you just need to know 110% of the content to do at least OKAY on the exams. It isn't like you can know 80% and make an 70 on the exam, you need 100%.

Dr. Beaver definitely knows his chemistry and is good at teaching it. He just creates next level difficult exams that are hard to do well on unless you 100% understand everything in the class. My highest score on any exam was a 66% and I would study about a week in advance.... I did much better in Zurcher's 261 and found her exams to be more fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Organic chemistry is just such a hard and content filled class. Dr. Beaver was a nice guy and lectures seemed to be helpful but his exams were next level hard. He is not the worst professor but if there Is an easier option, go with that one. Office hours were only held in 8 minute increments and sometimes answered questions a little backhanded.

Man, first stem class I took at unc as a transfer student and it makes me want to switch my major. Required iClicker in class, weekly quizzes online, no required practice but you're screwed if you don't do the recommended. Hard exams, I thought I could study but it just got worse as the semester went forward. Probably will retake w/ someone else.

I took CHEM262 with Dr. Beaver over the summer, and I can confidently say it was one of the best classes I have taken. Orgo is a dense subject, but with how lectures are given, the support outside of the classroom, and with enough practice problems, an A is possible. I plan to take intermediate organic chemistry with him! Do recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Literally the least accessible person on the planet. Ignores every email ever and didnt respond to any office hour requests. Went to one problem sesh and he made me feel stupid. Mid teaching style. Lectures weren't horrible, but him ignoring me made them horrible. Overall, came in with high expectations, left with a low GPA and anger in my veins.

Like other reviews are saying, Beaver is a good guy but his exams are awful. I did much better in orgo 1 with Zurcher and also prefer her teaching style. Beaver does want you to succeed and is nice in lecture. Can be oddly passive in office hours/1 on 1 interactions. Again though, his exams are SO hard so be warned

I took Orgo 1 with Zurcher and much preferred it to Beaver's Orgo 2. He has a tad bit of weirdness to him; gets very easily offended (became very passive aggressive the lecture after our second exam because students were less engaged and pissed at the exam difficulty). He wants you to learn, but its beaver method or death. Exams are hard .

Great lecturer, but was VERY standoffish 1-on-1 sometimes. Make sure he knows your name. Exams were EVIL & if you didn't know 100% of content exams will get you. I never got > a 90 on any exam but ended with an A thanks to Rogue Chem and solving every textbook problem. He was fair with points back and cared for his students-you WILL learn orgo 2.
Beaver wanted to see us succeed as shown by the 4 final EC points he provided. Be warned that he always tests the hardest parts of each concept and the "exceptions to the rule"

Orgo is difficult, but Beaver's engaging lectures and clear expectations make the class manageable and even enjoyable at times. He is tough, but honest and tries to connect with students and help them succeed. He knows it's hard and pushes you to get help EARLY. Keep up with your rxn cards, practice DAILY, and consider rogue chem for the final!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Please take any Orgo class you can with Zurcher. Beaver is not a horrible teacher; he is just condescending at times and creates the most diabolical exams you can imagine. 3 midterms (70 or below was the median on all) and just took the 70-question final. Class is hard but doable.
Dr. Beaver is an exceptional lecturer who really cares about his students.

Dr. Beaver does an amazing job working with the lecture hall, making the large lecture hall feel like a small classroom. You could tell he cares about what he's teaching and who he's teaching it to. His tests are supposed to be the hardest out of all the orgo professors, though. Also, his voice is very easy to listen to lol.
Dr. Beaver is great but the class itself is challenging. The material is difficult, but he makes an effort to give students the resources they need to succeed.

Dr. Beaver is truly a beacon of light in the UNC Chem department. While the class is difficult, Dr. Beaver made the material very accessible and was always down to help us out with material. He is a very effective and engaging lecturer. Sometimes he is a little sassy, but never condescending or mean. He also tries to be reassuring, which is nice.

Professor Beaver is a really great orgo instructor. The content is just really difficult. He is very accessible outside of class and makes an effort to learn your name and truly wants to see you succeed. I am satisfied with the grades I got in this course and feel that they were fair given I crammed before every exam.

Chem261 is a tough class, but Dr. Beaver was an incredible teacher. If you're considering taking orgo with him, do it. He's incredibly understanding and caring. He learned the names of everybody who participated in class and would say hi while walking around campus. Attend ULA sessions, don't be distracted during class, and STUDY! You'll do great!
It's a no from me dawg.

Liked beaver in 261/262, not as much in 460. 460 was v difficult & structured poorly imo. You must be VERY confident with orgo 1/2 content, esp orgo 2, even if you took it years ago. Majority of class did poorly esp on exam 1. Added 15 pt curve to exam 1, 10 pt curve to exam 2, & a curve at the end, which was v nice and unheard of in UNC chem dept

The class is definitely a lot of work, but Dr. Beaver's a good professor. He's very caring and explains the material well. Exams were also fair. Just make sure to keep up with the workbook problems and rxn flashcards.

Beaver's got good lectures and very accessible via OH so don't be intimidated. His LAs were just awesome! They single-handedly saved me in the class with super clear explanations. Study hard for the thermo exam, that by far is the hardest exam in the course. You've got this!

This class was so informative and engaging. Exams were hard but extra credit opportunities were given, and the final also had a take-home portion. Group presentations were a good grade boost and also enlightened us on modern orgo research. Dr. Beaver was also very helpful during 1-on-1 office hours.

CHEM 101 was horrible for me, so going into CHEM 102 I was terrified, but Dr. Beaver was a great lecturer and made the class interactive and easier to understand. The lecture was a launch so the class was only about 35 people. Dr. Beaver was respectful and his LAs were great too. The tests were difficult. Go to the LA review sessions!
this class was unnecessarily difficult with him. beaver is rude and condescending at times, and sometimes appears to have an ego issue. take with literally anyone else.

Chem 460 review. Lots of prerequisite knowledge required, make sure to brush up on orgo 2 before taking. Lots of pre-class reading, and exams were extremely difficult (be he did give a generous curve). The class has a large presentation component, which is fine, but just be aware.

This review is for 102. Dr. Beaver is a great professor. He made learning chem easier and made sure students understood as much as he could. Chem 102 at UNC is hard, and the exams are ridiculous. But Beaver is definitely the best professor I've had in the chem department and is passionate about what he does. I would definitely recommend him.

Verily, this course is no mere pursuit, but an odyssey of torment where only the steadfast glimpse enlightenment. The lecturer bestows knowledge in fire and fury, yet we, mere mortals, are left scorched, grasping at fleeting truths. My soul writhes beneath this incantation of madness! And yet, is not true wisdom born from suffering?

Dr. Beaver was awesome. Set the best foundation for Organic Chemistry and his lectures were very informative. He is very smart and forces you to think through the course material. His lectures are also engaging and I would definitely take him again. The only slight is his exams are difficult, but I learned so much in this course.

I was pleasantly surprised by this course. Joshua Beaver was extremely professional and knowledgeable. He always came prepared and stuck to schedule, never falling behind on the course material. He was genuinely compassionate with his students as well, encouraging participation and making a point to remember people's names.

Great course overall. Orgo here is hard but getting a good grade is definitely doable. Beaver is a very caring and engaging professor. I can see how he may come off as condescending sometimes but he's very empathetic and receptive in office hours. Don't take Orgo with too many other hard classes. That was my mistake and I didn't lock in enough.

It's UNC orgo, it's going to be a lot of content. I bombed the first test before learning how to prepare for this class. Skim the readings before class, don't spend too long on them, there's a lot of unnecessary info. Keep up with the workbook, it's the key to the midterms. Go to the ULA session and at least one problem solving session a week.

I love Beaver. He was amazing, and the class is very manageable if you stay on top of it. He has q&A sessions and office hours to help and genueinly wants to see you succeed. Many people said he seemed condescending, which at first he kinda did, but as soon as I talked to him a couple times he is the best prof ever.

It's definitely possible to succeed by doing workbook +textbook problems, ULA worksheets, going to q&a sessions -- uncommon most students with other hard classes. Midterms are pretty fair, but Beaver is not super accessible; condescending and judgy -- gatekeeps info at his q&as, so go to those if possible (or todd). Has a buffer for graded work.

Prof. Beaver was a nice guy and could be pretty engaging during class. However, lecture slides were often vague. Midterms were significantly harder than the final exam, and final grades experienced a slight curve. When in doubt about whether you should have received credit for an answer on a midterm, submit a regrade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Beaver is a wonderful lecturer and instructor.  Organic Chemistry is hard, and requires lots of practice and attention to detail; Dr. Beaver emphasizes these things daily in class, and puts a ton of effort into helping people correct their misconceptions.  Easily approachable, spent a lot of time making the class digestible. Curved final grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Beaver cares about his students but I do not think he is a good lecturer. The slides are a bit confusing and his explanations were vague so we could "teach ourself". The review sessions only helped if you knew what you were doing and had a few questions. Orgo is one of those subjects that requires consistent studying so don't fall behind.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Orgo is fairly challenging and requires a lot of practice. Attention to detail is key in the course. As for Dr. Beaver, I don't have much positive to say. You ask him a question, he will not only not answer your question, but he will make u feel like a fool for even asking. I got more clear answers on EdStem, the TAs do better than he does.

I quickly came to the realization that some people are good at orgo and others just aren't. I did the preclass, ULA sessions, the GPSS, workbook, and slides every week and still did bad in the class. Some people that didn't even do half of what I did would do better. Make sure you don't take any other hard classes bc this class is time consuming!
Doctor Beaver's lectures were interesting and easy to follow, but you have to be prepared before the class. Make sure you take his advice in the syllabus and you will do good in this class

Doctor Beaver's lectures were interesting and easy to follow, but you have to be prepared before the class. He cares about his students; however, he expects a lot from you. I would say do absolutely everything he offers, and you will do great. 
Overall, Doctor Beaver is one of my favorite professors at UNC, even though Orgo1 is hard!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very intersting lectures and very nicely planned out lecture slides. Dr. Beaver wants students to do a lot of practice questions outside of class and I do not like the pre-class reading quizzes (Easy to get points but heavy reading and does not really help me to understand the content). Easy to get daily participation and graded work points,.

Organic chemistry is very difficult to navigate, but Beaver truly explains these concepts and ensures his students have a deeper understanding of the WHY behind everything. I am very glad I took this class with him!!

Organic chemistry is going to be hard no matter who you take it with. Beaver was a good lecturer and provided lots of problem-solving in class so lectures were never boring. The textbook for the course was actually very good and Beaver's slides were very helpful when studying for exams.

Extremely difficult course and main source of learning, his own written workbook has no solutions...so outside of the scaffolded answers he provides on canvas, ALL the other practice, good luck getting and if your schedule doesn't allow for you to go to office hours, sorry for you. Smart guy, fair but hard tests, and cares.

Lectures were engaging and easy to follow along, however the difficulty of the course was extreme at times, especially in the tests, tehy were nothing like the previous exam questions given for practice.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He does not know how to teach.  He is the most condescending man that I have EVER met and that's saying a lot.  He is also so misogynistic.  He is so self-centered, everything is about him and nothing is about the ACTUAL content of the class.  This class literally bombed my mental health.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Became an alcoholic, it was that bad. Honestly, the main issue is the problems done in class are infinitely easier than the ones on the test. That being said, he's a really good guy and cares about you if you put in the effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Beaver's approach is high structure active learning - it rewards students who practice every day using all resources (workbook, blank slides, worksheets, office hours). Was 261/262 hard? Yes! Does Beaver have high expectations? Also yes. This can be intimidating for some, but it motivated me to try my best. Orgo @UNC is high risk + high reward.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: In 262, there's SO many rxns to know; prioritize this class. Keep an errors notebook. You need to understand WHY things happen. Beaver was more personable in 262 than 261, but still had high expectations of depth of understanding. Have him and the ULAs answer all of your questions, all the time. He is more willing to help if he knows you by name!
Do not take a class with him

The best chemistry teacher I've had.  You definitely have to put in the work, and go to his Q&As and LA sessions as much as possible.  Content is difficult but he genuinely wants you to succeed and will take student feedback to heart.  Test questions are pretty straightfoward and fair.

This is a very difficult class and Dr. Beaver is known for making hard tests, however, he genuinely does want his students to learn and succeed in the class. You will need to devote a lot of time to studying and practicing the material but you definitely can do well in the class.

Def a tough class and still harder than 261 (esp the second unit). Having a good foundation in 261 is KEY. Insider info: every test had a huge predict the products section, and acid-base shows up every time. Encouragement: first midterm=worst grade in orgo ever, last midterm=best grade in orgo ever. Midterm med were 77, 74, 77; final med was 79.

Dr. Beaver is a great guy! I had him for 261 and 262, and you can tell he really cares a lot about his students. Orgo definitely was not my favorite subject but he was always engaging and it was nice to come to class where the professor knows your name in a big lecture room. The course is hard but if you take his advice, you will do just fine!

Seems to be a genuinely good guy and a solid teacher. However, he expects all of his students to have a near-perfect understanding of all of the material. It comes across as if he thinks this is our only course.

Orgo 2 with Dr. Beaver is way better than orgo 1 (had him for both)! You NEED to do the legwork for this class - do the workbook/textbook problems concurrently with the lectures, study well in advance, and you will do fine. I got a B- in orgo 1 and I'm maintaining an A- in orgo 2! He cares a lot about his students - work hard & you'll be fine!

Beaver is a difficult professor no doubt but I accredit much of my ability to study and learn effectively to his guidance and mentorship. He genuinely cares about your well-being and if you show effort, he'll reciprocate. Exams are pretty difficult but not impossible by any means. Go to class, participate, do the readings, don't fall behind.
poo. avoid.

His exams were definitely the most difficult to take and understand by far. If you do not have a thorough understanding of the material, and fall short of 100% understanding, the exam will be challenging. They are not impossible; rather, they test your overall comprehension through every possible question that could be asked.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Organic chemistry very difficult in general, especially when you're taking it here! Dr. Beaver, however, is a very good professor and I really do think he cares a lot for his students. You have to do the reading, practice, study and work very hard!

Dr. Beaver is very knowledgeable and truly cares about his students succeeding. However, he has a very condescending demeanor when explaining concepts in office hours or review sessions. He expects students to learn at the rate he would which comes across very heavily. He is very organized and lectures really clarify the textbook readings.

Dr. Beaver was nice and clearly knowledgeable about organic chemistry. However, I felt that he did little to explain any difficult concepts during lectures. All midterm medians were in the 60s and there was about a 1% point curve at the end of the class. Exam questions are harder than lecture and practice questions.

I'll try to cover what the other reviews haven't covered already. I honestly thought Beaver was a great teacher and I always found his problem sessions helpful. I know it's hard, but try not to stress too much about your grade; there is a slight curve at the end. Here are my grades for reference: mid-80s on every midterm, low 90 on the final.

Beaver explains concepts well & learns names but orgo itself is a menace. CHEM 101/102 at UNC were pretty easy A's for me, but I spent several hours a day on orgo just to get a B+. Tho its possible to get an A- or A if you get in the 80s on exams bc they curve slightly at the end. Redo the slides, go to ULA sessions, do as much practice as you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Beaver is a respectable guy who deeply understands Orgo, making for a good professor, but he also has extremely high standards for students, so merely keeping up during lecture will not get you a good exam score. Tests medians were around 68, so you must deeply understand the material. This course is what you can expect of a Orgo course at UNC.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I don't know why everyone talks badly about Professor Beaver but he is a very caring man. He is straightforward and will say that a problem was "easy". However, don't take that to heart.  Attending his office hours is also great because he gives you tips on how to succeed in the course and he wants everyone to succeed.

Nice professor who learns your name if you participate. He can be pretty fun to learn from when he's in a joking mood, and is clearly passionate about chemistry. Chem classes here are what they are, but he does his best to help you succeed. You have to be the one to put in the hard work to succeed. Medians on tests were 66-68 so study hard.

I know orgo is notoriously the most difficult class at UNC, so I'm trying not to let that get in the way of my rating, but Beaver didn't help my understanding of the material. The workbook was helpful, but to get the answers you need to go to ULA sessions, and they only solve a few problems. I worked my butt off, and I'll still probably get a C+.

Dr. Beaver is a decent lecturer. Not the best by any means, but he was also not the worst I've had. Nonetheless, tests are very tricky and grading can be pretty cut-throat, so make sure you study and understand the material very well.

BEST CHEM PROF!! Made an effort to learn everyone's name. Commended individual students for improvement on exams. Explained the material so well. I did so much better in ORGO2 than ORGO1 w/austell. I absolutely adore Beaver. Extremely kind. iClicker for attendance. The exams were what I expected. I did devote a lot of studying time, but u should.

Dr. Beaver is the best chemistry professor I have ever had. He genuinely cares about his students and tries to get to know everyone's names. He wants the best for everyone and always had great advice on how to succeed in the class. I would definitely recommend taking a chemistry class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I feel like a lot of Chemistry professors get a bad rap because they teach a difficult class. CHEM 262 was definitely not easy, but Dr. Beaver explained content well and clearly wanted us to succeed. I wish he had written all of our exams rather than alternating with the other professor, but that is not his fault. I'd take another class with him.

Dr. Beaver was extremely kind and respectful. His lectures are interesting and engaging, and he's a very smart, fair person. The exams are stressful, but Dr. Beaver does his best to make sure you're not too scared for his exams. I recommend him wholeheartedly.

Pretty solid professor and a good guy. He seemed to truly care about his students and their success. He understands that the material is hard and does everything in his power to allow students to be comfortable with it. I enjoyed taking his class.

Beaver is a good teacher. The test were hard but fair and they are always good about giving us the partial credits. I believe Beaver wanted us to succeed and provided tips outside of class material on how to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Beaver seems to be universally despised for no reason. Organic chemistry is never going to be a cakewalk. However, Dr. Beaver was a funny guy who often told us many anecdotes. He did a great job with conveying difficult orgo 2 concepts to students. Exams were graded generously and Dr. Beaver actually (wait for it) wants you to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Orgo 2 is naturally hard, but I think Dr. Beaver gave us everything we would need to succeed. He is available for questions, has regular office hours and problem solving sessions, and responds to emails promptly. He overall hasn't done anything wrong in my book, even if he may not be the most exciting or charismatic guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Don't listen to anyone who says that Dr. Beaver is uncaring, manipulative, etc. They are just people who have become frustrated with organic chemistry - its a subject that takes a lot of work. Dr. Beaver truly cares about his students, is willing to help them in any way, and also is quite generous with his exams.

Orgo is obviously a hard class but Beaver is a good professor. His lectures are always clear and have lots of class participation, and there are tons of resources to get help and practice after class. He's also very generous with partial credit on exams

Dr. Beaver does a great job of making lectures engaging. He also makes a conscious effort to learn student names, and is really invested in helping students be successful. He is also a big help with study strategies.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Chem 262 is a hard class regardless of the professor. Dr. Beaver does a really great job of making the content on the tests reflect what was taught in class. He is very accessible outside of class and makes a conscious effort to learn everyone in the classes name.
absolutely never again. The exams were incredibly hard and Beaver would talk to us after exams and tell us how disappointed he was in us lmao. He simply was not a nice guy and orgo already blows.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The best way to learn organic chemistry is through practice and Dr.Beaver provides a lot of optional practice. You do not need to complete all these practice problems but I found that doing 3-4 problems a day (or a worksheet) was enough to make sure I understand content. Be proactive about solving your problems! He cares and will help you succeed!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Students write fake review to counter the good reviews. Plenty of people do well in ORGO and still dislike the class. Even if you did well, many agree that the class was such a bad experience and horribly taught. The constant wrong answers on PollEv or failed quiz average for most of the class is a reflection of the professor. One horrible class.

Dr. Beaver is a caring professor that encourages group discussion and practice problems to learn material. I think many negative reviews on here are a result of the difficulty of the class, not the professor.  Yes, orgo is hard, but this is universal everywhere and Dr. Beaver was effective at outlining what his students need to do to succeed.

Took him for a summer session and it was the best chem experience. He really got to know us and our names. Tests were definitely difficult and tested your abilities on all the past lessons, but was for the most part fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Beaver is an amazing professor and genuinely cares so much about his students. He is super supportive and encouraging. 262 is very challenging with any professor, but Dr. Beaver is very accessible. He is amazing at explaining difficult concepts, and gives more than enough exam-level resources/practice to succeed. Take him for organic chem!!

There were 3 professors for this class but I think Dr. Beaver made the exams and they were extremely difficult. I genuinely love orgo, but his exams made me feel terrible about myself. While I liked the content of this course, Dr. Beaver made it so difficult to get a good grade in this class. It almost felt like he didn't want us to do well.

Beaver is one of the best chem lecturers at unc. it sucks ppl rate him low because orgo is just hard, but he basically gave us enough leeway with covid that u barely had to come to class for full pts. i visited other sections this semester, but beaver is the best at understanding how students approach the material imo

Beaver is ruthless, but if you can look past his personality he is actually a reasonably okay organic chem professor. The exams are ridiculously difficult compared to class, homework, and the practice tests, but that's just classic UNC chem dept. You might pass with a C+ if you dedicate your entire life to the class.

Orgo chem is a challenging course. Do not come into this class expecting to get a good grade without putting in any work then blame the professor. Dr. Beaver has high expectations for students but this is consistent with all chem professors. His office hours and problem-solving sessions are very helpful and he genuinely wants students to do well.

It is SO easy to blame a professor for poor performance on exams. Dr. Beaver has always gone out of his way to support students in their success. He is by far the best professor I've ever had. Participation and dedication to class will matter 100%. Follow the way they teach you to study and you will do so well.

Organic chemistry at UNC is very very hard and to blame Dr. Beaver for that seems unfair. His lectures were engaging and helpful. You must come to class with a fair understanding of the material that gets solidified during class to succeed. Beaver wants his students to succeed! I failed the second test and still made an A-. You can do it!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Dr. Beavers class! Every lecture was very structured and he laid out exactly what we need to do to succeed. I wish more professors were as organized as he is! The tests were hard but if you do all the practice problems he offers and focus on understanding concepts rather than doing a bunch of meaningless problems you will do fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Honestly, Beaver is a condescending person. This class is the gateway to many health professions and he is aware of that. Beaver made it impossible to do well in his class due to his poor attitude and sarcastic behavior. This class was terrible and the amount of stress and sacrifices I made for this class was ridiculous. DO NOT TAKE BEAVER!

I felt like they didn't give us enough practice for what they expected us to know. On exams focus on what you know and not what you don't; try not to get hung up on trick questions (they do give partial credit). There were suicides on campus and we're still in a pandemic, and to say I felt like Beaver cared about his students, would be a lie.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Beaver's rate my professor is pretty derogatory but not entirely accurate. It's Organic Chemistry at UNC, it is going to be difficult. However, Dr. Beaver does care. The reality is, if you care he will as well, but he is not going to beg you to care. He is very accommodating actually, but you need to attend office hours and ask for help early!

I enjoyed organic chemistry immensely. It's a difficult subject and you have to be prepared to reckon with that when aiming for a high grade in the class. Rarely have I had a better lecture structure than with Prof Beaver. The problems in the lecture go over every piece of info from readings and makes it digestible. Loved the prof and the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This man does not care about the well-being of his students, especially considering that he continued lecturing while someone was seizing on the floor. Class is impossible to get an A in, curves are implied through what turns out to be empty promises. Do not take this class with Beaver at all costs. Take it anywhere else and youll probably be fine

Orgo here is going to be difficult no matter what. Dr. Beaver makes it very clear the class is hard. That being said, just going to lectures isn't enough. You also need to attend problem sessions/office hours if you want an A. Def makes you work for it. Practice problems were very useful, only complaint is he expects you to learn from the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Beaver's class has a clear structure and expectations from the get-go. He teaches at a brisk pace so it is important to read the textbook ahead of class. There are around 10 basic practice problems throughout the lecture. However, these questions are more basic so it's imperative to go to peer mentor sessions to get hard practice before exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Beaver was a very fun and sweet individual, but the tests him and Johnson gave were very very uncalled for. Tests were hard. We were promised a curve because our medians were in the low 60s and averages were consistently in the 40s and 50s. We did not receive a curve at the end. Very upsetting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Beaver was the worst professor I have ever had at UNC. The midterm medians were consistently Fs. At some point, its not the students fault for everyone getting failing grades on midtermsits the professors fault. Additionally, he claimed he would consider the suicides on campus when curving our grades. There was NO curve for the students.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This is a very hard class regardless Of who you take it with. Dr. Beaver is an amazing professor and I am thinking of mentoring for him even though the class is hard. This class needs a lot of effort and students complaining simply didnt understand that. It isnt the professors fault as he is very accommodating. Take him in my opinion!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Beaver is actually kind of nice. He also provides many opportunities to review outside of class. However, he makes the tests unnecessarily hard. reviews.comment: Good guy

reviews.comment: The chemistry labs at UNC are beyond awful. My TA took 10+ points off of my reports because of the way they looked, not even the content? Then, Dr. Beaver didn't curve the class. Great new head of the chem 101l lab department! You can tell he cares about the students and he made the class more manageable than previous years. Lab was still a lot of work for a one hour class though. Your TA determines whether or not the class will be hard to get an A. Mine was amazing.

Dr. Beaver truly wants everyone to pass. He's over CHEM101's lab department at the moment and he made it a better experience than previous professors (based on prior undergrads' experiences). I was TERRIFIED of chem before this class, but I loved it. I'm excited to take more chem now! Dr. Beaver it the best professor I've ever had, and this is the best class I've taken. reviews.comment: Good professor in office hours, but his class is way too difficult for an intro course. Practice problems he gives are no where near as hard as what is on the exams. Just a warning that you should know literally everything in the textbook for exams.

Dr. Beaver really cares about his students and their success in the class. He provides tons of tutoring opportunities throughout the semester, and will take the time to help the entire class at times, if no one is understanding the material. I highly recommend him for CHEM101.

Joshua Beaver is a great teacher and passionate about teaching chemistry, but is rude in office hours and overall extremely unapproachable. Nice guy to the students he likes, but to everyone else, incredibly rude and honestly scary.

reviews.comment: Dr. Beaver was extremely caring and dedicated to his students, making my experience with chemistry at Carolina much better than expected. Don't be afraid to approach him, he really is a great person!

reviews.comment: For some reason Dr. Beaver gets a bad wrap but he does his absolute best to make chem interesting and easy to understand. he really cares about his students and wants everyone to succeed and enjoy the material. Go to his problem solving sessions, do ALL of the extra practice he assigns, and be engaged in class and you can totally do really well!

Chem 101 at UNC is one of the toughest courses around. The good thing is, Dr. Beaver gives you all of the tools you need to succeed. reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: I loved taking CHEM 101 with him so much! He does a great job of teaching a large amount of students what they need to learn, and in a fun way!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Dr. Beaver was a great professor. For chem 101, he does a good job of introducing the material to what is most people's first chem course at UNC. reviews.comment: He was an absolutely amazing professor, but the class was literally the hardest thing that I have ever done. I went to countless office hours and spent hours reviewing the material, but Dr. Beaver helped me through everything.

Right off, DO THE HOMEWORKS DO THE READINGS. They may seem boring but they will be the reason you pass or fail depending on how hard you work at them so you understand the material. reviews.comment: I'm not a "science" person, I've never taken chemistry before, and I liked this class, and Dr. Beaver is great. Dr. Beaver killed the Chem 101 game. Take this class with him if you can, he's an awesome lecturer and very accessible outside of class, gives great feedback

Dr. Beaver was never very clear on anything that was important for exams, which were a huge part of the grade. I mean I'm not a chem person, but the class felt super difficult.
He cares about making the class engaging.

I agree that Dr. Beaver could get moody during class - but it was also his first semester as a lecturer. He nailed the "disappointed dad" speech, but wouldn't do it if he didn't care. reviews.comment: Professor Beaver was good, especially for having such a large class.  You get out what you put into the class.

Offers a lot of opportunities for office hours though.

In the beginning, you could tell that Dr Beaver was new, but towards the end he definitely improved. Go to office hours, because they help a lot, and he makes an effort to know as many names as possible. He's actually a really cool guy and wants to help his students succeed.

Dr. Beaver was a great teacher.  He was always excited to teach and explained concepts in a way that made sense. He was also very helpful and cared about his students' success. If you read and do your work on time an A is very possible.

Dr. Beaver is amazing, enthusiastic, caring, and puts effort into teaching the class. Class setup? Lowkey trash. You can PASS Chem 101, but you have to work for it. Don't wait until 2 days before the exam to actually start studying, you won't do well on them. Now this professor. reviews.comment: Allows you to drop your lowest test grade but if your overall test average is still a 50 or below, you're screwed.

reviews.comment: Dr. Beaver is a great professor for Chem 101! He is extremely enthusiastic and really engages the class during lectures. He is especially helpful in open group office hours where he will clearly explain any topic that a student is having trouble with.

Chem 101 is going to be challenging no matter who your professor is at UNC. Office hours are tremendously helpful, especially open group because you can get to know Dr. Beaver while actually understanding the material. This class makes you think, not memorize.

While a decent professor, the homework (due every few days online) helps you learn way more than you do in class. Many people only go to class to answer clicker questions to get all points for participation. Can get irritated and condescending during lectures and this can impact the amount of material you cover significantly.

reviews.comment: Not a good professor. Be prepared for clicker questions which barely work and no explanations for the answers. If he does explain something, its usually explained wrong and he leaves the class confused. TONS of homework and extremely hard tests.

Beaver knows his stuff, but isn't a great lecturer. He does tons of clicker questions instead utilizing lecture time to actually teach and explain the content. reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Take 101 with someone else. This is a flipped classroom, which is ridiculous for such a difficult subject. He expects you to know things coming in that people with little chem background know. If you didn't take AP Chem in high school, you're screwed. reviews.comment: Dr. Beaver truly cares about his students and takes time to explain whenever someone has a question. His explanations are comprehensive yet easy to understand. He's a really great guy!

This is his first year teaching so I have to cut him some slack, but Dr. Beaver is mediocre at best. He gets angry when a select few don't watch his videos or study hard enough and takes it out on the rest of the class. He posts practice questions with no answers so if you don't know what you're doing, you'll probably end up teaching yourself wrong
He believes in posting questions but not the answer key. How are we supposed to know if we get the questions right?

So far, Dr. Beaver has been a decent professor. CHEM 101 is not an easy class but he's very energetic and wants everyone to succeed. He usually explains everything clearly and also gives you time to process and understand the chemistry problems that are done in class. As long as you continue to study consistently and do the HW you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Beaver is an excellent chemistry professor. He is clearly very smart and knows what he is talking about. Dr. Beaver basically just reads directly from the PowerPoint slides with little additional explanation. He often seems confused when solving problems. If you don't go to office hours or peer tutoring, you basically just have to teach yourself everything.

Dr. Beaver is new.  Don't take his class if given the opportunity to take another teacher's class.  He always reads off the slides and doesn't explain much on each slide. Deaven is a great professor who makes you think!

reviews.comment: This class has readings, an essay, and presentation projects. Katie clearly cares about making the class interesting and informative. You can tell she's very passionate about what she teaches and only wants you to succeed. If you put in the work and listen in class then you'll be fine. I will say that it is homework heavy, so a good amount of readings that can be quite difficult to understand.
amazing, would take.

I really enjoyed her teaching honestly, very enjoyable and the way that she would make the content was engaging. I would say that there was a lot of reading at times even though she tried to get the readings as short as possible. She's very engaged and passionate about the material and wants us to do the best we can in the class.

This is for 102 but there wasn't an option. Katie is very kind, accessible, and fun in class. Heavy emphasis on classroom discussion and participation. Easy to get B+/A-, not an easy A due to lots of reading and high expectations for understanding. I really loved this class and feel like I learned a lot about philosophy and good communication!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Deavon is genuinely one of my favorite prof! She is so caring/accommodating to everyone's needs. She'll work w/ you if you talk to her. She has a clear outline of what she expects. There are 1-3 readings each week (some are dense some not), video diaries, no exams, a final presentation, 3 big papers, + student facilitations. TAKE HER CLASS!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Katie clearly cares about her students and classes. While sometimes a little disorganized, she does not hesitate to adjust class or grades around it. Very generous with deadlines and assignments. Clearly loves philosophy and wants her students to learn. She really just wants people to participate, discuss, and ask questions. Would highly recommend!

I really enjoyed bioethics, not just the content of the course but also the materials Katie used to teach.  I loved the class was hands on and discussion based. I felt like I got what I brought in. I worked hard and got a grade that reflected that work. She is a fair grader, but it is def not a class you can coast through.

Katie genuinely cares about your learning. She focuses a ton on small group discussions and truly values every idea brought forward in class. When discussions weren't flowing she always adapts and gets people involved, super engaging and genuinely cares about her classroom environment and student success.

Topics in this class were a bit confusing, and her explanations were super long but I felt like I never gained much insight. Our first paper went well, but it was confusing when it came to the final paper draft as we got the rubric 4 hours before the deadline. While unorganized, she was understanding and fun in lecture.

Katie offers an inspiring list of topics and approaches them in a contagiously enthusiastic manner. Sometimes her lectures are overly "improvised" as she attempts to respond to whatever question someone raises. She may appear a bit disorganized, but at the end of the day she's a very charitable grader and the course overall was pretty low-stake.

Great person, Awful professor. Katie is terribly disorganized, doesn't tell her students what is expected of them, then proceeds to grade harshly. She doesn't do a good job providing advice and feedback on the papers, which make up most of the grade, and rarely has time to meet before big assignments are due. Would not recommend this experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment:
absolutely goated. class is very discussion and small group heavy, and she cares a lot about students' learning. no midterm and the final is just a presentation. class was pretty disorganized, but this was her first sem at unc, so i doubt it'd be an issue in the future.
idk why people are wining about her grading; it's pretty average in difficulty
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Katie is a little disorganized and grades go in late. There are lots of readings in this class (PHIL 143). There is also a lot of writing and your grade is determined by this. The final exam was extremely easy (a really short presentation). As long as you stay on top of the work and put effort into your papers, you should succeed in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: There is no grading criteria so you will never know what she wants. So, so disorganized. It almost feels like she has never taught before, everything is so unclear in this class. Do NOT take it. I have no idea what my grade is in the class because she's graded like 1 assignment total. Avoid at all costs. Class consists of random tangents.

Extremely intelligent and makes interesting connections from our readings. Class discussions were engaging. Some people got by without reading the books, but I'd recommend doing them. I'm a slow reader, and some of audiobooks were 15 hours, so keeping up was hard with quick turnarounds. Need to take quality annotations, books are used in exams
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I took this class because Professor Dore spoke to my class the previous semester, and I found her to be an inspiring and engaging lecturer. The class was difficult but so rewarding, and as everything came together towards the end of the semester, I became convinced she is a genius. I highly recommend taking one of her classes and hope to again.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Unless you're passionate about the South, useless class. Dore had us read "The Sound and the Fury." Don't read the book last minute, and make good annotations in the book. Buy it, don't rent. Essay grading was a bit harsh, but you'll be fine if you know the book. Other readings don't matter. She can appear condescending and cold calls.

Everyone had pretty low grades until Assignment 2/3, and then they dropped our exam grade. It's a dreadful class and I absolutely hated it BUT most people ended up with an A in the end so it wasn't that awful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things
