Prof Daye is great. You get out of the class what you want but it's very easy. Recommend for an easy gen ed and he's super chill.

Professor Daye is really approachable and overall, just a really cool person. The workload isn't too bad with about 20-30 pages of book reading every night. You are graded on participation (go to class), one short paper and a final creative project that can literally be anything you want. Great class to get a lot of gen ed credit and an easy A!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I wish all professors were like him. He wanted everyone to participate but class was far from stressful. This class was a breath of fresh air and I would take any class with him again!

THE ABSOLUTE BEST! This was the one class that I actually looked forward to during my week. Prof Daye is truly a caring individual that wants the best for his students and he actually checks in on his students during class. As long as you try your best and participate, grades shouldn't be a concern for you.

Professor Daye has been my favorite UNC professor! He is very passionate about poetry and truly cares about his students. The course isn't too difficult, but get ready to read a decent amount of poetry. There is one short paper, a slides presentation, and a creative final project. The course is really insightful and I had a great time! 10/10

Professor Daye is such an amazing person, and he truly cares for his students. He tried to be intimidating in the first class, but he is actually a teddy bear and someone who is knowledgeable in his criteria. Absolutely loved the workshops and I would love to take another class from him!

Professor Daye is such a kind and hilarious person. At the beginning of the semester I was nervous because he comes off slightly intimidating, but he really just wants everyone to participate. He's a lenient grader and the workload is manageable (50ish pages of poetry reading each week, one 4-5 page paper w/ presentation, and a final project)

Professor Daye is a great teacher, he is occasionally disorganized but that is my only criticism. Took him for poetry workshop, some might think his class is easy or whatever but I don't think it's about whether it's hard or easy. Prof Daye's goal is to help you develop as a writer and if you put in the effort, pay attention and write, you will.

One of my favorite professors I've had so far. He is super engaging and is actually interested in what we have to say. He encouraged me and pushed me to be better at writing. He grades super easily too and you will most likely get an A as long as you participate in discussions every so often. Would definitely take him again!

engl105 with prof daye was sooo easy. he just wants u to come to class & participate, & he likes talking to us about stuff other than english. sometimes hes vague about what he expects for assignments but they were all super duper easy & were not graded harshly at all!
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Daye is very caring and isn't a difficult grader. However some of the assignment expectations can be vague and thus tricky to know what he wants. He LOVES poetry, pretty cool guy overall!

easily one of the best teachers Ive had at UNC. Such a great, caring guy and loves to hear peoples stories. When I first joined the class I was afraid to speak and share my poems, then towards the end I wouldnt shut up since I enjoyed the class that much. If he offers another class, Im in.

Definitely the best choice for 105. He's a great guy and he makes showing up to class easy (even tho he cancels A LOT). As long as you put effort into the assignments, you will do well as he is not a tough grader. I will truly miss his class because he's just the best. Also he's a published poet if you're interested in that!

Literally the most chill professor ever. He would cancel class half of the time and the other half we'd spend the 50 minutes just talking about random things. There were maybe 2 projects I had to put effort into. We didn't have a final or quizzes either.

Professor Daye genuinely cares about each and everyone of his students. He gets upset when people don't participate or skip class without a good excuse. All his quizzes are open text book. His projects take a while to do but if you put in the effort you will get a good grade. HE HATES WHEN PEOPLE PUT IN NO EFFORT. Overall very chill guy.

I thoroughly enjoyed Professor Daye and looked forward to his class each day. He is very chill, easy to talk to, and he is guaranteed to make you laugh. Assignments were simple, lots of time was given to complete them, and they were not graded harshly. Highly recommend this professor!

Prof. Daye if a kind hearted individual with a great sense of humor and a passion for English. He makes an effort to take with everyone in the class atleast once and often tries to connect the topic of discussion with everyday life.

Professor Daye is a really interesting person, which means he sometimes talks about irrelevant topics in class. He's an easy grader when he knows that you put forth effort, but won't let you get away with murder. He genuinely cares a lot about his students, and I would recommend taking his class.
Daye is the absolute best. You won't have daily homework assignments, just projects that you have A LOT of time to do and are not graded harshly. 10/10 recommend him.
Great professor!

You complete assignments based on lectures recorded during COVID. It feels more like a formatting course with little real instruction rather than a high-level modeling course. There was little relevance for banking or high-level finance roles. Overall, gets you more comfortable with Excel, but a certification would have done the same.
Professor Day is a very enthusiastic and knowledgeable professor. The assignments can take a while, but class only meets once a week, and he's always available for extra help. Really useful class!
Travis is the best! This is the most useful class I've taken at the B School. The weekly assignments can take a while, but he gives clear instructions and feedback.

reviews.comment: Travis is great. Take the class if you can it'll help you a lot. Pretty low-commitment too
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Most useful class you'll take. Assignment+Quizz every week but it helps practice.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: you learn so much, assignment directions are super clear and very manageable.
Professor Day is one of the best instructors I've had. He combines high standards with genuine support and clarity.
Great guy, funny, and cares about his students. Highly recommend as a MAC student or anyone using excel.

Professor Day runs a very well structured and formatted class. His notes files are very helpful, and he is very receptive to helping you out in class. The work is a lot and is challenging at times, but if you manage your time you will be ok. I learned a ton about Excel and recommend taking this class.

Note that the final is 50% of your grade.

Professor Day is an exceptional teacher. While the material was quite dense, his methodical approach to teaching made it easy to digest the information. 

In response to the comments about the final being heavily weighted, as long as you are diligent in completing the assignments, there should be no reason for you to not do well on the exam.

Final is weighed 50% of your grade and you cannot check your answers. Content is very useful but directions are often convoluted. 1-2 hrs of async that tbh could be 15 mins if edited down. Lots of overlap between lecture and async so its kinda boring. Grading is always quick and feedback is great. Useful and necessary class but needs some revision.

Great class - Professor Day makes things super accessible and assignments are clear. Content was very well organized and there was a lot of transparency surrounding expectations and grading. Class was held once a week online and was easy to fit into my schedule. Super useful content, highly recommend.
Professor Travis is an amazing professor and person, he made learning new things in excel fun and interesting. Really a good class to get an edge on excel modelling.
Practical course, good sense of humor, solid teaching and presentation skills, definitely recommend.
Has an extreme attention to detail in grading of assignments. Final exam is heavily weighted, which makes some of the assignments feel tedious in comparison. Professor is hilarious in class.
Prepare your mind ahead of time, as not everything will be taught in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Day expects much but also gives you all the tools and knowledge you need to succeed. I found his teaching style and class format to be very informative--his notes were an excellent resource and the assignments helped to lock in that knowledge and skill. His enthusiasm for the material made it my favorite class this semester!
Very strict and tedious but the course is useful.

Travis is the GOAT. Easily the most useful class I've taken so far at UNC. Assignments take awhile, but at the end of the day they teach you how to be an excel demon. Took on top of a super heavy course-load–wouldn't recommend but definitely doable and still learn a lot.
Travis is an exceptionally knowledgeable and professional teacher. I've learned a tremendous amount in this class—thank you!

This was one of the best courses I've taken at UNC. Prof Day makes Excel so accessible and if you at least start the assignments before the Wednesday classes, you can ask him questions live (gives you "lab time" to work on assignments during class). He was honestly hilarious too and made me look forward to class.

Helpful and realistic class for jobs/work. If you frontload a lot of the work (do the assignment and the quiz before class - 3/4 hours a week) this class is super easy. If you wait until Fri/Sat this class seems hard. Hang out in class with camera on and just watch the show for free. Can't complain.

Professor Day has mastered teaching Excel. His explanations are clear, he covers the important stuff, and his instructions for assignments are detailed and clear. He has high expectations but he is fair and supportive. He really wants to help you learn the material. The assignments are carefully designed so that you practice what is useful. A+
Awesome teacher! Very clear instructions and grading. I wish all my professors were such great communicators!

Professor Day was among the most well-organized, present, and thoughtful professors I've had at UNC. If you dedicate time to knowing the material and completing the assignments, you will do well. I recommend doing every assignment a week in advance and coming to the class sessions with specific questions, which he will answer, ensuring you do well.

Professor Day is by far one of the best professors I've ever had at UNC. He's a very enthusiastic professor and loves teaching this class, and cares a lot about his students.The final is tough, but as long as you have a good understanding of the notes provided and do any practice quizzes or redo assignments, you will be okay.

520 is without a doubt the most useful class at UNC - take it. That said, make sure to get an early start on the homework every week, or it'll make for a lot of miserable Saturday nights (ask me how I know).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Super practical class across disciplines. Travis is awesome - super accessible outside of class and helpful assistance on assignments. Weekly assignments are very time consuming but are incredibly straightforward after watching Travis's videos. The final is worth 50%, but if you put in the work on the assignments and quizzes you will succeed.

Do not take this class if you: 
- alr have a heavy course load (this class will DOMINATE your time)
- are a bad test-taker (the final is worth 50% of the class, there's no backtracking or notes allowed, and tbh the test is not reflective of a true Excel real-world application)

TAKE AT YOUR OWN RISK.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I avg 95% on quizzes and assignments but the final tanked my grade. I studied, but the final will have you second guessing everything. NO BACKTRACKING ALLOWED. The final's worth 50% of the grade. I'm concerned that people could easily cheat on the final, skewing the class performance. Helpful, practical course to learn excel, and would recommend

Professor Day is awesome. He cares so much about his students and truly wants to maximize everyone's potential. Professor Day looks to challenge you while also providing tremendous support. If you put in the effort, you will do well in this class. While I would not say his class was a walk in the park, I learned so much which I know is his goal.
Very applicable and practical course.

reviews.comment: very understanding, class is extremley straight foraward and easy to understand. Assingments take time but very helpfuul
dedicated prof with lots of knowledge, practical assignments
Amazing professor, I learned so much about excel. Only critique is that async and sync sessions cover the same material, so it's repetitive.

Busi 520 with Professor Day is a VERY useful class. If you aren't familiar with excel already it will be a tough class but it is worth taking for the experience. Expect a weekly quiz, assignment, and video lectures. Professor Day is also a great teacher and is very responsive to emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Really great class that is useful for every day life! Professor Day was great at communicating and reinforcing the concepts taught from the asynch videos. You won't regret taking this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I started this class with little Excel experience. I am so proud of my hard earned grade! Excel, in general, is applicable to the business world. However, this class will take you to another level and the skills learnt will distinguish you from the rest. It was well worth it! Thanks Travis!

If you think you know everything you need to know about excel, think again. Travis Day's course is one of the most practical courses I have taken in all my academic ventures. Must take for anyone doing accounting or who works with excel and wants to know how to be beyond proficient.
Professor is really particular about his grading criteria, but he backs it up with a lot of help. I really enjoyed him! I've also used the material in my current job right away
Good teacher. Useful skills. Very detail specific grading.

Professor Day is very clear on what he expects, and he is almost always available if help is needed. Don't expect a cake walk for a class, but if you put the time in learning what he teaches, you will gain far more knowledge than most other classes.

Prof. Day is a great teacher an Busi520 was arguably the most helpful class I have taken at UNC. He is responsive via email and quizzes / attendance are extremely manageable. Be prepared to dedicate 4-5 hours of your week outside of class for the assignments. Work must be completed on time. Overall take the class, but only if you have some time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Amazing very good class

Trust me, It's highly grateful to have this professor and learn from him because he makes so much efforts to teach us useful functions and improve our excel skills. 
I wouldn't say it was easy, it was definitely challenging and sometimes I was stressed out because of heavy duty homework but his class was worth it for sure! Thank you, Travis!

The Professor has a clear passion for both Excel and teaching, which made his class enjoyable. Despite the strong focus on the final exam, the course provided a lot of practical knowledge and was thoroughly engaging.

i'm sorry but the way each homework takes over 10 hours to complete (4+ hour async lecture videos with 10+ sheets of files), I always get the biggest headache when trying to read his instructions. He needs to be more straightforward and concise, I shouldn't have to read a whole two paragraphs for something he could have written in 1 sentence.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Although you absolutely have to put everything into the course, you gain so many valuable skills. This class took a lot of time to prepare for but after I completed everything I realized how much better equipped I was. Professor Day is also so kind and available to students. Just push yourself to learn as much as possible and you will be fine!
Professor Day is an exceptional, dedicated professor with a sincere interest to help serious students grasp difficult content. He cares and is very generous with his time
Travis is very helpful on assignments and usually responds to emails within several minutes. The weekly assignments can take many hours if you are not super familiar with excel.

Travis is the best teacher I've ever had. He loves teaching and he really nerds out on Excel. The homework and quizzes are tough, but you get out of it what you put into it. I started my first finance role after 10+ years in sales/marketing/PR. My Excel skills were far behind my colleagues. After his class, my co-workers ask me Excel questions.
Really passionate about Excel and the things you learn can be applied outside of school. Assignments are a beast so give yourself plenty of time to work on them.

Such a nice professor! At first he comes off intimidating but he is really warm and he really cares about everyone doing well. I could sit on zoom and ask him as many questions as I wanted, and he wouldn't say anything like "we are over class time." He is very selfless.

reviews.comment: Prob the most useful class to take in the B-school, will help out with internships and anything that uses excel. Assignment every week that takes 3-5 hours. Final is worth 50% so that could ruin ur grade. But, Travis is the Goat of excel and teaching it.

One of the most useful courses I have ever taken! Amazing instructor! I learned so much and truly appreciate the amount of detail, effort, and clarity provided in the async videos and during class. He provides impeccable notes to match the modules. He is very passionate about teaching and genuinely cares about the quality of work    he expects!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: A little heavy on the "dad jokes" but I didn't mind. Professor Day knows his materials backward and forward. He's also willing to help you with Excel and Microsoft problems unrelated to coursework. Even as a well-seasoned, Excel user, I found his course useful to improve my skills. Highly recommended.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He's an amazing teacher who's always there to help and easy to reach. His classes are super interesting and fun. He's very detailed about homework, but you'll learn a lot from his class.

The only thing I did not like about Professor Day's class is the fact it went from 10 PM to midnight.  Still, he is a very engaging professor, so it was not hard to stay awake during his lectures.  The class is really useful and Professor Day does a great job teaching Excel's important tools.

Prof. Day is incredibly knowledgeable about Excel. He's very accessible to all students, even in the online format. He is also clear and objective about grading because he cares about accuracy and quality of work. I learned a lot from him and sincerely appreciated the way he runs his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: The class is very applicable to professional life regardless of industry. I learned a ton and will carry these skills with me going forward. The teaching style is mostly lecture, but the notes are extremely valuable and very thorough. I would recommend this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Most useful class at UNC. Usually 90+ minutes of videos each week, just watch on 2x or 1.5x speed to help go faster. Assignments are easy as long as you watch weekly videos. Very time consuming class but also very rewarding. Only bad thing is assignments are due 8am on Sunday, so don't procrastinate! Watch the videos each week. Highly recommend!!!

Professor Day loves what he does and is passionate about excel. This class was one of the most helpful classes  I have ever taken! I learned a lot about excel and I know it will greatly help me in the future. However, the assignments took me about 3 hours a week to complete. It was a lot of work but definitely worth it!

The BEST class I have ever taken in my time at UNC! Everyone talks about how hard the class is, and I was scared going in, but it really is not that bad. Travis is such a good teacher and you will learn SO MUCH useful Excel stuff in this class. The assignments are long, but start early in the week & you'll be fine. TAKE THIS CLASS!

This class is useful but be prepared. I didn't find lectures to be valuable so you just teach yourself as you work through the hw (which took 4-6 hrs on avg). They're pretty tedious but it's not too hard to get good grades for them. The final exam was 50% of the grade which I found a little dramatic, so that dropped my grade from a 96 average lol.

MAC 707 is the most thoughtfully planned online course I have ever taken. His instruction is crystal clear and in total alignment with the notes he provides. Live sessions are a review of the week's lectures and notes. Homework is time consuming but every task is straight from the notes. He is very caring and responds to questions quickly.

Professor Day is really good about being available at all times to meet with students. If you put in the work, you will do well. BUSI 520 is an extremely valuable class, as most top tier banks look for students who have extremely good excel skills. If you have the chance to take it, definitely do as it helps you a ton after college.

Travis is one of the best professors I have ever met. His class materials are most valuable and practical. Travis is very good at making difficult parts of the course easier for us. He made lots of tips and explanations for course materials and homework assignments. He knows which part could be a problem for students.  I am so impressed.

Prof. Day is extremely talented and knowledgeable. The course structure of MAC 707 is well-planned and paced and the lectures were in-depth. It was a pleasure to attend his classes and I'd like to thank him for his continued efforts to make his courses relevant and palatable for students coming from different backgrounds.

Overall, Travis's teaching style is comprehensive. He really wants you to learn Excel. At first, I was a little overwhelmed by his vast notes files, but ultimately I came to view them for what they are: extremely useful resources that explain and demonstrate the functions and features he wants you to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Class was awesome!

I say very difficult because I'd been out of school for years and only used Excel for basic data entry. Professor Day's enthusiasm is infectious, and he wants you to succeed. Yes, he has high expectations, but this is a master's level course. Lots of homework, but you'll only learn Excel by using it. This class greatly improved my Excel skills.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable and makes excel easy to understand for beginners while also teaching new skills/tricks to students with lots of excel experience. I came into this class with no excel skills and left feeling very comfortable with using excel.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you view the professor as a resource he will be. If you ask for help it will be given thoroughly! If you want to sit quietly and breeze by, this will not work as well.

Overall this class was very useful to learn the basics of excel. My main issue with the course is the unrealistic expectations set by professor Day. HW assignments that take 3-6 hours every week, a 2 hour zoom lecture, and often 4+ hours of weekly videos. It is too much given that we have other classes. Grading depends on your TA, and final is 50%.
Professor Day is definitely knowledgeable about Excel. The class itself was alright. Assignments took a while so be prepared to dedicate some time for those. The final is 50% so be prepared to study.

I enjoyed this class - you can get a reasonable grade without going to class and you get out what you put in with your Excel skills. Travis replies quickly and genuinely wants students to learn from the class. Assignments take 2-5 hours a week and grading can be picky. The final is worth 50% of your grade but curved so A/B range is doable.

Professor Day definitely cares about the material, but the class is tough. Assignments take 2-5 hours and are due on Sunday mornings. The final exam is 50% of the grade and it's pretty tough as well. The class is once a week, but it's 2 hours and not the easiest to follow along with. I will say that the actual material is useful.

Extremely tough to please with ridiculously detailed assignments, which can take up to 6 hours to complete
Will convince you to buy a windows laptop, even though a mac works perfectly fine
Needs things to be done ONLY in his way

Professor Day is a super understanding professor who clearly cares about the development of his students. Busi 520 is a great course that I would recommend. From a work load perspective, it is very manageable. There are thorough notes and pre recorded videos (essentially in place of lectures) that are helpful, even after you finish the course

Travis Day is the worst professor I've ever had. I don't know if I can even consider him a professor as he doesn't lecture, assign peer or group work, or is really there for his students. Theres 1 session per week (doesn't teach), and so you use prerecorded lessons to teach yourself. Weekends are ruined, bc 4-5 hr assignments are due 8:00 Sunday.

Great class to take. Homeworks are laid out well and the notes he gives are super useful to help walk through the assignment. Not a huge fan of the grading structure and his grading scale is harder than a normal one (95 to get an A). He did curve our grades at the end and was very helpful over email for any questions. A tedious but necessary class
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Super useful class. Weekly excel projcts that take like 3-6 hours each. You can easily get an A on the projects (55%) because you can work with others. You don't have to go to class. 45% of grade is the final exam which is tough. If you take this class be ready to grind before exam. You don't have to go to class at all. I never went.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Terrible instructor. Course materials are minimal, perhaps to prevent redistribution. Ridiculous to pay tuition just to be told what to learn and then have to search the internet for answers. Live sessions are just lame summaries of pre-recorded videos. Zero feedback on assignments; questions were dodged both during and outside of class. Shameful.

The class was almost entirely online. He gives you reading and powerpoint slides but you have to teach yourself the entire course. He does know it front and back and can help over the phone if you need it. The material is super helpful and in depth so that makes it worth it. Tough grader and final is 50%.

If you are an undergrad and not great at computers.. BEWARE. Homework assignments take about 4-8hours each and are graded extremely hard. Also, homework is 45%, quizzes are 5%, and the final is 50% of your grade. I had a 90 avg before the final and it brought me down to a C+ overall. Try to take another elective if possible. Yes-useful.. but hard!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Your final grade is determined by homework and the final exam. Homeworks are graded incredibly hard with point deductions for so much as not CC'ing your own email.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Not MUSC 89, but MUSC 150 Intro to Hip Hop is the best class I've taken at UNC. So chill but I have learned a lot from the class. He's great and I would highly recommend you take it for FC-AESTH
Super chill guy and very cool -he's a rapper and poet. He really cares about his students and its truly a free class
Not sure if IDST 101 can even be hard, but Dr. Livingston was such a nice professor. You can tell he loves his job.

He is very kind and you can tell he loves his jobs and students. Grading criteria was unclear at some points so points would be deducted by surprised. He was not the most accessible by email, but you shouldn't need to contact him if you submit assignments and go to class.
Had for college thriving - super sweet and open. Definitely wants to know all of his students. Highly recommend!

Dr. Livingston is one of if not the best professor I will ever have. He is truly a great guy and is super caring for everyone that he teaches. He will talk with you after class about topics that you are interested in and genuinely wants to help in any way he can.

I LOVE Professor Livingston!! The best guy, both inside and outside the classroom. I don't think you can choose who you get for college thriving, but if you get him, thank your lucky stars—the nicest, most caring guy ever who truly wants you to succeed. I genuinely feel better about myself every time I leave that class.
Hes awesome everyone should take a class of his

He has lots of knowledge on hip-hop and the history around higher education. His class is very engaging and fun. It took me out of my comfort zone but it was probably the best class I have ever taken.

Dr. Livingston is the most down to earth, kind hearted, selfless professor there is. He was my first ever professor and genuinely the best one I think I will have. Very clear grading scale, a lot of emphasis on growth, and very understanding of situations students have outside the classroom.

Genuinely the most down to earth kind hearted professor I've ever had. He is so obviously caring about his students and really helped us be successful throughout the tough times of freshman year. The man never stops smiling and it's contagious, I didn't think IDST 101 would actually help me thrive in college but it really did with him.

AMAZING prof for idst101, super cool guy, let me miss class for a family emergency and was SO kind about it. He won't cold call on you, he is incredibly respectful and genuinely an interesting person. IDST 101 is a drag of a class, but he makes it lowkey kind of fun.

Prof. James is approachable and kind and gives good lectures. She's open to all perspectives and brings a sense of humor to class. She helped me improve as a writer. The reading load is completely manageable (~25 pages a class).

THE HARDEST A I'VE EVER HAD. I'm a dual stem major and this was way too much for a 100-lvl class. I really enjoyed the format and lectures but the workload/grading are par with my 400-lvl core classes. I did every reading (10hrs/wk) and studied 20hrs per exam, and BARELY managed to scrape up an A. Rating isn't lower bc problem is the class not her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor James is incredibly kind. I honestly learned more than I expected in. I earned an A but this required an EXTREME amount of hours and effort. I would compare this 100 level class to a 300 level course at UNC. Feedback on midterm is only available via office hours and is largely based on the “vibe” of your writing rather than a rubric.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nice professor, I really enjoyed
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This NEW 100-level entry course only has 4 grades in the class: 2 papers, a midterm, and a final. There are no assignments, activities, slides, or lecture notes. Read 5-6 readings before each class. Her extremely harsh grading is only acceptable for a higher-level required class for SCLL students. I don't recommend this class at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Would not recommend at all. The professor is very kind and actually gives decent lectures. However, this is essentially an AP Gov/US history class with nonexistent grading criteria. Her midterm and paper grades are completely arbitrary with no clear explanation as to why she took off points. Otherwise known as "the vague B." Would avoid if possible
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: lots of busy work and the lectures are hard to follow, exams are hard for no reason. attendance is graded heavily and the group project that goes across the whole semester is unorganized and not easy to follow.

Really nice prof. The lectures are really boring, but he really knows his stuff. Exams are trickier than you would think. I pulled out a B on the first one after starting studying the night before. There's a big group project and you're randomly assigned to groups, so as long as everyone does stuff you will be ok. Offers extra credit.
Gives extra credit which is nice, really boring lectures he just talks the whole time, strict attendance requirement, and just so much busy work
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: DeFreese's voice is the most monotone, boring voice ever. The content in this class is organized a little bit oddly and could be done better. It is just about a bunch of different theories you need to memorize. This class is one of worst classes I've taken at unc. Also, there is a big group project that is so busy work.
exams are trick questions and you must memorize every slide. average was a 65 for exam 1. he makes the class harder than it needs to be. dont take

JD is a really good professor. He's very understanding and responds quickly to emails. He also grades really quickly. Our exam grades were released the afternoon after we took the test. Class can be challenging and instructions aren't always the clearest for the big group project. Exams are fair but not the easiest.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Defreese is so kind and a great professor! He is a quick grader and gives you feedback to improve on future assignments. Class was group project heavy, but if you get a good group you are fine and he is not too harsh on the group papers or presentation. Tests straightforward. Groups made doing class assignments easier. Take him!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: One of the best professors in the department IMO. Definitely recommend!

I love Dr. DeFreese and would take another class with him. He is very understanding of students! Despite having a pretty tough attendance requirement, he really cares about the material he teaches and makes class engaging.
I really enjoyed his class. And he's just a nice guy.

Defreese is definitely one of the dryest lecturers I've had, but he knows what he's talking about. I just sometimes find it difficult to stay engaged. The class is broken into groups which honestly is helpful and I enjoyed talking to them. The semester long project is a bit of a pain, but not too hard, nor graded too harshly.

Quizzes are straightforward, with the answers coming from the textbook. The group project can be daunting but very manageable. The groups are randomly assigned. Exams are fair. For exams, make sure you understand the models discussed in the lecture well. Extra credit is offered. Dr.DeFreese is very understanding and patient, so reach out.

I liked 181, but be prepared to read the textbook and turn in an assignment before each class. There's also a semester long group project, which was frustrating at times. All exams given were fair in my opinion. He is an understanding individual and is willing to work with you to accommodate your needs outside of class or his office hours!

I loved Dr. Defreese, his lectures were straightforward and exams matched the material presented in them. Lots of low-stakes assignments that you pretty much will get credit for if completed. There is a big group project that is considerable for grades but if you have a good group (assigned) you'll be fine. Take with Defreese if you can!

Recommend taking this class with the other professor. If you are not a good test taker don't take this class. Test were made hard for no reason. I made a 100% on every quiz and most assignments outside of class besides a few and receive partial credit with no feedback. If you get a bad group for the semester long group project then good luck.

Such a great professor! He gives extra credit, which I wish I had taken advantage of earlier. Quizzes are easy, straight from the textbook. Most assignments are group work (assignment groups). Just make sure to put effort into having good communication within the group. Overall wonderful class!

Overall, Dr. DeFreese is a good professor. He gives a lot of examples to understand the material. He is a fast talker so be ready for that. The tests are mainly based on memorization and being able to apply the material to "real life situations". This class I group work heavy also. Overall, other than exams this class is easy its not really to much

Dr. DeFreese was an OK lecturer, if I could do it again I would take this class with Ling Beisecker. She did a guest lecture for our class and she was much more engaging and interesting. The class is based around group work (groups are chosen for you), which was sometimes difficult but overall fun. The exams were worded poorly and were difficult.

Everything was pretty easy except for the tests. Even though I studied a few days in advance, the tests were heavily memorization-based, which I struggled with. My test average was in the mid 80's and it brought me from an A to an A-. There is a group lab project and partners are random and it is relatively time-consuming. Overall an easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Defresse is a great choice for 181. The class is lecture and terminology heavy, but it's not conceptually difficult, just a lot of memorization. Not a huge fan of the group project, but it's manageable and graded easily. He seems super serious but he does care about his students. Do the extra credit! Mandatory attendance (you can miss 3 classes).

Dr. DeFreese is a great professor, although his lectures can be a little boring. There is a group project which takes most of the semester and a presentation. Two exams and a final, which is cumulative. I would take a class by him again, just really did not like the group project.

One of the easiest classes I've taken. All exams come from in class slides. I got a B+ cause I never studied but if you put in like 3 days to prepare for each exam it's an easy A. A lot of your grade is a group project. 
Homeworks take like 2 seconds. Genuinely enjoyed this class. Dr. Defreese is a nice, interesting professor

Dr. Defreese's class is a little lecture heavy, but the material is interesting and easy to understand. Tests and quizzes aren't bad if you are paying attention and doing your work! Definitely recommend him for 181.

Defreese is really kind and caring and his class is pretty easy but also, interesting! There is one group project which is difficult over Zoom. He takes attendance every day so be sure to go to class but all powerpoints are posted and tests/quizzes are straight from the powerpoints.

Prof JD is super chill... class is so easy. Attendance is taken, so go to class and you will do fine on the exam. Very sports psych and super interesting. A lot is common sense just elaborated upon. Genuinely enjoyed this class. SUPER EASY AND INTERESTING!!
The class was easy, but the group projects were annoying, especially if you don't have good group members because you all get graded for their poor work.

DeFreese genuinely loves what he does and this is conveyed through his lectures. His exams are not hard as long as you study the material and read the textbook. He's willing to work with you to make sure you understand the concepts and get the best experience out of his class.

Dr. DeFreese is a kind man and is very knowledgable in the subject. Despite COVID-19, he was still easily accessible via email and answered questions to the best of his knowledge. There is a lot of group work, but I had a good group. Quizzes/tests are straightforward from his lectures. Attendance is important and there are EC opportunities.

I feel like its probably unfair to rate a professor under these circumstances with COVID and everything being virtual. However, In this particular course I thought it was very odd the amount of group work we were made do. I have never done so much group work in a normal classroom much less in a virtual one. This made things very difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He gives lots of group work & projects but they're not hard. His quizzes are from textbook but exams are from slides, questions are always direct, he doesn't try to trick you. Dr. Defreese really cares about his students and the material is interesting, he gives so many opportunities for extra credit, overall a great guy!

Dr. DeFreese really cares about his subject and his students! He is very personable and understanding. The test questions come form the slides and he does not try to trick you. The quizzes are very simple but you will need the textbook. The group work/papers are not graded incredibly hard, either. He also gives out EC throughout the semester!

a pretty easy class. The exams were straight from the power points, and a lot of the class material is common sense. There are a lot of opportunities for extra credit. If you go to class, pay attention in lecture, and study a little you should do fine. The group projects are annoying, but they aren't graded too hard.

The class is mostly common sense. Simply go to class and pay attention and you will succeed. The textbook is used for weekly quizzes (not hard). He is not the most exciting man and a lot of the material is redundant. There is a lot of group work interaction but they again are very easy assignments.

The content makes a lot of sense but it is the terminology and theories that make it hard. I got a 76 on a test and still got an A so one thing doesn't define you. If you get a good group that makes all the difference. He grades the papers pretty easily, the tests are harder, but they're all MC. need to read/skim well the textbook for the quizzes
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Defreese is a fine teacher. He will lecture all class which yes can be boring, but the content is simple and easy to understand. You WILL have to read the book, but if you do a chapter a week you'll be fine. This class has a heavy emphasis on group work. While it can suck if you have an unmotivated group, it can also make things a ton easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: At the beginning of the semester you're put into groups that you will write two papers and do one presentation with throughout the semester along with other small in-class assignments. Test are relatively easy and straightforward as long as you pay attention in class. Very approachable & nice professor who clearly cares about his students.

The class is very group work heavy, but the assignments are basically just busy work (not difficult). The tests are very fair, based mostly off class material, all MC, and honestly very easy if you just review the slides and have a clear understanding of definitions. DeFreese is easy to talk to and gives many opportunities for extra credit. 10/10

This is perhaps one of the most boring classes I have ever taken. All of the information seems super redundant and most of the information is very general and common sense. However, JD makes the exams very specific to counteract the "common sense" material. Most of the class is doing pointless group work since he doesn't have a ton to teach.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GROUP PROJECTS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Such a boring lecturer. Also the class information is boring and kind of a joke. Sport psychology isn't a real subject and shouldn't be included in the major. Avoid this class if you can.

He's a good professor and was accessible. Lectures were kind of boring but the material was interesting so it was fine. A ton of group work and group projects but overall it helped my grade. Exams were kind of hard just because it was a lot of material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: One of the worst classes I've taken at UNC. Probably the most boring professor. Focuses too much on useless group work when the room isn't even set up to work in groups. Makes the tests extra hard for no reason. This class is the reason I'm dropping the EXSS major

He is the only one that teaches EXSS 181. DO NOT, I repeat, DO NOT take this class for granted. I went in thinking this class was easy, when it definitely is not. Tests are hard and I did worse than I thought I would in this class. He is a good lecturer and makes for a lot of group projects. There are peer evals, so make sure you contribute.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: This class is so awesome and so interesting, especially if you want to go into therapy or counseling, or care about family dynamics in general. You do have to do the readings, however, they are generally not that bad. The grading is pretty fair, but the essays and faciliataion do take a lot of time. And there is a learning reflection every week.
Great teacher, lots of readings to do though

Overall a good professor, however theres a lot of readings and participation is necessary. We talked about topics that were kind of controversial and she would sometimes challenge peoples ideas if they were different from her own which lowkey made me very uncomfortable.

Dr. Riger is a very intelligent and authentic professor, I recommend any of her courses. You will be required to do a lot of reading and participating, but I personally think learning is facilitated well in this course.

I cannot recommend Dana as a professor enough! Lectures were in-depth and engaging, and the content itself was fascinating. There were three exams total, and she gave study guides for all of them. Dana is caring and considerate, and easy to get a hold of. If you're thinking of taking a class with her, absolutely take it!

I definitely recommend taking EDUC 181 with Dr. Riger. Attendance is mandatory, but she is very accommodating if you email her beforehand. Her lectures are very interesting and engaging. The only reason I gave her a 4 instead of a 5 is because I think sometimes the class spent too much time "reviewing" than going deeper into content.

EDUC 181 was one of my favorite courses. Attendance is mandatory and class was mostly composed of lectures, but Dana's a great professor and definitely prepares you for exams (she's also hilarious). There's a good amount of homework, but grading is pretty lenient and there's lots of extra credit opportunities.

One of my favorite professors I have taken a class with. She is not only so funny and caring, but so knowledgable. It is impossible to not be fully absorbed in her lectures because she makes everything so engaging. The exams are straightforward and are not meant to trick you. I studied from the exam reviews and study guide, and did well.
Best teacher ever. Lectures are so fun and she is such a funny person.
Overall just a nice human who is very knowledgeable
Great overall! Lots of extra credit and overall really clear lessons, guidelines, and expectations.

Dr. Riger's lectures were very clear and easy to understand. She was also extremely kind and understanding when you had a question. The assignments weren't too much and the grace periods were life-savers. Also plenty of opportunities for extra credit.
Awesome professor! She is extremely knowledgeable and truly cares for her students and their ability to succeed. There is two exams but both online and then one in person final exam! Overall amazing!

It's clear that Dr. Riger really cares about each and every one of her students. She asks relevant and insightful questions to the class and is respectful of every person's points of view, whether everyone agrees or doesn't. This class did have a long semester-long paper that was a bit overwhelming, but she helped break it down in easy sections.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Dr. Riger is an AMAZING professor. She is hilarious, and she makes her lectures engaging. Tests were all take home, except for the final, but they were super easy as long as you pay attention. I highly recommend taking this class with her!
Amazing Professor and great lectures! There are three projects and 3 exams in the semester, nothing insane, and her lectures are actually helpful. She also does extra credit assigmnets

with her, you know what to expect from class and assignments. participate in class and she'll like you. she's very organized in her teaching, however, some things she says in class might be on the test, even if it isn't written down on the slides.

She makes her lectures very interesting and engaging. Her class is made of 3 assignments and 3 exams. Assignments are easy but can be time-consuming. Exams are application-based, so you really have to know your material. Offers plenty of extra credit and really wants you to succeed!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I have taken two classes with Dana at this point! She is one of my favorite professors at UNC and SoE. This class was very interesting content-wise, but her personal teaching style is so engaging and helpful. She grades well with clear expectations and a thorough rubric. I wish I could take more of her classes!

Dana has very engaging lectures and the assignments are always interesting. She grades very fairly, with clear grading criteria and so many opportunities for extra credit. You can tell she cares about people and her students.

Dr. Riger is an amazing lecturer and makes the content easy and fun to learn. There are 3 sort-of long papers and 1 video assignment. Exams are online take home (except for the final). The is a lot of reading and a lot of content to learn, but overall its pretty easy and Dr. Riger makes it even better.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: 10/10 class and teaching. She's funny and entertaining but also keeps the class on the subject. 2 take-home and 4 assignments that are very gently graded. As long as you come to class and pay attention, she makes it incredibly easy to do well in the class. She is pretty strict about attendance so be aware of that.

Dr. Riger is an incredible lecturer and makes talking about "awkward" topics very comfortable. She is clear in her rubrics, and is a fair and pretty easy grader. Drops questions on tests more than half the class gets incorrect and offers a ton of extra credit. Made me enjoy taking a summer class!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This was probably the best class I have ever taken. She is such a captivating teacher and she really wants the students to succeed. She is accessible and is one of the greatest teachers ever. Even if you are not interested in the subject, take one of her classes. genuinely.

Dr. Riger is my favorite prof so far at UNC. She is very knowledgeable about the course material and always knows how to make the class interesting and entertaining regardless of the content. Workload is not overbearing and I was able to take this as a gen ed and be fine. COIL project was difficult but she helped whenever asked and was pretty lax.

Awesome and accessible outside class. Loved this class and its content. She's empathetic and typically willing to work with you if you give an effort and approach her. Gives good feedback. Makes content very accessible. COIL project is kind of a mess, though. Thinks she's always right but asks for discussion and challenges those who speak up
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Riger is kind and tries her best to make an intro course interesting and engaging. She gives 4 assignments, 2 midterms, and a final exam. She /really/ wants you to do the readings which is kind of annoying. The projects start off fine but get exhausting by the end. She's accessible outside class and generally a good professor.
Dr. Riger was such a fun teacher. I learned so much and found the class very interesting. Attendance is required and it will bring down your grade if you don't attend.

Dana is by far my favorite professor I've had at UNC for the past three years. She is extremely intelligent and cares about her students. If you can take one of her classes I highly encourage it! She gives a lot of opportunities for extra credit and makes lectures fun and engaging.

I absolutely adored this class. Dr. Riger is such an understanding professors out there and she has this awesome thing called AMA which is an ask me anything section of class where people can anonymously ask her questions. It takes out the fear of looking dumb in front of a large class. I genuinely adored this class and would 100% take it again!
Lots of work in the two-week Maymester course. You should go in expecting a lot of work. However, she does provide extra credit and opportunities to learn from previous mistakes from projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Definitely an interesting professor. I would only take her Maymester course as its pretty easy if you spend a decent amount of time with it. Definitely look out for your tests/quizzes because they can get pretty tough but sometimes she will give you credit back. Overall a good teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Riger was...interesting to say the least. She had her own opinions and wasn't always receptive to hear from others. While I think she is in the right profession, she wasn't necessarily reasonable with the assignments we needed to complete. A lot of them felt disconnected from the class. Beware, she thinks she knows best about everything.

Dr. Riger is the best professor I have had at UNC. The class itself is really interesting and she cares a lot about the subject matter and her students. She is extremely kind and passionate. I would recommend this class and Dr. Riger to anyone and everyone

Definitely my favorite professor throughout my time at UNC. Lectures weren't too overwhelming, and participation is voluntary (anon pollev's in most classes); one group project in the class, but everyone in the class was also amazing to get along with, so it wasn't a big issue. Generous grading; would highly recommend!!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: TBH I took this class after seeing reviews and  thought it would be easy. Dana was kind of intimidating but accommodating with assignments. Tests were take home, but assignments were tedious and required you to do a lot of much work. Not a bad class but be prepared to put the work and effort in.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I have taken all of Dr. Riger's courses, and all I could say is that I wish she taught more. She is so caring, intelligent, and engaging. I've been in 50 minute, 1.25 hour, and 3 hour courses with her and they all sped by because of how in tune with her classes and course content she is. Can't recommend enough!!

Dr. Riger is amazing! She cares for each student's success and wellbeing. In class lectures, she makes it fun by using tik-toks and relatable examples. Her class is graded on a syllabus quiz, attendance, 3 exams (including the final), and 4 writing assignments. She also gives extra credit so don't worry too much! Take her if you need a GPA booster!
absolutely an amazing teacher. I recommend this course to everyone I meet!! She is so down to earth and gives so many opportunities for extra credit.

Professor Riger is great!!! I loved this course. Class was very interesting and the workload was manageable. She offers extra credit at the end of her course and was very accessible. Attendance is mandatory.

Great class I have enjoyed all the classes I have gotten to take with Dr.Riger. Some of the topics are hard to discuss but small class size helps. She grades all assignments and is super responsive to questions or concerns. If she doesn't know the answer she will find out! A GEM AT UNC. Extremely passionate and that makes the class better!!!

LOVE Dana and EDUC181. Because of her and this course, I am switching my major to HDFS. Dana is so funny and caring, and her TAs grade the work. Overall a pretty easy course if you do the work and take notes. I look forward to coming to class daily. TAKE THIS COURSE WITH RIGER!!

Professor Riger is amazing! She's funny and cares about her students and what she teaches. She is strict but will give extensions if you just email her, and her assignments/exams take effort but make sense and are engaging. Her passion and teaching style made me want to major in HDFS! EDUC181 is a great class to take, even if it's for an elective.

Riger is such a great professor. She makes lectures interesting and engaging, and will genuinely make you laugh. She cares about all of her students. Provides clear expectations of the class and will have you fully prepared for any exams. She is awesome!!

Dr. Riger is one of the coolest professors at UNC. This is such an incredible class that everyone should take. IT is barely any work and every lecture was interesting. I actually enjoyed reading the textbook. Got extra credit at the end for making three memes which took about 10 min total.

One of my favorite professors at UNC! She is so understanding and funny. Her assignments are helpful and do not feel completely useless. She really tries to reduce the stress of testing by giving us the option to create our own test and offer it online so we can do it on our own time in the comfort of our own home.

Great class made me become an HDFS major! Super understanding professor that responds quickly and uses in class resources to ask questions! Make your own exam is something this class has or you can choose to take the exam or both super cool class! Lecture wasn't boring just pay attention and take notes BUT ask questions if you have them #micoff
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: LOVE THIS TEACHER SO MUCH. I'm a STEM major and I took this class on a whim, and honestly one of my favorite classes I've ever taken at UNC. Dr. Riger is so respectful and kind, and is one of the best lecturers I've ever had. She is incredibly knowledgable about her subject and is inclusive and respectful of all backgrounds and cultures.

Dr. Riger has been great for my other courses. 605 has been a different story. The material is interesting however if your answer is not exactly hers, you are treated like an idiot. Also assigned a paper due the SUNDAY during SPRING BREAK and only gave feedback on our last papers 3 days before/ taught 1/3 material for paper 3 days before.Ridiculous

LOVED Prof. Riger! My favorite professor at unc so far. She is so funny, cares about her students, and is passionate about what she does. I took this class on a whim and realized I didn't really need it but I don't regret it at all. TAKE HER CLASS. Grades based on 3 exams, 3 bigger assignments, attendance, and extra credit. Easy A but learned a lot

She's an AMAZING professor! She's very understanding and is very easy to talk to when you need to. She is also very good about emailing you back as soon as she can. I really enjoyed her class and her teaching style and I hope I get to take another class with her. #NothingButLoveHere
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: An amazing professor!!!! I would recommend this class to anyone who is thinking about it. Just do it. It's so worth it. Lectures are fun and entertaining and there's limited assignments. Do the reading and the study guide and you'll pass with flying colors. Professor Riger is my absolute favorite and never fails to make me smile during her lectures

Took this course to see if I really wanted to major in HDFS, and I loved it. Professor Riger was amazing; lectures were fun and to straight to the point. There really wasn't that much work just 3 exams (study!!) in total and 3 assignments (papers/presentation). There were times in the semester where you were able to do extra credit opportunities.

literally the best teacher i have ever had. currently in the class and absolutely love it. make sure to start your assignments early, and follow the rubrics as closely as you can. if you are thinking about taking her class definitely do.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class was very unique, and the first time it has been offered. The assignments and readings were actually interesting, and there were no exams. Grade is based off of 4 papers and discussions/participation. Dana is the most passionate professor I've had and this class was super organized. Loved the material and the professor. Take her class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--So many papers

reviews.comment: Her lectures are always so organized. Her teaching style helped me so much, the content didn't even feel so difficult because of how well I understood her teaching. The class was never boring, but you do have to make sure you take notes. She is a great professor and gives helpful feedback when it comes to exams.
The content is not dense but there is a lot of it. Be prepared to work.

This class was by far my favorite class I have taken so far at UNC. Dana was the coolest, most understanding, and passionate professor I have had and this class was super interesting. The assignments were very reasonable and clear. Even during online school, this is the class I looked forward to every week. Take any class with Dana if you can!

Really organized and clearly structured class. A great class to take online. Weekly pre-recorded lectures and discussions. Only had to attend one fun Zoom recitation a week. 3 assignments with a clear rubric. Super understanding and willing to help. The TAs (Fiona and Evan) were great! Interesting content and awesome instructor!

I was looking forward to taking this class but was really disappointed. It's mostly all about sex and not enough about identity or intersectionality. You can also tell that she is used to teaching this course as a maymester. We had to watch 2 lectures and attend one live zoom lecture every week.

Super easy & interesting as long as you do the work! Graded on a syllabus quiz, 3 assignments, 2 exams, weekly forum posts, and recitation attendance. All assignments are straightforward and graded pretty leniently. Exam questions are based on a study guide she gives you before each exam. There are also lots of opportunities for extra credit.

Professor Riger is such an amazing professor. She really accommodated for students this virtual semester and is very lenient with when assignments are due as long as you let her know. She is very inclusive and tries her best to make sure the class is comfortable with what we're learning. The class is also very interesting!

Professor Riger is super approachable. She tries to make the lectures as engaging as possible during Zoom meetings. Not a rigorous course and doesn't have a heavy workload. Content is very interesting and applicable to everyone's everyday life since it's more than just a class about sexuality and identity. Also, several extra credit opportunities!

Riger is AMAZING!! She is so understanding and genuinely cares about her students. Great at explaining material and v engaging in class even on zoom. EDUC181 is super easy but still interesting and the workload is v manageable. The 3 main assignments throughout the semester can be fun if u care. 1000% would recommend her and the class.

Prof Riger is Amazing!! I only took this class for the education credit, but it taught me so much about myself and culture surrounding sexuality/identity. The tests are worth a lot so I would study for those and the grading criteria is kinda confusing but Prof Riger is super helpful! TAs might grade the papers harshly so watch out for that.

I LOVED PROFESSOR RIGER! She is by far my favorite professor I have had at UNC thus far and EDUC375 has been my favorite class! Never wanted to miss a class. Her lectures are so interesting and she is really good about handling hard topics with respect. I would recommend taking this class with Riger to everyone I meet! Super fun class!

Professor Riger is AWESOME! I took her EDUC181 class at UNC and loved her enthusiasm and genuine care for her students that I ended up taking EDUc375 with her even though I'm not an HDFS major. She provided me with so many resources for success and even met me one-on-one for coffee to just chat about life. She's cool and one of my favorites!

I adore Professor Riger! I had her for both EDUC 181 and 532 and my roommate had her EDUC 375 class, and we often talked about how much we enjoyed all of her classes. 181 is primarily graded by the TAs and I thought the grading, exams, and extra credit opportunities made for an easy A. 532 was more difficult but definitely doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Great class & GPA booster. Dana's lectures are easy to follow and interactive. Very friendly and engaging professor. She does take attendance, but we're allowed 2 skips. You will need the textbook. One group project and three solo assignments. 3 exams & the final was not cumulative. Xtra credit offered. Would recommend this class to anyone.

Dana really cares about her students and her subject. With that being said, her class is very challenging. I had heard EDUC181 was easy. This was not the case. Daily participation activities (done for attendance) are graded harshly, and so are the tests, group projects, and essays. UNC is definitely trying to make this course more difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I had EDUC 375 with Professor Riger, the fall of 2019 was her first semester at UNC but her class was my favorite class of the semester! She is incredibly reasonable with grading (will give points back if she believes it's fair) and as long as you try, you should get a good grade! I would take any class she teaches, it's my least stressful class.

An amazing teacher who genuinely cares about her students. She will always take the time to meet with you outside of class if you need help, and she is a very lenient grader. The exams are not very difficult and if you ask for extra credit she will always give you something to do.

Russian Department Legend. She is super sweet, caring, and funny. Participation is a must, and her lectures are engaging. She simply wants all of her students to learn the Russian language. All the resources are available, and she provides excellent feedback. As long as you show up, participate, and do your work, you'll succeed.

Truly my favorite professor I've had at UNC, will do anything and everything to help you succeed in her class. She's so funny and makes me really look forward to coming to her class and I literally structured my entire schedule next semester so I can take 204 with her
I had her as an undergraduate in 96 and 97.  Loved her and her classes.

She's great at making the class engaging and really cares about each person's success. She will call you if you're falling behind/haven't been in class. A lot less talking in class than McGarry's class and harder to get an A. Still lots of small group work in class. Very funny
Simply the GOAT of the Russian department at UNC. The best lecturer there is, with a nice sense of humor. She is joyful and passionate about what she teaches.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Magomedova truly cares about all of her students and wants them to succeed. Russian is an extremely hard language, but her class makes it seem manageable and I found myself wanting to study. She is engaging and extremely knowledgeable. Take a class with her if you can!

Eleonora is one of the kindest people I have ever met. Had her for 101, 102, and 203. She really cares about her students and is willing to help them succeed.  You will have homework every day, but they are short and take between 10-20 minutes. Easily the best professor I've had at UNC.

I haven't had much contact with literature and was nervous to take this class, but I ended up loving it! Eleonora is extremely caring and accommodating, and I loved every piece we read over the semester. I'd take it again if I could.

Really good teacher. I rarely use RMP but Eleanora did a great job making a difficult language easy to understand. She is very popular for a reason and will do literally anything she can to help her students, including letting students call her cell phone for help and having flexible deadlines.

I love Eleanora! Seriously try to take RUSS 101 and/or 102 with her because she will make anyone fall in love with the language and the culture. She is incredibly kind and really cares about her students. As long as you consistently do homework and study, you should be fine (at least for RUSS 101).

I'm pretty sure I've rated her before, but I took another class from her this semester and I cannot stress enough how amazing she is. She's hilarious, fun to talk to, sweet, and a genuinely incredible instructor. Her class is consistently my highest grade in a semester, and she's so lovely. Not quite as good over zoom, but she's still amazing.

Eleonora was an amazing and caring prof. She really wants you to succeed. Definitely recommend if you're looking for an easy FL fulfillment. She gives your her number to call anytime. She is so funny and loves to make jokes and pick on you. Small classes so you get to interact. Wonderful professor and you'll learn a lot too. The textbook is free!

Eleonora assigns homework every night. She is an extremely fast grader and has literally left me voicemails to tell me when I do well on an exam. She teaches to teach, not to give grades. She will be flexible with you if you need it. Get to know her, spend time with her, and you'll get an A even if Russian isn't your strong point.
Russian is not a very easy language to learn but she makes it enjoyable and pleasant. This was probably my first positive experience in learning a language.

I love Eleonora! I look forward to her class every day because I can always count on her to make me laugh. Four hours a week with her doesn't feel like enough. I considered taking 102 just to have another semester with her, but I was just taking the class for fun. I also found the language to be quite easy under her instruction.

I love her so freaking much. I cannot tell you enough that you HAVE TO TAKE HER. She's the best. She's so understanding and really cares about students. She's also hilarious and makes going to class a real treat. I cannot recommend her too much. Just take her class. Take it. Go to connect carolina and register for it right now. I'm waiting.

Quite literally the best professor at Carolina. She will go out of her way to help you succeed. She's a lenient grader and also one of the funniest people I've ever met. Truly a gem. If you're considering taking Russian as your language, please do it. Seriously. Best decision I've made in college.

Eleonora is my favorite professor at UNC if you're thinking about taking this class, do it! She's extremely caring, there's a little homework every day but she won't penalize you for turning it in late. It's okay to miss class if you just email her and don't make a habit of it. She's really funny and her expectations are very clear. I'll miss her!

Eleonora is the best teacher I've ever had, hands down. She is so caring about her students and wants them to be successful. She regularly meets with students outside of class and gives individualized feedback so the student can improve on specific areas. If you want an amazing class and professor, this is it.

Eleonora is a great teacher and really cares about her students and wants them to succeed. Russian is hard, but if you put in the time and effort and get help from Eleonora when needed it is easy to do well.
Eleonora is great! Cares about her students, teaching, and being inclusive! Makes class fun because she is so enthusiastic!

Absolutely amazing. This is my 6th year of college (and 3rd college), and I can honestly say she is one of my ultimate favs! SO caring, wants you to succeed, understanding and down right awesome. Russian is hard, you can't get past that, but I never thought I'd say I got an A in Russian until her! She really knows how to teach.
I can't say enough good things about her. She met multiple times off campus to help one on one. She is such a great teacher and kind soul.
She is the bee's knees. She will certainly pique your interest in the Russian language and culture. She cares for her students and is very passionate about teaching. Take Russian with her!!!

SHE IS SO GREAT!  SO funny and soooo nice! Willing to help you whenever you need it! Genuinely cares about all of her students! Study for the tests and they are not very hard. I'm terrible at any and all foreign languages and I did very well in RUSS 101. Take her class!
She is absolutely amazing, I lover her and wish I could have her for every class at UNC.  She makes the material fun to learn, and her personality can't be beat

Eleonora is the best professor at UNC! She is really funny and is a lenient grader. She understands if you are busy and will push back quizzes and tests for you. If you have a chance to take Russ 101 with her do it!
Excellent teacher who constantly makes you laugh. Not an easy class but definitely worth taking, she wants you to succeed.

Love Eleanora! Specifically signed up for her class cos I'd heard good things about her. She's funny & will help you if you struggle. She calls on students regularly, so you have to pay attention. HW is to be handed in every lesson, which got old fast lol. She grades very generously though. Found her class very worthwhile & made my semester shine.

Eleonora is highly entertaining and engaging. I absolutely love her! I really enjoy going to this class and she is very understanding about circumstances keeping you from class. She is very willing to help you with material outside of class. Genuinely excited about the material.
Absolutely loved her. One of the best professors I've had in any subject! Hilarious and extremely fun. Pretty easy class too.
She is a little crazy, but very entertaining. I've never had a professor who cares so much about her students!

Eleonora is the most amazing teacher!  She's hilarious and sweet and really cares about the material.  If you're having any trouble, she's more than willing to help you.  The best teacher and I highly highly recommend her!  She makes Russian so much fun!
Great professor, great class!  Highly recommend!
Very entertaining and funny in class.  Keeps you engaged.  Very helpful outside of class if you don't understand the material.  She's very sweet and just an interesting person in general.
Probably one of the most interesting characters in the Slavic Studies Department.  Anyone who has the chance to take a class with her should.

Nice person, but assigned an infeasible amount of work and relies on a group project format that simply doesn't work the majority of the time. Also is constantly interrupting his own students. Do not take this weekend class, and this is coming from someone who's taken almost all of the KF weekend classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Elad is a cheerful teacher, and the class is fairly enjoyable, but he crams WAY too much work into one weekend and gives you absolutely no feedback. Also wish the activities were a bit more creative since it's a creativity class (maybe a real-life Shark Tank as a team assignment). Overall, it was nice, but causes a ton of burnout and lacks support.

Great weekend class. Interesting lectures and enjoyable activities made the weekend fly by. Fair amount of material to read in preparation for each day, but not unbearable by any means. If you need a weekend class, take this one

Elad is a good person and is engaging in class, but the amount of work he expects to be completed in such a short time is crazy. His grading criteria is extremely tough, he grades on tiers and for large assignments he will not give anyone higher than a 90.

Took creative thinking over the weekend. He's super engaging and makes the day go by faster. Only complaint is that the class is more like 9-9 than 9-5, but the grind is worth it and the material is fun. Worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great class, lectures were engaging, interesting, and had lots of activities to break up the long weekend. Knows the material very well. A lot of work outside class that weekend but doable. Grading is a little harsh for certain assignments but not too bad.
one of my favorite weekend classes. class is group work heavy, but pretty engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: My favorite professor at UNC
Really nice guy, not a ton of work but definitely fills your weekend. Not a ton of lecture, pretty fun activities
Awesome guy
