Not a good teacher... makes you do a ton of work and pretty much lets other students grade your homework and assignments. Avoid him at all costs, he's nice but does not know how to teach and surely does not how to grade papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Terrible grading criteria based on peer reviews. Assignment information subjective and no clear guidance. Weekend course, professor cares more about minimizing time spent grading than actually giving fair grades. Participation grade made no sense, people who participated every day received the same grades as people who did not participate at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Horrible experience. Grading is incredibly subjective and assignments have too much nuance. Very inefficient notes and teaching style, overloading you with info on basic principles. Tanked people's participation grades and barely allowed time to participate. Avoid.

Dr. Pieri clearly has no interest in teaching and her class reflects that. Your grade is 100% exams. She doesn't provide resources. No learning objectives, no class schedule, no practice problems, she doesn't post her notes, her lectures are objectively boring, she has difficulty explaining topics, and she often makes mistakes in her lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not take her, grade is 100% exams. Gives no practice problems except 1 practice midterm which is different than the content on the exam. Just derives equations from the textbook. Doesn't explain anything well.

Dr. Pieri was very nice and will make you tea/coffee in 1-on-1 office hours. She tried relating the material to real world implications which was cool due to how abstract thermo usually is. Her classes are 100% lectures and derivations from the textbook, so we didn't really get to do much problem-solving which I would've preferred. Exams are fair.
Learned PChem and how to make pasta. 5 stars, would recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pieri lectured verbatim from the Atkins textbook, so if you read before class, you'll be fine. Problem was she didn't give us reading assignments or have a schedule for what she'd be lecturing on, so I had to guess. Lectures were not engaging at all. No class curve, but no homework & she dropped the lowest midterm. Office hours were very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Class was a lot of work, but its very easy. Takes a lot of time but all grades are easy As. If you put a little effort into studying, the tests (1 midterm 1 final, both writing) are pretty easy. Would reccomend only taking this class if you are genuinely interested in the topic, as you'll be learning a lot about it and spending a lot of time on it.

(Fall 2025) Loved this class. Marienberg can be a bit of a character (in a good way!). Absolutely hilarious guy, great stories, and still gets you immersed in the content. Grading was very easy: mostly completion-based, and what wasn't was fine if you skimmed the reading and paid attention. Loved the course and professor. Will take him again.

Dr. Evyatar has a wealth of knowledge and shares it enthusiastically. He's honestly a funny guy and shows videos in class, along with bringing in prayer shawls. Classwork is easy, you just write a discussion post before each class based on the readings.

Prof Marienberg is super funny and a great guy! His classes are lectures, but he is very funny and adds videos and time to discuss the topics with your classmates, which helps break up the lectures. He is very accessible and helpful outside of class. Great class!
As long as you pay attention in class. You will be fine! Take Dr. Marienberg because he's super fun and nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Not sure why the ratings are so low, I had a great experience with Professor Marienberg. He's very understanding and his lectures were very engaging. There is often a good amount of reading per week and a discussion post or quiz for every class. The midterm and final were relatively easy as long as you studied the concepts and reading material.
Dr. Marienberg is so funny and so kind! I really enjoyed this class and hope I will get to take another with him in the future.

Nice man, though he was difficult to reach. Class content consists of readings and discussion posts due every class which, if done well, will take multiple hours each. The lectures are basically a recap of these. Exams contain very specific knowledge, but if you actually do the readings (and not just put them in ChatGBT), they're very manageable.
Nice in person. Not nice on email. But SUPER funny. Love this guy. Be prepared to read.

He is a very chill dude and lovely professor. Probably my favorite professor at UNC so far. He just wants you to understand the basic concepts and occasionally talk about what you think in class. As long as you do the 1-2 hour homework every week you will do well. Would very much recommend the class and professor.

As long as you keep up with the discussion posts and readings, this class is not too difficult. Dr. Marienberg is a caring guy who genuinely wants his students to succeed. Would recommend for anyone interested in taking an intro level RELI course.

Truly one of the best professors and nicest people I've met. Maymester is already a VERY condensed class but due to personal reasons I fell behind. Not only was he accessible outside of class, not only was he accommodating, but he acknowledged that as humans these things happen.100% recommend this class and his book and am grateful to have met him.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Marienberg is an exceptional professor who deeply cares about his students. He is passionate about what he teaches, and knows enough to tell you what he does and does not know. He encourages you to participate, but you don't have to if you don't want to. Would 100% take a class with him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Be ready to read for his classes! He can be a bit strong headed at times, but never once stopped a student from expressing their views. He is very open about what he will talk about, and gave anyone the chance to step out of the room. Overall a great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great professor! Highly recommended!
Wonderful man and amazing professor.  Knows a lot about his field and really cares for the students.

Only take this class if you like to read! Aside from that, this was a fantastic class, and the Professor has a way of keeping the class engaging at all times. I can't recommend his classes enough, a true gem!
Awful

Professor Marienberg was a great professor and I highly recommend his class! It is true that there can be some larger reading assignments, but given that there are generally just two forum posts due each week. The exams weren't too bad if you pay attention in class and skim the readings.

- Readings before every class. Long but fair for a 400 level.
- Students choose topic to research and present to class.
- The final is a research paper on a topic selected by the student.
- Professor Marienberg is VERY knowledgable about his subject. He presents issues in a nuanced way. 
- I highly recommend this class + Professor Marienberg.

Dr. Marienberg is a fun lecturer! The content is kind of dry but no single subject is dwelled on for too long. Moderate to little amount of reading + forum post before each class. He grades the posts and a final reflection gently. He can be a little intimidating and hard to understand (accent) but I think he's a cool and interesting guy. Recommend!

Dr. Marienberg is a very interesting lecturer and is extremely knowledgeable in his field. The course is overall interesting, but attendance is mandatory. There is a lot of reading for homework but it isn't hard, however, the exam and the midterm were very very very difficult, containing niche information that only someone with a degree would know.

Theres a lot of readings but you don't have to read them all. His grading is quite simple -as long as you do the discussion posts you will be fine. He is very understanding w/ attendance and is lenient with due dates. The midterm and final was difficult- the material was very specific and kind of insignificant to what we actually learned in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: This is a hard class/professor to rate. The course content is interesting, but the readings can be a bit long at times. It's graded based on forum posts, 2 short presentations, and an oral final exam. Grading is pretty lax, but prof. can say things people would find offensive at times. He's well intentioned but don't take if you have thin skin.

He was so kind and willing to work with me throughout a hard first semester. He worked with me when I was out for sickness and various appointments. There is a lot of reading, but if you do it, you will make good grades on your posts and quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Cares a lot about the topic but it's brutal online and probably normally too. There's a discussion forum due before each class that has to be about a page long which is hard to do if you don't do the reading. Also you will fail the quizzes if you don't do the reading. The info in class and on quizzes/midterm/final isn't stuff you can just lookup.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Marienberg was the most flexible and caring professor I had during the Fall 2020 semester. He does truly care about his students. The class contains a good amount of reading. The tests are rather specific. Readings and lectures are very interesting. I enjoyed the challenge of the class and I am glad I took this instead of an "easy A" course.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: I had him in the Fall 2020 semester and he talked through the entire midterm. When the median grade was a 54% he blamed it on the students. All of our lectures were from 2016 and I do not believe he reviewed them. I say this because our quizzes and exams were absurdly specific and difficult. You only get a number back and can not review the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I enjoyed the content of Professor Marienberg's class, and I think he is a very nice man. However, his exams and quizzes were nearly impossible. The questions focused on insignificant details of readings and lectures. Adding negative grading on top of that made for a tough semester. You can do all your work and still score very poorly.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He obviously was very knowledgeable about the subject and I learned stuff. However, the homework was busy work based on readings and in class we simply went over what we put down for the homework, so it made the lectures pretty pointless. The tests were easy and I made As on them. He has weird rules about grading and homework is weighed heavily.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I loved having Dr. Marienberg! I would not recommend taking the class if you have little to no interest in the subject since there is quite a bit of reading. There are sakai posts about the reading due before class but they are very straightforward. Doing the reading and coming to class will get you a solid grade in the class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Love this man SO SO SO MUCH. I told him that I wanted to bring my grade up and he helped me so much and I eventually finished with a 97. Don't let other people scare you off by talking about the homework. there is a good amount of it but if you do it, you'll get a 100 on it every time and that will really supplement your grade nicely. TAKE HIM!

TONS of reading (more work than in his grad classes he said) and posts. Only 1 assignment other than posts. The exams are ridiculous. Has a negative grading system: -1.25 points for wrong answers. Also the final was 30 questions TRUE AND FALSE. I got 100 in all posts and assignments but failed both exams. My grade does not reflect the work I put in
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took RELI697 for my religious studies capstone seminar and Evyatar is hands down one of my favorite professors I've ever had. He is really kind and understanding and really wants to make sure you succeed. He gives really good feedback and acknowledges hard work when you go the extra mile.

The most important thing to know about this class is that there are Sakai posts due before every class. This class ended up being really easy, I got an A with only skimming the readings and posting but it was still time consuming. I would advise to take it ONLY if you don't mind putting in a little "busy" work (its not difficult) to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I did not enjoy taking this class. He is a good professor and knowledgeable but requires A TON of reading and videos to be done and posted about before coming to class. If you aren't particularly interested in this subject, like me, don't take it. How to study for the test was also very unclear. His lectures can be entertaining and funny though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I took this FYS expecting it to be my easy class for the semester, but I ended spending more time on the assignments for this class than any other one. This class has a lot of homework so DO NOT get behind! Professor Marienberg also tends to be condescending and rude, which is one of the reasons I do not plan on taking another one of his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: An FYS on medieval literature where we read four books. Twice a week we would have forum posts on Sakai about the chapters from the book as well as supplemental readings. After each book, there is 5 question quiz with a guessing penalty, so read carefully. Overall, Dr. Marienberg is a nice guy that cares more about his students that actual grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Interesting FYS, and he is very open towards his students. He allows students to facilitate discussion in the class, and he helps us understand the literature that we read for this class. The only drawback I see is that he uses a guessing penalty factor for his pop quizzes on four books in Sakai, so make sure you read the books really carefully.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Have an interest in the class topic, and you will learn lots! My class was on Catholicism, and you don't have to be Catholic to do well.  He loves class discussion.  Homework is easy, but there is lots - but it's not that bad.  He's an interesting, witty, and knowledgeable professor.  Utilize his office hours to talk about anything!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Dr. Eskew cares about teaching the content and walks around the class from time to time to answer questions. Exams are difficult but fair, with very few curve balls (Looking at those energy diagram questions). Overall, a great teacher, and I highly recommend her for orgo. Watch Chad's Prep 2x speed before the lecture for an A.

Dr. Eskew is sweet and fair. She tries her best to explain concepts to students and help out anyone having questions on Orgo. Her exams are straight forward application and very fair. This is a hard class indeed and she did a great job getting the most important information into the lectures. Definitely attend class, GPSS, and ULA sessions.

She does not explain concepts or mechanisms well, I found Beaver to be way better of a prof. I went to GPSS, ULA sessions, and all the workbook problems and still barely passed the class. Exams were unnecessarily difficult and written sloppily. I did better on Beaver exams than hers. I don't learn much in lecture, she goes over things too simply.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Eskew is super nice, but was a pretty average lecturer. My main complaint is that professors constantly failed to address student questions. Exams were written sloppily, not super difficult, but would make mistakes and go to unnecessary lengths to cover their tracks. Ed Discussion is encouraged until it becomes an inconvenience to the professors.

I found Dr. Eskew's lectures to be a bit dry at times. However, she's a very calm lecturer, and I appreciated this as the class stressed me out at first. I did much better on her exams than I did on Dr. Zurcher's and Dr. Beaver's at the beginning of the semester.

Orgo is going to be hard. I think Eskew does a pretty good job of teaching, covers the material and gets through what needs to be done. Not much to be said, regardless of what professor you take you really just have to do a lot of practice and lock in on exams to do good.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Exams were difficult, and were graded harshly. The first exam (taught be Beaver due to Eskew's absence) went much better compared to the exams done with Eskew. The final exam she wrote was abysmal. I would not recommend this experience. The class is graded off exams, which are much more difficult than they need to be for a college level class.

Eskew's a pretty good professor. She started out a little shaky, but I'll give her grace because she came in halfway through the semester, which is tough. Overall a solid professor and exams are straightforward with her.

I mean orgo is orgo, but she didn't make it any easier. I had Dr. Beaver for a little bit and my first exam was my best score, as soon as eskew switched in, the concepts started getting fuzzy and the exams were kinda all over the place. She is extremely dry and i am not excited to take 262 with her to say the least
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her lectures are dry but she doesn't overcomplicate topics. Sometimes she doesn't go in-depth into a topic and then it shows up on the test but it's not too bad. I also only had her for like 1.5 months so I don't know what she's like for teaching all of unit 1 and half of unit 2. The one test she wrote for us was pretty easy.

Dr. Eskew is very caring and always willing to give extra help. Her lectures aren't the best, but orgo is orgo and requires a lot of self-teaching no matter who you take it with. Her exams are super straightforward and it's not hard to do well if you practice consistently.

I do not know what happened to Dr. Eskew. She used to be great (hence the old and incredibly positive reviews), but this semester she was just awful. Boring lectures, didn't answer questions in class, slides where illegible at times, exams were graded incorrectly-- I could go on. Please take either Dr. Zurcher, or  Dr. Beaver.

Prof Eskew was supposed to teach my class all semester, but randomly took off for the first month. I had Prof Zurcher, and she was amazing. Then Eskew came back and my grade tanked. She's just such a boring lecturer, and she doesn't explain anything. When people ask questions, she doesn;t actually answer them and just moves on.

I liked Dr. Eskew's lecturing style and her very fair exams. Class content isn't bad if you try to learn instead of pure memorization. Since the content builds off the last it's vital to keep up with whatever is going on in class. Do practice and understand the why behind the madness. Also, don't bother wasting money on the model kit; it's useless.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Eskew is a caring professor and really good at teaching orgo. She explains things clearly and answers questions in class well. Orgo is hard, but she approaches it with low drama and seems to really care about her students. She was patient and responsive about a tech issue I had. Has a good sense of humor too!
Great professor. Very clear and understanding in lecture. Exams were fair for the most part and I enjoyed the course overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easily the best choice for orgo. Eskew actually tests on what she teaches in a fair way and genuinely seems to care about her students. Office hours/problem sessions are helpful and her lectures are clear. She is very caring and helpful despite the class being inherently very difficult. Definitely choose her over the other professors.

Dr. Eskew is a very knowledgable professor who clearly has many years of experience teaching organic chemistry and knows how to best present the information to students. Orgo 2 is hard at UNC regardless of the prof and takes a lot of dedication and practice, but Eskew seems to be the best choice if you want to do well.

Orgo 2 with Dr. Eskew has been the best chemistry experience I have had at Chapel Hill. She is extremely caring, answers all questions, and is very nice in and out of class. I didn't get below an A on any of the exams and she is a major reason why. 1000% recommend taking both Orgo 1 and 2 with her if possible.

Dr. Eskew was very kind and approachable, often making an effort to connect with students in class despite it being a large lecture. Her slides were well put together, and she explained things clearly. Exams are tough, but that is to be expected from orgo. Just do the homework and practice problems, and you should be fine. Best orgo professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Just no. Her lectures are confusing, she doesn't know how to pace herself and barely glances over difficult problems. She always makes mistakes while teaching, which confuses the students (she is constantly being corrected by LAs mid lecture) yet her exams are very difficult and barely any partial credit is ever awarded. Terrible overall.

Best CHEM prof at UNC!!! She is very caring and has a sense of humor. She is also very kind and explains everything clearly and patiently, like your grandma. The 2nd exam was difficult but I know it wasn't written by her. Her exams were the easiest orgo exams I've taken! Take her orgo she's the best!
Incredibly caring and exams are very fair - challenging, but nothing unexpected.

Professor Eskew is very kind and knows chemistry well, but she's not the best lecturer. The course was fun and cool if you're into nature/medicine. It switches from chemistry to native history suddenly though but overall was easy to comprehend. Professor Eskew is great during office hours too and easy to talk to.

Amazing professor. I think one of the best chem professors at UNC. I loved her, her class, and everything we did in it. It is hard, but why is everyone complaining, its chem, its orgo, its not easy. But Professor Eskew makes it accessible and makes sure the content is covered, gives fair exams, and I never felt like I got blindsided. like genchem

I've had bad experiences with gen chem at UNC, but having taken CHEM 261 and CHEM 262 w/ Dr. Eskew, she made orgo not as bad as everyone made it seem. She offered us all the resources to succeed, and having attended her office hours, she is very accommodating and always willing to help. If I had to take orgo again, I would do it again w/ Dr. Eskew

Dr. Eskew was lovely to talk to, and made a strong effort to take us on field trips and engaged with speakers. The major projects were interesting and engaging. However, taking this FYS with very little chemistry knowledge is way too difficult. Her quizzes are graded harshly, and she was teaching us organic chem basics along with ethnobotany.
Exams were difficult.

I had Dr. Eskew for Orgo I and II, I thought she did a good job with class engagement and was always willing to answer questions during PM sessions. The nature of the class makes it very difficult to begin with, but Dr. Eskew makes the exams fair and makes it possible to succeed (but you are going to have to put in a lot of work).

i absolutely LOVED taking this class w eskew, she was so incredibly sweet and helpful during office hours, i was very unsure about taking the class and she was so encouraging and kind. the best prof to take any chem class w imo, HIGHLY recommend her!!

Orgo is hard regardless of professor; Eskew's class was fine considering this. Lectures covered < half the material tested; review sessions were "optional" (I never went and struggled). You have to put in a full-time job's amount of time outside of class to keep up with material, which made me so upset I quit premed. The content itself is not bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was going great for me until the third midterm, which most of the class failed.  Eskew is a fine professor, but I'd take this with someone else if I could do it over again.

Dr. Eskew was one of the best professors I've had at UNC, and Orgo quickly became my favorite class. She is caring and deeply values student feedback. Although her lectures can be a bit dry, she makes up for it with incredibly fair exams. Orgo is a very content-heavy course - don't fall behind. I adore Dr. Eskew - take it with her if you can!!

Overall, Eskew is a good teacher for 261. Sometimes she dosent go as in depth, but her exams reflect that and as long as you keep up with studying you can get good grades on them. She is very understanding to her students and gave us bonus points on the last test.

nita is a very sweet woman. her lectures are not the best, nor her teaching, but she really cares for her students and is accessible outside of class. she's really sweet and i like her a lot. her exams are SO straightforward compared to gen chem. take her solely for her exams!!!! just make sure to keep up with the material !!!

Orgo is generally a tough class, but Dr. Eskew makes it so much better by being clear with lecture content. What is covered in class is about the depth of what you need to know for exams. Her exams are not out to trick you; when our third exam average was ~50 she gave hella extra credit (my grade got bumped from a 66 to 82). DO PRACTICE PROBLEMS!!

I would 100% recommend taking Dr. Eskew for o-chem at UNC. The class is going to be hard regardless of the professor, but she made it bearable! The exams reflected what we had discussed in class and were fair. Go to the peer tutors at the learning center for extra help - they are such a GREAT resource for this class! Good luck with o-chem

Dr. Eskew made CHEM 262 my favorite course I took at UNC Chapel Hill. Take the class with her and try to get to know the material instead of treating it like an obstacle - it's very fair and when it's not, Dr. Eskew takes the feedback and incorporates it into the next exam. You can tell. Seriously one of the most lovely professors I've ever had!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: After exam 1 start a reagent list, add to it, study it for the rest of the class
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Eskew is a good prof for orgo, use lectures for practice and use the panopto videos for understanding/explanations. There is a lot of supplemental videos that touch on every topic, they are thorough and give grids for sub/elim reactions. Don't forget the second exam topics, they are important for third. 261 is a hard class but not because of Eskew.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I succeeded in Orgo 1 with Eskew. But in Orgo 2, she seems to struggle with teaching some of the concepts, but is overall very helpful outside of class. My poor grade was due to the onset of a chronic health issue, but overall if you put forth effort and study hard- she helps you succeed. Orgo 2 is the hardest the premed curriculum gets.

I loved Dr. Eskew! Organic chemistry is a challenging class, and all UNC chem is test-heavy. However, I felt like she had good explanations, and was always happy to answer questions. She even opened extra office hours if hers filled. Definitely not an easy class and you need to stay on top of content, but her exams were very fair- highly recommend!
ACHOO! I don't know how all she's getting such good reviews from the 262 students... sus

Nita is truly the best for orgo. It's an extremely difficult course and you have to spend hours each day on content, reading, practice problems, slides, and reactions. Probably the hardest class I've ever taken but she makes it doable. Compared to the other orgo profs, Nita is an angel. Fair exams and a great professor. She is also the sweetest.

Def take orgo with Dr. Eskew! I really enjoyed her as a person and also as a lecturer. She geniunely cares for her students, and it shows by how fair her exams are (never really had any trick questions). The only thing is that there is very little partial credit on the exams, but again how fair the content is makes up for this.

Organic Chemistry is a hard class, but if you had to take Orgo, take it with Nita. Nita is good about answering questions in class and her tests are very similar to the practice tests. I have heard she is one of the best for Orgo before I took, and I still believe it after I took the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you can learn outside of class and want easier exams, take Nita. Nice lady. Don't expect partial credit or any help though. Think of it like an online course at NC state. Orgo is generally just a lot of content. She pulls straight from the slides, don't overthink because there isn't many tricks.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was my first chemistry class at UNC and heard really bad things about the chemistry department before. However, Dr. Eskew is a very sweet person and wants students to do well in her class. Exams were fair and based on lectures, so you should be fine as long as you attend lectures and do the workbook problems.

DO NOT purchase her modeling kit, you use it for one lecture. Her lecture style was a little hectic and didn't make sense to many people. She isn't great with technology and wastes 10 minutes a class figuring out how to work her apple pencil.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Eskew was very hard to access outside of class, and did not do a good job of explaining trouble concepts. She's a very sweet lady, but don't take her as a professor if you want to keep up your self esteem. You think you understand it all to a T and then you take the exam and then you want to hide in a hole forever. Use Khan Academy instead.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Eskew is nice but the grading in this class is SO unfair. Half of the class seemingly was curved up half a letter grade while half of the class was stuck with the grade they received. Still waiting on an explanation from Eskew as to why that is, but for now incredibly disappointed with grading unfairness.

Orgo is very hard class, but that is with any professor. Prof Eskew explains material well and wants her students to do well. The workbook is an excellent resource for studying for exams. Make sure to attend class and do practice problems and you should do well!

Orgo is a really difficult class, but Dr. Eskew's lectures and tests were very clear, and she strongly encouraged students to get help with concepts if they were having trouble. Also, the lowest midterm grade is weighted less than the 2 higher exam grades, which is nice. Don't fall behind on the readings or weekly assignments!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Orgo is just a genuinely difficult subject but Dr. Eskew made it genuinely quite fair. The tests are challenging but based on lectures. there's barely any partial credit or ec. Fall behind on reading and it becomes a lot more difficult and confusing. Class is for practice, not learning. Read textbook before class and try to stay on top.

I really like Professor Eskew! Despite being challenging, her exams were very fair. She doesn't try to trick you with questions on the exams, they're straightforward and gauge your understanding of the posted lesson objectives. Her review sessions were always helpful and she made Orgo a fun class to take!

Orgo is very difficult and you have to put in a ton of work outside of the class but Dr. Eskew is a really great teacher. She makes learning what feels like a foreign language manageable. Her tests are very fair and if you put in the work you will be happy with your grade. Problem solving, studying everyday and the workbook are your bffs.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Eskew is the best professor that I have had after 2 years at UNC. Organic chemistry is an objectively difficult course and you must put in a lot of work in order to succeed. Dr. Eskew is an extremely caring professor who is very well-versed in chemistry and was an amazing aid in succeeding in this course.

Orgo II is gonna be tough no matter who teaches, but Prof. Eskew is a solid option.  While her teaching is scattered and confusing at times, she more than makes up for it with her easy exams.  If you're able to learn well outside of class, you'll do the best in this class out of all the orgo II profs.

This class was extremely test heavy. There is no partial credit so even if you get 90% of a problem right you will end up getting a 0%. Horrible teacher and most of the learning comes from reading the textbook.  If you are the type of person like I am and do not learn well from textbooks, this class is not for you. Take it with someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I was very scared to take orgo at UNC, but Eskew is by far one of the best chem professors I have had. Her lectures are very clear and as long as you put in lots of effort outside of class it is manageable to do decent. Her exams are very fair and are actually similar to lots of problems we do in lecture, which is a blessing.

She is one of the best options for orgo at UNC.  She is very patient and the lectures involve a lot of problem solving and participation.  There are plenty of opportunities for getting help outside of class.  Her tests are pretty straight forward and typically more simple than practice problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If ochem wasn't hard enough, the way Dr. Eskew lectures and organizes the class makes it far worse. She is a nice lady, but obviously could not care less about her students. 90% of the grade is exam based with no curve. Avoid this class / professor if at all possible!!!

Dr. Eskew invalidates your problems when you present them to her and she is hard to access outside of class. If your TA is not treating you fairly, good luck because she will 100% take their side and not even listen to what you have to say. Grading criteria is very unclear and rubrics do not reflect what it is actually graded. Avoid at all costs.
Really bad experience both in academics and talking to profesor. I would avoid if I could.

Dr. Eskew is a kind person, but this class sucked. The content is challenging, but her lectures are dull (she's monotone) and consistently taught against what the book says. The exams are 90% of your grade, and overall the work put into this class is seldom reflected in the grades. She also blames us for info we don't know that she hasn't taught.
Has a bad attitude towards students, which creates a learning environment in which you do not want to be there. There is a lack of basic respect and abuse of power in the department.

Took her for 262 over the summer. She was a very fair grader and clearly wanted her students to succeed. Orgo is always going to be a difficult class, but it did not feel like she was trying to weed out her students. She was very generous with re-grade requests. Your grade is overwhelmingly going to be based on tests, but that's all chem at UNC.

Reached out to help for class but came off as condescending and passive aggressive. They do not really care about you and that reflects in student performance and the rates.

There were no improvements, horrible TAs and baseless threatening of honor court. Horrible leadership and thoroughly disappointed.

Has bias against students who are from poor backgrounds, awful.

CHEM is awful at UNC.

The entire class was based 90% off of tests. This was absolutely ridiculous. She was not understanding or helpful in the slightest. Do not take her, Beaver is just a little bit better. Chem at UNC is not a good idea in general. Professor Eskew is a great example of why this school needs different chem professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There is a condescending attitude towards students from different socioeconomic backgrounds. Low quality lab videos during COVID. TAs insulting the performance of students rather than helping and supporting them.

This lab is only as tough as your TA. Labs are back in person and I will say Nita was in the actual classroom way more than any other lab professor I've ever had. She's fun to have a little chat with and is there to help you with equipment if you need. Again, she doesn't do much in terms of grading but her presence was appreciated :)

There were complaints about TAs in ORGO lab for acting indecently towards students. These were constant instead of just a few. Laboratory was difficult as it depends on your TA. Never got changes for it.

your grade fully depends on TA. overall a lack of guidance and instruction from both head professor and TAyou would have to constantly email them to double check deadlines before getting penalized. there was not a midterm or a final, just a final research project with a partner. overall delivery could have been a lot better.
This was actually the worst lab Ive taken at UNC. Low quality videos to watch, unclear instructions, and poor organization. Waste of my time, but glad to be done with UNC chemistry labs.
Indifferent teacher with no time for her students.

Dr. Eskew is kind, but the truth is that her method for teaching organic chemistry is not sufficiently structured, and her tests are inconsistent. The clicker questions and homework we were given were as least helpful as possible.
Dr. Eskew is a good professor and very sweet. Goes through her slides at good pace. The only reason I didn't get a good grade is because orgo is very difficult for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She's fine. I didn't really put much effort in this class and did fine. Class isn't very helpful. Read the textbook before class and you'll be very prepared. Study the powerpoints after and do the end of chapter problems.

Nice lady and decent lecturer. But for probably grade average reasons she often include trick questions on tests to mess you up. Questions that are exceptions to the rules she teaches in class that somehow you are suppose to know. The course is three midterms and a cumulative final. Orgo is always tough so she's a decent choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Eskew is not only a wonderful person, but is a genuinely kind and caring person as well.  She is always willing to answer questions to help her students understand the material.  The tests are straightforward and are similar to the practice exams.  I would definitely recommend her.

Dr. Eskew is a very sweet teacher. She is willing to help those who come looking for it. Her lectures are not that helpful, however, she uses clickers to mark participation so you do have to attend. Her exams are very straightforward. There are no tricks and they are similar to the practice exams. Compared to other chemistry professors, she is good

Soft-spoken and explains concepts poorlyincompletely.  Gives up to 10 clicker quizzes daily and doesn't upload the answersexplanations after class.  Loves MasteringChemistry.  Doesn't provide review packets, videos, or anything but copied-from-the-book lecture slides and a schedule of other profs' problem sessions.  Students teach themselves.

The title of this class was very misleading. Rather than doing archival research, we used pre-existing small datasets to learn the basics of the programming language R. Most of the lecture was given over to personal stories, and the rest was on basic coding.

Incredible professor. Had the absolute pleasure of having him as my Developmental Psychopathology prof at KU and he was honestly out of this world. Super kind to students, fair exams, engaging lectures, and gives lots of insight into the research world of psychology. Would leap at the opportunity to work with him again if i ever got the chance.

Dr. Youngstrom is an incredibly professor. A lot of students complained about some of the assignments but he does everything for a reason. The assignments are meant to prepare you for graduate level work, but it wasn't too difficult. He's super funny (maybe a little awkward-funny at times) and really cares about his students.

Dr. Y told us this would be taught like a graduate-level class, but definitely not. Very lecture-heavy. However, Dr. Y is a great lecturer! He's an incredibly funny professor (lots of in-class demonstrations of concepts) & is always available to answer questions. Did a great job transitioning to online. Bonus: Two quiz grades replaced by the final.

Dr. Y is AMAZING! He is the best professor I have had at UNC. He really cares about his students and you to succeed. It is possible to get an A if you work hard and show you are putting effort into the class.  I would highly recommend taking this class. His lectures are entertaining and he has you apply what you've learned to cases from his clinic.
If you enjoy psychology at all, take any class you can with him! He definitely enjoys the material as well as wants to helps his students succeed. One of the best professors I've had at UNC.
Great professor! Highly recommended for any psyc majors. Especially individuals considering graduate school
HE IS THE BEST!!!!!!!!!!!

This class was horribly boring.  He tries to make it amusing but I constantly had to fight off sleep.  Nice guy though.  Approachable and always looking to help.  But if you prefer a structured environment, look elsewhere.

Dr. Youngstrom was a great professor. I'm innately horrible at math, and with his help (his TA Andrew Freedman is really good too) I got an A in statistics! Always willing to help, and he obviously designs the class so you can get the highest grade possible. If you have to take PSYC 210, definitely take it with Youngstrom!

I took this class in summer session. It went fast. The professor tried to make stats interesting, did the best he could with the material. The TA does all the grading and was extremely strict. I disagree with the other student, when the TA made an error grading, he fixed it. The TA was extremely fair.
This dude is goofy as hell.  He does his best to makes statistics interesting.  Take his class if you get the chance.  You'll actually learn the material without being bored to tears.

He did a great job of making this a good class.  The class itself is incredibly easy/boring, but he did an awesome job of giving engaging lectures.  He's a really nice guy.  I would definitely recommend him as a professor.
Best Prof Ever! Makes Stats fun and very good at explaining. Recitations are not mandatory, but can be helpful. I totally recommend this class if you have to take psyc 210.

Wonderful guy!!! He made stats painless, which was great since none of us wanted to be there. He also gave us a spreadsheet before the final that told us exactly what each of us needed on the final to get the next highest grade and the next highest etc up to an A, but I think there was a curve at the end too, which explains my solid A.

Dr. Youngstrom is one of the greatest professors I have ever had. He managed to make something as boring as statistics extremely fun! I would recommend this class to anyone who is a psychology major or who needs a statistics class!
Easiest class you will take at UNC. Easy ahh workload. Take this class

She's a great and lenient professor! Loves to talk, easy A. Weekly journal (one page). 1-2 question quizzes, usually true or false, with 2 attempts. Very low stakes class. One group presentation. She's very funny, does random activities for the classes like yoga, rock painting.

AMAZING PROFESSOR! Being in Dorothy's class was incredible. She would tell many funny stories and is relatable, especially because she knows what students go through while in college. If you're lucky enough, she'll bring her dog George to class some days! Easy class in general, reading quizzes and midterm + final paper. TAKE THIS CLASS WHILE AT UNC

Overall, amazing amazing professor. I also engaged with her class and cares about what she is doing. Nothing too hard in her class, just a final campaign/presentation, but it's in a group and very fun to do. Dorothy is hilarious and would always enjoy being in her class.
TAKE HER CLASS!! Dr. Espelage is the best professor I have ever had. She is caring, realistic, and funny. She truly wants you to grow from her class.

She is AMAZING! The class is not challenging, and the content is honestly so interesting. 2 simple exams as long as you pay attention in class. One group project and one final paper. Dr. Espelage is super passionate and one of the most hilarious people you will ever meet. I highly recommend taking any class offered by her!

One of the best professors at UNC! If you are able to take EDUC 403 with her, consider yourself lucky. She is hilarious and has so many stories to share that are related to the course content. I would take her class again if I could. The exams are very simple, and so is the course as a whole.

Easily my favorite class I've ever taken at UNC! Dr. Espelage is so funny and such an engaging lecturer. She'll tell the best stories and she makes the topics (which are very deep) light-hearted and easy to talk about. Graded nicely and quickly and always provided encouragement. Defintiely take a class with her if you can!
Espelage is a great professor! Super fun and relatable. Her lectures are engaging and makes you think about the material hard. She got my grades back fast and loved having her as my prof!

Grades fast, accessible TA (Tati really is amazing), and she tells great stories. It is a lecture heavy class but she kept it interesting. Great guest speakers, lecturers, and she allowed us to share our stories. Also inspired me to reach for the stars and roots for all of her students to succeed.

Dr. Espelage is everything you want from a professor. She's funny, knowledgeable, accommodating, and grades fast/easy. 403 is a great class whether you're an HDFS major or have never taken an EDUC course. Coursework includes a weekly one-page reflection, group project, and research paper. Great lecturer and if you do the work, you'll get an A.
AMAZING COURSE! Weekly 1 page essay, a few small projects, and take-home exams!!! Great class for HDFS majors or Conflict Management minors

I had Juan Carlos for SPAN 363, disease in hispanic lit. He is indisputably the goat. Good amount of readings and 2 weekly forum posts + journaling, but readings are reasonable + very interesting. Class discussion is the core of this class so you must come prepared. The discussions are fantastic though, JC is an amazing lecturer. Take this class!

Juan Carlos has been my favorite Spanish professor at UNC so far! He is very clearly passionate about the subject matter and leads engaging discussions. His energy is unmatched and I looked forward to every class! He creates an environment where it is easy to participate and contribute to the discussion, even if your Spanish isn't always correct.

I loved JC! He cared so much about the material and subject matter and the class was super fun. I also appreciated how he was not a strict grader and cared more about the content of responses on homework as opposed to proper grammar.

Juan Carlos is such an engaging professor. He digs deep into the assigned readings and encourages students to participate. By fostering a welcoming class environment, I always feel welcome to share my thoughts and opinions. Homework was minimal. He's one of the best professors I've had so far-- take a course with him if you can!

I felt as if this class was a lot more difficult than expected. He was not easy to access via email outside of class and graded very difficult. At times, I felt like i was being graded more for my punctuation and not my writing in spanish (we were never taught grammar either). Take with another prof if possible.
Amazing!! Super caring and has a very nuanced approach to all subjects. Lectures were heavily based on participation. The class was a bit unorganized, but I learned so much. Love Juan-Carlos!!

If you can take a class with JC, take it. He is so passionate about teaching and genuinely cares about his students. It is easy to succeed in this class if you do the work. The final project, which is a big part of our grade, was a class-wide project and actually fun. The course content is really diverse -- music & poems, queer rep, indigenous rep

Juan Carlos was so enthusiastic and passionate about class (got annoying at times but really he's just excited!). He wants lots of participation but it doesn't matter if your spanish isn't perfect, he just wants you to try! I actually learned a lot about the short stories and poems we studied in class. Fair and reasonable grader for the most part.

I think Profe is an entertaining teacher (be ready to move around and leave your seat) but beware that he gives almost no direction in his assignments. We had no rubrics throughout the semester and it made it hard to know what he wanted. I also think it made him an inconsistent grader. Overall, a good person but a very disorganized teacher.

Juan Carlos was so wonderful in SPAN 373. He is engaging and hilarious and made the content really interesting even though it seemed boring at first. He was also a very generous grader and really flexible. The more you participate the more flexible he will be. He can be disorganized at times. Do not expect him to respond to emails.

This was one of my favorite classes to attend every week. I actually looked forward to it. Juan Carlos is so energetic and passionate about the subject matter that it is infectious. I found myself excited about learning stuff that probably any other professor would have made boring. A pretty lenient grader overall as well. Would recommend.

Passionate, compassionate, approachable, knowledgeable and energetic. Juan Carlos has it all. The only class I ever missed was because of a doctor's appointment; he's THAT good. He's among the top three professors I took in my undergrad career at UNC (I'm a senior). Highly recommend for poetry.

Only the best (plus great facial hair). Took Spanish American Lit with him. He loves the subject and loves sharing it with his students. Works to engage you - took us on a tour of campus to look at architecture from various periods that corresponded with the literary movements we were reading.

Juan Carlos is by far one of the best professors that I've had at UNC. I had him for SPAN 260 and SPAN 373. Although he uses old Spanish texts, he makes them very relatable to current events on campus/in our personal lives. He also isn't afraid to talk about sensitive topics. Furthermore, he encourages participation in Spanish which is helpful.

Juan Carlos is my favorite! Most genuine and caring professor I've had, because he genuinely cares about your success as a student and as a person. His lectures relate everything to the present day and current issues which makes his classes easy and entertaining. One of the few profs I see as a "real" person rather than just a teacher. Def take him

Juan Carlos is a great professor! He is always energetic and fun, coming up with creative ways to get students to participate. The reading was reasonable and very interesting, making for some very interesting discussions in class. Take him!

Juan Carlos is an amazing professor. Class was always very engaging, and he tries very hard to make it interesting. We often went outside as a class, and did lots of different activities to change it up. He's the coolest guy, and really cares about you grasping the material. Take from him!!

Juan Carlos is a fantastic professor!! He makes class very interesting and fun for the students, sometimes we went outside for class or played games as a class because he is a very active and energized professor. The readings are not difficult and he makes his lectures very inspirational. TAKE HIS CLASS!!

Juan Carlos is the professor you want to take if you want a challenge. With him, you will improve your Spanish and citizen-of-the-world proficiency. He teaches Spanish reading comprehension and analysis, and that analysis makes you think about who you are and where you belong in society. An amazing individual, the best of the best!

Juan Carlos is an incredibly passionate professor. He knows what he's talking about.  Most of the time you feel overwhelmed with the amount of content covered in a day or in a week, which may affect your performance on the exams. Overall, his classes are very unique and discussion-based. My recommendation: Always participate, read, and just enjoy.

I can't speak for semester classes, but I took him over the summer and he had daily reading quizzes that were worth 40% of the final grade, which seemed a little absurd (one screw-up and your grade is in serious jeopardy). Takes off points needlessly sometimes on assignments, but he's also very passionate and lively, and a cool person.

I don't understand his criteria for giving students a certain grade. His assignment instructions are never clear, and going to office hours doesn't help you out. It's perplexing how a student is expected to succeed without clear instruction. The way he grades is incredibly harsh. You can bank on this class lowering your GPA.
Genuinely struggled to understand what was expected throughout this entire course. Materials were unclear, and the grading felt disconnected from any clear rubric. Get another professor for 401.

The irony of a Communications professor with unclear communication is hard to ignore. Guidelines were confusing, course materials were confusing, and feedback was minimal — and again, confusing — leaving you no real way to improve. He proudly claimed to be a tough grader. I left more confused than I entered. Would not recommend.

If you can take any course at the business school, make sure it is not with Tim Flood. He is the most arbitrary grade I have ever encountered. This is a group consensus. While he presents the assignments as manageable, he grades with little feedback and a lack of standardization. Save yourself.

Prof. Martinez Franco is such a sweetie and clearly loves her students. She does grade somewhat harshly (I'm always getting A-s and never As :C ) and you have either a quiz or in-class essay to write every week, but she doesn't assign homework so it cancels out. Attendance is mandatory, but class is easy to go to.

Such a nice and caring professor. She really wants everyone to do well in the course and generally grades pretty easy. I am horrible at spanish and still passed 203 with B+ which was mostly due to sandra being my teacher. Great professor would highly recommend after hearing how hard spanish can be at UNC.
Professor Martinez was lovely! She is very understanding and genuinely wants to help you learn.

Ive heard nightmares about Spanish at UNC but Profe Martinez-franco was super sweet and did the best she could to make the content as understandable as possible. It's important to remember that for most of the stuff, she doesn't control what she has to assign us, it's the department.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This is the hardest class I've ever taken. Dr Franco is a very nice person. But she only speaks in Spanish. This makes it extremely difficult to understand what is going on in class. Also isn't helpful for understanding the material when confused or lost. It was her first year at UNC, so Ill give her some slack. But I wouldn't do that again.

I was very intimidated by taking Spanish 203 in college as everyone was advising me to take Spanish online through community college instead, but Professor Martinez Franco is so kind, patient, and makes everything easy to understand. I feel like I learned more from her class than from five semesters of Spanish in high school.

The sweetest professor I've taken!! She cares so much about us as students and people in general. And even gave the class candy! Exams are hard, but that's for the whole Spanish department, so make sure to study!

The most absolutely caring professor I've had!! She's super nice and wants us to succeed, so if you don't understand a topic, she explains it super well. She's not a harsh grader at all, and even one time helped our class when we had a quiz. Take her class, you won't regret it !!

Fan Laoshi is so invested in seeing each one of her students succeed and learn. She is very accommodating and understanding and gives amazing feedback to help you improve. She also pushes her students to do better!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof. Fan is really nice and easy to talk to. She explains things well and actually gives useful feedback. The class takes some effort, but it's fair, and you learn a lot. Definitely recommend taking 102 with her.
Very understanding of late assignments and is a very easy grader but also her class is entertaining.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Fan Laoshi grades harshly, but she is fair, kind, and has a great sense of humor. You will get at least a B as long as you put in the effort. I had about 2-4 hrs of homework every week, and an hour of studying. Don't take this class if you aren't conversational in Chinese. Hit the anki flashcards for every vocab quiz, and you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: fan laoshi and this class can be intimidating at first (esp if you can't speak fluently/read/write at all like me) but my improvement has been insane. she is very funny and understanding. lots of hw and vocab words to learn in a short amount of time, but if you put the work in you'll be fine. 2 oral presentations (generous grading imo)

Fan laoshi is really kind and easy to talk to, and the class vibe is pretty relaxed. It feels okay to make mistakes, and she genuinely cares about students. The class can be challenging sometimes, but it's manageable and not super stressful. I'm glad I took this class.

Fan Laoshi is a great instructor for Chinese 111. She explains concepts clearly and is very patient when answering questions. She encourages group discussions, which makes the class more engaging and helps with speaking practice. Overall, I learned a lot and would definitely recommend her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: she is understanding but there is so. much. work. like we would learn 50+ words in one class and have the vocab quiz the next. her rubrics can be a little vague so don't be afraid to ask because she is pretty lenient on some project deadlines and explains things well. fan laoshi also encourages group discussions so be open to that!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: super sweet and funny, genuinely had a lot of fun in this class. if you're going to take chinese def take it with her. lots of homework, but very manageable and gives lots of extra credit opportunities as well!! weekly quizzes but they're very easy!

Took 111 and 212 with her and loved it. She's super funny and you can tell she cares about her students. These classes really improved my Chinese, especially reading and writing. There's a large workload but it's not too difficult, mainly practicing vocab.

204 is structured pretty much the same as 203. I definitely recommend taking it! This class is way smaller, and you get a lot of speaking and writing practice. I took Professor Fan for both, and my improvement from 102 to 204 has been huge.

Professor Fan is a great professor. The class is definitely fast-paced and intense, but very similar in structure to 101 and 102, just with more heavy-hitting tests. She's a kind grader and highly available for meeting outside of class. Ask lots of questions and you'll be okay!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: her syllabus is very clear and fairly accurate, however be ready for a vocab quiz every other day (the day after 'learning' them in class). you do make a lot of friends in this class! and there are two oral presentations that you do with a partner. overall, a very good course, don't drop it, she's pretty generous with the final grade!
Fan is a good and friendly professor, but expect lots of hw, quizzes, and exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Fan laoshi was a good professor. Assignments were not bad but could take a while if you don't know how to read Chinese. However, she is a very easy grader for homework and presentations. Some students did not like her, but I think it was just hard for them to accept that you have to study a bit for your ethnic language. Take about 30min-1hr a week.
Take her class if you want a professor that cares about you. She's a very good professor, especially for students who want to get better with chinese. Her office hours are also very helpful.
Fan laoshi does listen to her students and will change aspects of the course based on feedback.

SO MUCH WORK. literally took the class just for the language requirement and had more work in it than any other class. also fan laoshi is definitely biased and favors some students, which definitely showed in the grading. will grade based on experience so tell her if youre not exactly a fluent native speaker

Fan laoshi is so lovely. She genuinely cares about her students and puts a lot of thought into how to make her class relevant to her students. I had her for 111 and it helped me adapt to 212 faster. Her grading criteria is clear and fair and she gives great feedback. I was able to make great friends in this class as well!

Fan Laoshi is a resource you need to take advantage of if you want to learn Chinese. If you participate in her class, you will have a great time and make friends with others that does the same. . It's unfortunate that she doesn't teach 313 or else I would take her class again.

Very nice professor who teaches class in interesting approach. I advice to anyone who wants to improve their Chinese. Get ready, Fan Laoshi has a lot of assignments, so you will need to some effort to be successful in this class.
She cares very much about students, participation matters tho. A lot of textbook work and reading, vocab quizzes are straight from textbook. Overall pretty average difficulty. Awesome teacher!

Fan Laoshi is special. She is humorous, has a confident personality, puts hours into her lectures and clearly loves teaching. Students may start as frustrated with her structure, but later discover the reasoning behind it.  LOOK. AT. THE. SYLLABUS. Everything is laid out and explicitly stated. You will make many close friends here. Don't drop 111.

111 is a hard class, but Fan laoshi genuinely cares about making it relevant to her students and addressing their questions. She can be really funny, and her lessons are engaging and interesting. You'll make close friends with your classmates! I got very confident with my speaking in this class. It's very hard. But don't drop it, it's worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Fan Laoshi used to be my most feared professor but slowly turned into one of my favorite professors. She takes feedback very seriously in her class and *sometimes* allows extensions (with excuses). In the past, she was told that there was too much homework, so she decided to assign less. The syllabus is going to be your best friend in her class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Fan was a really kind and down-to-earth professor. To no fault of her own, this is a challenging course, and she tries her best to ensure that what we learn in class is feasible. She always takes feedback and always strives to improve the course, so whatever bad things are said about previous assignments usually changes for the better!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Fan Laoshi's class didn't have a lot of homework to do, except when you had to prepare for presentations. The presentations required a lot of preparation, and you can't use speaker notes when presenting. The reading quizzes were also difficult, but other than that Fan Laoshi was actually a really sweet, funny, and caring professor.

She a nice person and professor. Lessons are very easy to follow (better if you take notes) and homework doesn't take a lot of time. Make sure to attend classes when there are unit quizzes, as they're pretty influent on the final grade, otherwise you'll get a 0/10 and won't be able to do a make-up.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Fan laoshi is a good professor don't get me wrong, but she is very inconsistent with her grading. Somedays she will take 0.1 pts off for an incorrect character and then somedays a whole 0.5 pts. However, if you study a lot and practice your pronunciation, you should be well prepared for the presentations and weekly vocabulary quizzes.

This class is difficult. The professor did give us the materials to succeed yet sometimes there were quiz questions that weren't remotely covered during class but for the majority of it if you studied you wouldn't be too far off from reaching a A or a B in a class. I did learn a lot of Chinese from it which is invaluable but it's a lot of stress.

Solid prof. I took her class over the summer, and she always graded homework and tests within 2 days and gave very good feedback. The class was still really hard, but I think it comes down to effort in the end. She has clear grading criteria on her rubrics, but if you or the class do bad, she'll probably give you a higher grade than you deserve.

Jesus was this class a lot of work, but I genuinely learned so much from it I don't care if it tanks my GPA a bit, I have the rest of college to bring it up. People who leave bad reviews probably just didn't work hard enough and are salty about the course load, but she's just like another mom but in class for me.

I love Fan Laoshi. She is a tough grader and pretty strict about attendance, but it's clear she just wants you to learn Chinese and see you succeed. She has full faith in you to do so too. The course load is very large though, but I don't think she controls all of it. There's a quiz almost every week, but it's not too bad. Overall, love her!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Fan laoshi is a really sweet lady, but she is a tough grader. The class was difficult, because you have a quiz every week, but if you read the textbook story before the quiz, you will be fine. Make sure to study a lot for the tests because they cover a lot. You make a lot of good friends in the class, and she is very fun to talk to.

After reading all of the reviews they had for her I was skeptical about taking this class but in general, it's not that bad if you actually try. We have vocab quiz once a week (in the beginning of the semester she'd tell you the key words) roughly 10 mins per quiz. Be aware she is known to call on people when you least expect it.

Tough grader. Not sure if she's a good teacher, really, but she wasn't a bad one. It was mostly her not being empathetic to the student experience, and very strict on being precise with grammar. Expectations were a little high, even though she recognized that we were beginningers.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Class is incredibly hard. People who do not have a solid understanding of Chinese are better off flunking the placement to get into 101. Test/quizzes every week on everything. Group Projects, lots of homework, quizzes are hard and 5-10 minutes long. Doing work for this class for 15+ hours a week for 3 credits. 60+ Characters weekly.

I really enjoyed professor Fan's class. She was direct and her lessons were really engaging even though I took her class on zoom. She's also really niceencouraging and patient, receptive to questions when we had trouble with class participation things, etc. I learned a lot and I definitely want to take her class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Fan Laoshi is a very nice person who is willing to help you if you go to office hours. That being said, do not take this class. The workload is immense and we had at least 15 quizzes over the semester. You are expected to know new material before it is taught in class for the first time and when it is covered it would be done so extremely quickly.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Strict on assignments and lectures get boring. Expects you to know the material beforehand. She gets upset when students cannot answer correctly. Do not be surprised if she randomly calls on you to answer. However, she is helpful during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Awful. Avoid her at all cost.

This class was geared more towards those who have an already solid understanding of written Chinese. Although it is marketed as a class where the written/reading portions are introductory, this is not true. The bulk of the class is memorizing about 60 vocabulary words a week and lectures have little to do with actual graded work. Time heavy tests!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Don't get fooled by the course description, this class is for HIGHER LEVEL native speakers. You are expected to be able read and write a decent amount already. Half of the tested material is not learned in class. If you cannot read or write Chinese, do NOT take this class. It doesn't teach you how to read or write, just expects that you know.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Fan Laoshi's class ended up moving very fast due to the crammed fall semester. Lectures contained material we were never tested on, and when the day came to learn new vocab words, she already expected you to know the 70 words before class has started. The class required lots of out of class learning and quizzes often had words we have never learned

Did I put inspirational? I didn't mean to. Fan laoshi's class moves quickly and much of the learning is done outside of the class. The class is mainly conducted through her lecturing (quickly) over a powerpoint with some class participation interspersed. Some of the class participation is voluntary, some involves her cold calling.

Fan laoshi is very strict and lectures tend to be very boring. A lot of the learning is done outside of class. During class, we would just read through the list of vocabulary words for the lesson, but personally, I have to spend about 4-5 hours every week learning how to write every single character. Grading honestly depends on her mood that day :(
Took him for 323 and 565, free A.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The professor is very supportive and approachable. He is easy to reach outside class, office hours are helpful, and he patiently clarifies any questions.The course is challenging, but he makes it manageable. Homework is flexible and helps learning, and midterm grading is lenient.Overall, a great instructor and you will learn a lot. Highly recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Had for STOR 565. Homeworks can be challenging and are assigned monthly  but graded very lenient. Tests much easier than homework and also graded lenient. Decent lecturer but very inaccessible outside of class.

I learned a ton in this class, improving both my grasp of history and the Spanish language. I found the workload reasonable, and the final group project was really creative and actually fun. De Fays was kind and a super interesting lecturer as well; she's very well versed in the subject matter. I would highly recommend this class!

De Fays is very nice but can seem a bit intimidating at first. Classes involve a lot of participation and group work, but is very helpful to improve Spanish. Midterms and final are difficult, but doable if you study. Challenging class, but would recommend De Fays.

Profe De Fays is so kind, funny, and caring. She explains concepts pretty well, and she also makes class sort of conversational, which makes it easier to learn (though my class did have 7 people). There is a decent amount of online homework, but it's not awful. The final research paper could had more instruction, but she wanted us to succeed.
best spanish prof ever.
Very good professor, funny, cool creative project across the entire semester, very tough grader, very difficult exams. If you are a history buff this class is for you.

She is nice but didn't really seem to care about us. After I went to her with a personal issue and asked for some leniency with missing a few classes due to a family medical issue, she seemed understanding and said that since I let her know it was an "excused absence" but then gave me a low participation grade.

She is such an amazing Spanish professor. 261 has a lot of content so if you are not a strong speaker, you should prep in advance, but it was very easy and manageable. Tests are straightforward if you study for them, research paper is not complicated. Great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: A lot of HW for the class for a 3 credit language class. Be on top of things and make friends to form a study group. Any test was very hard and writing-based. On paper she will take off points for many simple things. I put in 10+ hours of work every week for this class to get a B+. But De Fays is very nice and funny!

Overall, this class really helped me with my Spanish and grammar usage. Doctora de Fays was a very nice professor and explained concepts well. Don't take this class with her if you don't enjoy participating and speaking a lot in Spanish because you will get a C- or lower for participation (and I mean participating multiple times per class).

Meant for SPAN261: Overall, this class really helped me with my Spanish/grammar usage. Dra de Fays was a kind professor. However, don't take this class with her if you don't enjoy participating and speaking a lot in Spanish because you will get a C- or lower for participation (and I mean participating multiple times per class).

Profesor De Fays was honestly so fun and engaging. She really cares about her students and wants them to succeed. This class did involve a lot of writing which made the class a little more challenging but she organizes it in stages so it is not as overwhelming. She genuinely wants people to love spanish and it shows in the way she teaches!

I loved this class, but it required a lot of work. Get comfortable speaking Spanish with classmates and Prof. de Fays because that is a big part of your participation. Reading comprehension and grammar homework each night, 5-page research paper, round table talk, and 3 exams. It is doable, but you need a good Spanish foundation to get an A.

This course is far from easy, but Prof. de Fays makes it a good experience. She's incredibly knowledgable on the coursework, so she encourages participation & different perspectives. Her lectures are engaging, and I feel like she genuinely cares for her students. Outside of class, she gives great feedback on assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: She is super sweet, open, and honest with the class. The entire semester, she was understanding of the difficulties of being a student and was flexible as long as you explained yourself. She was not too hard of a grader for this class, but attendance and participation is needed to succeed in the class.

Absolutely loved class with De Fays! She is so funny and makes lectures so so interesting! Loves it when you ask questions and participate. Exams are challenging, but the way your grade is made up of so many different projects and papers, it isn't too hard to get an A! Would 100% take more classes with her

Prof. De Fays is very nice, but her grading is very tough. She is very nitpicky in homework assignments and on the final project. You will lose 10 points for grammar issues and you will lose points for word choice, even if the grammar is correct. Overall, there is not much work in the class but the grading can be very harsh at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Love her! Very kind and understanding, accessible outside of class, and very funny! My favorite Spanish professor I've had at UNC.

De Fays was a really good lecturer! She really knew her material and was willing to explain concepts and provide feedback and help. She could be condescending or brash at times, but she was overall very funny and caring towards students.
