Profesora is one of the most considerate professors I have had at UNC. She is very respectful of her students and is very fair with the material. I had specifically chosen 3 classes in the past just to have her as a professor again. She cares for her students and provides the necessary materials and class environment for you to succeed. 10/10 :)

She's amazing. It was my first college course, but she was very unintimidating and cared a lot about her students. She takes great note of participation, so be ready to raise your hand when you come to class. You'll have a lot of homework assignments, but nothing that takes incredibly long.

While she's a good option for lower level spanish, her grading gets incredibly tougher as you move up the levels. Participated everyday and only got 70s. Her test/quizzes are nothing like practice she gives, and her feedback doesn't help you learn how to improve.

She is the WORST Spanish teacher I have ever had period. She is such a hard grader and you learn nothing from her during class. I participated every day multiple times and she still gave 70s in participation. I do not know who is giving her good reviews but she is not a good teacher and is very quirky. Do NOT take her class if you want an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: De Fays is a great professor that truly wants to make sure you're engaged in the course material. Expect to receive detailed, specific feedback on essays and be prepared to memorize and apply about 20 pieces of vocabulary per quiz.

French 101 is hard but she explained things very well. There is A LOT of homework assignments, but nothing that takes too long. It is also operated using a flipped classroom so def be ready to study and learn a lot outside of class.

She is a very caring professor! She does all she can to help you. Make sure to prepare well for the tests and you will be fine. For writing assignments, make sure to set aside time to complete them and try out new grammar structures as she grades on quality and advance content. There is a lot of content to cover.

Profesora de Fays is awesome! She's so friendly and easy to talk to, emails back really quickly, doesn't make you feel stupid for asking questions, and is very enthusiastic about the subject material. She allows for questions during class if you're ever confused but is also willing to answer over email. Take her if you can!

Dra. de Fays was an awesome instructor, I was thinking that this course would be more difficult but it was relatively average. There were readings/movies and homework for every class but it was enjoyable considering Dra. de Fays really encouraged everyone to speak. Very great professor, very humorous and very knowledgeable.

I LOVE her. She does a great job at grading in the context of your ability, so even if you aren't the best speaker, you'll get a decent participation grade as long as you make the effort. I thought she graded pretty fairly/easily for papers. It was annoying to pay for access to her website/textbook, but the readings were pretty easy. She is great!!

Dra. de Fays genuinely cares about her students and is very understanding, especially due to the pandemic. The course entailed several papers which were based off movies we watched. The quizzes were not too difficult, but the midterm and final exam were.

She really cares about teaching and gets excited about what she teaches. There isn't too much homework, but the textbook is actually just a website she created that you have to pay for which is annoying. She also grades a little harshly for the rubrics she gives. Very willing to meet outside of class and responds quickly to emails

Such a kind and caring instructor. She really cares about the students and tries to be as accommodating and transparent as possible. Really interesting subject matter. However, is a pretty tough grader. You will really have to work for your grade. Also, if you don't participate in class, your grade will be in trouble.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor de Fays is very nice and helpful at a surface level, but sometimes she can be intimating and a bit demeaning when you make a mistake in Spanish. She tracks your participation but does her best to get everyone to speak. If you are serious about Spanish, I would take her, otherwise I'd go for a graduate student (who are more understanding)

Fantastic professor, even though this was a difficult class. I had to work hard for everything, but she showed me what I needed to do in order to drastically increase my Spanish proficiency and showed me that I had the skills to accomplish this. Also, she really cares about her students.

Professor De Fays is really sweet and interesting but her class is pretty hard. There is a LOT of homework and projects, all of which is graded pretty hard. She was also very inflexible with deadlines and did not reduce work when the semester was disrupted by COVID. If you work hard and do the work though, you'll do fine.

Blech. Gotta love getting an email letting you know that you have homework due today, when the last day of class was two days ago. Someone brought this up in class two weeks ago and she said the work was optional? She's nice, but clueless. Mid Covid-19 and she acts like everything is totally normal. Pushing work beyond the semester end is not ok.

She's a sweet lady and has a good sense of humor. She's a good teacher but this course (SPAN 321) was repetitive from SPAN 261. I wish she was more specific with her essay grading because she does not grade by a rubric which can be frustrating. Not too bad of a grader but it can be frustrating sometimes because she's very specific on what she wants

Best professor I have had at UNC. She makes you work for the grade but it is worth it in the end. I learned so much from her. She will stop class and make sure everyone understands the material before moving on. She cares about her students. Go out of your way to take a class with her.

She has definitely been my favorite Spanish professor at UNC! She's so funny and sweet and genuinely cares about the success of her students. I took SPAN 203 with her over the summer and it was a lot, but she kept us engaged and made sure we weren't too overwhelmed. All in all a great professor and I would definitely recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Wow, one of the best professors at UNC for Spanish. She's funny and caring and is quick to abandon a powerpoint to go to the board to explain things if needed. She really knows what she is talking about and encourages students to practice speaking while giving corrections to help them improve. Her exams are very consistent with what she teaches.
She is a friendly person but an unfair grader. Okay at explaining concepts but not really.

De Fays is such a kind and inspiring professor. She is more than happy to help outside of class which is super helpful and clearly cares a lot about her students. Just ALWAYS be prepared for pop quizzes and know that participation within class from the start is very important.
Hélène De Fays was my first Spanish professor at UNC and she was so fantastic. The class was hard, but was super enjoyable. She's very sarcastic, but super caring.

Definitely one of my favorite professors. It is so clear that she really wants her students to do well and she is always accessible for extra help. Class was actually really interesting and enjoyable to be in. Tests were more difficult than in previous Spanish classes, but this is an upper level class so that's expected.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I love Helene. Had her for Spanish 204. So, so , so caring and open with her students. An absolute gem. Participation really matters though, so get comfortable with talking.

I love that she displays a good sense of humor towards her students, especially if Spanish 204 is one of the most challenging gateway courses. She does a good job explaining grammatical concepts, and she does grade grammar in a strict manner. Prepare for her exams by doing the problems in her exam review activities, and you'll do fine.

Incredible professor. She was like my mom all semester and really cared about her students and teaching. She was pretty flexible on due dates and was always available for extra help. Easy B or an A if you try hard.

SPAN 204 was difficult, but Prof de Fays was amazing, I loved her as a professor. She really made me feel prepared for the exams, even if the exams themselves were difficult (she didn't write them, the Department does). So much in-class practice, it was fantastic. Overall, like she was seriously a 10/10 professor. Funny, nice, great.

She really knows what she is talking about and clearly explains grammar. You do a lot of practice in class that prepares you for the exam. She grades very hard on pronunciation and you have to participate in class. The voice threads were annoying, but they really help. She's so nice and funny and cute 10/10 would recommend.

I've loved nearly every minute of this class, which I didn't necessarily think I would. She's funny (sometimes unintentionally so) and she's pretty relatable as a human being. Sometimes she's tough on grading, but if you have some kind of extenuating circumstance she will gladly work with you to figure things out.

I LOVE PROFE DE FAYS!! she is absolutely HILARIOUS and truly cares about you! i have had some attendance issues because of things going on outside of class, and she really is understanding and works to meet you halfway. she does give points for partipation everyday, so it is important to raise your hand. she is great if you truly want to learn span

Profesora de Fays is really funny and engaging in a small (20) class; she makes jokes and can tell when we're bored. She really wants participation and you get daily points for it. She was available for help and very forgiving if you attend class and engage. Importance of readings is inversely related to how well you understand her spoken Spanish.

I personally didn't like her. When we did presentations, I spoke fluently and with a pretty good accent (I've taken Spanish since 2nd grade) but I'd always get a B or a B+; yet, the girl with a pretty bad accent and constant pauses gets an A...

Excellent teacher. She is knowledgeable, approachable and reliable. She respects her students and encourages them. You have to work hard and cover a lot of material. She brings it all together with a sophisticated, cosmopolitan sensibility.

Super nice and approachable. The class can get boring at times, but she does her best to keep it interesting and keep students engaged. It's also pretty much a guaranteed A or B if you do the reading and study for the quizzes.

I took Spanish 101 last semester, and, while being very likeable, it seemed like she was impatient/uninterested with teaching us beginners new material. She covered subjects too fast and did not seem sympathetic to beginner problems. She was very funny and pleasant to be in class with, though, and i ended with a B+ in the class.
Very friendly and easy going person.  330 covered a little too much (ancient times through 1917), but was extremely interesting.
One word, boring. Had a big lecture class with her. Easy though.

She keeps the class interesting and definitely has a sense of humor.  Her class isn't the easiest but as long as you pay attention and ask questions, it turns out fine.  She is a great person in general!
Chem 101 is very hard, but she does her best to make the content seem less daunting and lectures as interesting as possible!

Hands down my favorite chem professor so far (junior chem major). I love Dr Fostvedt so much. She cares about your learning, is kind, and is very accessible. She also wants you to succeed and do your best. Dr. Fostvedt will meet you where you are and try to help you every step of the way. Truly a wonderful human being--her kindness is contagious.
Take her. Favorite class ever

Dr. Fostvedt is awesome! Super sweet and takes all the time needed to answer questions. Since CHEM101 is 90% freshman, she validates us by acknowledging that chemistry is hard. Most of the TAs are great too

Fostvedt is literally amazing, she always has fun ways to teach you content (dances, yoga, models, etc.) and is sooo caring. She will slow down to answer questions and makes jokes inbetween. I only need to take chem101 for my major, but she also teaches 251 and her personality is tempting me to take 251

Her office hours are extremely helpful. ULAs are very helpful too. She has extra credit opportunities. I would take her again. I have never had a more understanding and kind professor, which is rare in UNC's CHEM department. She had helpful practice sheets. On the downside, multiple-choice questions on tests were difficult, in my opinion.

Would give 6/5 if it was an option. Fostvedt is incredible at explaining difficult concepts in ways that are understandable to students. She is also extremely caring and wants all of her students to succeed. She has options for 10 minute meeting every week — strongly recommend. Side note: If you're taking 251, don't read the textbook, it's useless
Dr. Fostvedt is a great profesor and makes sure her students succeed in class

Dr. Fostvedt is by far one of if not the kindest and most down to Earth professor I've ever had. She makes chem 251 and absolute joy, and is one of the most accommodating professors ever. Her exams are always fair, and her lectures are really interesting and taught extremely well. Additionally, she gives a lot of practice.
Leaving love

One of, if not the best professor I've had in college. I learned a ton in this class and had fun doing so. This course was also not overly-demanding at all and I enjoyed it even though synthetic chemistry is not my field of interest within chemistry. Definitely take a class with Dr. Fostvedt if you can.

Dr Fostvedt is the best professor i have had at UNC! The textbook for this class is DENSE but in class her explanations make it so clear. So many opportunities for practice (TONS of practice exams) and her exams are so fair! Hard material but if you go to class it makes so much more sense.

Dr. Fostvedt is incredible--truly a gem among an otherwise heinous Chemistry department. No rating below a 5 here has anything to do with her, or is at all under her control. She is inviting and engaging--I enjoyed chem because I looked forward to learning from her. One of the best and sweetest professors I've ever had the privilege to learn from.

Professor Fostvedt is so sweet and caring! She tries to make CHEM 101 as engaging as it can be. The class is definitely very difficult but that's because of the department, not her, since all the professors follow the same format and use the same exams. As for the class, practice is very important and what helped my study best for the exams.

The best professor in the UNC chem department. Amazing lecturer, tried to make how boring chemistry was into something great. She was always caring for EVERY student. Chem is very hard because of the terrible department, but not Dr. Fostvedt. I love her!

Dr. Fostvedt is a QUEEN in all aspects. She's super fun, caring, and conducts very engaging lectures. She also plans fun activities like bingo and jeopardy where you get the chance to win fun chemistry stickers. Exams are fair and straightforward if you pay attention and do the problem sets. Every exam also has an extra credit question.

Best wet lab I've taken at UNC. To my knowledge, Dr. Fostvedt is the only lab instructor that actually releases the grading criteria used for evaluating each assignment. This course is 100x better than it used to be, and the pigment synthesis is actually pretty fun. Group research project at the end of the course with a poster presentation & paper.

Fostvedt is hands down the best chemistry professor at UNC. Shes so kind, good at teaching, and approachable. So reasonable with grades and classwork and takes feedback from students fullheartedly. An angel sent down to bring a little light to the hell that is the UNC chem department. If youre a chem major or need to take a chem class PLZ TAKE HER

FY-Launch section. Hands down best professor ever. So sweet, knowledgeable, and flexible. Outfits consistently eat and her explanations make you laugh. She gets us to enjoy chemistry, which is a talent. Class itself is not hard, especially if you do the recommended textbook and recitation practice problems. Nightly reading and completion hw grade.

Fostvedt is AMAZING. I loved inorganic chemistry with her, loved the content of the course, loved going to lecture, loved being taught by her. Could not recommend her enough. She is so caring, she is so smart, and she is so good at teaching. If I could take 251 again, I would :)

She is such a great person and great lecturer. She is open to feedback and is very passionate about her subject. By far the best chem prof I've had so far (chem major). She writes very fair exams and gives an extra credit question at the end of the midterms and final. There is also an opportunity to memorize the periodic table for a grade boost.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She's nice but this class was not it for me. Content feels very hand-wavey at times and not very interesting to be honest. Exams are difficult, final was marginally easier. Extra credit of +1% to course grade is available for memorizing periodic table!

Dr. Fostvedt is the most caring chem professor I've ever had. She wants you to succeed and is always available outside of class to help. She even asked the class halfway through the semester how she could improve. Lectures are great and exams are fair. I hate the class but love her as a professor.
Not her fault, but the class is designed to hand-wave a lot of physical principles, which results in the need to memorize seemingly random facts for the exam.
Amazing professor who explains concepts very well. Slows down when needed and will give additional examples in class. Great at her job fr and passionate about chem which made the class more engaging

Couldn't recommend Fostvedt enough! Caring, great at explaining hard concepts, and sets very clear expectations. Learning Assistants are truly the best in the Chem Dept as well. There's one bonus question on each exam, and she gives one extra credit opportunity for overall grade. Not an easy class, but not impossible. Study from the slides!!

I had Dr. Fostvedt for 102 and she was an awesome teacher. The lectures were amazing and engaging, and the class was always fun and informative. The class is even more test heavy and harder than 101, but none of that is Dr. Fostvedt's fault. An amazing class overall, absolutely get Dr. Fostvedt for this class.

I look CHEM 101 With Dr. Fostvedt, and she was absolutely amazing. She is very caring, her lectures are phenomenal, and she is always willing to help. The class is slightly difficult and test heavy, but that is due to the chemistry department and not her fault. 10/10, definitely try and get this class with her.

Fostvedt is amazing but 102 w/ her wont make it much better bc all 102s use the same teaching+slides. Def take her; dont get stressed if you cant. To pass, go to 2 LA/TA sessions weekly & re-do all class slide problems plus the practice exams (sometimes theyre exam questions). Plz do hw, dont stress over text readings, & go to class its important!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Fostvedt is great but this class is very difficult.  Exams make up the majority of your grade and they are not easy, although the final was significantly easier than the midterms in my opinion.

As any chem, this was test heavy. But her tests are fair based on lectures and participation. Be sure to go to every class and have a good understanding of content. She has a lot of resources outside of class as well and is very understanding.

Dr. Fostvedt is the literal only good professor in the CHEM department here. Her tests are fair to the point where you could earn up to 5 points back on the last test because she thought it was "too long." She has a lot of opportunities to practice exam-type problems, and is very willing to help you improve if you seek it out. BEST CHEM PROFESSOR

Professor fostvedt is the best of the unc chem professors. This department is rough but professor fostvedt explains the material really well, great depth, and actually cares that we understand the material. only note is that she does frequently spend so much teaching a topic that we then fall behind on notes and material.

I LOVE FOSTVEDT. She responds to emails very fast, is VERY thorough, and genuinely cares about her students. She is just so sweet, really tries to learn everyones name(even in a HUGE lecture hall), and is very involved. She is amazing.
She is really passionate about chemistry and takes time to get to know her students. The UNC chem department is a BEAST but she tries to help us out the best that she can.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is hard but take it with Fostvedt if you can. She is super engaging and enthusiastic during lecture and really approachable. Be prepared to attend outside sessions, get a tutor, and/or do a lot of practice problems. The midterms varied in difficulty but overall very challenging.

Dr. Fostvedt is the most kind, respectable, humble, and best lecturer I have ever had! She genuinely cares for her students which shows as she learns the names of half of her students when they ask questions! Any chem class is hard at UNC and you will have to work diligently, but if you have the chance take a class with Dr. Fostvedt!

Dr. Fostvedt completely changed chemistry for me. She makes complicated concepts simple and approachable. Chem102 is not easy, but she made it great. That being said, I sometimes felt like I lacked the nuanced understanding of concepts needed to succeed in difficult exams. You should attend the sessions outside of class! Take her if you can!!!

Dr. Fostvedt is incredible! She always brings joy to the classroom and provides lots of extra practice through PSS, PS, and LA worksheets, and practice exams. The exams aren't too bad and any other work is collaborative.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is amazing! Clearly cares about her students. I literally switched my major to chemistry because she made it seem so interesting. Very available outside of class. As long as you do the abundant practice problems she provides, you will be fine.

Dr. Fostvedt is an incredible professor! She goes over the material thoroughly, and goes the extra mile to make her lectures engaging. She cares a lot about her students, and provides useful feedback in class, GPSS, and six-minute meetings. Still study well outside of class, as the course material is objectively challenging.
Dr. Fostvedt is such a kind, caring professor! She makes the lectures so fun, and really makes an effort to get to know her students. I'd definitely recommend going to her 6-minute meetings.

Dr Fostvedt is an amazing professor who cares for her students success. This class is very manageable especially if you go to the office hours she offers throughout the semester. Not a lot of homework and gives extra credit opportunities.

Prof. Fostvedt is incredible. She takes the time to explain everything in a concise manner and often uses analogies that we can relate to to make the concepts more accessible. Chem is a tough subject, but she tried to make it as straightforward as possible and provide us with all of the resources we could possibly need. Would 3,000% take again.

Great professor who tried her best to make the class as easy as possible, unfortunately the class is too hard cause we have to be up to standard with our "top 10 chemistry school" so in the end it technically doesn't matter who you take either get the concepts or you don't but probably best to go with fostvedt.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I have never enjoyed nor understood chemistry until I took 101 with Dr. Fostvedt. She is extremely caring towards her students and very responsive to any questions asked. She makes her lectures easy to follow and straightforward. It is a flipped classroom, but I think it helps in the end as long as you put in the work to understand the content.

Fostvedt is by far the best professor, she made a very difficult course like CHEM101 very understandable and simple as possible. She is super encouraging and actually learned names in a big lecture (if you are in the first couple rows). Her GPSS sessions are the best and I wish everyone could take 101 with her! Put in the work to succeed though.
she's a good teacher it's just the chem department is so hard, there's almost nothing she can do but try and teach. Sometimes her age and how new she is to teaching can show

Prof. Fostvedt is an amazing teacher. While she is confined to the standards/exams of the chem dept, she makes lectures easily understandable and engaging. She is always willing to answer questions and wants everyone to do well. CHEM101 is difficult no matter what, but she is a fantastic professor to take it with. Also a very kind and cool person!!

Dr. Fostvedt is definitely one of, if not THE best chemistry professors at UNC. Her lectures are extremely easy to understand, and she's always willing to answer questions. She's extremely kind and friendly, and genuinely cares about her students. I'd definitely recommend taking advantage of the "Six-minute meetings" as well.

She is so sweet and she is an amazing teacher. There were very few lectures where I came out confused. I also went to her GPSS sessions which were also awesome. She carefully went through everything we asked and made sure we understood what wwe were doing. She also learned so many peoples names for such a giant lecture hall.

Prof. Fostvedt is an amazing lecturer who I felt like really cares about her students. I would recommend her GPSS if possible. Chem 101 has the same tests department wide so if you are worried about hard tests taking it with a different prof will not affect this!

She is the nicest professor ever. I think she is probably the best out of the chem department. She is very understanding and always willing to help. Now with that said, Chem 101 is very hard at unc. But if you have to take it I would try to get her.

Professor Fostvedt keeps our attention in class effectively transmits concepts.  We thought we were well prepared with materials to succeed on the first exam we took recently.  She even gave us last years exams, but when we took this exam it was much more difficult.  The guidance we were given was far from parallel to what we were presented with.

Professor Fostvedt=great lecturer. We were provided with last year's exams in preparation for our first exam last week. We got slammed because it was tremendously more difficult.  We feel like we were misled.  Perhaps she was told to make the exams harder this year because last years exams were too easy?  New professor to the school=easier exam?

I LOVED Prof. Fostvedt! The class itself isn't an easy A, but she was able to make the material very interesting to learn and I thought her tests/grading were extremely fair. The few assignments she assigns aren't just busy work, but actually help you learn which was much appreciated.

She was hands down my favorite chem professor. She taught the class really well. By no means was the class easy but with the problem sessions and office hours the challenging concepts I didn't understand in class became so much easier. Anyway, take the course with her if you need to she's great!
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Fostvedt was such a great 101 professor!! The chem101 curriculum is tough no matter what professor you take it with, but she did such a great job explaining the new topics and realizing when the class needed more time on something. She gave time for us to practice in class, communicated any schedule changes, and really cared for the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The best professor I have had at UNC, bar none. Dr. Fostvedt is incredibly passionate about her material, and it shows. She explains difficult concepts in a simple way, and is very accessible outside of class if you need anything. Could not recommend taking a class with her enough.

Dr. Fostvedt was great and made learning fun. Her tests were fairly difficult, but the other assignments weren't too bad. The class gets easier as it goes on and the final was extremely fair. Dr. Fostvedt is very approachable and fun to talk to about chemistry and non-chemistry topics. Overall I think she's a professor every chem major should take.

Basically no homework, so unfortunately I fell behind and thought the tests would be very easy. I did not do well in the beginning at all. Inorganic was a tough subject for me but then the final I aced it after finally understanding so don't fall behind! She is very nice tho. Textbook is useless. Personally, orgo 2 was easier.

Dr. Fostvedt is easily my favorite professor at chapel hill. She actually cares about her student's success, and willingly helps you. Regardless if you have her for chem 101 or not I HIGHLY recommend going to her GPSS on fridays at 12 (this time might be changed though). This is easily the best way to stay on top of her class and to study as well.

I though Professor Fostvedt was alright. We ended up behind in lectures often, she starts every lecture with like a 5-10 minute talk about a fun fact or person that she wanted to share with us which really took away important time from class. This made it feel like we had to rush through some of the later material.

I honestly don't understand the Fostvedt hype. In my opinion, students were taught to memorize rather than understand the material. This was evident when taking the midterm exams in which virtually every question included some niche exception to the more common physical principles. The final exam was much more straightforward.

Dr. Fostvedt has been my favorite Professor at UNC so far! She is so sweet and really wants to see her students succeed. When she goes through problems she walks through every single step no matter how simple which is really helpful. I always felt prepared for the tests if I did the homework and payed attention in class. Absolutely loved her!!

Dr. Fostvedt is hands down the best professor I've had at UNC as of yet. She's super sweet, so passionate about chemistry that even lectures on boring mathy stuff become engaging and fun, and she's a lenient grader even on exams. There's extra credit on exams as well as an additional extra credit opportunity, and there was virtually no homework!

Pls take any class u can with her- shes super nice and approachable, and shes really a great lecturer! You can tell she genuinely loves teaching and wants to help you learn, and is super smart and good at teaching. 11/10 one of my best instructors ever

The tests for this class are hard, so do lots of practice, but they're pretty reflective of the practice problems and lectures. The class was hard, but I I LOVE Professor Fostvedt. She's makes it all worth it and just brightens the day of everyone around her.

Dr. Fostvedt is the best Chem professor you will get at this school. The Chem department is overall like a 4/10 here, so do yourself a favor and take fostvedt. Makes topic simple and is very accessible outside of class. The effort you put in is basically the grade you get out. She made my 9am chem bearable because she was so good.

Just take her, it's a no brainer. I'm convinced that she is the best professor you can get for a general chem class. She's incredibly patient and practically defines how a good professor acts and teaches like. Hard to believe that I found myself enjoying this class at times... something that wouldn't have happened if I wasn't in her section.

Jade Fostvedt is amazing, chemistry is not. She didn't control the material that was on the test, but believe me they were extremely difficult. She is a passionate and interesting lecturer. If you have to take this class I can't recommend her enough.

Dr. Fostvedt is a great professor! She's very passionate about chemistry and is frequently accessible outside of class. The practice you do in class and for homework very accurately reflects the tests. The material isn't easy, but if you come to lecture and practice you'll do well. Wouldn't recommend taking this class before orgo though
Honestly, Dr. Fostvedt was an amazing professor. The reason my grade isn't super good is because I did not try anywhere near as good as I should have. My grade does not reflect her she was the best.

I took CHEM 101 last semester with Dr. Fostvedt, I just forgot to do a review for her. I found her to be incredibly nice and caring about her students, as well as a great professor. She also made chemistry very interesting, despite it being a hard subject. Chem at UNC is difficult, but it is not impossible to get an A.

She is one of the nicest people ever. She's so understanding if you're ever sick or out of class, and tries to explain the material so everyone understands it. She is one of those people who would genuinely never hurt a fly

Very chill and likable person. Whole chemistry department is very organized, I would recommend using all of the resources offered. Clearly shows how to do problems. Answers everyones questions. Only trouble was with running out of time towards the end of class because she answers so many questions.

I can't express my love for Dr. Fostvedt enough. Super caring, listens to students, excellent lecturer, super knowledgable, but has no problem admitting when she's unusure of something or if she's made a mistake. If I could take all my chemistry classes with her I would. Could've done better in her class but that was simply me being lazy.

Fostvedt is great for 101. Her teaching style shows that she really cares about her students gaining a true understanding of the material. Learning chemistry for the first time is hard work, but she approaches questions + concerns with respect. I felt engaged in her lectures; I totally recommend taking her class!

Dr. Fostvedt is amazing! She is so great during lecture and you can really tell how passionate she is about the subject matter. If I could take every class with her I would. Her class made me remember the reasons why I became a Chemistry major in the first place and I am incredibly grateful for that. Take her class if you can, you won't regret it!
i only got a d because i am stupid. dr. fostvedt is a queen and my grade doesnt reflect her amazingness

Her lectures are great, she makes the material easy to understand and is always willing to answer questions. Would recommend her office hours for practice problems and more clarity as needed, I found them super helpful. Exams are tough but totally fair and from lecture (I didn't open the textbook once).

Dr. Fostvedt has a great personality and is enthusiastic about the content. She answers any questions in class, although this can cause her to not completely go through the slides in class. 

Make sure you pay attention to the in-class slides, even if you did not entirely go through them. Chances are it's on your exam. Also, attend chem-possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: While this was her first semester, she was an amazing chemistry professor and really cared about learning. She knew the material really well and explained all the concepts succinctly. Go to office hours and review session as those are great ways to ask questions and get a lot of practice! Exams are difficult but extremely fair!

Was extremely sweet and understanding and went out of her way to help students who asked for it. Was her first semester teaching here and she did an awesome job, was so down to earth and transparent. Only thing I'd say is that there was more material than there was class time, so I would advise going to office hours/ review sessions. 11/10.

Though this was her first semester, she taught like she's been a professor for many years. Clearly knows the material, and she's always willing to explain content. Attend office hours and ask questions. Exams are difficult but always reflect the material taught in lecture. One of the best profs in the chem department. Take inorganic with her.

great professor in a disorganized department. Easy-to-understand lectures, answers questions, kind person.  Go to GPSS, work out practice problems, read chapters, watch "The Organic Chemistry Tutor" on YouTube (my saving grace), and make a study guide for each chapter, this allows you to have your notes summarized for exams.

Dr. Fostvedt is an amazing professor. Chemistry was difficult for me but she went above and beyond to answer everyone's questions. I do recommend going to class to get participation points and to ask questions about the material!

Prof. Fostvedt is a very sweet first-year instructor! Made coming to class at 8am worth it, very enthusiastic about the material, + never failed to put a smile on my face. She is also so stylish and humorous :) Participation based on responding to questions using an iclicker throughout lecture, incorrect answers do not affect participation grade.
She's a fine Gen Chem professor. She didn't always get through the material in class, but that was usually because she was answering people's questions.

Took her lecture in freshman year for CHEM 101. She was really enthusiastic about learning and helping students understand things that puzzle them. Helped me to find opportunities for chemistry teaching within department, outside of class. Super receptive to feedback, like when making a mistake in class.

Professor Fostvedt was an amazing professor who really cared about her students. You can tell that she worked really hard to make everyone understand the material and wanted everyone to do well. I loved her lectures and felt like she was really easy to understand. I would definitely take her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Fostvedt is an amazing lecturer. She explains each and every concept very well and concisely. She wants everyone to succeed and is very caring, especially during her office hours. She also tries to understand and personally know her students. I 100% recommend taking her!

STAY FAR AWAY!!! This was the worst class I have ever taken at UNC. The exams were not fair at all. He included trick questions on all the exams that were already out of line with his lectures. His handouts weren't even his, and I don't think I learned a single thing from his teaching. Run as far away from this class as possible.

This class is extremely evil, but so is every STOR155 section. Mario is the only professor who teaches 155 that is NOT a grad student, so he has much more experience teaching the coursework. His lectures are hard to follow, you will need to read heavily. Midterms are extremely difficult, but he is VERY generous with his curving and gives a HW curve

Mario's a great guy with great sense of humor, but Disclaimer: THIS CLASS IS HARD. If you do not want to challenge yourself, do not take this class. If you took AP Stats, it will assist you a fair bit, but it will not enough. The tests are all multiple choice, have excel functions as answers, and are worded to trick you. Make your choice wisely...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: AVOID AT ALL COSTS... Mario is undoubtedly the worst. He will tell you to read the textbook, but not have the same material on exams, ridicule you, and waste your time. If Mario only curves to "fix the mistakes in his teaching," but there is a 20% curve, how can he claim that he's a decent professor? Nightmare professor for an introductory course.

If you do not have a foundation in statistics please find another Stor 155 professor. His lectures are very unclear and do not match the textbook, which is the first and only resource that he will tell you to reference when you have questions about the material. Exams also do not accurately reflect the homework. Save yourself the trouble.

Midterm averages in the 50s because he designs the most absurd, convoluted questions to trip you up. It's obvious he despises his students' success: he just rambles about his own code and the "slides" are just ss of his own code. He offers a 7% curve, since only two people had an A before it. It's a masterclass in cruelty masked as "teaching."

Mario is not a good teacher, he talks very fast and goes off on tangents. For an intro level stats course, this class is way too hard. The tests are designed to trick you. Additionally, his attitude is rude and derogatory. Nice curve at the end of the year but would recommend taking with a different professor.

Don't take Mario, the first week he said we would hate him and that it was his job to weed us out. The workload was really easy, but it almost would've been more helpful if he posted more practice before exams. Studying was stressful, he was rude, lectures made no sense, didn't grade ANYTHING until 2 days before the final, did curve heavy though.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's really funny and makes the material memorable. The class can be challenging, but the curve helps. Overall, he's a great professor if you pay attention and put in the effort.

Good teacher if your willing to learn, ask questions, and go to office hours if you need help. Goes in depth about every topic if you ask. Super rememberable and funny. Practice the homework, don't use AI, create one pagers, & study. I wish the curve was lower, seriously, some people deserved to fail.
Do not take this class. truly the worst professor I have had at unc. even though he curves at the end, the amount of pressure during the semester when you saw your grade was a 40% was insane.

My rating probably would have been lower but the professor gave a 20% final curve, effectively bumping my C+ all the way to an A. The things you hear about Dr. Mario are partially true; somewhat of an ego, but will help you if you really want to learn. Tests are intentionally made to trick you. Must study. But again, fat curve so I can't complain.

Listen, this is a HARD class. If it was supposed to be easy, everyone would just get an A. It's HARD. Dr. Mario is a nice guy who laughs at himself and cracks jokes. When you ask a question he will thoroughly go through it with you. He holds office hours and responds super quick. I once emailed him at 11:30 and he responded in 5 minutes. Good dude.

Doesn't explain concepts well and over complicates things, also goes on lots of tangents during lectures. 2 midterms (25% each) and the final (35%) are all MCQ but he intentionally makes the questions very tricky. Teaches some things different from the textbook he assigns. Unlimited hw attempts and applied a 20% curve at the end of semester.

Mario was a pretty mediocre teacher. He was a nice guy overall, but his lectured were pretty confusing. He makes very difficult exams and you will have no idea what your final grade is until the end. With that said, he gave a VERY generous curve to the final grade. This class will be a grind, but ending with an A is achievable if you put in work
Do not take this professor. The class isn't hard, but the exams are poorly written and don't match the lectures. A midterm had to be curved by 20% because of how badly it was designed.

Hilarious but extremely egotistical and conceited. Don't take this class if you've never taken stats before, but if you have, you'll be fine. Generous with curves mostly because he values his reputation more than your life. Lectures are relaxed but full of tangents, so little gets done. Gives zero insight on exams, so studying feels like a gamble.

Condescending, egotistical, bad lecturer, and exams don't reflect the homework at all. He wants his students to fail and has a weird complex about proving that we "don't belong at UNC Chapel Hill". Pope Francis once said that he hopes no one goes to hell, but I promise you he wouldn't have said that had he met Mario. Horrible. Save yourself.

Confusing lectures and tests that look nothing like any materials given. Said he hopes we get weeded out and have to work at McDonald's. Super unhelpful and rude. Some may say he's “funny” but it's just a waste of time. I was a straight A student before this class.

He's intelligent and personable but I have some gripes with his teaching style. He offers no resources outside of lecture and claims the textbook is supplemental but often teaches completely different material. He makes things unnecessarily complicated and that is reflected in low test averages. Curves are fair though. Take it with someone else.

He gave us a 12% curve at the end (14% with the course evals) bc only one person received an A- and no one received an A with raw grades. Projects are graded EXTREMELY harshly and one person ends up doing all the work because of how the projects are set up, so you're screwed if you get a bad group. Not enough time for quizzes. But you can get A.
horrible....
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not take stats with him. Exams are not a reflection of what is taught in class. He wants you to fail. A 20%  curve on the midterm is a reflection of his poor teaching, not the students. I took stats in high school and understood it, there's no reason for me to be failing midterms. Save yourself and take stats with another professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took this class last summer, and I just saw the reviews for Dr. Mario and was SHOCKED. When I had this class, it was tough but he ends up curving so much at the end that you end up with a good grade despite how tough it was. idk where all this talk about him being rude is coming from, he was legit the nicest, funniest professor I've had at UNC.

hatred against him is an understatement he doesn't know how to teach and talk to students and only wants everyone around him failing. His humour during lecture is also really derogatory and rude. I wanted to drop him so bad but couldn't as it was too late. Take his classes if you want to tank your gpa

horrible experience. 0 study material given outside of notes outlines. Exams are MCQ but are worded so poorly and designed to confuse you and are NOTHING like the homeworks. Midterm 1 is fine, Midterm 2 was universally so TERRIBLE that we had a 20 (!!!) percent curve. Says it was unfair but says that now that we've seen it, it is fair for final????
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Avoid him at all costs. Unhelpful, confusing, rude. I had never had a grade below an 86 before this class and I took calc and I am a stem major. Exams are nothing like lecture, homework, or textbook. DO NOT take this class with Dr.Mario!!!!!!!

Please save yourself from a bad stats experience and avoid this professor. He is not very good at explaining, his lectures are poorly structured, and his goal is to do the opposite of help you succeed. Take this class with someone else

Genuinely have never been more confused and frustrated in a class. I was a straight A student in high school (out of state student) and usually study really hard for my exams. Claims that reading the textbook helps, but his exams are NOTHING like what's in the textbook. Please. Save yourself from heartache and depression. Don't STOR 155 with him.

Mario is just straight up not a good educator. What is described as a "first year friendly" course is made completely unmanageable by a professor who has no business teaching. His lectures were confusing and his exams were completely different from lectures and homework. He is condescending and unhelpful. Take this class with a different professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: No study guides, no cheat sheets, got upset when no one was asking questions, but ridiculed students when they did ask questions. It seemed like he wanted the students to fail, perhaps so he wouldn't have to teach the course again. I spoke with people who took this course with other professors, and it was way easier and easier to understand.

Mario was extremely unclear about content, passive-aggressive, and downright discouraging. Multiple times throughout the semester, he told students that it's his job to make us suffer, we should have taken another section. The exams were multiple choice, however, Mario wrote the questions in a way that was so confusing and unreadable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Mario is not a good teacher. He over complicates material and is not helpful at all. His exams are confusing and he had to end up curving them by an insane amount. His lectures are hard to follow and he is condescending and rude. What could be a interesting stats class is ruined by his big ego. Do not take this class with Mario.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr Mario is a poor teacher. He does not post grades, so you have no idea how you are doing. He overcomplicates material and the exams are so difficult he ends up curving them a lot. He is easily the worst teacher I have had. If Mario is the only Stats option, wait for another semester or find another professor. Do not take his class.

If I had no prior knowledge of stats (I've taken AP Stats), I probably would have failed this class. Dr. Mario clearly has a strong understanding of his field of work; however, this causes him to severely overcomplicate even the simplest topics. He goes off on side tangents and has to heavily curve exams because of how insanely confusing they are.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Day 1 he gives a disclaimer he will be a tough professor, quote "I am your enemy", "Hopefully competition eats you out, and you work at a Taco Bell". What should be a fantastic course is spoiled by a condescending professor with a large ego, who mistakes arbitrarily tough grading across the board unrelated to his rubric as fairness. Good projects

Above all else Dr. Mario comes off as condescending and rude, creating an extremely harsh and negative learning environment. He will intentionally write questions on HW and tests to trip up students, and provides little guidance on the semester-long group project but expects students to use advanced techniques learned outside of class.

The group projects were graded super subjectively, and were 28% of our grades. You can make up for a crummy group by doing well on the exams, but these also require hours studying. Don't take this class if you already have a busy semester. On a positive note, I did learn a lot about R, and I feel like his standards prepare us for internships/jobs.

Honestly the worst prof. Graded the group project harshly and subjectively. Did not seem to care for students in the slightest. Gave insanely hard midterms with obscure questions that had failing averages that he then had to balance with a 7% curve. We had to self-learn R bc his slides were just screenshots of his own code.

I'm relieved to be finished with that class. I found Professor Mario to be one of the most challenging instructors I've had during my time at UNC. I consistently struggled with his teaching style. Engaging with the course materials or attending class was difficult, and overall, the experience was quite frustrating.

Pretty terrible experience. Mario is egotistical and overly critical. Exams are difficult. Obscure questions that he wants you to miss. The end of semester curve is intended to make up for it, but depends on how good your class is and the group you get for the group project. Useless lectures, some days I only recorded his funny quotes, not material

I am convinced Mario just likes to hear himself talk. The lecture content isn't relevant for any of the assignments and is essentially just repeating what's said in the readings. You don't actually learn sports statistics or get to really apply anything he lectures about. He grades super harshly and doesn't actually prepare you for group projects.

Insanely hard grader, doesn't want students to succeed. Group project is awful, there is little to no guidance but yet he takes off a ton of points for little things like grammatical errors. Midterm averages in the 50s/60s.

Giacomazzo is an unfair/tough grader who acts like his class is students' only commitment. He offers no practice tests and doesn't prepare students for exams. Unclear, confusing lectures necessitate self-teaching of coding, and exams require handwritten code. The heavily weighted group project lacks guidance, and he harshly penalizes minor errors.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Mario is knowledgeable, but parts of the class felt uncomfortable, and navigating the course wasn't easy. He can be confusing, and he does not fully prepare students for midterms. Success requires a lot of independent studying and figuring things out on your own.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: He seems harsh at first, just wants to establish his presence and make sure that the students understand how important the class is. It really depends on what group you get assigned for the final, but you have so much time to get the stuff done so if no one is doing anything you can grind it out on your own. Curve was double digits for everyone.

Lectures are horrible and ineffective. Often rambled on and on about huge chunks of convoluted code. His slides have basically nothing on them to study off of. Both midterms had failing averages. Final project took an insane amount of time to complete. Gave him a 2 because he can be funny in an awkward way, and did try his best to answer questions.

Do not get fooled this is by far the worst professor I've had at UNC. He's funny, but he does not care about you whatsoever, and not a single student out of 150 received an A or A- on any test this semester. Tests are impossible.

This class was frustrating. The professor talks at 2x speed and doesn't record lectures. It was hard to follow or review. His slides are confusing and filled with unnecessary Mario images instead of helpful content. Office hours weren't useful. I left more confused than when I came.
Being in his Stor 320 class feels like you're in a class meant for high school freshmen, and no, not in terms of difficulty.

Very unhelpful lectures and midterms are incredibly difficult (average in the 50/60s). Lots of homework that you will mostly have to teach yourself since the lectures are so bad. He curves grades at the end. If you can take this class with someone else, do that.
Be prepared to teach yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: He can be funny but is also very condescending. He enforces a strict grading policy and late-work policy, is strict about group projects, and does not adequately prepare students for midterms.
Mario is a sassy man. He is sometimes nice but sometimes very sassy.

Taught STOR 320 for 6 years according to him, makes every class rather filled too much of materials or nothing. Over confident, ignoring the importance of basic learning, makes me felt im a idiot. Hard for beginners, but if you are already a master of R studio, take it bc this class is all about self study.

Professor Mario's class is a unique experience - lectures can be hit or miss, but the group project is the real challenge. Leverage resources like ChatGPT and unstuck AI for study prep to navigate this course smoothly.

Boring, ineffective lectures. Doesn't help that he is so adamant about his way of teaching either. Grade set up + course are both poorly designed, but it is still possible to get a good grade in this class. Personally, I had to see my TA every week and studied like crazy for the paper midterms because the group projects are crapshoot.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Most good reviews are from the time when he didn't gave midterms. After that, the class became very difficult. He is an extremely poor lecturer, writes horrible exams, one will definitely struggle if having no coding experience before. The average for our midterms was around 28/60, which says a lot. You don't want a A- for a 4 credits class.
Average midterm scores were 60 and 50. No final exam, but he is insanely harsh on the final project grading. He's not a mean person or anything, but makes his class ridiculously hard for no reason.

Dr. Mario is...one of the humans of all time. You will quickly fall into a state of not caring and occasionally perk up when Dr. Mario says something notoriously awkward. Course is an asynchronous walkthrough of basic R skills. Paper is likely challenging and you need to approach with humility, but I enjoyed my group. Boomerang level of curving.

Mario is funny/likeable but the group proj is genuinely awful. Too many people in the group, randomized grouping is hit or miss, grading is harsh (kinda valid). But if your group sucks, you're stuck doing all the work for a bad grade & others barely lose pts for not participating. Would make sense in a capstone where people actually participate.

Dr. Mario is funny, the course material isn't hard, but you have to teach yourself a lot because lecture isn't application based. This hurts for the two midterms (class averages were 65% and 55%). Group project is super hit or miss because groups are randomly assigned and the grading of the paper is harsh. Balanced it all with 10 point curve tho.

Course content is certainly interesting and I think Mario does a fair job of teaching, but I was very disappointed with how harshly he graded our heavily-weighted projects. Nothing that I ever wrote was worthy of even a C in his opinion. As a result, there were 0 As and 1 A- at the end of the semester. He did curve a lot, but this is still absurd.

Before the curve, 0 A's and 1 A-. Not sure why he doesn't just grade easier so he doesn't have to implement a 12 point curve. Quizzes were insanely hard and the projects were graded harder than any other class I have ever been a part of.
he is not a good teacher. he takes off points for no reason. his average midterm grade was a 53.

HATED this class. It has nothing to do with the difficulty either, I have taken Linear, Discrete, all the Calcs, and know what an actually tough class is like. Mario is just an incredibly rude and disrespectful person. Assigns a ridiculous amount of busy work for no reason and grades harshly. Has an ego/power trip. The group project is TERRIBLE.

Very condescending, just talks about himself and shows code he wrote. Seems kinda egotistical as he gives incredibly low grades for everything in the expectation that you know what he neglected to teach us. Just an impleasant professor to take a course with.

Terribly boring lectures consisting of pictures of code, ranting about his PHD work, and self deprecating humor. Teaches R but not data analysis so when he asks you to do anything quantatative the instructions are super unclear. On paper exams which are egregiously difficult. Semester long project graded insanely harsh. Bad group=fail. Big curve.

He teaches you how to code in R, but not how to actually analyze data. He expects you to already know lots of statistical methods and HEAVILY penalizes you for not meeting this expectation. My group lost a ton of points on the final project for minor things that we were expected to know, but never taught. If you value your GPA, dont take his class.

Both of our midterm averages were failing. He gives so much homework that is hard to complete based off of his lectures. There is a semester long project that he grades very harshly even after all the groups had to spend hours on them. One of the TAs laughed in my face when I went to office hours. Do not take this class with him.

So our midterm 1, midterm 2, and final paper class averages were all F's. May that be sign enough to stay away. Also a ton of homework, labs, and assignments. His lectures are v unhelpful and his grading on the project is insanely difficult. We dedicated SO much time just for him to give us an F because of completely out-of-pocket reasons.

Recently added midterms to his STOR 320 class, which tests our understanding on R. I personally didn't feel was necessary, especially when combined with all the homework, lab assignments, and analyses, not to mention the final project. Was also a strict grader, to the point where my group got -5% to one of our assignments for one spelling mistake.

He tries way too hard to be funny in his lectures, which takes away from his ability to actually teach the material, and his slide decks are completely useless for review or studying. He gives impossible on-paper coding exams. There is also a final project worth 30% of your grade that he grades extremely harshly/subjectively. AVOID HIS CLASS!!!

I HATED this class. The grading was so harsh and the class average was in the C's because no one could get above 50s/60s on anything. The quizzes were harsh and only a few questions in a few minutes. He didn't drop any quizzes or midterms or do any replacement. The final grade was curved because less than 10% of the class could get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
Solid Professor. Attendance was required and Stor320 just added midterms to the class which didn't make much sense for the group project premise of the class. Midterms were the hard, but not impossible if you just pay attention during lecture. Group project is tough to coordinate, but he curves good. Project is also great for internships.
'

Dr. Mario showcased his willingness to help students succeed as long as they work for it with sufficient dedication. The assignments implemented for this class were doable given that you are keeping up with the R material consistently. Only thing is that the final project, especially the final paper part, requires you to think outside of the box.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Fantastic professor. He explains the material very well. The class is group project heavy. He grades harshly but the raw cumulative grades are curved generously. If you want to learn how to utilize R in a collaborative environment, take the class. One con is that the weekly labs are really just additional homework posed as a lab.

Dr. Mario is remarkable and has humor, a genuine attitude, and kindness. I appreciate him for a myriad of reasons. He sets clear expectations from the beginning and constantly encourages questions during class. He even lets you feel comfortable reaching out to him in office hours. Point is he wants you to succeed. And he curved our final grades.

Mario is hilarious and gives great lectures. The workload of this class is high but it's good-quality work, and I learned a ton. The tests are poorly designed but curved. The project is a great experience although very difficult to coordinate. I hope Mario is aware of this.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Overall, he was a fair professor. As long as you went to lecture and did the assign reading its basically an easy B+ or higher. Overall I learned a lot of R coding and its function. If I could retake the class I would because Mario was overall a good professor!

Mario is a great guy, but his lectures can be boring. Mario does try his best to make his lectures more enjoyable through encouraging participation, but most of the information is basic if you already know a lot about sports. Highly recommend because of the 2 group projects which are heavy in analytics and can be used to show in job applications.

Graded group project harshly and graded more on his personal view of the topic than objectively. The hw + labs + analyses were a lot, but overall not rigorous. No required attendance (beside labs) was the biggest benefit.

Average professor and not a bad choice. No one really went to lecture but I did and felt like it helped. Homework and labs are easy, analysis can be hard. Final group project is a lot of work, so hope you get a good group. I definitely learned a lot and really like coding in R! I would take him again if I needed to.

This class is difficult and I highly recommend reading the textbook (which is dense and relatively boring reading), but I do not believe Dr. Mario described all the concepts thoroughly enough to receive a good grade in the class without it. The exams were difficult and his grading criteria was vague. Don't take this class unless it's necessary.

The whole class basically builds up to the final group project, but it's easy to leave each part until the last few days and spend hours the day before it's due to submit something. The homework assignments are easy for anyone who has any experience with R, but the final paper is a lot of work. He also takes off points for very minor mistakes.

I'm begging you to pay attention from the start of the semester. It can be really easy to let this class fall to the side but the content is COOL and it will be really hard to learn it all at the end. Mario will get frustrated at the end but that's because no one does anything all semester. You can enjoy and learn from this class I promise.

Mario is arrogant sometimes, but I appreciate that he also tries to lighten the mood with jokes. His style of lecture/notes is really easy to follow and it made learning the material a lot easier than it could have been. Homework every week but it's not too bad considering you have textbook help. The 2 midterms & final were pretty difficult though.

He seems funny the first week and then you realize he's bad a teaching. He takes screenshots of code and puts them on powerpoint slides... The whole class if fairly easy but there's a lot of stuff that's a waste of time and if you get a bad group good luck. It starts off easy but if you've never done modeling before, you'll struggle with that.

This class was really hard. Mario is arrogant and not the best teacher so you have to teach yourself pretty much everything. I had to work extremely hard in this class to get a good grade. However, Mario did curve everyone's final grades 7 points (as there were only 3/101 people with an A before the curve). Don't take this class unless you have to

he is so boring, i never could make myself go to class. however, it is an easy A and is basically only dependent on the final group project. he was rude and all over the place, but masks it as being the "funny guy". there is a lot of homework but it isnt a hard class so definitely recommend for stat majors and minors!
Lots of Homework  grades heavy he can't say concepts really clear, it's better to look over the textbook and learn, bad and tough person, don't take his class ever again

One of my least favorite professors during my time at UNC. Sarcastic to the point of being downright rude and condescending. Provides "constructive" feedback that is ineffective and oftentimes just another excuse for him to be rude to students. I did well in the class, the content is not bad, but I will never take a class with Dr. Mario again.

Dr. Mario is an extremely funny and knowledgeable professor. STOR 320 is an introductory class for R, and no prior knowledge is needed. There is a final group project where group members are randomly assigned and harshly graded, so make sure you start early. I also prefer more live-coding than the slides Dr. Mario used, but I still learned a lot.

On the first day he seemed really nice and funny but it later became clear how tough of a grader he is, and how perfect he expects everything to be. Unreasonable expectations from students who are working in r for the first time
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved Mario as a teacher, he was very funny. This class was just VERY hard. I recommend not taking it if you don't absolutely have to for a major. Homework took hours and tests were very hard. He did give a very generous curve and encouraged questions. I might have just been bad at it, but if you aren't good at proofs, this class is not for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Mario is a very funny, caring guy. Truthfully I did not attend class much because his lectures were not helpful with homework/exams. It is graded solely on homework and exams but he does provide a nice curve to the class final grades. If you have some knowledge of statistics he would be a fine choice but if you dont it may be difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I enjoyed Professor Mario's classes. I do feel like he could have explained some of the concepts better in his lectures, but the workload was very manageable. Some of the exam questions were a little confusing, but the exams were not that difficult overall. I also appreciated his self-deprecating humor and his encouragement of questions in class.

Really funny guy with great lectures. Fairly heavy workload that will probably be difficult for people programming for the first time, but not hard for more experienced programmers. Very transparent and fair grading process.

Mario is hilarious. Such a good guy and a good class. He is a little bit all over the place with his lectures, so it's important to stay organized yourself. Honestly, I put no effort into this class and hardly paid attention. He let us take our midterms online which helped a lot and he curved our final grade by a LOT. He's a goat.

Dr. Mario tries really hard to make class interesting, however, lectures can drag on. Make sure to stay on top of the content as it is very easy to fall behind. If you need to take this class I'd definitely recommend Dr. Mario.

Dr. Mario is very responsive to emails/questions. Though the class is self study heavy, he's very reasonable, and writes exam problems similar to his lectures/labs (if you do the work you'll be fine). Exams are a good test of applied knowledge (some tricky questions tho), grades are curved, and overall he's very nice about helping if you reach out!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Basically just a bunch of boring lectures that are confusing and hard to follow. Mario is a good guy and offers plenty of comedic relief but overall does not teach the material well. Would not recommend if you actually want to learn statistics.

Overall awesome professor. Definitely my favorite lecturer I've had at UNC so far, he keeps things entertaining while also explaining content well. All exams were online and homework wasn't more than a couple hours a week. Not an easy A, but if you go to class and put in the effort, you'll do fine.

His lectures were very boring, and hardly any of the material could be applied to exams. He provided an online option for exams, making all questions free response. He ended up grading so harshly that even correct answers got you points off. He wasn't as rude as people said, but not a great professor whatsoever.

Dr. Mario is a great professor, he posted all of his lectures so you could go back and look at them and he was receptive to point changes on exams. The class is a little exam heavy so definitely study what he says. He gave multiple chances for questions and even went over what to study question by question for the final.

Solid prof. Knows his stuff, great sense of humor, clear lecturing, and very fair exams. And contrary to other comments, he always, always encouraged questions. It's possible that he read these comments and subsequently changed his approach to student interaction (a clear sign of a good professor). He's occasionally forgetful, but easy overall.

Mario is a nice person, but the lectures and homework are not reflective of the exams. He is transparent, which is nice, but at times it felt disrespectful. Ex: We took a midterm on a Monday, and he wrote the midterm a day or two before. When there were confusing questions or students felt blindsided, he was generally combative towards concerns.

Not as fun as it sounds. The lectures are extremely boring and there is a good deal of meaningless busywork. The group projects are seemingly hand-crafted to be impossible to do as a group, so one person ends up doing it all. The grading of the projects is subjective too and totally inconsistent with the rubric. Avoid if possible.

Hes overrated, cool guy but the class is taught horribly. Quizzes are way too fast and difficult and grading criteria is not clear. He will dock you points more for grammar than any statistics. The course title is way cooler than the class don't be fooled.

Professor Mario is an amazing professor. His lectures are easy to follow and he's genuinely a really funny guy. He is a really enjoyable professor and I would recommend his classes to anyone. The course work is not too difficult and Professor Mario makes it really easy to understand even if you've never done compsci before. I would def recommend!!

I took STOR 155 with Mario in the fall of 2020 when everything shut down, and this class was one of the most challenging tasks ever. Mario, on the other hand, is an extremely kind, smart, and humorous professor I have ever seen. By finally talking to him in person, I have realized his passion. I strongly recommend any in-person classes of his!

love mario! he was kind, funny, and respectable. delivers material entertainingly and HW/ quizzes are pretty straightforward. he does projects instead of tests, which is nice in applying the material we learned. as long as you do your work and attend class, it is an easy A. even gave our final grades 3 more points just to give more students A's!

Dr. Mario is a fantastic professor for any data analytics course. He has a unique sense of humor that can come off as condescending, but he really does love all of his students. Grading is super easy for most assignments, and the worst raw grade was a B, but he still curved final grade by 3 points. Only reason to avoid him is if you are soft.

After taking a few classes with him, his humor can get kind of annoying and condescending. But still, he is better at conveying material than most profs in the STOR department. And he curves his classes like crazy. Anyone who manages to get a B or C in his 155 class probably isn't a reliable reviewer. Cool guy, good professor, easy and fun class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Not gonna lie, this was by far the hardest and worst class I have ever taken, and I have always loved math in the past. Midterms made up most of the grades, and they were incredibly difficult and all open response. Dr. Mario said we did not deserve to be at UNC if we had a B or C, and he was very degrading when answering questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: After taking an in-person class with him, his style of teaching doesn't translate to online. His jokes and tangents are not as funny via zoom. That being said he's a good lecturer. The projects are graded very harshly but he gives a clear rubric. The quizzes are pretty tough too and he doesn't give feedback on them.

if you love yourself don't take this class. exams were so hard (all free response) and lectures were just from a powerpoint he didn't even make. i low passed the class despite math being my favorite subject
Bad prof for online classes

Mario is a nice and funny person, but he gets off topic a lot. His online lectures were hard to follow, he would refuse to answer certain questions, the textbook was more helpful tbh. The final is a group project worth 30%, the group is randomly chosen. The labs for the class were a bit harder than the hw, but hard to do in 50 min.
I give him a 5 for being generous on the curve.

Dr. Mario has had high reviews in the past, however, he did a mediocre job at best throughout the duration of this semester. He constantly clowned his students about having the lowest exam scores despite switching from multiple choice to short answer midterms/exams. Very boring/powerpoint based lectures. He may have been a better prof in person.

Took this class bc of older RMP scores but seems like his teaching didn't really translate to online well. Super condescending and told us to ask questions while constantly discouraging us. The curve was significant but imo doesn't make up for the lack of teaching.

I chose his class for his ratings on RMP, however, it was a truly disappointing experience. He is not only an arrogant individual who constantly looks down on others but also a harsh critic of his students who are suffering through this COVID semester. If you were to take his class, prepare yourself for harsh criticism and condescending attitude.

Dr. Mario is a great professor and really cares about the students. Exams were difficult and worth a large portion of your grade, but were curved generously. A large portion of the class ended up with an A due to the curve. Mario sets students up for success as long as they are willing to study and work for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: It was clear teaching online definitely hindered his style of lecture, but it felt like he did not seem to care whatsoever that it also was very challenging for the students. He even adjusted his curriculum to make this virtual semester even more difficult. He was very ambiguous the whole semester making it difficult to gauge performance in class.

Covid semester is already challenging enough for the students and while many professors have tried their best to alleviate students' stress, he actually put more towards the student body. I chose his class because I saw his ratings yet his teachings and attitudes do not deserve his rating, at least not this semester.

This class is really what you make out of it. Remote learning is difficult as it is, but in my opinion Dr. Mario made it very doable. With all of the grading and curving done at the end of the semester, you have to, at the very least, give some effort and it will pay off. The exams were difficult, but not impossible: do the hw, go to lecture, study

I took STOR155 with Mario because of his reviews. I regretted this decision. He straight up told us if we weren't doing well in the class we didn't belong at UNC.
