The tests were abnormally hard (even my STOR major friend couldn't help me) but some people did well. Take this class if you enjoy condescending professors and confusing lectures/slides.

Professor Mario was highly recommended to me coming into STOR155, but this class proved to be far from what I had heard. His class was very dense with slides and lectures, and the homework was much more challenging then the problems done in class. His tests were much more challenging than both, and he was very vague on grading/curves.

All things considered, Dr. Mario is a very good professor. I learned more in this class than probably any other class I've taken at UNC. The final project accounts for a big chunk of the final grade and is largely dependent on how good the group you get is. He often made me feel stupid for asking questions, but for the most part, he is very kind.

Second class I've had with Mario, as all the other students say he's a diamond in the rough. Learned a ton from him and am hoping to take another few classes with him in the future. I'd take any class he teaches.

I took Mario for STOR320 in the spring of 2020. He was awesome! There is quite a bit of assignments (no tests/ quizzes), but they aren't too difficult if you follow along with his lectures. There is also a big project instead of a final exam, which I appreciated because it is applicable if you want to pursue data science as a career.
Tough grader but the material is not that difficult. He's a funny guy but that sometimes hinders his lectures. I found myself not getting much from them. Powerpoint and tutorials are very useful.

Dr. 305 is the absolute man! He is a legend in the STOR department. This was my second class with Mario and he exceeded expectations once again. My knowledge of excel was 0 going into this class and I left an excel wizard. Dr. Mario is a gem in the STOR department and given the opportunity everyone should take at least one of his classes.
I think sports analytics is now a 500-level class, but I enjoyed this precursor. Mario is the big dawg and he is especially creative in structuring his classes.

I love Mario- one of my favorite profs- but I do not like the way he teaches this class. He goes fast without really explaining and assumes that everyone already has a lot of coding and higher level stats experience. And the group project is just tossed at you without any guidelines, making it very confusing if you don't already know R

i admire what mario is trying to do in his data science class, but it ultimately fails to be effective. the homeworks pigeonholes you into doing data analytics the way he wants you to, which isnt necessarily the best way, but is his idiosyncratic way of doing it. the group project has the same problem: he forces you to approach it the way he wants

Funny, approachable, and clearly loves his job and puts a lot of work into the slides, tutorials, and assignments he gives the class. His class lectures aren't the most helpful, though. No tests, just assignments. The group project felt like hell, and I thought my project was hot garbage but I still walked out with an A. Thank you, king.

People will complain because Mario gives a lot of homework in his courses, but if you're trying to learn code, then having to practice is the best way anyways. He could honestly make a lecture on paint drying interesting, and if your GPA is struggling this man gives out A's for days. Take him at all costs.

People recommend Mario a lot, but it's really because he's funny and friendly, not because of his pedagogical acumen. He spends most of class cracking jokes and flipping through powerpoints TELLING us about how to do stuff, but he DOES NOT DEMONSTRATE. Very accessible, easy to talk to. I like Mario, but you need to raise your hand to understand.

Dr. Mario the best, he is my favorite professor at UNC. He cracks jokes throughout the class and it makes it a very enjoyable class. He is willing to work with his students outside of class to make sure they can succeed. In his class, his students are not just numbers, and he wants everyone to succeed. Dr. Mario is a must-have professor at UNC.

Dr. Mario is my favorite professor I have had at UNC. He is hilarious in class and it makes the class enjoyable. Had him for an 8 am and it was not hard to go to because he is such a great professor. He cares about his students and wants everyone to succeed. Dr. Mario is willing to work with you outside of class. He is a must-have at UNC.
Favorite teacher Ive ever had

Mario wants you to succeed and makes that very obvious from day one. The way his class is set up is very helpful to achieving success, unlike most of the other statistics teachers here. Mario is a goofball, and while he will most certainly teach you everything you have to know, youll enjoy yourself every step of the way. Funny and nice guy.

I would hang out with Mario outside of class if given the opportunity. While Mario is not strict on attendance, youre really missing out on a lot of fun mixed in with learning if you dont show up. Mario had the whole class roaring with laughter through out the entire class period. He makes concepts easy to understand and gives great examples

This guy was highly recommended, but taking stats with him was a big mistake. While he is a funny guy, he spends 90% of the class joking around and not teaching. In a typical class, he will teach you MAYBE 15 minutes worth of material and then just mess around. Although its easy to get a good grade, you won't learn anything. His shtick gets old.

He does NOT want to fail you and makes it clear so as long as you do what you're supposed to do (HW, study) you should get a good grade in this class. He's really funny and there to help you out! He is very generous with what he tells you about the exam before you take it, and generous after. Lectures also SUPER organized and easy to follow.

Dr. Mario is the best. Sometimes his jokes fall flat, but he is mostly hilarious and keeps class light. He also challenged me to take more initiative for learning (he says this class will help you land a job, and it really will). There are no tests or finals, only a semester long group project, which I personally enjoyed and learned a lot from.

Dr. Mario is a super cool guy, he had a real passion for stats. Attendance is not mandatory, and he post his slides online. Curves assignments generously and is a fair grader. Overall a really easy class, definitely recommend!

Mario honestly was the best. I took STOR 155 with him and I despise statistics and was terrified for this class and he really made it enjoyable. 8 am was a little rough so I didn't make it to every lecture, but when I did go he was absolutely hilarious. The exams were fair, always curved some and he graded on a 10 point. 10/10 recommend him!

Mario was a real gem, his lectures are hilarious and he actually made math fun. Don't get me wrong, this was a pretty tough course, but Mario was more than fair in grading and was extremely transparent about what he was doing and why. Take him if you need discrete math, excellent professor.

You could take discrete math with someone else and be miserable, or you could take it with Mario, where every class is a party! Okay, that's an exaggeration, but Mario is hilarious and does his best to keep the class lighthearted. His lectures are clear. He makes sure you know exactly what to study for each exam, which is a lifesaver in this class.

A true gem. I can't say enough good things about him. He is hilarious and engaging and made me look forward to coming to class. Some of the topics are hard, but he makes them as easy as he can and he states very clearly what he expects us to know for exams. I would literally take him for every class at UNC if I could.

He doesn't have enough teaching experience, if anyone really wants to learn Discrete Mathematics, please do take MATH381 instead. He is a funny guy, but he's not the one you can learn some mathematical thinking and knowledge from. He uses a 50-min lecture covering just 15-min contents. He's fine if just for the STOR major requirement.

I took STOR 155 with Dr. Mario at 8 AM. Although it was early, it was totally worth it. His lectures are so great that you can do very well in the class and understand the concepts without relying too heavily on the textbook or outside resources. He is also very caring and funny. I would say his grading is more than fair- with curves on exams.

Doctor Mario is a real beauty. By far the best professor I've had at UNC. Took him at 8am M-W-F, but I did not regret it. He is super funny during lectures and knows how to crack a joke. Exams are easy and most of the class normally gets a B or higher. There is normally homework on Web Assign after each class, but its easy. Mario is a real homie.

Best prof I've ever met at UNC! He is truly caring and amazing! I made a huge mistake and he helped me solve the problem. Easy class, clear demonstration, the homework and tests are of similar level of difficulty. Take it. It's worth waking up at 8 am.

Dr. Mario is hands down one of the best professors I've had at UNC. The class is both very entertaining and pertinent to the data science field. He is also very accessible outside of class and cares about his students. He makes his class suitable for both advanced programmers and people with little experience. I would take any class he offers!

Gabor Pataki massages your brain to think outside the box, iykyk. He cares lots about his students, and it shows during his lectures. If your bad at math this class is pretty easy, just put in some work and you will be fine. He does have an accent, but worry about his handwriting more. He's also pretty funny too, in a mathematical way.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I would definitely recommend taking this class with him. He is good at his job, and the class is not very hard. Just make sure you take notes and put in effort to study, and you will be fine. Not really sure why he has bad reviews. He can be a little blunt sometimes, but I don't think that's an actual issue or reason to not take the course.

He assigns too much homework for how little it impacts your grades. If you do not do well on one exam, you are going to have to get around 94-100% on every other midterm exam and final to end with an A in the class, and if you do bad on more than one you are basically screwed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a great professor for STOR 113. He's very respectful, teaches with intent, and constantly checks in with the class to make sure everyone understands the content. He's always happy to answer questions, explain a concept more, and is very helpful outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: not too easy not too hard. if u don't like him it's just an iq filter

Don't understand where negative reviews come from. Dr. Pataki is caring and patient, willing to put tons of time into teaching, whether in lecture or in office hour. His lectures, though can be clearer for some concepts, is well prepared and align well w hw and exams. Exams are graded harshly, but you will do well if you read questions carefully.

Cannot imagine what this person had against professor Gabor.  His passion was infectious, he held engaging lectures, and gave very fair exams. Course material was super interesting and made me understand what linear algebra is actually good for. People say that anyone getting a letter from him to grad school gets in!

He's very condescending when you ask questions and will make you feel stupid for not understanding. I would recommend going to TA office hours instead. However, exams are similar to homework, but are graded very harshly. I lost all motivation for statistics because of the professor and this course.

Go to class...don't assume you will pass this because you've taken calculus before. Just like study and find someone to do the homework with because running it through ChatGPT it'll be wrong...pretty boring lectures and I was always just waiting for the class to end but I guess it was pretty solid.
Great professor, fair exams, hardass grading.

Boring lectures. Some of the methods he teaches are outdated/have simpler alternatives. 

The content is easy, especially if you've taken 305. The homework doesn't take that long, not sure why people are complaining. The exams are VERY straightforward. You can skip class and still get a good grade, just read his notes.

Course content isn't super difficult but Gabor isn't great at explaining concepts and teaches outdated methods. He grades leniently compared to other courses/professors in the STOR department and will ask students for feedback during lecture, which is helpful. Weekly homeworks are time consuming but prepare students well for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very interactive lectures, very willing to answer questions and help. In some lectures students talked more than he did. Lots of hw, but not too difficult, and they will prepare you well for the exams and quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Somewhat scary guy. Gives pretty straightforward and easy tests but is a harsh grader. He will ding you a couple percent for the smallest mistakes but pretty easy to do well. Tests are very similar to homeworks

Professor Gabor takes  some getting used to, as he can come across as grumpy some of the time. But he explained the course material very well, and was super helpful in OH. He really wants you to learn. Exams were just like the hw, so if you study, you will do well.

The course teaches you very useful skills. Rather than teaching flashy stuff, prof. Pataki goes into the math of optimization, and uses a language to solve big problems. Simplex was kinda boring, but the many problem sessions were super interesting.

I strongly recommend avoiding this professor if possible. While the course content itself is manageable, his teaching style makes it unnecessarily difficult. He consistently comes off as condescending and dismissive toward students. Even when students ask genuine questions, his tone often feels rude or belittling.

Very straightforward professor. His notes are pretty helpful if you don't attend class. HWs are extremely long but not hard at all. The class itself is not hard, you just got to do the HWs that's it. The midterms seem hard but it's all questions that he has asked before either in HW or quizzes. Nice that he drops solutions though.
Go to office hours and ask questions in class. Professor Pataki likes to answer them and will take as much time as needed to make sure you understand even if he seems intimidating.
Professor is mind numbingly boring. Homeworks take longer than your lifetime and somehow get progressively longer each week. Class is a real grind and pretty miserable.

I've been in this guy's class for about a month now, and I have probably spent more time doing his HW than all my other classes combined, and no, I am not exaggerating. The HWs get progressively more difficult as you work through them and are insolvable with the techniques he actually teaches in class.
One of the worst professors I've ever had.
Gabor is demeaning to students who ask questions. He uses the chalkboard exclusively and grades homework harshly. Hard to follow his accent.

A genius instructor who comes across as slightly abrasive some of the time. He explained things very clearly and was always available before, during, and after OH. He really cares that students learn, though his passion is also reflected in the amount of hw he gives :)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: It's obvious that Pataki is a super smart person, but I feel like he teaches the course in only a way that he understands. He does care about his students but his grading is strict and its sometimes hard to understand what he is saying in class. He also changed our grading scale with a couple weeks left in the semester and barely uses Canvas.

Gabor is a terrible professor. He is hard to understand because of his accent and his handwriting is also hard to understand. He doesn't give leeway for mistakes on exams and homework is extremely long and grades every aspect of it. Do not take him.

The class is difficult, but if you truly put in a lot of effort, you can get an A. Weekly HW can take a while so don't wait till last minute to do it. It is also graded very heavily. If you mess up on one exam, you are kinda screwed so be sure to prepare a lot in advance. The exams are very similar to the HW, so just practice the HW. Good luck

Very rude towards students and only cares about his top students. He has a heavy accent and can be difficult to understand his accent and handwriting. There is lots of homework and takes off lots of points for mistakes, even if not clarified what to do he just expects you to know. I would not recommend him and would suggest you take Calc before him

Pataki is an OK teacher at best. He sometimes complicates things more than they should but if you put in the work you'll be fine. Go to OH to check over HW's (which take a while). I found that the TA's help way more than him. The quizzes and tests are easy but the final was harder. Go to class, go to OH, do the hw, and study and you'll be fine.

I think the people who gave him a poor score  are fresh out of high school. I am a sophomore, so better used to university courses and was never good at math, but still got an A. What you need to do well in this class is not AP calc, but algebra. He does give a lot of hw, but this course will prepare you well for the B school.

Professor Pataki gives way too much homework and it's all graded on accuracy. Homework will take you minimum 3 hours each assignment but there's only one a week. Both midterms were relatively easy and exactly like the homework. Final was a good amount harder. Lectures are difficult to follow as he's bad at explaining and often makes you feel stupid

professor Gabor goes veeeeeryyy slowly, he has to, so that everyone cam follow. So it may be boring for some. He is very open to meeting students on zoom and really cares that students learn. Exams are just like the hw, so redo all hw, and you will do well. From what I hear, this is the best option for B school calc prereq.

Gabor was a good math teacher. He simplifies things down to the max and does lots of practice problems. While he sometimes make things confusing, all quiz and test are just homework questions so not hard. One homework assignment per week so not bad. If you understand the homework you'll do good. Very strict grader. Not time consuming.
Wow, this class was a bore. He is by far the worst professor I've had at UNC yet. It's easy, but he does not understand students or how to teach them. Goodluck.

Goes at an extremely slow pace in class and simpifies things so much that it actually overcomplicates simple concepts. The HW is way harder than the stuff taught in class but the quizzes and exams only consist of the main easier concepts. TAs knit pick the crap out of HW. Honestly worth self studying bc Pataki moves at a snails pace.

Pataki explained all material very well, and he regularly asked for student feedback in each lecture. He really cares that students learn, but has a habit of answering a question with another question. He pestered us a lot abt catching up on algebra, which sometimes got annoying.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This professor is not a good teacher. This being said, I have never taken calc before and did fine in the class. There is tons of homework that is graded very harshly. As long as you understand how to do the homework you will be fine. I would definitely recommend this class over the other options for business pre reqs.

He is not a good teacher. He expects you to follow along scribbled notes that are uncomprehensible because he deosn't providew context or even explain what hes doing. Good luck learning everything he assigns throiugh the TA or online.

I think prof. Pataki means well, but when asking questions he almost makes you seem dumb for asking. Exams & quizzes are fairly easy. 1 HW assignment a week that's graded very harshly, takes 2hrs MINIMUM and could be on the previous week's lectures. Just walks in and starts writing on chalk board. Overall not a fan of his lectures/teaching style.

He is not a good teacher, he scribbles on the board and when you have questions he is super demeaning. Many students just went to the TA to learn everything. the homeworks were super hard and took multiple hours but the midterms and quizes were easy.
Dr. Pataki gives a lot of hw, but then makes the exams exactly like the hw. Midterms were basically 3 hw questions, and midterm  scores were in the 80-90 % range. So if you study, you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Please never take him! He is insulting when I genuinely want help and essentially calls me stupid whenever I have a question. Study guides are not like exams; exams are like 3-4 questions, so you can fail if you miss one part. He has a heavy accent and gives lots of homework that are graded harshly. Does not give any extra credit. Just do not take.

In his class, you may have to teach yourself how to do some things if you space out in lecture, and it can be challenging to figure out. I found tests and midterms to be easy if you study. You do have to be very precise on homework and exams. My one qualm is that I don't know what my grade is. I estimate I'll get roughly a B.

Pataki does genuinely care about his students and always asks for feedback on tests, quizzes, and lectures. That being said, even with having calc experience, the homeworks are graded very harshly for no reason and the tests/quizzes having so few questions makes it hard to get an A
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Don't take Pataki; HWs are so tedious and long, and I still get BIG deductions on them despite my clear understanding. Lectures are so boring, and I failed the first midterm, partially due to me understudying, having taken calc, but MOSTLY his grading and lack of care for his students. Class is so much harder than it should be. Quizzes are easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the better professors in the STOR department, did tons of examples which made studying for exams easy. There is always homework, but usually not that difficult if you went to class and doing so much homework builds in studying. He has a particular style of teaching and applies the socratic method for hw help, but he wants students to learn.

Some of Gabor's jokes made me groan and some of his hw turned my brain into mush. But I learned an awful lot. He is  nice and helpful  in OH but he surely makes you work for your grade. I cannot imagine what the person below me had against him, other than the  grade they got.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Gave a lot of homework, along with 2 midterms and 4 quizzes. All of them are fairly easy. Boring lectures, possible to learn from notes instead of attendance. Used AMPL software for solving LP. Class could have been way harder, so I appreciate him going easy on us.

Easy A class but the semester was miserable. Professor Gabor's lectures are extremely boring, and the homework assignments are unnecessarily long (4-5 hours each with very repetitive problems.) He does not have a grading rubric for the exams and you can get a 10%+ total grade off for copying down the wrong number. Mandatory in-person office hour

Gabor is a true gem. He is definitely one of the best professors in the STOR department. His exams are fair and makes sure you understand the material but does not try to trick you. He is very kind and will learn you name rather quickly if you come to office hour/participate in class. Wish he taught more upper level undergrad classes!

Gabor is a great lecturer with a kind and quirky personality. Exams were very fair with an 85 or better average. But you must put in the work, and review stuff regularly, since there is quite a lot of hw and some are tricky. He really cares that students learn: he sent us an email every time we did well on the exams and told us that he was happy.

Though Gabor portrays a strange but friendly persona in class, I found him to be quite abrasive in office hours. It seemed as if he grew frustrated if you didn't instantaneously understand his explanation, which were not particularly clear. His grading is very harsh. On the midterms, I felt as if it was up to his grading, not what I actually knew.

Dr. Pataki is the sexiest mind at UNC. His lecture goes into depth and is super clear and extremely organized. Many lazy students may have a hard time following his lectures as he requires a deep understanding of the materials, but if you paid some attention, all your efforts will pay off. Lenient grader and gives partial credit.

The best professor I had at UNC! Super clear lectures, kind and caring, and helpful in office hours. He constantly asked for student feedback in lectures, and clarified things if people were lost. Course material was very interesting and useful. The programming language he uses takes some getting used to.

Dr. Pataki was an excellent lecturer, he made complicated concepts look easy. He explained everything well, often stopped during lecture if anyone needed clarification. He was kind and accommodated students in need with extending deadlines. He gave a good amount of hw, but it was well designed and helpful to learn the material.

Dr Pataki does not care about how well you understand class material. He is extremely rude and when grading tests takes an abnormal amount of points away for seemingly small mistakes. Example: I got a negative number for my answer when it was supposed to be positive, I lost 2 letter grades for that mistake alone. Other students did not lose as much

While there was a lot of homework, I think the people who rate him poorly just didn't get a good grade. He's quick to fix mistakes, a good lecturer, and doesn't write super hard exams (the final was a little harder than the midterms, but the midterms had mid 80 / low 90 averages). I really liked his personality and teaching style.

If you don't have time to take care of two homework for the same class in one week, don't choose his class! He doesn't know when to stop during his lecture. So you won't be able to find out what he's talking about until you face the homework. Also, he is the kind who will have homework due on the very last day of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I have no idea what the person below me is saying. Pataki is excellent at explaining the theory and helpful in OH. The course material isn't very difficult and the homework is great for understanding the uses of the topic and studying. Pataki seems to really care about students. I would say the course is like MATH 347 part 2 but much simpler.

If possible, avoid taking one of Dr. Pataki's courses. He is kind and can be funny at times, but his class is insufferable. Even a 50-minute lecture feels like hours when he lectures on abstract material the entire time with very few examples. The entire course is extremely unorganized and tedious. No respect is given to you and your free time.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Pataki is an amazing teacher, he spends time fully explaining concepts so that everyone in the class understands the material. The way he does partial grading is also super helpful and saved my ass many times. If math isn't your strong suit, Pataki is a great professor for you!

Super nice and makes sure to ask for student feedback in lectures. The tests were pretty similar to the homework which was nice. He had to leave halfway through the semester, and the transition without him was felt amongst all of the students. Overall, an easy A!
His lectures were always clear and if it wasn't he was always open to questions. He really wants people to understand the material.
A sweet, sweet man.

Professor Pataki was very kind during the difficult Fall 2020 Semester. At the end of the day, he did just about everything he could to make his class as manageable as possible in the online format. He was very nice and kind to his students, and he seems like he genuinely cares if we do well. Didn't do as well as I would've liked, but he was great.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I haven't shown up to synchronous lectures much because honestly I've just been sad, but Professor Pataki has been such an uplifting professor this semester. His emails are so nice and caring, and from what I've heard from friends he's been really accommodating with students who are struggling. It's so nice knowing our professor cares about us

Professor Pataki is an amazing choice. He makes an effort to ensure that all students are able to keep up with the material, which means he may be slow for some but for me it's been a nice change of pace. Quite a bit of homework, but it's helpful. Grading is straightforward, as are exam questions. Very nice professor who cares about his students!

He's super sweet and wants to make sure every student can understand the material, so he goes a little slow at times. Exam questions are straight off the homework which is nice. Very solid choice for 113, this was an easy A for me and I and terrible at math

Coming from someone who did Calculus in high school, I think he makes lots of things way to complicated. Nothing against his nationality, but his accent is so heavy that lectures are really difficult and sometimes it can be a struggle for in-person communication. Confusing lectures just make the class really difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Pataki was a great professor. I did not take AP calc in high school and math is not my strongest subject. However, I did really well in this course. I recommend taking him for credit. He is caring and takes time to teach concepts from the beginning. He provides great resources and the tests are just like the study material. 10/10!!!!

This semester Professor Pataki was well liked and excellent at teaching. I was so nervous based off the reviews but they couldn't be farther from the truth. Very kind person and went slowly to make sure that everyone in the class understood before he moved on to the next topic. Tons of extra credit as well!

Dr Pataki is an AMAZING professor. I didn't want to take his class at first because of his poor reviews on here but don't let that fool you! He teaches comprehensively so that EVERYBODY understands and he just really wants you to learn and feel confident with the material. His class isn't too hard and he's very willing to help. TAKE THIS CLASS!

Pataki really takes his time to go through each concept, which can be frustrating/boring, but helpful in the long-run. If you didn't take calc in high school, then I would def recommend this class. Also, he gives a lot of extra credit at the end of the sem.

Prof. Pataki is so underrated. He's definitely a bit monotone but he is absolutely hilarious if you pay attention to what he says. As a lecturer, his class is pretty basic stuff but he leaves no one behind and makes 110% sure that everyone is clear on what he is doing. Lengthy but really easy homework, extremely easy quizzes. Very caring and nice!

Professor Pataki is a great professor. He is very clear about how to solve problems and definitely shows you step by step. As someone who has never taken a calculus class before he really makes sure to outline it for you. Quizzes are usually pretty easy and homework can be challenging. Overall great class!

I made an account just to roast this man. He has no empathy whatsoever, cannot teach, feels challenged by his students and he also sucks. Do not take this class with him. The material is not hard but he sucks.

Gabor makes you print out the notes he makes every class and then makes you take notes on his notes. His homework is graded harshly and his teaching style is extremely confusing. If you have an A the whole year and do poorly on one test, it's pretty much over for you.

I really liked Gabor and his teaching style worked for me. Even though this class is in the stats department, it is 100% calculus. While this subject can be hard, I think that as long as you do the homework and go over his notes, getting an A is doable.
Take a discrete math and/or an algorithms class before this class, then it's not so bad (still a lot of homework)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Listen to me, save yourself now and do not take this class with Gabor. Although he does seem to care about his students, he gives three midterms that are roughy 7 free response questions each with little to no partial credit. The home works are easy and the practice exams he gives are simple but neither resemble any of the questions on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Gabor can be a picky grader, and sometimes he goes so slowly he will put you to sleep. He wants to explain everything step by step. But he is basically a good professor, who is helpful in office hours, and cares that students learn. Make sure to brush up on precalc, because he takes it seriously.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: A good professor, who really cares that students actually learn. Get ready to brush up on precalc! He gives no calculator parts on every exam. He wants you to think, not just memorize formulas, which may not be to everyone's taste.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: A good teacher, but a tough grader. Went into extreme details in explaining derivative, percentages, and precalculus. He  learned everyone's name in a month, which was pretty impressive.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Gabor is the worst professor I've ever had. He is rude to students and is inept at answering questions. He is unable to explain even the simplest of concepts well and uses an arbitrary extra credit coupon system. A real jerk, make sure to do his way of calculus or you're screwed. If you haven't taken Calc before, you need an outside tutor.

Quite possibly the worst professor I have had in my life. Wastes time in class, does a poor job explaining concepts, long homeworks that are graded very harshly with little to no partial credit, and he is very cold. His tests are terrible because they are short and full of random problems that were not covered in class.  Avoid him at all costs!!!

Not a good professor at all. Exams are not tough whatsoever but if you use a different method to solve a problem without using his preferable way of solving it, he will mark your answers wrong. Does not explain things well. Very rude when you go to his office hours and he does not care whether you learn the material or not. AVOID his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Heavy accent. Bad lecturer.

Gabor didn't seem too bad at first,but things got progressively worse as the semester progressed. He wastes a lot of class time, and doesn't do a good job explaining things. Tests are 85% of your grade, so you have to do well on them. His tests are short, and he always throws in a poorly worded problem that no one knows how to do.

The material he teaches is tough, and his poor  teaching only makes it more difficult and complicated. The textbook did a far better job at helping me understand the material we were covering. He assigns lots of homework, varies widely in how tough he grades, does little to help you prepare for exams, and is a pretty cold person. Avoid if you can.

Absolute worst teacher I've had at Carolina thus far. He graded homework and tests based on if it was done using his method, not on correctness. He was also not great at answering questions or understanding what students were asking.  100% would not recommend Gabor. But if you do choose to take his class don't forget about Khan Academy. Great tool.

Gabor has a very thick accent and you can't understand a lot of what he says. Be prepared to teach yourself most, if not all, of the curriculum. He will not explain questions one-on-one in class since "you'll forget it before the exam."  He grades right questions wrong and vice versa. Avoid his class at all costs. Horrible professor.

He is quite possibly the worst teacher I have ever had. This isn't because the material isn't made clear by him as he does a very good job of explaining concepts. He is the worst teacher ever because he simply doesn't understand basic grading. He takes off points to a magnitude that is nowhere close to proportionate to the mistake one made.

Gabor is an extremely tough grader, and his tests don't have many questions so making a minor mistake on a single question is the difference between an 100 and an 80. He has a thick accent and is not very charismatic, seems very detached from the needs of his students, sometimes treating us like were idiots and sometimes like graduate students

Hands down the worst class I've taken at Carolina. My biggest complaint about Gabor is that he doesn't give partial credit on exams, which earned me a terrible grade in a class that was supposed to be a refresher. Besides that, he is kind of a jerk to students, and is pretty arrogant. He will call on you in class if he thinks you're not listening.

This class isa mix of Algebra 2  and applied Calc 1. That being said, Gabor overcomplicates the material to an extreme. He's not the fairest, and his extra credit system is super arbitrary, but he is pretty knowledgeable and makes sure that you understand why formulas are the way they are. Not a great prof, but might be best for STOR 113
Worst teacher I have ever experienced at UNC. Avoid taking a class with him at all cost. The class I am taking now was supposed to be easy, but he has made it 1000 times harder than it needs to be.

This is a "wake up, you are not in Kansas (ie highschool) anymore kind of class. You need to be prepared in precalc, and if you are not, you will get tons of help to catch up. He goes really slowly to make sure everyone keeps up, and explains things to death -- you may get bored, but you will learn. Great professor overall. Gives extra credit too.

The fact that he has an A- grade is one of the most absurd things I have ever seen. His grading is the most ridiculous things ever and I truly suggest getting out of this class before you even enroll in it.  Pataki's way or the high way. Also do not let him learn your name because he will constantly call you out in class. AVOID GABOR PATAKI!!!!!!!!

Many homework are fun but tough, the hardness of exam varies a lot among years, and the grading scales are not very clear, so be prepared!  But Prof Pataki is a good guy who is funny and kind to students most of the time. His teaching style is confusing in the beginning, but once you get used to it, the lectures turns out to be easy and clear.

Gabor is a very good professor if you are willing to put in the effort. You can earn a ton of extra credit in class by his funny coupon system. He wants you to learn, and understand math, instead of just memorizing formulas -- this was actually my first math class ever, where I really UNDERSTOOD stuff. He has some quirks, as previously noted.

Basically if you've never taken Calculus before you are finished. Even if you have taken high level statistics classes or a fair amount of high level Math courses he will make you think you know nothing about Math. Worst professor I have ever had.

This is a really easy class, especially if you've taken calculus before (highly recommended). Tests are identical to homework, so redo all of them before the test and its not bad at all. He does grade very strictly, so its good to come to class to learn how he likes things shownexplained. Plus he gives out A TON of extra credit for coming.

Incredibly arbitrary grading. If you know calculus, he will make you think you know nothing even if you aced it before. The way he makes you think makes the math unnecessarily difficult. Even if there is an easier, clearer way of doing something, it is wrong.

If you haven't taken calculus before this class, I suggest doing so as he is not the most clear professor & makes you learn everything the long way, which can be very confusing. The tests are directly from the homework, so as long as you redo them before the exams you should do fine. You don't need to attend class, & he gives out extra credit daily

His class is like being in middle school all over again. You may know how to do calculus, but if you don't show it in "patakulus" formatting then you're wrong. Answer right? Half  Credit because you didn't show your work right. Answer Wrong? Most you can expect is half credit IF you do your work right. Beware of this going in.

I took his class because it was required for my major and he was the only professor teaching it. Gabor has a lot of quirks that you'll notice right off the bat but overall he knows his subject really well and is helpful at office hours. Attendance isn't mandatory but I highly encourage it because this class waits for no man.
Very Nice person and and good at explaining concepts. HW are helpful but time consuming.

You will use the textbook for all of the homeworks. I think there were 18 HWS. He drops the lowest (one or two) homeworks. Redo ALL of the hw for the exams and you will make an A in the course. The only reason I made a B+ was bc I didn't redo the hw for the second exam (everyone butchered that one). Overall I  think he is a great teacher.

One will need a fifth of vodka to get through this class; the time spent on pre-calculus in a calculus class is beyond ridiculous. Over half the class was spent doing tedious assignments that must be completed in a very communist-like fashion; Only one way to do it down to the letter. Leaving this class makes one so mad they will see red.

Gabor is very helpful and fair-paced. He goes over every step to ensure clarity. HOWEVER, he has a very unfair extra credit "coupon system". He definitely has favorites who get all the coupons, while he ignores the others. Also, it affects final grades so the grading system is not standard at all. These coupons challenge UNC's academic integrity.
Goes very slowly which is good and bad. But all around really nice patient guy who makes sure that you understand what's going on constantly.
One word... SOVIET! But really he's a funny guy who tries his hardest to be as clear and basic as possible. The TA's who grade the homework and tests aren't so nice though.
One of the best teachers I have ever had. Explains even the toughest of concepts very well. Makes things look very easy, gives very difficult and fun HWs

This class was ok.  Gabor does take everything step by step, but the pace is really almost too slow sometimes.  He wants a lot of details with steps explained, so I felt kind of like I was in a middle school math class.  His handwriting and accent are both kind of hard to understand at first.  Overall a pretty easy class though.

Great teacher, in my opinion. Here's why: he is like a high school teacher; does everything very slowly, showing every step. So even the dumb-asses (sorry) in the class understand if they pay attention. Do the extra credit!! Also, I don't remember if a book was required for the course, but if it was, we never used it.

His accent needs some time getting used to. but he is a good teacher. he does everything in detail (step by step), so even people not good at math can  understand the problems. Do the extra credit!!! helps your grade by up to 3 percentage points. The first part of semester is hardest; 2nd part easy; 3rd part is also very easy if you've taken calc.

The first half of the semester is fine.  Second semester, Gabor starts teaching Calculus, and it is a disaster.  His teaching style is very different (confusing).  He can be funny at times, though, without even knowing it.  You just have to experience this class to know what I'm talking about.

Better read the textbook than attend his lectures, which somehow makes more sense. Even then, you're not surviving the exams because he "Hates multiple choice questions" and loves to throw curveballs on the free responses.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He had a substitute teach us for the second to last week of classes. The substitute taught me more in one day than Dr. Terlov taught me all semester.

His teaching style involves reciting the textbook very poorly and very quickly.  Sets unrealistic expectations for exams and pays no attention to where his students actually are. You are better off reading the textbook directly than attending his lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Incredibly difficult midterm 2. One of the hardest I have ever taken. He allows a cheat sheet but these exams certainly favor the math majors in terms of required intuition and problem solving experience. Be very smart about how you prepare.
Lectures are disorganized. Very hard to follow. Tests are designed to trick you. Focuses more on a complex problem set up than actual probability concepts.

Lectures are hard to follow due to the fast pace. The professor pauses for questions, but most students seem too unsure to ask, so it doesn't help much. Concepts move on before they fully sink in. Slowing down and spending more time reinforcing key ideas would make the class more effective.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: accuses everyone of using chatgpt on homework and not studying because of bad exam grades. very disorganized lectures. take with someone else

On our second midterm, he gave a question that he briefly talked about in class before our very first midterm. It was an interview question for one of his past students. His explanation after the exam was confusing. Don't take this class, take another section.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are very confusing and hard to follow. The homeworks are manageable but the second midterm was very difficult, questions written in ways we had never seen before.
Hope he doesn't teach this class in the future. Poor students.

Not the greatest teacher. Not accomodating at all. Just finished midterm 2 that had no correlation to what we learned in class. Designs questions to trick you before you even understand what concept it is testing. Would not take for this course.

Greg isn't bad but his lectures are disorganized i.e he doesn't provide notes but its bc he teaches from the textbook so j look at that. The key to being successful in this class is going to office hours. His lectures are theoretical so it is really helpful to go to office hours to get help applying concepts from lecture. Hard, but def manageable!

On the midterm I used the correct formula to get the correct answer, wrote everything out step by step and still got 11/14 points on two questions because I didnt write a sentence in english explaining it at the end. I simply didn't have time to focus on this, but he requires it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: while the homework is manageable most of the time, it doesn't really feel like the lecture material applies to it. his lectures are a bit unorganized because he often jumps in without telling us what section of the text he's working from. no example numbers from text. he does all of his notes in chalk, so write fast and never be absent.

His lectures don't really make sense as he tends to go on tangents about random things. When asked what he refers to in the textbook, he says to pay attention in class. This class is already hard as it is and other than offering office hours which don't really help imo, he doesn't do anything outside of that. Would not take :(

Even if math isn't your strength, a good grade is achievable. Greg genuinely cares and gives generous curves to balance harsh grading. Lectures can be hard to follow, but he is very accessible outside of class. Be wary of bad reviews as most people just skipped. I definitely recommend him, especially if you have prior knowledge.

Greg is a super nice professor but for an intro course the class is difficult, especially if you are not good at math. He gives past exams for you to study but he make mistakes on the answer key which makes it hard if you are already confused. Tests are a big portion of grade and are graded very strictly, he does give extra credit and curves exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Didn't show up to class once and got an A. If you know your derivative rules it is a super straight forward class, so having no required attendance was very nice.

The lecture was useless and very hard to follow. The exams and midterms are graded much more strictly than the answer key. Not to mention he even makes mistakes on the answer key. There are no helpful files or a summary for exam reviews. Textbooks are super expensive.

If you're bad at math and you have a busy course schedule dont take this class. Lectures are useless and hard to follow. Grading is very specific. He posts study guides for the exams but the tests are so much harder than what he gives us. Textbook is over $100. Final exam is 35% of your grade. Tests average in the 40's he gives a curve though.

His lectures are hard to follow & he doesn't interact well with students in class. He makes mistakes in his own work that students have to correct & is very inconsistent in grading tests. This does cause massive curves on the tests which is a redeeming factor. Attendance isn't mandatory and often it is easier to learn concepts outside of class.

Class materials/concepts were not too complex until multivariable calculus. Sometimes talks/goes through problems very fast and asks for any questions but doesn't look for any raised hands. I recommend going to his office hours as he is very approachable and wants you to succeed in his class. Very easy to get an a if you go to the lectures.

I thought Greg was going to be easier due to these comments however he does not explain anything at all. The class content isn't that difficult but he can't teach, I'd recommend using a different teacher if possible.

Greg was the helpful math teacher I've had. He cared a lot about math & his students. He explained concepts well enough and provided resources. I've never been a math person but found this class to be pretty easy & straightforward. Very decent curves on all the exams & final grades. He even drops your lowest exam score completely. 10/10 recommend.

Im just gonna start with saying im not a math guy. Ironic because i am an econ major, but regardless, i thought greg was great. He gives you the previous semester midterms as study material, and it was very similar to the test he gave me in the class. I worked really hard in this class, but it was nothing unattainable. I would recommend him 100%

Professor Grigory is nice guy, however the class is very test heavy. You have 3 midterms (one is dropped) and a final that comprise your grade. Lectures are sometimes hard to follow and I wouldn't recommend taking the class without some sort of calculus experience. Extra credit was offered at the end and he curved every test (including the final).
Test heavy course and crazy exams. Practice exam will have apples and oranges while exam will have you calculating the percentage chance of nuclear fission in south african soil. Chill guy however.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor who cares about his students. Grades consisted of a weekly HW assignment, 3 midterms (2 which were curved) and a final. He even curves final grades but not by much. This class builds off calculus concepts and there are lots of word problems involved. Don't love the subject but Prof. Terlov is awesome.

Very solid lectures, tests were pretty easy other than a few questions. Very helpful, thorough explanations. Overall pretty easy class, if you are at all mathematically inclined this is a very slight class. Test heavy grading scale.

Professor Terlov is very understanding and truly loves the subject he teaches. Exams were a little tough, but all except for one was curved. Definitely need to put some time into the material outside of the class to make sure you understand, but overall he provided us with many resources that made it easier to succeed on exams.

Great class and professor wants his students to succeed! Lots of review if you've already taken calculus in the past. If you attend class and utilize the resources (office hours, tutoring) it's very easy to attain a good grade. Highly recommend!

You spend most of the class looking at the back of his head as he is writing on the chalkboard the whole time, but it is a small enough class where you can interrupt to ask questions. He is very understanding and clearly loves math. Exams are tough though. So make sure to take time and study.

Prof. Terlov is kind and patient and it is clear that he wants students to succeed in his class. My section was held at 8am MWF and I attended maybe 10 classes total. The material is just basic calculus and the whole course builds from the basics up. All the resources are there if you need them (TA tutoring, office hours, etc).

401 is already a pretty weirdly structured course. Professor Geil makes it pretty manageable and in most of the other courses the feedback kind of seems arbitrary; hers is more concrete and very easy to implement if you read through it, grades a bit harshly but I was never upset about my grades in the course. 10/10 would recommend for 401

This class is amazing- essentially just a three hour class comprised of two guest lecturers plus commentary from Geil and Zoller. Fun, engaging, practical, and intellectual. This course is amazing and Geil is an asset to this class. If you can take this class, I cannot recommend it enough!

Super nice and caring person. Grades were't put in until after finals which made for a roller coaster of emotions. Tough grader with very vague expectations and guidelines. If possible, consider taking with another professor.

Dr. Geil is a fantastic professor due to her passion for teaching the class and her understanding of what she wants each student to learn. She wants each student to grow, is easily accessible outside of the course, and is very open to answering any questions during office hours! I definitely would recommend it to any student!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Synchronous. Super sweet woman! Like all of us, she seems like she is having a very tough semester, and halfway through the term, we didn't have any grades in. She took that into account and decided not to take points off the next assignment. We also had a group project with a client, which was overwhelming, trying to navigate with others.

I'm a STEM major, so I had to take this class. If you need an english credit as a STEM, I would certainly recommend it. It was very easy with not a ton of work. In addition I did learn some valuable business tips. She is also very funny and caring. Take this class with her!

took this class for GenEds, I'm a STEM major and I'm not comfortable with literature analysis and paper writing. That being said Geil was a super great professor for me! She kept lectures pretty interesting and the grading was pretty easy. Make sure you read when there's a reading quiz and try to read 2/3 of the stuff for tests and you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Fantastic professor. I will undoubtedly take another class with her if the opportunity presents itself. She gives great feedback, and really values simply putting forth effort in the class. If you have the option to take a class with her, do not miss out!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GROUP PROJECTS--Would take again

reviews.comment: Great professor! My favorite class that I've taken so far. Geil provides her students with instruction and assignments that teach them practical skills for life (including help with resumes, interviews, consulting, and entrepreneurship). She is very caring and understanding of other classes students may have.

Dr. Geil is one of the best professors I've had at UNC! It is evident that she loves her job and that she truly cares about her students. English 105i for Business is not bad at all! The class is interesting and relevant to the business field which makes it super fun. Show up to class and do your work on time and you should not have any trouble.

Dr. Geil is the best!! Her class is very straightforward and is group oriented. She is always available outside of class and genuine cares about her students. I would highly recommend her to anyone looking to take ENGL 105i for Business! So much fun, always entertaining, not too much work. Overall, great experience!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Dr. Geil is not only a wonderful human being, but also a fantastic teacher. She is very clear in her explanations and expectations and also a fairly easy grader. The projects in this class are engaging and super fun. 10/10 would recommend this class to anyone!

Even though she is in the English department, she utilized all her business contacts to give our class the best experience possible. She makes the class easy-going but you learn a lot. Just a 10/10 teacher who really cares about the lives of her students even outside of class. A definite must, the best teacher I've had thus far!

Dr. Geil is legit. Super easy class and a great way to fulfill my English credit. There are essentially 3 big projects and she is a very lenient grader. I actually got really good feedback on my resume and other things which were required for the class. I got a very easy A in this class and would recommend Dr. Geil to all.

I took this class for the 105i, English for the professions. I would highly recommend Prof Geil, she cares about her students, is engaging and understanding and really just wants every student to learn the information. Our assignments were extremely relevant for business majors, I used her assignments for applying to internships!

Dr. Geil is a very nice professor and her class is very relaxed.  It was all basically discussing the books we read and taking basic reading quizzes on them.  However, her grading for papers was very difficult and her grading criteria is sometimes vague.  The papers are a majority of your grade so her difficult grading makes it hard to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The class was great! Based on a few short papers and a final shark tank project, which weren't necessarily easy but she gave great feedback on them, allowing you to succeed if you try. Highly recommend for your ENGL 105 credit!

Professor Geil really takes her time to know her students which I think is something you don't find often. She's very kind and really wants you to do well. I liked her English 105i business class a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Fantastic class. Enjoyable to go every day. Tough but fair grader and has high expectations.

Awesome experience! I want to take another one of Dr. Geil's classes in the future. Great organization and love for teaching. I especially enjoyed the group project, workshop, style class. The skills we learned in the class are actually USEFUL (Resume, Negative Messages, Informative Message, etc.)
she is a professor that actually cares and is ready  to help. She also makes a business english class fun.

Dr. Geil is an excellent professor for students that are new to UNC. For writing I'm business you will have to show up and do the work but it's nothing overwhelming as business doesn't require long essays. Would recommend Dr. Geil for any course

She is a teacher that cares for her students. She knows all of our names and knows who is who by reading our work. The  English 105i class for business is a perfect introduction class for those who are looking into working on their resume, interviews, and a shark tank presentation. She gives really good feedback. I haven't gotten a 100, but all 90s
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Always engaging and made the small classes that I usually hate fun. Always available to talk before or after class and in her office hours. If you are thinking about taking 105i, TAKE BUSI 105i it is unbelievably easy. The most I wrote for an assignment was maybe two pages.

Super exciting and makes not so interesting material interesting. Really love her class and would take it again just for fun. Helpful, never patronizing (even if you ask a dumb question). Quizzes are super easy. Overall great professor and person

Professor Geil is the best! I took her for Popular Genres and it was my favorite class at UNC. She is very excited about teaching the class and willing to work with you if you need a deadline extension or something. Her quizzes are so easy and the class is actually fun. She grades on participation, so make sure to raise your hand. Highly recommend!
AMAZING professor!! she's flexible and understanding, but also sets reasonable expectations that aren't impossible to meet. She's open-minded and always willing to help a student.

I've only been at Chapel Hill for one semester, but thus far she is my FAVORITE professor by far. She makes class fun by being herself--which is corky and funny. She's a nerd and won't deny it. She's super understanding, helpful and encouraging. The biggest assignments we had were 7-8 paged paper and a group project. Fun class, fun teacher.

I took ENGL 105i - Writing in Business with Dr. Geil and it was a wonderful experience. I thought the class was very useful and I developed writing skills relevant to my future career. We also had a mock Shark Tank presentation, which was actually quite fun to work on. Learned a lot from Dr. Geil, guest presenters she brought in and my classmates.

Attendance is a must. Fair grader, very approachable and friendly. Two papers: One group based paper (5-6 pg) and Final paper (9-10 pg). Weekly quizzes-only to help boost your grade. 8-9 plays over the semester. Midterm: Snow days were a factor, so we had to write essays based on prompts. More  than likely you will take the standard midterm.

Dr. Geil was a wonderful and engaging instructor. She was willing to help with anything you needed and always took everyone in the classes' opinions into consideration. She illuminated the material in a way that seemed interesting to the whole class. (Oh, and she was occasionally hilarious.)

Take everything she teaches. She's funny and really knows her stuff. She pushed both papers back almost two weeks, and held extensive reviews for the midterm and final. Weekly quizzes are a great way to bolster your grade, and she drops the lowest one. She was always available for help with papers, and she'll even send promising sources your way.

Dr. Geil was so helpful and she was so entertaining. She kept her demeanor friendly and she was a bit quirky. She grades strictly, but fairly. The course was incredibly interesting and she was the primary reason for keeping it interesting as Shakespeare is sometimes difficult to grasp. I would absolutely recommend taking her class if you can.
This was my favorite class I have taken this semester! She is a great professor and I recommend everyone take this class.
So Free. Literally Take notes and do ur work for a guaranteed A. ZERO flexibility on missing assignments or turning in late tho, so if you do that even once you might be cooked.

She is one of the best professors I have had at UNC. Her lectures are very information heavy but it you pay attention and take notes then everything is easy for her exams. She knows how to keep people engaged and is very funny. Def recommend her for everyone!!!

Dr. Guzzo is such an amazing woman and professor. Genuinely hilarious, cares about the subject, and tests are very straightforward and easy if you go to class. If you need to take Soci 101, take it with her for sure. Hardest part of the class is remembering to do the reading responses.

Allow me the honor of telling you how AMAZING Professor Guzzo was. Funny, intriguing, and passionate, Professor Guzzo was always available and open during class. Her slideshows were easy to follow and informative, the readings were chill, and the hardest parts were the reading response papers, which you could easily forget about.

Professor Schwinke was incredibly kind! When reading her reviews I was a bit scared as I am generally a sensitive person, but she did her best to make everyone feel as comfortable as possible. There were many opportunities to collaborate with my classmates, which I feel added to the good energy. I will be taking her again for voice training 2! :)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Gwendolyn was the kindest and most supportive professor I had during my four years of college. The coursework was manageable, consisting of just three short projects (a poem, a speech, and a monologue) throughout the entire semester. All works are done in class. You'll get an A as long as you attend class.

I have no clue why Professor Schwinke has low reviews. She is an excellent teacher who provides an energetic approach to sort of "black and white" topics. This class is not difficult at all. She is a tough grader but if you follow the rubrics for the essays you have nothing to worry about!

Super kind and energetic!! This is a theatre class so PARTICIPATE. Don't be afraid to be/act silly during class -- both your grade and speaking ability will improve if you go along with it. Take this class !!!!!

Gwendolyn is divisive. Some people found her fun, others found her condescending and stressful. Be prepared for her to call on you and kind of pick on you in class. Again, some found it funny, others would get upset. It's an easy class but a strange one! This review is for 154, Performer's Awareness (wasn't available as a class code.)

Drama 140 with Schwinke was fun. Not sure why there are bad reviews on here for her. She was very nice. Pretty vague grading criteria for the speeches/monologues, but nothing too serious. This class was entertaining and the readings were actually very interesting. I recommend it.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Learned nothing

I got added late into the class but she still counted me absent even though I wasn't enrolled yet in her class. If you miss two classes your grade gets dropped by half a letter grade. Comes off as really snarky and arrogant. Some of her comments I found inappropriate and unprofessional. Avoid her at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: POLI 100 is a very introductory class and is very lecture heavy, so it can get a little boring. I did think Dr. Gebremichael did a good job trying to spice things up by incorporating current events. Attendance is mandatory and there is one midterm, one essay, 3 quizzes, and a final. Grading is very fair, and the class is really just not that hard.

Super fun guy with interesting lectures. You get 3 unexcused absences and my notes were just the slides copied down. didnt read the textbook and did fine. make sure to study for quizzes because if you bomb one you have to do really well on the midterm/final. He curves well though. Try to speak at least once every class as participation matters.

Attendance required, note taking required to do well, slides are posted tho, curved midterm and final (generous 10ish points) so that one person just did really bad, just talk in class and study, its a easy and interesting class

I really liked Professor Gebremichael's lectures and the group discussions! If you aren't comfortable speaking in front of the class, you may not score well in participation though. The material is very interesting and he often incorporated current politics into class. The exams were difficult but curved very generously (15% curve on the midterm).

Prof Gebremichael is extremely strict in attendance and participation, which altogether count as 25% of the total grades. He is also really strict in marking, not giving curves, and is not really helpful when you ask him about how to participate more in class. Would not recommend taking his course at all.

Professor Gebremichael was awesome. I had him for my African American Economics and Inequality FYS, and he had great content, excellent and funny lectures, and was an overall great professor. His grading is stricter for the final presentation and paper, but he gives you more than enough notice to complete them well in advance.

I enjoyed Prof. AG's sense of humor and how much he cared about our individual opinions in class discussions. Compared to other poli prof.'s, he is definitely more difficult. The class is graded on 3 five questions quizzes, a midterm, and the final. If you don't do well on all of the quizzes, it'll be very difficult to get your grade up. He curves!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Gebremichael is down to earth and engaging during his lectures. We had very interesting discussions and his quizzes were super easy. Don't underestimate the tests though, they are pretty hard and have a detailed written portion. The exams were based on the lectures, so I never did the reading and did just fine. Definitely take this class!

Dr. Gates-Foster is clearly very knowledgeable about Roman history and archaeology, and she seemed very nice. However, I found the lectures to be somewhat repetitive. Grading was fair, and was half determined by her and half by a TA. Turn in the work and read at least some of the required readings and you'll be fine.

class structure wasn't my favorite but project based which was nice. weekly check ins were often confusing and drew questions from more abstract concepts. simple enough but easy to fall out of A territory if you're looking for an easy gen ed.

Could probably lecture about paint drying and make it at least somewhat interesting, she grades fairly although the TA might not be as fair (50% chance the TA grades your stuff I believe), and hope you get lucky with your group members for the project worth 20% of your grade.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. Tests on the smallest details said in class even though she claims otherwise. Crap ton of reading. 2 exams and the first one is 15% even though historically students don't do well on it and she's aware of that. Weekly quizzes and weekly attendance. Barely lenient. Not your easy gen ed please skip out and save yourself

Professor Gates-Foster is a passionate lecturer, though can come across as distant at times. The class is manageable with a focus on lecture slides and attendance. unstuckstudy proved helpful for preparing for exams.

Controlled, calm and engaging lectures are brilliant. Dr. Gates-Foster does an excellent job at making this material accessible to people outside the department, but there is a lot of reading involved so it's not easy. Tests are 95% from the lectures and she does not post notes, so you have to attend and pay attention. Easily one of my top 3 profs
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: worst IDST123 prof by far. She cares way too much about making her subject of interest seem like the most challenging/important subject in the class. She talks down to students and seems to think she is generally better than everyone else in the room.
in my opinion, her lectures are the most interesting and easy to follow. The test is almost entirely based on lectures and ppt even though readings are assigned for every lecture.

The test is completely based on slideshows AND information discussed in class. She is a good lecturer but not great outside of being your teacher. Information on the tests is pretty straight forward if you came to class and did the readings. Read the text for examples you can use on the test, not for understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Borders & Boundaries is not that bad. The readings can be long, but there's not a ton of work and it's really not difficult. Jen was definitely my favorite of the three lecturers, although she also assigned the most reading. I actually really enjoyed her lectures. Archaeology wasn't something I expected to enjoy, but she made it interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I had her for B&B and out the three teachers, she was the best lecturer. However, her exam was the hardest. To do well in the class, you must attend lectures so you can get credit for the in class assignments and study for the  exams - that's it. Study guides are helpful but TA's and teachers will not help you with your grade or even respond.

Professor Gates-Foster cares a lot about her area of study. Her lectures were very entertaining even if you did not care too much about archaeology. She assigns a lot of readings but as long as you review what is on the slides and take notes during her lectures you should be okay. Would definitely take another class with her again.
not very approachable & passive aggressive. assigns lots of super long readings but you don't need them for the tests, just review the lecture stuff

Prof. Foster was an amazing lecturer. The exam was difficult with no study guide and just a "read the slides" for advice, but overall it wasn't too hard. I wasn't too interested in the material, but Prof. Foster lectured in a way that didn't make it boring. There are readings every class, but reading them isn't necessary

Lengthy readings every night, but in all honestly they're not necessary to do well on exams. Didn't read any and did very well on the exam. Her lectures cover all the material you need to know, and everything on the exam is laid out very clearly and explicitly. She's understanding and lays out expectations well. Would highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Respected

reviews.comment: Very organized and efficient compared to other triple-I instructors. Clearly very knowledgeable, slightly sassy, and expects a lot from you on a topic most students were not interested in unfortunately

Fine as a lecturer but very condescending and rude to students. Will ask students questions and then belittle them for answering, even if they answer correctly. Often walks around the lecture hall to hawk students when she isn't lecturing. Generally seen as a pretty mean and disrespectful professor. However, she is knowledgable in her field.

Professor Gates-Foster in Borders and Boundaries was an interesting lecturer, but the class overall was poor. The constant shifting in topics was confusing, and TAs determine your entire grade. The professors were unprepared for such a large class. I would not recommend this class.

If you are taking this for a gen ed, don't. She is a great professor but unless you have a background in this content it is extremely difficult and the format of exams make it very challenging to do well. I am typically an A student and this class killed me even to get a C+. Very lecture heavy and tests weigh a lot.

Dr. Gates-Foster is one of the best professors I've taken a class with so far at UNC! Her lectures are excelllent, and super fascinatingl; this is a great class to learn about Ancient Egypt in-depth, but may not be a good choice for anyone looking for an easy gen ed credit. 

You HAVE to go to her lectures; otherwise, you definitely won't do well.

I will take any class that Professor Gates-Foster offers. She is an amazing lecturer and willing to answer any questions. A majority of your grade is comprised of the three exams - you have to study but they're not impossible. Attendance is not technically mandatory but you will not pass the class if you don't go to class.

If you're interested in Classics/Archeology, Professor Gates-Foster is absolutely the first professor I would recommend: she's very knowledgeable and an incredible lecturer. If you're looking for an easy gen-ed and nothing else, I would recommend you look elsewhere.  Attendance wasn't taken, but test material is taken from lectures, not readings.

I adore Gates-Foster! She is certainly a no-nonsense professor but she is very clear about her expectations. Readings and attendance aren't mandatory per se but the test content is straight out of her lectures. She answers questions with both clarity and incite. I definitely recommend this class and this professor!

Jen is very knowledgeable about the subject matter, but I often found her inaccessible. Her lectures are packed with information, but lack the inspiration and narrative to engage my thinking. I also found her a bit intimidating as a first year, but don't worry--she's just a serious person. Lots of assigned readings, and expect pop quizzes on them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Excessive reading! The reading quizzes she assigned were unnecessarily difficult and a lot of her content was not required to know for the exam nor was it connected to the themes of the class. I had trouble staying awake during class and being motivated to read 80 or some pages each night, in addition to assigned papers and study guides.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Do not take IDST 190. She assigned a ton of reading in short time periods and the tests were extremely difficult. If you skip class, you won't pass, she made attendance difficult even if you were present in class.

Jennifer gave a ton of readings (200 pages in with 1-day b/w classes) and came up with the most confusing test questions possible. She was really hostile toward students' questions, and her lectures were clearly repetitive. I would not like to take another class with Jennifer, and if I had known this, I wouldn't have stayed in B&B.
