reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Most people are greatly exaggerating the difficulty of this class. There are a lot of readings, but the grading is comically generous. Gates-Foster is a good lecturer and generally choose interesting things to talk about. I think she would be a lot better in a different. Personally, I would give her like a 3.5/5.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: hated this class with a passion, she was my least favorite teacher, had the most vague concepts to remember, however she is an amazing lecturer, called out someone for sleeping in a 300+ person class, and called people out for coming in late
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Gates-Foster was the epitome of a "college professor" (from what I would expect), she was very professional in the way she presented herself but could come across as too stern. There was also an outlandish amount of reading (especially for a triple-I course) often 50+ pages in one night. Good professor, but difficult and not for everyone.

Gates-Foster was knowledgeable about her field but could come off as arrogant/disrespectful. IDST-190 was painful. Up to 60-page readings and 5-question 10-minute quizzes before every class, & the midterm was awful. Assuming they even keep Triple-Is around after this semester, do yourself a favor by trusting these reviews, and don't take this one.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Out of all three professors in this course, Jennifer was the most accessible and interesting. She was responsive to her email and willing to help out when there was an issue.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: People are def exaggerating how bad she is and how bad b&b is. there was definitely a lot of reading, but if u used command f to search the pdf for quizzes it was fine. she was the most engaging lecturer of the three and I liked her topic. exam wasn't too bad, but definitely specific. 100% need to put forth a good amount of effort

This class sucked but Professor Foster was probably the best lecturer of the three. Her portion of the content was also interesting. She probably assigned the most reading and had some fairly specific questions about them on midterms and reading quizzes. I would recommend a different Triple-I but this wasn't the worst experience

If you have to take a Triple-I, DO NOT DO BORDERS AND BOUNDARIES!! Not even if you like history or the Middle East, do not take it. While Gates isn't a bad lecturer, she can be quite condescending. There is a quiz before every class and you are expected to read long passages before them. AVOID THIS CLASS.

This is one of the worst gen eds you can take. If Borders and Boundaries please do not take the class. The class is lecture heavy and involves a quiz due before every class. Also, the professors half the time repeat material from previously lectures that is identical to previous lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: While a great professor, I would not recommend taking this triple-i. She often assigns long, complicated, and tangentially related readings that do not seem on the same level as the course, and while very organized and clear, her material is very boring and specific (especially for a gen ed).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE BORDERS AND BOUNDARIES. Save yourself time and energy, this gen ed is not worth it. Extremely boring and time-consuming for no reason. Professor Gates-Foster has no respect or empathy for her students and expects freshmen to treat this gen ed as if its their entire career. A LOT of reading (50-100 pages) and nit-picky quizzes 2x a week.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Worst class to take for a Gen Ed. For a 100 level class she treats it like we are in grad school or something. Many quizzes and test are crazy hard. She expects you to know every little detail about every picture, architecture, or statue. WOULD NOT TAKE unless you want a challenge.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She cares about every little detail and there are so many readings that make no sense and tests that are graded on the smallest details. Would not recommend this course (borders and boundaries). Honestly take any other IDST triple I course for gen eds.

Not worth the gen-ed!!!! This class was so hard for no reason. TONS of things covered in every lecture and she wants you to memorize all of it for the tests. Which is all written response. Have to memorize pictures too. Not worth the work. Hated the material, overall she is a nice person teaching a bad class. Avoid this class if possible!!!!!!

Prof. Gates-Foster is very no nonsense but she cares about all of her students and outlines her grading criteria very clearly. All you need to do is attend lecture and take good notes, study guides are also helpful. She cracked a few jokes that I thought were quite funny, and as a teacher its very clear she wants you to succeed.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS FOR A GE! While the lecture material may be interesting, the tests make this class very hard to do well in. 100% memorization to the smallest detail mentioned in class. A general understanding of the material is not good enough to do well. Iit will be impossible to do well without attending class. DONT TAKE IT

This was one of the most interesting courses I have taken at UNC so far. I can see how the amount of content and the difficulty of the tests (blue book, memorization) would be off-putting to someone taking the class for a gen ed, but I really enjoyed this course. Dr. Gates expects a lot out of students, but is reasonable, knowledgeable, and caring

Dr. Gates is very passionate about what she teaches and you can tell she is good at what she does. Her lectures are amazing, but the thing to know is that her exams contains a lot of material. You have to memorize a lot of information(bout 10 google doc pages very exam). With that being said she is a lenient grader and does care about our wellbeing

She's a really nice professor, but the class is very difficult. The class is basically graded by three exams: two midterms and a final. For each exam, you are expected to memorize so many details about the material. The study guides I made were about 20 pages per exam, and I struggled to memorize everything. Not worth the Gen-Ed.

For being a 100 level course there is a lot of material you need to memorize. Lectures are long and packed with a lot information you're expected to memorize. In my opinion this should not have been a 100 level course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class and her lectures. This class is definitely not an easy A. There was a lot of material we needed to know for each exam, and the final is really lengthy and covers a lot of content.

test content is lecture and overall information heavy, but the lectures she gives covers content well and aren't super dry. start studying earlier than the week of the exam and use the textbook for supplemental reading to get an A

I really liked the subject matter and found it interesting. However, this class requires a lot of reading and a lot of your grade is made up of hard midterms. You will have to study a ton for them. Professor Gates Foster is extremely knowledgeable and always willing to answer questions. Attendance is optional, but you will not pass if you don't go.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's a great professor and I loved the class, but be warned, this will not be an easy gen-ed. I took this class for my major and found it very helpful, so I was annoyed how much people who were taking it for a gen-ed complained; the tests are hard and that's most of your grade but if you show up and study, you'll get an A.

She is a very nice lady but the tests, which make up most of the grade, are so so difficult. slides have no information and even with going to every lecture and taking good notes, i still felt as though there is way too much material covered and the tests are extremely specific. Not consistent with 100 level courses and not worth for the gened.

DO NOT TAKE ANY CLASS WITH THIS PROFESSOR. She is nice but her lectures are so so so boring and her slides are not helpful at all. You basically have to memorize everything she says in class in order to do well on the tests. There is so much reading for no reason. Every question on the tests were just tiny detais she discussed for 10 seconds.

I really enjoyed this class and professor, but it takes a lot of work/studying to do well. Do not take this class if you're only interested in the GenEds or you have a heavy load! Tests are based on her lectures (don't miss them!) and there are pop quizzes on the readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She was a really thorough professor but her lecture slides were often somewhat vague and you really have to note every little thing she says about specific artifacts and sites. The class was very interesting having known nothing about ancient Egypt. I now know more than I wanted to. I had to make a 117pg doc of every artifact and note to study!
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You MUST attend lectures and pay attention during class to succeed. She is very passionate about Egypt and it is clear in her lectures as they were always interesting. The class was not easy but not impossible, it takes a lot of time but in the end, I would take this class again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Tests are based on memorization of details (of which there were many, and little of which were actually written on slides so you have to take really careful notes). The material is interesting, but it is far more work than it's worth if you aren't genuinely into ancient Egypt.

Don't (DO NOT) take this class if you are just trying to fill a gen ed. It was an excessively insane amount of material that is way too much to memorize. The class would've been more interesting if it wasn't so incredibly detailed. I cannot stress it enough that taking this class was one of my biggest mistakes ever.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Gates-Foster is extremely knowledgeable about the subject and very responsive. Most students should probably avoid taking this class simply to fulfill GenEds. Take it if you are actually interested in Egypt architecture and mythology. Otherwise, you will be unhappy by the amount of reading and study required to succeed in the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Simply do not take this class for Gen Ed. Requires hours of meticulous studying. Pop quizzes worth 25% of the grade, so you have to do constant readings. Only what she lectures on is on the test, so can't miss any lectures, PowerPoints are unhelpful. Easily more work than any other class I've taken at UNC. She tests on details rather than concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

hes literally so nice and caring and this class was so easy

There's also a final project, but that was chill.

I took this class for a gen ed credit but honestly loved this professor. The topics were interesting, and you can tell that he is passionate about what he teaches which makes for amazing lectures. He also is very understanding and the class is well organized!

Dr. Mendez's RELI 104 is very clearly structured. You'll have weekly readings and response essays. Participation matters in recitations and in lectures (in the form of lecture responses on Sakai). Weekly response essays are graded for completion. The tests were graded very fairly.

Hugo is a dramatic (good) lecturer. The course was taught w/ the premise that all students know abt Christianity to begin w/. Only a limited # of ppl can get 100 for participation, so ur at a disadvantage if u haven't been going to church for 18 yrs & ur classmates have. Did 14 2pg P/F papers but only got a grade back for 1. Never got midterm grade
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Only need to attend lectures to submit the post-lecture forum post, otherwise no need to listen in class. Homework is one two-page paper a week for recitation but theyre graded P/F so theyre so easy. Midterm/final have a study guide with everything on it. Mendez is so kind and really understanding of his students so dont be scared to reach out!

Professor Mendez is hilarious. I learned a ton from this class. Arguably one of the best professors at UNC. The TAs can make this class make or break, however, they prepare you very well for his exams. Phenomenal class, attendance to lectures is not required but is important.

This class was great. I learned a lot. There are readings which I almost never did, the weekly papers take an hour at most but usually less (2 pages is nothing), the forum posts take 2 secs and are graded for completion, there is extra credit and detailed study guides. Show up for all recit./classes and do all of the assignments and you'll get an A

Not recommended. If you are a Christian, be prepared to hear lecture after lecture attempting to disprove much of the Bible. Forums due after each lecture and a pt is deducted for each one missed.. 2-3 pg papers are due weekly; 2 pts deducted for each not completed. Unreasonable grading of midterm and final. Waste of time. TA was awesome!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Hugo was awesome, very welcoming of all sorts of religious views, and never forced his own personal beliefs on anyone. He gave great lectures and I learned a ton. Take him if you need a gen ed, you won't regret it.

Hugo was a solid Professor, and his class is a solid choice to get the PH requirement out of the way. Graded on participation in recitation, forum posts, papers (due weekly and are graded pass/fail), and a midterm and final. Lots of memorization for the two exams, but this is still an easy class to do well in.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: I will give Professor Mendez credit for making the subject material interesting. The reason I didn't like this class was because of the busy work. I found the 2 page response papers each week to be a waste of time. This is one of those classes where you learn the material to pass the test, not to actually learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: TAKE A CLASS WITH HUGO!! reli 104 was super interesting. even though it was for a gen ed, i enjoyed the class a lot! Hugo is super nice and funny at times during the lectures. there is a recitation but all of the TAs are cool. there is a 2 page, double spaced paper due every week but theyre graded pass/fail. gives exact study guides of tests.

Although the subject matter of this class isn't the most interesting, it is a solid choice for a PH credit. Mendez is really likable and funny. Short responses due every week, but they are mostly opinion based. One midterm and a final. Really easy class to manage.

Dr. Mendez is truly passionate about Religious Studies, and though he personally is Catholic, he takes an extreme amount of care in not applying actual religious beliefs to his lectures. Attendance is checked through a forum response to every lecture, but it is worth it because he reads every single one of them and responds in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: I love Dr. Mendez's passion for religious studies and the historical approach. Analyzing ancient texts can get boring or confusing, but he makes it relatable and approachable. He is always willing to listen to students and honest-to-God reads each forum post in order to make sure we understand the concept. Very funny and relatable, easy to follow.

Really great Professor. Does speak a little fast but he's very interesting. Really cares about his students and wants to make sure everyone understands. Not condescending about your religious beliefs and jokes a lot during class. Overall 10/10.

Professor Mendez is my favorite professor that I have ever had! He is the most genuine person and he cares about each and every one of his students. He's also very open-minded, contrary to other RELI professors that I have taken.

I actually learned a lot in Professor Holt's 'Writing in Law' class. She was always caring, her classes were engaging, and her grading was clear and fair. If you have any interest in the legal field, I'd take this over the regular ENGL 105.

Prof. Holt was wonderful and so caring for all her students. The class is very chill and she makes it lively with class discussions and activities. Gave us extensions on over half of the assignments without us even asking. Gave insightful and encouraging feedback on all assignments. I always looked forward to this class, can't recommend her enough!

even if your interest in law is small, take this class!! prof. holt is so kind and an easy professor. we were only graded on a few assignments and she gave us extensions on half of them. for the assignments that she did grade, she gave very insightful comments on how to improve for the next assignment. loved the environment of class and the prof!

Professor Holt is AWESOME. She makes the class so fun and is super easy. We only had two major assignments, and the work was interesting and fun. You'll have the chance to either work in groups or alone, whatever you prefer. Seriously consider taking her to fill in any of your focus capacities - she's the best!

She is one of the funniest professors, she talks about funny personal situations. She does care about her students and wants you to succeed. There are three main assignments, and the class is not difficult. If you like to talk, then this class is for you. The warm-up discussions took most of the class, which was fun.
She is the nicest professor I've ever had. She isn't a harsh grader, and even though this class was late in the evening, she made it engaging and fun. It's easy to get a good grade.

Actually the most amazing teacher, so caring and such a fun class. If you don't like talking, then don't take the class, but everyone in the class got so comfortable with each other, and it was just such a fun class, and I learned a lot. If you are into law, take this class. You get to learn so much about argumentation & just a great class overall!

Love Professor Holt! She is super sweet, and you can tell she's passionate about law. She is super available when you need to ask her questions and creates an engaging, fun classroom environment. If I could, I would 100% take her again. Enjoy her class!

Kelli is super nice and understanding. My poor grade is no fault but my own bc I submitted one of the three big projects without one of the components. Assignments: 3 projects plus in class writing- that's it. Do your work, participate, and go to class and you'll probably get an A. Fun class and she lets you out early a lot if it's a 75 min period

Super easy, and useful class. Ms. Holt is a very caring, chill, and knowledgable professor. Just put in a good amount of work and you will thrive in this class. Also just a great small class in contrast to huge lecture halls.

Dr. Holt is extremely knowledgeable about writing for the legal field and overall becoming the strongest writer you can be. The class is literally 9 assignments and the last unit is barely any work just a simple presentation. 25% of your grade is participation and you technically only get 3 absences, but she is super understanding!!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is so awesome! Tons of time to do all the work in class, not a difficult grader at all, and interesting in class discussions

I love Prof. Holt's class! She is so kind and enthusiastic about the material! Class was so chill.  Only consisted of easy free writes during class, discussions, and 3 big projects.  Prof. Holt is a very chill grader.  Great class if you want to learn about podcasting or need a chill class.
Super caring and understanding professor! She really made ENGL105i a pleasure to take.

I LOVE Prof. Holt makes class very fun, and as long as you show up and try, you will do well in this class. Many non-pre-law students were in my section, and everyone seemed to have a great time in this course.

Dr. Holt is probably the best professor you can get for English 105. She is super accommodating and understands that students have other classes and responsibilities. Additionally, her lectures are usually very interesting, and the projects are often not that hard. She is also super kind and offers really good feedback for feeders

Professor Holt is really kind and allows students to do lots of in-class work. Your grade is based on a couple small feeder assignments and 2 large projects, along with a presentation. Showing up and participating is mandatory, but she makes class interesting! Really good class, take it w her.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: really good prof, super nice and understanding. really helpful and gives good feedback. coursework isn't too difficult and you get enough time to complete it. good amount of reading which is expected given it's an English class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great class to take if you are interested in law but don't have much experience. You will learn how to read legal cases and brief them. Professor Holt is super kind and doesn't give too much work. Low stress class overall. Just go to class, participate, try your best to follow instructions on assignments, and you'll get an A.
I love Professor Holt, she's amazing. I took her class “Writing in the Law” and it was really great! She is very accessible and approachable.

Dr. Holt was astounding. So considerate and always tries to push you in the direction of your best possible writing. Where I lacked in certain aspects of writing, she encouraged me and provided resources to help make up for that, and I still was able to produce high quality writing within the class. She truly gets to know you and you feel bonded.

Professor Holt was hands down one of the best instructors I've ever had. The class was writing in law and she made the aspects of legal writing intriguing and always encouraged us to put forth our best work. If you are unsure of your work, within reason, she will always work with you. As long as you try and participate you will do well.

At times, she felt passive aggressive and did not explain assignments clearly. At other times, she had interesting assignments and helpful writing tips. Her grading took awhile, but overall it was a good course. I recommend.
Kelli is amazing when you take your ENGL 105 take it with Kelli she is amazing!

Dr. Holt promotes positive discussion and takes innovative approaches to teaching the law-related material in the class. She gives helpful feedback on writing and provides useful guidance as we progress through assignments. She also provides class time to work on assignments and ask questions.
She is SOOOOO caring! She definitely respects individual differences and she is very reachable after class. Take her ENG105i.
She's great, 100% recommend.

Great professor overall. Really cares about all of the students and all of the assignments are very manageable. When it comes to grading, she tells you exactly what she wants and if you follow her instructions and do all of the assigned work you will get an easy A. Not much homework if you use classtime to work.

Prof. Holt is very knowledgeable, caring, and chill. The workload is very light, and she is very willing to give feedback on your writing in office hours. The only 9AM class I've looked forward to going to!

ENG105 with Holt is manageable and seemingly easier than other 105 classes. There are 3 unit projects and some discussion posts, but the assignments are clear and the class is an easy 100%. She gives great feedback and is a sweet woman. Definitely recommend her for 105 - the coursework is light and she assigns interesting projects besides papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Kelli is super sweet! Very understanding and makes her class enjoyable and manageable. Recommend 384 especially if you are interested in podcasts.
Recommend

Professor Holt is incredibly sweet and gives great tips on how to improve your writing. This course was an easy A; just 3 manageable projects aside from a few small assignments. If you need any extensions, communicate it to her and she will make it work for you. The workload seems a lot lighter than the other ENGL 105 classes.

Professor Holt was AMAZING. She is one of the kindest people and her 105 assignments were not difficult at all. She gives you lots of time to complete assignments in class. She is very transparent and helpful with feedback and is more than accommodating with office hours, responding to emails, or in-class feedback. Highly recommend!!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Holt is nice. The bulk of your points will be from projects which should be an automatic 100 as long as you follow the instructions. 25% of your grade is participation, so as long as long as you participate, you should be fine. She does pick favorites, though, and is reluctant to curve or regrade assignments.
This course must be a good start in unc and she is so nice person. You definitely will get high grade once you attend every class and try your best to do every homework.

Dr. Holt is very caring and compassionate. She genuinely cares about her students and is very approachable. She is very knowledgable on the subject matter and is very willing to go over your work with you and provide feedback before you submit it. She is a very fair grader and provides clear rubrics that are easy to understand. Would recommend.

I took Kelli's ENGL105 class over the summer and it's probably one of the easiest classes at Chapel Hill. There were only 3 very easy assignments over 5 weeks, and she gives you lots of class time to write. Kelli cares about your sucess so make sure to talk with her. Her feedback is great, and she is a very light grader. Take her class if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Holt is one of the most caring professors that I had this semester. She works hard to give good feedback on assignments and makes the class engaging through different activities and projects. The assignments never felt like a chore, and they always felt as if they were working towards the goal of literacy in legal writing. Take her class!
Arguably the best class that I took this semester. She is very caring and knows the subject at hand very well.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Holt is a great teacher, she was always super understanding and always made class interesting.

I love Kelli. She has been a great prof. Get ready for few assignments that are worth a lot each, but you get the chance to make corrections. Kelli is very approachable and accessible outside of class. I recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Kelli is a great professor, one of the best I've had. She is caring and makes the class incredibly easy and relaxing. She's passionate about law and social justice. You read a lot of Supreme Court cases and discuss them in class, sometimes you get to argue your side. Kelli lets u fix papers after grading for extra credit. overall great professor.

Such an awesome professor. This was my first English class in a couple years and she made it super enjoyable and understandable. Our assignments were focused on encouraging new ideas and drawing implications from the text which was an enjoyable style. Always made time to make sure the students were doing well and seemed to genuinely care about us.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Professor Holt was such an amazing professor! She adapted to the change to online school and recognized the difficulty it added for students. Always prioritized our health and well-being and helped in any way she could. She was always available to chat and worked her schedule around what was best for students. Great Books. She is the best!

Kelli is a great teacher that seems to be bound by the 105 curriculum. She was incredibly nice, and as long as you put in effort, you'll get an A in the class. Watch out for participation, and make sure you're not on your device. Overall, great person but office hours can be a little awkward with her.

I took english 105i writing for law with Kelli. She is a very sweet woman and good teacher. Her classes were often seminar instead of lecture based which made the class go by quickly. She is a tough grader on some assignments and lenient grader on others. There were no quizzes or tests in my class.

Professor Holt is amazing. I took her ENGL105i: Writing in Law course and she made me such a stronger writer. The MOST caring professor at UNC honestly. I totally recommend!!! Also, this course is just a really awesome class. If you interested in becoming a lawyer, this is the course for you! My favorite class of freshman year!

Kelli was fantastic. I was assigned to her ENGL105 class and loved it. She really wants you to care but also understands that you're there because you have to be. There isn't a lot of work, but the projects are pretty open ended and she's super clear about what she wants and gives a ton of class time.
reviews.rating_tags: GROUP PROJECTS--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Holt was a great professor and as long as you show up and participate you will get an A.
Professor Holt truly cares about her students and wants them to do well. If you show effort and try, chances are you will do very well in her class. Not a lot of work, but go to class.

Kelli Holt was awesome. She is such a nice teacher. She was a very fair grader and is very easy to talk to outside of class. Great ENGL 105 teacher if you are lucky enough to get her. Make sure you participate a lot in class and follow her instructions for getting a good participation grade.

Ms. Holt is a great!! If you can get her for ENGL105, do it! She is very caring and is always willing to help you with classes besides just hers. Make sure you participate. This is a big deal to her. Do not use your phone during class.
Really enjoyed this professor. She cares about her students and is always available if you need help. You need to put some work into the class for an A but it is definitely doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Kelli is such a cool teacher. She's young and really relatable. Since this is a mandatory freshman class, she goes pretty easy and understands we didn't choose to be here. She has a passion for english which makes things interesting and we only had 3 papers (never more than 3 pages, always given a month to do). 10/10 would recommend

Prof Holt was perfect for a 1st year English class. There are very few homework assignments and when there are, she usually gives time in class to finish. There are only 2 papers that you get to choose your topics for. The business unit is very helpful and the interview was very casual. I took the class from 5-6:15PM, but she made it very bearable.

Kelli was sweet and always happy even at 8am. I went to her office hours and she was very helpful, and on random Fridays she would bring donuts and juice! Definitely take her for english 105, or any other class you can take with her!

Kelli Holt is a really laid back teacher. She is willing to help with all aspects of writing. She appreciates students who are invested in the subject matter, and is even more helpful if a student shows interest.
Best professor I have had at UNC! She is so caring and willing to work with students. Tons of reading but all of it is very interesting

Professor Lithgow focuses on students' improvement. She will sit down and provide as much feedback and guidance as needed. Classes were very participation-driven and focused on students sharing and discussing their thoughts on readings. She gives extensions and is understanding of extenuating circumstances.

Dr. L is the BEST! Although her ENGL 105i class comes with a relatively heavy workload (assignments every two days), it really pushes me to work hard on my writing. As long as you put in the effort on your essays, you're guaranteed to get a great grade. Her feedback is incredibly detailed and helpful. HIGHLY RECOMMEND if you really wanna learn

Do NOT take this class if you want to get your papers back on time, she STARTED grading half of the assignments we were given a week after LDOC, so you will have no clue what your grades are going to be. Even though she seems to really care about you and your success, it is ridiculous and I will never be taking another class with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr L is an icon. I'm so glad I chose to take 105i because it forced me to work hard and think critically. Dr L was flexible with deadlines since she really just wants to make sure you are submitting your best work. I would recommend taking a course with her if you can.

This is my second Lithgow class, and honestly, I'd take one of her classes every semester if I could. She is so sweet and goes above and beyond to get you helpful feedback to help you improve. This class isn't an easy breezy ENGL 105, but you learn SO much and it prepares you to write like a college student. 110% recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Lithgow is one of the best professors at UNC. You have to put a decent bit of time and effort into her class, but she makes it worth it with her amazing teaching and clear desire for her students' success.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: she's my goat

I loved ENGL 121 with Dr. Lithgow! The class is entirely discussion-based (only one paper), so as long as you do the readings, participate, and take the class seriously, you'll do just fine. Dr. Lithgow is flexible and does her best to work with each student throughout the semester. I enjoyed class discussions and would 100% take Dr. Lithgow again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Though this class was very difficult, Dr. Lithgow made it worth it! I couldn't recommend her enough. SHe really cares about her students giving extensions with no questions asked. She is a slower grader but she gives so much commentary on how you can improve. I learned a lot in this class and am already signed up for another Lithgow class!

Dr. Lithgow is genuinely so fantastic. The class is incredibly enriching and useful, even for someone like me, a transfer student who had already done college english. Dr. Lithgow is so kind and willing to work with you on deadlines and your grade as long as you ask for help. Totally recommend!

Dr. Lithgow is without a doubt one of the best teachers I've ever had! It is clear how much she cares about her students and she goes above and beyond to meet with us one on one about papers and give specific feedback. Classwork is worthwhile with a clear end goal - 2 feeders and a final paper per unit. Highly recommend this class and Dr. L!

I'm so glad my first English class of college was with Dr. Lithgow! She may be a tough grader, but she gives A LOT of helpful feedback on ALL papers. She's very lenient on deadlines and is very open to meeting outside of class time to discuss classwork or feedback. Highly recommend taking her for ENGL105i-writing in humanities.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Absolutely love Dr. Lithgow as a person. She creates a welcoming, inclusive classroom environment and provides pages of feedback per draft/outline. She is also accessible outside of class if you want to discuss an assignment or life. However, this is the toughest ENGL 105i and has significantly more homework (most is useful, but some busy work).

Dr. Lithgow is a gem!! Her class seemed impractical if you have written academically but she still provides lots of amazing feedback that helps to improve your writing for college. Attendance is really important and there were times that it could bring your grade down. Three unit projects with lots of small "feeders" and she grades fairly!

Though Dr. Lithgow can be passive-aggressive and assigns a lot of homework, she provides excellent feedback and is more than willing to help you in any way outside of class. She is an interesting teacher, and I enjoyed her class. For English 105i, you should take her class as I have heard other English 105i professors are very difficult or boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Although I struggled at time in Dr. Lithgow's class because I was unfamiliar with research writing, she invested heavily in my success and it was clear that she cared greatly about each of her students. The assignments were often long and time consuming but I do feel that the payoff was 100% worth it

Although it can take a while to get feedback, the comments that Dr. Lithgow provides are extremely valuable. She definitely helped me become a better writer, and it is clear that she cares about her students. Dr. Lithgow definitely holds your hand through the writing process, but it never felt like she was dumbing anything down.

Such an amazing and kind professor! She gives extremely detailed and specific rubrics, so you know exactly what to do for an assignment. Expect to spend time completing work for this class, but all of her assignments have genuinely helped me after the class. She really makes an effort to get to know you and immerse you with other students. The best

If I could give her more positive accolades I would, 3 is not enough to fairly encompass her character. She is so kind and great at working with you. She works hard to have you succeed and only asks for a comparable effort from you. lessons are insightful. She cares about her job and her students- this will be one of the best classes you ever take.

Dr. Lithgow was so kind. She inspired me to finally declare an English major. One-on-one meetings were required for papers so I really got to know her- she encouraged and helped me through all of my essays. I could tell she just wanted me to succeed. The only people in her class that didn't do well were the ones that didn't care.

Dr. Lithgow is an amazing professor and I learned so much in her class! If you actually want to improve your writing skills, this is a great class to take. She is very passionate about helping students and gives great feedback. There was typically an assignment due every class, but the assignments were usually not incredibly difficult.

Dr.Lithgow is the best professor I have had and is arguably one of the best in the school. Super interesting class, with great discussions. Everybody in that room enjoyed being in the class which is a great feeling. Very accommodating and caring, and works with you on assignments and issues in the class. Fantastic teacher!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: She starts off by trying to intimidate you, but don't let it scare you away! She is extremely kind and guides you through the class. Set up the same as all ENGL105 classes. I am not even a humanities major and I thoroughly enjoyed the class. My one critique is that sometimes you have to change your ideas to match her image of what your topic is.

Def one of the greatest prof I've met at UNC! She is very caring and gives great feedback on every single assignment. Her course is organized in a way that you will learn how to write by taking "baby steps". So though my native language is not English, I can handle the assignments pretty well!

Professor Lithgow is the best! She gives great feedback and her class is very interesting. Classes are discussion-based, and she assigns a good deal of reading but it was all very worthwhile and intriguing. Participation is key if you try, you will pass with an A or B for sure.

Taking ENGL 127 with Dr. Lithgow was simply delightful! I literally cannot find anything negative to say about her. She's very understanding and accommodating. I actually feel sad about our classes ending. The readings are quite long, though the quizzes are very manageable if you read. There are two papers due, but she gives excellent feedback!

I love Dr. Lithgow and this class! For each class you have a reading (parts of a novel or a fiction short story) and you take notes on it, then in class you take an open-note quiz and discuss the reading. The quizzes and most readings are pretty easy. You have a few essays, but they're pretty easy. Dr. Lithgow is so helpful, and the class is fun.

Dr. Lithgow is my favorite teacher that I have had since being at UNC. Her English classes do have a lot of reading, but the literature is engaging and I enjoy it. Discussion is a big part of the class, but she does not pressure you to talk, however participation matters! She is very compassionate and always willing to help, def recommend her!

Lithgow gets to know every single one of her students. She prioritized our mental health over due dates, and was always available to chat outside of class over projects or just about anything else. She would listen to our feedback to improve class. Truly wonderful and caring. A tough grader, but easy to succeed if you put in effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Lithgow is seriously the best. Even in an online setting she was great and definitely made me a better writer. There were multiple 1-on-1 meetings throughout the class where she gave awesome feedback; you're also able to get extensions on anything if you ask ahead of time. 12/10 would recommend to anyone unsure about which ENGL 105 to take.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I loved her!!! She was amazing and so so so caring. Clear rubrics and great feedback.

Hilary is one of the nicest professors I've had and truly cares about her students. She gives very good feedback and is very lenient with extensions. If you want a good grade, she will help you every step of the way on papers and give you feedback before you even turn it in. She makes time for one-on-one meetings outside of class, too.
Dr. Lithgow is one of the most amazing professors! She gives extensive feedback and is always available to help. She truly cares for her students and really does not want to see anyone fail.

This is absolutely the BEST class I've ever taken at UNC. Truly a world-class professor who cares whole-heartedly about your development and mental health. Treats students with the utmost respect at all times, and understands that sometimes real life interferes with college. TAKE THIS CLASS! You won't find a better professor than Dr. Lithgow.

Professor Lithgow is easy-going and very understanding. We had homework assigned for every class. Never felt like we were assigned busy work, every assignment/homework was relevant to the class projects. Not a hard class at all, doubt anyone got below a B-.

Dr. Lithgow will definitely make you a better writer, regardless of what major you're in. If you're in this class for an easy A, you're in for a rough surprise. Most assignments require thorough redrafts. It is, however, an extremely valuable class to take and I recommend it.

Dr. Lithgow and Bovens are amazing professors. Stay atop of your readings, for there are quizzes that are a reflection to your participation. There are reflection papers throughout and they grade fair (not too easily nor harshly). Instead of a final exam there is a final paper, and you have quite some time to work on it. Overall, an awesome class.

Dr. Lithgow is fantastic. She is so kind and caring and wants you to get better at writing and succeed. She's really willing to meet outside of class if you ever need help and is encouraging about participating in class. Super accommodating. Take this class if you can!

I literally love Dr. Lithgow! 105i taught me such useful information. You'll learn how to write a research and a humanities paper, and a grant proposal. AND she helps you all the way through so that you actually understand the process. She also knows that other classes actually exist and will almost always work with you to meet or extend a deadline
I loved Lithgow. She is super caring and anxious to engage with student's contributions. It's evident that she loves what she teaches. Super engaging and accessible. She really wants you to succeed.

This was one of the most difficult/rewarding things I've ever done-I definitely hated this class at times but I know I can write a good research paper now-She really wants you to get it and will meet outside class until you feel confident with your writing skills-The assignments feel redundant at times but theyre worth it for the dedicated student.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Lithgow is brilliant, kind, funny, and clearly cares about all of her students. ENGL105i Writing in the Humanities with her is one of my favorite courses this semester. She gives great feedback that I think will help me write and do research in the future and the course is very fun and interesting overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Dr L is by far one of the best profs I've ever had. She cares deeply for each of her students. and she'll literally spend hours reading your paper trying to give you the best feedback possible. Not a tough grader, just wants to see you develop and engage. Class usually feels more like a book club discussion than a lecture. Absolutely recommend.

I had Dr. Lithgow last semester for ENGL 105I. I made some of my best friends in that class, and definitely partly because of her group match-making abilities! She is very easy to talk to, and to keep in touch with! She gives a lot of work, but does not grade it harshly. You won't regret taking ENGL105I with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Fantastic. Highly recommend. This teacher wants to teach, likes to teach, and is good at teaching too.

Dr. Lithgow truly cares about her students. She wants to see you improve as a writer and gives excellent feedback. There are three required conferences with her to discuss your papers, which I found useful. You will get an A if you do the work and participate in class.
Philosophical approach to writing/communication was much appreciated in what could've been a boring, straightforward introductory English class. Engage with Dr. Lithgow! You'll have good discussions!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Dr. Lithgow is hands down the best professor I've ever had - teaches interesting material and very charismatic. Most importantly, she wants you to succeed and get an A. Make the changes that she suggests in the outside of class conferences and you will get a good grade. Her feedback on papers is incredibly helpful - specific and clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: I'm so glad I took Lithgow when I did because I'm able to write college level papers because of her. I would highly recommend her. You will most likely have homework due every class, but there is no midterm or final exam. Also, she helps you with literally everything on your papers and she is always available for office hours.

Lithgow was a phenomenal teacher. I had her for ENGL 105i and she's a huge reason for why I did so well on papers for other classes. If you try, you'll do fine. She cares immensely and is very flexible. Entertaining and open to new ideas as well.
She is a very involved teacher and wants everyone to do well. If you put in the effort you will do well.

Professor Lithgow is one of the most helpful professors I have ever had.  She gives deadlines if you need them, always offers helpsuggestionsoffice hours for any assignment, and truly cares about your education.  The class requires work, but she is extremely helpful through every step of her assignments.  Definitely recommend her.

Fabulous! Gives extensions, no questions asked, as long as you're 48 hours before the deadline. Class is discussion based. Reading is heavy (similar to ENGL 120), and she does quiz frequently, but she's a moderately easy grader on papers. Incredibly nice & supportive - couldn't recommend her enough!

Lithgow is the most helpful and caring professor I've had at UNC. Classes are totally discussion based. There are reading quizzes but they are super easy if you do any of the reading.  Also, Lithgow is an adviser in the English dept so she is super knowledgeable about the entire department!

Dr. L is a great professor. She is very thorough with paper comments and is helpful every step of the way. The research section of 105i is excellent and Dr. L did a great job with the material. Take the research ENGL105i with Dr. L if you can! Great transition class from high school to college.

I may have only been at Carolina for one semester now, but I know that Dr. L has got to be one of the best professors here. She is so energetic and really gets you excited about the class. ENGL 105 was easily my favorite class this semester,
My favorite professor i've had at Carolina so far.

Super helpful. There is a ton of reading for this class, and she'll quiz you on most of it. There is a LOT of listening to lecture, but it's not boring. Though attendance is mandatory, she's understanding of illnesses and will give extensions if you ask early enough.

Dr Lithgow is one of the msot helpful and engaging professor I met. She is pretty demanding for her students but she makes sure you become better in writing at the end of the course.the content is very engaging as well, but definitely need to put in the effort.
Lithgow is an extremely helpful professor who really attempts not to waste anyones time. Her classes are really engaging, especially for non-english majors.

It seems like she pretends to be really nice in class but it feels so, SO fake. This class feels like college thriving-level basic material but somehow worse. Made me cry when she pointed out my mistakes on an assignment that I failed and passive aggressively said "this is definitely one of the more...interesting ones I've seen..."

Robin can come across as patronizing, but many reviews feel exaggerated. Attendance is strict (only 1 absence) and she enforces rules on phones and punctuality, though you can request to switch sections up to 3 times. The work is easy, less than an hour a week, and you can do other homework if no one comes to tutoring. Overall not bad for 3 cred PF

DONT. TAKE. AT. ANY. COST. 

You will hate yourselves.

ABSOLUTELY, DO NOT TAKE. Too many readings, useless assignments, a test for a class that shouldn't have one, and a very unforgiving attendance system. If you want to be a tutor, do not take this class if you enjoy your sanity.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Worst professor ever. Don't take this class, save yourselves. I took this because I just wanted to peer tutor, the peer tutoring part of the class is great but the actual class is so gruesome and she's so condescending and just genuinely such a horrible person.

Robin will open up the class for questions but if you actually ask she seems to be irritated and gives a condescending answer. She was highly passive aggressive both during and outside of class. The lectures are just bullet points of the readings which I actually found interesting, but this was a lot of work for a pass-fail class.

I don't think I have ever described a professor as "mean" in my life... she might hurt your feelings but this shouldn't hurt your grade! Other than participation she was fair enough. Still a little more work than usual for a pass/fail but it is mostly tutoring and I found the course material pretty interesting and learned good study strategies.

Will fail you for missing more than one class. Not accommodating whatsoever. Believes her class is the most important thing in the world (sorry to say, but ts actually quite useless). Not approachable and very condescending. Would highly suggest you NOT take this class ever. Way too much work for a pass/fail credit.

Her attendance policy is unforgiving--whether you have been hospitalized or someone close to you dies, she won't care (real examples). At the same time, she treats you like you're in preschool. It's a pass/fail course but she still grades strictly(shouldn't be difficult to pass though). She must be tenured bc there's no other reason she's not fired

I try really hard to build relationships w/ professors & do well, but it feels impossible with Dr. Horton. She is incredibly condescending and comes across really fake. She is pretty unreasonable grading-wise and unwilling to work w/ students w/ uncontrollable circumstances. I don't feel respected at all. Tutoring = good/fun! Professor/class =BAD.
Dr. Horton is the most passive aggressive prof I have ever had. Loved the tutoring, it was fun, easy and a good time. The actual class she teaches is so miserable to be in.

Robin is one of the worst human beings I have ever had to take a class with. She is extremely condescending and treats her classes like they're in preschool. She took this class way too seriously and had no grace for students who had to miss class for a valid reason. The tutoring part of the class was fine, but that was it. Do not take this class!!

One of the rudest professors I've had. She constantly belittled and called out students for the smallest things. She needs to become more self-aware that this class is pass/fail and does not require all of the quizzes and assignments she assigns. This class is helpful to learn more about tutoring but I would avoid taking with Robin if possible.

She is incredibly condescending and will call out students if they even touch their phones to move them in class (absolutely no tech). For a pass/fail class, she is overly harsh and mean. You only get 1 missed class even if it is university approved. DO NOT TAKE. 100/10 do not recommend.
ROBIN IS AWFULLLLLL

I am usually able to adjust very quickly to the teaching style to any teacher, but Professor Horton was by far the worst. Her condescending nature made it very hard to ask questions without making it feel like I was being insulted, and the assignments took way longer than they should have. She also grades extremely slow.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I dont say this lightly, but Robin is the worst. I dread her class because she is so rude and condescending, even when you clearly express interest and show that you are trying your best. So condescending. Her grading criteria is questionable. You either get a 100, 85, 70, 60 or 0. No in between, so if you don't get a 100, its automatically an 85.

Extremely passive aggressive and one of the most (if not, THE most) unpleasant teacher I have had at UNC. The small number of comments claiming she was nice are people who didn't get to know her well enough to discover her extremely passive aggressive, arrogant, and unaccommodating behavior veiled under a very thin mask of pretend niceness.

The class itself is actually pretty fun and engaging, and I learned a lot about tutoring, all despite Robin's best efforts, there's a lot worse you could do for an EE credit. Ideally try to take this class in a couple years when the uni eventually wises up and kicks her to the curb.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I don't get these reviews, unless Robin has massively changed. I found her to be very friendly and helpful. The material is often obvious and boring but still a great option for EE credit!

She will force feed you asinine self-help books that don't apply to tutoring and test you on them. Since they're asinine, you don't need to read them to easily pass. You do need to show up. More than one absence and you fail. Oh, yea, there's a final and essays which she grades arbitrarily. It'll take her a month to get your grade back, too. Yike.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Horton is truly a terrible professor, and EDUC 387 is a massive waste of time. I'd recommend that you don't take it or any other class with her. She's patronizing, disrespectful, and will try to trip you up any chance she gets. Miserable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Participation matters. If you are an anxious and introverted person like me beware you may lose participant points. Made me super uncomfortable and will call you out during class. Watched us when we filled out course evals and made us email that we completed it. I felt extremely disrespected. Not worth it. Take another class if you can.

She is definitely the rudest professor I've ever had. Horton is extremely passive aggressive, to the point where I was too intimidated to ask her questions. She also takes forever to grade stuff even though she only "teaches" 2 classes and has a TA. She is completely unfit to be a teacher. She's has zero empathy and consideration for her students.

I can't imagine a worse professor. She is over the top about the material and wants to micromanage students. She even made the course evaluation mandatory and watched us do it. There is absolutely no clear grading criteria for papers. You'll just get vague comments. Not to mention one section is graded entirely by her assistant, who is much easier

Imagine experiencing a Karen at Walmart. Now imagine said person is your professor. That is the experience of each student in Peer tutoring. She is overzealous about the material, a literal control freak. I mean you can't even glance at your phone during class. She makes helping students the most painful experience possible. It's not worth it folks

Robin was extremely passive aggressive and way too obsessed with this course. It's p/f but she makes it seem like the most important class at unc. 1 hour of lecture, 2 hours of tutoring each week. She will call you out if you weren't paying attention, no phones allowed. She made me uncomfortable every day. Take a different EE credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: dont take it. so much more you have to do than is needed for p/f class. i felt that she treats students poorly. not fun.

Entirely way too much work for a P/F class where you are essentially volunteering your time to tutor other students. Every class felt like I was reading a chapter from every single self-help book available. There are better EE classes out there and I wish I dropped this one.

Not a hard class, just one long class block that can get tiring. 

Just do the work on time and you'll be fine.

There are no clear expectations for grading. It's a pass-fail class. Why is there a 15 point deduction for late assignments and no credit for quizzes? I didn't feel respected or valued and lost my passion for tutoring. I'm volunteering my time, stop treating me like a warehouse worker. Awful communicator. I felt attacked and gaslit.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: . Imagine you are in a boxing ring with Mike Tyson ( in his prime) and he bit your ear off. Imagine you are playing football, and all the sudden you get ran over by a 300lb lineman. Imagine you are at a baseball game, and when you look away, a bat hits you in the face. These are things I would rather have happen to me than take a class with Horton

Horton is by far one of the worst teachers UNC has ever had. She differentially treats her students. And while it is not explicit there is preferential treatment. Take this advice very seriously and don't register to be a tutor if she is the so-called instructor.

I just completed EDUC387 with Horton . If you asked me to swim in shark-infested waters or take another class with her, I would chose the former. If you asked me to fight a grizzly bear or take this class again, I would choose the former. These are not difficult decisions. Neither should yours be when registering.

Ms. Horton is quite possibly the worst professor I have ever had in undergrad. Do not under any circumstances take peer tutoring with her. She treats EDUC 387 very seriously. She only has a job to police the tutors and make sure they don't break university guidelines with regards to cheating. Nothing more.

Really nice person but there is way too much work for a p/f class. Readings almost every week. 5 essays throughout the semester. 6 reading quizzes that are actually pretty hard and an excessively long final. She thinks this class is way more important than it is and takes it too seriously imo. Not bad for a service learning course but not the best.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Definitely too much work for a pass fail class.
Peer tutoring is a really great class for the EE requirement. The work is very manageable and applicable. Robin and the TAs were always helpful during class and tutoring and fair when grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class is extremely unorganized. If you like clear grading, rubrics, syllabi, and structure, this is not for you. This class is not hard but you don't learn much. We have only had 2 or 3 lectures and even those are hard to follow along with. He has not shown up 3 times with no email. I strongly advise taking a different leadership course.

The waste of time and frustration of this class is not worth an easy A. Professor rambles, provides little instruction for assignments, and does not teach. It is spring break, and we have had one lecture. Two days out from submitting a 5-7 page essay, he changed the guidelines to make us have 5-7 sources.

Unfortunately, this class is extremely unorganized. Attendance is taken every class, but I learned nothing from lectures. I feel bad but, Professor is late/just does not show up multiple times and often looses track of the topic and rambles; it is hard to understand him when he talks and his rubrics and material too.

He talked very much. I loved the TA, Katie, but I feel like Dr. Hughes wasn't talking about course material. He posted the syllabus a few days late, rarely responded to emails, and took a while to get to a point he was trying to make. His rubrics didn't make any sense, and even the TA didn't know what it meant half the time.

Dr. Hughes seems like a sweet guy, but he should not be teaching a course. For a class with assigned group seating and heavily weighted attendance, we learned nothing. We had one class on hits, misses, and false alarms and one class on debiasing strategies, and learned nothing else. He would say a word and then ramble on about something irrelevant.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Truly got so bored during his lectures, he doesn't teach anything he just rambles on about his life that has nothing to do with the course work. All of the assignment are easy but being there for attendance is miserable. The final makes no sense because you don't learn anything all semester so get ready to teach yourself. nice guy bad teacher

Professor Hughes is an overall great dude. However, there isn't much teaching that goes on in the class, no quizzes, just the final and project-based work. The TA is absolutely amazing! She is caring and flexible. She would make a great professor. Make sure to attend every class because attendance is weighed HEAVILY!!!!
he is so nice. seriously the sweetest most caring man ever and i feel like i could talk to him about anything. assignments are fair and you usually have a lot of time for them

Dr. Hughes is such a nice guy and truly cares about his students. When lecturing he seems to lose his train of thought and talk about random things. If you are fine with an easy A without learning this is the class for you.

Dr. Hughes is an amazing human being. I learned a lot this semester and did enjoy the class. My only qualms were long, boring lectures and lack of specific requirements/schedules as a whole. I spent a lot of the class confused on what I should be doing.

Dr. Hughes is a great guy. He cares a lot about his students and the content he teaches. He tends to go off on tangents and the class can feel disorganized at times, but the major assignments are productive (though group work can be tedious) and the in-class discussions are generative. The class is very self-reflective but not too time-consuming.

Dr. Hughes is a really nice guy and really cares about the subject matter! the class doesnt require a ton of work but I felt like I learned a lot! Just make sure you're in a good group for the final project!! i would definitely recommend!!

Extremely easy class. Took it to fulfill a gen ed. Put in very little work all semester and pulled an A-. A 5-7 page paper (autoethnography), a group powerpoint presentation and a group video project (both of which were very easy), attendance, and a final reflection paper made out the grade. Learned a good amount about myself too. Take this class.
Dr. Hughes is awesome! He's a great mixture of an academic and a caring mentor. Taking his class taught me a lot about myself and how I interact with others.
Dr. Hughes is one of the best professors that I have ever had at Carolina. 12/10 recommend.

Dr. Hughes is very passionate about education and cultural competence. However, he is not very funny, although he thinks he is, and lectures are long. The second half of the semester was all group work and we didn't even have class for like 2 straight weeks because of this group work. Easy A but this class and Dr. Hughes will bore your brains out.
his quizzes can be rough so just pay attention and you'll do well. a really funny professor and very passionate about tax probably the most interesting class i took at the b-school

I bombed first exam, hence the grade. Not an easy class but not hard either. Great lecturer and nice guy. Daily quizes that are just common knowledge, basically his way of taking attendence. Easy HW's, exams are similar to practice exam.

Dr. Hoopes is an absolute gem of the KF department, and I was so lucky to take his class. The 407 pre-req is entirely optional, and the energy he brings to class every day is the only reason why my trip to KF was worth it. The content is super interesting, and he's always flexible to talk about anything related to the class. Would take again 100%.

Jeff is probably the most passionate professor I have had in college. While it is true that taxes may not be the most appealing subject, his lectures are great and easy to understand. He calls exams "celebrations." As long as you keep up with the content, he will make sure you succeed.

I had Jeff for BUSI 574 (Taxes & Business Strategy). If you're planning on taking this class, make sure it's something you're genuinely interested in. His teaching is fast-paced and lecture-heavy. The class average on the midterm/final was pretty low (C- to C range). Nice and funny teacher overall, but not the easiest elective.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I had Prof Hoopes for Taxes & Business Strategy. He's really funny, but the lectures were a bit boring (it's a tax class, what do you expect). He was great about answering questions, especially in office hours. I'd recommend this class because of him, but the subject itself would probably be really dull if you're not into tax or corporate finance.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Most entertaining class ever. Henry listens to his students extremely carefully, and takes careful measures so everyone is satisfied with due dates. In addition to being a great professor, he is a hilarious person. Personality is often lost in gen-ed classes, but NOT in his. He is an amazing storyteller and keeps students engaged with the content.

Henry is awesome. You will find yourself captivated by a long-winded fantastic story that initially seems completely irrelevant, but somehow at the end, every single time, he pulls the story to relate perfectly to what we are learning about in class. You will write in this class, but primarily only on topics that you are interested in.

While the daily lectures were just him going off on a tangent about his life or something he thinks is interesting, the class was generally okay, just kind of boring. Daily homework assignments and quite a bit of writing, but his feedback is good and mostly helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Veggian is an interesting guy but he loves to take up large amounts of class time with his tangents. He's an easy grader but assigns way more pointless work than other ENGL 105 classes.

Took feedback and added plenty of space between readings and films from big-name auteurs. The few texts he assigned were long but worthwhile for those interested in film adaptation theory. Two 5-page papers and weekly blog posts. Went on tangents, but always had great insight in setting up cultural and historical context.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He cares a lot about his students and makes a point to listen to them - changed homeworks or syllabus to fit what we thought was better, I've never met a professor like that. Definitely a lot of reading and movies to watch but most of them are fun. Does go on tangents and seems to get a little lost in his own head but he's funny.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I found him to be a very laid-back and thoughtful professor. Others say he is full of himself, but I think he simply likes to offer his perspective on the topics in the class. He's an interesting guy, and his discussions always held my attention. He's clearly very knowledgeable in his field, and he makes an effort to get to know his students.

Don't take his class for ENGL 105 unless you want to spend the entire semester hearing about how every other freshman in every other ENGL 105 class has loads less work than you. He goes on random political rants every class and is completely full of himself. Did not learn anything about writing except how to cite sources properly. Do not recommend.
You will learn how to write. Stuck up.

gives good feedback, is very helpful during office hours (as long as you have a VERY specific question in mind), and I feel like I learned a great deal from this class. Only downside is he makes the class atmosphere feel very tense so not a lot of people participated in in-class discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class was easy to get through. Ridiculous amount of reading though. Professor gave weird vibes. Talked about himself, tangents, etc. etc. You'll make it through, but be mind-numbingly bored and left with a weird aura that follows you around for a semester.
Dudes self centered
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: While this was my most intensive class of the semester, I feel as though I substantially developed my writing capabilities through his clear and strong feedback. The classroom environment was a bit tense, but he still cracked a few jokes and had some interesting lectures. There was a lot of writing, but it was worth it.

An ungodly amount of homework. Completely useless assignments. Henry has the aura of a pseudo-intellectual who definitely thinks he is the preeminent expert on every topic. He also loves to talk about his personal life for the entirety of the lecture. You should probably try to get a better professor to fulfill the ENGL105 requirement.

Dr. Veggian is a nice, smart guy. He clearly cares about what he's teaching. That said, he can be intimidating- he always seems like he's going to be mean, even though he isn't. His ENGL 105 class has so much writing. 3 units, 3 papers each (in my experience). He gives good feedback when he returns your papers, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Henry is a very intellectual person and perhaps one of the smartest people I have ever met. I think the topic of the class is what made his lectures boring but he tried to put as much emphasis on the historical figures as possible and how to "find the nail" (deeper analysis). He seems intimidating, but once you meet him he's a really nice guy.

Don't take this class if you don't like writing. There are a lot of papers in this class compared to other Engl105, but I really liked the topics and the assignments were buildable so u weren't doing a ton of work. He does tend to go on personal rants but he is very good at explaining what ur paper should be and how to do it. He is also a bit rude.

I took this class over a year ago, so I have had time to reflect. Henry is personally my least favorite of all of the professors I have had. I feel like much of our class was spent talking about his personal life, and we got an insane amount of work for an ENGL 105 course compared to other classes. I did well, but it could have been better taught.

This class wasn't very structured and consisted of open-ended discussions, so he went on tangents often. Grades included discussion forums due before every class, a midterm paper (many options, any topic), a speech (any topic), and a final paper (again many options, any topic). He was mostly a chill guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Veggian is a passionate man, but tends to go off on tangents. Getting used to his class structure was difficult and he does forums for homework before every class. The assignments in this class compared to other ENGL105 sections was very paper heavy and the topics were arguably boring. There is no group work besides peer reviewing.

CHOOSE ANOTHER TEACHER FOR ENGLISH 105. This class was more time consuming than necessary. You will spend most of the time trying to figure out what the assignment is. Class teaches nothing, talks about himself the entire time. Takes forever to grade and sooo hard to reach. Other 105 classes are so much easier.

Was for ENGL 147, he had forum posts before most every single class that were simple, and he had it so you could see other people's responses without posting one.  Pretty easy teacher, besides the forum posts we had a midterm essay that we got about a week to do (on any topic of your choosing), a speech (again on any topic) and a final essay.

Professor Veggian is an awful professor. I read his reviews before I took this class and everyone seemed to like him but his teaching style is terrible and he has no respect for anyone in the class. He lectures for the entire hour 15 about nothing related to the papers and calls out students during class. He is not the best and I don't recommend.

Don't take this class. Veggian hides behind a veil of self-indulgent drabble. Class time was filled with narcissistic ramblings about Veggian himself, extremely personal information about his life, or entirely unrelated anecdotes about random things that he took a fancy to. There was far too much work assigned with no time to complete it. Horrible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Terrible at communicating with everything. Doesn’t explain assignments well, hard to talk to through email, and not accommodating for any complications. The whole class had no idea what we were supposed to do half the time. Doesn't grade that hard, but still would not take him unless you want to be always trying to figure out what's going on
loved the class and loved the professor! super easygoing but lots to read, try not to fall behind, it's impossible to catch up. discussions were amazing and i felt really heard.

This professor honestly made me such a better writer. Expect at the very minimum three essays a week for homework though. If you put in the work, you're going to see results. He was understanding about everything going on during covid but not too lenient. He tends to ramble, but it's interesting. Also, he is also not very responsive to emails.

He's a bit rough around the edges and intimidating if you take the wrong approach to his class. He is there to make you better at writing and he WILL make you better at writing. Once you actually speak with him you can tell he cares and really wants his students to get As. He expects a lot from you, but he rewards hard work. Wonderful professor

Such a great professor. He does seem very intimidating in the beginning but he so approachable and really just an inspiration in general. The work he gives is a lot but not very hard and helps with your overall assignments so they are important. Very doable class and it definitely helps you become a professional and concise writer. Loved this class
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Best professor I've had at UNC!! Henry might seem intimidating at first but he is honestly the man! His lectures are fantastic and he cares about his students very much. Although this class does contain quite a lot of work, your writing will improve greatly! He will prepare you for everything at UNC! 100% recommend.
