The class consists of lectures, with a few in person multiple choice tests that most people will need to study for. There are two papers for the class that are not very research heavy and not very difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: While I really enjoyed Professor Roberts's lectures, his exams are unfair. Specifically, I would do all of the readings and feel as if I had a great grasp on the material, and then receive a 70 on the exams. You are basically graded off of two papers and 3 exams. If it wasn't for his trick questions on tests, I would be giving him 5/5 stars.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Roberts is very accomplished and intellectual in his field making him a good lecturer and easy to listen to. Readings are assigned but don't stress over them, they are there mainly for context. Grade is based on two papers and two exams so beware. Class was not stressful as long as you put forth effort. Would take again.

Professor Roberts is extremely smart and intellectual about Political Science, so lectures are not boring. Only bad thing about the class is that you are graded on only 4 things, 2 papers and 2 exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He taught with another professor for 384, so it's hard to distinguish who graded what, etc. However, his lectures were interesting considering the content. And to respond to the reviews that said he was rude, I don't think he is whatsoever. Solid professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I enjoyed this class for it being my first POLI SCI course at UNC. The lectures were long but Professor Roberts did try to gauge discussion throughout the classroom. The readings were very important and were applicable to discussions. Paper was long but attainable, final exam was a little off putting but relevant to current events and class topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Awesome professor. The content isn't difficult and he makes the class interesting with lots of open discussions. Super nice and interesting guy, try and do the readings before class so that you know certain details before class. Would highly recommend

Dr. Roberts & his class were a very enjoyable experience for my first POLI course. He is well-versed in politics, and class discussions were great. He was always willing to spend more class time to explain topics if needed. Only complaint is that readings were a bit superfluous (do them to succeed), but he's a solid professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof Roberts is an interesting guy. The lectures are of decent quality and address current events but the readings are extensive. Grading varies between TAs but the tests are very straightforward and you will be fine if you read. If you get Kevin Roach as your TA, I would recommend trying to get a different one.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Book is very long winded but you have to know parts of it for reading quizzes and the test. Sometimes the lectures were dry but overall the class was very straightforward and a solid teacher for an intro course
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: tests are somewhat confusing and challenging. but he is funny and the material is not very hard
Rude, inappropriate and very neglectful of his teaching duties. Worst professor at UNC

Very unclear expectations, very rude. He always has to be right. You have to write a 20-25 page research paper for this class without any instruction whatsoever and then he grades you like a PhD student. His humor is raunchy and he is extremely dismissive. Don't take his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I learned more from my recitation than I did from the lecture. The readings weren't very difficult, but the textbook was long-winded, so what could have been a 20-page chapter was usually 40+ pages. Professor Roberts made the tests himself, and I felt like they didn't go with the reading or the lectures very well. No more poli sci for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Roberts is a solid choice for an introduction class. His lectures are large discussions about politics and currents events to keep the class interesting. Attendance is essentially mandatory because he gives reading quizzes using poll everywhere, but he tells you when he's having a quiz. If you read the book, you should be fine on his exams.

Solid teacher, talks a lot about elections and current event, not just the material. Tests questions are all multiple choice but very ambiguous question wording. If you read and understand core concepts you shouldn't have trouble getting a B or an A
Class was pretty standard, but the tests were not very content based. Hypothetical, ambiguous questions leave you guessing, usually wrong.

TAKE HIM FOR POLI 100!!! He is awesome and has the best lecture, I actually look forward to going to his class. He uses poll everywhere for quizzes and always tells you when there will be a quiz. there are 2 exams which aren't bad. The TA's are great also. Would for sure recommend.

Roberts is a great Professor. Had him for POLI 100- Intro to US Gov't and Politics. My class was pretty unique since I took this class in a semester with the 2016 presidential elections. Lots of discussion and opinions. He uses a lot of polling and survey data taken in class. Hilarious guy and made the class fun.

I took 418 this semester. Dr. Reissner is very kind and loves to know her students! Her lectures are entertaining and very fascinating, and she loves answering questions. Tests were fair and were exactly what was mentioned in class, and her slides are very helpful. I would love to take another class with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took 418. She's super funny, lectures are engaging, exams are fair and not many other assignments. Her grading is good, nothing to complain, I would definitely take her again

Reissner is the sweetest person and amazing teacher. However, her tests are tricky because there is so much information and little guidance. Same goes with her papers-you never get a score back and have no idea how you did.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
She really enjoys what she's teaching! Very approachable. 
She was quite accommodating and seemed like she cared about how we were doing. 
However, she takes forever to give back grades. 
Tests were not bad. Doesn't give a rubric for papers, kinda vague.

Dr. Reissner was one of my favorite professors at UNC. You could tell how passionate she was about the content of the class and it made lectures so exciting. NSCI320 in general was such an interesting class, and she made accomodations for every student and truly cared about our well-being throughout the semester. She wants everyone to succeed!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Reissner is one of the kindest professors I've ever had at UNC, esp. with COVID. Willing to extend guidelines and work with the class if everyone agrees that something doesn't feel fair. She does grade pretty strictly for the tests, and they're really difficult if you don't take good notes. Two small papers, one longer research paper.

Dr. Reissner cares so much about the topic and that everyone is stress-free while learning it. A super interesting first-year seminar that everyone can relate to while Dr. Reissner being super nice about grading. She cares a ton and is always available. 3 papers graded nicely and a few fairly easy quizzes made this class super enjoyable

Professor Reissner is wonderful!! She cares deeply about her students success both in and outside of the classroom. Her lectures were very interesting. I would be excited going to her class. The quizzes and papers are not hard because she outlines the necessary information clearly. This is such an eye-opening first year seminar. I loved it!

Dr. Reissner was the best professor I ever had at UNC. Her lectures are extremely straightforward and in-depth. She's extremely efficient at preparing you for the four quizzes and four papers. She genuinely cares about her students and always puts their interests first.

Dr. Reissner is absolutely amazing! Her depth of knowledge in the subject makes her lectures very dense and informative. She is very good at explaining the material and always answers questions! Although the material is difficult, she really wants her students to do well! My favorite class ever at UNC- it inspired me to be pre-pharm! Amazing class!

Dr. Reissner's FYS was awesome. You could tell she really cared about the material and tried to get the class interested in it as well. Class was a super easy A- only homework is 3 short papers throughout semester graded basically for completion. Course material was engaging and relevant. Highly recommend taking this course.
Very hard class, practice exams are no where similar to the actual exams and you don;t feel prepared going into the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you ever become sick in his class, your grade will feel it, he gives pop quizzes every single week on random days and doesn't do make ups. Lectures are boring, and he expects you to know everything in the course.

Knows the material, can't teach. Basically a self-taught without recorded lecture or notes. Being in class isn't helpful either, since he mumbles and assumes knowledge of future material. Exams are 80% of class grade, but aren't too bad. Little to no practice available, only the homework and maybe a 10 question review without answers.

I do not think his lectures were boring. I found them very engaging, and he covered good example problems. The tests made up almost the entire grade but they were extremely fair if you study. It is crucial to do the homework and make sure you have all the material down. I liked Sawon a lot. I would really recommend him for math233.

sawon is so kind and this class was not too difficult, but the lectures were painstakingly boring and hard to follow. he was kind of all over the place and the most monotone lecturer. however, the two midterms were easy and the final was doable. just do the edfinity and read the textbook and you'll be fine. GREAT guy bad lecturer

Dr. Sawon is very nice and clearly knows a lot. HOWEVER he doesn't curve anything, doesn't drop a single thing, and exams are almost 90% of the final grade. Cannot stress enough how frustrating this class was.

Tests were all very fair and not difficult if you put in the effort to study. Unfortunately, Sawon definitely lacked enthusiasm towards class and his lectures were often hard to follow. I appreciated him going over homework problems in class. Exams make up pretty much the entirety of your grade, so be aware of that before taking it with Sawon.

Sawon seems like a very smart guy, often to his detriment, as he's not great at explaining the concepts to people who have never seen them before. Mostly teaches in proofs, followed by examples. I often understood, but it could be explained better. That being said, Sawon is a nice guy and grades his exams generously, so the class isn't too hard.

Sawon has the harshest grading policy of any 233 prof at UNC—90% of your grade is based on exams. No midterm replacement, little weight on homework or recitation. Other profs give more free points. The course itself is easy, but take someone else if you want a lighter grading policy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really appreciated his accessibility and personality, but his lectures were often somewhat difficult to follow. While the midterms were fairly easy, it left me relatively unprepared for the final. If you're okay with putting in extra hours to learn material yourself, you'll be okay; however, make sure you're extremely thorough.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Overall, a great experience! Lectures were always well documented, and the notes were uploaded afterwards onto Canvas. The midterms are also not super challenging, and I always found myself confident while taking them. I hope to take more classes from him later on!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Sawon is super chill and makes the easiest midterms. He basically writes proofs/thrms at the beginning of each unit and then goes through practice hw problems. His midterms are very simple, literally the same stuff we have done in class, some q's even easier than the hws. Hes accessible in office hrs too.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I can tell he knows a lot about math, but he doesn't seem to particularly like teaching it. Puts minimal effort into his lectures, teaches very fast. I was better off just reading the textbook. But he did do homework questions in class & was semi-helpful in office hours. Midterms were really easy, but 20% each, and the final is 45%.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easy course, 4 solutions and attendance are all you need to get an A. Suggested for students in majoring in Mathematics.
Had him for three lectures when my professor was travelling to Italy. Honestly, one of the best at teaching!

Justin Sawon is one of the best professor I've had in the UNC math department. He gives daily homework with plenty of extra credit opportunities, as well as group homeworks and quizzes, that keep his classes rigorous but as low-stakes as stressful. He showed up daily for office hours and held extra review sessions. If need 521, take Sawon.
I learned all of the course material through YouTube videos. Most of the class was taught in proofs which made it much harder then it had to be.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is incredibly difficult to follow, there is little access to help outside of class and your entire grade comes from the impossible exams. The lectures are so boring and are so hard to stay focused on.

Just wasn’t really that helpful. As a new student I didn’t really know a lot of the resources that I could make use of and he wasn’t that helpful letting me know. Plus he passed a lot of work down to his TAs and sometimes they didn’t know the answer and that just gave me headache cause he wouldn’t answer my question

If you have not taken a calculus course before I'd advise you to not take your first with Dr. Sawon. The entire class was taught in proofs and I frequently had to watch youtube videos to understand what was going on. Thankfully the practice tests are very similar to the midterms.

I took Calc before and got a 5 on the AP exam, but retook it and he made me more confused. He is obviously incredibly smart, but has trouble explaining nuanced topics at a beginner level. The final had a 59 average...

I'm a freshman so it was difficult to get used to how fast-paced this class was but he is a very understanding professor. It can be difficult to grasp some of the concepts but he is a really fair grader and will give extra time if the class needs it on an assignment.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I'd say Prof. Sawon is your best choice for 231! He was very lenient with homework due dates and is very understanding. My class didn't do well on the final at all (59% average lol) and he gave us a huge curve, plus he gave us an extra credit practice final! Lectures weren't the most entertaining ofc but his Australian accent was awesome

He frequently extended homework deadlines, especially for holidays. A calculator is useful for the mylab homework, but not necessary on tests (be sure to do the homework it's worth like 30%). He provided practice tests for both midterms and the final. Tests reflected lecture content and did not require proofs as I've heard other sections do.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof Sawon is one of the nicest teachers I've ever had. Calculus is going to be hard regardless of who you take it with, but Sawon is very understanding and willing to give homework extensions if you reach out. Also, his midterms aren't made to trick you (like other professors that teach the subject) and generally mirror problems we do in class.

Dr. Sawon is a great professor for a really hard class. He has tons of office hours were he walks through how to do some HW problems, and HW is worth a lot (25%) so take advantage. The 2 midterms (20% each) are tough but fair and he gives a lot of extra credit in the HWs to boost your average if you don't do so well on the midterms.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Sawon is very nice, but his lectures focus heavily on proofs when beginning a new concept which aren't actually very useful when coming to actually operating with the concepts. Tests are very fair and super similar to study guides. Do not forget to do the homework, as it is cumulatively equal to a test grade. I did not know this...
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Would take again

reviews.comment: Honestly,  I love this man. He saved me in calculus. Whenever I needed help, he was there. His lectures are long and tend to put you to sleep, but if you can stay awake through them, you'll understand how thorough and well put together they are.

Sawon is brilliant and helpful, very clear but class moves quickly so pay attention. also, do the effing homework - annoying but worth it! class is longest ever but passable without always attending lecture. overall good professor - and an aussie! ;D

Sawon was not a difficult teacher, easy B if you pay attention in class and easy A if you have taken calculus before. (You will still need to pay attention in class). Attendance is basically optional, so it is harder to pay attention in class than it sounds.

Sawon is clear throughout lectures and always asks if anyone has questions. He does a great job at explaining concepts and taking his time. Homework is online, which is really annoying, but it is doable. The tests get progressively harder but are also doable. Dont really need the textbook, just the webassign code.

Quiet, mild-mannered, math-magician. Intelligent, but a really nice guy if you get to know him well enough. Go to class, and try to stay awake. If you have trouble with web-assign, speak up in a recitation. Sawon loves to help, often with a quiet joke a soft smirk. A mystery, worth getting to know better.

You don't have to show up to class which is nice. 2 tests are fair, one sucks for the midterms. Trust me, you don't need to understand the Web Assigns. Just do them by whatever means necessary and don't take them lightly. This curve needs to be huge though, I'm anxiously waiting to see how nice it is.

Very clear in his examples, willing to answer questions, and discuss any problems during office hours. He assigns homework based on the material covered during class, and every now and then will throw a curveball. He uses webassign, which isn't the most user-friendly website, but the problems are relevant to the test. He has an Australian accent.
Sawon is very clear in his examples, and will answer any questions.  Also, he is very helpful in office hours.  He also has a British accent.

This class is pretty silly and I don't think it should be required, but since you do have to take it, you should take it with Prof Smith. She graded quickly and fairly and she was always kind in class.

Prof Smith is a lovely person, and it's clear she genuinely cares about her students and wants them to do well. Class is very easy for the most part, and there are only six in-person meetings and you are allowed to skip up to two of them.

Great, easy-going professor. The Data Lit Lab is asynchronous and you can even skip up to 2 of the in-person classes if you do the module make-up work afterwards. Pretty simple assignments and she's a super lenient grader. As long you are aware of what's happening throughout the semester, this was a great class to take with her!

I had her for Data Literacy Lab, so it doesn't really matter but I found that she was condescending towards students (not only me) and did not have the very basic level of knowledge that is needed for teaching Data Literacy Lab.

Was rude in answering reasonable questions and unable to help with basic tech. issues when it was needed.

Profa. Smith is great. She speaks well and clearly, wants you to do well, and is willing to help you out. The material can be tough just jumping straight in but she emphasizes the important parts. Speaking and listening comprehension will be the hardest part, the rest she prepares you for very well.

Profesora Smith was nice and very helpful. She clearly wants her students to succeed but she does expect you to put in the work. There are many opportunities to bump your grade up but you still need to practice and put in the effort. This was my easiest class but the only thing that was poor was how they would prepare us for the oral quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Profe Smith is amazing! Intro to Yucatan Mayan is so interesting and an overall easy class! I'm taking this as a Spanish minor elective and she is very respectful, considerate, she is flexible, and if you put in effort you will do well. Study for maybe an hour or two a week and you're golden.
i love xka'ansaj smith. would recommend her class!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Profa Smith is the BEST!! She definitely does her best to explain spanish to students, especially in ways that our generation can actually understand. She is funny, kind, caring, always wants students to succeed, and very open to talking about what you need. SPAN102 can be hard, but really, flashcards will help a LOT. Also kind ab missing homework

Profesora Smith is very accessible outside of the classroom as well as during class. She made learning Spanish fun for her students despite the very rushed curriculum of 105. I recommend using Quizlet and Conjuguemos to study for this class. Anyways, great professor!
I LOVED Profe Smith. She made the classroom environment comfortable and fun! She is a great teacher and always open to questions, she is also very understanding! Take Span with her!!!

Class is rushed but Profe Smith makes it more manageable. Most difficult class this semester but she doesn't have control over the curriculum and does her best. There's hw before every class and 2 midterms. Make sure you study vocab/grammar weekly. There are two midterms and a final (all tests end up being 65% of grade). Great option for any class.

Profesora Smith is a great professor. She keeps the mood light and is always willing to help. Span 105 is a hard class, but she makes it a lot more enjoyable and is willing to help and answer any questions. I would definitely  recommend taking her class!

Prof. Smith created a welcoming environment in her class. Make sure to participate and study grammar and vocabulary outside of class. She provided great feedback on flipgrids and papers. The class itself is a bit infuriating but Smith doesn't have much control over the curriculum. Good option for 204.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Señorita Smith is an amazing professor. She is super sweet and super patient! I definitely would take this class again and I loved the material. The homework was not at all overwhelming and the tests were very straight forward and followed the same format every time.

Srta. Smith is an amazing Spanish teacher and this class was the best online class I have taken. You have to participate and be engaged, but if you do that then you will most likely do well. She is so nice and funny and online classes aren't boring. You do have to do a good amount of homework.

Srta Smith is fantastic. She is young and understands what it's like to be a student so she wants to make class as fun and easy as possible. The main bulk of the work is on MSL and you can do the homework assignments as many times as you want so it's easy to make a 100. There are occasional quizzes she tells you about ahead of time. Great class!

Señorita Smith is great! She is hilarious and keeps the class atmosphere really light, even when the material is tough. She is always available to meet whenever YOU can. SPAN105 has a lot of material, so if you don't have a strong Spanish background, get ready to work. It is a lecture heavy course, with daily required homework, so expect that.

Lectures were not very helpful as he would just copy examples from the textbook onto the board and expects us to know everything. Even though he was a pretty nice guy, I would NOT recommend taking him for discrete. Classes are very disorganized, and you are honestly better off self-learning. The homework's were also graded pretty harshly.
Bro it was so haed to underrstand the writing bro
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I took in Spring 2025, and I believe it was his first time teaching. He was not very confident at the front of the room, and he could be somewhat condescending at times. He was late to his own office hours and at times wouldn't show up. He grades the homework strict but drops the lowest 2, and the class was curved. I would avoid taking it with him.

Nice guy but harsh grader. He took off points easily by a few things, and homework were harshly graded. Final was not easy as agreed. It's hard to get decent grade in his class although he curved the boundary.

Nice guy, horrible teacher. Unorganized lectures, unclear expectations of students, no resources for success. HARSH grader - doesn't accept certain proofs even if they're correct in the textbook. Was late multiple times to his own office hours. DO NOT TAKE DISCRETE WITH HIM. but he is willing to work with students.

He was an okay professor for discrete, but sometimes seemed confused on what he was teaching or by simple questions students asked. A very tough grader and doesn't accept methods other than what was taught in class (even if its in the textbook/still correct). Office hours are slightly helpful for explanations.

Lectures can be a little dry sometimes, and the time would be better spent going over textbook yourself at certain points in the class. The class can be pretty hard but eventually becomes pretty easy. It was also pretty hard to do well on the homework assignments. He's a genuine guy despite that, and made sure we know how to write good proofs.

He was not super great at communicating what we NEEDED to learn during lectures and seemed to focus more on what he felt like teaching versus what would be on the overall (professor determined) final exam
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a wonderful prof, and it's a privilege to have the opportunity to take lessons with him. He's genuinely interested in his students' lives, not just within, but outside of music, too. He wants to see everyone succeed, and his teaching methods and life advice will do just that. He's the prof I hope most to stay in contact with after graduating.

He is genuinely one of the best teachers/professors I've ever had in all of my schooling career.  He consistently pushes students to be better without being rude about it.  He is very knowledgable but never talks down to his students.
His teaching methods are superior. I feel very comfortable learning from him and he is super knowledgable. Easily one of the most valuable music professors employed at the school.
Great teacher! Very clear and caring!

Too many quizzes and lab which was a sure fire way to make everyone feel burnt out. I did not enjoy this class. Fair warning. Avoid professor if possible. Lectures were disorganized and it was hard to study.
She's pretty cool and relatable. She also listens to her students and changed her methods based on student feedback.
KAKI IS THE GOAT!!!!!

She makes COMP 311 a breeze. Actually cares about her students and wants the best for them. Lectures are easy to follow, quiz heavy which makes it easy to stay consistent with studying, very accessible outside class. Genuinely loved her and the class. ENROLL WITH PROF RYAN SHE'S AWESOME TRUST ME.

Amazing prof. I thought I'd hate this class but her teaching style made it so engaging and interesting. Frequent quizzes make sure you stay up to date on material, and slides are clear and easy to study outside of class. Can't wait to take 435 with her, kaki is my goat
A bit timid but wonderful teaching. Makes some mistakes in lecture but catches them. Would 100% take again, you can tell she cares about her students and content. Highly recommend!
Really cares about her students and cares a lot to the subject. One of the best teachers I have had in the UNC CS department. She da Goat
Truly cares about her students and really wants them to succeed. I wish we as a class were a bit more quieter but she really is one of the best in the department. TAKE HER
Very nice person, class is not difficult at all, a lot of partial credit given on exams

Professor Ryan made COMP435 a wonderful and interesting experience. Topics ranged to give overviews of various security topics. Not difficult, quizzes were easy with light studying, labs were enjoyable!

Kaki was amazing. 311 is a tough class, but she made the class very easy imo. 6 quizzes worth 8% each (all very similar to the worksheets you're given for HW), 6 Worksheets worth 20%, 5 labs worth 20% (designing circuits), and 1 final exam worth 12%. She dropped lowest 2 quiz grades for your final too, and always gave extra points on her quizzes.
I love kaki
this course was great and kaki handled the incredibly disrespectful class w positivity and humor. idk how she did it i wouldve crashed out

i honestly was so scared of 311 before taking it but it was my favorite class this semester. i took 435 w/ her too, she structured them both similarly -- lots of quizzes, labs, practice problems (in class, worksheets for credit). 435 just had a project too, which was fun. and the TAs were amazing!!

Kaki is my angel. Her lectures are kind of boring, but the slides are clear and descriptive enough that I was able to get >90 on every quiz except quiz 6 without too much studying. Quiz 6 was the assembly quiz and we were a little rushed content-wise, but she had a generous curve. Final was the easiest final I've ever taken in a CS class
Shes very nice, but uploads stuff way too slow
Kaki was a great professor for a historically more challenging class. Assessments are frequent but fair and Kaki cares a great deal about her student success. Highly recommend for 311!

the course is like a sampler of different areas of security, so she covers a lot of ground but doesn't go super deep. smaller quizzes, a final project & final exam too. lots of labs + written assignments too but it felt reasonable. loved her as a professor

Her lectures can be a little boring which led to low class attendance, but overall she is a really great person. She responds quickly to emails and is understanding of extenuating circumstances. Had short quizzes throughout the semester instead of midterms which is super helpful. Lowest quiz gets dropped. Really tries to help you succeed.
Amazing professor that truly cares about the success of her students. I wish she taught my other classes fr.
she's such a sweetheart. expectations straightforward, grading super fair. she does frequent quizzes vs. big exams which really helped me stay on top of everything. highly recommend
what they said ↓
Kaki is the best thing to happen to this department.
I appreciate how this class is set up so much. Kaki really cares about students.

Kaki is very kind, but her lectures can be more confusing than self-studying. As a newer professor, her lectures are still developing. The quizzes are harder than her practice questions, though she offers a small curve. no midterm, 48% on 6 quizzes, 12% final, 20% hw,  20% coding hw, 2 quizzes can be replaced by the final grade
I am in kakis 311 and 435 classes this semester and loving both. The grading is fair and the lectures/practice clearly set us up for the quizzes. she is a real one

I am beyond excited that Kaki is faculty now. I had her when she was still a TA for COMP 110 and she's genuinely the best. Coding has always been difficult for me but she truly put in the time 1 on 1 to help me whenever I asked. Would definitely recommend her classes!!

I tried getting help during office hours, but all I got was a “go watch the lecture” response. The lectures are long, and the way they explain things doesn't match the exercises. There's zero follow-up from the professor if you're stuck.

Honestly, office hours feel like a waste. You wait in line, ask a coding question, and they tell you to watch the lecture again. The examples in that lecture don't even resemble the homework, and the professor doesn't seem interested in helping students who fall behind.
learned so much, but I wish I took this during a regular semester -- material moved FAST. Class was hard, but Kaki is great. She made the 8am semi-bearable

Kaki and Ajay both are superb instructors in their own ways. Quizzes are challenging but fair (2 each week so study consistently). Make sure to start programming exercises early. The Final exam replaces up to 4 of your lowest quiz grades. And the written report and presentation are straightforward.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Kaki is super sweet and caring! It was a decent amount of work but office hours saved me. Ajay (the TA) was awesome too!
A lot of work for a summer class but she makes it doable and is very reasonable + sweet.. Shoutout to the amazing TA Ajay!!

Kaki is an amazing professor! She is extremely kind, helpful, and accommodating. All her lecture materials are available outside of class, and she provides plenty of office hours and helpful resources. If you show that you are willing to put in the work to succeed in her class, she will go above and beyond to help guarantee that.
The most caring and kind professor you could have. She delivers material concisely and cares so much about student wellbeing. Would highly recommend her class.

I had Kaki for her summer 210 course. You could always tell she deeply cared about her students and wanted them all to succeed. She also encouraged curiosity and the joy of learning, not being afraid to go on brief tangents about things that weren't exactly in the curriculum to help students understand the larger subject on a more holistic level.

Kaki is a genuine instructor. She explains concepts very well and answers questions in office hours. 
We had 4 hour office hours every weekday. The 6 quizzes were hard. We had 15 programing assignments, a written report, presentation and a final exam.
I hope she continues taking this course as it was an exceptional experience being her student.

Kaki is excellent. Quizzes are quite challenging, but if you come to class and do the work they are more than fair. She is generous with her time and I would definitely take a course with her again if I get the chance.
KAKI IS THE GOAT!!!

Never have I had a TA or a professor for that matter who cared more about the well being and success of the students. Really helpful review sessions and always available outside of class. Literally she is an angel
lol i would not be passing these quizzes in 110 without kaki. she explains things differently than kris which can help a lot getting a different perspective
kindest professor Ive ever had.
I never knew I could learn so much in such a short amount of time. Kaki is so knowledgeable and her class was epic!!

I am in Kaki's summer class right now and it is honestly the most well-organized and thought-out class I've taken at UNC so far. It is pretty intense and a lot of work, but she is very flexible and willing to work with everyone 1:1. She is very accommodating and I hope I will take more classes with her in the CS department!

Kaki was my TA for Comp110, and her reviews really helped me get a grasp on the topics I didn't quite understand in lecture. She explains things so well, and made it 100% easier to understand. If you have her for Comp110 or any other class, you're in luck!
Kaki cares so much about every student being successful and her review sessions were SO helpful. Those were my saving grace.
I would not have passed COMP110 without Kaki. She is literally amazing and so kind. if she is reading this, thank you!!
Only a few months into the semester but Kaki is by far the best TA Ive had at Carolina.
A true gem
Professor Ryan is Amazing! You must take her class.

Kaki was the most kind and understanding instructor I had during my first semester at Carolina during COVID. She helped me catch up when I was behind and never gave up on me. I was nervous about comp, but she encouraged me to continue in the major.

I would not have passed COMP110 without Ms. Ryan's help and consideration. The first half of the semester in learning to program was very rough for me, but she never gave up on me and made sure I could still succeed. She is very good at explaining the concepts of programming and never makes you feel judged.

Kaki was the best TA ever for COMP110. She always was willing to make time to meet with students outside of class and whenever we requested any type of review materials she made sure we had it. Very kind and knowledgeable. She especially helped hard recursion topics make more sense.

Could not recommend him more for MATH231. He is hilarious and genuinely cares about his students. His exams are fair, and he will actually answer your questions thoroughly if you are confused about anything. Edfinity homeworks during the week and quizzes, with 2 midterms and a final. The final can replace the lowest exam, and he gives extra credit!

He did not perform his duties as instructor at all. He never puts himself in others' shoes. When students are in great need of help, he always chooses to ignore it, which is such a blow to the students. He is indeed kind to this course, but he is definitely not an understanding and caring prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He always uses the excuse of having a lot of classes to teach and being very busy to not fulfill the necessary duties of instructor, such as providing support to students in need of special assistance, which he basically completely ignores. It's basically impossible to reach out to him by email. Don't want to take any classes with him anymore.
Hilarious, fun, and easily approachable.
absolute goat
Amazing teacher! Super understanding and will work with you. Make sure to show up and participate. Definitely reccomend taking a class with him!

I think Shahar is a great professor but only for the more advanced math lectures. This was his first time teaching MATH 231 and it does show. If I needed to take another more advanced math class I would definitely take it with him. Just not Calculus 1.

Kovalsky is super nice and a good lecturer. After the first midterm the exams are open note/open internet. It was a super reasonable lin alg class (I've heard other professors are a lot more difficult). Def recommend taking his class!
Best professor in the department by far, take a class with him if you can!
Very chill guy, open note midterms and final. Homeworks were tedious but prepare you well. Take him!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Goated professor. In class worksheets used as participation grade, fairly weighted midterms and exams, lots of homework on Edfinity (usually weekly). Exams after the first midterm are open note, that may change though. Hilarious dude, always knows how to make class engaging and interesting. Highly recommend taking 347 with him.

Best choice for 347, hands down. In-class work and homework focuses more on application, and it's helpful to have some experience with proofs for tests. EXTREMELY open note exams but may change after this semester so don't count on it.

Shahar is such a gem in the math department. I'm not a math major and have previously struggled in other math classes required from my major. His lectures are engaging and I genuinely looked forward to going to his class. He doesn't overcomplicate concepts and is very clear about expectations. All around fantastic teacher.

The best thing to happen to the UNC math department. Keeps lectures clear and entertaining, makes sure he takes every measure for students to understand the content. This course content shouldn't be too difficult, and it seems like other professors overcomplicate. Hoping I get to take another class with Shahar.
G

He is the best professor in the department. Very funny and knowledgable. You really can't learn anything like this in the department as well. Not an overly difficult class, as he is a somewhat slow lecturer and the class is not too proof oriented. I would take any class taught by Kovalsky. He is very good at forcing you to develop intuition.
Favorite math professor. Very nice guy and very great lecturer, I think every math undergrad should have one class with him. For a 500 level class, not too difficult and very fair.

Great professor I agree with most other reviews. The content of the class can be difficult but the way the class is structured makes it one of the easiest math electives. Many people who did well in this class would not last a day in MATH 521.

I had him for Linear and was super excited to see that he was teaching 560 this semester. Coming into this course and the first few lectures and HW's, I was scared that the course would be very difficult. However, Shahar is very caring with his office hours and has extremely engaging lectures. I loved coming to his course and definitely recommend.

If Professor Kovalsky only has 10 fans, I'm one of them. If Professor Kovalsky has no fans, then I must be dead. He is a great lecturer who strives to emphasize the intuition behind the math rather than blind memorization. If you're not quite sure what math class to take next semester, I promise you can't go wrong with MATH 560 with Shahar Kovalsky
Great professor with engaging lectures and friendly grading with finals!
I didn't understand anything and I made it take it!

Prof Kovalsky is hilarious and a great lecturer. There are no midterms in 560 and the class is mostly graded on homework - which is challenging but doable and relevant. I really, really enjoyed this class.

Grades are 30% final, 40% homework, 30% participation. Not an easy subject, but Shahar is a very caring guy who explains difficult concepts well while not overcomplicating anything. Homework is pretty difficult, but his office hours are really helpful. Really funny lecturer, really interesting subject.

He is a great professor that really cares about his students. The exams were kinda hard but he reused most questions from practice exams and if you study the slides well you'll do fine. The worksheets are a pain but you can have a friend send them to you and you'll be fine. Based on everything I heard he's the best Linear prof at UNC hands down.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really liked shahar! He's super accommodating when it comes to exams and genuinely wants people to do well in his class. As long as you work additional problems, you should be fine for exams. He's also great w answering questions in and out of class

Excellent class, excellent teacher. He gives more of a theoretical background rather than testing strictly computational abilities, which is great for long-term learning and higher level math-classes. Everything is very straightforward, and he makes lectures very enjoyable. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great guy, this class was not nearly as difficult as advertised thanks to Shahar. He is very kind and funny and his lectures were enjoyable. The homework is basically completion and he really does the most to ensure the class averages are high enough. I would absolutely take another class with him.

Lectures were incredibly engaging and transparent -- Kovalsky was an absolute gem to have in my last semester at Carolina. The class was tough, but fair (as higher-level math should be) and truly, truly enjoyable.
man was awesome. he was pretty funny and really wanted everyone to get an A. he dropped a lot of our lowest grades and also rounded my grade up without me asking. 10/10 great guy

Professor Kovalsky did a good job of explaining material, although translations to homework assignments and exams, which were very challenging, felt a little loose at times. It was definitely manageable though, and I do feel that he did his best to be understanding and make sure we knew what was going on. He's definitely a funny guy, too.

Shahar is the best. As someone who normally struggles with math, linear algebra with him was very doable, and he was funny as well. I particularly liked the in-class assignments (worksheets) and found them, along with the lectures, to be very clear and helpful. I highly recommend taking him!

Best professor I've had so far. Really funny and genuinely wanted us to do well (he thought that our second midterm with a 73% average was disappointing). If he's not available one semester for linear, I would wait to see if he is teaching later because it was such a great experience.

Kovalsky is a good choice for 347. I had him the first semester he taught it so I think he was still getting used to it. He didn't post any kind of reviews for the tests and told us to look through the hundreds of ppt slides from class instead. Otherwise, he was a good professor and it wasn't too hard of a class, he knows what he's talking about.

Kovalsky is a solid choice for MATH 347. He is quite funny, understanding, and lenient when it comes to exams. I felt it was hard to follow and understand the material in lecture, and I found it easier to reread the slides and look online later, however I might be able to chalk it up to my learning style. Still overall, pretty good professor.
He is amazing!!!!!!!!!! He is definitely one of the most humorous prof in UNC! I would love to take his course again!! Just follow his lectures and do the homework, you will end up with an A!!!

Shahar is awesome. He was very caring about the class and really wanted us to do our best. Linear algebra is a tough class but he gave everyone ample opportunities to suceed and do well in the class. Lots of opportunities to better your grade even if you didn't do great on the midterms (I didn't).

Professor Kovalsky is an amazing prof. He understands that linear algebra can be tough to understand and did his best to explain even the most abstract topics concisely. He cares about students, and he doesn't want this class to crush our gpa (he gave a minor curve). He also was a wonderful teacher, who frequently cracked jokes during class. 11/10.

Kovalsky is really one of the best professors this place has. Didn't do too well on the second exam, but he was very lenient with the grading since the overall class didn't do too well either which really helped out in the end. Super funny and caring, 10/10 would take linear with him.
Shahar was a great professor especially for his first time teaching. I would recommend taking this class with him as a majority of students got either A or B

Great professor and great for his first time teaching linear! He's funny and makes lectures entertaining. Material definitely picks up after the second midterm, but he wants you to succeed. He doesn't try to trick us and wants everyone to receive an A. He also has a good grade breakdown (so that it's too test-heay) w/ HW and participation points!

Great guy. For his first time teaching this class it seemed to be very well put together. Makes lectures entertaining, exams are not as heavily weighted as other math classes, and homework is not bad if you go to class. Good lecturer too, and explained a lot of concepts very well.

If you have the option, take 347 with Kovalsky. He cares much more about students and our genuine understanding of the material than anything. He's funny and exams were very reasonable, especially with how much insight he gave us for how to best prepare for them. Attend class! He posts slides with no recordings, but he makes lectures interesting!

I was extremely nervous taking this class, but Shahar always ensured that his students were well prepared and not blind sided by exams. Throughout the semester, he was always asking for feedback and input on how he was teaching the material and the difficulty of assignments. Shahar is a super funny guy and a pretty good lecturer. The grade in this class is made of hw's, 2 midterms, final, and daily in-class worksheets. What a G. Good lecturer, he's entertaining. Tests are not bad at all. He accommodates to his students. Id def take linear with Shahar

His lectures are poorly organized, the homework does not follow from the lectures or textbook, and he makes obnoxious jokes the whole class. He answers questions poorly and is rude to students. The only reason not to get an A is not working hard enough, a fair amount of work for a college-level class. Nice to students, and very open to feedback. Legit the best professor ever!! She truly cares about students' well-being and will work with you if you have questions/concerns. She is an easy grader and gives clear instructions for what is expected. Her lectures were kinda boring but they were manageable.

The BEST English 105 professor!! If you can take this class with her please do! She was always making sure we weren't stressed, and had lots of accommodations.

The GRQs had a lot of irrelevant content, but they weren't terrible. One midterm is dropped and she offers lot of study resources, which is awesome!

Professor Ott's lectures can be really monotonous and boring, but her grading criteria are clear, her tests are fair, and she answers questions clearly. Attendance is weird as the points are partially based on accuracy, but overall it's not bad. You might not love going to class, but if you do, you should do pretty well.

dr. ott's class was challenging, but her lectures were engaging and the workload was manageable. GRQs were long and sometimes unrelated to what we were learning. she drops quite a few grades at the end, including the lowest midterm, but exams are still weighted very heavily. even if content on the exam was easy, her wording made it a bit confusing.

Didn't love her at first, but as the semester went on she really grew on me. May seem a bit intense but you can tell she really cares about her students and I felt like exams were about as fair as they could be. She will try to trick you pretty frequently, but I felt like the lecture style did a great job of preparing me for the exams.

This class is hard, but doable if you pay attention and use the resources.  Exams came from lecture and there were no surprises.  Drops your lowest midterm and allows a cheat sheet on the final exam.  Ott is direct with students, but I found her to be kind.
I found her pretty passive aggressive and sassy. 103 is quite challenging for an introductory-level bio class. Her office hours were very helpful, though.

Dr. Ott is not a bad professor, and this class is NOT easy. She is very caring and easy to reach outside of class, but can be very passive-aggressive. Exams sometimes feel like they're completely unrelated to class content, and GRQs are often unnecessarily lengthy with little connection to class content. Review lecture slides to do best on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Her class was somewhat overwhelming, but Ott does a good job of making it manageable. I think she was really nice and was engaging throughout the class. Her exams are quite challenging, but everything has been covered in class, so review the class slides and quizzes, and you should be fine.

Dr. Ott is very kind and approachable. Lectures were engaging, but exams were full of trick questions that did not always feel like she was testing your knowledge of a concept. Heavy emphasis on molecular techniques. GRQs took forever and were honestly useless.

Dr. Ott is super smart and great at her job but can be a bit condescending. Going through the lecture slides is by far the best way to study. GRQs were long and not always helpful, but it was nice to be told exactly what sections of the text to focus on. Lots of drops for lowest quizzes etc. and lowest midterm is dropped too.

Would recommend taking with Dr. Ott! Her lectures are pretty engaging and straightforward. Everything that is on the test is covered in her slides. She is also pretty accessible outside of class for extra help. Tests are pretty heavily weighted but they aren't too bad in terms of difficulty and she also drops a midterm. GRQ's are time consuming.

Dr. Ott has been one of my favorite professors at UNC so far. In my opinion, she is a clear lecturer (mostly) and has a lenient grading policy, as she drops the lowest midterm and several other homework assignments. Dr. Ott is also very accesible outside of class, offering both group and individual office hours. I would take another class with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ott, in my opinion, isn't the best lecturer. It could be my learning style, but all the material appears very vague and disorganized. The homework and assignments are completely unrelated to class content, and I've had to teach myself the entire course. That being said, the course is fairly easy, except for the reading comprehension exams.

Biol 103 is a deceptively hard class. It's interesting, however there's a lot of busy work (useless/unhelp GRQs imo, more useful Pearson assignments. I learned everything needed in lecture. That + quizzes & practice tests helped me do well. Tests are difficult though: questions are hard to understand and correct answers feel ambiguous.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Her exams are weighted very, and i mean VERY heavily. However, your lowest midterm is dropped. I would watch out for how she phrases the questions on the exam. I also would strongly advise to drop everything (like don't even take notes when you're doing the GRQs) and to just pay the most attention to the slides.

Don't skip 101, especially if you are a freshman. She's amazing at teaching, but exams are super tricky and there is a TON of work to do outside of class. The exams are weighted very heavily (48% midterm, 24% final). There are many resources outside of class, so it isn't impossible to do well. If you have to take this class, take it with Dr. Ott.

I thought this course was very doable. I did the homework and made Anki decks from the slides she provided in class. Overall, very great and entertaining lectures, would highly recommend! Just study and definitely do the practice exams, she bases a lot of her questions similar to them, especially the final.

She is direct and doesn't take crap from students, but I think she's effective and generally understanding if you seriously have things going on.  Exams are hard, but all her questions come from class.  She also drops the lowest exam and is allowing us a cheat sheet on the final exam.

This class is unnecessarily difficult. I swear to god the amount of times I have been screwed over by the wording of her questions is unreal. I am sorry, but this class is absolutely not it. Avoid if you can.
Had her last semester and she was a horrible professor. First, professor to ever make me cry.

I feel the way Ott teaches some concepts makes them more confusing than they should be. Instead of explaining what each concept is, she instead goes through participation questions (graded for accuracy) and complicated examples, which are more confusing rather than helpful. Her lectures have a lot of group work though, which makes it interesting.
So tricky, she purposely makes exams super hard.

I don't even know where to start honestly. She's smart and good at what she does, but she's so rude and backhanded at times that it negates the former. I didn't enjoy lectures, homeworks, and DEFINITELY not the exams.. very difficult and she loves to include trick questions. The material was somewhat interesting but the experience... frustrating.

Solidified my love for bio. Cares so much for her students and makes lectures actually interesting. Witty and fun which makes it exciting to go to class. She gives me the motivation to learn and understand all the biological concepts. Class isn't hard if you don't fall behind and keep up with the readings and pay attention in lecture.
Don't do it

Despite personal struggles throughout the SP25 semester, Dr. Ott still deeply cared for her students and taught concepts clearly. The class builds in repetition to solidify important concepts. Practice exams and lots of problems are great preparation for exams. GRQs are not exceptionally useful. Dropped exam :))) But they are pretty challenging.

Pros: Dr. Ott is very thorough on content, lectures are engaging. The mastering HW was fine. 3 exams, Lowest dropped. Final was cumulative and hard. 
Cons: tests are very semantics heavy, not only do you have to know the material inside and out, you also need to decipher what Dr. Ott is trying to ask you. Her voice gets on some people's nerves.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: There are three exams and one gets dropped; she does have “flexibility” thing where she drops a certain (1-2) number of assignments but they don't apply to certain ones so make sure to stay on top of due dates
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Take 103 with a different professor. Lectures were so boring, plus we had assigned seats that made class even worse.

Dr. Ott can be condescending and rude at times and even though she takes the flipped classroom to the extreme, her lectures are very helpful for the exams. I also had Dr. Garland, and exams are hard no matter who you have, but I thought Ott's teaching style was more appropriate for an introductory course and better prepared me for exams.

My favorite class at UNC. The content is HARD, and there's lots of memorization -- but it's possible and you got it. Lowest exam grade was dropped, GRQs were useless and I never did them. LOTS OF MEMORIZATION but you also need to know how to apply the stuff you memorize. You make no cheat sheets except for the final but she gives one for exams.

Ott gets a bad rep but she's really good. Students struggling in the class (this is a HARD class) struggle because of the material/course, not because of her. Sometimes takes questions off tests or quizzes cus they were wrong. LOTS OF MEMORIZATION but you also apply it. Unless its the final no cheat sheet (but she provides diagrams for exams).

This class is super content heavy, and the exams are made to trick you. Ott was an ok prof, but she was rude to students and her lecturing style often annoyed me. Pretty much all homework is useless busy work and not relevant to what you need for exams. Focus on lectures, practice exams, and peer mentor resources and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: most people who say her exams are hard took AP bio — imo if you took BIOL101 here at UNC BIOL103 with ott is ALOT more straightforward. she is really annoying and condescending (one of my friends switched out of her section cos he couldn't physically stand her voice) and her quizzes have trick questions. overall ALOT OF work but lots of materials.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Was in the Co-Taught Section. Otts personality is very abrasive… but a better lecturer than Garland. Exam 2 with her was a nightmare. Wish she had stayed for the full semester.

I love Dr. Ott. I had her for 103 and loved her, so I took her again for 252. I knew I would love the content, but I really enjoyed her lectures. Exams were tough but I felt like they matched the learning objectives fairly and were similar to questions asked in class. I even liked her assigned seat system (ik) bc the consistency was helpful for me
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I was in the co-taught section with Dr. Garland and Dr. Ott. They are both great professors, but definitely have different styles, especially for tests. Dr. Ott's are more application while Dr. Garland's are more memorization. Dr. Ott was great during office hours. The tests are difficult, so be prepared to study.

I took Ott & Garland. Ott was a better lecturer for sure, but the tests sucked. More reading comprehension than anything else. Lots of select multiple, all, and none of the above. They dropped the lowest midterm and gave 4 points EC on the final, but the tests still weren't really fair. You'll be teaching yourself in this class.

This is in my top 3 least favorite classes at UNC. She isn't super considerate towards students. Plenty of times she has cut students off while they ask a question or while answering one of her questions, regardless if the answer is right/wrong. She will literally say "nope!" or "no agreement" or "wrong!" when students share an answer in class.

Dr. Ott is my favorite professor in Biology and I had her for 103 and 252.  I agree that she can be direct, but she's not mean.  She is very clear about her expectations and I thought all of her exams were very fair and based on what she covered in lecture.  She drops the lowest midterm in both classes.

Her exams have confusing questions and are difficult to do well on (I got 3 questions wrong and got a 90 on one). Weekly online quizzes that you can't miss or you get a 0. I had a lot of personal issues this semester and ended up not having time for some of the quizzes but she gave me no help. I would've gotten an A if I didn't miss these quizzes.

Dr. Ott can be curt sometime, but she really does care about her students success. She is a no BS type of teacher and teaches material very directly. Going to class is pretty much required to get a good grade. GRQs are optional, but you should do them. Hard to get caught up if you get behind as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Ott is a great lecturer, and I learned a lot. She is very condescending and does not help when you ask and question and just says it's not correct. To the most recent BIOL252 review, her mom has cancer. Of course, she is going to be more concerned with her personal life, and you would be too.

dr. ott is condescending and makes her students feel beneath her. I went to her office hours a few times and she was so rude the whole time. her exams are felt more like reading comprehension exam than a biology exam. however, she is an AMAZING lecturer and I did learn a lot from her. she is a much better teacher than dr. garland.
literally horrible. don't listen to all the reviews and steer clear. was more concerned with her personal life than teaching and honestly knew next to nothing about anatomy and physiology.
I felt that a lot of this class built on what I learned in AP Biology.  Ott was a good professor and was direct, but fair overall.  Exams were tough, but lots of resources are provided.

Very homework heavy class with lots of reading. But as long as you pay attention in lecture and come to class prepared, you will do fine. As for Dr. Ott herself, she seems nice in lecture but she can be very condescending and rude if she is in a bad mood, especially during 1-1 conversation.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Do not take Ott. Extremely rude and disrespectful to her students. Test questions are so hard even if you know all of the material by heart. Take Biology with anyone else.

I think Dr. Ott had some pretty good lectures. She did explain some complicated topics pretty well. Her office hours were also helpful. However, she is a touch sensitive and can sometimes be a bit dense with students. Just don't ask any questions that you think she would view as silly, because she might just say "we went over this." Good, not great
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Honestly, I don't understand the bad rep Ott gets.  Anatomy is just a hard, content heavy course with a lot of information, and if you are pre-health taking many of the other pre-reqs it can be a lot to manage but it's doable.  Her midterms were fair and were definitely skewed more towards lectures rather than GRQs.

Good organization and I thought Dr. Ott was fair.  The exams were tough but doable and she provides a multiple practice problems.  She is loud, but I found her engaging and would take a class with her again.
Do not take this with Ott. Thinks she is better than everyone and is not a good lecturer.
Terrible. Screams in the microphone and asks everyone to be patient with her but is never patient with others. Thinks she is a celebrity?

Ott isn't bad at teaching by any means, but her exams are more about reading her crazy wording and making up insane scenarios than about any actual Biology content. You could know everything and still do awful on her exams.  Don't recommend.
i swear she centers her lessons around her sob stories so that she can make sure everyone knows

Childish, rude, loud. Maybe thinks she is a celeb? Exams/quizzes poorly written, making them hard. Often says things wrong or backwards. For immune system, she skipped a lot of material that is needed for tests like MCAT. She had things come up a lot in personal life and asked us to be understanding, but wasn't when I had stuff come up. Steer clear

Convinced she writes her own good reviews on here. Worst professor, very condescending, even worse than Garland tbh. I had a good knowledge of anatomy prior in but did poorly on the tests bc her questions were so horribly written. Not guaranteed a 100 on participation even if you attend every lecture. Would not recommend taking her class to ANYONE

DO NOT TAKE. Worst professor I've had at UNC. Genuinely doesn't know A&P or how to teach it. Students would call her out on errors bc she didn't know what she was saying. Exams are worded so confusing for NO reason and have few Qs. Made me hate this class and the bio dept as a whole. Would rather transfer schools than take another class with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She writes questions as though she is the riddler when the material is not difficult if you study. Going to class is important in order to get the material, but she struggles to teach it in a way that is helpful to you. So would I say she is a good teacher, no, but if you go to class and do alot of studying outside of lecture, you will do fine.

The weekly assignments are long and a PITA. Profs for other classes manage to assign homework that covers similar amounts of content without assigning huge, unhelpful, unengaging documents of fill-in-the-blanks. 

Also, I personally do not vibe with her lecture style. She seems to think yelling louder into the mic = teaching more clearly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: bio 103 was one of the hardest classes I have taken and not because the subject material is difficult. dr. ott is not the best at explaining although she does know her stuff. also she yelled at someone during an exam in front of the class for no reason. the exams are hard with lots of trick questions. I switched my major after taking this class.
Writes unnecessarily hard midterms, and exams are much harder than content discussed in class. Lecture heavy with a lot of assignments, and attendance is mandatory.

Take this class with literally anyone else. This class isn't supposed to be hard at all, but she has split up her grading scale to make it impossible to even get an A-. There's not a single category in the gradebook you are guaranteed 100% in (even participation)! It's like she purposely made this class impossible for no reason.
Do not expect her ever to answer any questions on Piazza or her emails.
She can be a little passive-aggressive at times, and I thought the exams were created to trick me. :( However, she was very enthusiastic, so she was alright.

The review from 4/22/25 just wants to flex their grade… her exams are worded weird and if u ever try to ask for clarification or questions she is very short flamed. Also every lesson ends up as a pity party for her it's like she purposely makes her lessons so that she can add in her own personal sob story in relation to the unit. she's also so loud

Not sure how caring doctor Ott is but she is a good professor. She gives clear criteria for what you need to do to pass her class. She's a little rude to students sometimes but if you don't take it personally you'll be fine. Just do what she says to do and the class is good. Participation does count and you have GRQs and quizzes for every lesson.

Dr. Ott is a passionate professor. Her intentions mostly seem innocent, but she frequently gets impatient and/or can embarrass a student for not knowing something/asking a question. Many are scared to ask her questions out of fear of being ridiculed. I don't believe that she wants us to feel this way, but this is how she presents herself.

I got an A on all of the exams -- class is a lot of work, but if you pay attention and use the resources, you will do fine.  I have heard that the final exam is easy and she is allowing us a cheat sheet on the final, so I am anticipating an A in the class.  I would definitely recommend.
Confusing test questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There is a lot of content, but it's truly not too bad if you are able to dedicate several of hours a week to work. Dr Ott is an okay professor & is good at communicating content, but tends to overshare about her personal life which can be uncomfortable. Exam questions are also worded in the most confusing way possible.

If you pay attention and do the work, this class is easy. She is annoying, but a good teacher and drops questions that are unfair. Just pay attention to her guidelines - she will bust you if you have your cell phone out during exams.

She is extremely condescending, and she does not answer questions. She has failed many students for having their phones in their back pockets when leaving the exam room. She also gives assigned seats in a lecture hall.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: i have had ott for 103 and 252 and shes always just been mid. she seems like a fun person outside of class but in class she can be so mean omg. im not one to dislike teachers but every class she somehow makes it easier to dislike her a little bit more😅 content is easy but tests are genuinely so confusing for no reason. she makes me feel so stupid

Had her for 103! I like her! She can sometimes be direct and mean, but it's nothing crazy. Just don't do anything weird/bad. Tests were hard for me, but not impossible, with lots of prep. Had 3 midterms (lowest dropped) and the final. HW before each class and optional GRQs, but highly recommend if you want to succeed. Lots of pre-class reading.

Favorite professor in biology. Class isn't easy, but if you use the resources she makes available, you'll do fine. Ott expects a lot from students, but gives flexibility to make mistakes that others don't like dropping lowest exam.

She's good, not great.  She has clearly communicated expectations and her exams are fair and based on what we cover in class.  If you pay attention and use the resources, you'll be fine.  She doesn't always handle students who don't follow the instructions well, but that's also on them -- they are clearly communicated.

Does not seem to care about students. Extremely condescending, makes the class more difficult then it needs to be and also takes her bad mood out on students. Content is not difficult, exams are not necessarily hard but they are clearly meant to trick you rather than assess your actual understanding. Voice is really annoying.

Laura Ott made BIOL 103 more difficult than what it needed to be. She was very condescending when you meet with her one-on-one and all she talks about is her research. BIOL 103 is not a difficult class, but was made more difficult because of her failure to teach the material and her condescending nature.

bro she will yell at you at 9:30 in the morning, every morning. she also lost her marbles at multiple students when they were trying to turn in their exams because they took out their phones before they left the exam hall. her class isn't hard shes just irritating.

Does not care about student success and frankly if her students live or die. Always concerned with her personal matters without thinking others may experience life struggles too. Unprofessional control of her anger towards students and takes revenge on entire classes for singular students ill-choices. Confusing and unintuitive lecturer as well.

Professor Ott was great. I enjoyed her lectures and thought she was very informed in the course content. Sometimes the lectures would get boring, but she was very clear as to what was expected in the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Bio 103 is a challenging class regardless of who teaches it. I utilized the resources at the learning center and they really helped me. Dr Ott is a caring person, I think she just really emphasizes student independence and it can come off the wrong way. Taking good notes in class is super important, no cheat sheets but we got on one the final.

This class was an extension of AP Bio and I think Ott did a good job teaching it.  She offers a ton of practice problems that if you work them and understand the answers you will be prepared for the exams.

Although the material wasn't too difficult, she tends to talk down on students regularly and designs test questions to trick you. It's definitely possible to do well but there's other professors who'd respect you more as a student.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Explains things WAY more complicated than they need to be. Learning catalytics for participation. HEAVY on flipped class format. have to teach yourself. test questions often try to trick you. did offer 4 extra credit points for course eval on final and cheat sheet. kinda annoying voice and VERY loud, didn't even need mic. little condescending.

My only complaint about this class is the GRQs and Mastering seem like busy work, especially since all of the exam questions come from lecture.  Your lowest midterm and a handful of quizzes are dropped.  Ott is a solid choice.

Dr. Ott was a good lecturer, but she was very sassy. It's almost impossible to get all the notes going to lecture so make sure to watch the recordings after. Beware of TAs and LAs watching you during exams, I got accused of cheating 🙄. Nevertheless, the tests were fair, just make sure to study and use all the resources available.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Overall, the class is structured well. Sometimes learning catalytics questions were unfair, but she does knock off a lot of points in the end + your lowest midterm grade. Tests and quizzes were fair - if you just look over the slides you should be fine. GRQ and Mastering hw don't really help as much for test preparation.

Dr. Ott was consistently being so condescending and rude to students. The course was ridiculously difficult. Although difficult courses are unavoidable at UNC, avoiding an extremely difficult course paired with a rude professor is always recommended. Steer clear of this course! Better options at UNC are available, Dr. Ott should be avoided.

Not a very enjoyable class. Felt like AP Bio just unnecessarily harder. Dr. Ott's tests aren't easy and often feel designed to trick you. She's quite accessible and helpful though. Not the worst, just not the best.

She was not very approachable during office hours, she would give learning strategies rather than answer your questions, overall I got a very judgey vibe. Also the exams are a freaking riddle, and she offers regrade requests but good luck telling her she wrote the exam wrong

Not a very good professor, dosent really teach you anything. Have to teach yourself with flipped classroom. Exams cover PowerPoints but she makes it all mostly true or one part is wrong so all is wrong partial credit types. I would take garland, she was better than ott when I had her last semester, also a lot friendlier. Dr ott is rude

Don't listen to any of the negative comments about Dr. Ott.  Worked with me when I had to miss class due to personal emergency and has flexible grading - drops lowest exam and quiz s. and Great class and great professor!
Exams aren't too hard, nor is content. However, she can be incredibly rude and mean to students in lecture and office hours. Her class was much worse because of how she acted.

Exam difficulty is over-exaggerated, questions are application-based but not as bad as others make them out to be. Very generous amount of grades are dropped, including a midterm grade. GRQs/mastering are not helpful, focus on lecture slides to study.
Tough class, but doable if you go to class and do the work. Ott is annoying, but she's not horrible like people make her out to be.

She thinks she is funny and relatable, but she just comes off a rude and demeaning. The exams are unnecessarily complicated. Take garland if possible. Rating way to high, spends more time talking about Milo (her dog) than teaching

Laura is the most condescending and rude professors I have ever had at UNC. She targets certain students she does not like and treats them terribly if they ask questions in class. Her lessons are scattered and her quizzes are tough.
