He makes a lot of typos, but he's a very new prof so I get that, but he is like a drill sergeant during exams. 70% of your grade is from exams where the average is in the 60s. You have to study A LOT to get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you don't have the discipline to read and study outside of class I'd look to take another section. I never went but heard he was pretty condescending and useless in office hours. The three exams (which determine most of your grade) were all full of typos and inconsistencies and when grades came back there were always grading mistakes.

It is apparent through his enthusiastic lecture style that he is passionate about his subject, which is why it was so disheartening to witness him crush my excitement for the content. Exams are weighted at 70% of your course grade, and averages are consistently in the 60s. Whether you pass this course or not is in god's hands.

For a teacher who cares so much about cheating and enforces a strict test-taking environment, he's very disruptive. During the final, he announced something about every 20-30 minutes. Also, tests are way more difficult than the actual homework and problem sets, partly because of typos he makes and because the exam content is 10x more difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It's clear from these reviews that he has far more respect for and is better at teaching honors students. He is not cut out for class of 800 people. He thinks we are dumber yet doesn't explain things and gives out far more difficult exams. He gave us the exams from honors and they were a joke compared to ours now. If you take him, take honors only.

pretty normal class and not hw is easy but the tests are crazy difficult, hard to comprehend what questions are asking and just beyond poorly made. For the first test 2/20 of the multiple choice questions just simply didnt have the correct answer listed. During every test he has to make at least 3 announcements about how we need to correct a typo.

It's as bad as they say. McDonough's exams are impossible. I can't count how many times we have been interrupted mid-exam because of multiple errors and typos on them. Spends more time worrying about cheating than teaching the material or checking his exams for errors, which are 70% of your grade, and the average is a 66%. Avoid at ALL COSTS.
Professional gaslighter. his class was so hard but he wouldn't even acknowledge it. Proud of a class avg of a 60 on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: run away while you still can. he takes pride in his exam average of a 60, makes typos on the exams, gives us no time to complete tests, and doesn't teach what we are tested on. hardest class I've taken at UNC--a lot of people are just trying to pass the class at this point. never have I tried so hard only to fail so miserably. good luck
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The biggest problem with this class is that his exams are wayyy too difficult. He provides practice exams that are straightforward then gives you material on the test that even the TAs struggle with when going over the exam in recitation. Not to mention every exam had errors on it and his vibe is just not my cup of tea.

The one takeaway I have for this course is to lower my expectations before checking canvas. He prides himself on class averages being below 60%. The only things this class has taught me are to humble myself and that i'll never be prepared enough for his exams. This class is unnecessarily hard and he refuses to acknowledge it. King of gaslighting.

Robert is honestly one of the worst professors I've had here. The exams are virtually impossible and he likes his averages to be in the 60s. He makes TONS of mistakes on exams which causes grading to be delayed and overall confusion. You might as well guess on the short answers because he never explains how to do them. Good luck if you have him.
Lowkey worst experience of my life....can someone please explain to me why his exams are so much harder than anything we ever learned/practiced in the class? Like does he just want us to fail?
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very exam heavy. Exams are way harder than everything learned in class.

Professor McDonough is very enthusiastic about the material but his exams are unnecessarily complicated. I found the multiple choice sections to be a joke, while the short answers were very difficult solely due to poor wording rather than students lack of understanding of the material. Also, he just pisses me off sometimes.

Has a passion for economics but exams are unnecessarily difficult & are way harder than the course content requires. He designs the exams to keep class averages in the mid-60s, & the free-response questions are based on pure intuition & are never taught. Either you have it or you don't, and you probably don't. Much harder than other 101 professors.

Robert is a real-life Spencer Reid with extra spunk. He is knowledgeable, passionate, and funny. His testing structure needs work but he improves with every assessment he administers. I would recommend getting to know him personally and sitting towards the front, as it has made me successful in this class. Econ101 with him is the best option at UNC
He was new to ECON 101 making some of his exams and guidelines confusing but overall a passionate professor.

Robert is extremely enthusiastic about economics and it comes across in the way he teaches. If you attend lectures and pay attention/take notes, you will do well. He is clear on grading criteria and generally fair in how he assigns practice (there are many low-stakes ways to assess your own understanding). If you can take 101 with him, go for it.

A very empathetic professor who appears to really care about students and their wellbeing. Lectures are engaging and easy to understand when you pay attention. This is an additional requirement for my major and I enjoy it better than my actually required ones.

He was an absolute ANGEL. I took econ 101 with no prior knowledge of economics and he made the material so easy and digestible. Super easy to talk to and very accessible outside of class. Genuinely wants you to succeed and will go out of his way to help you if you ask. Take any class at UNC you can with this man.

Dr. McDonough was very passionate about labor econ which clearly translated to his lectures. I appreciated the that there were few assignments (~10 short, at home quizzes, 4 problem sets, and 1 project). The true/false were difficult on the exams, but the extra credit on the problem sets definitely helped. I enjoyed this class and Dr. McDonough!

I don't think I have ever met someone so enthusiastic about talking about economics, which made lectures engaging. Grade consists of 4 homeworks, 2 midterms, the final, and what he calls 'valuing your degree' project. The midterms were fair, but the true/false section could be tricky sometimes. Definitely take his class if you get the chance!
If you have to take ECON 101. TAKE IT WITH HIM. Loved him. 10/10 . An engaging lecturer who knows his stuff, and is willing and ready to help/answer questions.

He is AMAZING. Such a wonderful, kind, engaging professor. He had so many opportunities outside of class to help us (pizza review sessions, lots of office hours), made class so fun, and gave us fair tests. However, it was very easy and he curves extremely at the end. I did not feel challenged by the material and the exams were very easy, but fun!

By far best ECON professor at UNC. He's young, personable, and normal (unlike the strange buggy professors the econ department usually hires like Roark) Content actually mae sense because he knew how to teach.. unlike Roark. Made the class interesting as well. Very helpful when you ask questions as well.. opposite of Roark in just about every way.

Prof. McDonough is the best Econ professor at UNC. He held multiple review sessions where you could ask him anything about the class and it was usually helpful. Exams were kind of hard, but it was up to you if you did good or bad. I actually wanted to go to every class and learn and have never wanted to do that with an Econ class.

Robert was a really lovely professor and that made all the difference when taking a tough class like ECON 101. He was always available to answer questions during and outside of class. It was encouraging and helpful to get  feedback and explanations from him. I would definitely recommend taking this class with him even if it is a hard class.

Staub has absolutely nothing on this wonderful man. I genuinely really enjoyed having him as my professor. Incredible lecturer who actually taught us everything we needed to know IN CLASS. I wouldn't have liked this class as much as I did if it wasn't taught by him. 10/10 If you're reading this Robert, thank you again!

Professor McDonough makes himself super available with office hours which I highly recommend going to. His lectures are really interesting and he posts the slides before class so you can follow along. He's probably the best professor I've had at UNC so far so definitely take him if you can.

Very good lecturer. He really does clearly explain everything for the exams. It works best for me to sit through the lecture only paying attention to what he is saying and then go home to look at the lecture slides and drop down notes. I would take his class again overall if I wasn't graduating this semester.

Such an amazing and smart teacher. He genuinely cares about his students and doesn't grade harshly at all. Very engaging lectures and the simulation portion of the class if not too hard. The quizs are easy and sometimes even done in groups, exams are challenging but if you pay attention in class then you will be good. Take this class!!

He does a great job teaching and making topics understandable. As a non-poli major (took for the gen-ed credit) I found this course interesting and digestible, with a reasonable amount of work for a gen-ed.
Sometimes dawdling in lectures, but very kind person and passionate about the materials.
Great professor. Funny and just an overall good dude. The class was fun and engaging
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Weidenfeld was great, I took poli 59 as my first year seminar and I am very thankful I did. He made the class a lot of fun and a nice way to spend the mornings. You get to know the people in your class and most quizzes and even exams are able to be done with classmates.

This class was so much fun and I would highly recommend you take it! It consisted of a speech, 6 quizzes (one dropped), 3 tests, participation, and a final discussion (10%) of grade. As long as you read the required pages listed in the study guide you will do well on the quizzes/tests, overall very fun class and a great way to get the theory credit

The Reacting to History format was engaging and fun, using a historical character to do a deep dive on different parts of political history. Mr. Weidenfeld was not often available over email/outside of class and the organization of the class was not great. Most of the benefit I got was from group collaboration and challenging my perspective.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Weidenfeld is capable of being very engaging, but the class was incredibly disorganized. I learned almost nothing in the class and not challenged by anything other than keeping track of Weidenfeld's mess. Small classes or ones with no simulation component with him could be great but he can't manage a ~100 person simulation.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is beyond unorganized and students suffer as a result.

Professor Weidenfeld is a great professor who demonstrates a deep passion for his field and is dedicated to helping students succeed. My only complaint is that he semi-frequently fails to communicate well (or at all) on assignments or class cancellations.

Weidenfield is a great lecturer as he is very engaging and truly knows the material. However, he is completely inaccessible outside of class, and his disorganization and bias in simulation made the course much more unenjoyable than it needed to be. I enjoyed this class, but you are pretty much on your own in the second half and grade is up to you.

He was entertaining but almost entirely inaccessible outside of class, so if you needed him for something, you better catch him before he scurried out of the room. As long as you did the necessary reading, you could make the class your own, i.e., you could play NYT Games during lecture/simulation. Unreal but definitely fun professor/class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was one of my favorites! Lecture on political philosophy the first half, then simulation on the Constitutional Convention the second half. Weidenfeld creates an engaging environment and lets the class run the Convention. Only critic is that he never answers emails and is rarely available outside of class, but I overall recommend.

This is the most fun class I've ever taken. The first five weeks are content based with two quizzes and a midterm, but the rest of the semester is a simulation of the Constitutional Convention. Make sure to really play into your character and participate as much as possible. The midterms and quizzes were not super hard and they were graded fairly.

Weidenfeld is a great professor. His lectures are engaging and we have spent the last month or so doing a simulation based on the French Revolution. You can tell he is really passionate about the things he teaches. A lot of people are complaining about the quiz that "bombed" everyone's grade, but he let us use the readings. A bit Disorganized.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Weidenfeld is the goat. Really funny and very, very passionate about the topic. This course is a super unique format so you really have to buy into the whole thing but it's a lot of fun if you do. Quizzes and exams are on the harder side as it is an upper level course. Overall would recommend to anyone considering taking this class!

Nice guy and fun lectures but recent quizzes have been so difficult. Quiz 4 was literally impossible for everyone I know. Totally destroyed my grade and not sure what to do now. Again, fun lectures, but the quizzes feel super unreasonable :(

Everyone I know in 271 (including myself) is panicking about this course. The last quiz we took (1 out of 5 quizzes) hurt our grades so badly & was so difficult. I did the readings & really studied hard & didn't know half the questions. I don't think my peers or I can recover our grades from this. Weidenfeld is a good prof but this is so stressful
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a nice guy and obviously knows a lot about what he's teaching, but he can't get things graded in a very timely manner. Didn't get my midterm grade back before the p/f deadline. His lectures are somewhat rambling and hard to follow. The simulation at the end of the course is also very unclear and hectic; I feel he could have explained it more.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A delightful instructor. I wish I encountered him before my senior year. Exceedingly good at making complex concepts accessible. Not a harsh grader. Readings were dense but short and manageable. Loves to talk ideas after class.

I cannot emphasize how much I enjoyed this class. His method is unique but it works. You get to be the constitutional convention. Just make sure you study for the midterm! Take notes and come to class everyday !
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: I took this teacher for Poli59 as my first year seminar. It was my favorite class I have taken thus far at UNC. It was incredibly engaging, hilarious, and overall just so much fun. I loved the teacher and the way he taught. He was a very kind grader and was super helpful during class. I would recommend this class to absolutely everyone.

Kind professor although very inaccessible (rarely responds to emails). The class itself was chaotic since half of it is a simulation of the French Revolution. The readings were well-chosen, though, and the assignments were graded fairly. I learned a lot and liked interacting with other people in my recitation. Would recommend to majors/non-majors!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The most inaccessible professor I have ever had. Sent over ten extremely important emails throughout the semester and never once got a response. Even when it concerned mistakes in grading and time sensitive questions. Nice guy, passionate about teaching, but his inability to respond or communicate is not fair to his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very nice and funny but extremely disorganized and difficult to reach outside of class. Respect him a lot as a person, but I do not recommend taking a class with him simply because of these issues.

I had Professor Weidenfeld for Poli 59 and it was a great experience. Not only does he create a classroom environment that is fun to be in, but he also does a great job at teaching the material. Grades in the class are unfortunately on few things, but he is a generous grader and you should be fine if you do the reading. Overall, highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I don't like theory classes but Weidenfeld made this one bearable and even interesting to a degree. His lectures were always thought-provoking and the assignments & quizzes were pretty easy. The historical simulation/roleplay in the last 6 weeks was super unconventional in a fun way. Make sure you understand the theories and you'll be good to go.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Weidenfeld is an incredible and engaging lecturer who made me want to attend class. None of the assignments were too hard and the exams were very fair. However, grading is up to the TA's so keep that in mind. Just attend  and pay attention class, understand the readings, and put thought/effort in your assignments and you will be fine!

Prof Weidenfeld uses some unconventional but highly entertaining methods in some of his courses, including a complicated role-playing historical simulation in this course. The latter half of the class was some of the most fun I've ever had in college, and his encouragement of engagement and questions in the lecture half was great. Would recommend.

Professor Weidenfeld is an awesome teacher to have. He is super passionate about the material and has engaging lectures. Really hated the content of POLI 271 so I didn't like the class, but Weidenfeld as a professor is awesome!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Whether you are a poli major or not you HAVE to take this class with Weidenfeld. I took this class as a freshman and it still is my favorite class I have ever taken at UNC. Weidenfeld is so funny and helpful with the simulation. You basically become the constitutional convention and is seriously is the most fun!!

Professor Weidenfeld's class was engaging and entertaining and I really enjoyed the way he set up the simulation. The workload wasn't terrible - two papers, two speeches, four quizzes - but quizzes can be tough. Be prepared to participate in class and read a lot of political theory, but the class is really fun overall and I would take it again.

So chill, amazing guy. Reminds me of Hamilton debate kid class. If you like history, absolutely take it. Readings are kinda difficult, but he gives notes in class. 2 papers and 2 speeches total, not too bad. Never knew what was going on, but it was still fine. Hard quizzes but they are online and answers on quizlet, let us take some w/ groups.

Weidenfeld is the best professor I've had at UNC. This class simulated the French and American Revolutions and everyone played a character. I was scared that it would be a lot of work, and it is (a lot of reading, political thought, and meetings outside of class) but it's fun and not unmanageable. Take it!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Echoing other students here, the man makes the cumbersome world of Political Theory deeply enjoyable! He makes dated philosophizing relevant today, and helps guide ones imagination to the meat of the info, so we may critique it better. My only complaint is hes so good he seems like hes juggling numerous responsibilities at times. Still love him.

I loved Dr. Weidenfeld's class. I was a freshman STEM major in a POLI class full of seniors so I felt a bit out of my element but ultimately was happy. Fun game structure. There isn't much to grade (3 papers and two or three exams) but that's it, so beyond that, you work as much as you want for your role. Teaches you much more beyond poli sci

Great professor who is passionate about the material and an outgoing guy. The readings are challenging and he doesn't use PowerPoints. You'll have to be able to pick up on larger themes and ideas instead of details. The simulation was fun and a great way to conclude the course. I recommend this course, the stuff you learn will apply to your life.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I love Professor Weidenfeld! You can clearly tell that he is incredibly passionate about the materials he teaches. I am taking this 400+ class as a freshman but I really loved it! He makes everything fun! My best online learning experience! The exams are very doable. The midterm paper was challenging but only the second draft is graded so its fine
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Coming from a Poli major, prof. Weidenfeld is probably the best teacher in the department. His lectures are engaging, personal, and entertaining. He's very knowledgeable about the material and he solicits and respects different interpretations of it. The workload and grading are intimidating at first but really are on par with most other courses.

This was probably my favorite class at UNC! Dr. Weidenfeld really cares about what hes teaching and makes it fun. I thought the simulation was going to be a little intimidating at first, but it was actually pretty chill and hilarious. If you have a chance to take this class, do it!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: LOVED this class! Political theory is tough, but Weidenfeld really breaks it down and makes it easy to understand. Very engaging lecturer and super interactive class. Papers and exams are tough, but if you go to office hours, do the readings, and go to class, you'll be fine.

Weidenfeld is very knowledgeable and a great lecturer. He is available and approachable and puts a lot of effort into his classes. In addition, Poli280 is the best class I've ever taken. You learn deeply about the subject matter and develop important skills while having fun with other students. The "Reacting to History" courses and Dr. W. are great

Dr. Weidenfeld is awesome. If you have the chance to take his class, do it. He's an engaging lecturer and clearly knows his stuff. Also! Take his "reacting to history" style classes! We took on founding fathers' roles and reenacted the constitutional convention. I've never learned more while having fun. You'll write a few papers, very doable.

He really cares about the class and puts in extra effort to make sure everybody has fun but also learns the material. The best professor I've had at UNC! There are a couple essays, a midterm, an essay project, and a final, but read a little bit for the papers and you'll be fine. Kind of a tough grader but the class is fun and worth it.

Probably one of the best teachers I have had at UNC. He truly cares about his students as well as the material and it really shows. Although you will have to do your part to get the work done, Professor Weidenfeld is a professor that is worth taking. Would highly recommend this class to anyone and everyone that can possibly take it
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Gives really good lectures that engages the class to understand the material. Essays are based on the readings. Flexible class schedule and final assessment, overall has fun with the class and is highly enjoyable. Would recommend for gen eds or satisfying political theory requirements for POLI majors
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This was easily my favorite class of the semester. Dr. Weidenfeld made class so enjoyable that I'm actually sad about the semester ending. He will definitely make you think and work hard both in and out of class, but he knows how to make the content engaging. Highly recommend taking a class with him before leaving Carolina.

He was by far my favorite professor this year. He was always enthusiastic about the material and made sure we were just as engaged. Overall, he created a really fun environment and it was a great break from all my other lecture heavy classes. The class is paper based but they're all short papers and he gives great feedback on them!

My favorite professor hands down. Hilarious and engaging, always looking to have fun with his students and create an interesting class. He is always willing to help students and wants them to succeed. He is very passionate about what he is teaching and it shows. You will have to write papers and read, but content is very interesting.
He is the best. The whole class is a simulated game in which you debate and act as the French and American revolution.

Amazing class. Philosophy based political science completely transformed into a discussion based class in modern terms. He is very funny and makes you understand concepts in today's context that blows your mind. Most informative, engaging, and fun class I've ever taken hands down, all thanks to this professor. Missing out if you don't take it.

I took his section because of the great reviews on here, but I would never take him again. He is a nice person and means well, but we are extremely behind other sections and are so close to the final. Notes are inadequate, lectures are unhelpful and insufferable to sit through, and there aren't enough external resources/ practice supplied.

Not sure what most of these reviews are on about. Although he is a great person, his lectures are incredibly confusing. You can barely hear him, he goes on long tangents on unimportant topics, and he generally makes no sense. Although his midterms can be easier than other sections, this just means the common final will be atrocious for you.

Math diva with a dog! Makes calc so approachable. Please go to his office hours because he is super helpful and passionate and caring. He's not the best at explaining things, but he'll try very hard. We love the effort! And his stories!!

While the class wasn't hard besides the final, which tanked my grade, do not take him as your 381 professor if you need to take 521 after. I am coming back to write this review because it has made 521 nearly impossible to understand, because he did not prepare us at all to build off the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Mccombs is a very kind person. I found his lectures to be pretty unhelpful, so I skipped a lot. The best part of the class are the MyLab assignments; they allow multiple attempts, so I ended up teaching most of the course content to myself. PREPARE TO TEACH YOURSELF EVERYTHING.

He's very entertaining, but not good at teaching large lectures. He's amazing one-on-one. He takes ages to grade things. I didn't know my midterm grade until the week before the final. He cancels class at the last minute constantly.

McCombs is a genuinely great, warmhearted guy who wants his students to succeed! He often shares stories of his family, childhood, and dogs during lectures. There is a lot of work outside of class you need to do, though, since lectures alone aren't really enough to fully understand the material.

2 tests + final = 90% of your grade

McCombs is THE GOAT and famous. take him you won't regret it; He's known for his high heels that he wears one time in class... He cancelled class 3 times and that was really good. However, you will have to learn some stuff by yourself because all he does is go through a slide show and just explain what is done.
TAKE THIS CLASS, TAKE THIS CLASS!!!

McCombs is a nice person, but an inadequate teacher. He repeatedly canceled class hours or minutes before the beginning of the class and did not finish teaching us all of the units necessary for the final. If you have the option to take this class with a different professor, DO IT.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: So nice. Lectures are pretty boring but they are straightforward. He cancels class from time to time and attendance is not mandatory.There are mylab homeworks for each unit, but they can be done in about 2 hours and they are due the night before the exam. There are only 2 tests which are simple/fair and then the final. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!!!!!!!

As a person, Professor McCombs is the best! As a professor, I found it hard at times to understand his teaching as he solves his work via talking it out, which isn't a good way for me to learn personally. Really nice guy, I think it depends on if you are able to meet halfway and learn portions from him, and self learn the rest yourself!

This man did not know this subject. He's probably great at other math concepts that he teaches, but he even said in lecture that he does not know this subject, and he has no idea what its purpose serves. I could go on, but I feel bad, he's a nice guy but for the love of GOD he should not teach this course.

if you don't have a religion, get one and pray. If you love listening to people yap about anything other than what you're supposed to be learning, he is fantastic for that! I had to teach myself everything, going to his class and attempting to follow his erratic lectures was a waste of time and money. Save yourself and take it with someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor McCombs cares a lot about his students and their feedback. In fact, for this course, he even handed out a feedback form based on RMP feedback he recieved asking what kind of class format we preferred. Very clear and helpful and is always willing to work with students to help them understand and improve. Awesome professor!

Best professor for MATH 381! Discrete is a hard topic no matter who teaches it, but McCombs made so much easier. He is really accessible out of class (having office hours almost everyday) which made really easy to get help. The midterms were fair but the final was extremely hard (I found teacher made part harder than common part).
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Easy during the semester except the exams are basically your whole grade. He is also very unorganized. The final was extremely hard and almost made me fail the course despite having a A the whole semester because he doesn't make the final the other professors do and he doesn't prepare you well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: McCombs is a good guy. His example problems and homeworks were very basic, so I did not feel prepared for the level of sophistication on the common final. I would recommend him, but definitely be prepared to do way more practice than the assigned homework if you want to absorb the material. Midterms were fair and lecture was pretty solid.

Literally the sweetest guy you will ever meet! I hate math so much, but I could definitely do this kind of "math." An A in this class is 90-100. He drops your 2 lowest HWs. If your final is better than your worst test, it replaces the score. Definitely take this class if you are a humanities major who has never been "good at math."
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great class for Non-stem majors, however it is somewhat hard to succeed in the class due to it being very test heavy and your grade depends on midterms and the final. McCombs is a very good teacher though and truly cares about his students.

Prof. McCombs was great. His lectures can be a bit disorganized, but you can truly tell he cares about his students. I enjoyed his lectures, and I would definitely take this course again. He is a fair grader.

He is so funny, but it is hard to understand material by his lectures. You practically have to teach yourself. 3 total exams, and 10% homework credit. Had no calc backing coming into it and it has been very hard. TA's help explain some, but you have to do a lot on your own! Other professors give you participation credit and he does not

His lectures are a bit disorganized and he speaks quietly but besides that, he is a very good professor and has a good heart. Grades very fairly and gives lots of partial credit. Make sure you read the textbook as some topics aren't covered in great detail. Overall a good teacher and a great guy.

Mark McComb's class was overall excellent. He gave detailed notes and slides in Canvas for each lesson, followed by corresponding homework assignments. However, the downside of this course was the lectures. The lectures consisted of McCombs reading off Canvas sides, which may not be useful or a great use of time for many students.

My whole entire heart to Mark. Truly. As a person and a professor. Workload is very fair, as are exams. Lots of office hours available, and he is a very engaging lecturer. 52% of your grade is midterms, 38% for final. 10% homework. Every kind thing you hear about him is true. I feel so lucky to have been his student.

Made his own study guides and practice problem sets (solved himself) for every exam, explicit about what you need to know/don't need to know, and his lectures are so well thought-out and detailed with examples, etc etc. The most caring prof I've EVER had, loved discrete so much bc of him. PLS take him if you can, it will make your life easier

Best professor for math 231. He gives study guides for all the tests, and those study guides outline everything that is on the test. He also gives a lot of partial credit for your work, and although his lectures sometimes feels confusing, he makes the tests very manageable. He's also a very fun person so it makes me want to come to class

Professor McCombs is truly one of the kindest and most understanding math professors. His lectures feel like a casual conversation, making the material much more approachable. Leverage unstuck ai alongside the practice worksheets he provides for great prep.
Great professor.

Mark truly is a kind individual. However, he is not a good lecturer. The class structure itself was disorganized with constant revisions to the course schedule and lack of consistent office hours. Test and homework scores took a month to receive back which left many students questioning where they stood in class.
Great class and great guy. By no means a super easy class but its great for non-STEM majors.
Super caring and awesome!!

(I only had him for half a semester, so that's what I am basing this off of). I thought that his lecture slides were helpful. The homework was harder than lecture examples and was around the same difficulty or easier than midterms (But doable). Have heard that people had difficulty contacting him. Lecture pacing wasn't that helpful.
Wish you recover soon and well! He is funny, has clear lecture and expectation, lenient, and understanding. He makes Calculus easy for you.
This man is the goat his stuff is very easy and he is very lenient just do the HW and review a little for the tests. The tests and FE exam are not difficult at all.

Prof. McCombs cares about teaching and cares about his students. Lectures feel more like a conversation between him and the students, so I felt like I really got to know him beyond being a professor. His slides have everything you need to know. Make sure you're doing practice problems and applying the material as you go.

Incredible professor. Clear explanations for difficult concepts, and makes lectures entertaining with anecdotes and jokes. Always willing to answer any questions you might have, and ensures that your question is answered before moving on. Couldn't recommend him enough.

Don't even need to talk about professor McCombs. He is exceptional! The most caring professor I have ever had. Please take him I gurantee that he is the best math professor you can take. Matthew, a TA in his class, is also the best TA I ever had. Both made this class one to remember!

This is the easiest math class you can take at UNC (professor calls it "math for tourists"). As long as you go to class, you're fine, and he's always available for office hours. Only graded by a few tests and one homework grade, but your lowest test grade can be replaced by doing better on the final. His lectures are hilarious and entertaining!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: McCombs is sweet and funny, but definitely grades a little bit harshly. You can have a very solid grasp on the content and still not do very well on exams. His notes are amazing, though his lectures can be a little confusing. Do the textbook problems and extra worksheets he gives; you really have to put in that extra effort to get an A.

I found this class EXTREMELY hard (I'm a math major plus scored the highest on 2/3 of the exams for context of difficulty). The exams tested random concepts. You can definitely take the class and still do well, but skip class and do the highlighted text book problems instead. Great partial credit, so show ALL your work/thinking. Slight curve.

Prof. McCombs is genuinely one of the kindest people ever. He is very understanding and really wants students to succeed. Midterms were not very hard at all. He makes PowerPoints for lectures and doesn't solve problems by hand in front of you, so if that's not your thing then it may make this class a bit tougher. But I rlly enjoyed this class!
The greatest professor there is.

McCombs is a great person that cares for his students but I EMPHASIZE DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS IF YOU RELY ON LECTURES, NOTES, OR ORGANIZATION. You have to 100% teach yourself as his notes make no sense and he goes on long tangents in class. he is very unorganized and slow with grades which made it hard to even know what material we should be learning

Professor McCombs tries his best, our semester he was having a hard time and still showed up with plenty of jokes. However, his teaching was clicking through slides, making it hard to actually learn the material. Tests are nothing like practice. Never answers emails but curves and is flexible with deadlines. Uma superiority!

Most understanding math professor ever. I don't like math, but the casual structure of his lectures was encouraging & made calculus approachable. He extends HW deadlines & provides his own practice worksheets (not graded) which are very helpful. Unlike other egotistic profs, he's sympathetic towards students who have real lives outside of school.

Professor McCombs gave great lectures, and was very clear and helpful in teaching the content. Tests are worth a lot in this class (final is 38% of your grade), but they're super straightforward. He can get behind in grading, but his lectures and resources made up for it. Easiest math class I've taken at UNC.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
There's no denying he's a likeable man, but not a great professor. Lectures were fine, but reading off a slide didn't help anyone. Many topics were not covered due to running out of time, HW was never graded on time to be helpful for the exam. Extremely scatter brained. 
If you need 381 for future math classes, take it with someone else.

He had personal issues this semester, but he was still so accommodating despite it. I really like him, and he tried to make the material in this class as digestible as possible. If you just study and memorize the methods he gives, you'll do good in this class. Beware, 90% of your grade are based on tests, so that does make it harder to do well.

I really wanted to like Prof McCombs cause he is a really cool guy, but I don't think his class is very helpful. He goes on long tangents which can be entertaining but wastes a lot of time. He also isn't great at explaining problems. You're graded almost entirely on exam scores. Not bad but would take with someone else if learning for first time.
Professor McCombs is a really great guy, but his lectures are not super helpful. He gives a fair amount of homework. He holds office hours. Gives extra credit.

Fair grading system with optional lectures overall make this class relaxed. However, homework can pile up. Lectures were informative but not very helpful for me since he often went "too in depth" for certain concepts rather than doing more practice problems. The two midterms were easy but the final was very difficult. Best prof for math 231.

His grading criteria are very straightforward; you're able to calculate your grade before the final. On the tests, he offers partial credit for work that proves you know what you're doing, even if you might end up at the wrong answer. The lectures are so entertaining and he really cares about students. Probably my favorite professor at UNC.

Let me say McCombs is a very caring professor. His lectures were well written but clicking through slides in math didn't really help us learn. He made typos on our final exam, forgot to give us a formula, and said he couldn't get an answer to a question. Great guy, just a bit scatter brained. Tests are worth a lot of your grade.

Mr. McCombs is a great professor and cares about each one of his students. You will need to put additional work into learning the material, but he provides so many resources and worksheets for extra practice. He hosts office hours a few times a week, moves back homework and test dates if needed, and heavily curves the final.

Professor Mccombs is an amazing guy but not the best professor. He is very caring and sweet to his students but his lectures are often unclear as he doesn't provide work and presents math on a powerpoint. During class, he would tell stories pertaining to his life and not math. He tends to curve grades and will extend homework deadlines if needed.

Mark is a VERY nice person, let me get that out of the way. I enjoyed his anecdotes and he also had a generous grading system and I thought all the tests were of a fair difficulty.

That being said, I don't think he is a good teacher pedagogically.  His lectures were just clicking thru slides w/o doing work live which doesn't help learning imo.

I have never been a good test taker when it comes to math exams, and 90% of your grade is composed of two tests and final ( no exaggeration).  Homework is 10% of your grade and is based on accuracy; there are no do-overs. There are very few grades to determine your final grade, making it difficult to succeed.

Attendance is totally optional. I only attended class on exam days and still received an A by studying the textbook and lecture slides on my own time. I definitely recommend MATH 118 with McCombs for non-stem majors to fulfill their Gen Eds. I do not consider myself good at math, yet found this class entirely manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor McCombs is an amazing person, he truly cares for his students. However, if you would not like to spend a lot of time outside of class trying to understand the material, you shouldn't take this course. His lecture slides are unclear, and he doesn't really lecture well. The class isn't organized very well either.

Mark has been the best math teacher I've ever had!!! The assignments are very easy if you pay attention in class, and can be done in literally 10 minutes sometimes. He made class fun to come to and is very understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The course structure is simple, and the lectures are always available online if you miss a class. Office hours need to be more consistent, and recitations can be unhelpful. Practice problems constantly and get clarification; McCombs will help you! He also gives away points and drops assignments as a bonus!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very sweet and understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Mark Mccombs is easily the most caring, respected professor on campus. It is clear from his lectures and teaching style that he cares about the well-being and success of his students, and this shines through during office hours, and in and out of the classroom. If you need MATH 231, make your schedule around Mccomb's section of it. He's worth it.
Great lectures! Mark makes calculus bearable. If you need MATH231 Mark is your guy!

This was the best professor I'll probably have in my entire life!! He is the kindest, funniest, most engaging, and most understanding guy. He truly wants all his students to succeed and treats us with so much respect. You would be sooooo lucky to take a class with him. Everyone loves him! I can't say enough good things :)

Professor McCombs is a great man, and can be a great professor depending on how good you are at math. His notes are a powerpoint that you click through and sometimes full steps can be unclear, however he is always accessible outside of class and would always meet with me outside of office hours if I needed it. Very easy to do well in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super funny and has a cute dog. He's very understanding and cares about his students. I hate math but if I pass this class it's only because I took McCombs, or else I would probably fail. His tests are a very heavy percentage of the grade which is a little scary (90%).

I had a different professor for calc 1 and got a 32 on my first exam. With McCombs for calc 2, I got a 95 on my first exam. His tests are very fair and wants you to succeed. His notes are the most helpful resource. Gives a lot of resources for practice. Use those & you'll do amazing on the exams. Funny guy and always answers questions in class.

Mark is one of the best professors and his origami class is amazing! If you have the opportunity to take it, DO IT! It's so easy and fun. All you do is fold paper and as long as you do the super easy, in-class assignments, you'll get an A. He doesn't take attendance so you don't have to go but then you'll have to do the assignments at home alone...

He is amazing! I was so scared taking calc because I'm not really a math person but McCombs makes the content digestible. He is also very flexible with due dates and cares a lot about his students. You can tell his passion is teaching and interacting with students. TAKE CALCULUS WITH THIS MAN!!!!!!!!!!!!!

Discrete SS1 online: McCombs might be the GOAT professor. He is down to earth, helps with any question (even hwk), and puts himself down to make us feel better when concepts are difficult to understand. He's sometimes late or just leaves in the middle of class, but no one really minds. Notes are laid out on Sakai and you can tell he loves his job.

The best professor I have encounter at UNC! He is literally the best. I am currently taking him over the summer and though the work load is a little heavy and fast paced, he makes it so easy to manage. I got a B- in pre-calc, but with Mccombs, I scored a 86 on my first exam. HE IS WORTH IT! He actually cares about his students.

He's an extremely nice person but his class is hard. Homework assignments took hours to do and he's not great at lecturing - he goes 0 to 100 real quick. Problems on exams can be harder than what you've learned/practiced and those are usually worth a lot. Often he posted answer keys and they would be wrong, he seemed confused a lot of the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Seriously for someone who isn't amazing at Math, take McCombs. When I first saw the coursework on the FDOC I assumed I was going to fail. He makes everything so easy and while yes some of the tests have 1-2 questions that were a lot harder than the study guide overall he sets you up very well. He also curved our final scores, 95% class passed.
McCombs is amazing! The best professor at UNC, he really cares about his students.

Mark is one of the kindest prof's I have had at UNC! This class is a super easy QR gen-ed, and Mr. McCombs obviously cares about his students, their success, and UNC basketball!! The class is only graded on MSL homework and 2 tests and a final, but the final replaces one test grade if you need it. His study guides are super helpful for the tests!
Took his origami seminar. It was super easy, relaxing, and the perfect mental break from all my other stem classes. Mark is a cool guy. He's the man.
This man is great, and has a lot of passion for what he does. This is probably the best FYS at UNC!!!
Literally the best professor there is. He genuinely cares about every student and makes sure that is known. Class is not hard AT ALL. Super easy QR
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: An amazing professor that cares about his student. We are halfway through the semester and he made me feel confident in this class.

I wrote the review from February 2nd and felt a need to give him a slightly better rating. He did contact me, although hours later, to ask me to meet him the next day and allowed me to turn the assignment in after our meeting. Still not too happy, but it was better

We are a month into the semester and he has changed office hours within 20 mins of it starting at least 10 times (was in the zoom waiting room when he canceled). Asked him to meet at another time, & he said he would at 1. It's 30 minutes past with no email, no contact, no cancelation. Feels like he doesn't care abt his students. DONT TAKE HIM

Though he had to step out halfway through the semester for health reasons, Professor McCombs is one of my favorite teachers at UNC. His lectures are informative and often injected with humor, he makes sure to properly prepare everyone for the tests, and he likes to end class with pictures of his dog. An awesome teacher who I highly recommend.

Mark is a great professor. I only had him for half of the semester, but while he was here, calc was one of my favorite classes. His notes are extremely clear and easy to understand. Midterms were also clear and lots of partial credit was given. The common final was hard, but doable too. Practice problems are key for this class.

Mark is a very emotional professor who cares about his students. His notes and test practices are very good, I can learn almost everything from his notes, and if you can do a dozen test practices well, then you can do very well in the test.

HARDEST CLASS EVER. Came in as a math major, thats gone. Failed the midterms, saving grace is that he replaced my lowest midterm with the final bc its higher. so my final ended up being 62% of my grade, that was only because of a 12 hr proof grind session. Thought I would get the F but ended up with a C-, he bumped it up to a C. Nice guy though.
Prof. McCombs is a really cool guy. His lecture can be unstructured sometimes but it is not hard to follow him. Also, everyone with 90+ gets an A, which is truly amazing.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: McCombs is a great person and his tests are easy. DO the test study guides and memorize how to solve those problems, they are basically the test. McCombs was out the last 1/3 of the semester due to any injury and the class was awful after that The final exam was HARD mostly because McCombs was out but also because he didn't make the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Nice guy, but was very slow at teaching and only read off slides. Class skipped a bunch of topics that every other discrete class covered, so if you want to learn discrete math comprehensively, take another professor. Tests were fair if you study. Not much homework.

He shows there's a difference btwn being a nice person and being a good professor. Unfortunately, i think I would've done better if I had a diff. prof. He has all hws (which is not even many problems) due the night before the tests, and this didn't help me practice outside of class. Plus his teaching style with powerpoints is worse than i expected

Mr. McCombs is truly a great guy, he is so funny and I can tell he cares about us. I am not good at math so the structure of this class was a little too loose and unstructured for me- the tests weigh a LOT so beware. He was out of class the last full month of class before final (due to valid medical reasons), so we sorta got screwed with the final.

McCombs is more understanding than most professors but generally, my style of learning did not fit his style of lecturing, where he just reads off his notes without working out problems. I honestly learned more from the substitute professors than from McCombs himself. The class is graded on two tests (28% each), homework (10%), and a final (34%).

Prof. McCombs was a very relaxed professor, and math 118 is very straightforward. I did not find the material difficult, as long as I studied a bit. He goes off topic during class a lot, but seems to be very kind. I probably would not take one of his classes again, it was test-heavy, and did not feel rewarding.
He goes off track a lot but he is a super nice guy and cares about your well-being. His lectures are great and he keeps students engaged.

Please do not take this class. I read the reviews and thought it would be easy and it is the opposite. Professor McCombs is a nice human being, but likes to go off topic during lectures and doesn't reply to emails. Tests are weighted really heavily and his testing format is weird, so it's a recipe for disaster. Do NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.
Mark is a gem of a professor, and a wonderful choice for calc 1-3... Ask about Uma!
Very good Prof. Easy class. No textbook. The grading policy is very understanding and he tries to make sure everyone receives a good grade. Best math prof at UNC for sure.

MATH381 is a super confusing and scary class but if you can take it with McCombs DO IT! Hes your best option! This class was not easy at all, but he does try his best to make it better though. Hes super funny and relatable, but sometimes at a cost. He often goes on tangents and skips around material in a confusing way. But hes still a good prof!

Mark seems like a nice guys and is fun to talk to, but his online teaching skills are subpar. He didn't stay on topic, which made it difficult to stay engaged and follow the learning material. Additionally, he is inaccessible by email. I might have liked him better in-person, but I wouldn't recommend taking his online class.

Professor McCombs was honestly a really nice guy but SO boring to listen to. It was so hard to focus on what he was saying. He did provide a lot of great resources and was always available during office hours and via email.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: BEST PROF. Mark is so caring and always tells the best stories. Every class is a show! I was more than fine skipping classes occasionally and just reviewing the slides. He gives a LOT of partial credit on exams, and his grading scale is super generous (90-100  A). Take him if you can!!!!!!!

If you like dad-esque jokes and stories strung into your lectures, this is the professor for you. McCombs is, by far, one of my favorite professors because he genuinely wants us the learn the material, explains the concepts in simple ways, and tells fun stories (ask about the platform shoes)! Tests are not bad & straightforward.

Mark is such a 10/10 professor!! I took this class to just get a credit, but I ended up really enjoying it- the tests are easy if you pay attention to lectures. Mark is nice and funny and always talks to us before class and I liked that he did that instead of just jumping into the lesson. Plus he always shows off his pets which is a crowd pleaser.

Frankly, I was terrified to take MATH 232. However, Dr. McCombs made it worth it! Review his slides, worksheets, and practice exams, and you'll do well. He's super caring and does a fantastic job of making complicated topics easy. I never post on RateMyProf, but I wanted everyone to not worry too much (like I initially was). Only take Mark!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: He's a great person but a HORRIBLE TEACHER. Lecture feels like a waste of time because he gets distracted easily. I can see he's loved by many but as a teacher, he's awful, especially for math (he teach math with powerpoints instead of writing out work......).
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: McCombs is the best!! He is so funny and you will definitely meet his dog. Makes class fun and engaging. If you have to take a math class definitely try to get him!!!
Like your cool, hip grandparent.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Mark is an incredibly fun individual. He had a bit of problems this semester with family issues and was unable to attend class, but made sure we still got lectures on the material in an appropriate timely manner. He was very understanding of our problems with online school and made taking math online enjoyable. I could not recommend him more!!

I loved Professor McCombs! I was not a fan of math at all until I got to his class and he just made learning so much easier. The class was so much fun and he was very easy to talk to. The class is test heavy, but it is not impossible and if you work for it u will definitely get higher than a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: I hate math and had to take Calc 1 and 2 for my major. I took calc 1 with him and he made every day fun and digestible. I refused to take calc 2 with anyone else. There were a few times when he would re-teach a whole class because no one understood and he said that was on time. Also he is hilarious.
Take Math 118!!! Mark is such a sweetie. Easiest class I've ever taken, though maybe it was because this was all online. Mark is the most genuine and caring professor I have ever met.

I love math so calc 1 wasn't too bad for me, but McCombs is an awesome professor and he made calc at UNC bearable! The exams are straightforward and aren't meant to trick you. Make you sure you pay attention in lecture and PRACTICE problems! He's a cool guy and is very passionate about calc/math. Definitely put in the effort to learn to do well

McCombs is a great guy, funny yet accessible and his class was one of the best parts of an online semester. Deadlines are flexible. But he gets diverted a lot during lectures, and though his stories are hilarious sometimes there are too many. The lack of deadlines also makes it easy to procrastinate, so don't take unless you can keep a schedule.

Professor McCombs was absolutely amazing and always made class enjoyable. He always tries to relate to students, and is understanding of the stress of school. He is very flexible with hw assignments. The only complaint I have is how much of our grade depending on the final. The class avg on the final was a 66 and it counted for 38% of our grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Amazing person, cares for his students. Class is loose structured and deadlines as well, he ended up extending the homework deadline until the last day of class. Very accommodating in general and answers questions very well. Would recommend more if you have previous knowledge of the subject.

I really don't like math. That being said, I looked forward to every lecture that I had with Professor McCombs. He is such a caring and funny guy who makes calc a digestible class. His classes are quite unstructured and he tells many stories, so if you require structure his teaching style might not be for you. Online 231/232 was tolerable bc of him

Mark McCombs was a great choice. His lectures were recorded and he provided so many resources along with ample office hours. Your grade is heavily influenced by your midterms and final exams so be sure to do well on those two assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor McCombs was very down to earth and kind, however, if I had not taken calculus in the past, I would have struggled a lot in this class. The lectures were unfocused and we only covered about two or three practice questions per lecture. There's a time and place for that, but I felt very unprepared when it came to the final exam.

One of the nicest people you'll ever meet. He likes to tell stories and make things personal, and sometimes he'll go off on a tangent and only does 2 questions in a class period. He gives you 24 hours and open notes on tests, but that hurt me when I had to take the final in 3 hours with no notes and no calculator. There are both pros and cons here.

While the lectures could get a little off-topic, McCombs clearly cares about all of his students and wants them to succeed. He gives very generous partial credit on exams and his grading scale is also very generous.

Prof. McCombs is a very caring guy. As long as you do your best and follow along with the lectures (that he records & puts on Sakai) you'll do fine. He's super lenient with deadlines & assignments and wants to accommodate every student. I despise math but was able to pass with almost no issue, all thanks to McCombs.

He is so amazing! Very funny and always there to lighten up class and help us learn. Calculus is always hard, but he was very accommodating and tried his best to give us extra help this year due to the circumstances. Everyone in our class loved him and his dog Uma!
Great and funny professor and class :)

Dr. McCombs is simply excellent. He made sure to answer every question a student asked him during class, and it was abundantly clear that he wanted all of his students to succeed. Genuinely kind and caring, and a very capable instructor too. His dog, Uma, made regular appearances as well!

Professor McCombs made me excited to go to class. Lectures are often times off topic, and I did self-study way more than I learned from notes. However, he is such an understanding person and is so so patient. Grades slowly, but generously. Your grade is pretty much all tests, but he is straightforward about content and practice matches the exam.

I would most recommend this teacher for those who are very bad at math or those very good. For those very bad, McCombs is patient and really works hard to help you understand. For those very good, his teaching style allows you to follow your own learning style. Overall, amazing teacher. About COVID: VERY understanding about tech issues

This class was online for Fall 2020. All of our midterms were open note and you had the whole day to take them. He does tend to tell a lot of stories during lectures, so I preferred learning at my own pace and if needed, all lectures were recorded. Participation was optional for class and recitation, and grades were two midterms, final and pearson.
What a king. He's so respectful and funny and will always help with questions. Hands down the best professor I have ever experienced. Take him if you can!

McCombs is the most understanding, hilarious, and down to earth professor in the math department, if not UNC. Calculus isnt the easiest subject and McCombs understands that. He makes class entertaining and ensures youre learning things. Any complaints I have for this class are due to other professors trying to tell McCombs what to do. 10/10 class

Professor McCombs is a savior to the Math Department. Tests got extensions due to power outages, and in many classes, he would spend the entire time answer questions we had on the past lectures. Lots of examples were given to us and MyMathLab used more for practice and completion rather than correctness on the first try, as homework should be.
Dr. McCombs is a true gem. He truly cares about his students and is very accessible outside of class. He will help you learn mathematics.

Easily the best professor to grace the math department. He is very caring and accommodating (sometimes a bit too much for my level). He is great at explaining concepts and truly cares about his students. I also took his Math 89 seminar, which was great too. If you need a math credit or easy math class, I would take him over anyone.

Math 381 was a very confusing class. However, Mark allowed us to have around 24 hours to take each of the tests, which was great. It was also open notes, so thank god for that. The only downside that I had for McCombs is that he would occasionally not show up to class or start class late. Also, sometimes he can make problems confusing.

The hype about McCombs is REAL!!! 381 can be really confusing, but McCombs is always very clear about the concepts he is explaining, and is really kind as well. Fair tests and homework. Honestly, if you read the textbook before and do his practice worksheets you will succeed. If you're struggling, go to office hours, he's a damn LEGEND

Mark is as great of a guy as he is a prof. Hes funny and a good lecturer. He tries to put in content in a different light, often with visuals, that really helps students who are confused. I was always intrigued with his origami and videos of his dog, Uma. 232 will make you put in work, but Mark was a crutch I dont think I couldve done without.

What a great guy. McCombs was such an understanding professor and I truly enjoyed math class with him. He explains hard topics in a very understandable manner and has very fair assessments. At times he was a bit difficult to get ahold of, but I am really glad I took him. Plus his dog is adorable!

I honestly do not understand the hype behind McCombs. He is an incredible person and funny, but I found it way more worth my time to not go to lectures. However, tests are fair and it is not hard to do well on them.
I hate math, but McCombs made it so much better. He is super funny and approachable. I like how he doesn't lecture over anyone's head like some STEM professors do!

He really cares about students and it shows! Lectures are funny and he does his best to be entertaining. Grading was extremely reasonable and i would take again. My only complaint is that because of COVID we dropped most of the last unit which I need to learn for future courses, but nobody was expecting this all to happen!

McCombs is legit the GOAT. He genuinely wants to see his students do well and succeed in his class. He does everything he can (especially during quarantine) to help us out and is very understanding of the difficulties of life. He also has an amazing grasp on the materials and teaches the most challenging concepts in ways that makes them seem simple
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: This man is a Carolina gem, and he shaved his head to teach us math. He works extremely hard as a teacher and is insanely caring about his students. He teaches you how to think about math, and grades generously so long as you can show that you understand the material. Overall this class was awesome and McCombs helped me remember that math is cool.
only reason I passed calc 1 with an A. take any class you possibly can with this man.

Professor McCombs is an amazing teacher. You will not regret taking his class. His notes are the best math notes I've ever seen, if that makes any sense, that basically take all the crucial info from the textbook. He cares so much for his students that it might make you cry, like it almost made me. I finished with a 95+ .

McCombs is the best professor I've ever had. He tries to make the material as easy to understand as possible. He is so kind & loves to tell anecdotal stories about his life to break up the monotony of math. It's so obvious that he really cares about his students and loves what he does. I took MATH 231 & 118 with him and couldn't recommend him more.

Mark is a stand-up guy and one of the most genuine people I've ever met. He's clear from the get-go on what to expect on tests and he doesn't throw any curveballs. He was super understanding when we switched to remote learning and I still learned a lot from his zoom lectures. TAKE HIM!!!

Professor McCombs cares so much about his students succeeding - he is very specific on what he wants from us and doesn't throw any curveballs on the exams. As long as you know how to do what's on the study guide, you'll be solid. Also, he was super accommodating during this whole pandemic so props to him on that!

I can not say enough good things about Mark!!! He is simply the best!! I was intimidated to take this class as I have no experience with origami or Illustrator, but he was so sweet and always willing to help me outside of class!! He is also so funny and I loved hearing all his stories. Take this class!!! You won't regret it!!

Second semester with Mark. He's literally the best professor I've had! His slides are extremely useful! Calc3 can be daunting for some but he made it easy to digest with the slides and 3d diagrams! Study guides are helpful and doesn't test on anything that isn't in the slides. Also drops your first test if you do better on the final. TAKE HIS CLASS

Mark McCombs is a true GEM and easily one of the best professors I've had at UNC. Not only is he amazing at explaining calculus, but his personality is 11/10 and he truly cares about his students. I love that guy so much I took 2 calc classes with him and wish I could take another. He also runs an IG for his dog Uma and takes her to campus!!!

Mark is hands down one of the best professors I've ever had at UNC. Calc can be really difficult, but he finds a way to make it make sense. He genuinely cares about his students, and it shows. I seriously considered taking differential equations with him, even though I don't need it for my major. That's how much I love him as a teacher!

Prof McCombs is amazing! As long as you use the study guide and do the homework the tests are not crazy difficult. He also tells amazing stories, makes super cool art, and has an adorable dog. Also, his transition to online because of COVID was very smooth and he has been very understanding and flexible with the weird circumstances. 1000/10

No professor has EVER been so caring. His class is so big, yet he makes such an effort to connect with each student. Whenever you email him questions he responds by the end of the day with a written out pdf that explains the concept with examples. He is so devoted to you learning the material and is an amazing teacher of it.

Mark is the man. He genuinely cares so much about students and is always there to help you. The best professor Ive had and I would take more calc classes with him (even though I dont need it). The tests are very reasonable and he provides study guides/helpful worksheets. TAKE A CLASS WITH HIM!!!

By far the best professor I have ever had at UNC. He makes expectations super clear, teaches in an easy to follow way, entertains his class, cares deeply about his students, and doesn't make us do much busy work.

Math89 can be fun and easy with Mark but also pretty boring. Hardly any homework, and Mark is willing to slow down and help people who need it in class or during office hours. Not the class to take if you want something interesting, but he does make the class pretty easy and doesn't want to stress any students out.

The best professor I have ever had at UNC. Great person and wants students to succeed. He does not judge and is more than willing to help if you make mistakes. I would take him for every single math class if I could

Mark is definitely the best professor I've had at UNC. Aside from being a great lecturer and teacher of difficult concepts, he is so caring for all his students and wants everyone to succeed. His class is definitely hard, but that's only because the material itself is a lot and often hard to understand. I always look forward to going to his class.

Mark McCombs is without a doubt the best professor I have had at UNC. Going into this class with the notion that "MATH 232 is the most failed class at UNC" is definitely very daunting, however, McCombs really does his best at setting students up for success in his classes. 1000/10 recommend. Plus he has a cute dog.

Prof McCombs is by far the best professor I have had at UNC! His lectures are clear and engaging, sprinkled with funny stories about him and his dog, and pictures of his incredible artwork. He gives very little homework, posts all the notes and handouts online as well as study guides for each exam. Exams are short but very fair. Great class!!

Mark McCombs is undoubtedly one of the best professors/teachers I have ever had! If you are looking for a math professor I cannot recommend Professor McCombs enough. Not only would he teach the class incredibly well, but he would also crack many jokes and tell us stories about his dog Uma! 10/10, will take again.

Mark is the man! I haven't taken a calculus class in a long time and Mark really helped with catching up to speed and understanding the material. He doesn't overcomplicate anything and is a godsend for the department. His class made me drop all my plans just to take calc 3 with him next semester. He's THAT good. Study guides are really helpful too

Prof. McCombs is by far one of the best professors I've had here. Math 232 is hard, but he thoroughly explains all of the topics and wants you to succeed. If you have to take math 232, definitely take it with him!! He's hilarious during class and makes it enjoyable!
Take this class its amazing!

Definitely take this class if you are not a STEM major. You learn obscure things, but it is seriously one of the easiest classes I've taken at UNC. We only had 5 homework assignments all semester that weren't too hard. Mccombs can get off topic during lecture, but go to office hours or recitation and everything will be made crystal clear.

Prof. McCombs (or Mark), is one of the best professors I've ever had. His class, Math 118, is great for non-science majors and Mark makes it engaging and fun. Although the material is difficult at times, Mark makes sure that you are prepared for the exams and prides himself on never going more in-depth on material than necessary. Mark is a UNC gem!

Professor McCombs is undoubtedly the best professor I have had at UNC. Prior to taking the class, I had heard Math 232 was one of the hardest and one of the most failed classes at UNC. The difficulty level is certainly high, but Prof. McCombs makes it an enjoyable experience. He genuinely cares about his students and wants to see everyone succeed.

The rare class and professor that will appeal to both those who love math and those who hate it (that's me). He clearly has a profound appreciation for mathematics (especially the artistic element) but is understanding of the fact that the people who are taking MATH 118 do not, at least initially, share that appreciation. Also, hilarious. Easy too.

Mark McCombs is the best professor I have ever had. He cares about his students so much and genuinely cares about you doing well in his class. His power points and lectures are very easy to follow, and there are never any surprises on the test as long as you study and do the test reviews. Highly recommend taking his class.

Mark McCombs is a genuinely caring educator who enjoys seeing his students learn. It's possible that others could have taught Discrete Math more excellently, but his instruction is quite sufficient if you're willing to study on your own as well. Taking his class was a rewarding experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. McCombs is a wonderful and hilarious professor. while 381 is a somewhat difficult class, he made it easy to take. Your grade only depends on your homework, two tests and final, so everything weighs much. Prepare to work hard because by no means 381 would be a elementary class. The tests can be tough, but if you put effort you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The skill and genuineness of this man cannot be overstated! He's amazing, and the best professor I've ever had for math. He explains concepts super well, has great resources, and is very kind and understanding of students. 100% solid choice.

One of the best professors I've had at UNC. I took him for discrete math over summer session one; he gives very clear expectations and explains the concepts well. If you make use of the resources he provides and put in the effort, you will definitely succeed!

Mark is one of the most caring professors I have had at UNC. I was terrified to take Calc, but I took it with Mark and the class was a breeze. He makes it very clear what he expects of you, and really wants to make sure that every student understands what is going on in the class. If you have to take this class, take it with Mark.

If you're crazy enough to take calc at UNC, TAKE IT WITH MCCOMBS! He's extremely caring and if you put in the work, you'll do just fine. He replaces your lowest exam score with your final if the final is higher which is how I was able to escape with a good grade. TAKE CALC WITH MCCOMBS!!!

McCombs is one of the best teachers at UNC. He posts his lectures with step-by-step examples so that if you miss anything in class you will be able to easily go back over what you missed. During lectures he will make sure to answer any questions that you have and work as hard as he can to make sure you understand the material. Take him if you can.

I took calc one with mark over the summer (5 weeks) and he cut a lot of material out due to time constraints. If you do not need any calc above calc 1 then i suggest taking mark because it really is an easy A if you put in the slightest effort.
