He is a goofy man but i do not think his class would prepare you for calc 2 especially at unc.

McCombs is a great choice for Math 231. He posts all of his notes online, which makes attendance optional, however, he is a very funny lecturer, so you will miss out by skipping too many classes. The tests are extremely fair and he will drop a few of your lowest homeworks. If you have taken Calc before, this class will be very easy to do well in.

McCombs is fantastic. He's a teaching professor, not a research professor, which makes him available to actually help students. It's clear that he cares about us doing well. He's also a genuinely nice and funny person outside of class. Discrete is a pretty feared class, but I understood the material because of him.

Professor McCombs is one of the best professors I had at Carolina. Truly cares about his students' success. Super, open, fun-loving guy, and good at explaining complex concepts. Literally changed my Math 232 afternoon class to a morning class just so I could have McCombs. Highly recommend!

McCombs is just an icon. Makes the material understandable and he is a really interesting person. He gets off topic some and speaks of his time spent on mtv, his heart attack and most importantly his dog, Uma. The class is truly enjoyable and has been one of my favorite classes.

If you're planning on taking calc, take it with McCombs. I hated calculus in high school and was dreading taking it again but McCombs wants everyone to succeed and enjoy calc so he explains each example as clearly as possible and is willing to work with students to master difficult concepts. He definitely prepared me well for calc 2.

Mark is an amazing teacher and person in general. He somehow makes calculus somewhat interesting and genuinely cares about his students. His class is pretty easy and he's a very fair grader, dropping several homework grades and giving us a curve after the final. Go to office hours and get to know him! He has a lot of funny stories.

McCombs is the best professor I've had at UNC, he's very caring and WANTS you to pass. He works with you and is super understanding. Attendance isn't taken during lecture, but may be taken during the recitation, and missing class is to your disadvantage since calculus can be a difficult subject. He loves teaching and his students.
Amazing prof! You HAVE to take him. He can be funny at times, and he's very caring. For this class you didn't really have to show up, just look at the powerpoints.

Mark is such an amazing professor for 231, he takes the time to explain topics that students are unclear on. He always has a great attitude and keeps his lectures upbeat and funny which is saying a lot for a calc class. He also does add some personal elements and speaks about his life and actually tries to connect with his students.

Mark Mccombs is my main man. He not only cared about our class but taught well and fixed issues with our online homework in a timely manor. Mark drops your lowest exam and homework grades for the semester and his tests are fair and on the content he teaches. He provided us with study guides on the exams and gave us the opportunity to learn calculus

Professor McCombs is a great professor. He is very understanding of circumstances going on in your life outside of class. This professor is easy to approach with questions about the material and truly wants to get to know his students.

I was super scared to take calculus as Pre-Calc was very hard to me and I had never taken calc before but Professor McCombs made me feel very confident in the material and was always able to explain ideas clearly and accurately. I would definitely take again.
Great professor. He does a really good job explaining problems. Class attendance does not matter. He is very good about posting lecture notes online and he's very accessible outside of class

At first I was unsure whether he would be a good teacher or not, but he has definitely helped me understand calc better. He explains things well and gives good example problems although you still have to do extra practice problems outside of class to do well on the tests. The tests were difficult, but doing practice problems and homework helped.

Any teacher that includes memes in their study guides deserves respect. McCombs is a swell guy; he doesn't assign excessive homework and his lectures are extremely interesting and to the point. If you took calc in high school, you'll be fine. Even if you didn't, he's such a great professor that you'll fall in love with the subject.

I love this guy. He is really an outstanding professor. For all you non-math people, he is the one for you. He cares about his students. He believes math is the real magic. He's pretty darn funny sometimes too. He drops the three lowest homework grades and replaces your lowest test grade if your final exam score is higher. Absolutely amazing.

Dr. McCombs is the man! He recognizes most of the people taking this class are non-math majors and makes it so that you can easily pass. There is only one homework assignment due every 2 weeks, so there is not a lot of outside work. Recitation attendance is not required and this class is very manageable.

Mark McCombs is possibly the most down to earth faculty member you will find in UNC's math department. He's really accessible outside of class and is pretty hilarious. I made a D on my first test, but was able to pick up my grade to B. You should definitely check out his office, it's awesome.

Mark is a really nice guy, and I think he really cares about his students. This past semester he cancelled a lot of classes, and I don't think he adequately prepared us for the final. He doesn't return emails, but he's very accommodating in person. The webassign homework was overly difficult, and his examples in class are way easier than his tests

McCombs as good as it gets for proffesors. I took him for Calc 1 and now 118. He doesnt try to trick you, only test your true understanding of the material. Grades on a 10 point scale. Best of the Best. Take him you wont regret it

Material is pretty easy, and McCombs is really sweet! Great for non-math majors and people who may struggle with other math classes. 2 tests, about 7 WebAssigns, and the final. He replaces your lowest test score with the final if you do better on the final! Recitations are only for doing homework, so they are pretty much optional. Would recommend!!

Professor McCombs was a really nice guy and made the course material easy, but class was cancelled a lot and there definitely could've been more content covered in the time we had. Really nice guy and easy QR credit though!
I LOVE THIS MAN. So cute, you never have to go to class (if he doesn't cancel it) and replaces your lowest grade. If you aren't good at math, for sure take this class. you won't regret it!

Prof. McCombs is a nice guy, but he is harsh about grades and isnt very caring. I missed an exam because of a medical emergency (that my doctor wrote him a note for) and he still wouldnt let me take the exam and gave me a zero. Luckily, your final replaces your lowest grade, but if he had let me take that exam, I wouldve done way better.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Mr. McCombs was the GOAT! He is the sweetest guy ever and he cares for each of his students so much. He's very understanding and willing to help you with anything. Im not a big fan of math but he made it a whole lot more bearable with his sense of humor and kindness. Take his class!!

This professor is a great guy who cares about the material he teaches. He understands that this particular class (MATH118) is for non science/math majors so he does not try to make the class super difficult. The recitations are only mandatory on test days and the homework takes no longer than 20 minutes a week.  Overall the class was an easy A.

Generally MATH 110 is taught by graduate students, but Mr. McCombs was the head of the MATH 110 department when I took it so he made the exams that all of the sections took. I stopped going to class after the first exam because the web assigns will prepare you for his tests. Just know how to do the web assigns before the exam and it's an easy A.

Mark was a really great teacher and he makes sure to care for his students. If you have any questions whether in class or out, he will definitely be willing to help. He was also pretty funny so that made class a bit interesting. Definitely recommend 10/10.

Mark really cares about his students and genuinely wants them to succeed. Coming from someone who never really cared for math, Mark teaches in a way that is easy to understand and he is usually available when you need help. Only downside to this class were the webassign homeworks. Overall, great professor.

He is the best professor I've ever met in the math department. If you didn't miss too many classes, you'd definitely pass. The exams were not hard and there's not much homework. He gave really great lectures and plenty of time in class for review.
Great teacher! seriously recommend him. He is helpful and kind. I am a student-athlete and he is great about making up tests and understanding when you need to be away. TAKE MATH 110 FROM HIM!!!

Brilliant teacher; understands how to teach math; had him over the summer for calc 1, and he taught a lot of material well in a short period of time; keeps class interesting; actively works to improve his teaching method

Mark is a really nice guy and willing to help if you ask, but he cancels classes a lot and doesn't provide much time for hands-on work except prior to exams. Lectures do not help with hw. His teaching style just did not work with my learning style-had to hire a tutor and use math center to understand. Stay away unless you are good in math.

McCombs is a great guy, and it really comes across in his teachings. He's passionate about math, and that may sound like it would make for an uncomfortable class experience, but i was very happy with him in Discrete. Tests are pretty fair if you study the homeworks, which are easy 100s. He also curved our course grades up at least somewhat.
McCombs is great! This FYS was super fun and easy. Would definitely recommend.

McCombs is a great professor and a great guy. He was willing to help out if asked, and definitely cares about his students. His tests are very difficult, however. Be prepared to work hard, this course is far from a easy A.

McCombs is a great guy.  He is so funny and explained the material well.  Super nice and always there if you need extra help.  Bit of a slow grader, but not so much that it bothered me.  Definitely take him if you have the chance.

McCombs had a really rough semester, but he still found a way to be a great professor. He's a really nice guy and he loves his school. Homework is given weekly, but you complete it in recitation so it's an easy A.  Will bump up your grade if he can. Not super responsive with emails, but he really cares about his students' success.
McCombs is cool and relatable and is very thorough and clear in his lectures. His class is very easy and great for humanities majors (like myself).

Professor McCombs describes his course as "for people who want to learn math and live to tell about it." If you want an easy math that makes sense in the concrete and is designed for humanities majors, I would strongly recommend this class.

Professor McCombs is very funny and likable. The material was pretty easy but be careful because he grades tests very strictly. You don't really even have to go to class since all the notes are posted online.

HE IS AMAZING! I had the absolute best time in Math 110. I would take any course taught by Mr. McCombs! If you struggled with math or simply don't enjoy it, I recommend taking a course with Mr. McCombs because he is truly helpful and committed to his students. If you do the assigned work, you will be absolutely fine.
GREAT PROFESSOR. FUNNY.  Webassign math homework was way harder than the test. Test  SUPER EASY. Lectures pretty easy to follow. He doesn't take participation but lectures are essential
Super easy A. Also fun!
Math sucks at UNC
Great Professor!
Great Teacher!
He is an easy teacher and a relatively interesting lecturer with few quizzes or tests.
He made class very easy and went slowly. Almost painfully so. However, his method of teaching made the class seem so easy. Definitely recommend.
Very easy class as long as you do the practice problems before every test. No tricks or overly difficult questions on tests.

Professor McCombs is funny and nice, but he misses class too much, leaving us to be taught by second-rate professors. He's so far missed 5 classes and that makes it difficult to really learn the material.

I hate math. Like, I hate it. But from the first day with McCombs, I didn't mind going to class. His lectures are straightforward and if you just complete the practice questions before the test and understand how you did them all, you will literally make an A every time. He's very helpful with those who need it and genuinely wants you to succeed.

McCombs is a wonderful professor who really cares about his students doing well and does the most to make sure they succeed. His teaching is clear and this class was extremely easy for me, so if you need an easy math credit, this is the class to take with McCombs.
Professor McCombs is simply amazing! I would recommend anyone to take a mathematics course with him. He made it fun, easier, and actually interesting!
Easy going, easy test, easy homrwork and very flexible

He is one of the best math teachers I have ever had. He explained things in a way that was clear and for someone who sucks at math, (i.e. me), it was refreshing.  He was always super helpful and willing to work with you to help you understand the material.
He was okay.
One of the best math professors I have ever had - if you have the opportunity to take a class with him, I highly recommend it! Amazing at explaining calculus - he makes it seem simple and fun!

Easily the best professor I've had at UNC so far.  Mr. McCombs makes a fairly tedious and challenging subject interesting and understandable without diluting the material.  His lectures are wonderfully structured and worth the full 50 minutes every time.
You will know calculus after him!

Prof. McCombs is a SPECTACULAR professor.  He is extremely personable, approachable, helpful, and dedicated to teaching.  He will do whatever he can to help you succeed. If you have any trouble, go to office hours and he'll clear things up.  The class is fairly easy, and exams are extremely fair.  But, you will learn the material.

Great Professor! Funny and knew me by name...so he was intimate. Class was pretty easy. He taught lessons on Mon. and Fri.--we did our own thing on Wed.(HW problems)! So you really did not have to come to class. He is very down to earth and this was one of my favorite classes/teacher this semester! <3 McCombs
Great professor, no tricks or anything to confuse you. I mean he wrote the book! He went to UNC so he knows exactly how students think. Great man and professor, highly recommended.
No Comments
Awesome teacher, pretty much the best at the school, funny in a boring, geeky way, very clear and helpful made the hardest class in the school pretty easy.
Best professor for this class. very clear with examples, homework and tests are based on what you do in class.  plus, he's funny.
Awesome teacher.  Easy to talk to and even easier to understand.  If you have any problems, go to his office hours and he can clear anything up.

Little know class you can't take for credit, but it's offered by McCombs and his buddy throughout the year.  McCombs won't even acknowledge it's existence unless you know the password.  When you're in his office tell him you want to learn "all things assymtotical" and for the "earthlings to behave."
Good teacher. helps out with homework during office hours.  Helps explain stuff.

I have taken A LOT of math classes here, and he is head and shoulders above them all. If all the teachers here would take an interest in teaching as much as he does, more people would take math at this level, and actually enjoy it.
McCombs is a great teacher, probably one of the best I have ever had for math. He is very clear and gives you tests on what he teaches, so you always know what to expect.
Great guy, always willing to help.  Tests aren't too difficult if you do look over all the practice problems on his website.
If I wasnt in the self paced class, I wouldve done a lot better grade wise, but he is always willing to help, easy to understand, and has been teaching for 10+ years. Great teacher!
Coolest guy... talks like the guy from Wild America! Loves Simpsons &South Park

Dr. Steiner is great and really knowledgeable on the topics he teaches on. He genuinely cares about his students as people and wants to see them learn. Most of his grades are from essays, which he grades with a pretty high standard though. If you want an easy A, then he's not for you. But, if you want to learn, then definitely go with Dr Steiner!

Prof. Steiner is an amazing teacher, would definitely recommend taking a class with him! He's caring and passionate about the subject. It is a discussion based class, so come prepared. There is a lot of reading and material so definitely make sure to do it. The majority of the grade was in-class essays, with several small reflections and quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Seminar style class with short reading quizzes and discussion posts weekly, one group paper as well as in class essays for midterm and final. Steiner is a great professor who really does a good job of teaching the material while getting students involved. This class was so impactful to me and I cannot recommend it enough.

Steiner is an amazing professor, I'd recommend this class ten times over! He is very caring and genuinely wants his students to have a strong understanding of the content. Personally, I thought he was a fair grader, but it's crucial that you pay attention to the readings to make A's on essays and quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: AMAZING class. Learned so much from Steiner and will actually apply it to real life. Lots of readings, but don't skip them because it will be evident in your work. Short reading quizzes and minimal cold calling, so come to class prepared. Group paper and 2 in-class essays for midterm and final. Do the work, be thoughtful, and you will be rewarded!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: He is a super great guy and very passionate about the subject matter. He is, however, a harsh grader, and you have to write a lot in this class. Be ready for a lot of reading and writing, but classes are not mandatory, and they are discussion-based based which is super fun.

Prof. Steiner is a great guy. Gives good advice & clear feedback on writing. 

3 in-class essays & a group paper make up most of the grades, he also gives a lot of reading quizzes. Do the readings thoroughly & take lots of notes. Lots of writing, best tips are to cut the fluff & write a strong introduction. Participate in discussions & be present.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Steiner is the BEST professor at UNC. This is not an easy class, and he makes you very aware of that at the beginning of the semester. You can definitely get an A in this class, as long as you do the readings and think deeply about the concepts. This is the most impactful class I've taken at UNC.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: This is the best class I have taken at UNC. Incredibly caring and kind Professor. The readings are long and dense but very interesting. Be ready to speak during class! It's a good environment to speak, so don't let that deter you. Grading is fair. Avoid any fluff in your writing. Just get to the point.

POLI 255 with Professor Steiner is discussion based so be prepared to participate in class. The topics are interesting and he cares about the students being able to engage with the content. Two take home papers, quizzes, and a group project, all of which are reasonable. I enjoyed this class but be ready to talk!

Graded by 3 equal papers but he is a TOUGH grader. I got a 91.5 on the first, which was the highest for the entire class. The class avg a B on papers, which is kind of crazy for a FY seminar. The content is interesting and he knows the subjects, but grades harsh on papers. Our group paper went to office hours, took his advise, and still got an 84.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Super engaging and interesting professor. Graded by 2 take-home exams and a group paper, plus some quizzes and discussion posts. Grading is done mostly by the TA. I found the grading to be a bit harsh.

POLI 255H is, hands down, the best class I have taken during my time at Carolina. Dr. Steiner is magnificent and the class is powerful, makes you want to be engaged. Readings are dense, but genuinely interesting and relevant to class content. He grades essays predominately for clarity and readability, don't waste time with flowery writing.

Professor Steiner is the best professor I have ever had throughout my academic career. His class opened up a respectful, comfortable space for students to have conversations about immigration. I could not recommend him enough. He is caring, funny, and an overall wise and knowledgeable professor! Show up to class and spend adequate time essays.

One of my favorite classes and professors. I truly learned so much about immigration in this class and really benefited from the discussion format of the class. Steiner created a safe and open environment to share your thoughts on the readings and topics. It's a decent amount of reading and writing, but super interesting and worth it. A must-take.

This class is very discussion based to be sure to participate. Dr. Steiner is very passionate about migration and very knowledgeable. Grades are based on pop quiz (that can be random) so be sure to do the readings and take notes. He is also somewhat a tough grader on the 3 major papers so be sure to go to his office hours and ask for help!

I highly recommend this class and Professor Steiner. He is very knowledgeable and helps you to dive deeper into the material. The readings are all very interesting and the 2.5 hour long feels short when you are there. I came in as a Business Major with no interest in immigration, and am leaving very interested due to Professor Steiner!!!

Dr. Steiner is an amazing lecturer - he is passionate about his work in Migration. His POLI77 class is very discussion-based. Readings aren't difficult as long as you manage your time well. Super kind, thoughtful, and trustworthy. He wants you to succeed in class, so being present in class and following directions is important.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: His class is super interesting and engaging, but he's a pretty tough grader when it comes to papers.

The BEST professor and class I've ever had. Classes are discussion-based, but they're really engaging and interesting. Readings are reasonable length and interesting. Prof Steiner is incredibly kind and understanding about life events. You will come out of this class with an immense amount of knowledge and expertise on the subject. Take this class!

Dr. Steiner is personable, but I very much disliked this class. It is heavily based on group discussions, which are poorly led and do not encourage critical thinking. He doesn't respect the depth or breadth of the topic or the readings he teaches and is inflexible in how he approaches arguments. Grading was also harsh and based on unclear criteria

Professor Steiner is super passionate about the topic he teaches and very caring and understanding. He gives extensions when asked and is willing to work with students. He gives pop quizzes to take attendance/ see if you did the reading. The grade is heavily wighted on midterm and final papers but they are take home. Overall the class was great.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Steiner is amazing! This is the second class I've taken with him and I loved it. The readings are super interesting (some are long, but worth it), and there is a midterm paper and final paper. If you do the readings, listen/participate, and follow directions, you'll do great.

Steiner was super nice and very knowledgable! Discussion based and some of the readers were long and boring but fine for the most part. Discussion board posts about like all of the readings and quizzes almost every class. Group paper + presentation was actually better/easier than expected. Definitely learned a lot and dont need any prior knowledge.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Steiner was wonderful, and this class was great. I went in knowing little to nothing about European politics and came out with an abundance of knowledge. He has a discussion-based format, so come to class prepared (he does occasionally cold-call). Overall, if you are interested in European politics, definitely take this class.

Professor Steiner is awesome, even with a 2.5 hour long class, it doesn't get boring and the discussion based format is excellent. He always challenged us to think about every perspective and consider different sides of a situation, I learned a lot in this class. He is a fair grader and the group paper is annoying to coordinate but very doable.

Prof Steiner respects students and encourages critical thinking!! He does ask for participation and perhaps a deeper level of thinking than students are prepared for, but I felt that he does a good job of balancing high expectations with a work-load that is not overwhelming.
Great professor. Very engaged and excited about the material. A lot of reading, but great course overall. You learn a lot

Incredible professor! Be prepared to spend time on the readings - class is discussion-based and lectures are few and far between, so understanding the readings is crucial to earning participation credit. 3 papers and 1 group presentation/paper instead of exams. Tough grader but fair and grades anonymously - feedback made me a much better writer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Steiner is a very caring and engaging professor! The class is quite difficult and requires a lot of reading. There are several pop quizzes, but they don't count for most of the grade. He cares about how his students feel and is a fair grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The class wasn't bad per se. It just was a lot of reading and the lectures were drawn out and long.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Steiner is the best! He's knowledgeable, interesting, and engaging. Classes are largely discussion-based. There is a decent amount of reading, but it's all worth it. Grades consist of a midterm paper, a group paper, and a final paper along with discussion posts and weekly reading quizzes. Not too hard of a grader. Take his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Steiner is a great teacher! He cares about his students and actively tries to include them in class discussions. He does require you to read multiple times a week and participation is mandatory in class. He is a slightly tough grader, but overall it was a great class. Highly recommend!

Steiner is such a great teacher! I really enjoyed his class you just have to make sure you read the materials that are assigned outside of class. There are 3 essays and 1 group essay and he grades those pretty tough but its a great class to be in.
Incredible professor. Really cares about his students and is engaging. Take his class!

Best prof by far so far at UNC. Truly cares about the students and the subject and wants students to learn/excel. Grading was tough but fair and his feedback on each paper made me a much better writer. If you put in the effort, you will take a lot from this course, if you just want easy credit, there are way better options.

Steiner is really excellent. He makes an already engaging class even better. Great feedback, understanding, easygoing, smart, etc etc. POLI can easily be boring but he picks great readings to discuss in the next class so it was much more engaging than my other POLI classes. Take a class with Steiner if you can!

this class was very discussion heavy and there are few grades, with the majority of grades relying on papers (in which steiner can be a harsh grader). there are many readings, all of which require a forum post. this class is very writing-heavy but incredibly informative.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Best professor I've had thus far. I learned so much from this class. A good amount of reading but all the articles are interesting and are discussed thoroughly in class. Papers are graded tough but it helps you become a better writer. Definitely not easy but it is so worth it. TAKE THIS CLASS!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Really fun class as long as you do the readings & engage in discussions. Prof Steiner is accommodating & fosters a great classroom atmosphere.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Steiner is the best teacher I have had yet. He truly cares about all of his students and wants everyone to feel comfortable to participate in group discussions. Each class began with an icebreaker then went into discussion that was based on a reading from the previous night. Essay grading is hard, but fair. Take his class if you can!!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Hands-down my favorite professor at UNC! I have never been compelled to write a review before, but I appreciate his class so much that I am. He goes out of his way to make sure everyone understands the material and he doesn't lecture, instead we discuss the (short) readings in class and he tries really hard to build a community in the online class.
Dr. Steiner was one of my favorite professors at UNC. He's an incredibly interesting individual, and he loves talking to students one-on-one. Put in the work and you will do well in his classes.

Steiner really focused on creating a community during our online class. He made sure that we got a chance to talk before jumping into the lecture. For the pop quizzes, make sure you have read. However, you can honestly reading the intro and conclusion and be fine. The papers are graded hard but fair. However, grades are cumulative so that's a plus.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Caring--So many papers

reviews.comment: Highly recommend Prof. Steiner! There is a lot of reading but they are fairly interesting. The group paper (honors version) is not great, but he is an easy and fair grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Significant amount of reading, but you can get away with skimming and just paying attention in class. To do well, you have to know the argument specific authors make. An A is set at a 92, and he is generally not a super tough grader, just be sure to make an argument in your essays and be able to back it up with the stuff from the readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: I liked Dr. Steiner a lot--super nice guy, interesting readings, and he's not too hard as long as you keep up with your readings. The one thing that I didn't like about him was that he didn't give clear grading criteria. He told us that reading pop quizzes wouldn't count at all towards our final grade, but they ended up counting 12.5%
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This class has a lot of homework and one midterm as well as a final exam; they are both on the lockdown response browser, and the grading is very nice, because you automatically get 25% for one of the essays out of the 3; you choose 2. However, Professor Bri has high expectations and isn't very understanding when it comes to work questions.

I hated this class. Bri was mean to all of us, spoke condescendingly, and didn't seem like she wanted us there, and tbh we didn't want to be there either. Just not a fun class with her. TAs are what determine your grade, and rubrics were not clear, with some TAs being "oh let me text her and back to you."

She made this class a snooze fest. Every lecture took a year off my life. Redeeming quality: you don't need to go to class at all. Class only helps with the midterm and final which we're free. There were 4 papers, had nothing to do with the lecture, and your grade solely depended on which TA you got. Regardless should be an easy A

I went to maybe 5 lectures the whole semester, so if you want a class you can skip this is it. However, there are about 5 major assignments, and the TAs seem to grade more harshly as the semester goes on. midterm and exam are EXTREMLY easy and identical to the study guide, which is amazing (I "studied" 2 days before both and got a 96 and 97)
Professor Nave really tried to make the class engaging, the assignments just didn't do a great job of supplementing learning within the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Pretty boring, especially considering that its a jazz class. not sure how that happened. feels like she doesn't like students or something like that. its an easy A but was probably a waste of money to take. maybe went to 3 classes total throughout the semester.

This class is so buns holy. Every lecture is so boring and I now hate jazz which I didn't know was possible. The TAs are on a power trip taxing you for stuff for the love of the game, and the assignments take so long and don't even correlate to the class lectures. All in all, please avoid this teacher, prob would've been a fun class without her.

Nave was okay, lecture was boring. Getting a good TA was gambling, only Mick A. knew what they were doing. I lost all interest in this class due to the constant passive aggressiveness from a certain TA and how all assignments were just busy work. Don't take this class.

Briana is very knowledgeable on this subject, but this is a lecture-heavy course. I enjoyed the class because of how passionate she is about the topic. I will say that some of the assignments seemed like busywork, and your grade depends on the TA you get. Mick Anderson is amazing and was the only one who provided feedback. I enjoyed this class!
Briana Nave was not the best teacher. Very condescending and didn't really enjoy going to the lecture. Grade is really dependent on the TA. If you get Mick Anderson, you are in good hands.

Many of the assignments she created for the class felt unfair and far too long for what should be required of an intro to jazz course. Nave often gave off a vibe that she feels she is better than you simply because she is pursuing a PhD. Unfortunately I am limited by space on this site, but in short: don't take her class.

Interesting material and class. Professor is knowledgeable, kind personally and clearly cares, but low-energy for a jazz course. Lectures solid but repetitive. Interesting perspectives and engaging guest speakers. Assignments felt overly long and not always relevant. TAs were bad except for Mick A. Learned a lot about jazz culture and history.

Briana very obviously cares about what she is teaching, and I would say the content was engaging. As someone who knew next to nothing about jazz culture and history going into this class, I can say I am pretty knowledgeable now. Some assignments seemed like busywork, but the content of them was interesting. Very TA dependent, some grades confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She clearly knows what she's talking about and puts together decent lectures. Buuuuuuuuut, class is quite boring, I'm not too sure she likes students, and you never know what you're gonna get with the grading.

Briana is really passionate about jazz, but the class itself is pretty challenging. You have to put a good amount of effort into the papers if you want an A, and the last assignment took way longer than expected. The exams weren't too bad, though. Memorize a few paragraphs, and you're good.
Acted like we don't know how to write and made us use only the UNC library and JSTOR resources for our Lesson Plan assignment. Effectively doubles our research and wastes your precious hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Made jazz so boring. Assignments were too long and didn't feel a value add. TAs were random with grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I signed up for the class because it was supposed to be taught by my guy Stephen Anderson, and I got stuck with a teacher who makes jazz so boring. Lectures suck and she somehow makes learning jazz terrible, and I grew up playing in a jazz band. The TAs other than the homie Mick are all doing too much, and every assignment makes me tweak crazily.
Professor boring. Terrible assignments that don't add to the course. Horribly rude TA's.

Absolute waste of time and energy. The grading in this class is a joke. The TAs themself don't even know what they're doing. They take off points for things that are never mentioned in the rubric for assignments. Ms. Nave speaks to her students condescendingly as if undergraduates don't know what they're doing. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.
Mick Anderson was a great and fair TA. The only good thing about the class.
Unnecessarily long, dry assignments of little value. Condescending tone towards the class. Overall just not a good time. Jazz should be fun.

This class has so much random rigor it's not even funny. We've had many guest speakers, all have been more engaging than her. Lesson plan assignment in particular has been nail in coffin in terms of unneccessary work. She should not be teaching this class. Great interesting subject, terrible professor and course structure. Mick A is only good TA.
She gives 30,000 assignments. DO NOT take this class. She made me lose interest in Jazz which I didn't think was even possible
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: SHE SHOULD NOT BE TEACHING A CLASS AT UNC
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I'd give 0 if there's an option

Decent person, horrible lecturer. Talks condescending at times, gives a lot of tedious assignments that takes up more time than my actual major classes and didn't really feel fun or were related to the course. SOME of the TAs are unhelpful and didn't give good feedback. Made us get a textbook that we barely used. Don't take this class with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HER
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Bri talks to the class in an off-putting way and calls people out for not paying attention. She is very easy to contact, lectures are easy to follow, but assignments are long and tedious. Do not get me started on the TA's. Multiple people, including myself have been graded unnecessarily harshly by a TA, and in some cases they're wrong.

I don't like Bri Nave. Turned a gen ed about jazz into a boring and sluggish class. A very bad lecturer and speaks to the class in an odd, condescending tone. Mentions the masters thing a lot, almost as if to show authority over students beyond being their professor. Assignments are long and don't further your learning at all. Steer clear

DO NOT take this class with her if you are looking for an easy A Gen-ed grade or even have an interest in Jazz. The class lectures are boring and tedious. There is just a lot of content to memorize. For a simple Gen-ed, she treats this class like this is every student's most important class at UNC.

She is a nice and kind professor in-person. But she doesn't understand that this is a class students are taking for a gen-ed and small interest in jazz perhaps. There is just so much content and lectures are boring. Do not take this class. I lost interest in jazz after this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She needs to cut down on essays/assignments for the class. There are wayyyy to many. Treats it like this is our only Core UNC Class. Lectures are boring. Just a jazz history class with so much information to memorize.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Cool guy, easy class, sometimes boring but I'd take boring over evil any day.
Exams are tough, but the overall class grade is determined by a lot of different things.  RA projects help to boost the grade as long as you put effort into them. Textbook reading is long
Great guy, great professor, and so interesting.
This dude is amazing. Fantastic professor. Ethnography can be a bit time consuming.

This was one of my most favorite classes I've taken at UNC. While you do have to put work in in reading, getting to know your character, and writing and memorizing speeches, this class truly helps you become a better public speaker. There is no judgement and the more you engage with the material and design of the class, the more fun it is.

Professor Caren is an amazing professor with such a welcoming personality. I took this course to fulfill my minor, and it was a great class with wonderful people in it as well. We have speeches to give, but the process leading up to the speeches is structured so well that you truly shouldn't feel scared. Take his class, you'll love it!

He is so funny and I would retake his class. Although my friends who had other professors for Soci 101 said their exams were easy, which is the downside to taking his, I found his exams to be challenging after spending days studying to prepare. However, if you follow the criteria for the homework, you get a 100, so it's a pretty easy course.
One of the best professors at UNC. Take Soci 101 with Professor Caren, you won't regret it.
Great guy -- gave everyone a free 100% on a midterm!

This is the goat of Sociology 101. We all got 100s on our last mideterm since more than 60% of the class didn't take it(He stated if more than 60% of students get a question wrong it will be given full points). Not much work other than Research Apllications and Inquizzitives. Pollev is used for attendance. Overall show up and it's an easy A.

Neal Caren is THE SWEETEST prof you will ever take at UNC. Everyday, he arrives so excited to teach and engage with students. He is extremely knowledgeable and makes his course engaging with online polls and halftime quiz games (i got to play soci family feud on LDOC). Easy homework, bi weekly assignments, 1 midterm exam, 1 final exam.

Wow. One of the funniest and nicest professors of all time. Tons of easy extra credit. The only downside is having to write about 3600 words of "research applications" throughout the semester. But even as someone who hates writing, take this class.The exams are easy and he made a custom quiz website so you can study for the exams in no time at all.

I love Prof. Caren.  His lectures are sometimes boring but more often than not fun.  The assignments are very easy, and you don't have to read the textbook.  There are 2 midterms and a final but he'll replace your midterm with the final if you do better.  I would highly recommend him to everyone!
The BEST professor. He's amazing, I love his class.
G.O.A.T Professor. Definitely for the memory books!

Just dont consider any other options, he is GOAT!!! His assignments and class both are fun. For someone who really struggles to go to class I have been going every class!! I just love being in this class
About as easy as a gen ed you can take. Exams can be aced simply by spending 30min on the cover quilt. The textbook very clearly tries to influence you to think like a Marxist though

This guy goes out of his way to make studying for exams as easy as possible and hands out extra credit. Really a nice and hardworking professor. The research applications (8 per class, lowest score dropped) are kind of a lot of work but not difficult or heavily graded.
Such an easy class and I learned so much. He was super interesting in lectures, would recommend to anyone. Tests weren't very hard either.

This is by far the BEST class I've ever taken. It was so interactive and engaging and everyone in my class got so close. I never missed this class because it was that fun to go to. Prof. Caren is hilarious and super chill. If you try a little bit you'll get an A. There is a public speaking component but Caren creates a really safe environment.

Dr. Caren was fine. He was funny and witty. This class, for me, was kinda difficult. The papers were easy, but its veryyy participation heavy. I'm sure it was easier for people more extroverted and social, but for introverts, I think it can be anxiety inducing and exhausting. Just understand what you are signing up for; its almost an acting class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: SOCI 274 is the best class I have ever taken!!! The way the course is designed is very interactive and really really fun. Dr. Caren is interesting, knowledgeable, easy to talk to, and very reasonable. There can feel like a lot of reading at times, but honestly if you're engaged in the class you'll do great.
Highly recommend. Class was chill.

Caren is hilarious! I loved coming to class everyday and reading the textbook for his class. The material was so interesting, and we watched movies pretty often in class. Great professor, I already signed up for his other class because I loved him so much. He curves every test and will drop lots of things at the end of class, hard to not get an A

Professor Caren is great! You have to do a little bit of work for this course, but it isn't terrible. For exams, make a Quizlet with the terms and do the practice exams, and you will do fine. Honestly just try your best in the course and do the extra credit, and you can get an A easily.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class was very easy yet very interesting! If you are looking for an easy elective, I definitely recommend this class. As long as you take the practice exams, study keywords, and memorize the vocabulary, you will do well in this class. The documentaries that were sprinkled throughout the semester were also a nice break from lectures.

Lectures were pretty boring and they didn't really connect that well with textbook readings or exam material. I never paid attention during lecture, didn't do a single textbook reading, and my exam average was a 96. This is SOCI101 so it isn't hard, but if you want to actually learn the material, maybe take a different professor.

Profesor Caren loves what he teaches and it shows in his lectures. He makes class engaging especially when we watch movies and genuinely wants his students to succeed. At first, the class may seem like it has lots of work but it is very spaced out and doesn't take long to complete the assignments. I would totally recommend taking a class with him.

Gonna keep this short and simple. Prof Caren is the best teacher possible for SOCI101 and if he teaches it, take him. Projects are basically graded for completion and exams are pretty straightforward and if they weren't he gives us points back. Barely studied and got near-100.

Prof. Caren is great. Lectures were sometimes boring but he tried to make them fun and interactive. He gives tons of opportunities to get a good grade and all assignments were pretty easy. Short quizzes & papers. He posts possible midterm/final questions and gives plenty of study resources. Would highly recommend this course for an easy credit.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The coursework (textbook quizzes and research applications) set you up really nicely for the tests. He drops at least one assignment from each category and gave back points on each exam so your grade will be really boosted by the end of the semester. Utilizes PollEverywhere throughout the lecture for attendance credit.

Professor Caren is super nice and easy to talk to when you have issues. The homework and projects are super easy and interesting you just have to make sure to plan ahead for them. Participation is very important in this class because it counts for your attendance.
Dr. Caren is a really nice guy, however how he runs this class is a bit boring and he can make some weird comments that could be perceived as hateful towards certain groups of people.

Extremely passive aggressive professor, but overall a very easy class. I took SOCI100 and it was rather interesting, but the way he lectured was terribly boring. On-time submission will typically lead to an 100% on the assignment, except the final and midterm were significantly more difficult. Staying on top of reading the textbook definitely helps

Dr. Caren is great! The exams are the hardest part of the class, so definitely take the practice tests many times. However, there are a lot of other assignments to balance out exam grades. The final exam included questions from the midterms, so definitely go back and review those questions when the final comes along. Very knowledgeable guy.

Lectures are not helpful, just read the books. Hard to get good grades. The class has tons of assignments. However, the exams largely determined the grade (so even if you got 100 on every other assignment you might still mess the grades up) and it test literally everything. Never got exam scores higher than 85 and ends up with an A-.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures and readings for this class can be pretty long. The class consists of applications, case studies, film discussions, inquizitive, midterms, and the final. TA's are great and allow you to resubmit applications if necessary. You need to thoroughly study all of the vocabulary in the textbook. Take practice tests MULTIPLE TIMES.

Grading criteria is super clear. You can get a decent grade without putting in much effort. Lecture can be interesting and Neal is knowledgeable. The exams are likely the worst part of the class but even then, the reviews and Quizlet help with studying. Overall, not a bad course if you're looking for an interesting elective that isn't too rigorous.

Neal Caren, I love you so much. Best professor I've ever had hands down. I took this for PH credit and had so much fun. Truly got to be me in this class and have never had a better time. Neal literally catered IP3 for our final... king. Easy A if you put in a little bit of effort and honestly such a rewarding class... gonna miss this class so much

I was super nervous about Caren's 274 section because the teaching method was so unusual (you have to take on the perspective of historical figures) but I learned so much and this class was something I looked forward to. Dr. Caren is super chill and we had a pizza party during our final if that says anything. Take this class!!!

Dude is hilarious and clearly knows a lot about sociology. Assignments are fairly easy to complete and have very clear grading criteria. Has offered extra credit opportunities throughout the semester as well. Tests are pretty difficult so I recommend actually studying for a couple days in advance. Very helpful and has interesting classes as well.

Prof Caren is funny and his lectures always have something that make me laugh. Multiple extra credit opportunities. Know the key terms/do the practice exams before exams and you should do well. Not a hard class to succeed in if you put in some effort and understand the material, was never stressed about this class.

Super knowledgeable and great at facilitating a hands-off experience where students can truly immerse themselves in the simulation. Will help when you're stuck. A lot of reading is required to truly understand the material, and you have to put in a lot of effort, but it's worth it. Grading not bad. Class is different, but my favorite one I've taken
Assignments have clear grading criteria and are relatively easy although time consuming. Tests are pretty hard, definitely need to put a good amount of time into studying.
pretty easy as long as you do the work and study, many movie days and few papers and case studys but nothing too difficult

I really loved Professor Caren. He was engaging in class and had very clear expectations. His tests are not hard if you take the practice exams he posts a couple of times (there are infinite questions). The applications every week are not hard ... I don't think they are actually graded for content, got 100 on all of them.

Professor Caren is an AMAZING guy. His classes are fun, entertaining and thought provoking. However, the tests are disproportionately hard compared to his lectures, so be prepared to not do well on those versus other assignments. Overall, highly suggest his course.

He's a chill guy and a nice person but there's way too much work he makes you do for a stupid intro to sociology class. Every other teacher gives less work - he's so extra and for no reason. Would have never taken this class if I knew that he made you work like a donkey for even a B.

The lectures and readings for this class are so boring. There isn't enough engagement in class to keep you focused it's just him talking for 1 hour and 15 minutes straight. The applications also take you a long time and the due dates are too short for a project of that manner. Midterms are okay it's just memorizing like 100+ terms.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: SUCH a great professor. Super easy class if you just do the PRACTICE EXAMS MULTIPLE TIMES. Some of the exam answers are on Quizlet if you know where to look; hint use practice exam problems to search. Great and engaging professor. DON'T READ TEXTBOOK. Complete waste of time, j skim for answers and study vocabulary.

Prof Caren is an extremely nice professor. He chooses interesting documentaries to watch and is funny with the lectures. He is well respected by the class and there is no way you can get less than a B in this class unless you genuinely do not do anything. Love him!

Professor Caren is a delightful professor. He's kind, funny, and does his best to keep students engaged during lecture. However, much of what is required to succeed in this course comes from the textbook, not the lectures. As long as you do the required readings, the class shouldn't be too difficult.

Massive lecture, interesting content but midterms are tricky if you don't study the right things. Hard to have a connection with your Professor if you're with 350+ other students. Read the bolded terms in the textbook if you're short on time, do the Inquizitives, and always shoot for a high pass on the projects. Definitely show up to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof Caren is a super nice guy and quite funny. I didn't enjoy the class though, as it relied heavily on textbook readings. The lectures were a bit useless since most of the material came from the textbook. The projects seemed to be busy-work, as well as most of the other homework.

SOCI 101 was an amazing class to take with neal. as long as you met the requirements for the assignments, did well on the quizzes on sakai, and participated in the discussions; you'll get a good grade. 10/10

This class was interesting and assignments were easy, although some were time-consuming. Class was watching a movie and tying it to course concepts every Thursday (if taken on a Tuesday/Thursday schedule). He makes the material extremely interesting, only downside is that grading depends on which TA you get assigned.

Neal is awesome. Best class I took this semester. His ability to make it interesting with documentaries each week is something I have yet to see in other classes. Is very clear about what to do for each assignment. Super Easy A. Good lecturer too and can be funny. Very easy to get in touch with. I really suggest taking this class!

I loved this class. Very easy A. Consisted of one lecture per week and an interesting documentary each Thursday. Very laid back and easy material. Basically just show up, do the few and easy assignments, and you'll do well. Caren is good at lecturing and seems like a really chill guy. This class fulfills a gen-ed so I 100% recommend.

This class was my favorite this semester! Prof Caren is super accommodating and makes class interesting with a film every week. You get to drop assignments and some are graded P/F so you really never stress about your grade. Tests are easy; some assignments are more time consuming but still not hard. Definitely got me interested in sociology!
worst professor i've had in my entire life. not personable at all and hardly paid attention to his students. took forever to grade anything.

Super easy class. Made one lecture async and we watched a movie for the other every week. Just get all the assignments done and the midterm/final will be a breeze. He's super accommodating and flexible--I took this class during the pandemic. Awesome guy too.

Drops lowest quizzes/assignments in all categories. Very understanding during pandemic. Actually cares that students engage with/learn material. Great online class. Options for students who cannot attend class due to work or other obligations. 11/10. Easy A if you do what is expected most of the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Neal Caren is the best choice for Soci 101. He did an amazing job with online classes and we were connected without too much lecture. We had lots of projects and opportunities to apply sociology in movie discussions and case studies. Super interesting and easy and Prof. Caren is a funny, caring, understanding guy! Great class.

Professor Caren is the most disengaged professor I have ever had. He took forever to grade assignments and did not release many grades until right before finals. He was also not accommodating nor understanding in regard to circumstances surrounding COVID. The class website was unorganized and the communication of his expectations was horrible.

Dr. Caren was extremely accommodating with assignments and work due to COVID. The Tuesday lectures were recorded and usually pretty enjoyable. We also watched a documentary every week which always ended up being pretty good. The homework didn't take too long and the assignments were a pass/fail type.

Kept class interesting during online instruction with having us watch a film on Netflix each week that pertained to that week's concept. Normal amount of assignments and an easy A! Zooms once a week but were optional and were posted online if you wanted to watch later. Has his own website for the course keeping it separate from Sakai which I liked!

Loved this class. Optional Tuesday lectures that I attended in the beginning and stopped going to at the end but still did well. Netflix Documentaries on Thursdays! Multiple assignments could be dropped, with clear grading. We didn't have to read books like past classes since he switched to docu's. Very easy class.

I absolutely loved taking this class with Professor Caren. The assignments were all self-explanatory and easy to do well on. I also really liked the way the class was structered. We had an optional lecture on Tuesday and watched a film on Thursday. I definitely recommend taking a class with him!!

Dr. Caren was very easily contacted, as well as the TA's. His grading criteria was very clear and the assignments were mostly busy work but were still very interesting. Caren gave the option to skip certain assignments and dropped the lowest two grades for each assignment type. He was very caring and understanding of the stress of this semester!

Literally the easiest into class to exist. Caren was so accommodating for our COVID semester and allowed multiple drops for each type of assignment. Homework can be corrected until you get a 100. Everything else is graded pass/fail. If you put in effort it's easy to make 100's on the assignments. Interesting class with fun films, too!
Took his class for a PH credit and am so happy I did. He handled the COVID 19 shift to online learning so well. He really cares about his students.

Definitely lots of busy work, but overall I found the course interesting enough that it made it bearable. The lectures are generally interesting, I really liked the books we read, and lots of extra credit opportunities. Overall a solid class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Not really sure how I got a B in this class because there are SO many extra credit opportunities. Caren is an awesome professor and I would probably take him again if I get the chance. He is very accessible and willing to help! However, there is a lot of extra/busy work done in this course and some of his lectures can be kind of boring.

Professor Caren was great! The workload could be a lot sometimes but it really furthers your understanding of the topic. Book groups were a thing in this class but I enjoyed the books assigned for the most part. Overall a great class to take!

LOTS of busy work/ reading but as long as you just do it, you'll do great. graded on a lot of different things & he gives curves/drops lowest grades. doesn't take a lot of effort, just a lot of time. Caren is funny & keeps lectures interesting. I only read 1 of the 3 books & still made an A. A lot of the stuff on quizzes/test are common sense
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Caren is a boring lecturer but he's funny and makes the class easy. This class has weekly readings, a couple bigger assignments, a few online quizzes, book clubs and he monitors attendance through the check in app. Overall, it is a super easy class if you do your work and briefly skim the textbook and the three books! There's also extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: no saying his class is hard. its just way too much unnecessary busy work that doesnt rly prepare you for anything. hes funny and interesting but i dont like how some extra credits are given based on huge groups. Also, most of his assignments are graded by his TAs, one of the TA is very nice but the other one isnt that nice. Soooo good luck
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Literally one of the easiest classes I've took so far. Why are the reviews so bad? literally his class is sooooooo easy. Yes, there is a lot of work but the grading is so lenient it's impossible to fail. Out of all the 101 classes I've took so far. This is by FAR the best choice you can ever make. Maybe another teacher is better? but he's chill.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The workload for this SOCI101 class is actually ridiculous compared to every other 101 course. You will read at least 3 books completely and be expected to have at least 10 pages of notes for each. The quizzes aren't the worst thing but they are definitely not easy; you will need to study a lot. I took this class thinking it would be easy, it's not
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Prof Caren is really nice, but this class was a little ridiculous. The lectures are useless, there is an exorbitant amount of homework for an introductory class, and attendance is mandatory 100% of the time. The tests are pretty easy, so it isn't hard to do well in the class, but the amount of useless busy work and useless lectures make it a chore.

Homework seems extensive for an introductory course, but is generally an easy grade. Best reading list I've had for a class. As a professor, Caren is fairly inefficient. Being entertaining and empathetic does not make up for a lack of substance in every lecture. A straightforward course with disappointingly little content in the classroom.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Neal Caren is the one of the nicest professors I've had at UNC. He genuinely cares and even though his class has a lot of assignments he makes sure not to heavily weigh your grade on one exam which allows for plenty of forgiveness. As long as you go to class and do the work you will do well.

Neal Caren is the worst Professor that I've had at UNC. His focus seems to be more on brainwashing young adults with an agenda than with teaching and runs much of his class with strict, ridiculous guidelines. Class activities are awful. His "book groups" are bad as well and seem to be used to get him out of actually teaching a class hald the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He's a great professor and for SOCI 101 being a big lecture class, he makes the class seem king of small because of the many group activities. I would definitely take another one of his classes.

If you want an easy class, pick a different professor. Disproportional homework amount for introductory class, required attendance, weekly graded quizzes and assignments where in order to get 100% you need to include an extra paragraph explaining why you deserve it. Gives huge extra credit based on luck, making it unfair to most of the students.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Caren definitely makes a large lecture class interesting. I was surprised by how much I enjoyed this class, and it was definitely not as difficult as the rating might make you believe. There's a lot of busy work, which is fair, but it's easy, and usually not time consuming. Exams are basically the study guide, so if you study, you'll do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: It felt as if the professor thought that we didn't have any classes other than his. 3 tests, 3 novels to read(with reading notes, reading questions, and a book review on one), and online book quizzes before every class. Also 4 other "applications" to complete. Unless you love homework do not take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Great guy. He's a little dorky but very sweet. His class is not hard, but there is a good amount of work to do. Reading the textbook is how you learn the information. The class is just small group activities but it counts for participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: Neal is adorable & such a sweetheart. Even though there are a lot of assignments to do like reading due every class etc, it was not that hard. He assigns book clubs that meet a few times throughout the semester which is a fun way to meet other people in the class which you do not normally get to do in a large lecture class.

Professor Caren is a very sweet and caring teacher. He requires us to attend book clubs but the books were pretty interesting. Also he provides us with study guides so if you do them, you will be fine on the exams.
This class was so boring that it made learning tough. We had to learn everything ourselves and lectures were a waste of time. It was an easy A tho.

I took this class because Sociology was a recommended course for my track; I took SOCI 101 because I thought it was the easiest option. The class isn't extremely difficult, but Professor Caren is big on busy work. If you're wanting to take a class where you show up and take notes, this isn't it, expect a lot of unnecessary group work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Was a bit unorganized throughout the semester... I would have done things differently. However, he was really nice and was good at taking into account our requests for due-dates, projects, etc.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: He is a funny but slightly weird professor. The class, in the beginning, is fairly confusing but as the semester goes on it becomes extremely easy. This is not your typical lecture class, it is very hands-on and interactive. There is a few quizzes that he won't grade, 4 short papers, and a take-home final which was a 600-900 word paper.

He's a funny professor, BUT you will be swamped with work. So many things are going on at the same time in this class (assignment wise) that it's overwhelming. You have a lot of reading to do, a lot of acting out to do, and a lot of group projects. This class is NOT an easy "A."
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Proffesor Yaqub put together interesting readings, but was not a great lecturer. She often goes off topic and doesn't get into the meat of her lecture. She also will try and keep you after class is over to continue her lecture if she got off topic. I wish she was a better lecturer because what she has to say is often very interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: These classes are not easy, it is very reading heavy and she is a harsh grader. But she really cares about students and is very understanding of any outside circumstances you might have, which can't always be said for other proffessors at UNC. I was very grateful that she was so understanding.

I really enjoyed the class. Dr. Yaqub is very knowledgeable and approaches the subject very well. She is a little disorganized, and the class is reading heavy, especially for the first two exams. Other than that, I enjoyed the class and learned a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Super interesting and intelligent professor! I loved the Palestinian literature and films that we read/watched during this class. I gained a lot of important knowledge. She probably would be better in a smaller class though.
Not recommended. she is always unprepared to class which makes it hard to follow

Lectures can be pretty hard to follow. The test relies too much on lectures and ppt slides. If you find lost with study guides or how to prepare for the test, just approach the TAs. Some might be unwelcoming or not very enthusiastic but the one I usually had the review sessions was superb.

20% of your grade for the class is the test. She harshly shuts down people's opinions if they don't match her own. Big classes are not her forte, maybe she would be better in a small class. The content is interesting but she rarely stays on topic. Test is class attendance heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class is really not that bad. It's interesting and I learned a lot. That being said, Nadia was not a good lecturer. She's clearly very knowledgeable and passionate about what she teaches, but she just doesn't do a good job teaching to such a large body of students. Students should know that her unit focuses on the Israel-Palestine conflict.

She seems to not be open to students perspectives. She quickly shuts down peoples opinons and judges people harshly. She does not stick to her PowerPoints, and instead will go off on tangents that do not relate to the test material. She is hard to follow and does not seem like a genuine, caring, person. I would not take another class with her.

Her lectures and exam were centered around multiple readings and videos during the weeks she taught so as long you do those, you will be perfectly fine. She cares a lot about her content which is very apparent during her lectures. Overall good lecturer.
interesting readings, lectures can be confusing. the tests are not bad if you pay attention in lecture and review the slides

I had Nadia for Borders and Boundaries and she honestly just could not lead a clear lecture well. Everything felt very frazzled and the way that she presented her content was a bit unclear. Overall I would probably not take this class if I had another option, the tests were graded very harshly and randomly by TAs.
She's a caring teacher she's just all over the dang place and it seems like she can't control her own thoughts, not the best lecturer

Lots of reading and movie-watching, with boring lectures. Is not a good lecturer, but tries her best and is very nice. She was hampered by the other 2 professors, overall not awful, but would be better in a smaller class.

I took my first-year seminar with Dr. Yaqub and absolutely loved it. She was a very caring teacher and really encouraged the class to participate. Expect daily homework in this class, but nothing over the top.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: This class had a homework assignment every day but none were graded until the end of the semester when they were looped into one cumulative grade. The final project is a group project, and all the groups have very different prompts. There are a lot of readings and films to watch. However, I could tell she was really passionate about the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: average. wasn't a good lecturer for a big class, but wasn't the hardest prof for the course.

Professor Yaqub is a great person and is passionate about her work. However, in the new course setting she was often hard to hear during lectures. She assigned lots of reading but reading quizzes were moderate difficulty. Even though she's great, don't sign up for this class, it will be too much on your work load for a gen ed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Generally a fine instructor, she was helpful in office hours and helped me understand what I needed to study for the midterm. She assigned SO MANY MOVIES. And books. This class has a quiz for every class meeting and the questions are very specific. I wouldn't take a class with her again but she's not the worst B&B professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Her lectures were somewhat boring and often more about artistic interpretation than borders, etc. When she isn't talking about a book or a movie she is actually pretty interesting. This class isn't hard at all if you just put in the base amount of effort, but Yaqub could have been better. She also has a notable bias towards Palestine.

She really struggled to control a large class ("Borders and Boundaries") and lacked assertion/authority. The biggest problem was I couldn't hear/understand her: she spoke very quietly, she mumbled, she had an accent, and she always wore a mask. She also never presented the other side of arguments which I thought "analysis" was supposed to be about.

Seemed like a sweet person, but clearly wasn't used to handling such a large class. Her classes were very slow and dragged on, and it almost seemed like she wasn't prepared for each lecture. Mostly just assigned long documentaries for homework. I'm so serious, don't take Borders & Boundaries. The difficulty and frustration just about killed me.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Seems like a very nice person, but she clearly didn't know how to lecture to such a big class. A lot of her portion was just assigned movies and then we'd just go over the movies in class; it really dragged. It was okay for me bc I'm interested in the subject, but it was hard to get through her lectures. Sure she's better w smaller classes.

Professor Yaqub was not very good at lecturing to a large class. She assigned a ton of movies and then would spend the next class basically recapping the movie we already watched. Her portions of class were probably my least favorite but she seems very nice and knowledgeable. I think if you're interested in the topic she would be great.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: With this being a 300 person and 3 professor class, it was often choppy and disorganized. It felt as though Professor Yaqub could not control the class, and often rambled. She seemed like a really nice professor who cared, but was not used to handling 300 students.

She is very passionate about her work and teaching and that allows the students to become passionate. She is willing to help you if you put in the work. During her lectures, you just need to pay attention and you will get all the information needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Respected

reviews.comment: This class was so. boring. Do not recommend. There are 50-100 pages of reading/2 hour documentaries before every class along with a reading quiz that asks the most obscure questions that are often written poorly. The exams were too hard. The professors are not funny and slow with tech. A Gen-Ed should not be this extraneous.  Save yourself the time

Literally the most boring lecturer I have ever had the pain of listening to. Nobody pays attention or cares about the class and she is droning on continually for the entire class. Class is not hard and she is not a hard grader, just a ton of reading and a soul-suckingly boring class.

A real gem. I took her FYS 'Imagining Palestine.' Lots of reading for an FYS but all very interesting (and lots of variety). As a teacher, she cares so much. I once fell asleep during a class and when I woke up she had emailed me asking if everything was ok (not mad at all)! She is the least intimidating teacher, 10/10 would take her class again :)

Dr. Yaqub was really interesting to listen to and she was very educated. It is a lot of reading and a lot of films to watch. It takes a lot of critical thinking, but I loved the class. It's just difficult because you have to really work and think to be able to participate.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Took this first year seminar for 2 gen-ed fulfillments, but would not recommend it for incoming freshmen. I had to work for an A-.
