There were at least 4 papers, you have to go to class, and you have to participate in lectures. There are lots of FYS that are easy A's & the profs don't care about attendance. This FYS was not one of them
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is very willing to give outside help and loves it when it visit her office hours to discuss the material. A very good communicator and wonderful, knowledgable professor

She is so inspiring, one of the most wonderful professors I've had. She is so invested and knowledgable about the material, and is really interested in our thoughts and opinions. She works are to help us formulate ideas and gain a thorough understanding.
Very challenging class but if you do your work and she knows you're trying hard you'll be fine. You'll finish al-Kitaab 2.

A generally decent teacher. A good amount of reading and short written responses, but covers everything thoroughly in class and encourages a lot of discussion. Midterm and final are both take-home essays.
She's perfect I love her take any class she ever offers
Second time I've had her as my professor!! One of my favorite teachers here at unc
I'm not convinced IDST is much different between professors but she was nice enough and an easy grader
She was a good Data Literacy Lab instructor. If you turn in your work, you will do very well. There are only a few in person meetings of the class but she made those as engaging as possible.
Natashas amazing, no work, everything so slight, and shes so sweet
AMAZING! A wonderful class with a wonderful professor, who gave great, informative, and USEFUL lectures that all of the quizzes/exams were based off of. Take this class if you have the opportunity!

Amazing Professor! She made retaking stats an enjoyable experience. The one downside I had with her is that she often would respond to emails very late, and many times she wouldn't even respond. But, it was not an issue as she was very welcoming and always had time before or after class to speak. I would recommend taking a class with her!
The best professor ever. She is so understanding and welcoming to everyone. Work is not difficult because she posts in-depth explanations of content.
Genuinely easiest class if you just submit the assignments and do the pollev. She is super sweet and understanding so no worries taking this course with her.

She was wonderful. The course was structured where you watch lectures before class and do some compression questions (but that should take about an hour at most). In class we do review, poll everywhere, and work on assignments, which is really nice because you can get a lot of help from both Dr Parikh and the ULAs/IAs. Overall a great course!!!

Prof Parikh is a wonderful teacher! All assignments are online and take a short amount of time to complete, can finish in class with time to spare. Quizzes and exams are online, open note. She is very good at answering questions and will go out of her way to help your grade.

Prof. Parikh is a great professor! 210 content was a bit dull just because it's statistics focused, but she made it as interesting as it can be. Easy A! Labs are automatic 100s as long as you try, and assignments are pretty easy. I liked how detailed instructions were provided. Overall, take it with Prof. Parikh.

Professor Parikh is really caring and sweet. In the class, there is weekly assignments and labs which are not hard at all to complete. And all the exams will be taken online. Easy class and the lecture could be a little be hard to concentrate.

take this class! pollev in class, so attendence is required but u get 2 missed days. tests and quizzes are online at home. labs and assignments are once a week for accuracy. prof. parikh is a great instructor! i am taking another class with her next semester :)

Fantastic professor that truly cares, the work she assigns is very simple and can usually get done during class time. She provides so many sources to help, if you even need it because she is a fantastic teacher in the first place.
She is so great! You have an online midterm, and some assignments but they are very easy and straightforward. I would 100% recommend taking this class with her.

Prof Parikh is a great professor! Her lectures are easy to understand, and the structure of the overall class is very organized. Quizzes and exams are take-home on Canvas, she gives us a lot of time in class to work on assignments, and is very accessible through Piazza. Take this class!!

super nice, class was rly easy, poll everywhere everyday, labs every week for completion, assignments every week for accuracy but super easy and using jamovi. take home quizzes, midterm and final. uses piazza for participation

She is a great person! But on top of that this is the best class I have taken. The lectures are actually interesting and all test are take home and open note including the midterm and final. The only thing that you are not guaranteed to get an 100 on is the in class assignment but those don't really impact your grade. Take this easiest A.

Great class overall to get the Research credit, but make sure you pair yourself with a good group. Collaboration and communication is key to doing well on research project. The exams are super easy and asynchronous. Assignments could be graded a little harshly, but in general if you follow the guidelines for the paper you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This was my second time taking Parikh. Both times, she was an amazing professor. She made information very accessible and easy to understand. Most of the work is a semester long group project so make sure you have a good group. Exams were fairly easy. I never had a good grasp on research until this class. Would for sure take again.
Professor Parikh was very kind and always happy to help!

The group project was very easy if you have good group members that actually do there part. Lectures were pretty boring and very redundant if you have already taken 210. She was super sweet and understanding. Also I  wouldn't say participation matters a lot but she will have random assignments due that are completed in class.

Dr. Parikh is an incredibly kind professor. I had her for both 210 & 270, and I had a good experience in both. She recognizes that students are people, too, and is willing to work with you. Content, expectations & grading are clear & fair. Grading issues (slow; subjective) were due to the IAs, & Dr. Parikh was willing to talk through any concerns.
Amazing professor who clearly wants you to succeed. Class was structured around a semester long group research project. Online assessments and occasional worksheets were very manageable.

I love Dr. Parikh's teaching style and lectures. Her assignments are pretty straightforward and easy to get an A in. She is also very helpful outside of class. Tests are online and the only assignment that really matters is the research paper due at the end of the semester. 10/10 recommend her classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I LOVE Prof. Parikh, she is easily my favorite professor at UNC. This class focused on an overarching research paper, and every Friday was a work day without a lecture. I met with her multiple times to discuss the project in office hours, and she always seemed super excited to chat. Can't recommend her enough!!!

Parikh is amazing! Over the semester, you will be writing/conducting a research paper. She breaks it down and gives good deadlines, but the UA's grade VERY tough. Grades do take a minute to get back, and you often get feedback for your ideas after you've already had to write/conduct it. Learning checks along the way are application based.

Ever since I took 210 with her, I've looked to take other classes she teaches. She is amazing! She is so caring and her class is overall pretty easy! She cares about effort, not getting everything perfect! Take home exams, mostly homework and projects for grading.

Dr. Parikh was by far my favorite professor for Fall semester! She was very considerate in terms of helping with practice problems, questions on Jamovi Labs, and preparing you for the main exams! In addition, she offers a little bit of EC plus drops many of your lowest assignment grades, so getting an A is extremely doable. Highly Recommend!

For PSYC 535!
Dr. Parikh is incredibly kind. First 1/2 semester is Python, then midterm, then second 1/2 in PsychoPy and R. Big partner project makes up a lot of your grade, but graded generously. Weekly homework assignments and attendance taken on "lab" days. She starts from the very basics and is very approachable + reachable in office hours.

I love Prof P! She is the sweetest professor I've ever had and she makes class so enjoyable. The class structure consists of watching lectures online before class and then during class she reviews the more difficult concepts and does examples. All assessments are done outside of class, including the final. I could not recommend a professor more!!

Typically has a video/quiz before each class, then in class reviews the material. She spends the last part of class as a work period for the lab/assignments. She and the TA's circle answering any questions. You have to do no math! It is an easy class with a caring professor. Final exam was application based and by far the hardest thing in the class

Dr. Parikh was a very caring professor. Every first class of the week she asked if anyone had anything good to share. The assignments were completed in class and could be completed with peers. The lectures were videos that we watched before class. The exams were asynchronous. Overall, great course!

Super chill and sweet professor! I was scared about taking this class initially because I thought it would be super math heavy but it wasn't at all! The math was more conceptual and often didn't require many calculations! There were also a few extra credit opportunities throughout the semester!!!

Super interesting course structure, the lectures are recorded and you do outside of class, and you complete the homework in class, so that help is readily available. I loved her class because I learned a great deal from it without being constantly stressed. She is very sweet and I highly recommend her 210 course!

I'm convinced Dr. Parikh is the kindest person to ever grace the Earth with their presence. She begins every class by asking if anyone has good news to share, which is always a morale booster. She explains everything very well, and made what was seemingly a dry subject pretty interesting. The quizzes are easy, but make sure to study for the final!

Great professor and great class! The class was mainly flipped, watching lecture videos at home and doing assignments in class which worked great for me. Professor Parikh is amazing at explaining concepts and clearly cares about her students and wants them to succeed. I definitely recommend her!

Dr. Parikh is absolutely amazing. She is incredibly warm and encouraging, and made statistics fun! The class itself was very reasonable. All tests and quizzes were take home and open note, which helped me focus on actually applying/understanding the material. As someone who dislikes math, this class was great and convinced me to pursue research!
great professor, teaches well, quizzes are online, take home, open note. learned a lot, and grading is very fair. as a premed love the A in an intermediate psyc class for my gpa

The TAs were a saving grace. The class is online and maybe because math is not required, it's hard to figure out what you're doing half the time. It felt very hand-holdy the entire time. Also the Piazza requirement was pretty annoying. Not my favorite way to take a class.
I loved Dr. Parikh! She is just the absolute sweetest and cares deeply about her students and their success. The class content was incredibly fair and applicable.

Prof Parikh is the best! She is so kind and always available to chat about course material during office hours. The class content is fairly digestible and there is time to ask questions and work on assignments during class. If you have taken stats before, this class will be easy! If not, you should still be just fine as long as you pay attention!

Dr. Parikh is literally an angel on earth. She's the nicest human and her lectures are very clear and concise. She gives A LOT of extra credit opportunities, her quizzes are two attempts online, midterm and final are online, and she finishes the lecture early if she's done teaching. Her TAs' feedback is also very helpful for assignments.

Dr. Parikh has got to be the kindest soul on Earth. Her lectures are very straight forward and easy to understand, and she is also always willing to explain concepts that students may struggle with or answer questions. Please take her class, you won't regret it!

Prof Parikh is the sweetest and she genuinely cares about her students! She is always willing to answer any questions on the material and is super knowledgeable. All coursework is online and attendance is taken through in-class polls. Easy material if you've taken a statistics class and she provides plenty of resources to succeed.

Prof. Parikh is amazing at explaining concepts and incredibly kind. Quizzes and tests are online, and the coursework is pretty light. However, keep in mind that this class is just an introductory statistics class, basically none of it has to do with psych.

Material is very digestible, and tests are take-home. Prof. Parikh does a great job at breaking the concepts down and she's very kind. Assignments are easy. If you've taken any sort of introductory stats clas before, this class will be a breeze.
She's so nice, the tests are take home, and you learn a lot.

Pretty easy class especially if you put in effort. Assignments get trickier over time but quizzes and midterm are easy and straightforward. Final isn't super hard. Although attendance itself isn't taken, there are in class polleverywhere that count for part of the grade and using the piazza site. Extra credit is offered for the midterm and final.

This class was very easy, but you could also learn a lot about statistics. There is one midterm and a final that are both straightforward and very easy, all alone. The weekly homeworks do get hard overtime, but two of them are dropped along with extra credit at the end on the final. very easy class, best professor to take it with.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This is a great class and Dr. Parikh made it very easy to get a good grade. There are weekly homework assignments that can be tricky, but there are plenty of opportunities to receive help. There is one midterm and a final exam that are both very straightforward.

Dr. Parikh was an awesome professor. There are online lectures to watch before class so the class itself never lasted longer than 30 minutes. Assignments were tricky and graded meticulously but nothing too hard. Probably the easiest class I've taken at UNC so far. Dr. Parikh was very knowledgable and passionate. Take her class!

TAKE 210 W/ HER!!!!!!!! PLENTY of dropped grades, open note quizzes/tests (take home), and easy weekly assignments. I'm not a big stats person and I killed it. I adore her and she does this thing at the beginning of every class "does anyone have anything good to share" and it makes a big lecture hall feel a lot smaller! Love her! Take it!

Super clear grading and very supportive. All tests and quizzes are taken online and are open note. There are weekly assignments and she gives you time in class to do it with the help of her/TAs if you need it. Take 210 with her if you can!!

Prof Parikh is excellent. All tests are open-book, open-note, and take-home. Class never goes the full time. The problem is her IA's: a different one grades all your assignments so you never know what you're going to get.

Parikh is genuinely one of the sweetest and smartest professors I know. She is very passionate about promoting equality. I have a ton of respect for her teaching style as well. The class is easy yet informative. She helps you learn the necessary information without making things unnecessarily difficult. Very understanding and empathetic

Nicest person I've ever met. Easy material and well explained. Midterm, quizzes, and final were online and open note with 2 attempts and your scores averaged. She's accessible and an engaging lecturer. She gives SO much extra credit. You could have a B and bring your grade to an A solely from extra credit. I can't recommend her enough! Easy A.

Parikh's teaching style didn't come naturally to me, but I still enjoyed the class. She genuinely cares about her students and wants to get to know them. Sometimes I think she made things more complicated than they needed to be, and there are a lot of lectures (two 30-min videos a week along with the in-person class), but it was still pretty easy.

Parikh is great & cares about her students! The class is a lot of writing over the course of the semester, and you do your research in groups. As long as you pay attention & stay on top of things, you will love her!

Overall a good mostly async class. We had a zoom call once a week, but attendance was not required, could be made up by watching and answering questions. Quizzes and tests were fairly easy, although final was a little more difficult than I thought it would be.

Dr. Parikh is great. She teaches about the things that matter. It wasn't that hard of a class considering it was a stat class. I wouldn't say it should really be a psychology class, though. Either a stats or maybe ethics class, but it wasn't psych heavy at all. The software was super easy to use.

I loved having Professor Parikh for this course!  She is super understanding and gives the perfect amount of work that isn't too overwhelming.  Attendance isn't mandatory and is done on PollEv, and there is a midterm and a final that are both open-note and moderate.  Overall, I really enjoyed this class and loved having Parikh as my professor!!

Dr. Parikh is a great professor, and she really wants her students to do well. This is not a difficult class as long as you attend class and watch the video lectures she posts online. She gives you time to work on the assignments in class and ask questions if you have any. Great class, but beware the final was extremely difficult for no reason.

Really easy class if you are decently ok at stats. The assignments are written out step by step. She is extremely flexible and caring! The two lowest grades of everything were dropped (minus the exams), but we only had a midterm and final so it was worth it for sure. Recommend!

Assignments in this class are kinda hard and the TA's grade very harshly depending on which one grades yours.  Final exam was nearly impossible and brought a lot of people's grades down, did not match the energy of other quizzes or midterms in the class, the final was just unnecessarily hard

Dr. Parikh is an amazing professor. She cares about her students and allows them to work on extra credit. In my opinion, the hardest item in her class is the final. Attendance is not mandatory, but if you do not go you might miss something very important. She also has review sessions that are very helpful. I would definitely take her class again.

Loved this class, she is very kind and truly cares about her students. She is always offering help and making sure you are graded fairly. You get to select your group for the final paper and although it is really long it is split up throughout the semester so it doesn't feel too bad at the end.

Does PollEV for attendance. Quizzes and Midterm are super easy, everything is online. Makes sure you never fail and can never get lower than 75 on the comprehension Q's. Some of the assignments can be hard but you are allowed to work in groups. Great professor and wants you to pass with an A and you will understand the material, if not you'll be ok

Take this class with Prof P! There are online video lectures before each class so you learn at your own pace. She ended class early on Thursdays to give us time to work on the assignments. There are weekly assignments, a few quizzes, and a take-home midterm and final. All quizzes and exams are open-note and online. Super easy and not a lot of work!

There is a reason Professor Parikh has 5/5. She is awesome! There is one semester-long GROUP paper that you submit parts of along the way, so submitting at the end isn't too difficult or overwhelming, and you get feedback. All of her classes were zoomed and did poll ev, and every Friday the whole class was given to work with your group.

Professor Owre was one of the best professors I've had here so far. His lectures were engaging even though they were long and he is very charismatic. He's also very caring and genuinely wants students to succeed. I really liked his teaching style and personality! Class is reading heavy, but not too bad.

Professor Owre is a such a caring and funny professor, but the structure of the class was not the best. The lectures had too much information, and I didn't know what to focus on. Your whole grade depends on your TA. They say they don't expect you to be a historian, but the grading was so critical. Better hope you get a less strict TA.

Max gets so disorganized that it's hard to understand the point of the lectures. He gives no context for a lot of it, ultimately making it hard to understand for a beginning history class. All of the grades are based on the TA's, so you better hope you get a good one. I felt like getting an 'A' was practically impossible, even while going to hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Owre is an amazing professor. He took the time to learn my name in a large lecture class which I loved. His lectures are easy to follow and pretty interesting. All assignments are graded by a TA but the TA's are pretty fair. This class surprisingly barely had any reading which is amazing. Overall, He is 100% one of the nicest humans I have met.

You really can't miss with this guy. He is incredibly engaging, and when he isn't, he realizes and promptly takes a break. The course material is super interesting and the TAs are probably one of the best groups at the uni. He makes it really easy for the student to excel in his course and actually remember his material. Definitely recommend!
One of the best professors I have ever seen!

Max is truly one of UNC's best. I took this class for the gen ed's and honestly enjoyed it. Lecture was honestly interesting and Max takes breaks when it gets dry. Recitation and the homework sheets was not the same (so boring) but I liked lecture. Max cares you about as person, even having office hours outside when the weather is nice. Take this!

HIST is not easy. You have to work hard to get good grades. It is possible and with his help it's more than doable. GO TO OFFICE HOURS. He is so helpful and will work through any problem you don't understand.
Mr Owre is one of the best history teacher I've ever met, his courses are well-organized and his lectures are interesting. You will regret not choosing his classes!
GOOD PROFESSOR
BEST!!
Best professor I've ever met!!!

Dr. Owre is a bit disorganized, but overall a really great professor. His lectures are interesting and he's very passionate about his material and students. The course portfolio is a lot of time and work, but you really will learn a lot. History 140 is a good way to satisfy three gen ed requirements.

I wanted to like Max and this class but I just couldn't. His lectures are overly verbose and since he slacks on posting the readings, I was constantly confused about the material. It is obvious that his other job, exec. director of Carolina Public Humanities, is his priority and he doesn't make enough time to be an organized/effective professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Owre is a glorified high school teacher. Lecture is usually boring but class is easiest I've taken. Im a B+ student that will probably make an easy A. Busy work for recitation, but TA's were great. 2 easy take home midterms (only time I used the white textbook). Requires out of class activities for "course portfolio" (most of grade). Easy 3 geneds.

I feel set up for failure in this class. I want to stay on top of the readings, but he doesn't post them for class ahead of time or even for weeks after the fact. Also, engaged activity reports  dumb. I go to every class and recitation, but still think the best possible grade I can get is a B. I feel like I work so hard but it doesn't even matter.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: LOVED MAX! Not only does he have an awesome & funny personality, he's also an amazing & caring professor. He genuinely wants students to come to his office hours & ask him questions about the material-I went and he eagerly helped me write & outline a research paper for a DIFFERENT class. Reading isnt totally necessary but go to class & u'll do well

Max is such an energetic and upbeat guy. He really is passionate about history and cares about his students. You can tell he is here at Chapel Hill to connect with students and teach them about life. His lectures are very interesting, however they are random and jump all over the place. Overall, I really enjoyed Max.

one of the best professors I've had here at UNC, took three classes with him and would take them all over again. He is very enthusiastic about history and making sure you know the material. Does require lots of reading every week. Overall his lectures were interesting and his choice in music as well. Definitely  worth taking a class with.

Seriously he's incredible. I think the most important thing to consider is how much he somehow makes you want to know more about the subject. It's a LOT of reading, but his enthusiasm is really inspiring and he's always there to help when you need it. He expects a lot, but he gives so much in return.

Max is a exceptional teacher whose genuine enthusiasm about the topic makes often long/content-dense lectures entertaining and enjoyable. He knows most students in this 125 class by face and name. The class entails a lot of reading (textbook and novels) and is essay-based. Would highly recommend both this class and teacher.

AWESOME PROFESSOR. Class was always fun. He's really funny and enthusiastic and genuinely excited about history. Not an easy A... BUT even without an aptitude for history, if you go to class and read the text you'll probably atleast get a B.

I loved Max's class! This was the second class that I had taken with him and it was even better than the first. It was smaller in size and there was a greater level of discussion. He expects a lot from his students, but you also get a lot out of the class, so it's a fair trade.

Max's lectures are entertaining and packed full of information.  He is smart and passionate about both history and teaching.  Reading is very long and dense.  Be prepared to read a new book every week, in addition to daily readings in the text book.  Takes attendance in class.  Good class to learn, not a good class for an easy A.

Awesome professor. He clearly loves what he does and does it very well. His lectures are very entertaining and he is just a very likable guy. Always very helpful and understanding. Seems like he genuinely cares about his students. Very highly recommended.

Very hard grader.  Barely touches on the book but speeds through pertinent information in the lectures so he can sing/talk in French/discuss hippies. Kind and helpful, but grading system is very unclear.

Very hard grader.  Barely touches on the book but speeds through pertinent information in the lectures so he can entertain the sing/talk in French/discuss hippies. Kind and helpful, but grading system is very unclear.

Max (he is very informal) is a great teacher. He cracks a lot of jokes...he reminds me of Conan O'Brien. He is a hard grader but I didn't try very hard. When I went to see him, he was very helpful. I wouldn't say he is "hot" but he grows on you. He is definitely not ugly.

Owre is a really great professor. You can tell he likes what he teaches and knows his stuff. His lectures are dense, packed with information so taking notes is a must. He can be a harsh grader, but he's also really helpful if you go to his office hours. Talking one on one with can clear up any confusion on grading and how to make your papers better

Max was awesome. He clearly has a good time teaching. His lectures are just pure entertainment but there is also tons of information. He wraps things up and has really helpful reviews. Not an easy grader but very explicit with instructions and available to help. He's smart and nice.

Professor Owre was AWESOME. He is very funny and yet his lectures are serious and really packed full of information. He is the most helpful teacher I have ever had for writing. I went several times to his office and he took all the time in the world to help me. He looks and acts a lot younger than he is. Did I mention he is hot!
No Comments

He is funny, smart, and cute. Cracks a lot of jokes and doesn't take himself too seriously. He is a HARD grader, very demanding with writing but fair. He is also the most helpful teacher I have ever had when it comes to learning to improve. His lectures are very entertaining.
Lots of reading and writing and the contents feel super boring and dense. Plus, this class has high threshold (95%) for getting an A. Take this class if you truly enjoy religion.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Very nice and helps everyone

Todd was great for RELI 121, lectures were mostly discussion based and centered around groups of 4. You should really do the readings if you are going to have any hope of understanding the class, but if you buy into it it will be top their!

Professor Ochoa is a very kind man and assumes excellence in students. You have a discussion board and a short writing assignment every week(allowed to skip 3). From my understanding these assignments were graded based on completion and you just had 2 longer papers graded by TAs. I took notes in class and had no trouble writing them.

Passionate and caring professor. The small group oriented lessons implemented for this semester were a miss (especially if you're anxious speaking in a massive class hall). Class attendance is graded but may be *ahem* bypassed relatively easily with the check-in beacon system. Lots of homework is assigned, but was ungraded and therefore optional.

Awesome professor. Really knows what he's talking about is my favorite type of nerd/geek. He really does make the class engaging and provides nice discussions in class. There is a lot of material you need to read, however Ochoa does clarify ideas and concepts from them in his lectures. I would highly suggest taking this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Grade is mostly made up of two papers (a midterm and a final), while the rest of your grade is just attendance and doing the required work for recitation. Lots of reading but Dr Ochoa does a great job explaining them during lecture, and making intentional time to review the text before beginning lecture. Ochoa is a fascinating man.

Ochoa is one of the best professors I've had at UNC. Lectures were amazing and extremely interesting, class was fun and interactive. He makes very deep topics about religion and society very accessible to people of all backgrounds. I'm a CS major and Todd made me want to add a RELI minor. Not that hard if you just do the work and skim the readings.

I liked the setup where we were in groups and would always discuss the readings in class, although that meant it was a flipped classroom. He is a great, funny guy and he manages to make the theories of religion fun and interesting while being fair in grading and assignments.

I love love love Todd. He makes abstract topics and learning as a whole really personal. I'd describe RELI 121 as an introduction to the philosophy of religion class and I found it to be really interesting. Todd is realistic and understanding. You could get a good grade with little work, but I really loved engaging with both Todd and the material.

Cannot recommend prof Ochoa more. He was able to make deeply complex topics interesting, understandable, and relevant, and is able to make you feel important and heard in a large lecture class. There was a decent amount of weekly hw, but it was not too difficult, and the only major grades were 2 papers. Great prof, caring, def would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Sometimes his lectures were a bit confusing but recitations helped a lot. Easy class though for gen ed credit!

TAKE THIS CLASS!! I never would have thought I would enjoy a gen ed but this one was entertaining, very lecture heavy but interactive with peers, no quizzes or tests just a midterm paper and final paper. Recitation grade is worth a lot so easy to get a high grade in the class as long as you show up. highly recommend todd is the goat

TAKE. THIS. CLASS. TAKEITTAKEITTAKEIT!! Todd is an amazing prof. I've never been so engaged during lectures. Recitations and discussion posts are the only grades besides attendance and midterm and final papers which are graded super easy. Class is super open ended and engaging and content is fascinating. Don't do the readings, just watch the videos

The content is super engaging Professor Ochoa is the most engaging "lecturers" that I have had. I put that in quotes because his lectures are more group discussions than lecture. Your own thoughts about the content are important. There are very helpful videos that explain the reading content.

This class is interesting- it's honestly more of a philosophy class than a religion class. Lots of very philosophical readings and concepts. Attendance is important (20% of grade), and then weekly reading responses, midterm (20% of grade), and final (30% of grade). Class is overall not a ton of work, Prof Ochoa is also a lovely guy, kooky but nice!

The class was a pretty easy A. Showing up to class/recitation and weekly forum posts were worth half of your grade. The other half was 2 papers which took a lot of time, but even with my low-quality papers, I got an A on both. However, Todd doesn't grade these, it's your TA. So choose Arpan to be your TA if given the choice.

This class was super interesting; I'd never taken a religion class before (though I took philosophy in high school), but Prof Ochoa made the material as accessible as possible. Every lecture was so informative and interesting. He's also just a lovely guy; he's caring and funny. He cares a lot about this class, so he wants you to care too. 10/10!!

So far, Ochoa's reading assignments are incredibly philosophical rather than on the topic of Religious Things. If you're into roundabout ways of overcomplicating simple concepts (philosophy), then this would be fine, but as a RELI major this isn't what I signed up for. Plus, he has a weird pedagogy which leads to him not really teaching any content

I thought Prof Ochoa was alright. I did not enjoy this class at all. There were lots of readings you were expected to read before class, but if you pay attention in lecture they aren't really necessary. He would post the lecture videos online and have you watch them before class which I did not like. You are graded by attendance and like 2 papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Whether you're passionate abt reli or taking for PH credit, TAKE HIM! The class is def not your normal religion class, instead it makes you think about society. There's readings and videos, but you just need to do enough to complete the assignments (which are very easy). Overall really chill and caring professor, would take again in a heartbeat!
Todd is a good professor. I never read the material, just watched his videos. Lecture will clear up the reading.

The material was difficult to understand but Todd and the TAs made it easier through class discussions each day. The grading scale isn't optimal, as an A is a 95, so would avoid if you are trying to find an easy A for a class. Otherwise, grades are mostly made up of weekly small papers/forums (which can be easy to forget) and 2 longer papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very engaging and interesting. The readings were dense but he provides video lectures that basically summarize the readings. The lectures were kind of useless but fine. He changed the minds of students on the idea of religion in the best way possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof. Ochoa was great! I learned so much from his class even tho it was challenging. There was a good bit of writing, but there were no "wrong" answers. The weekly assignments were for participation because he just wanted us to learn, not say the "correct" answer. Class was mostly working in groups. I definitely want to take another class with him!

GREAT professor! Such a nice guy and made lecture very interesting. I took this class just for the PH credit but ended up really enjoying it. Participation and two papers make up the majority of your grade, so if you put in a little effort you'll get a good grade. Definitely recommend!

Todd is a pretty good professor and the class was super interesting and pretty slight with the exception of 2 long papers. It truly depends on your TA since they all graded differently. You could skim over the readings and be fine for the lecture as we all discuss in groups. Overall a good and interesting class and lenient professor

GREAT guy. I am a stem major and was dreading taking a PH credit, but this class was fun and interesting and easy. He made me excited to come to class and was super engaging with his students. He genuinely wanted to hear each student's thoughts on the topic even if it was a hot take. Participation is like 70% of your grade, so pretty easy class.

Overall he was an ok professor but his lectures were somewhat boring, the cause material is a lot, and he is horrible at responding to emails, and most of the time you won't get a response. I think it was overall a pretty easy class but if you have another option for this credit I would take it.
The course was okay but did not show any consideration to students for personal circumstances or even tried to be considerate.
Often wasted class time not on material and did not consider personal circumstances, did not bother to accommodate.

This was a great class! Grades based on forums and weekly writing, a midterm project, and a final project. The class is dicussion-based but since it's on the smaller side (20-25), people actually participate and it ends up being very interesting! There are readings, but they are not too long and usually we go over them in class. Highly recommend!

Todd and Montek Singh co-taught this first year seminar. It is very philosophy based and a little tough to grasp, but as long as you participate in class and get the gist of the readings and his lectures (they're a little confusing) the class should be easy.

What a nice guy! Accommodating and helpful. Be ready to laugh during his lectures - really funny professor. In terms of the content of the course, it was about COVID-19 and philosophy. He is really passionate about his subject and wants you to learn through communication with others instead of reading a bunch of material and making no sense of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: You can really delve into the readings or just skim them, either way, you will receive an A. the class is interesting enough where there's some joy to actually putting in the work to understand the material, but the TA's are very lenient graders so it's really your choice.

Personally, I found this class to be boring and was assigned many readings. Grading is determined based on the leniency of your TA, I really recommend Bryce! One thing to note is we started using the UNC check-in app to take attendance and there are NO absences, I think there would be some lenience if you email your TA. There is a lot of material.

Todd is a great professor! There are a lot of readings but as long as you show up to class he basically explains everything you need to know, attendance is taken on the UNC Check-In app. You will pretty much entirely be graded by your TA and the midterm and final paper make up about half of your grade. I would definitely take for PH!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Todd was a very easy professor for the PH credit, but your grade depends on your TA. That said, I think he is very lenient with how he tells TAs to grade, most people in my recitation got As on the midterm and final papers. No tests, just papers and a lot of readings.

This class is fine. Not too much work, but I did find it boring since I was not interested in the topic. You are graded on attendance, forum posts, a weekly 250 word response, and 2 papers. There is a lot of reading and I personally found it confusing but after attending class it became more clear.

Todd makes the class very easy. He lays out everything we need to do at the beginning of the semester. You have to do 2 major writing assignments: the midterm paper and the final paper. It is a very reading-heavy class but the recitation and lectures make it very easy to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I personally really enjoyed this class; there's a lot of reading and some of it is pretty difficult, but the lectures and recitations make it a lot easier to understand, especially if you have a good TA like I did, and overall there's not that much work for this class as long as you go to lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class is very lecture heavy, with no laptops allowed, but is for the best with the types of notes that you take. There are only a few essays for the class, and the rest of the grade is attendance and completion-based forum responses. If you show up to class it isn't very hard to finish with an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: A really good professor and very passionate about subject material, but I just found the class a bit boring.

RELI 121 was my favorite class this semester. Ochoa's lectures were always engaging and always left you in thought after. The assignments were very manageable and the 2 papers throughout the semester were graded very graciously. I highly recommend this class and professor Ochoa!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Todd was a great professor! He was charismatic and passionate about what he taught. I found lectures to be boring and hard to sit through, as well as the many readings for this course but overall I would take Todd again, maybe not this course though because it was not at all what I expected it be, and very philosophy heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Ochoa was by far one of the best professors I've ever had! He's very knowledgable and charismatic about what we were learning, which made the lectures really interesting. The class wasn't what I had expected but I ended up enjoying it much more. There are weekly forum posts and responses to the readings, but not too much to handle.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Great professor. said if you didnt read you wouldnt pass- not true I only read the first one and am on track to get an A. attendance is required and he seemed to be very repetitive and loved synonym but overall the lectures really helped to understand the readings- especially if you didnt read them.

Professor Ochoa is a really great teacher. I took this class for a general education credit, but I ended up throughly enjoying it. Lots of readings, but Professor Ochoa makes the class enjoyable through his discussions. You're graded on a paper and a presentation, and you often have to do readings to participate in the discussions in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Ochoa is such a good teacher!

I took RELI 322 with him and it was amazing! You do have to read to course content and weekly reflections are assigned. However its fairly simple and discussions he held in class are very insightful to those assignments. There was only two big assignments he required, other than that he was pretty chill and rather students participate in class.

Though this class is fairly reading-heavy, the material was very interesting and you can tell that Professor Ochoa is truly passionate about what he teaches and his students. The class was well organized, and the two papers we had to write were not very difficult. I would highly recommend taking this class with Professor Ochoa!

Since the class was online, I couldn't interact much with Dr. Ochoa. However, this class is interesting and it's a relatively easy course! The lectures were sometimes hard to digest, but they weren't too bad. The work load is manageable and it's graded fairly. Dr. Ochoa also had a clear layout of what each week would look like. Highly recommend!

The readings are long and confusing at times, but the lecture videos generally help out. The forums and weekly writings do not take long at all. There are 2 fairly long papers that are difficult at first, but should not take too long once you get started. Easy-going professor that is clearly passionate about what he teaches. Overall great guy!

The class is reading heavy, but it's nothing impossible. Professor Ochoa and the TAs were super insightful & welcoming, and I had an overall great time taking this class. Weekly 250 word responses & two 4-6 page papers. The curriculum doesn't focus on actually teaching about certain religions, just concepts. This is a pretty easy PH credit.

I took RELI 127 for a PH credit and this professor made me more interested in both religion and philosophy. It led me to take his class the next semester, which was similar but with different readings. There's 50 pages of reading a week and two 5 page papers, as long as you go to class and participate it is easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Todd is my favorite professor at UNC. He really cares about the topic, but is well aware that many students in his class are only there just for the PH credit. His lectures are great, he breaks down the readings and explains the theories with illustrations. Your grade in the class is pretty much determined from 2 writing assignments and attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I loved Todd's class. His lectures are intriguing, if you just skimmed the readings they made sense and his classes all tied well with each other. The class is heavily based on the written assignments which are two 5-6 page papers. The final holds essentially no weight so put a lot of effort into the papers! I would take another class of his again.

Although the lectures are extremely boring, it is clear that Professor Ochoa is passionate about the material and a very nice and funny guy. The grade for the class is based on 40% attendance and two 5 page papers which take time. The final exam is only worth 5% and is an easy exam. If looking for an easy PH credit, I recommend this course!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: reli 121 was a relatively easy class if you're good at writing long papers but his lectures are beyond confusing and there are literally never any grades posted.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Todd was a enthusiastic lecturer but sometimes did not explain the material in the readings well. There were lots of readings in this class - some of them were very dense. My TA broke down the material into manageable chunks that Todd lacked in lecture. Only 2 papers but weekly small writing assignments. Very low stress!

The reading for this class was pretty long but you can tell Professor Ochoa is super passionate about the subject and he explains everything pretty well in class. However, the papers were pretty difficult(graded by the TA) so make sure you attend office hours and participate in recitation.

Todd Ochoa is a very friendly professor that is passionate about the course material. 50 percent of your grade is determined by just showing up to class and recitations, while the other 50 percent is made up of paper grades that completely depend on your TA. Overall, you will have to work hard for a good grade because the essays are not easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: You can tell Ochoa is very passionate about his work. He will lecture for the entire period, and many times he opens the floor up for questions. The class itself is kind of difficult. You will have to read about two different readings each week, each reading could average around 30 pages. The readings are very dense and are about religion theory.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's a great guy, very passionate about what he teaches but the course itself its very annoying. The readings are very intense and it's hard to comprehend sometimes so you get lost. He will talk for 50 minutes straight, sometimes lets questions occur but it's a boring and frustrating class unless you like philosophy -- barely is this religion btw.

Todd Ochoa was my favorite professor here at UNC. The class is very easy and there are not many assignments. The final is given in advance so you have plenty of time to do it. I would definitely take this class again if I could.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Todd is extremely knowledgeable and has personal experience with much of what he teaches.  He's very enthusiastic about his class and wants you to think outside the box.  Explains things really well and loves to talk in office hours.  Only grades were participation and 2 papers.

The title of this course is very misleading as it is philosophy heavy and not religion based. Tough grader on papers and only a few grades are given throughout the course. Does attendance "pop quizzes" so attendance is required (most of the time I wanted to sleep during class). It gave me the PH credit but it was boring and frustrating.

Todd was a great lecturer, I always looked forward to class. He assigns a lot of reading but you don't necessarily have to do all of it all the time - just try to look over it before recitation so you can say a few things. He's a tough grader on papers but pretty easy with everything else so shouldn't be that bad.

Lectures are really enjoyable. Breaks down major concepts and heavy reading to digestible bits. Central focus on anthropological perspectives rather than theology and religious studies. Grading is mostly done by TAs and pop attendance quizzes, but they are definitely fair.  Final is 5% which is a plus.

I thoroughly enjoyed Todd's class. He truly cares about the topics he discusses, as well as his students' understanding of the material. All grading is done by TA's, but the only assignments are weekly recitation responses and 2 short papers. Definitely recommend this class!

Todd is truly passionate about this class. He makes a conscious effort to make the lectures relatable, which is nice because some of the topics discussed are a little abstract. Homework consists of readings which range from 10-40 pages. Todd stresses the importance of writing and editing. Attendance determined by sporadic attendance quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Todd is amazing. He doesn't believe in tests so the final only counted as 5% of our grade. There are two easy papers and the TA was amazing as well. They both really cared and wanted the best for you. The readings can be tough but Todd explains them all in lecture. Not what you expect but an awesome class nonetheless!

I wish I could take it again! it was definitely unexpected because it was more anthropology than religion, but I still loved his class. He always kept me interested. I took this class as a freshman and it definitely opened my mind. He clearly explained the readings better than any other prof I've had.  Grades depend on TAs though

reli 236 & 140: Todd is absolutely one of my favorite professors at UNC. He's a little out there, but he respects his students and makes difficult concepts more clear. He's very approachable.  If you aren't interested in philosophy/religion you probably won't like the class; but it's easy to succeed if you follow the readings & put in some effort.

He is very invested in the material, although he focuses far more on religious theory than religious practice.  I had him for religion in America.  Has midterm and final papers rather than exams, and uses attendance quizzes.  Doesn't make you get the textbook, loads readings onto Sakai.

Hated this class. Worst class at Carolina because of Todd.  Disliked his spin on INTRODUCTION TO RELIGION AND CULTURE due to his Anthropology background. Very Atheist and publicized his views. Confusing lecturer- not what I expected at all. Wish I would have read reviews first. Even our readings were titled Anth, not Reli. Not a fan. Very unhappy.

Liked the class but it was nothing like I expected. Viewed as more of an anthro category instead of religion and talks about lots of abstract things that you have to be open minded to listen to such as possession by gods or magic.
Really interesting class. This dude knows what he's talking about. Be warned - this class isn't about religious practice, as I expected, but about the thought process behind religion.

Lectures are interesting and Todd is obviously engaged, but he also talks in circles and the content is not AT ALL what anyone comes into the class expecting. Only take this class if you're interested in religion as an anthropological category and in abstract religious ideas

It's undeniable she is a great person passionate about the subject and accessible outside the classroom. However I would not recommend taking this if you don't have background in stats or math. The lectures are extremely confusing and require you to know the material beforehand. Hardest tests ever. If you take 435 with her good luck you'll need it.

I had her for 435 and 445. I really struggled through 435 and her lectures started getting pretty confusing, but shes still an amazing prof and person. I'm half way through 445 right now and I do think it's a lot easier than 435 and I am enjoying my second class with her a lot more than my first.

To be honest I did not know what to expect with a 400 level class called Introduction to Probability but it was like two weeks of introduction. PSA that you need to do calculus in this course and I spent like 14 hours a week on this class. Go to class and do extra practice problems because honestly understanding the question is half the battle.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She was amazing at explaining really hard concepts and connecting it to the broader picture of what we were learning. Definitely worth it to go to lecture. The tests were very hard to even just pass after studying a lot, but the curve at the end helped so much
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lower averages than other sections. Failed several of her students. Insufficient prep materials for the exams. No recorded lectures. Exams were much more challenging than other sections. Homeworks take a ridiculous amount of time to complete. Professor has been falsely represented in her ratings. You've been warned. No curves when over half fail...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Stor 435 is an extremely hard class. Wouldn't recommend taking it during a stem-heavy semester. Homework was given weekly, but was extremely challenging most took me around 8 hours to do. Exams are also challenging but they are open-note. Her lectures are great and she clearly knows her stuff. I recommend going to office hours the prof is very nice
You have been warned.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was by far the hardest class I have ever taken. The exams were very hard and you needed to study for two weeks to just pass the exams. Mariana however is accessible outside of class and wants to help. Just know if you plan on taking this course, buckle up. Originally, I had a D but my final grade was "curved" to a B so that slayed.

Class started off strong with a decent first midterm. However, the second exam had an average of 40 with most of the blame being put on us, with content we really had not seen before. 80% of your final grade is exams, it requires a lot of work and studying with no results, seeing as how the final was also extremely difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of our midterms class average was a 40. She just reads exactly what the textbook says and makes the tests harder than the homework. She spent 2 classes asking us why we did so bad on the exam that she wrote. Do not take a class with her.

Weekly homeworks which get very difficult and I spent a lot of time on them every week. Attend lecture but if you really can't, she follows the textbook closely. Tests are hard. Our second midterm everyone failed so she released the same exam as a take-home to count as 40% of it, so she tries to help when she can.

This is by far one of the hardest class I've taken, but Prof Olvera is a great professor. She gave good examples, but she did go pretty fast so you definitely have to pay attention closely to pretty much everything she says. The tests are super difficult and require A LOT of studying and practice.

Prof. Olvera has a clear passion for math and teaching, she's so understanding and holds your hand through otherwise impossible problems. Homeworks and long and incredibly difficult, midterm exams are just as hard even though open note. Open note final is 40% of your grade but almost copies examples from lecture notes.

Super sweet lady. I like her as a person. Hardest class I've ever taken x1000. Tests were nearly impossible. Other stor professors would look at exams and be shocked she asked us those questions. Said she was giving same tests as she did to engineering students at Columbia University. I have never worked so hard in a class just to get a C.

Overall a good lecturer, but she missed a week in the middle of the semester and then tested the class on concepts that we had not learned yet. She also moves through examples a bit too fast, essentially copying from the textbook with little extra explanation unless questions are asked.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good professor. Lectures were straight out of the book, but she answers questions well and attempts to help people understand. Regardless of the professor, the class is extremely difficult. Two midterms: 1st easy and 2nd very hard, final tough, and homeworks are weekly. If you have to take 435, try to take it with her, but be ready to struggle.

Professor Olvera is a genius and she is extremely well spoken when it comes to statistics; however, that does not take away from how difficult this material is. If you fall behind, it is almost impossible to catch up. I respect her so much as a professor and it is clear that she wants her students to learn, but be prepared to fight for your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: very hard! the tests are way easier than hw (so much hw) but still hard. the first test was easy and the second was hard. avoid taking her for 435!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Didn't enjoy 305 (stor minor). Really wanted more active learning opportunities in class. She gave us a 2-part HW due 2 days before the final. The HWs require excel and on average took me 10+ hours each but exams don't even use excel. Stingy exam partial credit; 1st exam median was 77. 2nd midterm and final pretty easy though.

Dr. Olvera-Cravioto is a pretty good lecturer but it was very clear during the semester she had other priorities. She legit left during our final for a "very important meeting." There are weekly homeworks that will take you about 3-5 hours and its not worth nearly enough of your grade. I will say the class is very useful and still worth the hassle.
Really good professor and was super caring and flexible throughout the semester. Grading was a bit tight, however, on the second midterm and final. Would reccomend!

Professor Mariana Olvera-Cravioto is the best teacher that I have had in the Statistics department so far. She definitely knows what she is teaching. Her grading criteria is very straight-forward. If you attend all the lectures and do the homework, the class should be a breeze. Compared to STOR435, this class felt like heaven.

Easy A if you've taken 415/435 and want to strengthen your Excel skills, good introductory class to those topics if you haven't. She explains topics well and her exams are very similar to in-class examples and homeworks. She's accessible and communicates with students often. I wish more STOR profs were as structured and straight-forward as her
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Olvera is one of the nicest, most fair professors I've had. Tests are open note just like her 445 class. In hindsight, I shouldn't have taken 305 as a stats major. You can do zero work and do well (that's why I signed up), but it's far too elementary for anyone who's taken, say, past 435. She's still a great professor regardless

using chegg for the HW problems is essential: you won't survive the acute boringness of 305 unless you dodge the HWs. the lectures are necessary only insofar as learning the excel commands for the HWs. using clunky, boring excel, when you could learn python or R, is an enormous waste of time. take another STOR course if you can, you wont regret it

Mariana is one of the best prof's I've had at UNC. I had her for stor 305 and 445. Her ability to explain difficult concepts is amazing. She is willing to meet w/ students outside of her office hours and emphasizes that she wants to help us. Exams are fair, she is not trying to confuse her students. Take a class with her.

Heavy on the reading, but very entertaining lectures, talks as if he is telling a story and is easy to learn from. Easily accessible outside class, very kind and very understanding. Encourages people with no outside knowledge to take the class. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor O'Sullivan gave detailed lectures and made sure to show every side of the various historical debates that we covered throughout the course. He provides good feedback on writing for history and is willing to talk and answer questions outside of class in general. He is very smart but also very down-to-earth, and kind to students.

Dr. O'Sullivan is my favorite lecturer at UNC. He is passionate and pretty funny, although self-deprecating at times. I liked learning how history is still very relevant today in stuff like politics. Few assignments, and most are completion/effort. There is a lot of reading, but take the time to go thru everything to ace the midterm and final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Best professor I've had at UNC. 2 big assignments are midterm and final (both papers). He helps you with them before submission and provides great feedback.

Hard to take notes on his lectures, it's a LOT in a short class period. Very story telling adjacent, so he's fun to listen to if you enjoy the topics. Amusing, very caring, chill professor. Very understanding. Graded on midterm paper and final paper, and a few reader response. Lots of reading and one group presentation.

Professor O'Sullivan is so nice! The course is easy overall: 3 reader responses, a map quiz, a mid-term, and a final exam. Don't stress if you are struggling, go to his office hours and he's always willing to help. This course is reading heavy and quite fast paced, so make sure you do your readings or else you'll feel lost in class

Professor O'Sullivan is a very kind man who cares about his students, as long as you try to connect with the material you should be able to do well in this class. There are readings every week but he provides the material through PDFs. This class does not have many assignments so make sure to actually put effort into them.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Overall, a good professor but the class material is boring, it's based around a lot of readings and court cases, so she can only make it so interesting. The quizzes online for each chapter can be difficult but are not too hard if you go to class and pay attention. Quizzes could probably be done w/o going to class but would definitely be harder.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Not an easy course, but with 100% online quizzes you can do well on them. Attendance is optional and overall just boring lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You will not regret taking Professor Osborne! She is hands down one of the best professors I have ever had the privilege of taking. I highly recommend her course and she will always do whatever it takes to make you successful in the course. She definitely cares about her students. The course has challenging aspects of it as it is a law class.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took this as asynchronous during Summer I. Grade was completely based on 12 quizzes. I enjoyed the class overall, and Prof Osborne was super available to answer any questions, or just chat during office hours.

Very nice and helpful if you ask for it. The class is graded 85% on online quizzes which sounds like an easy A but even reading right out of the textbook the law principle is tricky. Would recommend going to her for help when you need it

I loved Prof. Osborne! Truly caring for her students. Her 326 class is graded 85% on open-book, open note quizzes and 15% class participation, so doing well on the quizzes really matters. I was having trouble with the quizzes for the first part of the semester and started emailing her specific quiz questions and it saved my grade. So helpful!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took her EXSS326 summer class and she rocks. She's really funny and gets to know all her students really well. She tells personal stories related to the law that are actually interesting, and she will help you out if you're ever confused or having trouble with anything. Participation is a big part of her class.
very easy...keeps you interested

Sports Management with Barbara Osborne Esquire was awesome.  She brings experience (she was an Athletic Director at a University) and enthusiasm.  I'd definitely recommend this class as an easy elective that's also interesting.  NO EXAMS AT ALL!  Only 3 written assignments!  What more could you ask for?
No Comments

Dr. O is odd, but I do recommend her because she'll change the way you look at the world forever. This class can be frustrating at times in the way that's like those tiktoks where the girl is like "when a man has a thought I had when I was 7," but don't take it to heart if she comes off as patronizing because she really does just want you to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. O is a great professor! The class itself was honestly not too bad, you just have to keep up with some readings (and you can honestly get away with not doing a lot of them). The tests were mostly short response with some multiple choice, but Dr. O and the TAs grade pretty leniently. Overall, fun and straightforward class!

Dr. O is a genuinely good person who cares about the class, her students, and the content. This being said, the class is semi-disorganized and can be redundant. Lots of reading, but you only really need to do it if you're doing the reading responses. Pretty liberal and not very open to other perspectives, so prepare accordingly. Go to office hours!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Attendance not mandatory, so I didn't go to class once. Assigns a good amount of readings but you only really need to do them if you're doing a reading response on them. If you know how to study for the tests effectively, you'll do good in the class.

We meditated before each class, which was kind of cool in my opinion. The course material is interesting and progressive, if you're into that stuff. The papers and exams were graded very leniently. If you can showcase within them that you did the readings / kept up with class, you will do very well. Attendance is not mandatory, but I recommend it.
Readings are long and tedious, watch a lot of very long films/videos. Exams are extremely easy. Papers are very straightforward, just follow the instructions.
By far my favorite class; she was a great teacher and made the content fun!

Dr. Osterweil's class was definitely the most unique I've ever taken really - it is obvious she cares about the material very deeply and really gets you thinking. Even though the class could've been a bit more organized and straightforward, I really enjoyed the energy and knowledge she brought to the course. She's also very kind, open, and driven.

Dr. O is a good person, but not necessarily a good professor. The beginning five minutes of every lecture were spent doing a grounding exercise and she rarely got through all of her slides. Reading was very heavy and mostly one-sided. She's very spiritual and Type B, which is fine, but might be better suited for a yoga studio than a classroom.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. O might be a good person, but as a professor, not very much. She is less like a professor/educator and more like an activist, constantly trying to impose her soft agenda on the students. Not very attentive, and her course is utterly disorganized. I highly DO NOT recommend her. Undergrads, please be aware!!

I was in her graduate seminar.
Dr. O is very polarizing. I like the readings, because I like to read things that challenge the mainstream. As a professor, I find Dr. O pedantic and critical, she is not good at active listening or constructive criticism. I am unsure what I am supposed to have learned in this class.

This class felt very skewed and assumed many things that felt extreme. I felt very unheard, and felt that Professor Osterwail would dismiss anything I had to say in class, and developed a distaste for me due to my views. I also strongly felt that this led to her and the TA grading my papers more harsh if they expressed differing views.
It is discussion based and you should be ready to hear out a lot of unconventional and different opinions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Osterweil is very passionate, knowledgeable, and interesting. This class was a bit more work than I expected, but was really valuable to me.

Nice professor, but the lectures felt very all over the place. It was often hard to take clear notes because she tends to go on tangents. However, the subject matter was interesting and she is very knowledgable and passionate about it. If you do most of the readings and pay attention in class, you'll be prepared for the exams and essays.

Dr. O is a hard one to rate. The concepts she teaches are very skewed-- very one sided, incomplete, and unacademic. Simply put, she says a whole lot of nothing... Nice professor, but really pounds her perspective only. Very liberal. If you are good writer, you will do well. Several papers, TA's grade everything, and a lot of work for a gen-ed.

Cool professor, but lectures/slides are all over the place. Concepts are vague, no clear definitions provided. Tons of reading every week, but not necessary to do well. Graded on 2 papers, 2 exams, recitation attendance/participation, 5 reading responses, 2 small assignments.

She's a super cool and passionate professor with a lot of knowledge. But to be honest, I learned very little from this class. Don't take 220 unless you need it for your major, she just makes things overly confusing and talks in circles during her lectures. The things she teaches are difficult concepts and she doesn't make it any less complicated.
Unless you are doing this class for your major, dont take this, its not worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: talks too much, says too little. unorganized.

I took this class in my second to last semester because I thought it would be an easy and interesting class. However, this turned out to be the worst class I have taken at UNC. There is no organization, the slides make no sense, and the lectures are incoherent. I would not recommend taking this class at all, let alone if you are a first year.

Professor Osterweil is very passionate about what she teaches, and I can respect that. However, what she teaches is incredibly politically biased. Be prepared to agree with her political opinion on tests and homework. Additionally, she's incredibly cluttered and jumbled with her reviews. It's hard to know what's going on most of the time.
she could not have made this class more disorganized if she tried

While very passionate about the course material, there was very little else I could appreciate regarding the course. The lectures were scattered, and most of the terms on our final study guide were either only brushed over or never discussed. She was so focused on "making connections" that we never learned what the things we were connecting were.

Lectures were extremely disorganised and often felt like a waste of time, but luckily the course is not too difficult so it is not too much of a problem. TAs are generally understanding and mark kindly. I would avoid this professor if you can.

Professor O truly cares about the material she is presenting and is passionate about her work. She comes across as very scattered as she always runs out of time for her lectures, refuses to allow proper time for understanding, and cannot figure out the room's technology. The work is not difficult but there is a wild amount of reading.
nice and cool! Lectures are interesting and insightful

She is very knowledgeable and passionate about the class! We love a professor who teaches radical ideas and questions the status quo. There are a lot of readings but lowkey you don't have to do all of them, the class was pretty easy and you get grace periods for a lot of assignments. She does move pretty fast in lecture so you have to pay attention

Insane amount of work. Each class period she assigns about 50-100 pages of reading and usually 2-3.5 hours of videos to watch. And then lectures are so disorganized that she never goes over what we read. Additionally, most of the readings assigned are so overly academic that have no real point. Missed opportunity to cover important content :(
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She is very passionate about what she is teaching; however, she often gets behind schedule so she ends up having to teach the material very quickly which makes it difficult to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would avoid taking this class at all costs. Her lectures are extremely confusing and god forbid you miss a class and go to look at the slides--it's just a bunch of random words and pictures that make no sense even with context. She spends so much time talking in the abstract that I have not learned anything concrete so far.

We have a midterm this Wednesday and on monday instead of teaching us the material she ranted about the Israel Palestine war, and how it was born and Irsael but supports Palestine and all that, we are all sitting here like we have an exam coming up, could you please teach us instead of giving us your personal opinion on a war

Dr. O does a good job synthesizing so much material into one course. Her lectures were engaging and helpful when doing the readings. There is a lot of reading but the majority of it is pretty interesting and valuable.

Great professor and overall the class structure is amazing -- very orderly and makes sense. Please note that she teaches radical ways to view global institutions + processes. If you can't handle that, you might end up like the upset people leaving 1 star reviews solely based off the course content!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. O is nice and cares about what she teaches! She also posts her slides and lists of key terms needed for exams. However, lectures were unorganized and rushed. And there was an overwhelming amount of long readings which didn't end up being necessary for exams. Content is interesting and valuable, but class was a bit stressful sometimes.

Her lectures didn't really make sense, and she tried to cram too much information into each one. The midterm test made no sense, the essays were confusing, and she was very unorganized. A lot of points she tried to make were common sense and repetitive.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: GLBL 210 is interesting But that doesn't make up for The amt of reading assigned. it is 100% unachievable. Lectures are crammed and hard to follow. She has issues with tech every lecture&forgets to upload things. centering activity gets old when we already don't have enough time for lecture let alone discuss the assigned readings. don't take her

Dr. O was probably the best professor I've had at UNC so far! She's very caring and passionate. I switched to Global Studies, and her class was a perfect start to the major.
