Really causes you to rethink topics often perceived as normal. Readings were very interesting! I recommend this class to everyone even if you're not a Global Studies major!

I really have not enjoyed this class... and it is my major!! far too much reading, readings for every class. The class is spent with her lecturing, they are rushed with many things crammed in and it has been very hard for me to follow. a little all over the place.. i am always bored during class.. I thought I would love this class and am kind ofsad

Absolutely amazing class, showed me Global Studies is exactly where I should be. If you learn better through concepts rather than chronological timelines of history like me, this class is for you. The themes are deep, complicated, and made me rethink the construction of society. A class I think everyone should take with the most understanding prof.

Professor O was not the best. She is a bit unorganized and rushes through the material and you are left confused. There is too much reading--hard to digest and rarely gets any attention or clarity. I would not suggest taking this class unless you must. It is a very polarized environment and not suitable for any divergence or vocalization. Not good.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Osterweil practices what she preaches, which makes her class that much more inspirational. Its one thing to teach socially inclusive and sustainable practices; its much more difficult to demonstrate them. While her class was incredibly reading heavy (and I don't typically enjoy a lot of reading), the material is very thought-provoking.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Like other reviews have said, Professor O. can be a little all over the place and the reading can be excessively long at times. Despite this, I did enjoy the class and like Professor O. as a person. If you're interested in capitalism and its shortcomings you'll probably enjoy this class and not find it too hard.

Dr. O cares about what she teaches and it's really interesting material. However, if you value structure DO NOT TAKE A CLASS BY HER. She does not give direct answers to questions, contradicts herself, and even the TAs have no clue what's going on with her. Midterms, Finals, and Essays were a nightmare to understand what she wanted.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Osterweil is a nice lady but she is very scatter brained. Most of the time she does not finish her lectures and the topics are very abstract. She doesn't do a good job of explaining things in class. However, the course load is manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Osterweil is easily one of the best professors at UNC. Don't let any negative reviews turn you off. As long as you're willing to read and come engaged to class, you'll absolutely get something out of it. Dr. O's class is really helpful for unlearning many of the things we take for granted ideas about the economy, power relations, justice, etc

One of the smartest profs at UNC imo. Her class can really rock your world. Class structure not traditionally organized, but I found it refreshing. Take this class if you want to start unlearning the toxic evil that you learned in ECON. Very anti-capitalist/anti-colonial. Not too difficult, I always skimmed readings and did fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Honestly everyone at UNC should take at least one of Dr. Osterweil's classes. This class was so transformative and eye-opening - We learned lots of untold histories and realities of the world that everyone should know about. Dr. O cares a lot about her students and is readily available outside of class. Your grade mainly depends on your TA.

Dr. O is very passionate about what she teaches and I learned things in this class that changed my worldview. However, she isn't very clear about her expectations and doesn't communicate great overall. The lectures were always rushed and it felt like she was trying to cram everything in, so it felt like we never learned what we were supposed to.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: The lectures are all over the place and don't make a lot of sense. She may advocate for understanding different perspectives, but if you don't agree with her very out there views, your essay and exam grades will automatically take a hit. It's a lot of fluff, and there's an excessive amount of readings that are all somehow necessary for the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: It is either a hit or miss with Dr. Osterweil. While I agree she is an awesome person and really seems to know what she is talking about, her expectations are extraordinarily high for her students. There is a ridiculous amount of reading and writing required. Lectures were just confusing and scattered (PowerPoints were not helpful whatsoever).
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: To be honest, one of my least favorite professors this year. She projects the image that she's flexible, but really, she can be nitpicky and kind of rude at times. She expects a lot out of you (which is expected in a college class) but she takes it to a new level by assigning things that we will not discuss in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. O hands down has made the largest impact on me in my entire academic experience. She is insightful, thought provoking, understanding, and kind. She is brilliant in the way she engages you in the interconnectedness of everything. Very accessible outside of class. She truly cares and it is so visible. Lots of really fascinating readings too!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: SOOOO cool. We begin each class with a centering meditation. She really cares about the health and wellbeing of students. I haven't gotten any grades back yet but it I've had to do some work. Tons of reading each night, and you discuss it in lecture. Very interactive, participation required. She's very flexible if you communicate with her.

Dr. O was an AMAZING professor. Class was discussion and not lecture, and we did field trips like eat lunch at her house and go to a meditation site. The class changed my view on the world. Participation is 50%, with midterm essay and flexible final project. Go to office hours for paper and project. One of best classes at UNC!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. O is one of my all-time favorite professors. I had her for GLBL 210 and adored her/the class so much that I signed up for 450. She is incredibly intelligent and encourages divergent thought and conversation. I would absolutely recommend her, the classes are life-changing.

She can be petty and unprofessional and it's the same with her TA's. If you have a disability do not take this prof. I have trouble paying attention and the TA misperceived it and punished me nearly every class. I emailed the TA about problems in class and she literally said there were none and wouldn't acknowledge it and it continued every class.

Dr. Osterweil cares deeply about the course material and her students, especially for her students to understand her point of view. She only shares one side of the story, painting the other in a negative light. The readings are extensive and sometimes not discussed in lecture. In the recitation, papers and attendance are many and mandatory.

Dr. O cares a lot about the material and her students, which is clear in the way she is accessible to us and holds a short meditation session in each class. It's not officially a seminar class, but it is, and participation is very important. The readings are mandatory to understand anything that's going on, and there is a lot of reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is an awesome gal who truly cares about her students, their education, and the topic which she is teaching!! Recitation is not that bad & I would take her classes again!!

While Dr. Osterweil is a great professor and passionate about what she teaches, she has an unrealistic expectation of how much time students can dedicate to her class. She assigns an absurd amount of reading for every class, minimum 3 readings, usually more, and they are all quite lengthy. She also expects you to watch lengthy videos outside class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Osterweil has been the most influential academic at UNC for me. Her classes carry a lot of reading, but she generally explains things well. Her passion and unique ability to make everything profound really engage students. If you want to learn something new and change the way you see the world, take her classes. If you just need a credit, don't

Dr. Osterweil was one of the best professors I have had a UNC so far: incredibly passionate in her lectures. Beware there is a LOT of reading assigned and you do need to know the readings for lecture. However, the syllabus is very direct and what is expected is always clear. So as long as you are engaged as a student, you'll do great!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Osterweil is a very special lady. She's very passionate about the subject matter, but as a result, she assigns too many readings and her lectures are disorganized. Often shows films in class and repeats herself over and over again. I would steer clear for the intro class GLBL 210, but one of her more specific, in-depth classes might be better.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I really liked the class and all the information we learned. Definitely a prominent bias in her lectures, but still helpful in seeing things differently than you might have before. TA grades everything but if you ask is clear about what they want. Not a heavy workload if you keep up with readings and various short papers assigned.

The material discussed in class is very interesting. However, there is a huge reading load and she expects you to know every single reading for the exams. The tests were way harder than they needed to be and she was inaccessible outside of class. She is disorganized in lecture and she doesn't clearly communicate her expectations.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The class was definitely interesting and we talked about many aspects of globalization. However, she's highly disorganized during lecture and she can be hard to follow. She's ambiguous with everything, so it's hard to know what is expected out of you in class and for assignments. When I would go to her office hours, I would leave even more confused
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Class can sometimes have an overwhelming amount of info, especially from powerpoints and long-winded discussion/lecture. But overall, this class was one of my favorites here as it opened up my perspectives on globalization as a whole. There are many sides to the story of globalization. Getting through the readings is the toughest, but bearable.

Very good readings, but unfortunately to an excessive amount. Lectures were usually engaging, but sometimes redundant if you do the readings. Heavy workload. Part of the course centers around debates, and only one side is ever presented. Occasionally, the opposite side is trivialized.

Two of the best classes I've taken at Carolina (GLBL 210 and 490). I recommend her to everyone I talk to interested in Global Studies. Incredibly intelligent and insightful, I could listen to her lectures all day.

This professor made the course tougher than it should have been. Slides were very disorganized. I always got lost during lectures because she tends to go all over the place. Role was taken in recitation, but not during lecture.

She covers the topic of global issues pretty well. Tests (one midterm and the final) & recitation weren't too bad. She probably relies too much on movies & clips to explain things, and her personal radicalism is obvious in the way she teaches (could be off-putting to some.)
Very in depth class that challenged the way I thought--not always easy to come by at Carolina.
She has been, by far, the most influential instructor during my time at UNC.

Globalisation is by nature hard to teach, but Osterweil is incapable of teaching it at all. Powerpoints are vague at best. Never follows through on interesting questions raised. Her left leanings taint her lectures too much. Readings were sometimes useless, had little relevance and were just things she thought were interesting that week.
Lacks depth. She makes simple, recognizable trends in the world seem as if they are profound. She continually poses questions without offerring concrete answers to those questions.

She is very passionate about the course material, but she has a real inability to articulate her points clearly. She uses long, incomprehensible run-on sentences that string together incredibly diverse topics. The class lacks real structure and concrete content. Makes easy, introductory concepts seem complex. Never really achieves any depth.

Attendance played a big role in grading. Students were often asked to upload photos, which were then used to track attendance. The class felt quite boring, relied heavily on cold calling, and the slides were very amateur and could be much better. Overall, grades seemed to be based more on attendance than on actual learning or engagement.

Long cases and a quiz required for every lecture, were just a large amount of time and super exhausting. Ott is a good lecturer, however, the final project (which is a presentation) is a large amount of time and the average for the final project was a 75. I felt like it was hard to know what he was looking for since the TA graded our quizzes
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: I personally like Prof Ott, but know others who didn't. He's a tough grader, good lecturer and a nice guy. This course is based on 9 case studies with quizzes on each and a final group project. Grade-wise, it's 30% - Participation, 40% - Quizzes, 30% - Group Project. This class has a lot of reading, and if you do it, you'll do well.
this guy bruh. unbelievable. idek what to say about him.

one of the meanest professors I've ever had. one of my best friends & I took this class together, and she got low-key persecuted the whole class by the professor. He was unbelievably rude to her & conveyed no respect over emails. He will say criticisms in the most unnecessarily condescending ways. also, 0 structure, no curves, & interrupts you.

Z-man is a great man and scholar, but an awful teacher. His disorganized teaching style, combined with the esoteric/incomprehensible subject material makes for an absolutely baffling class. He doesn't post grades until the last week, gives rubrics for nothing, and will never assign anything normally on canvas -- only through announcements.

This guy looks nice but turns out to be MEAN. He never released the grades during the semester, and he sent me sarcastic email when I argued about my grades and asked for grade breakdown during the final weeks. He is also not responsive to emails and not helpful during the semester.

Z-man is the goat, without a doubt the best professor I had at UNC. He is an amazing lecturer and super funny. With that said, this class is a lot of work. Weekly one-page writeups on the readings (which are very long), one in-class presentation, a midterm, term paper, and final exam. The midterm and final have hard passage ID sections.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Z-man is super nice but there is a ton of content and a lot of reading. One-page papers are required weekly (on readings) and there is a term paper. The midterm was hard but graded fairly. Both the final and midterm have a lot of information on it. I would not take this class if you are not a religion major.

Overall a great guy and you can tell he cares about his students. I had difficulty in this class not because of him, but because I could not comprehend the content. If you genuinely enjoy philosophy you will do fine in this class. He made sure to help us review and prepare for exams/papers and genuinely put in time to create resources to help us.

Z-Man is a nice person and very knowledgeable in the subject. The readings and curriculum is VERY difficult for a first year seminar. His comments on your work will be harsh, and sometimes mean, but I believe he means well. He's a very tough grader but can be reasoned with. Take another class unless you're up for the challenge.
The rudest professor I've ever seen. Very passive aggressive.

Z-Man was such an amazing professor. While his class requires a lot of reading and studying, if you go to class and keep up on readings, you will be fine. Plus, it helps that Z-Man is funny, caring, passionate, and helpful. He really cares about teaching and getting to know students which is why I'm taking another class of his next semester.

Z-Man is one of the best professors I have had at UNC. A lot of people in this class know a lot of information on Christianity going in, but I knew nothing and was still able to do well, but probably just with more effort. He is a very passionate and fun guy, just make sure to pay attention in lecture and write down all the important stuff.

I am graduating this semester; this was the best class I took at UNC. Z-man was amazing. I took this class to fulfill a WB credit and became so interested in the topic. Course topics are engaging and class discussions are respectful but truthful. He is also world-renowned for his research, I ended up citing him in my final essay.

Zlatko seemed nice, but put us in uncomfortable situations in class. The readings were complicated and often very long, so when asked to recall info during class, people obviously had a hard time. He took it personally and got super intense and accused students of not reading. He was also a bit passive aggressive and was a terribly hard grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof. Plese is a very intense teacher and gets really annoyed when people don't do the reading, which there is way too much for this class in my opinion. I got overwhelmed and basically stopped doing the reading halfway through and then just crammed for the midterms and the final. I still found it a pretty interesting and fun class though.

Loved Z-man, but the class was much harder than I expected. I'm pretty sure the amount of reading/writing is supposed to be standardized across all the FYS though. It is a lot of work and not always easy to understand. Z-man is very engaging and cares about his students, but his grading scale was not clear at all
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: For someone who is not a religion major, Z-man was great. He helps ease you into material and makes it accessible. The lectures are a little all over the place but if you pay attention you will be able to do fine on the exams and on the paper. The midterm was tough but if you understand the structure you will do well on the final.

Z-man is the MAN. Awesome professor, nice, funny and makes the content extremely engaging. Not a completely give me A, and you do need to attend class, but not a difficult class. Engage in lectures and study for exams and you will do well. Exams were graded a little tough.

Z-Man was such a joy to have this semester. His lectures were extremely animated. He playfully yelled at the class when we didn't know the answer - not because he was mad, but because he wanted us to engage and understand. The write-ups are super easy if you read the passages, as well as the term paper. The midterm and final exam were also easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Z-Man was a great professor and he was a very interesting person. I enjoyed taking his class and the topic of the seminar. However, I will say that you don't know what your grade will end up being until the day grades are due and he's a tough grader. But he really wants the best for the students and teaches you to think critically about everything!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I took this class as a seminar credit, and although I learned a lot and was challenged in a positive way, I wouldn't recommend if you want an easy first year seminar credit. Z-man is a really interesting guy, but beware of all of the readings, it would take hours. I would recommend if you are very intrigued by philosophy and can grasp it.

Zlatko is a cool guy but the class is not so fun. Lots of reading, essays, and very difficult midterm/final. If you want to be a religion major, I would say take it. Any other major? Not worth your time and effort. Take any other class if you just want the gen ed. Class itself enjoyable, work outside of class is brutal. Grades are harsh as well.

He was the best professor I have had at UNC by a mile. I normally hate being in class and find it to be a waste of my time, but the content of the class at Zmans passion about it makes it really interesting. The reading is long and dry, but you can read Wikipedia summaries of it and get the rest from class. Not an easy class, but interesting.

No clue at all how he has this many positive ratings. Class is extremely incoherent. Midterm and final are the hardest tests ever and the only thing ur graded on. 350 characters isnt enough to express all that is wrong with him. Even the religion majors in my class had no idea what was going on. Again incoherent is the best adjective for this class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The midterm and final are some of the hardest tests I've ever taken and I studied a week in advance. The class itself is extremely boring and your grade really only comes down to the final, midterm, and one paper. Would not recommend taking if you just need a WB credit there are definitely easier ones.

Z-man has been my favorite professor at UNC by a mile. He is entertaining and very knowledgable. He is also fair with his grading. I would highly recommend taking his courses but be ready to read a fair amount.

Z-Man is a fantastic professor. His lectures are enthralling and kept me interested throughout a gen-ed religion course. Z-Man is caring and understanding while also hilarious and he really made this class a treat. However, I do not recommend taking RELI 617 for your WB gen-ed, I am a real idiot for choosing a 600 level course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Enjoyable class with material completely new to me. workload was manageable (readings for each class and 1 pg 2xspaced writeups for completion once a week), plus one very easy presentation, one paper, a midterm, and a final. The midterm and final both are challenging but prepare ahead of time and it's manageable.

Z-man is one of the best professors I've ever had. So charismatic and loves the material he teaches. Lots of readings, a weekly write-up, term paper, midterm, final, and participation. The midterm was a lot harder than necessary for a 200 level class but he definitely wants you to learn and succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Readings assigned every night and starting week 4 there is a weekly one page reflection on them graded on participation as long as you show that you read. Other than that there is just one midterm, one final, one presentation (very easy), and a term paper near the end of the class. Z man is great, 10000% recommend.

Plese is a truly bizarre but incredible guy. Loves to talk outside of class and rewards intellectual curiosity. He will try to convince you that you can destroy the material world with your mind, but what else could you want from a professor?
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Z-man is the absolute best professor I've had at UNC so far. The curriculum for this course incredibly engaging, and I learned so much throughout the semester. He has pretty specific expectations for written assignments, but it's very reasonable for such a high-level course. Definitely take a class with him if you get a chance.

Love this professor so much! So nice and really wants his students to succeed. A lot of the topics covered were things I have not learned about, but Zman's lectures were helpful and he is so passionate about this class. He really wants students to participate during class, so make sure to do most of the readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Z-Man is the absolute truth! Online classes can feel monotonous but Prof. Plese's moxie and charisma helps his students enjoy the class. He does have an accent but it's not bad at all. Don't skip out on the readings or you may have a tough time doing well in the class. Overall, listen to Z-Man and you will come out of the class with a good grade.

I seriously love Z-man, I changed my minor to Religion because of him! He genuinely cares so much about his students and the subject, and it really shows in his lectures - so entertaining. Although sometimes he is a little too passionate and his lectures go a bit all over the place, he gives you all the slides to use to study & they are informative

Fantastic man. This has been objectively my toughest (and worst) semester so far at UNC, and Z-Man was the one prof I genuinely enjoyed, looked forward to, and who actually cared about how I and my classmates were doing. Very caring, very understanding, very real and very funny. Absolutely take him if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Although Z-man cares a lot about his class, he can be rather difficult. He will take assignments late and not penalize because he is "a nice guy", but this can be problematic for everyone who turned it in on time. Furthermore, he's asked specific things of me and then when I do them, he penalized me. Finally, he will grade things he said he won't.

Z-Man is full of charisma when teaching. He gives a lot of reading assignments but if you read, the 2 exams are super easy. He is passionate about teaching religion and makes learning fun. A weekly 1 page double space analysis is the toughest part but it is not graded harshly. 10/10 would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: Can be kind of hard to understand because of his accent. The tests were hard and you won't pass unless you really know the readings. He was very enthusiastic but sometimes hard to follow.

Z-man is by far the best professor I have had at UNC. He is so passionate about the subject and has a great energy and is so much fun. There is a lot of reading assigned but not all is necessary. There are only two tests during the year and one big paper, so your grade rests heavily on how you do on those. Phenomenal class, wish I could take again
Z-Man is the goat and that's all that needs to be said.

Z-man is the best!! This class got boring at times, but overall the material was really interesting and he is a great lecturer. There is reading assigned every class but you really only need to read the primary sources, since that is the stuff on the exams. As long as you put in a little bit of work you should get an A!! Totally recommend!

Z-man is a revelation all by himself!  Listen, his topics are difficult to explain and it takes someone with an enormous intellect to get these ideas and concepts across.  He invests a lot of energy doing just that.  He is an inspirational professor and he's a pretty groovy guy to boot.

Prof Zlatko is truly an inspirational professor and someone who knows how to keep students engaged. The class had lotssss of reading but it was mostly very interesting. Really nice professor and a challenging, rewarding course

Z-Man is amazing. He keeps you engaged in all of his lectures and is super funny. He really expects you to talk and answer his questions but if you do the reading then it's not hard. I would take him again in a heart beat
Interesting guy and great class.  His attitude towards the subject makes you want to learn more and keeps your attention.  I would take another class with him!

Z-man is the best professor at UNC. He is engaging and funny. You do have to work for his class, but it is well worth it if you are into Religious Studies at all. Even if you are just a Christian and interested in the early centuries, take his "Varieties of Early Christianity." Well worth it.
It has been 4 years since I have graduated, and I still have respect for the man. His class was one of the most memorable for me in my career at Carolina.
No Comments
Zlatko is the man!  How dare you attack his accent!  His accent is frikkin cool!  Great guy, one of the best people I've worked with at UNC.

Zlatko is a great professor, and you cannot expect to learn anything from a great professor without doing some semblence of work.  The Id's could be difficult, but if you've done the reading you should be able to recognize the different tones and writing styles.  Overall, i highly recommend Z.

Zlatko's accent isn't that hard to understand.  There is a lot of reading for this class and you have to identify verses on the midterm and final which is a bit rough.  The class is fun though because Zlatko is really energetic and engaging.

This class is a little hard and Z-man's accent definitely doesn't help matters... But he is funny and likeable which makes class interesting, even though its not always clear.  could be organized better
Z tries really hard, but his accent is hard to understand (not to mention his handwriting). I'd avoid his class, the reading, and the exam ID's.
I took his eng146 and liked it a lot! A big part of your grade is participation in small groups.
This class isn't easy but Prof. Peterson is funny!

His grading doesn't go by points, so everything in Canvas was just shown as "completed" meaning you don't know what grade you have in the class until the semesters over. Still, he's really nice and makes games studies interesting. If you wanna play some games, try to take his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Peterson is an amazing guy and really cares about what he is teaching. I took him for his game studies class and I really enjoyed it. I am NOT a gamer but the class was still very easy. It's mainly group projects and essays, but every assignment was done step-by-step. We also always had a long time to do each assignment. I would take him.

Peterson's humor is very nerdy but funny. Lots of pop culture references in his lectures, so despite them being pretty long-winded, they were managable. His writing assignments were fairly easy and his section of the class was by far the easiest.
Very boring and basic class but since it's required he's great to take it with. Super easy grader and very flexible with missing classes and working around it.

IDST118 is a very boring and semi-difficult triple-I, but unexpectedly, I enjoyed Peterson's lectures the most. His assignments are usually rhetoric and analysis-based, so if you know how to write those assignments will help your grade in the class. His content is easy for quiz questions too.

Peterson, himself, is fine. His lectures are nothing special but he clearly knows his information. His assignments are not enjoyable nor are they helpful. The class itself is difficult and a poor representation of UNC's classes. The class is extremely difficult to recover from if receiving even a 70 on anything so I do not suggest.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's nice enough, but can be a bit annoying. It all depends on what type of person you are, but sometimes I found his humor to be a bit off and it made it hard to take him seriously. He is a passionate guy, and his lectures were fine but nothing special. I wouldn't say never take him, but if the millennial humor style annoys you maybe avoid it.

He was an absolutely amazing professor. He cared both about the students and the curriculum. Being that the class I took had a large focus on climate change, he emphasized on taking care of ourselves in this difficult time. The final was a website of revisions of the 3 essays we were given feedback throughout the course. Loved this class!!

Professor Peterson is easygoing and makes english 105 a stress free class. Everything is graded on participation, including the three major projects, and as long as you put in a little effort you will get an A.
Lectures were boring. Lots of busy work but it was easily graded. Information hardly related to the course. Overall the course was very hard and boring. Hard to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: As one of my friends described him, Dr. Peterson is "aggressively millennial". However, I really enjoyed taking his class this past semester. His section of ENGL105 is game studies specific, but I think he makes the couse accessible and fun for the average UNC student, not just gamers. We played games during classtime so automatic 10/10 rating.

In general, the class is challenging. DO NOT TAKE IDST 118 IF YOU ARE LOOKING FOR AN EASY TRIPLE-I. It is uninteresting but difficult, which makes the entire experience insufferable. DO NOT TAKE IT FOR AN EASY A. IT WILL TANK YOUR GPA. Peterson seems nice enough, just a little behind on today's humor I'd say. He seems very kind.
Terrible and long lectures, humor sucks, gives really mid assignments also.

Prof. Peterson is awesome. The class is super easy. Three major projects (article, podcast, and research paper) that are broken up into small increments so they're really easy if you don't procrastinate. The final is a website with all three projects. Prof. Peterson is quirky, funny, and cares about his students a lot. Best ENG105 option

Professor Peterson has been my favorite professor at UNC so far, really understanding and funny! All assignments are graded based on completion, even the 3 projects (one per unit) you do across the semester. These 3 projects also form the "final exam" which is really just a website with your 3 projects revised based on feedback and a short bio.

Dr. Peterson took the essential parts of ENGL 105 as a FY requirement and created a course that isn't unnecessarily difficult. Primarily consists of 3 unit projects that can be completed w/o stress as long as you're consistent with progress and participating in class. Lenient with grading and understanding of things like mental health. Cool guy.

he is a good lecturer, created an environment in his classroom that encouraged creativity, and gave students flexibility to pursue topics that interested them in the course. this course was more workshop based and most assignments differed from what youd find in a typical english class (podcasts, videos, etc). he was also accessible outside class.

Took Prof. Peterson for ENGL105 and he was great! I'd highly recommend him for this course. Assignments weren't too demanding, but still interesting, and they were very fairly graded. Very funny personality and he genuinely cared about his students.

2nd semester of teaching. Gets the job done for a class that is required for graduation (ENGL105). The syllabus is clear and as long as you put in effort towards assignments and follow the rubric, the grading should be mostly fair. Lectures may contain dry humor. Nothing too out of the ordinary (for the worse or the better) in this class.

Grading scale was a little strange (out of 700 points if I remember correctly), and for every paper he would not return a letter grade but rather a "strong" or "outstanding" etc. However, he gave good feedback on how to revise your papers so that you would basically be guaranteed to succeed on your final portfolio.

I had Dr. Peterson during his first semester at UNC, and I can say he was a great ENGL 105 professor! We learned about climate change in the video game industry and had the opportunity to play Civ 6 in class every other week. Go to his office hours often for feedback! As long as you put effort into your papers, you'll finish with an A!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class and Professor Abayomi's teaching was not very intuitive for someone who doesn't have any coding/limited stats experience. It isn't necessarily extremely challenging, but I would recommend taking this class when you have a lot of time to rewatch Abayomi's lectures and dedicate to the labs. He is funny and friendly, but pretty strict
Very strict professor, not care for or support students. Only create difficulties for our group project. DO NOT RECOMMEND.

I loved this class. Dr. Abayomi makes sure no one is left behind when teaching new content. He is very nice and didn't make it feel like an 8 AM. SQL is a straightforward language and has some cool nuances. Not that much work outside of class so can't complain. Exams aren't too bad and you have a cheat sheet too.

Very fun, approchable professor. Passionate about teaching and patient at explaning stuff to you. I feel he is too lax in this course. There are only 4 homeworks over the semester (each takes 0.5-1h to do) and there are not enough exercises provided to master the class.
Does not respond to emails.

Dr. Remi is a very funny and good teacher. He has a no nonsense mindset though, so don't be suprised when he doesn't give any leeway around late work. The course content is not that hard, but you need to actually put in work learning it yourself if you want to crush this class. Got by doing sort of the bare minimum and got an A-

Dr. Remi's personality made it worth it to take an 8am statistics class. He is a charming guy, and likes joking with his students. He taught pretty slowly- but only because he wanted to give everyone a chance to understand the material in this course. The workload for this class is very managable, and we had cheat sheets on the midterms/final.

Dr. Remi is an amazing lecturer; he explains concepts very well & repeats important ones we should know. However, he is a ghost outside of lectures. Never responds to emails & is not accommodating. I was one correct question away from getting an A- but he didn't even respond to my email about bumping me up. Make sure you have friends in this class.
Very mid lecture. Easy content, but the harsh grading makes the class harder than it needs to be.

The worst professor i meet in unc. The lectures were unclear, yet we were overloaded with assignments . The professor made no effort to support students, making the course feel unfair and needlessly difficult.
He is a good teacher and explains things clearly. However, he assigns a lot of work, sometimes not in a timely manner. You might have homework and midterms due in the same week.

The class itself is useful, but the grading was unnecessarily nit-picky. The professor was egotistical and unwilling to answer any questions or provide any sort of help. They spoke with an air of superiority and disrespect that I've never received from any other human being. I've never cried so much over a class. Do not take this class.

Overall, Dr. Remi was a good professor. Although this class has a lot of homework, it was relatively manageable. If you didn't take AP Stats in high school then this may be a difficult class. It is taught in python but you are expected to understand basic statistical concepts. I would recommend taking the class with him.

Old review got removed because I did not speak graciously enough about our lord and savior Dr. Remi. This class was not fun and he barely taught stats yet all the exams are about statistics. Take 155 instead. Also, if you ask a question in class he responds very condescendingly.

Extremely unaccommodating professor. Offers no extensions or drops on homework assignments, regardless of the circumstances, which makes the course unnecessarily stressful. Communication is a major issue—they rarely respond to emails, and when they do, the tone often comes off as rude or dismissive.

If you put in the work and time to really learn the course material, you'll do fine (think a few hours each week). However, the grading criteria isn't very specific, so there are many loopholes he can (and will) use to deduct points. Also, when going to office hours, he doesn't try to answer questions but makes you find out the problem on your own.

Take STOR 155 instead if you can, it is much easier. Got the worst grade of my entire UNC career, and I've taken chem and calc ll. In-class MC never reflects what we're learning and awards no drops for HWs, even though there are over 25 assignments. Also, emailed him more than two weeks ago and still haven't gotten a response. This guy is bad news.
The class isn't too hard, but the grading can be ridiculously meticulous at times. However, this is a great course for learning python and statistics.

We took our final exam on Friday but we still haven't received our grades. He was extremely rude to people who asked questions and he frames his final coding section with things we aren't familiar with and expects you to be able to complete it in 3 hours along with the multiple-choice section

Be prepared to hear, ‘Are you following the story?' and ‘This is very, very crucial,' along with gems like, ‘I'm already making my money; I don't care if you learn or not,' and, ‘In my side of the world, we did it this way...' all shouted at 8 a.m. on a Monday. If you don't need it, don't take it.

He says he's accessible, but he'll shame you for asking for help and make you think you're asking dumb questions. He argues that ‘it's 4 credits, so it's hard,' as if we signed up for boot camp. In his mind, students are the enemy, I guess we declared war by enrolling. Good luck surviving his battlefield of homework and take-home exams!

Beware of this class! It is insanely challenging for an intro-level course. There are no HW/lab drops or curves. You could be on your deathbed and Dr Remi still would not give you an extension. Never answers emails and talks down to you during office hours and when asking questions in class. Goes indepth on easy concepts, but breezes by hard ones.

Hardest 4-credit class I've taken at UNC (even compared w/ chemistry + physics). Workload and expectations are disproportionate for an intro level. He spends significant time overexplaining/ complicating straightforward concepts, while breezing through the difficult coding. No grades are dropped and no curves.

This class is just a cheap knockoff of UC Berkeley's Data8—he's stealing their work word by word and claims it as his own. At times he would switch the states from CA to NC to not make it as obvious. If you want to get a feel of how the class would be I encourage you to look it up, and practice. You'll pass the class with flying colors!

He presents himself as accessible but isn't. He shames students for asking questions, making them feel inadequate, and seems to view students as haters. The workload is excessive, because is 4 credit course you'll be finishing a take-home exam and multiple homework assignments at once. It feels like he prioritizes his ego over student success.

Dr. Remi is very smart, but he is not good at teaching the things he knows to others. As a student with no coding background, this class is very hard and Dr. Remi does not provide sufficient support to help you succeed. He does not respond to emails and is not approachable to ask questions, saying we would know had we paid attention in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Overall I  think Dr. Remi is a good professor and I  believe the exams are fairly easy. However, when it comes to asking questions about the content or meeting with him during office hours he is very discouraging and almost looks down at you for asking a simple question. On top of that some weeks we would be piled with so much work and assignments.

His teaching style is very engaging so time flies by in class. The content he teaches is interesting and he often draws illustrations on the board to help you visualize and better understand the material. He is clear with what he expects from you, reviewing outside of class, submitting labs/homework on time, etc. Definitely recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof. Remi is really nice and makes this class easy to understand. The material gets more difficult once the statistics part starts, but it is not bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Hard to understand. Accent is so thick that I was left wondering what he was trying to say. It was online which made it that much harder to understand. He's extremely cocky. Felt like he was mansplaining everything with an attitude that he was better than the class. Math is not easy and he didn't help this. I suggest finding a different teacher.

He doesn't care if you fail or pass. He won't take extra time with you outside the classroom because “he's busy”. Not a very good professor if you have to get any extra help. I did this all on my own because he wouldn't help me in any way.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: not a good teacher for STOR320; didn't grade final project EDA part as stated on the requirements/rubric(ie. rubric said to use table or graph for each question; deducted points on putting only a table or only a graph and said in class that it is because only one table or graph is not enough; argued but didn't work); TA too strict for hw/analysis

Professor Remi is a great professor who really seems like he enjoys what he teaches. Took his class in the summer but the work didn't seem like too much. Very reasonable and the tests were manageable. Very respectful of student's times. He made statistics understandable and provided many examples with opportunities to ask questions!

Dr. Remi is the sweetest. He made lectures engaging and easier to understand. The homework didn't seem like a lot, but towards the second half of the semester, it piled up. It was also very time consuming. There is no extra credit!

Dr. Remi is always respectful and fair to all his students. I was originally scared as someone who had never taken a stats class before, but his lectures made it so easy and he is willing to meet with you outside of class to answer questions. Although his homework deadlines are strict, he is very understanding and wants to help you succeed!
His written portion of the exams are easy, but the multiple choice make it to where its so easy to miss a few but they count for a lot. He makes class fun which is important!

The class is demanding and time-consuming, but Dr. Remi makes expectations clear at the beginning and provides helpful resources (lectures/notes posted online, accessible outside of class). There are 12 homework assignments, 11 labs, 2 in-class and 2 take-home midterms, and a 3-hour final. Pay attention and it will work out.

STOR120 is an easy class, especially if you have prior statistics/python experience. Most lectures consisted of him re-explaining the same things over and over, which got pretty boring after a while. He seems nice enough, but I will say he does come off as a bit condescending when answering questions from students. Just an okay professor IMO.

Love remi! he is great and is very clear about grading and what he expects of you. not a difficult course if you stay on top of your work. only 8 hw assignments for whole year, 2 midterms, final exam. gives a lot of study resources that will prepare you VERY well for the exams if you do them(DO THEM).
Take this with him!!! He is so nice and cares for his students. Tests are just like the study guides and quizzes

I learned so much in this class and it definitely challenged me. Professor Remi is a wonderful professor and cares about all of his students. He challenges his students, but his class is do-able with a lot of practice. I would not recommend taking this class with a lot of other demanding classes.

Easiest class I have ever taken. The homework is pretty much the exact same as the exams. I always struggled with paying attention during lectures but still managed to get a 100% on one of the midterms. The attendance grade is incredibly generous.

Dr. Remi uses lots of examples, which helps bring some life into the material and make lecture interesting. He's careful to clearly explain difficult concepts to avoid confusion. His guided notes and study guides are great when you have to study for exams. Dr. Remi is also a friendly guy and seems to always be in a good mood for class.

Dr. Remi was a great professor and lecturer! His exams were 60% multiple choice, 40% written. He gives a study guide before each exam that is helpful. He also allows a 1 sided cheat sheet for each exam, and both sides for the final. Definitely recommend.

Remi is the goat. He is an amazing teacher and an even better human. Despite having big classes, he cares about every student and is easy to reach outside of class. I'm not a stats major, but I hope to take another class with him one day. He definitely knows how to teach the content in an easy-to-learn way. Take any class with him.

I think the class has helped me learn a lot. However, the class meets four times a week, with only 2 unexcused absences, which is kind of insane. It is also A TON OF WORK. Like kind of a crazy amount. He assigns take home midterms and in class misters, so if you have any other homework or exams, balancing them will be difficult.
Remi was a good professor. Be prepared to study and review lectures! He was very accessible outside of class.
If you make a mistake he will not allow you to correct it and has no grade space.

I took Remi for STOR 155 and STOR 120 and he was great in both! He really cares about his students and is knowledgable about data science. Remi makes sure you understand basic concepts rather than focusing on the small details. He is strict about deadlines, but if you stick to them there shouldn't be any issues.

Dr. Remi is quite caring for his students, though he could be stubborn sometimes. Most learning are through his lectures which is quite fast paced, so pay close attention during class. The exams have 2 parts, in-class multiple choice and after-class coding. I would say the coding parts are easier than the statistic-focused in-class parts.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Good teacher and super easy class. Very easy and low effort homework, midterms, and final. Got an A+ on everything with minimal effort. This class gives me breathing room for more demanding classes. Good lectures too if you're genuinely interested in statistics.

Had great lecture notes that made homework fairly easy. Offers plenty of office hours if you are confused. Posts completed notes so missing a lecture isn't the end of the world. Would definitely recommend for STOR120.
He does not remove two of the lowest grades in our grade books.

Dr. Remi is a hilarious guy and makes this class fun. Strongly recommend his STOR-113 class to those applying to the b-school over MATH152, especially those who are not the best at math/calc. He reviews algebra at the beginning and takes all material very slowly. His main priority is that the students understand. I suck at math and got an A-.

Dr. Remi has been the best professor Ive taken a class with at UNC. His lectures are clear, interesting and fun. He wants the best for his students, is easy to contact and is by the book when it comes to grading and exams. He makes the work easy to understand and links it to real world examples. I will most definitely take another class with him.

Dr. Remi was amazing! Dr. Remi gave amazing lectures and provided plenty of examples that made the concepts so much easier. He also had very clear grading criteria and exams were straightforward. He was obviously passionate about what he was teaching and wanted his students to succeed. Highly recommend him for STOR-155!

Remi is easily one of the best professors at UNC! He is routinely disciplined, intelligent, and very caring. Strict with deadlines, but with good intentions. I had Remi as a professor during his first semester at UNC (he was great)--he has grown significantly! He is organized & communicative while retaining his kind heart and sense of humor.
Dr. Remi made me care about statistics and I am not a math person, nor am I a statistics lover. It is clear he cares about his students and his work.

prob one of the best teachers I've had as a freshman. He explains EVERYTHING so students are able to follow his classes and makes sure students really know what they're doing by going back to old material while teaching new material. Tests were very fair. Many laughs in this class, a non stressful course, gonna miss this class next semester!

Dr. Remi is an excellent professor and was very thorough in ensuring that we understood the lesson materials. He would make sure that we understood a concept before moving on and encouraged questions and concerns. I could tell that he cared about students' wellbeing and took his role as an educator seriously.

He makes jokes in class, and actually cares and answers questions in multiple ways to make sure you understand the material. 8 homework assignments total, throughout the entire course, about 20 questions each- very doable and understandable to what we are learning. Tests are worth abt 75%, but he preps you well (do study guides!). Def take him!!!

Dr. Remi is an amazing professor who truly wants you to get your money's worth out of the course. Even though this class is a lot of material, he tries his best to condense the information for anyone to understand. Can be a bit hard to follow sometimes, but overall is the best option for stor 120.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Probably only has such a high rating because his homework and tests are so easy. But the lectures are hard to follow and have no clear learning path

Professor Abayomi is one of the best Professors I have had. He is a great lecturer and the problems provided prepare you well for his exams. Some say he is repetitive, but he repeats topics that are important to your foundation in statistics. In STEM classes this is a luxury, most professors would cover a topic once (or not at all).

I appreciate how he takes his lectures slowly as that is unlike many other math or statistics classes. This makes it easy to understand the material and I don't have to spend much time outside of class teaching myself. His tests are also fair if you study and pay attention in class. He is also engaging in lectures and makes class more enjoyable.

While his lectures are slow-paced and often slightly repetitive, his class overall is very easy to follow and does a good job at teaching the basics of statistics. Homework assignments are clearly communicated and not overbearing. I would absolutely recommend Dr. Remi for this class, I feel as though he has taught very well.

Remi doesn't explain things well. He always makes mistakes unconsciously in lectures; you will be extremely frustrated if you don't figure it out yourself. Assignments are also confusing, which is even worse if he is not a good lecturer. Be prepared to self-teach if you choose a class with him. NOT going to take any class with him.
Not too much outside work and he is a super energetic and thorough lecturer. Would highly recommend.
Dr. Remi was a great professor really new how to make STOR 155 really fun. Made the class really interesting and made me more interested in statistics.

Dr. Remi is a great professor that was extremely clear on what he expects fro, his students. He always tries to make his lectures entertaining and push students to participate and to ask questions. He is very understanding and eager to improve. His well-rounded knowledge of soccer is a huge plus (he supports Chelsea). Definitely recommend!

Tests and quizzes are not an unfair percentage of the final grade. Participation and homework still mean a lot which helps cushion your grade. Remi is incredibly passionate and knowledgeable about the subject matter and he explains every topic in depth. Tests and quizzes are easier than the homework so you feel extra prepared.

I see negative reviews for stor 120 so it must be a lot different than stor 155 because the class was so manageable and easy. His exams were completely fair and he taught everything well. Definitely recommend for stor 155

I loved Dr. Remi's class! He is super passionate about what he teaches. His classes were very straight forward and his study guides are extremely helpful for the exams. If you know how to do the study guide questions, you will be prepared for his exams. The homework can be time consuming so I would recommend doing a portion each day.
Remi is a really good professor he explains so clearly the concepts and will help you out of class if you still have some doubts.

Excellent professor, and makes introductory statistics fun and comprehensible. We got behind in lecture but this was always accommodated for, rather than leaving us to self-study foreign material. Exams are very fair and have study guides; however, don't ever become complacent or it will reflect in your grade.

I'm not the best at statistics so I was very cautious to find a good professor before a stats class on. Dr. Remi is the best professor for this, he's straight up, extremely intelligent, has guided notes, and more. He made this class a (somehow) enjoyable 8am class. If you are questioning if you should take his class this is your sign you should!

Professor Remi is great! He makes sure to stop if anyone has questions during the lecture or if he senses the class is not understanding. He uses great real-world examples to help the class remember concepts. My grade could have been better if I studied differently for the first midterm. USE THE STUDY GUIDE/PRACTICE PROBLEMS!

Dr. Remi was an amazing professor! He teaches passionately, and has a sense of humor. He explained topics with clear and concise real-life examples that made it easier to understand opposed to other stat professors who just throw you the complicated looking formula straight from the text book. He makes stat easy you will not regret taking his class

Dr.Remi is a great professor who takes pride in his ability to help his students be successful in their coursework. He makes difficult concepts easier to understand and is very considerate of students circumstances outside of the classroom.

Dr. Remi was a very thorough teacher but was very condescending as a professor. He had very little patience and was rude to students on occasion. While his lectures were thorough, he spent a lot of time explaining simple concepts that everyone already knew.

He is the best choice for Stor 155. He reuses so many in class/study guide questions on tests that really reward you if you show up and pay attention. You also get a cheat sheet. I never had to worry about my grade in this class because I showed up and did the study guide before tests

Dr. Remi was a great choice for STOR 120. The midterm exams DO reflect what he lectures about in class for the most part. He explains most things more than once and will almost always ensure the class follows before moving on to the next topic. He is a really caring and passionate guy, and I would 100% take another class with him.

Professor Abayomi is awesome. He is very organized and provides many resources to prepare for exams. 2 midterms and 1 final. Midterms are fair and very similar to the study guide. You will do well if you pay attention in class, watch the recordings (if necessary), review guided module notes, and complete the study guide he provides.

Professor Remi is such an amazing professor and his class is so well organized. The exams are exactly like the study guides so it was not difficult to study. We were also allowed a one-sided 'cheat sheet' for every exam. His notes are so helpful! I definitely recommend taking STOR 155 with him!!!

Dr. Remi was not clear with lectures or material. Half of the time we would not finish the lectures in class and our homework and labs were graded incorrectly. Midterms were graded very harshly and were not very correlated with material learned. He seems like a nice and very knowledgeable guy but I would not recommend taking STOR 120 with him.

Dr. Remi seemed to randomly grade the homework and lab assignments which made it difficult to get feedback on how you are actually doing in the class. He doesn't convey the material well and puts concepts on the exams that were not clearly talked about. You'll have to teach yourself if you take 120 with him.

This was my first time using Python, and I think Dr. Remi did a good job teaching first time users how to code and then apply that to stats. He takes his time in lectures to repeat key things, which some people feel is repetitive but I thought it was helpful as someone that struggled in the class at first.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Remi is great!! The material is not easy, but he explains concepts well. The study guides are very similar to the exams and you get a cheat sheet. He is lenient on HW due dates and not a tough grader. Gives fill-in-the blank notes. The exams are hard to complete in 50 mins, but he does give some credit even if you haven't completed it.

Dr. Remi is awesome! His lectures are great, engaging, and fun. The material isn't super easy to understand but Dr. Remi makes it enjoyable to learn. Great professor and would 100% take his classes again.

Remi is the best for stor 155. Tests are fair and just like the study guides and homework, he doesn't try to trick you. You also get a cheat sheet. Requires barely any time out of class just 1 homework every ~2-3 weeks and then complete study guide/review notes a day or two before exam.

Dr. Remi is a nice guy but doesn't get through the information we need in lectures. The in-class exams test on something entirely different too. I would not recommend taking 120 with him unless you're prepared to teach yourself a lot of the material.

Professor Remi is a nice man, but is unfortunately disorganized at times. However, it was his first semester teaching at UNC so it's understandable. Exams were difficult to complete within 50 minutes while other classes had open note take-home exams. Sometimes, he was slightly condescending during class when questions were asked and through email.

I can't recommend Dr. Remi enough, he makes concepts so simple and the exams are literally exactly like the study guide he doesn't try to trick you and you get a full page for a cheat sheet. 4 free unexcused absences, the hw give you 5 tries per question and he drops the lowest 2 hw. Couldn't have picked a better prof for this class
Super clear guidelines. Review guides pre-exam were very helpful. He wants you to succeed. Very funny guy as well! Made the concepts seem simple.

Very friendly, but lectures were not very beneficial and our class fell behind the others. It was Dr. Remi's first semester at UNC, so I hope this problem doesn't happen in future classes. Work isn't too difficult, especially if you have some coding experience.

Dr. Remi's lectures were very long and tedious. He taught the material good but it would be very hard to keep concentrated with him. He has a strong accent, which at times was very entertaining. Tests were just like the in class problems. Homework is insanely long and takes forever. Overall an ok professor.

Probably the easiest class I've taken at UNC, and with an uplifting professor! It had middle school style fill-in-the-blank notes and 4 free unexcused absences before grade was affected. Exams were never surprising b/c Remi followed his own notes/study guides. Grading was lenient; HW was minimal. You're able to get a 100 on almost every assignment.

Absolutely unprofessional. Made this class much more difficult that it needed to be. Constantly spoke about how important respect is but failed to show any to his students through his actions in handling this class.

Remi is great. He provides fill-in-the-blank notes which he fills out along with you and while he talks fast and does have an accent, he literally posts every single class lecture online where you can access whenever. Always pushed back hw and web-assign gives 5 tries per Q. My friends in other stor 155 had to use my notes for their exams.

Remi is enthusiastic about data science. But he failed to return work, update the syllabus, and upload assignments when he said he would, preventing students from completing assignments on time. Even though he blamed his disorganization on his own poor time management, he was not accommodating of student latenesses due to his inconsistencies.
Remi is a good stats teacher and his passion really showed. We did get behind because he does over explain. Test were just like the review sheets.

Remi is the kindest person ever, but bad prof. Only had 6 HWs the whole semester, so was always unprepared for exams. Homework difficult and irrelevant. He explains things incredibly slowly but it is still confusing. Entire grade is pretty much based on 2 midterms and a final. If you do bad on one, your grade is done for.

The class is pretty straightforward if you know python already and honestly don't even need to show up to class because the material is pretty self-explanatory. Professor Remi is super caring as a professor but as it was his first semester, he was very unorganized with the schedule but it didn't impact my learning that much.

Prof Remi is super friendly during office hours. If it's your first data science class with no coding experience - it's not easy. The class and syllabus were super disorganized. We had to watch the videos on our own to catch up with the material. Exams are open-book. I hope he changes his time management in the future.

Pretty easy class if you know python. This class was EXTREMELY disorganized. No clear due dates. He overexplains, which led lectures to be kind of pointless and we ended up being behind the entire semester. While he is a nice man, I felt him to be somewhat condescending in class when students asked questions. Took forever to get my grades back.

Easy class if you know python already. Nice guy but wildly disorganized. We were behind the whole semester despite him constantly saying not to worry and that we would catch up. Eventually he just created videos and made us watch them by ourselves at the end of the semeseter to make up for the disorganization.
Pretty easy class if you already know Python beforehand. Tends to overexplain everything making lectures pretty useless IMO. The class is basically the exact same as the textbook

The class was very straightforward. 3 exams and homework assignments are due every other week. The exams were exactly like the lecture notes from class. Homework was annoying because it was always much more difficult than the tests themselves. As long as you attend lectures and study the notes given, the class is pretty easy!

Prof. Remi over-explains everything to the point where we had to complete learning the final material on our own time over Thanksgiving break because we ran out of time. His "review" of previous material takes over half the class every time and is extremely counterproductive. He does know the material and is passionate about data science.

He's such a nice guy who really knows the material, but his exams are extremely difficult and long. Cheat sheets are permitted tho, which is great. Lectures based on guided notes make things easy to follow. Homework felt like busy work a lot of the time and often wasn't helpful for learning the material better.

I loved Remi! First teacher at Unc to care about students. Didn't rush through material just to stick to a schedule, made sure we knew what we were doing and why. Study guides and homework matched exams! I actually learned with him despite hating math. great person overall, and an amazing professor. Take his class for stor 155!!

Prof Remi was awesome! He was very friendly which made it really easy to ask him questions. He will over explain (which makes him much better than other stat 155 profs) but he will stop if given confirmation that the class understands. The only complaint was that I wish we had slightly shorter/less test questions, but it is still easy to do well.

Dr. Remi is incredible and everything about the way his class is organized is perfect. No textbook readings, 1 homework for each unit, and 3 exams. The exams were easy and most of the problems were very similar to the examples we covered in class. Goes slowly to make sure we're understanding (this resulted in us not finishing all the units though).

He is a very great professor and really loves what he does. However, his tests are very long and you must really know what you are doing to finish on time. He spends a lot of time on one topic and tends to over explain things causing the class to fall behind. Thus, we did not finish every section that was written on the syllabus.

Dr. Remi is extremely kind and accommodating. His lectures are easy to understand and he goes through tough material several times to ensure everyone is on track--this is his downfall. We're very far behind the other class and the exams are falling out of the scope of what he's gone over. I'm worried for the final. Subject is easy if caught up.

He is one of the most personable, funny, and caring professors I have ever met. He is a tough grader, but he is always understanding and gives great feedback to improve. The way he acts out words sometimes is so funny. He always tries to be a good professor, and he does great. I would take this class ten times over, he's so great.

Professor Huesa is super nice and explains class content very well. The class requires a good amount of effort and studying, but it's not too overwhelming. Class is very interactive, so I definitely recommend making it to as many classes as you can and participating a lot. He is also very accommodating and understanding if you have any issues.

Insane amount of homework, very harsh grader. He's a good lecturer, I had him twice but he was a lot harsher for this class. I would not take this class with him if I had known. Also seems to cater to native speakers so fair warning. He's very approachable and nice but as a professor I would not recommend to a friend.

Prof Huesa is really nice, and even though Basque was challenging, he did a great job breaking it down into digestible parts. He is a really harsh grader though and expects a lot from his students, so get ready to work. Not an easy course, but definitely doable and I learned a lot.
Very nice professor but sometimes wasn't the greatest at helping answer or clarify content-related questions. He does cold call and participation matters so be prepared for that if taking his class.

I  love this man as a person but unfortunately he is a rough professor. He isn't super knowledgable about certain topics and isn't super helpful with learning new materials. He also is a very very tough grader and there is no such thing as completion grades for this course.

Such a nice man and you can tell he cares about the class and students. He does cold call every class and tends to grade harshly, so prepare for that.
The Spanish department creates the tests/quizzes, NOT him, so sometimes we'd have ridiculously long tests and he'd do what he could to talk to the administrator and shorten them.

He is low key a bad teacher, but it's not really his fault. The Spanish curriculum is horribly designed. The course, and definitely the way he teaches it, is pedantic. He isn't very understanding, is a tough grader, and didn't really help us learn the language as much as he drilled in grammar rules and taught us irrelevant info for learning span.

He is the worst grader I have ever had at UNC. He takes off points in almost every single sentence, but when you try to talk to him he doesn't tell you how your fluency can be improved. He will make you laugh in class, but cry every night. Worst professor at the UNC spanish department, if you ask me, and I've had almost 8 professors at this point.

This professor refuses to take into account that his students are learning a new language. He grades as if we are fluent... and we are not. For the spanish major we have to have 261, and despite my love for learning spanish, I would NEVER take this class with him again - i don;t even know if Spanish is for me anymore because of him. DO NOT DO IT!!!

Did not give consistent feedback on the paper we wrote and when I asked for additional help outside of class he advised me to consult chat gpt. I found several problematic issues with the content in the book, which he authored, such as using slurs for LGBT individuals without clarifying they are slurs. Poor feedback and stubborn.

He is understanding and passionate about his work. If you are not sure about a question, he won't force you to answer. He is always happy/upbeat. If you need extra time on work, he will work with you. Readings/homework have to be done before class but it is all on VHL and not hard. Great experience for 1st foreign language class here at UNC.

IDK what professor these other people had, but pretty chill HE IS AN ABSOLUETLY IRRESPONSIBLE GRADER. He takes away points for random reasons and he never really explains why. He's incredibly pedantic, which to some is a benefit, but for me it's been very annoying. He's all right, can definitely make you laugh.

Professor Huesa is very kind and caring. His lectures are unfortunately very boring, as is the homework. This class goes at a fast pace and class is a review of the homework. He is a tough grader on the research paper but an easy grader on the exam and round table discussion. Class overall is a snooze, but he is a VERY nice professor.

PELLO IS AMAZING. Super easy to understand and I learned so much in his class. Genuinely the nicest person and he cares deeply about his students. SPAN 261 in general is a lot of work- but the grading is lenient. He is very engaging. 1000/10 recommend (:

If you want a Spanish professor that loves what he does take a SPAN class with him! I took both SPAN 204 and SPAN 261 with him and he truly cares about his students, and is a very passionate professor. Even though there is quite a bit of homework outside of class and he is a tough grader, it is all to benefit your learning. HE'S THE BEST!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor was awesome and the class was fairly easily if you participated. I recommend.

Super nice professor, a bit of a tough grader at times but completely fair. Cares a lot about students and wants everyone to learn - very good class environment. Homework on top of other materials can sometimes be a little tedious but still manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Huesa is pretty fun and understanding, however the course material is pretty boring. The classes were all very lecture heavy and there's a bunch of homework. He is one of the better Spanish teachers here, though he is a tough grader. If you study the grammar well for all exams and quizzes, you should be fine.

I loved professor Huesa! He is always available to meet outside of class and really cares about his students. He is a tough grader, so definitely triple-check compositions, but overall he was amazing.

Like all Spanish classes, attendance required, Professor Huesa is awesome, nice, kind, very good class to get better at spanish. However, class can be difficult and exams and papers are hard. Apply yourself in every assignment, as if you slack off you will not do great.

Very hard subject to learn so be prepared to do some extra studying outside of class. Pello tries to make it easier, though, by listening to our feedback about quizzes and material and working with us. He genuinely doesn't want you to fail, but you will have to try. Beginning of the class is mostly history and culture, second half is the grammar.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lots of work, but he is a easy grader and very understanding. Best spanish teacher i've had here at UNC
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I had him for both 204 and 261 and he was amazing! I would take him again if I could. Although 261 is inherently difficult with tests that are very fast paced and multiple essays, Pello was very kind and did a great job explaining material. He once gave me an extension when I really needed it and is pretty flexible. He wants to help you!

Prof Huesa was absolutely the best. Once we got to the grammar section things got tough but he adjusted the syllabus to give us every opportunity to do well. The class is work heavy on the front end of the semester but that made finals season much more manageable. He is a joy in class and very passionate about the Basque language. Highly recommend

I had Professor Huesa for SPAN 204 and 261. He is an amazing professor and I would recommend taking any Spanish class at UNC with him.  He genuinely cares about his students wellbeing and wants them to do well! SPAN 261 is a difficult class but Professor Huesa is flexible with deadlines and ensures students have enough time to complete assignments!

Pedro Huesa was the sweetest professor and cared a lot about his students. He is very approachable so go to office hours. It probably isn't his fault the material was not engaging, I could blame the textbook and class requirements but the class is very much teaching to the textbook. Pedro Huesa expects you to participate and will dock points.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: (also listed as Pedro Huesa Otegui) -- I loved Profe Huesa! He was super kind and funny. If you can get the chance to know him, do it! SPAN 261 can be a difficult class but Profe Huesa is always available to meet for office hours and help however he can.
