Not keen on giving extensions unless you have accommodations, but it really wasn't too bad!

A great Spanish professor and has really helped me be more confident when it comes to speaking and writing in Spanish. He wants his students to participate willingly and will most definitely call on you even if you have participated several times in class! Spanish 204 is a harder class in general but he grades harshly on tests and papers so beware.

Professor Huesa was a very sweet man who didnt make you feel bad/embarrassed when you messed up speaking during class. Super understanding and lenient on due dates, he can just be a tough grader. I would definitely recommend him to anyone not super confident in their Spanish, I learned a lot from him!

Fantastic teacher - he is kind, encouraging, and funny. He is a harsh but fair grader, and provides excellent feedback. He is also highly organized, and deadlines are regularly communicated via email as well as found on the syllabus. The course itself is fairly fast-paced, so some studying is necessary. Great prof, good class!

Professor Huesa really cares about his students. He does what he can to make sure your experience is smooth. He is indeed a tough grader though and the exams are very difficult. This class requires a lot of effort and time to get a good grade. The exams can get very difficult especially since you learn so much material in not enough time.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Profe Huesa was so kind and sweet to his students. While I think he grades a little bit harshly, he is an exceptional teacher and did a great job even in the midst of a pandemic.

Profesor Pello is nice but he grades pretty harshly, especially when it comes to writing compositions or writing on tests/quizzes. As in he takes off points for incorrectly using a comma and didn't give anyone in our class a 100 in participation (despite calling on us everyday). He speaks very clearly and pretty slowly though.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Hard to understand. Grades exceptionally hard. Not enough time on tests.

He is the best Spanish professor at UNC!! So caring, kind and accessible. He really wants all his students to do well, and he assigns a large, but totally manageable, amount of work. You have to put a good amount of time into this class, but you have to do that for every SPAN 261 professor. He's easily the best option for 261. Take class with him!!

Pello was an amazing Professor; very caring, very thorough and very charismatic so the class was always fun to attend. I thought the material was challenging, but Prof. Huesa used class to do lots of practice which was very helpful. He really cares about our success, and the course was fairly easy, though the material itself was challenging.

Pello is that sweet, caring, older professor who everyone loves. While he expects a lot out of his students, he's always really patient and kindly corrects his students if they get something wrong. The workload isn't that bad, but he has a tendency to grade things more on the strict side, but don't let that scare you away because he's really great.

He is a very nice, approachable man. He wants the best for all his students but he's not afraid to take off points for accents, spelling, or other grammatical errors. He's pretty tough on grading compositions but overall it's pretty fair. He's full of energy and makes the class interactive with a good mix of speaking, writing, and listening.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He really cares about his students, wants us to succeed, & understands that we are constantly learning - he expects everyone to speak in Spanish in class but will very nicely correct you or translate if you can't think of the word you're trying to say. There are pop quizzes but he will hint at it at the beginning of class. Overall the best prof!

He is an awesome Spanish professor and is very clear and understandable. There is a lot of homework, and some of the material is difficult, but there are lots of grades. Pop quizzes almost every week, so be sure to review any textbook pages he tells you to. Doesn't have assignments in syllabus and he sends them out day by day through email.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Tony is the goat! He is so fun, a great professor, and really knowledgeable about the subject he teaches! He wants all students to succeed and is so caring. The class environment is super chill and he makes it enjoyable to go to. I would take him over and over again if I could! The work is super easy as well, guaranteed A!
Great guy, even better class. Super easy material has a midterm and final, but both are online. Take this class, even if you don't have interest in sports field.

Great and engaging professor, but meh class (very boring material at times). All classes he teaches are graded by a total of 100 points, so just make sure to be on top of assignments. Exams are online and are pretty easy. Be careful about letting the little points missed add up and tank your grade, as it happened to multiple students.

Dr. Patterson is wonderful and gave me a lot of opportunities within the Sport Admin realm. I have test anxiety so I struggled on the midterm (which is to account for my A-), but if that's not a huge issue for you, the tests aren't hard, you just HAVE to read the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Very very easy class I took over the summer. Do the work and read the assigned chapters, you're guaranteed an A. I highly recommend anyone who needs it for a gen ed or just as an elective to boost gpa. Would take any class this man teaches if I need for credit or have room for extra classes to boost my gpa. A great class

Dr. Patterson is a very kind and understanding man. With my tough schedule this semester, this class was a breath of fresh air every day. This class was not hard at all and if you do your work you are pretty much guaranteed a good grade.  Dr. Patterson is very easygoing and you can tell he cares about his students.

Professor Patterson is an awesome hilarious guy who cares about all his students. He is super lenient on due dates and assignment criteria. He loves what he does and makes that clear. I 100% recommend taking his class.
Dr.Patterson is engaging and is positive when teaching. You learn a lot, while grading is so easy. All exams are online, individual and group activities, guest lectures, and more. Highly reccommend!
TP is the best, super cool guy. Easy and interesting class. Online midterms and a final paper and group project are most of grade. Take this class with him for sure

I enjoyed Dr. Pattersons class. He's very personable and willing to help wherever he can. Only negative I would say is that he's very lenient with group projects, and often times some put in more work than others. Overall easy A for a class

Awesome professor. He was very caring and clear in terms of grading, including extra credit opportunities, and the class overall didn't require me to spend too much time on it outside of class. He genuinely wants his students to succeed—one of the best professors I have had at UNC.
Take the class do the work and you'll pass.
My favorite teacher, take him if you can. Trust.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Patterson is the absolute best. He is so kind and caring, but is still passionate about sports admin. He definitely reaffirmed my decision to be a sports admin major. If you get the chance to take his class, you should!

Dr. Patterson is amazing! He cares for his students and makes his lectures engaging and interactive. I probably opened the textbook 3 times max but you do need to read it to do well on the final. There is a group project at the end and a couple of homework assignments, but he gives enough time to complete everything without getting stressed.

Dr. Patterson is one of the best professors I've had at UNC. He is there for his students and structures his class accordingly. As long as you take lecture notes and read the textbook, you will do great in his class.

Dr. Patterson is great! Lectures are easy to understand and interactive, and Dr. Patterson makes an effort to get to know all of his students on a first-name basis. Makes sure you're interested in what he's talking about, and will go out of his way to make sure you're successful/interested in the course.

Tony is a great guy who is always there for his students. Attendance is not mandatory, but there are in class assignments that count towards your grade, and if you are not there you do not get credit for at the end of the semester. He is flexible and will work with you to make sure you succeed. Highly advise taking him!
Tony is great, very caring and flexible. The class has two major group projects with the same team so pick wisely.
He is always willing to take the extra time to go over anything and is there for his students. A must take for any EXSS class!

Dr. Parr is one of the best professors I have had at UNC - he is very caring, and genuinely just wants his students to learn. This is really exemplified with his 'unique' grading scale he has in place - it makes the class less stressful because it's a lot easier to get an A and you can focus more on course content and work than fighting over points

Dr. Parr is a great teacher and a jolly, caring guy. The class was easy but uninteresting. The grading is this random letter scale he made up, but he outlines it very clearly so you know what you need for an A or whatever. If you are taking GEOG 115 he is a great option.

Dr. Parr is the goat. The grading criteria are clear, and he prioritizes the students' learning over exams. With how the class is set up, getting an "A" is achievable as long as you're not lazy. All the resources are there, and the lectures are engaging. Dr. Parr is a cool professor who is willing to help a student learn and grow in the class.
Dr. Parr is the best data science related professor I've had as a data science student. He is incredibly caring, funny, and incredibly engaging in lectures due to his personality.
Dr Parr is so amazing! He makes this class super fun and the content is super interesting.

Dr Parr is a wonderful individual who genuinely makes an effort to get to know each and every student. The class is perfectly structured and the grading criteria is very clear. As long as you do the work and make an effort you can set yourself up for an A rather easily.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: LOVE DR.PARR! Took both 215 and 370 with him. You definitely need to learn the concepts because you need to code yourself in the assignments, but 90% of them you copy and paste from his example. His exams come straight from the assessments. Definitely an easy A, but you need to put a little work in. Please be nice and engage in class- he cares.

Amazing, wonderful and intelligent professor. He was so caring for his students and obviously passionate about teaching, which is rare in a lot of professors at UNC. He always makes sure his students understand what is going on and feel comfortable.

Really good grading scheme that made it low-stakes and extremely easy to get an A. If you get an 80% cumulative avg b/w the 2 exams, complete 8/9 assignments, complete 3 small projects, and deliver 1 presentation, you will be guaranteed an A in the class basically. As a teacher, Dr. Parr is accessible and really understands how to teach new coders.
Super sweet guy, absolutely loved his class! He made spatial data science easy for a non-STEM major, which is saying something. 10/10 guy, and I learned a lot from the class.

This class is an easy A IF you do the work. The final project was interesting, the final exam was easy if you come to class throughout the semester, and the lectures were straightforward. I respect Dr. Parr immensely for emphasizing learning over grades in today's academic system. I actually remember everything I learned in this class!

Dr. Parr planned this class and executed it in an organized structure that makes it incredibly easy to succeed and actually learn the material. Assignments are clear and well thought-out, & the course feels planned and perfected. He is also incredibly caring and kind, and makes himself very available to students in and out of class. 100% recommend.

Dr. Parr was one of the most caring professors I've ever had. He is a very clear professor, who genuinely cares for his students and has all the motivations that make a great professor. The TA's I had were amazing too, they and Dr. Parr were always willing to help outside class and never make you feel discouraged. Made me like R!

Dr. Parr's criteria grading system made it very easy to set yourself up for an A in this class. I enjoyed the assignment's in this class, but the lectures could be a bit dry (as GIS lectures tend to be). Dr. Parr seemed very kind, and there was plenty of support offered so that students could succeed in this class.

Grading policy makes it clear what is needed for each grade and helps with stress. Very approachable and office hours are helpful. Beware of pop quizzes though, that is the attendance mechanism. Projects are interesting and the final isn't bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The grading criteria make securing an "A" in the class manageable. I enjoyed the class, and overall, he's a nice and chill professor. He cares about your success and is willing to help if you're having issues with software or assignments. It was cool to learn about QGIS, and overall, the class was pretty light.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is super nice and caring, and his lectures and in class activities are engaging. He used a different grading criteria that made it easy to get an A if you wanted to. There were a lot of quizzes, some of them pop quizzes, but you only need 70/100 points between the quizzes and final for an A. No midterms.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment:
*FOR GEOG 370*
Dr. Parr is one of the best professors in the Geography department, he knows what he's talking about and is willing to answer any questions you have. There were 10 quizzes in this class, some announced and some not (we had 2 in one week once). Grading criteria is different, but it's not hard to get an A.
Literally nicest professor I've ever had. Was honestly unsure of the class before I took it, but he's awesome and the class is awesome.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class is literally so easy. Great guy. Teaches so well and the assignments are a breeze.

My favorite professor !! UNC is lucky to have Dr. Parr in their geography department. Like all the other reviews said, he cares about all of his students and will put in work to help you if you put in the work to learn.

Dr. Parr has been one of my favorite professors at UNC so far! He genuinely wants his students to succeed and was very accessible outside of class. Don't worry if you do not have prior coding experience because the class provides all the basics. I learned a lot and will be taking 370 with Dr. Parr next semester!

Professor Parr makes Spatial Data Science super accessible with clear lectures, lots of room for practice, so many office hours, and SPECIFICATIONS GRADING - which honestly made the class very low-stress. Group work is a big part, not too many assignments and only 2 exams, final is a project, if you want a great introduction TAKE THIS CLASS!!!!

Dr Parr is the best and uses an alternative grading method to the benefit of a student. Genuinely wants everyone to learn and is super approachable. Gives many chances to succeed on assignments quite honestly if you dont get an A in this class it is completely your fault. Also learned a good bit during this class.

Dr. Parr is one of my favorite professors. He genuinely cares about his students' success and works with you to create a plan to help you thrive. His deep knowledge of R programming is impressive, and even though I had no prior programming experience, he makes complex concepts accessible and manageable. I'm taking GEOG 370 with him next!

dr. parr takes the time to explain every detail of code, and is willing to answer questions that may seem trivial. the assignments are fairly easy, just take a lot of time (usually 2-3 hours). the first exam is massive, but easy to prep for. his grading scale is fair, but requires effort to make an A. he is very knowledgable and cares a lot!

Dr. Parr is one of the best professors I have had. He uses a different grading scale, but that is done very fairly and there are plenty of opportunities to get more points. His lectures are also very engaging and the in-class activities are extremely helpful for the exams. He is also very accessible outside of class and will help in any way he can!

Dr. Parr is probably the best teacher at UNC by far. He is very compassionate and understanding of student's lives and varying circumstances that could impact their academic career. He makes sure that students understand the content and will answer any question regardless of how it may sound.

Professor Parr is one of the sweetest and best professors I've had at UNC. I took this class for the data science elective and I'm so glad I did. Learned so much from him, he's genuinely passionate about the material. He uses his own grading schema - attendance is not required, no final exam, and you can retake up to a passing grade.

Dr. Parr uses unique grading criteria, but don't let that scare you. He's incredibly caring, a great teacher, and makes coding and data science accessible even for people with no experience (me). While data science isn't my major, I really enjoyed this class and highly recommend for anyone looking to expand their skills or further their major.

Take Parr for GEOG 215 if needed for data science! Super nice, caring, understanding professor and makes learning R really digestible. 2 easy midterms and a group project, easy to get an A as long as you don't slack off like crazy.

His teaching style and dedication plus the TAs are great. I'm learning so much but not overwhelmed! Would definitely take his class again. He answers questions without judgment and typically explains why we are coding something and comments in the code which are so helpful. I feel like everyone can do well in this class.

Amazing professor, like genuinely great at teaching. GEOG 215 is an easy class and if you don't get an A or B it's because your lazy. You can retake any assignment including exams.

The content isn't necessarily easy (especially if you have never coded before) but the grading and pace make it very easy to stay on track.

Gave very vague instruction and would often change up what she wanted from you. Never ask her for advice on a project because she will most likely dismiss all of it and tell you you did the entire thing wrong. The class material would be interesting, but lectures drag on and are boring. Some of the projects were fun.
this professor was not kind or understanding, nor accommodating. class was incredibly boring too.

It has been a week since LDOC, and she has not submitted any grades so far. When you ask for feedback on a project, she is very vague and not helpful. There are better first-year seminars than this course. It is very lecture-heavy and boring when not completing projects. The professor is kind, but does not grade on time.

The worst professor I've ever had at UNC. Her class was so unorganized and nothing was made clear. Would get mad and snap at students. Spent the first 5 weeks going over the same 20 page powerpoint and just read off her notes the entire time. Multiple people dropped the course and I wish I could have. I would never take a class with her again

Roxana is my fave professor at UNC. I understand the low rate bc a lot of my ppl disliked her teaching style. But as a professor and artist, she's great to learn from. Her class is not easy, it challenges you, and she doesn't take nonsense. You have to be willing & engage. She was my only professor who accommodated my predicament with genuine care.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Took class Spring 2022 and was skeptical because these reviews are horrendous!!! The class was very enjoyable and it was nice to make tangible things by hand. Project deadlines based on class progression. 3 very simple review papers. Small final presentation on assigned sculptor. Overall grades on effort & at least coming to class. Highly recommend

PM gave me a 2nd chance after threatening to fail me, so credit where due. She also disrespected me when I tried to explain my situation, and it genuinely hurt my feelings. PM goes on bizarre, biased tangents in class. She actually gets offended if you miss class. We used Dropbox and Flipsnack instead of Sakai, and blamed us for issues. PM aint P.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She often gave very vague instructions and actually banned group chats so communicating with classmates became more difficult, and would not give clear due dates or grades for projects. Very poor teacher and would never take her class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Genuinely have never met a professor that seems to hate their job more. Never considers the perspective of students (might be helpful to... see our grades, have coherent lectures, invite questions/feedback rather than discourage them). Take this class and you will dread it each day.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Singlehandedly worst professor I have ever had at UNC. Refuses to use Sakai, didn't show grades until a week before the LAST day of class, useless lectures, the most convoluted grading criteria you've ever witnessed. Forbids groupme in her syllabus because she has been criticized on it so intensely in the past. Truly authoritarian class environment

I'd rather retake the class with TA at 7am. Gave grades back @ END of semester. Her entire course is a huge mess of information. You have to search high and low for simple information/clarification. Her lectures are POINTLESS. My entire class taught themselves the work. Prepare for lots of confusion! I could've done better than her. Huge disappoint
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--So many papers

reviews.comment: I was extremely excited for this FYS, but this class is definitely not a grade booster. Roxana gives no clear instructions on assignments, yet grades them very harshly. You do not receive any grades back throughout the semester and her lectures often times do not even relate to art subjects and instead are about her personal thoughts about UNC.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I ignored Rate My Professor because I was excited for the class content, but boy was I wrong to do so. We hardly ever received grades back, criteria for assignments was vague and confusing, and most of the time we ended up watching documentaries during class. If you're looking for an easy and enjoyable FYS, this isn't the one to take.

If you enjoy being confused and/or put down, this prof is for you. Expect assignments to be unorganized, grading criteria to be unclear, and interactions with the prof to feel demeaning. Expect condescension in lectures, personal conversations, and non-verbal interactions. Would NEVER let a friend take a class with her, I hope you don't either.

Do not take a class with RPM. She gives few guidelines yet penalizes you if you break a rule that she hasn't told you exists. She doesn't return any grades and only collected the textbook once. We often watched documentaries that were sort of relevant, when we needed to be working on our projects. Take the class with a TA, even if it's at 8 AM.

Roxana is often judgmental and can be unnecessarily rude in critiques.  I enjoy constructive criticism in art courses as it helps us grow, however Roxana had us critique the entire class for days on past work where she was uninterested in what was said about the art from each artist and had no helpful feedback.  Negative, unprofessional & arrogant.

Roxana is a very kind person, but as a professor she was very inconsistent and vague with her expectations, due dates, and grading. I had no idea what I had in the class or on any of he group projects until the end of the semester. Not a difficult, but frustrating course.

-extremely unclear due dates -no sakai use -no updated grade  everyone was terrified of failing -inconsistent expectations for attendance and participation -no clear guidelines for any projects -helpful critiques

Wonderful if you need a GPA boost. However, I was really disappointed in the class because we didn't end up following the syllabus, and we didn't seem to do any real work until the final project. She is very vague about her expectations, and didn't return any grades throughout the semester, which made me nervous about my standing in the class

She's an accomplished artist and has made some great work but admittedly doesn't want to teach and this blasé attitude is evident in her lack of syllabi, unclear instructions, non-existent due dates, and spotty class attendance. As a one-on-one advisor, she can be very helpful. Unfortunately, she is the only sculpture professor at UNC.

This class is mainly centered around a group project with different assignments throughout the semester. The groups are random so be ready to make up for your groups lack or work. She is a pretty tough grader. 1 midterm and 1 final, both are allowed a 1 page cheat sheet which really helps (its straight from textbook). Most classes are optional!
Dr Pratt is an incredible professor, her lectures are always so insightful and if you follow the rubrics it is very easy to do well in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Pratt is extremely kind in person, but is also an extremely stingy, tough grader. The course is group project heavy (all randomly assigned groups), so be prepared to put in overtime to make up for others' lack of work. Exams are straight from the book and can be challenging, but not impossible, as she allows a note page while you take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Pratt is an excellent support system to get you through this class. She is very compassionate, and genuinely wants her students to succeed. EXSS 493 is hard no matter which way you cut it (reaching the required hours is the hard part) but she gives very good feedback and is generally very understanding about any issues you might come across.
This class was very easy to do well in if you put in the work. Dr. Pratt was very engaging and helpful. Overall class was wonderful

Would not recommend, only take her if it's a last resort. Takes off way too many unnecessary points, grades way too hard, it's like she grades papers how she wants to see them, and doesn't understand that she can't grade by her biases. Like papers are subjective, keep your opinions to yourself??

I love Dr. Pratt! She is super kind and always wants to go out of her way to help students. There are many small assignments to balance your grade and there are many days that aren't mandatory. A great class if you work hard!

Same teaching style as 322, tests were difficult, lots of random information I don't remember reading. She's nice and def recommend going to office hours, but just beware of tests and group projects. Took last min to grade them! Also your group members rate you on you participation and communication (which isn't always fair).

She is very nice. I like the guest lectures! Only criticism I would give is that her tests are extremely hard. You get a cheat sheet but even then people were averaging 70's! Group projects are weighted heavily and got placed in a bad group which dropped my grade. You def will be needing the book!

Dr. Pratt is knowledge about her topics and is a nice person, I found it difficult to engage in her lectures and she is a relatively tough grader in comparison to my other exss classes. The group projects are easy but grades were not released which was frustrating. A few extra credit ops– take advantage Read the textbook chapters or fail the exams

Dr. Pratt is very knowledgable and is truly passionate about the content! The class relies heavily on in-person lectures and in-class activities so attendance is important. The class is also built to allow for guest speakers within the sports industry which was very insightful. She's very approachable and wants her students to succeed in her class
toughest grader in the entire department and the tests were not relevant to lecture material at all

The lectures were very boring. One midterm/one final. Barely any of the material from the textbook/lectures were on the exams and the average was the lowest I've seen for an EXSS class.Grades hard and posts the rubrics after due dates?Would not discuss grades for the semester, would only discuss them next semester when class would already be over

This is for PHYS115 but I agree this guy needs to take a public speaking class before he can lecture.  I can't imagine him teaching his own class don't take him if you don't want to raise your cortisol levels.

This is actually for Phys 115. I cannot hear Qiu, he just reads off the slides and WHISPERS. He doesnt explain anything or write anything to solve it he just talks. Please avoid him, you will not learn.

Prof. Qiu does not explain concepts in class: he reads straight from the PowerPoints. He doesn't even try, even if students ask him to write out explanations in class. Stay away, if possible. I do not know why he is teaching intro physics as he does not seem to care whatsoever.

Professor Qiu struggled to read the slideshows, which made understanding difficult physics topics even harder. In fact, I got a better grade in 118 than 114 just because of how bad professor Qiu was. He also never answers questions, always seems nervous to lecture, and seems so out of touch with his students. if you have a class with him, DROP IT.
He's an awful lecturer, and reads off the PowerPoint word by word. He also just doesn't explain things even if someone asks him to.
He is awful

He needs to take a public speaking seminar before teaching again. Also he needs better awareness instead of staring down, as I saw a girl with her hand up for over 3 minutes without him so much as looking at her.

Just don't. It's clear he's very nervous up there and I feel bad for the guy, but you literally can't hear a word of what he says. And I sit near the front of the lecture hall. He's someone who may be too smart for his own good. It's much more productive to watch the YouTube lectures from 2020 during class and follow along with poll everywhere.
Writing this review as I'm sitting in class. Awful lecturer, reads off the PowerPoint word by word,  sounds sleepy a bored doing it.
Jesus christ, this guy is an absolutely HORRIBLE lecturer. Thank god that he's not the only professor for this course

Professor Gong was a great professor because she actually put effort into teaching rather than the flipped classroom style of some other econ classes. Problems challenged us and really tested our understanding of the material without being "trick questions." I loved this class and thought it was relevant to contemporary policy problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Gong is one of the best econ professors I've had. You can clearly tell that she is passionate about the subject, and mentions real life applications. If you're confused on anything, Dr. Gong will clarify everything during office hours. The class isn't as easy as some claim, and you do have to put in effort.
Easiest Econ elective, very few homeworks. Fair exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Gong is a really great professor and lenient grader. She really wants you to do well which is uncommon in UNC Econ. Best professor I have had in UNC Econ not because I did well but she is so passionate about teaching. This is good to see and something that UNC Econ needs more of.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Excellent econ professor, wants you to learn and that's it. This was the easiest 500-level econ class ever; great choice for an easy semester but still worth taking seriously because the material/skills are important and Dr. Gong really cares a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I LOVED her. She doesn't try to trick you at all and gives you everything you need to succeed. Exams are extremely similar to problem sets and hw. She is always there to help if anything is needed and such a nice person. Can't speak highly enough about her!! 100% take this as an Econ elective.

Professor Gong was one of the kindest professors I have ever had. She is very accessible outside of class and she genuinely wants to help you succeed. The class consists of short homework assignments and one group project that you work on throughout the semester. I cannot recommend this class and Professor Gong enough. Take this class if you can!!

Only thing that I found slightly annoying is she does not take any questions during exams at all, not even clarifying ones. However, overall this class was one of the best econ ones I have taken. She is not trying to trick you at all where it feels like a lot of econ professors try.
Makes it very easy for you to succeed, if you go to class do the 3 problem sets and do the practice exams this class is barbecue chicken
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The nicest econ professor I've ever had. She told us on the first day she wants us all to get As and she makes it very manageable to do so. The problem sets are for completion except one randomly selected question for correctness. The tests are never cumulative and exactly like practice and old tests. So funny and nice!

Super nice lady, she really takes the time to explain everything clearly in case you ever forget the basics from Econ 101 or Econ 410. You have the option to take the class form zoom instead of showing up in person.

Agree with others - best ECON prof at UNC. 552 is a readings/policy-based class, doesn't really involve typical econ math, just understand and apply data analysis. Dr. Gong is a great professor. She explained concepts clearly, gave good feedback, and overall seemed to care about our success. I would definitely recommend that anyone take her for any econ course. I wish I could've taken more of her classes.

Very easy class if you want an A, The lectures can get a tad boring but again, it's easy and you could get an A just zoning out in lectures and reading the slides later.

TA's did majority of grading and gave good feedback, class was not hard at all, although the lectures could be boring at times.  Quizzes came straight from the slides as well as the final, which was online.  Pretty useful class and information.  Final questions were pulled from quizzes

Very easy class, good easy A. There is a financial plan that TAs grade, my year the TA's were very nice. There are 2 "true/false" questions every class to make sure you're present. reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Quercia is a wonderful professor. He wants to help you learn life skills regarding your finances. I maintained nearly a 97 in the class because the quiz questions come straight from the slides. The large project of the class is up for interpretation and easy to do well on (since it focuses on your finances). Really informative class.

This is a really good class and the things you learn are very practical. There are one or two attendance questions on Sakai every class but they are easy. There are 2 quizzes in this class which are easy. Low workload. One of my favorite classes at UNC.

super understanding and flexible prof that listened to students' feedback. course material is very easy, his lectures and quiz/test questions are very straightforward and directly from the class slides. just go to class for the attendance quizzes and review the slides before exams and you'll get an A.

It seems the other comments are fake. The professor expects students to master material that is barely or never covered in class. The exams and assignments include topics unrelated to lectures, making it frustrating and unfair for students trying to keep up.

I really enjoy Prof Qi's course. The best class ever taken. Qi is very responsive and always ready to answer questions, usually by offering helpful hints rather than direct solutions, so solving problems feels rewarding. The coding is challenging, but the puzzle game makes it fun. Plenty of group activities and collaborations, which are engaging.

Taking Geog 567 with Dr Qi was a honor. I left this class with more knowledge, super cool projects, and the desire to learn more. Dr Qi went out of his way to make sure I was learning and understanding the material. He would encourage me and I never felt stupid. I wish I could take all my classes with him.
Qi is a great dude and loves himself some Geography. This is a great class for the research credit. DO THE CODING PUZZLE :). He gives every opportunity to learn and the labs teach you about GEE well.

I enjoyed this class & Qi's teaching; it was one of my top 3 at UNC. He often gave extensions and was great with partial credit for late work. There were times in class where he didn't give us answers, but after he hinted that the question was on the midterm! Attendance & group work are important, but I'd def take another class with Qi

Professor Qi is a passionate teacher regarding Google Earth Engine (and the research of such in many different papers) and it's obvious in his lectures. He is a fair grader and gives lots of opportunities to make up work and to work in groups if you're falling behind. Although the content is initially intimidating, Qi Zhang makes it engaging.

Nice and genuine person, but everything he said was way over my head. When I would ask questions, he would make it a point not to give an answer or even point me in a direction. I can appreciate the value of learning on your own, but this class was just a professor who presented the students with problems and refused to help us understand them.

Class consisted of weeklyish lab assignments, midterm exam, a presentation, and a final group project. Lots of collaboration in this class. Class content is almost exactly the same as GEOG477 tho
Easily one of the most respected professors at UNC, take Prof. Zhang!

I absolutely loved Prof. Zhang! He is such a nice, caring, and considerate guy. Definitely one of the best professors I had at UNC, and I will for sure take his class again. He gives really good lectures. Do not hesitate to take his class, it's an easy A, I promise.

Probably the best professor I ever had. Dr. Zhang is super knowledgeable in his field and a great lecturer. Really cares about his students and their progress. And he is so passionate about the subject that you can't help but love it too. Would take this class again!

Dr. Qi is an amazing professor, who offers great and enjoyable experience to students in class. He does excellent jobs to help students understand the concepts and develop programming skills with hands-on exercises. He is ready to give feedback and cares about your performance. I would definitely take his other classes if any.

He is a sweet person who cares about students and someone who likes to see you truly understand and learn from class content. This is the most diverse class I have every took with people coming from all kinds of backgrounds and ages. 10/10 would recommend!

The worst professor I have ever had. In addition to everything else that has been said, he simply doesn't care about teaching. Professor Sun was a really nice guy and accessible during office hours. His lectures were not the best, and were very theory heavy, especially for only a first course in differential equations. I took the German summer course online, and unfortunately, I found the experience quite frustrating. Terrible professor, doesnt care about his student at all, do not take his class

Wei was a great TA! Wei is a great professor. Given that we are learning a new language, he explains the information very well. While I was lost in the new grammar being taught at many points, he was more than willing to meet outside of class to explain it to me. Very happy to have had him!

Wei was great! Super kind and very knowledgable. Dr. Quinones-Ayala was an absolute joy to have as a professor. So caring, enthusiastic, and engaging with her students. Genuinely one of the best professors I have encountered during my time at UNC. Take her class if you can, while SPAN203 can be difficult, she will do anything to support you and make learning Spanish fun and accessible.

Dr. QA was extremely kind, caring, enthusiastic, understanding, and accommodating. I am not the best Spanish speaker but was able to get through this class because I made an effort. If you care, you will do fine because she cares! A great option (if not one of the best) for 203.

Professor Quinones-Ayala was my favorite spanish teacher of all time! She was hilarious and generally cared about her students. Professor Quinones-Ayala was a very kind and generous person. Her grading was very favorable and she always encouraged participation. I love Senora Quinones-Ayala. I haven't had this much fun learning Spanish in a long time. Highly recommend!

Professor Quinones-Ayala is so passionate and energetic! She is also super accessible outside of class. The class has a lot of assignments and homework, but she makes class pretty fun and explains the material well.

Oh gosh Brenda is great. I came into SPAN 204 not super confident in my Spanish but her kind direction and interesting activities left me much more sure in my skills. Funny and bubbly- Brenda is my favorite out of all instructors I've had thus far at UNC. While obviously a smart guy, absolutely horrific as a professor. Lectures were almost useless to even attend because they were nonsensical and his accent was difficult to interpret. Professor Quoc treats being a professor like a second job. Quoc is a fine professor. I liked that he uploaded his slides ahead of time so that we could follow along during his lectures, as they could be quite boring. Quoc is a mediocre at best professor. He definitely puts effort into his course, but it seems like it's effort in the wrong places. His tests are theoretical and hard, and his posted solutions often literally say "solve this as we would in class", as if that is helpful.

he took over halfway for another teacher, and his tests were harder but his teaching was better. he follows along w the textbook, so everything you need is literally in there. the last few assignments were kind of difficult because it's on GAMS, but he gives pretty helpful examples to aid you through them. he's very understanding and accommodating!

Overall, he is a pretty boring lecturer, but if you just want to skip class, read the book and have an easy B+, he'll do.

I loved this class and professor! He was really understanding, and everything in the class was manageable. Pay attention in class, go to office hours, and keep up with the weekly homework assignments and you should do very well!

Professor Tran-Dinh is incredible! So caring, and genuinely wanted to offer a good learning experience, despite the online nature of the class. Lectures were straightforward and informative. The workload for STOR 215 (weekly homework, 2 quizzes, a midterm, and a final) isn't too difficult, as long as you pay attention in class and put in the work.

Professor Tran-Dinh was wonderful to have! Truly caring throughout the semester and you could tell he wanted to foster collaboration although we were online. STOR215 isn't bad just make sure you actually go to the classes and do the homework. Very much a "you get out what you put in" type of class but not at all unreasonable.

The WORST professor i've ever had at UNC. His lectures are dull and useless as the HW is on material that is much harder. Quoc is a great guy with good intentions but is simply not a good professor and fails in delivering the content. Wait to take STOR215 with a different professor.

He's a nice guy and it's very evident he tries to teach and wants everyone to do well in the class. His lecture slides and textbook are very detailed and useful. Also helpful in office hours. The class is tedious but not too hard conceptually. Homework usually takes awhile. Exams are similar to old exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: While Quoc isn't the best lecturer, if you pay attention and devote time to learning the material, this class isn't too hard. His slides are actually pretty detailed and well-made. He is a very nice guy and willing to meet with students whenever they need help. Brush up on your Linear Algebra before taking this, and you should be fine.

The lectures are quite heavy and you need to be good at linear algebra to understand all the concepts. He is fully prepared for his lectures, slides, and lecture notes, so you can learn and review a lot after class as well. His office hours are definitely helpful and he is willing to help on any questions. (Homework is a headache.)
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Quoc clearly cares about his students and does everything to make our lives easier. But if youve never had calculus before it might be hard because he can be confusing and only reviews the subject. If you have to take STOR 113, than choose his class because your chances of having easier homework assignments and tests are bigger.

Quoc is a great guy. His english is really not that bad and it's actually super easy to understand him if you give him a chance. His class, however, is kind of all over the place. I didn't get much from lectures, but that's mainly because it was very, very boring. There's a lot of homework (good way to learn). Only take this class if you have to.

I made a 4 on the ap calculus exam and this class was still a struggle for me. He made it much harder than it should have been. Tests were much more difficult than homework and class examples. Homework graded based on accuracy. I usually regretted going to class because  lectures were confusing.  Do not take him.

While Quoc means well he is not the best teacher. If you have taken calculus before you will do fine in his class, but if you haven't then stay away from this class. The homework is graded very closely and the midterms (three of them) are only out of 35 points, so tiny mistakes cost you. The final was really tough but the grades were curved.

Prof. Tran-Dinh is a good lecturer so far I have had. He taught everything in detail and had reasonable homework load. His lectures was posted online. The exams were fine and the grades were reasonable for ones who studied hard for this course.

Quoc is a good teacher. He made a lot of effort to help students in order to let them study better. I got a lot of help from him. The final exam was a little hard, but questions were that in the HW and practical sheets he gave. The final grade was curved.

While he is a nice man, he is not qualified to be teaching. He speaks english very poorly which makes his lectures difficult to understand. His lectures are very dry and confusing, and oftentimes I would have to go to Youtube to learn material. His exams were almost always much harder than the material warrants. Don't take his class.

Quoc is a good teacher. He really cares about his students and is very responsive. Every time I have question, he really helps to solve it in detail and re-explain it until I get it. He is not a native speaker, sometimes it is a little hard to follow him, but he teaches everything very details and tries to engage students with coupons and questions

This class is essentially applied calculus. I never took calc in high school so I found this class to be extremely difficult (If you're familiar with calc you should be fine). Quoc is a nice man but it can be difficult to understand his lectures, and I usually regretted attending them because I'd have to teach myself the material at home anyways.

Quoc is a very nice man and means well, but DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS.  Lectures are very difficult to follow even though the material is not terribly difficult.  He assigns homework pretty much every class and then never goes over them in class.  Also he grades very strictly and will take off a lot of points for a small mistake with no feedback.

Quoc means well but he is not a clear teacher. The material is easy enough, especially if you took calc ab in high school. Have to go to class to turn in homework. one midterm and a quiz besides the final, and the final counts for most of your grade. If you end up with him it's not end of the world, but try to take another teacher.

If you have taken Calculus, this class is a breeze. Sometimes I skipped class and will still be fully aware of what was going on, and most of the time, I regretted showing up. He was hard to communicate with at times and I think the class was a little more difficult for people who didn't have a strong background in calc.

Prof. Tran-Dinh, in both his first year of teaching and first year in the country, graded strictly, and rapport with students was nonexistent. He seems like a very nice man, but lectures were confusing, and office hours confused concepts further. Definitely the hardest professor for STOR 113. Hopefully his teaching will improve with experience.
I would consistently not wear my seatbelt on the way to this class hoping that I wouldn't make it. Genuinely a top 3 worst professor I've had at UNC.

I took POLI 100H with TJR and it was honestly the most frustrating class. He told the class that he “doesn't give A's." Others reached out to me because they felt I was being singled out during conversations. I never explicitly shared my political views, but it sometimes felt like certain perspectives were treated less favorably in discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: TJR might be the worst professor on the east coast. He grades based on an algorithm that he does not share with students. Only about eight assignments/exams for the whole class and he provides little support and when combined with his extremely harsh grading, this is a hard class to get a good grade. Please, DO NOT take this class. It really sucks.

reviews.comment: Timothy Ryan is the worst professor I have ever had. He provided little feedback and EXTREMELY unfair grades on the few papers and exams we had. His grading is very inconsistent–he took points off my work for things that he did not for other students. He is VERY stuck up. Go ahead TJR, attach your "Course Evaluations" - they just prove my point.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Genuinely my hardest class as a PRE MED. Tougher grader than the chem department. All exams are open note, yet I never made higher than a 62. He will assign 50-70 pages of readings A DAY and will pop quiz you or call on you so watch out. He has no grading criteria or rubric and is just rude about you not understanding content other needing help.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He brings his dog to office hours... and that is enough for me (he's also pretty good at explaining complex topics).

Absolutely amazing lecturer, I learned a lot. As far as graded assignments, you play to an algorithm of what Professor Ryan wants to hear rather than memorizing or analyzing the concepts. Most arbitrary grading I've ever experienced. If he does not agree, -10-15 points. Not focused on learning, focused on his algorithm. Would not take again.

I would honestly not recommend this class. I found this class to be my hardest last semester and it was my only 100-level course. He is a tough grader and never has clear rubrics. Readings are long and time-consuming and if you do not take detailed notes, you will not do good in this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class is amazing so long as you're actively engaged in the subject matter. You must prepare for class and take detailed notes, but that's to be expected in an honors course! His grading can be harsh at times on the amendment proposals, but his exams are lenient enough to make up for it. You should be fine if you read, engage, and study.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: ABSOLUTELY DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. I came into the class thinking it would be interesting and an easy A. I COULD NOT HAVE BEEN MORE WRONG. Exams and amendment proposals are graded on feelings. Readings are also very long. He seems like a nice guy, however he has a very vague rubric to when he is grading things.

Would not recommend this course! I took it hoping it would be an easy gen ed. It ended up being my hardest course and I'm a STEM major... He is a tough grader and participation is weighted heavily. It was way too difficult for a 100 level course. If you are an honors student I would honestly take the regular version.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I would not recommend this class. It was way too difficult for a 100 level course. I would honestly take the normal version if you are an honors student. The readings are insanely long and attendance is mandatory. His grading is confusing and harsh. Participation is weighted heavily. He seems like a nice guy but this class gave me anxiety.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Honestly, do not take this class as an honors student! He makes up grading rubrics as he goes and grades harshly for a 100-level course. If you need the credit, just take the normal version, which is 100 times easier than this class! Exams are all free-response, and he counts participation but will not call on you when you raise your hand ?!?!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Nice guy, but I found it hard to do well in his class. Two huge papers are amendment proposals, which he grades harshly with no clear rubric. Seemed as if he graded more on feelings than the quality of your writing. He is the type of professor who reserves 100's for students who go above and beyond. Loads of heavy reading and very lecture-heavy!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Knowledgeable on the subject and interesting material. class is not an easy 100 course as it should be. He is a tough, arbitrary grader. No clear rubric, and honestly, most students in the class felt their grades were unjust and unfair, with no good constructive feedback. be prepared to read a lot, and attendance is mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr Ryan might be the most stuck-up and pretentious person I have ever met. He is wholly in love with himself. He grades holistically and makes up grading criteria as he goes along. When you go to office hours, he only answers in riddles. I would rather stick my hand in a cheese grater than ever take another class with Dr Ryan again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Ryan while nice is kinda disorganized and sporadic.Class moved at an extremely fast pace and the main coding assignments often had questions that not even the ULAs who had the answer key really understood how to reach the correct answer.Assignment guidelines were often confusing and having the right answer doesn't equal full credit
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Grading is a complete mystery done by a TA with minimal explanation. At first, the lectures walk you through coding but then you get nothing but definitions. The assignments and final were insanely difficult and he kept falling behind schedule. This meant we had greatly reduced time for the final and it was graded harshly compared to the rubric.

6 assignments and a group final project. Extremely boring and inefficient lectures but easy enough to get through while mastering almost none of the material. He does not explain grading criteria very well so you can get a bad grade out of nowhere. Not difficult, just causes unnecessary amounts of stress and very boring lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class gave me so much anxiety. Assignments were graded harshly and instructions were unclear.
A friend of mine is taking it now and I was reminded of just how tough the class is. It would be helpful if lectures were a bit more useful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof. Ryan is a great professor in terms of learning practical data skillsets in R. I would highly suggest that all POLI students take his two Data in Politics classes (281 & 381), since they develop essential skills for social/political science research. This class also got me into coding, which I never would have expected.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: POLI281 is a great class for people who need the QR credit but can't code/do math! Professor Ryan teaches in a way that helps us understand what's going on, at least most of the time. I found the lectures to be redundant so didn't pay attention much, but the groups help. The format of the class does a good job of actually helping us understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Ryan is an amazing professor, he is very receptive to and understanding towards his students. I had previous coding experiences so I didn't have too much struggle with the assignments.

Def take POLI100 with Prof. Ryan! The only papers are two dope amendment assignment and both midterms + the final are take-home, open book, and open internet. He's a really kind and open-minded guy who won't hold it against you if you disagree with his POV as long as you give solid reasoning. Chill with deadlines and is always cool for extensions.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Really nice guy who gives super engaging lectures and is really supportive of students.

He's one of the best! Has a great, intriguing personality, is extremely helpful, and WANTS his students to succeed in the course. No, he won't give you an A if you don't deserve it, but he will spend whatever amount of time it takes working with you to get you there. Definitely take a class with him if you get the chance!
Honestly incredibly underrated. Class has a lot of readings but prof Ryan is fantastic. He challenges you to think critically. A's are not too hard. I learned a ton.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Ryan was amazing! Very easy class if you do the readings (which are interesting) and participate in class. There are papers are projects but are easily graded. The tests are open note and they are fair questions that are discussed in some way in class.
Professor Ryan is an awesome teacher and is so passionate about what he teaches! He inspires students to dig deeper into class topics and is always super helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Ryan is one of my favorite professors of all time! He is an amazing teacher and you will learn so much from his class. He loves what he teaches and really wants his students to succeed. The class is so interesting -- one of my favorite I've taken at Carolina.

Professor Ryan is a fun guy in class. He keeps you engaged but has a problem ending class on time because he's a talker. Midterm and final are only 5 questions, but he does let you use the readings. Research project at the end of the semester is fun but takes time

Professor Ryan is a great professor, who manages to make class exciting even when the subject material isn't always exciting. He is super passionate, and will go out of his way to make sure that you understand the material. Great professor, and if you are a Political Science major his class is a must take.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Professor Ryan is a really great teacher. You can tell he knows what he's talking about and he's really good at staying un-biased/not letting his political views affect his teaching. Not too heavy of a workload, the tests and blog posts are very manageable if you put in the time to prepare. I would take this class again, definitely recommend!

Professor Ryan is a really chill dude and while you don't have to go to class, it will affect your participation grade. He doesn't like tests and as such the few he does give are easy and the class is geared mainly toward learning how to do things rather than learning a bunch of random information. Class was loaded with group projects though.

He's a nice guy, fair grader, wants the best for you. Really into the blogs which is the better alternative than the NYT thing with Conover. He doesn't get visibly annoyed, although you can tell he's not happy when half the class doesn't show. (Attendance wasn't necessarily mandatory) You get what you put into the class. Take notes.

Really engaging professor. Took the time to make sure students truly learned the material, and did a great job at not showing personal political affiliation (non-biased). As long as you come to class, you'll be fine. Tests were based mostly on notes and some readings, which wasn't overbearing or uninteresting. No papers, only 2 blog posts.

Dr. Urquhart is a great prof who won't shy away from sharing his real-world experience with the class. Teaching-wise, he's very direct and has been using the same assignments since forever, so there are clear expectations. However, since the semester project is a group one, you better pray for good teammates. Good class and great portfolio booster.

This class was a huge waste of time. I heard that 382 with other professors is actually really helpful but I feel like I didn't learn anything. he was not clear at all on what he wanted and graded harshly. Didn't learn much he seems like a nice guy but takes himself too serious and doesn't teach any material. You have to cheat on quizzes due to ts
Boring 2.5 hour lectures.

Super student‑focused. He invited feedback throughout the term and actually used it. His real‑world examples helped the material stick, and he made sure everyone participated. Would definitely take his class again. To stay in the loop, you must come to class.

Loved the class. He checked in often, adjusted based on our feedback, and used real‑life examples that made the content practical. Lots of participation, but low‑pressure. I'd absolutely take another class with him.

Amazing professor. If you're struggling in this class, it's not on him it's on you. He's tough, blunt, and expects you to act like an adult. People who complain are just soft and not ready for real expectations. If you can "handle" honesty and want to actually learn, take his class. Highly recommend.

The other reviews aren't wrong, he definitely gets cross with the class sometimes. However, he did a good job of putting us in an entrepreneurial mindset and I got more out of this class than I was expecting. He also offered to write us a LoR for grad school which was unprecedented. Was he my favorite prof? No, but he far exceeded my expectations.
Horrible professor and grader. Did not give me any reasons for the grades he gave me so I had to drop the class. Changing majors because of him.

Switched directions a lot in the class during the semester, never made full use of the lecture time and would go on random tangents and impassioned lectures. Very funny and approachable, but unsure what the point of the lecture was. Semester long project also felt purposeless, could have been completed within a week.

I read the comments and had some apprehension coming into the class. I was amazed about how the comments were totally wrong. I'm a Jr and many of the ppl were Sr. who were complaining. All you had to do was come to class, complete the assignments. He was always available to meet via zoom, b4 or after class. Don't pay attn to the crybaby comments

This class is a joke and not worth my time or money, but it's mandatory and easy so whatever. Prof randomly gave us a pop quiz one day and no one even knew what it would be on since we weren't learning anything...

He spends most of the lecture telling stories that are not relevant to the course work -- also a very subjective grader. He is "against rubrics" so he will give you the grade he feels like giving you and you cannot dispute it utilizing a rubric.

The class is fairly easy, though. He is upset that it is considered an "easy A" class.

Just a horrible professor who does not respond to emails at all and gives really long and boring lectures. But you are pretty much on your own because he will not respond to any sort of communication so if you have any questions about your assignments you are on your own.
This class is super easy if u just show up. Literally all you need is common sense and like attempt to make a decent thing and he will give you a good grade

He started out very nice, but halfway through the semester he got mad at the class and suddenly everything was graded harder. He changed due dates, directions were not very clear, and he had no office hours on his syllabus. Grading seemed subjective as well. Hes not a bad guy, but he definitely needs to create rubrics for his assignments.
Ryan was all over the place. I could not tell you what I learned in this class and I went every time. He changed criteria for grading and never gave good feedback. It was an easy class.

This class is composed of four easy quizzes, a presentation and a project. Each week there is a lecture and recitation but attendance isn't taken. Prof Urquhart is a cool guy and you can get whatever you want out of the class. Probably the easiest class I've taken at UNC.

A low-stress class that was very manageable. Just follow instructions and you'll do fine. Sometimes they can be vague so you just have to ask questions but overall the class was really reasonable. Prof. Urquhart was very nice and generally cared about the students. Grades mostly come from 1-2 quizzes, article pres., and a semester group project.

Really enjoyed class. The students wanted to be hand-held, was frustrating.  Just do the work. He told us what to expect&gave examples. Most don't pay attention. My team made errors, he graded us hard and we corrected the errors. Can't ask for more than that. Gave a pop quiz, ppl got mad. Still got an A. This is college and not middle school.

I'm still confused by this class. I came in thinking it would be pretty easy, but halfway through, the professor told us he was done with his easy A reputation. After that, he started nitpicking assignments and gave a test with a 60% class average. He's very unorganized and constantly changes assignments. However he gave me an A at the end, so idk.
The only bad thing about this class is that nearly all grades are group projects. Professor Urquhart is a great person and tries to inspire all his students to be the same. Gem of a professor.
It was a really interesting class that explored product management. Professor Urquhart was super nice and easily accessible during the summer. Definitely recommend his class to anyone considering.

This class was quite enjoyable during the summer. We learned some interesting information about systems and got to design our own interfaces in the form of a mobile application from start to finish. You can tell he really cares about the content and the students. I highly recommend this class.
Boring tech bro, told a lot of rambling stories about his job. There's very little to his classes, basically any submission is a guaranteed 100.
This was one of the best INLS classes I've taken, and Dr. Urquhart is a gem! Great lectures, gives good feedback, and is easy to get along with. Definitely recommend.

He's pretty long winded but beyond that he is a good professor to have. Understanding, passionate and collected at all times. The class itself was surprisingly easy for UNC, without a doubt an easy A if you do your work.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Truthfully, I did not enjoy a single class period of his. We either had boring lectures where I regretted showing up or times he didn't even show up... I spent most of the time teaching myself the material. He doesn't respond quickly to emails, provides little feedback, and overall, is just disorderly. Fair tests were the only good thing.

Lectures are a little fast and he assumes you know stuff that he hasn't taught often. Seems like he would be a great prof for higher level math but not the best for the basics. Exams are very fair and cover the same kinds of problems that we did in class. Lowest midterm gets replaced by the final.
Good class and good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: MATH 383 is difficult regardless of the professor, but I think Tamim made the content as understandable as possible. I felt like my midterms were graded harshly, and some homework was difficult, but I was always able to get help.

Wonderful professor, gives clear explanation for all concepts. Cares about his students, very accommodating. Class is not difficult if you engage with the material, do the homework, and practice problems. There is nothing on exams that is not covered in class; very straightforward, I got a 100% on every exam. Lowest exam grade replaced w/final.

Great for a math prof. Got an A. Let us replace our lowest test score with our final if it was higher. TONS of resources available for outside of class (i.e. practice problems, so if you do all of the practice you'll do well on exams). Never puts anything on the exams that we haven't covered in class with practice problems or in previous exams.
I was crying after leaving this class.  His political based problems and Naruto problems cracked me up!
amazing class loved his naruto problems!
meh class i guess.

Saiful moves kind of quickly through the material, but he explains things well. Tests weren't easy but they weren't too difficult either (not actually a big step up from homework), especially since we were given a one-page cheat sheet for each exam. Definitely recommend taking advantage of the textbook practice problems he gives for exam prep.

Tamim is a very genuine professor and his class is pretty manageable even with a hard course load. His exams are doable but do require some studying if you want to do well. Highly recommend him for 383.

Saiful is a great lecturer and teaches 383 very well. It can be fast if you aren't well-rooted in previous math classes, but it is still doable. He is nice, pretty funny, and considerate. It is best to go over lecture notes and provided worksheets to study for his midterms and finals. The tests are hard and worth a lot of your grade, study.

Tests make up almost all of your grade, and he doesn't do a very good job of presenting what will be on the test in class. Lots of people say he is a good lecturer, but he mumbles a lot. Doesn't give many resources to study, and the homework and textbook problems don't adequately prepare you for the tests, which are typically 4-5 questions.

If you are at all good at math then there is no need to attend. He provides about a worksheet per class, combine reading his posted class notes for 5 minutes a day and solving the worksheet, you will do very well and save several hours per week.

Tamim is a good professor and gives great lectures and is also very engaging in class. He wants the students to understand the material. But if you care for your grade, I do not recommend him. His exams are harder than the worksheets and review material he gives but he is a great lecturer so you will learn the concepts if you attend class

Explains the content well but the exams and homework problems are much more difficult than what we go over in class. Many worksheets and MyLab's to complete. If you care about your grade, you may want to consider another teacher.

Saiful was excellent at explaining the concepts clearly, and the class moves at a great pace. There are two exams which are difficult to finish within the 50 minutes. However, the final exam was rather easy and you have plenty of time for it, and it can replace your lowest midterm. Definitely recommend for diff eq!

If u are the type of student who depends on good explanations, take this professor. He explains things super well. However, his exams in 50 minutes were brutal and rushed. Final was super easy. Nice bc no attendance. Content is very easy to learn. Great teacher = Hard asf exams. If you can learn from a textbook, take another prof for easier exams.

He's very smart but the lecture pace is often too fast. Concepts are introduced quickly with little algebraic explanation, making it hard for first-timers to follow. While questions are encouraged, his responses can feel dismissive, which may discourage others. Providing more detailed steps would greatly help in understanding the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Credit where credit is due, Tamim is a great lecturer. However, he is genuinely terrible and rude in office hours. He once told me, "you know, you can ask the TA these questions at his office hours", and when I came back another day he told me "you don't know what you're doing, I can't help you with this, it would be a waste of time"

Even though it is easy to mess up in this class, he has a midterm drop. Midterms are fair but somewhat tough, need a 95 for an A. As far as math classes go, difficulty to make a high grade was average but content wise it was mad easy. Def recommend Saiful he was super chill.

Professor Tamim tried to ensure students followed through his lectures. Midterms were fair and straightforward. The final was more challenging though so make sure to study hard for that towards the end of the semester.
It was MATH 116. It was a pretty tough course towards the end but go to class everyday and ASK QUESTIONS!!!!

Tamim is a good lecturer with good humor, and all of his lecture notes are accessible on Canvas. He usually lectures for 30 minutes or so and lets students work on the lesson worksheet in his presence. His midterms were alright, but you might need to manage your time well. His final was brutal, but he must have curved the hell out of it.
Good lecturer explained the subject material in a concise and easy to understand way. Tests were difficult but with a bit of studying an A is easily achievable.

He does in class worksheets due at the end of class which can be annoying because they usually required more time than was given to do properly. Other than that though, his class was pretty easy and he posts the lecture notes online so you can skip if needed. Tests were pretty reasonable. Workload is very manageable too.

He had good lectures and always made sure to leave time to go around and help out. Attendance wasn't really necessary, but that's just because the material is pretty easy. Would definitely recommend Tamim for 383.

I really enjoyed his lectures. He was pretty engaging and made confusing theories and concepts relatable and easy to understand. There is a good amount of reading and notes but I highly recommend doing them. Overall the class was pretty straightforward and a good start for the comm major.

Professor May is an amazing lecturer, people have a "just get it done" attitude in this class, and it is unfortunate. He makes difficult concepts easy to understand. He is extremely accessible outside of class, I once emailed him about the lecture slides, and he got back to me within the hour with the slides from that chapter and the one after.

Hereallycaresabout the topic butsometimes overexplainedwhatsomethingmeantmaking it a bit confusing. He hosted review sessions before the midterm and final as well as giving us a list of the topics that were going to appear. Youhavetoread a lot, but I gotawaywithnotbyjustpayingattentionto the lecturesandtakingnotesbecausehetalks about the readings.

Professor May is so passionate about communication, and he cares about students so much. He took every email, feedback after class, and students' needs seriously. The course itself may not be that difficult, and going to the review session is almost equal to an A on the test, super helpful!!! 100% recommend Prof. May

I think I lost brain cells during his lectures. Better off doing poppers. 2 essays, midterm, and final exam= entirety of your graded work. Very easy and only requires common sense; no reading of textbook is necessary. The recitations felt like I was at summer camp. Cannot believe this is a required college-level class, a 10-year-old could pass it.

Dr. May is very kind and passionate about communications! He is very knowledgeable and respectful of students. The class is lecture-heavy and can be boring, but you will learn a lot about theories of communication from this class. Midterm was tough but final was easier. Take class with Steve May!

Steve was phenomenal. You can tell he cares about his students and he gives professional help in office hours (cover letters, resumes, job connections, etc.). It's a two-person presentation, a paper, midterm, and final paper. He wrote the textbook and it's very well done, you just have to purchase. Interesting and engaging class!

Very easy class but repetitive (nonmandatory) lectures and unproductive (mandatory) recitations. Very easy class but graded on few things so make sure you put effort into the few papers/exams.
