He made the final open note/at home because some people didn't do as well as he intended on the midterm which was super nice. Very caring guy and gave EC.

He is knowledgeable and passionate about his teachings. Fairly easy class, note taking during lectures can be important as there is not much info on the slides to look back on. The nights before the midterm and final he hosted exam reviews which was very helpful as it was an opportunity to ask any questions we had which he would answer in detail.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor May is an awesome professor and he taught this class very well. Two lectures a week  (not mandatory attendance) and one recitation a week (mandatory). Only graded work we did all year was discussion form responses every other week and two four-page papers. Midterm is a mix of multiple-choice and T/F and final is four essay questions.

this class was easy and a good filler/elective credit. The professor is nice and the content isn't that hard. Sometimes we had guest lectures. Attendance to lecture is not mandatory but recitations are. Mainly just discussion posts about the reading but you only have to skim it. There were two papers that weren't hard but took a bit of effort.

I took COMM100 with him. He is a great professor, but I am not a communications major, so this class was soooo boring. 2 papers, a midterm, a final, and a few discussion posts. Super easy class though.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor May is amazing. He's kind and passionate about what he teaches, and he makes sure it's applicable to your future. Class time is group work discussing organizations through different metaphors and answering questions about entering the workforce. Midterm, final, and one ten page paper, each 30 pts w/ 10 pts for attendance. Take this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Steve May is the best professor I have had during my 4 years at UNC. He is incredibly educated and it shows in his discussion. He is also very caring and takes time in class for students to ask questions regarding jobs and interviews. If you get a chance to take one of his classes, do it.

Possibly best professor I have ever had. Perfect mix of professional and caring. Clear grading instructions, do them and it is hard to not get an A. First month is reading and lectures, but the rest is presentations - no mandatory HW after you present in your pair. One 5 page paper, short essay midterm, and the final is a 8 page paper. Not hard tho

Dr. May is so kind and extremely available. He will look over your resume, advise you in your career, and is very connected in the business world. 10/10 prof and I would take all of his classes! He is knowledgeable & reasonable, do speak up in class discussions for participation though. Material is based on ethical dilemma case studies.
Amazing professor, and more than willing to help with personal things outside of class. Top 5 professors i've had at UNC no doubt and the class is SO interesting!!
He was really nice and the class was interesting. You do not have to do much on the day to day but there's a few papers, a big presentation, and a couple small assignments.

Steve is the absolute best, so helpful and insightful. He is very well connected in the business world and you can always come to him for those types of questions or help. The class was based upon different case studies, done in partners which was fun and pretty easy. Would take this class AND professor again, 10/10.

He doesn't take attendance. Says participation matters but I showed up to 5 classes and spoke maybe 3 times and got a 93 for participation at the end of the semester. Midterm is multiple choice and based primarily on the textbook/readings/lectures he does. Final is a paper, papers are fairly easy. Overall pretty good and you can skip & still pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Steve is one of the best people I've ever met, not to mention an amazing professor. His courses are straightforward and he makes the course content relevant to workplace trends. You will always feel cared for as a student, and he loves to help with any questions you have about the job search. Take a class or study abroad with Steve!!
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: You will not regret any class you take with Steve. He is extremely caring and attentive and well-versed in the academics of UNC. He gives great feedback on papers and is always willing to meet outside of class

Dr. May is a great guy and a great professor. He really cares about helping his students whether it is for class or for beyond the classroom. He tends to talk kind of fast but he will answer any question that you have. I appreciated his feedback and how fast he is at responding to emails and questions pertaining to graded assignments. Great prof!

My favorite prof! His experience in the field is unmatched. He takes numerous occasions to ask how we are doing, express interest in our plans at Carolina and give advice. Supper good with freshmen. The course covers a lot of interesting examples you get to talk over with peers in class. The papers revolve around your own creativity and interests.

loved this professor and his class!! Was not too much work, just try to stay engaged in class and keep up with readings so that you understand the course content for the papers. Great professor and overall easy course.

May was a great professor! He lectures a little bit, but lectures with him was partcipation focused with real-life examples. There were readings almost every class, but we discussed them heavily. He takes a couple of class periods to let us ask work-related questions, which was really great!

Dr. May is the best! He takes a genuine interest that his students not only learn course content but also takes time to talk about "work related questions." It was so refreshing to be given "real" world advice. Readings are short and engaging, class discussions are always fun. I've learned so much and loved every second of this class!

Professor May is hands down one of the best professors I've had at Carolina. He is extremely knowledgeable and his lectures are always engaging. His class is discussion heavy, which allows for lots of different viewpoints on each ethics case you discuss. Take him before you graduate! You won't regret it!

Professor May genuinely cares about his students. If you're into Corporate Social Responsibility and learning about labor culture, he's your man. If you're not, you might find his lectures dull depending on the course content, but he tries his best to make it interactive. He always makes himself available to help his students.

Prof Marr is a nice guy, but his class is very unorganized and very hard to follow. No guidelines for essays; he grades based on his opinion. Huge final project as well as midterm and final. There's a reason there are seats open in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is my favorite professor at UNC so far
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Marr was very kind and knowledgeable. His lectures were long and had no structure. Rubrics were vague and confusing. TAs were confused too so had no one to get information but figure it out on my own. Very confusing but relatively easy class if you study.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While Prof. Marr is one of the sweetest professors I've had, the structure of this class made it difficult for me to enjoy. Super interesting concepts even if he is a bit long-winded. I didn't mind that but ALL of his assignments have lengthy, vague instructions with high expectations of content. I was constantly asking my TA for clarification.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Marr is such a jolly, passionate fellow. We went out as a class to watch a documentary at 10pm on a Thursday. If you like reading, this class is for you. Class sessions were all discussion. 2 10-page research papers were basically 90% of our grade but he grades easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Marr is incredibly intelligent and is knowledgeable about the lecture topics. However, the lectures can sometimes be boring and he rambles so for the final I recommend rewatching the recorded classes. Also, some assignments come out of no where and that feels overwhelming. He is a sweet guy but holds a higher standard than most100classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Has an unreasonable amount of reading due during the week, with very little actual directions on how to complete the annotations on them, and when to do them by. Lectures are impossible to take notes on because he just will put up one slide and ramble on for minutes on end. Other students and the TA's rarely had an idea about what was going on.

Professor Marr is a great instructor. There was a lot of reading material (first-year seminar), and the main assignments were two 8-10 page papers. He lead great discussions in class and cared abt his students. Would recommend taking this class if possible. We also went on a class field trip to the movie theater.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a professor who respects and cares for his students. You can reach him by email at any time, even on weekends. He loves his job and with responsibility. Although this course has a lot of reading, as long as you read the article or book he provided and think and discuss, then the essay and exam are not too much of a problem.

Honestly this class was a complete joke. The most absurdly whitewashed presentation of Islam in America. I'm not sure that Marr himself is an antisemite (also not sure that he isn't one) but the course is full of them, and Marr knows his audience. Embarrassing UNC has courses like this. He should go back to teaching Moby Dick or whatever.

Professor Marr was kind and enthusiastic about this class. All the assignments are SUPER easy and are graded very leniently. However, the class is reading heavy and you have to comment on lengthy readings before each class. Attendance is mandatory. The only hard aspect was the final. Nonetheless, super easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Marr is kind and truly loves the material he teaches. However, his lectures are very hard to follow and it takes a while to get used to the new vocabulary. There are a ton of readings but most of them are actually relevant. The final also comes out of no where and is overwhelming. Still a very interesting class!

While he's a really sweet teacher, his lectures are all over the place and really hard to follow. I don't feel like i've learned anything coming out of this class and when he tells you what is on the final exam it is overwhelming, especially when the entire class is hard to follow. There are a TON of really long readings with annotations.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr Marr was amazing! His knowledge is astounding and he treats every student with respect and care. He also takes the time to get to know his students and even their interests. All in all, he is a sweet older man
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took him for AMST258 and he makes you read ALOT. Roughly 100 page readings due before class everyday. However, he was a nice, engaging professor and made the class enjoyable if you actually do the readings and participate in discussions. The readings and topics are interesting. Just a lot of work, but focuses on areas in history rarely discussed!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: super nice,kind and understanding. if you have a chance to take a class with him, do it!! he holds office hours and helps you with any ideas you may have.  this was a PH credit so lots of readings but its just discussion based, you dont have to read the articles. 10 page research paper at the end with mini projects, not tedious at all
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: While professor Marr is one of the most kind-hearted and genuine professors I have met, this class was pretty difficult. Lectures were all over the place and there were SO many readings each week. The final exam is a culmination of all the readings, so if you're not good at history or reading take another course. Very interesting course nonetheless
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Unrealistic reading expectations (150 pages between Monday and Wednesday), along with vague assignment criteria. Very high expectations for a gen-ed. Classes were boring and very repetitive. Also, he cares a lot about participation so get ready to be cold called if you don't like speaking up (or don't do readings like me & most ppl in the class).
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Marr is a great and kind professor and I found the class super interesting. However, there is lots of reading and annotating every week. Lectures are interesting but feel like a waste of time if you do the readings. He also is not very clear on instructions about essays and you have to ask several times to get a grasp of what hes looking for.

He was a super nice man, but SUPER unclear. He would give instructions for major essays days before it was due, not giving much time to write a proper paper. One time we were told specific instructions AFTER we turned it in (our TA told us after). The class itself if interesting, but it was unnecessarily stressful due to the inorganization.

There are weekly annotations for articles that are sooo long sometimes with no heads up. The amount of reading varies from week to week, but around 1+ hours of reading a week. TA is great, Prof is nice, but sometimes grading is unclear. There aren't many assignments beyond the annotations. It's worth 3 gen eds, so expect around that much work.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed having Professor Marr for this class! Lots of reading and online annotating but it was just this and a few papers for the whole semester. TAs graded the papers, but Marr was accessible outside of class. Kind and cared about the students, you could tell that he missed in-person instruction a lot. Really informative class!

If you want a class that is has a balanced perspective it is not this one. I do feel like I was punished for not agreeing despite not disagreeing since so much of the course was political/social topics. Dr. Marr also did a very poor job of outlining what papers should contain and how they were going to be graded. Did not give back papers on time.
Gave a ton of reading and annotations weren't always a joy. Very passionate and kind. His TA's this semester were really kind so it was an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Marr is a good-natured and very kind man. He's the kind of professor you hate to disappoint because he's like your grandpa who believes in you. He'll give you a lot to read. His lectures are super interesting - but he won't record online Zoom meetings because he wants you there. He's a real stand out professor in my book. An asset to UNC.
There is a ton of reading every week that you have to annotate for a grade. I would not recommend taking this class unless history really interests you.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Marr is AWESOME!! His class gave such great perspectives on Muslims in the US, and we read awesome books. 2 essays, a creative final project or research essay, participation (no exams). He was really accessible outside of class and is so dedicated to teaching. He even gave one class from the hospital after a bike accident!! Definitely take!

Definitely do NOT recommend. Sure, he's nice to MOST students but is rude to others who may not feel that comfortable in class since he requires you to speak during every class. Does not respect boundaries and can be insulting at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: In-class participation, quality of reading annotations, and two 8-page research papers determine your grade, which can be nerve-wracking. Do the readings, annotate thoughtfully, speak up, and work hard on the papers. If you show that you care some, Marr will notice this. He is supportive, encouraging, and kind. An A is definitely within reach.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Marr is AMAZING. Birth and Death in America was a great first year seminar and I learned so much in this class. Make sure to read the readings her assigns. Your grade depends on participation, so try to say something at least once every class. There are two long papers, but you get to pick what you write about. 10/10 class!

Prof Marr is an angel. He took his time every day to greet each student as they joined the zoom call. He is passionate about teaching as well as learning from the insights of the students. There are a lot of novels to read, and a few papers to write, but prompts are general and grading is fair. He is such a kind person! I will miss his enthusiasm.

Professor Marr was a really great instructor. There was a lot of reading material, especially for a first-year seminar, and the main assignments are two 8-10 page papers, but Professor Marr was an excellent teacher. He lead great discussions in class, overall he was really sweet, and he was really considerate during this pandemic.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: I don't like how the class is set up, especially now with the stress of online learning and covid, our grade being made up of only 2 papers only added to my stress. Instructions for the research papers were not clear. Grading criteria wasn't clear either. He seems nice though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Rude, not understanding of the circumstances we are in, gave a lot of reading to do beforehand and was not very clear on assignments. Do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: To pass this class with an A or A-, you MUST participate EVERYDAY and read the readings that he assigns. You MUST show up to class. This is really all it takes to get a good grade in this class. He just wants to see his students grow intellectually. He takes the time to help each student individually and is easy to reach outside of class.

Took this class my first semester at UNC and I LOVED it. My favorite class by far. The discussions are mind-blowing and I felt like I learned so much from the professor and the other students in my class. If you show enthusiasm and participate in class discussions, you're basically guaranteed an A. Professor Marr really cares about his students.

BEST FYS!!! Research based on interesting topics. There is no structure but thats what makes it so cool. You learn things you never thought you would about birth and death. Marr is passionate and cares about every single student. Participate and put effort into the two research papers, he really just cares about you and how much you try.

TIM IS A GOD. he cares so much about his students and their thought & ideas. He is so so so smart and amazing and an actual gem. Birth and Death is such an amazing first year seminar that knocks out 3 gen eds and he cares so so much about the class. You discuss topics that you didn't think existed and it is honestly the best thing ever!

I took a class titled "Muslims in America" with Dr. Marr last year, and had a pretty good experience. He is clearly very bright, in addition to just being a good guy. That being said, he seemed to have a political agenda in teaching the course, and the class devolved into regurgitating left-wing talking points. Also assigned questionable reading.

While there is an absurd amount of reading, he is literally the MOST genuine and caring professor I have met at UNC. After the exam, he preceded to shake every student's hand and call them by name (100+ students). While his lectures are scattered/there really isn't clear grading criteria, you should be able to pull out an A or A-.

The amount of reading for this class was honestly unreasonable. About 100-200 pages of reading per class, with sometimes there being a little less. HE cares SO much about the students and content. I just think he cares too much sometimes and that neglects his teaching ability. A lot of unclear instructions on the assignments. Really nice guy.

Tim is the greatest kind of weird. He is crazy passionate about the content of this course and though assignments and expectations could be unclear at times, it would be hard to find a professor that cares more than Dr. Marr.

He taught one of the first classes I took at UNC when I transferred and I am so glad I took this class. He gave me incredible feedback and was encouraging of my writing. He can go on some tangents about subjects involving islamophobia or race but they are usually pretty engaging. All around a super nice guy!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Professor Marr is enthusiastic about what he teaches and it shows during his lectures. His class taught me how to think about history and memory.

Marr is so happy and enthusiastic about teaching and a little weird, and I loved it. He loves what he's teaching, and he knows so much about it, especially considering most of the topics were pretty out there. A ten page paper for the midterm and the final, a couple of opinion-based short essays, and that's pretty much it. Easy A, and cool class.
Marr's the man. Take this class

Very interesting professor.  Leads thought-provoking discussions and helps you to think on a higher plane.  Very available to discuss projects and willing to give helpful feedback.  Interested in students.  Most of grade is based on two main papers, which can seem daunting, but he helps and guides you as you work on each for half of the semester.

Professor Marr is probably the best professor I've had. He's extremely enthusiastic about the material, an animated, engaging lecturer, and thoroughly smart and articulate. He is heavily invested in his students--he took the time to learn all 60+ names and faces. Not an easy A: the average student is just  much smarter than the majority.

Professor Marr was an awesome guy, and he was extremely knowledgeable about his subject matter. I had such little interest in this class, and yeah, it was kinda boring for me, but professor Marr makes it so much more fun and is great at getting to know you and being a personal guy. I highly recommend this teacher.

Dr. Marr is brilliant passionate about both his subject and his students. I loved going to the lectures each week. The class is a bit disorganized, but I would highly recommend a class with Marr. His lectures broadened my perspective on American culture and history, and always left me wanting to talk about class material with friends.

TIM MARR IS THE BEST. He is very passionate about what he teaches and gives great feedback! He enjoys seeing all sides of topics and drawing them our so you can easily grasp them. I have no doubt that this class completely changed my way of thinking about everything. It was hard to adjust to the work load, but it was totally worth it! I loved it!
Dr. Marr is a genius  AND an amazing teacher. best class ever.

Very passionate and engaging.  Professor Marr made sure his classes were thought provoking and interesting.  Absolutely loved this class.  There are two major projects, both papers, and a lot of individual reading assignments.  But they are all interesting.  I recommend this seminar to anyone and everyone.
Genius. His class on Herman Melville changed how I approach literature.
MY FAVORITE teacher at UNC! Sooo interested in his subject matter and helping his students! A MUST for any Amst major especially!

Prof. Marr is very passionate about what he teaches.  He inspired us to do our best work.   There was alot of reading and writing, but you should take this class if issues of birth and death interest you.  Work consists of two major projects (papers), one on birth one on death.  I learned things unknown to me prior to class.

Professor Marr is a bit kooky, but very passionate about what he teaches and very good at engaging the class.  The work load for this class was moderate but always interesting.  You will excel in his class as long as you put forth effort and enthusiasm.

Dr Bergeton clearly cares a lot about the content but his lectures were not very captivating as someone who didn't already have a passion for the topic. I did enjoy the freedom in the final paper which allowed me to dive into really any aspect of Qin and Han history/culture. If you already know you love the topic, you'll enjoy this more than I did.
hard course but he is a nice guy.the materials are hard though, i don't know the stories in the slides even though I'm a Chinese
Good professor take his class
uffe is so nice in class and is really gentle during lectures, but the grading is absolutely horrible. TA also grades really irresponsibly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He is a tough grader. His lecture is really boring. He never check his email and always be busy during his office hours.

Dr. Bergeton explained things very well, and I have learned a lot from him. 

Although the course was challenging, I have learned a lot from him, and I will 100% take a course taught by him again. 

Thank you Dr. Bergeton!

There are quite a lot of readings, but they all relate in a way and most of the readings are online. 2 essays, one being the midterm, and the final being a 10pg paper along with a 5 min presentation. He is a very generous grader and the lectures were pretty interesting. He holds office hours for essay critique so you can score better on the essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Overall, decently easy gen-ed. If you're familiar with some Chinese history, this class shouldn't be difficult at all. There were a lot of readings and this class was very performance-based (90% of grade based on tests and papers). Tests were fairly easy but get ready to do some timed-writing

Yes, he is one of the smartest professors; yes, he is old-fashioned; yes, he is so very slow with grading; yes, the lectures get dry; yes, you will get an A if you put some effort into reading and throwing in a few of his vocab into the essays.
Great professor. He learns China a lot, if you follow his instruction you can get good grade. be prepared to read Chinese classics (in english)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Bergeron is really sweet! A lot of people didn't like his lectures and assignments but he just really cares about the material and you can tell. There was a LOT of reading. Few papers but he expected them to be done very well. Overall the class was not too bad but definitely a lot of work towards the middle and end.

Though I did learn a lot I would NEVER recommend this professor. He never answered emails and would cut me off in office hours. He said he wanted students to participate but when people did, he seemed annoyed. The workload was pretty light, but the class got extremely boring after a while. He is passionate about the subject but very condescending.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is very passionate about the class and its material but he lectured for most of the class period every day and they were incoherent lectures that didn't make sense. He assigned long readings and then didn't use them during class. He is a VERY slow grader. In general, he seemed very unprepared for class every day.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very enthusiastic and clear lecture style, though occasionally erring on the side of restating some points too much. Not a harsh grader, but reading the course materials makes a lot of difference for the assignments. Great class for anyone interested in the topic.

He was a decent professor. Readings were assigned but not used in class. He graded on 3 essay papers. He definitely has his point of view and if you disagree he makes it pretty clear he doesn't agree, but overall the class was pretty easy. His Powerpoints are pretty unorganized and not really used in the class.

The class itself was interesting, but Bergeton is a lecturer who stood and spoke with a slideshow for 1h30m each day. The readings were required, but I never did them and got an A in the class so don't let that scare you. Overall, an alright class but not a lot of room for discussion or disagreement because if you do, he can become condescending.

He never answers emails. He teaches in such a dry manner. He does not care about students at all. He is frankly rude to students. He is super unclear about dates and randomly changes the syllabus and assignment dates. He changed class from in person to online within an hour of class FIVE times this semester.

He may teach but he is not a teacher.

Pretty nice dude and interesting to talk to outside of class, but his lectures were pretty boring. He brought insight into what we read, but he was pretty monotone throughout the entire class. His exams and papers were a little difficult, but going to see him about it and studying a little more than normal and you'll do fine.

Exams test super-detailed stuff from the readings. Lectures are boring and dry. Never respond to emails. Recitations are not helpful at all. Paper grading is super vague and not lenient. Doesn't provide a rubric.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lecture is dry and boring. He wants participation but belittles students' opinions that don't align with his. He has a very Euro-centric view on eastern history and culture. He often suggests that because a student doesn't speak English natively, they aren't good at writing in English. But he does give extensions for papers.
Lectures are engaging and gradings are lenient. Workload isn't heavy since there were basically only 3 papers a semester. The class is very easy and enjoyable for student with Chinese background.

His lectures were long, uninteresting, and draggy. He asked for participation just to end up disagreeing with and belittling everyone's ideas. It was hardly a FYS, we didn't get to talk much, and he crossed out most of our original ideas in papers during office hours. He made Holocaust comparisons and was problematic overall. I do not recommend it
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: There's 2 papers and a midterm & a final in the class, if you get help with your papers beforehand he'll be thorough with guiding you in his OH, the test MC are always pretty easy if you do the readings, but DO THE READINGS! There's a lot of readings and keep up. Recitations were really easy but I didn't find them helpful, easy A if you work a lil
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Not a typical easy A class but as long as you complete assignments on time, he is a very lenient grader. Class consisted of PDF readings, watching films, and 3 papers + final research paper. He was very understanding, gave us many extensions, and was available outside of class. One of my easier zoom classes this semester!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Extremely caring and lenient professor. This class was a breath of fresh air especially during pandemic times. Class was lecture heavy, but easy assignments. Mostly graded on completion except for 3 main papers and a final research paper. Gives many extensions, and very willing to help you in office hours! Would definitely take his class again

Dr. Bergeton gives great detailed lectures. I definitely don't think CHIN 252 is an easy class because there are a lot of readings but he is always happy to help students in office hours. If you're interested in Chinese narratives then I do recommend taking it with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lots of reading, but you do not need to do them. For papers, just go to office hours--He is such an easy grader. I had no idea what was going on in the class and got an A. You vote of format of final, ours was you pick 2 out of 5 essay questions so you can get away with only doing the readings/movies from one time period. Also he bumps grades

Professor Bergeton is very knowledgeable about the Chinese language but he can't always explain his thoughts clearly sometimes being scatter brained or not directly answering the question. He is an easy grader if you submit your work but it is hard to understand/comprehend exactly what he is talking about.

Uffe is not a bad professor but it's obvious he cares more about his personal research than teaching his class. He can be a little condescending if you talk with him one on one but knows his stuff. Uffe is a bit unorganized as well. Pretty easy grader if you show you care about the class.
Nice guy. Can be a little dry but he tries. There might be better ways for you to spend your time but you won't regret taking the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Never have I encountered a man with more passion for Chinese culture than Prof Bergeton. Can seem cranky at times, but is actually a really nice guy. I would recommend taking LING 101 and at least CHIN 203/204 before taking this course, not because it makes it easier, but because you will probably learn more. Papers are graded extremely leniently.

Dr. Bergeton was chill. Super easy grader but his lectures can be scattered and confusing. Tried to make it seem like it would be a super hard class but in the end, it was a walk in the park as long as you paid attention to like 1 of the lectures a week.
Long, dragging lectures. Inaccessible outside of classes and office hours.

WOW. What a great professor. If you are interested in Asian Studies, do not miss out on taking one of Uffes courses at UNC. He will open your eyes to all different perspectives of linguistics, Chinese language, Chinese history, and Chinese society. Talk about a knowledgeable and passionate individual. I learned so much this semester.

ASIA65 wasn't too hard so if you need a couple geneds I would recommend taking it. He definitely enjoys what he does, but sometimes he likes to go on tangents about his work life so just be aware of that. Also his comments on your papers are confusing, but if you go to his office hours he can give you better advice.
Uffe is an accommodating guy and good conversation. I've taken multiple courses with him and he always managed to keep me engaged.

Lectures are really, really boring and long, and he can seem a bit grumpy at times, especially when people don't read. Readings are long and boring, and he expects people to participate in class daily. Grading, on the other hand, is pretty lenient, and there's only 1 midterm test.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is a very nice person and always give useful advice to your paper. A very intelligent and knowledgeable guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Class was way hard. If you have no interest in Chinese or don't know Chinese then do not take this class. Nice guy but way too much content and messy slides
Such a great guy and not that hard of a grader. He knows a lot and if you care even a little you will get a lot out of this class and do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Tests? Not many--Would take again

reviews.comment: Dr. Bergeton seemed more interested in his own research than helping his students pass. He didn't put effort into giving students feedback yet was a tough grader. Would not recommend this class unless you really know/care about Chinese philosophy
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He definitely knows what he's talking about, but is terrible at teaching a simplified version of it. He goes off on really long unrelated tangents and is generally confusing. Definitely go to office hours because he is picky. Not to mention, he is white but claims to be "Chinese" as a result of marrying a Chinese woman.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: Classes were fun, and he is a great guy.  If you have some interest in Chinese history you would enjoy the class, however if you're unfamiliar with Chinese, the names in the readings may become a bit confusing.

I enjoyed this class a lot and Dr. Bergeton was very helpful whenever I went to office hours about a paper or exam. If you ask, he will help. Also, the lectures were interesting and the movies outside of class were interesting. Overall, I would highly recommend the class.

Do not take this class if you have little to no interest in Chinese history or little to no knowledge of Chinese names. You will be given loads of assigned readings every class. Professor Bergeton is very knowledgeable and will help if you ask but he's is not very clear on what he wants in terms of assignments and papers.

Bergeton gives decent lectures and cares about the topic but only marginally helps you when you visit him for office hours to discuss papers. He'll literally take out a big sharpie and write sloppily all over your rough draft. Most of the time it isn't even legible, just HUGE circles and underlining that obscures the text.

Profe is amazing and a true gem at UNC. Her class is so interesting and a must take for any Latine person at UNC. It is a great class to explore your own identity and understand the world around you. Profe creates a safe space for people to be vulnerable and honest about their experiences. You really begin to feel at home in class.

AMAZING! Elaine is a true gem and I would HIGHLY recommend anyone to take her class. It is full of so much helpful and important information and she has passion behind everything she does. She is also super compassionate, and understanding of the chaos that was 2020. She held plenty of spaces for healing and for growth in combination with learning.

As an Education Professor Elaine really knows how to effectively foster a nurturing learning environment where everybody feels heard and respected. She is sweet and fun and lights up every class with her bright attitude and passion for what she teaches. She may honestly be too good for the classes she teaches. She takes radical pedagogy seriously.

You definitely need to have a good understanding of stats to take this class (and understand it). You can get by with all of the assignments by going to office hours and simply doing the assignments (those are 80% of the grade and no exams), but you won't really understand it without a baseline understanding of stats.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: It is true that his lectures are a little vague and he speaks really fast but there is a lot information that he has to cover in a small amount of time. He tries his best to be helpful and make the class interesting and overall is not a bad professor. The class is tough but the exams are not impossible and the curve is usually pretty good.

Umbanhowar's lectures are worthless. He stands up there and discusses vague examples and graphs, and doesn't have a clear point. It's better to just read the textbook to understand the material. The tests aren't too hard and are curved ALOT because everyone does poorly. I would stay away from him and his poor ecology teachings.
Absolutely terrible.  Lectures made 0 sense. The recitations are the only thing that  saved me from failing

Terrible.  Not even worth going to class.  I started reading the book before the class lectures and I started to think I could have taught the class better than he did.  He stutters a lot and spends the vast majority of the time talking about simple concepts and completely avoids the nitty-gritty details.  I also hated his voice.

Here's the deal: any class you take with this man will most likely end up in you getting a low grade UNLESS you have the initiative to read the book and study a LOT. The recitation section was helpful, but the professor himself is worthless. He jumps around in his lectures, he is hard to follow, and his exams are hard. Just saying' good luck.
Terrible professor, I could barely understand what he was saying because he mumbles and corrects himself so much. Regularly cancelled office hours and did not seem invested in teaching.
Avoid! He mumbles and has no clue what he is saying half the time. His drawing and diagrams are completely useless. You will be teaching yourself from the book if you want to even pass

Overall his class is very enjoyable, he makes the class very interesting. Although the class might seem very easy watch out! His exams are very detailed you have to really know it all. A lot of reading, in the book and articles he assigns. Overall I liked him
A wonderful man!
No Comments
she was very nice funny and helpful

Profesora Venegas was a great professor! She's super caring and made classes enjoyable. The SPAN 261 curriculum (at least when I took it in fall 2024) was standardized between all of the professors, so I can't really say anything about the course itself that applies to just her. I'd definitely take a class with her again though!

Professor Venegas clearly cared about the content shown in class in context to our heritages as students. She is super bubbly and provides a comfortable environment to discuss perspectives on the material provided. Gonna miss her and mis compañeros!

She is the most caring and understanding teacher I have ever had! There's homework for most class days but it doesn't take long at all. One midterm and one final exam and a project. I would highly recommend taking span 267 with her. She is not a harsh grader at all and gives helpful feedback.

She seems nice, but I was having a tough time understanding the concepts, and when I approached her during office hours, she refused to help. She also grades very strictly and gives few and unhelpful comments. The class as a whole is set up awfully, but that's the department's fault.
Very nice, but refuses to give 100's unless it's an online assignment because she believes "not everything is perfect". (I am a spanish speaker).

Profesora Venegas was super sweet and a great choice for SPAN 261. The Spanish department controls the content and grading for 261, but she was flexible when she could be and did her best setting our class up to succeed on the exams. 3
Great Spanish Professor- Super nice and caring. She is unfortunately constrained by the department's rules on teaching and examination.

Prof. Venegas is very caring, understanding, and excited to teach. She prioritizes learning language "the right way," so a lot of the class is based around partner discussion activities (very informal). Participation matters, but it's a very low judgement space. She is a pretty relaxed grader and understands that new speakers make mistakes!

Professora Venegas is a wonderful lecturer and a great Spanish teacher!! She is very sweet and understanding so never hesitate to go and talk to her. Her grading is also pretty chill and she will help you as much as she can. There's a lot of in-class participation and quite a few quizzes but just pay attention to deadlines and you'll be good.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Pablo is absolutely the best professor! Super awesome and so gifted!

The classes were not organized very well. His feedback on assignments was often limited to only 2 words. Assignments should have been more hands on instead of watching him read off a doc for an hour. Obvious this is just a paycheck for him, but an easy grader.

Pablo is an incredible teacher. I took this class fall of 2024, and he canceled class a lot - this has since changed in later classes. For the final project, we recorded and mixed a live performance, and we only had 2 analysis papers and 2 music projects, plus 2 quizzes. He takes a while to return grades but pushing back our due dates as a 'sorry'.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Vega is extremely knowledgable. can't really teach. I could have learned so much from him except that we barely got through any material. Cancelled class all the time, didn't grade anything till the last week, but did give feedback on assignments.

Pablo was super nice and the class work was not super hard. There was an online quiz that i missed as I had work and it brought my grade down to a B- from and A. I was not allowed to take it with a penalty or anything, just lost the points. This was frustrating as the class was not supposed to hurt my gpa and inevitably did.

Pablo is awesome. He is a great teacher and will work with you personally on anything you have trouble with. He is incredibly expereienced in the field of mixing and is great at passing that knoweldge on to others. There are two projects you have to work on and some quizzes that he gives you a study guide for.

Hands down the best professor at UNC. He is incredibly knowledgeable and passionate. He's super accessible if you need help and he truly cares about his students and their well-being. Best professor I've ever had, and the best in the music department. If you want to learn the ins and outs of music and production, the best possible way is thru Vega!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Vega was an awesome resource in further developing my skills in music production. His class was mainly project focused which was perfect for a class of this type. Professor Vega was always willing to help give advice on personal projects and class projects and has tremendous industry experience himself. Field trip was my favorite part!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I'm not a music major, I just decided to take Music Production cuz I needed a class to fill my schedule. This class is an EASY A and actually quite interesting. This was a class I actually wanted to go to each time, just cuz it was fun to learn about! But even if you missed class EVERY DAY, you'd still get 100 on the exams if you memorize the terms
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: sweet person who seems to care about helping her students. lots of discussion with neighbor in class. tests are the hardest part even if you study well. if you answer correctly but dont put enough detail she takes off. the lectures are so unorganized but i think her teaching style could work for people who like to learn just by listening over notes

Dr. US really is a kind person, but she is probably the worst professor I've had at carolina. She has incredibly unclear expectations, is an extremely tough grader, and will not give you any detailed feedback. When we got our first test back, all of her comments were written in "chicken scratch" the she couldn't even read. Do not take.

Dr. US' class was one of the best psychology classes I've taken at UNC. The 3 exams were tough, but Dr. US spent a lot of time grading them and giving us feedback which ultimately helped me learn a lot from this course. The content is also fascinating and I would highly recommend this class to anybody considering a career in mental health.

Dr. US is a caring person, but an inconsistent & unnecessarily difficult professor. The material isn't hard but she grades our short-answer exams like essays - no guidance as to what we missed. She will cancel class or move it online the night before at midnight. Exams are done and I still have no final paper/exam grade. Don't take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very lecture heavy, provides very little guidance on any assignment (of the very few we have), the exams are all open response and handwritten and she asks for tiny details or she'll take off points. She also is very poor in her communication with us and doesn't follow up to what she says she will do
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The material in this class should not be difficult for us to learn and to apply but she makes it increasingly challenging for us to do so by overloading us with paper/presentation project and long exams. She also doesn't even meet her own deadlines or do the things she say she will.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. US does not give clear grading criteria and your participation grade drops significantly if you miss even one class. She is one of the least accommodating professors I've at UNC. She will also make you schedule meetings on your own time outside of class with her and then she won't show up?? Its so bizarre.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. U-S was anal about participation but neglected to show up to our final. She also would email us like 30 minutes before class and tell us to join a zoom call, which was really annoying. She also doesn't enter any grades in the portal so you have no idea how you are doing in the class throughout the entire semester. Really disorganized and phony
Don't take this class with her if you can avoid doing so. She is inaccessible outside of class and unhelpful. You learn more from the textbook than you do from her.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. US is one of my favorite people, but not my favorite professor. I highly recommend a class with her just because she is very well connected and respected within the field, but she lacks clear guidelines and there are five total factors we were graded on. I wouldnt say shes a tough grader, but she is specific. Go 1on1 for help, youll do well.

She is a nice professor, but her grading criteria isn't very clear. Questions were open-ended and unclear and she wanted very specific answers. She knows what she's talking about, but she over-complicates it way too much
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr US was a great professor. Very engaging, I was never bored with her course. However, she's a tough grader and her exams aren't exactly easy. As long as you put in time and don't procrastinate you should be fine.

Lectures were horrible with no useful content. Group project created and graded unfairly with very few guidelines for both the paper and the presentation. Exams are unnecessarily hard and were entirely made of very minor details from the textbook which she never mentioned in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Super energetic and passionate woman, BUT is a harsh grader with little feedback on papers and exams. Takes a long time to grade assignments and you gain more information from the textbook than lectures, which you have to go to. Interesting material, but the teacher was not the most effective.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. US is simply an incredible instructor. She really cares about the success of her students and gives you all the resources you need to succeed. This class is not easy, but you will learn so much about psychopathology! Make sure you go to class - one unexcused absence results in a failing participation grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I'd take this class with her again. One large group project but lots of help was given from her and TAs. She does take attendance without telling you, so beware of that. Lectures are kind of boring. If you've got to take this class, Dr. US is a solid choice. Not my favorite class set-up either (lots of "turn and talk to a neighbor"). Overall fine!

Dr. US is a really awesome professor but the course load was a bit much for an intro-level course with a rather long paper and group project. She was one of the most outgoing and personable professors I've had at UNC and she is extremely articulate and responds well to feedback. Clear expectations.

Dr. US teaches the material well enough - it helps that the slides are posted on Sakai. However, I hated the structure of the course work. We are graded by few things (1 paper, 1 group presentation, 2 tests, and some small stuff). The paper and presentation are due at the same time, but different dates for different groups. Going 1st is miserable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Tests? Not many--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I've taken 2 classes with Dr. US, and she's the most passionate and supportive professor I've ever had. The negative reviews are horribly exaggerated. Her tests are challenging bc they're application, not memorization, based. You're provided with all the resources to do well. Dr. US only wants you to succeed in her class and in your future career.

Had a phony and fake nice personality in lecture but if you approached her one on one, she was inflexible both in her availability and in her willingness to help outside of class. She assigns an case study paper with vague and unclear parameters and expectations, and she has questions on the test from videos we watched in class weeks earlier. SUCK!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Super nice individual and wants everyone to succeed and understand, but no one does. Tells you the tests will be straight forward and easy but are actually super specific with trick questions. Had to write a 10 page case study report and gave extremely vague requirements but when grading had very specific expectations.

Dr. US comes across as nice and bubbly, but her exams are hard and her grading on papers and projects is even harder. Her expectations are very unclear. The class is a lot of work for what the material is. I would take her again if I wasn't getting graded. I loved her lectures, but she has high expectations and gives little guidance.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Dr. U-S is a strong professor, but sometimes the grading criteria is unclear and the grading itself is very tough. I loved the material which helped, but you definitely need to put in a lot of work to find success in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: If you can avoid taking Professor US for Abnormal Psyc (or any class), then PLEASE DO. Horrible professor. Ridiculous grader. The group project and accompanying paper was a complete joke, as she graded unfairly, extremely harsh and her rubric was unclear. Don't let the happy demeanor fool you. Also, 1 unexcused abstence failing attendance grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Although she was a bubbly professor at 8 AM, I learned very quickly that turns into a very condescending demeanor. She grades incredibly tough and does not give good feedback. It's really disappointing considering how much I was looking forward to this class. The lectures were mandatory but not helpful, pretty much taught myself all the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Dr. U-S will come to class every day cheery and smiley but DONT LET IT FOOL YOU. It is mandatory to go to class even though the way you will learn the material is purely through reading - she does not help. She will assign a group project and about 11 pg paper but don't count on a good grade, she'll rip you on both no doubt. Tests are ok if you stu

She smiles a lot; don't let it fool you.  Instructions for things are completely unclear.  EXTREMELY harsh grader, tests on things that we never talked about in class.  Scope of information way too large.  Extremely picky.  She was late to every meeting I had with her (meetings that she required), didn't show up, or just postponed them last minute.

Dr. U-S is very understanding and wants her students to do well. I loved her lectures, however her grading criteria is a bit heavy on tests (worth 60% of your overall grade). They aren't extremely difficult if you really study. The group project isn't terrible, but can be difficult since your group members are assigned for you.
She's awesome. Total sav

She loves her material, but tests are super hard. You can know the book and notes backwards and forwards and still have a hard time. Also, participation in class is mandatory, but class itself is basically just powerpoints. The group project is graded unfairly- she doesn't even watch you present, she bases it off what your classmates saw/thought.

Ulku-Steiner is awesome & has the best taste in style. She's super peppy and adorable and is so passionate about child development. But beware because the tests are SO HARD. The tests, along with the group projects killed my grade. But the research paper helped me out.

best prof i've had so far. helps students relate with funny anecdotes. assigned a project that was fun and helped make the material more comprehensible. cares about students doing well and understanding. i looked forward to going to this class every week, which was surprising as it was at 8 am. definitely sign up for any of her classes.

She was bright and sun-shiney at 8am...Attendance is pretty important. I do believe I learned most of the material from the book-READ IT!! Her tests come straight out of it, and her tests are tricky. Ultimately though, whatever she did worked! In the end i think she gives benefit of the doubt. She has students teach most of class w/presentations.
This Professor is obsoluterly awful. She does not know what she is talking about, she is biased and simply annnoying. Her test are IMPOSSIBLE
She doesn't teach to tests at all, going to class is worthless but she requires it. If you like teaching yourself, then take this course.

Her excitement in class is just a facade because she is not a nice person outside of class.  Purposely likes to make things more difficult and not at all understanding.  Told one girl that "It's not the end of the world" when she couldn't graduate 'cause U-S wouldn't give her a C in the class

Her tests are hard, which knocked me off at first, but she hung in there with me and helped me improve. You definitely gotta go to class - she counts attendance and tests on discussions. But she is a dynamic, smart, funny, and fun prof. No doubt. I took psych because I needed to fill a requirement, but she made me care about the material.

by far the BEST professor i've had at UNC so far.  makes class really interesting and is always excited about what she's teaching.  take this class if you have a chance but make sure you study because the class isn't a breeze.
Awesome professor -- inspiring, enthusiastic, extremely intelligent, and respectful.
Best class I've taken in Psych. She is smart, funny, and really cares about the topic and how it will affect our lives. Also spent lots of time counseling me about grad school choices.
I loved Dr. Ulku-Steiner! She was sooo enthusiastic, it was inspiring. Her class was challenging but not intimidating.

I've had her for two classes and would take ANYTHING she teaches. The most enthusiastic and caring professor I've had at Carolina. Varies presentations every day, brings in all kinds of speakers and extra materials, takes the time to get to know students out of class. Excellent prof.
Very demanding and you ABSOLUTELY must attend.

Material is very interesting and she is an awesome professor.  tests are hard and you really have to study, but its worth it. NOT an easy A, but if you are really interested there is no one better for this class
Not clear at all with instructions! Tests are tricky!
Her Engl105 is focused around environmental studies, which usually bores me to death, but she kept things interesting. If you're a competent writer you'll be absolutely find with her.

Krysten was awesome. Her class is environmentally focused, which is not usually something I would enjoy focusing on, but she ran it so well that I ended up liking it a lot. She encourages discussions/debate in class (especially materialism vs. idealism). If you are a reasonably strong writer, you will have zero issues and appreciate the discussions

She was great, very approachable, an excellent choice for ENGL105. The class will be environmentally focused, even if you're taking a specific concentration of the class like humanities. I found her grading to be very lenient, everything I turned in was an easy A.

Krysten is such a unique and interesting professor to have. She really just cares about you becoming a better writer, without making you jump through hoops. She is very clear on what she is looking for and will let you resubmit papers for a regrade if you are not happy. I think most people in this class will end with an A.

I loved Krysten and I'm not even an English person in general. She's funny, I will say her classes are pretty much lectures but they're very engaging and she's super understanding about missing class.

She is great. She's super down-to-earth, gives no tests, and pretty much grades all projections/essays on completion(I ended with a 100.0), as long as you put effort and follow her instructions. She focuses a lot on plants from various perspectives to teach class, so if you find that boring, she may not be for you, but definitely extremely easy A.
Krysten is great, really funny and passionate about plants. Super chill with grading, and I'm really grateful she was my ENGL 105 professor!!

Given that you put effort into assignments, it is very likely that you will end the class with a 100. This is one of the best professors you can take for ENGL105, and she is very caring to her students. There is an attendance/participation grade, but she is very lenient with grading it.

I loved this class, and the teacher was very passionate, making each class interesting! There was a lot of writing, but she graded easily and helped whenever needed. I love her, she is hilarious, definitely take her class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Hilarious

reviews.comment: She is literally amazing! She is super into plants and coloniality so be prepared to talk about that for the entire class. She is very kind with her grading and attendance policy as well. I was really glad to have her as my ENGL105 teacher!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Easy A, just go to class and write the papers and you'll get a 100, definitely sounds easier than what I've heard from friends about other professors.
Easiest A ever. She is also very kind and understanding. She gets that we're just there to fulfill the requirement. I didn't go to half the classes... She is really cool definitely take this class!
She's great, easy A for 105
She is a really nice professor, and grades the assignments very easily. I've only not gotten a 100 0nce.

Great teacher. Gives in depth feedback and cares about your success. There are a lot of readings but she doesn't expect you to comprehend all of them in depth. Moderately easy assignments and opportunities for regrade and revisions on papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Krysten is a great english teacher. You have 3 main units; the first two are essays and the final one was a group podcast. As long as you revise your work and keep improving, you will get an A in this class. Definitely try to take it

Krysten is such a chill professor that balances her class better than I've seen any other professor thus far. I came out of her class feeling like I learned a lot but also never felt overwhelmed. Do whatever you can to take this class, you will not regret it.

Prof Voelkner has been my favorite instructor thus far at UNC. Her course material is SO engaging and interesting. She is super chill and I always looked forward to attending her class. She is also super accessible outside of class and understanding of personal conflicts. Take her for 105 if you have the chance!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Krysten is a really great instructor for regular 105. You don't follow the normal 105 structure, so you're able to write about things that actually interest you. I highly recommend signing up for her section of 105. There are some extra readings as well, but you can just look up summaries online.

Krysten was so accommodating and genuinely cares about her students. There were 2 projects: 1 literary analysis and another which you could choose between a creative/art project and an autoethnography

I was automatically put into her class for the required freshman English. Very easy. Had three papers over the semester, no final exam. Most everybody got 100s on all of the assignments. She is very nice and cool. A little boring during class but I am not a fan of English at all. Good choice, easy A, and some interesting topics.

I LOVED this class. I took this class my freshman year, terrified because there was a lot of upperclassmen but the professor was very welcoming and the class environment was definitely stress free. The readings aren't hard, the class definitely helps explore oneself. I would take this class again without a doubt.

krysten is so nice, understanding, & very passionate about what she does . The topics she chooses for us to right about were very niche and weren't always the most interesting which made them kinda hard plus she did grade a bit harshly. she lets you resubmit but i resubmitted using her comments and didnt improve a ton. solid pick for 105 though

Loved her class. Fully conversation based and you only have 2 papers and a final presentation based on the last paper. She cares about her students and the material is also super interesting. She also lets you re-submit the midterm paper if you want a better grade. Super cool, definitely recommend

Great choice for ENGL105! She has 3 units, with each unit having 1-5 page papers due at the end of them. She's a very lenient grader and doesn't expect too much out of you. She's also super personable and understands if you need extensions or anything like that. If you need to take ENGL105, she's a very good choice for an easy A.

Professor Voelkner was so kind and caring! She was always available for questions outside of class and gave great feedback. She was willing to understand our situations, which was really helpful in an online class. While I did not enjoy waking up for class at 8 a.m., this class was pretty manageable and helpful as an intro to writing assignments.

Krysten is really chill and nice and a good teacher. We had mandatory zoom once a week and could keep our cameras off. There are weekly writing assignments and a presentation at the end. Sometimes it was stressful but other times easy.

Voelkner is kind and funny and is a lenient grader. She wants you to do well so she gives good feedback but isn't too harsh when grading papers. This class was three papers (one of which required a visual presentation and 3 minute speech) and the final was just a portfolio highlighting these papers. Loved having her class!

This class is a hidden gem. Dr. Vyas is kind, understanding, and a lenient grader. His lectures are engaging and clear, and readings are always interesting and relevant. Highly recommend taking this class to fulfill gen ed requirements while learning about one of the most interesting figures in history.

Prof. Vyas is a really cool guy overall. His lectures are interesting and it's clear that he is very knowledgable about the subjects. I took this class for an FC and it actually expanded my POV on a subject I wouldn't have otherwise studies. Prof. Vyas is great and this class is not stressful, a nice break from harder classes. 100% take again.

He is one of my favorite professors I've ever had! He's a super kind person and very clearly extremely knowledgeable on what he is teaching, and passionate about it. However, he still gives students ample time to discuss topics on their own, which is probably my favorite aspect of the class. His class Reli 388  isn't very work heavy either!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Honestly an amazing professor. One in class test that is graded well and showcases what one truly took from the class material. He is extremely accessible outside of class and so caring. Truly knows the content and welcomes differing ideas and opinions. I recommend taking his course(s) and if I can, I will again.
Very intelligent on subject, lectures were interesting and assignments were engaging and very do-able
He's a very kind and compassionate professor allowing us student to make mistakes and is very lenient on grades

Professor Vyas is a great teacher who has helped me understand all of the content. He grades very fairly, is very kind, and is easy to talk to even if you don't need to talk about the class, and just life in general.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Respected

reviews.comment: Great class! Very supportive and engaging class. He is very flexible and understanding!

If you are interested in learning more about Hinduism and Hindus as a diaspora I recommend RELI 281. We learned many interesting things about their history/religion/culture and how communities adapt to new settings. Prof. Maharshi is very nice, a fair grader, and all you need to do is read the material and participate to earn a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: M. Vyas is a great professor! Super engaging during office hours and cares about his students ability to succeed. Had a small class cohort this semester but he's looking for new students to join and I would def encourage you to do so! His RELI 388 class has FC Global/Ethics and there's only one SHORT midterm exam. The rest is fun projects, etc.

wonderful lectures and knows the material quite well. A very nice and genuinely understanding person outside the classroom. Had daily in class quizzes that were usually easy if you pay enough attention. Loved the detailed feedback on assignments. Could provide more time for discussion during the class in a structured way.
Nice guy but couldn't really understand him half the time, I feel like his grading practices were also flawed and unreasonable, would not recommend this class for a GenEd, it's not worth the headache
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Very kind and passionate about what he was teaching. Only in person exam was the midterm besides daily quiz and the rest of grades were essays. Only complaint is you need a 95 to receive an A which can be very hard with the midterm being somewhat difficult. Overall great professor and would take another one of his courses.
Very kind and funny, listens to class feedback well, and flexible. A little bit of a slow lecturer but good overall.

If you're thinking of taking STOR 120 over STOR 155, I would take 155 instead if you have little to no coding experience. Weekly labs and homeworks take about 2-3 hrs each. His lectures consist of him doing the code and you copying it down but fairly quick. He is a nice guy but overall goes quickly and lots of homework.
Professor Pipiras is a very impressive man with plenty of knowledge and accompanying wit. The class is difficult, but doable. You get out what you put in.

You had to calculate your grade yourself, which isn't ideal, but overall the professor is nice, and he helps a a lot.
This class, however. It's hard if you have little to no coding experience.  Stor 155 was better

Professor Pipiras was great. Although teaching seems very fast paced content coverage was excellent.
If you do put time in you will definitely get an A . Extremely easy tests and if the entire class is not doing good in it he reduces 0.5 points instead of 1 point for every wrong question. Very easy going grader .
Recommended for everyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This is a good class. It is a little difficult for those without much coding experience. However, the professor makes it easy to learn and as long as you are being diligent and learning, it's great. Grading is pretty chill and a lot of boosts come in later on. Prof. Pipiras is decently lenient on grading tests which helps a lot.

Lots of homework and lab assignments. Test are pretty difficult and require a lot of studying. I mostly taught myself everything in the course and went to the bare minimum amount of lectures required. If you have the option to take Stor 155 like if you are a premed definitly choose that.
Do not take this class, take 155 such a big mistake

Professor Pipiras is excellent and easy to communicate with! Sets clear grading criteria, has well-prepared documents, and gives moderately hard midterms. STOR 120 is not a very challenging class and you get what you pay for.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Pipiras is very kind and understanding. He uploads a lot of useful material on Canvas for students to use. The class is well-planned.

Vladas seems to know what he is talking about but he doesn't have a great teaching skills; not engaging or friendly AT ALL at office hours. Gives zero help before midterms, he just tells you to reread everything you did up until the test and I had no idea what to expect going into exams. He goes fast in lectures. Don't take this as an 8am class!!!

So he is a good person overall but moves fast in lectures. I took this class with zero coding ability so there is a learning curve. The start is so easy and I had an A but all of a sudden that tanked with a plummeting homework average and a 63.5 on an in class midterm. All I can say is study the homework and labs, you're going to need it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Start of class is easy but if you fall behind it's hard to catch up. Exams have in class and take home portion. Lectures are boring and sometimes confusing but is a nice person overall.

Vladas was a decent professor. I found his lectures hard to follow at times, but he did upload all of his notes to Sakai as well as the TA's own personal notes. The homeworks were difficult and time-consuming, but it was easy to get help on them. Exams were fairly basic in comparison and required very little computations. Good choice if taking 556.

Dr. Pipiras is an outstanding professor. Lectures include many examples, which is helpful. Lots of homework but they are very helpful in understanding the material. He is entertaining and the exams are easy. Probability is difficult but Dr. Pipiras does all he can to make it not so bad. Strongly recommend.

Truly one of the best professors I've had. He does give a lot of homework and it's a hard class, but he genuinely tries to make it as easy as possible for students while making sure we are still learning. The exams are just like the HW. He interacts with the class during lecture a lot so its engaging, he's funny, and very approachable. Great prof

An efficient lecturer with an almost postmodernist taste of humor. The clearly defined grading scale, the unchanging format of scantron exams and quizzes, paired with a rigorous schedule with everything planed left no surprise. A solid choice of 435 for the studious, as all were too predictable.

STOR 435 is hard class no matter who you take it with. That being said, Pipiras goes through lecture problems very quickly and can be difficult to follow. Exams consist of problems straight from homework and lecture, but study well in advance since there is a lot to review. His class is tough but he grades fairly. I definitely learned a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: We had homework every class, quizzes every week, and lectures were definitely quick and required you to pay close attention and take careful notes. If you're not afraid to stop him to ask clarification questions and put time into understanding the homeworks, the class & exams are straightforward. He's also SO funny.

STOR 435 is a hard class, so be prepared for that when you sign up with Pipiras. Nonethess, I personally think he does a great job. There are homeworks due every class that make sure that you keep up to date with what he's teaching. He also gives quizzes so there are lots of grades and not just midterms.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Pipiras is an entertaining lecturer. His tests are reasonable, they are a combination of lecture and homework problems. You will definitely want to take notes for every class and re-read the example from class as they are also in the book. I recommend reviewing the notes from each class before doing the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Not a good lecturer at all. He mostly faces the board, and goes really fast. Homework is worth a lot and graded for accuracy, so make sure you're getting all of those problems right. The tests are based off old exams and the homeworks, but are generally still really difficult.
DO NOT TAKE THIS MAN FOR STOR435. JUST DON'T DO IT YOU WILL HAVE TO LEARN EVERYTHING ON YOUR OWN AND HE GIVES A HOMEWORK DUE EVERY CLASS PERIOD. He cares not at all about teaching this class

I could never recommend this professor.
