His lectures are uninspired and quite frankly a waste of time, his homework assignments are extremely inflexible (especially to those who have work hours), and he gives quizzes on material irrelevant to anything we've done in class.  He rarely answers class questions and also curves downward.

Don't take this guy. He doesn't care about teaching and he'll basically blow through class with his powerpoint. He asks hard questions in class and doesn't give you time to read the question. He does the problems correctly so write everything down and learn it later, at least that's how I did. midterms aren't bad, but try to not take this guy

Lectures were not very helpful. Had to google most things for my homework, didn't buy the textbook nor did I need it. Doesn't take attendance so don't need to go to class. Not a stimulating class, not an easy class. He's a cool guy, but not a good professor

Tests are very tricky.  I thought I did really well on the final until I saw I got a C because he recycles old midterm problems, but slightly changes the wording so don't expect it to be the same answer. My advice would be to write out all of your homework and save it when studying for tests. He replaced our lowest midterm with our final exam grade

Overcomplicates all of the topics, going to class hurts more than it helps. He burns through the material, and the review sessions and practice midterms had nothing to do with the actual test. Gives lots of notes and examples in class, but uses totally different ones on the homework. Would not recommend
A very good professor. He cares about the students, he is fair, he presents the material in a clear way. Absolutely recommended!

Take it with some one else. He is a nice guy, but over-complicates topics that should be easy to understand. Awful at explaining the material. If you don't have an innate knack for stats, this class will make your situation even worse.
Very difficult class.  Didn't help that he burned through the material.  Nice guy though.  Knew what he was doing.

He goes through the material very quickly. Class was relatively pointless except to turn in homework (which is graded!) Review sessions were pointless, and the previous exams he posts are nothing like the exams he gave my class. He is a nice enough guy, but you have to ask specific questions if you expect any help from him.

He's a really nice, generous and helpful guy. Makes the occasional joke in class. Goes through material somewhat quickly and isn't always clear in answering questions. Review session before final hurt more than it helped. Overall a good class and a great guy.
Most examples are from text. Test questions based on homework and notes. Review midterms before final.

Prof Wiener is very focused on readings and not so much lectures. She wants you to work with others as much as possible. Almost no homework or tests--you're "graded" on your final portfolio. This class could've been an email.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very sweet/caring professor. You can skim readings. As a first year seminar, this is many students' first anthropology class so at first it seems she believes that she's "always right", but she really intends to challenge the way you think. Particular about grading, but learn her language, ask questions, participate, and you'll do really well.

Take this class if you're ready to read a lot and discuss readings with groups. Grades are extremely harsh and hypocritical. You try and do one thing and she says it isn't fine, then you do what she says to do, and she says that isn't fine either. Wouldn't take this class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Assigns multiple readings due at the start of each class. It was so much reading that after the first week, no students did it. We did group discussions on the reading and then she would lecture and it was so boring. The entire semester you work on steps to your final research paper and she grades each of them HARSHLY. Take a different FYS.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment:
Miserable. Grading criteria unclear, when she doesn't like your stuff she will let you know in the most rude and condescending way ever. 
Avoid this class at all costs. also it's boring

She's very nice & understanding. I got sick and couldn't get a university-approved absence,  but she totally came through for me and sent me the work & didn't count the attendance against me. There are a lot of pre-class readings.
She's very knowledgeable in her field, but she is a little strange (isn't everyone in the anth department though?)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I hesitated to take this professor because of the reviews calling her arrogant and entitled. However, I found that these comments couldn't be any farther from the truth. She is one of the most insightful people I've met. She is educated and passionate about her field and it shows. I've never felt more inspired and excited for my future! So thankful
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Be forewarned that she is very nit-picky with her grading-- even if you send it to the writing center or use Grammarly you can count on her to find an error. Her comments are passive aggressive, a bit demoralizing, and often left me feeling discouraged. Wouldn't recommend for a first-year seminar.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is a nice and polite lady. However, she is a VERY strict grader, especially considering this is a first-year/entry-level course. This class is very heavy on reading; you will have at least 20 pages of reading to do before each class. The lecture material itself does provide a unique perspective on dogs around the world.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She feels she is always right. Loves to assign long text. Your work is ever good enough to her.

Dr. Wiener assigns tons of reading, and will grade your writing by challenging you to think deeper about topics. As long as you think deeply and express those thoughts, she will appreciate your work. She cares very, very deeply about her students and wants them to succeed. Her greatest aim is to see you grow as a student and anthropologist.

SOOO MUCH READING AND WRITING. The class is self-graded she says until the end because she doesn't think you deserve the grade you think you do. Is extremely rude in her portfolio edits and emails. Also very passive aggressive. Expects way to much from her students in a 200 level course, probably one of the hardest ANTH courses in the department
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This professor is extremely discouraging and I lost some of the passion and interest I had in anthropology. If you don't agree with her on something, she won't really hear your side (she is always right). She came across as arrogant, and some of her comments were pretty degrading. AVOID, there are many other amazing anth profs!

Classes were primarily discussions about the texts, which could be extremely tough to get through. She did not show very much genuine care for the well-being of her students - on days that the university cancelled classes for mental health, she still gave assignments and even suggested we still have class. It's also true she can be condescending.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her assignment feedback was great, but at times condescending. She leaves so much feedback (literal essay PARAGRAPHS) to the point that you'll question whether or not you even understood the assignment. FYI: She HATES the passive voice and will dock off points for the smallest things...I've never been more thankful for an A- in my entire life!!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: At times, Professor Wiener comes off as condescending if you don't think on the same wavelength as her, especially in terms of dissecting the heavy readings. You aren't graded on a lot and she tends to be a harsh grader for the papers. It is clear that she cares about the subject a lot, but she may come off as brash.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: A lot of conversation in class. The required text was challenging at times, ultimately excellent. Given the nature of the course there is no For Dummies option. In hindsight, its the best elective class that I took at UNC. Very reasonable and talented professor.

Overall, the class (Canine Cultures) was interesting, but frustrating at times. She knows what she's talking about, so if you don't, her feedback is condescending. Very vague paper guidelines, and then she'll mark you off for being too vague in return. She gives A LOT of feedback almost to the point where it's unhelpful. Very specific on grammar.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Almost 100% discussion based. Almost no assignments besides readings (some of which are torture to get through). 70% of your grade is based off of two essays, each of which have extremely vague prompts. She's a stickler for grammar and seems to think her opinion is the only valid one. Says she grades based on how she feels "your presence" in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The class is almost completely discussion based, which is good as long as you actually do the readings and can contribute to conversation. Your grade is mainly based off the midterm and final, both of which are finals. She is a pretty tough grader when it comes to the papers, but she gives lots of good feedback. The class was fun and interesting!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This professor knows her stuff, but be prepared to work harder than ever. She is exacting and very particular regarding papers she assigns. Her edits are so extensive that you will wonder if she even thought you understood the assignment, and that is for an A paper! However, I learned more from her than from any other prof at UNC.
She requires a massive amount of reading that I assume most people did not bother with.  She is a stickler for grammar on the four papers.  No final exam though!

Interesting subject for ANTH or INTS majors.  Must read, go to class, and pay attention.  Essay topics are vague, but if you are interested in anthropology it they are not difficult to write, just make sure they are analysis based.

I would not recommend this class to anyone. Not only is it boring and completely unorganized, she is unable to communicate her thoughts effectively. This is my biggest complaint. The class is based on four essays. Each essay prompt is more vague then the next. You don't know what it is that she wants. HORRIBLE! DO NOT TAKE CLASSES WITH HER!

Her section of Introduction to International Studies was blatantly anti-American and anti-capitalism.  On our final exam, we basically had to describe for two hours why the United States was the cause of all the world's problems.
Don't bother- no matter how hard you try, it won't be right (i.e. HER opinion)
good class, good professor, tests were fair and so were essays
Attendance isn't mandatory but such an easy class if you go. 6 participation in class writing assignments, a midterm, final, and a few essays. She's very understanding, highly recommend.

She was very sweet and very passionate about Pompeii. Very easy tests and assignments, just make sure to put some effort into the 2 essays. Almost completely homework free, and prioritizes your learning over your grade. Unexpectedly interesting, easy, and professor Valladares is awesome. I would recommend this class to anyone
Dr. Valladares is well established in this field and if you have any interest in Pompeii or the Roman Empire, you should take this class! It's an easy gen ed, but lectures can be pretty boring.
took as a gen ed and learned a lot! definitely take if you are interested in Pompeii/Rome. lectures are long but it's a T/Th class so it's to be expected

No required attendance in lecture unless you are worried about missing the notes. She is knowledgeable about her field and is an amazing class if you are interested in classics. As a non-history major got kinda boring. Easy grades, graded by a few in class writings, 2 papers, a midterm and a final. Midterm and final are nothing to stress over.

I loved this class. It was so incredibly chill; they just want you to learn. They send all test material out beforehand. Valladares was so kind. Her lectures could be a little boring, but it wasn't her fault; it's just that it was a Tu/Th class, and it loses your attention at some point. Overall, would definitely recommend for an easy gen ed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Rarely showed up, attendance not mandatory and really not necessary. Exams were super easy and lenient grader. 2 papers, midterm, final, in class assignments (completion grade). Easy double gen ed class if you can put in just a bit of work.

Super easy class, lectures are long and dull but 90% of the information in the lecture is in the Cengage textbook. Attendance non-mandatory and I didn't feel like I missed anything when I skipped. Exams are easy and study materials include everything covered. Professor is knowledgeable but seems (unintentionally) condescending at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Valladares is incredibly knowledgable and know A LOT about antiquity. Some people had a hard time with the exams, but overall I thought the class was pretty interesting and easy. She really cares about her students, however the lectures can be a bit boring at times.

I'm honestly surprised by some of the lower ratings here! Yes she is lecture heavy, however she is one of the most knowledgeable people in the world when it comes to anything antiquity. She's also super caring and considerate. I've taken two classes with her now, and she has personal connections with her students and knows the answer to everything.

Loved this class! Prof Valladares is so nice and her lectures were amazing and fascinating. Our museum based projects were interesting and also relatively simple. For both the midterm and final she posted all of the information we would need to study beforehand. Definitely take this class if you like Pompeii or Roman history in general!!

Professor Valladares is so sweet and knowledgeable! She is also very flexible and adapted the course in light of a difficult start to the semester. I would 100% take one of her classes again! Just make sure to go to lectures because even though they are not required, you will miss out on a lot of information that the slides alone don't cover.

Professor Valladares was a great professor! She is extremely caring and gives clear instructions for any assignments we have. Quizes are counted for participation and she prepares you for midterm and final beforehand. Lectures can sometime be boring but other than that it was a great class!!

Great lecturer and super interesting. This class was very easy, there were two museum papers and quizzes that counted only for participating, and then a midterm and a final. If you look over the material from class, you will be totally fine for the exams. She emphasizes learning over stressing about grades and the TAs were super easy graders.

Professor Valladares is a wonderful professor. I've taken 2 of her classes. Her lectures are very interesting. She makes the exams super easy and just wants you to understand the material rather than stress for exams. I love Professor Valladares and would recommend her to anybody especially if you're interested in archaeology and classics.
Outstanding classics professor! Engaging lectures, deep knowledge, and passionate about the subject. Highly recommended for any classics enthusiast.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: DO NOT take this class unless you are at the bottom of the bucket. Not only is this teacher extremely boring, but you will fall asleep and lose track of everything very quickly, especially because there is no supplemental material to refer back to! Also, she only speaks subjectively (her opinions) and uses no words on powerpoint slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Valladares was awesome! We had 3 papers and two presentations (the final one was a group project and she deleted the third paper from the syllabus) and she was very understanding the whole semester with all the students. She was very encouraging and lovely to work with. I highly recommend her class, specifically the CLAR/ARTH465!

I learned a lot from this class. Prof and TAs are sweet. But the exams are really hard and tricky. She went through lectures so fast. You rarely have enough time to write things down. And the little details that you missed could potentially be on the exams. I learned a lot but the exams are unnecessarily tricky.

Tests and quizzes were really specific and tricky; even with a lot of notes and constant referencing to the textbook and preparation you can easily get a B+ if you make a few mistakes (or if you're tricked by the wording). Lectures are really dry and ponderous and she does not release the recordings unless you make a request with a valid reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It depends all on her exams. They're typically open note online, and she gives you a study guide for them, so if you fill that out, you can typically get a b plus on exams- don't expect more.I honestly wouldn't recommend- the dual gen eds are not worth the work- take drama and an easy history instead- you'll thank yourself. LECTURES ARE SO BORING.
I found the class to be organizationally a bit messy. There didn't seem to be really any professor-student interaction and the lectures came off as incredibly boring.

If you do the readings and pay attention, the class is really interesting and makes sense. It is pretty slow paced, and we didn't make it through all the material, but I really feel like I learned something from the class. Just be prepared, the tests and quizzes are hard.

All I have to say is to be ready. I don't understand why we have to fill out an form to request recorded lectures that should be available freely. During lectures they are so boring and dry, all we do is look at pictures and listen to her talk. Also, the exams are very challenging and tricky.

I could not imagine taking her in-person. I took this asynch S22. Exams are basically verbatim tiny details she mentions in passing in lectures. I'm lucky we had recorded lectures so I could pause and take notes on everything. It was easy to get an A in the class because of this, but it took up so much time and I couldn't have done it in-person.

She seems nice, but she moves incredibly fast and her lectures make little to know sense. Exams are only trick questions and very challenging. She also only lectures for all of class and doesn't put any information on the slides so if you miss one thing she says you are in trouble... and she talks really fast. Don't take Clar 247.

Had I known what this class would entail I never would have taken it. Your entire grade relies on two midterms and a final. Furthermore, Prof. V began to remove student's access to helpful study material (lecture videos) midway through the semester. Grading also takes a really long time, so I never really knew where I stood in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I love Professor Valadares as a person and think she was a great professor, I just think that I was misled by the course pre-requisites. It was really hard to participate in the class because there were grad students that did it for a living and had studied for years and classics students, where I was neither. Definitely did not know enough mythol-

Professor Valladares was really nice and knew her stuff. Her lectures were interesting but it was just a sold hour and 15 minutes of her talking. Sometimes we would have 3 lectures a week to watch and it's only supposed to be 2 and that was annoying, but I think that was just because we were online. Overall I would take another class with her.

The class itself was easy, interesting, and I learned a lot, the TAs were great, weekly quizzes were 4 questions and super easy, exams were take home and open note, one essay that was fun and simple. Her lectures always went wayyyy over time, though, which was annoying and a bit inconsiderate. She could be pretty condescending to students, too.

Best professor at UNC! She is so kind and really wants you to pass. All of her exams are open note and the TA's will give you the benefit of the doubt always because they are just as kind as her. Not only that but the whole thing is asynchronous and being able to watch all of the lectures at my own pace helped me learn the material so much better!

The class itself was easy and I liked the content. The class is asych but scheduled for 9 am and 50 minutes long, but she would post lectures at 1 pm and they would be 60 - 90 minutes long, which was very annoying. There are quizzes after every lecture (very easy), final and midterm are take home and open notes.

Would highly recommend Herica. CLAR 380 is about Pompeii, so the course itself is interesting. Very easy class, just watch the asynchronous lectures 2x a week and attend recitation and you'll get an A. I never even bought the textbooks and I got an A. 1 "paper" and 2 exams, both take-home. Sweet lady, little work, easy A, cool topic. Worth it!

Shes a great professor and this is an amazing class. Her lectures were all asynchronous and we had weekly quizzes and writing assignments but they were all fun and easy. She assigns a lot of reading but covers it all in her lectures so just watch those and youll be good. Midterm and final exams were take home. I would highly recommend this class.

Took this class for gen ed's but also ended up learning a lot about life in Pompeii. Many assignments and quizzes but they were REALLY short so were easy and didn't take that long. Lectures tended to be long but I think that's because Professor Valladares loves the topic. Take even if you have nothing to do with classics/archaeology.

Professor Valladares is an amazing lecturer and I absolutely loved the course she taught on life in ancient Pompeii! The lectures were fascinating and we had fun--and very short--writing assignments! I highly recommend taking a class with Professor Valladares!

CLAR 200 wasn't really my cup of tea, but Valladares was nice enough and the class was pretty easy. I didn't try too hard at it and that reflected in my final grade, but it's a solid class to fulfill a few gen ed's. Attendance and readings are not really mandatory, you can just google the answers to the pop quizzes, quiz gets posted before lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: A good lecturer, and seemed really nice. This class had a lot of contact with the TAs, who were super chill. The class/lectures themselves were a bit disorganized, but the class wasn't really anything to sweat.

Professor Valladres has been one of the best professors I have had at UNC. She doesn't so much care about grades but only that we are growing as learners. Her lectures are interesting and the assignments aren't too difficult but require you to do a little bit of research and use your thinking skills. Ultimately learned a lot from her.

10/10 take this class! Dr. Valladares is so sweet and caring and a very easy grader. Class time is primarily a powerpoint lecture on a topic. Don't really have to show up or do the readings to get an A since short, easy essays make up most of the grade. My final average was a 100! She offers extra credit opportunities too. WB and BN credits!

Professor Valladares is absolutely wonderful. Her lectures are very informative and interesting and she is a very lenient grader. She is also a very sweet woman, which only adds to how great of a teacher she is.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: I took Hellenistic Art and Archaeology with Professor Valladares. The class itself was fantastic and Professor Valladares did an amazing job making the class interesting and thought provoking through her lectures. Definitely would recommend to anyone who is interested in art history or Greek art.

Herica is such an amazing woman. She really cares about getting to know her students and figuring out what we are passionate about. She's somewhat disorganized, but owns up to it and then makes the class easier for the students because she feels bad. I highly recommend getting to know her if you're interested in Classics or Art History.

Herica really cares about her students and she herself interesting. The lectures are kind of dry, but look engaged and you'll be fine. It's a small class and she will care if you miss a bunch. There are readings for every class, but I stopped doing them and it was fine. Short reflection essays and in-class essays, but I never got below a 90.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Herica was a great professor. Honestly the topic of the class is kind of dry, but she was able to make it more interesting because of her personal connection to the class and her history with the topic. There are several short essays and a couple of decent essays to write in this class, but it is totally worth your time!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Life in Ancient Pompeii: interesting to some; boring to others.  Regardless, Valladares is one of the best people to learn about it from as she is very knowledgeable.  The course isn't hard and she is a very easy grader (I got a 90 and above on every assignment).  Put in a decent amount of effort on the assignments and you'll get an A.

She is a nice person, but takes the class too seriously. Lots of homework and lots of essays, she is a hard grader. She does help and point you in the right direction, but save yourself the time and take a different teacher for ENGL-105, a lot of easier teachers out there.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class definitely had a lot more work than some of my other friends with English 105 teachers that grade easier, but Professor Watlington tells you exactly what you need to get a good grade for each assignment and it's not too hard to get an A. She's very kind and creates a good vibe in the classroom. Good teacher!

Professor Watlington is very caring and the units of the class are interesting and give students room to explore their fields/interests. Her grading can be a little tough, but I still definitely recommend her.
I was actually in ENG 205 but option wasn't there. Save yourself and do not take her. She is a tough grader. She seems excited about teaching but she also seems to be on a power trip
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I enjoyed this freshman english class. She gives clear instruction/rubric and feedback that makes it easy to correct things and improve grades. There are also extra credit opportunities. I would recommend!!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Watlington is a tough, but fair grader who sets clear expectations about what she wants her students to accomplish. She's very organized and if you put in the effort, an A or A- is certainly obtainable. Nice lady.

Watlington graded tough but fair. Her feedback was very constructive and her rubrics were extremely clear making it easy to get good grades. She is passionate and knowledgeable about the subject matter and challenges you to become a better writer in a caring way and is accessible outside of class. I would recommend her for ENGL 105.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I went into the class comparing how hard the grading scale was compared to other asynchronous ENG105 classes. Watlington is a harsh but generous grader. Definitely had to utilize my writing skills and work hard to get an A, but there are opportunities to meet with her and gain extra credit. Getting to know her also allowed me to do better in class.

This class was taken asynchronously during summer. Professor Watlington gives great feedback. There is extra credit and points for participation. Compared to other friends that were in a different section of English 105 my class was harder but, this class made me a better writer and researcher.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Watlington was a good professor. I wish the topics we picked were different, and Art museum visits not required, but overall a good professor who gives good feedback and understands what ENGL 105 is supposed to be. I would recommend taking her class, she fosters a great environment.
She's not bad. The topics she chose for our units though were bad. They were to complicated and excessive and overall didn't really make me a better writer.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Although this professor has wonderful research, his teaching style was inadequate for the average graduate student. It was very hard for both PhD students and MPH students to understand the professor. This was NOT an intro class; it was more rigorous than that. Be prepared like your life depends on it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is not an intro to epidemiology; it is a PhD-level course, and it's taught like a philosophy class. It is very hard to understand. Personally, I think it should be an elective and what MPH students take for the intro to epidemiology.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: he teaches a graduate level class, and does an amazing job at it. love the subject, and love the class.

Mr. McCance is a nice guy- but if you want to learn stats, I would suggest taking a different professor. He uses the chalkboard- often with illegible writing. His lectures are not well planned, often reads slides off his phone. I basically taught myself the entire course. Exams curved 20-30% because so many people fail. UNC stop making TA's teach.
McCance is really nice, but at the end of the day his lectures are very difficult to follow.

This guy did not show up for the last two weeks of classes. Took forever to grade midterms. KhanAcademy might be your best friend if you end up taking a course with him since you have to teach yourself a lot.

Easy class if you have previous experience with stats, but lectures were extremely boring and hard to pay attention to. Exams were medium difficulty but get insanely curved, so its hard to get a bad grade in this class. Also takes forever to grade exams. Only allowed to miss 2 classes before attendance deduction. Prof is funny sometimes though.

Kind and caring professor outside of class. Accessible for office hours, but the lectures were very boring and hard to follow. Basically taught all of stats to myself using the textbook. Very disorganized professor and takes forever to grade. However, the curve is generous, and he is accommodating.

Canceled classes the last weeks of the semester, gave us our midterm back days before the exam. Notes were all over the place and he would sometimes get his own problems wrong when writing them down. The homework was inconsistent and I had to teach myself most of the material in the class. He does heavily curve the exams though.

McCance is probably one of the easiest professors to take STOR 155 with. He starts with the basics. We only had 7 homework assignments which take about an hour. He does take a while to return the midterms but curves them a lot. The exams are fair and he allows cheat sheets, so you can write all the equations and steps down.

McCance was very nice and tried his best to be helpful. Overall, the class was challenging and I had a hard time following lectures. I had to learn a lot on my own and the midterms were kind of unreasonable and took a long time to grade (but he didn't have TAs), but they were curved a lot, which made this class worth it.

Very nice guy and cares about his students, but his lectures were pretty disorganized and confusing. Also took ages to grade our midterms. However, you do get cheat sheets and curves for the exams, which made it fine, but I didn't really learn statistics.

Not the best teacher but i only attended like 4 lectures. Exams are difficult but curve is INSANE taught myself the whole course because hes lowk a bad teacher but super kind and cares a lot about his students. Gives great accommodations lectures put me to sleep though lol
Very little homework, easy exams with heavy curves, allows cheat sheets for exams. You don't learn a ton but can achieve an A with very minimal effort.

He is very nice, but very disorganized and unresponsive to emails. He hardly posts materials/hw for review and lectures were very confusing. He curved the tests a lot, which made the class worth it tbh. Don't take this class if you actually need/want to learn stats. Not having taken AP STATS made me struggle more than others lol

took forever on grading midterms. made office hours at 7pm to find out our midterm grades and didn't show. he barely posts study material for the midterms. lectures are terrible and he says intuitively a lot lol. he never answers emails even though he says to email him. he cancels class a lot (says he's sick tbf). this class made me WANT to do hw

barely homework, and tests aren't impossible, but he doesn't show up (idk how else to say it) for the last two weeks of school he cancelled basically every class because he was sick to be fair but he didn't even hold zoom or offer alternative ways to learn the material. He doesn't answer emails and is inconsistent w being present at office hours
Very unorganized and hard to follow. Lectures are super boring, he just reads off the text book the entire time. He lost my exam I took in October and still hasn't graded it almost 2 months later.

Very unorganized. As of May 12th at 9:48 p.m. (graduation was two days ago), our grades still haven't been posted. Be prepared to deal with this during the whole semester. He quite literally took 1 month to give us our first midterm grade, which was about a week after the last day to withdraw.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's super unorganized and hard to get a hold of because he doesn't answer emails. Simply a bad teacher but luckily he curved the tests a lot because we all did badly. The lectures were boring and he explained every topic poorly.

Nice guy, horrible lectures, curves a lot. Terrible attendance policy, which is why I have a B+ and not an A. Also takes FOREVER to grade. Took him 1 month to grade midterm 1 and 3 weeks for midterm 2. Took even longer for him to give us our curved grades back. I wish UNC would stop making grad students teach because they're just not good at it

Lectures were awfully boring and I hated how he used the chalkboard instead of slides because it was super unorganized & confusing. Attendance was required but I never paid attention and just read the textbook sections. Midterm 2 was crazy difficult but he curved it a lot. My score went from a 52 to 92. Cheat sheets allowed and each midterm was 20%
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: lectures the entire time, everyone falls asleep. teaches on a chalk board with his own page of notes. taught myself the entire course from youtube. second midterm was extremely hard for no reason. Nice guy tho, cares for his students. But course was harder than it needed to be.

CHEM 101 is standardized but Werley does a good job of getting through the topics.  She is very concise, gets the point across, and consistent every lecture. She was very engaging for an 8 am class and would start the morning with a cat picture or a meme. Sit in the front where you can ask questions during practice problems.

Even though I am having to retake CHEM 101, that is not a reflection of Professor Werley. She is incredibly encouraging and kind. I constantly find myself remembering things she said during lecture that are finally clicking now. Professor Werley truly cares about her students, and I am very grateful to have had her as a professor.
Enthusiastic about teaching, GPSS is a great resource for chem students

Very chill and engaging professor, sometimes would go too in depth and would miss the rest of the lecture leading us to get behind a little bit. Stay on top of studying they are not joking with the 3 hours a day to study.
Werley is a very engaging professor, especially for an 8am class. as long as you put extra effort you'll probably do better than i did

Surprisingly somewhat engaging as an 8 AM lecture professor. This is Chem 101, so expect lots of studying outside of class and treat the lectures more like a review session of concepts you might've not understand from the readings and smartwork.

no matter what Chem101 class you take they are all the same. Werley was more on track with lesson plans, but she often rushed through it. If this is your first time taking chem ever (i never took chem in hs ) UNC chem is really hard.... I got weeded out! Read, go to tutoring, dont cheat on smartworks. The actual exam is 2x harder than the practice.

chemistry is a difficult class in general, especially if u didn't take AP Chem in HS (like I did). she's an okay professor, the 6 min meetings r lowk stupid imo since you can't discuss much during that tine, but she is very sweet and knows her stuff. I barely passed the class but put the time and effort in and it'll pay off

Managed to enjoy 8am chem after being convinced chemistry wasn't real in HS. Loved the consistency of the lectures. Super standardized course, but after Zurcher subbed I was grateful for Werley's lecture style! Would def take with them again and I learned a lot :)
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Werley is clear and her lectures provide really useful content to know what to study for tests. She has the perfect balance of asking students questions and talking, creating an engaging environment. The readings can be tiring, but if you stick with them and the homework, you should be successful!

Chem 101 is a weed out at UNC, so no matter the professor, the class is hard and takes a lot of work and studying outside of class time for you to do well. However, I found Prof. Werley to be a lot more engaging than the others. The one time Zurcher had subbed for Werley, I found the lecture extremely boring and just unengaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It isn't the professor that is hard, but rather the content and class itself. A fast paced class, and heavy on content. Tests are extremely challenging, and weigh heavy into your grade. It is nice to have a recitation to talk things through. Professor was easily accessible and willing to meet outside of class time to go over study habits, etc.

Like someone else said, Chem101 is a mandatory prereq so every lecture is probs the same, but I think Prof. Werley is pretty chill and detailed for a MWF 8am lecture. I like the memes they choose for Monday because the corniness wakes me up lowkey. They also actually care to answer questions in deatil

Chem 101 is a standardized course, so it doesn't matter which professor you take, but Werley is pretty good. In her lectures, she often goes into detail and asks for questions from people. Chem 101 is a hard course - I recommend finding another student who has already taken the course and asking for advice on studying, you're going to need it.

she was a really good prof. this is a hard class but she made the lectures useful and worth going to. if there's logistic issues with the class, she's not incharge of it since its a common course. she's really as good as a chem 101 prof can be

not the most friendly professor but they are very good at explaining and i actually learned a lot in lecture despite it being a very fast-paced class. chem 101 is difficult and standardized so it really does not matter who you take it with.

Since all chem 101 tests and content are standardized, it doesn't really matter who your professor is as long as they're not absolutely horrible. I would say Professor Werley is decent, not the most engaging lecturer but not super boring or anything either.
I mean chem 101 is a hard class, especially since it's a weed out. Werley wasn't exceptional, but there are definitely worse professors for this class.

Werley is extremely sweet and makes the most out of this team taught class.CHEM 101 is a flipped classroom, so the clarity, consistency, and reliability that Werley brings to lecture is amazing. Sit in the front rows. CHEM 101 is cutthroat b/c there is no exam drops, but exams are genuinely straightforward. Great class, contrary to popular belief!

Bryn Werley is a new teacher, but she was good nonetheless. She is extremely thorough with the lectures and oftentimes did not get through all of the material intended for the given day. The tests were extremely fair and overall it was a good class.

The professor was new and was not the best at explaining concepts, often leaving students confused. As a new professor, she wasn't the best at managing her time and pacing herself. She often didn't finish the day's lesson and would carry it over to the next class, which was inconvenient. Also, she was passive aggressive towards students.

This class is difficult and a weed out, but it is doable if you stay on top of it. She was not bad for a first-year professor, but she was not great at explaining the material and moved quickly. She is also disrespectful of the students at times, which I did not appreciate. Outside help is definitely helpful if you want to do well in the class.

The exams are quite challenging and make up a large percentage of your grade. Make sure to do all other work to help your grade. They are a good lecturer but can be short if people are talking or not listening. For a first-time teacher, they were impressive. The class is often called a weeder class and is definitely challenging.

ENGL 259 is an improvisation class that fulfills my GE requirement and the screenwriting track. The class is fun and low-pressure. We practice improv in class and write weekly journals. There is no midterm or final. We have two formal theatre performances, and you can learn a lot from performing in public and developing comedy-writing skills.

He's so caring about us as people and our growth. Accessible outside class. He will push you HARD but it's worth it. Be ready for a lot of work, but know it's not pointless and all very thoughtfully designed. Great guy willing to go to bat for anyone, and well respected

Prof White takes your work very seriously and expects that you will too, but if you work with him your writing WILL improve a great deal. This class was a LOT of work but it hardly felt like work, it was all edifying and will stretch you in the best way. If you're willing to put in the effort to learn and grow, Prof White is a fabulous instructor.

Prof. White was a difficult professor, but if you are serious about poetry, he makes your writing GOOD, really makes you think more broadly than you might have coming out of an intro/intermediate classes. He is almost clairvoyant when he prescribes you individual readings, and he will make your poetry better with his challenges.

The workload is hefty, but it never feels like busywork. Prof White makes it clear that he cares about you as an individual and your personal artistic growth. His feedback is sooo helpful (def go to his office hours!) and he has definitely helped me to become a better poet! I would 1000% take a class with him again, and you should too!

The most fun course (because of the freedom in creativity and comradery amongst students) at UNC which students dont know about. Make sure your sketches conform to the prescribed grammar if you want their likelihood of being selected for the final script.  Just have fun and a blast! I promise you that you will never regret taking this course.

Had Ross for Gramorama. Really likeable guy and the class was probably the best class I've taken at UNC. Was sometimes frustrating when he would force a sketch to conform to a sketch's grammar rules in place of coherence or comedy, but overall he did a pretty good job leading us through the bizarre concept of a grammar sketch comedy class. 4.3/5.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He made every class as entertaining and open as possible, he is really funny and laid back. Although, the class is operated entirely out of Dropbox, and assignment instructions and turn in policies can get confusing. He is nit picky with feedback on weekly poems, but you get a 100 in the grade book just for trying.

It's very clear that Professor White deeply cares both for his craft and his students. He was always willing to communicate and work with me when I was facing some difficulties that semester, and he was very encouraging which was valuable as a beginner in poetry. Assigned readings were mostly engaging, though we didn't always get to them in class.

Don't take his class expecting a light workload-- you will write and read a LOT of poems. I enjoyed the assignments, however, and I can see a marked difference in my poem quality before and after this course. Professor White's lectures were very illuminating and had directly applicable advice for becoming a better writer.

ENGL 351 has a good concept and is so useful.Ross himself is not. He has unclear guidelines and rubrics, unclear feedback (if any), and a snarky and backhanded way of speaking to students in the discord. Ross acts like he wants his students to succeed and then boohoos when we don't but won't change a single dynamic of the course or his behavior.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Ross White is hilarious so lectures are never dull but he does expect everybody to be there on time to participate in in-class collaboration. It can be intimidating getting that much feedback on your original work but the environment he creates among the students is right for it and the structure of the course overall makes sense and is well done.

Ross has been one of my favorite professors at UNC so far. Attendance and participation are mandatory and I found his grading of our annotations to be strict but justified. His lectures were very engaging and you are given a lot of creative liberty.

IF YOU'RE SIMPLY A WRITER LOOKING FOR SOMETHING  DIFFERENT, TAKE 384! This class seems like a burden at first but is actually enjoyable once you make the podcasts. Make a few friends in class, workshop with the prof, do the assignments (the non-podcasts stuff weighs more than the episodes), and you'll get an A. He's meticulous but amazing!
Ross is a caring professor and genuinely wants his students to succeed. There are a lot of small graded assignments for this course.
Prof. White is so funny, so caring and his lectures are chock full of material that he teaches in a relatable way. He truly cares for his students and wants them to succeed.

Ross White is my least favorite professor. His grading was so unclear and he could never justify why I received such a low grade. I get that poetry is subjecting, but I don't think you should get a bad grade just because the professor "doesn't like it." 0/10 do not recommend this professor for anyone. He's also just rude.

I think it's strange to see Ross have negative reviews, but I realize they probably just come from people who took a class with him as a "gimme" which, although he teaches several niche classes, is not the attitude to approach with. Ross is easy going, flexible with due dates, but VERY good at his craft and expects students to care like we should.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Group projects

reviews.comment: This class was quite a burden yet I'd still take it again. It was a LOT of tedious work, but I learned a lot abt a niche topic w/ an amazing prof. He's strict about deadlines & details, but tried to cultivate a friendly atmosphere in class. He lectured me for not asking for help sooner (in a kind way). Genuinely wants students to succeed. Cool dude

Ross is great. I have had him for three different courses now at UNC. He is a tough grader, he assigns a lot of work, but he is aware of that and will tell you upright that you will need to work for a good grade. The pay-off is absolutely worth it, and he is one of UNC's finest.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor White has been amazing, and his Podcasting course has been one of my favorite professors. He is one of those professors that just makes you care about doing well, not because you have too but because you want to succeed and make something you care about. I highly suggest taking this course with Professor White.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Do not recommend taking a class with him; he is the one of the worst professors Ive ever had. He is rude, condescending, and unhelpful. His grading is very arbitrary, as well as incredibly harsh for an introduction class.
Loved the class. Professor White is very easy to talk to and very understanding.

My writing skills before and after this class are like night and day. Prof White gave detailed, honest feedback that genuinely helped me grow as a writer. There were a lot of assignments so be prepared to dedicate time to this class, but all of them felt valuable and like the time was well spent. Not necessarily an easy A, but was so worth it!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ross is a great guy. Sometimes I get frustrated with the use of class time (it's not very efficient and we often get behind) but I'd be lying if I didn't say it was my favorite class. It's so much fun, definitely engaging, and you feel like you're on SNL. There's an assignment due each class, but writing sketch comedy doesn't really feel like work.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Doubt I'd ever take a class with him again. I thought his curriculum was over-demanding for a 100-level class. Considering that this class is essentially an elective, he needs to be more realistic about how much time we can put into it. Know also that he can be very rude; I would describe him with one word hidden in this review.

Avoid this professor at all costs. Assignments were poorly described and harshly graded with no rubric, the final project was graded based on how much money a student spent on making it (and it cost me $150 when he said it would cost $20 at most), and the attendance policy is ridiculous. Prof refuses to have a Sakai and used Dropbox
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I expected to like this class way more than I did. Professor White can come across as pretentious and a lot of the speakers were disengaging. The class required way more work than anyone expected - the final project was incredibly time consuming. He is a critical grader for a 100 level class so a lot of effort is required to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: i loved professor white and this class - one of my favorites at unc so far!! he makes class really interesting, and though its a bit more work, as long as you do what you need to do and participate in class then you should get a good grade.

I was excited to take the class to learn more about the book publishing world as a possible career, and I am disappointed to say that his condescending and judgmental attitude toward my peers and about the industry in general discouraged me from pursuing this field. Professor White is an intelligent man, but I would not recommend taking this class.

Professor White seems like a great guy on the first day but he can actually be quite rude and condescending to students over time. Additionally, the monotony of the outside speakers coupled with the tediousness of assignments is not appropriate for a 100 level English course. It dissuaded many students from joining the book publishing world.

Professor White is great. He's funny, caring, and deeply passionate about poetry. There are a few deadlines to keep track of in this course including biweekly annotation papers and poems, weekly prompts, daily readings, and pre-workshop comments, but all of the work is engaging and doable. A worthwhile course for beginner poets and experts alike.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Ross is a super cool and funny guy. Always willing to help you and is super approachable. Enjoyed his class a lot and it covered a lot of different things that I never thought I would learn. Material isn't too hard but he does give a lot of small to medium size assignments. Definitely worth taking any class you can with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Nice, but he kind of acts like your weird uncle who wants to be cool with the kids. Spends the whole class time on discussions about minutia that doesn't matter like "Is an e-book a book?". I dropped the class because I realized I was wasting my time and wasn't going to learn anything. Don't take if you dislike corny jokes.

There is far too much to say in the word limit but Prof White was fantastic. His class is easy but you learn so much from it and he's really accessible outside of class. You can come into office hours to ask about anything, even if it's not about class, or even just to talk.

Prof. White is awesome, his class is fun, and Id recommend his class to anyone. Hes hilarious in general, and helps you develop in your own style as a poet with detailed feedback while pushing you to write outside of your comfort zone. He really cares about all his students and is more than willing to help you out in office hours as well.

Ross rocks. He's got a self-deprecating humor that makes him approachable, but also explains things clearly and is very passionate about his subject matter. He assigns a good deal of work, but he's always eager to help when you need it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Awesome dude, awesome class
Awesome professor. He is passionate and also hilarious. If you put some effort into the class and show improvement, it's an easy A.
White is pretty cool. He's laid back and very relatable. He grades paper toughly, because he expects you to write eloquently.

Professor Wu was fantastic, engaging, & informative. I learned a lot, and would absolutely take another course with him. There were only about 3 assignments total, and the semester focused on building final projects, making the end manageable. He cares deeply about his students and creates a collaborative environment. Highly recommend INLS 382!

I learned a lot and really want to take time the amount of effort Professor Wu took to make sure his students learned the topics in the most meaningful way. Always went above and beyond and really a gem of the INLS department!

Danny is such a caring professor. The course is graded based on three short homework assignments and a multiple-choice final, for which he provides the correct answers beforehand so students can study.

Dr. Liu is a GREAT prof. He rescheduled two exams to fit classes needs, includes extra credit, and has great lectures. He is hilarious, and very good at explaining concepts. Highly recommend taking. If you pay attention, you will get an A.

Professor Liu is very caring and understanding. I struggled a bit for the exams but if you show up to class, pay attention, and start studying early you'll be fine. 
His lectures are great and really clear, and you can tell he cares about the subject and the class. Great professor, choose him!

Excellent professor. He explains things so well and he is very patient with his students. He is willing to repeat his explanations until everyone gets it. The only complaint I have is that he didn't let us struggle through the examples in class enough.

Dr. Liu is a very great lecturer who explains thing pretty well. His midterms and individual part for the final exam are easy. The common part of final exam is kinda challenging... but Dr. Liu's easy individual part really makes up for my bad grade in the common part. He is very accessible and really cares for the students. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!!!
GOAT, choose him
iconic guy. loved xinyun and his class. enthusiastic and caring

Amazing professor who does not rush through certain difficult topics of DE and actually spent time on the non-covered pre-requisite topics. Homework and test are pretty much identical---just go to lectures and write down notes and you will basically be guaranteed an A. Great professor overall and wish him the best! ^_^

Good choice for 383. Explains computational strategies well but theory isn't as good. Tests generally reflected homework and review assignments well with some challenging theory questiosn thrown in. Recommend taking 347 before or with this class.

Dr. Liu is a very understanding professor, and I really enjoyed his class. It wasn't my main focus this semester because I was also taking organic chemistry, but it had a manageable workload and the content on tests was extremely fair. He is an engaging lecturer and really wants his students to succeed!

Material was not overly difficult and his lectures were very clear and organized. He cares about how students are doing in class and will continue to help until you fully understand the material. Liu was an incredibly nice teacher and I would absolutely take him for another class again.
Great professor. He is very excited about the material and makes sure that everyone understands.
Great Guy. Easy A

Xinyun was a good professor. He was always accessible outside of class and was always willing to help you understand the content better. The exams were more than fair difficulty and the homeworks were at a good difficulty to understand the content better. Sometimes, he inserts an unexpected joke that always lands. Overall, highly recommend.

Professor Liu was great. I loved watching him get progressively covered in chalk throughout the lectures. 

Seriously though, Professor Liu is a great guy and his lectures cover enough content so reading the textbook is unnecessary. My only note is that there can sometimes be a slight language barrier when asking questions.

Xinyun is a good time! Never read the textbook and was able to get all necessary content from lecture which typically ended early for time to ask questions about HW (or eat lunch early lol). He's funny in class and cares a lot. I can't recommend him more.
She's just professional and cares about students. She made things more flexible for students even during a hard time. I got more feedback than I expected as a junior. I will say take her class again!

She's the nicest professor I've ever met at UNC! She hopes students can learn from the course and makes the course as easy as possible. The topic is interesting and we have lots of case study about different worldwide cities, such as Chicago, Beijing, etc. She is very reachable after class. I will definitely take her class again.

She cared about her students and was very enthusiastic about teaching. Attendance was not taken and the class was graded by 7 short open-note quizzes, a presentation, two papers, and a final. All were very easy.
She's very kind and sweet, and always willing to help her students with anything.

She was always available to help and had the best, most welcoming attitude. She tried to make learning the material fun and enjoyable, and I believe she succeeded. One of the best professors I have ever had. She cares so much about her students and her field.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: It was clear that he had not taught for long, as he struggled a lot early on. His teaching got better over time, and he has office hours sections where he will sit and explain material to you. The first midterm was incredibly easy. The second midterm was a lot harder, but still chill if you study hard. Final is demonic, but he curves accordingly.

Tiger is a really funny and patient professor! He is very approachable and wants all students to do well in his class, but sometimes his explanations were hard to follow. Reading the textbook is optional, but I would highly recommend reading it + doing the practice problems if you want to do well in the class!

I left this class most days understanding the material! He starts with easier content and then builds on it so we have the foundation to understand harder concepts. Some proofs can be a little abstract, but lots of practice can help you be prepared for tests. His study guides were helpful but looking up other practices can be helpful.

Office hours and in-class questions were available and very helpful. The second midterm and final were more challenging than the first test, but he curved generously at the end. The textbook aligns well with the course material and is a useful reference

At the begining of this class he did not really know how to teach well, but as the class went on he got better. There are 3 exams, homework due usually every Wednesday and a final. On exam 2 and exam 3  we got opportunities for extra credit which are the harder exams that really helped my grade. If you pay attention to lectures you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Terrible teacher don't take if u want to learn

50 min mandatory lectures twice a week, but are incredibly simple and not helpful for homework or tests. Unreasonable grading of labs, and no communication with TAs on how to actually support us in labs. Don't reach out over email and expect a helpful or caring answer. The class is fine if you know what you are doing, the professors are lacking.

I LOVE JENNIFER WEINBERG-WOLF. When she started talking about shooting neutrons into an apple, I was inspired. She completely changed my perspective on life. Imagine shopping in a grocery store... LOOKING for the perfect apple to shoot a neutron into, ultimately turning it into a Hulk Apple.

She is a nice person, but this is a hard class to take as an introduction to physics, especially for people like me who aren't physics majors. The class requires a lot of time outside of class to understand the concepts and examples in order to answer the questions the way she intended them to be answered on exams.

Physics 119 is obviously an extremely difficult course, but Dr. W does her best to alleviate this pain. She is consistently available outside of lecture, provides clear testing expectations, hosts review sessions, and reaches out to congratulate individuals who improve throughout the semester. Since this class is probably a requirement, good luck!

Difficult course to take, especially if this is your first physics course ever. A lot homework and every lab you have to complete on your own time. Very slide heavy for the lectures, but some very cool in class demonstrations. She does give lots of partial credit on exams and gives lots of preparation materials which makes it manageable.

Although Dr. W was not my main professor for this class, she gave very useful feedback during our one-on-one post-midterm 1, and it helped me improve my test score greatly. This class is extremely tough, but it is clear Dr. W wants to help you succeed.

This class is difficult for a physics course for non-STEM majors. I wouldn't recommend taking it to fill a FC unless you have some physics background. Dr. W is very accessible and does a great job explaining material in lectures and office hours. Lots of textbook readings, assignments, and labs graded on accuracy.

This was the hardest and worst class I've ever taken. It took over my life the entire semester and ruined my GPA and my mental health. Every time I tried to communicate with Dr. W she was so passive-aggressive and rude. My final grade was 0.3 points away from a B- and she refused to round up and was straight up mean when I emailed her about it.

Only take this class if you can spend all your time focused on it. The number of assignments is absurd (51 in gradescope), and there is lots of required reading. The tests are almost impossible to complete in the allotted time. With that said, Dr. W is very nice, but there is so much material the lectures tend to scratch the surface of the topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class caused me so much stress. As someone who has taken physics classes, this was the biggest mistake of my life and ruined my gpa and mental health. I am having nightmares about the clock I had to build. As someone who works hard to maintain his stem GPA do not take this class RUN AWAY. this is not worth it at all take something else.

I think Dr.W is very nice but I hated this class so much so I highly recommend dropping it! It was interesting for a bit but really not worth all of the assignments and labs that occur outside of class. She would give us equations without teaching us how to use them. I don't think you should take this class for a FC credit; don't tank that GPA.

nightmare class, no correlation between content in class, exam practice and exams. I'm convinced she doesn't write them. Effort will not translate to grade purely because the class is so disjointed. INSNAE amount of work - don't do it.

I have nothing against Weinberg-Wolf. She isn't the main lecturer as there are 2 for the class, but her office hours are helpful for specific problems. For learning concepts, studios/labs are best for that as she doesn't explain the complex concepts very easily. If you put in the hours to practice problems and study, you'll be fine.

I have nothing against Weingberg-Wolf. She is cheerful about the class, but she does not actually teach the lectures very often. She is helpful during office hours for specific questions, but not much for learning the concepts in my opinion (TA's and Studio is better for that). The class is very hard, but it clicks if you put the time into it.

Dr.W is literally born to be a professor. She is incredibly caring and wants you to succeed, the content is very difficult but she is so so willing to work with you and help you. For the content of the course Dr.W made this class the absolute best it possibly could. She constantly asks for feedback and again she is super willing to work with you
I think she might be evil.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU ARE A NON-PHYSICS MAJOR AND JUST NEED AN IDEA CREDIT. I wish I would've listened to the 1 star reviews. Insane amount of work, exams are unnecessarily hard, labs are stupid, and lectures only scratch the service level of understanding. Spare yourself unless you want your semester to revolve around an INTRO LEVEL CLASS!!

I took this course with absolutely no physics background and was quickly humbled by it. Dr. W seems like a great person, and she definitely does care, but just be prepared for the heavy workload and difficult exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: If you want to take this class solely to fulfill the FC-Create requirement, please reconsider. There's an ungodly amount of homework & labs. There's interesting demonstrations during lecture but the focus on concepts for exams was considerably less, attending SI session and doing lots of extra studying is really the only way to get by on the exams.

PHYS 100 was the worst mistake of my life. It says it's designed for non-physics majors, but it is extremely difficult and time-consuming. It may be 4 credits but it takes up much more time than that. Labs are difficult without clear instructions, and midterms are very hard and graded strictly. She is disingenuous and doesn't care about students.

Writing this while studying for the third midterm. For the love of god, don't take this  class. This is the most needlessly difficult class I've taken at UNC and even though I underloaded, this class took up basically all my time. So many homework, labs, and impossible exams.

Please spare yourself from this class if you can. Took this class to cover a focus capacity and have regretted it ever since. Lots of assignments, often due at once, midterms vary greatly from homework and lecture material, and Canvas page is a labyrinth to coordinate in addition to Gradescope which, for labs, contains few instructions.

Please, please, please, never take PHYS-100 with this professor if you're not planning on being a physics major. It was advertised as a class that required no prior knowledge and DESIGNED for non-physics majors. Worst mistake I've ever made. I should have dropped the class when I had a chance. This course will consume your life. Tests are awful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The workload is reasonable and the lectures are interesting. But please, make sure you submit your homework properly on Gradescope. You will NOT get any of those points back, so DON'T MAKE THE SAME MISTAKE AS ME! I definitly lost a good chunk of my grade from that. Otherwise, study hard and you should do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Genuinely please never take this class. I took it to cover one of my focus capacities and it WAS THE WORST MISTAKE I've ever made. It's not worth it. The midterms are so confusing with barely time, theres like a million assignments every week and don't even get me started on lab 3... Don't take this expecting an easy intro physics class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
Amazing professor, especially when she teaches it with another professor (Dr. Branca). Test-reviews often weren't helpful, but the lectures were very relevant and is generally a good professor.
This is just a difficult class with so much to learn, but she will do everything to help you succeed.

Literally do not take this class if you are trying to get ur create credit or anything, it may say meant for non physics majors but this was a pain and I would pay to have never taken this class. Would not recommend to anyone, egregious workload and midterms graded very harshly

I would never recommend anyone to take her PHYS 100. She makes the lectures very easy and the practice exams. She then makes the exams so hard. I was in a tutoring session and a graduate level TA said he did not know how to solve one of our problems. This class requires no baseline knowledge by the way. I would never ever ever take this class.
She is a great professor, but it takes a great studio group and a ton of work to get a good grade. Tests were fair, but studio assignments were just as hard

Dr. W seems nice, but a lot of it seems really disingeniuous. She talks about how "we don't want to trick you" and gives some of the hardest exams known to man (the 2nd midterm with a 55 average, the final). Warmup, HW and long studio assignment for every module will really drain the life out of you. Take during the summer if you can.

Dr. W is an amazing professor who genuinely cares about her students. The class was very difficult -- lots of group work in studios, multiple homeworks due each week, several lab reports, confusing topics, and three midterms. However, Dr. W provided lots of resources to succeed. Go to office hours and pay attention in studio and you'll be fine!
The course is hard but there are so many resources available to succeed. Dr. W is a very likable person and taught her portion well.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: You work more with TAs than Dr.W, but she is still there if you need help. Course is challenging, but you CAN do well with some effort. Performed 7 labs, wrote 6 lab reports, did 3 presentations (one being the final), along with small hw assignments. Extra Credit available for all labs. Start lab calculations and report writing ahead of time.

She is super nice and understanding! There is a lot of homework for this class as well as three midterms, a semester long project, and 6 at home lab assignments. The class was fun and interesting. She replaced our lowest midterm grade with your final grade. Just go to class and make sure to study. Lots of math!!

PHYS 119 is probably the hardest class I will take at UNC. Although the actual concepts aren't too difficult, the way they ask will be extraordinarily difficult, in a way different than other subjects including math and stats. If you actually want a good grade, prepare for this class to become your life and something you study daily.

Physics 119 is very hard and math heavy and it's very helpful to already have taken calc 3 before. Dr. Weinberg-Wolf is amazing and wants you to succeed and is very encouraging, and makes sure your grade is not only reflective of your performance on tests.

pretty fair professor. Follows the syllabus, if you miss a deadline for some things makeups may not be accepted. Class itself is challenging but if you're good at math it shouldn't be too hard. Midterms are tough, especially the third one. Equation sheet is your friend, make sure to use it. Homeworks aren't very hard, but the studio's a pain.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She actually WANTS you to succeed. Midterms were difficult but fair, and not worth that much. The final was pretty easy compared to the midterms.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. W is incredible. It's apparent that she cares for her students and tries her best to help them succeed. This class was possibly the hardest class I've taken here at UNC, but she makes the class as manageable as possible.

Felt like she wanted us to succeed compared to 118 instructors. Fair tests especially including the take-home portion. Will be hard but Dr. W is very good. I didn't do the readings but focused energy into homework, review sessions, and practice exams and did well on tests. space out learning each module at a time. would not recommend cramming here

Dr. W is a very caring professor, she really wants her students to do well, even though the material is difficult. I took this class as more of STEM person and it was definitely more conceptual than I expected. I notice physics in real life all the time now, so if you want to feel smarter than your peers and challenge yourself, take this course.

Informative lectures with cool demos. Great teacher who is passionate about physics. Also very nice. Medium workload - 20ish min guided readings for almost every lecture + occasional hw and take-home lab. MakerSpace training! I did well in physics in high school and found the class easy. Tests were not hard, difficulty came from time constraint.

This class is the hardest thing I have done at unc, the homeworks take all weekend and feel almost impossible, the exams throw things that are hard to comprehend in a short time; if you take this class, your entire life will be physics. However, Dr. W is super caring and really wants you to suceed, she and the TA's are the only positive.

Dr.W does a great job administering a hard course! Her and the instructional team are really fair in my opinion. They provide all the resources and more to succeed. It is up to you to take advantage and stay on top. Don't underestimate the calculus pre and co-reqs.

Knowledgeable teacher but a lot of work. If you are taking this class for the fc create credit I am sure you could find other options because I really do not think this is worth it just for that credit. This class makes you do more work than other courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: PHYS 100 has a LOT of work, but it prepares you for the lectures. Dr. W fairly understanding about struggles to meet deadlines for labs, and if things become too much, you can always talk to her and she will help you work out a solution. This class has very little math, being made for non-STEM folks, and as long as you come to lecture, you're fine.

Dr. W is a great professor, and I'm glad I took physics 100 with her. That's saying a lot considering I broke my finger doing one of the labs (don't do labs when you're in a hurry). If you took physics in high school, you should find the workload very manageable. If not, it may be challenging. Dr. W is a great lecturer, and her tests are very fair.

Dr. W is one of the best professors I've had at UNC. In addition to being a great lecturer, she truly cares about her students and structures her class to help you as much as possible. The Phys 119 material is really tough, but you can still do well if you put in the effort in studio and go to office hours
Extremely difficult course. Dr. W makes sure to explain concepts thoroughly. Very fair with partial credit.

This so-called "physics by firehose" class is extremely difficult, but Dr. W does a great job of enabling the success of her students. You probably won't enjoy the content at all, but you'll enjoy your professor.

Dr. W is a very caring professor and teaches a tough concept very well. She is very willing to answer questions both in and outside of class which is essential in such a difficult class. Don't be too discouraged by the low midterm grades, the studio section will help your grade.

Dr. W was honestly great and 119 covers some extremely interesting content. However, as so many others have said, this class is flat out ridiculous in terms of the amount of work required and the number of topics it covered. 

Summary, Dr. W fantastic, PHYS119 interesting but ludicrous.

Physics is going to be difficult no matter what, but Dr. W explains things well and is extremely responsive and accessible; she genuinely wants her students to succeed.
