There is an exorbitant amount of homework at times, but the expertTA questions come with an extremely lenient late penalty. Overall a very tough class but a very good professor.

If you have to take this class, take it with Dr. W!! One of the nicest profs at unc. She takes the time to learn everyone's name and check up on students throughout the semester. It's a notoriously hard class, but compared to other profs she seems invested in student success. Definitely study w/ practice problems and stay on top of deadlines.

Really wanted you to know the material and gave a lot of practice problems to that effect. While I think this course is pretty difficult (evidenced by my grade), I don't think it's necessarily a bad thing since I learned a lot. In general, 119 is more lenient than 118 (exams + studio are graded slightly easier, content is just harder)

PHYS 119 is already a tough class, but Dr. W (along with graduate student Tim Osborn) made it as doable as possible. There are a lot of assignments, but I think they actually help you learn the material. They also provide plenty of practice questions and materials to help you prepare for the exams. It's a difficult class but I got a lot out of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: PHYS119 is brutal with whatever professor you take, but Dr. W is one of the best in the physics department. She takes the time to learn students' names and meet with them 1-on-1. The course policies are also more lenient than 118 (take home midterm questions, studio extra credit). If you have to take this class, take it with her!!

This prof's absurd workload is like trying to slay a hydra: complete one assignment and two more take its place. Holding onto a B-, but it will surely drop. Five assignments (including two labs) to complete over Thanksgiving break. Eyes gloss over in lectures. Other grades suffer because of how much work it takes to stay afloat in this class.

Per the syllabus, we are expected to do 15-25 hours of work per week--for a single 4-credit-hour course. The others saying that this course eats up absurd amounts of time are right. She's also very condescending/passive-agr. Grades are very harsh (per bright friends who have taken it before).  There is a midterm on the first Friday of the semester.
Dr. W is a good professor. She will always reply to your emails, and she is caring. She grades exams fairly.

Hardest class I've ever taken but there are a lot of opportunities to bring your grade up, daily homework that is done for completion boosts grade a lot. I took it for an easy lab credit and it certainly was not easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: 119 is notoriously hard but Dr. W was always eager to help students succeed! She replied to emails quickly with thorough and helpful answers. You have to do the homework intensely and ensure that you understand why you are doing the math to succeed. There are 3 tests but the professors were very understanding this semester and gave us extra help.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. W is a fantastic professor to have. She is great and she cares about her students. There is a lot of work to do outside of class, but you can easily get help. There are three tests and a final - if you study the homeworks and the guided readings, you can do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This was a tough course for me and also my first physics class. Dr. W is a tough grader and there was always something due it felt like. Be prepared to spend most of your extra time on this classwork. Also, book the maker space ahead of time. You'll thank me later.

Class was really interesting and wasn't too too hard. The course long project was a challenge, but there is more than enough given to work on it. The homework is graded pretty hard, but will help you understand the material on the tests. Labs with groups were nice. And some really cool demos shown off. Overall a good class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. W was a great professor and always had lots of fun demos during class! There is a lot of homework and labs, but I think it's manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She makes class fun with demos, however I truly couldn't understand the concept of physics. I didn't feel as though I could ask her things because sometimes there would be a hint of condescension in her voice when answering other questions. She didn't give enough practice with the math part of it, so on the 3 midterms, I was totally lost.

You are graded on guided reading questions (graded on participation), accuracy graded homeworks, 6 at home labs, and 3 midterms (10% each), a cumulative final. If you pay attention and study you will be fine, and Dr. W is very accessible outside of class. Great because it is 4 credit hours and the labs are at home

She herself would be the most-fulfilling person throughout the semester. She was under the illusion that there were another 100 students equipped with a clearer vision to understand the world. However, the fact was that everyone was frustrated by the sisyphean assignments.

Dr. W. is a great teacher, but as a non STEM major this class was difficult for me. She tries her best and is genuinely so sweet but sometimes just moves a little fast and doesn't explain everything the best. She is super understanding and wants to see you do well. If you need a lab credit not a bad choice but it is far from an easy A

Had really high expectations and in the beginning, she posed it as a stress-free gen ed class. Despite this, she gives an absurd amount of homework and makes you attend every lecture which is painful. Felt like no matter what I did I had more work to do and this class took up so much. The final project is AWFUL and she is not accommodating.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Jennifer is very nice and understanding, this class is very base level and interesting

She is the best! I had PHYS 119 over the summer with Dr. W, and she did such a good job with that class. She explains material clearly, is available to answer questions, and always graded fairly. She really helped us succeed and learn the material, and was understanding during the pandemic. And her exams were fair. I really recommend her!

Was very difficult concepts, horrible to learn online. Tests were so hard, pretty much failed every one. Practicum never helped esp bc lab was online, didn't know anything. She's really nice but the class was just not organized well and that made it super difficult.

Dr. W was very kind and accommodating - esp with covid- but she also meant business. I always read the textbook, but even though phys100 is the easiest phys class, I was still confused. Most of the test/homework questions can be found on Quizlet, which makes it easy to study. Nice woman, but the class made everyday things more confusing
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Overall, I think this is a good course if you're looking to satisfy a PX credit. There are 3 midterms which are pretty difficult, but the final was really easy. Homeworks are graded tough by TA's, but your take-home Labs are nearly all 100s and can balance out the disparity. The professor is pretty nice and has good lectures.

I'm not gonna sugarcoat this. PHYS119 was one of the hardest classes that I've ever taken in my college career. I spent more than double the amount of time studying / doing homework for this class than any of the other classes I took this semester. My best advice is to study and work out practice problems in the textbook, that's how I survived.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very accommodating during COVID-19 pandemic. She is very passionate about teaching physics and is an understanding teacher. The concepts can be hard, but she will help you in any way she can to help you succeed. Highly recommend her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Really understanding about individual circumstances during the pandemic. Super engaging in lectures and interesting. Work isn't that hard - especially if you took high school physics - but can be really specific when grading. Labs, homework, and pre-class work can really add up and the midterms are definitely too long for the time allotted.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. W is not a bad professor, physics is just badly organized at UNC. They minimize student's confidence in themselves by giving unusually difficult midterms while only counting them for 9% of the course's overall grade. She's funny and clearly cares about her students and has been accommodating during this pandemic.
I love Dr. W. She is the best that UNC Physics department has to offer. She is extremely intelligent, super kind, and very engaging. Please try to get her as your professor at all costs!!!

Dr W is amazing. Let's state the obvious, PHYS 119 is brutal. Might as well get it done with someone who cares about what she teaches. If you show dedication, she will notice this and help you more. However, the grades are based on mastering of the material, so putting in effort is not enough (you also need to do well). I'd def recommend her.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: This professor made our physics class incredibly reasonable. E&M is a notoriously difficult class and the physics department at UNC is notoriously harsh on students. Dr. W is caring and an clear communicator of what is expected from students. Lectures were clear and informative. Tests are difficult but showing understanding guarantees partial cred.

Caring professor. Good, clear lectures. Extremely tough grader. Extremely hard tests. Do not take as a summer course, especially after taking phys 118 in the summer. You will burn out. Studio is okay, instructions often hard to follow. The TA's do not know what is going on. Got a B+ in 118 and p/f this course. My advice? Avoid this class.

Took this class during the summer session. Labs had little instruction and took all day to complete to only get 10 points off on little things. She gives us assignments saying they're 11 points, then makes them 40 points after they are due. Felt that she was trying so hard to make things as difficult as possible, and does the opposite of her words
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I honestly don't know how she has so many good reviews. Her actions don't reflect her words at all. They take off points on the smallest things. Many mistakes on answer keys. When asking questions, she rarely ever answers the question completely and simply only sets it up. The expectations are too high for the quality of teaching she gives.

Studio is a massive waste of time. TAs/Prof grade severely unfairly(3-4 pts for unit, or they bc don't like the format). Never answer questions, avoid giving a response or misdirect you. No chance to correct mistakes, because grades are not returned in time before 14 point heavy (NOT JOKING) assignments have been due.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She says she cares and understands, but her actions don' reflect it. Vague, ambiguous exam questions. They grade everything so hard. They have million and one mistakes in their documents, tests, practice problem answers, yet they take off so much points for missing units like one time. Take off points to just take off points. Really annoying class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. W is one of the best professors, if not the best, I've had at UNC. Even in the ever-worsening COVID-19 pandemic, she cares for all of us as if we were all on campus and she explains things very well. PHYS 119 is a notoriously difficult class with anyone, but 10/10 recommend

Dr. W. taught this class really well, going reasonably in-depth with a wide variety of topics while still keeping the class well-organized and engaging. She is very open to student feedback and makes a considerable effort to provide the best learning experience possible for all of her students despite the often challenging course material.
She is a very kind and approachable teacher who just happens to teach a very difficult class. She is a very solid pick for this class.

Dr. W is a very passionate teacher. Physics is a difficult subject, and she made most of the material understandable. Although this class was a bit harder than 118 (the tests are no joke), I did find everything to be more interesting to learn. Dr. W is a pretty safe bet when it comes to PHYS119. If you can, take it with her.

Dr. W is a very effective teacher. Even though we only had lecture twice a week, she communicated the content well through both the slides and her explanations. Physics is hard stuff, but she made many topics understandable and promptly answered email questions. The grading scale is also nice, as each midterm is only 9% of the grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. W was great. Good person, and just about everyone in the class loves her. Hard to disagree. This class is 10x better than 118, even though it is a little harder.

I can't say enough how much I love Dr. W! Phys 119 is hard, but she's taught the class for years and does an amazing job explaining really tough concepts. Grading is divided into many different areas, and even tests have multiple parts to help students who aren't good at testing. She's a professor who truly cares about her students, and it shows.

This class is "notoriously hard" as everyone else says, but Dr. W really cares about her students, like more so than I have seen in any other STEM class. This made me love the class even after failing the first midterm. There are so many resources to help you succeed, that I was at to get an A on the 2nd midterm. Great class, incredible professor.

You will go into a test feeling as prepared as you ever have. She will then grade the questions that are not specific enough harshly. Questions are harder than anything she goes over in class and seems impossible to prepare for.

To all the physics majors taking this class please do not feel let down by your performance thus far. I just graduated with a B.S in physics and I can say with 100% certainty that this is about as rough as it gets. This class is known for being notoriously difficult but if you really put forth the effort you will find success.

PHYS 119 is notoriously hard, and even harder during the summer. But Dr. W is a phenomenal physics instructor; the material is simply hard, she does not try to trick you. Despite the workload the class was very enjoyable. You will have to work hard for a good grade in this class - midterm averages tend to hover around 60 - but you will learn a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: the average score given by different sessions varies a lot and she didn't curve or balance even a little bit. so much work and terrible organization in studios which is actually a waste of time. the thing that is really useful is the optional homework, which will never be covered either in lectures or in studios. feel upset about this class
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Great prof, tough class
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: She is an incredibly caring professor. She wants to see students learn and improve, so there are opportunities to make up grades when the class does poorly. PHYS119 is a very hard and demanding course with a lot of outside work, but she lectures very well and is very accessible outside of class.

physics 119 is the hardest class you will ever take. don't take it unless you absolutely absolutely must! Dr W was a good lecturer and knew her stuff, but i took one point off because she expected a little too much from us. average midterm grades were 55, 75, 58 with no curve, and everyone in the class is a genius so getting average is tough

Dr. W is an amazing lecturer and genuinely cares about her students and wants you to succeed. The class is definitely up there with the hardest at UNC, but she provides opportunities for test corrections and extra credit that make it possible to survive.

119 is definitely a difficult class, however, Dr. W does a really good job of trying to make it the best experience it can be. There's a lot of work in the class and the material is difficult, but she's very organized and always willing to help.
119 itself is definitely difficult but Dr.W actively tries to make it as easy as possible. She really cares that you learn something. Also her office is filled with star trek stuff and memes.

The material in 119 is very difficult but Dr. W is a really good lecturer and has fair exams and gives extra credit opportunities to make up for exam grades. You are expected to read the textbook before class but she clarifies concepts in lecture. Overall its impossible to make 119 an easy class but Dr. W is an amazing professor

Dr. W is easily one of the best educators I've had the opportunity to learn from in my academic career. She is incredibly passionate, caring, and willing to help you learn in a way that suits your needs, on top of being astoundingly knowledgeable. You'll have to work for an A, but her class is well worth it.
Everything is extremely fair, give feedback real quick. I am not a math person, but I did better than I thought in this class. My favorite professor!
She is definitely the best professor I have ever met at Kenan Flagler! Would love to take her class again!

She's a really good prof, the material is fairly easy and up until the final its pretty fair. The final was painful also she puts in grades extremely fast (same day we took the final) the final was really hard so just prep for that. I did not hence the grade (had an A all sem)

Dr. Xu truly cares about her students! She teaches at a very fast pace so we always get out of class early. She's very eager to answer questions and make sure students are successful. She also is open to helping students in non-class related things

Professor Xu is a fun and engaging professor. Her class covers all the content you need to know and I felt I had everything I needed to thrive. Class consists of problem sets, 2 midterms, a final, and a group project. the final was the hardest part of the class, but overall, I enjoyed this course and would take Professor Xu again.

Great teacher that clearly cares about her students. Class was pretty straightforward until the final which felt like it was trying to hurt our grades. Dropped a fair amount of people a full letter grade. Just be well prepared for an entirely different final and you're good

I'm so glad I took this class with Professor Xu! I've learned so much over the semester. She's super smart, but what really stands out is how inspiring and encouraging she is. She has this amazing way of making you feel confident and excited to learn, which makes the class even better!
Professor Xu is fantastic! Explains concepts super clearly, is always accessible for questions, and has very fair exams! Genuinely the sweetest professor!
Easy to understand everything. Awesome class.
Great class, take it if you can!
I love this class!

Professor Xu is the best professor I have ever had at KFBS. Materials and exams are hard, but still manageable if you spend a reasonable amount of time studying. She even replied to my question at 1 am!!! Would take any other courses that Xu teaches at KFBS!

Class was extremely misleading. HWs and midterm was quite easy but for some reason, she decided to make the final very difficult with no practice material being nearly as rigorous as the final. Would recommend taking with another professor. There are definitely other sections that are much easier.

Final was brutal given that both midterms were easy and that problem sets were also easy. Xu is really sweet and is a lovely person, but the final really felt like she was out to get us/bring down the class average.
Final absolutely screwed me over by a whole letter grade. Lectures I will say were very understandable, but holy cow, brace yourself for the final to see things beyond the scope of this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Yuqian is a great teacher and person, but I disagree with other reviews. Class is extremely test-heavy and the final was surprisingly difficult compared to other exams and course sections. Final dropped my final grade 3 thirds of a letter grade.

Professor Xu is attentive to student's needs and is genuinely just such a sweet professor. She's very fair with midterms and really cares about the wellbeing of students. Please take her class, it is worth your time, and I wished I did more to connect with her.
Xu was probably the best teacher I've had at KFBS. Such a positive person who would always smile and answer any questions I had. PLEASE take her if you have a chance
unbelievably easy class. the content is literally for middle schoolers. Xu is nice and cares a lot about teaching but the fact the class content is so easy makes it hard to rate her low

Professor Xu is an outstanding professor at KFBS. She is clear about her expectations and what she wants you to do to succeed in this course. I learned a lot from this class and her. She is also very understanding and caring. She doesn't make you stay for an entire lecture if it's not necessary. Review all slides and homeworks before exams

Professor Xu definitely made this class very understandable and easy to succeed in. She is clearly very intelligent and has a very impressive background. Despite that, she is not arrogant or short with students but is always willing to answer questions and make the material as simple and applicable as possible. Definitely would recommend.
Super nice professor. Easy material and clear explanation. She even replied to my email within 1 minute at 1 AM.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Xiaoming is a kind professor who is very passionate about what she teaches. She is slightly disorganized, and slow with grading, but she makes it relatively easy for students to succeed. She doesn't take attendance, and it's not necessary to come to every class.
She is very passionate about the topics!
She is super passionate about the topic and willing to help you to understand it!

Xiaoming as a person is a really nice lady but as a teacher, leaves much to be desired. Attendance isn't mandatory so only about 40% of the class shows up on a regular basis. I attended every class but didn't get much out of it. I wondered "why am I here?" The slides are boring and can be accessed online. Not a terrible class but needs improvement.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Xiaoming Liu is a good professor. The class only consist only of three exams and attendance isn't mandatory. Make sure that if you aren't going to attend class you keep up with the powerpoints which are all uploaded. If you can't hold yourself accountable avoid this class.

I would steer away from taking a class with Xiaoming. Her class this semester was solely based on exams. There were no attendance checks, quizzes, or projects to motivate you throughout the semester. Many people did not show up to class and didn't do so great on exams because attendance is not checked.

Xiaoming was an excellent professor! The only grades were attendance (Poll Everywhere in class) and tests. She did a fantastic job making this class a really fun introduction to geology, and covered the entertaining topics like earthquakes and volcanoes heavily.

Xiaoming is extremely sweet and approachable. She understands that it is an intro level class that most people are taking for gen ed credit and even tells you that reading the textbook is not necessary. Her only grades are two midterms, the finals, and participation so it is essential you study for tests, but overall not a hard class.

Xiaoming is a sweetheart. She is really kind and you can tell she wants her students to understand and love geology the way that she does. With that being said, I found it difficult to pay attention in this class, for whatever reason. The material is not terribly difficult to understand, so take some notes and you should be fine.

Very structured and clear-cut class. Xiaoming is a wonderful person and she teaches the material very well. I'd highly recommend for students to take this class whether they are interested in geology or just trying to fulfill a Gen-Ed. Take caution though- you will have to study the lecture slides hard to get an A.
Extremely sweet and helpful woman! I took the class for the mandatory science credit and was dreading it and she has made the class enjoyable and bearable. Wonderful lady!

I really like her as a person, she was very approachable and you can tell she knows what she is talking about. However, lectures were pretty uninspiring and the tests were horrendously written. Good news is about half of the questions on her exams are free points, but the others were often very ambiguous and did not focus on core concepts.

Dr. Bustamante-Marin is a GENIUS in the field and is very knowledgeable. She's the sweetest person if you take the time to actually talk to her. That said, she is a tough grader with exams with tricky wording (which she will not give points back on), and omg the lectures are so fast with sometimes 100s of slides. you learn a lot! DONT CRAM!!

Though Dr. Marin may seem strict, she is genuinely really nice! Class content is difficult and requires a lot of memorization to be prepared on tests, so definitely do not study last min! But it is really interesting to learn if you are interested in nutrition. Her office hours were pretty helpful to go over exams or any content related questions!

unclear guest lectures. exams questions not released for review. course flow doesn't make sense. homework doesn't impact class grade. often quizzed before lecture on the topic. bar for an a is too high (94). overall her lectures were unclear. difficult to anticipate exam qs. she is somewhat nice but i wish she would've cared more.

Dr. Marin a little more on the serious side and she goes through slideshows fast. There's LOADS of information and cramming will not do you any good. BUT Dr. Marin DOES care about you. If you're not doing well, she will personally reach out to you to chat. She's understanding and wants you to do well. But don't take this class unless you need it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I think Professor Bustamante-Marin. While the class was difficult, it was not as bad as it sounds. If you make sure to review the lecture slides and take notes on the textbook, you should do fine on exams. This class is not as hard as others at UNC, but I would not recommend taking if not required for your major.

Dr. Marin is overhated. Just study the slides thoroughly and they align pretty well with the exams, tho some questions on the exams were pretty tricky + I didn't find the textbook to really be of use. Dr. Marin was very helpful and accessible to me in and out of class and really did want the best for me. She comes off blunt but is truly caring

Horrible class. Lectures make no sense, she reads off the slides word for word with no explanation. Test style is horrible. Practice exam answer key was wrong ALL the time, so do not even waste your time. Practice exams looked nothing like the real exam. This class is straight memorization and is very content heavy. She is also very rude.

This is the hardest class I've ever taken, mostly self-study. The professor is smart but just reads off the slides. Exams are entirely based on the slides, so skip the textbook—just memorize the slides, including wordless images. Her exams are extremely tough. You have no option tho she the only profressor and her accent does not help.

This professor is very knowledgable about the subject but fails to transfer that knowledge to her students. She is very blunt and if you don't know the information inside and out she gets frustrated with you which makes it difficult to ask questions. I dedicated so much time and effort to this course and was barely scraping by with a B.

very few grades were put in the grade book (2 midterms, 20ish quizzes, recitation, & final). average for the midterms (worth 40% of our grade) was a c. the midterms were incredibly hard and very detail heavy & based on like 5 30-40 slide ppt so lots of memorization. also, lectures were just her reading of the slides (so hard to learn based on that)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Marin is a sweetheart, but at times her lectures seemed very rushed and lack luster as she read word-for-word from slideshows. She is very knowledgeable though! I wish she were able to translate that knowledge better for us. Very caring lady and funny. This course overall was challenging for me, even though I've taken upper level chem and biol.

Dr. Marin is caring, but exams are difficult, and you need to memorize EVERYTHING from slides. She read off the slides and moved SUPER fast in lecture, so I needed to spend lots of time outside class. Make sure to do the EC. Only 1 section, so don't take it if you don't need to, but also don't let it stop you from applying to the Nutrition major.

Nice person but genuinly the hardest grader at UNC. When I took this class, I was surprised at the fact that it easily surpassed the horrors of the chem department. 
The class, hard as is, tests on biochemical metabolic reactions without us given background information how they work. Also, get ready to be tested on the most minute details possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Seems like a nice person, and very knowledgable at the subject, but for your own sake take with another professor! Genuinely one of the most difficult classes I've taken at UNC, and I've taken a good amount of chem and bio.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: TAKE NUTR 240 WITH SOMEONE ELSE. Dr. Marin seems incredibly smart, but intelligence does not equal good at teaching. Her exams are insanely difficult, and when the class average was a C for BOTH midterms, she placed the blame on the students. reviews.comment: Her teaching style involves reading off the slides. She expected her students to know everything in the PowerPoint and the textbook. She would not give hints about what we were expected to know. This class is a big time commitment, and homework is not a part of your grade. Her exam questions are sometimes confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her lectures are boring. They only go over a small part of the assigned readings, so you are basically teaching yourself. If you read the chapters you could skip the lectures. Exams are hard. Multiple select questions. For example, the choices would be A; B; C; A & B; or A , B, & C. Over half of the test consist of question in this format.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Genuinely worst course I've taken at this university. I am in orgo at the same time and am even doing better in that class. She reads off the slides, tests are unbearably hard, and I have had a medical emergency, and she refuses to even take that into consideration or even respond to emails regarding the situation in terms of points.
Awful experience!

So much to say, so little words. Lectures were a waste of time, she reads directly off the slides and still finds a way to tell us inaccurate information (takes a true genius to do that). Dont bother asking questions because she wont answer them. Pros - she's funny and sarcastic, really appeals to my sense of humor. My advice, dont take this class.

Professor Marin reads directly off of the slides. The class purely based on memorization and the tests are built to trick you. I am a nutrition major and am interested in the subject, but she made this class miserable.

Dr. B-M reads directly off her slides. You are expected to teach yourself many of the learning objectives outside of class, as well as memorize nearly slide she presents (usually upwards of 30-40 per class). Unengaging and entirely depends on your ability to memorize as much information as possible before tests. Do not take unless you have to.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Only reads the slides in lecture and expects you to memorize 400 slides for exams. Exams were mostly multi-select questions with no partial credit! She doesn't take feedback well, when a question directly from the practice exam was on our exam we all got it marked wrong because her practice exam key was wrong but she refused to give us points back.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She is an unorganized lecturer who just reads off the slides. There is almost no clarity about what content will be on exams. This is her first time teaching the course so it could improve but given her response to feedback I wouldn't expect it. The exams are very large parts of your grade and have lots of content along with unclear questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I do not understand why this class so hard! The material is interesting, but the exams are legit impossible! She makes her exams in a way that trick you up!!!!!!!!!! The dumb A, B, C and AB are correct and that format just did not work with me! Take this class only if you wanna fail.
Instructions so unclear, lots of reading, very boring lectures and is kind of condescending to students. If you need this class, you can survive it, but I would not take it if I didn't have to.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super important in her field, very knowledgeable, but lectures can be a bit dry. Try not to take this class early in the morning if possible. Grading criteria for papers is a bit unclear, but if you are willing to go to office hours to ask that could help. Lots and lots of articles to read.

Overall, this was an ok class. Almost all classes were just straight lecture without any engagement, which makes it hard to actually learn the material, but if that's your cup of tea then this class is fine. There was often pretty ambiguous grading criteria on what was wanted for assignments, which just took trial and error to figure out.

Dr. Huang teaches and links concepts well, but she overestimates students' computation skills, so the lecture can be hard to follow. Lectures can be better paced to increase attendance. Contents are pretty hard, but her tests are fair and much easier than hw in terms of high-level thinking. Providing more basic prob and calc practices should help.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hard class, have some exposure to probability/stats or this is going to suck. Gives really hard tests (all MCQ) but makes up for it by offering 4% of EC to your overall grade. Must do more problems beyond homework/classwork for practice, since there are so many topics covered we do not go over all relevant examples in assigned work.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Generous weighting and extra credit are blessings. She honestly provided good explanations and solidly attempted to engage our uninterested class. Your experience will likely be determined by previous exposure to the material. I'd imagine Zoe is the best option for 435 and would be excited if she was the average teacher in the STOR department.

Exams are worth 75% of your grade, so do not mess up. She gives 4% extra credit at the end, which was a little bit helpful. Lectures are pretty difficult to follow, so I recommend reading the textbook. Do not leave studying to the last minute and do a bunch of practice problems. Exams are all MC.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: very difficult. practice every day. tons of stats majors and they bring up the average bc they have done stats before. i have no stats experience. this class was so difficult for me bc i did not have the time to sit down and practice. take this class with max 2 chill classes bc this one will be your priority. exams are all mcq (cries)

Very sweet.class is really hard. She explains stuff well but if you have never had any stats experience, it is really hard to keep up in class and it will probably take you hours longer to understand a problem than someone who has done stats before. its a completely new way of thinking that requires a TON of practice. read the textbook b4 lecture

1st midterm, 18 questions MCQ. Not difficult but if you have never taken a stats class, you NEED TO PRACTICE A TON. I am a math person and got a 56. It wasn't hard but it was just too much for the time. Practice, practice, and practice every waking moment you have. The hw is not enough, open the textbook and do everything. Find more probs online.

Clear schedule, clear lecture notes. U don't need to go to the lecture if u understand all the homework and lecture notes. There's also extra credit added to the final grade on midterms like 0.5%. I didn't get any grade yet but bro rescheduled the midterm to next week, which is huge for me bc otherwise I will have 3 midterms this week on 2 days lol

HWs were manageable, and tests were not too bad. The final is worth 45% of your grade, so make sure you don't mess up. Don't know if she even curved it towards the end, but the 3% EC she offered definitely helped. If you practice from the textbook you'll be absolutely fine, and the MCQ format for the tests help as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She tends to give about one homework assignment a week, which is very manageable. Her exams are multiple choice and are in many ways easier than the homeworks, so as long as you pay attention in class and go over the content in the homeworks and lecture slides you'll be fine. Be aware that difficulty ramps up significantly after the first exam.

this class isn't that bad... i would recommend not going to class and just doing reading from the textbook and doing the practice problems. i got a B+ but couldve pulled off an A if I didnt sell on the final

I went to a few classes before realizing she lectured pretty much directly from the textbook. However, this is not a bad thing -- it gives you the full freedom of whether you would rather read the textbook or go to lecture (I never went to lecture). She is very nice and the exams were quite easy (you can't really make a super hard MCQ stor exam).
She's super nice, but RUN. Midterms and final are hell.

Really nice professor. Homework is easy (takes like an hour to do each week). Exam are tough but fair. Study hard and you will at least get a B. If you put in the work, A range is definitely attainable.

Taking class 24F. If you are good/talented in math, take it. If not, consider others. Her class is full of proof with had nothing to do with exam. Exam based on textbook, so BUY IT and go over textbook before exam. Her practice exam is JOKE, no connection with exam. If you are not good with math, RUN. Did give 3% free EC. not sure with curve yet

Lectures were focused on proofs/theorems, but tests (which made up 75% of the grade) were entirely based on applications. To succeed, you have to do textbook practice problems on your own. She provided several extra-credit opportunities and was very accessible during office hours to explain HW (which was the main workload on a weekly basis).

Painfully boring lectures that aren't super helpful with completing the assignments. HW answers are pretty available online, and the exam questions are relatively fair. Final Exam was 45% (crazy) but there are some extra credit opportunities and the curve at the end hit like a truck.

cannot stress enough that you need to READ THE TEXTBOOK FOR PRACTICAL EXAMPLES. the lectures are proof-heavy so that you understand why the formulas are what they are. homeworks are short and simple, midterms are MC and directly lifted from the textbook/lecture examples. the textbook is very detailed and follows directly with the lecture proofs.

Don't bother with lectures. They are just 50 minutes of proofs and overcomplicated explanations of theorems and definitions while skipping most of the examples. Midterm 2 is cumulative. Gives subpar practice material that doesn't map onto the exams so just do examples from notes. Will curve if the average is low. She is pretty nice.

Great Professor for STOR 435! Go to the lectures and do homework carefully, you will succeed in this course. I don't know why others complained lectures were useless. Actually, it helped a lot. Also, go to the OH, it's really helpful! Professor Huang is sooo caring and gave 3% extra credits after final.

One of the best professors in STOR department! I learned lots of useful content from this course. Although I needed to spend some time to learn the proofs(not included in exam), it helps me in other higher-level stats and math courses. If you are interested in stats and want to learn something, take Professor Huang's course without any doubts!

Professor Huang's teaching is exceptional. The course content was extremely useful and well-structured. She proved a lot in class but all contents were useful. If you can understand in-class notes well, it's easy to complete homework and exams. There was a BIG curve here after final. So don't worry about your grade if you spend time in this course.

I am having a hard time understanding all of the negative press. Professor Huang is very clear during her lectures and thoroughly answered student questions. She also offered 3% extra credit on top of the final grade in addition to a generous curve. Just read the textbook, ask questions, and go to office hours and you will succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A good grade and even a small social life are mutually exclusive in this course

Worst class I've taken at UNC. So much homework and the lectures will put you to sleep. She refuses to give practice problems because she doesn't want to put anything similar on the exams. Each midterm is 20% and has 12 multiple choice questions. Huge curve on the class thankfully, but this class will be the most painful 50 minutes of your day.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It's her first semester here so people should cut her some slack. Exams were all mcq, but all 435 are like that, and the content was fair. Lectures were ok. Read the textbook, you don't even have to go to class. Do the HWs, she reuses them on her exams. I do wish we had more problems. Extra credit and great curve, raw grade was a B+
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was based almost entirely on 3 multiple choice exams. The lectures were majority proofs, with very few examples, making the exams overly difficult.

She spends most of the class time doing proofs rather than providing examples to explain the concepts. She moves extremely fast and barely explains difficult concepts.Two tests that are 12 question MC, which make up a significant portion (40%) of the overall grade. The final (40% of your grade) is a a MC test w/ no partial credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I don't understand people complaining about Zoe doing proofs/abstract concepts - I found that was most helpful/the best use of class rather than practice problems that you should do on your own time. I actually felt like I was learning what a distribution represents rather than a generic cookbook of formulas. Overall a great professor

She's an okay lecturer and her tests are hard, but not unfair. One issue, though, is that she does not provide enough practice material for the tests. If you want to do well, make sure to do the textbook problems and review the homework before the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Although friendly, professor Huang's lectures are impossible to keep up with. One week she says she is uploading her notes and the next she says she has stopped. Exams are multiple choice but extremely difficult to understand. Her lectures include maybe 1 or 2 examples while the rest is just her doing proofs that aren't helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her lectures are not helpful when it comes to homework and exams. Exams are multiple choice and do not properly test knowledge of the course (almost impossible to adequately study for). She talks more about the philosophy of statistics and goes through difficult proofs during class rather than covering necessary material that is tested on.

Goes through the material as if everyone in the class has already seen it and just needs a quick glance to understand the topics. Does complicated proofs in class; homework and exams are unrelated and difficult. Unless you have already taken STOR 435 and know all the material, this is a terrible professor to have to start learning it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof Huang moves very quickly and has had me lost in confusion since day 1 of the class. Her homework assignments often cover nothing done in class and as such I cannot practice what I learned. The class is graded 80% on multiple choice tests, but with no practice questions, I'm often lost on what to study. She is nice, but her class is very hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: For the Econ 420 class, the lecture is ok, but not very clear. The exam is long and difficult. The exam time is less than 75 minutes, which is too rushed for students to finish in time. Although she curves a lot on the exam, it still makes students feel unprepared for the class. However, Professor Chao is a very nice person, caring about students.

The exams are completely different from the lectures and homework. To make it worse, multiple-choice questions can have up to two correct answers. I fail to see the educational value of setting up assessments this way.

She's nice, but she can't teach. The course is unclear, quiz answers on Canvas conflicted with the answer key, there was basically no feedback. The slides aren't helpful, and the exams were so hard and too rushed. She rarely grades homework on time.
She is kind but be sure to see her outside of class for the best understanding of things because her lectures can be confusing

Having exams worth 70% of your grade is unreasonable when lectures are unclear, the slides are filled with AI and memes, and the textbook offers little support. The exams don't reflect what's taught.

She is kind and accessible outside of class, but I don't think that makes up for what you'd get out of it.

she probably isnt bad for Econ 101 b/c the content is straightforward, but she is not equipped to be teaching Econ 420 at all. she seems nice but she cannot answer questions clearly and her lectures rarely stay on topic. the exams are not bad if you use outside resources, but in general her lectures offer little help with understanding the content.

She is the sweetest lady, don't get me wrong. But she can't teach. Most of her slides are AI memes and she deviates so much from the content. She doesn't grade the homeworks till more than a month after it is submitted.
What you are taught in class is NOT what you are presented with in the exam. And you're not allowed to ask questions on the exam..

The majority of the slides were AI generated pictures of herself or random AI pictures/memes. The lectures were not very helpful and most of the learning is done outside of class. I think she's really nice and knowledgeable about economics, but it didn't really feel like a whole lot of teaching was going on.

Truly such an amazing teacher. I would take many more classes with her. The material was not necessarily easy, but her lectures and demeanor helped deliver it clearly. The class never felt like a struggle to follow. She is so welcoming for office hours and coffee chats.

Econ 101 at UNC is not the easiest but professor Chao most definitely made it really easy to learn. Her slide shows are posted and are easy to learn from, her lectures are pretty funny and engaging with the effort that she puts into teaching the class. Make sure you work hard on the first and second midterms because the final is pretty difficult.
Dr. Chao is the sweetest! She really cares about her students and made economics interesting. If you can, take ECON 101 with her she is AMAZING.

Dr. Chao is my favorite professor I have had so far at UNC. While the tests were definitely hard, the problem sets, review exams, help sessions, and care she put into the class made them manageable. She made lectures engaging with the images in her slideshows and really tried to see what students were not understanding in order to help. Great prof!

Ying is super caring and a great person; however, she isn't the greatest lecturer and I learned most of the material on my own time from class slides. If you want to do well, you have to commit time outside of class to really understand the material and come to office hours with good questions. Generous grader, but exams were still very difficult.

Dr. Chao is amazing, and such a kind professor. That being said, this class is HARD. Exams are much harder than content learned in class and the final exam was almost impossible, even after days of studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Chao is the sweetest instructor I have ever had. She makes sure to remember your name, brings snacks and candy to class, and gives genuine feedback on any questions or concerns. Lectures can sometimes be a little messy, but if you are able to follow along, you will learn! Econ is a hard class, but Chao makes it very possible to succeed.

Dr. Chao is an amazing professor who cares for her students deeply. She actively sends messages of support if we seemed down in class, was engaging through the lectures, and had snacks in class if we were hungry. Rare to see a professor like this, definitely sign up for her class!

As a person, Dr. Chao is extremely nice. However, her teaching style is not for everyone. She tends be disorganized with her lectures and tends to do things in a more complicated sense. The final was pretty rough but I think that econ 101 is just a tough class. Probably the best out of the 101 teachers.

Dr. Chao is literally the sweetest professor ever! She tries to make lectures enjoyable and is super accessible outside of class for extra help. She genuinely cares about her students and wants each one of them to succeed. Econ 101 is challenging but she breaks down hard concepts really well. There isn't too much busy work outside of class either.

Chao was lovely for Econ, truly cared about her students and their success. Much less work outside class than Staub but still had to work hard and study lots. Sometimes was kind of confusing while teaching but is mostly due to the speed at which econ 101 needs to be taught.
shes genuinely so sweet and caring- econ101 was lowkey tough but she makes it easy to learn if u put in the work

The best Econ professor you can get. The lectures are very clear and Chao is very caring, breaking down concepts that are difficult. The tests are very manageable as long as you complete the practice. If you are taking Econ101, I highly recommend Chao as a professor.

Take Econ with her! She is the BEST Econ 101 professor. She is so caring and even provides snacks in class! Dr. Chao offers to meet with students individually because she genuinely wants you to succeed.

Hands down the best ECON prof. at UNC. Super sweet and wants her students to do well. Super responsive to emails (fixed a problem with my grade in 5 mins on the last day). Homework is very manageable, midterms and final are definitely tough but not impossible (multiple choice only). Grading is very fair, midterm 1: 15%; midterm 2 and final: 20%

I LOVE DR. CHAO! If you have to take Econ take it with her I am begging you. She is extremely sweet and actually cares about her students. She knows that we care about our grades and gave us bonus points on our final. I feel like the difficulty of Econ 101 is exaggerated; If you read the textbook chapters and do all the practice, you will be good.
Genuinely one of the most caring professors ever!

Chao is genuinely the sweetest person I have ever met and she wants to get to know you. I didn't love her teaching style- I struggled focusing. 2 midterms worth 15% and 20% and a final worth 20%. Content is very hard- exams are very challenging but she is the best option to take it with. Does only multiple choice and is so accessible anytime.
Amazing person. She is incredibly caring about her students and truly wants what best for you. Econ 101 is a hard class, but she is definitely the person to take it with.

Her teaching methods are not the best but she is understanding and the lecture is small enough you can ask her to explain or go back. There is a solid amount of work in this class that's always due Sundays at midnight (no late work accepted) but is completion grade. Do not leave it til the last minute. Definitely the best of the 3 ECON 101 teachers

Professor Chao is amazing. ECON 101 is a tough course, but she's 100% the teacher you should want to take it with. She has note outlines for the lectures and has set weekly office hours that make her very accessible. She's very willing/enthusiastic about getting to know you on a personal level. Go to class and PAY ATTENTION!

Chao is the goat. Econ 101 is a hard class conceptually, but she makes it enjoyable enough to want to come to class. She is very personable and is very accessible outside of class and really cares for her students as people. This class is legit though so you will have to put effort into it to do well, but she is definitely the best choice

She's such an amazing teacher and is very passionate about what she does. I highly recommend her class. Although ECON 101 can be pretty tough because of the material itself, she does an amazing job of providing time outside of class to study it and explains things very clearly.

she is so amazing and makes me econ fun. Her tests are not super easy, but also not hard if you study. She gives you handouts to do every day that will help you study, and I would say that attendance is kind of important. She cares so much about her students and I don't know anyone who doesn't like her

Dr. Kerr is supportive and encouraging throughout the senior honors thesis process, and challenges you in the best way. Feedback is detailed and helpful, and time is always made to talk about challenges. Dr. Kerr clearly cares about student success as expectations are clear, communication is consistent, and support is always there. Highly rewarding

If you have the chance to take a class with Professor Kerr, take it. He is a phenomenal professor who is so understanding when it comes to his students and is willing to do whatever to help them out. He is so funny and makes going to class at 8 am worth it. You will not regret taking a class with him.

Dr. Kerr is one of the rare professors on campus who considers the fact that his students are people with lives outside of his class. He is very willing to be flexible as long as you are willing to demonstrate you are putting in effort to the class. Makes an otherwise really boring topic and 8 am class really enjoyable. I would highly recommend.
Data literacy is a very annoying class, but Dr. Kerr is awesome. He made a boring class as fun and easy as it could be. Could not recommend him more!
Zach is such a chill guy. He didn't make this (bs) class harder than it needed to be and understood the importance of it to students. If you still need to take IDST111L, take it with him.
Kerr's great. One of the best professors I've had up until this point. Super understanding of students lives but also does a fantastic job teaching and challenging students.

Zach is such a great professor. He seemed to really understand the point of Data Lit Lab and didn't make it more demanding than it needed to be. He was extremely engaging, understanding, and flexible with the class. Overall great guy.

Honest and understanding of students lives outside of classes, especially for a one credit course. Take this class with him if you can, it seemed he was able to be more flexible with the material than other professors because he helped create the course. Met six times throughout the semester, with biweekly online work and a final group project

Zack understood that the class was only a single credit hour, and only had us do what was necessary to learn the content. I had to meet with him for help with my final project, and I mentioned that I was looking for some good study spots on campus. He took the time after our meeting to send me a list of his favorite places to get work done.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Kerr is a great professor. He actually cares about his students and wants them to succeed. We had 2-3 assignments each week, but we didn't have any tests. Best professor I've had at UNC.
I wish every teacher were like him; he actually understands that we are college students.
Take this class with Professor Kerr!

Professor Kerr was one of the best professors I have ever had. He makes class entertaining and truly cares for his students. He is one of the most energetic and fun professors I have had at UNC, especially with his endless jokes and memes. His workload is VERY manageable, and he is very passionate about research. I would 100000% recommend!!

Dr. Kerr has been one of my favorite professors at UNC so far. I genuinely felt that he cared about his students and their success and well-being. No exams but 85% group work. He does grade assignments a little harder, but usually you can submit revisions and get points back. He's also extremely funny and entertaining. Worth taking 273 with Kerr.

Professor Kerr made class entertaining and fun. You can expect to have 2-3 assignments per week, but a lot of the assignments are group work. He doesn't give exams, which means he grades take-home quizzes and writing assignments more critically. Overall, he really cares about you and wants you to succeed! Highly recommend taking EXSS 273 with him!

Great professor and person all around. I am in my 4th semester here and this is the first professor I've had that truly cares about student well-being. He is very open and the way he speaks about himself shows that we are all human and it's okay not to have everything together all the time. No exams but learned so much about the research process.

Zach is the best professor that I have had in my college career. Zach truly cares about the success of everyone in his class and his students feeling validated, understood, and cared for. His lectures can be lengthy, but he adds memes and funny aspects to them to keep you engaged. Could not recommend taking his class enough!

I've never taken a class with him, but had to rate him. He called out names during graduation. He ensured everyone's name was pronounces correctly, which means a ton to me. My name isn't easy to pronounce which caused me stress, but he MADE SURE he said it right. This is a testament to who he is.

The most entertaining and engaging professor I've had at UNC. He really cares about how you are doing and what's going on in your life. Dr. Kerr repeatedly followed up with me about what I wrote in weekly reflections, which I thought was really thoughtful and showed genuine concern. SUCH A GOOD CLASS. 10/10 recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Kerr is great!

Amazing professor all around. Cares about students, grades fairly, gives opportunities for revision. The course content itself is pretty dry and it's amazing how he makes it come to life. Often focuses on bigger picture ideas that I felt really contributed to my development as a student outside of just my grade in this class.

Dr. Kerr is hands down the best professor I have ever had! He does not give any exams, most of the work in this course is completed in a group that you will be assigned to on day one, but you learn to love the people you are working with. The material covered is informative, but Dr. Kerr does not expect you to understand everything immediately.

Dr. Kerr is a super energetic and caring professor- you'll have a fun time in his class. The whole semester is group work, but it's actually manageable and I enjoyed my group a lot. He's lenient on deadlines and always checks in to make sure you're doing okay. He gives personal feedback on every assignment and really wants you to succeed. No exams!

The best professor I've had at UNC. Genuinely cares for his students and constantly makes sure theyre doing good. Class is mostly group work but you get good feedback on assignments and can submit revisions to improve your grade. Some weekly quizzes, not too hard. Lectures are so fun so make sure to go or you get a makeup assignment that isnt fun.

Best professor I have had at UNC so far. He is hilarious and is one of the only teachers I know that checks in on students and puts them first. Class is all group work but he gives a lot of time to complete it. If 273 satisfies a Gen-Ed or you are looking for another class, take it. Goat teacher.
Amazing professor with a great intro to research topics. His lectures are hilarious and made me never want to miss a day. Best professor for EXSS 273 hands down and would take any class he teaches.

Dr. Kerr is an exceptional professor who genuinely cares about his students' success. He's super chill and creates a relaxed atmosphere in the classroom. Group work in his class is surprisingly manageable. He's understanding of life circumstances and always available as a helpful resource. Highly recommend taking a class with him!

He is the best professor at UNC. He genuinely cares about his students mental health and lives outside of school. He does everything in his power to help us and gives incredible lectures that made me love going to his class at 8am. Highly, highly recommend.

Do yourself a favor and take 273 with Zach. No exams in this class (unlike other sections), only graded by a group project and some easy mini quizzes that you have unlimited attempts. He's so funny and friendly. He genuinely cares and checks in with students to make sure they are okay. Really values course feedback and tries to improve the course.
One of the few tenured professors that actually gives a crap about teaching. Also really funny.

When I tell you that Professor Kerr is how I wish all professors at UNC were, it's the truth. Professor Kerr cares about you as a person before a student & is always very interested in how you're doing outside of class. He understands that college is hard & will help you in any way he can to meet deadlines & answer your questions. HE IS THE BEST!!!

Dr. Kerr is one of the best professors I've had at UNC. He is SO funny, which makes class enjoyable, and he cares about students' success more than any professor I've had.  He was always quick to answer questions via email, and despite being an online class, I got to build a relationship with him. I wish I could take another class with Dr. Kerr!

Zack is one of the best professors at UNC. He really does care for students and their well-being and allowed extensions. His lectures are funny and interesting to watch. There are a lot of assignments, but they are super low-stress and easy to complete and mainly graded on effort. No final. He truly is a gem, couldn't recommend him enough!

truly the best professor i've had at UNC. he is genuinely one of the most caring and understanding professors you can ask for. there's two lectures due a week and usually an assignment in between, but everything is super easy and rubrics (and extensions!!!!) are provided. cannot recommend him enough!!!

Dr. Kerr is SUPER funny and cares a lot about his students!! This course wasn't super hard aside from that statistics portion, but he helps in that unit to make things not as bad as it could be. No exams when I took it, but quizzes after each lecture (mostly completion) to make sure we were on track and no questions. Great professor and course!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Fantastic professor. He really cares that you learn the material and cares about his students as people. He is incredibly knowledgable about research and is great with explanations. This class is labor-intensive, but there is no busy work. Everything is intentional and designed to ensure you learn the material.

Zack is one of the best professors Ive had at UNC! His class requires a lot of work on your end, but every assignment has a purpose and he gives great feedback. The class is not easy, but he sets you up for success. Zack is hilarious, understanding, knowledgeable, and very organized. Be prepared to think critically. I recommend Zack 10/10 for 273!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Kerr is one of the most phenomenal and understanding professors I've had in college! He wants you to excel and will make you work for your grade. It's one of those classes where you get out what you put in. Although asynchronous, he put forth his best effort to make the class enjoyable. He's truly deserving of tenure.

TAKE KERR... everything is pretty much just graded for completion and not accuracy and if not he lets you redo it for full credit. HE IS THE GOAT. always willing to give an extension on assignment... can be somewhat of a boring class towards the end but makes it tolerable. 10/10 take 273 with Kerr

First, its Zack, not Dr. Kerr. Provided daily memes and even brought coffee one day. Most understanding and accommodating professor at UNC. Opened every assignment early during the pandemic so I could finish the class on April 1. If he does not meet tenure, then UNC aint doing something right. Dont pass this opportunity up.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Zack is an awesome, kind professor. He truly wants you to exceed and is more than willing to answer questions. There are 3 exams (questions come from PPTs) , 10 HWs and a group research project. Attendance is mandatory and after 1 unexcused absence you will lose 1% off your overall grade for a maximum of 5% off, so definitely don't skip class.

Amazing professor & person, genuinely cares so much for his students. Very group project based and attendance is mandatory. Such an awesome & funny professor, very accessible for help & a reasonable guy. Would take this class again just to have him as a professor if I could
Zack was a great professor for 273! Really cares about his students and wants them to succeed. There is a group project instead of a final!
One of the best professors I've ever had!! He is so incredibly kind, really cares about his students, and makes a point of getting to know you. If you have the option, TAKE IT WITH HIM!
Dr. Yackulic was great at keeping us in the loop with Honors Carolina events and resources and has some super interesting anecdotes of his own.
This is a very easy pass/fail class and Dr. Yackulic is a very kind and understanding professor.

Professor Yackulic is amazing! He really cares for his students and gives great advice for freshman to use for their future college careers. Easy class, only five assignments total and a very easy final exam but class is pass or fail. Kayden Hunt is also an amazing TA!
Dr. Yackulic is a great guy who cares about his students. HNRS 101 is Pass/Fail with few assignments, so very easy to do well.
Great guy who cares, Honors 101 is super easy with almost no assignments
Extremely easy class. Dr.Yackulic is extremely easygoing and the class is very laidback.
Super nice and a great class. You learn lots of good skills for job searching and building your resume. Pass/Fail so just turn things in on time.

Dr. Y is a walking W. He's interesting, funny, caring, & inspirational. HNRS 101 is EXTREMELY easy: it has 6 simple assignments total & is graded on a P/F basis. There are a lot of resources you get exposed to, and the material can really help orient yourself at UNC. Just attend class, do your small, easy assignments, and you're done!
Great professor. Hopefully you are lucky enough to be stuck with him!
If you have to take HNRS 201 definitely take it with Dr. Y. Class was fun and he made some boring material interesting

This class was great. It was an introductory course to get familiar with the university and what resources we have access to. Some of the material isn’t the most exciting but he makes it fun and really cares about the students. Would definitely recommend!!

Dr. Ariel is fantastic! His classes can be hard to follow and he interrupts presentations. BUT! He is a wealth of knowledge and I have never had a professor be more complimentary and supportive of my passion. He can take a joke, is willing to be (respectfully) challenged by students, and brought food to share at the beginning of class. He is great!
Great professor, gets to know his students, very personable. Would recommend him to anyone.

Great professor. Provided clear expectations for exams and opportunities to help prepare the class. Would highly recommend any class with Dr. Ariel. Honestly, a gem of a human. 

The topic of 242 (New Religious Movements) was unlike anything else I've ever learned and broadened my understanding of other faith communities.

I LOVED this class. Favorite professor and favorite class and i'm about to graduate. I would take any class he teaches. It's not hard if you try and are thoughtful. I really enjoyed the topics and Dr. Ariel always brought snacks, which was super kind. For the class, we got to visit churches and write about our experiences visiting them.

Dr. Ariel was the best professor of the three. He kept the class engaged through clips, texts, and slides. His essays were the easiest of the three, if you listened to him for 5 mins you could easily score an A. Plus, he gave you hints ahead of time. Great professor, especially if you are a history buff.
Professor Ariel is not engaging. The slides were all over the place and very boring class overall. Would not recommend.
horrible class. ariel is mid.

Yaakov was a bit eccentric, but always kind and caring. The class isn't difficult at all as long as you show up and participate in lecture. Grading criteria can be unclear at times, but contacting him via email/outside of class is easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Ariel is an extremely genuine and passionate teacher. There were just a few church observation papers due throughout the semester that he graded pretty easily, and you could observe online. He brought snacks to every class, which always made my day. Readings were assigned but never mattered for class.

Semester consisted of four written assignments plus a comparative midterm assignment. Classes were very lecture heavy and at times a bit boring. Professor Ariel's feedback was not always super clear but he does offer regrades and wants everyone to succeed. Be prepared to put in a moderate effort to secure the grade you want.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I don't think he was a bad professor. The class just sucks and the location was not helping me learn. The microphones in the Stone Center were always hard to listen to and honestly I never could understand what either of the professors were saying. Yaakov definetely was the funniest one and liked to make a spectacle of students.

You can sit in the back row and avoid eye contact and he will still make you stand up in front of the class and say something. He's really funny and definitely a great personality but he doesn't really teach as much as he tries to facilitate discussion. This is a terrible class (mostly the TAs and UNCs faults) but Dr. Ariel is a great teacher

His assignments are broad, but he expects specific criteria in writing. It gets frustrating when trying to do assignments since his instruction is so broad and is usually only discussed in class rather than posting guidelines. Nice guy and occasionally gives second chances.

This class requires a lot of writing: there are four reflections on online church videos, at least two reviews, and an essay midterm, all of which are graded somewhat toughly. He let us write the midterm in advance and gave us all the terms that were going to be on the final, though. There's also a lot of reading, but you can get by not doing it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: I recommend both this class and Professor Ariel. He is an understanding professor that gives clear, precise feedback. You are graded on multiple papers (at least 6), but he offers extra credit in the form of redoing your papers for a better grade. Attend class! Lectures were slow and boring at times, but this class is an easy Gen-ed to knock out!

This class was super interesting to me, but often the lectures were hard to follow. Papers were graded harshly, but many opportunities were available to improve upon your work. Professor Ariel and his TA were easy to work with and wanted us to do well.
Prof. Ariel is personable and understanding. If you're a self-starter and remain engaged, the courseload is pretty manageable.
the guy is a jerk and the material is so boring and hard. worst class i have EVER taken (I am a senior)

Do not take a class with him. The most unorganized professor I've had. Syllabus was so confusing which caused problems for everyone in the class. Lectures hardly made sense because he went off on so many tangents. I feel liked I barely learned anything because I was confused the whole time. I'm a RELI major but I dreaded this class.

Professor Ariel is kind, but classes with him feel like they cover 20 minutes of content in a 70 minute session. He doesn't teach to the textbook. The only graded assignments are digital church visits and film/book reviews. He asks questions on the material before he teaches it, so if you have no background knowledge, you won't have answers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not understand other comments complaining about a Christian bias. Professor is Jewish, and REL242 discussed other religious groups besides Christian offshoots. Prof. Ariel made a solid attempt to bring the class together as a group. Granted, knowing something about the subject beforehand was beneficial.
Prof Ariel was great. He is the sweetest teacher and is clearly very knowledgeable. I learned a lot in his class, and you're graded on only a few assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: By far the worst professor I've ever had! So rude....
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: dont take if you don't have any knowledge ab Christianity. Prof Ariel is the sweetest but the lectures were SO BORING and so hard to follow especially bc he teaches the class as if everyone there is christian--I AM NOT, so I never knew what was going on. TA didn't grade above a 90 all semester but he pulled thru w an easy final and no other tests

Dr. Ariel is a very knowledgeable man who gives solid lectures and structures his class well. He is also funny and caring, which makes him a good professor to get to know. This class wasn't totally inspirational or one of my top few, but it was very good and taught me a lot of relevant history.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Ariel is confusing in his lectures, doesn't stick to the syllabus, doesn't tell you how assignments are graded (if he even remembers to tell you what the assignments are), and is just generally rude. Regularly makes you watch movies that have nothing to do with the class and penalizes you if you're not there to watch them.

Professor Ariel gives lots of opportunities for extra credit and replies to emails very quickly. His lectures can be dull at times as he can get lost in his thoughts and go off on tangents, but you can tell he is very knowledgable and passionate about the subject. 3 short papers plus a couple more for extra credit.

Definitely the most boring professor I've ever had. He gets off topic almost every sentence and is just too dry to even follow. But watch out he does like to strip if you if he sees people falling asleep. Just don't sign up, you'll be happier without him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I loved Professor Ariel! He was lowkey a savage but was great. His lectures can be dry at times, but they were pretty informational. There were lots of interesting guest lecturers (and some not interesting ones) too. His tests were easy and readings didn't really matter. Basically, go to lecture and listen/take notes and you'll get an A

Dr. Ariel veered away from the syllabus to say the least. There was a required reading of at least one novel, usually more per class.  The readings were dense, the videos were boring, he was confusing, not to mention the 12 pg term paper. I would not recommend. He was also HATEFUL if you ever had to miss a class, even if you were sick.
Amazing!!
Very enthusiastic and knowledgeable.

Attendance is mandatory, but you really don't have to pay much attention as long as you look at the study guide before tests. Requires a lot of outside commitment - visiting synagogues and outside lectures. Ariel is funny and the TAs were helpful this semester.
