Great professor.  He is funny, engaging, and keeps the class interesting.  He is big on participation, so doing the homework is beneficial, even though it's not graded.

Dr. P is amazing and one of the best teachers I had this semester. She is always available during office hours and always checks in on students. The classwork is useful and not too difficult, with only a few hours of work outside of class each week. No exams.
You can tell that Dr. Panter actually cares about her students and she makes her classes enjoyable. She wants students to succeed and if you put effort in and participate you will do well.

Dr. P is really awesome. She cares very deeply about her students and her class is not hard at all. I had no tests. She is an easy grader and wants you to do well (very flexible with deadlines). However, her lectures can be very long and all over the place. It's fine because no tests means you don't need to be fully attentive and can space off.

Dr. P is great. She is completely bonkers, but so kind and sweet. She really cares about her students and makes you want to do your best. The class itself was very interesting and didn't have too much work associated with it. I would highly recommend her!
Dr. Panter is awesome!  She really cares about her students and is really easy to talk to.  She super enthusiastic about stats.  I would definitely recommende her :)

Dr. Panter is the most caring professor I've ever had. She really cares about each individual student and always takes the time to ask you how you're doing. She is SUPER enthusiastic about statistics. She's kind of a perfectionist, but always has a positive attitude. I'm definitely going to keep in touch with her after this class!

Dr. Panter is a wonderful woman and professor. She is so sweet and is always concerned with how people are doing as individuals, not just their performance as students. She is not always clear and doesn't always answer e-mails but she is brilliant and more than willing to help you with anything you could ask for.
Amazing!!! She is THE Prof. to take. Any class that she is teaching....TAKE IT! You will not be disappointed.

Dr. Panter is absolutely wonderful. She's brilliant and cares so much about her students that it's insane. Every once in awhile you come across a professor that truly makes you WANT to learn and master the material and come to class! She is one of them and I adore her.
She is a very fun teacher who loves working with research and numbers.

I overall enjoyed 360 and learned a lot! There were times I stressed about assignment detail, every time it was fine and I received good grades. The exams were fair and she never set us up for failure. The case studies were the main assignments of the class but if the directions were followed and effort was put in, a good grade is very achievable!

Massively regret taking this class with such a disorganized professor. ASR has very unclear grading criteria and is very late on communication. Boring lectures and extremely out of date and unreadable slides. Lots of projects on short timeline and inconsistently tough exams. She feels very cold, arrogant, and unapproachable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I would not recommend taking nutrition with ASR since it isn't required. Its a tough class with lots of projects and some difficult concepts. Some criteria isn't well outlined and ASR is not lenient. Long lectures and tons of pointless, hard-to-digest (lol), literature you have to read. Also, be ready to get cold called in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Had a hard time following lectures, class slides were out of date, and the tests could be pretty difficult if you did not record every detail discussed in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Interesting material but lectures were all over the place. Assignments were easy and helpful in actually understanding material but I could've skipped all the lectures and still done well, just boring

This class was very interesting and I enjoyed learning a lot of the topics we covered. She also was very good to answer questions and really encouraged us to participate during class. The quizzes were pretty hard and it was really unclear what we needed to know to prepare. Also was quite condescending when you were called out and answered wrong.
Graded only by a few quizzes, a couple assignments for grade boosters and 4 exams including the final. Attend class, her office hours and study and you'll make a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you can take her exss 360 class, do it. she is so intelligent and is clearly very passionate about her work. The content you learn in this class is so applicable to real life and it changes the way you view nutrition. she is extremely helpful in office hours and is interested in getting to know you. you get out of this class what you put into it

Dr. Smith Ryan is intelligent and bases this course off of her research, but lecture slides get confusing without her comments, going to class was the only way to truly understand what she wanted us to learn. Patronizing when giving feedback in class if you answer/ask questions. Class conversations initiated by students were more engaging

She encourages class participation and asks questions to the class during her lectures. The lectures are engaging and she knows her stuff but the exams are difficult. Biweekly quizzes and 4 exams make up your grade. No homework!

Smith-Ryan gives enjoyable lectures. However, she makes you feel incompetent for suggesting an incorrect answer. Assignment instructions are confusing and vague. She nit-picks everything you turn in. If you are sick, have family/mental health issues, do not expect her to accommodate you in any way. Interesting class, but not a great professor.

If you have the chance take this. It was super interesting and Dr. Smith-Ryan was very accommodating and kind. This class is very applicable for the real world and was a class I always enjoyed attending. The class was mainly projects/assignments w/ 2 exams and a final. Majority of class focused on projects to help with the final. Take this class!!
Smith-Ryan is a great professor. She truly cares about her students. She is a pretty lenient grader and is even more helpful during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class was so interesting, 1 because it was about nutrition and 2 because she was a great professor. She really enjoys discussion and questions. I liked that she could give you good examples on the spot, and case studies were interesting.
This class was atrocious. Take another professor.

Not sure why the MATH186 ratings are so bad, I guess you guys didn't study. Class is super hard, but Andy's a great professor and really accessible outside class. Doesn't give much material for exam prep, but class problems and reviews outside of class are very representative of what the exam looks like. Work is hard but doable, very fun class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Does not care for your grade. The hardest professor to take for stats at Lafayette.

Professor Ackerman is nice, though his class is extremely difficult. His review sheets are no where close to what an actual exam looks like. His grading is harsh and he does not like to give out good grades. Look to take another statistics professor because he is not caring of your grade, though says he is. Dislike him a lot..

Concepts are hard but Andy was helpful in OH. Virtually no material to help you study for exams and HW questions did not always relate to class / exams. Great lecturer and educator in general. Looked forward to class.
Horrible. Grading is harsh. Does not drop lowest midterm. Grading unclear. Don't take.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: WOW, andy is one of the best teachers I've had at UNC, he is the sweetest guy who cares about his students. He is very open to meeting outside of class and tests are very similar to practice problems

The goat. Awesome guy who loves to teach. He genuinely cares for his students, their well-being, and their performance in class. He talks to the students often and wants to know them well. He's super chill and loves to help also. 5/5 Great guy and would so take his class again!

Super cool chill guy and good lecturer, very passionate about his job and statistics. 2 or 3 easy homeworks a week, drops lowest midterm(if final is higher) can overexplain things but sometimes that is appreciated. Best Stor 155 professor based on those I know who have had different ones. Straightforward and approachable. Take his class!

*ANTHRO 364*
I loved this class. Dr. Dorsey teaches us about professional development as an Anthropologist, and I still use the notes I took in her class to this day.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Love her! One of the best professors at UMass. Her classes and lectures are interesting and easy to follow. Provides slides before class. She does have a lot of readings but only a few of them are compulsory reads. Fairly easy midterm and final. One final project, 2 other projects and a few Course Reflections.
Dr. Dorsey is a great lecturer and a very kind professor. I would highly recommend her classes, especially Anthropology 313 (Nutritional Anthropology).

Professor Dorsey was one of the best professors I had at UMass. She makes learning content fun and super interesting. I have a lot of respect for her. Take a class with her! You'll learn so much without being overwhelmed, and she's always willing to help if you need it.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: amazing 10/10 recommend her

Achsah was my TA for this class, and it was a pretty TA heavy class (meaning they did all the grading and that's who you actually interacted with in recitation). I enjoyed her a lot! She's really nice and has a pleasant personality, and she got to know us all by name. She isn't an easy grader, but it's nothing insane. Solid choice overall

I really loved this class! It was probably my favorite that I've taken for my minor! Professor Dorsey is super nice and accessible and I loved the content and assignments. The group project and paper are also not bad at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I enjoyed SPAN344 (not 373 344 wasn't an option). This course was chill & insightful. Sometimes it was hard do all readings. Professor wasn't perfect (a bit unorganized... FYI to ppl who get stressed over that lol) BUT he was really flexible and understanding throughout the class which is rare in the ROML department. 8.5/10 class would take again!

This was probably my favorite class at UNC. I usually struggle with participating but the prof is so knowledgeable and funny I felt really comfortable! He is also very kind and willing to work with the class on due dates. Iffy about Canvas, but everything was clear in the syllabus. 11/10, unique experience!

It is clear that this is Rafael's first semester teaching here, which can excuse his unstructured and uninspired way of teaching. Class always felt incredibly dull which is surprising considering the class was about fiction writing (one of the most entertaining forms of writing). Excited to see how he structures future classes, he has the passion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Greatest class I've ever taken. Most classes are just him telling stories about his life -- which is super interesting. The class is like an interactive stand-up comedy show that gives you a super easy A for very little work. (VERY little)

Mike Acosta is an incredible teacher. Class is never boring and he actually cares about each student. He has a wealth of knowledge and shares it in an understandable way. He emphasizes that the class is to grow, and you don't have to stress about turning in perfect work. You can genuinely learn. If you can take a class with Mike, do it.

He was by far the best professor I have EVER had at this school. I am a premed stem student and I took this class as my sanity class and it was the best decision. I enjoyed this class so much because of Dr. Acosta. The content and the class were enjoyable but it was Dr. Acosta who brought the class to life.

What a guy. Easily the best professor I've had at UNC. Acosta cares so much about his students. The man has lived three different lives and has countless hilarious stories he loves to share. He is so knowledgeable and inspirational, and he feels more like a friend than a professor. Cannot recommend him enough. Amazing final lecture too.

One of the best teachers I've had at UNC! Acosta tells hilarious stories that connect back to screenwriting and gives very good advice for life in general. He's very knowledgeable and truly cares for students and their education. Take this class if you can!!

Dr. Acosta has been the best professor I've had at UNC thus far. He is so funny and actually cares about us as students, which you don't see from the other professors at UNC. The lectures were so funny and he related it to screenwriting, which allowed me to learn in a way that I haven't in any other class in my life.

He has some of the most engaging lectures and every class he'll tell an incredible story. Assignments are graded for completion so as long as you submit them on time you'll get an A. He makes the group projects fun and I learned a lot over the course of the semester. Left the class with a new outlook on life.

Acosta rocks. He has lived a thousand lives and has the best anecdotes. As long as you really try in his class, it will pay off. If you're even slightly interested in screenwriting or movie production, take a class with him! He has a lot of valuable knowledge and advice about the industry, great guy!

Mike is and will probably continue to be the best professor I have had at UNC. While I am really bad at regularly attending my classes, this course is one I made sure to always go to. Not necessarily because I have to, but because I wanted to and looked forward to it. He is genuinely caring and pays attention. I could write so much more about him.
Professor Acosta is the best professor I have ever had. He is entertaining, funny, and knows what he is talking about. You must take his class if you get the chance!!
BEST PROFESSOR AT UNC!!!

Professor Acosta is one of the most influential and memorable professors at UNC. He has a plethora of knowledge about screenwriting and tells incredible stories in class. If you attend class and apply his notes/feedback, you will do good. I only hope I can take him again.

I truly believe Professor Acosta's classes have taught me more applicable knowledge than any of my others combined. Between learning how to screenwrite from scratch, to all the life skills he tries to instill in his students, I am thankful to have been a part of WSS and to have learned from him the past two years.
Mike is awesome. It's clear he cares greatly about his students. He is here because he actually loves teaching. He knows so much about screenwriting. Take this class.

Laid-back, witty, smart, cares deeply about film and his students. Some may dislike his blunt, old-school attitude but I appreciate that he always says exactly what he thinks. Cultivates a genuine connection with students and turns lectures into a conversation, making every class engaging and fun. Easily the best professor I've had at UNC.

Mike is the best professor I've had at UNC. He's hilarious, and his bluntness is never insensitive. He really cares about his students and treats them like the young adults they are. He's been a hugely influential mentor. He's not an Ivory Tower professor - he's pragmatic, no-BS, and empathetic. Take as many classes with him as you can.

One of my favorite professors I've ever had. That said, there's not much middle ground with Mike, I find that people either really vibe with him or they don't. He's got a really refreshing perspective on teaching and the industry as a whole and you'll learn a ton from him. He loves his students and wants them to succeed. Take a class with him!

Super hilarious and very knowledgable about the industry, I recommend this class for anyone who is interested in screenwriting, even if you don't plan on applying to the minor. Mike also makes it a point to give the class opportunities outside of school to gain industry experience. Class is not hard as long as you put in effort.

Professor Acosta is hilarious. Constantly made me enjoy my time in his classroom and was very caring when it came to students learning. He gave great feedback that helped me improve in screenwriting and even tried to give opportunities outside of class for students to expand their portfolios.

Professor Acosta is my favorite professor I've had at UNC so far! He was hilarious, encouraging, gave very applicable and useful lessons, and got the whole class excited about screenwriting. Assignments were very doable and graded for completion. I highly recommend taking a class with him if you get the chance.

(This rating is for 330 but still applies) Acosta is an amazing teacher!  Take a class with him if you have any interest in writing or media.  He is a very engaging speaker and you will enjoy going to class.  The workload is not heavy and he says that you can get an A as long as you put effort in.

Acosta can be a little irreverent so i might avoid him if you know you've got a thinner skin, but as a writer and teacher, he is amazing. Great feedback, great handle on storytelling and art direction, and underneath all the rowdy exterior he's a big softy who cries at well-written scripts. Class is super entertaining and it's easy to do well.

Absurdly easy. Lectures aren't mandatory and all material comes from slides, which he posts online. No point attending class if you don't want to. HW can be done as a group. Tests are really easy (my ECON 101 class was 3 times as hard!) He's pretty funny and a good lecturer.  Microeconomics need not be daunting with Ackermann. Recommended!19940

Jeff is a super nice guy and his lectures (that you definitely don't have to attend) are funny. However, his tests are not written by him so they don't relate well to what he lectures on in class. It should all be super easy, but I was definitely caught off guard with a horrible final that ruined my grade. Glad it's over.

His class seems easy until you have a test. He doesn't writes his own homework or tests so they don't correspond to his lectures very well. Also, a lot of times he doesn't really know what he's talking about. He's funny so his lectures aren't too boring and there's not much work outside of class but the tests took me off guard.
This is a tough class mostly because the professor doesn't know what he's talking about. He is good at teaching the specific material, but he lacks basic knowledge of topics taught in ECON 101.
Class was not the best. The professor also made me feel uncomfortable. Like, my eyes are up here.

Great FYS - delved into a lot of interesting topics. Extremely discussion-heavy. You get as much out of it as you put in, learning and grade-wise. Besides being a cool guy, he will save your life if you need any help at all with your papers so go see him! Grading's a bit unclear but he seems to notice effort and it reflects. Got an A.

The papers are the main part of the class. They were slightly difficult because they were on such odd topics I was not used to writing on. Overall, the class was really good. Discussions were very interesting and you read good documents and novels. I would definitely take this class again.

Neel is a super nice guy who is very knowledgable about Caribbean literature. That said, when it is time to write the multiple 7-page papers, you will end up in his office hours and he will save you. He doesn't grade easy and expects you to have it together when you come to class. Participation is key in this class. I would take it again though!

Mr. Ahuja taught the most interesting freshman seminar I could've imagined. He was clear and the work was SO manageable, he was understanding and encouraged us to participate (very necessary!). But overall it was such a great class and there aren't many assignments- barely even did the readings. Take his class!

This class was awesome. Dr. Ahmed was super layed back and the entire course reflected that. Your grades off of 2 midterms and 1 final (not cumulative) and 2 group presentations. It's very much show up do the work and an A is almost guaranteed. I don't think anyone got under a 80 on any exam or presentation.

This class was very easy in comparison to other bio courses. All midterms and final was take home and were graded very fairly with clear feedback. Only two group presentations and you get to choose your groups. Overall, I highly recommend this class to help boost your science GPA.
Great prof, never showed up to class and only showed up when it was my turn to present. Take home test and finals. He also records lectures and host it on zoom. Easy BIOL 400+ class!!!

I actually took 546, but it was an easy class, as long as you take enough notes to understand the material, all you have to do to succeed is rewatch the lectures and write down what he says with your understanding on the open note tests. He clearly wants everyone to get an A and grades group presentations nicely. Helps if you go to office hours.
This man does not tip servers when he goes to restaurants.

Professor Ahmed is a wonderful professor and is highly educated on the topic of genetics. I was able to appreciate the in-person class environment which was helpful. The lectures are dense but thoughtfully developed. Fair grading for the take-home exams. Attendance will benefit you. Overall a kind soul and low stress environment.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Overall great class and, Professor Ahmed is one of the best professors I've had. He's always happy to answer any questions in/outside of class. Classes like this where you're genuinely interested in learning about certain fields is why I chose to be a bio major at unc! but guess you gotta go through the sometimes not so fun pre-reqs first.

I had the hardest semester of my undergrad career due to personal reasons, but I feel so fortunate that I took his class bc he was super caring and passionate about the material. The written exams are more application-based instead of retaining specific info & the class was actually interesting. Definitely learned a lot about aging.

Amazing lecturer and explained concepts really well. You can tell he really cares about his students and teaching. Very test heavy however but not too difficult of a course as long as you go to class. Really accessible outside of class and posts his notes right before the midterms/final. Not hard but you'll have to put in some effort for an A

Andy is a great and caring person who answered every single question with much consideration and patience. My only issue with the course is the structure of the class (2 exams, final replaces lowest midterm, homework grades). Very little resources to help students properly prepare for exams and a bad exam can tank your grade. Great guy though.
WOW, andy is one of the best teachers I've had at UNC, he is the sweetest guy who cares about his students. He is very open to meeting outside of class and tests are very similar to practice problems
Eh ok I guess

Fantastic lecturer, always energetic and engaging. You can tell he is truly passionate about the material and teaching it to his students. He cares about each of his students on an academic and personal level. His class was genuinely interesting and the material was important. I know many other STAN majors who are interested in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This was the hardest course I ever took, but Andy is a FANTASTIC teacher. He truly loves the material & is very enthusiastic. You'll be writing R code to analyze complicated stats, so knowing calc helps. I understood very little of what was said in lecture just because I didn't know math. Overall, a rewarding class if you're willing to put in work!

Andy genuinely cares about his students. His grading criteria is clear but if any questions arise, he is quick to clarify and communicate. His aim is clearly for the students in his class to actually learn, grow, interact with each other and the material, and come away with a stronger understanding of both statistics and ethical considerations.

Andy is the best instructor I have had at UNC Chapel Hill. He is extremely accessible and cares for his students, having great availability outside of class. Andy's passion for teaching is inspiring and his class is applicable to all aspects of life, making it well worth it. I continue to build off what I learned in lecture, I highly recommend!

i am of the belief that actions speak louder than words and it felt that often this professor was focused more on sounding like they had good intentions than actually acting as someone who truly had good intentions towards their students. to clarify on this, i often felt that the bare minimum effort was put in covered up by enthusiastic lectures

If Andy has managed to keep me, a graduating senior in an 8AM class, then you know he's done something right. His enthusiasm in each lecture makes the most boring topics engaging. He encourages students to participate, from discussions on ethics to math principles. He is accessible via email or OH and goes above and beyond to support his students.

Unclear grading criteria and a bit argumentative at times in class. I don't think that he takes diversity into account much when creating his syllabus or discussing outcomes of thought experiments which myself and a few others students in the course felt was ironic given this special topics course focus on morality and ethics.
Overvalues participation being that many topics can be self taught but is an interesting lecturer to listen to.

Grading expectations are made clear on syllabus however exams count for majority of your grade. If you aren't a good test taker, he makes the exams heavily conceptual and does not provide many resources outside of class. Office hours are limited and he/TA would not provide feedback on any of the exams, so you'd have to meet with them personally

Great professor, what a wonderful guy. Super caring, and will answer every single question you throw out at him, and is great for office hours. Beware, he doesn't record lectures, and only writes on chalkboard, other than that, I loved the guy, but his class is a little harder than every other professor. I would take him again for sure.
Really good professor for Statistics. If you're taking STOR 155, this is the guy you want. Explains things very clearly and the class never feels like it's going too fast.

STOR455: Andy has by far been my favorite professor at UNC. Andy went above and beyond to care for and ensure that every student understood the material. the most caring, sweetest, knowledgeable, respectful, and overall amazing professors I have ever had the opportunity of learning from. I will definitely be taking more classes with him.
Review for Stor 113. Great guy! Genuinely wants students to succeed and is always willing to explain concepts. Lets you replace your lowest midterm with your final.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: You get a cheat sheet on your exams & drops the lowest midterm if your final is higher! Overall, he's great and genuinely wants you to succeed. He's very accessible and a good teacher, even though math isn't my strong suit. All lectures are on a chalkboard w/ no recordings, so if you miss content, you'll have to ask a friend for notes. Recommend :)

Super cool chill guy and good lecturer, very passionate about his job and statistics. 2 or 3 easy homeworks a week, drops lowest midterm(if final is higher) can overexplain things but sometimes that is appreciated. Best Stor 155 professor based on those I know who have had different ones. Straightforward and approachable. Take his class!

The goat. Awesome guy who loves to teach. He genuinely cares for his students, their well-being, and their performance in class. He talks to the students often and wants to know them well. He's super chill and loves to help also. 5/5 Great guy and would so take his class again!

Excellent professor, super passionate, and very caring. Though, exams are difficult and tested a lot on statistical concepts. He was generous in providing practice exam problems, but ultimately we had no good way to practice for concepts. Too much to bank on when exams are weighted so heavily. No stats exam should have a true or false section.

Super chill and cool guy, very personable. I believe he taught the class well, some people complain that the course was quite difficult, and that's going to come with any sort of statistics class. Overall, I thought he was great and it was very cool that he made an effort to get to know students.

Pretty cool guy. Chill, easy to reach, and always super helpful! Though would teach things a very specific way and then would throw curveballs on exams. No matter how confident I was in the material, exams were super stressful, even with a cheat sheet. Had plenty of conceptual questions on exams that didn't make sense for an intro level course!

Very available outside of class which is great however he is not very accommodating for extenuating circumstances. Tests are extremely conceptual based and conceptual-based material is barely brushed on in lectures making the exams quite hard. Class was done completely on a chalkboard and refused to post notes until a few days before the exam
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Andy is really good. Many office hours and very kind. THe only thing is that he did not give practice exams. You may need more time outside the classroom.

Great teacher, genuinely cares about stats and explains the material thoroughly. But the exams he makes are really hard compared to the classwork and homework. Even if you really know the material, exams are still bound to be challenging. Would not take again just to save my gpa but overall super nice and funny guy.

Andy was a good lecturer and funny. He was passionate about his teaching, explained concepts well in class, and was ready to help students. However, he was a bit stringent with deadlines so don't expect extensions. The course should involve more hands-on coding instead of just looking at code in lectures as I had to revise old lectures repeatedly.

Andy is one of the best teachers I've had in 4 years at UNC, and easily the best Statistics teacher. He genuinely cares about his students and is always available to answer questions. I had a bad experience with the group project, but Andy was very sympathetic and accommodating when I talked with him. Take him if you get the chance, I promise.
Nice guy, nice lectures, easy homework and labs. HOWEVER, GROUP PROJECT GRADINGS WERE EXTREMELY TOUGH SO BE AWARE OF THAT.

Best professor I have had in the statistics department. Actually cares about teaching and for his students. The kind of teacher you actually want to be friends with. I had a family emergency and he was super accommodating. Whenever I asked questions during office hours or over email, he was extremely helpful. Would give him a 10/5 if I could.

Andrew seems to care about his students, but it isn't always apparent in his actions. He has highly stringent deadlines that have sharp grade cut-offs for even being just a few hours late, (sometimes even a 0%). Lab TAs lack any semblance of motivation or urgency to help students. Andy seems nice but he doesn't really care.

Andy is one of the best professors I have had at UNC. He genuinely cares about each of his students and wants you to succeed. His lectures were interesting and easy to understand (and I am not a math person). Expectations for exams are clear and he prepares you well for them. Take Andy if you have the chance!

Andy was the best instructor I've had at UNC thus far. He was kind, patient, and cares about his students. He actually made math fun. I took Stor 113 and 155 with him and it's not an easy A but if you put in the work you will get good results. Definitely choose Andy as your instructor he is great!
The best, super cool guy, for sure take with him.

Andy was really great. Expectations on tests are made clear with review sessions and he's very cool and approachable. His explanations of concepts were great. While we worked out problems he walked around & asked everyone how they were doing (alleviates question-asking anxiety). If you're gonna take STOR 155, take it with Andy.

Stan was a very kind and considerate professor however was not the best lecturer. The lectures were mainly watching professors code and follow along without a lot of explanation as to why things were done. This course would be much easier if you have an understanding of programming beforehand, however is not impossible without any.

Stan is a good professor but the class design for Comp-116 was not good at all. It was all lectures, including the recitation, where the class would only involve copying what the professors are typing down. With it being a lecture heavy class, there was absolutely no engagement. Also, there was a big leap in difficulty in the assignments.

Professor Ahalt taught this class with Professor Krishnamurthy, and I loved it. For me, the workload in this class was very manageable. Both professors were extremely understanding of students struggling with mental health and other issues that kept them from completing work. I would highly, highly recommend this course.

Dr. Ahalt taught this class with Dr. Krishnamurthy and together they were an awesome dynamic duo! The workload isn't tough and it's easy to end with a good grade, but the best part is listening to two great data science minds work through problems in lecture. You get a great intro to Python, and I would highly recommend taking the class!
Goated

A fantastic professor and cool guy. He taught this semester tag-team with Dr. Krishnamurthy, and both were great! The course is very well designed. Lectures are helpful but not required if you read the book. Course is easy not in the sense that it's a joke but that you'll know how to code by the time it's done. Highly recommend!

One of the better lecturers I have had at Carolina. He used a lot of mathematical terms to explain some of the concepts and then explained it in a more general way. Overall, I think he was one of the most enthusiastic professors I have had when it comes to being excited about the material.

One of the most passionate and compassionate teachers I've ever had at UNC.  The work is substantial but relevant and interesting.  The final is a creative group project which turns out to be pretty fun.  He's a really cool guy that really just wants you to learn code and it's importance in our world.

The best professor I've had at UNC. He obviously cares about what he's teaching, and that the students learn the material. He asks for input changes the pace of the class based on what students tell him. It's easy to understand him and to get help from him. As an added bonus, he's actually an entertaining professor even in lectures.

I had to take this course for my major but would recommend to anyone. LOVED katie-- there was a lot of reading assigned but honestly if you don't do it she does a great job of explaining everything in class. only 2 papers and 2 exams and both were straightforward and graded very fairly. 10/10 would take another class with her!!

Katie is great - lectures can be a little dry, but readings aren't necessary because she explains everything in class. Always willing to help outside of class, very helpful. As long as you take notes and pay attention in class, you'll do well
Enjoyed her POLI 236 class. Interesting topic--lectures are sometimes a bit long, but grading criteria and exams are straightforward.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Even though the material wasn't the most interesting Katherine was able to clearly and concisely convey it during lectures. Exams were straightforward and there was only one paper. I would definitely recommend her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: WORST poli sci class I've ever taken and I'm a poli sci major who's loved every class so far. She is completely unclear in lectures, has white slides with black writing and she always stood in the corner and talked pretty quietly. Her voice tapered off toward the end of really important sentences so you wouldn't know what was going on. STAY AWAY!

Favorite prof at Carolina. Class is so engaging and fun. He has many stories from his AT days. If you study you will get an A. That said I'm not done with the class but I have a 99 rn. Very accessible and so kind. You have learning checks and exit tickets that you get the dates for, so don't miss those classes. Such a fun class so show up.

Really enjoyable class, he teaches things multiple ways to accommodate different styles of learning, and is always happy to answer questions and hear what students are struggling with. Class is very centered around the needs of the students, and his learning checks and exams are written very fairly and do not try to trick you. Take his class!!

EXSS 265! Have nothing but great things to say about this professor. He is so accommodating and noticed the needs of the students grades and offered extra credit. He has personal experience from being an AT, which was interesting to hear different stories. I would take this class and highly recommend and class with him!

(FOR 265) Prof Aguilar is very funny and understanding. The class is QUIZ HEAVY and it makes up most of your grade. They can easily be tricky so keep up with ULA reviews, go to class, take notes and ask questions. Hes very accessible to help you out and offered extra credit that rlly helps ur grade.
Unorganized and unfair. Not consistent between semesters and many exam questions are worded esoterically and he expects you to read his mind. Not as lenient and fair as he tries to let on.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very fun class. He's hilarious and I would recommend the class for anyone who may be interested.

Took 265 with him. He was a very entertaining lecturer which made things easy to understand and remember. Class is very chill and easy. He's the type of professor who is happy if everyone gets an A. He has lots of stories from personal experience which are fun. He also keeps standing on top of his desk for no reason which is funny

I took 265 with him. Dr. Aguilar is probably the best professor I've had at UNC so far. His lectures are engaging, and he really cares about what he is teaching which makes everything so much more engaging.

Alain is nice and very accommodating. He tries to be very understanding. I just found lectures to be a bit boring and I did not like his use of nearpod. The course was also pretty unorganized and I'm sure it will become better with experience. Felt like our class were the guinea pigs a bit. The test format is very strange. I took 265 with him.

I loved 408 with Alain. He is a super chill, kind guy with a lot of knowledge about strength training and exercise in general. Some classes are hands-on (going to Ram's, using foam rollers), which I enjoyed a lot. Grade is based on a few assignments, class attendance, an exam and two projects. Great for lifters who want to learn more!

Love professor Aguilar, he might be my favorite at UNC! Only 1 exam which is take home and like 12 questions. You will learn so much and Aguilar is so insanely nice. His class is engaging and often you participate in the exercises you learn about which can be fun. This is a great class for aspiring fitness/rehab personnel, I recommend it!

Dr. Aguilar is my favorite professor I have had at Carolina. His classes are relatively easy, but I learned so much. Alain has a way of making everything interesting and engaging. I have never written a review on RMP, but thought he was deserving of one. Dr. Aguilar was kind, compassionate, and made me want to come to every class.

Professor Aguilar is one of my favorite professors to have had at UNC (I'm graduating and specifically came back to his page to recommend him). The class is interesting and very applicable to people that go to the gym and enjoy working out. Aguilar is incredibly kind, approachable outside of class, and all-round a great teacher. Take Alain!

I love Prof. Aguilar! Probably the best professor I have ever taken. He's super funny, kind, understanding, and knows his stuff. Never makes you feel dumb for asking a question. I wish I could take him again!

What an awesome professor. He genuinely cares about his students and is passionate about what he teaches. He knows what he's talking about and he will help you get unscrambled. Take good notes! I should've taken better, but if you put in the work, listen, and take notes, you got it.

Mr. Aguilar has been one of my favorite professors at UNC so far. He is very knowledgable about what he teaches and his passion for the content and his students comes through in his lectures. He makes sure each person gets their question answered. If it is not answered in class, he is always just a text away.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Really passionate about the material. Genuinely wants students to learn and succeed. Fair grader but you need to study constantly.
She is super sweet and the class itself is not hard if you pay attention. No textbook or anything like that and the homework she assigns takes like 5 minutes. I love her she's the best
Prof Majewska is so kind and genuine. She prepares us well for exams and announces what topics will be on each quiz/test beforehand. It is not difficult to get an A in this class.

Professor Majewska is a very sweet and authentic Polish Professor. She gives a daily completion homework, the occasional graded homework, four quizzes, two tests and a final presentation. Everything is super easy and requires mild-to-moderate effort. Everything is easily outlined, and her lessons are easy to follow. I am\ taking 402 and 403.
Pani Majewska is such a nice lady and she will give you feedback on anything you may have questions with. The homework and quizzes are light. Excited for the next 2 semesters!

Majewska is an absolute gem. I went in with 0 Polish knowledge and ended up having her for 3 semesters. She is very understanding and is as helpful as she can be. The key to her class is quizlets and repetition. There are plenty of opportunities for grades and the final exam is a low percentage of the grade.

Dr. Majewska is an awesome teacher and human being. Even though I was TERRIBLE at Polish, I still enjoyed all three semesters I took with her. If you are looking for a new language to try out rather than go through Spanish or French for your language credit, Polish is definitely worth a try.

Dr. Majewska is awesome. She's really funny and caring, and the class itself is quite easy, especially compared to other language classes at UNC. I am a very poor language learner, but I was still able to be quite successful in polish. I would encourage anybody who does not already have their language requirement completed to take polish with her.

Polish is a niche language- classes are small & Dr. Majewska is an incredible professor. I've had her from 401-403 & couldn't recommend more. The class is very participation heavy but if you can't make a class she records them. Short daily homework, a few quizzes, 2 tests, a short final project, and a final. Easier than most other language classes!

Professor Majewska is awesome. She really encouraged us to participate and become better at speaking Polish. She was always super open to questions and had a really easy-to-follow curriculum. About 15-20 minutes of homework each but no big large outside-of-class time sinks. Highly recommend.

She loves to quiz you on tiny things she mentions in lecture. The class is not hard overall, but you have to memorize specific details (ex: what species is the first to use tools). The assigned books (4) are interesting, but you have to read a lot each week. Recitation attendance is taken and focuses on the book vs lecture being random material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I found the subject matter very interesting, but it was sometimes difficult to follow what she was trying to get us to learn. The tests were very easy, with huge extra credit opportunities (eight points on each one!). The projects were great introductions to each field of anthropology. She seems quite passionate about the subject.

This class is very easy. Lowest test and quiz grade is dropped, the final counts as a quiz. She offers extra credit on quizzes. Projects were easy and fun. Going to lectures is very important, the slides have little information. I recommend taking detailed notes in lectures. She is very passionate about her research and and I enjoyed her lectures.

Terrible lectures. Overall, the class wasn't too bad, but I didn't learn much from her teaching style. She talks slowly, and her lectures are hard to follow because she doesn't put the important information on the slides. The projects are straightforward and generally enjoyable, so getting a good grade isn't hard.

lectures can get boring sometimes and are a lot of information with barely any words on slideshows, have to actually attend lectures to do well on quizzes. instructor really cares about what she talks about and i found the lecture content to be super interesting and cool to learn about!

The class in general was not that hard, 5 projects over the course of the semester that are relatively easy. Her lectures however are all over the place with little to no explanation on her slides. The quizzes are hard for no reason, 50% of the questions are common sense and the others are about things she briefly mentioned in lecture.

I love Dr. Agbe-Davies! She's an incredible person and spoke about her research a lot during her lectures, which made the class interesting. She simplifies major concepts in anthropology and assignments are easy. She made me fall in love with anthropology (med-anth is my major now!!)

The class itself isn't terrible and is actually relatively easy. Agbe-Davies is a very nice person, but she is just a really bad lecturer. She tends to go on rants about her own experience and doesn't teach much material. The slides have one word on them so notes are incredibly difficult to obtain. Plus she doesn't record any of her lectures.

I didn't know my grade the entire semester because everything was weighted weirdly, so it was hard even to calculate it myself. The quizzes were hard for no reason. You have to go to every class to do well on the quizzes because they ask extremely specific questions. Lectures are so boring, I fell asleep a lot. Shocked that I got an A.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While the content discussed in class was interesting, it was presented to us in an extremely unorganized way. Terms were shown with no definition unless you raised your hand to ask and it was a large lecture hall which made doing so difficult. Information on projects were given to us the week that project was due so we could not work ahead at all.

The structure of this class was very lecture-heavy, Professor Agbe-Davies has interesting content however, her PowerPoint slides had little to no information on them which made it difficult to prepare for the quizzes. We were given a project in the last week of class and we could not see instructions for it until the week of.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The structure of this class is extremely frustrating. While Agbe-Davies presents interesting content, her slides are unhelpful w/ one word + pic. Assignments are either graded harshly or easily, and grading timelines are inconsistent. AND we were given a project in the last week of class and we could not see instructions for it until the week of.

If you don't go to lecture, you won't know what's going on.
She doesn't give definitions unless you raise your hand in lecture and ask. 
She assigns chapters upon chapters of reading every week.
DO NOT take this class if you want to learn. BECAUSE YOU WONT!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She was a great professor. Her lectures were interesting, but she was a very slow grader. She was clearly invested in her subject.

Professor Agbe-Davies was very kind and passionate about her work as an anthropologist. You can tell she enjoys the subject and it's very contagious. There are very few graded assignments other than class participation and papers, but be sure to attend class. She's not the best at email replies.

If you want to learn nothing and be in a "woke" class this is perfect for you. No teacher feedback, each class period is her rambling the whole time. Learned nothing, first test was on September 15th... got my grade back December 16th. Bullshi*t man.... felt like a middle school environment and there was never emphasis on helping students grow

Great teacher and a nice person... however the way she teaches her class is absurd. 3 grades the entire semester, and you won't receive a score for any of them until two weeks after the course is over. Lectures weren't informative, boring, and had to relation to the 3 assignments. Assignment instructions also were no help. Avoid this seminar.

Professor Agbe-Davies is very passionate about her teaching, however, she is a very slow grader. Throughout the whole semester, I did not know what my grade was because she didn't put anything in the grade book. This makes it very difficult for me to calculate my GPA.

This was a wonderful class on professional development. Professor Agbe-Davies clearly respects students + their contributions and uses a grading contract that is very fair. She is very open to student feedback + taking lead of the class. One of those classes where you get out what you put in.

Tbh not worth taking. It was super boring and just not what I wanted. Keeps 4 out 5 quiz and project grades with an additional participation grade. No final or midterm. Read four books instead of a textbook. I only liked one of the books the rest were not interesting. The prof was nice it just isn't interesting and I really like social sciences
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Agbe-Davies is pretty good. I find that the lectures were pretty iffy. It's hard to catch up if you miss stuff, so hopefully your recitation peers will be helpful. But she is very reliable and gets back to you in a timely manner. As long as you go to lectures and take notes, you should be fine. Tests and projects are easy.

I enjoyed her class but I  was a little confused by her way of teaching. The slides do not help, especially if you are not in class. She does not record the lectures, you have to be in class in order to get the information. She also caps project grades at 95 which is frustrating.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: attendance is optional but she makes it impossible to get the material outside of class. she doesn't film lectures or provide material if you were out sick. her slides just have pictures and maybe one word, which makes it pretty hard to learn from if you are not in class. there are 5 projects that are all unnecessarily hard and hard to follow.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Agbe-Davies is extremely nice! However, I personally found the class to be very confusing and found the work load to be unnecessarily heavy. While there aren't too many assignments, the ones we did have were challenging from start to finish. Though, she does welcome students to ask for clarification and feedback.

Professor Agbe-Davies was great! The content was interesting which made the class bearable. The lectures were long and not much on the slide, but important information came from them. She is super understanding and really easy to talk to or email.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She is so enthusiastic about her work and makes it fun to learn. She's also very understanding!

This was just a dumb class. Powerpoints had one word and pictures that had nothing to do with it. It doesn't really matter how much you study, you still won't know what you are doing. I thought this was going to be an easy A and it was anything but.

Despite ANTH101 being a huge lecture, Professor Agbe-Davies still manages to make it interesting. The readings and course material were very interesting to me and I learned a lot. When I took this course there were 5 quizzes and 4 projects that our grades were based on, and all were relatively easy and straightforward.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Prof. Agbe-Davies is very enthusiastic about teaching this class, and seems like a really nice woman. However, I personally struggled with tests (which are a big part of the grade) because she is very vague in her lectures. She does not give concrete definitions and goes off on tangents while lecturing.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She's chill, interesting, and caring. Need to go to class bc her slides only have vocab words. I thought the class was fairly easy. Get a good TA, do the readings, and take notes.

Professor is really sweet and passionate, but she doesn't go in depth in lecture yet asks tricky questions on the tests. Only a few questions come from the books,so reading them is not essential to doing well. Overall, you must do a lot of cramming and looking up things she never explained. Projects are grade boosters (make sure you get a good TA).
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests? Not many--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: lectures are very abstract and hard to follow. many questions on quizzes seemed to have nothing to do with her lectures or the readings. if you take this class find quizlets before each quiz
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Grades based on tests and projects. Lectures are so boring and vague. They aren't a lot of work and she drops the lowest but not an easy A. She never answers questions. She goes in circles and never gets to a point. You can study for a long time and maybe do well or maybe not. Studying is irrelevant because her tests are so random.

Agbe-Davies is extremely passionate about Anthropology, and her own work especially. Her lectures mostly consist of her incoherently rambling and going off on tangents about unrelated topics. Her lectures slides are just photos with a green background that have no terms or definitions. Sometimes she doesn't even define the terms in class.

Get ready to google a lot of terms for yourself to figure out what the heck they are. Her lecture presentations are incredibly abstract and useless... you end up having to teach yourself everything while you study. Being in class is better than not being in class, but incredibly boring and tangents are frequent.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Overall, she tries to make the course interesting and engaging but fails at times. Doesnt give good definitions and her material/presentations can seem disorganized at times. Dont take her class if you plan on skipping class bc although her exams are pretty easy you need to show up to class to do well. Her projects are pretty useless.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She's a good professor but the quizzes are straight from the lectures and the books. If you're not paying attention every second during the lecture, you get screwed over in the quizzes. She calls them quizzes but they're 60% of your course grade. The good part is you don't have friday classes if you take this Anth class except when we have a quiz.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Prof. A-D was a really great prof! I was always engaged by lectures, but beware - she puts barely any words on her slides, so attendance at lecture is important. I never had any problems missing info tho, even taking handwritten notes. Recitation sucked, but Prof was interesting and very responsive to questions. Highly recommend!

Professor Agbe-Davies is a very nice person, but teaching is not her strong-suit. Her PowerPoints are pretty useless as slides only contain about 2-3 words. When asked for concrete definitions she usually fails to give one. The quizzes are also very ambiguous.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Very nice and cares a lot about her subject. Does not give definitions for terms so outside work is necessary. you could skip class once a week and still probably pass. Quizzes are tricky.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: This is a solid choice for a first-year seminar, especially if u want to take a class that is not high-strung but still interesting. Prof. Agbe-Davies is very knowledgeable about anthropology and is both approachable and a fair grader. It was cool being able to work with artifacts from the site
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: She is a very lenient grader and is willing to help students in completing assignments. There are weekly reflections that are completed for participation purposes. Your grade will be determined from your scores on a test, 5-page paper, and the final project. Professor Agbe-Davies is a down to earth person and definitely a good connection to have.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: I took anthropology/archaeology in bronzeville as my first year seminar, i would def. reccomend if you don't want to work hard it's super easy and interesting. i almost never show up to class and my grade in there is still fine. a midterm, 5 page paper and a final project is all you have to do besides show up. and the professor is really kind and knowledgeable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Did not enjoy.

Just terrible. Extremely boring and CONFUSING lectures that had to be rewatched multiple times to understand, homework and exams that had little to do with what was discussed in class & were both extremely hard(a lot of extrapolation to do well), and not that many assignments to be graded on. I'm an econ major, and this class made me hate econ.

Loved the class! I consider myself a micro person, so I found the material challenging, but Dr. Aguilar has a way of making things interesting and relevant to current events. You definitely have to work hard and attend office hours to clarify concepts, but as long as you stay on top of your game you can definitely do well in the course!

ECON 420 is a hard class, but Aguilar & the TAs are both helpful & friendly. The content of the the class is TOUGH. At first, the lectures can be overwhelming as he moves quite fast through the material, but reading the textbook in advance helps a lot. In order to get an A in this class, you'll need to put in more work than the average class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: A lot of people fail to study or reach out for help when the need it. 420 is really hard and if you dont put in the work you will not do well. Most students in this class when they do bad just blame the prof for their incompetence. pay attention and you will do well, Aguilar is great!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: During lecture he talks a lot about current events & not enough about what we should be learning. He flies through tough concepts & doesn't post complete note sets until after lectures. His exams are extremely difficult & impossible to do well if you don't understand the beginning of the class. He loves econ, just isn't the best teacher to have.

Dr. Aguilar definitely makes you work for a good grade in his class. However, once you get the hang of how his class runs, it's really not that bad. The homeworks are challenging, but you can work on them with friends and the tests were curved. He often gets distracted by discussing current events, but ask him questions to get him back on track.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: 425 is probably the hardest class I've taken at UNC. That said, I would strongly recommend this course to anyone looking to work in finance or just anyone with an interest in finance. You need to make sure you are good with basic finance, stats, calculus, and macro. Learned a lot and will be applying it at my new job, that's what matters.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: ECON is challenging at UNC, everyone knows this. Aguilar is very knowledgeable and you can tell he really wants students to succeed. This class is extremely hard and if you don't get concepts initially you will struggle because you build on everything from the very first lecture. Go to the ECON aid center and office hours and you'll be fine.

425 is impossibly difficult. Avoid it at all costs. I really regret not dropping this class. His curves are the only reason anyone survives. He's a generous grader, but the tests and homeworks are really ridiculous. His practice exams are pointless because they look absolutely nothing like the actual exam. Seriously difficult class. Avoid!

Professor Aguilar has, BY FAR, the best resources I've ever seen for a class. He has dozens of practice problems (with youtube videos explaining them) for every class topic, and impressive "templates" to help with math-oriented stuff. However, his midterm is nothing like the HW, and you will fail it. Curve helps your overall grade though.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Tough grader

reviews.comment: ECON 420 with Professor Aguilar is not an easy class in any way, but he gives you all of the tools you need to succeed. There is a lot of information and you will have to work on your own at times to connect it all together, but it is very rewarding if/when you do.

Best professor I've had. Teaches all perspectives and not just the perspective of the left like many UNC professors. Take this class if you want to learn the Economics of the real world. It's hard work don't take it for an easy A

Dr. Aguilar is knowledgeable and a great storyteller. However, the class structure is a bit messy. It would be a lot better if they added a recitation to focus solely on the math every week. Its easy to feel like you understand the theories he talks about in lecture but then not recognize any math once you open the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He is full of knowledge, but cannot teach it in a practical way. I don't know how to apply these theories after learning his class.

Reiterating what many have said, Aguilar is a cool person and very knowledgeable. The class is poorly structured, and the homework assignments/practice exams don't bear much resemblance to the exams. Be sure to be thorough with homework, and go to help sessions. He makes this class pretty math-heavy, so be ready for that.
He's a nice guy but not a great lecturer. He describes the materials rather than explains them which makes no sense to me. He puts lots of weight on current events so make sure you get those points.

Mike spends a lot of his time keeping the class up to date on current events. The homeworks are doable and end up counting a lot for your final grade, so make sure you get the points here. The midterm and final are completely blinding material and there is not much for you to prepare for them.

Alright, so this class is challenging, but dont be fooled its not impossible. You can do well if you read the textbook and do a lot of practice questions. Aguilar is a decent teacher. Hes not bad but hes not great, despite the two extremes you usually hear about him.

Aguilar is nice but his class is terrible. He expects everyone to know a lot about macro coming into the class so he doesn't explain topics in detail. The exams are nothing like the homework so it is hard to prepare. If you pay attention in class and write everything down, you have a shot at doing well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Aguilar is a well-respected guy, but he made this course unnecessarily difficult. It was more math than concept/theory. If you also don't have any background knowledge about macro, you will struggle. He assumes that everyone has knowledge about macro and doesn't go in depth when he explains concepts.

Worst prof I've ever had. He just runs around the classroom and never explains anything. If you get confused in the slightest you won't be able to figure it out because he doesn't give any resources explaining anything and he changes the notion from the book a lot so you can't even look there for help. Cool guy and approachable, but awful teacher
Mike Aguilar's financial econ was the single most valuable class from my four years in college. It is the one that will set you up for the real world.

Aguilar is a great professor but definitely has his drawbacks. He focuses on the theory in class and is a great storyteller which makes class interesting, but it means that you have to read the textbook and do problems on your own. Many people expect that just going to class is okay, but if you read the textbook and do hw you'll get an A.

Dr. Aguilar is one of my favorite professors at UNC, teaching one of the hardest courses I've ever had. He understands how difficult the work can be for incoming students, and tries his best. Sometimes his teaching style (or how he explains the math) can be a bit obtuse, but he is always in office hours or ready after class to answer questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Quite honestly the hardest class I've taken at Carolina. ECON 410 was a breeze compared to this class. Also, MSA is so much more organized and clear in her instruction than Aguilar. Try to take the class w someone else that can explain content in a less convoluted/frantic manner. Save yourself the trouble and avoid.

425 isn't as bad as 420, especially if you've taken 470/570 and a decent amount of statistics. Still difficult but smaller class size makes the atmosphere feel more fun. As with 420, the HW has very little to do with lectures and you must teach yourself most material. The group project is a total pain

To be completely honest, it's pretty unlikely you're going to pull off the A in this course. If you come to terms with that then this class isn't that bad, just go to the TA's and beg them for the HW answers and you'll end up with a mid to high B because they're worth almost as much as exams. Your mental health will suffer, your GPA will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I do not understand the Aguilar cult following at all. I found his lectures to be extremely dry and unnecessary to understanding the material. He makes the class very calc heavy which is completely unnecessary. Also he does not give you near enough time on his tests. After you finish the essay section, you have about 5 minutes to guess 6 MC ?'s

Aguilar is kind and helpful if you actually go to him with questions, but he doesn't put effort into the class organization. He gives you everything you need to succeed - but you need to be prepared to piece it together yourself, because there are NO resources to help you connect the dots, which is SUPER time-consuming, but SUPER rewarding

Dr. Aguilar is another math-happy econ professor that makes the content seem much harder than it is by throwing 75-minutes of math at you twice a week. With a tutor, I discovered I didn't need to do 90% of the calcs shown in class to get the answers/know the material! Aguilar is still great - HWs count for a lot, MacroJournals are fun & relevant
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Objectively the hardest class Ive taken at Carolina. This class was a nightmare to complete and the professor didnt help much. Aguilar is terrible at lecturing and attempts to explain complex concepts through running from one side of the classroom to the other.

Dr. Aguilar is a great guy, but the slides, textbook, and lectures are useless. Running wall-to-wall, arms flapping around like a coked up muppet is fun to watch, but it only taught me that Keynes is demand side, classicalists are supply side. Are the test and homework questions that simple? No way

Dr. Aguilar is the best professor I have had during my time at UNC. He genuinely cares about the learning experience. However, expect to work incredibly hard. His classes are not easy whatsoever. Despite the challenging subject matter he is more than willing to help outside of class time. I highly recommend Dr. Aguilar.

Worst professor I have ever had at any academic institution. He just can't teach. He walks from one side of the classroom then to the other (as if they were Keynesian & Classical) with his arms flapping around (not joking) telling you to use excel. I had to teach myself everything using YouTube

Dr. Aguilar is hands-down the best professor I have taken at UNC. The class may be one of the most challenging, but never have I learned so much and taken away so much value from 3 credit hours. I would highly recommend taking, but note that it is an extremely rigorous commitment.
Awesome professor that really cares and teaches very well but the class itself is very challenging. Be prepared to work hard and be confused all the time.

Aguilar's lectures, in the brief moments he would be lecturing, were fun and insightful. He's direct about what you need to know. He stops lecturing for group discussion too often though. His homework is brutal. Go to the LAs' hours. The multiple choice on his exams are similarly tough and worth too much. Negative curve makes getting an A hard.

He's a super nice, charismatic guy, which makes a lot of students (including myself) willing to overlook some of the flaws in the class. It is challenging material, but Aguilar could do more to make the class less painful. He posts very few materials online (in contrast to MSA in 410) and the textbook is quite poor.

Brilliant and nice guy, but the absolute worst professor I have ever had at any academic institution. He just can't teach. He was teaching the MAC Finance class, and it was basically him walking around the room with his arms flapping around (not joking) telling you to use excel. I had to teach myself everything using YouTube.

This class is very challenging. That being said, Aguilar does a great job teaching it. Compared to Micro (410), you will end up spending more time on homeworks and such because of the macrojournals. The material is very challenging and hard to grasp without textbook use. Take advantages of all the resources on the Sakai site.

Aguilar is a really likable guy and I think he's mostly popular because of that. This class is not easy, and it does not care if you succeed. That being said, it's very possible to succeed. Do the homeworks and understand the material and then attend help sessions for them, exams are very like the homeworks.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I am a computer science and econ double major, and this is the hardest class I have taken at UNC so far. Mike is an excellent teacher, the material is just extremely challenging, and the structure of the lectures and powerpoint are very disorganized. Get ready to work.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Great teacher, very hard exams though but marks very fairly. Lots of connections high up as well, be prepared to work hard and reading the textbook helps too.  I came very unprepared to the midterm and failed it because the material seemed so much easier when he explained it in class. picked it up for the final though

Aguilar is a great lecturer and keeps you engaged. However, the material is extremely challenging. Homework assignments require great effort, but if you do these, use the resources provided on Sakai, & read the textbook for clarification, you will be prepared going into each exam. Also, do the group extra credit. It upped my final grade!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He's obviously very passionate which makes the class more enjoyable, but the class isn't really set up to make A's very achievable.  Concepts seem simple in class but tests and homeworks are very different.  I don't think it would be possible to pass if you skip class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Does a good job connecting material to RL. Lectures give a general sense of the concepts, but you have to apply them to questions you've never seen on the HW/exams. He curves until the avg is a 75. Hard to get an A due to the grading scale, but hard to fail (generous with Cs/Bs). This is a class that's really hard to do alone. Find study buddies.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: There are times in your life when you just know a professor teaches for the right reasons. In those moments, you pause to look up and realize you are witnessing just that. Mike Aguilar is a fantastic professor. I had taken 3 courses with him at UNC and have now gone far into a PhD elsewhere. Without him, I would have never made it off the ground.

First of all he is an amazing teacher. No doubt about that.  However, the emphasis in his lectures can be misleading. He tries to give students a general sense, but his hws and exams are 90%  math. He would casually mention some points and you would likely think those are not important; they are. Don't let his economist charm fool you.
Great lectures, but difficult tests. Overall a really interested and engaging person, even if the class is really tough.

This is no easy class. Do every extra credit opportunity. Go to the help sessions and I don't just mean the one that's the night before the homework is due. Do practice questions. Ask questions. I recommend office hours for concepts/theory and help sessions for homework. Tests are doable with practice.

Very hard class but Mike is the man. Super 90's Wall Street. You will have to put in a lot of your own time if you want to do well, but it is worth it for future econ classes. The tests are very hard but not impossible. Homework is difficult but the TAs offer lots of review sessions to go through them before they are due.

Very poor quality of instruction. Class topic is complex and broad, but the professor barely explains the materialhe'll brush over it in a few seconds, and only uses about a third (literally) of total class time actually teaching. He almost never does examples, though difficult math is on tests. Expect to struggle unless you're a math genius.

420 is the bane of every econ major's existence. Aguilar makes it interesting, although the exams are impossible and the homework takes time. However, he curves well and gives opportunities for extra credit.

Professor Aguilar is clearly very smart and enthusiastic about what he teaches, which is good, except that he assumes everyone else is equally as smart and enthusiastic about the subject. I looked forward to his class every day because lectures were interesting, but the class moves very fast and the material is extremely difficult. Lots of hw.

Professor Aguilar is a great professor with extensive and interesting knowledge about the economy and its various nuances. While his lectures were fascinating and relatively easy to follow, the homework and tests were very difficult. You will not do well in this class if you don't go to lectures and TA sessions. Optional extra credit debates.

Professor Aguilar is very smart, although probably too smart for his own good. His homework and exams are very difficult and asks questions about material that hasn't always been covered.  He isn't the clearest professor, but his inclusion of current events makes the class fairly interesting. You should read the book, but you will learn a lot.

One of the toughest courses I have taken at UNC, but definitely worth it. Honestly, in this one class I feel like I've learned more about the economy than all of my other econ courses combined. AMAZING teacher. He is very difficult in terms of content and grading, but Aguilar is incredibly helpful and wants you to succeed in his class and beyond.

I got 100 on the midterm and became really lazy, so I did poorly on the final and got a B+. There are only a few multiple choice questions on the tests, which makes grades a little arbitrary. People who you know are a lot worse at the class than you can end up doing a lot better if they are lucky when guessing. If math is hard for you, good luck.

Aguilar is the best economics professor at UNC, hands down. He is not only a good researcher (which is how many professors are rated by the school), he gets really high marks on pedagogy. He just knows how to teach. We were learning some of the most difficult material I've ever seen, and he made it feel easy (sort of). Take if you like challenge.

By far the most difficult class I have taken at UNC, but even as  an intern in a totally different field, I use information learned in his class on a daily basis. If your GPA can afford to take the class, do it. Oh, and make sure you know Excel.
Tough class, but you will learn a ton through the work he requires. Any econ major should definitely take his class, otherwise you might want to save your GPA.
