I learned nothing & had a terrible experience with the project because she didn't follow the rubric & it wasn't right if it wasn't how she would do it
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She is a nice person, but she grades so so so so so much harder than all the other 203 professors. She shows no mercy for anything. I spoke during class every single day multiple times and she gave me an 85 for participation, which was very unfair. Also, I went to office hours regularly for help and she was not very helpful. I do NOT recommend her.
Extremely condescending. Not a very kind person and makes me feel like the fact that I don't know Spanish is a flaw. The fact that I have a question does not mean that I did not do my homework.

Professor Aaron is super sweet and southern! She has a fun easy going personality, but when it comes down to the actual work, she cuts no slack. she is strict to the rules and will only give you what you deserve, nothing more or less. She's  a little on the tough side, but a challenge worth taking if you want to improve your spanish.

If you are going to take SPAN 265, I highly recommend someone other than her.  She is a nice lady but doesn't teach.  Relies on class conversation for you to learn.  Then, the tests are extremely hard.  If you could get anyone else, I would highly suggest you to do so.

AWESOME TEACHER! she's so nice and genuine and really teaches with enthusiasm and passion.  She gave us gifts sometime, BUT she cuts no slack with grading. I always seemed to get 1 point away from an A -___- Other than her strictness to the rules, she's great!

Aaron was a strict teacher, but honestly that made me love Spanish and learn it a lot faster than I would with one not so strict. Sometimes she could come off as rude, but she really was one of the best professors I've had.
Great professor! She is very funny.

I don't know how she has bad reviews. she was one of my favorites. she is very nice and enthusiastic about teaching. she is very helpful and tries to clarify when people are confused. i've always been good at spanish, but I still worked hard for my grade. i think i will get a B or A in the class. overall she is a great teacher. i recommend her.

Despite all the bad reviews, I thought Dr. Aaron was very kind, enthusiastic, and helpful, if a little bit odd. Her style of teaching and obsession with the Honor Code are hard to get used to, but once you show some interest and talk to her outside of class, she is very helpful and really cares about her students.
All I have to say is that I have no idea how there are so many favorable reviews of this woman because I had a terrible experience. Her assignments and tests are nit-picky and ridiculous.

Definitely the worst professor I have had at UNC. A picky grader that does not teach you a concept, then grades you on something she has not told you how to do. For example, in my midterm she wanted me to use an example, but but that was nowhere in the instructions. She took off points for it.

The fact that this woman is a professor for upper level Spanish is an embarrassment to UNC. She does not speak Spanish fluently, her tests/quizzes/assignments are unrealistically difficult, and she doesn't tell you what the assignments are until 2 days before they're due. She is also condescending and is terrible at answering questions.

I have a 4.0 in my spanish major and got an A in professor Aaron's class despite the lack of clarity on material we would be tested on.  She is completely condescending and constantly paranoid about being taken advantage of and students cheating.  Punished the whole class for one student's complaint that test-prep info was incorrect.

Prof. Aaron is by far one of the very best professors at UNC. She is approachable and helpful, but expects your absolute best. She does not tolerate attitudes from students. She grades fairly and will go out of her way to investigate answers to questions she doesn't know off-hand. Amazing professor!
Amazing! She is very useful and makes you feel comfortable. Best language course I've taken at UNC
not approachable, condescending, horrible.

Professor Aaron teaches as if her students were in the kindergarten. She's condescending & power-hungry. She accuses students of cheating and is unforgiving of tardiness. She assigns an unreasonable amount of work and makes impossible tests. One of the worst teachers at UNC.(SPAN 369)

I took SPAN 101 at another university over the summer, and I had to make a HUGE leap into her class. I still feel like I am behind. She definitely favors the students that speak better spanish and loves students to suck up to her. When I ask for help, I feel like she is condescending and makes me feel dumb for not knowing something. NOT RECOMMEND

Aaron is an extremely enthusiastic teacher who clearly enjoys teaching. However, she can be condescending and sometimes expects more from her students than she does from herself. She's inflexible about student's homework but then takes her time getting back any grades. If you want to learn Spanish, take her. But don't expect much otherwise...
If you have a choice do not take it from her. Felt like I was a kindergardener and she does very little to answer your questions. Unapproachable.
She was awesome, really knows the material, very helpful and kept me laughing the entire time.  I would recommend her to every spanish student!
Extremely friendly, knowledgeable, approachable, and helpful.  Definitely one of my best profs so far.

Dr. Aaron was by far the best spanish professor that I have had at UNC thus far and I have taken upwards of 7 courses over the past 3 years.  I would definitely take a course being taught by Grace again!
great professor!
It's a hard class but she cares about how you do and will do anything to help.  She makes the class interesting and involves everyone, but you'll have to work hard to get the grade.
bad teacher. Don't take the class
GREAT teacher! very clear and very involved, shows obvious concern for every student and makes herself available for any student.
Nice lady, made class interesting, first Spanish class at Carolina during which I did not spend the entire time staring at the clock. Worked incredibly hard for my A, though!
Really great professor and very accesible outside of class!  But don't be expecting an easy A, even if you speak spanish well.  This is definitely a class on literature analysis!

Deb is a very funny guy who made class more enjoyable. He really wants you to ask questions. Material was a little scattered but before exams he will tell you what will be on them, I just memorized those things and got a high A on every exam. Rarely gave homework either. If you want a chill class take one with Deb.

This was a fun and low-stress class for me, the assignments might take some time but they're not super challenging. Professor Aikat is really nice and funny, and always asks if people have any questions in class.

I love him so much! While definitely not tech-savvy, he is so helpful every class and will allow you to directly ask him if your work will net you the grade you want, and he will give areas to improve if it's not what he's looking for. A delight to talk to.
Would do anything for Deb. He is so chill and truly just wants his students to succeed. Even though this was just an introductory MEJO course, Deb took everything so seriously. Just a kind soul.

Deb is super nice and helpful. His class is pretty easy minus one paper. But his grading rubric is very clear so you can achieve the grade you want if you put in the work. Other than the first paper he grades easily. He is accessible outside of class and he has several guest speakers present which are always interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: MEJO 101, in all honesty, was a complete joke of a class. I learned absolutely nothing from this course, and Professor Aikat just does not teach. Instead, he relies on the work of guest speakers to carry the entire class. It is dull and boring, and an absolute chore to pay attention to. Do not take this class unless you want an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I literally did not pay attention during class at all and I got an A+ guys. When I say that they want you to pass, THEY WANT YOU TO PASS. Just review the slides and reading lists they make before exams and you'll be good to go. The MC exam questions are so easy they're "this close" to being common sense. Take the GPA booster. You'll need it.

This class is a must take for anyone interested in the MEJO school. Classes are lectures from professors explaining the opportunities within the school. There are only a few assignments and no homework. Minimal effort required to get an A-, but if you want an A you'll definitely have to work hard and pay attention because an A is a 95. Deb is great
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This is pretty much an easy A. Lectures are interesting as they're led by various faculty in the J school, and they talk about all the different concentrations within the Mejo School- usually they were very interesting. Only 2 tests, which are comprised of readings and the lectures, so make sure you take notes during them. Attendance is mandatory.

Super easy class and Deb cares a lot about his students. If you need to take a class to add some credit hours this is a great class. Two very easy exams and a short essay. Attendance is taken every class though so you must go.

Deb is hilarious! Such a fun guy. It's somewhat hard to judge his teaching ability because the class was taught by different guest lecturers and Deb coordinated. But he communicates (A LOT) about upcoming assignments and whatnot. Tests were really easy. Super easy class, very interesting too usually!

Deb Aikat is one of the most enjoyable classes I have taken as a transfer student (including my previous college). This class is definitely one of the classes I will look back on as one of the highlights of my college career. Classes were very fun, never a dull moment and full of inspiring lectures. This class is informative, yet not overly hard.

Dr. Aikat is the most entertaining professor Ive had so far. He is a quirky guy, but is very knowledgeable about MEJO and loves teaching the subject. You definitely have to go to class because he takes attendance, but most importantly, all of the classes cover at least one topic that will be on the exam. Its an easy A as long as you go to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: I think Deb is a great teacher he sends a lot of emails but he wants his students to succeed. The class is meant to be an introductory class into the school if you are thinking journalism but aren't sure I recommend this class. This class gives you the run down from all majors within the J-school. If you are a MEJO major, this is an easy elective.

He includes a lot of guest speakers who can be very intriguing, although some are not. Very easy class, no homework except for assigned readings and then midterms/2 exams, and I highly recommend you attend class. It was very easy (for me) but sometimes can be a little inefficient, but he is a really fun professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The most inefficiently run class I've ever attended.

Dr. Deconinck was an amazing professor for BIOL 250. Her lectures are amazing and very well explained. She is accessible to answer any questions in and outside of class. I can tell that she really cares about Evolutionary Biology. Her exams can be a bit tricky, but if you study you will be fine. Project was really cool to do.

Took BIOL 250 online over the summer. I was scared from the old reviews, but I was pleasantly surprised. Might have been because she had less students in the summer, but I recommend. Open note exams worth 66% of grade, so study graphs / concepts in the slides! 12 quizzes, two dropped and a group project. Encouraged questions and answered kindly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Okay, ignore those old ratings, seriously. This professor is an absolute delight, like a caffeine shot for a class that's otherwise comatose. She's out here putting in 110% energy while half the room is basically a graveyard. Exams are based on lecture/quiz content + its open note, I don't think she can make the content any easier to understand.

Deconinck did a great job of making an easy biology class incredibly painful. She does not teach the material and she has unreasonable expectations. I went to office hours to talk about my poor exam grades, she expected us to look up primary literature about class concepts to do well on the tests.  Unfair, condescending, quick to blame students.

Not only does she teach things incorrectly, but she also blames you for being confused. She seems to have a knack for making the simplest concepts utterly confusing. Unless you enjoy banging your head against the wall in frustration, avoid Dr. Deconinck. Save yourself the headache and find a professor who knows what they're doing.

Lectures focus on everything but what is tested on exams. A lot of unnecessary material is covered in lecture, and it seems really simple and easy to understand but the exams (which she writes herself) are all trick questions or test you on reading rather than actual content. Avoid this class!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is very disorganized and taught us the wrong things during lectures. There are lots of reading quizzes that are often very confusing and can hurt your grade as she only drops 2 of 25 quizzes. While many of the concepts are common sense, the test are very confusing and she does not curve despite low averages. Avoid this class if possible!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Decononck isn't that bad, just sometimes a bit boring with lecture. The class material itself is really easy so grades aren't too much of a stress. The textbook isn't particularly helpful and can be a lot for a simple topic but if you want to be safe to get a good grade on the quizzes then read. Just use common sense and take lecture notes.
The class in general is very confusing and her responses on Piazza further confuse. My only saving grace is the BioCell notes and watching YouTube videos. Try and avoid this class with her.
I don't expect this class to be so annoying.
You'll hate biodiversity by the end of the semester.

Disorganized. Lectures, content & hw is super easy but the exams are all trick questions that tank your grade & averages were lower than what's expected for this kind of content. She is patronizing when you ask for help. I enjoy biodiversity as a subject, but this is such a frustrating & stressful class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Do not take! Says one thing then the next class says the complete opposite. Very confusing and the material isn't taught very well.

She is very disorganized and has no idea on how to properly teach information. Quizzes are worth 17% of your grade, not fair. They are due before we learn the content. The piazza is never answered. If you complain about the quizzes, she says it's your fault. I loved biodiversity, now I don't. Please, save me from this semester.

She has absolutely no clue what is going on in this class. The piazza is constantly confusing and she frequently contradicts the syllabus in terms of what is graded and required. She is quick to blame others for her poor class structure and lack of prep. Decent person but has no idea how to teach and makes this class an anxiety-induced headache.
I really enjoyed her class :)
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: First of all, he is condescending. Second, he grades homework very harshly. Third, no curve. The perfect class to fail even if you study for it.

Don't take the class with him whatever it takes! He is a very tough grader and condescending. Even if you are smart, your grade will tank for sure. He is even bad as a lecturer. He talks fast and does not explain things clearly.

Besides the fact that Aidan curves, I don't have one good thing to say about the class. Homework was horribly graded as he takes out points for everything wrong but doesn't give you points for everything correct. The exams were super difficult and much worse than previous exams. The whole semester was stressful and I was lucky to end up with a B.

He grades the homework really harshly, but goes easier on tests, so it balances out. If you get frustrated by unclear handwriting, definitely listen to the other reviews. He isn't a terrible lecturer, he mostly just copies the book in what he covers in class. No zoom option. Also I was scared to ask questions, he can be condescending.

One of the hardest classes I've taken in 4 years at UNC. Aidan is definitely not a bad guy, but he came across as condescending at times and the lectures were very hard to follow (illegible handwriting and spoke way too fast), so I had to teach myself the material through the textbook. Exams were hard, and grading was often contradictory.
Tough class, but good guy. Really helpful during office hours, and curves the exams to help students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I'm going to disagree with the bad reviews. I have had serious health issues this semester and Mr. Young has been accommodating, professional, and kind to me through it all. This is a tough class, which is no fault of the professor despite what others said. Expect to study hard because it is not an easy class. If you don't study, you won't do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: often condescending when answering questions. very knowledgeable, but poor teaching practices.
He is so caring with his students, an awesome professor, and an easy grader
Best professor ever!!! Super caring and understanding, lenient and flexible for grading and turning in homework.
No plusses or minuses in the course and there was a negative curve when he said we would be given a positive curve. Content itself is learnable though, try reading the textbook before lecture.

His handwriting is extremely difficult to read. He knows the material well, but struggles to teach it; textbook has more clear explanations. He also gives inaccurate approximations on where students are on the curve throughout the year. Each exam I scored within his "A range" but the final curve didn't align with his mid-semester updates at all.

Contrary to common belief, I actually really enjoyed my time in Aidan's class. He gets a bad rap for his grading scale, but I can understand why considering the easier tests relative to the other sections of 381. Lectures are optional, but the exact content of the exams is covered. I only attended a few, but he's a lot nicer during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Grading scale is a joke and his lectures were impossible to follow. Hw difficulty and midterm difficulty isnt even close to comparable

Hard to understand and often taught too fast. His handwriting was incomprehensible and I often had to teach myself topics. Seemed condescending when asked questions and was not transparent at all about grading. The grading scale was very harsh and punished all students who got less than an A. Knows the material very well, but a horrible teacher.
His lecture was hard to understand, with bad handwriting. He was condescending when answering questions.

Not a very good instructor, despite being obviously very knowledgeable. Grading curve at the end of the class was a joke, so take someone else if you want to ensure a better grade than I got. Ended with a C despite a B or B+ on every assessment.

Aidan is good with the math but created a poor learning environment for undergraduate students. He gave consistently unsatisfactory and combative responses anytime we asked him a question throughout the semester & as someone stated below often came across as condescending. I wouldnt say stay away, just know what youre getting yourself into
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Extremely confusing and boring lectures. He comes off as condescending, but I don't think he means to. He didn't decide on the grading scale, but it's stupid and unfair, so FYI: A 91-100, B 85-90, C 77-84, D 66-76, F 0-65. Imagine getting an 84, but it's actually a C. And the inconsistent point ranges (9 point range for A, 5 point range for B, etc)
The worst class I took at UNC was this Math 381 by Aidan Young. Going to his class is even not helpful so just preparing to teach yourself
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Aidan knows the material well but tended to rush through lectures, however, I took this course over the summer so that's understandable. His handwriting was hard to read at first but over time I got used to it. He responded to most questions on piazza within a couple hours. His tests were doable and there weren't any surprises and the EC was a plus

Not good at teaching. He rushes through explanations and skips many steps. I had to learn thing on my own and he isn't that accessible outside of class and is sometimes rude when you ask questions. Tests had extra credit points which was generous and were graded leniently but if you don't understand something, going to him won't help.

Aidan definitely knows how to do the math, but I think that he still needs some practice when it comes to teaching. He taught at a very rapid pace and gave tests that were much more difficult than what we did in class. He also didn't always know how to answer questions we had. However, he was a nice guy and was very helpful during review.

Professor Aikat was nice but it is very easy to tune her out in class.  She takes attendance daily so it is important to be there.  The first half of the class is straight forward, but it is very easy to become lost in the second half.  Going to TA office hours is crucial.

I ended up taking COMP110 just to maintain a 15 hour course load, and it ended up being one of the bests classes I've ever taken here.  Professor Aikat is very clear with instructions, and drops your lowest assignment grade, which makes life so much easier.  Lectures were fun, and she is quite funny at times.

She drops your lowest assignment and quiz grade and gives clear instructions about what is expected of you on assignments. Easy A if you pay attention and make sure you can do the examples from class yourself.

The second half of the semester the material is a lot more challenging and confusing. It is really easy to get lost in lecture, but going to office hours helps out a lot. Parts of the assignments are difficult, but there aren't many and you can go to office hours and knock them out in two hours or so tops.
Pretty easy class with a few assignments and labs. There are multiple opportunities for help if you're struggling but overall its relatively manageable. She's a good teacher.

This class definitely required effort. Lectures were ok; easy to tune out or get lost. However office hours is very helping and the assignments help you understand a lot; that why they are worth 50% of final grade. The midterm and final are not so horrible. As long as you understand basics, you will do fine on those. Got 70% on both and got an A.

I took this class Spring 2014; it was 300 kids in GNS lecture hall. The first half of the class is easy; the second is confusing. She had 5 personal office hours a week and 10 with the TAs. She offered 9 points on your final letter grade throughout the semester. Do the work; the first half gets 60% of your grade and is easy. Tests are tricky.

Midterm and final were sort of tricky, but similar to study guide. Programming assignments are 50% of your grade so if you do all of them and study for test you can at least make a B. TAs are very helpful. She gives extra credit opportunities to add 3 points on to your final grade. Class was boring, but she has daily attendance quizzes.

If you are not a math person, do not take this class. Probably the worst decision I've made at carolina. Daily attendance. She gives tests that are extremely difficult and lots of trick questions. The class has about 10 TA's who do not communicate correctly with what will be on tests. She gives you study guides but they are LITTERED with errors.

There is very little graded in actually participation which goes against the idea of a "seminar" class. Most grades comes from out of work readings. She grades very vaguely and harshly. Even if you were to follow the rubric word for word, the chances are you will get a grade much below what you are expecting.
Unclear grading scale and changed the syllabus multiple times throughout the semester. Weaponized sarcasm during lectures.

Her lectures are funny, but she is generally a very passive-aggressive and not very understanding professor. Was very disrespectful during Creativity Relay presentations. My group had an issue because a student wasn't doing any work, and she was not very understanding or helpful. The class is easy, but she tries to make it unnecessarily difficult.

Took SOCI89. She can be sassy, and her lectures are somewhat interesting. Her homework is structured oddly, due the morning on the day before class, and the homework was often 25+ pages of readings. However, she is really nice and rounded up our grades at the end of the semester; a big part of our grades is based on projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Sassy but somewhat entertaining in lecture. Everything online except for one group project (lowkey she was annoying about these). The kind of class you do other homework during- only took attendance twice in the semester

She makes her lectures entertaining, however she is really rude and passive aggressive during the creativity relay presentations, obviously aggravated and corrects the content students share immediately after their presentations. Grading is really harsh, its not a difficult class however the grading style makes it hard to get a good grade in class.

I took SOCI 89. She's an extremely harsh grader, gives passive aggressive feedback, and doesn't provide good instruction on what she's looking for. Homework due before every class which includes multiple readings that can each be 25+ pages. Her lectures are somewhat interesting and sometimes she shares funny stories, but overall not worth it.

Painfully unfunny. Sent the syllabus for the group project AFTER we had completed and presented it and graded us based on it which dropped my grade down to a B. Everything else is just quizzes and take home exams with questions that she lazily pulls from quizlet. Unaccommodating/Only professor I've ever had a grudge against. Dont buy her book
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: funny but sassy. everything is online. attendance is spot-checked. never opened the book once other than the group project. definitely take for an easy A

If you just want to get your A and be done with it than this class is a good one to take. However I honestly think she is extremely rude. Would make rude comments in class and tell us that she would not bother to respond to emails if she thought our email was not worth replying to. The exams were all online and she did take random attendance.

There was a group project that wasn't hard and is pretty expected for a 101 class; however, the grading criteria was not fully available and then she wanted to grade heavy. It is clear she knows what she's talking about and cares about students, but sometimes her comments can rub people the wrong way. For credit though, this class was easy.

Unprofessional, out of pocket, unorganized professor. She was condescending, and never gave clear directions/expectations for the course/assignments. She was funny at times & the content was interesting, but it doesn't make up for the fact that she made the course way harder than it needed to be. She did not set up the class to succeed at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: She tries really hard to be engaging & is funny most of the time (some jokes just don't land). The group project is annoying, but if your group is on top of it a good grade is doable. The TA grades just about everything so as long as you have a good TA it's fine. There are small responses due at the beginning of each class based on the reading.

She's really passionate about sociology and tries to make lectures fun. Bottom line: the material is not hard and you don't need to attend class at all. Grades are based on weekly quizzes and a few tests and papers; easy to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Honestly yes sometimes the lectures are a bit dry, but if you have a solid TA, the class will be a breeze. If you do the readings and take notes you'll get extra credit at the end of the semester just for doing them. I recommend her if you can get her, attendance is mandatory but also not at the same time. Midterms and final were pretty easy too.

In one lecture she had twenty students come to the front of the lecture hall and line up by skin color in some backwards way of trying to make a point. She is well-intentioned but tone deaf and just misses the mark. Required attendance (even though lecture is large), made us read her own book even though it wasn't relevant to the course content.

Dr. Ravenelle is really funny and her lectures are enjoyable. Although I agree with some of the comments saying that the group project was frustrating, I wouldn't let it stop you from taking the class as you can learn a lot from it! The grading was very fair and the readings were also really interesting.

Dr. Ravenelle's class was not too bad. Readings were not dense but you need to do the daily participation assignments. Both the midterm and final were online, essay-based. About a month and a half is centered around a group project that was a frustrating experience. We were trained to use a coding platform that was not very helpful. TA was great!

She was ok.  Her lectures could be hard to sit through.  She tries to be funny/snarky, and it often doesn't really work out.  Pretty easy class, though.  I wouldn't say I recommend her, but I also didn't absolutely hate her.
She had really entertaing lectures and all of the homework/ tests were very easy.

On top of her unbearable lectures, Ravenelle had a terrible attitude towards her students and gave poor instructions for assignments. Grades were seemingly determined by her TA flipping a coin and were inconsistent across students and assignments. Rubrics were poor, and she had a group project as the final and the highest grade was an 80 lol.

Tries very hard to be funny but isn't. A lot of the lessons I learned from this class (which mainly came from the readings and videos she made us watch, not necessarily her lectures) I also learned in MNGT 131. What I couldn't stand is she would read emails but not reply. She would condescendingly tell u she read ur email. Very wishy washy.

She's a smart lady, but very condescending and not considerate towards students. She gives no rubric or clear instructions on anything and grades very hard. I would avoid this class unless you need it for your major. Super lecture heavy as well, and very boring.

Professor Ravenelle's class was not extremely difficult (attendance assignments with readings, essays, essay-based midterm/final, and a big group project). There is not a rubric or grading criteria provided for any of the assignments, and she is a tough-grader. Not too hard of a class, but extremely boring lectures, and not very accommodating.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The class overall was fine. Our TA was amazing and she did 90% of the grading. However, none of the professors assignments had guidelines and the one thing she did grade she was super harsh for no good reason. Lectures were extremely boring too. Overall the professor was not great but the class was fine.

Would not recommend this class AT ALL unless you have to have it. I did not enjoy it and honestly, the material is all pretty much common knowledge if you've watched the news once since 2010. It's not hard but extremely boring and rather irrelevant. I also did not like the way I felt the professor had extremely vague instructions. Don't take :)

Do not take the class unless it's for a major. Professor Ravenelle is a nice lady, but not a considerate professor. There was many changes throughout the class which were not updated in the syllabus, like attendance! Lectures are very boring and a waste of time. No lectures are posted online for reference, so good luck on midterms/finals!

Dr. Ravenelle is a great choice for SOCI427. There is a lot of work including a group project but, it helps your grade in the long run. Midterm and final not super hard, just essays. She is pretty funny and keeps lecture entertaining. Definitely feel like I learned a lot too!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Professor Ravenelle made a class about labor force fun and enjoyable. She also loves to play John Oliver clips once in awhile and she always assigns interesting articles related to class content. Highly recommend taking this course with her and also I love her humor!

She's awesome! She bring real world experience as a planner, and always keeps the class engaged. This was a really fun class to understand various aspects of urban planning. There are two big projects though
Wonderful professor and great class content! Very thoughtful and understanding!

Really enjoyed this class and this professor. Class was not very challenging but graded by a few things. Would recommend for anyone interested in city planning and no experience alike. I was not familiar at all with anything about city planning and was really struggling to find a class for freshman but stumbled across this one and loved it.

Genuinely the best professor I've taken at UNC. Her lectures are entertaining, and she's very passionate and knowledgeable about the content. She's also extremely accessible outside of class, through both email and her office hours. She had one midterm and the final; it was an extremely manageable course load. Can't recommend her classes enough
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Really good professor who cares deeply about her students!

Dr. Septer is AMAZING! There are 16 quizzes, a midterm, and a final (but she drops the lowest 6 quizzes from your final grade!!!!) The class covers a lot of material, but the concepts aren't difficult. If you have any interest in marine science, I highly recommend meeting with her. She wants to help all of her students!
LOVED her class. easy to follow, interesting and she is very nice. definitely an easy A as long as you do the homework and follow the study guides for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Fabulous lectures! Dr. Septer was passionate about the material she taught and made sure all students succeeded. There were weekly quizzes, all of which were open note with unlimited time to complete. She was also generous with quiz drops and exams were very reflective of classroom material. I recommend taking Dr. Septer if you need an easy class!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of my favorite bio professors! Dr. Septer really cared about the success of her students, providing us with the BEST study guides and making herself available outside of class! I would definitely take a class with her again!

Super energetic and passionate about the subject. Assignments provide a clear rubric and grading generally isn't harsh, granted that good effort is shown. Lectures aren't super helpful but all test material goes along with the readings and slides he provides. Very fun class.

Deb's class is not challenging if you show up to lectures (attendance is mandatory) and follow assignments' requirements (his grading is very clear). The content is not difficult and you do not have to deeply understand it to succeed in the class, knowing the terms/events discussed in class and their impact on media is sufficient.

Deb is SUPER nice and the tests are very easy- mostly common sense and based on all of the readings he gives us. There were a few projects, all of which were graded easy as long as you follow directions. The lectures weren't ever helpful (it's mostly Deb asking if anyone has any questions), but overall would recommend- Deb's a great guy!
Deb is a great professor! I took MEJO 141 over the summer online, and it was pretty easy. He was always available outside of class for help on the very few assignments we had.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Deb is very but, but he's all talk and not much knowledge or teaching. He really pushed us to give good evaluations, which is outa hand. I don't dislike him but I also didn't really learn anything. You don't have to do much to pass.

Deb is really cool. He ALWAYS will answer whatever question you have. He wants questions. But just a APA citations project, easy presentation, midterm, more citations and final. He cares a lot about the kids and participation not graded but participate -- it'll make him happy. Nice old Indian guy

I had this class from 5:45-7:00, but Deb was always so positive and uplifting. The content of this course was very manageable, going to class and participating in lectures made it MUCH more engaging. Highly suggest MEJO 141 with him!

This class was a 7:15PM, but he brought the energy every single time. He is nothing short of a phenomenal professor, who keeps lectures interesting. If you need credits or a good grade and want to enjoy the class, take Deb. He is an amazing guy and a great yet understanding teacher.

Deb is kind, fair, and loveable. While not very tech-savvy, he always provides space for student questions and suggestions. His syllabus and grading criteria were the most well-organized and clear that I have ever seen. Most people I know got high A's in this class just by participating and following directions.

He is a very nice professor, but does not teach much. I was often confused about the material on the tests because most of it we had to learn on our own. He constantly is asking the class if they have any questions and gets annoyed when no one does. That's the majority of the class. But it is easy, most of the tests and projects are common sense

Professor Aikat is incredibly kind, and it's clear he wants his students to get a high grade. Expectations and grading criteria couldn't be clearer, and he spends a lot of time (maybe too much) answering questions about assignments. All of the assignments are easy, just a bit tedious at times. Even though an A starts at 95, it's still doable.

Deb is an amazing and extremely caring professor. He is there to answer any and all questions that you may have about his course as well as help you outside of his course in any way he possibly can. MEJO 101 was a class that I always looked forward to going to.

Took off points because I used a citation machine and then took off 3 points for the letter not being capitalized in the citation when that's how the title was written. There's like 5 grades in this class so not very confident going through. Takes off a bunch of points for trivial things.
Deb's class was fun, and really gives a good foundation for the field of journalism, and even touches on the basics of Advertising and PR.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super energetic and cares about his students. You can tell he's really passionate about the class too. I thought this class was easy but an A is a 95 which is kinda high. Diff professors from the MEJO school come guest lecture for every class. You take a couple of open note quizzes, a take-home exam, and the final exam.

Deb is extremely knowledgeable, sweet, and caring. Even with a class period starting at 7:15 p.m., his humor and personality made it worth going to class. Deb is one of the best professors I've had at UNC and even if you aren't a MEJO major, 141 is enjoyable and interactive if you take it with Deb. The assignments aren't hard, just time-consuming.

This course is awesome. Many guest speakers from different Media and Journalism areas introduce the basic knowledge about their teaching field. Deb is very strict with the deadline, but overall friendly. The quiz and exams are pretty easy.

Only take this class if you want to get to know the BASIC concepts of MEJO and some of the professors. You will not learn much. Deb is interesting but unclear. They test on readings and concepts but also just specific things that lecturers and the readings say.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I honestly really enjoyed Deb, but he only taught one class. Every other class we had quest speakers who could NOT keep my attention. Really the only thing I can complain about are the tests, they told us which lectures to study, but the tests did not match up to the information they were giving us. Thought it would be an easy A, I was wrong :)
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: A 95 is an A which is annoying but overall, pretty easy class. He took attendance every class but we never actually got an attendance/participation grade so I don't think it matters. He had really interesting speakers and the assignments were pretty easy and easily graded he just takes like so long to return it to you. Bad at answering questions

I personally really liked Deb, but I didn't like the class. There were a lot of guest lecturers that basically repeated the same material, and the quizzes were pretty tough. If you really want to take the class then don't be intimidated by these reviews... Deb is pretty awesome it is just the class content that isn't great.

Deb said at the beginning of the semester attendance was not mandatory, but then changed the syllabus without telling us so you fail with three absences. He also made it seem like tests and quizzes would be easy, but even if you attend class the wording of questions made it hard to get A's. Lectures were very boring and not even by Deb. Not easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class is beyond boring, he is not a good lecturer. Most of the lectures are guest lectures who repeat previous points. Deb comes with a lot of energy, but it does not help because it is all useless information. Avoid this class, while it is not hard, it is incredibly boring and you do not learn.

In the middle of the semester, Deb randomly changed the syllabus to include a strict attendance policy. Before, attendance wasnt mandatory. Rather than be understanding about the mental health crisis on campus, he tried scaring us into attending class instead. While we dealt with student deaths and mourned, he reminded us about a quiz and exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Deb is a wonderful instructor who truly wants his students to succeed. If there is an assignment with complicated instructions, he provides all resources needed to complete it. His final exam was a little difficult, though. I was making an A until the exam and it brought me down to a B and I know many of my classmates has the same experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The MEJO101 team is okay, as someone who is not majoring in MEJO I found the class to be slightly boring. Took it with the impression it would be an easy A but unfortunately some TAs grade harsher than others. Overall not a bad class, an A is certainly attainable. Attending lectures is a must, if you take good notes you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Deb was a very fun professor to have. Like the other reviews said, he didn't teach much because the class relied on guest lectures. He was always so accessible outside of class and a great communicator and resource. Although I really liked him, the class itself was not the easy A I thought it was. Still glad I took it though!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I loved Professor Aikat! The class was mostly based upon guest lecturers, but he was always available to help you outside of class. I didn't really enjoy the assignments we had to do but they weren't too bad. I wish we had more lectures taught by him, but his presence in class made it fun and interesting. If you work hard, it's an attainable A.

They had so many awesome guest lectures and had an awesome format. Were very understanding and extended deadlines. Weekly quizzes with two papers. The papers were laid out exactly the way they wanted. Easy A. Just do the work. Midterm and final based off of weekly quizzes. Highlighted material on the midterm and final for easy study guide.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Class was taken all on zoom, different guest speakers pretty much every class so don't really hear from Deb except funny introductions. All lectures are recorded and posted, attendance isn't mandatory but quizzes each week to test attendance are pretty specific. Midterm and final are a lot of memorization.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was almost always guest speakers, so we didn't learn from the Professors. It was more like Deb was a funny moderator who graded our work than a Prof who taught. I didn't enjoy the class, but that is because I wanted to hear more from Deb.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Just here to give my praise to Dr. Deb. The class is almost purely a new lecturer each session discussing a different aspect of journalism, but Deb helps fills the blanks nicely with a great personality. He truly cares for his students and reaches out by email with many help sessions for those that need it. Class relies too much on memorization.
Loved the variety of this class! There were lots of different guests speaker. Professor Aikat is so funny and caring. He really wants you to get a good grade on everything and helps you through it.

Mejo 101 was such a great class! I took it fall 2020 online and it was one of my favorite classes. We had so many interesting guest lectures. Attendance was not for a grade, but I recommend going to get a good grade on the weekly quizzes. Deb & Lee are hilarious and we talked about so many interesting topics. Great class!

This class proves that no matter how good the professor is if you're not interested in the subject, it's harder. TA's were amazing! Test questions sometimes required you to recall what a guest speaker said word for word. We had a new guest speaker in almost every class, which was fun. This class is great for anyone looking to explore MEJO careers.

Mejo 101 literally only consists of guest speakers. every. single. class. So this is more of a critique on the class and not necessarily the professor because Aikat is HILARIOUS! Since there are guest speakers everyday, it is crucial that you take notes EVERY class because you will be tested on exactly what they say. GRADED BY FEW THINGS  my B-

Professor Deb is definitely a professor I won't forget. Unfortunately, I did not enjoy this class very much but none of that is attributed to him. Each class had a guest speaker which meant he would rarely teach. However, I really really enjoyed his presence and looked forward to seeing him each class!

Deb is hilarious, but he doesn't really teach the class; almost every class is taught by a different guest lecturer. I found most of them to be extremely boring, and the worst part is that you're tested on their exact wording on the exams. There are 2 essays that are also graded pretty harshly. I thought this class would be an easy A but it wasn't.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Deb is good in making his class really simple and clear. No textbooks, everything in one place, always taking time for questions. The worst thing about this class was attendance because he would require you to write a paper for each time you missed class. Also, outside of class he is very unwelcoming, like he does not care about you AT ALL lmao.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class consisted mostly of guest lectures from people in the fields of Media and Journalism. This is a great exploratory class if you are interested in this area. Professor Aikat is very dedicated to the success of his students and makes his expectations very clear.

Deb is the best, but the class isn't really run by him. It's all guest lectures, which are usually boring. There are 2 essays, a midterm and a final exam. The essays are not difficult, but are graded really harshly. You can do well on the midterm and the final if you do all the readings and pay attention in class, which can be hard to do sometimes.

Deb is an awesome man and I loved talking to him but the guest lectures that you have everyday in no way prepare your for the assignments. You're graded on 2 essays plus the midterm and final and all four are extremely difficult with unclear grading criteria because everyday is just a guest lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: For a guy who teaches ethics you would think he would be impartial and fair. He is not, he has screwed me out of getting the grades I deserve because I ask questions in class that he cant answer them because he's incompetent, then gets mad at me. Life deals you a crappy hand of cards sometimes and this was my crappy hand. Don't take him, just dont.

Hilarious. I love him. Lots of guest lecturers. Some are really great, others very boring. Learn about J school and careers. I'm not a MEJO major. Can do other work in this class. The 2 writing assignments are hard because they don't teach you to write so you don't know what they expect stylistically, but I did fine. Only take with friends!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I literally did not pay attention during class at all and I got an A+ guys. When I say that they want you to pass, THEY WANT YOU TO PASS. Just review the slides and reading lists they make before exams and you'll be good to go. The MC exam questions are so easy they're "this close" to being common sense. Take the GPA booster. You'll need it.

When asked for an explanation, he cant give one. He ignores questions because he also can't give an answer to that either. Lovable guy, but hard to respect as a professor when he can't do basic teaching. Nice person, but take class w/ someone else. Frustrating to be held to a high standard when he doesn't have the same standards for himself.

Deb is sweet, but no one takes him seriously. In class we do nothing and nobody knows what is going on. Seems great until he takes 2+ months to return a test and gives hard tests that are crazy specific. Have 5 big assignments, he adds the grades together / 500 and thats your grade. Hard to do well. He dodges all questions bc he doesn't know answer

He thinks he's a kidder. Extremely hard to understand -leaving the class silent after some questions. He gets great speakers in which is the best thing about the class. Several group projects. Takes half the semester to grade long-form projects despite promising grades each week. Multiple choice tests are confusing - no one got higher than a 94.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: he is the realest man i have ever met.

Mejo 101 is structured around guest lectures and assigned readings. There are two exams and an essay assignment. Attendance s mandatory. Exams are not hard if you review the readings and and your notes.

Deb is a very cool lad. He is always cracking jokes and makes class enjoyable to attend. MJ101 is graded by 2 short papers, attendance, a midterm MC exam, and a final MC exam. The papers are graded very easily and the exams are almost a joke considering how easy 90% of the questions are. Take this class and you will not be disappointed.

The wording in his exams is soo confusing. Midterm, final worth double, and attendance determined grade. They are both multiple choice, but he makes his questions long and confusing. Worst prof in my Carolina career

Deb is hilarious! The ironic part is he doesn't really teach. The class is composed of lectures from guest speakers which are really awesome for the most part. Topics discussed range from PR to fashion to motion graphics to journalism. The midterm is sneaky-hard so don't blow it off. As long as you show up and take some notes, it will be easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Deb is a very responsible teacher. He's from India, so his speaking style and teaching style are very exotic, which is fun. He gives clear lectures, prepares heavy material for us to review for exams and prepare for classes, which is very helpful. He emphasizes feedback from students a lot. He is willing to change course plans and exams accordingly
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Aikat is pretty nice but don't take this class. Only like 5 assignments factor into your grade (graded pretty arbitrarily) and the wording on the test questions is unnecessarily confusing. The class should be an easy A but it is not. The teachers are very nice, though, but absolutely no extra credit is given.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Really really caring professor. Didn't love the class, especially the way we were tested on remembering the exact wording of the guest lecturers, but he is a really nice guy.

MeJo 101 is a class that has different lecturers every session to talk about real world applications of journalism. Some are pretty entertaining. The class is easy as there is no HW. However, test scores are everything. This was also the strictest attendance class I've ever had. Don't miss more than 2 classes or it will hurt your grade severely.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Almost every week is a guest lecture and it's always such a treat to hear what professionals in the field have to say. Aikat and Dean King are also wonderful. Graded by few things, so be wary. You can usually get away with not doing the readings. Be warned, though, that if you skip class you have to write a whole absence paper, which is ridiculous.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Deb is a host of Mejo 101, the class is filled with guest lecturers from a wide variety of MEJO fields. These lectures are intriguing and Deb and Dean King find professionals to come and teach the class. Deb gives you so many recourses and aid and genuinely wants everyone to succeed. There are readings but you can usually get away with not reading

Deb doesn't exactly give the class. He just has lectures come in and tell you about different topics pertaining the subject. It's not a hard class, just make sure you do the readings for each class and take good notes because the midterm and final is based on the things each lecturer talked about during class.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Deb was so much fun to have as a professor. The class was mostly guest lecturers and there was only a couple tests and papers. Deb made it very clear what you should do to get a good grade on the tests and papers. His class was a great introduction to the journalism school.

Deb is very funny. The class is all guest lectures though so he only taught at most two class periods. Easy A if you show up to class. Final and midterm are all based on guest lecturers and assigned readings. Easy papers. Don't take the final as a joke though it is 40% of your grade.
Deb is so passionate and funny. You can tell he really cares about his students. The class is an easy A and pretty much all guest lectures. There are not many assignments.

I honestly didn't love this class, I just loved Deb. Hilarious, kind, caring man. when he says "Dean King, katria, veasey and I care about your success in mejo101" he means it. basically all guest lectures. most are boring some are good. Katria is a goddess. a couple easy papers and tests w/ very clear criteria

Deb is so so hilarious. He honestly is a really good guy. The class seems super easy with all of the guest lecturers and stuff, but don't overlook the final exam too much. Bumped me down to an A- when it should have been an easy A.
Easiest A at UNC. The final is worth 40%, but the study guides are super clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests? Not many--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's so nice and hilarious. The class is mostly guest lectures but god bless him he's a gem.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: We had guest lecturers every class but they were all very interesting. The professor was very caring and e-mails back quickly (he even emailed me back on Thanksgiving). If you go to class you will do well, this is by far the easiest and most interesting class I have taken.

This class was mostly taught by guest lecturers, and to be honest, it was kind of a mess. Whenever Deb taught, he had a hard time getting his point across and instructions for assignments were repeated an obnoxious number of times. If you know want to be in the MJ-school, don't take this intro class. A waste of time
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: This course had a ton of guest lectures - good and bad. The few times Deb gave lectures, he was completely rushed. Deb is a funny guy and is very enthusiastic. Unfortunately the course itself is pretty bad.  A lot of common sense information being thrown at you in the form of lectures and readings. The final was hard and had tricky wording.

Dr. Aikat is hilarious and committed to his students' success. However, the class is composed of guest speakers' lectures. Some were great, others weren't. The midterm and final were a big portion of the final grade, but the material wasn't that difficult (the wording was tricky sometimes though). Great class to introduce students to MEJO!

Deb is one of the most entertaining people I've ever encountered. He really cares about the students but is not very gifted at teaching. Most classes are lectures given by guest lecturers. Very little structure to the class, and 80% of your grade is determined by exams. Fun class, but you don't learn much.

Dr. Aikat was a really caring professor who tried his best to make the class great. The structure of the class was just hard to overcome - every class there were "guest speakers." The midterm and final were terrible. But he really values feedback and cares about students and their grades.

All guest lecturers. Some are interesting, some aren't. Class does absolutely nothing to improve your writing skills. Deb is a genuine guy that cares about students but tries a little too hard. Sends daily emails that are usually repetitive. Final exam is 40% of grade. Show up to class (attendance is always taken) and you'll pass w/ a solid grade
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This class is all guest lectures. Professor Aikat introduces them every class, but doesn't do any of the teaching. He sends way too many, confusing, emails. Assignments are tedious and not helpful in learning about Journalism. Lots of irrelevant reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Class is completely composed of guest lecturers. Deb is very unorganized and confused 90% of the time, but it's not really a problem. Definitely a fair grader, will go above and beyond to make sure the class is satisfied with their grades. Great class if you're looking to explore the MJ and school and not break your GPA!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class is taught by a different guest lecturer every day. Deb is "the opening act" everyday, is a very entertaining guy, and "committed to your success in MEJO 101." He can be extremely vague at times, which causes confusion. The class covers the surface of all aspects of the MJ school. Great class to take to explore majors in the MJ school.

Deb is a really nice guy who obviously loves his job. He can be entertaining to listen to, but sometimes his directions/answers are unclear even after asking for clarification. His JOMC101 class is mostly guest lectures, but he is always happy to answer questions. He sends A LOT of emails to the class. I like Deb, and find him very endearing.
Deb is a great professor and he's very kind and cares a lot about his students! He's very passionate about the subject and helpful in class.
Ai-kat understand what he is saying sometimes.He can be pretty easy sometimes. ;)
Extremely helpful prof.  The class covered a lot of ground with some basic stuff and some high-end topics.  Deb seemed to genuinely care that everybody ended the class knowing all the content.

Entertaining, but it took me about 2 weeks to get on grip on what we were supposed to be learning.  There is a ton of information to sift through, but I did learn a lot and am glad that I took the class.  I still use some of the stuff I learned.
No Comments
I loved Deb, he was awesome
Funny and entertaining

Boring, repetative, he never teaches...just random lecturers, too much work.  Don't take it if you're looking for an easy A...and after all the random tests and useless busy work...you have to build a website...Oh and attendance in your "lab" is a big percent of your grade.
absolutely horrid
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments

Nice person, but not good at teaching. Instructions for assignments are unclear, and grading feels pretty nitpicky. I lost points on a 3D puzzle assignment even though I made six pieces because she said they weren't “distinct enough.” Also be prepared for random pop quizzes on stuff if she thinks people aren't paying attention during lecture.

Do not take this class for a focus capacity. Easy A, but way too much work to justify a gen ed. It is the work of two classes combined. It is very based on group work, and the grading criteria is slightly unclear. Dr. Gillmore is really nice, and is an understanding professor that wants you to succeed but the structure of the class is not worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Unless you really like building things, I would not recommend taking APPL 110 to satisfy the focus capacity. Nothing you do is very difficult, but it all takes a ton of time. Prof. Gillmore is an energetic lecturer and generally amiable, but grading is inconsistent. TAs grade leniently, but she doesn't. You don't know who is grading what either.

Dr. Gillmore is a lovely person, and largely very fair. The assignments did have some confusing guidelines, because the class is taught by multiple professors with countering philosophies. Even with hellish partners in the two major group projects, this class was fairly easy. Start assignments ASAP and have fun in the makerspace.

She doesn't communicate with her TAs at all. They say my design is fine, then she claims it doesn't meet expectations. No clear grading criteria, completely inconsistent. She's passive-aggressive when you ask questions and dismisses your effort by saying it looks “too easy,” so it doesn't count the day before the due date.  This course sucks.
RUN
took stor 415 with him, this professor CANNOT teach

Took stor 415 with him, he made hardest exams and homework take forever to do. In class, he will give you the most basic examples, but then have the exceptional cases on the quiz and homework, where you have no idea how to even approach them. Lectures are super uninteresting.

Currently taking for STOR415 (not listed on ratemyprofessor). Held class on Tuesday despite class being cancelled due to the winter storm (we were in condition 2 until 12pm, and he held class from 9:30-10:45AM). Holds quizzes throughout the semester, and makes you to stay in class 10 minutes late if you want a chance at completing the quizzes.

I liked him overall. A bit difficult but that's discrete, not him. Overall, he graded pretty leniently and I only got a B because I sold on the final (maybe not a good first semester class while taking 17 credits!) BUT that's more on me and I think if I had less credits and more college experience it wouldn't have been such a crunch at the end. W!

I had Prof. Nezhad a few semesters ago, and I'm not sure why there are so many negative reviews. He went above and beyond to be accommodating when I was having a tough semester. Lectures were detailed and clear, discrete is just a challenging subject. It's possible something's changed since I've taken a class w/ him, but I had a good experience.

He should not be teaching Discrete Mathematics. He implied a curve that he did not deliver on, was difficult to understand, and did not take our critiques for the length of exams. The second midterm saw the entire class scrambling to finish. He rambled on in class but to be fair was a kind professor. Take MATH 381. This is not worth it.

Took him a while ago. He was not an understanding professor and could not teach the material well. Would get hung up on seating assignments during quizzes, so much so that he would single kids out to move around the classroom as if we were playing musical chairs until it was to his liking.

got 100 for both 2midterms but for final only 86…Really hard!!
Quiz is based on homework but with slight change, homework is long and weekly, lecture is good but his handwriting is hard to distinguish
Hard class Hard professor...RUN

Very difficult professor that didn't understand the needs of the class. I found it difficult to study for the course due to the lack of guidance on what would be tested. There are slight bonus points on the midterms and no curve or bonus points on the final. I would not recommend.

Worst professor I've had so far at UNC. When the class expressed concerns over a lack of time for the midterm, he dismissed us and made the next midterm longer. He responds in a demeaning manner that makes you regret participating. Half of the semester was spent on unit 1 (out of 5). I wouldn't wish taking this class with him on my worst enemy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's one of the most unapproachable professors at UNC. He tends to mansplain and answer questions in a way that makes them seem insignificant. The homework was a nightmare and midterms and the final were much harder. We didn't even get a heavily implied curve at the end. Overall I would recommend switching majors over taking this class with him.

He pretty much summarizes the information from the textbook without going into much detail. Tests have a slight curve, but the material is more difficult than that of the homework. There was no study material for the final exam either.

Professor was not understanding of my circumstances. I had some personal problems going on and he did say he would round up letter grades but did not do that despite many emails discussing it with him. Did not explain course material properly either. Worst experience at UNC (coming from a straight A student)

One of the best professors I've had in the STOR department. However, the final in this course on probability was much more difficult than the midterms and what we did in lectures/homeworks. He is also a very generous grader if you show your work.

Agreed with the last comment on Piazza over office hours. He did seem distracted in person but I prefer Piazza so that's alright with me. I have not had many professors lecture like him before as he is very interactive with the class. I enjoyed him stopping to ask us questions to be sure we understood but did feel he was a bit patriarchal at times.

Lots of homework but he gives great feedback on Piazza if you ask questions. I'd recommend this over office hours because you can definitely tell his mind is elsewhere. In class, his interactions were a bit off at times during quizzes and tests like singling out students to be moved around, but he is super open to class participation

It's not the most interesting subject. Pretty easy class, as the grading is just very generous. Whether that's on homeworks, quizzes, or tests, they always give heavy partial credit. The first 3/4 of the class is very easy, the last unit on probability is a bit hard. You learn a good amount, some real world application especially with excel.

Professor Ali is a great lecturer and teaches concepts really clearly and well. His homeworks are straightforward and relates well to the lecture content and exams. Lenient grader on quizzes and exams. Gives extra credit questions on exams as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: You can expect discrete to be hard no matter who you take it with but Prof. Nezhad made it as easy as it can get. His lectures, assignments, and exams were structured very well which made it very easy to stay on track of what concepts are being used where, something that helps immensely with discrete. If you can, take it with him!
Fantastic lecturer, but exams are difficult.

Take discrete with him if you can! Great lecturer and tests were on homework problems or straightforward examples similar to those in class. He always wants you to participate and if you do sometimes he will give extra credit points on the midterms! Graded fairly and made discrete much easier to understand than most STOR professors do at Carolina
Her lectures tend to be dull, and her exams are difficult and often unclear. While the class material itself is not especially challenging, the exams do not seem to reflect it well.
Boring lectures and exams are really difficult.

Dr. Hussong is one of the most genuine professors at this university. She provides a level of flexibility for her students that shows she really cares about what is going on outside of class. Most assignments are easy, the lectures are repeating the textbook chapter so just read at some point. Exams were a bit hard so be sure to do the study guides
I absolutely adore her. She's wickedly smart, loves her work, and is dedicated to making sure her students understand the "why" rather than the "what" of psychological research.
Really helpful professor and very nice person.
Nice guy who seems like he's trying his best, but the whole class is confused and not doing as well as they should on the exams. I have a tutor and learn from YouTube better than he explains it.

Professor Pease made math 130 much harder than it should've been. The class is graded majority from midterms and the finals. I recommend not taking this class with a heavy course load and getting a tutor asap.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Bad professor. Clearly thinks he's too good to be teaching precalc since he teaches it in a complex/ confusing manner. You'd be better off learning from YouTube

10/10 would not recommend. TAs were SO unhelpful and the professor overcomplicates simple topics. I definitely could have done better but l think the way he teaches is directed for higher level math and not pre-calc. He is a very stylistic and funny person and very accessible outside of class with his office hours.

I took MATH 130 with him. He is a cool and stylish person, but not a good teacher at all. He deserves to be teaching higher level maths and not pre-calc because he overcomplicates simple concepts making it very hard to follow along. I strongly advise not taking this class with him if you are taking a lot of other STEM courses.

I took math 130 with professor pease, it was terrible. The class itself is not too hard, but the way he explained concepts got very confusing very fast. You have to spend a lot of time outside of class learning the concepts before you can get to actually studying them.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Terrible at explaining “basic” mathematical concepts. If you want a straight explanation, you're not going to get one.
Andrew is very sweet but explains things horribly. He makes everything sound more complicated than it actually is. Learn things on your own and you will do well.

Objectively a really bad professor- made MATH130 feel like rocket science. If you are in his math 130 class, i HIGHLY recommend getting a tutor or use outside resources. The tests feel nothing like what we go over in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class itself was not too difficult, but I went to office hours and he was really short with me. I never went back again.

I took Andrew for MATH110. This class was supposed to be way easier than Andrew made it. His teaching style was very interesting, he goes way too fast, and is just kinda bad at teaching. I ended up just not going to the lectures anymore and teaching myself. He is a very nice and caring person though, and always made the class laugh.
The class was okay, and he was super friendly outside of class. The way he explained concepts was another story….

I took math 130 with Andrew and he is the most sweetest/ caring person ever! however, his teaching style and the way he explains things is absolutely ass. Other than that he never makes you feel dumb for not knowing things that should be "simple"!

He's so nice, caring, and accessible outside of class. Great person, but his teaching style was so confusing and he made simple concepts seem SO complicated. I've taken algebra 1 and many maths higher than this in hs before, but his teaching made the info feel 100x harder than it is.

I had Andrew for MATH110, one of the easiest math classes at UNC. But, at no point throughout the course did Andrew make us feel "lesser-than" or stupid. He never gave us an overwhelming amount of work and heard our frustrations when we had them. Held office hours constantly and was always warm and inviting when you attended them!

Andrew was my TA for calculus and our class would not have survived without him. He basically taught us the course and always helped us work through our homework. He is also a very generous grader and so hilarious. Shout out to Andrew!

The UNC chem department is tough, but Dr. Curtis does a great job teaching students the content needed to pass exams, and she does so in a way that is easier to understand than the textbook. Dr. Curtis is also a friendly person, and it is clear that she wants her students to succeed. Definitely take with Curtis if you can!

If you are a pre-med and thought this course was difficult, you should take a step back and reconsider your long-term goals. This class is by far one of the easiest STEM classes you will take. If you got anything below a B+ and are not 100% sure if becoming a doctor is what you want to do, drop medicine now. It is easier to pivot early on.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis is wonderful and very accessible.  However, exams are 85% of your grade (20% per midterm, 25% final) and they were tough.  The rest of your grade is homework which is graded very leniently.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I had her class in Spring 2025. She was a fine chemistry teacher, and she is definitely passionate about her job. I didn't really find her inspiring, and some days she could go from being the sweetest lady to quite snarky. The chemistry department is also just tough. Self study and practice is super necessary, but take with her if you can!

101/102 get a bad wrap, but they're some of UNC's best-designed courses regarding evidence-based learning and avid practice problem exposure. PAY ATTENTION AND BUY INTO THE SYSTEM. I learned so much + Curtis was clear + qualified. Take accountability for your learning, and trust that 102 provides everything you need to succeed. TLDR: loved Curtis!!

The UNC Chemistry department is extremely difficult; however, I found her teaching to be extremely helpful. She really emphasized understanding the underlying principles of chemistry - the “why” - which, once you actually learn, is crucial and helps with your chemistry intuition. If you take 102, definitely take it with her!!

Chem is hard no matter which professor you have for 102, as it is the same slides and the same exams for everyone. I think Curtis was a great professor, especially outside of the lecture. In GPSS she was very sweet and helpful, and she was great help for study habits in office hours. She's a little corny and had a few laughs in class too.

UNC gen chem is definitely not perfect but Curtis is super caring and approachable and explains examples/topics well in class. Class is designed for you to learn from the textbook and lectures just reinforce the topics from readings. If you read the textbook carefully her lectures are helpful and you will be fine.

The way gen chem is structured at UNC tend to be more dependent on how well you prepare yourself and less about the actual professor you have in my opinion. Curtis was clearly passionate about chem and was kinda entertaining and quirky, but because of the nature chem here I simply can not give her above a 3. chem here sucks but it is what it is.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Anna Curtis is a great professor, chemistry here is just difficult. She is a little quirky but is genuinely excited about chemistry and helping students learn.
