She really emphasizes knowing the reason why behind concepts and equations, which does make exams harder, but she does a good job explaining things.
If you're not religious, pick a religion and pray. I have never been in such a difficult and unnecessarily confusing course like this. Truly good luck to everyone who has to take this. Godspeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's very passionate for sure but only teaches surface level, and on the midterm, they expect you to be Antoine Lavoisier (the father of chemistry). The class is 84% midterms and finals together. The lectures felt pointless but you have to go because attendance is graded. Go to GPSS if you want to pass. GPA killer for sure.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you have to take chem 102, I would take it with her. It's a super hard class and the tests are awful, but she as a teacher is very nice and enthusiastic about her subject.

Professor Curtis is not a good professor by any means. She is very bad at explaining basic chemistry concepts and prepares her students in a poor manner for every midterm. The averages in her classes are incredibly low because it requires students to self study to the fullest to perform well. Do not take chemistry with her by any means.

She is incompetent. I would rather watch paint dry than sit in her class. She does an awful job of keeping students engaged. She goes over what 2+2 is like we are in first grade and doesn't prepare us for the exams.
Doesn't do a good job of explaining anything. Very incompetent
She is a very sweet lady but tends to repeat herself. Also, her pacing varies: one day she moves through the slides very slowly, then the next class time she rushes. Wouldn't recommend her :p

I am not joking when I say she is likely the worst professor in the chemistry department. During her lectures, she repeats the same idea numerous times and takes forever to finish simple problems that anyone in the class would understand. If you are taking Chem102, take it with any other professor who doesn't waste their students' time.
She was a good teacher, but chem 101 will be hard no matter who you take it with. Ask questions and go to GPSS if you are having trouble.

Prof Curtis is a great lecturer! She is engaging and kind. When she explains things she shows her thought process so you get a better idea of how to approach the problems. An A is achievable if you put in the effort.
My advice:
1) Read chapters to understand, and put what you're learning in the context of what you already know
2) Go to CHEMPossible

Standardized class but her lectures were by far the best. She explained concepts and thought processes instead of step by step instructions which aligned perfectly with the challenging tests. People with all deferent grades in the class respect her greatly and would take again.

Curtis was a great lecturer overall. Only issue I had was that she would often be very behind on lessons so it was a bit frustrating at times. Class was pretty difficult but you will be okay if you focus on understanding concepts and doing LOTS of practice.

I would say Anna Curtis is one of the best Chem 101 lecturers. She seems to really care about the subject matter and is enthusiastic while teaching, without being too overboard. Although chem 101 is a flipped classroom format which can be somewhat difficult, I feel like she addresses all difficult content and allows time for questions always.

CHEM 101 is standardized, so the formatting of the class and its assignments are the same no matter which professor one has, but I really enjoyed Dr. Curtis as a lecturer.  She was very kind and always full of energy while teaching.  She made difficult concepts easier to understand, which was great because I hadn't taken a chem course in a while.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Honestly, it doesn't matter what professor you get Chem because it is standardized and you will teach yourself most of the content, but Anna curtis is absolutely the best professor that you can get for chem 101. She explains concepts in a way that is digestible to anyone. You will have to put in the work though because Chem at UNC is hard.

Dr. Curtis is a great lecturer and teaches concepts in a digestible way. The formatting of Chem101 is mostly textbook heavy, so the professor you have won't impact your grade nearly as much as how much you read. To get a good grade in the class I recommend staying on top of your pre-class assignments and attending ChemPossible.

Dr. Curtis is a pretty good lecturer, however the content is difficult. Chem 101 really shows you what studying is and you are going to have to learn it on your own as well. Just attend GPSS sessions, watch youtube videos, and study the concepts rather than just memorizing the formulas.

If you're taking 101, take it with Dr. Curtis! This is a tough class no matter what, but Dr. Curtis is thorough in her explanations and goes really in-depth on concepts she knows students struggle with. Collaboration and participation is heavily encouraged in her class.
Dr. Curtis is a caring professor, but Chem 101 is a tough class overall. Attend office hours, use the free textbook, and try Unstuckstudy for extra prep - it really helps.

Dr. Curtis is probably the best professor in the UNC Chem department. If you have to take chem 101 DO IT WITH HER. Her lectures are clear and she explains things well with examples and applications. She also great at getting a feel for that the class doesn't understand.

She was good in her quirky way. She genuinely loves chem and wanted us to see the beauty in it, unfortunately I just could not. Remember to redirect your anger from chem teachers to the chem department, they are the real enemies. She held really informative GPSS and would take thorough time in class to explain concepts and exam-type questions.
Chem101 is hard, but she's nice and always had so much energy. Don't take chem if you don't have to.

CHEM 101 is hard no matter which professor you take. Professor Curtis is a really sweet person and very approachable and I appreciated how she took things slow until she was sure we understood basic concepts before moving on. I felt like we did a lot of easy stuff in class and were expected to do challenging problems alone, which I struggled with.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Curtis is fine but Chem is really tough and takes getting used to. Make sure you work outside of class to understand everything
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis cares about chemistry and her students. I just wish that she would've spent more time in class going over exam-type questions rather than explaining the basic concepts to us (that we were already expected to know before class). The chem department here can be frustrating so I honestly don't think it matters who you take the class with.

Dr. Curtis is kind and attentive to students. Chemistry is a hard class regardless of professor and your grade will rest heavily on exams. However, Curtis is easy to reach and available to help students. Lectures are pretty standard between professors (use the same slides). If you have to take chem, Curtis is a great option!

Anna Curtis was very sweet and an engaging lecturer. Chem 101 at UNC is just extremely hard and requires extensive practice (recitation, Chem Possible, GPSS, etc). I think she moves at the perfect pace for students who are just learning these chemistry concepts for the first time.

Chem here is annoying, but Dr. Curtis made it better. She's very sweet and quirky and cares a lot about her students understanding the content. Her lectures can run slow/long, but it's because she takes the time to explain the concepts. GPSS is a must for 101 though; lecture and homework will not be enough to understand the content fully.

Offers good explanations especially in GPSS, but moves extremely slow during lecture. Ultimately, the course is not a reflection of her, the chem department is just terrible in itself. You will end up teaching yourself most of the content in chem, but that is not because of Dr. Curtis. She has clear enthusiasm for the subject.

Whoever you take chem-101 with, it's gonna be hard and you're not gonna like the professor. Go to GPSS, and find a study group if you can, and you'll do fine. Overall, she was good though, and if you have to take chem-101, I'd recommend.

Chem is hard, but Dr Curtis is a good teacher and truly cares about all of her students. She is accessible outside of class and gives plenty of opportunities to attend group problem-solving or other forms of tutoring. Her instructions are clear and her canvas page is detailed. I do not recommend the class, but if you have to then take it with her.

Chem 101 in general is a tough class but she made it extremely digestible. She thoroughly explains the concepts and is available for problem solving sessions outside of class. Many people don't do well and blame it on the professor but as long as you practice outside of class and re-write the lecture notes you will do fine.
Do. Not. Take.

The way Dr. Curtis lays out her train of thought when approaching problems is incredible. She emphasizes application over memorization. The grade I received isn't a reflection of her abilities. This was my first semester at UNC, and I also had bad study habits. One major downside is that there were no office hours where you could meet one-on-one.

Curtis's lectures are engaging and she explains the material well. This class is tough because the exams dictate the grade. Instead of going to GPSS or UL sessions, I did the UL practice problems they posted on Canvas. One bad move that Curtis made was that I proved that I was right on an exam question I got wrong, and she kinda blew me off.

Cons:

Tests do make up a majority of your grade but go to class and do the homework so that you don't miss easy points.

Dr. Curtis is awesome! reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I love Dr. Curtis. She's incredibly knowledgeable and super nice. Definitely read the textbook and go to GPSS and her 6-minute meetings. Always has a positive attitude and is supportive. Take her for any class you can!

The chem department is not great- if you do bad on one exam it can screw you over and the final is worth a lot. However, Anna Curtis is a kind queen and I enjoyed her lectures. She's very sweet and loves chemistry and is overall just an enjoyable professor.

Ms. Curtis is probably the best chem 102 professor at UNC. She was sweet and cared about the success of her students. Dr. Curtis is probably the best 102 professor. She is engaging and decent at explaining concepts, though not particularly available outside of class. But the Chem department is a mess. Curtis is a good teacher, but I feel like there isn't enough practice especially with questions that are similar to the difficulty and wording of the exam. reviews.comment: TAKE CHEM 101 WITH CURTIS!!!! Any chem at UNC is going to be hard but Curtis makes the lectures very tolerable. She is very consistent.

She's super sweet and I really like her as a person- her enthusiasm about teaching chemistry is admirable! UNC Chem Department is terrible in general and will make your life hell, but Curtis is one of the best options. Just make sure you pay attention during lectures and attend review sessions

Professor Curtis is great. I think CHEM101 is just a stupid hard class and since the pace of the class is fast, you might get left in the dust trying to understand one topic (i did). I would say just study way before midterms and exams as they are a big chunk of your grade. Other parts of the grade are easy like homework, participation, etc.

Chem 102 is a difficult class but Curtis is a good professor. Tests are sometimes unreasonable but that has to do with the department more than the professor. GO TO PEER MENTOR SESSIONS, Isabella is amazing and will help you do well in the class. Stay on top of reading the chapter and seek extra support outside of class to do well.

The chem department at UNC is always tough. Dr. Curtis is definitely knowledgable, but her lectures were too slow and we were always behind. Wish she spent more time explaining rather than giving us excess time to solve practice problems. She's definitely a kind and caring person - just not the best style for me.

If you have to take chem, 1000% take it with Dr. Curtis!!! She is an amazing lecturer and she helps make the material feel doable. I love her as a person and as a prof even though chem is hard.

Dr. Curtis is your best choice for CHEM 102! I had Dr. Curtis for both 101 and 102. She's a great lecturer and I liked the guided note and problem-solving layout of 102. Dr. Curtis was an amazing lecturer and really cared about students! CHEM-102 has always been hard, but she made it bearable. I personally did not read the textbook; instead, I thought it was helpful to study the lectures and redo the Mastering.

I had Curtis for 101/102 and she was good. She covered the material well. Her test for 102 at least seem to have focused more on if you knew the material rather than tricking you. The questions were pretty straight forward. You will need to put in work, but you will have all you to succeed.

Curtis is very eccentric. Honestly, I don't even know if she's a good lecturer because I took this class Fa2020 and didn't watch any of the video. Chem 102 is a very hard class for many. I struggled a lot, but Dr. Curtis will give you the best chance of passing. I have heard many bad stories about other Professors, but I have had her for 101 and 102 and can say that she is probably the best.

Professor Curtis cares deeply and wants the best for her students. Chem itself is hard but taking Professor Curtis definitely relieved some stress. She also made our lowest midterm weigh less compared to the other two. Take her!

Lectures were 20 min going over questions, I often didn't pay much attention. Learning is up to you.

The course load isn't bad at all, and Professor Curtis always had a positive attitude. She prerecorded lectures to watch outside of class but they were only about 15mins. We spent class in breakout rooms working on practice problems which was helpful. The only complaint I have is that we were not given enough time on test, many people didn't finish

Class was only for 20 mins where you're in a breakout room and answer questions on PollEv for participation. Dr. Curtis loves chem and you can tell by how enthusiastic she is. She was always there after class to answer questions. Dr. Curtis makes most of the pre-class videos and she explains concepts very well! Chem is hard, but she makes it fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This past semester was different because both chemistry teachers taught both classes. Sometimes Prof. Curtis made the lecture video and sometimes the other guy made the video. She definitely explained things a lot better than he did and I would totally recommend her for Chem 101. During class we went over problems and she explained how to do them.

With the online format we only had class for 20 minutes and just did practice problems in breakout rooms for that time, but Dr. Curtis always stayed on the Zoom answering questions after which was really nice. I didn't think the class was too bad! You can tell she loves Chemistry.

This class was good overall. Study! The materials and work she gives us really line up with the midterms, and practicing makes them so much easier (I learnt later on). The downside was that the exams are linear, which is terrible because you can't go back and check your work. Overall, participate, study, do homework, take notes, and you'll be fine.

Professor Curtis gave short lectures which were very helpful of course material and included practice exam questions. Lectures were not mandatory as long as you answered poll everywhere questions during class time, questions were given the night before. But I recommend attending lecture to get the correct answers on the poll everywhere questions
She is a nice professor, but she doesn't make the content easier to learn, in my opinion. One of the better professors you can choose to take this class for, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis is so nice; however, the lectures were not helpful. Class was 20 minutes, and she didn't even teach during this short amount of time. We would go into break out rooms and do practice problems. There were lecture videos on Sakai, but these were 10 minutes long and only covered basic information. Wouldn't recommend taking this online.

Dr. Curtis is sweet and her recorded lectures are easily understood. There is a lot of work and participation points, but pretty much all of the exam questions were solved in lecture/class. Though the exams were linear, the practice exams helped gauge the time limit and type of questions that would be on the exam.

The lectures were all videos and the class forced you to teach yourself most of the material, but Dr. Curtis was a very kind and understanding professor with the unusual circumstances of this semester. I would definitely recommend her for this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The online format makes this class easier. Tests and quizzes are open-note, which helps a lot. Curtis seems friendly and kind, and she explains the material fairly well. Her recorded lectures make learning easier. Take copious notes, show up, try, and practice concepts thoroughly to score well on exams, which comprise a large portion of your grade.

The synchronous portion of this class only focused on examples rather than lecture material so we couldn't ask questions right when watching the lecture videos. Recitations were especially helpful but Mastering Chemistry was quite tedious. Overall, this class wasn't bad and Dr. Curtis explained most concepts clearly.
I really learned the material in 101 because of her. a lot of my friends had another professor and were struggling much more than I was.

Curtis is very quirky, but she's such a sweet professor! Lectures this semester were pre-recorded and very short, and the synchronous meetings were also short and we didn't cover much so you really have to take the initiative to learn and practice problems on your own but recitations are extremely helpful. You definitely have to put in the work

With this class being online with about 400 students, Dr. Curtis did as good as you can do in that situation. Her lecture videos were informative, but oftentimes, extra research was required to answer homework questions. If you're ever struggling with a concept, please go to office hours. Definitely what got me through unit 2.

Class was pretty easy but the teaching style was not very clear. All exams were linear, but grading was easy. Accessible, TA office hours were very helpful. All lectures were async and class activities were sync, met for 20 minutes 3x a week. There was a lot of homework but it definitely helped with understanding the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis is nice. I don't like the linearity or the time limit of exams; those aspects just make it hard for no reason. Try to do all the other work in the class, because exams are difficult. I wish we were given more actual practice exam-type problems & exam resources. For example, the practice final didn't help me at all for the real final.
Hated this class more than I hate Collegeboard. Do what you want with this information.

Dr. Curtis was willing to help her students throughout the semester. There was a lot of work however, if you did a majority of the homework then you ended up having almost another midterm grade to help boost your grade. I also would recommend peer tutoring if you aren't familiar with chemistry because some concepts just need further clarification.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Chem at UNC isn't easy so obviously this class won't be any different, but Curtis is a solid choice for Chem 101. If you pay attention to her videos and supplement it with the textbook, it clicks and you can do well. The tests weren't too difficult but due to covid they were linear, you can't go back, which sometimes made them stressful.

Professor Curtis is a very good teacher and explains all the concepts very well. There is a lot of work because we had to watch lectures outside of class along with completing the homework but it was worth it. You can definitely get a good grade in this class if you put the effort in.

Professor Curtis did a great job organizing an online curriculum for chemistry where there is a good amount of collaboration and practice. All of the chem 101 classes were the same except for the online meeting portion. Prof. Curtis answered any questions we had and explained each practice question in a way that was easy to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The online semester was challenging, but Curtis understood that and was lenient with missing class, messing up during exams, etc. Tests were all open note and taken online, not proctored however, they were linear meaning that you couldnt go back once a question was submitted. Chemistry content is difficult but study/participate and you'll succeed.

Curtis wasn't too bad but not great. Assignments include weekly graded hw's, warm-ups before class, quizzes before tests, and forum posts. Forum posts were really annoying, but if you put in the effort and respond with a couple of sentences to the prompt you should be fine. We also had 20min lectures that went over example questions.

Dr. Curtis is a really kind person and provides a lot of resources to help students. However, you really have to put in a good effort or you will struggle. The actual class period kinda sucks since you spend most of the time in breakout rooms, so definitely go to office hours if you can.

Professor Curtis was overall great considering it was online! You have to do most of the work, but if you put the time and effort in you should do fairly well. Don't skip out on the homework, participate and go to office hours. Use your resources and PLEASE STUDY: I didn't and failed my first test. Teaching yourself is hard, but it is rewarding.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The chem 101 professors prerecorded lectures that honestly didn't go into much depth, so you gotta work for understanding. It's not impossible because of outside resources. Breakout rooms during class, which was 20 min, for a few practice problems. Definitely do practice problems/practice exams they give. She holds great office hours!

Curtis is a great professor! She really cares for her students, but you have to work for a good grade in this class. Chem is notoriously hard but not impossible. Technically, the chem profs do very little teaching but they provide the resources for students to succeed. They have a ton of students so this is understandable.

Dr. Curtis is an okay professor when it came to online learning. She pre recorded lectures which didn't go too in depth for the lessons. The actual class comprised of being 20 minutes long and often she would run out of time and rarely go over the problems in depth. The class isn't too difficult if you read the textbook and do the homework.

chem online was actually super organized & structured, and Curtis was super nice & understanding. Our class time was actually only 20 mins so most work was done on our own. theres a lot of TAs and opportunities to get help. Curtis was supa nice tho!!

You have to be willing to do the work in this class. Dr. Curtis provides a ton of materials to help prepare for the final/exams, like practice midterms and quizzes and I would suggest reading the textbook to clear up confusion from the lecture videos. Overall, Dr. Curtis was truly a passionate professor with a great deal of knowledge to share.

Most work is done outside of class with video lectures, forums, before class assignments, and homework. The workload is pretty manageable; it usually takes me about an hour to complete the assignments before class. The quizzes and practice midterm she gives before each midterm is super helpful. Very nice professor!

At least in the online format, all CHEM 101 classes have the same asynchronous lectures, assignments, tests, and quizzes. That being said, they should all be the same difficulty level. Professor Curtis is a great choice for CHEM 101 because she is sweet and understanding when you ask questions in class.

Dr. Curtis kinda sucks. Her teaching style is subpar, she never sounds confident in her explanations, and she honestly just confused me more. Once, she explained an entire problem for 15 minutes just for a student to call her out for getting the wrong answer and she never went back to explain the right way. She seems like a good person but.

There is a lot of material in Chem 101 and it can be overwhelming for any student. There's little instruction and lots of group work. This sounds great until the entire group doesn't know what to do and we teach ourselves wrong. Curtis is a great person, but her online style of teaching isn't good for students well-being.

I had Dr. Curtis for Summer Session 1 and would definitely recommend taking her. She really puts in time for her students and does tons of exam like practice questions throughout lecture. She does grade on participation in lecture and recitation. She also puts you into groups with other students for projects and practice problems.

Dr. Curtis is a wonderful professor IF you are willing to commit to daily readings and homework. If you are not prepared to work for at least an hour a day then I would not recommend this class. The tests are challenging but fair. If you are applying yourself and using all the resources, there is no reason you shouldn't earn a stellar grade. READ!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis has a spunky personality which makes her class a little more entertaining. She does a good job at thoroughly explaining concepts and will work though problems until she feels the majority of the class understands it! She definitely made this class better than I expected it to be.

Dr. Curtis tries her hardest to be a fun lecturer but it just doesn't happen. If you have any sort of high school chemistry background then you wont have any trouble in chem 101 w/ Dr. Curtis, but this class is not a fun experience. Be sure to know how to do all the problems on the practice tests. If you can take this w/ another prof. you should.

Dr. Curtis was a great professor for Chem 101. It is a hard class regardless of who teaches it, but I think she does a great job of giving everyone the opportunity to succeed as long as you work for it. I read the textbook and took notes before class and then studied her slideshows for exams as well. If you do that it will be easy to get an A.

Professor Curtis is a good gen chem professor! Despite what some of the reviews say she has a ton of information to cover and has not much time to finish it. Her exams are very fair but beware test 2 as it is very difficult material and the test is difficult too. She is very accessible with Q&A sessions and her 6 minute meetings. I would recommend.
Dr Curtis was a fun professor to have! Her classes were very easy, and her exams were mostly based off of notes given in the class. Definite recommendation for an intro level Chem class!

Chemistry at UNC is hard regardless of who you take it with. You will have to put in the extra work to understand chemistry. Dr. Curtis is a very understanding and approchable professor, and the best professor you could have for a chemistry class. Taking her class will make your overall chemisty experience better at UNC.

Dr. Curtis was pretty alright until the pandemic hit. She is very enthusiastic, which helps not get bored during lecture, but I fear this class is pretty fast if you don't have a background in chem and you'd need to put in a lot of work outside class. Watch out on Mastering for last minute homework due date changes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis is a good professor! CHEM101 is a difficult course no matter what professor you have, but Dr. Curtis provides many opportunities to succeed in her class. I took her class during the pandemic and she was very great when it came to helping us perform our best. She always has Q&A's which I recommend attending!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis is a good professor. CHEM at UNC is hard, but I did not think Dr. Curtis' class was hard to understand. If you go to class and study for exams, it shouldn't be hard to get an A or B. Tests are not that hard and reflect what is learned in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis was not my favorite. There was little to no application of the topics we were learning to real life or even broader chemistry topics. The "purpose" behind everything we were learning was just to get us to chem 102, but after how dull this class was I don't even wanna take 102. Not a terrible class but so boring and dull.

CHEM 101 is a hard topic at UNC overall, but she was very enthusiastic about teaching it despite it being 8 in the morning. She's a nice person but not the best lecturer, but the class is standardized so it doesn't really matter. If you want to actually learn the material, I would advise taking another professor if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Despite what most of these reviews say, Dr. Curtis is a pretty good professor. Her notes are helpful and tests are similar to practice problems. Chem 101 has a lot of material so she has to go quickly which just means you have to put in a little extra work yourself.

Nice person but doesn't respect the fact that students have other places to be outside of her class. She often continues teaching two to three minutes after class is supposed to be over which isn't very accommodating to those who have class directly after hers. We end up missing explanations because she refuses to stop teaching after class is over.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis was new when I had her, but you can see her enthusiasm for chemistry. In the beginning of the semester they will tell you to not rely on the textbook. Ignore that completely, to succeed I would suggest to read the part of the book before the lecture or you will be completely lost. I highly regret not doing that and thats why I did so bad
The professor is very quirky but sweet. You're graded mainly on tests, so studying is very important. Most of the work you do HAS to be done outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis has a good attitude and is enthusiastic about the subject matter she teaches. She places a lot of emphasis on students showing her they know what to do, so during lectures students have to complete examples of concepts they're working on. Chem 101 is a standard weed-out class, but study the slides and you'll be just fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Curtis was fine. At times, I was confused by the way she explained things. The CHEM101 department works together, so all the sections have the same homework and tests. She wasn't my favorite, but I got through most of the material okay. Your grade really depends on your test grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis is fairly average when it comes to other professors at UNC in terms of the structure of the class, but don't bother asking her questions. She will try her best to come up with some form of response, but in doing so she just ends up confusing the entire class. Also, MC test questions are meant to trip you up, not to gauge knowledge.

Dr. Curtis is super enthusiastic about chemistry but it is really necessary that you read the textbook in order to do well. Lectures are basically the textbook on slides. Overall chem 101 is hard across the board. I don't really think that professor really matters that much for this level of chemistry. She's quirky and it makes 8am classes better.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis is alright, but I tend to get so bored during lectures that I fall asleep. It got to a point during the year in which I was only showing up to lecture for the iclicker points. If you read the book on your own, you'll probably learn just as much, if not more than at lecture.

For chem 101 it really does not matter what professor you have, but out of the ones at UNC I'll say Anna is average. Don't expect to learn everything during lectures, chem 101 is a flip classroom and the bulk of your understanding will come from outside of class practice. Quizzes like every other Wednesday

Chem101 is hard regardless of the professor. You'll have to read the textbook, NOT fall behind, and practice often to get a good grade. Professor Curtis is bubbly and gives alright lectures, but most of the class you have to take initiative and learn outside of class. If you have specific questions, she's always SUPER approachable and helpful!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis is a young and super enthusiastic professor who really loves chemistry, but some of the concepts are just over-complicated. Can get side-tracked and start rushing in lecture. Really helpful during office hours. You will basically teach yourself but she helps a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Anna Curtis is such a goofball! She is a pretty good professor overall. Honestly, Chem 101 wasn't as hard as it was made out to be. I didn't even read the textbook. Make sure you study hard before each exam, do a lot of practice problems, and read each slide! You've got this.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Andrews-Lee is by far one of the best professors at UNC! She is so smart and really cares about her students. The work is 100% manageable, the final and the midterm are very achievable.

Best polisci professor! So passionate about her work and super engaging. Almost too smart for us, so sometimes we leave her hanging when she asks us questions in class. Overall, highly recommend her class! 2 exams, 3 in-class writing assignments, and a final policy simulation. Meet with her in office hours if you want her to explain/help review.

Professor Andrews-Lee clearly cares for her students and their wellbeing both inside and outside of class. Lenient on attendance if you are sick, but make sure to show up as much as you can, as the exams are directly based on lecture slides and conversations held in class. Exams were easy if you studied the way she said. Lots of reading.

Prof Andrews-Lee is such a knowledgable professor on comparative politics and one of the nicest professors I've ever had. She truly wants her students to succeed and the assignments she chose for class are interesting. The midterms and finals are not too difficult and she makes her lectures really engaging! I would definitely recommend her class.

This course deals with Latin American politics, and it is clear that Professor Andrews-Lee is extremely knowledgeable about this topic. I also found it highly beneficial to speak with her during her office hours when I needed clarification on the course. She will suggest scheduling appointments so keep that in mind if you plan on speaking with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Andrews-Lee is one of the most kind and caring professors I've had. She is so great at making the material easily digestible. If I had any questions I found she was more than willing to answer them during office hours and over email, and often went the extra mile to help. If you review the slides before exams you should easily ace them.

Professor Andrews-Lee genuinely cares about her students and the topics she teaches. She's passionate and encourages students to participate regularly in discussions. No textbook, but there's still quite a bit of reading outside class. I learned so much, 10/10 would take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Professor Andrews-Lee is genuinely passionate about what she teaches, and she teaches in a way that's very easy to understand and relate to politics around the world. She's always open to answer questions and takes care to make sure everyone understands the material. Homework was very manageable.
Great professor! Overall, she teaches very clearly and connects topics well. She gives good feedback on all assignments. Very calm environment with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: She cares deeply about her students and is invested in our growth as people. Class is thoughtfully designed and really interesting. She took us to see Wilson Library's archives which was really cool. Great first-year seminar––interesting and fun but not overly difficult

She lectures very clearly. She grades written responses clearly and fairly, although there isn't a set rubric. Group presentations are fairly simple and she's very encouraging and respectful with her feedback. You are expected to do the readings, annotate, and participate in class.

I took LTAM314 with her. It was ok, wouldnt recommend. Topics felt random & irrelevant to modern law. It's graded by maybe 6 things total, so doing bad/ok on one of 2 in-class assignments will knock ur grade down bad. Most ppl didnt read before coming to class but plz do! Even if you like law like me, just take something else there's better classes
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Silva was a delight to have as a professor. She was very kind and I loved that she incorporated different methods of getting participation points for people who may not have been comfortable speaking in front of the class. I loved the readings, and it's clear that she has a passion for the subject. One of my favorite classes of all time.

Only reason I wouldn't take again is becuase no one really seems that interested, so he lectures for a long time. Otherwise, easy exams, short writing assignments, and he is very accessible outside of class. I think he should just teach higher level classes and not a 100-level class, maybe he would get more engagement.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor, I loved his LTAM 101 class. Expect to have 20-45 page readings per class, but the lectures broke down all of the denser, more complex concepts into something that anyone can understand, so it truly wasn't bad at all. Definitely would recommend taking his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He gives students opportunities to come to their own conclusions, help them learn how to work collaboratively, would recommend this class and teacher to anyone interested in the subject

Dr. Walker is an incredibly nice guy and cares a lot about his students. He is newer as a prof but has his stuff together way more than any other prof I had this sem. He makes learning fun and approachable. Don't hesitate to take one of his classes

Dr. Aksin is fantastic! Very nice and understanding, easy grader, and my favorite professor at UNC so far. I never felt like I had to be perfect to answer questions, and she never made learning feel like a chore. Some homework outside of class, but never anything crazy. Overall, very happy with Dr. Aksin, and am excited to take 204 with her!

My German made leaps and bounds under Dr.Askin. She learned German in middle school and as a result better understands the many struggles people learning German experience. She's able to break down complex German topics and make it easy to understand. Also very understanding, clearly hates to grade and doesn't put a lot of emphasis on it.
Dr. Aksin was amazing! I greatly enjoyed GSLL 89 and would take it again if i could! Her lectures were great and I loved the class participation.

This is for GSLL 89 FYS. Dr. Aksin is amazing!!! She picks the most interesting literature/movies and gives fantastic lectures on super interesting topics. We think about language in a totally new way, and she has unique perspectives because of her background in Germany and Turkey. Highly recommend her seminar, and getting to know her as a person!

This is for GSLL 89, FYS. It was such an interesting course and I loved it, it was so easy. She's an amazing teacher and such an easy grader. If you are interested in the holocaust or anything this is the course you should take. Yes, you read a lot but its so fun!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: THIS IS FOR 203. Great professor, her lectures make learning a language easier, totally understanding and flexible, The entire class taught in German but makes sure to keep students in the loop and focused. Grading structure is favorable and encourages you to just come to class and learn. Would recommend to anyone trying to learn German

This seminar was really fun - small class size and pretty much all grades were very creative assignments (presentations and essays). Dr. Aksin speaks with no accent, and she does a lot to keep class topics interesting. This was the best type of environment to learn German in, and my favorite out of all of the German courses I've taken here so far.

This was Professor Aksin's first semester teaching at @UNC. She's a generous grader, an active listener, and has been my fav prof this fall. Class grade depended on 3 large presentations, 2 (5-10pg) essays, and a paper final exam. Very manageable homework load. Small class size too.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: The TA teaches, grades and creates homework for the lab section. Professor simply gives the recitation lecture. In those lectures he is a slow speaker, does not get through all the material in a timely manner. He is also a poor communicator outside of the classroom. He once forgot to tell us about an assignment and then tried to blame us.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lecture plus supplemeting with textbook make the material clear and manageable. Fun lecturer and engages with students. Grades exams rather strictly, (i.e., you want textbook work) but is very lenient when it comes to getting points back. Akaa wants you to succeed, and he was very forgiving with final rounding. Put in the work and you will do well!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor. The midterm exams were both a bit disorganized, but he was honest and fair when grading them. Doesn't take attendance traditionally, but gives pop quizzes throughout the semester as a substitute. Overall very understanding and a funny guy in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Akaa is a caring instructor and wants us to do well. He goes through lectures very diligently and they are easy to follow. Pop quizzes are nice to help provide extra practice problems outside of hw and midterm reviews.

He's a very decent professor. He's a funny guy and clearly knows what he is talking about, and he expects that from you as well. If you put in the work, you'll do just fine. Only reason I didn't get an A is because I was lazy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Made mistakes on each of the exams. Strict grading scale. Provided a lack of practice for final due to poor lecture/hw planning.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Changes exam grading criteria during the exam, grades were always over a month late, consistent mistakes in derivations, didn't appear to truly understand material. Slides copy and paste from textbook. Homework supposed to be consistent over semester, ended at spring break. Disorganized, better off skipping to study and do practice problems.

I took 281L with Dr. Ayangeakaa, and again I found that he was a caring professor that only wanted the class to learn and succeed. Homework sets are a little disorganized and can be long, but the lectures are well-structured and clear, and include examples to work as a class or in small groups. Tests are fair and he prepares you well with examples.

Akaa is amazing. Great lecturer and you can tell he really cares about you and will do anything he can for everyone to succeed. He does not want anyone to fail his class and he really shows it. He's able to take difficult material and break it down for students to understand.

Akaa is a really sweet professor. I will not lie, PHYS 281L is a tough class. There are a lot of lab reports (a handful of group ones) which take quite a bit of time. If you stay on top of your work in the class, you'll be fine. Overall, I really enjoyed the class and would absolutely recommend taking it with Akaa!

Akaa is very kind and personable. My lab section was taught by our TA, so I can't speak to his teaching there, but he was very engaging in our Friday lectures. This class has a pretty high workload (there is a lab report due every week), and he does his best to make this manageable for students, but I would recommend staying on top of things.

281L can be a tough class in that there is a lot to do, and a lot of concepts to learn. I found that Akaa (he goes by his first name) was caring, funny, relatable, and accessible throughout the semester, as well as being a fantastic lecturer and instructor. He was not just a good professor, but a good mentor, making connections with his students.

Hands down the best professor I have had at UNC. Really cares about the students and their concerns. Made it the best and most enjoyable learning environment of any class I have taken at UNC. THE BEST!

Best instructor I have ever had. Very understanding during pandemic. Listened to what the students had to say about their situations & really took that into consideration. Not a hard grader at all as long as you follow the rubrics he provides. Lack of pressure in this class really allowed me to learn a lot. Textbook/readings are provided for free.

EE's tend to be lots of work but I found the amount of reading and writing required for this course outside of class to be hard to keep up with, especially when you're spending about 3 hours a week volunteering for the course and not getting any additional credit for it. Disorganized, but a reasonable prof who will work with you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: Akram seemed to really enjoy teaching the class and the material, and it was actually interesting despite the readings being 20 years old. As long as you make an effort to meet outside of class and get feedback on assignments, you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Akram is a really cool guy that knows a lot about subject matter. The class is pretty laid back and free-flowing and he tries to help the class seems to not be able to grasp a concept. The class isn't SUPER easy, but considering that all the tests are open-note, take-home tests, you should be able to get a solid grade as long as you put in the time
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed my class with Akram. I learned a lot and had a good time!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class is really chill and laid back. Professor Al-Turk is a super chill guy. We learn a lot about the material at hand but he makes time to discuss things about the outside world as well. Not a crazy hard grader, and overall just an enjoyable class.

this class was weird. very high school like, with lots of vanilla discussion. Akram was nice, but didn't necessarily facilitate the strongest discussion, so I wish he would've pushed us more. overall i wanted more from the course
Seriously the nicest guy. You can tell he really cares about his students and he's super easy going.

Akram was well-liked by everyone in SOCI 133. He does a great job facilitating discussion and connecting material on a grand scale. The class is consistently interesting, and Akram is always willing to make time to help students that needed it. Students learn not only about political trends on an abstract level, but also perform data analysis.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Akos is a really cool guy and is very passionate about what he teaches. There are so many different grades so if you bomb one thing its not a huge deal. He makes the class v interesting but you must attend or you get .5 off every time you miss and its only out of 5 points
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Akos is easily the best professor I've had at UNC! He is a tough grader though!!!!!! If you say one thing off or wrong, that's half a point off of something you can only get 3 points on. He truly cares about his students and commits to the material he is teaching. Wouldn't call this an easy A class, more like an easy B. Love Akos, not his grading!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Beware! Bad experience, unfair grader. All grades are final even if .6 points from different letter grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Unfair grader, does not bump your grade even if half a point from next letter grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Professor critically grades. There are group based projects and if you are in a bad group you suffer. Will not move you grade up even if half a point away from a higher grade. Overall bad experience.

A class that you get out what you put in. Akos is reading heavy and this takes a lot of time but it helps you understand class comments. Stickler on grading (points taken off easily) but a cool guy and fun professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Dr. Akos is really nice and cares about his students' well-being. Work isn't super hard, but you still need to take the class seriously because the grading can sometimes be ambiguous and tough. Be sure to participate frequently and read because the reading quizzes are specific. Course material is interesting and very useful for college students!
Tough grader Not much to grade Lots of paper/book to read Pop quizzes
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Tests? Not many--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Akos is such a nice guy. He really cares about his students and their well-being. Course material was very useful. The reading quizzes can get very specific, so make sure you are reading closely. Overall, a good class. Would take again!
Class consists of multiple guest speakers who lecture about boring things. There's a huge final group project and too many readings. The class is super boring and you don't learn anything useful.
If you don't pass this class, you're not alive.
No Comments
Very nice and very helpful professor.  We did a lot of group assignments which were sometimes a little elementary but the class is really easy.
She seemed to really care about us understanding the material and doing well in the class. I really liked the videos and guest speakers.
The class wasn't that hard. Just had to go to take class take the notes that she wanted you to know. Read textbook and get a general idea of whats going on. Not too bad other wise.

Heather is incredible! She is the best professor I have had at UNC. She provides feedback in every class and encourages us to produce our best work. Additionally, she is a creative genius, always coming up with ideas on the spot. A true professor of practice. Thanks to her facilitation, our class became friends. TAKE HER and cherish your time.

I could not recommend Heather more. Class is primarily presentation-based, but she gives super in-depth, constructive feedback. Lots of guest speakers and practical, real-world advice. I learned so much from Heather and I wish she taught more classes because I would absolutely take more with her.

Heather was awesome! She is so cool and kind and her industry experience makes her an awesome resource. Assignments were easy and graded generously. You're required to stand up and present your work almost every day, but it was never intimidating and was just an opportunity to get detailed feedback. Definitely take her if you can!

Best teacher ever! I dreaded having to take ENGL 105, but April made it SO fun! She is lenient, funny, and so personable. She fosters such an amazing classroom environment and allows students to pace themselves throughout the workshops rather than micromanaging. April is laid back and always so helpful if you need to speak with her!

April is such a caring teacher. She is always understanding of students needs and the pressures of being a student. She uses a very creative connection between literature/writing and conspiracy theories to make the class interesting and educational. Although there were more assignments than expected, I enjoyed doing them as we chose the topics.
April is amazing! She's very nice, her class is fun and easy. You do a lot of work in groups with a lot of independence. Very little homework, and a pretty lenient grader. Take her class!!!

All hail April Munroe. She is such a nice and caring ENGL105 professor. She made the class fun and interesting. She was a very relaxed grader and made it very hard to get below an A lol. I am a STEM kid and hated English but she made me love going to her class.

Very chill and easy professor. Super nice, had cool assignments for a freshman english class. She was very open to others opinions and ideas in class and it was hard to get lower than an A on any assignment.

April was a really chill and fun professor! Her topic was conspiracy theories which was super interesting. There are a couple papers (expected of an English class) and a video group project. Definitely reccomend!
April was great! She chose really interesting subjects for the essays, which is hard to do in ENGL 105. Highly recommend for 105!
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: This class was pretty chill and super easy. It's pretty much like a book club. 2 papers based on analysis of your chosen book. Midterm was super easy, she gave us the test the class before. Final exam was to make a playlist on another book of our choice. Don't even have to talk in class, just read books you plan on doing papers and final on.

Pretty standard class. Four papers. Very heavily discussion based. Really thought provoking class about mystery novels and conspiracy theories. One of the better and more fun classes I have taken at UNC. Pretty easy to get a good grade too. Didn't read all the books but will still probably make an A.

This guy is the man. Is very approachable and friendly and wants you to succeed in his classes rather than perform poorly. The presentation you have to do forces you out of your comfort zone and helps you learn about the psychology behind legislature and political issues and bias present today. 10 page paper but makes it an interesting task.

Professor Chakraborty is great. He's not an absurdly hard grader like most of the Poli profs I've had. You can tell he really cares about his students and honestly just wants you to learn something. Definitely a solid choice.

This guy really wants his students to succeed, and while he won't tolerate slacking, he definitely strives to allow everyone to get an A if they are willing to work. Participation matters, but he does a great job of explaining the readings, so just skimming them works. One ten-page paper, but no other homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: She's one of the most understanding and sweetest professors at UNC. I was hesitant to take this class because I had an interest in creative writing but I wasn't entirely sure if I'd succeed in the class. Lawson makes it a great experience and supports you through any issues you have.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: April is not only one of the nicest English professors I've ever had but also one of the most creative and considerate. One ten page paper and daily pop quizzes for ENGL 130. Class discussions are always riveting and her paper feedback is so thoughtful. Definitely take a creative writing class with her if you get the chance.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: omg so talented, please stay @ unc forever
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: April is super nice and chill - the class is very laid back and not difficult if you do the reading (which arent demanding or difficult but are necessary). There are daily quizzes on the readings, and a final short story. A good class to take 'for fun'.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: I enjoyed this class and ultimately learned a lot, but the class did feel disorganized at times. The Canvas page was confusing and work was returned weeks/months after we turned it in. However, for someone interested in GIS, I would recommend this class, as it covered a lot, and Professor Delvecchia was very  helpful and accessible outside of class

Gave many basic assignments, did them all well. Graded 2 months after assigned, I got 7/9 8/12 etc. Couldn't change my strategy for doing those because it was end of year. She gave surprise grade # of perusall comments we made. Never told us to write comments on all but 2. Got a 14/30 on it dropped my grade by 7% got me a B. Super unfair ridiculous
wouldnt take again. Lectures were hard to follow. Everyone completed activities at a different pace. Grading criteria for quizzes was unclear. Not enough guidance

Dr. DelVecchia is sweet but her class is disorganized and her grading criteria is unclear. There's no way to know what she will decide deduct points for in written assignments. 591 needs a recitation to justify the amount of labs. The pacing and structure is nonexistent, and she is unavailable outside of her office hour.

Dr. DelVecchia is the best professor at UNC hands down! She genuinely cares for her students and wants to help them achieve their goals. She will work with you to find what you want to do then help you figure out how to get there. I haven't has a professor as influential as Dr. DelVecchia in my four years at UNC
She is super approachable and passionate. She sticks to policies in the syllabus and doesn't give extensions as much as other professors have because she wants to keep the course consistent.

Professor DelVecchia was very enthusiastic about the content she lectured about. I sometimes felt lost in the class, but I did fine. She prepares you for quizzes and normally offers some extra credit questions. She also drops your lowest quiz grade. There aren't any tests or a final exam, but rather a project. I enjoyed it and would recommend it.
Respectful teacher, really nice. Probably easier first-year seminars based on the course content but she made the class very easy for us.
There are probably better FY seminars to take.

Awesome professor that respects each student! You can tell she really cares about what she's teaching. The class only has a few assignments and a final exam consisting of a paper and a presentation. It's a fun and easy class that I recommend to anyone seeking to fill out a gen ed requirement.

I took this class my first semester and was by far the best class taken at UNC. Not because I have any interest in freshwater ecology-- but rather because I think so highly of Dr. Delvecchia. She is an amazing professor-- cares about her students, is passionate about what she teaches, and grades timely. Take her class if you get a chance!

Dr. DelVelcchia is a kind and enthusiastic professor. GEO 89 is a stress-free class (aside for a 2k final paper) that I always enjoy.

Lectures are interesting if you are invested in the subject matter.
GEO 89 might not be the best class for those with neither a background nor interest in hydrology/freshwater ecology/environmental science.

She is very sweet and caring about her students and is very passionate about what she does which makes it more interesting to learn. The class structure changed throughout the course which made the class seem unorganized. I enjoyed this class this semester.

Prof. DelVecchia's class is one that many people are auto-assigned to and it's not the most interesting class. However, she is clearly very passionate about teaching and she cares about her students. The class could be organized better though.

She's very participation heavy, which makes sense with an introductory language course. She's always happy to help and offer office hours, extra practice, and support when students ask for it. She's very patient and encouraging, the class is a very welcoming environment.
She was really nice and really made sure the students understood the material. I slacked off pretty bad and failed the first 2 test but she worked with me and I ended up doing ok. Don't fall behind.

I absolutely adore Professor Chambless. She is a fantastic professor. In-class time is typically spent practicing skills, so I would recommend taking time to read/take notes on the assigned textbook pages so the content doesn't sneak up on you for the test. Grades fairly and generously, and always gives clear feedback. Take ITAL 101 with her!

I highly recommend Dr.Chambless for Ital 101 and 102; she is an amazing lecturer and has a lot of empathy towards her students. She grades fairly and provides plenty of feedback, as well as resources, to help you improve your Italian. She is very knowledgeable about the textbook content and is always available to meet with students.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She is very friendly and encouraging! Classes have a lot of fun activities to encourage constant learning.  There are short quizzes (vocab or the grammar concept you are learning), but they are easy and only count for 5% of your overall grade. There are also assignments w/each unit to record a conversation about a certain topic with a partner.
Highly recommend Dr. Chambless for any italian course at unc! Great lecturer, very friendly, and very caring

She is very well-organized and supplies a lot of resources to help you practice and understand the material. She also is a very fair grader and truly cares about her students. Participation is a super important part of the class but you definitely don't have to be perfect at the grammar construction or the pronunciation.

This was ITAL 300 not 203, but Professor Chambless is simply an amazing professor. Super kind and accommodating. There were 4 tests, a group project, and a final along with homework and participation. Definitely take Italian at any level with her if you can

Professor Chambless is an outstanding Italian professor. She makes learning a language fun and engaging! You focus on speaking and listening in class, and reading and writing on the homework.Your expereince in the class is very dependent on your partner (who you sit beside in the class). If you pick a good partner, you'll have a blast in her class!
The sweetest woman ever.
Genuinely just the sweetest, cutest woman ever. Such a great teacher! Adore her.

Amy is a wonderful teacher! She is so kind and caring. Something I love about UNC language classes is that the teachers just really want you to love the language as much as they do. I can say that by the end of this semester, I learned a lot and have more motivation to learn more about Italian culture and language.

Professor Chambless is genuinely so kind and patient with students. She's super flexible and understanding when it comes to grading and due dates. She's very encouraging and uplifting. I would recommend her for everyone but especially people who feel like they struggle in language classes. Love her!

Professor Chambless is amazing! Super nice and accessible outside of class, grading criteria is clear, and provides tons of useful resources to study for tests. Classes are mostly spent practicing in groups, so attendance is mandatory. Read the textbook and study and you'll ace her class
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Amy is such a good prof! She was super helpful and easily accessible for office hours or after class. She would quite literally tell us what would be on the exams, which was very helpful. The class itself is similar to 101 and 102, but she focuses more on culture than exam prep in class. Overall I would recommend and would take her again!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Gives good feedback--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Sometimes professors have it out for you, that was my case. I will never take a class she teaches ever again. She gave lots of ways to learn though. I had a lot of test anxiety, I told her with each test I would have to leave and use the restroom (yay IBS) and I guess this made her so suspicious that she never treated me fairly again

Prof. Chambless is so nice! She is completely understanding that we are obviously not going to be near fluent in a beginners class (which isn't as common as you would think) and encourages you to just do the best you can. You get so many grades in this class that even if you bomb a test you still have a good chance of getting an A. 10/10 recommend

I absolutely love Professor Chambless! She makes learning a language so much easier and has so much knowledge that she wants to share with her students. She gives back lots of feedback on assignments so you know what you did right and wrong, but is not a harsh grader. I would take a class with her if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Chambless continues to be one of, if not my favorite professor at UNC. She's literally a dream professor. She's fair in her grading, and creates a great and respectful learning environment, which is important in a subject such as learning a new language. Could not recommend her more!!

Amy Chambless is an amazing professor and one of the best I've ever had! She is extremely approachable and very friendly. Her ability to teach students language is excellent and is no doubt derived from the above qualities. She really cares about her students success and gives ample opportunity to excel. Simply eccezionale!

Prof. Chambless is very helpful and encouraging in class. She is super nice and cares about her students. In my experience, quizzes are always easier than I expect them to be and the midterm was fairly easy as well. There are a reasonable amount of homework grades (including 3 oral grades) and you are graded on participation.
She's a great teacher, taught the material very well and she's a very nice lady. Would recommend her 10000x over.

She is extremely clear during lectures and has no problem with helping you on an individual basis during office hours or after class. She encourages everyone to participate during class. She pretty much tells you what will be on your tests and quizzes, and is very clear in what she expects for an writing done. Would definitely take again.

I don't do well with languages, but she is incredibly supportive and works to help you. She clearly explains the material and provides enough work to solidify it. Her lectures are very clear, and she is a honest but forgiving grader. There was a lot of group interaction. She even graded my final after I finished it so she could go over it with me.

Took the class in Fall of 2025. Class was TA-graded, but Dr. Cooper structures it well and doesn't set expectations terribly high. Show up, follow along, and you're in a solid spot to get a good grade. Course was mainly surface-level, though definitely more covered than your typical person would know. Lectures weren't boring or overly interesting.
Take her class! She's amazing and so chill. Dr. Cooper genuinely cares about her studnets, and it's so refreshing.

Lectures are a little boring. 3 essays and 2 exams (also essays) are graded by TA generously. Can learn a lot about academic writing from this course. Dr. Cooper is helpful with essays and arranges the course carefully (in Canvas). Only issue: she's from Duke
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Cooper is an amazing lecturer! Though some lecture topics were not as interesting as others, overall, her style of teaching is really nice. Only drawback was the TA grading which was pretty harsh (at least for my TA). Felt they were too difficult considering it was just a gen-ed class. Otherwise, I'd recommend!

Mandy Cooper was an excellent professor. While some of her lectures were a miss, most were interesting. Everything was good, except for the TA, who graded every essay pretty harshly, in my opinion. There were multiple readings, but they were interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Cooper is super nice and caring. Lectures were very hit or miss imo; some were super interesting, and others felt like a chore. Lots of writing but graded pretty easily (may have been specific to my TA). No tests at all and offers a ton of extra credit; pretty easy A overall, but there are definitely more interesting gen-ed history classes.

As a person, Professor Cooper is amazing. She truly cares about us as students, even in a large class. The way she set up the midterm and final was great. However, my TA who graded all my essays was unfair and difficult in grading considering it's a gen-ed. The lectures also weren't the most engaging although she is very passionate about her work.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I loved this class and it was pretty interesting most of the time. Dr. Cooper is very passionate about what she teaches, making the class great. There were a few essays, which I found to be a little harshly graded by my TA, but overall I enjoyed the class and totally recommend!

This class is great easy gen-ed to take. 5 essays throughout the semester that make up most of the grade, which are graded by the same TA. Gives opportunities for extra credit and different opportunities to earn your participation grade. Dr. Cooper was passionate, knowledgeable, and very willing to work with students.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class! As someone who loves history her lectures were very engaging and she often kept things light and easy to understand. Assignments weren't bad at all and she offers a lot of extra credit. Great Professor.

The lectures could get a little long, esp if you're familiar with US history already, but Dr. Cooper was super cool and knowledgable, regardless. Her assignments are very clear, but you are being graded by a TA who can be inconsistent and give little feedback due to the volume of papers. office hours and the writing center can help you do well!

Professor Cooper is a great instructor, and the class is very manageable. Most assignments are papers, and she gives plenty of time to complete them. Your grade can depend on your grader, since some are stricter than others. Still, her lectures are engaging, and you learn a lot in the course.

Dr. Cooper is very knowledgable! She is passionate about what she teaches and is easy to talk to and encourages group discussions. Your TA will be grading everything so I would say to make sure to go to both their office hours as well as Dr.Cooper's if you feel like you should have had higher scoring/asking how to improve for future assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Love her, great lecturer and very knowledgable of class material. HOWEVER, your grade will entirely rely on who your TA is. I am averaging a B in this class, while my friends with other TAs are getting As. Don't be afraid to go speak to her about problems you are having, very kind, very understanding. W
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Cooper is knowledgeable and very passionate about the material she teaches. Do the reading and participate in lectures, and you will do great in the class. I have been to her office hours and she is very approachable and always willing to work with students. I wish I could take more classes with her, she is amazing!

Angela is one of the best Spanish professors that I have ever had. She is an extremely fair grader but also provides good feedback. She made each class fun and not boring, even when using slides to teach. She is hilarious and always made class feel like a welcoming place, and she gives you lots of practice to prepare you for the tests and final.

Angela is so sweet and entertaining, but she genuinely wants to you to learn and understand topics in class. I never once dreaded going to her class. Participation is required and recorded throughout the semester, so try to answer questions frequently even if your not 100% sure. Definitely take Angela's class if you have the opportunity.
Very doable SPAN 105 class. She was kind and graded fairly, and class was genuinly fun to attend. Participation does matter a lot, so keep that in mind.
Great TA. She was very helpful and understanding. Reviewed necessary material and explained the labs thoroughly. Would recommend.
** EMES 101L** she is the best. checks off your labs! she understands you are taking this lab for the credit. Took her at 8am bc of how much you want to take her lab time.
Such an amazing TA! Very helpful during office hours!
Easy class. Amy is great with giving feed back. Not a hard class just turn in stuff in time and review notes.
Great TA. Always available for office hours / Zoom. Helpful with any and all questions!

For EMES 101. Ami was the TA for this class, and I'm not completely sure she knew what she was doing. She didn't answer a lot of questions thoroughly and was not always available for office hours (consistently rescheduled them) or in class. Nice person though.
Ami's great. Easy A, not afraid to give good feedback and answer questions. Would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: *WGST 270 Women and Sport. Good lectures and discussion about modern topics. I have no interest in sports but learned a lot from this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Ashley is wonderful! We had a group book club project, which was really interesting and something I haven't seen before in a class at UNC yet. She clearly cares about her students and makes sure everyone feels comfortable and safe. Her feedback on assignments is great, and she tells you exactly what to fix and why you got points off.

*wgst 340* Professor Ashley's decent. You can tell she cares about the material. LOTS of reading and weekly journals that are pretty tedious and boring. The material was interesting if you are interested in the topic l. Has barely graded all semester so no idea what my grade will be. Service learning for apples was the best part of the class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: If you are interested in the content you will love this class. class is split into lecture, activity, and discussion. You can miss 3 of each. She covers a wide range of topics and truly wants you to enjoy the class. Exams are online with clear feedback for how to improve. One of my favorite WGST classes at UNC!
This class was great, and prof Ashley was super kind and definitely very knowledgeable. Class can be boring if you dont care about the content but still very engaging.

Dr. Ashley is such an amazing professor! She is so understanding and really cares for the wellbeing of her students. I actually had her for WGST 340 and had a lot of readings, but she is very knowledgeable in a plethora of topics, so I highly recommend taking a WGST class with her.

I loved Dr.Ashley's class. super interesting but you def have to do the readings. She had a lecture, activity, discussion setup for her MWF class which I really enjoyed. Had to read a book for a book club but it was engaging and not overly strenuous. You will learn a lot and should get an A if you do your work and participate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Wonderful professor, very understanding and super lenient. 100% take this class if possible
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Everyone can tell that Amalia puts so much hard work into her lectures. She seems genuinely interested in what she's teaching and is happy to provide additional resources if anyone has questions. Amalia is a very understanding person and allows the lowest grades to be dropped. She's very engaging and loves to learn from her students.

RELI 101 ended up being one of my favorite classes I've ever taken at UNC. Professor Tsoulouhas gives amazing lectures and makes complicated ideas easy to understand with real-world case studies. I would definitely take a class with her again!
