Really nice and wants you to do well. Extremely knowledgable about Eastern European Jewish history. I learned a lot of history I wasn't familiar with. Graded by forum posts, participation, 2 regular papers & a research paper. A bit unorganized- didn't always answer emails and didn't post grades. I didn't know how I was doing, so I pass/failed.
I got a lot out of this class. It is a lot of reading but it is worthwhile, and Professor Auerbach is sensitive to her students. Her lectures are interesting.

Even though I found this my most challenging class, Auerbach is a great professor. She drops your lowest quiz grade and I didn't receive any grades under an 80. Her lectures can sometimes be hard to follow so I found it better to just listen and write notes based on the readings, but the content is really interesting and it's a great class overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Auerbach is a wonderful lecturer. She cares a lot about what students have to say and their progress in learning. The powerpoints for every class are online, too, which helps a lot with note-taking in and out of class. She can be pretty long-winded sometimes, but she's insanely knowledgeable on what she teaches. Recommended.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Would recommend taking this class. Professor Auerbach really cares about the topic and you read interesting things. Grading is fair. The course is really well organized and the lectures are interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: I loved this class. The professor is passionate about the topic and makes it interesting. Quizzes are easy, and she tells you what to study for exams. Worth taking.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Good professor and interesting readings and lectures, but lectures can be a bit confusing, as she jumps around a lot. Dr. Auerbach is nice and knowledgeable and the papers and quizzes aren't that bad. The exams can be tough, but she gives you a list of IDs before hand which make it easier. Very interesting topic, take if interested in the Holocaust
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Okay. So I would advise against taking this class unless youre pretty tolernat of professors. She is pretty scatter-brained and her lectures are so long and so power point heavy. I cared about the Holocaust going into the class, and honestly going to class every day was a struggle. You can skip some and still be fine because she posts lecutre

She is the best teacher I have had in terms of hearing students out and respecting their opinion. She never makes anyone feel stupid and is great at allowing the students to spark a conversation. Do the readings and show up to class and she will not give you any problems. Grading could be much more clear but overall a great woman.
Great class. Lot of reading, but all really interesting. I learned a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: This was one of my favorite classes. She made her lectures interesting and paid attention to comments that students made. She made everything clear in lectures and what we had to prepare. Tells you what to study for the final. You will do well if you read and study for the exam. Quizzes are easy and count for a lot.

Worst class I've taken so far. Listening to her lectures was incredibly frustrating. It was as if she wasn't speaking English at times because I really couldn't decipher what she was trying to get at. Super disorganized. Also says 'um' about 600 times per lecture which drove me mad.
Interesting class, lots of reading but worth the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Just to give you a general idea of how disorganized and pointless Karen's lectures are: we have been sitting in lecture for over 45 minutes and are still just going over the outline. She rambles on and on and never makes any coherent point. Worst class I've ever taken.
Very caring, I went to office hours and she helped with my essay. She's not as tough with grades if you read. I liked the lectures and readings, essays are difficult but exams aren't.

Good class. Participation counts for a lot and exams are easy, she lets you prepare answers ahead of time. Good lectures, a lot of reading but interesting and many diaries and things like that, so it was a lot but not difficult to read.

Worth taking. There's a lot to read but it's always interesting, so are lectures and if you pay attention you'll be fine. Grading can be tough if you don't read but I read and did well. She gives the questions before the exams so as long as you prepare, they are easy.

This class was dreadful. Each lecture felt like a stream of consciousness and she never got to the point. She was very disorganized and her teaching style was very ineffective. The amount of reading was ridiculous, for example: an entire book and four primary sources as a night of reading wouldn't be out of the norm. Avoid at all costs.

You can tell that she is very smart but her lectures are terrible. She is very hard to follow and I often walk away from class not being able to tell you one thing I learned.  There is an absurd amount of reading for an introductory course and the grading on papers/tests is harsh. I would not recommend this class to anybody!

Shes awesome. Show up to class and youll do very well in the class. She genuinely cares how youre doing and was willing to move assignments around based around how we were doing. Tests will push you for time, but getting 90% on them padded with all the homeworks will give you a pretty easy A

Dr. Younge is super nice, upbeat, and willing to help. The class material for Busi405 is commonly seen as common sense, but she finds a way to make it interesting through class activities and games. The tests are a little long and will push you to work a little more quickly than normal, but the classes tend to performs well. Homework is minimal.
Super nice professor. Always had interesting exercises and brought lots of energy to class. The tests were insanely long and difficult for no reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: ABY was one of the nicest professors I've had. She speaks very fast but she has a true passion for teaching french and ensuring that we understand everything. I would definitely take another class with her.
SHE IS THE BEST! Was so encouraging and always so helpful. take her for 105!!

Azza is such a light spirit who makes learning french enjoyable. She has a sense of humor which is refreshing in a classroom environment and she grades very fairly if anything she tries to give you as much credit as she can within reason. The course covers a lot of material, but she makes sure to go over specifically what we will be tested on.

She is such a kind, supportive, and funny instructor. She treats each student with respect despite different levels. She also explains cultural and relevant background info. She is just funny and seems to really enjoy teaching. Make sure you do the pre work. She is a fair grader. Participation matters and will help you succeed.

Azza is the best professor I have ever had. She encourages everyone to speak in French each class and I can testify that this has improved my French so much. She is very graceful correcting us when we make mistakes so we learn but are not afraid to mess up. She wants everyone to learn and succeed and knows how to help us do so!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is really funny and is very understanding of students and respect their time. The class was taught solely in French which really helped me develop my conversation skills. She can be a little intimidating but she is a really nice person.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof. ABY is excellent! She speaks almost exclusively in French (as expected in 204) but will kindly answer vocab and grammar questions at any point. Not a harsh grader but definitely values hard work and participation. Compassionate, encouraging, and accommodating. Take class from her if you have the chance!

Professor Youssef is by far the better of the two french professors I have had at UNC. She is much easier in grading and is sassy which I think is super funny. She is also super accommodating with grading (I forgot to submit half of a HW assignment and she gave me full credit for it). Overall, her class was the best french class I have taken.

I loved Professor Youssef! She is by far my favorite french instructor I have had at UNC. The french department in general is difficult but Youssef made it much more manageable. She was much less strict when it came to grading and tried to award as many points as she could on exams.

She grades a little harshly but not too bad. The homework is required for all FREN105 classes and usually takes about an hour. All papers are turned in twice and she gives a higher grade on the second. Participation is important and she will be nice when correcting you but mistakes show on your participation grade.

Native French speaker - she gives great feedback plus the curriculum is structured to give a good basis of the language compared to simply memorizing a load of vocabulary. 20% 4 tests, 10% in class participation, 15% 3 single page papers, 10% midterm, 15% Homework, 10% 5-10 interview (all in French), 20% Final
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Amanda was a good professor. Her lectures were very informative and she cared a lot about students' well-being. However, her criteria weren't always clear when it came to grading papers. I often got feedback that I didn't follow the prompt when I would address everything in the prompt. The class was easy, but don't expect to ace the papers.

Amazing professor and person! She cares about her students mental, physical health and wellbeing. I learned so much about myself and about how groups function within society in her class. I would highly recommend her.

Amanda said at the beginning of the semester that she wanted this to be a class that you could put on a temporary back burner in times of stress or difficulty. She values her students' physical and mental wellbeing above all else, which is clear in her easily approachable demeanor and ability to accommodate each student in their unique situation.
Amanda is such a wonderful professor who really cares about her students. The class was an easy A but was super interesting. Her lectures were very insightful
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Amanda is one of the best instructors I have met at UNC. She tried to make everything easier and more convenient to her students. She could explain some confusing concepts very well. She is always very patient and very responsive to emails. The short answer format of the midterm and final is not easy, but overall I enjoyed taking the course.

Amanda is very nice and caring. If you ever need assistance or leniency, she is eager to help. She is a decent lecturer with a passion and competency in her subject. Pretty easy instructor too. I recommend.

I loved POLI 215 with Prof Aziz! She is always available via emails or at her online office hours. Although the course was async and there were lectures 3x a week, she kept them pretty short (25-30min) and always asked us for ways to make class better. She was very accommodating and she's a great person! 10/10 would recommend

Her tests are incredibly difficult, and large portions of your grade rely on group projects. I HATE the way she organizes her canvas. Arguably the most engaging and easy to understand class of the semester was the day our TA taught the lesson. Also 2 points are taken off your semester grade for every class you miss starting day one. Good otherwise.

2 tests, 4 individual assignments, and 4 group assignments ending with the final research project. Tests were moderately difficult; use flashcards for vocab and practice quizzes for question style. Focused mostly on application. No final, just comment on other projects. Great instructor, super experienced and friendly if you showed you cared.

Prof. Entwisle is nice, but she will get mad if ur on ur phone. The class is okay, basically one big group project the whole semester and the grading criteria for it is unclear, and if u miss a class its 2 pts off ur overall grade. It was not hard to get a B+ or an A, but only take this if ur interested in the subject, or ur gonna be really bored.

Barbara is VERY knowledgeable, but she occasionally was condescending when speaking to students. Her feedback was great and fair, but sometimes grading was harsh. Overall not bad, but I wouldn't choose to take her again.

Barbara is amazing and clearly knows what she's talking about. The class was pretty easy, there were clear rubrics for everything, and you learn a lot about research processes. Exams were a bit tricky with vague study guides, but its fine cause you can ace everything else. Lots of group work, so depending on your group you may have more work.

Prof Entwisle can be a good prof at times but sometimes it feels like she has 0 humanity. There were several times people expressed concerns and she seemed like she couldn't care less. We had two tests that were less than 10% of our grade and I failed both and still got out with a B. Easy B to pass but no one felt great about tests.

Professor Entwisle was very knowledgeable about the subject. The individual assignments were easy and graded fairly, but the semester-long group project was somewhat difficult and graded harshly. Also, the multiple choice questions on the tests were unnecessary difficult.

It is evident that Dr. Entwisle knows her stuff and is passionate about the course. TA gave very vague feedback which was frustrating. Odd grade scale (ex. a test is 8 points). Tests are difficult. She is very understanding about attendance as long as you communicate. The course is tough but Barbara really cares.

Assignments were generally easy to complete and the material wasn't hard but the exams felt like you were set up to fail. There wasn't any one I spoke to who felt confident about the exams so no matter how much you study, its not going to work out. Also the group projects felt repetitive.

Prof Entwisle makes class easy enough, but the big project we worked on all semester was broken into small assignments that felt repetitive. No tests or quizzes though, just open-note in-class assessments, which was great.

Prof. Entwisle entirely re-structured the class once COVID started. There were no exams, quizzes, etc - only small individual assignments and a large group project that spanned over about half the semester. Participation is important. Overall I really liked the way the class was designed for online learning and would highly rec this course.

Her classes are very structured and you can tell she has done this for many years. She is clear about what we are learning and explains concepts well. The vocab quizzes are really easy and straightforward, but you will need to study well for tests. She is a very kind and competent teacher - not sure what others are saying.

She doesn't give tell you much about what's on exams. Exams cover things not always covered in class. Exams have test corrections, but you need them because typically people make in the 70s for her exams without test corrections. Class is a little boring, but just show up.
Professor Entwisle is very knowledgeable, but the class got a little boring at times. This seminar on American universities definitely didn't feel like a sociology class.

Super simple and easy to understand interesting assignments, no exams, straight forward lectures, tons of guest lectures from the insurance industry, and I left the class feeling like I learned a good deal. One of my favorite classes here

Decent professor for a decent class, very much focused on developing industry knowledge and applications for the insurance/risk market. Show up, generally express interest, and you'll get an A if you don't screw up the assignments. Much more valuable for the guest speakers than the lectures. Dr. Baum has a lot of connections and wants us to learn.

Rachel is such an amazing professor. Super knowledgeable in insurance. She will connect you with so many industry people, and help get internships set up. She is a legend. DATA540 is really easy, but the final project was unnecessarily confusing. The part of the class with Steve Bennett was really tedious and boring though.

She taught this class for the new risk management minor, and she is so amazing. For a first time teacher she is so good at explaining things, the class is engaging, the material is interesting, and her and Prof Bennett bring in a ton of guest lecturers. Cannot recc this class enough.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best EXSS class I have taken. Take this class if you can.

Best EXSS class I have taken at UNC! Exams are very similar to the study guides, and we were given the prompts to the final exam question a week before. Loved her lectures as they were interesting and engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took Professor Baez the first year she offered EXSS 581, I loved the assignments, and she was clear about what she wanted. The content was interesting and if you have a psychology background, it's cool to see topics and how they play a role in sports injuries.

Please do not take this class if you are looking for an easy gen ed. I worked so incredibly hard for the B+ that I go. Professor Bauer is kind, but her lectures are incredibly disorganized and the amount of material included on midterms is insane. Get ready to study and memorize your heart out if you take this class.

Very difficult considering it is an introductory level class. Her lectures go incredibly fast and are very disorganized to the point where I had to reorganize all my notes after every lecture. Midterms and exams are written only and require very dense knowledge about the structures covered and memorization of terms, dates, and architects.
This is a great professor and a great course to take some time here at UNC. Made learning more about the art styles in movies very entertaining and had good commentary on the aspects of movies.

This class was a lot of fun! I think this class is one that you can take regardless of your level of interest in film, because the movies were all very good and the lectures were extremely interesting! Just get ready to write a few papers, but overall the work is very manageable and the professor is so nice and accommodating!

JJ is one of the best professors I've had at UNC so far. This was a rough semester, but JJ's class was a bright spot. I'm not an art major and have never been the creative type, but the material in the lectures was pretty interesting and she is good at grasping students' attention. Great class and great prof

I am not an artsy person but was invested in Dr. Bauer's classes because of how she presented these buildings. She tells you about architecture as if she was there when every building was built, and it is genuinely so engaging. The paper prompts were unclear in parts, so work closely with your TA on how they will be grading essay formatting.

Amazing class! Every subject was not only interesting, but my favorite part is that Dr. JJ Bauer wears shirts every lecture that coincides with what you were supposed to watch before that class. Overall, it is a writing-heavy class, but nothing not manageable. Her pacing is perfect and recitations are interesting as well. Highly recommend.

I took this class for a VP credit and it was honestly pretty interesting. Im not an art person but I enjoyed Prof Bauers lectures and connections to history. The tests are relatively easy and she made them open note, but her lectures move really fast, so it's difficult to keep up. There are also 3 3-4 page papers but they're pretty simple
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: paper and assignment criteria is usually v unclear, usually its outdated. there are not 1 but 2 midterms in her classes. yeah, 2. on top of the 2 midterms, theres like 3 papers & a final, & post to a forum for 5 of the weeks. usually a recitation on fridays & made us write a 6pg paper in the span of 3 days only knowing the prompt on the 1st day.

Bauer is a sweet lady who is born to be into art history. She is extremely insightful into decorative arts of all aspects. We were required to finish a 10-page paper throughout the semester but once you have your topic in your mind or finish it partly, you can receive some of the grades. She always has good ideas to help you do your research.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Far too much work given the circumstances. Not interested in student feedback on onerous paper grades for a fundamental-level film course. When she assigns you a paper, be prepared to forget about the rest of your day.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: *taken remotely* -- Guidelines were unclear for the final project- given an example outline for an entirely different project than initially described and then criticized when we asked for clarification. Exams consist of lengthy papers but they are mostly graded lightly! However, a fun course if you love movies and want to learn more about them.

This class was really fun, but don't expect to breeze through, it's a lot of work, Dr. Bauer has you there to really learn about film techniques. She's fun in lecture though, it's all worth it. I was going through a tough time in my life and she was so caring. Very fun VP credit! You'll never watch movies the same way again, you'll love it
Not bad Just do the work and you will be fine.

this class was a gen ed for me but i loved this class. prof and TA are awesome and i learned a lot. not a lot of hw for the class, probably an 1-2 each week but readings are required and they do notebook checks. exams were easy and theres xtra assignments to pad out ur grade. overall a super nice guy who wants to see students succeed!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Respected

reviews.comment: I LOVED this class and the teacher. He is a great lecturer and I was never bored in his class. He is very clear on his assignments and exams. If you put in the work, this is a very easy class to get an A in. he gives and adequate amount of work. There is a lot of readings but they are enjoyable. He also made us food for the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Lots of reading to do with the required book. Honestly, most of it can be overlooked by the lecture and recitation. Very knowledgable about the content and created a light hearted atmosphere.

This was my favorite course so far at Carolina. It made me reflect on my own faith and consider ways we could be doing better. Professor Bayne is super knowledgeable about both Christianity and Native history. Sometimes it was tough to confront so many difficult moments, but he always gave us helpful context and led creative group discussions.

Dr. Bayne and Carla were amazing this semester. The classroom environment is very engaging and interesting, and both are very caring. As long as you pay attention and study the exam guides, an A is nearly guaranteed. The best professor and TA duo I have had at UNC so far.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lots of reading and lecture notes, if you pay attention and show up you should be ok. Tests can be challenging if you dont show up but you create a study guide together so no reason to do bad. Overall interesting class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Bayne is amazing! He is very passionate about what he's talking about and is very nice! definitely not overwhelming! LOVE Carla(TA), although I believe she will be leaving next semester, so hopefully the next one will be good too! Def recommend!

Dr. Bayne is a great professor who knows so much about what he talks about. This course was very discussion based but it was very enjoyable and easy to take part in if you did the readings. It involved also going to plays of UNC arts performances and all assignments were given plenty of notice ahead of time. Overall a great course, would recommend

Dr. Bayne is super nice and really knowledgeable! All of the projects and assignments we did helped me think more deeply about the topics we were discussing and helped me explore lots of arts forms I had never been interested in before. I really enjoyed the class and would definitely recommend to someone looking for FC-AESTH credit.

Bayne and his TA were very nice and incredibly understanding. The class has a lot of work, but the work itself is pretty easy. The readings are very long and boring but you can get around doing them except for when it comes to discussion posts. Make sure to attend class and take notes, as the slides are very vague and mostly consist of pictures.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I enjoyed Prof. Bayne's class this semester. There is a lot of reading and you need to be prepared to discuss it at length in class. The work wasn't too bad though - discussion posts and responses, 2 quizzes, 1 paper, and a final project (no exam!) He wasn't good at keeping up with grading though. Overall very nice guy who wants you to succeed.

The class itself wasn't that much work: 10 discussion posts and replies, 2 quizzes, 1 midterm paper and a final project. But Bayne had no rubrics, barely any guidelines for assignments, and grading was random and subjective. He also didn't grade the majority of our assignments until the last week of class which was stressful and frustrating.

Disscussion posts were graded easily, but the readings are such a drab, and some are quite long. He started out quite nice, but became super jaded as the semster went on. Lectures are helpful for the essay portion of the exam, but referring to the slides to study is useless, there is nothing helpful on them.

This class is just made up of discussion posts throughout the semester, book review paper, 1 midterm and 1 final. Super easy. Caring teachers, and a nice environment. Would recommend to take for a gen end. Easy A.
Great guy, very organized. Made his midterm very fair and explained exactly what students needed to do. Material could be dry at some times.

I really enjoyed taking IDST128 with professor Bayne. He made the lectures interesting and the use of Jonathan Haidt's book was very informative and compelling. IDST128 is overall a great class when choosing a triple I.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The topic of the course was supposed to be about how to discuss hard topics (race, religion, and politics) in a respectful manner, but I feel like Dr. Bayne didn't teach us how to talk about religion. Instead, he mainly focused on colonization and moral philosophy. He's a nice guy, but his content didn't allign with my expectations for the course.

This whole class felt messy. He was fine but really boring and often went off on tangents that did not relate to the topic. We were supposed to learn about religious nuances in conversation and spent 3 weeks looking at a map of the conquistadors...yeah. Quiz wasn't super hard but he had the hardest of the three professors. Lots of vocab.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Seems decently well-informed, but did not adapt very well to the needs of the Triple-I class format. Lectures were dull and often focused on the same topics over and over. Relatively easy to score well, just do the homework and study vocab terms for his quiz. He is much better suited for a small class.

While the general course is fairly disorganized, I do not attribute much of that to Professor Bayne, though, his lectures only really focused on one topic despite the course being supposed to delve into multiple. He clearly is passionate about his research and is caring, but his teaching was not consistent with what was expected from the class.

Overall the problem wasn't as much him as it was the chaotic organization that is Triple I courses at UNC. Though his lectures kind of drifted from the topic, he still clearly is a smart guy who knows what he is talking about.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Bayne is a legend. This course taught me so much I never imagined and his care for both the subject and us shined through. He genuinely gets to know his students and adapts to  your struggles. Sometimes the reading was pretty high level and he focuses on small group discussions, but they were well organized and I learned a lot.

Most of class time is spent in class/group discussions and activities. Seems poor at time management, we almost never did everything in class he said we would. He tends to be unclear about specific rubrics/instructions and due dates, and rarely answers emails, but he is also lenient in return. Wouldn't dread taking him again but would rather not.

Professor Bayne's enthusiasm for his class is truly infectious. There is some reading and long videos up to an hour but if you take 2-3 hours out of your day you're able to complete your response quickly. The articles and documents provided increased my fascination for religion in America. The e-book was my favorite part of the class. Was very fun.

I would certainly recommend RELI 151 with professor Bayne to anyone considering taking it. The class is interesting and taught me a lot while not being overly demanding. There is one book you need to buy for class (for a book review near the end of the semester). Professor Bayne and his TA were both very kind and cared for their students.

Overall, his class was easy. His exams are very straight forward, only one midterm and a final, and before each one he lets the class come together and come up with terms you based on the reading and lectures you may need to study, and then that list acts as a word bank for the exam. Exams are based on the vocab, and then 1-2 essays. Easy professor
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took this as a gen ed and loved it. The TA is caring. Starts each class asking you to check in with your peers. He let the class come up with the midterm and final topics, let me make up the midterm when I missed it. There are readings but I never read any of them. Just do the work, show up for class, and pay attention and you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Bayne's okay, his lectures are dry at best but the material is fairly engaging. There's a fair amount of reading, but you don't really have to do it unless you have a forum post for the day. He can be slightly insensitive about the material (white man teaching Latin American religion), but overall an alright professor. Loved the TA for the course.

Beginning of the semester, the TA's make the class a lot harder than it needs to be and often take off points for no reason or with vague directions on things like what "have analysis" is. Bayne is a nice guy, however, and definitely do the extra credit he offers. There are also pop quizzes which can be annoying. Most of the class got an A or A-.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I feel like I took a different class than the others who posted this semester. Assignments were easy enough and my TA answered my emails quickly. I met with Dr. Bayne in office hours and he was very friendly and even remembered my name from lecture. There's one paper and an E-book final. I learned a lot about different religions, which was cool.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class was pretty solid overall with the exception of questionable grades from the TAs. You must go to class everyday and take notes because there are pop quizzes.  Lectures were informational but could be pretty boring. There are is a large paper and an E-book throughout the course and Ta's just look for something to take points off for.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took this class for geneds and assumed it would be easy from reviews. However, you don't receive helpful feedback on graded assignments and the TA would take off random points for no real reason. Bayne was not very involved besides showing up for the lectures. Overall, I did not enjoy this class and the TA's have a huge impact on your grade.

I took this class to fulfill geneds and thought it would be somewhat not difficult through what I researched about the class. Grading in this class is questionable with the TA's, I found my TA taking off points just to do it and not really providing great feedback. Overall, simple class but TA's matter throughout this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This class isn't terrible but the grading policy doesn't make sense. You can be in class every day but miss one day, and if there's a pop quiz that day, there's no way for you to make it up and it's going to hurt your grade. The grading policies for forums and assignments overall are unclear. It was probably better online but this semester is rough
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Really interesting class and thought provoking. However, it was so much reading, more than I've ever had in other higher level histories. He makes the readings accessible, but they're often long and repetitive. Graded on forum posts, one paper, two quizzes, and a final paper or project. Rubrics for these are often unclear. An awesome guy though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Bayne has been one of the best professors I've had at UNC. His grading is very clear and reasonable. With the transition to online, he couldn't have done anything better. He truly cares about his student's well-being and their education He and his wonderful TAs fostered an environment that made me want to learn.

Professor Bayne is awesome. His lectures are very interesting. He always gives good feedback and interesting ideas to help you with your papers. Go to his office hours and he will help. He is extremely humane and caring, understands that circumstances can impact your performance, and is willing to give an extension on a deadline if needed.
Amazing teacher! So kind, funny, and really gets to know his students. Lectures a lot but is super passionate about his topic.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: His lectures are engaging, and he takes time to answer students' questions. You don't have to read, as he goes over everything you need to know in lecture, and he tells you the specific readings that will be discussed in reciation. There are pop quizzes but they are open notes and easy. There are two essays and a final, which are graded liberally.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Bayne is a true gem in the reli departmeny. He is brilliant, motivational and fun; you wont regret sitting in his lectures for a semester. Beware though, 2-3 pop quizzes! Also, the TAs do all the grading, so hopefully you have a nice one. Overall, I would love to take another one of his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Reli 140 with Bayne was easy and interesting! The TA's grade pretty easily which is nice. If you just do the bare minimum you'll be fine. Just go to lecture and recitation for the info on the 3 pop quizzes (which are easy too). Although lecture can be boring sometimes, Prof Bayne is a great guy and a good lecturer. Good class to fulfill a gen ed.

I love Bayne!!! He's the best. He's really passionate and knowledgeable. He also makes a genuine effort to get to know his students. I could not recommend him enough. I'm not a reli major but I loved this class. I learned so much and really enjoyed it.

Professor Blayne is a fantastic lecturer and definitely knows what he's talking about. He tries to engage with students and keep it as entertaining as possible. Beware of pop quizzes (it's how he takes attendance) and you HAVE to do the reading otherwise you will be VERY lost. Occasionally he does speak/go through slides very fast making it difficult to take notes but that's my only complaint
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: I LOVED professor Bayne, but the workload of this class was just too much. There are on average 4 readings you must complete before each lecture in order to keep up. There are no tests, but 2 long papers, which are either graded harshly or nicely depending on your TA. And pop quizzes make you regret that ONE reading you didn't do the night before.
I loved Professor Bayne! His lectures were interesting and he was easy to listen to and approachable.  Your TA is key because they do all of your grading so it is important to show them you care.

Dr. Bayne's class has been one of my favorites so far at UNC. He is a great lecturer and you can tell he loves what he does. Class is very substance heavy but he does a good job of peppering them with videos and jokes.  I would definitely take this class again.
Professor Bayne is one superb professor!  His lectures are well organized, well presented, and fascinating.  His TA's are his  team members and everyone is on message.  Professor Bayne is a star!

Bayne's Class was great! It was extremely enjoyable and made me want to take another religion class at UNC. The TAs do grade harshly, so be careful on your papers. I never did any of the readings, but still managed to pull a decent grade in the class. Only one exam (the final) so just make sure you study for it. He basically gives you the answers.

Professor Bayne is awesome! The lectures are boring and there's a lot of reading, but the class was pretty easy for satisfying 3 Gen Eds. Just come to class and put in the effort and its an easy A. The TAs are really harsh graders so make sure you see them outside of class for your papers and you'll be fine. Would definitely take this again!

Bayne is a very good professor and has a great understanding of the material.  However, although the TA's are nice, they are harsh graders and the directions on most assignments are very bleakunclear.  Also, attending class is a must, and there is a lot of reading for each class.  Only take the class if you are truly interesting in the course.
Awesome professor! He actually cares about learning everyone's names and getting their opinions on the readings.  He's approachable and the material is interesting.  Definitely recommend.

I had Bayne for RELI140, Religion in America. This was by far, the most interesting class I had at Carolina and Bayne made it that way. The grading is very fair and the TA's are all awesome. Bayne puts in so much time into the class, learning people's names in a 150 person class, and shares his passion for this subject with everyone.

One of my favorite professors I've had at Hussman!!! She is so funny and really cares about her students. Final project is a series of social media posts about a research topic and is not hard as long as you don't wait to the last minute. Take her for MEJO 153, you will not regret it.
If you're looking to take Mejo 153 take it with professor Benninger. She is super down to earth and genuinely cares about her students and wants to see them succeed. Literally goated.

If you are looking for a more hardcore journalist perspective that 153 is typically notorious for, this may not be the class for you. The class was comprised of a variety of smaller assignments that included interviews and answering questions from the textbook, and was extremely manageable. If you want to complete 153 with an A, take Benninger.
Dr. B is a great professor! She is such an engaging lecturer, using personal anecdotes to add personality to classes. All of the assignments were fun and low-stakes, with clear grading criteria.

If you need to take 153, take it with Dr. B! Not a ton of work and no tests/quizzes. The final project is a social media research project but you get to choose your topic and as long as you don't wait until the last minute you will be fine. She's awesome!

Dr. B was definitely one of the best professors I have had at UNC! She always keeps her lecturing super concise and engaging. She brings a lot of real-world and personal experiences to her class and would start every class by talking about news and sports going on in the world. I would 100% take her for MEJO-153 if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: If you pay attention in class you will get an A.

I am obsessed with this woman. What a sweetheart. Just a lovely human who clearly loves her job and wants us to learn. She is the best professor to take 153 with. Class with enjoyable and fun every day.

Dr. B is the best professor to take Mejo 153 with! She is super funny and genuinely cares about her students. We only took one test (mini quiz) the whole semester and our final was a social media project of our choice. She does not try to trick students at all. Big class discussions were a regular thing though, so have something to share.

Awesome teacher. She's funny, personable, and professional. Take her class for MEJO 153. She makes a hard class easy and manageable. We would start every class with a discussion on college football and the news world. A perfect teacher for MEJO 153.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Super knowledgeable and entertaining professor, and really cares to get to know his students. Participation matters and you will be expected to talk at least 1x a class. I would say he's a relatively harsh grader but his feedback makes sense and is helpful, so it's definitely easy to improve in his class.

If you want an easy A first-year seminar, do not take PLCY-76H. However, if you want to work hard, truly enjoy the history of health policy, and enjoy reading at least 20+ pages of reading each class, then do take this class. Professor Meier is very knowledgeable and really cares about his students, but his class is hard for a FYS.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: dr. meier's class is unlike any other class i've taken, he is an amazing professor who cares so deeply about his students and global health. i look forward to coming to class everyday. his class is one you listen and retain information from. he is such an engaging lecturer and would take another one of his classes in a heartbeat.

Meier was entertaining, but in retrospect I was a bit disappointed with the content in the course as he elected to touch on Ukraine and Russia, but not Palestine — a much more pertinent issue. To be fair, this wouldn't have sat well with the board, but to not acknowledge it in any capacity for a class called ‘Justice in Public Policy' is odd.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Meier is incredible. This class has been by far my favorite class I have taken at UNC. The class has been so fulfilling and I have learned so much. The class is not for the light -- it is a lot of work and constant readings but i can ensure you will never take a class where you will learn more. would recommend and he is very kind/understanding

A LOT of reading/work for a FYS, sometimes 50+ pages after each class. He's a tough grader so be prepared to work hard if you want an A. Great guy!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: this class is incredible and Meier is amazing! all students must take this class and it is accessible for both undergraduates and graduates. it is a class thats challenging but not overwhelming. AMAZING PROFESSOR

This class does a beautiful job of turning complicated subjects into something discussable and accessible without removing the importance of them. Dr. Meier is the most passionate professor I have ever met and he cares so deeply about his students. He will know everyone's name before you even walk into the classroom that day. This class is a must.

Dr. Meier deeply cares about his students and makes them all feel at home! I've been in his class for a few weeks now and would say it is already one of my favorite classes at UNC. super interesting material and engaging lectures! a solid amount of reading, but it is not overwhelming. definitely recommend
incredible professor and inspired me to pursue a degree in public health! Everyone must take a class with Meier, it will change your UNC experience.
must take class, extremely interesting content and fun interactions with students. learned a ton and would completely recommend. great professor and he is extremely passionate

reviews.comment: Extremely engaging and absolutely incredible class. Material is interesting and open my eyes to the world of global health. Even if you are not studying public health I seriously recommend! Both the professor and content make this class incredible. A definite take at UNC

Took this class last semester and I will miss being in class with him!! Incredible content, professor, lecture style! Every student of any major should take!! So happy I took it!! I didn't feel overwhelmed but also felt I gained a ton from the class!! it was a perfect class and also very flexible to student feedback. you feel very cared about!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I RECOMMEND. Dr. Meier is funny and uses current events to engage with students -- he is never afraid to belt a tune and is also the kindest professor I have met at UNC. He makes you welcomed and heard in his class! The material is interesting and extremely relevant! There are not exams, but rather papers which he provides accessible material for!

LOVE THIS CLASS!! incredible professor, learn a ton, solid amount of readings but not too much that it is unbearable. anyone can take it -- provides foundational understanding of global health! SO applicable to current events/other majors/etc. U HAVE TO TAKE!!!

MUST TAKE: I have gained so much knowledge about global health!! This class will leave you fulfilled and fascinated. Meier is incredible -- using songs to interact with students and truly cares about his students. He goes beyond being supportive in class and always has a door open to be there for any student. I always look forward to class!!

He is clear and answers questions. He engages with the material and is an amazing lecturer-- it is impossible to be bored in his class. He provides room for students to engage with other students and engage in larger class setting. You will learn tons from the class! You cannot graduate UNC without taking a class with Meier and this one is a MUST.

Incredible professor and fascinating material! Both undergraduates and graduates will learn A LOT from the class. Good amount of reading, but not too much that it feels unmanageable. Very understanding professor and kind human. This class is a must take! If you are not passionate about global health before it, you will be after!!!

I came into university not considering global health, now it is my major. The person I attribute this to is Dr. Meier. During a time when global health is under attack, we need more Meier's and more students to learn from him. Everyone should take this class. Also, it is an appropriate workload allowing students to learn but not overwhelming.

Dr Meier's class has been my favorite class I have taken at UNC. He brings an energy into the class that engages each and everyone of his students and he connects with them personally. Dr. Meier provides a foundational understanding of global health that is accessible for both undergraduates and graduates. I couldn't recommend his class more!!!

Dr. Meier is one of the most unique professors I've had at UNC and I mean that in the best way. Loved this class!

reviews.comment: Meier is a very accomplished person and well-versed in policy, and I do appreciate his animated personality and effort to make the class more entertaining than a lot of the conventional dry lectures in college. reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof. Meier does really care about his students, however, the content of this course is very repetitive and boring if you don't have a particular passion for global health policy. Meier is entertaining though!

He's a good teacher and is very passionate about what he teaches. There are somewhat lengthy readings due before each class and a reading quiz, but it's not too hard. Grade is mainly based on participation, two papers, and the final paper. I learned a lot and classes were engaging, encouraging students to participate and reflect upon the readings.

Such a strange man. VERY clearly cares about his students and their wellbeing, but that does not always translate into his teaching style. This is such a dense class with material that I often just felt went completely over my head. I would absolutely not take this class unless you are extremely passionate about Health Policy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

He is an enjoyable Professor and you will learn so much, however, the assigned readings are a lot and reading quizzes are hard. He has two 500 word papers and a final paper.

reviews.comment: Meier is the best professor I've ever had the pleasure of taking a class with. He cares for his students in a way no one else does and genuinely wants to know how you are doing. He may appear theatrical, but the class touches on all sorts of depressing, real-life topics and that's his way of inspiring his students to create change. Take his class!!

Professor Meier is clearly a well-respected and knowledgeable member of the policy world but this does not translate into his teaching skills. His musical outbursts during lecture are uncomfortable and not relevant, he makes students feel bad when they don't answer his questions "right", and he never provides clear grading criteria.

Dr. Meier is probably the most theatric professor at Chapel Hill, he really knows his stuff and obviously puts lots of effort into teaching it in an interesting way, don't take his class if you don't want to hear him sing. Paper heavy and he expects engagement online and in class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I wanted to love this class. Unreasonable readings. PPTs (not posted) have more flair than substance. The random musical outbursts were endearing until they quickly weren't. He lectures in this dramatic, rehearsed voice and at times it seems like he's more interested in putting on a performance than making sure students understand the content.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Everyone should take a class with Meier. He's passionate about the subject, and does a good job of explaining what the real world implications of ethical frameworks are. This class is great for anyone who wants to engage with public policy. For the people complaining about the difficulty or readings, maybe the honors section wasn't the best choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Meier is one of the best professors I've had at UNC. I couldn't recommend him more. He is by far the most passionate teacher I have ever had at UNC.

reviews.comment: I took this class to fulfill a gen ed and to get an honors credit. reviews.comment: TAKE A CLASS WITH MEIER!!! He does assign a lot of reading, but quizzes are short and readings can be skimmed for main points. His lectures are so entertaining and he really cares about his students.

reviews.comment: Really enjoyed this class- you definitely get back what you put into it. Prof Meier cares so much and is truly passionate about his subject (literally was Zooming in from Geneva if needed). Definitely some reading, nothing unmanageable, but don't expect to do no homework just because it's a fys. Would recommend!

This class will be difficult and you may struggle but not without wonderful themes and a caring professor. My knowledge on global health policy is limited but you do have a few takeaways from the class. Less guided thinking and more on your own. Overall I liked the time I spent and it was worth it and I might just know how to save the world.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The problem is how vague it is. Although he is fun will dance in the class, talks in different voices, themes, and plays music. reviews.comment: He cares about the material & helping students, but class was stressful, participation is absolutely mandatory (and he'll make you feel bad if you don't), the participation ?s sometimes don't relate to the day's readings, there are 4-5 long readings per class with daily quizzes, & no grading criteria for the papers worth 15-30% of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Amazing class with an amazing professor. In light of the class being held online, Professor Meier was accommodating and provided very engaging lectures and assignments. While the readings were a bit dense, Meier provided a lot of opportunities during office hours or other times to discuss the class topics in greater detail. Would highly recommend!

Hardest class I've ever taken. Meier is an amazing human who cares about his students, but his exams are unnecessarily hard and assigns hours upon hours of dense philosophy readings every day. Could never work on any of my other classes it was so much. Tough grader, expect to work your butt off with little reward. Screwed my mental health.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I looked forward to attending this class each day. I was new to global health and found the textbook to be comprehensive, insightful and thought-provoking. The lectures then enriched lessons from the text through class discussions, case studies, and informative PPTs. Make it a priority to take a class with Professor Meier!! He's truly inspiring.

I went into this FYS without much knowledge about public health and absolutely loved it! Professor Meier does a great job of making it enjoyable and memorable. There is quite a bit of reading (3 readings assigned per class), but overall very manageable workload. To anyone considering him and/or PLCY76H, 10/10 would recommend!!

Meier is definitely an expert & super passionate about global health. Every class has a theme (Hamilton, Star Wars, etc) which makes it more fun. We had readings & a (pretty easy) reading quiz before each class, & 2 papers + a final paper. Participation is key (20% of grade). I did learn a lot & people interested in health should take this class!

reviews.comment: Dr. Meier is an amazing professor. He is the only prof I am looking forward to taking another class with. He is always open for conversation & if you have differing opinions, voice them instead of writing online.

reviews.comment: Meier might not directly lecture opinion but he makes it very clear which side he thinks is right and chooses to only present certain information on a topic. Theres nothing wrong with professors being liberal, but there is something wrong with being unable to disagree with them

One of my favorite professors I've had at UNC, Meier truly cares about his students and it's very clear that he is teaching in order to help create a better future. He is inspiring and has incredible experience and wisdom in human rights. Lectures are o entertaining and musical. While you can tell he is left leaning, he doesn't lecture opinion

Dr. Meier is the most inspirational professor I have ever had. I left his class inspired to work and change the world. This class is very difficult and has a lot of readings, but all of the work felt worthwhile and necessary. His jokes and Hamilton references are hilarious and he is always kind and caring in office hours.

Dr. Meier is the most passionate professor I've had at UNC. If you never thought that human rights had musical themes, think again. Dr. Meier is extremely accessible and wants you to engage with the material which is easy given the interesting topics. PLCY 570 was a fair amount of work but I would do it again in a heartbeat.

He's an okay Professor. He can get kind of emotional though and wants pity from his students. His class is mildly interesting but he just kinda repeats the same things over and over again, like "institutions  norms +architecture." . His a little bit funny and makes a lot of self depressing jokes which is weird considering his hubris.
Great professor who really cares about the students and really passionate about Global Heath Policy with amazing musical references and puns!

Professor Meier is one of the best professors I've had. He is incredibly passionate about Global Health Policy, and is the reason that I became interested in the field as well. His lectures are engaging, and the reading-based discussions involve students and foster a deeper understanding of the material. I would definitely recommend this class.

Prof. Meier genuinely cares about students, in and out of class. He is funny and makes every class enjoyable. I would recommend every single first year to take his seminar. The readings and papers are important, but they aren't too hard. Participate, be willing to ask questions, and engage with the material, and you'll do great.

Professor Meier is a fantastic professor who really brings PLCY 76H to life. He balances the serious & dramatic nature of the course with his sense of humor & cultural references and is very accessible when needed. I leave every class inspired and wanting to learn more. He has opened my eyes to the world of policy and human rights in global health.

The material is intense for a first year seminar, but completely worth it. You leave class with a comprehensive understanding of global health policy, policy institutions and governance structures that will be applicable well beyond this class. Meier's lectures are incredible with themed discussions everyday that are engaging and inspiring for all.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed PLCY76H with Professor Meier. He has a lot of experience in the Global Health Policy field and he is really dedicated to teaching us everything he knows. His lectures are really interesting and funny as well. While the class has a lot of necessary reading, overall I think it's a great course for freshmen to take!

This seminar is definitely a must if you are a first-year. This class is reading and participation heavy, but you learn a lot about the different avenues of global health policy. Professor Meier is also super passionate about the topic and he makes the lectures very fascinating

Professor Meier truly cares about the development of his students. He is very open and hosts office hours every week. The class does have a lot of reading and is by no means an easy A, but Professor Meier is engaging none the less.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: you cannot go wrong with Dr. Meier for your first-year seminar. The class is super interesting, and really engaging. You learn a ton about the world as well as the United Nations.
