reviews.comment: She's the goat

I would not say this course is easy because sometimes you do need to do something comparatively tricky, like write the correct citation format and blend three articles into one. However, she is very nice and caring, which does make studying much easier. She is about to graduate; cherish and take your final chance to study with her!

The BEST professor at UNC. Bjelland is the sweetest human I have ever met and heavily reminds me of Ms. Honey from Matilda. The assignments are straightforward and easy to succeed on. As someone who isn't the best at English, I got great grades in the class and found the material super interesting and helpful for the real world.

I had my ENGL 105 class in the evening so it was hard to come to class sometimes but Professor Bjelland made it such a good class. She is one of the sweetest people and is very understanding. Her class was very enjoyable and I liked all the work she assigned. Each assignment was clear and had a purpose. This was a relaxing and stress-free class.
very understanding and also overall such a nice and sweet person. the class is insanely easy and if you turn in work you will be fine!!

She made English very enjoyable and it felt more like a summer camp than an actual class. It was very stress-free and the rubric tells u exactly what she expects. She is super friendly and always had a smile on her face.  I would strongly recommend Professor B for ENGL 105!
Caring, friendly, and cute professor. Her classes in summer sessions are pretty relaxing, and we have enough time to do our assignments. Also, there're lots of group activities on class.
Super nice and helpful.

Just follow the rubric and submit the assignments on time and you'll be fine. Pretty sure she didn't dock people more than two or three points on a fifteen point assignment. She's also very understanding about mental health and being sick.
very sweet and accomodating! the class is pretty easy as well

The grading scale is difficult, but it's not impossible to get an A. There are 8 quizzes; two are dropped. Professor Bickford is kind and knowledgable but her class is TOUGH. She's a very harsh grader and expects expert knowledge from her students. reviews.comment: Professor Bickford is an amazing educator and you will realize that if you engage and put in the effort like she asks you to. reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Ugh, love her! Very respectful towards students. The class is mostly a philosophy seminar (see: participation!) with lots of assigned readings & quite a bit of writing assignments. Dr. Bickford is a great professor in that she's incredibly knowledgeable and cares about the subject and her students. In this class, you have to read a lot for each period and write papers often. reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

Professor Bickford is incredible!!! Definitely one of the tougher graders at UNC, but I have learned so much from her class! reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Would take again

reviews.comment: Excellent class. It's not an easy course for anyone just to slack and get a good grade, but if you work for it, it's surely worth it. Professor is super helpful, friendly, and inspiring. Class discussion is always in a great atmosphere. professor smiles when you talk to her, and she gets so excited when someone come up with good thoughts!

Professor Bickford is a great professor. The first year seminar I took with her is one of my favorite courses I have ever taken at UNC. If you're taking it because you expect an easy A, you probably won't get it. But the class discussions are incredibly interesting, and you will improve your writing and analytical thinking skills.

Great prof!  Really let's everybody tell what they think about the questions at hand.  Also, she's very serious about participation so don't think that you can join her class and not talk or do the readings, which can get dull at times.  However, the great discussions make it all worth it.
I had her for Feminism in Political Theory, great teacher, SO passionate about this topic, but you definitely have to do the readings, which are usually quite long and sometimes really difficult

Jackson picked some really interesting papers for us to discuss this year! I learned a great deal about ongoing issues surrounding AI, as well as more general Philosophy topics! Jackson is an AMAZING professor. He explains concepts clearly and obviously wants his students to learn and succeed. Very accessible and helpful office hours. reviews.comment: You're better off self-studying than going to any of her lectures. It's rare for her to post any practice exams, and she'll never post a key.

the exams are actually bs and she doesnt explain things well whatsoever. there is no textbook and her handwritten notes have just random stuff that isnt tested on in it. the exams are actually unfathomably bad.
McLaughlin was a fair teacher who helped out on grades for the most part. Lectures weren't amazing but if you do all the homework you will do fine on tests.
do not trust her, she wont give any partial credit EVEN when you deserve it! i self studied everything for the final and ended up doing well ONLY because of that

People do hate on her too much, but she is not great at teaching. She does not explain things very well, nor are her lectures engaging or well-paced, making it very difficult to follow. This class is definitely still doable, but due to the poor quality of her lectures and teaching style it is largely self-taught.

Professor McLaughlin is extremely sweet and gives quite good advice in office hours. She will give you good, truthful answers to anything you ask her. She was mostly fine, the math department is awful, though. The first 2 exams were challenging but fair, the final was awful, but she didnt make it so. Shes nice though, and does want you to succeed.

Tests are pretty easy; they cover only the content she covered in class. A pretty light class for those good at math and can do the problems in class and recitation. - Teaches very well, very nice professor, but tough grading criteria

- Our class gpa average was high, around a B

I hope God blesses her for rounding my grade up. i didn't go to lectures after october because it was easier to self teach. she is not a good teacher but her tests are fair and you can manage with lots of studying.

She is a good professor, the attendance not required for her lecture. She usually uses well-written notes as class materials and there are recorded videos on Canvas for us to review. Midterms and final are not difficult and they aligns with the homework contents and class materials.

She teaches content pretty quickly and you definitely need some calc background if you're taking her class. She doesn't curve tests and that makes up the majority of your grade. But, overall, not terrible and if you just pay attention during her lectures, you should be fine.

Worst professor I have had a UNC by far. She is very old and seems to be losing it, lectures are unorganized and she does not explain content well. I had friends in 152 with Grey and Corbin who had better experiences
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

She's a great professor but she goes through the content relatively quickly, but as long as you look through the notes before hand, its easy to understand the content. Only reason why I didn't get an A+ is because I didn't put in any effort. Tests are fair and she makes the final as well, so if you do well in her midterms you'll ace the final.

ATTEND THE MIDTERM REVIEWS BY THE TAs!!! Everything they cover is word-for-word the same on the tests, and they single handedly prevented me from failing.

Self-studyable

Solid professor. She doesn't speak very loudly and is a little hard to understand. No major complaints. Be sure to go to recitation with the TAs and the review sessions before the tests- they will help enourmously.
Well taught class.

For the first 2 months of class she didn't seem to grasp which class she was in and what time our class ended. That's all you need to know. Crazy disorganized. Puts in little effort. Take anyone else.

reviews.comment: I'm honestly surprised the ratings aren't lower. Tests are hard with impossible algebra; doesn't curve anything; doesn't drop anything. It's clear she doesn't care for Calc 1 students.

prof mclaughin is able to complete all content and have 2 weeks left for revision. Homework is optional and is due right before the exams, it was not of much help. She does have a policy if you get 80% on the assignment you will get 100% on the homework grade. all of her exams came from her notes that she publishes.

Midterms were extremely fair, except that mcq were worth 10% each w/ no partial credit. Her lectures tend to be disorganized, but are usually helpful. Understand the problems in the notes inside out, and you'll do well on the exams. Lecture is optional and recorded, but make sure you watch them b/c that is key to doing well.

Professor McLaughlin is overall the best professor that taught calc 3 when I was taking it. She can get boring sometimes in lecture, but if you focus she does do a fair job explaining the concepts, and does offer extra help if needed. Additionally, her tests are fair and are very representative of the example problems that we did in class.

I have the utmost respect for Professor McLaughlin. She is a great lecturer and managed to explain abstract concepts really well to people just getting introduced to them. Midterms were very fair, and the final (which she wrote) was even more fair. She got me to understand what calculus actually is, not just how to solve problems. Highly recommend.

Very nice lady to talk to, but she doesn't seem to care about this class. I'm not sure if she thinks it's just light work and only focuses on higher-level classes, but it felt like teaching this course was a chore for her. I bombed one test, and it ruined my grade for the semester—she doesn't drop any exams. Take it with Miranda Thomas instead.

reviews.comment: Failed one exam and literally ruined

This class was a good experience for me since I had trouble with calc 2. The presentation of material was clear and she's funny and friendly. Good choice for calc 3.

Test heavy, harsh grader
Lectures are awful you have to watch another professors lectures just to understand

She puts little effort into teaching, but has intentionally harder exams than other professors and refuses leniency (i.e. dropping the lowest midterm) unlike other professors. She is passive-aggressive about people not coming to class, even though she knows her lectures are bad.
I was worried about taking calc 1 but Prof Mclaughlin made it doable and interesting. I'm definitely taking her calc 2 class.

Heard shes great for Math-232+ but do not. DO NOT take her for math-231. Shes horrible at teaching the material and KNOWS it and makes the exams insanely hard that even TAs have trouble explaining the material. Told TAs to "grade harshly" to spite students that didn't come to class. Go to another profs lectures to learn. Take exams when needed.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS I've had a mil. bad teachers and struggled, but this professor was the worst. Do not value lecture at all. She bounces around topics which only confuses students. I supplemented class by going to math plus and the math help center but I wouldn't even bother going to lecture.

reviews.comment: Anything on our exams is clearly discussed in class (attendance not required), all lectures are filmed and uploaded online, and she teaches you an intuitive approach to math. The only difficulty was that she relied heavily on everyone in the room having taken calculus before, which wasn't true, but watch some videos and you'll be okay.

Great class. She tells you what will be on the exams during class. The homework is long but we get full credit with 80% score. I need to take two more calculus classes so I appreciate learning concepts she says will be covered in those classes. Easy recitations. the TA is super helpful.

Worst professor I've had. Lectures are disorganized, rushed, and unhelpful. No study guides, unclear expectations, and tests include unseen material. Homework is overly hard but barely affects your grade. Recitation adds no value and feels pointless. Took 20+ hours of studying per exam just to pass. Avoid if possible.

Attendance not being mandatory was nice cause you could show up whenever. Homework was annoying cause some problems were hard, but u only needed 80% for full credit. Fair exams, her online notes are great, a pretty approachable lecturer, would def recommend! Be warned exams are ~85% of the grade (but they're easy if u just review practice exams)

She makes new notes for each class period and has not followed her posted curriculum.
She does test corrections. The exams are medium difficulty. Maths is hard for me and the professor is patient.
The homework is hard but the class notes are good.

This is a good class. Great prof. If you go to class and do the homework it's an easy A. Lots of complaining on this site. Must be students who can't do math because it's an interesting class and well taught. I have As on both exams so far.

She is the worst math teacher I ever had. Although she gives partial credit on tests (which is super helpful), the only way I understand the material is doing 2x more work outside of lectures (such as watching YT videos, AI explanaitons, and getting help from others) to even begin to understand the topic.

DO NOT TAKE CLASSES WITH HER UNLESS YOU ABSOLUTELY HAVE TO….if you can take a class with Miranda Thomas instead do that 100%. McLaughlin teaches as if it is a flipped classroom but with no outside resources. I skipped all of her lectures and just taught myself calc because her lectures made no sense and had no structure. tests were pretty easy tho

Take Mclaughlin. She does test corrections!  I had to take this class over and she is better than the TA I had before. The exams are like the class notes. I reworked the problems a few times before the tests and got As on both. The class can be boring at times because some students slow it down with ridiculous questions. But she's nice about it.
This is not a hard class. The prof is nice and explains the topics really well. The homework is long and difficult but she gives us full credit if we finish 70% of it.

McLaughlin is very confusing and very bad at answering questions. I would avoid taking her if this is your first time taking calculus, as she has a very harsh grading style. Be ready to put in a lot of hours of homework and studying to pass.

Do not take this class if you have not taken calc before. A lot of the material was taught very half-heartedly, and the only way to learn it fully was to learn it outside of class. Tests are challenging and each question is worth a lot of points, but other than that, she is a very kind woman.

If you have not taken calc in high school, do not take this class. She moves very fast and does an OK job explaining concepts. Her exams are harder than there sections and she does not curve or drop a midterm. Overall a nice lady but I wouldn't recommend unless you've taken calc.

I do not recommend taking Calc 1 with her. Her lectures are a waste of time. Her notes are very disorganized. She often makes mistakes during class and the students have to correct her. She does not know how to do the homework that she assigns. She does not follow the syllabus and does not inform students of what units are on the exams. Not a fan.
take stor113. if you are a business major, do not take this class. she rushes through lectures and does not answer questions effectively.
This is my second time taking this class. Prof Mclaughlin has made it a lot easier than the first time. It's a good class with good notes.

Awful, awful, awful class with an even worse teacher. By FAR the worst experience I've had here at UNC. Do not take this class! Do NOT take this class! If you absolutely have to, take it with someone else.
Probably my favorite professor, while this class is difficult, if you want to actually learn the material, read the notes and ask questions in class. Exams are just like the notes and homework.

I absolutely love having Professor Mclaughlin. She's such a kind and understanding person. I also took her for algebra, and she was always incredibly helpful. Her explanations are clear and easy to grasp!
Mclaughlin explains the homework in each class. Exams are like homework. Easy class. I like that the second exam is multiple classes after spring break.

Don't take this professor if you have no calculus experience. She teaches very fast-paced like she's reviewing the topics instead of teaching them. People who have taken calculus in high school do well. However, if this is not you, take a different professor who can actually teach you the topics like you're learning them for the first time.
Easier than my high school calc class. Good prof. Nice person.
Easy first exam. Questions are like the class notes and homework.

Nice lady who knows what she's talking about but can't teach it to save her life. Lectures are fast-paced, the notes she gives you are horrible, homework takes hours and is much more difficult than the material taught, and the exams are graded by nitpicky TAs who take a million points off for minor inaccuracies. Avoid at all costs, seriously!
She's very monotone, doesn't have much class resources, but is pretty nice.
Awful class, awful teaching style. Nobody takes this class for fun. Avoid at all costs.
Too much homework but overall a good prof and class.
No study guides. No extra credit or curves. All the other calc teachers gave their students review guides for tests and optional quizzes for extra credit. This teacher did not.

I had an ok experience, her lectures weren't that helpful so I had to put in a lot of work outside of class like reading the textbook and going through her notes on my own. I would recommend spending less time on the edfinity and more on other rsources such as the textbook or crambetter, which is a site with rly good resources for this class!

i took my first math class at unc with her and had a pretty good experience. the grading is scary (final is >40% of the class) but her tests/quizzes are very straightforward. as long as you go over her notes thoroughly and understand how to solve those types of problems, you will be fine. she wrote the final last sem so it was also pretty easy

Professor Mclaughlin's instruction is alright, not great.  She expects you to understand the material ahead of time, and that her class time is "review" and practice.  Hard to get a hold of outside of class, office hours times jumped around, not great at responding to emails. Homework is harder, but tests are extremely fair. Must work hard.

reviews.comment: Mclaughlin was a great professor. Calc 3 introduces a lot of new things but she was able to teach it in a way that wasn't overwhelming. The class is very test heavy, like 90%, but the tests were very manageable.

reviews.comment: Not an interactive or interesting lecturer. Hard to follow in class at times, but mostly fine. IMPOSSIBLE homework but VERY fair tests. Overall positive because homework was 4% of the grade and tests were 92%. Take if you can self motivate, self teach some concepts, or are a good test taker. Go to ULA sessions and pray for a good recitation TA.
Excellent class. Great notes. Tests are straightforward.

One of my best decisions was taking the course Pass/Fail. The classes were difficult to understand. Her explanations felt more like summaries than detailed instructions, and her notes were erased within 10 minutes. The homework was difficult and lengthy, with little relevance to the exams. I studied on YouTube for the final and got a better score.

MATH233 is tough no matter how you slice it. McLaughlin was a good professor and made all lectures available after the fact via recordings, as attendance isn't required. Tests were worth 90% and some HW on edfinity is very different from lecture so use ChatGPT and you'll be fine. Tests were fair and she's prob the best you'll get with 233.

She's not the best at explaining concepts, but her class structure is good enough. The homework is way too difficult to be useful (use the MHC! and TAs are helpful), but as long as you practice her drill problems from the notes and watch Prof. Leonard on Youtube, her tests are very doable. She will round up to the nearest whole # for letter grades.

She is a smart professor who understands calculus; however, intro-level calc is not her specialty. She teaches the course as if everyone has already taken it. Homework was about 10% of my grade, the rest being tests. The only people who succeeded in this course were those taking it again after high school AP. Be ready to teach yourself.

reviews.comment:
Okay experience taking MATH-233 with Prof. McLaughlin. Daunting grading criteria (final was like 41% of grade) and heavy amounts of material did set the bar early on. Interesting material, alot of self-studying (lectures were usually her reiterating notes written years ago). 

Expect this to be more difficult than 232 and a continuation of 231.

reviews.comment: Tests are heavy, but easier than homework (less than 5% of grade). Do all homework and you should be fine. reviews.comment: Inflexible. Uncaring. No empathy. Professor does not have respect for you and does not give any partial credit or respond to emails! Avoid.
No empathy. Tough grader. Inflexible with deadlines and does not give partial credit. Avoid this professor please if you want to feel valued and respected.

Let me warn you. No Calc 3 prof at UNC will be “easy”. The math department holds no kindness in its soul. If you are worried about this class, do not take it with her. Her lecture style was monotone and enthusiasm nil.
To do well on this course, you should find a good YouTube channel.
She seems to be a nice person on the outside, but the way she treats students is customer service.
She is the most boring professor I had at UNC.
Do not take this professor for calc 3. She doesn't know how to explain concepts in an intuitive way.

She is a kind professor and seems to really care for her students. I found her lectures easy to understand. The homework can be very frustrating, but as long as you get 80%, you'll get full credit. reviews.comment: Very very easy class. Too much time was spent on the people who couldn't do algebra. McLaughlin was a good teacher, but the class was slow.
Easy class. Edfinity homework had hard problems that were difficult to follow..

This is my favorite class this semester!!!! Prof Mclaughlin is an awesome teacher. The notes are helpful, well written and the exams arent hard if you do the work. The homework is long and not always helpful.

Clearly, she is a smart woman who knows her stuff and cares about her students... that being said, she cannot teach an intro-level, basic class. She was confusing and patronizing, and overall, it was a negative experience. The math here sucks no matter what, and this is NOT an exception. I would recommend taking this course with anyone else.

She isn't a super interesting, but she explains concepts clearly the first time. She doesn't answers question well, but she available to answer them outside of class. The homework is stupidly hard, just get through it and then use the notes and example problems to study.

I'm retaking this course and have never been more confused. You can definitely get by in McLaughlin's class if you put in the work.

Dr. McLaughlin is extremely kind and caring and will always go out of her way to make sure students understand concepts. Her exams are very straightforward and she explains concepts well in class. Amazing teacher! I was sooo scared to take math and Prof Mclaughlin has helped me.. 45 on the first exam and 76 on the second. Definitely take her.
The exams are straight forward and from the notes and homework. The lectures are interesting. It will be an easy A. She answers all questions in a patient way. Nice person.

Her lectures are all over the place and the homework is wildly hard. There are no practice materials for the exam so you don't know what to expect and they just continue to get harder each time (they are the majority of your grade). Lastly, she is simply just a very rude professor.

reviews.comment: Although Calc 2 is tough, Professor McLaughlin's detailed notes and practice-focused approach made it doable. Unstuckstudy AI was a lifesaver for study prep. Challenging but rewarding class.

She was absolutely amazing. Although lectures could often be a bit confusing, she was happy to answer questions and give feedback which made all the difference for my understanding. reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of the easiest classes I have ever taken. Her homework is brutal, but you only need a 40% to get full-credit. Her tests are an absolute cakewalk. Specifically with Dr. Mclaughlin, she goes through lectures extremely quickly, is not very concise, confuses herself, uses old notes and writes in disappearing ink. Any youtube video will do better at explaining material.

I was concerned about taking calc 2 as it has a reputation at UNC for being very difficult, but her lectures and notes helped me succeed in the class. I scored a 94 on the final. It was a good experience.

This class was an absolute nightmare. She did not use textbooks and her notes written during covid was used instead. The problem was that her handwriting was awful and hard to follow. Great notes. The exams are straightforward and not hard. The homework is ok.

I recommend watching a video on the material or reading through her notes before class. Her notes are a fantastic study tool.

She does not have the best lectures, but she posts her notes, which are clear and easy to understand. If you skip the lectures, read her notes, and do the assigned homework you can get an A in this class quite easily because the tests are extremely easy.

A very passive aggressive professor. Made things seem straightforward when they weren't. You will have no idea what your final grade is until the very end or how curves or test corrections will help you. Barely responded to my emails. You will have a lot of homework only for it to have no positive impact. If you do bad on her exams, you're doomed.

My favorite class by far. Love the way she teaches. The examples are intuitive and interesting. Definitely take her. It's hard to get in the class. Waitlist was messed up.

A nice person but not a good lecturer. Scattered and teaches in a way as if you already have a high level of understanding on the material. reviews.comment: Super detailed notes and interesting clarification in class. We worked a lot of in class practice problems that were helpful, especially right before the final.

Professor Mclaughlin is nice and her notes are very detailed, but her teaching style is odd because she is explaining notes that are already written down. Tests are also around 87% of the grade. You can still study and end with a good grade though.

Calc 3 isn't easy with anyone, but Prof. Mclaughlin is a great teacher who cares about her students. The lectures are fast, but they are recorded. Calc 3 is hard no matter who or where you take it just because of the amount of material covered. Only fault is having a majority of your grade come from 2 exams plus a final worth 38%.

reviews.comment: Very interesting class. Especially the way lectures involve an intuitive understanding of the material and how all the material connects. Nice prof too.

yawn. I don't blame her. She clearly doesn't care about calculus, but she cares about the class. She'll hold up the hoops for you to jump through, so for all you CS and physics majors who need calc iii, this is a really easy way to get through it all. Not a lot of actual "mathematics" so if you like proofs or the "art" of math, this ain't it.

Typical bad UNC math professor. My main problem with Mclaughlin is how fast she went through material, and the way she set up her lectures. People must just like her as a professor bc you can skip lecture.

Lecture is kind of boring/she goes very fast, but for a calculus professor she is great. reviews.comment: Lots of homework but do it to understand. Lectures are clear with good notes. McLaughlin is a good teacher. Strange reviews below. Not logical thinking. Maybe that's why they didn't do well in the class. I heard 30% of the class scored A- and higher.

The average on her second midterm was a 65. On the final exam, which was standardized for all the calc classes, our class had the highest average. We knew the most, best score on the final, worst class grade.
Definitely take this professor. She genuinely cared how I did in the class. The class was easy and there wasn't much homework. She gives test corrections worth a full grade.

Calc 3 is a tough class no matter how you slice it. My favorite class this semester. The practice problems in class helped with the exams. The homework is long.

Most mid professor ever. So boring, if you don't have an iPad just don't go to lecture because she moves at the speed of light with the most monotone voice to ever exist. the homeworks are ridiculously and unnecessarily long, the test averages are in the 60s. class overall not good, recitation garbage as well.

She teaches this class as if everyone has already taken calc, and she moves very fast. However, she is very very patient when it comes to explaining things as long as you ask questions. Professor McLaughlin was a very good lecturer and she did a great job at answering questions both in class and in office hours. Her lectures are a little dry and monotone, so I guess that's something to consider if that's an issue for you. Overall, highly recommend for your required calc classes.

Easily the best math class I've ever taken. Too much homework but lectures are good. The exams are similar to the notes.
I learned a lot in this class. Mclaughlin is a nice person who spent a lot of time helping me. Thanks to her!

I improved so much from the second midterm to the final and it seems like every other math professor take in consideration of that except for her. very nice person. easy class

Do NOT take this class if you haven't taken calc, you will be confused since she kinda jumps from a to b without an explanation, like i've taken calc and she confused things I was sure I knew. The tests are really broad which is good bc it's easier than the hw but the hw is very hard and doesn't represent what we actually have to know on tests
Easy A on the first exam. Not a hard class.

Prof McLaughlin's lectures do not help in the slightest and I have NO idea why she has so many 5 star ratings. If you don't already know some Calc you're screwed. Never explains things all the way/will assume you have prior knowledge even when she KNEW many of us hadn't taken calc before. You have to teach yourself!! DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.

wow Was just talking with my friends in the same 231 class about what a great teacher she is, super patient. She's traveling to her mom's funeral in October and is trying to not get covid. Sorry to see entitled bs posted here.
Her tone stays the same, making me wanna sleep. I basically learn through self-learning and recitation. btw, she's rly rly scared of COVID...

Honestly, I was super hesitant to take calc 2 over the summer cause of all the stories but its the best decision I made with this professor. Shes super nice and if you know the content she shows in class, the tests are virtually the same. Just do the homework she wants you to do well !!

McLaughlin is lenient and very caring: 70% on homework is full credit; and tests are similar to homework questions, with a lot of partial credit. She works hard to clarify difficult concepts and is direct with test expectations. Summer Session final exam was easy. Be sure to do homework every night, and you'll have no problems getting an A or B.
I took this class in summer. Really good class. It goes fast but if you read the notes ahead of class then it's not very hard. A lot of homework. Loved the lectures. She's really clear and detailed.

Her lectures did not help at all. She never explained how to fully do a problem, just spent all class going over highlights of her notes pages. I could've spent that time actually teaching myself the material. It is worth your time to understand homework problems because they will help with exams (the class is exam heavy when it comes to grading).

Hardest class I've taken at UNC. Took this during the summer so the already challenge course got even harder with 6 my math lab due each week. So much work and so much harder in the summer. Had to put so much work into this class. With that being said, McLaughlin is a good professor and is adaptable and accessible. Hard professor but is very caring

I took her class during a summer session and wasn't impressed. Her lectures via zoom were mandatory, though they weren't helpful in the slightest. She gave the option of video lectures which were much more helpful, but stopped posting them midway through the course. She also grades the exams fairly hard with very little partial credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: McLaughlin explained things very well and her midterms were really not too hard. Be aware that the final exam for MATH233 is written by all the professors and not just McLaughlin, so it was insanely difficult. The homework for this class is tough but I couldn't have asked for a better professor.
Math is hard for me and Professor McLaughlin was patient and helpful. I appreciate everything she did. I got a B+

The exams are much harder than material she goes over in class. It is a difficult class and she is not very accessible, I emailed her once trying to see if she could do appointment office hours since I had a class during hers and never got an answer. She is kind and funny but goes over things very quickly with little explination.

McLaughlin is a fair prof. Nice lady. Solid, well organized class. The homework is tough but necessary to get a decent grade because the exams look a lot like the homework. She has prerecorded videos of all of the topics which is helpful.
My final grade is 89.5 and she gave me an A- !!!!!!! I LOVE HER.
Very easy class. Some of my friends in the class were struggling and she was patient.
Shes extremely nice, however the exams are harder than what we do in class. There was no study material for the final and practice that was done in class did not look like final questions at all.

She really does love what she does and she is always down to help but I wish there was more that the class was not so test heavy. Mclaughlin is def the best 233 prof out there but if you are not a good test taker i do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Fair exams. Nice prof. Homework is hard.
Wrong! I loved this class. The notes are detailed and helped me get through this class. It's a tough class with a lot of homework.

Terrible. Do not take this class. The rating does not reflect the professor at all. Her lecture problems were all pre-solved and weren't solved in class. Her lectures did not reflect the homework or the tests at all and left you completely unprepared.
Awful professor. Her notes were terrible and she did not prepare her students well for the exams. She's a nice person and all, but not a good choice if you actually want to learn.
Just finished this class. The lectures were solid and the notes were very detailed. Really good lectures. I recommend taking her.

Not sure why Professor McLaughlin has such a good rating. Her lectures were rushed and difficult to follow - it was as if she expected us to have a good understanding of the material before coming to class. I had to do a lot of work outside of class to be comfortable with the level of difficulty in lecture and on tests. Pick a different prof.

Don't take this class with her if you don't have to. Bad professor that wasn't there to lecture for half of the class (her husband came in and lectured). Tests were way too hard and final average was really low for the class. Said she would curve but did not.
By far the best math prof I've had. She's detailed in her explanations. The notes are good.
Great notes and lectures.
Solid class. Excellent lectures. Was really into it because it helped me with physics.

She's not the most exciting lecturer on the planet, and she moves a little quickly, but she provides a lot of resources to help you out if you're stuck. Recordings from past years, very thorough notes, etc. Especially for a class as difficult as multi-variable calculus, I think she's the best you can get at UNC.

Prof. McLaughlin is a great calculus teacher, and with her fantastic note documents will give you the tools and knowledge to do well on the exams and get better at math. There is a good bit of homework, but it's acceptable and often helpful given the difficult content, which requires a lot of practice. I would certainly recommend her!

McLaughlin has a complete set of notes. We're asked to read them before class and watch a video explanation for clarification. Then she goes over them again in class. I like her intuitive approach to explaining the concepts. Interesting to understand why we are solving problems the way we are. It's been vey helpful for my physics class.

Professor McLaughlin is a solid choice for Math 110. The content isn't hard at all as it is mostly review from high school with a little new material. She was a good lecturer but can get confusing at times but is quick to respond to emails and very helpful in office hours.

Honestly, I'm surprised at how high these ratings are. Prof. McLaughlin was approachable, nice, and passionate about calc. I also know college calc is significantly more difficult than high school. However, the lectures were way over-complicated and didn't follow a clear format. Class made me more confused, but not attending made me fall behind.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: My issue w McLaughlin is that she can't dumb material down enough when teaching. She provides notes, but instead of going through the problems step by step, she shows it to you already done and hits the highlights, which made a lot of concepts unnecessarily hard. Tests aren't bad compared to other profs, but her teaching style isn't for me
Best math instructor I've had.

This Professor was very average, which can make things difficult if you need really good explanations for math. She recorded lectures which was helpful. Homework could be significantly different approach from the lesson at times. I think that she just has a lot of stress to follow certain standardizations.
Very clear lectures and a fair professor. Lots of homework and the subject is difficult. I did well because I completed most of it.

DO the practice tests she offers and you'll ace the class. Her exams are not hard if you use the resources she provides. Not the best lecturer but a solid choice for math 110. Pretty fair person and easy to ask questions.
This is not an easy class but Professor McLaughlin explains the ideas clearly and the homework isn't too bad. Reading the notes before class is important if you want to keep up.

Sometimes lectures can be difficult to follow if you haven't been keeping up. She responds to emails quickly and is very accommodating. She posts notes for every lecture on sakai which are very helpful. I recommend reading those before lecture to get the most out of it.
Best class I've taken! Clear and interesting lectures. Do the work and you'll do well.
If you have to take Math 231, TAKE HER!!! Her exams were 10x easier than other sections, and very very similar to the final. She usually gave out a study guide which was super helpful!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Mclaughlin is a really nice person. She was very understanding when I had issues when I was sick and she worked around them. However, I didn't really like her teaching style and I had to learn a lot by myself. The class is very test heavy so make sure you prepare well for them.

Took freshman year bc I liked math and got a 5 on the calc ABBC exam. Struggled so much. First 2 exams got Fs, the homework doesn't help w/tests. I finally learned how to study for her then got 100s on second two tests. Practice and rewrite her notes! Recitation is req but lecture isn't (I didn't go a lot). Try to take a diff prof
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Fair professor. Easy class. Prepare for the tests and you'll be good.
She was a fair teacher. The exams were easy enough and the lectures were good. She's a nice person, too.

Was no point in going to class, as she lectured straight from the textbook. None of the hw assignments matched with those on the test. The one time she did give study material was the one time in which I did well on a test. However, she only gave review material once.

Prof McLaughlin is not a good teacher in my opinion, be prepared to teach yourself the material. The tests define how you will do in this course, and some of which I thought were unfair. Not understanding of people who struggle/need extra help. Do not recommend.

Professor McLaughlin was really good. Her teaching style came off as a bit new. She will have all her notes already written and uploaded on the website, as well as videos going over the notes. However, don't skip the lectures. The tests are straight from the lectures and homework. Her tests are very fair, including the final. Amazing professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great teacher! Very clear lectures and is nice.
I had calculus in high school and placed back into this class. Prof McLaughlin is the best math teacher I've ever had. She's patient and explains the ideas in a clear way.

Lectures do not help at all. She moves quickly and expects you to understand from a Calc perspective when it's only algebra. This could be a challenging math course for those who even considered themselves good at math. Please choose another professor if you can, if not make group chats and actively study with explanations from other professors.
Professor McLaughlin's lectures are clear. Her exams are fair if you follow her study suggestions.
Calc 231 can be difficult for some people but Professor McLaughlin will make supplementary videos of certain lecture topics if you ask. The three tests are a large part of your grade, just beware.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best class of my semester.

Professor McLaughlin cares about her students, has fair tests that reflect the material covered in class, and is clear on what will show up on a test beforehand. However, her lectures are not very effective. Be prepared to teach yourself the material in this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: McLaughlin makes clear what concepts and types of problems are going to be on the tests, so its pretty easy to study and make sure you know how to do those. Her lectures do go somewhat fast, but if you print out notes that she posts on Sakai, it's easier to keep up. I also haven't opened the textbook since the first week and am doing well still.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: queen period! bestie! i love calculus with her!

Professor Mclaughlin isn't a rude or strict person, but her grading is pretty tough. I would always get points off my tests because I didn't solve the math problems exactly how she said to do it. However she does take the time to teach the material but the homework usually tends to be harder than the examples she does.

Her lectures are pretty fast, but she is really patient with questions, so don't be afraid to ask them. Her notes are super good and mostly easy to read, and are very similar to the exams. Exams are weighted pretty heavy, and you definitely need to study quite a bit to do well, but overall one of the better MATH 233 profs.

She's very nice and approachable. Calculus isn't exactly my strong suit, but she clearly knows what she's talking about, and doesn't look down on students for asking "dumb" questions. Tests are worth a very large portion of the grade, so make sure you're prepared. You will need to study for them, and don't procrastinate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is a hard class and Prof McLaughlin is very patient. I appreciate all the effort she puts in.

This teacher has made algebra far more difficult than it needs to be. Class time is spent swiftly going over a few examples of the unit, which forces the student to teach themselves the rest of the content. The teacher does not respond to direct emails about math problems. We are supposed to receive help from Piazza, but many are left ignored.
Great professor, knows the course content really well. Is very nice and approachable IMO. Would take with her again!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She 's about the best that you could ask for in terms of teaching math. Her patience really impressed me, and every day she was prepared to enthusiastically discuss the material. Her exams were straight forward and the material on them was clearly covered in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor McLaughlin is an amazing instructor who really seeks to ensure each student has a full understanding of the material. Although online, she was able to make this class feel as if it were a traditional, engaging in-class experience. She deals out a lot of homework but my class only had to do 75% of it. Lecture-heavy with lots of time for Qs

I took this class during the summer and it definitely took a lot of time each day just to complete the homework and understand the material. 80% of our grade was calculated from two midterms (20% each and final as 40%), but McLaughlin always directly told us what would be on the tests. Solid choice for MATH233 and explains concepts pretty well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Your grade consists mostly of the three tests but I found them to be pretty fair. The lectures weren't always clear to me so I ended up having to use YouTube video lectures to help and that made a huge difference. Overall, I think she's a kind professor but depending of the kind of learner you are, you might need to outsource some assistance.

Prof. McLaughlin was super understanding and was an amazing lecturer. Calc 3 is hard in general but her teaching style was very helpful. Her exams aren't bad at all and resemble the questions in her notes very closely. There is a good amount of homework and it is hard but very helpful to understand topics conceptually. Overall a great class!
This was a well organized class. I don't do well in math and appreciated all her help.

I had to drop the class. I am not good at math and found that taking it over Zoom with this professor was not the easiest. She was patient and nice, but I struggled too much to stay in the course. If you are already decent at math, you would be fine with this professor, but if not, you've got your work cut out for you.

I think she tried her hardest to teaching through zoom this semester, but often times I felt there was a miscommunication between her and the class. A large part of the grade is determined by tests and quizzes. I was not a fan of her style, I felt as if she only reviewed content than teaching it. However, she was helpful to any questions asked!
Very patient. Detailed class. She make calculus interesting.
Take this prof if you want to understand the material in depth. Very good so far.
She works hard to make sure each person gets their questions answered. She is very patient.
My favorite class this semester. She's an excellent teacher. Not hard if you do the work.
Although Ms. McLaughlin was kind, she was not the best at teaching. Her explanations were confusing and she made lots of mistakes, but if we did the same, we were given no partial credit on tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Calc 3 is def not easy, especially online, regardless of what prof you take it with. You will have to study super hard to get an A, but she always takes time to help. She has the most straightforward exams (all questions from HW and notes), which is great but also screws you over for the final since other profs write harder questions.
Its a hard class but her tests tend to be more straightforward. Can be time-consuming but doable to do well. Final may be curved a little, but not the midterms.
Exams are fair. A lot of homework. Class notes are clear and cover everything. Nice prof.
So good!

Professor McLaughlin's notes are usually really helpful and if you go to office hours, she can be really helpful. Your grade is almost entirely dependent on two tests and the final but the questions are almost exact copies of the examples she gives in class. Calc is going to hard regardless but I this definitely wasn't bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Midterms will not try and trick you. Most all problems will come directly from lecture and recitations. However, there is a boatload of homework that is only intended to further your conceptual knowledge, not help for exams. Just tedious work to do.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: We have the least amount of work among all 233 sessions (only hw, no participation) and Prof McLaughlin posts her notes online, which summarize the topics clearly and are much easier to read than the textbook. Tests could be a bit difficult but this is calc 3 after all. She is a very kind person and encourages you to go to her office hour.

Overall, the class isn't insanely difficult, but it definitely requires a good bit of work. Her teaching style isn't very good (in my opinion), so be prepared to teach yourself the material. With access to practice exams, progress checks, and past exams, doing well on exams is very possible.

I honestly didn't have a problem with her teaching style-- I think it could've turned out better for me if Fall 2020 semester wasn't so chaotic. I think the grading system is a bit harsh: only three tests w/ minimal partial credit, and the final is close to 40% of your grade. The homework inflation helps. Slightly disorganized but nothing too bad:)
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Good class. Not too hard. In depth explanations.
I put a lot of time into this class using her notes and videos. It was not an easy A, I definitely worked for it but everything is well organized and she's a good teacher.

We only had 2 tests for the semester and then the final, so if you did poorly on the tests, you better get a great score on the final. I, personally, had a hard time understanding the material during the lectures so I stuck to reading the textbook. Overall its an ok class, just put a lot of effort into the tests and homework and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: It's an ok class. Homework takes awhile but is easy to get a 100 on cause you get 3 tries to answer it. Exams are ok, if you study and do a lot of practice questions. I liked her class but that was just because I was ok with the lecture style of her teaching. I also like rewatching lectures to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Online format: posts lecture video/notes before class; goes over same notes during class; homework due on Sundays; two tests and final exam; suggests textbook reading. Overall, the class wasn't impossible, the homework is WAY more difficult than the exams, but she's approachable with questions.

I didn't have a lot of trouble in her class (took bc in hs), but I could see how learning from her would be hard. Read the textbook & watch videos of her going over notes before class. She stopped posting the videos halfway through the semester so that made it trickier. Do the practice problems! The practice problems are way harder than tests.
No partial credit was given on tests which make up the majority of the class grade
Interesting class. Nice prof.
Detailed class and good lectures. Definitely recommend this instructor.
Solid class.
lectures were not super in depth and the homework was very different than the class notes

I appreciate the amount of time she put into our class. The course notes are helpful and her explanations are clear. The exams are not too difficult but the homework is. This is a very hard class but I'll be getting an A- because of the extra help she provided.

I really like this course. McLaughlin provides detailed notes and corresponding videos. The lectures are clear. Very solid class. She's approachable and works with you if you miss assignments. Definitely take her if you want to understand concepts.

I am taking this class fully remote atm. Class is very lecture heavy and she isn't very good at lecturing. The homework is not relevant and often covers material outside the course and is auto graded. Most of the grade is from tests and have no partial credit. Class averages for tests are in the 60s with no curve until the end of course.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Took this class in the summer online due to COVID. I thought she was a pretty solid instructor. She was nice and would answer specific questions about what exactly we needed to know for tests. The online hw had unlimited attempts so was a completion grade. I barely passed the class but test averages were in the 80s so I would recommend!
The class was well organized and the videos helpful. She is a very detailed and quality prof. Definitely take her if you want to understand concepts.

Dr Mcluaghlin is a very good professor! I had heard some not-so nice things before taking her but she was actually a very good professor. She was easy to understand and was always helpful outside of class.

Not sure about the last review since she wasn't live lectures. It was all recorded lectures and was excellent. A very clear and organized class. She grades the exams with the other instructors. I'd definitely take another class from her.

Her TA's grade tests. When you're in class and she says that she would give you credit if you answered a math problem a certain way, don't trust it because she won't be grading your tests. Also, the problems you do in class are way easier than the ones on the tests. She can be demeaning and I think she cares more about her higher level math classes

Easy A if you read the text, go to class and do the homework. Her lecture style is detailed and informative. She really knows the material and doesn't dumb it down. I liked that about her teaching style. I feel prepared for the class I'm in this semester. Definitely take her if your priority is understanding the material.

Prof McLaughlin's class prepared me for calc 3 this semester. She is a thorough and detailed teacher. One of the smartest teachers I've had. If you take good notes and pay attention in class, getting a good grade shouldn't be a problem.

McLaughlin is caring but not great at teaching. You may fall asleep during lectures. The material taught was not difficult but wasn't taught well. Felt like the homework wasn't helpful. The recitations were more helpful than the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The best teacher I've had in math. Prof McLaughlin was awesome! Lectures were clear and she cared about how well we did. Definitely take her class.

I have never made below an A+ in a math class until now. She's hands down the worst professor I've had thus far and I went to just about every class. She sped through lectures, does not write out all of the steps/work in class and does not teach down to people without a calculus background and the average for the final (that she wrote) was a 65.
Tests are very reasonable if you show up to class and pay attention. Make sure to stay on top of work and ask questions if you are ever stuck.

Tests make up the good majority of your grade in this class, but McLaughlin makes her tests really easy. She gives really hard examples in the homework and in class, but the problems on the test are the most basic and simplified versions of what was taught, making it easy to do well on the tests.

The class was taught clearly and paced well. Lectures are a little dull, and the graded recitation worksheets and long homework assignments were a bit of a drudgery, but overall, the class is designed to teach the material thoroughly, and the tests are a pretty fair evaluation of how much you've learned.

I really liked being in Dr. McLaughlin's class. She was very clear about what kinds of questions we should expect on the exams (she also usually writes the math 231 final). I went to every lecture, took notes, and did many practice problems from the textbook and I was able to do well on her midterms. She is also really helpful in office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: McLaughlin was my favorite teacher this semester. She was super helpful in office hours. Very funny and smart.
Good class. Exams are easy. Go to class and review her class problems. Pretty much the same test questions.

Thanks to Prof Mclaughlin I passed calculus. She's an awesome teacher! She really cares about her students. She answers emails on the weekends and will work with you until you understand. I was afraid to take this class, but she was kind to me, which helped. She's also very patient so if you are freaked about taking this class, go see her in office

I enjoyed the course. The objectives were clear and her lectures and the homework prepared me for the exams. The final exam was fair. I worked for my A- and feel that it reflected my performance. I've never had calculus and I'm pleased with my grade. The homework is long and crashes, but that happened in my other classes too.

I enjoyed Professor McLaughlin's class; however, her teaching style is heavily centered around what students should have already learned from the textbook. She does not track attendance; however, it's hard to pass if you don't come to class. Sadly, our final exam grade was extremely low and although she promised a curve, it wasn't applied to A & Bs
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: McLaughlin spent a majority of the class solving problems incorrectly and then students would be forced to help her correct her errors. The final exam had no similarity to the midterms and midterms were graded in a manner so that one incorrect question would be deducted 14 pts. Seemingly simple material was taught in a complex manner.
Awesome class!

McLaughlin for MATH 232 was the hardest class that I have taken at UNC, and I'm usually a great math student. You have to teach yourself all the material because she is so bad at teaching the class. The tests are completely unfair, but she doesn't write the final, so that's the only way to save your grade. DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HER.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Definitely take this prof. She teaches beyond the text. More like a concept style class. Very interesting. Don't take her if you are looking for a teach and regurgitation type lecture. It makes getting an A harder, but will be useful for the next calc class I'm taking.
This was a very good class. She was helpful and provided examples in class that were useful for studying for the exams. She's nice and pretty funny if you get to know her in office hours.

Good class. Prof McLaughlin uses a lot of examples to explain the topics. It was helpful to hear what to expect in the next calculus class up. Homework is long. The recitations have worksheets which are helpful
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I LOVED this class. She explains beyond the textbook. Really interesting class.

If you're premed avoid this class like the plague. I screwed my GPA so bad by taking this class and it's only my first semester of college which means I'm only one semester in and I've already ruined my shot at med school. This class is absolutely impossible and McLaughlin doesn't explain anything. She's very smart/kind but a terrible professor.
Her class is not that hard. Don't slack off. The homework is long but not bad.
Easy class if you do the homework and not miss class. Lectures are clear and helpful. She's very nice and approachable. It would have been useful if she had office hours later in the day.

Lectures are all over the place and tough to follow. But if you go to class and pay attention, exams are pretty straightforward. She did not write her own final when I took the class and it was ridiculously hard and nothing like the midterms. If you are good at math, take her, but if you struggle please take with another professor
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This was a difficult class but Prof Mclaughlin explained ideas well and answered all of my questions in class. The homework is painful but if you do it all the exams aren't too bad.

Really excellent teacher. She makes difficult material easy to understand if you go to class and ask questions. She knows the math. I'm surprised how much I ended up liking calculus. Didn't in high school.

If you go to class and do the homework, getting an A isn't hard. Prof McLaughlin is very good at explaining the material and providing feedback via email if you need it. She's helpful in office hours and cares if you understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: If I hadn't taken calc in high school I would be beat. Try to find another professor if this is your first time learning it. She does not explain concepts very well and gets confused when doing practice problems. Tests are quite difficult and they count for like all of the grade. Recitation and TAs were very helpful though.
awesome class! show up, do the homework. easy grade

McLaughlin's class is interesting. Not very difficult if you attend the lectures. Exams are more or less the problems she works in class. She was very kind to me during office hours. I was sick a lot and she helped me to get back on track. I highly recommend taking her class.

Going to class confuses you rather than helps you. If you ask a question she never knows the answer and just tells you she'll get back to you and never does. If you get her for math and have to take her for some reason wait another semester for another teacher because you will struggle so hard.

Dr. Mclaughlin is nice but awful at conveying the material during lectures. She says she can slow down but will just speed back up 5 minutes later. 3 exams written by the TA's and not her. Funny thing is that TA's do not even show up to class to see the difficulty of problems we do during class. Overall, it is a stressful class. Don't recommend.
good class

If you listen actively during the lectures, you'll feel prepared by the time of the exams. Professor McLaughlin explains things at a good pace and has great explanations! Personable and open to answering questions or slowing down during lecture. The homework is usually harder than the exams, which actually helps in the long-run.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I was scared to take calculus but Prof McLaughlin made this class easy to understand. She's very patient. I recommend taking her !
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I'm in math 232 and I think it's an awesome class. Mclaughlin is very clear and interesting! Not sure why people review and speak for an entire class. if you go to class and do the homework you will pass.

Calc is hard in general, she is a very intelligent professor but she isn't the best at dumbing thing down which could make things very confusing to understand during lecture. We often have problems where the entire lecture hall of people all confused and lost. Also she speaks very soft and has monotone so it's very hard to stay away and keep up.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She clearly knows her stuff, but can't explain it simply during lecture. You're going to get a headache trying to understand her during class, and then get another headache later when you try to teach yourself the material at home. There's nothing more unifying than a room full of people that have no idea what is going... at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I won't pretend that Ms. McLaughlin is the best teacher ever, but she knows her stuff and she's not half bad. She has a relaxed personality which doesn't necessarily serve the enunciation of math concepts. Self study is definitely needed, but she's also very approachable in office hours. In the end, I sought her help and got an A in Calculus 2.

I personally loved prof McLaughlin. I highly recommend not skipping classes because she teaches concepts well and teaches from the book so you can use that as a resource as well. You have to work for your grade but it's not unfair or unreasonable. The tests are derived from hw and class exercises and are regular enough to reinforce the material.
Really good summer class. It went fast but McLaughlin explained all the topics very well. She gave plenty of review materials for the final exam during the last week of classes.

At first I really didn't like her disorganization. She didn't write her own syllabus. For some reason she had someone else write it so she was always a little confused on where we were and why we were doing what we were doing. After a while I kinda got use to her sporadic teaching. The only reason I did so well was that I had a calculus background.

I took Math 232 and 233 from Prof. McLaughlin. She's a detailed oriented teacher and very smart. Class lectures go quickly so if you keep up with the homework you will follow. Lectures connected key concepts throughout the semester so by the time we made it to the end the ideas came together in an interesting way. I highly recommend her.

Really good class. She gives problems for us to work in class and then walks around the room giving individual feedback. Super helpful. The homework is long and keeps crashing, but is necessary for getting a decent grade on her tests.

Monotonous and excruciatingly boring lecture style. It's hard enough to keep a 100 person class interested normally, and her style really doesn't help in that regard. Nice curve on the final grade, but I gained more from my weekly recitation with the TA than in any of the actual lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor McLaughlin does go fast, but she does care if you understand the material. It is imperative you practice outside of class, because she expects that you're ready to move on by the next lecture. She always seemed ready to answer questions and always used relevant examples in class. Graded by 4 midterms, a cumulative hw grade, and a final.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: While it may take a little getting used to her style, she's a really great teacher. Her lectures are full of good examples and she was very lenient with grading on the online homework. While she does not provide many worksheets, she often gives extra problems at the end of lecture or emails them out after class and provides the answers too.
I love this class! Ms McLaughlin has an interesting teaching style. Her examples are visual based which makes this class easier to understand.
Class is just a regurgitation of the textbook, and the professor doesnt help you much if you have questions of your own. If you want to do well in this class read ahead in the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I took Professor McLaughlin for all three calculuses (231, 232, 233) and I did this because I loved her teaching style. It isn't for everyone, but she's clear and does a lot of examples. Her tests are extremely fair- if you pay attention you'll know what's gonna be on the exam. She moves very fast, but she's reasonable and approachable.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very clear objectives. Excellent class. Easy A if you attend class, do the homework, and review class notes.

She has quick hand writings but a clear introduction to the things she would like to convey. To succeed in class, you can read the relevant chapters before head. She teaches the chapters based on textbook. If you do homework and the examples given during the class well, you will get good grades for it.
Only take her if you have to, the textbook saved me in my class.
Really awesome teacher!

I had an amazing AP Calculus teacher in highschool and so I was nervous coming into Math 232 with Mclaughlin after reading her reviews. Don't believe the lies! If you go to class and take notes there will be absolutely no surprises on the exams. I am taking her for Math 233 next semester because of this! She teaches the book so don't bother reading
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very good foundation for 233. Elizabeth delivers clear lectures-is easy to follow if you go to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: LOVED the class! She made calculus interesting with cool visual explanations.
Elizabeth is a clear lecturer. The exams are fair. I did well in the class. I dont usually like math but I liked this class.
Easy class if you do the homework. She curves the final grade so it didnt matter if the tests were curved. Clear explanations and easy exams if you take notes. Tests are like the notes.

This is the worst class I have ever take, the teacher is unclear about what she is teaching and require you to learn by yourself most of the time. Hard exam and hard homework, regret taking her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof. McLaughlin is a clear lecturer who gives great visual explanations where possible. Her exams are very fair, and you'll likely find them easier if you attend class to catch the hints she gives ahead of time. The WebAssign homework is good practice (and usually more difficult than the exams), but also the most time-consuming part of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Loved this class! I'm taking her for 233 next semester.

Elizabeth is very nice & not intimidating. She teaches straight out of the book & the class is lecture heavy. She may seem a little unprepared/scattered, but she has a passion for math. If you work hard in recitation and do the hw you should not struggle too much. When she makes her own tests they are always fair and on stuff we have covered.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The final exam was difficult but McLaughlin prepared us adequately. We were given review sheets in class. I appreciated that. Overall it was an interesting class and well taught.
Good class.
Ms. McLaughlin always explained topics in a methodical manner. Step by step. This gave me a solid foundation for continuing on to Math 233.
A lot of homework, but all of my math classes had the same. Very good teacher. Definitely take her.

Really excellent class. Ms. McLaughlin was a very patient teacher and always available. When I couldn't make office hours she would let me email screenshots of my work, grade and return to me. She answered questions with respect during class. I don't understand why some of these reviews say otherwise. I guess math can be frustrating for some peopl.

I absolutely despised this class. I have always loved math, but Ms. McLaughlin truly ruined that for me. She speeds through everything, and acts annoyed if someone would have a question. I also found it more helpful to go to other teacher's office hours because when I went to her she made me feel like I was an idiot for not knowing the answer.

Calc 3 was an interesting class. I really love math and wasn't disappointed in Ms McLaughlin's teaching style. The homework was overwhelming at times, but necessary, I guess. I wish she was teaching diff eq next semester.

I took her for 152 and had to take an incomplete. Finally finished. She was so patient and worked with my constant delaying of due dates and exam dates. When I sent screenshots of work, she corrected and returned them. She went out of her way to help me and I'm very grateful!

I liked this class. McLaughlin went very fast but there was so much to cover. Reading ahead helps. The material was interesting and she had a clear presentation of the concepts. The class problems were helpful.
This is a very good class! It's a lot of work but if you go to class and do the homork it's not so bad.

McLauglin has a very complicated teaching style. For the0 tests she did not give us any exam review material or old practice tests. She often can't explain concepts if you are confused about problems and her lessons are regurgitations of the textbook. Warning: take this class with another professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She was disorganized and basically taught straight out of the book. She never gave us practice tests or study guides so we were on our own for tests. Was very unclear about what would be on tests. Her teaching style is basically rushing through a few concepts, and then doing a ton of complicated examples. Advice if you take her: read ahead!

Unless you already know how to do calc 3 dont take it with her. Youll spend hours studying just to find out the test is half on material youve barely gone over. Bad lecturer. Does things old school when that obviously doesnt work. Fair warning dont do it

Nice person, but not great instructor. Lectures quickly and straight from the book- big lecture hall class so if you prep and read book well, don't need to go to lecture. Started incl. more practice problems later in the semester but often doesn't go over work/theories, just writes answers down. Lots of hard HW; test q's similar to HW. Practice!!!
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Lot's of work. Don't miss lectures and read ahead. Good teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: It feels like she does not understand what she is teaching us, yet she moves at about 3000 words a minute. Sometimes when she does not feel like explaining something she just tells us to learn it on our own. Our homework is horrible and is almost impossible to do and are due at the weirdest times. 0/10 would not recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I took her for both Math 232 and 233. She's a straightforward professor. Copy down all of her examples in class because she models her tests off of her examples in class and hw problems from webassign. Those will be approx. 3/4 of her exams. The other 1/4 will be problems out of left field. Both semesters there was a small curve at the end

Some students like her, but unless you vibe with her, you won't like her. She teaches incredibly fast and will write down problems and answers but not show any work. You are expected to read the chapters beforehand and know how to do the problems. If you take her class, get a good TA who will teach you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Shes not the best at explaining things, but practice problems in her lectures are similar to the ones on the exams, youll just have to teach yourself how to do them. The final was worth 45% of the grade, so make sure you really do well on it. In the past, she hasnt curved anything, but our final grade was curved up by at least 5 points.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I won't lie, she's hard to keep up with in lecture. You can tell she knows what she's doing and makes important connections, but the course itself is so jam packed she has to fly through everything. Still, her tests are fair and are based off the examples she does in class (NOT the webassigns), so those are best to study with. Read the textbook too
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Consensus was she has no idea what she's doing. I really hope that she just spends more time focusing on her other classes because multiple times she said, "I know this is Business Calculus, but I frankly know nothing about Business, so you can figure that out for yourself." I tried multiple times to talk after class and she said "I have no time."

One of the worst lecturers I've ever had. I went to every single class and took notes and almost failed. She gives horrible examples and doesn't even finish them sometimes. It's impossible to talk to her as there are so many students in the class and her TAs do their best but she doesn't communicate with them either.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Teaches by walking the class through an example problem, which I found helpful. Webassigns don't always completely line up with class material but tests are fair to what's taught in class. Is extremely patient (had to deal with so many first-semester freshmen attitudes so I really feel for her). Tests can be very short though (like 12 mc questions)

I love McLaughlin! My Calc teacher in high school had a similar style to hers, so learning was not that difficult. DO THE WEBASSIGNS and make sure you understand the problems. They are definitely harder than the problems she asks on the tests, so if you can master those, you'll be prepared. A lot of self-teaching, but nothing too bad. PRACTICE!!!

There are only 9-15 multiple choice questions on every test which makes it super easy to lose points. She also doesn't curve at all. Professor McLaughlin is available for assistance if you go to office hours, but this class is super hard! Definitely only take it if you absolutely have to.
