Very poor teacher. Doesn't teach topics clearly. Must teach everything to yourself. Not very helpful when asked questions. Very rude when asked for assistance. Condescending and doesn't curve grades no matter how many people fail tests.

If you don't vibe with her teaching style, talk to her and then decide whether you should go to a different section. She's a great professor and truly made my freshman and sophomore years great, I actually wanted to go to class over the summer when I had her!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: You can tell that she relatively enjoys the material she's teaching. The homework is pretty tricky but once you get the hang of it, it's not so bad. Her tests are very straightforward if you understand the material. However, her tests are multiple choice with only 10-15 questions, so every point counts. She doesn't tend to curve tests.

Class is spent entirely going over problems from the book, not actually teaching. Students who do well are those who clearly are already great math students. The material wouldn't be that bad if she would actually teach it. I asked for help,, she said "read the book". Wouldnt recommend, take this class with someone else if you have to have it.

McLaughlin is not a great teacher. You can tell she knows what she's talking about, but she doesn't do well in conveying it to the class. She basically writes on the board exactly what is from the textbook and only elaborates if someone asks specific questions. The tests aren't too bad, but they're very short so it's easy to lose points quickly.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Lecture is really fast paced but she still explains the material very well. She takes time in class to do practice problems and is very willing to answer questions during that time. Tests are only a few questions but they are not that difficult and all multiple choice. Go to office hours if you need help! She's always there.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I took BC Calculus before retaking it at UNC, and Math232 with her was not hard at all. She basically just goes over the different "types" of problems that you'll encounter and then you do the rest on your own outside of class. Pro tip: don't retake MATH232 unless you got a 3 or lower on the AP exam, it's useless for MATH233 and a waste of time.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: McLaughlin isn't as horrible as people make her out to be. MATH 232 isn't that hard either. Just study. She follows the flipped model, so you'll have to read the book and watch YouTube. However, her tests are easy and she puts test questions on the board when she has a review day for tests. She writes fast, so make sure you read before class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Terrible teacher
Never take this prof ever
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This class was my first experience with a flipped class. I struggled very much in the beginning but Professor Mclaughlin was still very encouraging to all of us. She would help us during class when we struggled with the homework and believed that we could do it. At the end of the class I actually liked math because of her and how she pushed me.

This is the hardest class I've ever taken. Pretty much every grade is based on 3 midterms and the final (she replaces a midterm grade). I think Mclaughlin is good but there is not enough time for the material so she has to go super super fast. If you get behind it's really tough to catch up, I would only take this class if you absolutely must

The exams she writes consist of 10 multiple choice questions, each covering a different complex topic with applications barely touched on in class. She does not understand what students ask of her half the time. As a student who attended every class, completed every homework, and studied hard for every exam, this was my least favorite math professo
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: She was not a great instructor. I stopped going to class after the first exam because I could learn better teaching myself the material. She mostly does examples in class so I would read the text book before each class and get ahead so you know the material before she starts doing examples. Exams and the final are straight forward but study hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Math 231 was difficult, but definitely doable. Professor McLaughlin does go fast, but she does a good job of explaining concepts in detail when asked. Having a prior knowledge of calc from high school will definitely help. Her tests are difficult, but doing tons of practice problems out of the textbook will prepare you best for them.

Be sure to take this class somewhere else, especially if you're not a math major.  Her test averages (she makes the tests literally so impossible that she has trouble answering the questions) are literally around the 50-60%.  The A's are people who already know calculus from high school.  Her tests are usually unrelated to the questions in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: She goes through topics very quickly and makes mistakes way too regularly making her class confusing and hard to follow. Doesn't really seem to care about students learning anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I had Mclaughlin for Calc 1 and 2, and she is definitely much better for Calc 2. She has much more enthusiasm for higher level topics, so she teaches Calc 2 more effectively. She is very fast paced, but does care about students and will go over certain topics if you ask for clarification. She will also personally go over your tests in office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Everyone complains about how hard math 232 is, but as long as you study and go over the webassign problems before the tests you will be fine. If you think you can skip class or cheat on the homework and pass, you are wrong. Speak up if you do not understand something because sometimes she assumes you know something/the steps & no one says anything
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: If you skip class you are going to fail, so seriously do not skip. Sometimes she assumes you know something and keeps going, so don't be afraid to speak up if you need explanation. Her 3 exams are not too hard, and if you go over webassign and notes you will know how to do the problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I enjoyed and made an A in my high school Calc class. McLaughlin made me hate math. She taught advanced concepts (which were not complicated but she made them so) abstractly with few  concrete examples. TAs and my recitation leader taught me everything and I got an A but put in tons of hours outside of class. I will not take anymore math at UNC.

Professor McLaughlin is far from the worst Calculus professor you could have. She really knows the material and is capable of explaining things in clear detail - if she wants to. However, she speeds ahead during each lecture leaving many questions unanswered as she assumes you'll already know what to do by reading the textbook.

She mostly spends time proving things and does not really go through how to solve problems. After a while I stopped paying attention in class and caught up in recitation. However, I found her exams very straightforward and easy, so I recommend taking her class.

Professor Mclaughlin is a very good professor, even though I did not do as well as I wanted to in the class. Math 233 is a difficult class and i recommend reading before class and doing many practice problems. I believe that is where i slacked and if i had a regime then i would've done much better in the class. Prepared me well for the final.

Professor McLaughlin clearly is passionate about math/calculus but is not a gifted teacher. She does not go out of her way to help students. The material is very difficult, and McLaughlin does not make it much easier. Avoid taking this course, take MATH 231 or STOR 113 if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Do not take her. I'm sorry, she may be very knowledgeable of calculus, and it showed during some points of the semester. However, she DOES NOT know how to convey ideas very clearly, and often times forgets what class she is teaching, and expects you to know higher level concepts that you haven't learned yet (she also teaches 232 and 233)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Goes through material very quickly and with not much explanation.  Very nice woman but a difficult professor if you aren't math-oriented.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: A straightforward teacher who worked closely to the textbook. Her tests are almost all based on questions shown in class or homework. She was always willing to take her time to explain something to any one student even if it took the whole class block. Overall, caring and rather straightforward tests. Webassigns took a fair amount of time though.

McLaughlin takes her time in lectures and provides plenty of examples to make sure you understand the material. The examples are much harder than the tests, so if you can do those then the tests won't be bad. There is homework twice a week, but aside from that its not a terribly demanding class. I feel like a learned a lot from McLaughlin.

She keeps it real and tries to put you in the best position to get good scores in the exam. She could be better with explaining sometimes. Take good notes in class because the problems she works on the board are likely to show up in one of the three midterms. Shes say it as it is and will usually give obvious hints for pop quizes.

Professor McLaughlin was oddly lax every time I reached out for help after receiving a not-so-great grade and just told me not to worry about it which was pretty frustrating. Unless you REALLY go out of your way to make yourself known to her (i.e. going to office hours, going up to the board, etc.) don't expect much help from the professor.

McLaughlin is a nice woman. However, she moves really fast and she doesn't clarify very well. It is extremely hard if you've never been exposed to Calculus concepts before. Tons of Webassign homework. Three hard midterms. Final can replace one of them. The important thing is to have a good recitation leader; they can really help you understand.

Lectures are her explaining and working out problems. Sometimes quizzes are given in recitation but its just more working out problems. Doesn't give partial credit. Claims you need to read the book in order to pass the test. Personally, not true. Read it once and it wasn't much help. Web Assign takes a very long time to finish. Tests are a bit hard
Terrible writing on the blackboard. She teaches really fast sometimes makes me confused.
she expects you to know a lot of stuff  prior to taking her class

I took calculus in high school and came in with a pretty good understanding. Somehow, through the course of the semester, I actually became more confused than I have ever been before. McLaughlin took the material I thought I knew, and explaining it in the worst way possible, managed to un-teach me all of it.

WebAssign is easy and helpful if you put in the time. She is willing to help if you come to class. Tests are very fair--more so than other calculus professors. Taking her for 232 next semester and would recommend. Class is a breeze if you had Calculus in high school.

While she is probably the easiest Math 231 professor, she's also the worst professor. Do not take McLaughlin if you have no calc background because she won't help much. She's confusing and does random example problems without explaining the concepts. This is the only class where my recitation actually helped because I had no idea what was going on.

Do not take math 231 with this professor.  She is very scatterbrained and her class is impossible. I got an A in AP Calc in high school and math was my strongest subject before now. I didn't get above a 54 on any test, including the final this year.

One of those math professors that, when doing practice problems, does not know how to explain what she is doing and why she is doing it.  Likes to skip steps when solving.  test avg has never been over 53. If you like math, don't take her because she can't teach you anything; if you don't like math, don't take her because you will fail her class.

I don't know if I am missing something with all of these previous ratings, but I am currently failing calculus and I have attended every class and have lived in office hours, relying on my TA to teach me the stuff she never taught us yet tests us on. She goes way too fast and expects us to already know everything, and her tests are HARSHY graded!

She is terrible. Very scatterbrained and flaky, and not good at explaining anything. The only good thing about my class is that I have an excellent TA, but it sucks that he's basically teaching us everything because she's so bad at her job. I don't know how I will pass this class. Avoid her at all costs unless you like being confused.

Not really a math person but I absolutely loved  McLaughlin. She was incredibly clear during lectures and made the material very easy to understand. The WebAssign is usually hard, but the answers can be found online and in the book. The problems on the exam are much easier and if you know the class examples and homework, its easy to make an A or A-

She goes pretty fast. Although very intelligent, not prepared for class at times. She did a whole problem on the board and never solved it. She changes homework dates a few times which sometimes doesn't help.

She is pretty clear in explaining her expectations, helpful and inspirational. Homework is lot more harder than test themselves but if you attend lectures and do homework properly than you should be fine with all her tests. I would definitely recommend taking her!
Excellent teacher. If you have to take calc I definitely recommend her.

McLaughlin is one of my favorite professors: she is extremely clear and is quite nice. Her tests are 'easy', but she gives no partial credit for your answers even if you make the smallest mistake, so averages are in the 60s. Also, the bottom third of the class drops, so the curves go away after the first midterm which is annoying.

She is nice and knows what she is talking about. Calculus is gonna be hard no matter what, but she is head of the math department and writes the exams so when you take it with her you know the types of questions that will be on there. Overall, I fairly enjoyed her class.
Horrible

Professor McLaughlin is what I would consider ok.  She explains concepts fairly well, but tends to do so rather quickly.  She does lots of practice problems in class, but SHE does them... and tends to do them pretty fast too.  She is fairly helpful in class, and very helpful during office hours, but her office hours are set in stone.

The lectures are fast paced, she doesnt appreciate being slowed down. She is inflexible with her office hours. If you can't make it, she will not make another time for you. Her tests are hard. The average right now is a 45. She comes to class and asks if there are any questions, then she tells people to see her after class instead of answering them
Very very hard class.  She is straightforward and not personal, but I really liked her.  I learned calculus completely and it challenged me.

Straightforward, no nonsense math. Class moves at a good pace, slow enough to digest a new theorem, fast enough to lessen redundant calculations. She doesn't assign too much homework and her tests are very reasonable. For once, your grade actually depends on whether you understand the material or not.
She is a pretty good teacher.  She tends to ramble on about the same concepts and she has a droning voice.  Tests are pretty tough, but the final is pretty easy if you study.

Professor McLaughlin is pretty nice and helpful.  Her teaching methods are pretty clear.  I would suggest trying to get into her class if you are ok at math but are willing to do some independent studying.

Great Professor.  I had her this semester for Calculus 3 and I like the pace of the course and she gives fair tests unlike most.  If you study you should pass.  I'm going to take her again for Calc4 or differential.  Thanks.
I hated this class. She never slows down in class, and her office hours are set in stone.  If you can manage to make it to her office, she'll usually help, but good luck if you aren't a math whiz.

She is a great teacher, and has obviously taught this subject before, because she is simple, straightforward, and to the point. No unneccesary material, and all tests/quizzes come directly from notes. Go to every lecture, and do the optional homework, and its an easy A/B.
No curve when the class average was a 60, students with 100 averages got 80's and not flexible during office hours.

Liked her so much for math31 that i took her for 32 Tries to make the material as straightforward as possible Has experience teaching these courses so they are structured & coherent. If you do the homework (optional) the tests are familiar Fair & understanding. Considering the options for math profs (not speaking clear english, etc) shes a goldmine
some confusing lectures, but no due homework, no absent policy, and extremely helpful with clarifying problems and is very open to questions

I fell in love with Calc after taking her course.  She has very reasonable quizzes and exams and is such a clear, straightforward lecturer.  She always made sure people understood the material.  I would recommend her to anyone.
good lectures, straight-forward quizzes, no due hw, no absent policy, good teacher
lectures were unclear and unhelpful

Hard class, but it's not her fault. She tries to make it as clear as possible and is very straitforward in her explanations. The material is a bit hard just because it is one of the hardest classes at Carolina, but very good teacher. I would recommend her.
No Comments
No Comments

I found his lectures to be pretty interesting since a lot were about personal work he did down in Peru. Quite an easy class if you put in work for the essays and keep engaged. Would definitely take him again I love his sense of humor.

Took this class as my friends as an 'easy A'. Easy A's do not exist here, you're gonna have to put work in to get the grade you want. You gotta go to class, pay attention, and study. If you do that, you'll get a good grade, but don't think it's gonna be a joke of a class you can take as a filler. Class is fun and interesting.
Lectures were always fun and exams were pulled from objective questions, you want to take note of things he says in class because they're not on the slides; Exam 2 was slightly harder for some reason
Good GenEd, although exams and papers are slightly hard.

i loved his humor and engaging lectures! i recommend this class however it can be hard to do well on exams if you do not attend every single class. there are few assignments so exams are weighted pretty heavily.

I loved this class; he is a great/fun lecturer! Your grade is 75% exams (3 midterms, the last midterm is the final, non-cumulative) but they're easy if you go to class and study at all - he gives a list of possible exam questions and pulls directly from it when writing the exams. Attendance is mandatory and recitation has a group project (easy A).

Honestly a sweetheart! You should go to class (attendance + need notes for exams). It was a pleasure to attend-- never a chore. Studying was even fun, because the content was like a fun game of composing the story of history.

Professor Billman was a great professor. He's in the center of all archaeological lessons he's teaching. He has a lot of connections with anthropologists and archaeologists out in the world. He's very lenient on the assignments as long as you do it. Don't be afraid to talk to him.

Knows not to be too serious. Notes are easy to complete if you go to class and mildly pay attention.  He will often have some goofy tale or joke to make class interesting. Exams are ripped straight from the provided objectives. TAs were also relaxed and graded easy. Chill gen-ed with a chill dude. Would recommend.

Billman was easily the best lecturer I have had at UNC. His lectures were funny and very helpful for the exams. Very exam-heavy, but with a little studying of exam objectives before the exam. As long as you attend lectures, take good notes, and study before the exams you cannot get a bad grade. Easy focus capacity credit.
Pretty easy A/A-. Billman is cool, and his lectures are probably as entertaining as they can be.

I took this class for a focus capacity and I am so glad I did. Although the exams/ 2 papers were no cake walk, he is such a funny professor and made class super enjoyable. Just go to lectures and take notes, and you'll be fine.

Funny guy. Lectures are chill, he just shows you some pictures and tells you some stories. Exams and assignment were very easy. You honestly have to try super hard to not get a good grade in this class.
Loved him, clearly very passionate about the subject

Professor Billman keeps the class engaging with his hilarious lectures. While attendance is mandatory, the easy exams and lax grading make this a great gen ed. Unstuckstudy was super helpful for preparing.

Dr. Billman is a phenomenal lecturer and incredibly well-traveled. He has personal ties with half the archaeologists in the curriculum, and he's got a great sense of humor. The class was super engaging; attend lectures and take notes, though, because slides are sparse. Loved him so much that I'm taking two of his classes next sem as a busi major.

Very TA based, 4 assignments plus a bunch of just show up to class and get easy points. Its essentially 4 papers are the only assignments however I would not suggest this class as a gen ed. very boring and very TA based. However I should've gotten an A had I done all of the participation questions
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Take this instead of Anth145 Prehistory

Billman is a nice, funny guy, and a solid professor. He was fairly accommodating. I am not an Anth or hist major, but his class wan't crazy. Might have just been the TAs, but midterms were graded a bit harsh. Two papers with a take home midterm and final. I put low effort into learning material and still finished with an A-.
Super funny

Billman is my favorite professor hands down. This class is easy enough as a gen ed. Recitation meets only a couple of times, I read one chapter of the FREE pdf textbook and didn't feel like I missed anything. Essays and tests are easy and taken directly from lectures. He tells engaging stories and lectures are never boring.

This class was so interesting and Professor Billman was funny and kind. I would say it is important to take notes during class and do the few readings he assigns to do well on the exams (*not referring to the readings associated with the recitation). Recitation met infrequently and I felt that papers were graded leniently.

I love Dr. Billman! He tells amazing and hilarious stories, and is just all around a great and cool guy. His exams are often take home and open note, and other assignments are interesting and engaging. Definitely take this class if you want to learn about the history of the Andes, or if you just want an interesting class with a great professor!

You can't go wrong with Billman! He brought us donuts *multiple* times, what more can you ask for as a final semester senior?? Just pay attention in class and engage with his stories and you'll be good to go. Few assignments, but graded leniently. Really cool and funny guy too.

I LOVE BRIAN BILLMAN!!! I took this class as a gen ed my freshman year and I'm so glad I did. Billman was so funny and amazing. I could've done much worse on my exams, but the grading is incredibly lax, and he provides huge curves. The exams come straight from the learning objectives, which are the same as the lecture slides.

Lord Billman is awesome. His lectures are informative and hilarious, and everything on the tests IS covered in the lectures. Take good class notes, and remember your notes, and you'll get good test grades. His class is clear cut, makes sense, with no funny business like things on tests that he didn't lecture about. Can't go wrong with Billman.

Billman is really funny and he is a very entertaining lecturer! The content was great and as a STEM major, going to his non-flipped classroom was refreshing and enjoyable. Tests were really easy and non-cumulative and TAs graded papers very fairly. Billman talks about personal experience which keeps class interesting, as he cares about the subject.

Billman was really funny, yet sometimes I just felt really bored. Wasn't too hard at all though, and if you memorized the material like a couple hours before you'd be fine. Powerpoints kinda suck though, and you need to be in class to actually get the material.
GOAT!!! I love him
I hate that there were so few grades; however, the class was incredible. He is such a great teacher and very inspirational. Definitely take a class with him if you have the opportunity!!

Prof. Billman is amazing. His lectures are extremely engaging and very funny. Just make sure you are willing to attend every class because the exams rely on very in-depth notes. Generally, I couldn't recommend his class more, I'll be taking his other course next semester because of how amazing his story telling is. 10/10
Billman is so sweet and funny. Really easy class if you pay attention. Not super interesting unless archaeology is your thing but Billman is very understanding and will work with you.

Really great professor deserving a 5/5. Don't skip lectures and take notes and you'll get an A. His lectures are really interesting and he's an all around great guy. If you're looking for networking, Billman is also great for that. Classes are PowerPoint heavy but he sprinkles in interesting stories that make going to class worth it.

Overall Professor Billman is a really good teacher and laid back guy. Don't skip lectures because he shares a lot of information that is not on the presentations. Tests are open ended questions and a short essay at the end, all based on learning objectives which are easy. The two essays are really lowkey so don't worry.

I really enjoyed the class and Professor Billman. As someone who is half Peruvian and had some knowledge on the region, Billman spoke very highly of the Andean people and culture and was very respectful with its history and had great stories. There was only two papers, a midterm, a few participation questions, and the final that we were graded on.

He doesn't record lecture, and his slides are bare-bones for the stories he tells (which are very funny!). Attend class and take good notes--that's all you need to do to do well. He draws directly from lectures for the 4 main assignments, all of which are very straightforward. Love this class and prof--he cares a lot about his students/teaching :)

This class is more about the history of anthropology and less about the Indigenous people. The class content is often sensationalized which is weird. Because of this students make ignorant comments about cultural practices they don't understand. This class might make any Andean students annoyed but he's nice and knowledgeable about the region.
Do not take this class if you want an easy gen ed credit-- the content is not hard, but Billman's exams are tough unless you take notes on nearly everything that he says during his lectures.

Professor Billman is an extremely kind, caring and overall hilarious person. However, his lectures are extremely boring and I fell asleep on many occasions in class. Tests are also difficult so make sure you are paying attention to lectures when in class and take notes on every single detail. Overall, class is difficult for a gen-ed.

He's definitely entertaining in lectures, I'll give him that. He can be a bit scattered sometimes, but the lectures are engaging and intuitive. The grade is based on a couple small assignments, 4 exercises, a test, and a final. Both tests were take-home, so were not too stressful. Overall good class to take for ANTH or ARCH.

Prof Billman is a great and funny lecturer! He has powerpoints for wmost lectures (which he posts after class). He also shares his personal field work experience, and it's clear he loves archaeology. Workload was light: textbook readings, four open note assignments and a few in class participation discussions. Midterm/final are also open note!

Prof Billman makes almost every lecture very interesting, and while some lectures have required prep readings, they're pretty rare and spaced out in the semester. Recitation also meets infrequently and assigns manageable projects. Lectures can also move pretty quickly, but overall I loved this class!

Prof Billman is a good and really funny lecturer. Some topics are boring while others are really interesting. He teaches about different civilizations like a story, which makes it fun. The recitation work seems very disconnected from class but its not too bad. A lot of extra credit so show up to class! Overall, a really nice lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor who engages and cares about what he teaches, can be lost sometimes but is overall a very worthwhile experience if you're willing to put in the effort (for a gen-ed it may be difficult!!)

Brian Billman is incredibly funny and cares about his content. However, the tests were extremely hard, and you had to memorize every single small detail in the class. He was forgiving with a curve, but still, this was the hardest gen-ed class I've taken. Great guy, hard class.

Billman is hilarious and a great lecturer, however you really need to pay attention to lectures because the tests are pretty difficult. He did curve the first two exams and then gave an extra credit question for the final, so that really helped. The essays aren't terribly difficult especially if you attend recitation. Everything is graded by TAs.

I loved Professor Billman. He is very passionate about the material and overall wants you to understand. Lectures are hilarious, no homework other than studying, and just a few recitation meetings each semester. Tests are a bit difficult, but really easy if you pay attention. He also curves a lot! Would highly recommend.

Prof Billman is the best! He is so funny and so passionate about everything he teaches - it was super cool hearing about all the places he has travelled to. You need to attend lectures and do all the readings to do well on the essays and exams though, but the effort is definitely worth it.

Prof Billman is awesome! He's so funny and clearly cares a lot about what he teaches. The only major grades were 2 relatively simple essays and 3 exams which you will need to study for, but if you pay attention in lectures and review your notes you'll do okay. He also sends out a study guide for each exam & is willing to give a curve/extra credit.

Prof. Billman is the funniest professor I have ever had. He is a wonderful teacher and cares about his students. We had 2 essays and 3 tests. The tests were each worth 25% of our grade so it is really important to study for the test/ Professor Billman is very passionate about anthropology and makes the class interesting.
The professor is a great guy and funny. I thought the exams were difficult. Low workload except for studying for exams.

Incredibly slow grader. Doesn't stick to his own deadlines. Changes deadlines. 3 exams and 2 essay. Exams were incredibly difficult and way too specific. The "study guide" doesn't help. Lectures are boring and dry. Slides are mostly pictures. If you want WB credit, look for another class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ok heres the deal. This class is incredibly, Prof Billman is hilarious and a great professor, but it is HARD. Your grade is made up of 3 hard tests, that will kill u, and 2 fairly straight forward papers. However, the TA's try to help you out and hes willing to curve and give extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Grade consists of 3 HARD tests and 2 HARD essays. No homework, so workload is low until tests/papers. He is a hilarious professor, honestly only stayed in the class after I bombed the first test because he's so funny! He really is a great professor, but super old so doesn't believe in extra credit or open note exams (which they should be)

Billman is a phenomenal lecturer, but it can be hard to tell what material will actually be on the exam. I attended all the courses and took lots of notes, but it was definitely challenging. Grades come from TA and are 2 five-page papers and 3 exams. Very entertaining guy, but the material can be overwhelming or boring.

Professor Billman's exams were extremely specific. He tended to get off topic during lectures. His essay prompts were not well thought out. He changed the schedule several times, moving due dates sooner and uncanceling classes. The recitations for this class hardly ever met. There were a lot of readings every week. Grades took forever to come back.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Billman is so funny and loves to joke during lectures. But when it came to the exams, he made them way too specific and challenging & did not adequately prepare us for them. Only grades are 3 exams and 2 essays. All reviews I read last year said it was easy online due to COVID, but I think going back in person he made the exams WAY too hard.

Dr. Billman is awesome! Class attendance isn't *mandatory* per se, but you'll be missing out if you don't come. Mainly teaches by example and posts materials/slides on Sakai. Textbook is needed for some homework, but he posts the free PDF on Sakai. Easy credit, as long as you do the major HW assignments.

Professor Billman is great! I took this class with him during COVID and I honestly really enjoyed it. I'm not an anthropology major, nor do I think I will become one, but Professor Billman really makes his lectures interesting even on Zoom. His exams are take home, and the textbook reading is very reasonable. Highly recommend!!!

Professor Billman is such a nice guy!! Didn't have to be on Zoom as long as you watched the lecture and responded to a (pretty easy) question on Sakai within 24 hours or so. I ended up watching them on 2x speed instead the next day, but his sense of humor is so nice & he has really great stories about his adventures!!

Prof Billman is extremely knowledgable and hilarious. Your grade consists of participation questions every lecture that are most of time just your opinion, 3 recitation assignments, and 3 open note exams. The grading rubric can sometimes be a little unclear, but he is extremely accommodating. HIGHLY recommend this class.

Professor Billman's lectures can be a little hard to follow sometimes because his PowerPoints are mostly pictures, you really have to listen to what he says, and his train of thought can be slightly confusing. He's a really great dude, though, really cares about the subject material, is very accommodating and lenient, and is absolutely hilarious.

Professor Billman was a good professor, this class is good if you need to knock out a few gen eds and is best to be taken online. He changed the formatting of his tests and assignments to accommodate for remote learning which made the class much easier. The class tends to be very boring sometimes and he goes off topic a lot so pay attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Billman truly understands his students and is a very caring professor. He cracks so many jokes during class, so you will no doubt look forward to his lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I love this man. He is the best professor I have had. He's funny and quirky, so if you like very serious lecturers steer clear. I have recommended ANTH145 to friends and they have loved it too. Billman makes what could have been a boring subject into something wonderful.

Brian is a great professor. I took his ANTH145 course freshman year, and then later took some higher level courses and worked under him too. He's a bit disorganized and a bit odd, but he's approachable, intelligent, and cares about his job. He does ask that you are at least familiar with the readings, but is otherwise not too tough.

I have never been particularly interested in archaeology until I took this class with Billman. He has a lot of experience in the field so he can tell the class some funny stories. The exam is kind of difficult and I studied a lot for it, but the essays are graded very leniently. Attendance is taken every day in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Brian Billman is the goat. He is super passionate about the class and tells great stories. The exams are based entirely on his powerpoints and although he assigns reading, they are not required if you listen to his lectures. The powerpoints are mostly just pictures so you have to pay attention. Even with corona, he made his lectures interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Billman is the bomb. He's basically a real life Indiana Jones. Didn't think the anthropology of Andean South America could be made so interesting.

Professor Billman rocked. He incorporated jokes into his lectures, which would sometimes stray from topics. Two big papers are the only homework. Exams were pretty easy to do well on. If you need a gen ed or are a first year, ANTH145 with Dr Billman is a great choice.

Billman makes lectures interesting & humorous , but most of the time it's tempting to just doze off since it's a lecture-based class. Definitely take notes bc his slides don't have much information off them; if you do, the exams are generally straightforward. The papers were also fair & do-able within a week or couple of days if you procrastinate.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Billman is awesome and super funny and lectures were really interesting even though i hate history. I would definitely take him again, but you definitely need to study and show up to class to do well. and take good notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Favorite Professor at UNC! Super interesting lectures, and he is very funny. He doesn't assign too much work, and the tests are quite straightforward. Overall an easy class, with some hard to grasp subjects.

Dr. Billman is an amazing guy, he is very funny and his lectures are interesting. He has the tendency to go off on rants which can confuse things in lectures but they are usually easy to follow. He posts power points but they are not detailed enough to be able to skip lectures and pass. Tests are pretty straight forward.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I'm no genius but this class is very simple. MUST GO TO CLASS! The lectures teach the tests! No textbook to learn the material from. He takes into consideration the student and his GOAL is to distribute mostly A's & B's! If you show up to class, pay moderate attention, and study the night before the exam you're going to be successful!!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Billman is a really funny guy and a cool teacher. You'll learn a lot about him in his class but that's not bad thing. His lectures are easy to understand but he does rely heavily on powerpoint with only pictures and a little text, so make sure you're taking notes. Just show up to the class and pay attention and you'll be good!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I took his class last fall and I really did enjoy it. It was my first semester of college and I was surprised at how much I liked the class. He set up each lecture as a story of sorts, which I really liked. The exams are not very hard, if you go to class and take very good notes, that you memorize and understand you can do well!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Funny, super nice, and his story is inspiring and interesting (dropped out of college twice, traveled, and boom professor). You MUST go to class because you only have your notes to study from (no study guides or textbooks). Multiple choice is hard and won't get 100 on your short answers even if you know everything because the T.A.s grade them.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Great sense of humor keeps lectures interesting, although if you're not interested in archaeology or anthropology, the course might not be interesting to you. Exams are tougher than you'd expect- short answer and answers, so class attendance is a must. Great guy!

If you aren't super into Anthropology, don't take this class. Lectures are very boring and the exams are not easy, mostly because you only have your lecture notes to study from- so make sure to take good notes and pay attention during the lectures if you want to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Billman is great! His lectures are really interesting and his tests aren't crazy hard. He takes attendance even though it is a large lecture class. There is some reading which should be done because it shows up on the test. He cracks tells funny stories which makes it feel like less of a lecture. Tests, rec sec, and papers are your grade.

The lectures were very dry and included him talking for 75 min with pictures on the slides. Paying attention the whole time was almost impossible. The exams were very difficult, multiple choice with an essay question. The two recitation essays were not bad, they are what probably saved my grade. I would not recommend taking this class for a gen ed.

I like his personality, but he tends to go off on a rant during lecture. I also find it hard to pinpoint exactly what I should be focusing on while I study. Going to class is a must. He uploads his ppts, but they don't go into much detail and are mostly pictures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Billman makes a rather boring subject, interesting.... going into the class I was expecting it to be a rather dry, difficult topic, but his lecture style keeps you engaged. The lectures are VERY important however, as they comprise most of the exams... definitely recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Billman is super nice and a great professor. He gives really clear study guides for exams so they're easy A's. You have to come to class as attendance is part of your grade, but he's a great lecturer and a very good natured guy. If you need help, he'll give it to you. Do your assignments and you shouldn't have any problems.

Took this class expecting an easy and chill experience. Not the case at all. The lectures are long and boring and most of the time don't pertain to the course material at all. His sense of humor is bad and gets in the way of proper communication of the material. Takes forever to receive any graded work back. DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS.

Billman has got to be related to Bill Murray. They sound so much alike and have the same wacky, dry sense of humor. Lectures were entertaining, and the tests weren't too difficult if you study the test prep guide. I suggest utilizing a google doc with your classmates.  Love it when he brings his dog, July, to class. She's the sweetest.

The class was extremely dry and boring for me. Many things covered in lecture were never tested on. I relied on Google docs and going over the objectives to study for tests. The tests were moderately difficult, all free response, and sometimes required you to give years for when things happened (which I never managed to memorize).

Professor Billman is a great guy, but based on others rate my professors I went into this class hoping that it would be an easy A.  That is not the case.  The tests are all short answer and an essay, NO MULTIPLE CHOICE. And there is so much information that studying seems impossible.  Billman is hilarious and makes the lectures interesting though.

Makes a potentially dryboring topic very interesting. As long as you go to class, take decent notes and do most readings you will be fine. Very approachable if you have questions, you might be annoyed by his humor but I thought it was endearing. Made me want to take more ANTH classes in the future.
Great professor, manages to make even dull subject matter interesting. Funny and laid back teaching style with entertaining personal stories mixed in.

The best professor I've had at this college. He loves what he does, which makes the class fun and interesting. He's funny and shares stories, which help you remember the material and understand practical application. His black lab is adorable, too.

He's a great professor! He's really laid-back and managed to intertwine stories of his college/youth years into the lectures to keep us engaged and entertained. He makes lots of jokes and was a great way to end my day. I loved that his dog always came to class, too. Only complaints are MC questions and the outside reading book. Textbook "optional".

Good lecturer, interesting class. He's funny and tries to make even the dry material interesting. The readings are a bit arbitrary, but the textbook is helpful when writing papers. Tests are fairly easy if you know the objectives. Definitely take this class.
Very funny and engaging. I didn't fall asleep in his class once. He brings his dog, July, to class, and she goes everywhere with him. This class helped me decide to major in anthropology.
awesome guy and easy class. his dog comes to every class. tests are pretty easy but mc questions can be random. don't bother getting the textbook. you only ever use it for the essays. just borrow it.
Interesting class, but not easy...do not take this class just to fill a Gen. Ed. requirement.
My favorite teacher at UNC so far. Always made class really interesting and had a great sense of humor. Tests weren't that bad as long as you know the course objectives really well.

Billman is an excellent professor and really knows what he is talking about. His examinations are what cause people to do poorly because his multiple choice questions are unclear and rather arbitrary. The book is useless and I never used it, except fro random quotations in the 2 essays. If you like dogs, take his class, because he brings her!
Very interesting class! Lectures go into great detail, but are engaging. Tests contain somewhat random material from the lectures, but overall a pretty easy class.

The tests are fair if you have studied the objectives. The ONLY time I used the textbook was to extract some facts for the 2 essays. It takes forever to get exams and essays back, and the TAs really don't work very hard. Billman is extremely entertaining and knowledgable. He is passionate about his subject, but does tend to focus on the details.
Anth 145 is the best class I've taken so far at UNC (only had one year though). Tests were harder than I expected, but the papers weren't as bad in my opinion. Has a great sense of humor.

LOVED THIS CLASS. anyone who is interested or needs this credit take anth145. billman is the man. dont take lots of notes, but remember key dates/points. lectures keep you entertained. reading the book isnt super helpful, i only skimmed it.

He likes to talk. He'll tell you more than you need to know - pages of notes that won't be on the test, but you're not going to know that until you see the test so write everything down anyways (sites are important).  He doesn't push his TAs very hard so expect your grades late, say two to three weeks or so.  Otherwise a good class and prof.

Funny, engaging. Very Bill Murray-esque. Material is incredibly dull, concepts interesting but exams cover inconsequential details. The course, while ostensibly about world prehistory, finishes its chronology with the Spanish conquest of the Incas. Pretty misleading course description. It is often hard to stay awake through class.
He brings his dog to class. He's a great guy but I found the class to be dull. Also the tests were really obscure.
Brian Billman is amazing.  I would reccomend Anth 145 to anybody just because of him.  Sometimes it is kind of boring, but its a requirement, and its easy. take it with him.

Billman is awesome. Class isnt too hard, the final isnt cumulative, and the TAs were solid as well. Class was boring sometimes, but he obviously really cared about what he was teaching. Great class, I highly recommend. Learned a lot about our roots as humans and the primitive people we evolved from.

funny guy, brings his dog to class. kind of boring, but it is antropology.  not a lot of work, two 5 page papers. gives objectives that will be on the test.  picks out random things so its hard to make a great grade.

Not too hard of a class, DON'T read the textbook (it made me drowsy) but DO go to ALL classes.  His tests are straight from the objectives (he gives them to you) and ONLY the sites and dates he has mentioned in lecture. Two exams, two 5 page essays and a final exam.  Pretty funny guy.

Billman is the ONLY reason that Anth 45 is bearable...otherwise it's unbelievably dull, boring material. His humor makes lectures worth attending. A note on the class though--the tests are all memorization based, asking extremely minute and otherwise unimportant details about the most obscure of topics.

Prof. Billman makes the material for class interesting, and fun. He has a great sense of humor. The class is not that difficult, but it certianly helps if you show up for lecture and at least look over the readings.
Good class, interesting, prof has a good sense of humor.  Definately not that hard, as long as you go to class and do the reading
Awesome, hilarious guy, easy class
Funny guy, interesting and on topic lectures, very personable and likeable, highly reccomend the class.
No Comments
One of the best teachers i've had at Carolina. He's fun, entertaining, and very helpful. I would advise taking one of his classes. He's a great guy
This is an easy A, even our basketball players could pass this course, lol.
He's a great teacher with a good sense of humor, and I can even stay awake in all his classes-it's great!

Lucia is very kind and a great lecturer! I wasn't sure what to expect from this class but I ended up learning a lot, she made the material very interesting. As long as you participate thoughtfully, this is a wonderful class
Very unprofessional and disrespectful to students.

Very disorganized. No powerpoints. She does not use sakai. She assigns these LONG homework assignments the night before they are due. Her test was take home and took like 7-10 hours for no reason. Even when you pay attention you cannot understand her Spanish and IM FLUENT! Impossible to pay attention. 10/10 would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The queen. Taught an enjoyable class, which was slow and confusing at times, but is a nice grader. Would highly recommend this class and I am sure she is great for other classes as well.

She is by far the funniest person I have yet to take a class from. She makes me excited to come to class everyday and learn. The topics are definitely unique as all of them cover sex and relationships. If you take her you will adore her she is so funny and passionate about her work.

Binotti goes with the flow, willing to change assignments if students are busy, and also passionate about Spanish literature. Participation, a group project, 5 small papers, and a final paper made up the whole grade. She is very friendly; loves when students participate (20% of grade) and share their knowledge of the few required readings/tv shows
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: The professor is very unorganized. The homework is not clearly explained and the assignments are very vague. She will call on you frequently and will be condesending if you do not know the answer. Everything is done digitally and she doesnt even know how to work it. I would not recommend this course unless you are a native speaker.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Oi if you have the option to take Lucia's digital spanish 260 course TAKE IT. It is much easier than regular span 260 and a lot more laid back and fun. I thought it was an easy A;  the end of year project can be a little demanding but it's a fair balance because you don't have to do very much during the year. Also it's an EE credit :O

Very caring. Very knowledgeable, but way too monotone and disorganized in this course (she warns you on the syllabus). I wish I'd taken a different course with her, but for SPAN 682 it's a no from me.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: It's easy to get confused, but she is super nice so just ask for clarification! Her class was one of my favorites and Lucia is a great prof that you can have a lot of fun with and who really cares about her students!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Dr. Binotti is still my favorite professor and this class is still the best I've taken at UNC. It's kind of a unique and weird subject but she is hilarious and you have a lot of really interesting discussions. You do have to come to class but honestly you don't HAVE to participate and the papers are graded very fairly and easily.

Lectures were a bit all over the place, but in the end, all tied back to main class concepts. Guest lecturers were mostly interesting. Actually take notes in class, and then when you have to write the vague-ish papers, you can just regurgitate your notes. Pretty easy A, just come to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Binotti is a very energetic and fun person, but the lessons are a little random and you keep changing to different works and pieces. Always nice when guest speakers come. Pretty easy, and a great first year class, just a little boring at times.

If you can get past her disorganization you will do well. Assigns things last min or changes due dates. Very passionate about material and wants you to understand it. She tries to make it fun. Final grade based on a group project.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Binotti is so energetic and fun in her lectures that they aren't boring; however, you do need to show up in order to get a good grade. There is LOTS of reading for her class but honestly you don't have to read it all. The only grades are participation and the occasional paper, which she grades very fairly and they are based on the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This was a surprisingly entertaining seminar. I learned a lot where I didn't expect to. The grading and work is pretty easy, it's a few essays every now and then.

very understanding teacher and cares about connecting with his students. all he asks is that you participate in class because it is primarily discussion based. even if you don't know the answer he only asks that you try and say something. very easy class, tests fair, homework is always very easy. love professor birya he's so nice and such a king
raphael birya
w prof fr fr

Amazing professor, but I wished he had given better instructions for assignments mainly the final paper. He encourages everyone to participate in discussions read the articles and watch the videos.  He does give extra credit if you attend all his lectures and submit all your assignments!
I would love to eat BIRYAni with him.

Dr. Birya is a kind and interesting professor with great stories. However, grading guidelines are unclear and there are often confusing typos on exams. An A is a 95. Fair amount of dense readings. Usually there would be a 10+ page paper and textbook chapter to read for each class. Come to every class, as participation matters a lot for your grade!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Birya is awesome. He is very engaging yet isn't very tech savvy and some of his canvas/online instructions or rubrics can be hard to understand. A 95 is needed for an A but he gave multiple extra credit opportunities.

Such an annoying class if I'm being honest. When asked for information on the exam all his responses consist of are 'Do not worry' and 'You will be fine'. Provides a tremendous amount of reading and work for an introductory class. I do not recommend taking him as this class mainly just memorization. The exams wanted you to remember specific quotes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr Birya is one of the nicest people I've met. He really wants students to succeed in the classroom and in life. He gives great nuggets of life advice. However, his canvas site is very hard to navigate. It has info from past semesters and is just very confusing. His tests have some typos and ask super confusing questions

His grading expects too much for how his assignments are - takes off points for small grammar mistakes but has tons of grammar and confusing errors on tests (which are overly difficult). Offers EC and is a very nice man but the class has significantly more work than is necessary esp. for 100 lvl. I'd avoid if you can its not awful but not fun.

Dr. Birya is a very nice guy but the lectures and discussions were disorganized. Exam questions were confusing because they were full of sloppy grammar errors like random words cut off or random words added into the sentence. There are a lot of readings and assignments on top of exams and papers. The content is easy, class is just a lot of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The most disorganized professor I've ever had. I barely learned anything and can't even have the most basic conversations in the language. He is not tech savvy at all which ends up causing a lot of problems. He also doesn't have grading rubrics for any of the assignments or tests so you never know what he is looking for.

Worst professor I have had. Expected us to take an exam after he was out for 3 weeks and had only taught us one lecture prior to his leaving. He seemed to think it was funny when we had genuine questions about assignments. We never knew our grades, even after submitting an assignment at the beginning of the semester. Do not take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I really wanted to like this class, but it was such a mess. The canvas site was all over the place and hard to navigate. Most of the time students had no idea what was going on. His rubrics were unclear, grades were not well explained, and exams had spelling and grammar errors. On the day of the final most of our grades were still missing.

Accommodating with late work. Extremely disorganized. 70% of our graded material hasn't been put in and the final is in 3 days. I never know what is going on in this class. I feel like there is so much but I've absorbed nothing as I have no idea what's happening.
I never have any idea what's happening in this class.

He is a very kind professor who cares for his students. The main complaint I had about the class was his lack of technological knowledge. The canvas site was impossible to navigate, rubrics were unclear, grade was hard to calculate, tests had typos, and overall most students never really knew what was going on/what we were supposed to do.

I've taken SWAH 401 and 402 with Dk. Birya and he is the best and he truly cares for his students. While his lectures are typically unorganized, he does not penalize students for this, and creates a great community within his classes. If you have the chance to take a class with him, do it.

TAKE THIS CLASS. Dr. Birya is so kind and genuinely wants his students to learn Swahili. He grades easily and the class is more focused on learning than big quizzes and stress-inducing finals. He will work with the class and change due dates. 3 quizzes, 7 homework assignments, an oral midterm, and a written final are graded.

The sweetest professor ever, Dr. Birya really cares about his students and shows it in every lecture. He is definitely all over the place frequently, and is known to postpone quizzes because he forgets about them until the day before, but this class really submerges you into the language and teaches you a lot. Be ready to participate!

Mwalimu Birya is the kindest professor that I have come into contact with at UNC. He truly cares about his students and will do whatever he can to make their life a little bit easier. I have taken Swah 401, 402, and 403 with him and I wouldn't change a thing. He does use a textbook, but 401 and 402 use the same one. I def recommend Birya!

Professor Birya is VERY accessible outside of class, which is good because some grading rubrics are very vague - you will need clarification. He does genuinely care about his students. Subject matter was fairly easy and directly correlated to quizzes. You will get random points off for the most random things though.

Birya is a sweet man, but his class is not well organized with very vague assignment instructions. Exams are very easy, and he is a pretty lenient grader on papers and forums but can take off points for unspecified rules. . Participation is weighted heavily. The class content is simple, but he can be hard to communicate with. Still, an easy A.

Professor Birya is very sweet and he makes it clear that he cares about his students. With that being said, lectures were pretty unorganized and often ran over time. Tests were easy but be ready for short answer questions. His guidelines for assignments were often unclear but he is easy to get into contact with.

Birya is a very kind, understanding, and caring professor. The material is relatively easy; however, the assignment instructions are vague, and the grading criteria are unclear (you lose points for things that he didn't specify to include, like citations). Recommend asking questions for more clarity. Despite this, the class is still an easy A.

He was the kindest teacher I have ever had and really wanted the students to learn Swahili. But while some of his expectations are a bit hard to understand, I believe that if you study about 5-10 minutes a day, you should be fine. Assignments aren't too hard but go to office hours before you turn in anything so you can get the best grade possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Sweet kind man loves his students! Great entry level class. vague instructions for finals and assignments, and marks down for debatably fine content in work. If you like structure wouldn't recommend. Very enthusiastic and enjoyed class which was inspiring. Great stories
Birya cares so much about his students and wants them to succeed. Lenient grader and very funny. A little disorganized.
Prof Birya is the sweetest man!! He is passionate about his studies and makes class interesting!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: You cannot go wrong with this professor. I have taken several classes with Dr. Birya and have not had one bad experience. Be prepared to get randomly called on in class though!
Cares a lot about you, a little disorganized if that bothers you

Great Professor overall! He respects and genuinely cares for all students. I was able to get a good grade in the class without any stress throughout the entire semester. If you are considering taking this class, he is undoubtedly the best choice!

Dr. Birya was the sweetest professor that I've ever had. He's not the best with technology, but he's always willing to accommodate to make up for it. He's so incredibly caring and does his best to keep the class engaging. I would recommend him to anyone. As long as you follow along with the PowerPoints and skim the readings, you'll do great!

Professor Birya was my favorite professor this semester. Even though we had class online he was still able to make it interesting and engaging and he motivated us to participate. He was very understanding as well which I really appreciated. He also graded things very easily.

He's not perfect, but nobody is. He is a little bit slow with technology, can be a little unclear with questions in quizzes and exact expectations with assignments, but he cares so much. He'll bend over backwards for us, extending deadlines and helping any way he can for his students if you ask. Pay attention in class, and you'll do just fine.

The content of the class was pretty easy but he's such a bad teacher it made it more difficult. Genuinely learned more from the TAs.
He is a nice guy, and grades pretty fairly, and he added a pretty big curve at the end though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Gary is a VERY nice guy. However, he taught us like we were phD students and I took nothing away from this class. All lectures were power points and there was 0 practice(besides extra textbook questions which were unhelpful). Help in the aide center was not helpful in any way either. If you want to learn 410 or even get a good grade, do NOT take.

Funny and knowledgeable guy indeed, but a bad professor. He literally taught us the same way he taught his phd students, you can't understand anything from his lecture. Do yourself a favor and take msa's econ 410 plz.

Very tough class. Tests make up 90% of the overall grade.

The homework was barely useful and the lectures were hard to follow.

The professor lied about adding curves and completely changed how he weighted the exams in the last few weeks. Also, I did not see a single grade posted until the final grade was posted in ConnectCarolina.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor. Pretty funny guy. The exams are not too difficult but the grading is ROUGH. Believe this is partly from the TA who pretty much took over the class when it comes to grades. Class averages on exams were usually in the mid 60s, and the curve was around 3 points. Would have been a much better class if there was a different TA.

Great guy, bad teacher. Very disorganized slides, few examples, mostly explained math but not how to apply it, still you had to go to class or you'd be completely lost (attendance not mandatory). HW assignments are only worth 10% but very long and only 1 problem picked at random is graded. 90% of grade is exams. Very arrogant TA, as clueless as us.

Gary is a very knowledgeable and smart individual who greatly struggles to convey information to his students. Lectures consist of him yapping in doctorate level terms about concepts that he introduced 30 seconds ago. Reads directly from poorly designed powerpoint slides. In class examples (of which there are few) and HW's do not translate to exams
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Absolutely terrible professor especially for such a challenging class like Econ 410. Get ready to self-teach yourself everything in this class because the slides and his lectures are absolutely useless. The 3 exams made up 90% of your entire grade.

Jawn was a grind, bank on riding the curve. Slides were never useful (majority of class). If he does a problem on the board though, it might be on an exam. Useful things: recitation, finding book answers online for hw problems and learning from those, old exams, review sessions. Dude also definitely has adhd

I really do not understand why so many people write awful comments about Professor Biglaiser. Microeconomics is such an awesome field that he has the mastery on. The lectures were inspirational  to the point that I was enthusiastic ( as a freshman) to go to the office hours and talked about microeconomic concepts. 
He is also a very funny guy !

Gary teaches the class as an honors class, uses poorly developed slides, and threatens to beat us with a stick. Homework accounts for 10% of your grade. The TAs do not understand the assignments/problems,the homework is completely irrelevant to the exams. The TAs would say "I do not expect any of you to get this right, I barely understand it."

This guy is a threat to teaching. In fact , there is no teaching only very disorganized slides as well as one bad TA that is arrogant (hashem amireh).I had to self teach myself everything and he gives the honors version to normal ECON410. Furthermore, multiple students have threatened to commit suicide since 30 % of the class is failing.

Gary is a terrible professor. He is nice enough, but his class is extremely disorganized and he makes it way harder than it needs to be. The homeworks take hours and are basically completely irrelevant to the content of exams. The TA's are also disrespectful, which is a shame because recitation is the only time you do problems similar to exams

Worst class I've taken at UNC. I'm a math and econ major and found Calc 3, Linear Algebra, and Discrete Math all easier than this class. Horrible at explaining concepts, does practically no practice problems in class. do yourself a favor and AVOID.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Biglaiser is a great professor for Econ410H. He moves fast but is always willing to work with students on specific concepts they don't understand. He is also very generous with his curve so as long as you pay attention and do the assigned practice you should be ok. Hard class, but I learned a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class is entirely taught by lectures, so if you miss classes you will miss the material. Your grade almost entirely comes from midterms and finals, but they are graded generously. Feels like a typical upper-level class (based on my understanding as a freshman), with small class sizes and a teacher that knows if you understand the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Biglaiser is a great professor. He will spend as much time as needed on any topic as long as a student is wiling to ask and is very passionate about microeconomic theory. Students with a poor attention span should stay away from this course - he is a little dry but very informative and thorough.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The professor is smart, but he's terrible at conveying the ideas to his students. He has an arrogant attitude and doesn't provide enough resources for his students. reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I heard a lot of complaints about the class before I took him, which surprises me in hindsight because I didn't have any problems with him. He explained the material well, answered questions well, had simulations and review sessions after class for students, and was a fair grader. Decent class, relatively exams. Says "suppose" a lot.

Codey is amazing. He's so funny and very easygoing. He is happy to help and meet after class anytime. For the COMM 113 speeches specifically, he's a tough grader, but if you put in the effort and show you care you will do fine.

Codey is great. The issue is the formatting of this class. There are only so many assignments so your grade is a reflection of how harshly you are graded on the final assignments which are worth a majority of your grade. Codey is helpful and teaches the class material well. He is hilarious and makes the class go smoothly. Harsh grader, though.

He was so laid back and funny and really made the class easily passable. If you show up most of the time you'll do fine on participation, the only downside was that it was only graded by 3 papers and the midterm and final.

Codey was a really caring and personable professor but there was never a moment where I could fully follow his train of thought and what he was saying. He was just so scatter brained that it was nearly impossible to follow the content of the class

Codey Bills aka the most amazing and funny teacher ever. He is relatable and real and we literally do no work. That can make the couple papers and midterm harder, but at the same time if you just put in effort and try you're set.

The class isn't super structured but I learned a lot! The entire class is basically reading and working on a final paper, so it's pretty low stakes as long as you put in the work. He's really funny and a good choice for a COMM professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: he was my TA for COMM120, definitely chillest of the TAs. gave us 100s just for turning most things in and wasn't nitpicky about other grading. usually late and sometimes cancels recitation, funny guy and doesn't expect you to be overly prepared (because he definitely isn't!) sweet guy

He's a real gem in the communications department. He is very knowledgeable on the topics he teaches and makes very abstract concepts easy to understand using references and lingo that students use. He is happy to explain any topic multiple times until it sticks. His anecdotes are always random but funny and do not drag on.

Great guy and very approachable. He made everyone feel as comfortable as possible when speaking. Gave back detailed feedback and was very encouraging. He is kindhearted and understanding. I would definitely recommend if you want to get an easy A with a kind and constructive professor.
Difficult class but overall 10/10, would take again

Have not seen Professor Birdsong in awhile and I hope they're okay. His lectures were entertaining and provided me with how not to be as a human being. I really wish I knew what their pronouns were so I could correctly address them. I was enlightened by Gary to stop eating Frosted Flakes because they promote premarital intercourse. Thank you Gary.

As a woman, Prof. Gary Birdsong made me realize that I am much too ambitious and strong-willed for my own good. Prof Birdsong is great. His lectures are based solely on the text and the tests are quote-based. I learned so much from him about how the world should actually be. Gary Birdsong provides interesting new perspectives and is extremely accessible outside of class. Gary loves lecturing outside, so it's always nice to get some fresh air when learning. Gary Birdsong is an amazing speaker, who teaches how Jesus is the way, the truth, the life,& the only way to God. I'm still inspired by his passion for sharing the hope we have n Jesus Christ!
I was a lesbian before taking this class. While taking the class, I realized my true calling and dropped out to become a heterosexual housewife. No way am I going to Hell. Thank you, Gary.
Best professor at UNC by far. Really passionate, knowledgeable and experienced.

Professor Birdsong is really open to different perspectives and is willing to listen to anybody. Without him, I do not know if I could graduate from UNC. 10/10 would recommend. His patience and open-mindedness inspire me.
No need to buy the book- he basically misquotes it the entire semester :-/ very enthusiastic but overall not worth ever listening to
Does a lot of lecture, kind of scatterbrained, doesnt always answer your questions but his lectures are really engaging

Prof Birdsong is easily one of the most passionate people on campus. Half the time I don't think even he knows what he is talking about. I'm also pretty sure that he wrote the textbook because he seems to know it almost word for word, or he says he does.
