Andrea is alright; no more, no less. Similar to my experience with her MUSC 120, we learned absolute nonsense the whole semester. We basically studied music through unguided interpretation. Andrea has a knack for calling on students but not really caring for their responses & for giving unclear essay criteria, but overall this class is an easy A.

Andrea is fantastic. I would happily take another class with her. I would also give her a 5 if this class wasn't pure fluff. This is more beneficial than music history? The curriculum is disjointed nonsense and the final project was a show and tell of everyone's musical interests. I think music conservatories would laugh if they observed MUSC270.

Andrea is great, I've loved her in every class I've taken with her. Unsure about the other review for 270 -- this class was totally fair and each assignment's instructions took you through baby steps to complete. Lectures were diverse and required critical thinking. Being the first semester of this course, some bumps in the road were to be expected

Course was very badly structured and not well taught. Assignments lacked guidelines and grading was tough considering how vague the instructions were. Lectures were incredibly tedious on topics that were totally unrelated. Bohlman was completely useless when you asked for help, and gave feedback that resulted in bad grades. Do not take.

Music 120 was an interesting class to be sure, it would be hard for me to summarize exactly what we learned as it was a bit all over the place. Lacking in structure. HOWEVER Professor Bohlman was fantastic. She took the time to be personable, tried to get to know each of her students and was open to differing opinions.

MUSC 120 was a frustratingly disorganized class but this was much more due to the curriculum than the instructor-- Bohlman did her best to teach us useful material and some classes were very enjoyable. Participate & put some time into bigger assignments and you can get an A. Take advantage of her office hours to get to know her outside of class!
This class was so easy. I took it for my VP credit. As long as you did the participation assignments & the unit assignments, you'll do well in the class. Definitely recommend :)

Literally SOOO easy. If you submit the assignments you'll get an A; I'm not exaggerating. And, the class is super interesting; you get to learn about gender topics, drag, and sexualities, while listening to music. We even got to bring in Polish students studying gender studies, which was super interesting. Take this class.
Very nice and sweet and probably the easiest class I've taken at Carolina. Literally all you have to do is turn in the assignments and you'll get a 100 in the class

My favorite professor at UNC. Uses discussion-based class to engage everyone in the class. Very welcoming and understanding. Took me out of my comfort zone in a good way. Had her for 291 as well, which had a different class structure, but still great lectures. Incredibly caring, and challenged my perception of music as a violinist. Highly recommend
Dr. Bohlman is a good professor. However, her quizzes are near-impossible to do well on. If you don't have any experience in music theory, it makes it even harder.
literally just turn in ur work and you'll get an A

The easiest class I've taken at UNC. Never did a single reading and could sit through lectures and do other work if I needed to. One class we literally listened to ocean sounds and she laid on the floor. So chill and easy, a few essays that I could crank in a few hours. She's super caring and extended quizzes for me. Take this for your VP gen-ed!
This is definitely not an Easy A/ GPA booster class. Lectures were unprepared and unorganized
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She's really chill and nice. I didn't find the class too interesting and actually wish she would lecture more (crazy to say I know but you'll understand what I mean). She's clearly really smart, it's just the classes can get boring since there's such a lack of structure.

Prof Bohlman is genuinely a good person. She cares about her students and is there to support you if you need. 355 is one of those classes where you can hear a bunch of different opinions and widen your perspectives even if the material is a bit out-there sometimes. Definitely a great way to get capstone credit class for a music major.

Andrea is a good professor, but the material is often disengaging. MUSC 291 is easy but boringthere's not much material to discuss. There are several rather difficult quizzes throughout the class, but she mitigates them with extra credit opportunities. There's no midterm and an insignificant final.

Andrea was a really nice teacher and the class was super chill. Only had a few papers and blog assignments but was graded based on effort. By far one of the laid back classes I've taken but really fun!

The most disorganized professor I've ever had. Already have had multiple assignments with due dates that weren't properly communicated or adjusted, even though she said they'd be moved. She's super entertaining, caring, and a fun person, but for someone teaching business communications, you'd think she would communicate more.

I honestly did not know how to rate Dr. Boyer; she's an incredible person who deeply cares for her students and is extremely reasonable. However, she is disorganized and often very behind in getting back grades to students, and in this particular class, grades are very harshly-like all other 401 professors. I would recommend taking it with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's funny and makes classes engaging. Hard to get an A, her grading criteria is very unclear at times and the feedback is not great either - sometimes even contradictory. 401 kinda sucks in general, so among the options I think she's one of the best to at least have a fun time. Just accept you will prob get an A- even if you try really hard.

Despite her slightly disorganized nature, this is the second course I have taken with Dr. Boyer. Her grading criteria is unclear and assignment deadlines and metrics often are changed, but she is truly hilarious and a caring professor. If you are looking for a laugh and a genuine connection, and are willing to work with her, take the class!

Boyer's cool and a great lecturer who made class engaging. That being said, she is so nitpicky when it comes to grading. You can clearly do everything on the rubric but she'll take off ten points for no reason. I guess that's just 401. Also all her assignments are written/graded by AI which is pretty annoying since it leads to unclear guidelines.

Difficult to get an A, A- didn't require much effort, but that's honestly just BUSI 401. Discussion based class with lots of small group work and in-class activities that aren't graded. Assignments were applicable and didn't take too long. They're graded harshly, but again that's just 401. Interesting lecturer, and I actually enjoyed going to class

Fun class but disorganized and expectations are unclear. Assignment guidelines would change right before they were due which caused a lot of time to be wasted. Finished the mod a couple weeks ago and still haven't gotten any grades back. Seems like one of the easier electives though in terms of workload.
Impossible to get an A, also incredibly unresponsive to emails or feedback
SUPER hard grader, impossible to get an A in this class. Seems to be the same with all professors though. She was funny and each class was interesting. She did not provide clear rubrics or criteria.

She's really nice, but wow is she a harsh grader. This is an email writing and presentation class, and she will nitpick you on the smallest things. Honestly though, no 401 professor will hand out A's, so go ahead and take her.

Lori has a super over the top personality. She makes class fun and engaging. She does grade things tough but all the assignments were super easy so if you put a little bit of effort in you are guaranteed a B. Be prepared for class to be a big group discussion every day.

Professor Boyer is a very engaging and funny lecturer but as other people have said her grading is needlessly harsh. Her harsh grading made this class more stressful and difficult than it needed to be when looking at the actual subject matter. Good person, bad pedagogy.

This is the first teacher throughout my time at UNC I would 100% not recommend to any student. I'm certain Professor Boyer is a wonderful woman outside of academics, but I can't appreciate her grading. It takes weeks for her to give feedback and when I tried speaking with her about the criteria, she was always unwilling or unresponsive.

Dr. Boyer was hard to reach outside of class, but she was a very easy grader and the material was interesting. She cold calls a lot to facilitate discussion in the beginning of the semester. One discussion post, 2 presentations, a midterm, and an easy final assignment.

Professor Boyer is super nice and caring and can be really fun in class, but she is the absolute worst about grading criteria and giving back grades. The grades seem arbitrary with little feedback and they aren't given back for months. I didn't know my grade for this class until over 2 weeks after the class ended, and we didn't even have a final.

Grading is awful. She assigns so much busy work and then grades harshly. Takes forever to give feedback on assignments and will find the tiniest issues even if you followed the rubric closely. On projects she gave everyone the same grade. At times it felt like she had unrealistic expectations while simultaneously treating us like children.

You will breeze through this class all semester until the end. She gives everyone the same grade on everything until after evaluations are due. She went through and changed all my grades. I thought I was chilling, but then found out I was not. Harsh grader and unforgiving for mistakes. Seems like a cool person but will screw you over for no reason
Professor Boyer is a nice person, but she is unforgiving and a harsh grader. I would recommend taking BUSI 401 with someone else if you want a good grade.

Professor Boyer's only weakness is her lack of communication which is odd given that this is a communications class. He class is fun, and there is usually no homework but she will grade you harshly for things she never taught you.
She extremely energetic and fun loving, only downside is that she is a tough grader. But 401 has a bunch of filler assignments which helps you get a good grade. Would definitely take her.

Professor Boyer is really sweet, but a deceivingly hard grader for no reason. I think that BUSI401 should be pretty easy, but she takes off for the smallest of things and turns an easy class into a hard on for no needed reason. I would try taking another teacher for 401 to get a better grade
Attendance is graded; just come and listen. Only 1 essay is graded at the end of the course. Gives you directions for every paragraph that needs to be on there.

Dr. Greg is great, I heavily recommend this class for anyone even slightly interested in public health! We just met once a week briefly on zoom with mandatory attendance, but Dr. Greg is very understanding and offers alternative options if something comes up for you. The only grade is the final paper and he wasn't a tough grader at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: super chill class. once a week class online and attendance was mandatory. had to have camera on. only assignment was a 800 word paper. learned a lot about how to get a health career.
Love Dr. Greg! Great class if you're pre-med or pre-nutrition. Mandatory attendance on Zoom once a week and class ends spring break. One 1000 word paper is the only assignment.
Dr. Greg is a really cool guy and this class with him was both extremely easy and enjoyable
Had a great time listening to all the lecturers come in and talk about their studies!

Your grade in the course consists of attendance and a final paper. The class is what you make it: if you are passionate about public health and interact with a guest speakers, you will probably get more out of the class. It's pretty easy to get an A, just show up and write a paper.
Greg is awesome, classes are super interesting, easy A and very informative if you're interested in behavioral health or public health in general.

I have no interest in Public Health but took this class because I needed one more hour to graduate. It ended up being really interesting! You do have to attend class with your camera on, but the lectures are engaging. I would recommend it (especially if you are actually interested in Public Health).

Dr. Greg is AWESOME! He really took his time with researching and reaching out to the guest lecturers, as they were super interesting. He's always willing to answer questions and genuinely makes an effort with his students. Wishing I could've taken this class in-person, but I appreciate the gesture of offering it online for more people to take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Bocchino did a great job with SPHG 101! The guest lecturers and the different degrees he highlighted were a wonderful introduction to the world of pubilc health. This is interesting pass/fail, 1 credit course, so I would definitely recommend it for pre-med/pre-health students. You do one final paper at the end.
Greg really cares about helping his students. The guest lecturers have a lot to share. You can learn a lot from this class if you pay attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Bocchino was definitely the best professor I've had at UNC this far. His class is very chill as your whole grade is made up of attendance and your final paper. Very interesting content wise and you learn a lot from the guest speakers. I would definitely recommend this class

This class that introduces you to every public health field out there. It is a pass/fail class with only one essay due at the end of the semester. The guest speakers would each come one per week to talk about their specialty and answer any burning questions you have on career choices. Dr. Bocchino is a great resource for future Grad level planning.

Dr. Booth is truly an amazing professor and human. You get out of her course exactly what you put into it. She is a lecturer who challenges you to think and especially encourages discussion, so get ready to talk.This is a collaborative learning class, so group and individual participation is ESSENTIAL. She is also WONDERFUL in office hours.

This was an amazing class! Prof B did a great job at explaining the main components of reproductive justice and she created a good environment for meaningful discussion. There is a semester long project but it was broken down into check points with feedback along the way.

Prof B. is a great professor! She is very knowledgeable and is able to teach a wide variety of topics. This is a survey course so there is a lot of material to go over but Professor Booth does a great job at explaining the nuances of all of them. There is a semester long research project but it broken up into manageable segments with feedback.

The class has assigned reading assignments followed up by in class discussion and pop quizzes. Talking with other students definitely helps with better understanding different experiences in the community. Overall I think this class is definitely worthwhile!

I was worried to take a class with Prof B due to her poor rating but I found her class pleasant. She can be a bit old school but I feel her class is accessible to disabled students and she's incredibly understanding. I also felt the class material and assignments were understandable/doable. Prof Booth is also a good resource for WGST majors.

I've taken and enjoyed two classes with Booth. This class emphasizes participation b/c it is a discussion-based class. Yes, Prof. Booth talks a lot, but I think she is insightful. Frankly, those who do poorly don't pay attention, do the readings, or engage with her. If you just engage in class, I believe she is a fair grader and you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Idk why there are so many bad ratings. Everyone who actually tried/cared about the class seemed to do really well. There were some that just didn't put effort in and I'm assuming they're the ones rating her. She's genuinely the sweetest professor I've ever had. She's so understanding and will work with you if you go to office hours.

IGNORE THE POOR RATINGS. They were in my class and literally didn't put effort into it/care abt it at all. They're just offended their grade actually reflected the quality of their work lol. Prof B is the sweetest. If you actually care abt social justice and you try in class, you'll be golden. Unfortunately those who liked the class didn't rate her

I highly recommend taking this class with professor booth. She is so knowledgeable of reproductive care around the world and you will learn a great amount in this class. This is the second class I have taken with her, and I will be looking for more classes to take with her in the future.

Professor booth is an amazing professor and I loved having multiple classes with her. I have taken 2 classes with her now and loved both of them. She is extremely caring for every student in her class and is very knowledgeable of every topic she teaches. She is an amazing person and I will be looking for classes to take with her in the future.

I was hesitant to enroll because of the ratings, but I'm so so glad I took her class. Professor Booth is kind, knowledgeable, and truly cares about her students. Discussions are open and respectful, and different opinions are welcomed. I would absolutely take another class with this amazing professor!!!

Do not let the other reviews lie to you. Professor Booth is extremely knowledgeable, down-to-earth, open-minded, and caring. Grading rubrics are somewhat tedious, but mundane compared to what college students should realistically be expected of. The class is quite elementary. Readings are simple and straightforward, as are class assignments. 10/10.

This was the first time that she taught the class. For the final, it is a research project and presentation, and the rubric was very unclear of what she wants and when you ask questions she doesn't give a solid answer. There were a lot of pre-class readings that were being discussed about during class, which participation mattered a lot.

unclear grading criteria and was late/disorganized with many assignments and their rubrics, cared about the class as a whole but made some portions unnecessarily difficult. research project was main part of grade

Solid class, but instruction was just plain boring sometimes. Dr. Booth has a very interesting collection of  personal research and ideas that reflects in this class, but she is not very engaging. Would take again tho. Maybe WGST388 is better since it directly relates to her field? All my papers and exams were graded fairly by the TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are long and boring. She was constantly late releasing rubrics for the final paper. She changed the rubric for the last paper, the day before Thanksgiving break to include more sources, which was due the day after we got back. She only calls on a few students that she knows will agree with her even if others have their hands up.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is very opinionated and her thinking is the only way of thinking. Very simple class but the professor does not do it justice for the materials since she wants to project only her opinions and not hear anyone elses.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures were boring sometimes, but not terrible. TAs graded all assignments. We had a semester-long paper to write in multiple steps, one campus engagement assignment, and a midterm and final. Not a difficult class, but felt tedious at times. In-class discussions were very interesting, and I learned a lot.

- Extremely tough grader. If you don't say exactly what she wants, how you want, as if she wrote it herself, you will not get a good grade
- Not good a critiquing things. She has quoted my work and criticized the quotes... except.. the quotes she used to criticize and explain why my grade was bad were quotes I NEVER USED IN MY ASSIGNMENTS EVER. So
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Booth is an incredible professor, super kind and supportive, especially of students go to her office hours. A lot of people take the classing expect it to be easy, but it is pretty integral that you do the readings and participate. She has a tendency to go on tangents, but she explicitly highlights main takeaways. Not hard to do well.

All you do is sit in a circle and discuss the readings, and all she does is shut down conversation and make people feel like they said something "wrong." by halfway through the semester we all just sat in a silent, tense circle because everyone was too afraid to talk. Really interesting readings though, I did learn a lot from them.

STEM senior here. okay yes, she is probably the worst professor I have ever had at UNC. yes, she is probably the worst grader I have ever had. yes, she's probably the worst lecturer I have ever had. however, if you don't really care about your GPA, she's alright. she's also nice in office hours
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I did do well in this course, but unfortunately I would not recommend it with Prof. Booth. Grading criteria was not specifically stated, feedback was harsh, and the assignments were not necessarily clear.

This teacher will only respond to your emails when she wants to and will wait several days to only state you need to discuss the concerns in person. Additionally, she does not follow her syllabus to the detriment of your grade. I was given an 85 on a completion graded assignment: complete (95), partially complete (75), and incomplete (0)

DON'T TAKE A CLASS WITH THIS PROFESSOR!! I cannot express how AWFUL she is; there is no clear rubric for anything, she gives extremely harsh and unhelpful feedback, and changes her mind on how she is grading papers with no warning, explanation, or rationale. As a WGST major, she has made me rethink that given I will inevitably have her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She eats college student's dreams for breakfast. Would have changed major/minor if i knew it would be this bad. Cant understand most of what she says. Subjective grading. Forces her ideas onto you. passive aggressive. Cried more times than I can count. Left all important work for last 3wks. Adds new/graded assignments w/10days left in semester. RUN

This teacher is such a harsh grader and I swear that I can never do anything right. I am trying to take her feedback but it is so convoluted, confusing, and unhelpful. I am exhausted and near tears often over how frustrating it is to try and do well in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: We're 6 weeks into class and I've already cried about this class more than once. She's worse than I expected, so unreasonable, and the class is absolutely useless.

I normally lend caution to RMP ratings- but don't take Prof Booth if you don't have to for your major/minor. She's exclusionary, isn't' clear on grading criteria, announces large syllabus shifts at random, and is not flexible or understanding to student's experiences. Listen to the previous RMP posts, they're right.

Do not take this class or any class with Professor Booth. She has an insane attendance policy. I missed a few classes due to illness and mental health. When I emailed her to explain she never responded or even acknowledged that she received my email. She tends to ramble and will take points off if your response isn't exactly what she's looking for.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Most of the material covered solely focused on the experiences of women. MSM, men of color, and even nonbinary individuals faced sexual and reproductive injustices yet weren't discussed in this class. To me, this class was focused on the white feminist movement. There should've been more discussion on all who suffered from these injustices.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Do not take a class with her if you can avoid it. Has an insane attendance policy. Is a very harsh grader on writing assignments (most assignments are writing assignments) and isn't clear on what she wants from your writing to begin with. Doesn't want to hear any opinion that is different than her own. Bad at using technology. DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Participation is pretty much the entire class, there are few lectures and everything is discussion based. She is very picky about terms/phrasing when you speak and it can get grating. Tends to assume you mean the worst instead of the best when you explain something. No rubrics for anything and inconsistent instructions for assignments and papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: If you are a man, do not choose Booth. It is nearly impossible for Booth to consider you a feminist if you are a man. I will admit that her feedback to students is extensive and that is a really great quality of any professor. However, I feel I have regressed in my gender studies major since having her as a professor. Simply do not take her, ever.

Karen Booth is awful at explaining things. We had an assignment with three different syllabi, all of which had different instructions. She'll give you a zero on an assignment if it isn't done exactly the way she wants it. She makes up assignments and tells us about them the day before they're due. Do yourself a favor and never take this class.
DON'T TAKE HER CLASS

don't take this class or anything by this professor. she never gave any clear instruction, changed the type of instruction constantly, and expected doctoral-level contribution to the discussion. she also always expected one type of answer and was disrespectful to anyone who said anything else, even if it was positive. her grading scale was wack.

Very unclear instructions when assigning work yet grades very harshly. Makes comments like "I bet none of you want to be here" when people don't answer her discussion questions. Extremely outdated course material. Classroom environment really does not feel like a safe place to answer questions incorrectly and that's why no one talks. DONT RECOMMEND
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: asynchronous lecture and synchronous recitation didn't really give us a chance to absorb any information. no preparation for what was required on the midterm and final. Participation was graded in recitation, one group project a semester and weekly quizzes. if you didn't agree with her opinion you were wrong, avoid her if you can

Honestly while I found WGST 101 informative and not hard, it felt very white-feminist and a little too #girlboss, but that might just be the department as a whole. Go take a class that focuses on women in another department, like the African American Studies department or Religious Studies - you'll get a lot more out of it!

Honestly didn't interact with Prof. Booth since my class was asynchronous. The material was interesting and the work was pretty easy. Show up to and participate in recitation and do the reading quizzes and lecture assignments and you'll be fine.
Midterm and final exam were incredibly complicated for a simple 101 class.

Prof. Booth is kind, but she definitely sometimes fishes for answers (in class and on papers), which can make it difficult to get things right. The class isnt always super organized, but we have some good discussions. If youre just interested in WGST in general, I would recommend a different course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Her standards are very high and the course is difficult. She has very specific criteria and expectations, but if you pay close attention to her feedback and use her critiques she'll notice!

I liked WGST 101. I did not like Prof Booth, super unclear and unorganized. Made it super frustrating to try to get things done on time because she would never post lectures until hours after they were due. Weekly quizes were due before "class" even started (even though she posted things late.) Bad with technology and frequently blamed students.

Professor Booth is very knowledgeable and passionate about the subject. She does have very specific standards for assignments which can be challenging, but if you do the readings and assignments you should do well in the course. She also seemed pretty understanding of students' needs and wanted people to do well and learn in the course.

Prof Booth is very knowledgeable about the material in this class, but is not open-minded enough when it comes to others responses. If you don't respond to a prompt exactly how she thinks it should be answered you will not do well. I did great on the mc quizzes, but the exams DESTROYED my grade. She's very nice but this class is not an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The worst professor I have ever had at UNC. This class in so difficult for no reason. The course material is interesting but the grading is so subjective and assignments have no clear grading outline. Also, every assignment has the most vague instructions. Overall, it seems as though she didn't want to teach this class.

In a glass about sexuality, she only mentioned trans people once, she refused to take any criticism from students and would constantly change deadlines. There was no consistency with almost any assignments, and grading is too subjective without clear guidelines. Refused to acknowledge students' analysis that varies from her own.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Do not take a class with Karen. She has impossibly high standards for participation, and her grading is incredibly subjective. She WILL give you a bad grade if she doesn't like you. These "subjective" grades make up 80% of your total grade. You can participate everyday and still get an 80% for participation for no reason. Such a subjective grader!

Do not take a class with Dr. Booth. She is unorganized, has very inconsistent and random deadlines ex. 4:15, and unclear grading policies. She randomly canceled class and added assignments at the last minute. This would not be such an issue but she was inconsiderate of student's needs, even if there were issues with tech or health (in a pandemic).

DO NOT TAKE A CLASS WITH KAREN BOOTH!!!! I have taken a class previously with her and thought I could manage another one but boy was I wrong. She is so disorganized and her lectures do not make sense. All we do is read and go into breakout groups, The material is interesting but she ruins the class for me. I dread going to this class every week.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: It was my least favorite class I took at UNC, mainly because of her teaching style. I agree with the comments here that she has a very subjective tone, and I'm afraid her grading of the essay-based final exams weren't much different. Makes one wonder whether it is possible to ever be properly prepared for this class. Try taking another prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I can't explain how much I disliked this class in 300 characters. Professor Booth lectures on her opinions and acts like they're fact. The readings are unnecessary and the recitations are boring. I am a feminist, but I'm also a Christian and some of the things Ms. Booth said felt like attacks (traditional marriage is stupid). Don't take this class.

If you aren't super passionate about feminism, do not take this class. Half of the subject matter is common sense, or it is so stupid that it will straight up ignore you. The lectures are extremely boring, she is so repetitive, and kind of scatterbrained. She is also technologically inept, which is annoying. She's nice though.

Karen is a good teacher, and the readings are interesting. You have to write either a 500 or 800 word response before every class, but if you do them, you should get a good grade. The midterm was a take-home online exam. If you write your responses/essays to agree with her point of view, you'll do well. Speak once per class.

Do not take this class. Dr. Booth uses lectures not to challenge students, but to find students who validate her own world view. The course does have very interesting readings, but you can do them in your free time. She is also incredibly trans-exclusive and has disorganized lectures. She is not willing to explain confusing course assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Booth is very passionate. She is a great teacher, as she puts a lot of effort into making class time engaging and worthwhile. The books we read for class were fascinating and not too difficult; the class's workload as a whole is very manageable. However, Dr. Booth does not give very clear assignment guidelines and can be a bit disorganized.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: She does search for the right answer out of students and is looking for a specific wording on exams. I felt like I had a clear understanding of all work and assignments but still received lower than par grades. You must put things in her words or you won't receive the grades you are looking for.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: I would seriously recommend you do not take this class. Ms. Booth spent a lot of time silencing students who challenged her in lecture, and then subsequently denied doing it. The class requires far too much reading for an introductory course, and does not attempt to teach or inform, but rather to indoctrinate. The recitations were also too long.

You can tell that Dr. Booth really cares about the material she is teaching. The class isn't designed to be challenging as much as it is getting you to think about things in a different way. Lectures aren't mandatory but recitations are. I would definitely recommend taking WMST101 with Dr. Booth.

I really enjoyed Karen's class, and by the end I felt as if I had learned a lot. She starts off by letting students know she has biases which made me respect her even more. Classes were very discussion based and she'd challenge our statements often. I believe she just wanted to think outside the box. I'd def recommend taking this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: It feels like everything we get back is based subjectively- not even on the criteria she gave us in the first place. This class is supposed to be a capstone culminating in an entire semesters worth of work on a 20ish page paper. She piled on all of the relevant paper work in the last 3 weeks, creating an undue burden for most if not all of us.

Not impressed at all. Class "discussions" entailed her calling on different people until she got the answer she wanted. She is very self-righteous & actively shut me down when I tried to bring up trans health issues in a sexual health class. Reading materials were interesting but I would suggest reading them on your own time.

Karen is the best professor ever. Don't expect an easy class though; she makes you read, do assignments, and actually work for it. However, it's totally worth it. She cares about the material and teaches it very effectively. She keeps class interesting, and facilitates discussion really well. This is my favorite class I've taken at UNC.
She is AMAZING. One of the best professors I have had at UNC.
Karen is hilarious and very down to Earth. I love the lecture and the TAs are pretty awesome as well!

It's a relatively interesting class and it is obvious professor Booth has a passion for what she is teaching. The class has made me think a good deal. Exams are easy if you've been to class and look over the study guide. Not much outside work either. Recitation is hit or miss depending on the TA. I personally love mine with Kim.
One of the best professors at UNC.

OHMYGOSH, karen booth is by far the best teacher i have had at unc thus far. after taking her 388 class (which i highly recommend if you can manage to get into it), i decided to double major with wmst. she is phenomenal. literally, every class discussion blowed my mind and it was the one class i had this semester that i actually looked forward to a

She was an interesting teacher who really cared about Feminism and educating the students (majority of them taking this class as gen. ed.) about feminism.  Recitation felt a little monotonous at times. As long as you read the required readings and look at the study guide, it's a good class to attend.

Such an interesting lecturer. I was initially taking the class to fulfill a curriculum requirement, but found a passion for the subject.  She really opens your eyes to feminist ideas and shooting down the myths.  I'm taking a smaller class with her next semester as well because I enjoyed her so much.  Highly recommended!
Excellent Professor! Interesting concepts about sexuality!

I did not enjoy this class, though I do have a developed interest in the subject. Although I learned a lot, I found the class unnecessarily difficult and I dreaded class time.  I found class to be formal, serious, and monotonous.  It was not a good learning environment and diverse opinions were not encouraged.

This class turned me off of women's studies altogether. She was extremely biased, and it showed in her comments on student's papers. There were meaningless daily papers that only served as busy work. Her lectures were scattered and pointless. Her pop quizzes were impossible regardless of whether you did the reading.

Literally changed my life. What an amazing professor. She's always ready for discussion and always made time for me. There were times when I did not agree with things she said - b/c they didn't fit into my life - and she was always courteous. It was a phenomenal experience for me.

Her wmst 50 class was the most amazing class I've ever taken. She was an interesting lecturer and was truly interested in getting her students to know the material, even if they don't agree with some of her ideas. She does an excellent job of bringing in movie clips, etc to make lecture interactive.

The problem with Prof Booth's class is that she treats her lectures as a way to advance an agenda.  That wouldn't be as problematic, but instead of allowing students to search, explore, and discover the issues that face women, she forces her class to adopt her views on the subject of women and specifically genderism and discrimination (hostility, etc).  Because I, at the time, didn't buy into what she and the TA wanted, I was graded harshly compared to other classes.  A joke of a class - b/c of above probs.
No Comments
AWFUL.

Her teaching focused more on gay/lesbian, and anti-war activism than anything having to do with globalization. Her schedule was never clear, her assignments were inappropriate, and her grading was personal and not professional.
ignore the above bad rating, i got her confused with karen ruffle
I have never had a teacher grade my papers so harshly, even in English classes.
Interesting lectures, good class, tough grading but worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Boittin's lectures are bone-dry, rambling, random, and occasionally border on offensive. My biggest gripe was our unit on terrorism, which Boittin devoted to justifying why the radical beliefs of those who murdered hundreds in Paris and Nice were not to blame for the events, but rather some abstract failing of European society. Just disappointing.

Class is alright but not very intersting. Quizzes are doable but don't have a clear rubric. If you try very hard in recitation you can get an 89/89 on participation which substantially boosts your grade so if you aren't willing to do that don't take this class.

Meh! That probably sums the class up well. Began interesting, but lost its intrigue as time went on. She is very knowledgable, yet this is quickly offset by her lackluster voice and seemingly disorganized lecture topics. Assignments were given at random and quizzes felt devoid of any lecture material. The recitations surprisingly saved this class.

The class really was not that bad. Many enjoyable movies and readings were assigned and watched during class. The professor and TA are clearly passionate about this topic. Only gripe, is that there is not really a clear rubric for any assignment and recitation participation can make or break your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: very difficult professor
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: No clear grading rubric. Quizzes were short answer style with little time to complete them. Feedback from TA's on quizzes would tell you to "add more detail" when you only had 10 minutes to handwrite an answer making it almost impossible to do so. Grade was essentially up to your TA. Unreasonably hard for a 100 level course. Would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Boittin is very smart. Lectures were boring and nearly useless as quizzes were almost entirely on readings. Grades were pretty harsh, arbitrary and TA dependent. Recitation participation is very important.

There were 6 quizzes and there was no clear grading criteria for any of the quizzes. You will likely get the same score 3-4 times in a row with no explanation why. Also, there are no rubrics or anything, and the grading is based completely on the TA.
Very unclear rubric

I have never used RMP in my entire 4 years of college because I haven't felt the need to; the fact that I am writing this review should demonstrate how bad this class was. The grading was random, there is a no grade change policy, and classmates of mine got worse grades for the same quality work I did. Feedback makes no sense when given.
Boring lectures, readings were okay with a few movies thrown in. Grading is up to TA, which happened to be pretty harsh for a 100 level Gen Ed. Unclear grading criteria for participation and quizzes.

Do not take this class. Most assignments are graded harshly with no clear grading criteria. Lectures are very boring. Participation is 30% of the final grade and guidelines are not outlined in the syllabus. Seems almost impossible to get an A even though it is a 100 level gen ed.
Weird grading with no rubric - almost impossible to get an A, as the TA's grade harshly. The professor is nice, but the class format is frustrating in terms of grading.

I wouldn't recommend this class as a GenEd. Professor Boittin is fine, but lectures are slow and lack clear slides. Grading depends heavily on your TA and often feels subjective, with little feedback. Attendance is a major component of your grade, and participation doesn't guarantee an A.

Professor Boittin is a nice person and an engaging lecturer. My issue with the class lies more in her TA's. I was graded very harshly on
few assignments and was not given a clear rubric or instructions on how to improve. Participation makes up a large component of the grade and despite attending and participating full credit is not promised

Super tough grader. Grading is very arbitrary and all up to the TA. If you get a tough grading TA, you will get a bad grade. You only have 15 minutes for 5 quizzes throughout the semester, and participation takes the majority of the grade.

They grade everything with no clear criteria, mainly participation; attending all recitations with some talking isn't enough: the participation is arbitrary with no input. There is a harsh quiz grading system with 15 minutes to develop a full-fledged argument. Few assignments, but even history majors struggle with the quiz grading.

I like taking history classes as electives, but this class was not one to be careless about. Like it's too serious for a history class, with group projects and a bunch of movies and full books you have to read/watch, none in english. The grading is also too harsh, this class was annoying. not necessarily hard, but annoying.

An interesting course that seemingly got less interesting as time went on. The topics she discusses are clearly the ones she knows best, but that does mean it occasionally felt random. Some assignments were created as the semester went on which made it difficult to know what to expect each week, but all in all quite easy. Recitations were good fun!

I had Dr. Boittin for my first year seminar, and I loved the class! It was an extremely interesting topic, and she taught it very well. There was definitely a lot of reading, and it's important to be prepared to discuss them; however, she is extremely encouraging and supportive of your interpretations of the text. I would definitely recommend her!

This class was very interesting and the lectures were super engaging! My only negative experience with this class was my TA and the weird grading with limited feedback. I would totally recommend it as it is a relatively easy class with some readings and quizzes instead of a typical midterm/exam format.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was Professor Boittin's first year at UNC and she was great! We did 5 unit quizzes where the 5th unit quiz was actually our final plus one simple cumulative question. 1 short paper. 1 group presentation presented in recitation. We read a few books and watched a few movies.
I initially took this class to fill a focus capacity, but it ended up being my favorite course of the semester. I loved learning and writing about comics at a university level!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: ben is such a chill dude. he literally says he tries to get everyone an A. there were maybe two assignments the whole semester that i thought were hard, but the rest were so calm cuz he gives rly detailed instructions and expectations. also i learned a lot! highly recommend if you have any interest at all in law.

Take the comics class when it's offered with Professor Bolling! I didn't know anything about comics before this semester. He clearly loves the material and it's infectious. Do the reading and you'll be fine.

Dr. Bolling was the best professor I had during my first semester and helped me transition to UNC. There's a lot of work in this class but he gives really detailed feedback and is always able for office hours.

I had Dr. Ben for 105 and learned a lot about writing from him so decided to take his comics class. Highly recommend. Made the material interest even though I didn't know much about comics going in. Always willing to make time to talk about projects during office hours.
I thought visual and graphic narrative was a film class but decided to stick with it because this guy was so funny. Knows the material like nobody else. Chill and kind.

Just straight up mean and condescending, easily offended. Took a student outside mid-class and I could hear him yelling. unclear assignments & class is a lot of work. assignments build on ones before which wouldn't be so bad if he could actually grade anything so u knew what was going on. when he does grade comments come back clearly ai generated.

Ben was so supportive and offered wonderful feedback. It was a go go go class, starting a project right after another, but it was manageable. I love Ben. I learned so much in this class and recommend him so much!! Very very funny.

Truly the best professor here at UNC!! He's so funny, caring, and easy to talk to. All his assignments were difficult, but they were also time-consuming. However, he provides samples for every assignment and is extremely helpful. He was such an amazing professor, I've decided to take another one of his classes next semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ben is an amazing professor and an amazing person. I thoroughly enjoyed taking Writing in Law and I learned so much from him. A couple group projects and every unit was structured. Definitely more difficult than a regular 105, but so worth it if you are considering law (also worth it if you aren't). Prepare for a busy schedule but a great class!

Professor Bolling is someone who genuinely cares about their students and their success. He provides really good feedback on assignments that typically involve analyzing constitutional cases and writing/presenting about them. The class was super interesting and I really enjoyed it.

Great professor. Grades come in somewhat slowly, but he's a very easy grader. Assuming you try and put effort in, you'll do well. Great class if you are interested in law. It is a very consistent workload and can be tough at times, but grading is easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Ben is super funny and clearly cares a lot about his students and the material. Sometimes felt like a lot of work for a 100-level class, but no assignments were that hard. The textbook reading is boring, but Ben makes the concepts interesting. Highly recommend.

Take ENGL 155 with Dr. Bolling! A few reading quizzes, one paper, and a project. The midterm was easy and he's a pretty easy grader. Gives very detailed feedback. Clearly passionate about the material and makes you appreciate comics in a new way.
Was super engaging and I loved class discussion. The texts were fun and Professor Bolling is so chill.
This class was amazing. The class is mostly based on readings, quizzes, papers, and projects, but they are not made to be too difficult. Read the required readings each week, and you will be fine.

Super fun and interesting class! I learned a lot and enjoyed all of the material. Very manageable work level and lenient grading. Professor Bolling is focused on making sure students get the most out of his class and the material and you can tell!

(Writing in Law) Super easy grader with rubrics to follow. Available for questions. Manageable/concise assignments, a few group projects, open note quizzes. Extremely thorough feedback. Nearly everything he says is funny. Slightly slow grading but many opportunities for revision. Not prelaw but no regrets on taking this course.

Class content can be kinda difficult and there's a lot of work but Ben is an extremely caring and funny teacher. Really cares about the subject and is a pretty lenient grader. Only complaint is that he's a slow grader.

Professor Ben's class was more than I expected. My friends in regular 105s complained all the time about the basic work they had to do. I'm not really interested in legal writing, but I appreciate what I learned in this class. I didn't enjoy all of the work we had to do in groups, but it wasn't as much as some other 105s.

Dr. Bolling is the best! His class requires a lot of work, but I learned a lot about the law and writing, in general. He was always willing to make extra time during office hours when I had questions about class or about school, in general. He's a real one

I didn't expect to enjoy ENGL 105, but Ben made it worth my time. Especially if you're interested in legal writing, he is knowledgeable and gives really good feedback. This is not a basic 105 and I'm glad I actually learned something in this class.

Dr. Bolling is a great professor who is extremely willing to work with students, field questions, and provide clear rubrics and guidelines for course material. His Writing in Law class is great at teaching students about the importance of consistency and brevity in writing, and I found the course material manageable to keep up with.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: None of this is accurate because he admits to constantly reading his own reviews on here and flagging stuff he doesn't agree with. steer clear

Ben is a very engaging teacher and gives helpful and detailed feedback on every assignment. He's also a pretty easy grader. He took a long time to grade on some assignments, but it was understandable due to various uncontrollable complications throughout the semester. By far my favorite professor this semester. Don't listen to the review bombers.
My entire group opened the transfer portal at least once a week
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Look, if you are interested in writing in the law, this class's content is valuable. However, beware of his inconsistent and sometimes even demeaning teaching styles. He claims to promote asking for help and feedback, but can be condescending when you try to do so. Each project builds off of each other, but he lays out expectations unclearly.

It is end of October, I have ONE of six big assignments thus far graded. Super inconsiderate and petty when it comes to grading - normally wouldn't complain about this, but each project literally builds on what you wrote before, and you have no idea how you're doing. A big project every week, a lot of work. I do well and the class is interesting.

Ben was such a chill but engaging prof. We did a bunch of projects in Adobe's CC and it was fun and useful to learn. Workload not heavy but you do have to put in a decent amount of effort. We read/discussed comics which was cool, good amount of reading at times though. Very easy grader
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Genuinely the best professor I've had at UNC. I wasn't looking forward to 105, but he made the gen ed practical and useful. He was easy to talk to outside of class and seemed to really care about helping his students.
the worst professor for engl 105, and possibly the worst professor at UNC overall.

I never thought 105 would be the most useful class I took first semester, but Ben made it worth it. He's funny and kind and always makes time for you if you need to meet outside of class. The work load is harder than other 105s, but you will learn a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ben was the best professor I had during my freshman year. He clearly cared about everyone not just as students but as people outside of class. He says he doesn't think his class is hard, which is mostly true. It's a lot of work, but if you show up to class and put in effort on the assignments, this is not a hard class.

DO NOT TAKE. There is a ton of work in this course. Regularly, I would have been fine with the work load if he made the learning and class room environment enjoyable. Spoiler: he did not. He is super nitpicky about writing and basically polices your writing. He says to "ask him for help if needed" and then is the opposite of helpful.

Ben is the GOAT. He is a amazing and hilarious lecturer, and I genuinely looked forward to class every day. Most of the assignments were fun and reasonable, but they often took a ton of time to complete. The only small issue was that he would take a long time to get us grades and feedback. He is very kind and understanding.

Overall, Professor Bolling was a good teacher and taught me some things about grammar that I didn't know. His class at some times was a little more work than other English 105 classes, but he is an easy grader. Attendance is required and class can sometimes be boring as he lectures a lot but overall it's an easy class so I would do it again.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He is hilarious and I genuinely enjoyed coming to class. There is kind of a lot of work due and it does take awhile to get feedback back, but that being said he is a very nice and understanding professor/grader

Professor Bolling is one of the best professors I've ever had. It's evident that he's passionate about what he's lecturing and that he has the experiences and skillsets to back up his lessons. If you are even vaguely interested in whatever class he's teaching, I highly recommend taking it (he's a really nice grader too).

Ben was so amazing. The course is well designed, and I learned so much. He is very passionate and clearly wants his students to succeed. This course teaches you Creative Cloud, which is so valuable. Definitely take a class with Ben if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Seems fine in the beginning and the work isnt hard (just a ton of it), but he can be condesending and rude at times. Also unprofessional and cusses a lot. I just took this class to get my engl 105 credit over with.

Ben Bolling was the best professor I could have had during my first year at Carolina. He very approachable and helpful, giving genuine and thoughtful feedback on every assignment. Not harsh on grading, he only really cared if you were learning something useful. If I could recommend only one professor, it would be him.

Ben is awesome. He is very kind, funny, and wants the best for his students. He is very open that he intentionally makes it easy to get an A/tries his hardest to keep your grade high so long as you put in a baseline level of effort. 100% recommend.

I love Ben so much!! He was the best professor I had in my first semester at UNC. He was super funny and loved the assignments he had us do. He and his niece even made us cereal bars one day! Ben wants the best for his students and always tries to make time to give students feedback.

Really amazing, caring, and down-to-earth professor. The class is a bit fast-paced, so be sure to be on top of the deadlines. It's also mainly group projects, but getting an A was not difficult. I took the Writing in Law, and it was a great first exposure to the legal industry. I would definitely recommend this class to aspiring lawyers.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Bolling is genuinely the most awesome person I have met at UNC. Such an amazing professor, such an awesome class, grading was super fair and lenient and yet I learned so much. He's such a cool guy and made super dense topics accessible, but also treated students like equals. 10/10. Everyone should take his classes.

Dr. Bolling is an amazing, caring, and lively professor. He just returned to teaching at UNC and I feel so grateful he came back this year! I got to work on case briefs, law articles, etc. in Eng105i for Law. He is not a super fast grader, but grades very leniently so I wouldn't be too concerned. Fair amount of writing but so helpful and worth it.

Ben is a great professor. He is very funny and personable. Not too much work outside of class. A couple of the books chosen were a little boring, but most of them were pretty good, and this is coming from a STEM major. If I needed to have taken another English class, I certainly would have taken him again. Take any class he offers!

Ben is the best professor I have had at UNC. From the first day of class, I felt comfortable participating in class and scheduling appointments outside of class to get more feedback. He gives you a chance to revise each assignment, which makes English 105 super easy. Could not recommend someone better.

Ben is SUCH a gem, and I'm sad that he is leaving UNC! Our class was usually a liberal echo-chamber, but I did enjoy the material and I felt like I learned a lot. Ben was great at fostering discussions, too!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Great professor. He cares about students and you'll care about him too. The workload is standard for a lit class- a lot of novels and a few papers- but he makes it really flexible and manageable. Occasionally he seems to promote his own ideas a little too much, but I'd chalk that up to enthusiasm. Would definitely take a class with him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Great class, great feedback given for practical assignments. Definitely take this class if you get a chance, you won't regret it.

This guy is amazing.  Show up to class and give effort; that's all he wants. He is helpful in answering your questions and gives honest and insightful feedback.  He's hilarious, and he makes the course assignments fun. And go to his office hours. He baked cookies for our last class meeting - if that tells you anything about how cool this guy is.

Ben Bolling is the BEST professor I've ever had. He's hilarious, he really cares about his students and gave me the most useful feedback and tips I've ever received concerning my writing. The class wasn't easy, but you will come out a better writer. He's seriously great.

The guy is seriously great.  He takes the time to analyze the arguments in your papers and reflections and offers suggestions.  Grading is fair and generally positive, all you have to do is put the effort into the course.  Show up to class and hold on tight.  He's hilarious and insightful--a bit opinionated--but damned if I didn't have fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Ben was definitely my favorite professor at UNC. He genuinely cares about his students and took the time to get to know each of us. He's an extremely fair grader and if you put an effort in, you'll get the grade you want. I highly recommend taking this course with Ben.

Funny professor, is very interested in what you have to say, and although he may have an idea in his mind, he always asks for comment. The books that we have read were interesting. In Eng 128, as long as you read the book, you will succeed in the class because all he wants is effort and is interested in what you have to say.

Undoubtedly my favorite professor my first semester. He knew his stuff and was open to new ideas. Reasonable grader. The work you put is the grade you will get out. He cares about the well-being of his students and is down to earth.

He was my favorite professor first semester as he really cares about his students. He was always checking in on the well-being of students which as a fist-year is nice to have in a professor. They're a lot assignments but most are pretty manageable and he is an extremely fair grader. He was quite funny and keeps your attention very well.

Professor Bolling quickly forms opinions about his students in the beginning of class. There is a lot of work for an English 105 class. His style of lecturing can be condescending at times. Overall, not a bad class, but not a great teacher.
Great teacher, interesting class  and readings. Discussions were great.
Prof. Bolling was very, very helpful. It wasn't the easiest class I have ever taken but it was easy to stay focused. As long as you do the readings and go to class, you'll be fine.

Class is only graded by 2 exams and a participation grade, but Bruno makes it as easy as possible. He is very passionate about linguistics and wants us to talk to him in class (will cold call). No course schedule, just occasional reading homework to keep us engaged. Attendance is important, and he is sure to explain concepts clearly in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a very passionate teacher but very strict. Make sure you go to office hours. No computers/phones/ipads allowed in class-- all hand written. The class was also quite difficult for being an introductory course.
Lit teacher played Roblox all class and leveled up in adopt me hella take his class for an easy A
great class took it with the fellas and day traded the whole time I put bruno onto forex

Forensic linguistics, new course. Bruno is scary, but honestly the sweetest. Mad respect he's so smart. The homework is hard but if you start early and ask he'll help you. There's hw every class but he only requires 5 graded, you can ask for an excuse if you ask ahead of time no questions asked. My 1st class with him, dunno what he's like in person

Estigarribia was the worst professor to have during a pandemic and civil unrest. For some reason, he decided to grade even more assignments than he usually does this semester. All homework was graded for accuracy and he will lower your grade if you don't understand the topic or don't use italics. I do not recommend taking his class during covid.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Bruno is hands down the best Spanish professor I have EVER had. He's hard, don't take any of his classes expecting an easy A, but he's such a good professor he justifies his challenging grading. He randomly grades homework and he grades it on a curve so you have to do it. His lectures are very though so take notes and ask questions if you're lost.

Bruno was one of the hardest professors I've ever had. We had no guidance for the exams (other than study everything- literally), would get locked out of the room if you left to use the restroom, and would have incredibly hard to follow lectures. In his office hours he wasn't much help either, and assumed you should know everything. Rough class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Estigarribia was one of the most unapproachable, and difficult professors I have ever had. Class was always just lecturing, usually no powerpoint. For the 2 midterms and final, there was no review, and only our notes and the daily homework to look over. After the class average for the first midterm was failing the students were blamed. AVOID!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Phonetics was my favourite course this semester, and not only because it's a fascinating field for me, but also because professor Bruno exceeded my expectations by far: knowledgeable, approachable, organized and enthusiastic. He's an amazing researcher but he also is passionate about what he teaches, and he does it extremely well. 10/10.

Dr. Estigarribia is a very good professor and he did an excellent job bringing in new research in the field of Guarani Linguistics to our class. I definitely try to take courses with this professor, because he can be depended on to help you get a solid foundation in the major. This was one of my favorite courses in my undergraduate career.

Very fair prof. You have to do the work (sometimes there's a lot of it) and know the material, but his exams are very straight-forward and his expectations are generally very clear. He offers extra credit throughout the semester and he is enthusiastic about his subject.

Hes a Goat. Always made it so fun to show up and as a student who is the type to sit in the back and be on there phone I was front row always paying attention to him. He does expect effort, but with how engaging his teaching is its impossible not to put in effort. Chill grader, genuinely funny guy, and great political takes. Made me want an A

Incredible professor with true passion and inspiration for his students. Gave so much grace when I struggled due to personal reasons and let me take the midterm a week late. Such an incredible professor, take his classes!!!! So funny and attendance isn't graded (but it's important unless u look at the notes) No electronics but so interesting.
He is a great professor that is easily reached outside of class and cares about the success of his students. I highly recommend you take a class of his if possible.

brian was a pretty easy grader. one 10-12 page paper, a midterm, a final, and a couple of assignments that required you to go to office hours for a bit. he was pretty nice but he did go on random rants about primaries where he screamed for like 5 mins. there are lots of readings but you can just skim them enough to write the discussion posts
Brian was a great professor for POLI 208! His passion for the material is evident in his lectures and he genuinely cares about his students!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Brian was a good professor and loved teaching the material. He was funny in lectures, or at least tried to be. There's a ton of reading each week, but you'll be fine if you just skim. There are two papers and a midterm and final that he graded pretty easily. Attendance isn't required, but participation is part of the grade.

Brian is pretty great. He clearly loves political science, and that is shown in his lectures. He isn't a very harsh grader, and if you are interested in political science, you will enjoy his lectures. POLI 208 had two papers, a midterm and a final exam, and none of them were too difficult. It's a good class to learn in and not worry about grades!

Brian's class was AMAZING! Engaging lectures, and he's very funny.  Midterm's not bad if you study, and final was open book.  Major papers (2) are graded very fairly, and he gives great feedback.  Mini short papers (2) were easy 100s if you just did them and followed guidelines.  Also did mini simulation in class and earned EC.  Highly recommend!
Great professor! Take him!

My favorite professor so far at UNC. His exam was so easy and was straight from the study guide. His lectures were interesting and he sometimes brought his dog to class. This course is taught with two other professors and he by far was the easiest one.

This is one of the best professor's I have ever had, he really cares about his students and is very passionate and knowledgeable about this course and topics. Definitely take this class, very easy and super interesting.

One of the best professor ever met! He really supports and wants student to learn how to do research and understand sustainability related topics. Grade is not a concern for this class (he's grading fairly and  leniently) but understanding science & research is the goal.

Dr. Bruno was an amazing lecturer, and super kind! The questions in our quizzes from his lecturers were often difficult, so make sure you take detailed notes on some of the exact numbers discussed in class. He has a really cute dog he brought to class as well! Super cool dude!

Dr. Bruno was by far my favorite lecturer on the FoF teaching team. His lectures were insightful and easy to follow, and he always brings his dog Mr. Lizard to class when he teaches. He gives an in-depth synopsis of the fishing industry and the fraud within it. He is also accessible outside of class and offers advice who show the initiative to ask.

Dr. Bruno was the best professor in FoF. He made lectures very interesting and was always knowledgable on what he was doing. Hes funny and is always very kind to the students. FoF as a class wasn't too hard but the quizzes were very detailed so I reccommend at least reviewing before. Everything else was graded easily, including the final paper.

Dr. Bruno is one of 3 professors in FoF. His passion for his field of research reassures me that there are people out there who care for our planet. You must take notes during lectures to do well on the 3 quizzes. There's a simple semester-long group project and final paper. Attendance not taken, but lectures aren't posted.
BIOL 221 was an amazing class. The TAs were great and so was the Professor. I genuinly enjoyed going to this class and it tought me a lot about research.
Professor Bruno was the best part of the future of food. The quizzes were difficult, but he made the lectures very interesting. He also always brought his dog to class, which was fun!

Prof Bruno was the best part of the future of food. While this class was challenging at times (mainly quizzes, but if you study and mostly pay attention in class you'll be ok), He was super funny and actually cares about what he is teaching, and wants students feedback and participation. Super cool dude, and brings his dog which is a huge plus.

idst 130 future of food was the worst class ever. they teach super basic things that are honeslty common sense and say we don't need to memorize anything. then its quiz day and the quizzes are based solely on important dates and specific policies that we were supposed to memorize. the group projects are a waste of time. no practice for quizzes.

Future of Foods was my triple I and Dr. Bruno was the best Professor out of the three. The class itself doesn't have any exams and your grade is determined by a few essays and in class assignments. Grading is done by TA's but mine was very nice and gave good feedback. If you put any effort and go to class at least half the time you will get an A.

This is a review for IDST 130 Futures of Food. Please do not take the class, super boring and the structure is awful. Dr. Buno is the only saving grace. Super cool guy plus he brought his dog to class regularly.
I recommend both this class and Professor Bruno. He is an understanding professor. Lectures were amazing, and this class is an easy Gen-ed to knock out! Definitely recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I love Bruno! He was one of the three professors for my Triple-I (Future of Food), and he gave interesting lectures that were very easy to follow. I'd highly recommend taking any of his classes. Also, he was always accessible outside of class, and it felt like the whole team of professors for this Triple-I wanted the students to succeed.

BIOL 221 was the best class ever. I learned more about research and science than I ever had before. Dr. Bruno is a kind and sociable guy who will provide you with connections as well as multiple opportunities. The class was graded on homework assignments, a midterm, and a final research project and poster that were truly interesting.

Dr. Bruno is a very caring instructor, but he does not lecture in class at all. You will have to learn the material on your own. TAs are extremely helpful and willing to answer questions. Grades are midterm, presentation, lab work, research paper (final), and quizzes. Would take again

I agree with the other review on here, super unorganized, little to no lectures, and TAs did most of the work. But Dr. Bruno is a great guy and I had fun. The class is one day a week, and you mainly work on your research project. Graded on weekly quizzes, notebook checks, a midterm, project, and presentation. Would take again.

Doctor Bruno was a great teacher but there was hardly any lecturing in class and a lot of things were not clear in terms of the schedule within class. Not very well structured. Super interesting content.

Dr. Bruno was a really amazing professor, he made sure we understood concepts. There is a scientific article to read every week and a discussion in class about the paper. The only critique I have is that because we were online, lectures sometimes lasted 3-4 hours, most of the time we were silent in breakout rooms. I definitely recommend his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Bruno is a great professor. His classes are very thought provoking and inspiring. He's such a passionate professor. His exams are pretty difficult, but if you put in the effort, you can do well.
Bruno is awesome! Super chill guy, great professor, and his class isn't very hard. Do the basics and you'll be fine.
Loved him

So many old, boring movies. Watched about 10 films, no color, silent, 3 hours long, and some in other languages, and most were not great. Had to read a chapter a week that barely related to move. There is a big group project, so hope for good group. MUST PARTICIPATE.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: This introductory class was unnecessarily hard. Don't take it for the GenEd requirement.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Whalen is obviously incredibly passionate about the Medieval period and his students. Interacting with him is an excellent way to improve the uniqueness of his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Nice professor but unnecessarily tough grader with difficult exams. Not an easy gen ed. Don't take unless you really like medieval history.

Professor Whalen is really passionate about what he teaches and brings a lot of energy every class. The main assignments were group presentations and papers, which could be long. He is very considerate and flexible. He made learning enjoyable.

Cool teacher who cares a lot about history. The class was not hard at all. The only assignments we ever had were papers. There were 3 online papers and 3 papers were in-class "exams." All you have to do is read the textbook to do well in this class.

Super engaging lectures. You can hear his passion for medieval history. There are only 6 grades in this class but just have a clear thesis on your paper with info from the readings and you'll be fine. He also sneaks in extra credit on the final if you attend Friday lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Amazing lecturer, however, doesn't take into account at all that this class is made of students fresh out of high school. Grades mainly consist of essays, participation, and presentations, which are graded fairly tough. There's definitely other professors who shape their first year launch better for freshmen, NOT an easy A by any means.

Dr. Whalen is a great professor who LOVES what he does and is always happy to give feedback on essays. The class was very interesting and discussion based, but NOT an easy A seminar. We watched a movie and read documents weekly outside of class. Part of your grade is from participation in discussions/group presentations and essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Choose another Gen-Ed. Professor Whalen is passionate, a great lecturer, and accessible, but the course is challenging.
