Office hours with the TA's will help, and it will be helpfull if you really try to understand the concepts and how to apply them

I absolutely loved Alyssa. She was super sweet and caring. The textbook wasnt required and I dont regret not reading it. Discrete math is obviously a hard subject and you have to put in the work. Alyssa was very fair with grading, gave points back, and wanted everyone to pass the class. Def the best instructor you could take this class with!

If you have to take COMP 283 take it with Alyssa. She is far better than the other options and her class is pretty easy. Just do the work and pay attention in class and you should be good. A lot of work is participation based so just turn it in. Exams are same difficulty as homework too if not easier.

If you have to take COMP 283/MATH 381, take COMP 283 with Alyssa Byrnes. She's young, new, and nervous, and sometimes confuses herself when explaining concepts, but she's so sweet and patient (and very intelligent when it comes down to it). It's definitely not an easy class, but hers is the best option for the credit/material.
LOL easy class. just study by yourself, no need to go to class.

It was straightforward and largely reiterated the material from ECON 420. Most students didn't attend lectures since the textbook covered the content just as well. Simply taking notes, completing the practice exam, and doing some studying was more than enough to ace the class. There were also a few homework assignments, all of which were easy!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This course really deserves a different professor given how important and applicable the content is for economics. Lectures are extremely uninteresting and provide no incentive to actually come to lecture and learn information - readings are better than lecturers. Not a lot of communication and you're on the hook for this class. Take with diff prof

Genuinely one of the laziest professors I have had in the econ department. Like, not once in the entire course did she pick up a marker or use an apple pencil to write something out. She straight up walks into class a minute before it starts, and shuts her laptop and bolts out of the room the minute class is over. Arbitrary grader. 0/10
If you want to experience the best courses and professors in the UNC econ department, choose her!
Easy and boring. Waste of time if you want to learn something new.

So far, Tian is one of the easier ECON professors I've had at UNC - tests are not bad and hws are reviewable pre-submission. However, it also may be the most boring class I've taken despite liking the material. She is nice and is willing to help outside of class if needed, but you need some serious willpower to pay attention to the lectures.

Dr. Tian is such a nice professor and I loved talking to her after class. SO knowledgeable in MACRO and monetary policy and her 423 class is very well structured and time-efficient, with ready made and current slides and she ends class perfectly. Exams are harder than the practice but doable, I think she curves at the end. Great chill ECON elective

Very nice professor, interesting class on the history and structure of banking/financial system. Homeworks were occasional and tests were very straightforward. I would highly recommend this as an interesting, low-stress upper level econ elective.

This class is on the easier side of economics at UNC. I certainly enjoyed the concept as a whole but I found it easier to just read the textbook on the hard stuff as the slides were vague. Homework and Exams are very fair and Tian is a forgiving grader. A great elective to take at UNC if you need it!

Professor Tian has a very unique course structure. All of the HWs are easy 100s, but the tests are very difficult. However, it is a mystery how she grades tests. I should've got around a 60 and 80 on the two midterms, but my grades came back as an 80 and 96. She doesn't explain any sort of curve, so it makes no sense, but grade ends up being easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best prof ever

I highly recommend taking ECON 101H with her. She is humorous, nice, and very knowledgeable. Class can get boring but everything was pretty straightforward. She was always willing to answer questions and responds to emails rather quickly. I would say it was pretty easy to get an A.

I was nervous about taking ECON 101 at UNC, but she made the material straightforward, even if lectures were pretty repetitive. Exams weren't too bad and she gives sufficient practice problems - some of the homework was tough, but she is more than willing to help if you ask.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Very funny. She is knowledgeable and knows what she's talking about. Loves the subject and is enthusiastic about teaching. Class is a little boring because the textbook and her slides say the same thing but overall very easy to get an A. A few homework assignments, two midterms and one final constitute your grade
Wow, what a fantastic professor. You will learn so much about PR, and you can tell she cares so much about the success of her students.
Seriously the best professor I've had at UNC. Took 332 and 531 with her and loved them both. Such a kind and inspiring person and learned so much

The comments speak for themselves so I am not really doing anyone a service by writing another. However, in case she reads these, I want Professor Campi to know that she greatly impacts each of her students in a wonderful way. I aspire to be more like her as a person and will always remember her 10 last bits of advice.

While Professor Campi's capabilities within the classroom are heavily reflected in her perfect rating, there is no rating that can encapsulate the quality of person she is on a daily basis. She is by far and away my favorite professor I have had at UNC, and is someone that I admire in every way I know how. I could not recommend her enough. 10/10
The comments speak for themselves. I wish she taught more classes so I could take her again. Possibly the best professor at UNC she's so awesome you won't regret taking her classes!
Professor Campi is a truly WONDERFUL professor and human being! TAKE. HER. CLASS.
Professor Campi is AMAZING!! She is so kind and truly cares about her students as individuals. The class is super interesting and pretty group project heavy. 100% my favorite Hussman professor.

She is the best!!! Only took this class because of her other RMPs but I loved it! Very team-based and presentation-heavy, but NO TESTS! Would definitely recommend taking classes with her. She is very understanding and truly cares about her students. She loves participation and is open to any discussion students bring up.

Such a wonderful professor. Clearly knowledgeable in her field and wants you to succeed. Take her if you can. Learned the most in this class without it ever feeling like I was having to work super hard. You do have to put in work, but it is interesting and you can make every project what you want it to be!

Professor Campi is the best. I took MEJO531 and MEJO435 with her, and they have been some of my favorite classes in the Hussman school. She is so easy to listen to and get to know as a professor, and I have learned so much from her over the past two years.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I LOVE HER I FEEL LIKE A BABY BIRD BEING FED KNOWLEDGE #CAMPI
I LOVE PROFESSOR CAMPI!!! Please take a class with her- she's the most caring, intelligent professor I've had so far!!

Nicest professor I know. Could listen to her talk all day! 
This class is based on team projects and has no exams/papers

Professor Campi is amazing! She really focuses on improvement rather than expecting perfection on the first go. She provides detailed feedback on every assignment and sometimes gives students the chance to revise mistakes and improve on graded assignments. She is extremely knowledgeable and experienced in the PR field.

One of my favorite professors at UNC. She went through lots of information fast, but the material felt understandable and doable at all times. She is so professional and willing to share her expertise with students.

Genuinely one my favorite professors here at UNC. I couldn't ask for a better PR writing professor! She took the time to break down all of our assignments, and gave us framework that she uses as a PR professor. I highly recommend!

She is AMAZING!! I've taken both 332 and 531 with her, and learned so much. She truly cares about your success and well being, her feedback is so positive and constructive. She is easily the best professor I have had here and value everything she has brought from her experience into the classroom. Take this class!!!

I would 100% take another class with her. She is so sweet and caring and gives you a lot of real-world examples/cases based on her experience and past case studies! TAKE IT!! I can't express that enough!

Professor Campi is THE standard for good professors. She is accessible, willing to talk, generous, engaging, and professional. The level of respect she has for her students as an entire being, rather than merely a student, is so thoughtful, intentional, and genuine. Professor Campi is wonderful!!

I had Professor Campi for both MEJO 332 this semester and for her MEJO 533 class during the fall. Both courses were very educational and focused on real-life skills and scenarios with practical applications. Prof. Campi is always willing to meet or talk and give feedback as well as giving very helpful comments on all assignments.

my favorite class thru hussman! you get to work with real life clients and get feedback from professor Campi. She truly cares about you as an individual and will help you achieve the best PR skills that you WILL use later in your career. I would definitely take another class with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Campi's real-world experience and warm personality make her one of the best professors I have ever had. She is very knowledgeable, and you will leave this class feeling prepared for a career in PR. You can correct graded work and there is only one writing-based midterm and a final.

Hands down the best professor I've ever had at UNC. Professor Campi is simply the best. She's caring and knowledgeable. You'll leave her class feeling inspired. She gives incredible professional advice, too. I feel more than prepared for PR internships and post-grad jobs. Take her if you can!

Genuinely the best professor i have ever had. I cannot say enough good things but she's so helpful and nice, really cares about us over grades and has so much IRL experience. She inspires me a lot and is a great mentor

ESTHER CAMPI IS THE BEST WOMAN ON THE PLANET. She even goes as far as to call her students "colleagues" to help us feel prepared for post-grad. Best feedback ever, and seriously, genuinely cares about each of her students. She gives extra opportunities to improve your work to earn an A. She is also so knowledgeable and the definition of girlboss.
Prof. Campi is one of my favorite professors in the Hussman School. She provided us with so much real-world knowledge, and I couldn't recommend this class more!

I absolutely love Professor Campi and her 332 class. I genuinely learned so much and she is an amazing professor. I gained real-world PR experience and came out of the class feeling much more confident and ready to take on the industry. If you have the chance, take class with her!
I love Campi so much. She is an outstanding Professor and a talented lecturer. She is highly knowledgeable about PR and truly wants to help her students learn.

she is so amazing. she is super knowledgeable and successful in the field. she provides resources to her students that she gives to her clients that are senators or fortune 500 companies. she only cares about the students' growth and encouragement, not really about grades, which makes the course so low stress

I don't think I've ever learned more from a professor than from professor Campi. She is incredible. Her lectures are thoughtful, informational, and helpful. You can tell she puts a lot of care into her class, is very knowledgable, and wants her students to succeed. One of my favorite professors of all time!!!!

An A was a 95, Dr. Castillo is a very passionate professor, but his lectures were quite long and fast paced. No textbook, only slides, and each slide deck was anywhere from 40-70 slides, each class. The tests were a lot harder than I expected (took this class for an upper bio). Lot's of extra credit though, he wants you to succeed.

GROUP PROJECTS (4). COIL makes class feel like 2 classes. Doesn't communicate well. Exams are niche and questions are worded poorly. Lectures are boring. Cold calls. Loved him for 490. Highly disappointed and frustrated with 441. Quizzes every class. Feels like he doesn't care about students and only wants to do his personal research.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: This class was about corals and it was so interesting. There is a project, but the topic can be chosen for wahtever you want. As long as you try, you will succeed.

Dr. Castillo is a passionate speaker. He is insightful and holds office hours and will work to make sure his class succeeds. I have taken 4 classes with him so far and plan to take more! There are also extra credit opportunities if you go to class.

Dr. Castillo really cares about his students' learning the material. There are quizzes in every class but they're open note. Even though there were weekly assignments, I didn't feel like they were busy work. He is very clear on grading and the class is well organized. I would recommend this class if you're interested in the material

Professor Castillo was a good professor. He made it clear he was more concerned about us learning than about grades. Your overall grade came from in-class quizzes (given randomly), assignments and exams. It was relatively easy to get an A even if you didn't do well in the exams as the other assignments made up for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Castillo is extremely intimidating and belittles students in class. He called out a girl for being on her phone in front of an entire class of at least 80 people. His lectures don't help at all and he pulls from a textbook that's simply too much to read for an entry level course. He is extremely unforgiving with grading/late work.

The lectures can be tough to understand but a lot of the grading is based on participation-based stuff. The textbook pretty much sums up all the stuff you have to know, its just really bulky. Hes really passionate about what he does though and it makes a difference.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Many extra credit opportunities. He is very passionate about his job. If you pay attention in class you will do fine.

Professor Castillo was one of the best professors I had during the pandemic, and he really wants you to do well. There are various opportunities for extra credit but attendance is mandatory! There are two midterms and a final but if you study (not thoroughly you'll do great! Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I'm in Karl's class during the pandemic and it's one of my easier classes this sem. I'm not a STEM major and he makes a lot of the concepts pretty easy to understand. Lectures are kinda boring but the test all comes from the textbook and that's not a hard read. TAs do most of the grading and if you put some effort in you'll do well in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class is honestly super difficult for a 101 level class. Don't take it expecting an easy A. Dr. Castillo is funny and does his best to make lectures interesting, but lacking prior knowledge of marine science makes it difficult to follow. Random attendance checks mean you have to go to class, but there is extra credit which is helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Castillo can be a bit confusing in his lectures if you do not have a strong science background. He loves questions though and will help anyone. His grading scale is kind of harsh, but there are plenty of extra credit opportunities. His exams are the most difficult part of the class, otherwise everything else really boosts your grade.

Ridiculous grading scale for a 101 class: only a 96-100 will get you an A. The tests are ridiculously specific. Random attendance means that you might skip one class and lose points for missing class (even though we're supposed to be allowed a certain number of absences per university standards). Just don't do it, it isn't worth it.

I really enjoyed this class. As a person who isn't really into science, he did a good job making the material easy to understand. While his exams were somewhat difficult, he provides study guides and lots of extra credit opportunities. Overall he is a really cool guy who can make this subject matter interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Loved taking his class as a freshman first semester. He's so engaged and easy to follow. Explains things very clearly. For his second test and final exam he lets you use a 5x8 notecard with information on it. He also gives a lot of extra credit opportunities and the homework is very easy. Definitely recommend!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests? Not many--Would take again

reviews.comment: Professor Castillo is nice. I am interested in marine science, but this class is pretty boring. If you don't read the book the tests will be very hard, even if you paid attention/attended every class. He does offer a lot of extra credit which boosts your grade and along with the many easy assignments, so it isn't impossible to get a good grade.

Don't let the 101 deceive you. I am a biology major with A's in many of my upper level classes, but won't come out with an A in this class because the grading scale is skewed (96-100 is an A), he asks very specific questions about things not covered in class on tests, and participation based. If you were thinking about this for GPA boost, it's not.

He's a nice guy, but his MASC 101 class is NOT interesting. His test are hard because he pulls straight from the extremely tedious textbook and he hardly explains in class. He loves Marine Science and wants you to learn, but this class was just painful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Your grade in this class basically depends on how much you read outside of class. Attendance & participation points are easy to get, & Castillo explains things pretty well in class, but if you don't study you will have no idea what's going on. He can also be a little vague sometimes, but his TAs grade & are great at clearing up any questions.
Great professor!

Professor Castillo is engaging and you can tell he is really interested in the subject matter. He listened carefully to feedback after each exam, incorporating the feedback into how he ran the class (almost personalizing it). His lectures are long and not very interesting, but you don't necessarily have to go to class to pass. Overall great guy.

Karl is very competent. He is extremely clear, creates all the notes you will need in powerpoints, and gives you study guides. I found this class *very* easy. That being said, averages on the tests were around a 2.5-2.6 gpa (?), even after he bumps them up by 6-10%. If you're competent, you should do really well. It is an interesting course.

The best professor I have had. I took his Marine Science class first semester of my freshmen year and he made the class so amazing I declared a minor and hope to take all classes with him! He is the most caring and understanding professor there is. He always makes sure you are on the right track and tries to get to know you. Awesome professor

MASC101 and GEOL103 are the same course - Karl is not just an awesome professor, he's an awesome person. exams are easy if you follow the notes. he gives a comprehensive study guide before each exam. really understanding and willing to help anyone!
Great Professor.  Very Enthusiastic!!!
Great Professor.  Very Enthusiastic.

He is from Belize and is difficult to understand. He also didn't wear a mic in a large lecture hall, very hard to hear! When going through power points he doesn't give you time to write down all the notes!
yep

Coming into Professor Byrns' class I had no desire or interest in economics. In fact, I was only taking the class so that I could apply to the Kenan-Flagler Business School. Upon arriving into Byrns class, I became interested in econ as a result of his genuine interest and his amazing teaching style! He's not only a teacher but also a great mentor!
Professor Byrns is a brilliant man who makes learning economics easy. He's also fun to talk to and always has great advice.

I consider Professor Byrns to be one of the most interesting people I’ve ever met.  He keeps classes engaged with stories about life and fun facts that you'd never hear elsewhere.  He’s always happy to take time to talk to students after class because he genuinely enjoys teaching, something that's often missed on college campuses.

Dr. Byrns's care for his students is deep and genuine, and his love for teaching economics is unmatched. When not lecturing, he could usually be found on the front steps of Gardner Hall, discussing economics, policy, philosophy, or life with interested students. Such commitment to teaching too often lacks among professors at large universities.
A really great professor who genuinely cared about his students.

Con't...Even in a large lecture setting he challenges students and takes the effort to know his students individually and help them reach their fullest intellectual capacity. When he left UNC, the campus lost one of its most brilliant minds, and I am truly blessed to have gotten the chance to learn from him.

Con't...He wants his students to do well and wants them to understand the fundamentals of economics, which is clear to anyone who sits in on his classes. His creative approach and the unique examples he provides truly demonstrate how economics is relevant for everyone, not just majors.

I never considered being an Econ major. I took Econ 101 because it was a requirement for the Journalism school and after Dr. Byrns’ class I was converted. professors is not his passion for the subject, but his innovative approach and his relatability and his genuine concern for his student’s performance.
Great professor, he got me to major in economics. This class changed my perspectives and is easily one of the best classes I've taken, ever.

Honestly, the only professor I had at UNC whose class I still tell stories about. Excellent professor who is always available to discuss economics (or anything else). Students loved him so much the newspaper ran a front page story when he left.

Dr. Byrns is the all in one package. He was the heart of the Economics department during his tenure. He managed to serve as a mentor, teacher, and above all a life coach to every single student who spent the time to listen and speak with him. Without him, I'm sure I would not be where I am today. Passing him up would be a tremendous mistake.

Dr Byrns is an excellent professor. It is obvious that he enjoys spending time with students and he learns everyone's name, even in large classes. He is passionate about the subject matter and probably the most approachable professor I have had. He engages students by asking questions and encouraging participation.

I took Mr. Byrns' Econ 101 class at UNC, as well as his class of History of Economic Thought. Both were entertaining and informative. Regarding Econ 101, UNC-CH requires both Micro and Macro to be taught in one semester, which is unusual for college level economics. Given this constraint Mr. Byrns was not only a good instructor but exceptional.

Raised my interest in economics to another level, could almost say he was the reason I majored in econ.  Took first “history of econ” then “financial markets” with Dr. Byrns.  He is the best professor I have ever had, wish he was still here.

I love Ralph Byrns. He is an outstanding professor with a talent for explaining abstract concepts or ideas in ways that are accessible and intuitive. Dr. Byrns' passion for his craft and his students inspired me as I developed my own vision for this "brief, glorious dance" and I think back to lessons and conversations with him often.
Dr. Byrns was the most entertaining professor that I had at Carolina! A great teacher with an open door.
Prof. Byrns is one of the best professors I have had. He made me understand economics and apply it to my daily life.

Professor Byrns is the reason I became and Economics major. His classes are engaging and more intellectually stimulating than any other econ course I took. He also highly values student input in courses, which makes even 101 courses especially vibrant. I took two of his courses and recommend that all students take his course.

Going into my first year at UNC I didn't know what to expect for ECON101. Byrns clarified that on the first day. His lesson plan encouraged participation, gave multiple sources for grade improvement (online assignments, & weekly quizzes), and was a great learning environment due to his enthusiasm and wit. There was never a dull moment in class!
Professor Byrns was a great 101 teacher. both helpful and informative.  Was quite impressed that he got John Edwards to speak to our class.
I took several Econ classes with Byrns and enjoyed all of them. He presented material in an inspiring and intellectual way. He'a a great lecturer.
Clear and Easy to follow. There was quite a bit of work, but with the weekly TA session everything is manageable. I took the class and became a Econ major. enough said.

Dr. Byrns' class was not easy, but it wasn't hard either.  He provided great knowledge of a subject and expanded the knowledge of his students.  As a teacher, he is a wonderful man.  As a person, he is even better.
Dr. Bryns is inspirational thoughtful and the highest quality lecturer.  I left his class's thinking not just about economics but on how to be better at life.
Dr. Byrns was one of my favorite professors at UNC. I had him for ECON 101 as a freshman and enjoyed him as a professor so much that I took ECON 434 with him as an elective (I was a Biology major).
Great Professor, really kept the class engaged even though it was a huge lecture.  Gave me a reason to come to class every day.  Highly recommend.

Dr. Byrns is one of the best professors I had a UNC. I knew next to nothing about economics/finance before taking this class, but gained a strong foundation and passion for the material afterward. He's zany...but I've never come across a professor more passionate about teaching and helping his students. He's kind and always accessible to students.
Very, very engaged and self-aware as an instructor. A professor who affects the future ambitions of students for the better.

I took 434 with Byrns on a whim, and I'm glad I did; because of him I decided to major in economics.  He is an enthusiastic teacher, who is easily accessible whenever you need help.  He also makes a large bank of practice test questions available before each exam, which were very helpful.

I consider Professor Byrns to be one of the most interesting people that I've met in my entire life. He did teach the history of economics (which can be dull), but he kept the class engaged with life skills and small tidbits that you'd never find elsewhere. I was so sad to see him leave UNC, but I know he loves to teach, regardless of the audience.

Dr. Byrns is an excellent professor. Many students who are writing on here mis-understand his class. He teaches an excellent intro to economics class. He doesn't focus on the technical and mathematical details but rather on helping students understand the broad applicability of economics to ones life.

I had a great time in the class and learned a lot. Byrns challenged our understanding of Econ constantly, and presented the world in a complex and interesting way. He is the reason I have pursued economics.

Simply put, this guy made me major in Econ.  No longer teaching but I just wanted to put my 2 cents in.  Tests came from the textbook but class was the best part - instead of spouting off abstract economic concepts he talked about real world stuff that really clicked with me.  Funny guy, loves the material, def. a great prof.

In class he likes talking about his life more than the content you need to learn for the quizzes and tests.  He uses a lot of examples and analogies but they are often hard to relate to the information at hand.  You're mostly on your own for learning the material.
Compared to the other econ 101 profs, Byrns is the best. BUT do not take his class unless you have to; he knows the material really well but isn't an effective teacher.

Byrns is interesting and I recommend him for econ101.  Great extra credit and decent curve. teaches straight from textbook (since he wrote it), but textbook is good for an intro-level class. Attendence is not necessarily important, but it definitely helps towards better quiz/test grades. Quizs every friday. Aside from grades, hes very entertaining

He went off on tangents far too much.  It was a total chore, going to lecture.  For a while I was only going on Fridays because they're quiz days.  My TA was kind of hard to understand, so yeah.  I came out with a C with about C-/D+ grades on midterms and barely did well on Aplias.  Overall, I wouldn't take Byrns..too hard to follow.

the only plus side to this class is the crazy amount of unexpected extra credit given at the end that prevents you from getting the horrible grade you think you have all semester. Minimal effort is need to pass this class with a C, and if you really want to learn you better read your textbook and ask your TAs for help, because byrns does NOT teach.

My T.A. was the only person who I learned anything from, and I failed most of the aplia assignments/quizzes and nearly failed the final, but an 'A' magically appeared on my transcript at the end of the semester. On the plus side, Byrns is entertaining, if slightly crazy.

If you are serious about learning anything about economics, be prepared to teach yourself basically everything from the book. Unless you want a laugh, don't go to class except for Fri. Byrns is highly entertaining but if he spent half as much time actually teaching econ as he did trying to be funny, I might have actually learned something from him.

EASY! I only went to class on friday to take the quizes, many of which i still failed. I never attended a single recitation and got a 57 and a 55 on my first two exams. Passed the final with a 87 and got a C+ for the year haha. He gives a survey at the end for a lot of extra credit. I didnt do a lot of the aplia assignments either. EASY!!!
Class is worthless. I only went every friday because those are quiz days. Just do the practice quizzes/tests posted online and you'll do fine. I got Bs on everything and ended up with an A.
His course it very easy to get an A considering all the extra credits he's awarding.

Byrns is a likeable professor, although he is really sarcastic and appears to be a bit senile. This is a class where you feel like you are doing terribly, because the quizzes and online work are hard, but in the end is grading system coupled with extra credit gives you a much better grade than you expected.

While Byrns is a really fun and interesting person to talk to during his informal office hours, I found that his lectures didn't help too much, however entertaining they were, and my TA was useless. But even with a terrible understanding of economics and almost never reading, I managed to pass with a high C.

if you are in this class, DO NOT GO TO CLASS--read the book instead.  his lectures are entertaining, yet completely irrelevant to quizzes and tests.  the only reason i'm passing this class is because of my recitation leader.

Whoa this class was great. He is a very entertaining lecturer. This class is A LOT of work but if you are willing to do it, you will be fine. If you have common sense, it will be even easier because most of economics is common sense.

Byrns class is interesting. The material is not the easiest to grasp but by curving and dropping half the grades it makes it easy to get a good grade. DO YOUR BEST ON THE QUIZZES EVERY FRIDAY...I was exempt from the 2nd exam by passing all of my quizzes. As a teacher Byrns is the best, but the class I hate with a passion

dont take this class if youve never had econ before. he gets off topic in class. if econ is your thing, then he appears to be the best for you. go to review sessions and recitations. he drops half of aplia and quizzes and curves, but gives hard exams.

Ok, so I didn't go to the 9 AM MWF class that had a quiz every Friday. I went to every recitation, and I kind of grasped the material. If you look at practice tests and do the aplia, it will help. I failed the tests but still ended up with a C-
The class was awesome. You have to go to class, and do the work to get a good grade, but it is more than worth it. Byrns is great.

He's pretty cool. Gives lots of extra credit just for answering questions in class&&other random things. Dont HAVE to go to lectures[tho they aren't boring!] just do aplia assignments[really study those] and study practice quizzes and go to recitations. There are 2 books to choose from, a new blue one and the old one w/color pages--use the latter!
Highly entertaining lectures that include discussion of relevant current events and plenty of extra credit opportunities. I would recommend this course and professor to anyone.

The lectures were interesting and entertaining, but disorganized and hard to follow. He really made economics interesting and relevant. Exams are really hard, but there are recitations, study sessions, and he posts practice questions.

Byrns is a great guy. In a class of over 400 students, he takes the time to get to know people, and cares greatly for his students (he lent me a textbook). Byrns makes Economics interesting. I wouldn't have enjoyed, or went, to class otherwise. Material is hard, but I highly reccomend his class!
awesome

Byrns = entertaining. Lecture is a waste of time. The lectures & textbook didn't correspond (but next semester, I noticed he's using a different textbook). To get an A, just study the practice quizzes and study guides that are posted online. Be prepared for quizzes every Friday, & he drops half of your grades so don't stress about your grade.
Not the most organized professor, but incredibly easy to make a good grade.  Didn't open the book 5 times, used the practice tests online, and made an A.  Keeps lectures interesting with his stories.

If you adjust your learning style to his teaching, his class is easy. First of all, don't use whatever book he assigns you - use Byrns and Stone's "Economics", he uses it exclusively. Paying attention in class isn't necessary, just reading the book and not skipping the quizzes. Easy B or A

Byrns is a nice guy. Very entertaining, yet not a great teacher. I shouldn't have gotten up to go to class. Extremely unorganized. Everything I learned I taught myself thru the book. His lectures do not make any sense b/c he is so unorganized. I would not have him if you want a prof that will actually teach, if you want a standup routine, he's fine

Byrns is horrible with his organization . The students and the TA's do not know what he is rambling about it class.  You are forced to teach yourself economics through the text book.  This is not a clss for students that like organization because that is exactaly what Byrns isnt.

Not a class for those who are just "interested" in seeing what economics is like. Purely a textbook course since his lectures weren't beneficial to me. I feel like he's a guy who could retire, but instead wants to teach and thinks he can inspire kids to learn economics. In my case he completely deterred me.

Incredibly funny and entertaining, but serious when necessary.  Byrns is a great professor - be sure to talk to him outside of class.  Friday quizzes, just make sure you've read and done PRACTICE QUESTIONS off the website.

I HATE THIS CLASS! This year he has switched textbooks, but he still teachers out of the one he wrote and references it often, as do the TAs. So basically, don't ask what section in the book we're supposed to be on because no one knows.  He's unorganized and he's lectures are mostly entertaining stories, he's a cool guy, but a horrible professor!

I feel like Dr. Byrns really knows his stuff, he simply can't explain it well.  He comes into class and I understand everything, then he starts flipping charts and throwing up lots of letters.  I wish he could make things more clear, not more confusing!

He makes class interesting and it isn't really boring, but it's still pretty hard.  He wrote the book he uses, so most of his material is from it and the website.  USE THE PRACTICE QUIZZES ON HIS SITE!

Byrns is really funny but his lectures are impossible to learn from because they're so scattered. Weekly quizzes and online assignments a week which are hard- but he drops half of your grades so it's actually pretty easy to make a decent grade in this class. Also, Byrns likes to call on random people and embarrass them in front of the whole class.

There are weekly quizzes and a ton of online assignments, but he drops about half of your grades.  Almost all of his test and quiz questions can be found in the practice section on his website.  He is entertaining and loves to get to know students.  I highly recommend the class.  An A is completely possible, but you have to put some time in.

The class itself is often boring and not always helpful - I learned much more in recitations than I did in class. He gives a lot of extra credit. Quizzes every Friday (though there are more quizzes and homework grades than there are points that they're worth, so tons get dropped). You don't really have to read the book. Do his practice ?s!
he is hilarious, loves the subject and cares about the students...work hard and you will be rewarded!

Only go to class if you want to hear some entertaining stories or see someone look stupid.  Only go to recitations if they are giving out EC.  You do not have to read the book at all, only the 1 page summaries at the end of the book before quizzes, but do know this material.  Do all quizzes on his site and remember them and you will make an A, mayb

His lectures are not helpful unless you already know what he's talking about, which is difficult considering the pace of the course. You're expected to read A LOT each week and are quizzed every week, sometimes more than once. Economics comes easily to some students, but not everyone, and if it doesn't come easily to you...GOOD LUCK.

Byrns is the only reason to get up early in the morning for ECON. The way he desings the class is great. Your grade is directly correlated to the effort that you put in. I put in a B effort and I got a B. I know for a fact that if you put in an A effort, even though you are not amazing at ECON, you will get an A.

Byrns is really cool, funny to listen to, but lectures were awful.  It was probably just because I'm not an Econ major and that makes it difficult to sit through.  Make sure you do your aplia assignments and go to class on fridays to take the quizzes.  Recitation is optional but if you don't go to class, I would go to them.
Very smart and quick witted. Seems like a college student still himself except he really knows his Econ. Gives lots of extra credit and curves all tests. Loved the class.

Was entertaining for a while, until I got bored of hearing the same exact thing in the lectures as in the text (which he wrote).  Don't go to recitation, its optional.  Class pretty useless, he just scrawls stuff on the board and tells anecdotes, just go to class fri and take the quiz.  overall, easy to get an a or a b, esp with extra credit.

His exams and such are difficult and it is definitely a lot of work, but it is sooo worth it in the end.  DO THE EXTRA CREDIT and you will def. get an A.  recitation is useless, I'd recommend spending your time elsewhere.  amusing teacher, definitely take him!
You'll learn the subject and his class is hard so study...LOTS.

Take Byrns.  Its a lot of material, but he gives a lot of extra credit opportunity and makes it fairly easy to get an A.  You don't have to go to recitation, or lecture either except on quiz day. I seriously never went to class and got an easy A.  A nice guy, and very helpful website with a lot of study aids and practice quizzes.
No Comments

Don't go to lectures expecting to learn anything that will be on the test specifically.  Study all the old quizes and exams, do all the homework, read the book, try to do as much extra credit as possible, and you'll be guaranteed atleast an A or B.  Weekly quizes, midterms, and final are challenging - when in doubt, just use common sense(it works!)

Byrns' lectures are completely pointless. He goes off on tangents and he doesn't cover much of the material he tests on. His books are also outdated and even he admits they have errors. There are also a ton of assignments, but he does grade tests on a curve and he is always willing to talk to students.

Very good professor, goes off on tangents but he explains econ in a real life perspective. fun class, especially for the subject.  TAKE HIM!! quizzes every week, hard exams, but MASSIVE curves and extra credits. should be an easy A if you try.

Easiest Econ professor out there.  If you read the book, you don't need to go to class.  Enough he drops about half the assignments and quizzes.  Great review sessions before exams where he gives you all of answers.  Many extra credit opportunities.  Easy to get a B and not too hard to get an A.

Ok, so the class is a little hard, but he makes it as easy as possible to get a good grade.  He curves everything, you can exempt the first 2 exams, and he allows you to get 10% of your grade back through extra credit.  Economics is boring but he makes it fun with his own special examples.  It's also helpful that he uses his own book.

Class isn't very helpful, what he does say about econ in class is right from the book (that he wrote). But you need to go on Fridays for the weekly quiz, which is pretty hard. Lots of resources for help outside of class and lots of online assignments (which you have to pay for).  "Does that sound right?"  Worst class at UNC though so....

class is pretty hard, but if you study you should come out with a B due to his grading system.  gives a quiz everyweek which are usually pretty hard.  in lectures he just rambles and says exactly what is in the book so no need to go to class except to take the quizzes or exams.  overall pretty good.
good class. You definitely learn a LOT but it's not as structured, but whe makes it interesting and there are many chances for extra credit. Quiz and problem set every week.
Sure he's easy, and he wrote the book....which costs a million dollar btw. And he's interesting. But I didn't learn a damn thing.
the most interesting prof available for this class.

He makes Econ fun during lectures and relates a lot of things to basic everyday situations. He uses overhead for graphs and formulas, but lectures. He wrote the textbook, and lectures are near identical, so the book is a good supplement. More than enough recources to get an easy A. TAKE HIM!
Best prof for the worst class.  hard tests, but curves them generously and gives extra credit opportunities.

LOTS of extra credit opportunity. he's just a fun guy overall, uses amusing examples, and the fact that he wrote the text book is very helpful bc he explains the exact material you read. HIGHLY recommend him.
BLAH!!! Worst class EVER!!!
Completely disorganized and dense.
Best teacher I've ever had, makes 185 necessary for all Econ majors, in my opinion.
Wow. This guy makes econ cool. He wrote the book for his class so its really clear. He gives so much extra credit and curves generously. Dont take any other econ 10 prof at UNC.
Great prof.
No Comments
No Comments
gave low final grades, we complained and he changed them, dont bother writing about your true beliefs, youll only get a good grade if you write about what he agrees with

Papers shouldn't be hard but turning them in and then receiving harsh rubric afterwards. Grading not based on the quality of arguments, but simply how close we got to his."here's a 100 if you say exactly what I want, 0 if you miss anything" Made fun of me for stuttering in class and rolled his eyes. Horrible experience.

Reeve is brilliant. His lectures are incredibly insightful. The papers are sometimes difficult but he gives you plenty of opportunities to correct them and improve your grade. One thing to watch for, if you show up with a lot of enthusiasm or confidence, he'll give you more of a hard time than the other students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --So many papers

reviews.comment: Easy as long as you are willing to rewrite papers, he lets you rewrite as many times as needed to get a better grade. Very easy A. However, he's a specific personality and interrupts students after begging for involvement. The class itself was fairly easy, but I was frustrated with his inability to accept other ideas & students to fully conversate.

This class was an amazing, in-depth dive into Plato's "Republic" by one of its foremost scholars. Reeve is very passionate, and while getting good grades on the papers is tough, he gives excellent feedback and allows corrections. It's clearly his goal for you to gain a deep understanding, and he'll help you work toward the grade that you want!

Professor Reeve is an interesting person, but his class lacks structure and clear feedback. Grade is based on best 5 of 6 papers, but the texts are rarely discussed in lecture (focuses more on tangential discussion than paper topics). Heavily focused on your ability to dissect old literature and isolate factual evidence.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Reeve is quite possibly one of the most intelligent men alive. He is just bursting with information. He doesn't really care if you speak or not because he loves to be able to just share what he thinks and why. Do your readings, it'll help immensely. He only gives 2 grades a semester & no exams, so you'll need to do well but he wont let you fail.
Reeve is brilliant. Like super smart. He can teach you everything there is to know about Aristotle if you read and pay attention. He grades harshly and the papers are monstrous

Reeve thinks that he knows everything about everything. He tells some funny and intellectual jokes and I enjoyed his profanity, but as far as actually teaching things you need to know for the papers, he is super unproductive.

Reeve is a great, clear professor who really knows what he's talking about. He is pretty intimidating though, so if you don't have a good TA, your questions may not get answered. He very clearly outlines the readings so you don't really have to read the books, but the exams are not easy at all, unless you're pretty good at philosophy already.

Reeve is a joy to listen to and he really knows his stuff (and is quite aware that he knows it). Readings can generally be skipped if you attend lecture, but they can help to understand the material. This class can be a challenge if you don't think the way Reeve does, but if you do you're golden
This man radiates wisdom! And his lectures are laced with wit!
Best class and professor ever. It's tough if you aren't philosophically-minded. This class changed my minor to philosophy.

Reeve is a great professor and a captivating lecturer. Lots of reading is assigned, but it is not essential as long as you attend the lectures. Your grade is based off 3 five page papers which are graded by TAs, so try to select a good one.

Great at simply laying out major problems. Enjoyable lectures that were well delivered. Many mostly well-chosen assigned readings in this course. I am sure his other classes are more difficult--PHIL 112 (sometimes taught by others) is an introductory/overview course. He knows his Greek! And he can rattle off extensive quotes from various texts!

If you think it's fun or entertaining to mock religion (especially Christianity), take the class. I could barely get through many of the lectures and some of the readings because they were so derisive. I'm able to think critically about my beliefs in an academic way, but the tone of this class felt snarky and childish to me.
reeve is a genius
AWESOME PROFESSOR! always enthusiastic! He's not easy, but he's not trying to fail you. He honestly wants everyone to do well. Participate in class and you'll do fine.

Honestly, THE BEST professors I've had here.  If you don't like reading or are closed minded you probably won't enjoy the class.  If you are willing to challenge yourself some then you will GAIN SO MUCH.  I could sit and listen to him lecture all day. Don't go into the class looking for a grade, look for an experience and the grade will come.
He is awesome. Reeve brings in humour, and at the same time makes the students understand the coursework. The ease of the class varies greatly by your TA, so be careful there!

Reeve is a genius. Given the choice, I would spend every waking moment of my life in this man's shadow. He's completely off in his own world and if you can't handle that, you'll hate him. Don't expect to have a relationship with him other than basking in his presence from afar. This is definitely  my favorite class this semester.
This course is awesome, but the papers are tough. TA's can be a pain, but they make your grade. Go to them for paper help, and you will be fine.

easy class- the reading is good but if you don't want to do it just go to class and recitation. lecture is funny and interesting. papers can be frustrating because there's not much room for your own ideas/interpretation. if you listen in lecture and write what reeve said or what your ta thinks then your grade will be fine. overall an easy A

class is good, lectures are pretty interesting. a LOT of reading that can be avoided for the most part if you listen in lecture and recitation. if you have any views contrary to the professor/TA be prepared to change them or get a poor grade. papers were graded very harshly, some TAs dont even give As, final was easy.
Very interesting and funny.  Requires a lot of reading, usually not very interesting but the lectures clarify everything.
Prof Reeve had great energy and made lectures interesting.
Great, interesting lecturer. Would definately recommend!

GREAT CLASS and GREAT PROFESSOR. I had very little interest in Philosophy, yet Reeve's lectures are so engaging that it became my favorite class. Although I didn't undestand everything, Reeve's lectures and the materials are interesting and I definately would recommend this class.
Reeve is spectacular.
Awesome professor. Best lecturer so far! Very interesting and insightful. A++ would definately take another class taught by him.
This was a small seminar with reeve and a whole lot of fun.  he's a funny guy and the stuff we talked about was extremely interesting and he is very smart.
this guy ****in rules
The best class/teacher i have ever had at this school.  Ignoring the fact that he is brilliant, the man is f-ing hilarious in lecture.  Very interesting anf griping lecturer.
It's all Prof. Reeve. Said to be brilliant. I'd say self-absorbed..

First time teaching this class, but very poorly done. Not all of the material went together well, the tests were not a good test of performance, and the TAs were out to lunch all semester. Take small classes with this guy, not big ones.

Brilliant man, but that's about it. He sexualizes all lectures, does not prepare you for tests, and once compared himself to GOD. the worst class i have ever taken at this school. but if you are a phil major, the man is brilliant.

Brilliant and incredibly interesting lecturer.  Most personal contact involved a TA, but his lectures are awesome and the tests, while hard, are strongly curved.  The papers were a little confusing but graded very fairly.  Take any class you can with him.
Excellent philosopher and lecturer.  Does not coddle students.
No Comments
Other professors claim he doesn't read students work and thus assigns grades randomly.  Witnessed him belittling students in every course I had with him.  He is brilliant, for what its worth.

Great professor who is passionate about material and intent on helping his students learn. Students could turn essays in again after reviewing feedback which was extremely helpful. Occasionally a little confusing with class schedule or due dates, but would always correct it and ensure everything was fair for students.

I only took this course because of the major requirement but thought Kyle was a great teacher. I am not super into philosophy and wouldn't have taken this if it wasn't required, but Kyle had nothing to do with that. He is accessible and willing to work with you if you are with him. The grading system was slightly confusing but overall good prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Mr. Cessna is very passionate about philosophy and managed to make a dry course relatively entertaining. You can tell he really cares about students and wants to see people succeed. His grading criteria is very clear and he provides constructive feedback on submissions.

I think the class is really easy, and it's not hard to get good grades if you actually try. Yes, sometimes we have to do unnecessary busywork, but Professor Seifert is pretty accommodating for most things and is pretty nice.

Super easy A for me. Just do what you're supposed to and you'll be fine. Class was mostly developing a research project over a semester, which wasn't too stressful, and the grading wasn't too tough either.

Celeste is a good teacher. She was very kind to me throughout the semester and tried to make lectures very interesting. Although if you look at the learning outcome from engl 105 then she is not the one. She is easy grader but you wont learn anything in this class.
Can come off as rude sometimes whether they intend to or not. Not much homework though. Not much they can do though its an english class

Easy class but professor is incredibly rude and condescending. Honestly treats students like they are in middle school. She is an easy grader but if you are looking for a respectful and mature professor I do not recommend. Also coming to class was the biggest waste of time, she would take 20-30 minutes on an activity that should take 5.

Don't take this class! They grade easy with a lot of papers, but if you want a teacher that will be at least a little bit respectful this is not for you. Celeste is rude and treats us like children. at points they were very rude when answering a simple question. I never wanted to participate in this class because of how discouraged I felt.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: English 105 with Prof Seifert is exactly what it should be. She is really sweet and understanding. She grades based on specific criteria and is helpful if you need guidance. I would totally recommend her!!

Engl 105 is a boring class but Seifert seemed to care about making it somewhat engaging for her students. The assignments take very little time and the grading is extremely lenient. Class is incredibly boring but I think that has to do with Engl 105, not the professor. She did get frusturated at times when people asked questions.

Classes are extremely boring and unnecessarily drawn out. Powerpoints each time where every line is read verbatim. Prof. Seifert is fine-- she usually is willing to help but sometimes she goes off on students when they ask too many questions

Professor Seifert has by far been my least favorite professor at UNC. ENGL105 is meant to be any easy class for freshmen to take and get through but Seifert makes the class unnecessarily complicated. She is unbelievably condescending and rude to her students. For a grad student, she has a very high ego.

Dr. Ceballos is a great professor and makes 207 super easy to understand while also teaching you a lot of useful information. Exams are very fair and are designed "for a bad day", so she makes it very easy to do well in the class. Homeworks can get a little tedious but you work in groups, and they prepare you well for the exams too.

She is a great lecturer and takes the time to review everything you need for the class. Exams are very straightforward with lots of partial credit given just for attempting. Super caring and seemed to actually enjoy teaching.

Dr. Ceballos is an enthusiastic professor and helpful professor. Her notes are always organized and well-explained. Her homeworks prepare you extremely well for her exams, since her exams are always easier than the homework. There are times when she goes over her notes too quickly during class, but she posts them online in a timely manner.

She's so nice and genuinely cares about her students. The material can be hard sometimes but thankfully, the homework overprepares you for the midterms and final too. Labs aren't too bad either, are graded leniently. Homeworks are long though so start on those early if you can.

I had her for both BMME 207 (circuits) & 365 (systems & signaling). She is an amazing professor that understands that the topics can be hard. Because of this, homework can sometimes be on the heavy side, but is always worth while and amazing test prep. Never grades harshly and always is clear for dates of tests or due dates.

I had Dr. Ceballos for BMME 207 and she was amazing! I was really scared about the class going in but she took the time to explain the basics really well. She had amazing methods for solving circuits which I had never seen before in other classes. The exams are based off of the homework she provides. I can't recommend this class enough!!!

She is my favorite professo!! She is so sweet and you can tell she is very passionate about what she teaches. While she can be lecture heavy, her lectures are engaging if you are interested in the class. She has a great sense of humor, is incredibly intelligent, and will draw on her own personal life experience which I think is valuable. 10/10 imo.

She is super sweet and passionate about the material! The only thing is that she doesn't really grade anything throughout the semester, so you won't really know what your grade is until the end. The lectures aren't super discussion based, but mostly her just lecturing, but she explains concepts pretty well.

In the kindest way possible, CMG is very disorganized. She is very passionate about the topic however the whole class is confusing. Unclear grading criteria, putting incorrect answers on exams, etc. She is impossible to reach on email, and we don't even know what our grade is in the class. It sucks because she's a great person but not disciplined.

She's passionate and very sweet but very hard to reach outside of class. Your grade is hidden the whole semester and you can not even calculate your own grade most of the time because she never grades most of her things. Midterms can be tricky, just study your notes hard because some of the questions are really specific.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: She is very passionate and kind but is not clear on grading criteria and refuses to open her email and respond to any questions. Only way to reach her is genuinely in class after the lecture. Super sweet but no sick days or absences so make sure you show up.

Interesting class, grade based mostly on low-stakes assignments. Do the readings/daily discussion questions, participate in class, and write a current event for basically half of your grade. The other half is a 5pg essay, group podcast, and 3 tests (multiple choice, short answer on final). She is super knowledgeable and made the class enjoyable!

She was a good professor who made the content and class interesting. However, if you like knowing what your grade is, don't take this class. She hasn't released any grades, and it's the day of the final exam. She also tends to make tests tricky, saying that there could be more than 1 right answer, but that she's looking for something specific.

She was going through some personal things this semester, so sometimes the class was erratic. In general, she is a good prof, but with all over-the-place lectures and focuses on things that fit her worldview, but which might not necessarily be the full story. Still, she's sweet and willing to work with you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Martinez-Gallardo could be all over the place sometimes in lectures, but it is strictly because she is passionate about the course material. I had a great time in this class. 55% of the grade is participation, so show up to class and pay attention to get a good grade. Basically, if you do the readings and discussions, you will succeed.

Poli 434 was a very easy class. 55% of the grade came from either attendance or assignments that were graded on completion. She takes attendance but does so randomly. As long as you show up to class and turn things in you will get an A or an A-.

She lectured a lot and would go off on tangents that meant we didn't cover all the material in class. Her lectures were also a little hard to follow at times. Overall tho, I learned a lot abt Mexican politics and feel informed enough to speak on current events. She gives lots of little low-stakes assignments. Its a lot of work but not too hard.
I absolutely loved profesora Martinez-Gallardo. She is so passionate about Latin American politics, and was so so kind. I'm taking her POLI-434 course this Spring, and I'm super excited!
Tedious lectures. Irresponsive professor. We didn't know any of our grades until right after the final. Pretty disorganized as well. Easy material, but the grading style was a little odd.

The absolute cutest. I love this woman. She's so caring, kind, and involved. Really stresses mental health and learning to learn, very flexible. Totally recommend her Poli 238 (latin america) or Poli 434 (mexico)!

She is clearly passionate and knowledgeable about Latin American politics, and that can come through by means of information overload - she sometimes gets lost in all the things she wants to say. However, she is very sweet, clearly cares about her students, and will give you plenty of opportunities to bring your grade up. Easy grader!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Gallardo-Martinez is super sweet, caring, and understanding. Lots of extra credit. Pretty easy course. Lecture heavy. Overall, pretty ok course, which I enjoyed it more.

Professor was respectful, knowledgeable, and understanding. This class is a good foundation for contemporary Latin American politics. Readings for this class were accessible, and the due dates were clear as well. I would suggest paying attention to the readings and studying reading questions will prepare you other topics and exams.

Super sweet, caring, and loves the topic. I recommend taking this class especially if you're a Poli Sci major! Cons: readings can be long, exams have few questions (but are fairly easy), she's a little disorganized and can get off topic Overall I def liked it, lots of EC, interesting topics, sweet woman!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Great professor. CMG was always willing to help and her class was very engaging.

CMG shifted the class so that 35% of course grade comes from participation--which I think was supposed to make it easier (given COVID), but actually just culminated in the expectation that you do like 100 forum posts over the course of the semester. The whole class is tedious busy work and is not very interesting. Take HIST 242 with M. La Serna.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: CMG is great! very kind and caring during COVID times. Lectures can drag if you're not interested in the material, but the content is very interesting! Midterm and Short paper and Final not too difficult. Discussion posts before every class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: She's truly amazing! In COVID times, she really understood that her class couldn't always be a mental priority for us. The class is very much based on paying attention to the notes so you get out of the class what you put in. The exams are very straightforward if you pay attention. I adore Prof. Martínez Gallardo as an instructor and as a person.

She really cares about her students' mental health and is not a harsh grader. I managed an A in both the midterm & final and studied 1hr for each. So long as you keep up w the little assignments it's not a difficult class! She's a great person in general & very knowledgeable about the content

A gem. She is very understanding of Covid plus gave us days where we chose to make class optional because of outside factors. Knows sooo much about Latin America. Participate and do the discussion questions and you should be good. Her paper is easy and midterm was quite simple. Overall a great professor.

great professor, sometimes a bit unclear but was always willing to answer questions. willing to stay after class. a bit hard to reach at times. PARTICIPATE in class discussions, she really cares about that. nice person who was willing to work with you if you had issues. if you do the readings, and the assignments (not many) you should be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: CMG is a real gem! Although this semester was hectic with things moving online due to COVID-19, she always made sure to let students know that she was available. Her lectures are engaging and even though the reading can be extensive at times, it is interesting if you enjoy Latin American politics. One paper, participation, a midterm, and a final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She is a nice teacher, and is very passionate about the material. Her grading rubric is clear, 25% participation, 25% midterm, 25% paper, and 25% final. If you skim the readings and take notes in class, you'll do fine.

Prof. Gallardo's class was impactful and engaging. She isn't always clear about what readings you need to be doing, but you definitely don't need to do all of them, just pay attention to her lectures. Her exams were difficult but the subject matter was fascinating and she really knows her stuff. All in all a very nice woman and cool professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Caring

reviews.comment: I cannot stress how there are only four grades in the entire class. You cannot do bad on one assignment if you want to do well in the class. The subject matter is very interesting but CMG seems very out-of-it in class. She gets off topic quickly and very often. Lectures were long and often boring. Don't take unless needed for your major.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Kind of disorganized, focusing more on themes which makes the exams harder to study for. Easy paper. Very similar to her other course on LA.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: CMG is a really nice and funny person, but her teaching could use some work. You only have 4 grades in the class and chances are, you won't know what your final grade is until it's too late. Her powerpoints are extremely vague and the information you need she will mention while speaking. Her tests are hard and test specific parts of lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Enthusiastic and knows her stuff, but she can get carried away with students asking questions sometimes. There weren't many powerpoints so you have to come to lecture and pay attention. Group podcast project that was pretty fun and laid back. She takes attendance randomly which counts towards participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Not a good professor. Boring long lectures but goes through the power points so quickly you cant write anything down. Very vague about what is on the tests and there's only 3 grades in the whole semester so if you mess up on test you will not do well. Don't take this class with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: CMG is super knowledgable about what shes talking about. That means theres a lot of talking during lectures. I love that because I'm passionate about the topic, but if you don't really care, it might seem like class drags on forever. The class has a nice flow. Her grading criteria isn't clear, but if you pay attention and go to class, youll be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Pleasantly surprised by this class, its structure, content ( countries and corresponding themes) were clear, relevant, + interesting. I liked that lectures were accompanied by a powerpoint (I hated this at first). If you print them out, write in the margins, and then review, you'll be gold! All in all, good intro. into this part of the world!
Preparedness for class did not appear to be a top priority for Professor Martinez-Gallardo. She has excellent credentials but seemed out of touch with the subject matter... Easy class though.

I thought she was awesome and very knowledgable about the material. Not sure how much I actually got out of the class, but you get out what you put in. Not very difficult, attendance not mandatory, you just have to write a couple long papers. She was also very caring and nice to me when I had personal issues going on during her class. Recommend!
The worst teacher I have had at UNC. She is disorganized, doesn't clarify what's on the tests and does not help in office hours and is forcing you out as soon as you walk in.

This class is not too difficult if you go to the lectures.  She goes everything from the readings that you need to know in the lectures and the recitations were helpful.  She can talk a bit fast, but her lectures are very comprehensive and helpful to doing well in the class.

Professor Martinez Gallardo can talk a little fast at times, but she is trying to cover a lot of material for POLI 238. Her lectures were generally clear and easy to follow. She is a solid, average professor and I would recommend her and her class to a friend. Nothing very negative or very wonderful to say about her.
I don't know why everyone gives her such a negative review. Honestly, CMG is an excellent professor, scholar, and and lecturer. I loved her class.
Scattered, disorganized, rambling. Sure she's nice and friendly, but boy is she a bad teacher.
I really enjoyed my 238 class with this professor.  She lectures with energy and is very knowledgeable about the topic.  Also, she's very kind to students.  I highly recommend this professor.

She is very much focused on key concepts and points, so if she makes sense to you then there isn't much need to do the reading (except for participation). Spend time on the essays, they count for a lot and help you understand the content better. Given the broad and slightly dull subject, I still enjoyed the class overall because of her and the TAs.

Overall, I liked her. She is extremely friendly and helpful. Some parts of her lectures were unclear to people, but the textbook helped clarify things tremendously. TAs were great too. Papers were easy, but the exams were pretty tough. If you want to take Poli 238, take it with Cecilia.

I was kind of excited for this class, but her lectures are really scattered. The TAs overall were good, the class was curved, and it was relatively easy, but expectations are very unclear. Not a very good class, overall.

I was so excited to take this class. Unfortunately, I learned nothing from her. Thankfully her TA's were good. Her exam grading rubrics are ridiculous. This class is a pretty easy B, but you wont learn much because her lectures are terrible and irrelevant to LA Politics. So disorganized and unclear expectations.
This course took exactly as much effort as it should have. Was a little difficult at times but none of the work felt unnecessary. Fair grader and funny, good energy in class.
Super nice and helpful, in class and during office hours! French 203 is pretty grammar heavy, but she does a good job incorporating cultural knowledge and conversation skills.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Ruel is genuinely the sweetest woman. She's definitely a tough grader but pushes you to be the best you can at French. She has so much advice for learning a new language, but her lectures are a bit boring. The small classes force participation but since she only teaches from the textbook the classes can get repetitive and easily skippable.

FREN 203 is a hard class, but Prof. Ruel makes it a lot of fun! Legitimately one of the sweetest and most compassionate people I've ever met. Native French speaker, speaks clearly and at a reasonable pace (speaks slowly during listening quizzes).

I love Prof. Ruel- take her for a language if you can. Normally these courses are taught by PhD students and it is so much better to have her- she is a good grader. She's as French as they get and does a great job getting everyone to speak. Our class has such a fun time speaking about all things French but she still covers content needed for exams.

Prof Ruel is awesome. She is so quintessentially French. She can come off a little intimidating and snarky, but she is actually so sweet. She's always available to meet one on one and encouraged me to speak in French more.

Actually for FREN 204 but that wasn't an option. 
I have very mixed feelings about this class- the class isn't hard but she grades very strictly with grammar. I must emphasize, YOU HAVE TO PARTICIPATE TO DO WELL, my good grades were correlated with how much I participated. It's not an easy course, but she's a sweet prof.

I took Roml-89 with Professor Ruel, she is kind but I did not appreciate her teaching style. Professor Ruel barely graded assignments, she also is unclear with instructions and talks in circles. Although the course is called French Coastal Ecologies, we barely focused on the environment of the coast and instead talked extensively about culture.

I am finishing up FREN204 with Dr. Ruel now and took FREN203 with her last year- there's a reason I signed up for her section again! She is passionate, engaged, and helpful. She welcomes participation from everyone and I never felt afraid to speak French in her class, even if I made mistakes. Always participate and listen to her feedback.

Prof Ruel is great she really cares about all her student's success and is super nice. Grading is very fair and theres a lot of assignments/ways to improve your grade. She's super accessible and encourages participation but doesn't put people on the spot. 100% recommend I'd absolutely take her classes especially for higher lvls!

I am currently taking her class again for fren 300; she is very caring and genuinely wants students to do well. She grades fairly. She encourages participation and she is very accessible outside of class and willing to help if you need any assistance!

Madame Ruel is so sweet. 203 is a relatively challenging course but Madame Ruel understands this and really appreciates any effort that you put into the class. She likes participation but won't cold-call. Email her if you have any issues and she's happy to fix it or help. (No extra credit)

I really enjoyed prof Ruel she was really understanding and took the time to explain concepts (she uses PowerPoint). While participation matters she does not force everyone to speak rather she lets you decide what you want to do. She is not too tough of a grader either. She also seems to care for her student's wellbeing.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: great professor to have for a language class. She was very organized and because she is a native french speaker, she helped out a lot with learning the language. Isn't a tough grader and encouraged learning french through speaking it, and didn't make you feel bad about messing up.

Dr. Ruel can come off as a bit intimidating at first but she is a great person and teacher. The flipped classroom style is not for me but she still was a good teacher in the class. Just participate, do the homework and show up and you should be fine
Dr. Ruel is very kind, understanding, and honest. Exams and quizzes are not bad if you study, and she is fairly lenient in terms of grading. Highly recommend Dr. Ruel.

prof ruel is such a sweetheart. her grading is very spread out (hw, quizzes, essays, assignments) which means if you're bad at one thing that doesn't mean you're doomed. she is very open to working one on one in office hours and helpful when you ask her to explain something. the content is pretty difficult but she makes it possible.

Prof. Ruel was so sweet and caring, and when I struggled with concepts she was more than happy to explain everything and help me practice. She's super respectful and genuinely wants you to learn French, and bc of Covid she was also super flexible with deadlines. I hate French, but she's one of the best profs I've had so far.
Prof. Ruel is really sweet and is pretty helpful in understanding French. She will push you in the right direction without being mean about mistakes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Ruel is a solid choice for FREN 300, she explains concepts well and gives good feedback. I also appreciated her flexibility with moving deadlines for individual circumstances. My only complaint is that during the first half of the class she would consistently go 5-10 min over time during the online lectures to finish her slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The class was daunting at first because it is in French and she is a native French speaker with a strong accent. However, I really feel like I have grown in my listening and speaking skills significantly. It is not scary to speak in class as she guides easy conversations about prevalent topics without pressure of a right/wrong opinion.
