She speaks entirely in French but encourages participation and grades easily. I recommend speaking up every class and doing the homework, but other than that youll be fine with minimum studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Celina is very fun! Energetic and engaging, she worked very hard to get everyone to participate in conversation and join discussions. Lots of readings, and participation matters a lot. Very little homework (other than reading before each class), and she's a very lenient and kind grader. Class content was boring sometimes but she made it enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment:
Profe Larios is so much fun. She creates a welcoming environment for students of all different Spanish levels to practice speaking. As far as 255 goes it is much more difficult than it was presented in 204.
Class time is fun but there are additional quizzes, projects, and large papers that are not related to speaking at all.
I had quite a bit of difficulty with SPAN203. Profe Larios worked hard to make sure her students understood the material. She was a fairly tough grader on things that I felt were subjective.

BIOL 545 was one of my favorite courses at UNC, largely in part to Dr. Shiau's teaching.  The 3-hour class structure was sometimes a little hard to sit through (not her fault), but she did her best to make the entire lecture engaging.  Literature-based teaching style was great and I would definitely take the course again.

Dr. Shiau was clearly passionate about the material, but lacked organizational skills. The class material was incredibly interesting and the small class size was great, but I often felt like she emphasized small details rather than the big picture. Overall, she is a great person, but the 3 hr lecture format of this class was not ideal.
Dr shiau was nice and helpful when needed but the class period was long. Class was also generally interesting with lots of topics. I think she treated students equally

Professor Shiau is a very nice person, however her teaching style can be difficult to grasp. Her exams are very straightforward and directly off the slides, and while long, her GRQs do prepare you well for class. She genuinely cares about her students, but her lack of practice exam questions can make studying for the first exam difficult.

This class is a challenging class. The way that she taught was very different from the first professor in the class, which is why her first exam is so hard. She is very lecture-heavy on exams, while I prefer textbook heavy. She also makes every class worth a bit. I don't think she is a bad professor, just different from the first half.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Nice and knowledgeable, but exams were tough. Required you to know very specific details and processes from her slides, but she said that she wanted us to remember concepts from her class moving forward, which makes sense. Use GRQs to get a sense of the topic, and then gain more information in class. Not a lot of content, just a lot of specifics.
All I can say is I do NOT recommend this professor. Shoutout to the first half of the semester for my grade.
Reading chapters is a terrible way to learn the material. I guess her slides are your best bet to do well in the class.

Dr. Shiau is an incredibly caring professor and is well-versed in developmental biology. Lectures were consistently interesting, though the material was often dense. Exams are difficult, but they're taken from her slides, so they're doable. Overall, great professor.

Previous ratings of Dr. Shiau are so misleading. She is a great professor. GRQs take up a lot of time if you really want to understand the material but worthwhile. Sounds like a you problem if you are not understanding the material. This is not an easy class but she managed to cut down on the material we need to learn for each exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Shiau is a nice professor that tries to make herself accessible to students. However, she is not an effective teacher. She speeds through lectures, and her explanations are vague, unclear, and will change. Best thing to do for this class is to get ready to read and teach yourself from the textbook. Exams were not bad at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Truly terrible class and professor. Dr. Shiau is super sweet and approachable in her one office hour, but cannot teach to save her life. Class was a waste of everyone's time as she could not convey a single idea. Textbook readings are awful and dense, but she tests from readings. If she's the only choice, take this class another semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Her lectures are very disorienting. She would not explain things clearly and would change her mind mid-sentence about what she saying. Class did not seem worth the time because nothing in the ppts connected and lecture was more about answering questions than learning the material. Lots of reading in a VERY dense textbook that had excessive content
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: This class straight sucks. Ms. Shaiu was not rude but at the same time she sucked. Lectures were not well prepared and questions in the classroom never felt fully answered. I would avoid at all costs unless you are prepared to learn all the material on your own using a source other than the textbook as it wasnt all that helpful

Not the best lecturer but certainly not the worst. She seems like a nice person and laughs but has a hard time conveying ideas clearly. Tests are reading heavy so if you do the reading and know all the GRQs she assigns, you should be fine, but it's a lot of reading. It's a difficult course to begin with but has vagueness doesn't make it any easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: AVOID AT ALL COSTS. If you want to accept the greater challenge and see how well you can teach yourself, then this class is just for you. If you have common sense, then drop this class, this school, and this life. Just quit.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: So amazing!! Please take this class if you have a chance, we learned SO much and Professor Cedamanos is an incredible teacher. Even if you struggle with Spanish she is so kind and accommodating while also pushing you to try your best. Learning Quechua as a language and a culture has been such a treat take this class!!! Fun projects as well!!
Very great in class with clear lectures and examples. Helped a lot with gestures when learning. There was a lot of homework and the class did move pretty quickly.

She is very nice and the content is not super difficult. The problem is that she grades much harsher on the pronunciation assessments compared to other teachers in the section. All in all she isn't terrible, just try to get Professor Lindquist instead if possible

Span 105 moved very quickly, about 1 unit/3 days. However, Prof. Cedamanos was a very kind and approachable person. She is a picky grader, and very detail-oriented. You must participate several times each class to get a good grade! Much of the pacing is out of her hands, but she follows it closely, so make sure not to miss any assignments!

Dr. Regester is very knowledgable about African History! The class is very lecture heavy and does not have any slides, so going to class is important. Grading policies can be unclear at times. I found the topics to be very interesting and I learned so many  things about the African Diaspora.
She is so kind but one of the hardest classes I have ever taken. The tests are incredibly specific and hard to study for.
Such a sweet and knowledgeable person but such a hard class. I really wish I did not take it even though at times it's been interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Regester teaches you what you must know for exams, but you cannot miss class. All notes are spoken and you will not get them if you do not attend. The paper guidelines are unclear as she gave me an underserved grade because she did not like my word choice and had no comments on my thesis or supporting arguments. Find another gen ed to take.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I loved taking her class (Fall 2023). I will say that taking good notes is required, as the test questions come straight from the topics she puts on her slides...and her slides were not available outside of class. So attendance was required. I loved her class though, all I needed to do was make in depth flash cards and I was good to go on exams.

There is no clear outline for what we will do each day, so you won't know if we are taking notes or watching a movie that day. If you miss a day of notes, you could do really poorly on the exams. She is a very tough grader and doesnt give study guides, which makes the tests really difficult no matter how much you prepare. Lots of athletes in class

Dr. Regester is an overall nice lady and compelling speaker, however, she doesn't prepare students well for exams. Attendance is MANDATORY because if you miss a single lecture it could be potentially detrimental to your performance on the exams. She has no class slides, so when taking notes, you must listen and copy every word she says verbatim.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE. THERE ARE MUCH EASIER GEN EDs. She grades the papers and exams EXTREMELY harshly. All the class content is also given orally, with no slides or notes to look on if you're sick and miss class. Overall, this class is very boring, and the grading is unbelievably unreasonable, with points being deducted for the most miniscule things.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Rarely ever showed up and passed. All assignments are papers, which she graded unnecessarily harsh for movie reviews. It's hard to achieve her analytical standards. All of class was spent watching movies or popcorn reading the readings that had been assigned. Find another AAAD/FYS class that you may actually learn something from. Waste of time.

Everything on the tests are from lectures and there is nowhere to find what was on each lecture other than being there and trying to catch every little thing she says in your notes. Attendance and paying attention to every word that comes out of her mouth is pretty much mandatory to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She was very unclear on assignment due dates and grading guidelines. Extremely hard to get in touch with you outside of class. I will never take another course with her. No extra credit and the entire grade is based on 3 papers. EXTREMELY hard grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Enjoyed the class content, but your grade is based off of three papers and the feedback is very vague.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
She is a great Proffesor but the grading is very harsh. Not an easy A, but a very intersting class. 
If you like writing papers- I reccomend!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Regester is very sweet and hilarious. This class is eye-opening and I would recommend it to someone who isn't just doing it for the gen-ed. I say this because this class is definitely not worth the VP credit, there is an excessive amount of papers (1 pg per wk, 2 7-9 pg papers). Dr. Regester values creativity even if your writing isn't great!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Very intelligent, funny, and caring! However, yes, theres tons of work :( 2 large (7-8pgs) papers, weekly 1pg critiques (although for completion, & can b double spaced), plus a lengthy midterm n final. Values creativity & unique ideas over all - if u can do that in yr papers ur fine. Lots of reading, but not mandatory - just pay attention in class!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Regester is one of the most engaging professors I've ever seen. She constantly wants the class to respond/interact with the material being presented during discussions. Your entire grade is based off of 3, 5 page papers that analyze different sets of films. Overall, this is an interesting class, but definitely not an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE HARDEST CLASS EVER. 4 major assignments (2 papers & 2 exams) each one is at least 7-8 pages. Honestly this class was not worth it. I love her as a professor because she is the sweetest thing and extremely intelligent, but she can't have a life outside of this with all the work assigned.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Regester is the nicest lady and super fun. However, this FYS is not an easy A as your whole grade is based on 3 papers with vague explanation of why you got the grade you did.

The material in this class was interesting & thought provoking. But the work load was INSANE. There's about 5 diff. readings /week (each 30 pgs give or take), watch a film every week & write a 1pg critique, two 10pg papers(graded harshly), & then the midterm/final are both 5 pgs of writing as well. DON'T take this if you have a heavy schedule!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--So many papers

reviews.comment: Proffesor Regester is very passionate about this class. We watched a lot of good films. The second half of the class is so much better than the first half. It's pretty hard to get an A though. I never really understood how to improve my grade and you need to come up with a creative idea. Your grade is based on the midterm, final, and two papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I took this class during the pandemic and she was very accommodating! We had four papers and weekly discussion forums. We did read a lot, but this class was very easy as long as you read enough to answer the essay prompts and followed her feedback. I would have did better in the class if I had spaced out my readings a lot more!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Would never take again. Class itself and topic would be interesting if the class structure wasnt so scattered. The lectures dont relate to the work for the week and the context in the lectures is not relevant. The amount of reading each week is insane and unmanageable and often not helpful for the assignments. Syllabus isnt helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Regester is amazing! She is hilarious, and genuinely wants her students to thrive. She will definitely push you to develop original ideas, which can be challenging, but her class really helps you hone that critical skill. Dr. Regesters passion and caring are evident. Take her class, you will never watch a movie in the same way again!

Took this class as a first-year seminar hoping it would be an interesting and easy class. It's pretty interesting and we don't do anything in class except watch movies. But DO NOT take this class for an easy A. Your entire grade is based off 3 papers which she grades extremely harshly and seems to take off points just for the sake of it

Her tests are the hardest I've taken at UNC. If you don't remember every part of an ID, you won't get full credit, even if you are correct. If you don't use every related vocabulary word on her essays, you lose points. I remember getting an 85 on a test only to check my answers to find that I did not write down any incorrect information whatsoever.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The exams are based off of mostly what comes out of her mouth. Tends to take off points for the sake of taking points off and when you go to her office hours, she cannot give you a legitimate reason why. Some of the stuff that she says is sexist, homophobic. This was for a gen-ed. If you can find someone else, do it. Regester is n't worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Regester is really funny and the movies were really interesting. BUT for a first year seminar she made it really hard to get an A. Your whole grade is based on 3 papers and she took points off just to take them off. It's not hard to get a B in the class but her random point deduction made an A difficult. Participating was also pretty awkward.

Dr. Regester is my favorite professor at UNC. She expects the best from her students, expects us to really think and come up with our own ideas. That can be hard but very rewarding. The class was graded on 3 papers and the final 1% was critiques. But, interesting films, fantastic discussions, and no tests. She is very smart and willing to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Regester was thorough in her lectures. The course contained A LOT of material which requires extensive reading however, the more you know from the readings and lectures, the better your success will be for the exams. There were two major papers in the course (25% ea), a midterm & final. I recommend going to her office hrs for help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Regester is a great professor. Her lectures are interesting and she asks you many questions about your opinions on films. We have weekly one page papers due that arent that hard to write if you pay attention in class. There is also extra credit for attending other screenings of movies. Midterm paper and Final paper are heavy but she gives you ideas
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Regester's class was not inherently challenging, but the tests were extraordinarily difficult and require hours of prior studying of the readings and lecture notes, the latter of which are regurgitated to you at break-neck speeds. Take good notes, show up every day, and get ready to have a sore wrist after taking one of her outrageous exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Professor Regester is very knowledgeable in her field and a passionate lecturer. However, her tests are scary difficult. Just looked at your phone to check the time? BAM - you just missed the who, what, when, where, and why of the whole lecture. Take good notes, do as many readings as you can, and try your best. The class is not impossible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Hardest class I've taken in my life. Prof Regester's tests are brutally difficult, demanding you to recall specifics from either her long lectures or thousands of pages of assigned texts. If you're a good reader and listener, however, you'll get a good grade. She's a passionate and energetic lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The hardest class I have ever had to take for a gen-ed credit. She assigns so many readings about 100 pages long for a two day period. The lectures are chock full of information and you need to show up to each and every one. She has no clear grading criteria on her exams (in which you'll only have two). Pay attention and try your best.

After you've acclimated to the weekly readings, you will be fine. The lectures are average, a lot of information to learn. Tests are not hard, but you have to remember important characters name, and not their actions/contributions.
Dr. Regester is willing to help you out as much as she can. She's incredibly knowledgeable about her craft but she doesn't dismiss your ideas and has no chip on her shoulder. And she's funny as hell.
She's very passionate. Pay attention to lectures because most of the test material comes directly from her mouth. If she can tell that you are trying then you will do well.

You cannot graduate from Carolina without taking one of her classes! Although the workload seems too much at first, the class is what you make of it and she will put forth just as much (if not more) effort into your education. She is very passionate about her work and it will rub off on you!

Great teacher! Though she comes off as a harda** to a certain extent, she's extremely helpful and informative. Did I mention she's hilarious? The class is slightly challenging ) but if you attend class and take notes it'll be a breeze. Her film class was probably one of my fav classes at UNC. Highly recommend her Black film course!! Enjoy

Professor Regester was a good teacher who explained the materials clearly. Expect to take notes the whole class while she lectures, it'd be helpful if you bring your laptop to class, sometimes she does talk too fast. The tests are a little challenging because some of the identifications are very obscure, but if you study, you'll be fine.
IF you are an athlete or male--beware of Ms. Regester, she has a chip on her shoulder.

Dr. Regester is a great teacher. She is extremely knowledgeable and her classes are always interesting. If you really want to learn something and want to be challenged, I'd recommend taking one of her classes.
Loved the class!  Can't wait to take her film class.  Great person.  Easy to talk to but firm and straight forward.
Dr. Regester is amazing!  She is extremely well informed, her class is challenging and interesting, and she is a lot of fun.  This was on of the best classes I've taken.

His lectures are very funny and engaging, but he can go off track at times, which makes some concepts harder to follow. His presentations can also be difficult to study from. The class overall felt manageable, but much of the grading (including the midterm and final) was done by TAs, so your experience may depend on your TA.

Christian Lundberg was my favorite professor out of the 3 for IDST132L. The class, however, is very TA dependent as the midterm and final are graded by them. Very fun class to listen to, most of the readings you won't have to read, but there are a select few (they will make sure you know which) that you should read.

He's just a genuinely great guy, and super personable. I'm taking one of his classes next semester. Probably one of UNC's best profs. His lectures are really interesting too, he's a great public speaker. I had a great TA as well, and just thought it was a good class. I always attended his lectures, even with attendance not being mandatory.

Dense readings here and there, but he had the most interesting and applicable viewpoint. The midterm was to define terms, then recap a specific reading for each professor. You get to make an exam aid for the midterm and the final, and they give you the questions.
A very easy class to get an A. Don't have to go to lecture at all. End of semester quiz was really easy. He allowed us to have a take home final.

One of the easiest classes I've taken at Carolina. For lectures (1x week), either show up or just skim the textbook. For recitation (1x week), you give 3 speeches of your choice. Do these and you get an A!

Really great professor, I learned so much. Lectures were only once a week and recitation once a week. Easy to do well on all the speeches with a little bit of effort. One of my favorite classes this semester, I would def recommend taking more classes with him! Wonderful experience.

I took this for communication beyond Carolina credit, easiest class ever. Only 3 speeches graded by TA, and you pick the topic. Overall, I learned a lot and enjoyed this class! No homework other than preparing for speeches. The final was take-home and you write what you learned in the class. He also recommends his textbook but you don't need it.
Easiest class ever, if you can confidently speak for five minutes three times its an A. 100% would recommend.
Lundberg is very chill. He is one of the most eloquent people I have ever heard lecture. I had him for IDST 132 "Science in Hyperpartisan Times". Really interesting class, definitely recommend.

He was one of the professors in my triple I and he is actually amazing. His lectures were engaging, fun, and educational. I learned so much from him and it wasn't hard. Anyway, if you get a chance to take a class with him, I'd say do it.
Dr. Lundberg is a legend, his lectures are well developed and insightful. He's a reasonable guy and doesn't include all the waste of time bs that fills so many classes

113 is made up of lectures/recitations. You can pass the course without ever attending lecture, but if you do, you'll hear Prof. Lundberg give great, funny lectures. Recitation is where you're graded and depends on the TA. Coursework includes 3 speeches, evaluations and an easy final. 113 can be an easy A or learning experience, it's up to you.

Professor Lundberg's public speaking class was very easy to manage and provides actual skills necessary for the real world. You give 3 speeches over the course of the semester, and the rest of the work is just participation or completion. Very relaxed but useful class, and no surprises for his students. Great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Amazing prof! The material was interesting and even though it can be confusing he makes it easy (ex. he sends out the 3 quizzes you have in the semester in an email like an hour before class so you can prepare). You have 3 easy quizzes, a fallacy quiz, participation, 3 easy papers on a topic of your choice, and an essay-based final. Take him!

Professor Lundberg is an amazing teacher- I have his Argumentation class and although the readings could be difficult, he always clarified the material in class and helped me make sense of things. His lectures are really interesting and he's always making the class laugh while teaching you something new. Definitely one of the best profs I've had.

If you are relatively strong at Spanish you will not find this course challenging. However, there are some weeks with a lot of condensed work. Prof is extremely caring and kind and is not a harsh grader. I just suck at Spanish.

I loved her!  She is super sweet and a very understanding professor usually willing to take things late as long as you contact her and explain. She never called on anyone or forced them to answer. She brought us candy and food for our end of semester presentations which was not required of her. She is very approachable and just a sweet prof.

I loved Professor Arango-Sosa!  She was super sweet and understanding.  Assignments were easy, and tests were fine.  You just have to study and make sure you understand the material. She was a very fair grader on papers and presentations.  Remember to keep up with MSL and participate in class!

I loved Prof Sosa! She's a really lenient grader and is so sweet and understanding. You definitely have to participate in class, but as long as you do, you'll get a good participation grade. It's a flipped classroom, but the exams were pretty easy if you've taken Spanish in the past (plus they tell you what's on the exam). Try to get her for 203!

I had missed out on two years of Spanish and was still able to keep up well enough, especially considering how little previous Spanish teachers had taught me. Every time I had to make up quizzes due to medical reasons, she was very understanding and accommodated for me. She was also pretty lenient with grading at some points. I highly recommend.

I have never enjoyed Spanish and this class proved it. Professor Arango-Sosa was amazing and was always willing to meet with me when I had questions. No matter how hard I studied, the exams killed me. A huge portion of your grade is participation. She doesn't care if you're grammatically correct, as long as you speak in Spanish.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is nice and a mostly lenient grader. She is not perfect, but if you need to take Span 203, try to take her. She does not make anything harder than it has to be in terms of workload. Make sure you participate in class, and you should be good.

She is nice, and has a pretty defined structure for the class. Occasionally, she struggled with the technology aspects of online teaching and she pretty much reads from the textbook, but she explains it well. Probably not the best SPAN 105 professor, but she is definitely better than a solid amount of them.

Such a sweet woman. Very fair and reasonable with grading. Clearly wants you to learn Spanish more than she out to get you grading wise (would rather you branch out and get it wrong, then stick to simple structures, and rewards you grade wise for trying). Would have loved to haver for 203.

Prof Arango-Sosa is really nice and a very very lenient grader. She encourages everyone to participate but doesnt call anyone out. Theres a lot of partner work and homework after every class but it doesnt take more than 30 minutes.

Massi is a great teacher as well as a person. While he is strict, he is also funny. He makes learning another language cool and fun. His positivity and encouragement he gives to students make them want to learn more. Because Spanish classes at KU fill up crazy fast, this language is a good alternate. Italian is closely related to Spanish.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Massi is awesome! He cares so much about his students and puts in a lot of effort towards class. You have to do work outside of the class- as with any language- but it is easy if you stay on top of your stuff. He makes the class fun and everyone is involved during it. Attendance is key
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Honestly, I didn't put in much effort and only took the class because it was a requirement. However, Professor Massi made it fun. He is an easy going guy, and the overall atmosphere of the class is relaxed.
truly caring and amazing professor

I had Professor Cilizoglu at St. Olaf College, where she taught Intro to International Relations. It was a relatively laid-back class, but paying attention, doing the readings, and participating in class certainly helped. She's passionate about the subject matter and entertains student questions. However, her class isn't very engaging so beware.
Never taking again, will waste your time. Very unorganized.
Worst Professor Ever.

Love Professor Cilizoglu, fantastic professor who is well qualified. She does a great job at making class interesting while combining wit and humor. Test's were pretty tough but would take anything by her again.

Menevis teaches POLI150 for a small class (30-40 students) and it makes it super interesting because she always tries to engage in a debate. Her course is clear and easy to understand, and she is always available if you have further questions out of class. The multiple choice part of her tests are easy, the short questions are harder.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The only hard part about this class is trying to pay attention and take notes for 75 minutes straight, other than that, the material that would be on the test was extremely straightforward and the tests were exactly what was in the notes/ power points. The textbooks aren't really necessary and they are really expensive I wouldn't recommend buying.

There is a ridiculous amount of reading for this class. Also, lectures are packed with a large amount of information that will not be on the tests. Note-taking here will give you a headache. Study hard if you still want to take this class, but for a 100-level course, I was struggling.

Cicek did not make lectures very engaging and interesting, so it was very hard to pay attention. Her power points were vague. My friends and I absolutely dreaded going to this class. The tests are very hard, she expects you to know all the drawn plans of each city. This course could have been better if taught by someone else.

Worst class I have taken at UNC by far. The lectures are long and boring, there is a ridiculous amount of material to cover for tests and exams, and there is a participation component in the class. Definitely find another class to get the WB credit.

This class wasn't too amazing, but it is a WB gen ed. It wasn't awful but the papers are tough and the tests are worse. Cicek was a pretty entertaining lecturer for the material but it wasn't enough, especially to keep my attention for an hour and a half. If you like ancient history, then go for it, otherwise you may want to look elsewhere.
She did not make the material clear at all especially the material for the midterm. She did not engage the class and her lectures were extremely boring.
I enjoyed listening to Cicek, however, Ancient Cities was hard to capture my attention at times. Her points however, are pretty clear and if you pay attention you should get out with at least a B.

Currently enrolled in the class, was told it was an easy way to fulfill a gen ed. Not true.  Class requires a lot of work, exams require so much preparation and it often isn't enough. The papers are graded with remorse for the ridiculous exams, but it still isn't enough to have a lift your grade.

I took this class having been told it was an easy A with a different teacher. This teacher in conjunction with Matt Schueller present long and extremely dense powerpoints on overwhelmingly mundane history. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. Working hard for a B-/B. With that being said, Beeby is more interesting than the other lecturer and teaches better .

You can tell she knows exactly what she's talking about and she's very passionate about the material, but be ready for long lectures and the tests are almost impossible after *15 hours* of studying. Would NOT take again

Do NOT take this class. Material was extremely boring, and the midterm was full of ridiculously minute details that nobody could be expected to remember. She is a nice person but not a good teacher, gives unclear instruction regularly and is difficult to understand. I would recommend avoiding this class at all costs.
Math 232 is a HARD class.  I have always loved math until I took this class.  He is a nice teacher but easily confuses students

Worst math teacher I've ever had. Always gets lost in the problems, can't use technology, made us all buy books that he wanted to use not the ones the book store sells. Unorganized. You never know what section you're learning anthe examples he gives have nothing to do with the homework and neither has anything todo with the tests. Enjoy

He grades hard and takes off points for trivial errors. Gets confused about his own problems, so he confuses the class. Has assigned nonexistant homework problems and has repeated homework problems. He seems nice enough, but don't take his classes if you don't already know the material or if you want a good grade.

He holds consistent office hours but his communication skills are so poor that it's pointless. He'd start on one topic and forget what he was doing midsentence and move on to a different example. He didn't know how to do half of the problems and mainly read frm the book. We had one test all year and ambiguous grading. Worst teacher I have ever had.

One of the worst math professors I have ever had!  This class is known to be hard, but his absent-mindedness and unrecognizable scribbles on the board did NOT help.  Had to drop this class.  He's crazy smart and has good stories, and he's nice (he pulled a box of kleenex out of his desk drawer during office hours one day) but he cannot teach!

The limit as x approaches a passing grade in this class basically doesn't exist. He has cool classical music playing in his office during office hours though, so take advantage of them. You're better off getting the cafeteria workers to teach you calculus than this guy.

HE IS THE MOST HORRIBLE TEACHER I HAVE EVER HAD. and i have had some bad ones. i really hope he reads this so he will retire and acknowledge that he CAN'T TEACH. he should retire anyway, he makes so many mistakes because of his age. please don't make the same mistake i did. DROP THIS CLASS

I frankly thought that he was the most horrible teacher there is!  I mean I didn't understand a word he was talking about.  You should only take that class if you are willing to teach yourself, which defeats the purpose of having an instructor, right?!  Anyways, never take his class...taking his class will mess up your gpa.
Professor Cima is impossible to follow while teaching and does hardly anything to help the students that are struggling.

This guy was a dinosaur when I had his class (about 8 years ago).  Loved to use the overhead, and we could barely read his scribble.  Assigned homework, forgot about it, then collected it 2 weeks after it was due, so you usually didn't have it on you!!  Tests were a nightmare.  Took Assani's class the following semester, easily made a B+ AVOID CIMA
Attempted to schedule a test the day after Halloween, but might be talked out of it.  Rather confusing at times, expect to teach yourself from the book.

This is the old Math 128.  The material is pretty easy, but it's easy to mess up on the quizes.  There was no mandatory HW, but you should do the HW he suggests.  It's very possible to do well in the class, but it's made more difficult because he is disorganized and often confusing.
He seems like a nice guy, but I didn't like the way he taught.  It seems like he spent most of the time going over problems that we had already done for homework.  I didn't understand why...
He should be fired. Too old to still be teaching. He's mean, too.

Very difficult class.  Even after going to office hours and getting a tutor I was still amazed to pass the class.  I never felt like we did sample problems in class that were similar to the homework.  A lot of times it was hard to follow what he was doing in class.
Teaching style is to write equations on the board, boring.

Lab assignments were pretty easy, but point penalties for tiny mistakes were large at times. Our reading quizzes were pretty challenging, but doable. He is very accommodating, and provides plenty of opportunities to make up points for late assignments. Overall, he is a great professor and this was a very interesting class!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: had weekly quizzes, really nice guy, would definitely take it again
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Extremely picky about grading papers/labs and would take off points for the tiniest things. Also had extremely specific weekly quizzes that were closed note and based off of multiple readings that were laughably long. Kind of nice, sometimes? Kind of also passive agressive.
Pretty straightforward class, interesting (but lengthy) readings and complicated quizzes. Grading was pretty inconsistent, but fair ins ome cases. He did not  fw me but was pretty chill to others.

Do not take this class if you are not good at weekly quizzes on lengthy papers. The quizzes are hyper specific and they are not open note making them quite tricky as they are a large part of your grade. The work wasn't necessarily bad, but Dr. Gray is not accommodating or flexible on any assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Love Professor Gray as a teacher. However, if you are not good at weekly quizzes, DO NOT TAKE. You will regret it and be very sad.

I love Clark! He's so sweet and teaches the class material in a very easy-to-understand way. Lectures were straightforward and you had weekly quizzes (they're easy if you did the readings/or paid attention to ppl presenting the week's readings) and a super quick and easy final presentation. I learned a good amount! Very nice gen ed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Super chill guy, really liked him. The setup of the class was a little weird- basically every semester he has students write their own variation of the exact same research paper and you work on this all semester. We used Stata but didn't actually write any code. I like how the work was spaced out though, nothing ever piled up or stressed me out.
Geog450/451 was super easy and manageable! you could easily get ahead on the papers and then vibe for the rest of the semester

I'm pretty sure this class is GEOG 451, not 450, but I loved this class! Dr. Gray is a great professor and definitely cares about the material and his students. There are lots of hefty journal articles that we were quizzed on, but if you pay attention to the class presentations on them you get the picture. Easy assignments and open notes quizzes!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This is the most caring professor I've had! I struggled getting labs turned in and he reached out to make sure everything was OK and allowed me to turn them in with limited late penalties. Quizzes were hard but don't majorly affect your grade. Final is a paper which he has you turn in sections throughout the semester. All around just a great guy!
Great class and great professor! Grading criteria is very clear and fair. Always willing to work with you if you have questions and is great at explaining material.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Grading was clear and fair. Weekly quizzes were hard but he dropped low grades. I was in his office hours every week and emailed him constantly and he was always super helpful and caring. 437 was one of my fav research classes. Really smart, good lectures, kind of matter-of-fact when talking about heavy topics. Great hands-on research experience!

Do not take him for GEOG120. He is lazy when making notes for class and his tests are way too specific. Unless you plan on dedicating a large amount of time to studying for this class, do not take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great professor. He's very lively & kept me awake despite my tendency to fall asleep in just about all of my classes multiple times a week. Weekly quizzes are harder than they need to be, wish he would've allowed us to get one of the 5 questions wrong without hurting our grade. Lots of reading, but skimming works fine. Tests/papers are easy enough.
Professor Gray is a pretty good teacher.  He certainly knows his lectures well and has a real passion for geography.   If you put in the effort this class is a highly enjoyable one to take.

Lectures were absolutely unendurable. I resorted to playing games on my computer and taking vague notes about the powerpoints he gave (although that's not even necessary, since he posts all the lectures). He is mildly amusing if you get his nonsensical remarks. Reading from the textbook is the best way to get an A, though each chapter is very long.
bro got the magic of explaining things so clearly and organized

By far the most organized professor I've had at UNC. Gives incredibly clear guidelines, grades everything in a timely manner with plenty of opportunities for feedback. Provides plenty of resources for each exam and is always in his office happy to help his students. I love Christopher Handy.
Hard class but great professor.
Very fair class structure. Lots of materials available for studying. Tests were very similar to the practice he gave and he makes the material very easy to follow throughout the semester.
Clear and to-the-point teaching style which is needed for this course content, have flexibility regarding the grading of homework and exams
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Econ 400 is a hard class, but Professor Handy is not a bad teacher. He does his best to make the information digestible, and honestly, you just have to push through how hard it is and be willing to work and use his resources as much as you can and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Handy is an awesome guy with a great personality. My grade was definitely a lack of understanding on my part, and not his fault. Was a very difficult class, never scored above a 60 on any of the tests. Curve saved me.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures were not interesting in the slightest. Homework was difficult, but he held office hours in the econ aid center and would answer any questions. Mostly a boring class and requires prior statistics knowledge to keep up with how quickly he goes through topics. 200 person lecture with no connection to the professor. Curve is lifesaving.

Handy provides every resource needed to succeed in a moderately challenging class. Tests are tricky but fair, and homework load is reasonable (1 assignment/week takes ~2/3 hours). Watch the couple of 5/10 min pre-class vids he gives before class and don't chatgpt every single hw like half the people and it's really straightforward.

Assignment workload was high. His organisation is great, records his lectures, posts worked solutions, good attention to detail. Not sure why there are 1 star reviews. If you've done stats before it's not a difficult course but hard to score high as small mistakes are costly. He's quite flexible and lenient, gives partial credit for wrong MCQ's.

Handy is one of the most organized Econ professors out there. He makes studying so easy and has so many different resources that people can take advantage of to learn, and even takes the time to answer every single online question a person will post. He breaks down hard concepts and actually makes them understandable.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: This course is basically an intro stats course (like AP stats). Dr. Handy is very good at explaining things clearly in a way easy to understand. He is very knowledgeable, approable, kind, and generous about grades. All of the class materials are extremely well-organized.

I'm not sure if it was because i've never taken any type of statistics class before, but I did not follow a single thing he said. The lectures felt really long and the exams were hard. He seems very nice tho. I would NOT recommend taking this class if you have never taken a statistics class before. There should be a stats pre-req for this course.

Do yourself a favor and do not take this class with him. TAs are 100% writing the good ratings. I will say he is smart, like every other professor here, but he is an awful lecturer and purposely makes the exams hard by trying to trick you. Least favorite class I have ever taken here.

I'm honestly confused how he has good reviews on here. His lectures are absolutely terrible and he makes the exams ridiculously hard. He may curve the class, but it doesn't feel like you are actually achieving anything when you are just relying on the curve. Terrible.

Prof. Handy is a great teacher who made difficult material in ECON 400 easy to understand. His tests are fair and reflect homework and in class activities. Be sure to take advantage of his videos explaining concepts and come to class prepared or you may feel overwhelmed. The lecture moves quickly into polls as he expects you have watched the videos

Most organized professor I've ever had. Provides so many resources to help you succeed. The content can be conceptually tough but he wants to see you suceed and is very accessible for questions. Tests are fair and grading criteria is fair/straightforward. Definitely would recommend. Students that have taken any stats class before have advantage.

Very straightforward lectures - tells you what you need to know! Very reasonable grading policy, and give extra credit. Love his class and genuinely cares about each student (answers all your online questions if you are confused)

Professor Handy is approachable and kind but also highly organized and skilled as a professor. He provides numerous resources to help students succeed in this course and is happy to answer questions outside of class.
Handy was a good professor, 400 is just really difficult material. He does typically curve pretty significantly at the end of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really terrible. The lecture is too terrible

Brutal class. Lectures are confusing and hard to follow—I stopped paying attention and just taught myself after class. Office hours helped, but I waited too long. Pre-class videos and the textbook are useless. Exams are awful and nothing like the practice, which has 150+ separate questions and is super tough. Only the curve saved me.

I have taken other classes that had content which overlapped with 400, and Professor Handy was able to explain concepts I struggled with before in a clear and concise way. He is clearly familiar with learning methods (unlike some professors who are an expert in the subject but don't know how to teach it). Very willing to help if you are confused.

If you're not particularly strong in math the course is exceptionally difficult. Handy is an amazing speaker who is always available through various resources, I enjoyed lectures even if it made no sense. Final grade curve is very generous, I think a C+ was a 55 most recently. If you're looking for more application based info, take handys course.

Handy is a very good econ professor; his class and Canvas page are organized well, making studying for exams easy and structured. Lectures are nothing special, and the homework can be a bit long, but most of the grade comes from exams. His study guide is very helpful and he CURVES so dont be scared by the low averages my grade went from a C to a B.

He makes information very accessible but you really have to stay caught up and engaged in all materials to do slightly well on exams. Certain exams can be different from practice problems just study way ahead of time!!
One of the GOAT in the ECON department. He is always patient with students. He curved a lot for your final grade. I got an 82 for it, and it is an A-.

Took 470 after also taking 400 with Handy. 470 is much harder but he does a good job of explaining content as clearly as possible - one of the most articulate econ professors. He records lectures so it's helpful to go back and watch them to review. He communicates well with his students and is very accessible on CampusWire. His curve is generous.

Any class that Handy is teaching is going to be hard, but he is the most organized and helpful professor in the econ department. His lectures can get boring, but he doesn't waste time outside of stuff you genuinely need to know or review.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor, very hard class
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I wouldn't say his lectures are engaging, but he is very good at making the content digestible. He answers questions regardless of how stupid it was, and is accessible outside of class. Pay attention, do practice problems, and go to recitation. Easier if you took AP Stat. Class gets harder as it goes though so you have to stay locked.
Honestly about as difficult as I expected a more upper level econ class to be, not unfair at all, but you have to do the homework and study for the exams to do decent overall
straight to the point, solid professor
Goated prof

Prof. Handy is an awesome professor. Homeworks and in-class examples were consistent with test material, and he did a fantastic job explaining the material. He also curves your final grade in the class, not to mention has generous grading thresholds. If you put the work in and go to class you will not only learn a lot, but do well in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Not sure if it's just the material, but nothing Handy said made sense. He seems like a really nice guy but I was lost when it came to the content - and so were my friends in the class. We still managed to get pretty good grades, but going into 470 I am concerned about my level of understanding.

Memorizing how to use the equation sheet can get you an A but it will be a lot more work than if you just sit and think about what's really going on with the math. Handy is very good at decyphering students' questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: This guy is a chiller. He loves econometrics and I felt engaged in the content, somehow. Hard class, just put some effort in.

Handy is super accessible on campuswire which is really helpful. Once the homework assignments start they never end. Watch the pre class videos so you don't get lost in lecture, but he pauses lecture to ask for questions, and he's available during office hours. Exams are fair and practice problems are on par with exam difficulty. Lovely curve!
Professor Handy's class can be challenging, but his thoughtful approach and helpful resources like Campuswire make it manageable. unstuck ai was a great study aid alongside the practice problems.
Unless you've completely dropped the ball, you will pass. I did the absolute bare minimum, pass failed the class, and scraped by with a PS on the transcript. HEAVY curve. Nice guy. You will be okay.
Good professor

Econ 400 is a hard class, but Professor Handy makes it doable. His lectures are nothing crazy or exciting, but he covers the material that will be on exams. He also gives sooo many practice problems which is super helpful. Do those and you'll be fine!

Two midterms, 20% each, final 30%, extra 10% for highest exam, 5% participation, 15% homework. HWs included R-studio which made them difficult. Watch pre-class videos to understand content or else you'll be lost in class. Posts 40-question exam reviews before each exam but almost too long to be helpful. Huge curve at end bc of low averages.
Handy is the peak

Dr. Handy is my favorite professor I've had since being at UNC. He's very clear with expectations and lets us know plainly how we can succeed. His pre-class videos are helpful so you can work on just practice problems in class. The formula sheet is very helpful and he is easy to reach on CampusWire. I'm excited to take another class with Dr. Handy!

He's a good professor but lectures can be a bit boring. I kind of just suck generally with numbers so look at pre-class videos they're very helpful. Textbook is good but take it with a grain of salt when reading it. Would take again but be prepared for a hard class if you haven't taken AP Stats or STOR-155
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Handy is a very reasonable person, he curves everyone's grades at the end of the semester, very clear lectures, highly recommended ECON professor!

Dr. Handy explains content clearly and thoroughly in lectures, and even provides pre-class videos that cover the material in brief. The pace of the class is quick, but if you've taken AP Stats or STOR 155 there isn't much new content. Test averages were mid-70s despite the tests covering similar content to class and the review materials.

Somehow manages to make the material harder than it is. Homework can be a bit difficult and definitely requires studying outside of class. Tests are basically the same as homework in terms of difficulty, so if you struggle on homework you will struggle on the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Class makes me feel like I'm being put to sleep. The professor talks for 90 minutes, yet I leave more confused. I've turned to Khan Academy and The Organic Chemistry Tour for help. When I'm lost, I can't even ask questions because I have no idea what he's talking about. He rambles on without engaging. He's not cut out to teach, more like a tutor.

Dr. Handy is my favorite. I do not have a strong background in math, but my grades are decent because I spend over 6 hours on class each week, not including the lecture. Both 400 and 470 are quite challenging, but if you want an A, the time you invest in studying will pay off. Besides, he is very caring, encouraging, responds quickly on campuswire.
Great professor, the class itself isnt that hard either but Professor Handy is by far the best professor I've had here at UNC, and his grading is clear and he curves the class as well.

Great professor. His arms can be slightly distracting but that is okay. He curves at the end because I definitely did notttt get an actual B, I'll tell you that. All of the resources to get an A are there, he gives videos to watch before lectures, practice exams, practice homework, all of the grading keys. I just fell off mid semester lol

Dr. Handy objectively lays everything out properly, but misses the "engaging" mark. Between spoonfeeding us coding content and dropping two of six assignments, I found myself ignoring the class until exams. Handy comes across as a robot presenting his same research papers with a few trick questions on repeat. Mildly more difficult 400 downgrade.

I have had Dr. Handy twice, and I wish I could take more. He is kind and fair, and while his class is hard, he acknowledges that we are all upper-level econ students and curves final grades heavily to reflect that. His lectures are well-designed so students can best grasp the material. He is also so intelligent and can answer every question well.

I enjoyed learning under Professor Handy for both ECON 400 and 470. He teaches remarkably well, frequently pausing during lectures to see if any student has questions. He is also very responsive on CampusWire, always answering students' questions. The practice problems he offered before every exam were very helpful in succeeding in his courses!

Chris Handy is a moral and altruistic person. He shows that a man can be absolutely shredded and embrace a nerdy fascination with economics. What distinguishes Dr. Handy from his contemporaries is his infectious sense of humor; He's undeniably witty. His ability to spread laughter effortlessly is a rare and invaluable gift. Do the practice tests!
Chris is a great professor, yet the classes he teaches have hard material. He cares about students' success and will curve the grades to adjust to the class distribution.

Genuinely god bless this man, his class is ROUGH you will have to pay attention and take notes to learn the concepts. BUT there's only 6 homework and 3 tests throughout the whole class. AND he curves the final grades so that the average course grade is in the middle of the 'B' range and adjusts grades accordingly #stats. He is EXTREMELY helpful.
G.O.D.
So nice professor, well-structured class materials and willing to take his class again!

One of the best professors I've had. Despite challenging material, he makes topics digestible. He is accessible (Campuswire) and answers questions in a way that students (not just economic experts) can understand. Exams are challenging but representative of class material (lots of practice problems). Attend office hours for help on assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Handy is great with explaining the topics in this difficult course and being available through office hours, after class, and on Campuswire to answer any questions you might have. While it can seem to be boring, he does a good job of using real-life studies and examples to make econometrics more meaningful.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Handy is a great professor who puts a lot of effort into teaching this course and gives us a lot of practice material as well. However, the content is hard and the exams were not easy. But he is very accessible outside of class and always does his best to answer questions when asked. Would definitely take a class with him again.

He was a great professor. Super accomodating and no questions were stupid to him which was great. I personally did not use all the resources available like his office hours, but I'm sure they would've been great. He was really quick to reply on campuswire which was a life saver. You can tell he really wants us to succeeed. Would 100% take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Handy is by far my favorite econ professor. His willingness to work with his students and adjust exam difficulty/curve is greatly appreciated. Lectures are thorough and he provides plenty of resources. 470 is definitely a hard class, but as long as you put in the effort, there's no reason you can't learn a bunch and get a good grade.
Really hard content. Solid teacher. Sligthly overrated but I liked him.
Couldn't pay that much attention to stats bc I was distracted by his shoulders

Everyone LOVES and is OBSESSED WITH Chris Handy. The way he structured 400 made a difficult class much more digestible. He offered plenty of resources to help students learn, was very organized, and was generous with the curve at the end. I'm walking away from 400 with a strong foundation in statistics and I highly recommend taking a class w/ him!

Awesome professor and one of my favorite classes this semester. The smaller class size gives a lot more ops to ask questions imo!

The class is weighed heavily on exams. But don't be scared because they reflect the class material and are fair. He's knowledgeable and super willing to answer any questions to help you out. Take this class if you can!

Great professor who cares about his students but the course itself is kind of dry. Exams were a lot tougher/more conceptual than in-class problems and homework assignments, so make use of office hours if you can!

This class was super tough but Professor Handy is a great teacher. He does videos that you must watch before class that are about 15 minutes or so before each class then goes back over it in class alongside practice problems. He does a curve at the end of the class as the tests are very hard. Overall just a great teacher teaching a tough course.

ECON400 is a hard class but Prof Handy gives you tons of practice problems and materials to succeed. He's very accessible outside class with Campuswire. Performance on exams is pretty low, with class averages being around 70/71, but he curves the course at the end of the semester to compensate. Overall I  would recommend him for this course!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Handy clearly cares about teaching his students.  This class was very difficult for me and my performance was poor, although I can really only blame myself.  If you want to learn this subject I would recommend taking this class but you will probably need to put in a decent amount of effort.

Great professor, and loves statistics. it's just a hard class. He wants you to do well, and all the resources are there, you just have to put in the work. But don't miss an exam, even for a legitimate reason, you can't make it up and that puts a lot of pressure on the final. but I found this class very interesting and would take it again.
Great professor. Well structure course. Lots of help and practice problems. Cares about students' success.

ECON 400 is neither an easy course nor really an economics course as it is more Statistics Part 2 but Handy is a great professor who explains things well and is incredibly accessible outside of class and on campus wire. Make sure you put the work in and use your resources as the class is difficult but manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
ECON 400 is a tough subject but he makes it so digestable and is excellent at explaining every topic.
Cares so much about students and outstandingly organized and helpful teacher. Great guy.

I was dreading taking 400 because I'vge heard awful things about 400 and 470 but this was easily one of my favorite classes this semester because of handy. I LOVE HIM. He is incredibly kind and intelligent and does his best to teach each concept in several ways ti appeal to diff students' learning styles. I hope he has the best life ever
He is incredibly organized, and he gives you all the resources you need to succeed. All you need to do is put in the effort. Just take his class.

Definitely one of the hardest classes I've taken at UNC. Show up to the lectures, stay on top of the material, and you will be fine. Watch the pre-recorded videos before class. I'd highly recommend doing all of the practice problems before exams as well as redoing the homework; they prepare you best for what you might see on the exam.

Prof Handy is a knowledgable and caring professor, and his grading is very fair, with a generous curve for final grades. His lectures are extremely easy to follow, and are very clear and straightforward. The homework and exam practice problems are very representative of the exams, so if you do those, you'll likely do well in the class.

This class wasn't bad, but I found it more challenging because there was less intuitive content and more data science heavy. Econ concepts that I normally find interesting weren't a big part of the course. The exams were pretty challenging, definitely study a lot and do practice problems and redo homework. Caring guy though and very accessible.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: 470 is a very difficult class, but Handy is a great professor. Was very generous with curves and final grade cutoffs. Also was very accessible outside of class.

Best lecturer I've ever had. He is so clear, concise and offers lots of practice. You can tell he's an expert in the subject and is really passionate too. He is very easy to reach outside of class and on Campuswire. The topics on midterm 2 can be a little confusing but asking questions in recitation and doing practice in EconAid Center really help.

Handy is a nice guy and a decent lecturer; however, his exams were extremely hard to the extent that he will add up to 10 adjustment points to each Midterm and then add something like a 10% curve for your final grade, and still it would not be enough for you to get an A-. Be prepared to dedicate a LOT of your time to this class as it will be tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Nice professor, but a tough class. He is super inspirational, caring, and accessible, definitely take ECON470 with him too.

The class is built for you to succeed you just have to try. I made the mistake of not trying for the first part and it almost cost me a D. He puts so much effort and shows that he really cares. Tests are worth a lot and make sure to do the homework, it's a lot like the test.

470 can be confusing content but Handy does the best possible job explaining it and is always available to answer questions, the campus wire platform he uses is especially helpful. It's not the easiest class but if you have a math background it will be much easier. Tests could be challenging but there was a generous curve applied at the end.

Chris Handy is a kind, gentle, and extremely knowledgeable professor. I have taken both Econ 400 and 470 with this gem of a human being. While 470 remains the hardest class I have ever taken in my life, he has done absolutely everything to help me, and I truly appreciate him. Take his class if you can, you will not be disappointed.

I LOVED this professor! I honestly don't know how he doesn't have a higher rating. His lectures were great and easy to follow, and he always allowed you to ask questions in class. Yes, tests and assignments were hard, but ECON-400 is a hard class. Nothing insane, especially with how accessible he is outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor, had very clear lectures, and a much better choice than Guilkey. If you did the pre class notes you came into class with everything you needed to do that class' problems. Never went to office hours but any question that I asked on campuswire was answered fairly quickly by him or a ULA

The professor is nice. I slept in his class, but he still treated me well. And the class material is not hard as long as you watch the pre-class videos and do the homework carefully. Though the attendance is counted, the class has recordings. I really cannot understand why there are students who dislike the class...

Hard class-be sure to always do the pre-class vids and take good notes. He's a good professor (despite overestimating our background knowledge on topics at times) and really strives to give everyone all the tools to succeed. Great guy. Keep up w the classes and go to TAs for help on hw.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Difficult material but not due to Professor Handy. The class is built for you to succeed but you need to stay engaged. Lots of examples and problems during class. Only weird thing is you have to use R code for homework assignments and he doesn't really teach you how to use it.

Dr. Handy is one of the best professors in UNC. He cares about his students and uses interesting examples in class. Stat class is unsurprisingly hard but it is worthy at the end. I would definitely take his other advanced econ class. Highly recommend!
He is not a bad professor or person, but it does seem like the exams were a good bit harder than the practice. He assumes people have more of a background in stats than they do.

Lectures gave little preparation or help for homework or exams. You know a class is bad when certain letter grades need to be curved by around 10-20 points at the end. It's not impossible to do well in this class but you will want to already have an extensive background in math/statistics that goes beyond the prerequisites for this course.

Chris was a good lecturer and genuinely wanted to help everyone do their best in the class. That being said, Some of his test questions were terribly worded and often did not resemble hw or practice problems at all stylistically. Final was 75% based off of the last (and easiest) unit though so great bonus there.

As someone who struggled with math and statistics most of my life, this class was no different. Learning in class was fine, because he is an okay lecturer and spends extra time on people who don't get it. However, I struggled on all homework and exams. I felt like the material on those were much harder than anything we practiced.

ECON 400 with Handy is the hardest Intro Stat class you'll ever take. That said, he's a great teacher with deep knowledge of the subject. Quickly responds with detailed explanations to questions online. Lectures can feel dry, but if you want to get into research through ECON, feels like this is the guy to take this class from.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Handy will feel cold on the surface. But he's a nice and caring guy. He doesn't intentionally make exam questions hard, super fast email responder, has pretty generous curves, and isn't too strict about things. But it is a bit hard to concentrate on his lectures and it feels very distant to me. It is a hard class and the office hours are very short

He is very caring but his lecture problems don't match the hw and exam rigor. I've made As in two other stats courses. Although these were the same concepts, I never scored over 65 on an exam. MC answers account for all common mistakes. I spent $240 for 8hrs of tutoring before the final just to make a 53. A 67% was a C+ with the curve this semester

Dr. Handy is great! Lectures are pretty boring but that's only because the content of ECON400 is boring. Weekly/bi-weekly HW is lengthy and first exam is most difficult (probability). Responds fast to emails and is very helpful and kind in office hours. Lectures at a good pace. Curves final course grades at the end of semester generously.
Hard class, but Handy was a very good professor who made it manageable. Provided lots of resources to study for exams and his lectures were very clear.

Handy is a cool guy. I think it must be what he teaches, but his lectures make him seem very robotic. Overall he outlines the content you need to know very well. Lots of exam practice problems and homework, all representative of the exams. I goofed off in the middle of the class (see my grade) but the material is very manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Really good professor. Very conscientious. The practice problems before the exam is very useful.

Overall pretty good professor definitely doesn't deserve the hate he gets on here. Class can be challenging but if you put the work in you will be fine. Definitely go to class and don't fall behind and you'll be fine.

He is kind, accessible & understanding. Explains things well tho slightly complicated. Problems in class are very similar to the exam. HW is hard but allows TA and peer help, and he gives extra credit. Only thing is that exams have more mc than problems, and each mc worths 3-4 points. Gives a decent curve. Definitely would take 470 with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Honors is the same workload, but offers more personal relationships with Handy and peers. Handy is funny, understanding, and even gave us cookies twice. Course is ambiguous and poorly structured, only giving a surface-level rundown of concepts taught more effectively in a stats course. Study the homework and do well on the heavily weighted exams!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Handy is an amazing person who really cares about students. His lectures can be a little complicated, though, and his exams are pretty difficult. Yet, he does his best to explain everything in detail and gives out numerous resources for students to complete assignments and prepare for exams.

Homework was always very tedious to do. Exams for this essentially being a beginner stat class are still harder than should be. 

But if you want to do good in this class, you will. If you don't put in the time per week then you will fall behind and crash. 

Overall pretty decent course but frustrating at times.

I loved Handy in 400. He's a smart guy who knows what he is talking about. Handy is so great in part because he doesn't ever put his students below himself. He gets on the level of his students and makes learning the material very doable. I'm taking him again for 470 and would highly recommend him to anyone looking to take 400.

This class is overall pretty boring but Handy was fair and clear about his expectations. There is a wide range of content in this course so understanding overall may feel surface level but his tests and homeworks don't expect more from you. His in class examples are helpful and he doesn't expect you to learn on your own.

This class was pretty hard. The homeworks were difficult and long, the tests were challenging, and his lectures were sometimes difficult to follow. I ended up supplementing his lectures with youtube videos (Organic chem tutor) just to understand the class, and that helped a lot. Just don't get behind and it should turn out alright!

Chris Handy is a very very strong man. I can tell he works out by the size of his enormous biceps. While the class may be difficult, i get motivation that my hard work will pay off every time I look at his arms. I wish he would hold me. Overall great class.
His homework is too difficult! Many concepts are not taught in class, though office hour is helpful.

Handy is a solid professor and a total dilf. Handy is very knowledgeable and makes the lecture interesting, but can sometimes over complicate simple topics. R is used on some of the work, but he normally helps with the code. The test are hard but fair and doing well on them is possible and he gives fairly generous curve. He also had amazing calves.

Dr. Handy is a nice, well-organized, accessible, and cute professor. Econ400 itself is hard, and he has already gave his best way for students to feel easier. Homework and textbooks are not enough, also need to know the definition, and spend time outside classes. Also I indeed like take his class again, but I choose Econ470 with another professor.
This class is hard material but he does a great job with the class structure. There are lots of practice problems and he tries to answer all questions. He is very reasonable and understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Handy gets a bad wrap. As long as you pay attention in class and do the HW you're supposed to (i.e. watch pre-class videos, read/skim assigned readings), you'll be fine. He gives formula sheets for exams, records and posts all his lectures, and posts all his annotated slides. Super nice and willing to help; responsive on email and CampusWire.

I took ECON 400 over the summer. Handy is willing to help his students and is good with communication. He also was good about posting practice materials (and incorporated practice problems into his lectures). Exams were a bit tricky at times and his lectures sometimes focused too much on tangential material, but overall I'd recommend his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Chandy was a very nice professor but I felt like the exams never accurately described what we focused on in class. Gives lots of materials to practice with, it's very possible to get a good grade in here but you have to focus and make sure you study EVERYTHING because he will try to get you on something he only mentions once.

I took 400 this semester. Let me tell you: It was a JOURNEY. Handy is a nice, caring, and smart guy. I always enjoyed speaking with him. However, the lectures over complicate otherwise simple topics. The hw and exam questions can be extremely obscure, because we have very few prep materials. It is possible to get an A but very tough. Tough class.
