reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Clark has been one of my favorite professors during my time at UNC! He is very engaging in lectures, is a fair grader, and is easy to reach if needed. Cannot recommend taking one of his classes enough.

Prof Clark is one of the most caring professors I've had at UNC. Although his classes are lecture-heavy, he throws in lots of engaging material (campaign ads, speeches, etc.) and plenty of jokes. Take a class with him if you can!!!

Amazing guy and very personable. Very easy A but as a southerner, I was really disappointed with the substance of the class. It was kind of structured as an orientalist view of the south through a northern microscope of awe which lowered my respect for the course. A southerner who understands southern culture and experience should teach the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great professor, but lowkey not the easy A I thought it would be. Exam questions come from study guides. Essays were a time crunch since he tended to delay releasing prompts, but they were not too difficult. He has funny tangents in class. Great guy, make a lasting connection with him! Grades: 3 essays, 2 exams, participation (attendance)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Clark is a professor who will make you want to come to class on a snow day. From his vast knowledge of political theory to his desire to hear all students' opinions, he is extremely respected and beloved in the POLI department. He doesn't take himself too seriously and always has a fun anecdote-do yourself a service and take one of his classes.

Dr.Clark is a great professor! He is very passionate about the topics he discusses and it's obvious he cares for his students. A bit of a slow grader but he doesn't grade harshly. Would definitely recommend this course.
Great guy - super caring and an awesome personality. His lectures were entertaining and the midterm was not insanely difficult because of the resources he provided.

Clark is one of my favorite professors I have had at UNC. He is energetic, funny, and super engaging. He uses different media forms to teach like slides, ads, and discussion, and really cares about what students have to say. Papers and exams were straightforward and super easy if you review notes and ask for help when needed.  Take him if you can!

Dr. Clark was alright for IDST 128. He was the last professor so he was kind of in a time crunch. The pre-class materials were literally his papers he wrote so that was kind of weird. Didn't really teach enough about politics, more surrounding race which was odd. Easy class though, would take if you want an A!

The Triple-I format at UNC is undoubtedly poorly organized, and I think Dr. Clark would've been better in a smaller class format. That being said, his lectures had the tendency to be long-winded, and he tended to be slightly patronizing. Easy enough to do well, though.

He was the best professor in my triple-I. He is the only professor who could get all 300 students to speak. He knows what he is talking about and made me more interested in the topic. He shows fun videos that break up the length of the class. Discussion posts were a huge part of this class and there was no final- only a "hard conversation."

Professor Clark was one of the most entertaining and passionate professors I've had. He was so funny and welcomed student input a lot. It took some time to figure out how he wanted you to write, but overall he was a fair grader and inspirationally excited to teach what he did.

Professor Clark was overall really great this semester. He has an amazing personality and is certainly a funny guy. Class is very lecture heavy and readings are not required. Sometimes it was a bit unorganized, but I definitely learned a lot. Grade is based on participation, two papers, and two exams. Didn't find any of them too challenging.
One of my favorite professors ever. Dr. Clark knows his stuff and teaches with a passion.

Overall, I really enjoyed the class and topics. He is an amazing lecturer. I struggled getting responses via email during this semester. Additionally, I found the exam grading to be a bit picky about details when compared to the instructions. Just be sure to ask questions.

Dr. Clark was a great professor, he genuinely cares about what he teaches and for the well being of his students. Two papers, a midterm, and a final, and random attendance throughout the semester. You get a study guide for both exams covering everything that would be on them so it's an easy A. Readings not required, went over main points in class.

The class was rather straightforward. One midterm was easy with an hour of studying, two papers, a question, and a final group project. Not that much work. There was nightly reading but it was not mandatory and you can get away without reading it as long as you pay attention in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great professor! He was really engaging, encouraged good class discussions, and was open to all students' ideas. Poli 204 was pretty easy when I took it - he gave us study guides for the exams and you can probably get by without doing all of the reading. Class attendance matters, so if you skip you're grade will be impacted.

Dr. Clark is one of my favorite professors at UNC. He is clearly extremely interested in politics and, will often go on tangents in class. A lot of his tangents are really entertaining, though, which make his lectures really easy to pay attention to, with him encouraging lots of participation. His lecture slides are easy to reproduce and useful.

Take classes with Dr. Clark! He is clearly passionate about the topic and encourages class discussion, which is super interesting. As of fall 2022, there are a lot of readings in this class and your grade is based off of a few assignments, but it is manageable. Not sure if that'll be changed up in the future. Nonetheless, great class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Loved Dr. Clark! Lectures are interesting and engaging. Lots of class discussion. Only downsides are that he sometimes rambles and that the class is graded off 2 essays and 2 tests. However, you will learn a lot from the class and the classroom is very engaging and respectful. I would totally take him again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: TAKE THIS CLASS!

Your grade consists of a midterm, 2 papers, a group presentation, and participation. Prof. Clark is a fair grader for all of those assignments, and is always clear with his expectations. He's clearly invested in what he teaches, which always makes his lectures interesting to listen to. Take this FYS if you have the chance!

Dr. Clark is definitely one of my favorite professors at UNC. He is very passionate about what he teaches and encourages students to participate. His class consisted of readings, 2 papers, a midterm and a final group project. If you are interested in learning about the topics he teaches I would definitely recommend taking a class from him.

Professor Clark has been my favorite professor so far at UNC. His lectures are engaging and he clearly cares about what he teaches. If you are passionate about the topic of the class then you will surely enjoy taking his classes. He goes out of his way to create an inclusive class environment for all students.

I would 100% take Dr. Clark again. He was able to distill difficult information to us in manageable terms. His tests were not too difficult if you watched the lectures. You do not need to read the textbook to get a good grade either.

This was my second class with him, and I loved it! I learned a lot of useful information about Southern politics, and you can tell he loves what he does. He is an engaging lecturer, gives good feedback on papers, and his exams are straightforward. Definitely take him if you have the chance.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Super awesome guy and extremely knowledgeable, but he was slow to grade and we never got lectures on time, which was stressful for the COVID semester. Still a king tho and I would definitely recommend if the class is in person
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Clark is kind and cares about what he teaches, but this class was not enjoyable online. Class was asynchronous, and he sent out lectures SEVERAL days after the day we should have had them. The 2 papers were difficult but the midterm and final were easy! This class was not a lot of work, but I'm not sure if I'd take a class with him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Clark is a solid professor! I learned a lot from him and you can tell he is really passionate about the material. He is easily distracted which means his lectures can be a bit convoluted, but I didn't really mind. His class is definitely not an "easy A" because the exams are pretty tough, but the papers and projects help make up for that.

Clark is so enthusiastic abt his subject and is great at explaining the material even in the asynchronic format. There's A LOT of reading for POLI76 so be prepared but tbh u can skim and as long as u watch lecture u'll get the main points. Not a super harsh grader and there are few assignments other than reading/lecture. 2 papers and 1 group proj.

Great professor. His clear enthusiasm and interest in the topic made me really want to learn. Do your readings, take notes in class, and spend time thinking about the issues and topics this class discusses: you'll do well. Funny guy as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Loved having him as a professor this semester! I definitely plan on taking a class with him again. This class isn't necessarily an easy A, as the second midterm and final are pretty difficult. Attendance is taken occasionally, but info directly from lectures is on tests. He is very passionate and makes boring subjects more relevant an interesting!

Dr. Clark shows that a class doesnt need to be insanely hard for you to learn a lot from it. The tests are very consistent with the lectures/readings, and you get to spend a lot of time on discussions and current events. It can get a little dry/awkward if no one is participating, but hes very enthusiastic and knowledgeable about what he teaches.
Dr. Clark is awesome! One of my favorite professors at UNC. He is hilarious and genuinely cares about his students and is passionate about the class material. He also makes lectures interesting.

Clark is one of my favorite professors i've had at UNC. His exams come straight from lecture material so I recommend going to class. Also takes attendance once in a while. A fair grader & made lectures enjoyable! can tell he is passionate about politics & a super nice guy!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: My favorite professor at UNC. Absolutely incredible lecturer. I had Dr. Clark for 101 and 204, and thoroughly enjoyed both of them. The grades I received in both classes were not ideal, but that was not necessarily because of him. He's a fair grader and knows how to explain what he's thinking. He's so funny and I never felt nervous in class.

Dr. Clark is an amazing professor. This first year seminar was easy and very interesting. He is so encouraging when students share their thoughts and I always enjoyed going to lectures. Grading was based off pop quizzes, 2 papers, a group project and a midterm.

Dr. Clark is one of the best lecturers herehe's entertaining, animated, and passionate about the subject. He supplements lectures with videos (sometimes SNL) and class discussion. The overall class difficulty was about average for Political Science. Class always got out 2-5 min early too.

I loved Prof Clark! He made a lot of sports metaphors which I enjoyed. The tests are multiple choice but they are a lot harder than they seem. The class average on both midterms were in the 70s so don't expect an easy ride. You will need to read the textbook alot! Come to class because some questions will say "according to lecture" so beware!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Clark is amazing! Truly one of UNC's best. POLI 101 was an enjoyable class-- but beware, you MUST study. Multiple choice exams seem easy, but could easily bite you! Didn't particularly like the 2 midterm papers, but I loved Clark's lectures. He's funny and wants you to succeed (both as a student and as a person). Take his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Clark is a great guy, but the class overall was only okay. Some(not all)TA's grade papers and recitation participation strictly. The tests are really hard and are more based off the textbook than lecture. Really scrutinize the textbook, because many questions are about minor details. Careful because one bad test grade can quickly limit your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Clark is a great lecturer. Class is very lecture heavy but not monotonous. He is funny & approachable. I don't know why people have said the tests and papers are hard, tests are all multiple choice w/ a study guide and papers aren't graded harshly. You don't really have to come to class a lot and it's very manageable.

If you could take this class without the TAs affecting your grade maybe this wouldn't be the worst class ever. The test are made by the TAs and unbelievably hard. They also grade papers very harshly and without rubrics or logic. Clark tends to ramble in his lectures which makes it impossible to learn. Clark is a nice guy but I would avoid.

Dr. Clark is an excellent professor. He is so enthusiastic about the material that his lectures are pretty engaging even though the material can be theoretical and about specific journal articles. He asks a lot of reading but he goes over the points in class so the reading is not 100% mandatory. The paper is huge though, so start on it early.

Professor Clark seems very funny/considerate, and his lectures are nice but not mandatory. Tests are needlessly difficult, even if you read the textbook inside and out. The class is graded by few things (2 papers, 3 tests, and your recitation (which is only 15% of your grade!)). TA's were incredibly unfair for this class, so choose a decent one.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Clark loves to talk and will ramble during class. Class grade really depends on your TA. Tests are easy if you memorize vocab from both lecture and the textbook. Paper prompts can be very vague so definitely go to office hours. Probably the easiest poli class I've taken

He's a pretty cool professor and loves to tell jokes and anecdotes, but your grade depends mostly on the midterms and papers. Be sure to read the textbook and pay attention to lecture in order to even think about getting a decent grade on exams. TAs grade papers and mine is pretty strict.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took this class as a requirement for my major. Political science is not my strong suit, so I took this class thinking I would gain a lot of learning experience out of it. We have three weeks left in the semester and I'm doomed to fail, despite all the hard work I've put into this ridiculously hard class. Avoid if possible.

This wasn't a bad class but not my favorite. Dr. Clark is personable and if you go see him during office hours he is really nice, but your grade is more dependent on your TAs because they write the test questions and grade your papers. The lectures were fairly interesting but he gets off topic sometimes. Tests were also very nitpicky.

I really enjoyed this class. Dr. Clark is very passionate about what he teaches and wants students to succeed. He is also funny and personable - I'd recommend taking a class with him if you ever get the chance! He provides study guides for exams so you know what to study.

He is a nice person, he gets off track a lot. The class had a lot of open discussions which was nice. There was two papers, a midterm, and a final. So everything was weighted pretty high. He grades pretty hard, and even though this says intro to southern politics, it didn't wasn't an intro level class. Don't let this be the first poli class you tak
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: If you are interested in the Political Science major at UNC, I highly recommend taking one of Dr. Clark's classes. It is obvious that he is highly invested in the material for the class and is a very kind, respectful professor who listens to what his students have to say. Exams can be difficult, but Dr. Clark made sure that everyone was prepared.
He's the best. Genuinely cares about his students and his curriculum. Highly recommend him one of my favorite profs at UNC. Also, he is funny and open to class discussions.

He posts his slides on Sakai, so you can miss a few and still do fine as long as you study effectively. The (multiple choice) exams include information from the slides and the textbook with no curveballs, which is really nice. He likes to tell some anecdotes while he lectures. At 9 am, it's nice to get an occasional pause in notes during lecture.
Dr. Clark is awesome and super passionate. You will do just fine in the class if you go and listen and do well in your recitation.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Love his lectures and enthusiasm for the class. His slides are organized, and lectures are eloquent and easy to follow, and exams are reflective of what you've done in class. Attendance isn't mandatory, but you need to go and also read the book to do well. TAs are in-charge of 35% of your grade, so make sure they like you in recitation.

He's a great guy and cares about his students and the material. Southern Politics just wasn't interesting to me. All the homework is reading, and his lectures essentially break down the readings. There were two papers, and he is very clear about what he expects. He makes study guides for his midterm and final. He also enjoys class discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: I love this man!! He is one of my favorite professors at UNC and makes class so interesting. The exams aren't hard and he seems to be an easy grader.
Chris Clark is great!! He takes attendance occasionally, but he tells good stories. He makes an effort to make the class engaging.

Dr. Clark has a great personality and really cares about his students! He can get a little off topic, but attend class to get a better understanding of the material. 3 exams, 2 papers, and recitation. The exams weren't bad (not cumulative) if you study the PowerPoints AND read the textbook. TAs grade the papers so they have a big say in your grade.

Dr. Clark is a great guy. Only a few grades, and half of them are graded by your TA. Having a good TA can make or break your grade. The exams are a mix of very easy questions, and difficult questions. All questions come from the textbook. Attendance isn't mandatory.

Clark himself is amazing and lectures aren't mandatory (he puts slides up) but he's easy to listen to and funny. However the grade for Poli101 is entirely based on about 6 grades, three of which are graded by the TA. Exams are fair and easy but you do need to study. But the papers and the rec grades can literally flunk you if you get a bad TA...

Clark is actually amazing and really funny. The lectures can get boring but you should still go to class to know the material. However the tests are for some reason quite hard even with studying. Also your grade in the class entirely depends on your TA's. The class has about 5 grades too (3 tests, 2 papers) which can really hurt you.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class is Minority Representation. There are 3 exams (none of them are cumulative) and he gives you a study guide a few days before each exam. There is one research paper towards the end of the class. Really interesting and fairly easy class. He goes over the readings in his lectures
I love Professor Clark to death.  He can ramble sometimes, but he means well and facilitates good class discussion.  Professor Clark took attendance occasionally, but you'll want to come to class.
Professor Clark is awesome. Focuses on the significance of the material, not facts. His tests are reasonable and he is an interesting lecturer.

Dr.Yang is great and super caring for students! 
Def needs a lot of practice to make lessons smooth, and it matters a lot whether you've worked on the things taught in the previous lessons. 
Piano is never easy but Dr.Yang makes it inspirational.
One of my favorites at UNC. Just one of the kindest and most intelligent people on campus. I love this woman.

Took Piano Lit with Professor Yang. Great teacher. Really wants to see all her students succeed. She is very accommodating of students and, as long as you let her know ahead of time, you can miss class occasionally. Her lectures were clear and captivating. All in all, a great teacher, passionate about the subject material.

Dr. Yang is one of the best pianists and professors I have ever had the pleasure of meeting. She always finds ways to improve your skills as a musician and is there to help you achieve any musical feat you desire. I have seen so much progress  and development in myself as an individual since taking lessons with her.
Easily the best professor I've had at UNC! He is fair and non-judgmental, and he turned around my entire perspective on Spanish. He's a talented professor, and a cool guy all around.
Absolute baller

Prof. Clemente is the best ever. Super caring and kind guy who recognizes the common pitfalls and works to help you avoid them. He is Spanish himself and likes to share fun phrases or stories about Spain. He cares about you as a person and you learning Spanish. He is just awesome!!

This professor was one of the nicest and most understanding professors I have ever had. He always helped with any homework, test, or general questions I had and did whatever he could to make sure students understood what he was teaching. He always made everyone laugh and wanted everyone to succeed.

very cool man that definitely is passionate about teaching. gives clear feedback with homework. participation in class is very important for your grade. his powerpoints are useful. it has a textbook but you honestly DONT need to buy it

Sr. Clemente Rodriguez is a professor who demonstrates ample passion for the Spanish language. He always ensures students feel comfortable to participate and get out of their shell to converse in Spanish without pressure. You will love Spanish more if you take 204 with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This class was so much fun! Profesor was kind, funny, and helpful.  He gives good feedback on homework, and he's a chill grader.  Make sure to study for exams as they make up a good portion of grade! As long as you study, the exams will be fine.  He provides practice exams that mimic the actual exam.  Also make sure to participate regularly!

If you can take any class with Prof Cristobal, take it! He has 100% been the kindest, most helpful, and most genuine professor at UNC. He cares about his students and is very accessible outside of class. If you show him you care, he will work with you above and beyond

Professor Clemente was incredibly kind and funny. He also understood that many students in 203 are still learning some of the basics of Spanish and teaches accordingly. I hadn't taken Spanish for 3 years when I took his class and still did well. Would highly recommend.

The best thing about Prof. Clemente is that he really understands that we aren't fluent in Spanish. He comes prepared to class every day and tells us about his own life and experiences, which is really interesting. He makes class fun by encouraging participation and discussion, which is a must for Spanish. He is also hilarious. Highly recommend!

Professor Clemente is great! He definitely challenges his students to participate, but I feel like we all improved our Spanish skills so much during the class. Fair grader and obviously cares a lot about his students. I would recommend taking a class with him to anyone!
Favorite teacher at UNC. Take him if you can. He is so kind and understanding and a great teacher.

Profe Clemente is amazing!! He brings his own experience into lectures, and rather than just going through a powerpoint, he takes time to explain concepts and make sure each student understands the material. If you are taking Spanish, take it with Profe Clemente!

Mr. Clemente is a great professor. He understands that his students are beginners in a foreign language and really works with them to assure they are understanding the material he is teaching. He is not a super harsh grader and is a chill, funny, and personable guy all around. I would definitely take a foreign language course with him again.

Chris is very chill and a very easy grader. He really cares about his students and wants us to learn. He understands we are spanish beginners and is very accommodating. I would 10/10 recommend. It's an easy A. He's a great guy, funny, and very understanding.

Such a nice professor and really cares that you understand rather than pushing you to memorize. He was so caring and understanding. I actually learned a lot and he wasn't a harsh grader. Don't forget your online homework and make sure you actually try and you'll get an A. Love him!!!!

Cris Clemente is by far the best professor at UNC. He shows how much he cares about his students and how he wants them to succeed. He is the nicest guy ever. If you have the opportunity to take Professor Clemente, please do it! The class is a lot of work, but it is also 4 credit hours. Study and you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class! Clemente is a really nice professor and cares a lot about his student. I struggle with Spanish but I went to office hours, participated a lot in class, and studied for the quizzes and exams. As long as you come to class and try then you will be fine!

I LOVE THIS PROFESSOR! He is super helpful both inside and outside of class. The actual class is filled with a bunch of participation but he makes it fun and doesn't judge if you say something wrong. Span105 starts off easy but starts getting tough around the midterm.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He is a great professor. He is very knowledgable and is willing to help out of the class. The content of 105 is not the easiest, and learning through the book is tough. Do well on the midterm and study for all of the quizzes and you should get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He is the best professor at UNC. He really cares about your grade and loves it if you go to office hours. you can make an A if you study, he is a fair grader, and he usually tells you what to study for quizzes and tests if you ask him. He doesn't tell you when assignments are coming so make sure you look at the syllabus. Take him for sure. 10/10.

I love Professor Clemente! He's so adorable and always wears really cool shirts/pins. He is super reasonable, is always there and willing to help, and really cares that you learn the material. You have to keep up with the syllabus because he doesn't usually mention upcoming quizzes or due dates. Also, you have to participate, but it's not too bad.

He is a great guy and really cares about his students. He's super nice. The class is difficult but if you study, you'll be fine! Lots of homework and this is a self-taught type of class. You learn the material online through Pearson before class and then review the information in class. The quizzes can be difficult. Study!

Cristobal is the best Spanish teacher. He really cares about his students and wants everyone to do well. He is also super funny and just so nice. It's a difficult class but he is 10/10 the best. I wish he taught 203 as well. Take him take him take him

The best Spanish teacher I have ever had hands down. Not only does he know everything about Spanish (native), he also tells you what is important and what is necessary to know to be an actual fluent speaker. Readily available to talk about topics outside of SPAN, he is constantly teaching our class the culture and history of spain. Take him!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: Hand down the best Span 105 teacher at UNC. Very sad he doesnt teach 203. There's a lot of HW from the textbook, but it's not too hard

Spanish 105 is a very work intensive class, but Prof. Clemente makes it a lot more exciting and he is a GREAT teacher and is very passionate about his job. I wish he would teach the next levels of spanish. The class is difficult but he is a great teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: random assignments built as busy work, makes you do an AI comparison....for what?
not much to say other than im not sure how she got this teaching position.
Go to a fortune teller to figure out what reasons she'll take off points for because it won't be stated on the rubric. Oh, also a billion points off for grammar. Take with someone else.

never hated myself more in this class. she assigns a lot of work each week and disregards the fact that we are students with other classes. she changes assignments halfway through the deadline, takes off loads of points for minor errors. I highly recommend taking a different professor if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Took her a different semester and still haunts me. Busy work every week, very condescending, has favorites, seems like one to date a student ngl
Literally don't take her if you want to stay sane. And if you take her, be ready to lose 50 points without her giving any feedback on why
I had her in a past semester--she's just not very inviting or engaging. Lots of busy work, curses, and a really strict grader. Overall, my least favorite class at UNC

So many projects and short deadlines. Super strict grader (you WILL get loads of points off for grammar), makes you go into random communities to do a walk audit (almost attacked by homeless people), gets annoyed when you ask questions, and has a fetish for the baseball dudes.
Very spiteful person.

Dr. Courtney was great! She really values participation and a good relationship with her will only benefit you. She wants you to succeed and is always eager to answer questions and give feedback. The class itself is heavily centered around group work but it's not too terrible. She gave extra credit and saved my grade even after I bombed the final.

Very confusing professor, gets aggravated with students when they ask questions. She is quick to judge her students and will hold grudges against an individual when she feels they ask annoying questions or takes offense when a student tries to explain why they are struggling and seeks help. She takes it as an attack on her teaching. She also curses

I hate group projects but that's not on her. This class is an easy A and she wants you to learn a lot. There are occasional homeworks but can be pretty tedious. I feel like some people may find her confusing but thats on them for messing around during class. She's a great prof

The class wasn't too difficult, but the assignments often felt surface level to me, and group projects were a big part of the grade. I didn't love the lectures, which often felt dry. However, Professor Song was caring and went out of his way to help students succeed.

The material and midterms aren't horrible, but Song is very pedantic in his grading; my biggest gripe though is that he docks 6% of your grade for only missing two classes, which is beyond unreasonable. Avoid if you're looking for a fun, easy A course.

Very easy class if you pay attention to the lectures and professor Song is great. Pretty test heavy with 3 midterms 7 quizzes and an exam but there is no homework besides the group debate project that is too much work and is pretty fun. Professor Song is very nice and a pretty decent lecture so if you take good notes as you go it can be a breeze.

Don't take this class unless you're looking for an extremely mundane course that requires you to memorize minuscule details on weekly quizzes that make up 20% of your grade and exams. Avoid if you're looking for an easy A!

I didn't take GEOG 477, which is a recommended prereq for this class, so I was nervous about this class' difficulty, but it wasn't bad. Just make sure you study for the tests and go to office hours before you get too confused. I'm not sure if this is normal, but he did give us a couple opportunities for extra credit, which was really helpful.

Prof. Song is a great person and lecturer! I learned a lot from his class and really enjoyed the course.  The tests would occasionally include questions on super minor details, but other than that were pretty easy to do well on, especially if you go to class regularly.  Very few assignments outside of tests.  A super nice guy and a 10/10 course!

Incredibly sweet, understanding, and caring. I missed several days due to graduate school interviews and/or mental health reasons and he was so accomodating. The lectures are alright and the class is moderately easy/difficult.

Extremely sweet and caring professor. Very patient and good at answering questions. Labs were super easy and fun, great intro class if you have never done any coding and are intimidated by it. Exams were a little tougher and covered pretty complex concepts that we didn't spend much class time on. Overall great class that I would take again.

I enjoy this professor as a person. I find him to be quite funny, actually. However, I learned very little from this class and I thought the material that was on the exams was extremely unclear. He does not communicate well in regards to what he expects you to know. The labs aren't too difficult, but the tests are.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Song is one of the best professors I have ever had! 410 focused on using MatLab to model the environment. He taught the program from scratch and was great at it. The labs were really cool and fairly straightforward. Also, he is very accessible outside of class!
Great class, although it is required for all environmental science and geography majors. I really enjoyed the modeling environmental systems computer lab work

He's a really nice guy who will try to help you out. He puts a lot on his website, but to do well in the class, you really have to go unless you enjoy the material. Very nice professor who is a good teacher and wants all his students to succeed.
Really nice dude, but hard to understand. Also, he's a bit on the boring side. Nevertheless, you tell he cares a lot about the class.

Great guy, one of the nicest professors around; truly cares about teaching. He can be extremely helpful if you approach him. He has a slight accent, which makes him hard to understand, but other than that, he's awesome.

May be the smartest person you will have the pleasure of listening to. Is an incredibly capable quantitative scientist. If you are interested in remote sensing and ecosystem modeling you will learn TONS from this class. Highly Recommended!
aweful
No Comments
Very great professor. Super understanding, entertaining lectures. Highly recommend. :)

Professor Stenz was a great professor and very helpful during office hours. I was worried about the workload since I had a heavy semester, but the class was manageable. There were four fair quizzes based on lecture material. Attend class, participate, and use office hours and you'll do well.

Connor is a great, welcoming teacher! He was always available to answer any questions inside and outside the classroom. He started and ended lectures with a song and honestly, that was such a highlight. I always looked forward to going to this class. He also is very knowledgeable about study abroad! His lectures were easy to follow and informative.

Professor Stenz is an incredibly caring and fair professor who will make your language course the best class of your semester. He goes out of his way to make class interesting with extra vocab or relatable jokes about the material. He keeps his had on the pulse of the class and makes sure that everyone is on the same page.

Mr. Stenz in an amazing teacher! He makes class engaging, and he is very encouraging/supportive. French is difficult to learn, but he is always willing to help you succeed. There is a lot of homework due before every class, but that is standard across the department. I highly recommend taking his class if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Mr. Stenz is a great instructor! French is a very difficult language to learn, and he truly tries his hardest to explain difficult topics in an effective way. He is very caring about his students and wants to see them succeed. When asking some clarification questions, he can get a little off topic, but overall he was great instructor to learn from!

Professor Stenz is a very kind person who cares about his students very much. He is also very knowledgeable about linguistics. However, this can be difficult because when students ask him a question about content, he goes very in-depth, which can be hard to follow along with. Overall, he is very good at explaining French in a way that makes sense.
Very Charismatic and flexible teacher
Had Mr. Stenz for FREN 101 and 102. He makes class fun and is a very fair grader. He's also super helpful and is forgiving if you miss an assignment or need an extension. 100% recommend!
Teaches very well.

Professor Stenz was super sweet and funny. He cared about his students and wanted us to succeed. Homework was given after every class and wasn't horribly difficult. Tests and quizzes were ok! If I had studied more I probably would have had an A!

Mr. Stenz is an excellent teacher. His class follows the schedule, and homework is assigned before every session, as is standard for all 101 courses in the department. He is encouraging and supportive. Grading is easy as long as you do it. Yet, the listening of his tests is close to the natural speed of native speakers. It was a great semester.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Stenz was an amazing teacher for this course! He truly cares for his students and their success. He responds to emails in a very timely manner and always offered to go over certain material more if the class needed. French can be a pretty difficult language to learn, but he is a great teacher to learn from.

Mr. Stenz always made his classes engaging and really fun! He always makes sure that you are understanding the content and gives good feedback quizzes and papers. Overall he teaches this class very well and makes it a fun class to go to in the morning!

I am so lucky I got Mr. Stenz as my professor this semester! I think if I had a different professor, I would be failing the class. He is super caring and accommodating, and his feedback is incredibly helpful.
He is a great teacher. While the content might be tough for some, he is by far the best Prof to teach it. He is very understanding and overall wants his students to succeed. 10/10 recommend.

Mr. Stenz was awesome! Very understanding of first time french speakers and was able to help with lots of feedback and help inside of class. The class is challenging but him and prof demsey try their best to make it easier!

Go to office hours, do the homework, and ask questions. The class is very hard and requires significant study time. The first test is manageable, but the second is much more difficult. Dr. Compton is super nice and explains the material very well; just be prepared to put in the work. Im on track to get a B.

I love Dr. Compton! He was an absolutely amazing professor. His tests are hard but are always fair, if you study the materials he gives you you'll do great. Make sure you study, you cant pass this class without doing so!
This is a super hard class. other sections easier
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Compton was a great teacher! He really cares about students and whether they understand the material. Calc is test-heavy, but he always offered at least one freebie on each exam (apart from the final). The final was hard, but the entire department made that final. Overall, a great teacher, and arguably the best one for Calc at UNC.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Had a very hard time taking this class. Did not end well
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Really hard class in comparison to other sections. Only if you really want a big challenge
His test are way harder than the level he teaches.
There HAS to be better teachers to take this class with...

Professor Compton was able to make us laugh and make good connections while teaching. He recognizes which students attend every class. He's very clear in his explanations and tries to provide help outside of class. His exams are difficult but he also tries to give extra credit. No matter the professor, calc 3 is going to be hard.
Great in office hours but lectures felt a little fast and kind of jumpy at times.

Good at explaining content in class but the homework is completely different and challenging. Be prepared to go to office hours if you want to understand it. Even though lecture is not required, not everything he talks about is on the posted notes so I would recommend attending most.
Way harder than other teachers…

He is a silly and entertaining professor. His lectures were very clear and understandable. The tests were difficult, but expected with this class. He did randomly call on students, which was terrifying. Also, I had university-approved absences, and he took points off for them.
He is super funny and made learning fun, but has a bit of an ego. Made tests super hard for no reason and just graded harshly
Just not a great person to take any class with. Hard class to begin with, tests are hard and unfair
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is super accessible and presents the information in a way that is easy to understand. He is a very nice guy, and enjoys teaching. However, the tests were really hard and we didn't have many resources outside of homework and recitations to study for them. Lowest midterm is replaced with the final, making the final theoretically 48% of your grade.
I really enjoyed the class and his lectures were very informative. He is a very hard grader so it's hard to justify taking any class with him

He is able to teach the material well, but everything is so much more difficult than what is learned in class. Definitely pay attention to what you did on the homework and if you don't understand something ask in office hours because test questions are often similar to homeworks. Look at book practice problems, they are sometimes on tests too.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He is a nice professor and is clearly passionate about the subject, but his exams are incredibly difficult with no review material or practice exams given. I took Calc 2 with him and liked his teaching style, so I took 381 with him. But compared to the other sections of this course, Compton makes it unnecessarily difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Joe is a solid option for 233. He's caring towards students and encourages you to come to office hours. Lectures are clear, but some topics are only covered in recitation so make sure your recitation TA is good. His exams are no walk in the park, but they prepare you very well for the department-created final.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: great lecturer and very funny! unfortunately his exams are insanely hard, and he provides zero study materials.  he pulls from recitation, HW and lecture notes, so to prepare for the exams you need to practice everything. I still suggest him if you actually plan on learning calc 3, because i doubt youll find a better or kinder teacher then him
He is so funny. Overall really great person to take a class with. The only issue is that he will destroy you with his grading...
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He seems like a nice guy, but his lectures were pointless. He spent half of every class trying to develop analogies that were unhelpful and sometimes inappropriate. Once we got to the actual material he would breeze through it. Tests were fair though and the class itself isn't too hard if you put in the work to study and do practice problems.
Would rec that you consider other options. Good teacher incredibly hard grading for no reason espescialy for first semester of college.

Dr.Compton is a great professor if you attend lectures. I found him to be very accessible outside of class and helpful. However, I found his exams to be quite difficult they are nothing compared to recitation or lecture. He does drop lowest homework and replaces one test with final. P.S. This was my first semester at UNC
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Half the class did horribly other did fine. He didn't seem to be too upset about how poorly some of us were doing.

Lectures don't match the difficulty of exams/hw. Midterms and final exam decide your grade, and the 5% project is hours of work with strict grading. No practice tests or guides, and Edfinity isn't aligned. Many with strong calc backgrounds struggled (class stats shared only on first midterm, and it was a 67%). ONLY take if you can FULLY commit.
Very good lecturer and a very nice prof. Also very helpful in office hours. The class and tests are tough, but if you are willing to put in lots of effort it is possible to do well
Don't take if there are other options.

Difficult and time consuming homework, no practice exams or study guide, not clear on what he puts on midterms. Grading was harsh and unfair. He's fine in lecture, but makes the class entirely more difficult than it needs to be. Random quizzes to count for attendance & only drops one to account for sickness, so if you have to miss more you're SOL.
Very harsh grader. Terrifying.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I'm not sure why he has good ratings on here... He is very condescending, which is not a productive enviornment for learning difficult subjects like math. He doesn't give any practice for exams. Also, you can do great and understand all the topics on midterms, but then do slightly bad on the final and it will tank your grade.

Took him for Calc 2 and really liked him, so decided to take for discrete and regretted it. I know discrete is supposed to be hard, but not this hard. Homework is impossible to do with going to office hours and/or using AI/internet (and even then still incredibly hard). Test questions are also unnecessarily difficult. Don't recommend taking him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great lecturer. Tests were so hard I had to start therapy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great teacher. Do not rec taking unless you are very strong at math. Think deeply before taking this class.

I loved dr. Compton's lectures, he really teaches the concepts in a way which makes them easy to understand. My one big problem with this class is the tests.From what I saw with friends in other sections, our tests were more difficult and had way less study materials.

I love Dr. Compton! He's a great lecturer and truly cares about his students. I'd def recommend showing up to lecture and doing your homework w/out ai. Also go to office hours! He is super accessible and helpful in smaller group settings. For exams I go over his worksheets and I use my friends' old exams for practice. Exams are fair imo.

Super nice guy and definitely a good teacher. The only thing is the exams are nothing like any of the practice you do in class, homework or recitation and he refuses to give practice tests. Also can be unorganized as multiple times we have had homework for topics we need to know on a test due weeks after the test.

Dr. Compton is an amazing lecturer and strives to ensure that his students truly understand the content. If you don't show up to class, you're cooked, but if you do an actively take notes, you'll be fine. Make sure to study before midterms though! Midterms are a hefty portion of the grade, but he replaces your lowest midterm with the final.

Great lecturer and super funny but the exams are very hard and it's kind of hard to determine what you need to know for these exams. He will make questions based on things outside of lecture that you practiced in recitation or on the homework. Wish he was more clear on exam topics and expectations

I took this class with him over the summer after not doing so well on Calc 3 the semester before. He made the concepts easier to understand, and would help so much during office hours, and was very approachable. For this class, it seemed like the class had a structure, and the guided notes were very helpful in following along.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Haven't finished the course yet, but I am a big fan of Dr. Joe. He comes from teaching high school and it's very obvious. He goes very slowly in class and explicitly outlines instructions and the mathematical intuition that is very hard to teach. However, examples in class r nothing like the exam. prepare to do a lil self study.

Really great professor. I took this class during summer, so I don't know if a smaller class size makes a difference, but Joseph made sure to try to keep every student engaged. He also had prepared notes that you filled out in class, so it made it easy to follow along.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Class pacing was poor (his first time teaching the course), but the content was quite easy. Some homework questions were deeper topics than what we learned in class which sucked. I thought he was funny. People say he was condescending: he was sassy when you asked a question 10 minutes after he asked if the class had questions about that topic.. lol

He was an alright teacher and was very nice. Homework took a while but nothing insane. Midterms were very hard and did not give study material. I do not feel like he prepared us well for the final. A lot of it was just the class, it was by far my least favorite class. Midterms + Final were 75% of the grade, and no drops which others teach's offered

Curved 2 midterms, then told us we were “cooked” right before starting the final, then dropped the curve entirely. No grading scale, no clear policy, and final scores hidden until grades were locked. Some secret points added to the final after complaints. Grading felt arbitrary, dismissive, and shady. If you value fairness, avoid this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He was very full of himself and often skipped steps that seemed "easy" to him. The first few units weren't terrible but the semester went down. He favors power series and put them on every exam where as other sections only had 1 exam on them. Class structure is super random and not linear. He has a great attitude tho!

It was the attitude that got me. He's a fine professor and the class wasn't too hard if you showed up. He said that he used to be a high school teacher and would bring those methods which could've been helpful without the condescending tone. Not hard but I definitely wouldn't take a class with him again.

Chill professor overall. not sure if this is a him thing but grading for this course was super unclear and people often didn't know where they stood. he grades homework unnecessarily hard too, but his lecture style is pretty good. don't like how hard his exams are especially compared to other sections.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I'm not very good at math, and the first unit was honestly incredibly easy. Everything went downhill from there. Pacing was awful, lots of homework, no curves, no extra credit, 3 midterms, a 3-part final research project, and a cumulative final exam. One of the worst 100 level classes I've taken. Compton is rude, condescending, and hard to talk to.

Not a horrible class to take, but he spent so much time on the first unit that we didn't get enough time for the other units and it screwed us over during midterms. He got a bit rude to us and would ask us to ask questions but then gave attitude if we did. I would still give him a chance though!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very tough class compared to other 100-level classes. No extra credit, no make-up exams, no curve. Lots of homework. And he is not very nice to change the grades when you forgot to sign up during class.   And there is no review session before the exams. Time for preparing the exam is limited.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very condescending and not great when you have to ask questions or for help. Often times the homework was not things he taught us, and he tries to shove a lot of information into a unit test that should've been spread out across a few units. Four units, 14 homework assignments, final was a project and a cumulative exam.

Compton was a great lecturer and made himself available during office hours. 232 is a difficult course but the tests were made fairly based on the problems seen in class. I would recommend reviewing in-class notes if you have him before the exam, those are the kinds of questions you will be tested on, not whatever is on Edfinity.

he chill imo
does a good job explaining stuff in class and during office hours
Very hard grader, take a grad student

Overall, I really enjoyed taking Math 232 with Joe this semester, and I would totally take another class with him in the future. I'm not a big fan of calculus, but I really like Joe's personality and he is super approachable outside of class! You definitely can't go wrong with him for 232.
Professor Compton is excellent at explaining concepts, and his classes are great!

Compton is a great professor. His lectures are easy to understand, and he always stops before and after class to answer any questions that people have. His tests are fair, and he hosts office hours that are very helpful to figuring out the homework and studying for exams. If you need to take math at UNC I highly recommend!

I would highly recommend Dr. Compton for any math class, especially 110. He does a great job simplifying topics and making sure everyone understands the class concepts. He is kind, funny, and genuinely wants his students to succeed. Algebra should not be a difficult class, and Dr. Compton makes sure of it.

Dr. Compton was my favorite teacher so far at UNC. He was so helpful and easily accessible when having trouble in class. Lectures went through how to do everything we needed to learn and was open to answering questions. He also hosted review sessions before exams. I 100% recommend him.

Dr. Joe is an amazing lecturer. He taught high school previously, and I found he was really able to connect with the students in a more down-to-earth and approachable manor. Tests were manageable, however, homework didn't always align with what was taught in class. If you pay attention in class and do the study guides you will get a good grade.

As most math courses, this was very heavily weighted on midterms and the final. Tests were difficult and long for the amount of time we got. Despite the difficulty of the class, Compton made the content as clear as possible. He was very accessible and good at answering questions. I highly recommend!

Dr. Compton is an excellent teacher. He is friendly, funny, accessible, and has a knack for breaking down tricky concepts very well. Midterms were not easy, and class averages tended to reflect that (~70%), but Calc 2 is hard in and of itself. Irregardless, I highly recommend Dr. Compton.

Prof Compton is easily the best math teacher I've had. He explains content thoroughly and makes the lectures rly engaging. The homework can be difficult but if you can understand it then midterms shouldn't be too bad. Although the timing of the midterms wasn't ideal, he curved the final, which boosted my grade from an A- to an A. Def recommend!
Overall really good professor, homework was tough at times and not always related to test materials, exams were all fair, replaces lowest midterm grade with final.

Given how difficult Calc 2 is, Compton made it seem very straightforward and easy to understand. He explained concepts so in-depth, and his lectures were super easy to follow. He was also very funny and caring towards his students. Calc 2 is hard af no matter who you have but he was great.

I've heard a rumor that math 232 is the most failed class at the school (no idea if that's actually true) but Dr. Compton is peak. Exams make up almost 80% of your grade but he replaces your lowest midterm with your final. Tests are fair and homework is hard. Dr. Compton is overall a cool guy and checked all of the boxes and more. Engaging lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Compton is an amazing person! The class was tough but he did his best to help us on the midterms and the final! He drops a few homework assignments, which were online and more difficult than the exams, and also replaced our lowest midterm with the final. Overall, great professor just get ready to study a lot!

If you have to take a math class at UNC, take it with Dr. Compton. He made harder concepts easily understandable and really took the time to slow down if needed. He was very reachable outside of class and there were a few extra credit opportunities. Truly one of the best professors at UNC.

Notes during class presents the new topic with easy-to-do examples. Homework is quite a bit more difficult so the notes don't prepare you all too well. Midterms and final make up most your grade and the averages are in the low 70s. Tricky to prepare for the tests well since resources are scarce. Final was difficult.

Lectures are very clear, but the pace of the class makes it hard to keep up at times. The midterms created by him were much harder than the final, but the class never felt horribly unfair. The only unfair feeling part of the class was the midterms and final being worth 78% of your grade in total. Pay attention and you should be good.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Joe is the math prof i've ever had. takes a hard class and makes it enjoyable. knows most of his students by name.   lectures are so good and he posts all completed notes. midterms are hard and worth a lot of your grade, but if you pay attention in class and go to office hours you'll be fine. homework way harder than the test but good practice.

I really like Professor Compton because he is very caring and shows so much passion for teaching math. However, this class was the most difficult class I have ever taken and the exams were extremely hard. The class averages were never too great for these exams, but you genuinely learn a lot in this class. Also, make sure to go to class.

Great professor!! I had Dr. Compton for college algebra b/c of have no foundational math skills haha. He was a phenomenal teacher and introduced a conversational style in his lectures, as he used to be a high school teacher. He does a great job explaining concepts and always takes questions. I purposefully signed up to take math 130 w him next sem!

I loved him I had him for math 110!!!! So funny and caring!! He is so sweet attendance was mandatory sometimes (we did in-class assignments). I would so take his class again. after hearing what other math 110 teachers are like I think he is one of the better ones.
Hard class, but a good teacher. He wants to help you. Clear information.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I love Calc 232 with Dr. Compton! He is readily available, wants us to succeed, and funny in class. Clearly explains information and his teaching style is very explicative. Very very good teacher!

He is very good at communicating information and helping you understand how to utilize the theoretical knowledge taught in class on questions. Exam questions are very straightforward and reasonable. The final was pretty challenging and you can lose significant points for small mistakes on the homework. Overall, he is a very good professor to have.

Joe is the best. I've heard of much easier 381 teachers, but Joe is an amazing teacher even if his exams can be difficult. He explained everything very well and is super accessible, and we learned a lot more than other sections. He encourages participation, attending office hours, and working in groups all of which made the class great

Great class! He wrote me recs for some summer programs which I really appreciated. He teaches almost directly by the textbook (which you could find online), so reading outside of class isn't really necessary but it can help if you don't understand something from in class.

IMO one of the better choices for 381. Hard grader, but he curved the grade scale based on all sections' grade distributions (a 50 was a B on the final). Super helpful in office hours and over email, and genuinely seemed like he cared. Explained things super well in lectures. Mildly concerned about his work/life balance.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures are very clear and fun. Explain concepts well and provide specific examples. Frequently hold office hours. Homework are not too bad, take about one or two hours if use LaTex. The homework of lowest grade gets dropped. Three midterms each worth 15% and final worth 35%.

381 is a hard class, but I really appreciated the way Joe taught it. His lectures were straight from the textbook, but I liked that because I could check the book later if I missed something in class. Weekly homework was also problems from the textbook, and it usually took me 2-3 hours. The final was worth 35%, but it also had a massive curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very caring and approachable (frequent office hours). Lectures are organized and follow the textbook. I personally feel his style/pace fits those who enjoy taking notes in class. Notes are important. Exams can be tricky. HW grading is not his fault so reach out to him during OH. (and don't use latex for hw. It's great but exam is with pen)

So it is a very difficult class and that is obvious but Joe is quite possibly the most accessible professor I have ever had. Would almost certainly take the class with him again and he is one of the best professors I have had at UNC and he is only a graduate student I hope he continues to teach at UNC after his PhD.

Joe is a wonderful professor. While his tests and midterms were a little more theoretical and complicated than the homework and examples in class, he's does only test on what's covered in class and is super available during office hours. He's also very kind and understands that it's a hard class so he's always a great person to go to and talk with.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Pretty good professor, first year teaching discrete so I bet he would get better
Worst class taken here if you need this class don't take it with him
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Such a hard class, teacher expects you to know everything.

His first semester teaching discrete but he basically just read out the textbook and wrote it on the board. He also wasn't super clear on what his expectations were on hw and tests and then would grade very strictly and had low test averages. If you're ready to put in the extra studying time you'll be fine but its not an easy class w/anyone...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Compton is a very clear lecturer who does an excellent job explaining mathematical topics. He clearly wanted the whole class to succeed. He was always accessible for questions and gave quick and helpful answers. No test question was ever not representative of what was done on homework and in class. You can't go wrong if you choose his class.

Took Cervantes class with Dr. Collins - reading heavy, obviously, but we took Don Quixote piece by piece and she knows so much about the book, so lectures were interesting, even at 8AM. Did not provide super clear feedback about grading criteria, but wasn't harsh, either. Take notes in class and you'll be prepared for the minimal essays + exams
Such a great professor. Homework is just reading. Good books ngl and i dont even like reading. Participate and you will do fine. Everything is super chill too
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. You read a lot of books but she covers them thoroughly, so as long as you take notes you're fine! Few tests (Midterm, 1 paper, 1 group project and final). Gives comprehensive feedback and she's the sweetest teacher. Take notes and you'll be grand. Take this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This is the second class I have taken with her and it was the same format. There is one group presentation, a research paper, and two exams. She is very kind, but class can get kind of boring. It is all discussion and presentations. She grades fairly easy and I would likely take another class with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's very passionate, but she teaches in a confusing way. Classes were discussion based and exams were based on stuff mentioned by students in lectures. No rubrics were given for anything. You never know what she's looking for, and she mentions out of the box connections in your assignments and takes off points if you didn't make the connections.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class is discussion based and she chimes in to make sure the conversation is continuing. There is a group oral presentation that is fairly easy with pretty open guidelines. There is also one 12-15 pg research paper, but there was little instruction on what to do. No rubric provided either so really no idea what she was looking for.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Collins is hands-down my favorite professor at UNC. She is passionate about her work and truly values hearing the interpretations and thoughts of her students. She would guide the overall structure of the lectures but for the most part she let us provide our opinions, point to places in the text, and ask questions. TAKE HER CLASSES!

She is passionate about her lessons and tries to be as engaging as possible. It's nice that most of the material is discussion-based rather than lecture style. She isn't a tough grader but gives helpful feedback and communicates well via email. 10/10 recommend :)

A great choice for a 300-level ENGL course. There's a 12-15 pg paper and a lot of reading but you could get away without doing the readings because they're discussed in class. Beloved is an amazing book though and I would recommend reading it. The midterm was an open-note essay during class and the final wasn't bad either. Attendance is required.

Professor Collins has been one of my favorite professors I've had at UNC!! She is amazing, and truly cares about each of her students. The class has a fair number of readings, but if you keep up with them, and pay attention to lectures, you will do fine on the limited amount of assignments Professor Collins assigns.

She is the nicest professors I have had! She is constantly smiling & cares a lot about her students. You do have a 10pg paper at the end of the course but you pick your own topic. Theres a lot of reading, but as a person who usually doesnt like reading, I enjoyed reading for this class. She is very insightful about curiosity and makes learning fun!

Prof Collins is so kind, and super accessible via email/office hours/appointment. For 300s level classes, she usually has a midterm, a group project, a final, and a 10-page paper. She's a very lenient grader--as long as you put in the effort, she will reward your hard work. She also took our class to Ackland a couple of times for a change of pace.

Professor Collins is a gem! She is very eloquent in how she describes curiosity and the imagination and is so intelligent. On top of it all, she is one of the sweetest people I have ever met! If you have the opportunity, take a class with her. Although there is plenty of reading(I don't like to read), I thoroughly enjoyed the class and lectures.

One of my FAVORITE professors at UNC! I have taken two of her comparative literature classes (Romancing the World and Don Quixote) and plan to take more if possible. There is a lot to read but her lectures are always so interesting and insightful.

One of my favorite professors so far at UNC. As long as you come to class and do the readings, you will pass. Some of the readings were boring, but others were great and interesting (about half and half). Professor Collins truly cares about each student and what they learn from her. I would take this again.
She is the sweetest teacher. Her tests are very hard/specific, but she grades papers fairly. Lots of reading per class, but I would definitely recommend her!

I was delighted to have my senior seminar with Dr. Collins. For starters, she is SUCH a sweet, ebullient lady. She chose interesting texts, kept class discussions lively, and was reasonable with expectations/feedback. Also super knowledgeable in Renaissance lit and Cervantes.  If I hadn't graduated I'd be in her classes all the time!

I enjoyed this class because I love literature but I have a friend in the class who does not and she thought it was miserably boring. Overall, very easy if you read the books and attend lecture every now and then.

I took CMPL 390 - Don Quixote with Prof Collins and LOVED it. Stay on top of the readings, attend class and participate occasionally and you'll make an A. The tests weren't difficult if you did the reading and paid attention. Prof Collins is incredibly intelligent and very helpful! Definitely take her class!
Collins' lectures are very boring, she reads them directly from a piece of paper and they tend to be pretty unnecessary. You don't have to attend lecture very often to get a good grade in the class.

Dr. Collins is sooooo nice and very helpful. She really knows the material very well, and she is encouraging to all students. I learned so much from her. My only comment is that it would be better if she taught classes all in Spanish instead of English.

Dr. Collins is the best professor! She is very helpful, kind and patient, and she really knows her stuff. She works with both Golden Age and Twentieth Century Spanish lit and is well-versed in both. Her classes are not easy, but they are worth taking, and if you work hard you will do well.

Haven't finished the class yet but Dr. Johnson is by far my favorite Biology professor that I have had so far. He is really funny and very willing to help you if you are having trouble understanding a concept. Explains content clearly. Responds to email way faster than the average STEM professor. Class isn't easy but is doable with some studying.

This class can be very difficult if you don't make it a point to study the Anki in between every class session. If you do use the Anki and go to open labs, the exams aren't too difficult but are definitely still challenging. There is a lot to memorize in this class, but it is definitely doable!

Dr Johnson is really caring and very knowledgeable. He is easy to reach outside of class and is super accommodating to all of his students. His exams aren't super difficult if you go to class and study the material, as well as the only work outside of exams is a Mastering due before each class period. Would highly recommend!
I absolutely loved Dr. Johnson; he was a great teacher and had very fair exams. Would definitely take again.

Should not be a 1 credit class. It's hard but not impossible. DO THE ANKI and practice provided and you'll be pretty prepared. Is all memorization with some application -- the application depends on what you memorize. Review sessions, open labs, and LAs are excellent resources. Hope for a good TA they can make or break the class and your graded

The GOAT. Material is straight forward from lectures. He records all lectures, and attendance is lenient. Talk to him in office hours, he is so very understanding. Would not have taken this course with no one else.
Absolute beast. The most straight-forward UNC STEM class. I learned a lot too.

Dr. Johnson is awesome! He is an incredibly effective lecturer and funny. His attendance and homework policies were extremely lenient, leaving room to miss class and turn in homework up to a week late. His exams are extremely fair and consistent. Take 252 with Dr. Johnson, you won't regret it!!!

The best STEM professor I've ever had. I wouldn't say the content is easy but his exams are very clear and very reflective of what you learn in class. He definitely wants students to succeed and gives every resource possible to do well for exams.

my fav prof of all time without doubt. genuinely has the students in tears of laughter multiple times a lecture, and WANTS us to succeed. the course content is hard, but i find it so easy to understand with how his lectures are set up and the jokes he makes. i have a 97 in the class rn and the final should be a breeze. def take him for a&p!!
Corey J is THE GOAT. A simple guy who doesn't make his mission to make his students miserable. Not a ton of grades but exams are relatively easy if you study. Best Bio class at UNC. He is hilarious

Dr. Johnson is THE BEST professor I have ever had. The course material can be hard, but he teaches in a way that makes everything so easy to understand. The only assignments are GRQs through Pearson that you have unlimited attempts for. He also provides practice exams to prepare you for each exam. Could not recommend him enough!
So much memorization. Worse than the actual anatomy class.

Dr. Johnson is truly one of the best professors I've had at UNC! He is very kind, understanding, and easily approachable. He genuinely wants you to succeed! With that said, the class is tough, but it is fair. Put in the work and it pays off!

Take Johnson!!!!!! Best anatomy professor here. Made me actually enjoy the content, and gave fair exams. He is a Hilarious guy who keeps you laughing throughout the lecture, and you can tell he has a true joy for the teacher. Give him a raise!!!!

Most of the class is the TA; but overall this class was really easy. Start studying the Anki about a week or two out from each exam, do the labeling exercises, online exercises, and take GRQs/PLQs seriously and you'll get an easy A. The exams were some of the easiest exams I've taken at UNC, I didnt take more than 45 minutes on any of them

Professor Johnson is ABSOLUTELY the professor you want to take Biol 252/253 with 100%. He is a great lecturer and gives exams that are solely multiple choice. Provides practice exams and tries his best to teach at a pace that gives you time to process and understand concepts. Attendance is just PollEvs. I would 1000% take a class with him again.

Professor Johnson is by far my favorite professor I've had at UNC. In both 252 & 253, he breaks down difficult concepts & makes them feel clear and approachable. It's obvious that he truly cares about his students' success and puts in the effort to help us do well. He makes lectures genuinely enjoyable - I always look forward to going to his class!

Had him for 252, and I'm so glad I have him again for 253. His lectures are super well organized, he's great at explaining tough concepts, and I feel the exams are very fair. You can tell he really cares about his students and implements their feedback for the class. Plus he's a really funny guy.

I cannot express just how amazing Dr. Johnson is! By far my absolute favorite professor. He takes time to get to know his students, ensures you know the material, engages students in lecture, and genuinely loves what he does. I like his group office hours, where he has spent both group and one-on-one time with students. Take his class if you can!

BIOL252L is a tough class, but with the right study approach, you can definitely succeed. Consistent memorization and using resources like Unstuckstudy alongside the lectures and textbook make all the difference. The exams are challenging, but the TAs provide great support.

I cannot speakly highly enough of Professor Johnson. He's understanding, encouraging, and a delight for any student. He does not allow cheat sheets but his tests are noticeably easier than other professors who do permit cheat sheets. Professor Johnson is an incredibly lecturer, and just a good person in general.

Dr. Johnson is the best bio prof. I have had so far at UNC. He actually teaches the material. He also provides practice exams before each exam that are extremely comparable to the actual exams. The textbook and homework are helpful. If you attend class and study you will do well. He's also super funny.
