reviews.comment: On one of the last days of class we were put into groups and then asked to write what we liked about the class and what could be done better. When people offered constructive criticism they were shot down with excuses and disrespectful remarks. I have never been more afraid to offer my honest opinion in a class. Consider switching if you get her.

Dr. Crystall was a great professor, easy to talk to and made class interesting. The work assigned is not difficult at all and I always felt what she expected in an assignment was clear. The two textbooks required were not used except for one assignment at the beginning so find another way to get them besides buying.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She is no where near as bad as everyone on here says she is. Maybe it is just that I took her at 9:30am and everyone else had her in the afternoon? She is an easy grader and makes jokes time to time.

Prof Crystall single-handedly ruined my first semester at UNC. An extremely tough grader for a first-year level English class, and is not approachable at all. She is extremely condescending when you ask her for help and is so vague with her instructions. DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS.

She isn't that bad!! (at least in engl155). Even though attendance is highly mandatory, she was a fair grader. Her class was boring sometimes and sometimes interesting, but it was very possible to receive a good grade!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Crystall is a very interesting and quirky woman that makes this class enjoyable. She isn't too clear on what/when things are due, but makes up for it by assigning easy work that rarely takes more than 1-2 hours to complete. She talks for most of class, which means you can just listen and laugh. She's lowkey hilarious and cares about students

I never felt unsafe in a learning environment ever in my life until I took a class with this woman. She thinks her opinion is the only one that matters. If you offer a differing point of view or even just ask for clarification about an assignment, she will yell at your in front of the entire class. I once had a panic attack on the way to her class.

Dr. Crystall is by far the worst English teacher I have had in my education experience so far.  She is extremely vague, unhelpful, close minded, and disrespectful. I can't say I have ever enjoyed her class or her as a professor. Please avoid taking her class, no matter what it takes. The course work isn't hard but she is my least favorite professor

AVOID taking this class. She is very vague spacey, but manages to get snappy and angry when students make mistakes. I sat next to a slower boy in class, and she ripped into him often (cutting him off sharp tone eye rolling). SO RUDE!!  If you take it, buckle down, do your very best work, and always cover your butt by taking the extra mile.

Her assignments were very confusing and she was unclear about her expectations. She could be rude sometimes. She found no issues with any of my papers and I made As on everything, but I would really have valued some instruction there, as I really didn't know how to write college papers as a first-semester freshman.
Dr. Crystall was very unclear with most of her assignments. I'd recommend to avoid any class you have with her.
Really disliked Dr. Crystall mainly because of how unclear she was with all of her assignments. I'd suggest to not take any of her classes.
she is not a good teacher and does not respect others opinons.

If you are looking for a really easy class to fill your LA credit, TAKE ENGL 124!!! It's about graphic novels, which are essentially comic books.  Not only is it an easy grade, but the material is fun to read. Not a lot of effort needed. Two papers, two group discussions, a midterm, and a final. Great class, wonderful prof!!
If you have to rearrange your schedule not to take her class, do it.  It's worth it, trust me.  So mean and so stubborn.  A total headache.
No Comments

As previously stated, this woman does believe that her opinion is the only opinion.  As a very liberal person myself, politically and socially, I find her liberal bias in the classroom unnecessary and limiting to her young students.  She is SOOO politically correct that it makes real debate and dialogue in the classroom impossible.
a great teacher; entertaining and lively in class, kept discussion going; very tolerant of all points of view, even when we discussed controversial issues
Great professor. Very compassionate.
booooooo...terrible

Class is taught seminar style. Will occassionally pop quiz. There is one group project, and 2 papers only 1 serious one. Midterm and final are 1 essay. As long as you participate she likes you. Has some pet peeves with grammar though.
She is the sweetest professor and so funny! She cares about her students a lot. We did questions of the day at the beginning of class every day and it was so fun!

Cris was very chill and nice! There is not a lot of homework and two exams. Her lectures were interesting for the most part. Make sure you take notes and listen in class to do good on the exams. I recommend her!

Cristiana is one of the best WGST professors I have had. She is so caring, and her lectures are very engaging. WGST 224 is an interesting class, and I would totally recommend it. I would also recommend taking good notes during lectures and doing the readings so you do well on the midterm and final. Her exams are fair though if you pay attention.

Cris is really cool and her class was very progressive. She was really nice and there was literally no work. The tests were all multiple choice which sucked but also didn't. Just go to class to get participation points, I never went to class so that's why my participation grade was so bad. Otherwise easiest A.

Professor Crescenzi is a dedicated instructor who makes a genuine effort to support students. The class has a heavy workload, but his insights and unstuckstudy AI make it manageable. Worth taking if you're interested in the material.

Dr. Crescenzi had essay-only exams, but they were open-note and open-book. There were also tons of readings, but most of them were skimmable. I appreciate that he keeps it real with students regarding the state of school leadership and global events.

Professor Crescenzi is phenomenal. He truly cares about the wellbeing of his students and has a passion for the material at hand. Overall, the class wasn't too bad with lots of writing assignments, a midterm, and final. Some of the reading was dense, but he was understanding and lectures clarified any confusion. Take any class you can with him!

The best professor I have ever had. Incredibly responsive, intelligent, and passionate about his work. Lots of reading, and the economic units were a little bit miserable for me, but his lectures are very insightful and make the assignments easier to understand. Wants his students to succeed and devotes a lot of class time to answering questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Crescenzi is one of my favorite professors that I have had so far at UNC. You can really tell that he cares about his students and wants you all to do well. Professor was so understanding with all of the events of this past year and made sure to check in on his students. I always felt respected and supported in this class.

If I could only take classes by this professor, I would. He cares deeply about his students and the material and is super knowledgeable. I recommend mentioning the micro state of San Marino as he is extremely knowledgeable. He cares about learning more than individual assignments and allowed for late assignments due to the shooting on campus.

Easily one of the best professors I've had at UNC. Assigned readings are important and coincide with homework assignments, but pretty easy grader and the activities help to understand class content. Lots of class discussion, he really cares about his students and respects what they have to say. If you can get into a class with him, take it!

This class was alright. It wasn't my favorite, but I didn't hate it. The class has a ton of reading and several papers that you'll have to finish in a night or two. Most classes are lecture heavy, but you do a couple of fun interactive activities. The prof is super understanding and kind, the material is just not my favorite.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Crescenzi was awesome. Easily one of the best professors at UNC. Seriously, any class you can take with him, take it. You can tell he genuinely loves teaching and cares for his students. Felt really out of depth going into this course but felt fully prepared for the exams just from readings/class discussions

Professor Crescenzi is one of the best professors I've had! He is so caring, funny, and engaging in class. His deep knowledge and wide range of experience in international politics make his lectures very interesting. He is a very easy grader, but just be prepared to write a lot of essays. I know he loves helping students find opportunities, too!

Professor Crescenzi is the best. His course was very well adapted to the pandemic, he's understanding of all perspectives, and gives room to express your own beliefs and thoughts freely. The course structure was mostly asynchronous and super flexible. The grading seems TA dependent but his TA's are awesome. Take this class!

Professor Crescenzi is one of the best professors I've had at UNC. He really cares about his students and the course material. He was really understanding with the pandemic and tried to accommodate the class with the needs of students. I highly recommend taking a course with him if you can.

Professor Crescenzi is an underrated teacher at UNC. Was understanding of the situations of students during the pandemic and took it into account throughout the semester with syllabus adjustments. Lectures were rather interesting as he often tied it to current events. All assignments are graded by your TA, so the experience can vary by recitation.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Prof Crescenzi is one of the best professors I've had. He was very understanding and has done so much to make the learning experience more enjoyable and less stressful in light of the course going online due to covid. The class is fairly straightforward, and he makes the material super interesting and well spaced-out. Would definitely take again!

Prof. Crescenzi is the chair of the Political Science Department, and he is truly a gem. He is so kind, understanding, and down to earth. He wants students to succeed and will work with you to ensure you do. He is very well read and knowledgeable but is purposeful in making sure his students are receptive. I would definitely take his class again!

Great Class! I love Professor Crescenzi. He did so good giving us the perfect introduction to international relations. I had this class online because of Corona. He was so caring and really helped all of us out. I loved this class!

Prof. Crescenzi is one of the best I've had at UNC. He's SO incredibly kind and was extremely accommodating with COVID. He's passionate about what he teaches and genuinely cares about students. Class consisted of a midterm, final, and 8 one-page writing assignments graded by your TA. Take a class with Crescenzi if you can!!!

Prof Crescenzi is one of the kindest and most empathetic educators I've ever seen and taking his class made this entire online semester that much more enjoyable. He encourage feedback like no prof I've seen before. He's reminds of a skinnier political science genius Santa Clause. If you get the chance to be in one of his classes, go for it!

Great professor- as a senior I have NEVER seen a prof actually accommodate students on this level. Though there are weekly writing reports, there is no central essay. My TA graded somewhat harshly but turned out ok in the end. Midterm probs relates more to TA. Mark always checks in and actually hears students, it's beyond.

Asynchronous. Love this professor & can't wait to take another class with him. Acknowledged the pandemic & our stress & lightened our load to the extent possible. 8-10/16 1-page writing assignments are counted, one midterm, one final, participation. I liked my TA & I liked the material. A little boring at times but recommend taking online.

THE MOST AMAZING PROFESSOR !!! He actually acknowledges that we are in a pandemic right now !! Not only does he want each student to succeed, but he shows that he cares by constant encouragement throughout the semester in emails/Zoom meetings !! He is always available and helpful during office hours, easy to talk to, and has great lectures !!!

Prof. Crescenzi is amazing! So understanding of students' needs, good lectures. Super knowledgeable but knows how to teach an intro class in a way that is perceptible and interesting. This class is not hard to get a good grade in if you do the work. It gives you a great toolkit to continue learning about POLI!

Crescenzi is the best prof ever. He was so accommodating because of COVID and online learning. For example he basically cancelled our final which relieved so much stress off me. His lectures were super helpful and the writing assignments were not difficult. He gave us so many opportunities to get As. And the TAs are all awesome. TAKE THIS CLASS!!!

Dr. Crescenzi is awesome. i personally found the class really boring but that probably bc it was asynchronous! prof made this class a little better by giving really clear and helpful lectures and being super understanding. the online class is very well designed and adapted

Mark Crescenzi is an angel. The material can be heavy but he breaks everything down as much as possible in his lectures and is readily available outside of class to discuss anything you don't understand. He is one of my best-adapted professors to the online format and is still always willing to adjust assignments and exams to help students. Async.

His lectures are interesting and he is very accessible outside of class. He adjusted to online classes extremely well and he lightened the workload wherever he could to help us out. The class does have a lot of reading, but it's not too difficult and you'll do fine if you keep up with the reading and lectures. I could not recommend him more.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Crescenzi is one of few professors at UNC that recognize the difficulties of online learning and COVID-19. He found every opportunity to extend grace by making assignments easier, lightening the workload, even changing our final to reduce the stress of a timed final. He truly cares about our wellbeing. If you can take his class, DO IT!

Loved this class. Mark cares about us and wanted us to learn & do well. His expectations were clear and grading was fair. If you show up and do all the readings, you'll do well, but it's definitely not an easy- A. This was a small honors class, very discussion based. He's also chair of the political science department so he really knows his stuff.

Professor Crescenzi cares about his students' success and their understanding of the material. Class is discussion-based and necessary to do well on the tests. There's only a paper, a midterm and a final so everything counts. Very interesting class with really well-chosen readings. I learned a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Crescenzi was my favorite professor from this semester. He is very accessible and truly cares about his students. His lectures are pretty laid back but he doesn't use powerpoints. POLI150H was very discussion based so skipping class means you might not understand everything, but the textbook is very clear and honestly pretty interesting
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Crescenzi is a great professor who genuinely cares about his students and will do his best to make sure you understand the material. The class is graded by very few things though, so don't expect an easy A.

Professor Crescenzi is a great lecturer and really cares about his student's success. While his lectures can get a little advanced from time to time, he just wants us to know the material and succeed. Cares about his students in the long run.

One of the best classes I've taken at UNC. There is a lot of reading but he takes a lot of time to explain the material. You have 2 big assignments (individual and group paper) and he is really helpful if you reach out.

Hands-down the best professor I've ever had at Carolina. He's incredibly smart, passionate about international conflict, and cares about his students. He made me love game theory and international conflict. And, he is more than willing to provide assistance when material is confusing. I'd take anything he taught.

Not the most exciting lecturer, but he is very nice and helpful. He uses powerpoints but doesn't put notes on them. So you have to listen up in lecture. Exams and papers were reasonable. Be sure to take advantage of office hours. There is a lot of information to absorb in this class.

This was one of my favorite classes at UNC. His lectures were interesting and he's a funny guy. Tests are based on the recitation readings and his lectures, not so much on the textbooks. If you go to class and do the reading you'll do fine.

Does a good job in lecture of making the material interesting.  Attendance is very slack for lecture, but it helps to attend.  Tests require lots of detail but aren't overly difficult.  If you get a good TA, you're in good shape.  Class average is about a low B.
Lectures were interesting most of the time. Lots of reading. Tests were kind of tough but not impossible plus he curved. I would definitely take it again.

great professor, knows how to teach. class was on the difficult side. tests were tough, a combination of tricky MC and short answers with a longer essay. tough grader, and he enjoys it. i would recommend it, I think everyone should get some sense of international politics

Only gives about 12% A/A-, which is worse than intro chem classes.His tests were essentially a collection of the most trivial things he could think of.His goal is to think up MC questions that have never been used before anywhere, so they end up being tricky and nit-picky.His lectures are interesting enough and he's a nice guy, but avoid his class.
No Comments
Tests are pretty difficult, and he doesn't seem too interested in making them better.  His lectures are OK, but his tests ruin the course.  Avoid him.
interesting class. HARD tests. lots of reading. curves pretty well (altough he has too, av. on the firts test was a 60) be prepared to work very hard to get a good grade, but A's are feasible.

Well...if you love multiple choice tests that are tricky then do take his class. There is a lot of reading with this course. Other than textbooks there are many articles to read and you are tested on them. Recitation also requires additional reading which you are tested on. The class was not inspiring.
Interesting class...hard tests
No Comments

Dr. Cramer is caring but lecture heavy professor, I took this as a junior and thought it was comparable to bio 103 and 220 level of difficult. She always curves 4-5 points on exams at least. Very fair exams. Study organisms the most and rewatch lectures in depth! go to her office hours to review exams. do GLQs but hunt and gather for answers.

Dr. Cramer is overall a very sweet and funny professor. We did fall behind in class sometimes, but the exams were easy as long as you studied everything that was gone over in the lecture. She tells you what you need to know for the exams and the Anki and Organism Cards are good resources to study. It was also very nice that she curved.

This class was crazy hard, but Dr. Cramer always seemed to make an effort to make it a little easier. Every exam is curved by like 5 pts. The content and lab are super interesting, but there is a LOT of content. Lectures can be hectic, we fell behind a lot, but she took content we didn't get to off the exam. Stay engaged, you'll do fine!

Dr Cramer is great professor but her class is definitely hard! Beware there is a lot of information and it is easy to fall behind. Keep up with readings, Anki, and make sure to pay attention in class, she hints what will be on the exam sometimes. Exams are mainly memorization and covers every single thing she gives you. The lab is fun too!

If you want to succeed in this class you have to WORK for it. MCRO is VERY difficult and requires a lot of discipline if you want to do well. DO ANKI EVERYDAY!! It will help you A LOT. Anyways, overall, the class was good and Dr. Cramer cares a lot about her students.

Dr. Cramer is one of the best professors I have had at UNC! Mirro is content-heavy, but not as difficult as people say. The exams are primarily based on simple memorization and consist of multiple-choice, select-all, and fill-in-the-blank questions. As long as you keep up with the assignments (which there are a lot of) you will be fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I fully wished I had been hit by a car on the way to her classes. Not a single thing she said would be on the exams, were on the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is a HARD class, but an A/A- is obtainable. It really is just all memorization, but it is A LOT of information, so keep up with Anki, organism cards, and go to SI sessions! I LOVE Cramer and she really does care about what she's teaching, but honestly, she can be a bit frazzled at times. Still, the resources are there for you to succeed.

Her exams are EXTREMELY memorization based. I love a good application based test and these are not that so they were very difficult for me. ANKI is your best friend. And so is Dr. Cramer. So sweet in office hours, will give you fist bumps for questions you got right on the exam, etc. MCRO is hard, and needs a LOT of time but it is worth it.

MCRO is a difficult class, you need to listen to lectures and study to do well but I believe I was given more than enough resources to be successful. I personally found the lectures super interesting which helped. I also found the content to be pretty basic - there is just A LOT of it. Do not be afraid of Dr. Cramer! She was awesome!

Don't listen to the bad reviews. Dr. Cramer is the absolute best STEM professor at UNC. Yes, this class is a lot of information, and it requires a LOT of studying. But you can tell Dr. Cramer cares about her students and wants them to do well. Go to her office hours and STUDY!

This professor is hilarious, sure, sometimes she is a little disorganized and maybe a little insane, but I enjoyed her class. She made every lecture fun, and I could tell she really cared about the material and wanted us to do well.

Professor Cramer is an engaging lecturer who makes the material interesting. While the exams are challenging, completing the guided learning questions and using Anki and Unstuck AI for study prep can help you succeed. Overall, it's a tough but worthwhile class.

This class was interesting, and I learned a lot in the end. But this class is HARD, especially if you take it with other challenging STEM classes. Your grade is based purely on exams 2 Midterms, each 24%, and a Final that is 24%. These tests are DIFFICULT, but you can do well if you study at least 2 weeks in advance, DO THE ANKI, and meet with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I was scared going into this class because of her other reviews but I can truly say that she is an amazing professor and if you study and stay on top of the material you can definitely get an A. I have struggled in other science classes at UNC but Dr. Cramer does a good job on explaining content in a clear way. I would definitely recommend her!

She does care deeply for her students and you get that sense when you come into her office hours. She is a funny lecturer. The best way to stay on top of the class is to stay on top of your GLQs and rewatch the lectures!! After class print out the blank GLQ & treat it like a quiz to refresh your memory. She & her TAs are accessible through Piazza.

Professor Cramer genuinely cares about you and wants you to succeed. Compared to my other STEM classes, I really enjoyed this one, despite being scared to take it from the reviews on here. She is a very good lecturer and is very passionate about the material she is teaching. She curved all of our tests as well.

Dr. Cramer is very funny during lecture, and makes an hour and 15 minute lecture very engaging. The course is exam heavy as the three exams (2 exams and final exam) are worth 72% of your final grade. If you complete your guided learning questions, take good notes, and do anki, you will do fine in this class.

Dr. Cramer is one of my favorite professors at UNC! She is so sweet and really cares about her students and wants you to succeed. I highly suggest going to office hours and the SI sessions!! Although, the class is still hard and moves pretty fast. There is a TON of information to know. But getting a good grade is still doable!

DEFINITELY A HARD CLASS. Don't get me wrong. I would recommend studying 2 weeks in advance of every midterm because there is so much material and the exams are very tough. That said, Dr. Cramer is a very very kind person and is absolutely lovely and accessible in office hours.

One of the coolest classes I've taken. Do Anki decks, keep up with GRQs, and show up to lecture, and you won't get less than a 95% on exams. She can be a lil scattered at times, but her passion for her subject is evident, and she works really hard to make things interesting and relevant. I'd take another class with Dr. Cramer any day!

Dr. Cramer is kind and accessible in office hours. However, it was hard for me to follow her lecturing, and tested material comes from many different sources. Overprepare for exams; try to condense all the material from Anki, GLQs, and especially from the lectures, since any of it is fair game. Try to write down every point she makes in lecture!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you do the anki, do the GLRs before class, and just genuinely apply yourself, the class is not that hard. Cramer is super nice, ESPECIALLY if you make an effort to get her to know you. She does a great job of explaining the content and if you do the GLRs before class it is so easy to understand.

I loved Dr. Cramer, she was very funny/engaging and was always available to answer any possible questions, especially before exams. The exams were very difficult but she made the expectations clear and gave us all the tools we needed to succeed as well as curved every exam, as long as you put enough time into the assignments and study it's not bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Don't get me wrong: I love MCRO. But on the last day of class, she taught us completely new materials for 80 minutes, while the final was less than 3 days away. She is SO DISORGANIZED! Additionally, you need to memorize TONS of materials. Some people said on rmp that she is caring, but I really do not sense that from her pushy attitude in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I enjoyed the content we learned in class, it is probably one of the most interesting STEM classes I've taken. However, Dr. Cramer is SO unorganized. Her reorganization makes the class much more difficult when the content itself is already hard. She also makes her exams very difficult. As long as you are able to teach yourself well, you're good.

I have mixed feelings. On one hand, exams were very difficult in terms of time and content, if I had an extra 15-20 minutes I could have finished all of them. For the first two exams I had to guess on at least 6 questions each. But there is a lot of classwork to cushion your grade. Professor Cramer is an enthusiastic professor and nice human.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Cramer is extremely smart, kind, & has the potential to be the best STEM professor at UNC. Her lectures are interesting but she is VERY disorganized. She teaches this (mainly underclassmen) course the same as she would a med student. I think she forgets that all of these concepts are new & we do not have the experience or ground knowledge yet.

Dr. Cramer is fun, so sweet, and does want to see you succeed, especially if you take the time to ask! That said, the way she words exams is extremely tricky & confusing. I got a 99 on the lab final & walked out of the OPEN NOTE lecture final crying. Even if you understand the material, you can find yourself very lost on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Thought I could challenge myself with this professor but boy was I not ready. I was not able to finish most of her exams. She would put very specific questions in a limited time frame! The tests were open book but you didn't have time to look at your notes. I do not recommend taking this class if you don't have to.
Tests are way too in depth with little time. A majority of people in my class did not finish the last 2-5 questions on a 46 question test.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Her lectures are incredibly confusing and she blames her lack of teaching skills on her students. She claims to use a "circular approach" to teaching like in Med school but if this is how they teach in Med school I fear for patients everywhere. Do not take this class
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Her lectures make no sense and are all over the place. I learned legit nothing. Do not take this course with her

Amazing professor, very caring & enthusiastic. Many complain about her, but she is honestly super fair, there is just a large amount of material to know. I didn't find the material difficult, just a lot to know. Fav bio class so far. She will talk to you forever in office hours and wants to see you succeed.

Dr. Cramer is such a sweet person and I really do like her as a human, but her exams are just impossible. All of the questions are in a "select all that apply" format and are incredibly specific. Take someone else if you can, the exams will just stress you out so much.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Super test heavy and they're really difficult. Must dedicate almost all your time to this class. One bad test grade and entire grade is tainted. Need to do all other assignments perfectly to help your overall grade. Must read. Go to the Q&A and SI/PI session. Fight for points. Lab is cool tho!! Be ready for a ton of content that is all important.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: If you need to take Micro, she is the best professor. I would say she is the best professor I had at UNC. While it was also one of the harder classes I've taken, it wasn't because it was unfair but just the material is tough. She is super engaging and cares for you as a student. I and my wife still use her material in our careers

Dr Cramer is a really engaging and enthusiastic professor. Her lectures are pretty good and you can tell she knows her stuff, although she is slightly unorganized. Exams were nightmarish but she curved them significantly. She is really caring outside of class. Overall would recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: The test are awful. They are 40% of your grade and in a select-all format. You have to memorize almost everything to pass the test. There is pretty much no wiggle room or leeway for them. Even if you do good on everything else in the class, the test will bring you down.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: For a class that is necessary for nursing majors and pre-health majors, there is no reason for this class to be so unbelievably hard. I spent hours writing down the entire textbook in my notes and attended every lecture but still got 50s on the exams. The quiz questions are incredibly difficult even with a good understanding of the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This teacher is arguably the worst teacher I have ever had in my life. She is condescending, can't spell a sentence, and will make you absolutely hate your life. The test average for the last 2 tests was a "60" (according to her) before the curve and her grading format makes ZERO sense. The content is not the bad part, the way she writes tests is.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: To do well in this class you need to memorize all of the textbook readings and everything she says during lecture. The exams ask insanely specific questions and every question is a "select all" format. When asked about grading in review sessions she gets frustrated and defensive.

Dr. Cramer's class is very difficult. Thankfully... she goes over the topics several times before the exams. The lectures can be disorganized because she frequently goes down a rabbit hole but if you go to peer mentor sessions they help organize her thoughts and then it is much easier to follow during lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I loved Dr. Cramer--she's hilarious and pretty understanding, too. You definitely have to work hard in this class. Be sure to take notes throughout class because she will always include very specific concepts from lectures on exams. If you do the readings/homework and take notes it's not impossible.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Dr. Cramer is one of the worst professor's I have ever had. She did not make any of the material clear in her lectures. Often times, I was more confused on the material after the lecture than before the lecture. She pretty much expects you to know EVERYTHING in the book and in her lectures. My advice-take this at a community college.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Cramer is a good person sometimes but she just has no regard for students and their wellbeing during the pandemic. The only good thing is that she grades in a way that evenly splits homework, quizzes, and exams so your grade doesn't depend on only exams. Her exams are the hardest thing ever and she always goes 35 minutes over lecture time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: While Dr. Cramer knows her stuff, she is very unorganized and spends a lot of time being defensive in quiz reviews. She has so much potential to be one of the best in STEM but needs more organization within her lectures and overall structure of the class. I did LOVE lab though, as well as case studies and the blog.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: The material is super interesting, and Dr. Cramer is great. You really have to work for the grade here- it is definitely the most time-consuming course I've ever taken. Read the textbook!!!, and write down everything she says in lecture bc it is on exams. I don't recommend taking it alongside other hard science courses. Doable if you work for it!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class is HARD, but Dr. C makes it clear what you need to know. It's organized well, & if you go to class & do the GRQs/hmwk you'll be ok. You HAVE to read to do well! Definitely go to office hours &/or peer mentor sessions. Bkgnd in immunology would help a lot but not necessary.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very enthusiastic and knowledgeabl about all materials. Make sure to listen to every sentence in class because she will put questions on the exams that she only says one time in a random lecture. The class is really interesting and doable if you put in the time and effort. She does hold you over 20-30 minutes each lecture which is kind of annoying.

She's a GREAT professor who cares about her students, she even gave a take-home quiz and multiple retries on another quiz. Pay super close attention, 70% of what she says during lecture will show up on the quiz (annotate your PPT slides with whatever she says, I promise it's helpful!!). She gives you all the tools you need to succeed.

This class is the hardest i've ever taken at UNC. Dr. Cramer is a very knowledgable woman but can be somewhat condescending towards students if they ask questions she thinks are illogical. Be prepared to read a LOT and rewatch ALL of her lectures. She puts random specific things she says in lecture on test questions to the point it's ridiculous.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I liked her as a person, but imagine a prof telling your class that it is their fault the average on a test is a 60 because nobody is doing their work. No responsibility as a teacher. Lectures/lab were interesting/fun. But overall hard tests and disorganized class structure. SO many people I know had to take this class more than once. its crazy

One of the most unorganized professors that I have ever come into contact with at this school. Has no respect for students time and would go over lecture time by 20-30 minutes CONSISTENTLY throughout the semester. She also makes you take exams over the weekend on your own time. You are lucky if she finishes a complete sentence in lecture
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved Dr. Cramer! She's very goofy and the class is very interesting. It was one of the harder classes I've taken at UNC, but if you really put the work in, it's doable. My advice would be to do the learning objectives then add EVERYTHING she says in lecture to your notes because what she says always comes up on exams.

Online classes are a unique situation but she wasn't understanding & spent most meetings or quiz reviews defending her question choices instead of helping us understand the material. Ik it was an adjustment & she was receiving a lot of backlash, but students should never be afraid to ask for help out of fear of having her make you feel stupid.

Dr. Cramer is by far the best professor I've ever had. Dr. Cramer is very knowledgeable and truly cares about the students taking her class. Yes, the class is extremely difficult due to the amount of material covered and some of topics discussed. However, put in the work and an A is attainable in this class. Not to mention you get to learn so much.

She is a sweet person but it does not make up for the fact she expects you to be a microbiologist when you walk through the door. This is the hardest class I have ever taken. She expects you to know so much it is insane. She gives lots of extra credit opportunities though which is nice and lab was pretty fun and easy. Good luck you will need it!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Lorraine is honestly a gem. There is a lot of reading for the homework but she provides learning objectives that she uses to make the test questions. Very important to fill these out while reading. Her exams are very straightforward but requires studying ahead of time due to the large amount of material.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: So much homework, this class alone required me to do more homework for it per week than all my other classes combined (learning objectives are basically required). The lectures are dry and it's really difficult to ask questions since I worried she'll think my question is stupid and call me out. She also has a roundabout way of explaining things.

Dr. Cramer is very passionate about Microbiology and she cares about every student. This class is difficult with a lot of homework and reading, but that is what the class material is about and Dr. Cramer tries her best to help every student. I recommend going to her office hours as she is a great person to talk to!

Dr. Cramer made me anxious to come to class. She constantly yells in her lectures and is annoyed by any questions (even thought she mostly ignores them). The exams are ridiculous and the sheer volume of she wants you to know is insane. The material isn't really that hard, but the way she presents it makes you hate the subject.

Cramer treats you like you're already a microbiologist & expects you to know everything before you've even entered the classroom. A lot of busy work and reading & none of it is touched on in class. She is an awful lecturer & embarrasses students when they ask questions. In class, she told us that she was having a bad day & was taking it out on us.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I disagree with some. Even if you study your brains out, this class is difficult. DO THE EXTRA CREDIT, because you will need it! Cramer is fine, but she ADDS a lot of key info during her lectures that is NOT in the book, so record the lectures and listen to them again. She talks very fast. I learned a lot, but her tests aren't easy.

I LOVED this class! Dr. Cramer really values feedback from her students and completely reworked how she teaches the class this semester because of past complaints. You definitely have to put in effort because it is a lot of material to digest. But if you're dedicated to truly understanding the concepts, she will do everything she can for you!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Dr. Cramer such a friendly person, but her class is VERY difficult. Lectures are helpful because she tells you what to focus on, but her exams are literally verbatim from the textbook. If you actually do the readings and the learning objectives, you will be golden in this class (speaking from experience)! Lab is fun and really easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I absolutely LOVE Dr. Cramer. She is literally the best professor I've ever had and I 150% recommend her. Read the book, answer the learning objectives, listen to her lectures, go to her office hours, and you're golden!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. Initially, I was terrified to take this class, having heard about how difficult MCRO is. However, Dr. Cramer made this my favorite class. The class has been restructured to include extra credit and fun projects. If you read the textbook and re-listen to her lectures, you will be fine. Truly inspirational. I'm sad that it's over..

Dr. Cramer is a superstar. She goes above & beyond to try to be relatable, accessible, & make sure students learn the material. If you go to class, do the homework, & read - this is a very reasonable class. She's funny & has thought up fun assignments to further engage students - they're not as hard/time-consuming as they initially seem.

Dr. Cramer is VERY dedicated to her class and is trying her best to make things interesting. However, she recently switched up the coursework and the new format is NOT working considering a significant chunk of our grade is missing. The tests aren't too bad but does require you to extract random details from lecture. Go to the SI sessions!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: The class is fine; the material is interesting and important. Cramer-not fine. She doesn't know how to lecture at all. She can't finish sentences orally or in writing; lectures go over the book stuff without adding more to it so they're pointless but mandatory. Gives us a ton of work to make it "fun" but it's just too much and makes you hate it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I am in Dr. Cramer's class right now & I just have to say she is the most hard working & caring professor I've ever had. Yes, the class is difficult & time consuming, but the material is so interesting & applicable to real life it makes studying worthwhile. Her exams are NOT tricky! You have all of the resources you need to be successful.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: I have never seen a professor as excited about the subject material or more determined to help her students succeed. The class was the most challenging I've ever taken, but the difficulty is unavoidable, reasonable, and material is interesting. You will succeed by using every resouce and studying every day. Do not underestimate it, and have fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I loved this class. people complain the tests are tricky, but they are not tricky. They are rather simple. I think people are overly interpreting the questions. She really cares about her students. you should go to her office hours. at least study 2 weeks ago. recommend the class. go to the class since polleverywhere questions are provided everyday

Absolutely love Dr. Cramer. She is very passionate and very knowledgable! I was terrified of this class and the horror stories I had previously heard about. I studied weekly and attended each SI session for further help and reinforce the material. This class is NOT impossible and I recommend this class to those not even on the pre health track!

Dr. Cramer is great! Micro was hard, but that's kind of obvious because it's micro at UNC. Micro is do-able, don't freak out, just stay on top of the material. I actually did best on the final. All the lecture material is accessible outside class too, so it's ok when Lori gets off track during lecture. Micro was my favorite class last semester!

Dr. Cramer did a decent job teaching this course. There is A LOT of detailed material you have to learn but all the homework assignments help you learn it more in depth. Lectures can be very scattered and fast paced. This is definitely a class you have to work hard for your grade, but I enjoyed learning the material.

This class isn't a walk in the park. You have to work for your grade and you have to study at least 2 weeks before the exam! Go to office hours and SI/PM sessions. The content gets better as you go along, but honestly the exams aren't as hard as people say they are as long as you know everything 100%, forwards and backwards. Listen to lectures!!

The content is very interesting, however very difficult. The tests are very challenging, making the class averages very low, but on the upside the lab is included in the total course grade. The lab is very interesting and easy, so that is a grade booster. Dr. Cramer makes her students feel very stupid and she is unapproachable.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I absolutely hated this class. Dr. Cramer is the reason why I am no longer going to be a nurse. I felt like such an idiot during her lectures. She says things like "this is kindergarten level" when it clearly isn't. If you can take it elsewhere and transfer the credit in, I highly recommend doing that.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I love Dr. Cramer and this class! This class was definitely one of the most time consuming/hardest classes I've taken at UNC, but by far the most worthwhile. So much of what we learn is applicable to our lives/futures as health care professionals. She cares so much about micro and her students and is super easy to talk to. Definitely recommend!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: One of the hardest but most interesting classes I've taken. You have to work and dedicate a lot of time to studying outside class, but it is doable. I enjoyed lab, wasn't hard and was applicable to class material. She records her lectures and uses polleverywhere. Always curves at least 2 points. Dry humor but very smart professor.

Yes, you do have to memorize an irrational amount of info. The tests are extremely difficult and specific. Lectures repeat all you need to memorize (outlines). Go to office sign up hours, because she is the most generous prof. and only makes the class extremely hard bc she cares about your long term memorization that will help in grad/nurs/etc.

Dr. Cramer truly cares about both microbiology and her students. I did not think that I would like this class at all, but thoroughly enjoyed it because of her. You do have to put in a lot of work to get the grade you want, but she is more than willing to help you in any way she can. Just read, use the outlines, and start studying early!

Since this is a prerequisite for many professional schools, expect to do the work. Too many students complain about the rigor of the class, but honestly, the class will make you a better healthcare provider in the end. For all it's worth, those complaining can at least have a chance to change their academic path if they can't handle micro.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LECTURE HEAVY--Would take again

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. Class is definitely challenging, but if you put in the work, your grades will reflect it. The people below are complaining too much; you're at Carolina, expect difficult classes. If you do poorly on a test, Dr. Cramer will literally go over it with you question by question in office hours. Study the outlines thoroughly, and read!

YIKES. Don't take this class at UNC. I am warning you now. It's one of the hardest classes at UNC. I DO NOT recommend. Please take it at a community college or other university. This class is not worth your GPA. Seriously. I wish I would have never taken it. Worst decision of the semester!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Cramer is a fantastic teacher. Microbiology is by far my favorite course taken at Carolina. I find that I am never very good at multiple choice tests, but hers, I felt like, leveled the playing field for good test takers and those who are willing to work hard. And micro 251 lab was light years better than any other lab offered at Carolina.

Cramer asks way too much of her students. Hours of studying, and it's still hard to do fine (at best) because her exams are full of insignificant, intentionally tricky, overly detailed questions that are designed to make students fail. I truly believe she likes to watch her students suffer. I might have enjoyed this material if it weren't for her.

Good luck. Prepare for detail-oriented tests that cover an inordinate amount of material. The lectures are spastic, condescending, and mandatory. If you love memorizing a few dozen textbook tables and figures while Dr. Cramer lectures you on your incompetence, then this is the class for you. For what it's worth, Dr. Cramer does care about mcro.

Dr. Cramer is phenomenal. This class was the hardest I have ever taken. The material isn't really difficult, but there is SO much to cover. However, Cramer is kind, encouraging, and is one of the best teachers I have ever had. It's one of the most relevant classes you'll ever take, but you have to be really dedicated if you want a B- or better.

Interesting course, but do not take with a heavy load. Dr. Cramer expects very precise answers and there is a lot of content to learn. Tip: Find a study group early and get cracking for the final--it's a killer.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I LOVE Dr. Cramer. Her lectures are intense and packed, but she records all of them. Read the textbook, watch the animations, read the Sakai forum. She curves her exams. She is SO awesome and supportive in office hours. She's not easy, but her class is doable if you have the time. She made me fall in love with the subject. TAKE HER!

I loved Dr. Crammer! She really cares about students, this was probably my favorite class i have taken so far. If you put in  work, you should see results. This by no means that this class is a walk in the park. You still have to study the lectures and outlines religiously! She also curves tests!!! A first ever for me lol.

I wouldn't say that the tests are dificult, but covers lots of material. Just sudy in advance, and you will be fine. She also just started using Doceri to record her lecture, so if you miss a class, or need to review some materials, it's helpful to go back. She's also very willing to help, bc on test days she runs up and down to answer questions.
Very very very difficult tests on material you would never think you would be tested on (very nit-picky details). Participate, do well in the lab, study hard for exams and you'll do more than pass

Dr. Cramer's Medical Micro class is tough, but WELL WORTH TAKING. I learned so much. Paying attention and constantly reading and reviewing the lectures and powerpoints is crucial. But the lectures are entertaining, she's very funny, and you will really have to work for your grade

Dr. Cramer is an awesome person. She definitely loves what she teaches and it shows. However, She speaks super fast during lectures and at times, her power points are not very helpful. She does record her lectures, but they are not of the best quality. She is available to go over exams and help you with questions that you have. Be prepared to study

Dr. Cramer is funny and she talks super fast. She does record all her lectures, but the quality is not great. Don't get lazy in her class! You should review her material everyday no kidding. Her tests are extremely thorough you should study a week (or more) in advance. She curves the final. The final almost made me cry so STUDY I'M TELLING YOU

Dr. Cramer is very enthusiastic and talks really fast.  MCRO 251 is not an easy course, there is a significant amount of material, so very much self study was what helped me do well.  You can't study for a few hours the night before an exam and expect to do well.  Study diligently at least 5 days before the exams and you should do well.

Dr. Cramer is hilarious and makes the class super fun. She speaks very fast but records all her lectures. With that said, you should still go to class. Her tests are very thorough so you MUST study early Didnt know anything about micro and now I love it. She is really passionate and really knows her stuff. Definitely one of my favorite professors.

Dr. Cramer obviously really loves what she does and cares for her students. Her exams are tricky and frustrating, but the curve usually bails you out. The way she has structured the class allows you to fail one exam and not be completely screwed in the class. STUDY, STUDY, STUDY. Especially for the final exam. Seriously start studying ASAP.

Here's the deal: you have to work for this class. It covers a lot of material at a fast pace. If you're willing to study after each class and some on the weekends, you'll do absolutely fine. The lab is great! Best lab at UNC by far - fun, easy, and relevant. Cramer can be hard to reach if you need help - you have to schedule office hours in advance

Took this class post-bac while working and this class was not easy. Dr. Cramer's enthusiasm  and passion for the subject and her students made it a pleasant experience. She was always happy to talk with anyone if you made an appointment and give you advice on how to do better in her class.

Love love love Dr. Cramer! She truly enjoys the material and makes me want to come to class! That being said, she's not easy at all and she talks really fast. Overall, go to class, watch the animations, and go over her outlines and you'll do just fine! She's also really nice in office hours and really wants to help you do well.

Dr. Cramer is just amazing; she is undoubtedly the best professor I had at UNC. She is extremely passionate about what she teaches and very willing to help students out. She embodies what for me is the perfect Carolina professor, as she has a great passion for teaching and loves to reach students. Take her class, it will be worth your time.

Dr. Cramer is very passionate about microbiology. She is a very entertaining and engaging lecturer, and she very much wants her students to succeed. However, she speaks incredibly fast and does not do a great job explaining the subject matter. I really like her and the topic is very interesting, but she is not an effective instructor.

This class is awful. Homework takes hours upon hours and you still don't get a 100 and can't find answers. She talks so fast in class it's ridiculous. She makes it harder and more confusing than it needs to be. She will make you feel like you are stupid and doesn't care what you think. Hated Dr. Cramer although the subject material is interesting.

Just awful. More interested in making you think she's smart and you're stupid.Takes a subject that is difficult but understandable and makes it impossible.Encourages questions then insults you when you ask, especially if there's no one else around to hear it. Do yourself a favor and take this class with someone else so you actually learn something!

Dr. Cramer knows her stuff and is entertaining in lecture.  But the class is HARD and the tests are confusing (all multiple choice/matching).  Lab is easy.  Definitely requires a lot of studying for a good grade.  No paper.  Opportunity for extra credit.

Professor Cramer is clearly passionate about what she is teaching, but does a terrible job explaining what that is.  She gets excited and tongue-tied easily, making her lectures even harder to understand.  She jumps around on lecture notes and makes cryptic exams.  She encourages questions, and then makes students feel stupid for asking them.

Is obviously smart, but impossible to understand because she misspeaks in lecture all the time.  Her tests are equally unintelligible.  Also, you have to make an appointment to see her, even during office hours.  Not into teaching, just weeding people out.  Unfortunately you don't encourage people who would make great doctors and nurses that way.

Best teacher ever! The class is very fast paced and there is a lot of information but it is very interesting and she makes it easy to understand. She is very helpful and responsive to questions. I loved her class!
Class was extremely difficult..didn't like the multiple multiple questions..this class is definitely designed to weed people out.

She is an amazing professor.  Her test are difficult, but the remaining assignments/labs in the course compensate for her tests.  Even if you perform mediocre on the test, an "A" is still very much possible!

Dr. Cramer is a very effective teacher.  The content of this class was medium in difficulty (if you're familiar with Bio classes) but we covered a wide variety of topics at a fast pace.  Keeping up with the material is very important and going to class and doing well on the "clicker" questions is key.  Don't sweat the exams, just study hard!

This class was pretty hard, but she was so interesting that it made it easy to listen and keep up. As long as you go to class it's possible to get a decent grade. Definitely take this class because she's interesting and makes it fun; it's definitely easier to learn that way.
Awesome teacher, really hard class but really actually worth it, lectures are actually interesting...def take her class....She's "Fabulous"  :)
Great class.  She's pretty funny in lecture and very nice if you meet with in office hours.  She is tuff and the class is fairly demanding but if you keep up with it good grades aren't hard to make.
Absolutely loved this class. The lab rocks and Cramer is by far the funniest prof you will have at UNC. The exams are difficult though, study hard and an A is definitely in your reach.

Dedicated students will learn and succeed in this class.  Very interesting subject matter.  She's an entertainer.  The tests are very tricky multiple choice, but the lab grade and the homework will boost your grade.  She does curve fairly.  You can get an A- if you apply yourself.  Diligent lecture notes are more important than the book.

probably my favorite class i've taken at unc.  cramer is an effective teacher, the book is great.  the lab rocks a lot and really helps your grade out.  the only sticking point is the exams: to describe them as difficult is an understatement.  study hard and you'll do well.
No Comments

The class itself is pretty interesting if you are into that kinda stuff.  The class isn't terrible difficult and the lab for the class is very enjoyable.  The only bad thing about the class is tests and the quizzes because Cramer words them very tricky and they are multiple possibilites to what she is trying to say.

Very funny and extremely intelligent, her class was so much fun to attend and you  learn so much, and you have a great time doing it!  Plus, the required lab has to be the best lab I have taken here at UNC.  If you can take this class with her, do it!
Enthusiastic teacher.  Lecture was never boring, but tests are VERY hard (tricky).  Go to class, and study hard, it is worth it.
Great teacher full of energy.  One of my most favorite classes in all of college.
Grades very fairly...funny prof who makes 8 am class tolerable...test questions mostly from notes so definitely come to class

Easy A. Whole grade is based on a "performance review" at the end of semester where you convince him why you deserve an A. Lectures are boring but definitely don't need to pay attention or really even show up.

Kyle is the GOAT. Its lowkey hard to get a bad grade in his class unless you just don't do any assignment. Just do the work and you'll be fine. Super chill with extensions too. His lectures can be a bit boring sometimes but overall he's a great teacher for an easy A.
This is genuinely the easiest 105 course you could take. Such an easy grader and there is barely any work
Great guy, very accommodating, doesn't make his class stressful.

Choose Kyle as your 105 teacher. 30 mins of work PER WEEK, easiest class you will ever take, 1 assignemnt a week, asnychronus classes, at the end he lets you argue for an A if you somehow dont already have one. He's also super super chill.
Kyle might be the best 105 teacher. Allows late submissions, easy assignments that take 1-2 hours a week max. Also you can call him Kyle and not professor Cunningham

kyle was amazing! he is very kind, down to earth, and funny. he cares about his students and is very flexible with due dates and assignments. he also gives very good feedback and grades fairly. very chill and easy class, good for people who don't want much work to do for their 105 class.
best professor you could ask for, finished the class with a 100% (even though english wasn't my first language), very flexible with dates and assignments and care about his students

Professor Cunningham is incredibly kind and genuinely cares about his students' success. While the textbook is required, he doesn't use it. His assignments are manageable, effective, and well-structured, and he provides excellent feedback. Though attendance isn't mandatory, attending class occasionally is beneficial.

Cushman is a very interesting and intriguing lecturer. Which is why it was so disappointing his class became so disorganized the second half of the semester. Several assignments were crammed into the last few weeks of class (one being a group presentation) with little to no description, rubric, or due dates. Incredibly frustrating and stressful

Only did pop quizzes the first month then didnt do any more, midterm is super easy you study off a jeopardy, class seems so intimidating at first but it gets so easy so quickly, final is not too difficult, final project is super easy you get a 100 as long as you put in minimal effort, be ready to ask classmates for missed notes
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof is huzz

Professor Cushman if you're reading this I'm so sorry. I almost hit you with my car the other day on campus. I don't want you to know it was me because you're my favorite professor and I don't want you to hate me but I want to say I'm so sorry it was me who almost hit you. I'll be more careful I'm so sorry. I hope you have a great break!
I took this class a year ago and another class with him last semester. He is very kind and knows a lot about the subject matter. Not too much writing, which is nice for a freshman seminar.

I don't understand why all the comments are good. Dr. Cushman is a nice person and can be flexible, also knowledgeable about his field. But the syllabus is super disorganized and looking back, I learned zero stuff in the class and really thought it was a waste of time. To do the final project you really need background knowledge outside or prior.
This class is so special. It's unlike anything I've ever taken before. Just take it and you'll see.

Seriously one of the best Professors at UNC. This class was so amazing, and I would totally recommend taking it. Its easy to read when you know you get to go discuss and understand further! 10/10 class

i loved this class and really enjoyed the book. it felt like one large book club! if you are even considering this class, take it. in fact, even if you don't enjoy reading, take it. it was so fun getting to hear everyone's different perspectives and takeaways from the novel—that's what reading is all about, after all!
Great class, fair grader, interesting discussions. If you read the book and go to class you'll be fine.

I loved this class so much! He is such a great teacher, and he really helped us think about the text deeply. It wasn't very hard at all. I looked forward to the discussions because everyone in the class was so into it. He is a pretty relaxed grader and very nice person.

This is a life-changing class. I'm a STEM major and this was my favorite class I've taken at UNC (and it's not close). Take it if you're not an English major or anything like that. I learned to like reading again after falling off after graduation. Don't miss this one!

Really solid class and even better instructor. The book was good, but even better were the discussions. Perfect for a first year seminar. Met some awesome people, read something hard, and got to know a good prof.
The most amazing professor ever! Super accessible and helpful. Lots of reading but it was so worth it with the meaningful discussions he led. Truly loved this class, take it if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Such an amazing professor and class! The best first-year seminar I probably could have taken & I wish I could take it every semester on a new book. The class was mainly discussion based and Professor Cushman created an open, accepting environment for all answers and opinions. We did two interesting presentations on topics we cared about.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Great class. Did not think I would enjoy reading this book but I absolutely loved it. Prof. Cushman did a great job helping us through slowly and encouraging us to stick with it. I feel like I climbed a mountain. Would take again for sure!

There are so many amazing things about Dr. Cushman! There's definitely a good amount of reading, but his lectures help simplify any questions. Class is discussion heavy but is well-guided. Papers were graded with really good feedback and he would always make time outside of class to talk. The best though was him sometimes bringing his dog to class!

H.M Cushman is a very nice professor. He is accessible to students, funny, open to talk, and just a great guy all around. The reading can be a lot at times, but if you really pace yourself you'll be fine. Just try to participate, read what's required, and take notes on the class slides and you will be fine. He is also very passionate!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Cushman is a very funny and passionate teacher who really enjoys what he teaches. Although the reading can be quite heavy on some nights it was well worth taking the class. The homework mainly consists of reading while the class is heavily focused on the context and analysis of the tales. Overall great class and an even better teacher!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Prof Cushman is accommodating, friendly and very knowledgable about Chaucer. I took this course on a whim to satisfy the depth english requirement and I am so glad I did. I enjoy class a ton! The reading is a bit dense sometimes, but it's interesting. She wants you to succeed & tests have extra credit! Super funny as well :)

Had her for ENGL320 (Chaucer/Canterbury Tales) and ENGL120 (Early English Lit.). Definitely one of the best professors at Chapel Hill. She gives great feedback, is personable, truly cares about her students, etc. As with any class, office hours are an even better way to connect and get your ideas out to her. Don't be afraid to participate.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Cares about each of her students. She is funny, cusses a little bit, and is receptiveerested when students have thoughts/ideas. Her tests are simple to the ones who read, hard if you don't. Some pop quizzes. Attendance is not mandatory, but she does not release powerpoints until a few days before the exam. She never releases her lecture notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: You will not regret taking this course. He knows what he is talking about and makes class very engaging. Often makes you think outside of the box and dive deeper into hidden meanings of films. Make sure to participate, actually watch the films and memorize the facts he asks of the movies. Not being to check grades was no stress honestly.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Loved this class. Very discussion-based class, that's why participation and attendance matters. Usually a smaller class so he'll notice if you're not in class for a few days. Lots of reading but exams are easy and grading is lax. I enjoyed his class tho! Easy A if you're okay with reading and speaking up at least once a class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I LOVED THIS CLASS. It was SO interesting, and I would recommend it to basically everyone. If classroom participation really stresses you out, you might find this class to be scary, but he is so interesting to listen to and the seminar is very good.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I audited this class, so grain of salt, but Dr. Curtain is kind and extremely knowledgeable about horror movies. He isn't afraid to call on people out of the blue and challenge their answers, but he's also funny and encourages discussion. Really enjoyed this class.
Very weird about missing assignments. Definitely insecure about teaching a horror class haha.
Really chill class. Just watch movies and talk about stuff. Curtain is a chill dude who knows everything anyone ever needs to do about horror in general. Great dude with a great personality.

Genuinely a great class. Professor Curtain really makes you think about the films you watch, I have a whole new perspective of sci-fi film now. All you do is talk about the films/books in class, make sure to watch/read everything because he will cold call. All films except 2 books during the whole semester but easy reads. 1 midterm and 1 final.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Curtain is very good at what he teaches and is good at getting you to think more deeply about you ideas on the material. You are graded on participation in class, a midterm, and final but they are fairly straightforward if you keep up with the films needed for class.

This is a great class! I was worried throughout the semester as your final grade consists of participation, one midterm, and a final and you never know your grade for any of them. The material is interesting and attendance is never taken. Ended up with an A.

Overall, I enjoyed this course. It's pretty much entirely discussion based where you talk about films and books. Participation is really important, and you're expected to be active in discussions. My only issues is his viewpoint can be narrow at times and grading is very unclear (there's no canvas site). Easy filler course if you need one.

Hilarious guy and so nice. Our in class convos were thought provoking and deep. There's a midterm and final as our only graded assignments (they're straight up memorization). Homework is watching movies and reading 3 books that we discuss in class. Exams ask for titles, director, and release year of each work we cover. Awesome class and easy A.

We had two assignments and one final that was a breeze. Grades weren't posted until after finals though, which was frustrating. He also refused to acknowledge points of view that contradicted his own, which was rather disappointing, because I wanted to engage in the material. After I gave up trying, the class was fine.

Professor Curtain was very relaxed, so there weren't many assignments or feedback in general which was stressful at times. I ended with an A in the class but got no feedback whatsoever throughout the semester. This was a great class though, your grade is based mostly on participation in class discussion.

Professor Curtain is fun, if not a little unstructured. This class had a 1/2 page syllabus and about 10 books to read. Attendance was not mandatory, but he would assign items in class for the following week and not post on Canvas or notify students, so you had to keep your head on a swivel! His classes were fun, but he would cold call sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Midway the semester, as we were discussing a film by James Cameron, I pointed out the racial stereotypes. As I did this, I also voiced how I could not finish the movie due to the movies racist nature. Professor Curtain stated that my viewpoint, as a POC woman, was incorrect. He also said that I needed to learn how to be uncomfortable.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: As long as you watched the movie before the class and were prepared to talk, this class was a breeze. The only assignments we had were a midterm and final, and a final project sequence, which were all very easy. If you do the work, you pretty much get an A. Good easy filler class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class consisted of watching around 30 movies and reading 3 books. The classes were just discussions of the content. There was a midterm and a final, along with a group short film project. Really fun class, just show up and pay attention and talk every once in a while and you will get an easy A. Great professor, great content, take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I have had the honor of having Professor Curtain for two classes during my time at UNC. He is a really great person, and I enjoy his lecture style. He keeps you thinking and encourages participation. Watching movies as homework is a great escape from the heavier assignments from other classes, and the films are all worth it. Take a class with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Took Prof. Curtain's horror movie class expecting a typical english class, but was pleasantly surprised. The class just consisted of discussing movies we watched before class. The only assignments in class were a midterm, final, and short horror movie group project. Exams were easy and the project was fun. Easy and interesting class!
Amazing professor. Very wise man. Take the class if you can. Start reading early and enjoy the books.

Tyler is an amazing professor! He is so interested in what he teaches that it makes class such a pleasure. The class consists of watching movies/reading books and discussing them. He is a super laid back professor and I enjoyed his class thoroughly.

This semester was really chill. The reading/watch list consists of contemporary things. I'm very shy to talk in class, but this class made me feel welcomed and safe to talk about issues whether it be the news or controversial topics in the movies/books. Take this prof if you get the chance! We had a paper as our midterm, and no graded final.

This class was interesting and definitely an easy A class. If you don't have time to read the books or watch the movies you can just read summaries so you have something to talk about. Got off-topic a lot and talked about some controversial political topics so if those conversations can be triggering for you then I would not reccmonmmend.
Prof Curtain is one of the most caring and accomodating professors I've ever had. Class is very discussion-based, so as long as you know the material you'll be fine.

Prof Curtain has a great story and is very accommodating and welcoming to his students. Half the class is watching and discussing sci-fi/fantasy movies, the other was reading fantasy novels. Some of the books are tough to read in the time allotted before a class discussion, but overall the class was a breeze and I really enjoyed myself in there.

Prof Curtain helped me understand the meaning within sci-fi & fantasy films & books, rather than just the "wow" aspects in them. Each class consists of a group discussion based on the film or book you viewed/read outside of class (which can take a lot of time). He provides a lot of insight and makes class intriguing! Grading criteria isn't clear.

This has definitely been one of my favorite classes in college so far. Professor Curtain facilitates interesting discussions, and I always looked forward to coming to his class. I look at horror movies in a completely different way now. I highly recommend taking a class with him.
