It would be fair to assume it's mostly participation in class but he doesn't even tell you what the exam is weighted. It's easy if you participate and try, he's a good teacher and he really really cares about his students. No excused absences though.
Love this class, very engaging, lots of time to practice Dutch, and very clear expectations for quizzes and tests. Provides good feedback and cares for his students.

Professor Thornton is amazing! Take this class if you can! As a first-year student, this class was amazing for meeting new people and getting to know a tight-nit group. Participation goes a long way and he often just calls on people. Highly recommend spending some time with the vocab and practicing the material, it made this class a breeze.
Dr. Thornton was amazing! I was so excited to go to his class everyday. He made learning a language so much fun!!! Please take his class if you can!
Super simple language class, grade is mostly participation, great instructor. You HAVE to participate in class and if you do, you'll be fine.

Professor Thornton is the goat. He is a great professor and I am so thankful I chose to take Dutch with him. Easily my favorite professor here at UNC. If you need to fulfill your language requirement, CHOOSE DUTCH WITH HIM!!! The class isn't really a gimme, but if you keep up with the work, you will absolutely be fine.

Awesome professor! He's super caring and helpful. He genuinely wants you to succeed! You have to go to class and participation matters, so talk in class. Overall, great class and would take again. Dan also knows a thing or two about the Netherlands, so don't be shy about asking him questions!

If you need to complete your foreign language requirement, take Dutch with Dr. Thornton. He's one of the kindest people I've met at UNC, and he makes learning a foreign language very accessible. You take both 402 and 403 with him to finish the requirement, and you get to have the same class for two semesters which really builds a nice community.

This is one of the best professors at UNC! The professor cares deeply for their students and makes learning a foreign language fun and stress-free. The class won't be an easy A, but you're given all the resources to succeed. Also, you learn a great deal about the Netherlands.

I loved Professor Thornton's class. To succeed you MUST go to class, he covers things that aren't in the textbook. If you must miss class as long as you email him he is very kind about it. go to class as much as possible. His quizzes are fair and the study guides are very helpful.
One of the nicest people on campus. If you can take this class, regardless of your major or anything else, please do.

Dan is one of my favorite professors that I've ever had. He's very caring and really makes this a fun class. Dutch is definitely one of the easier languages to learn especially with Dan teaching the class.
Dan Thornton is one of the best professors at UNC. He is incredibly caring and truly gets to know his students. If you're going to take a language at UNC take Dutch with Prof Thornton.

Dan is so sweet and made learning Dutch a pleasure! He's super passionate about teaching, and this is by far the easiest language I've taken and there's not a lot of homework. He's also a very forgiving grader and there are a bunch of tests so if you mess up on one you're fine! Loved taking Dutch with him and feel like I learned a lot!

My favorite professor at UNC. Absolutely loved my time in this class and wish I could take it every semester. He is so obviously passionate about his work and his teachings which make the class a great environment to learn. Class size is small enough to where I learned every students name and built some new friendships. I recommend Prof Thornton!

Amazing professor! He went out of his way to make sure everyone understood the material we were learning. There are about 8 units and a quiz for each one, as long as you knew your stuff they were easy.

Dan is a good teacher who cares about his student's success. He tests comprehension every unit with small quizzes, but they don't feel overwhelming or too hard. Good class. This review was also for the 2nd level of Dutch - DTCH 403, but RMP doesn't have that option.

Prof. Thornton is a great teacher. He is passionate and engages nearly every student during every class. He's approachable and readily accessible outside of class, and he really seems to care about your success. The Dutch language itself is also relatively easy.
Really fun and passionate about Dutch culture.  He is extremely helpful, but requires a lot of speaking in class.  Don't be shy about reading aloud or asking for help though!
BEST dressed professor on campus. Do they have an award for this? Amazingly awesome teacher. He rocks. I can't wait to go to the Netherlands now.
Very friendly and enthusiastic.
Amazing, knowledgeable, worldly teacher, really has a passion for the Dutch culture, open to ideas and overall just a great guy.

This guy is awesome. I learned a lot about the Dutch language and culture. He's really nice, easygoing, and funny. I definitely recommend taking a class by him. If you don't understand something he's very patient and willing to help you until you definitely know it. Awesome guy. I can't say that enough.

He is very opinionated and you have the be an amazing writer for a first year class. If you are not a good writer and don't enjoy talking, do not take this class and if you do like discussions I also advise against it. There are a lot easier 105 classes that will allow you to enjoy the class while still earning a good grade. Do not take!

Dr.Ross allows multiple drafts to be submitted and he gives detailed feedback before they're due. He primarily lectures, but the workload was manageable throughout the semester and he was easy to meet with to discuss feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Ross is clearly a very knowledgable man, but we spent most of our discussion-based seminar listening to him talk about *his* opinions. I did not know my grade all semester... But, there are no essays only short-form discussions posts. It's a super easy class as long as you can stay on top of the readings (YOU 100% NEED TO DO ALL OF THEM!!!!!).

We had zero assignments the entire semester (other than online discussion boards), and not a single grade was entered into Canvas, so I didn't have any idea of my grade until I received my final grade. There's so much daily reading, and even in an opinion-based seminar class, if your view goes against Dr. Ross's, you are "wrong" (he will say so!)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It's clear that Dr. Ross is very knowledgeable and passionate about English. My main issue with him was how opinionated he was. English should be about interpretation, but with Ross, there is a right (his personal opinion) and a wrong (any other perspective, no matter how well-supported it may be).

If think if I could go back in time and have the choice between taking 105 with David again or pulling out all my hair one by one, I would choose the second option. If I had to pick one word to describe his class it would be frustrating. He grades HARSH, lectures are insufferable, and he treats his opinion as right and anything else is wrong.

Intense of a grader for English 105. I showed up to every lecture (except for 1), actively participated in class, and showed improvement in my writing. He would constantly leave degrading comments on my work and give extremely confusing advice. Makes weird comments about women too! DO NOT TAKE! Please just take an easy English for your own good

I took this class because it seemed interesting, but realized Professor Ross was teaching a class on something he didn't have any knowledge on. First thing he told us in this class on the use of AI was "I have never used AI in my life." He would cut us off mid-sentence when we would talk in class to express his own views. Do not take his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I have few qualms with Dr. Ross as a person, but I would advise against taking his courses if you have a history with sexual trauma. He would often make derogatory and uncomfortable remarks about fictional women and almost every piece of media assigned included and poorly addressed the topic of sexual violence. Please be wary when registering!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: UNC-Chapel Hill is one of the top schools in the country. It should not be admitting students who complain about having to show up to class or who moan when a professor has actual standards for written work. Ross's standards are high. But he's very thorough in his advice about how to meet them. He's a great teacher, if a little idiosyncratic.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: If you talk in class and offer your opinions during his unnecessary and endless tangents, he'll love you. Expect to write and expect LOTS of feedback in a pretty condescending tone. I wouldn't NOT take him, he'll definitely improve your writing, just be very wary of your grade.

Professor Ross is a very smart professor, but is way too far hard of a grader for an English 105 class. He provided good feedback for essays, but didn't take into consideration most people taking this course that it's their first college-level english course. He also had very strong opinions and could come off as pretentious lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Ross is a brilliant guy but should NOT be teaching a English 105 class. He's a tough grader and it's unfair how broad the spectrum of difficulty is for Engl105. Do not take him unless you are passionate about english. His classes are attendance mandatory and he sits in a chair and talks about irrelevant things the entire class period.

Ross is a lovely guy, but his grading criteria for English 105 is too harsh. Your grade is dependent on your natural skills as a writer. I spent hours revising my papers and could not get over a B+. For 105, this should not be the case. If you are Shakespeare, go ahead; he will improve you. If not, your grades will suffer.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Ross is extremely wise and well-spoken but continuously goes on tangents every class, and the lectures are almost useless. This class goes way beyond what a first-year requirement should ask of you, and you won't get an A unless you're Stephen King or Shakespeare himself.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Look, I understand why some dislike him. He can be a little insensitive, out of touch, and he is not tech savvy. However, he is absolutely passionate. He cares tremendously about students genuinely improving and will give you all the help you want if you ask. Also, he is forgiving. He has an abrasive personality but meets students where they are.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Ross is a very particular man; his essay prompts were very odd and didn't allow much room for your own interpretation. His feedback was very subjective, and my grades on the essays never improved throughout the semester. He tries to be helpful if you stay for office hours, but he kind of drones on (he does in lectures, too).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very reading heavy class. Took the class online so did not get to know much about him, but seemed to be very passionate about the books and films at hand. I am not sure what my grades for any of the assignments were after the class ended as he had ended the course on canvas and directly put in the final grade. Not bad but prolly wouldn't take agin.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you want an easy-A gen-ed professor (fair enough), then choose someone else. However, learning from Dr. Ross legitimately improved my writing skills. The essay topics were generally engaging and his draft feedback is gold. His actual lectures are hit-or-miss; one day it is an insightful lesson on concision, and the next is a huge tangent.

I have complicated feelings. On the bright side, I felt my writing improved under his instruction. For every essay draft, he wrote paragraphs of feedback. Incredible attention to detail. However, as for the actual class, it felt unnecessary... lots of tangents + condescending. He's extremely knowledgable, and believe me, he will remind you...
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would love to read an in-concise 800 page autobiography of this man's life. He is something else.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Ross was brilliant but don't take this class. I didn't take AP, I wasn't prepared to jump into a classic literature level of writing. I couldn't improve my grade, I went to the writing center, office hours, and it was useless. Also, he will call on Indian students to translate Hindi, even if you don't speak it. Why is he teaching Freshman

Dr. Ross gave extensive and personalized feedback that was extremely helpful. It is clear that he cares about his students improving in their writing. I so appreciated his attentiveness especially considering it is just a freshman required course. If you don't want to have tons of busy work and to actually learn something in 105, take Dr. Ross.

LOOOOOVE professor Ross!!! He is very passionate about the films we discussed. He was clear about what would be on exams and graded papers fairly. Attendance was mandatory but he let a few absences slide. He made me really interested in movies and while his lectures were long, they were interesting. Great professor.

Dr. Ross was hands-down my favorite professor this semester. He was incredibly knowledgeable and passionate about the course and his class style was very engaging. There are definitely a lot of readings and other materials (films) to complete outside of class but if you stay on top of it, you'll be fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Ross was very knowledgeable and really cared about the topics he discussed in class. Loved the class but so unnecessarily difficult. The content isn't hard its just so much material in so little time. I was doing hours of reading every day. This was a summer asynch class for me and it was unclear what my grade was until the class ended.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Ross was a very thought-provoking professor. His class was very interesting and the tests were not hard if you read the texts and pay attention. There is A LOT of reading so if you do not like reading DO NOT take this class. The midterm and the exam are based on the readings and the class discussions. The course is only based on 4 grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Ross will teach you a lot but his class is not easy. Taking his ENG 105 genuinely did make me a much better writer, but it was sort of boring. Also, he tends to sometimes have a condescending attitude towards students, this did not bother me too much but I know many of my classmates hated it.

Dr. Ross definitely gets valid criticism for his.. staunch.. opinions. He's obviously very knowledgeable and enjoys some back-and-forth discussion, so don't take the debate too personally. Engage in the material, try to appreciate the quirks and take his thoughtful feedback to heart- and you'll end up a better writer for it.

It took me a little while to warm up to Dr. Ross and his teaching style, but once I did I really enjoyed his class. He is super smart and knows his topics inside and out. This class ended up being pretty philosophical.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Ross is a good professor who does care about your improvement. Your paper grades heavily depend on weather or not he actually agrees with your points, which can get annoying. Make sure to particpate in class, since he deos factor it in your grade. His office hours are usually helpful. My writing has definitely improved this semeser.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Ross is a nice teacher who is understanding. He is definitely not one of the easier professors for ENGL 105 but if you have him don't worry about it. He is obviously very qualified but won't give out A's very easily. I will say my writing improved a lot because of this class and his feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Couldn't stand Prof Ross. He's pretentious and not open to any other opinions, and borderline disrespectful of students. He does give really thorough feedback on essays, so if you do what he says (repeat his opinions) you can score well. Class is entirely taught on his favorite songs and movies (all 50s-60s jazz and blues) and is incredibly boring
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not take this class if you want to keep a decent GPA. He grades at an oxford level for an entry level class. Very nice and helpful but does not grade fairly nor clearly

Professor Ross is very nice and willing to work with you if you need to set up a meeting or for writing help.  However, his expectations for a 100-level course are ridiculously high. Unless you are Emily Dickenson or Jane Austen, don't expect to get an A on a paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Ross has unrealistic expectations and grades very harshly for an English 105 course. I think a lot of the issue was that he comes up with very unique writing assignments that dont have clear criteria. If you want a somewhat easy A dont take this class.

His grading is very strict, but he is willing to help you if you are obviously struggling with writing. As an international student, it is hard for me to get a good grade in his class, even though I spend more than 30 hours on each paper.  However, he always returns me high-quality feedback for my drafts, improving my writing and English overall.

Professor Ross definitely helped me become a better writer. He did imply sometimes that anyone without his views is wrong. He did grade too harshly for an ENGL 105 professor, so make sure your papers are in good shape before submission. The digital media assignment was fun but time-consuming and not related to English or writing in any way.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Ross was very nice and provided good feedback on papers. This class required us to watch about 30 films, which was a bit intense. The exams were very difficult, but he curves them. He does not give a clear layout of how much the papers and tests are weighted, and his lectures are all based on his interpretations of the films.

Professor Ross was an amazing English teacher! He provided great feedback and really boosted my confidence as a writer. Be sure to have the drafts of your essays ready to go for the peer reviews - that feedback is crucial.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Ross taught my honors seminar on Sci-fi media. The lectures can be a bit dry, but if you take good notes you'll be fine. Be aware that he only lectures on what he thinks about the books/films you go through, so you can only really be creative in the writing assignments. Otherwise very informative and gives good writing feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Ross helped me improve my writing immensely. He provided thorough feedback that elevated my work to a new level. His assignments are challenging, but if you are skilled in critical analysis and can write with literary flair, you'll earn an A in his class. Take Professor Ross  you'll become a better writer.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof Ross is incredibly knowledgeable & well-spoken. He is a FANTASTIC teacher who really helps you improve your writing. If you are looking for an easy A, don't take this class. His assignments are quite dreadful and boring. However, I notice much improvement in my writing that I would 10000% recommend Prof Ross to anyone serious about writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Professor Ross is very nice and wants to help improve every student's writing. Grades heavily depend on three 4-6 page essays. The essays do not have clear guidelines but Professor Ross reads your drafts and gives thoughts and advice. Overall, do not take this class if you want an easy A. Only take it if you really want to improve your writing.

Professor Ross is a very good professor. He cares about the students and puts all his time and energy into making this class great. He's very smart and passionate about the class and it's noticeable. However, he is a tough grader and the class can get difficult. Needless to say, he definitely helped me become a better writer but the class was hard.

While this class was majorly asynchronous, I enjoyed the class and Professor Ross. The subject material was interesting, he gave lengthy feedback, and was encouraging. Would take a class with him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Ross made this online science fiction class incredibly interesting. He picked a very fascinating selection of films and novels and used forums to spark interesting conversations. He responded to every single forum post that students made. The class didn't feel like school, but more like an exploration of the themes of science fiction.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Ross is simply a great professor. The lectures are certainly dense with ideas and cultural insight but are by no means boring. He's exceedingly well-read and well-spoken, and he gives very detailed feedback on papers (so you know exactly how to improve). Everyone on here complaining that he's a hard grader is just mad that they can't write.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Ross isn't awful, but he comes across as pretentious when he speaks. He believed his opinion was the only one that mattered and talked AT students rather than to them. Classes were boring and he makes it hard to get an A--he loves giving B+s. Take 105 with a different professor if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Despite all the criticism he gets, Dr. Ross really cares about his students and wants everyone to learn. I don't disagree that the class is much harder than other English 105 classes, but I personally felt it improved my writing because of that. Overall, his class is difficult but rewarding, and he is always available to help outside of class.

Professor Ross makes English 105 much harder than it needs to be. The assignments are very weird for an intro class, like writing an album review and a movie analysis paper. He gives no criteria for grading, and you have no idea how he calculates the final grade. The lectures are sooo boring, and the way he talks just sounds very pretentious.

For a first year required course, Dr. Ross is unbelievably hard grader for the assignments he gives. Although there are only 3 papers that count towards the final grade, the philosophy that he takes on for grading is unfair and does not make ANY SENSE. Lectures are also VERY boring and make you want to take nap during the class.
Do not take unless you want to go to sleep and be graded on criteria not clearly explained. He also says HHMMM when students try to speak really loudly in an attempt the overpower and distract them.

Dr. Ross is intelligent, but he is not open to any opinions or interests besides his own. He forces you to write music reviews on his favorite music (all rock/jazz from the 60s and 70s), and you have to praise it if you want an A. He is a classic eurocentric professor so don't talk about other cultures. He also brags about Oxford and how UNC sucks.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Ross gives absolutely no grading criteria in his syllabus so you have no clue how your final grade will be calculated. His class is literally just him talking about his opinions on films and is incredibly boring. He is nice and will help you in office hours, but overall he grades very harshly so an A is impossible.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: David Ross is extremely educated and knowledgeable. This can be intimidating and can come off as a little pretentious, BUT he clearly knows what he is talking about. The workload isn't much and he gives lots of good feedback. He is also accessible outside of class during office hours. Not an easy A but you will definitely improve as a writer.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: David Ross is a very nice man, his lectures don't require anything more than a little participation, but his grading requirements are tough. There are only 3 music-themed papers and 2 feeder assignments. Almost everyone in the class received an A-/B+ for their final grade. Only "exceptional writers" make A's in his 105 courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Ross is a great person but his lectures are very boring at times. He is an extremely hard grader compared to other 105 professors and rarely hands out A's. He also says "mmhmm" very loud when other people are talking or answering his questions.

he can be quite condescending, classes mainly consist of him talking with limited discussion, interrupts students frequently when they're asking questions, doesn't adjust his syllabus even when the university is closed for a long period, tests are the hardest english tests i've ever taken, standards for paper grading are very high,
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: David Ross is very pretentious and will criticize opinions differing from his. His engl 105 class is just an all-around bad time. It involves a lot of lectures that don't teach anything that a high school class doesn't. Also he says "mm hmmm" to interrupt students, even when he is the one asking the questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: English 146 with Dr. Ross has been one of my all-time favorite classes. He is a tough grader, and does not hand out As. But the material is super interesting, he lectures (nearly) the entire class period with sporadic student involvement. His take on the material is always super interesting. 2 papers, 1 midterm, 1 final. Would take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Course is weighted heavily towards forum participation and the 2 papers. Online/Summer, so the reading was pretty heavy for me (books split into 4-6 chunks of reading/night; 40pgs 7 d/wk). I can guarantee if you want an A in the class, you should stay consistent w/reading and quality! posting.  Great insights, friendly, fair, & very accommodating!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Compared to other classes I've heard about, the work load is very small. There's only three papers and you get over a month to write each one. He edits your paper for you before you turn in the final draft, so as long as you take his suggestions you should do fine!

Dr. Ross is a very nice person and a good professor. His assignments are easy and he gives you plenty of time to finish them. His grading criteria is a bit rough, however. I don't think it's possible to get an A in his class unless you have an unnatural ability at writing papers. He gives great feedback though and I definitely grew as a writer.

He is incredibly pretentious and do not think of sharing an opinion that does not align with his own. 3 papers , all 5 to 7 pages each, and 2 feeder assignments. He gives plentiful feedback on each paper, follow the advice and its not difficult to make an A. Agree with what he says and nod your head to lectures. Much harder than other sections.

David Ross is a spectacular orator. He is very knowledgable in subject matter and beyond. Helpful if you ask for it. Class not too bad, although it's quite a bit of reading. Show up to class for key points, take two easy multiple choice tests, and write two papers (with generous amount of time to do them) and that's about it.

He was the most annoying teacher. He talks everyday with a powerpoint, and talks about one slide for 15 mins. He asks questions in class and then when you answer he says "mm hmm" and then disagrees with you. He's so picky about giving As and if he gives an A it's an A-. There are group projects too. DON'T TAKE ENGL 105 WITH HIM, you will hate it.

Dr. Ross is a great lecturer and ENGL143 was very interesting. I would recommend this class to anyone that needs the VP credit. You watch 2 movies a week and discuss them in class. 2 papers and a midterm, basically minimal work. He is also a fair grader!

Dr. Ross is incredibly intelligent and interesting, but his lectures can get a little dry. He assigns three big papers, along with a few feeder assignments. In my class, we wrote a research paper, a restaurant review, and a film analysis. He provides helpful detailed feedback, and I feel that I have genuinely improved as a writer.

The class doesn't have too much work, but David Ross isn't very helpful at all. The class is very boring, he hates giving As (likes A-s and B+s the most) and he's extremely pretentious. He doesn't like it if you don't write in his style or if you suggest an interpretation of something for a project that he doesn't agree with. Find someone better.

David Ross is not what everyone says he is.  He knows that he is smarter than you and you constantly feel that idea swirling around your head during each lecture.  He is not helpful and very slack with grading.  I really wish I would have taken anyone else.  Please do not be fooled by these reviews, he is not a good teacher for ENGL 105.

Dr. Ross is a smart guy and I actually feel like I've become a better writer after taking his class. There are only 3 papers, and you submit multiple drafts, allowing you to receive ample feedback. He's kinda dorky and really into foodmovies, but he is a kind person and does not grade very harshly.
I learnt a lot from his class. He wrote very helpful comments and suggestions about my papers. This course was not hard: just three papers (each paper has three drafts)and two presentations.

Just absolutely spectacular. I think he's probably one of the few people in the world who can transition between quoting Lolita and discussing it without sounding artless, boring, and stupid in comparison with Nabokov's beautiful prose. He's a brilliant man and a great talker without being incomprehensible or condescending. Hope to have him again!

Good class :) He is ridiculously intelligent... could be the smartest person I've ever met. Uses lots of big words but not incomprehensible by any means. I enjoyed this class; great course structure and good book and movie choices for the most part :)

BEST CLASS I'VE EVER TAKEN. It's not suggested for the anti-intellectuals, but for anyone interested in quality film, it's a must. Ross is extremely passionate about film and is one of the most scholarly yet easy-going people I know. If you're reading the other comments, don't heed them unless you exclusively watch mindless blockbusters.

I took this film class because I thought it would be fun...BIG mistake! Most of the movies are incredibly long and hard to follow. It didn't turn out quite as hard as I thought, but the lectures are extremely boring, be prepared to zone out for the entire class.

He is really passionate about the literature, but his voice is rather monotonous. He doesn't really encourage class discussion, but his lectures are pretty good - if you can stay awake for them. Grading is not too harsh, but he expects a lot.

David Ross is a very smart guy. But his interest was watching 2001: A Space Odyssey(old edition). It was horrible. However I ended up getting a B out of the class with numerous visits at the writing center and his office. Make sure u get plenty of sleep before coming to his class because he can be boring!

Don't take this class unless you REALLY love sci-fi.  The work load is really heavy...about ten books and four movies to watch outside of class.  The exams don't really count, just the papers, so as long as you're a good writer, you'll probably do okay.  But David wasn't helpful at all, so be prepared.

Professor Ross is excellent. He is absolutely brilliant, offers excellent insights on the works we read, and I sincerely recommend anyone take him. One of the smartest professors I've ever had, and overall a very fair grader.

spare yourself the pain of taking his class.  He is VERY BORING and it is annoying to listen to his monotone voice.  You watch several sci-fi films and write 3 papers and a few feeders.  The work isnt hard, but the time spent in class goes by painfully slow.  he put me to sleep in every class.  try another english teacher, there has to be better

Dr. Ross is a wonderful professor. His insights into Romanticism are fascinating and I thoroughly enjoyed going to his class. If you are a dorky English major like me, you will really enjoy this class and Dr. Ross as a person. Very nice man, very helpful. Two 8-12 page papers, and a final exam with 50 multiple choice and two short take home essays.

B-O-R-I-N-G. Although Eng12 isn't supposed to be fun. The class was easy, he was just a very boring teacher. He doesn't really answer questions so much as talk about himself. He likes to slip in comments about The New Yorker at least once a week, which is extremely annoying.

PLEASE spare yourself the pain. Just dont take his class. It is terribly boring and all assignments dealt with space and mars, it's monotonous and so is he. Don't take him if possible.. I mean he knows what he's talking about, but class just drags on for days...
This man enjoys hearing himself talk, and will do so throughout every class period. His assignments are difficult and ridiculously uninteresting. A 6-8 page paper about Life on Mars? Please.

Brilliant guy. An expert on his subject. Has a remarkable ability to speak lucidly in fully formed paragraphs. This course (taken 1.5 yrs ago) sparked my interest in this field, and I have since begun work on a (hopefully publishable) piece of criticism. Thanks David.
A TON of boring reading assignments, very difficult

This class involves a great deal of reading that you must keep up with to do well.  There are no quizzes, only 2 papers and 2 exams.  He expects a great deal from you on the papers and the exams involve essays and very specific multiple choice, impossible if you haven't read.
Professor Kedagni is the BEST professor. He is easy to follow and always available if we need help.

Desire is a great professor and also a joy to talk to. He made econometrics enjoyable to learn and his problem sets, although somewhat challenging, are great review material. I would highly recommend you study and understand the problem sets and attend each class since he goes through important math proofs.
The exams felt very long and math/proof and he does not curve
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: ECON 470 is very difficult, no matter who you take it with. Kedagni was a really nice guy, but resources were super limited outside of class. Thankfully, I passed/failed this course because the average on the final was a 70 with no curving whatsoever.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I didn't like Econ 400, but Kedagni made me love econometrics! You have to go to class, since he takes attendance for a grade and includes concepts from lectures on exams. He's a chalkboard lecturer, which isn't everyone's cup of tea. My one gripe is that the midterms are way too long. However, their content isn't difficult. You just have to study.

Desire is a good lecturer and kind to students. Easy to follow along with, and he doesn't expect you to do any complicated proofs. His exams can be (very) long, but are almost exactly like practice problems, and all exams are graded out of 100 points but have at least 10 bonus points on them. Good option for a class as notorious as 470.

The average on the final was a 72. He refuses to curve anything in the class. His actual teaching style was not terrible, and a lot of the exams reused questions from the problem sets, but the fact that he did not curve a single test with the justification of "if 4-5 people get an A, the grades work" was terrible. The average class grade was a C+.
I took ECON 470 in fall 2023 and this course covers everything you need to know about linear regression. The pace of the class is very reasonable and Professor Kedagni's notes are easy to understand.
Probably the easiest 470 professor. The concepts in the class are not that complicated, he just grades the exams really strictly. Really nice guy to talk to in office hours.

Kedagni never made you feel bad if you asked to go over a topic again. Exams were p long but many problems were repeated from problem sets. So just study those solutions you'll be perfectly fine. He also works through problem sets in office hours. Attendance is taken but also there's not many resources outside of class anyway so don't skip!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Professor Kédagni's lectures -- he's very enthusiastic about the material, making lectures very engaging. The problem sets are good practice for the exams, as the questions on the exams tend to resemble the homework questions. He also sometimes pulls questions from the textbook, so looking at some textbook problems is helpful too.

ECON 470 is hard no matter the professor, Kedagni has some issues with pacing/understanding our prior exposure but has the right idea. Attendance is mandatory and the lectures are helpful for actually applying what you learn, but working through textbook problems will help on the exams. Sometimes gives bonus points for answering questions in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Highly recommend taking 470 with a different professor. The class was disorganized and we didn't get through much of the material, which was super frustrating. The exams were really similar to the homework which was nice, but the lectures were really dull and overall left me with little new knowledge about the topic.

Must unorganized professor I have had. Was supposed to cover 6 chapters of material but only got through 4. Required to learn the other 1/3 of class material for the final independently during the last week of the course. Would not recommend this course for anyone, just wait and take 470 with different professor.

boring lecture and attendance not required so you can get away with not going. tests were pretty easy as long as you complete the study guide. tests were mcq, true/false, fill in the blank, and frq. has review days before exam where you can earn extra credit for the midterm. overall p easy class

For the semester long project, everything is peer-reviewed until the final research brief meaning that it could fail to meet her standards when it's worth the largest portion of your grade. Extremely strict on grading for exams and provides no flexibility in answers. Lost an entire point out of 30 for using a synonym instead of the actual word.

Horrible class, harsh grader, way too specific on her test for no reason, class was all done in lecture and a waste of time to go to, her in class assignments did nothing to reinforce the class content.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tests were horrible. She grades very strict and the questions are too broad. She gives barely any material to study and grades so specifically. Other than the tests the class is fine but the tests make it awful. You can skim the readings that are assigned every day. DO NOT RECOMMEND.

I enjoyed this class! She is very particular when it comes to grading exams, specifically the essay portions but as long as you complete the study guides you will do just fine in the class. Attendance is preferred but you can get by skipping if you need it. Easy A if you complete all the study guides!

The grading for the exams were ridiculous. Averaging low Cs on material that is straight forward. It wasn't very clear how she wanted the short responses and it made a lot of people lose points. Other than that is fine, but grading should not be so hard.

Loveddd Prof. Mitchell. The class itself was not that bad, as long as you follow the exam review sheets you'll do solid on the exams. You'll get a good grade if you follow the rubric for the papers. Prof. Mitchell was good at breaking down complex topics into something digestible. Take her!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Overall, this was a good class. Mitchell can grade strictly on exams and you need to know the material well, but it's not impossible as it's not that much material. The guidelines for assignments were pretty straightforward.

Denise was a good professor but very picky when grading. There are assigned readings for every class but you can get away with skimming them. The final presentation is fair and I think she has a lot of potential as a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. D is honestly one of my favorite GEOG professors! He explains concepts super well and actually seems to care and want to connect with his students. His class is pretty laid back and fun.

Comes off as a pleasant and understanding person but your first conversation with him outside of class will make you change your mind immediately. He's so incredibly condescending and rude when you ask questions in office hours and doesn't actually care about helping you -- instead he just belittles. The TAs were the only redeemable part of him.

This was my first time really working with R, and Dr. D made it super approachable. Everything we did on a "major" grade assignment (hw or project) came straight from an in-class assignment or demo that we had access to. Very easy to do well if you take the time to pay attention to the coding. I thought the class was fun, and Dr. D is a good prof.

I love Dr. D and this class! I learned so much (you learn R) & he was really helpful with feedback & responding to emails & discussion posts. There's a semester-long final project, many coding assignments, demos, and in-class exercises. It's a lot but if you pay attention to his (sometimes boring) lectures and do everything on time you'll get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class is INCREDIBLY organized and you learn R which is great but the lectures are beyond boring and Dr. D is honestly rly condescending which can create barriers when you need to ask for help. There are in class assignments for "attendance" but on canvas and you can do them from home. Exams are easy and its rly easy to do well in his class

My biggest problem with this class is that he waited till last minute to tell us problems he had with a semester long project. His class is not too hard and very organized which I appreciated. Attendance was not mandatory but there are in class activities (you can do these outside of class). You do learn R by the end though!

This isn't an easy A, but manageable. The class has a ton of assignments and two midterms, no final though. You definitely learn to code R and there's a class website which details all of the content and assignments. However, this guy is condescending and rude. Not a huge problem, but be aware. Overall decent class but I did not like the professor.

While there is nothing wrong with the course content, Delameter is very disrespectful and condescending in his feedback and when students ask questions. Never have felt scared to talk in a class before. For a class about technology, no question is a dumb question. Consider a student might be struggling with serious issues before you berate them.
GEOG 215 might be the most organized class I've ever taken. Everything was very clear and there were several examples given before we were expected to do stuff on our own.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I really connected with Dr. Delamater, and he ended up being my favorite professor. I had no coding experience coming into GEOG215, but picked it up really quickly. The TAs are super helpful too if you get confused. Material is easy to learn, just pay attention and do your work and you'll get an A.
Easy class. Straightforward directions. Can be condescending and assigns a lot of busy work.

Mostly graded by tasks that have very detailed instructions so its easy to do well but the lectures were super boring and frankly unnecessary. I skipped half the classes and got an A. Don't mistake this for an easy class though. Even tho the assignments were handed to you, they took several hours to complete. Learned R but did not enjoy the class
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: This class was so unnecessarily stressful and Dr. D is the most condescending person ever, he's so mean and degrades you if you ask questions, don't go to his office hours. Lectures are so painfully boring and participation in this class is so obscure. This class would have been more enjoyable if he wasn't teaching it. You do learn R though!

Dr. D is a great lecturer. He is very structured, organized, and transparent about what can be expected in assignments and exams. You will learn a lot about data science and R. My only complaint is that he has the tendency to be condescending and harsh toward students. If you have extenuating circumstances, please don't rely on his understanding.

Cool class. Great professor. Definitely recommend it.  Class is made up of many assignments that are easy to complete with the detailed instructions given. The final Project is a little difficult for me but that was only because my topic was weird. Just pick something simple. The participation grade is weird too, but it's only 5%. Awesome class!

We had 7 assignments, a (pretty simple) semester-long project, & 2 tests. Super easy to get a high grade if you follow the assnmt instructions & study a bit for the tests. He also provides many resources for success with writing the code. The lectures could get boring, but having an easy & semi-fun workload made up for it imo. Take this!

I honestly had no idea what I was signing up for when I registered for this class, I mostly used it to fill hours, but I ended up loving it so much! Dr. D was seriously great in every aspect. The lectures could get slightly boring from time to time, but you could tell just how passionate he was about the content. No coding experience required!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: He's such a cool dude. I love watching him lecture. I have had some family issues this semester and he was beyond accommodating even with the arrival of his baby. I really enjoyed the class, it's fun and easy if you like coding. But, even if you never coded before, it is beyond doable. Take it!

Professor Delamater is a really nice guy and also very passionate about what he teaches. He's a great professor that genuinely cares about his students and making sure they understand the course material. Personally, I thought the course content was a bit difficult, but if you pay attention, take notes, and do the exercises you will be fine.

This was my first class with Dr. D and I hope it won't be my last! We used R for every assignment and test (so beware if you didn't know) however, I had never used R and still managed to get an A in the class. He is EXTREMELY helpful and always makes time to sit down and talk you through the coding until you get it. Hard work in this class pays off

Dr. D is very organized and clear, both with expectations and learning material. He is willing to help anyone with any level of programming experience get through this class. I especially loved the ability to pick a topic of interest to me and research it all the way through. Though easy-going, he provided opportunities to challenge ourselves.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: 215 is a fun class if you want to learn data science or R in a unique and cool way! Assignments are very easy to follow thanks to Dr. D's instructions and the tests are very fair. I'd definitely recommend taking 215 if you're a comp sci student and need an extra class. It's a nice breather from the usual stuff but also extremely helpful!

215 was a good course, it helped me gain experience with data science and coding in R. The assignments were worth 30% of the grade and were easy, exams were also not bad, and the final project was interesting and fairly graded. Participation is part of the grade so if u want an A you need to go to most classes, however.

Dr Delamater is a really great guy and very easy to get on with. His lectures are engaging, interactive and clearly structured. He references his own work to explain aspects of the course (446 and 541) and is genuinely enthusiastic about his research and the education of students. I would thoroughly recommend you take his classes.
amazing professor-kind, funny, engaging-and the material he teaches is super useful! highly recommend his GEOG491 and GEOG215 classes
He's a really dynamic lecturer that keeps the class engaged. Definitely a great guy to take a class with. As long as you show up to class and ask for help if you need it, you'll do fine in the class.
She is really good.

Dr. Griffin was an amazing professor. The grading for the case studies are a little strict, but as long as you are extremely detailed in your responses you will do well. Dr. Griffin is super understanding and goes above and beyond to support her students inside and outside of the classroom.

Go to class! Lots of points from the exit tickets and group activities. The semester-long project was cool. I like how she focused on applying the content rather than testing. I learn a lot from her classes! Only downside was the final was oral, and was graded kinda harshly imo.

All of this class is is group work, which is horrible because a lot of the group members don't do the work and you get penalized for it through your grades. Get a good group for the final project because I  had to end up doing primarily by myself. She's nice but I swear half the time she doesn't actually know the facts she just speaks like she does
This class was great until the final. It was an oral exam, and Dr. Griffin asked very hard questions compared to what the TAs asked.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class was great until the final. She introduced a new oral exam that was poorly structured. We had 4 minutes for 3 questions, but my interviewer, Professor Griffin, asked harder, extra, and off-guide questions that were completely unrelated to my client. Other students with TAs had simpler ones. It felt unfair and biased.

She wants really specific and strong evidence for each case study. While that is not unreasonable, she sort of gives off the impression that there is only one right answer and grades harshly based on that. She expects extremely clear and detailed work while her questions in themselves are vague and feel like they're up to interpretation.
No tests, lots of group work. The homework and in-class assignments are pretty chill. She's a very knowledgeable and great professor.

Dr. Griffin is great and very knowledgable in the psychology field. I mainly interacted with the TAs, but she is very organized with her assignments and grading. There is a good amount of reading but it was helpful on the assignments and tests. The material is straight forward but can get repetitive/boring at times. Overall great class/professor.
For the group days, your grade depends on the TA you get that week, but otherwise the class was awesome. I was able to learn a lot with a reasonable amount of time going to the class.

Super great profession who wants you to learn and succeed, not just pass a test. Class very lecture based and homework includes lots of textbook readings and GRQs. Work with a group throughout the semester and on one big presentation for the "final."

Griffin is a good teacher, knowledgeable but understanding. 245 was a pretty easy class, considering there were no exams and only case studies. Plenty of leeway with missing classes (I think you can miss up to 20 almost) - most important consideration is to choose a good group at the start of the year, since you will be with them throughout.

Dr. Griffin is very likable, so much so I feel bad for not enjoying her class. Even more so because the content was interesting. The workload isn't too difficult, but it's poorly implemented. Restructuring the assignments could instantly lower to difficulty of this class to a 4 to a 1 or 2 without losing any content.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Griffin is the best! There are no tests, instead, you are graded by your analysis of a case study in class each week. The case studies are done with a group and include answering 4 - 6 questions with 1-2 paragraphs. Grading is super kind, and professor/Tas are very willing to help. Very little work outside of class. HIGHLY recommend.

This class has been my favorite so far! Every week is set up the same. Readings, short online reading quizzes, lectures on read material then group case studies. She is incredibly sweet and offers wiggle room. Allows drops due to potentially sensitive material (ex: suicide). No final exam but a large group project.

Dr. Griffin was a fantastic professor! I highly recommend taking any class with her. There was a very intensive clinical project, but it was interesting and we had a lot of time to complete each part over the course of the semester. Her TAs graded fairly. Overall, I loved this course!

Engaging lectures by Professor Griffin, with insightful guest speakers. Tests require prep, but Unstuck AI was a big help for studying. Assignments can be harshly graded by TAs, but overall a great class.

Dr. Griffin was amazing. There were no exams for this class but there was a lot of in class group work. As long as you do the readings and pay attention during lecture you will do well in the course. She is also very caring and understanding.

Dr. Griffin is an amazing professor! Our section had her new format with no exams but heavy class work and group projects with weekly reading quizzes. Although it made the course significantly easier, it made the class more interesting and easy to engage with. The guest speakers were awesome!

Griffin is a fantastic professor – her lectures, the readings, and the class content are all engaging and informative. However, with the new formatting (no exams/group project final), you could easily achieve an A without putting in any genuine effort. Great professor, but class grading is unserious. If you need motivation to learn, dont take.

loved dr. griffin!! she is a great lecturer and really cares about her students. it is majority group project stuff that are graded hard, but they are very engaging and educational. she is very knowledgeable and actually cares!

Dr. Griffin is a great professor and her lectures are easy to follow. There are no exams, instead there are weekly group case studies. The case studies are graded pretty tough but it's not hard to get a good grade in the course.

This was my FAVORITE class- there are no tests (only weekly reading quizzes that are guided by open-note GRQ questions), it has a group work component which is so nice because some case studies are confusing. She brings in multiple incredible people from a variety of jobs so this is the class to take if you want to know if you should be a clinician

Dr. Griffin is the best! I loved that she considered student feedback and even chose to stop giving exams. The majority of our grade is comprised of case studies, which are completed in a group during class to mimic actual clinical work. They were a little tricky to get the hang of, but the lowest two are dropped and help is available!
I love this lady so much I think I will be 50 years old still remembering how good of a professor she is I literally love psychology because of her she is so nice.

Dr. Griffin was great! She no longer gives exams for 242, but the material is interesting and really important if you want to go into any sort of career in psychology. The readings can get a little long but the guided reading questions make the information you need to pay attention to pretty straightforward.
This is your daughter Carolyn😜

This class was interesting.  The clinical project was fun.  TAs kind of graded things harshly tho.  Tests do require some preparation depsite being take home/open book.  Other smaller assignments were good filler grades for this class.

Clear and informative class, not difficult if you put in effort, show up to class, and pay attention 
Griffin is a great lecturer and has very interesting lectures that are applicable to the real-world 
I highly recommend if you are interested in Clinical Psychology!

The class was pretty interesting overall but your TA basically decides your grade. Throughout the semester there is a clinical project that is completed with essays.I received 80s on all essays (each 12% of grade) and when asked for a regrade the TA just copied and pasted the original piece of feedback(one sentence with no actual specific feedback)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: INCREDIBLE professor but your grade entirely depends on the TA that grades it...

Ok... I have taken her 3 times and this has to be the hardest class I have had with her. Be prepared for a in-class debate which is graded very very harshly. Also a really long paper but it is broken down into multiple sections. She is a sweetie pie though but this class was draining

Best PSYC professor and class at UNC. She is super knowledgeable and passionate about psyc and wants students to be too. Lectures were straightforward and soo interesting, and she is very organized. Graded on case studies, quizzes, in-class activities, and two exams (both open-note). All fair, and she lets a bunch of assignments be dropped. 12/10.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Griffin is one of the best professors at UNC! Take notes during lectures, guest presentations and readings and you should do well. Exams are online and open-note. Assignments have a 7-day window for turning it in. I found the papers were harshly graded by the TAs, but overall a great class!

Wasn't a fan of her in 242, but she's fine in 245. Drops the lowest grades, and has built in absences without penalty. Pollevs for participation. Not super flexible for absences or extensions, but that's what the drops are for. Class is clear cut, exam prep clearly defines exams. 245 is def easier than 242, so go for that if you can.

Dr. Griffin is amazing! Allows extra credit and drops lowest quiz/case study. Exams were online and kind of tricky, but I improved with each one. Case studies weren't too bad and were graded very fairly. Class was engaging and interesting and you can tell she is incredibly educated on the topic and cares about her students. 10/10 would recommend!!

Exams are low-key tricky in this class. I failed the first, but was able to make a comeback luckily- maybe had some animosity towards her for that but I know that's a little petty. The case studies aren't as hard as they seem. Will give practice exams which are helpful! Sometimes questions are reused for the 24hr open exams (including final).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Dr. Griffin was a great professor! She gave great lectures and brought in guest speakers from time to time. There is a decent amount of reading, but I found it to be really interesting. Exams really aren't bad, but a couple of the case studies were tough. Overall it was a great class!

Dr. Griffin is amazing! She brought in guest lecturers throughout the semester from different occupations in Psychology, which was super helpful in exploring careers. There is a lengthy project with a few papers, but exams are online. Grading was sometimes harsh depending on the TA. Overall, Dr. Griffin is super caring and I highly recommend her!

Dr. Griffin was so far the best professor I've had at UNC: genuinely so caring, attentive, and encouraging. She made the course material interesting and engaging, which made the weekly homework/reading assignments not too bad. There's also several guest lectures throughout the semester in various careers in psychology, which was super insightful.
Dr. Griffin is an awesome prof! Loved this class set up and would take it again! The case studies were interesting and the guest speakers were cool
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: In my years of higher education, I have never had a professor as subjective as Dr. Griffin. Her clinical interviewing project, specifically the narrative, uses a highly subjective grading system... which will not accurately reflect the work you did for the paper. Attendance is inflexible as well. Do not take her.

This has probably been my favorite class taken so far at UNC! Dr. Griffin cares so much about her students and the subject matter, and it shows in the lectures and projects. Exams are online and very easy as long as you take notes in class and pay attention.

Her lectures were really interesting and engaging! She had a fun group project that was super easy and if you put in the time and effort into the papers you could get a 100. The exams are appilcation base but taken online and open notes!! I would so take Dr,Griffin again!!

I can't think of many UNC professors better than Dr. Griffin! I have little interest in clinical psych, but she still made the class engaging and one of my favorites this semester. All of her tests and assignment are straight forward and easy to do well on, and they do a great job making sure the material is clear. Take a class with her if you can!

Dr. Griffin is great, interesting in lecture and at answering questions. Exams are online. Only con is that in 242 we have a project worth 36% of our grade and the grading on that is tough, due to TAs.

Really wonderful professor and super understanding. Case studies are graded a little harshly depending on your TA so be aware of that since it is a large part of your grade. Lectures are very interesting and easy to be engaged! Wonderful professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I love Dr. Griffin! I took 245 with her this semester and I'll be taking 242 with her next semester. She is very knowledgable and has worked in many different clinical settings so she has a lot of experience. She is also very sweet! I highly recommend taking 245 with her, it's a super interesting class and she executes very well. 5/5 quality!

The absolute best professor I have ever had. Dr. Griffin is absolute BRILLIANT -- she knows exactly how to teach in way that is clear and so easy to digest. She is ORGANIZED!!! She provides clear and organized modules and have so much helpful tools for studying. Dr. Griffin is the level professors should be compared to.

Dr. Griffin is great! She made lectures super interesting and offered 24-hr grace periods for almost all of her assignments. She's very caring and really wants to see her students succeed! 100% recommend her for any psychology course she offers (ESPECIALLY 242!).

Take 242 with Dr. Griffin!! She makes the material super interesting. You can tell she wants the best for her students and her class/homework just makes sense, she doesn't try to be difficult. She also brings in people to give talks which are super interesting. If you follow the rubrics and do the work, you will get an A.

Dr. Griffin is amazing! 242 has so many components that go into final course grade. Definitely a thorough class to take if you're interested in clinical psychology (guest speakers, hands-on activities, comprehensive readings and application-based questions)
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Griffin is a great lecturer, however her test can be very tricky being that it is mainly an application based test,  we had a clinical project that was 32% of our grade, the grading for that was kind of weird but if you followed the samples given it would be an easy A, overall I really recommend her!

dr. griffin is easily one of my favorite professors. she's literally the best lecturer i've ever seen, her lectures are so engaging and i genuinely loved going to this class so much. there's four case study papers (one can be dropped/skipped) but they're super easy too! midterm and final are open-note too :) take a class with her!!!

Dr. Griffin was a really nice teacher, but the grading scale for our project that determined 32% of our grade was very unfair, with everyone starting at an 85 and either getting bumped up or bumped down. Her exams were also pretty hard, nothing really prepares you for them but the second one is easier cause you'll know whats coming.

Dr. Griffin is a fantastic lecturer, and she makes the content in her lessons very interesting. She is constantly being named as a great, highly-recommended professor within the UNC psych majors community. Her tests can be a bit difficult, and there is one weekly reading quiz. Reading quizzes are no problem if you skim the readings!

She's a great teacher, but she does pronounce stimuli as "stim-you-lee". Since the word stimuli is brought up a decent bit in the class, if that procuration bothers you, then I would not recommend taking this course.

Hands down my all time favorite professor at UNC! Lectures are always very interesting and well organized! Her class never gets boring! Dr. Griffin is also very flexible with assignments by giving a 24 hour grace period for most of them! She is just a phenomenal human being and you can tell she truly cares about her students! Queen status for sure!

There are no words adequate enough to express what an amazing professor Dr. Griffin is. She is at the top of her field and it is evident in her lectures. She is, without a doubt, my most favorite professor at UNC. Her kind attitude and approachable spirit makes such an impact on any student that has the pleasure of taking her class. ENROLL NOW!!!!!

MY FAVORITE PROFESSOR AT UNC!! Dr. Griffin may have a lot of assignments but the assignments are so interesting and are actually kind of fun. There is a group project throughout the semester that is more hands on but it is set up to where if you do it, it will help you succeed in the overall class. Could not recommend her enough.

I like the class overall. Very interesting topics. She is not so accommodating and understanding. Many people are 0.03%, 0.05% away from the higher letter grade and she would not care about curving. That's my only complaint. Besides that, this class is great. I just wish she cares more about students' future and well-being over grade inflation.

First half of the class is about depression, second half about mania. The two largest assignments are the group presentation, and the individual paper on your group's topic which is scaffolded by smaller assignments during the semester. Exams are very fair. Dr. Griffin is a wonderful person who is always friendly and willing to answer any question!

While there is a lot of assignments for this class (3-5 weekly readings, weekly discussions, 3 papers), the grading criteria is explicit and the class is structured to help you succeed. I appreciated the grace periods on assignments and the time in-between the semester long project that consisted of 3 papers and a clinical interview. I recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I've taken three classes with Dr. Griffin and she's really just iconic. So knowledgeable and willing to help with any problems you may have. Despite teaching two courses in the same semester, she makes herself pretty available to meet outside of class time if you need help. 10/10 recommend.

Lots of reading and work that is due Monday, so you will be doing it on the weekends. Also, essay grades are 100, 85, 70. No 99 or 98, etc. This can be frustrating. However, the is very engaging and nice.

There was a LOT of reading for this class. It was asynch, but I felt like more could have been in the lectures as opposed to making us read so much. I also didn't feel like the grading criteria were explained well with the 1st case study - I did well on the others, but didn't feel prepared for the 1st. Overall, a good prof with forgiving policies.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Griffin has been by far my favorite professor at UNC. The lectures are super interesting and it feels like you learn more about her experience as a Psychologist to learn the topics. There is a huge project along with 3 papers plus the 3 exams but the exams are online. There is a huge chunk of reading plus reading quizzes every week.
Would not recommend. Unaccommodating overall and unclear of expectations.  Harsh grader.

Lots and lots of work. Tons of reading. Does not lighten up at all when additional assignments are added on. Everything just piles up. Zero sympathy. As a PSYC major with this having been my final PSYC class, this one by far had the most work.... and it wasn't even close
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Griffin is one of the best teachers at UNC. This class is by far one of my favorites I've ever taken. It is composed on a group project where you come up with a research question, analyze data based on that question and write a paper and create a presentation based on your results. It is writing and group heavy but you learn a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Griffin is simply incredible at what she does. This course is hands-down the favorite that I have taken at UNC. It wasn't easy in that you have to do the work and study, but it is easy in that if you do that and pay attention, then the tests are easy. I read the textbook not for quizzes but later to build and frame my notes. Take. this. class.

This class seemed hard at first but it was actually pretty easy. it consists of a semester-long project that is just overall a few papers which are like 2 pages long. Every week you do the reading, take a quiz, and a few discussion boards. The content was so interesting and I would 100% recommend this class. You can definitely do it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Griffin is an amazing professor! She is interesting, funny, and so knowledgeable about clinical psychology. The exams were easy as long as you paid attention in class. Her grading is pretty easy and you make an A if you put in some effort! I would highly recommend this class to anyone who is interested in psychology.

Dr. Griffin is really sweet and really wants her students to succeed. She's always available during office hours or after class for questions. Material isn't difficult, but there is a fair amount of reading each week (I found the material genuinely interesting though). Grading is clear, 3 tests and 3 major writing assignments make up your grade.

Dr. Griffin's lectures are very strong. Her powerpoints are clear and her lectures are easy to be engaged and interested. Be prepared a lot of work in this class and a lot of reading, both the textbook and articles. Her class is very work heavy, but her lecture style is very good.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Griffin is incredibly intelligent. She is able to clearly convey information in her lectures. There are three papers, a weekly reading quiz, discussion boards, and a few tests. The work wasn't too hard, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Griffin has built in 24 hour grace periods for papers. She isn't very accommodating to some and she makes it very clear what her expectations are from the start. I like honest professors so I say take the class. It isn't difficult however the multiple choice tests sunk my grade quite tedious just do good on the semester long project and final.

Dr. Griffin wore a mesh mask for the first few weeks of the semester. She is not sympathetic at all about mental health concerns, which is ironic since she teaches clinical psychology. She said she couldn't be a therapist b/c she would judge you. She is very knowledgeable about the subject, but the class was not enjoyable due to these things.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Griffin is clearly very knowledgeable on the subjects that she teaches, but she is not a caring professor. She is not at all forgiving about late work or make-ups, even with ARS accommodations, and there is SO MUCH busywork and writing that it feels like an English class. Also, semester long group project. No thanks.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: While you will have excellent lectures, do not expect much from this professor's "human side." She is inflexible and unsympathetic. If you think you will never need anything from her, go for it. But if you understand that life is unexpected and things happen, do not expect her to be accommodating or forgiving. You're welcome!

while there's no textbook, there is a lot of reading for almost every lesson, but as long as you do the readings, you're almost guaranteed an A. your final grade is based on 3 case studies, 3 exams, 10 reading quizzes, and lesson activites from each lesson so honestly a very easy class, highly recommend Griffin if you can take it with her!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: This class has a lot of busy work but it's not necessarily hard if you spread it out throughout the week. There is a semester-long project but it is spread out so it's not bad. Dr. Griffin is super nice and you can tell she is super knowledgeable about Clinical Pscyhology. I would 100% take this class again. But know that it is not an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Unnecessarily obscure grading criteria and not very nice in her interactions with students. This class was made way too hard and too much work for being a 200-level class. Absolutely ridiculous.

Gives a lot of busy work - it's all easy though! Very knowledgeable and a good lecturer. Slightly subjective with grading criteria, but if you put in effort, a good grade isn't difficult. Quality course content.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: One of the best psych professors I have had at UNC. I took this class remotely in the fall of 2020. It was asynchronous but there was a lot of homework each week and a group project throughout the semester that required writing a few papers. It is easy to succeed as long as you keep up with the class and do all of the work each week.

Griffin is such a wonderful professor! I had her in person fall 2019 and I looked forward to her lectures. You definitely have to put in the time to study for exams, but the material isn't difficult. She's a sweet lady, you'll love her!

Dr. Griffin is the best prof I've ever had at UNC! Her class is super organized and is incredibly engaging. The readings were interesting (and necessary for the quizzes) and the projects were fun. You learn a lot and if you ever have questions Dr. Griffin is always available. 10/10 recommend this class and any class Dr. Griffin teaches!

Professor Griffin is great. She did a fantastic job transitioning to online classes and was very understanding of the difficulties it can pose to students. She makes herself available to help students, whether it be in a Zoom meeting or through email. Her class was asynchronous when I took it (VoiceThreads) and tons of reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Griffin is one of the best professors I have had at UNC. She is so knowledgeable and is great at breaking things down so that they are easy to understand. She cares about her students and is extremely accessible. I am in two of her classes this semester and am taking another one with her next semester. Take her classes, you won't regret it!

Prof Griffin was by far one of the best professors I have had at UNC. Her lectures were always interesting and easy to follow. She also made it super comfortable to speak up in class and ask questions despite it being about 200 people in the class. As long as you show up and do the assignments, you should be fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great professor for an online course! Usually online courses are confusing and not well organized. However, the site was so easy to follow and the material was so interesting. It was a LOT of work for a summer class but it was doable! The GRQs are key in doing well. The only complaint I had was that she did grade slow.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT
