Professor Dixon was one of my favorite professors I had this semester. She is acutely adroit at managing students' questions, concerns, and personalities despite Zoom and size (lecture) limitations. She was always honest, equitable, and extremely professional, clearly possessing a wealth of knowledge from her vocational and academic journeys.
I love her class and found it to provide a lot of practical skills in an entertaining manner

Prof Dixon is so caring and supportive of her students. She offers lots of opportunities for introduction into the PR field. However, her lectures are mainly focused on herself, which is great for hearing about realities of the job, but I didn't learn very much.

Professor Dixon really cares about her students. This is definitely an intro course to PR so what you learn is minimal. Make sure to engage in lectures and group discussions because participation matters and the midterm and final ask specific questions but are overall easy.

Prof. Dixon is such a caring person, she really cares about her students well being and success. She does name drop a bit and talks a lot about her experiences in the PR world. I would take this class again but there are very few actual assignments for your portfolio.

Prof. Dixon is super kind, encouraging, and fun! She is so willing to help you not only in class, but outside as well. Responds to emails super quickly. Her name dropping can get a bit annoying, but not a big deal. She knows a lot about PR and is super passionate about it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Dixon was a great influence on my decision to change majors. She is phenomenal at what she teaches and is able to give personal anecdotes to accompany every lesson. I couldn't recommend her enough!

Prof Dixon really cares about her students, but only ever taught us about herself. Her lectures consisted of a few slides she took from other profs, and some brags about her accomplishments. We turned in maybe 3 assignments total, and never got any feedback. I left the class having learned nothing, with nothing of substance to add to my portfolio.

Prof Dixon is such a sweet, caring person, but unfortunately, I never learned anything about PR. I was excited to be able to build up my portfolio (something she promised), but we only wrote photo captions and press releases. I took MEJO 137 with her as well and that class went how 332 went.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I've never had a professor like this. She seems to care so much but never provided any feedback on assignments. I'm a PR major and feel like I need to take this class with another teacher just to get ready for my next classes.

Prof Dixon was a super cool and engaging professor! She incorporates a lot of her own experinces during lectures as examples and really wants her students to know what it's like to work in PR. I learned a lot from her even though people seem to disagree with me I guess.

I did not like this section of the class at all. She spends half the class talking about herself and her achievements, and I ended up learning nothing about PR from the class. Although it is an easy A, I wish I had actually learned something instead of having to constantly flatter her for participation points.

Professor Dixon is a truly awesome professor. She delights in talking about her PR experiences which are pretty interesting. She's accessible to students outside of class and really wants you to succeed!

Jules is such a kind person and highly revered in her field. I was really looking forward to getting feedback and pointers from her, but I never got feedback on any assignments. She didn't grade them! For all I know, she didn't even read it. Very frustrating. She's SO nice and you can get an A if you attend class but I didn't learn a thing.

Prof. Dixon is a very sweet person and cares so much about her students. However, her class felt more like a conference presentation. She never got back half the assignments we had and gave very minimal feedback. If you want to take a class with a nice person, go for this one. If you want to really learn a lot, then look elsewhere.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I'm sorry but she just provided a slide with a a quote from herself. This is what the slide said: "Stay calm. Stay focused on the truth. Be relentless about protecting your client's brand." - Julie Dixon, NC Hall of Fame Publicist

She is very nice, but the only thing I learned from this class was that she likes to talk about herself. I hope she is really as good as she makes herself out to be in PR. She talks about all of the famous people she has worked with and I wanted to take notes and learn if I want to do PR and I barely had any notes.

Honestly, I am not sure I can tell you anything I learned about public relations in this class. Jules always talks about herself, which is fine, but you don't learn anything. Her "tests" were open ended questions on Word docs and we would email it to her or the TA. This class is kind of a joke.

It pains me to say this because she is truly one of the sweetest professors out there, but she isn't a good lecturer and you won't learn that much about PR in her section of the class. Nevertheless, the class itself is very easy.

Professor Dixon spent every class speaking about herself and everything she has done with her career. She will name drop celebrities and ask students unrelated questions for the first 30 minutes of every class. She is a very nice person, but you really don't learn anything about PR.

Professor Dixon is really experienced in the field of Public Relations so anything thats related to that area of profession she can answer. Other than course work, she also provides great support outside of class!! Would recommend to all Journalism students!!

Professor Dixon seemed really caring and definitely is passionate about PR. MEJO137 is an easy A but if you are interested in PR (which I wasnt) you dont learn a lot. For more than half of the class she asks students questions (which is fine) but the same (her favorite) students got picked every. single. time.

This woman is an ANGEL FROM HEAVEN!!!!! I just took MEJO 137 because I was interested in it, i may minor in it who knows, but found myself very engaged in the material and thoroughly enjoyed every lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Jules was a nice professor but loves to talk about herself. We spent 30 minutes every class having students answer questions about themselves and ask her questions. She has a lot of experience and cares about PR but the lectures didn't have much actual content. I feel like I didn't take anything away from the class besides who Jules Dixon is.

Shawty loves talking about herself but actually so fun and such an easy class if you put in the effort. This was the first class I've taken at UNC that I got to meet people online and actually connect with them. Definitely a good class to balance out my others and Jules is so awesome. Everyone who hates on her doesn't know how to relax

While she did seem caring and energetic, she does tend to talk a lot about herself. Her lectures are very 'fluffy' so indeed, unless you're interested in going into PR, you won't take away too much. Participation definitely matters.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I've learned so much this semester about what it's like to be a publicist. Super engaging class and it's clear that she loves what she does. I def recommend her class if you have an interest in PR

Professor Dixon is such an amazing professor. I had her for the PR section of MEJO 137 and it was my favorite class Ive taken at UNC. Her teaching is clear and she connects with students on a personal level. I wish I could take her class again.
Super sweet lady but awful teacher! Most of her classes she spent talking about herself or asking students random questions. If you want to learn PR, do not take a class with her

My capstone class with Professor Dixon was fantastic. As an accomplished and connected PR professional, she gave us the opportunity to work with a huge client at a global PR agency. It was an amazing way to learn the ins and outs of client relations and the agency world. Above all, Professor Dixon cares so deeply for her students and their careers.

Professor Dixon is a true gem at Carolina. She's an incredible resource to her students in and outside of class, as she's an incredibly accomplished and inspiring PR professional and professor. She really helped me narrow my career focus and prepare for a high-level internship. Hussman students--you HAVE to take a class with Professor Dixon!!

I really liked Professor Dixon. She is one of the most caring professors Ive every had. She wanted everyone to succeed. I wasnt the biggest fan of public relations, but she was so passionate about the subject, that it made the class great. I dont think her MEJO 137 class was very hard at all. Id highly recommend taking her class!

This class is actually a joke. We spend the first 45 minutes talking about her or other students. I've genuinely never had a professor who talks about themselves this much. You don't learn anything, and you are very ill-prepared if you actually want to go into PR. However, it's an easy A.

I hate to say this because Prof Dixon is so sweet, but I'm not a huge fan of her class. She spends most of class getting to know her students and then shares a bunch of stories about herself from her PR days. She is a fantastic connection for anyone going into PR but I dont learn much from her. If you're not in love with MEJO or PR, maybe avoid.

She's very engaged and ready to get to know you- it's a little disarming at first, but overall she's very sweet. Show up to class because participation carries in this class. She's very knowledgeable about PR and is a great prof if you're interested at all in the PR world.

I love Professor Dixon! She is the kindest, most caring professor I have had in the MEJO school. She works her hardest to help you make connections with real world professionals, and ultimately find a job. She had an extremely impressive career working for GOLIN. Her knowledge and story telling is very helpful for the higher level classes.
Jules is so so kind but doesn't teach. I don't feel prepared for my upper level classes

Professor Dixon is by far one of my favorite professors at UNCI highly recommend taking a course with her. She values group collaboration & creates real-world scenarios that help build your PR writing skills. She has a ton of experience in the field and is always open to meeting with you in office hours. Her case studies class is great too!

She is a super sweet person but don't expect to learn much. This is a super easy class. I got a 100% on the midterm and I quite literally never paid attention in class because she just tells stories about herself the entire time (I'm not complaining though). Easy A with a perfectly nice professor, it just wasn't what I was expecting.

Professor Dixon was amazing and so inspiring! Even if you're not a MEJO major, I highly recommend taking her classes because she genuinely cares about influencing her students. I had her for a PR class (I wasn't really interested in PR before) but she made this class super interesting and had a lot of available life experiences she shared!

I love Professor Dixon! She is an awesome teacher and she often uses her personal stories of being in the industry as case studies. I learned a lot about PR from her and she is the reason why I decided to apply to Hussman. She is a real gem. I would take her class again if I could!

Julie is really nice but not a strong professor. Her class was basically her telling stories from her PR career. Her stories somewhat provided insight into the field, but I didnt learn the fundamentals of PR or anything really. Grading and exams are super easy and participation not required although she does randomly take attendance.

I was startled by how friendly she was over Zoom and how much she genuinely cared about getting students into the PR world. She shared a lot of cool personal anecdotes, she's hella impressive. She used powerpoints every class but it feels we didnt really learn much in the end. I see it more like a career fair and less like a typical class.

She's really sweet and has a lot of experience in PR, but you don't really learn anything concrete. Classes are mostly discussion/listening to stories. Personally, I didn't gain a lot from this class but she's a great person & seems like she'd be a useful connection if you go into PR.
She tells a lot of stories about her days as a publicist in Hollywood but didn't really teach us anything. Easy A, but I didn't really do any work. She cares but doesn't actually teach.

A fabulous teacher. I wasn't sure about the mejo major until I took her class. She is an inspiration and her lectures were my favorite part of the day. We covered a lot of basics, mostly through discussion.

Julie is really sweet and really cares about her students. Honestly, this class is mostly discussion-based - there's very little homework and she's a pretty easy grader. I think she just wants to know that you are trying and excited about the content she's teaching. She's just someone you want to be friends with outside the classroom

She taught the PR half and she definitely has a lot of experience and credentials. Lots of good stories. We had essentially no work besides showing up for an easy final. Still, the lectures didn't exactly have a ton of substance. Definitely an easy A, but I didn't feel like I learned much. It was still pretty fun and relaxing though.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Julie was the PR instructor for my 137 class (didn't teach advertising). She's super nice, and you can tell she's super passionate about her craft. She was a celebrity publicist, and believe me, you will hear about it a lot. If you really want to see if PR is your bag, try her out. I wouldn't take her if she's teaching both AD and PR, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: epic moment

This was definitely the hardest thing I've gone through. Often, I found myself up late at night grinding. The final was rough; I got a 56 on it, which would have given me a D overall. I asked if the professor could raise my D, but he refused. I even met with him in private after class. In the end he still gave me the D.
Professor Dick is very interesting, I highly recommend taking him and his lectures are the most interesting at school. If you want and easy A then take Dick!
Professor Dog D*ck is very cute, but not the best professor. However, he's always there "reporting for duty", and overall I would say its the hardest D I've ever received
I said it once and I'll say it again... hardest thing I've ever done. I think I attended too much.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dwayne is awesome. He is so passionate about his subject and was engaging even tho this is a gen ed for me.  Final was in person on lockdown browser, but only like 25 questions.
Do your bonus and you don't have to go to class. Respect for my GOAT professor
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very interesting lectures
Dixon is a great professor with interesting lectures! There are a lot of readings, some writing assignments, and a presentation but nothing too hard. Pretty easy class with an engaging professor.

Highly recommend taking Asia 150 with Dwayne. One of the best lecturers and provides generous extra credit opportunities throughout the semester. Grade is made up of 3 discussion posts, 4 short quizzes, a paper, presentation, and the final.
Dwayne is the best teacher I've had so far at UNC and probably the nicest guy I have ever met. Take his class, you will not regret it!

The class is so chill, take home quizzes and short responses every so often. The final exam is online but its so hard. I recommend doing as much Extra Credit and get 100s and all the assignments so your final exam grade doesnt really matter.
GOAT! AMAZING!
He wants you to succeed. He really cares for us.

Overall, Professor Dixon is a very passionate and caring professor. But my issue with the class is that he assigns too many very lengthy readings, especially for a 100-level course. Like 1-3 40+ page readings before each MW class. Do not take this class if you have a busy schedule or hard classes and are looking for a chill class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Dixon is amazing and incredibly passionate about his work. I really enjoyed his lectures and the class content, I definitely recommend this course to anyone especially with it's light workload.
Good prof, easy class
The goat, no more needed to be said.

One of the best professors I have ever had at UNC. He was extremely caring and very respectful of all students. It is evident he wants all of his students to succeed and is an invaluable member of the UNC community.
Dwayne is one of the most inspiring and talented individuals I've ever had the privilege to learn from.
Excellent human being and teacher.

Dixon was my best professor to date. Period. As a premed, asia 57 was an opportunity to explore something worldly and expand past hard sciences. Dwayne knows his place and doesn't make this a hard class, but provides more than enough space to make this an exceptional exploratory course. Talk to him after class; he is truly inspiring.

Took this class in the spring, very easy class as long as you keep up with it. It can be TA-reliant, but I've never heard of somebody having a tough time in this class. Dwayne is definitely an interesting guy, but I'd say the people in these reviews trashing him are overreacting.

Awful... the professor makes you feel super uncomfortable in class. Im not paying him for him to rant about his personal opinion on the political situation of the world. Definitely not a beginner's class, you need to have some basic experience with the material beforehand. DONT go to his office hours, he's incredibly judgy and rude.
EASY AF...TA graded leniently and generously offered numerous extra credit opportunities.
Great teacher, easy focus capacity. TA's grade very easily and the first quiz may be hard but they offer extra credit. Take home exam with 5 extra credit points.
Such an amazing lecturer, and the content was really interesting.

Professor Dixon is a spectacular lecturer and does make his class worth your time. Not completely necessary to attend lectures to receive a good grade but it does help for quizzes and building knowledge of information about topics. Would 100% take his class again and is an relatively easy focus capacity.

even though we disagree on many things, i have become good friends with him. he is an amazing teacher, and i actually enjoyed the class, even though it was taken for gen ed, and i would take it again. he is so passionate about teaching, not just in the classroom. he is amazing at fostering different ways of thinking in his class as well.
he was the goat. take the class you wont regret it

Professor Dixon goes above and beyond to help us be more culturally aware of what is going on in the world around us. His grading criteria is fair and reasonable and he tries to get to know every student on a more personalized level as well.

Really odd professor. Didnt know if class would consist of actual learning or off-tangents he'd go on based on current events. Would openly talk about his political views and be passive aggressive to those with diff beliefs. Final consisted of material we covered maybe 1% of class time. Wouldnt recommend, wouldnt take again

I took this class for a FC, and it was interesting. Professor Dixon is clearly passionate about the subject, which I appreciated, but he often got sidetracked with tangents seemingly unrelated to the lesson plan. There was a PowerPoint, 6 quizzes, and a final paper and exam. Overall, the class wasn't too difficult and challenged deeper thinking.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Wasn't exactly an "introduction" to Asia - you need to have some background knowledge to understand his lectures. It was still an easy class and you can tell he's really passionate about the subject!
So easy, i never study but get a 100 for the final grade
Really easy class, all the quizzes are asynch, and the final exam is too. Professor Dixon cares a lot about the class and is generally a very nice professor. Take this class!

One of my favorite professors. Dwayne is so engaging and is so willing to talk about anything, clearly passionate about what he does and really cares about the students. Material can be a little challenging at times without background knowledge but I really recommend putting in some effort since the course can be rewarding and pretty low stakes.

Professor Dixon is my favorite professor I have taken here. He is extremely knowledgeable about the subject matter and has many interesting tidbits from his personal life relating to his lessons. However, he frequently refers the class to current national and global events, such as climate change, that stress some students out.

He is great! Quizzes are very simple, and so is the Final Exam. Essay grading is dependent on your TA. There is 5 points of extra credit on the Final Exam which are not too hard to get which could boost your overall grade by 5 whole points!

One of the best professors I had so far. His sincerity and enthusiasm about topics could be felt by the class. His lectures are fascinating, and he sometimes talks about his experiences too. Graded on a few essays and short posts about current class topics, which he grades very leniently. Definitely take his class if you can!!!

Super funny guy who tells stories about his past. There are a few research posts on Canvas (super easy), online quizzes, and a recitation presentation you have to do based on a topic covered in class. Take a class with him if you want an A. There are some readings and films but honestly don't spend too much time on it. Overall recommend!

Professor Dixon was super nice! This class was fun and interesting and was not stressful, very good class to take if you are looking for a GPA booster. Everything is online, all quizzes and tests, there was one paper and one presentation for a recitation but overall totally recommend!

Probably the nicest professor I've had so far, considering how he is a lenient grader and accomodating to deadline extensions. Prof. Dixon is also well-informed on the subject and makes it both interesting and topical. You can tell he cares every lecture, especially during his personal anecdotes There is no reason NOT to take a course with him.

I took ASIA150 with Prof. Dixon, Fall 2023. Prof. Dixon is a really passionate professor who isn't afraid to give takes to students who care to hear and listen. Throughout his lectures, from modern issues to material covered in weekly readings, I love him for his caring attitude towards. By far one of the most influential courses I've taken at UNC!
There's a lot of reading, but the professor is really cool and knowledgeable. He tries to help students as much as he can and is clearly passionate about what he is teaching.

Extremely easy class. Attendance is not mandatory; hence, many people do not attend his lectures. However, the lectures were so interesting that I wanted to go just to hear his insights on current global matters. Gives a lot of extra credit opportunities and is very understanding.

Easiest class to fulfill a gen ed!! Lectures are very interesting but only recitation is mandatory (you do have 3 attendance drops so it's pretty lenient). Class has a few discussion posts, one presentation, a final paper, and a final project. TONS of extra credit opportunities that are weighted quite high! highly recommend for an easy class

The class was soooo easy and I learned a lot (if you pay attention in lectures). He clearly cares about his students and wants the best for them. He does get sidetracked a lot in lectures which is very offputting. You have like 4 actual graded assignments which are easy. I def recommend him.
Dr. Dixon is the GOAT. Please do your college semester a favor by taking this course. I guarantee you will love this class more than any gen-ed you have ever taken at UNC.

Dr. Dixon was a great professor; he always made an effort to engage the class in meaningful discussion and gave ample opportunity for extra credit, etc. Definitely one of the most stress-free and understanding professors at UNC. Would totally recommend this class, especially if you need something to buffer between more advanced/harder ones.

Professor Dixon was an amazing professor. He was very caring towards his students and made sure to prevent stress throughout the semester. He offered multiple extra credit opportunities during the semester as well as being very forward with his grading. He was inspirational throughout the semester and I would highly recommend to take this class.

Gives his own one sided perspectives to ongoing issues. Prefers teaching about certain ethnic groups over others. Certain groups were only discussed in a negative light and often villainized. Talks about Middle East more than Asia. Tries to relate to experiences of POC. But if you don't care about that not a difficult class.

Professor Dixon cares about his students and wants them to succeed. He can get sidetracked during lecture but they are interesting and valuable and some of the disorganization occurs in this class because of the sheer amount of content being covered in one semester. Readings can be long at times but they are always good, digestable texts.

Dwayne is the easiest professor I've ever had. I took both JAPN162 and ASIA150. Dwayne's super animated and engaging. Final grade consists of a few online quizzes and forum posts, a presentation graded by TA, final paper, and a take-home final. Readings assigned weekly, but only need to skim them, especially if you go to class. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I think he's a great professor, my only issue is that there are so few assignments that if you even mess up one all of a sudden your looking at an A- or a B+ even.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super great professor. The class was definitely a moderate load, but this is because we actually learned. I don't know why the reviews say the class was super easy. It definitely encouraged learning.

Very... eccentric character of a professor, but super easy grader and very accommodating of anything. Gives extensions for any reason. Class was basically just a discussion about random stuff lol and the class had no structure. Showing up to recitation gets you all the points. Did not try at all, extremely easy A for a GenEd. Definitely recommend!

Dr. Dixon was extremely accommodating to student needs, always responding to emails and understanding of student conflicts. There are 3 short research posts, 4 five-question quizzes, 1 long essay, and 1 presentation during recitation. Great professor as well as a great and easy course.

The class honestly has like no structure. We had to read a lot of stuff, but Dixon was somewhat vague on what exactly we had to retain. On the first day of lecture he literally said "the content material is too vast to really learn anything." Regardless, still an easy A and the readings are optional if you go to class.

Really easy class, and really nice and caring professor! His teaching/lecture style is kind of disorganized, but he's clearly very passionate about what he's teaching. The class is just a bunch of readings, a couple of essays, a final project, and the final exam is really easy.
goat
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dwayne was absolutely amazing! ASIA 150 is one of the most engaging classes at UNC, but also one of the easiest. Attendence not required, he posts everything online and quizzes are super easy. Only 1 paper what was 4-5 pages, super easy to write. Readings were long, but you could skim. Recitation had 1 presentation per person, was short and easy.

reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Take any class that Prof Dixon offers. He is passionate about what he teaches and that passion is reflected in his lectures, if you are at all interested in the course content like I was, you will LOVE his class! His JAPN 482 class was also amazing and a good step up from ASIA 150 in terms of rigor. Do your education a favor and take his class.
I absolutely LOVE this man. He's the best. Take his classes if you can.
Poor instruction!

This professor was the best I have had at UNC. He truly cares about you and the issues we face in the world today and hoe we are impacted by them. I have never met someone with something even remotely bad to say about this guy. He values you, your background, and your time and it shows with how he structures the class and assignments.

Smiling everyday, he is super nice and caring! His lectures are awesome! I always learn a lot and never feel boring. Respect every student from different countries. Encourage everyone to participate in the welcoming discussion. Nothing much to say just love him sooo much! Best professor for me in UNC! Really recommend this class!

This guy is a little weird but the class is very easy. Got an A without going to most classes or doing any of the readings at all. The class is fully online unrelated to covid rules, and involves very little actual work. The only real assignments are a short essay at the end and a short presentation in recitation; both were very easy
AMAZING!! He really cares about his students and will make sure they know that. Easy class, but you get to learn a lot.

Dwyane is understanding and cares about his students hes more focused on their wellbeing than anything else. He's super disorganized and the format of his lectures is him just talking at us no PowerPoints, textbooks, etc. which kinda made it hard for me to learn. we had an essay with no rubric and he never told me why he took of points, no feedback

Professor Dixon is a very funny and unique kind of professor - the kind that doesn't care about grades. He likes to introduce people to topics in Asia and Japan but doesn't care too much what you take away from it as long as you learn something. Just make sure to do the assignments since they are each worth a lot.
Best Professor at UNC!! Honestly nothing else to add! Take this class if needed or interested! :)
Love Dwayne so much! He is a wonderful professor and I highly recommend him! :) There are very interesting readings and he makes discussion very fun and interesting!

Dixon gives phenomenal lectures that turn into very fulfilling discussions. He also understands that we are human beings and is very caring and understanding of personal circumstances. Daily readings or videos are assigned, but all the material is very engaging and interesting. Highly recommend taking a class with him if you can!

This semester was really hard for me, and only his course saved my days. I felt like I was actually learning, and I didn't feel a lot of pressure. He was understanding, and he pays attention to each of his students. If you can and want, take a class with him.
Taken 2 courses with him in one semester, Best Professor ever!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Dixon is a very interesting and caring Professor. This class has a small number of assignments, a paper, and a presentation, which are easy to get high marks. His quizzes and final exam are very simple.

Professor Dixon is one of the more chill professors at UNC. He is easy on grading forums and the quizzes are simple as long as you pay attention in class and read the assignments. Finals are a walk in the park as well. Highly recommend for a gen ed credit or an easy A.

Dwayne was very chill and so caring to students. He's very passionate and knowledgeable in this subject and the class gives 3 gen eds too. The TAs are also very nice. The work itself is very easy - couple forums, couple 5 question quizzes, and typical final paper and final exam. There is a presentation in your recitation. Highly recommend!

Dwayne genuinely cares about his students so much and he is not a tough grader whatsoever. He always made his students feel cared about and if you listen to the lectures and grasp the concepts from the lectures even if you don't from the readings, you can easily get an A. Would highly recommend taking ASIA-150 with him, and his other courses too!

I absolutely love this man. He is by far the most caring professor at UNC. He cares so much about his students and is so passionate about what he teaches. He makes the topics so interesting and I cannot recommend enough that you take any course taught by Dwayne.

This class was super easy and enjoyable to take. This is the second class I have taken with Professor Dixon and I suggest to everyone to do the same. There was minimal homework and the assignments were graded nicely. The professor and the TA's want you to do well and they are quick to communicate whenever there are questions.

Dwayne is literally the coolest ever. His class was super chill and relatively easy. You will have to do the readings and listen to the audio lecture(s) every week, but if you take notes on the audio lecture by the end of the class you'll have no problem passing the relatively easy final. He really cares about his students and it shows!
I loved his class. It was very interesting. There's a lot to read, but he goes everything in his lectures so don't worry if you don't understand everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dwayne is amazing! He is very caring, understanding, and so passionate about what he teaches. Dwayne genuinely cares about us as human beings and taught us to think critically about the world. Dwayne definitely prioritized our learning and having an outlet to have fruitful discussions despite ZoomU rather than stressing us out with grades. Love him

Easily the most understanding teacher I've ever had! So approachable and engaging. Some reviews say that he's "too political," but Dwayne is open-minded, and we're living in a politically demanding decade. Plus the class is literally based on an entire continent. Everyone was so sad when class ended- now we stay connected on Discord! TLDR: Take it!

DWAYNE is OG LEGEND Super Prof who is SOOO OUTSPOKEN with principle in academic teaching and caring/understanding for students---especially in COVID season. He is so eloquent and knowledgeable and is passionate about what he teaches and stands for! He is open minded and will never impose beliefs on you. EASY CLASS, so meaningful!! TAKE HIM! :-)

This is a must have professor right here ladies and gents. Content is easy and life-changing If you hate discussing politics in a class that surrounds the topic of Asian nations, that might be your own problem. Either way, I can guarantee that you'll learn something new. Dude does not miss.

He is one of the most amazing lecturers I have ever heard. His goal is not to make his students memorize a bunch of useless facts, but to really cause them to think about the world in a different way. Though he talks about serious topics, he does not assign a ton of difficult assignments to stress you out or hurt your grade. Amazing and fun class
I loved this class! Dwayne is so nice and really cares about his students. His lectures are so interesting and the quizzes are NOT hard at all.

Although Dwayne is a super chill guy, he is extremely political and his lectures are basically just his leftist opinions and he goes off on many tangents to the point where its confusing. Don't take this class unless you're actually interested or you will just be annoyed like me.

I took professor Dixion FALL 2020 at UNC. He was amazing. I thought his class was interesting and it was easy to remember material. His class took me the least amount of time and could be considered an easy A as long as you do the work. This is definitely the GEN ED class you want to take (with this professor).

Dwyane is a Leader of an Antifa Group. He is a far-left individual. Most importantly, he's a chill ass professor. Take him your first semester if you are new or looking for an easy class. He assigns readings, but you can honestly skip them if you just come to class and pay attention. He has one paper (easy, 5 pages) and the final is easy as cake.
Too political

Professor Dixon discusses a lot of intense social concepts, and he really challenges society's thinking. He is an amazing lecturer and his class was easy to get an A in. There are not many grades in the class but the ones he gives he grades leniently.

He is a great guy who is very passionate about the topic but is extremely disorganized at times. Some of the topics are explained in a confusing manner, but if you do the readings, you should be fine. There are readings before every class, a few pop quizzes, a recitation presentation, midterm, 10-page paper, and a final. Overall, would recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Dwayne is the goat. Super easy class. Grading schemas were very fair and the final exam was a breeze. There are lots of reading but they are not necessary if you pay attention during class. Easy class.

Dixon was an amazing professor. He is very passionate about Asian studies and you will learn a lot. You also get to choose how you're graded and the final was a 10 question super easy T/F. Easy A and engaging material.

He is an understanding, passionate professor and just expects you to put in the work. You get to choose how you get graded based on different schemas. Although his lectures tend to be confusing at times, if you try to understand and do the work correlated with your schema it should be a relatively easy class for the gen eds.

Dwayne is super woke and cares a lot about what he teaches. It is easy to not pay attention in class though. He allows you to basically choose how you want your class to be structured. Schema 1 seemed easiest to me. Easy A and you learn a lot
Dwayne is the goat.

Attendance: Lecture is not mandatory, recitation is (this is where you get your "pop" quizzes) Workload: Weekly/daily readings, midterm, 10 page paper, final -- midterm was very easy and straightforward Professor: very understanding, funny and kind of quirky, he's very open and really advocates for students/listens to our concerns
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The best professor I have ever met in UNC. Graduate-level papers but easy A as long as you finish all the assignment (you could pick any themes you want). Treat students as human and share all of his own stories and perspective to the class deeply and truly. RESPECT.

Professor Dixon is a captivating lecturer who facilitates profound discussions during lecture. Although there is a lot of readings assigned, they aren't required if you go to lecture and pay attention. If you do the small amount of work he asks of you, you will be rewarded with great lectures and an A. This class is a great GPA boost/GenEd provider

Dwayne is a kind person, but as a professor, he was incredibly disorganized & the course overall felt chaotic. There are many readings assigned, & depending on which grading schema you choose, there are different assignments & he is a lenient grader. The course was not what it appeared to be advertised as, and was very complex and abstract.

Dwayne is a very kind man and a captivating lecturer who truly cares about his students. The course content was interesting and the grading was quite lenient. He tends to ramble about his strong political beliefs, which did annoy some. The lectures and GPA boost, however, are totally worth it.

Dr. Dixon is the most passionate lecturer and most well spoken professor I have had so far at UNC. Take his classes, he won't try to hurt your GPA, show what you have learned and you will be rewarded with a grade and some captivating lectures.

Dwayne is a great guy and the assignments you have are easy and graded leniently. However, he gets up there and preaches his political agenda which is kind of annoying. If you can deal with that though, it is definitely worth the GPA boost. The final is only worth 10% of your grade and the only reason he has one is because it is required.

Dixon is one of the most passionate professors I have ever had. His lectures are interesting and engaging. He truly cares about the subject and his students. At times, there is a lot of assigned reading (but they are almost always captivating). His tests are FAIR, not meant to trick or fail students. It is necessary that you are engaged in class

Dwayne is easily one of the best professors I have ever had. Besides giving amazing lectures, he is emphatically passionate and knowledgeable about his area of study. His class changed me in so many ways and it was one of the few I looked forward to going to. One warning I would say is that he assigns a lot of reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Easily one of the best professors at UNC. This class is a seminar and until now, I had never seen a teacher establish such a bond of trust with their students that students were comfortable enriching the class with details of their private life and experiences to such a large extent. This class made me feel valued as a person and gave me a voice.

Best of the 4 math profs I've had at UNC. Cares more about what you learn than your grade, which is something I always like in instructors. Tests aren't really too bad and he gives mostly A's and B's. Homework assignments are sometimes tedious or overly difficult, but besides that I have little complaint. Would recommend this guy!

Great teacher, makes everything clear and encourages questions. He is helpful, nice, and easy to approach. Exams were challenging but he doesn't adhere to strict number/letter grades, and he seems to care more about students learning than the grade they get. The only criticism I have is that homework was sometimes unnecessarily long and tedious.

Really knows his mathematics. Is utterly brilliant AND good at teaching. Very clear and concise. Does good examples.  Very nice, personable and approachable.  He teaches at a brisk pace, but if you do the homework, go to all the classes, and ask questions, you'll do fine.  Oddly, his Russian accent forces him to enunciate, making him very clear.

Really knows his mathematics. Is utterly brilliant AND good at teaching. Very clear and concise. Does good examples.  Very nice, personable and approachable.  He teaches at a brisk pace, but if you do the homework, go to all the classes, and ask questions, you'll do fine.  Oddly, his Russian accent forces him to enunciate, making him very clear.

Dr. Khveshenko is one of the worst professors ever. His lectures were useless and completely unrelated to exams. Anything he wrote on the board was impossible to decipher, and his accent is difficult to understand. He cannot answer any questions, and talked to us as if we are PhD students in physics. Please avoid for your sanity.
DON'T take physics with Dmitri he's hard to understand and doesn't show his work. He just clicks through the slides. Bad lecturer.
just a bad lecturer, will just read off of slides and click through how problems are worked out. 50% of the time when students ask a question he answers a completely different question

I wish I could give him zero stars. I have never encountered such an AWFUL professor. It is obvious he does not read the slides before class, nor does he care about teaching the material. No work is ever shown and explanations are always unclear. Take this course with a different professor, or at a different institution. AVOID HIM AT ALL COSTS!

I wish I could rate him zero stars. I have never encountered such an AWFUL professor. It is very clear that he does not read the slides before he comes to class, nor does he care about teaching it. He shows no work when solving examples and provides unclear explanations. Take this class with another professor or take it at a different institution.

I have never disliked a teacher enough that I have been compelled to leave a review until now. Do not take a class with this man AT ALL COSTS. He does not read the slides before the lectures, so he encounters them for the first time along with the students. Genuinely the most confusing and hard to listen to lecturer I have ever encountered.
i wish i could rate him a 0 but it is not an option. Avoid at all costs

Terrible professor. The mode for almost every exam was a 0-50. I am a STEM major that got A's in every STEM class BUT this one, I barely passed and had to pass/fail it midway through the semester. Every lecture he simply read from the slides and provided no practice problems so we all had to teach ourselves Physics. Just avoid him at all costs :)
worst lecturer I've ever had. going to class was useless except for the participation points. UNC physics department needs to make major changes to this course it was terrible

I am a hard worker and devoted entire days to studying for his exams. i have never felt so negatively towards a professor. Unkind, confusing, and a poor lecturer. I left every class confused and he often was unable to answer questions.

Picture this: the powers out when you show up to lecture, thinking youll be dismissed. Instead he gives the lecture in pitch black (yes this actually happened). So, among many other reasons (this example is just the cherry on top), AVOID THIS PROFESSOR. I genuinely believe that he didnt even read the slides before lecturing each day, good luck3
You cannot understand him and he's terrible at explaining concepts. Lecture is basically useless because you don't learn anything. Exams are impossible too, they want you to fail
Gives very little explanation towards concepts that are very hard to understand for the average person.

worst teacher I have ever had at UNC. I think he forgets students are just learning this content. Doesn't explain anything and just teaches terribly overall. Exams are pretty bad too and your grade depends on if you have a good TA grading it or not. avoid him if you can
No classes lasted longer than 30 minutes and he often failed to explain material in depth. Skipped over slides in lecture or didn't know what they meant a lot.

Be prepared to watch the online lectures outside of class. He typically just reads from the slides in lecture and does not give any explanation for the in-class practice problems. When students tried asking him questions during the Q and A session he often didn't answer them or gave a vague answer. Try to take it with a different professor!

Usually I would recommend that people take RateMyProfessor ratings with a grain of salt, but please beware of this professor. All of your learning will need to be done outside of class which is difficult with the extreme courseload with 3-5 homework assignments per night plus the studios twice a week. Very difficult for a non AP physics student.

Dr. Khveschenko is a very smart man; however, that is the only positive thing I can say about him. His lectures are impossible to understand, and have a loose connection to the homework. His tests are unbelievably difficult, with little to no curve. His class made me hate physics, and I didn't learn a thing. If you can, avoid him at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Good teacher, chill guy. Didn't seem like the type that would care if u failed his class, but during office hours he would help u work through problems even if it was hard to understand his work. He never rushed you out of his office. The curve was kind of annoying bc there were AP physics kids that took the class, but I never took AP and did well.

One of the worst professors at this entire university. He can't convey even a single concept clearly, gives impossibly difficult tests (and you always due worse than the average due to AP Physics students retaking it), and at the end you feel like you haven't learned half of what the other classes learned. AVOID HIM LIKE THE PLAGUE!!!!!!!
You have to teach yourself, but he records everything and will try to answer questions in class.

He's fine but try to get another 121 teacher if you can. He has no clear grading criteria at all and will take off points differently for each student depending on how he's feeling...I tried to talk to him about a grading concern I had and he responded with very rude emails. Definitely have to teach yourself all the coding and video editing too.

Peter can be hard to reach outside of class sometimes. While other times he is quick to respond. I guess it depends on his mood. Extremely easy grader, but the instructions are very unclear and confusing. Doesn't really teach. But honestly, as long as u put in a little bit of effort on the assignments, you'll get an A.
Take MEJO 121 with Doyle! He is so kind and helpful. This class is a lot of hard material to learn, but he does a great job teaching it and helping each individual student.

Take this class with Peter Doyle! He was so kind and approachable, as well as very accessible outside of class. He is always willing to help if you have any questions. I wish I was able to take more classes with him, he is the sweetest guy ever and has very interesting experience!

Professor Doyle is very approachable and knows his material very well! Be sure to pay attention in class and put time into doing your work well — the quality of your work will clearly show in your grade. Some of the material (especially HTML) is hard, but Professor Doyle is happy to give you help if you need it. Take MEJO-121 with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Doyle is the kindest guy ever! There were points where it felt like we had a lot of projects due at once, but he gives them out far in advance. He's very accessible and understanding of literally everything. This class really touches on every type of digital media and he gives great feedback without hurting your grade. Take his class!!

If you are interested in anything related to editing, filming, and MEJO, take this class with Professor Doyle! He is incredibly sweet, understanding, and helpful. I seriously have no complaints about him. If you are feeling unwell or away, he lets you join the class via Zoom. He is also a rather understanding grader.

Easy class, but Prof. Doyle teaches very fast and not always clearly, so would not recommend him if you aren't able to teach yourself the programs. Very nice, typically let out class early. Cares about his students and wants them to learn. Doesn't give an exact rubric, but follow the instructions and what he says in class and you will succeed.

He was a pretty good professor and let us join class on zoom, which was lovely. He sometimes didn't give us great lessons and class got boring. He also graded a little harshly and inconsistently, which frustrated me. Had to ask for a few regrades (but usually got them). Grading scale is a 95 for an A, but he doesn't give above a 95 super easily.

Professor Doyle is so nice and one of my favorite at UNC!! He is so caring and will give you extensions if you need them. He also lets you join on zoom if you need to. All project based, and they are not too hard if you try on them!! Love him

Doyle made taught the programs well and set realistic expectations for an intro class. He goes over everything you need to know how to do in class and posts videos to rewatch. Took attendance, but I don't think it was factored into grade, just the couple straightforward assignments. You do have to buy kinda a lot of equipment. Peter's a great guy

This is an introductory class so don't stress about the new, different programs. The coding with html and css was easily the most difficult aspect of the class, varying teacher to teacher. Be aware - classes are lecture heavy with little hands-on practice during class. Professor Doyle is a very experienced teacher and excited to teach y'all.
Professor Doyle is friendly, considerate, and helpful!

I liked this class and Professor Doyle. He talks very fast during lectures but records them so you can watch them after class. It is a project-heavy class, but Professor Doyle tries to make it as fun as possible. If you are not comfortable with Premier Pro or Word Press, he is very helpful.
Professor Doyle wasn't super clear with the rubric for assignments and not a very engaging lecturer. Overall I gained lots of skills from this class but wish my grade reflected it.

Professor Doyle is extremely kind and he is very professional and  experienced. I strongly recommend students who majors in mejo to take this course. Although 95 is A, he will give you some curve. All the projects are interesting and not heavy.

Professor Doyle is so kind, easily accessible, and VERY experienced. The class is project-based (5 + the final) with no rubrics, but he is not a tough grader by any means. He's also super open to discussing project errors. The only complaint is that he doesn't explain HTML/CSS very well, but a few youtube videos filled in the blanks. Easy A.

Peter Doyle is very kind and was flexible with office hours. His grading criteria is not always clear which isn't ideal for a project based class but he is not a harsh grader. I learned a lot of digital skills in this class. This is a fun and enjoyable class especially if you are interested in video, coding, or photoshop.

Professor Doyle is one of the kindest professors I've had while at UNC.  Classes are tutorials on how to use various media applications. Lectures are fast-paced but recorded for future reference. Professor Doyle provides good feedback and help on assignments. He's definitely a good professor for first-years still getting used to college academics!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a nice guy but gives very little instruction to assignments.

Professor Doyle is extremely caring and is always accessible outside of class. The assignments were super interesting and I learned a lot about Adobe software. He can be a little nit-picky with grading, so make sure you are submitting your best work. Overall, wonderful class!

Prof Doyle is a very nice, helpful teacher. I learned a lot from his video/coding class, and he always took the time to show us how to do things/give examples instead of outsourcing material. He also talked to us about the journalism/video industry, where he is very experienced. Overall, super useful class and an interesting professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: While it can be a bit hard to understand him at points with the mask and his British accent, he knows a lot about the field and is a pretty relaxed grader. He is also very caring and is always willing to talk about your work if you need help. However, he does go fast during lectures, but he also records them so you can just rewatch them later.

Doyle was one of my favorite professors this semester. His grading system is clear and easy to understand, and his lectures and instructional sessions are very informative. I feel that my editing skills, both web and video, have improved greatly.

Prof. Doyle's class was my favorite this semester. Assignments every other week and you get to learn video editing/shooting. Very low stress and honestly just a good time. Final is a documentary on anything you want and it's lots of fun to make. Take MEJO 121 with him! I've heard its unnecessarily hard with others. I did half in person half online.

Extremely boring if you already know anything at all about visual media. For MEJO majors, I would suggest making an appeal to not take the class if you've already taken COMM 130 and MEJO 187 like I had. It seemed to me like he hardly knew how to do the things he was teaching. I would have struggled if I hadn't already known the material.

Genuinely my favorite professor this semester. He takes the time to listen and engage with his class. He really made me feel seen and noticed, which is hard to come by with online classes. Everything was clearly explained and grading criteria was straight forward. Definitely would take again!
Peter is so kind and helpful. I loved 121 and how simple he made everything. He will give good feed back but make sure you know your work is good. Highly recommend!!!

Peter is genuinely the kindest professor I have had at UNC. He gives you the opportunity to re-submit assignments, move deadlines, and loves to celebrate student successes. He probs wouldn't be a great choice if you are *really* interested in learning the material, but he is lovely if you only want to grasp the basics of editing/coding (and an A!)
Peter Doyle is the best professor to take MEJO 121 with! He explains how to do things with editing so well, and he lets you resubmit assignments because he understands that you're learning!
Amazing professor. Very kind, reliable, understanding, and smart.

Professor taught very difficult and controversial subject matter in a clear manner. He is very accessible outside office hours and overall a very kind man. He posts class notes which he updates every time he rereads the class materials which are manageable which make the essays easier. Go to office hours.

Dr. Maclean taught me so many things in Phil 155. I went to his office hours and he cleared a bunch of things up for me. Then he took me into his big strong arms and said "this Mac'clean' boy is thinking some dirty thoughts." He porked me so thoroughly, I kept finding barbeque sauce on me for weeks afterwords.

PHIL classes at UNC are just hard in general. Grade comes from 2 papers, a quiz, a final, and recitation participation. Grade 100% depends on your TA. You're supposed to read a lot, but Doug covers readings in lecture, and posts his PPTs. Doug gives you quiz/final questions to study in advance, but the actual questions are slightly different.

Professor MacLean is amazing. He's talks a little softly but in a big lecture class he is mic'd so it's not really a problem. This course was pretty reading heavy but his lectures do a fantastic job of covering the reading material and he posts his slides. I would definitely recommend taking one of his classes.

Dr. MacLean has amazing organized lectures that completely cover the required readings for class. His TAs are super helpful and always available to discuss any philosophical or logistical questions you might have. Grading is tough simply because he makes sure the average grade is a B-, but work hard with TAs on your papers and you'll do great.

Great professor. Really enjoyed his class. He is laid back and is a straightforward lecturer. His powerpoint slides are interesting and VERY ACCURATELY and COMPLETELY cover the reading material, so you honestly don't have to focus too much on the readings. Go to recitations. GO TO CLASS even though he doesn't take attendance and you'll do fine.

Personally I am not impressed by his lectures, but fairly speaking,a 200 people philosophy class is hard to teach. I like the course material, but do not like that he basically reads from his powerpoint. Lectures seem very rushed and he pushes all the questions to the recitation sections which I really enjoyed. Maybe his smaller classes are better.

Professor MacLean is one of the best Philosophy teachers I have come across. The class is kinda hard and the reading are a lot but overall you leave the class with a strong moral sense of reasoning! You actually understand the decisions you are making far beyond just on the papers in your class.

Professor MacLean is a really cool guy. I had him for a FYS and all we did was discuss readings and write papers. His feedback on papers is really helpful too. Maclean is always there to help you understand the concepts, you can go up and ask him anything. The topics were proofs about the existence of god. Really chill class, would take again!

This class was one of my favorites yet. Professor MacLean is honestly one of the best professors and nicest guys I know. He is the most willing to help you out of any professors I know, & he always wants to make sure that you understand the material. If you show that you want to improve, he appreciates that so much. Wonderful professor & course

Great professor for an honors class. The readings were very interesting, as were class discussions. He gives good feedback for papers and gives students the opportunity to correct their work for a higher grade.
I could not agree more with the previous assessment.

If you're taking this class because you think it'll be extremely interesting...don't. He basically reads his slides in every lecture and I'm pretty sure half the people slept each class or played on their computers. This class was a complete waste of my semester. Extremely nice guy- awful lecturer. Maybe in a smaller class it's different.

Took him w/ a class of ~20. His voice is easy to tune out accidentally, but the readings he picks are so awesomely amazing that you want to pay attention and come to class. Papers are interesting and he takes improvement into account when grading.

You can just read, but if you go to class he will tell you what you need to know from each reading. I thought the class was easy, but there are others who would disagree. Your TA does the grading so once you understand the what they want it's pretty easy. I ending up with an A- but my scores were always above the class average (typically c+ or b-)
very, very easy class. i didn't even go to the lectures and still got an -a for going to the recitations and doing the papers.
No Comments
He basically never replied to student's emails. Important documents concerning students are not ignored by him at all. This is the most irresponsible professor I have ever met at UNC.

The midterm didn't seem to align with the study guide, which was also released only a few days before the exam, making it hard to prepare effectively. I noticed inconsistent grading between recitation sections. Additionally, communication could be improved, as emails often went unanswered and lectures sometimes felt difficult to stay engaged with.

Professor Smit was my favorite professor this semester. He is funny and enjoyable to listen to. He relates hard-to-comprehend topics to simpler concepts in a way that's engaging and fun. He knows what he is talking about.

Prof. Smit was such a lighthearted and kind guy; you can tell he cares about his students beyond just the content we learn in class. You do need to go to lectures to get the content for exams (not much posted on lecture slides) but his lectures are pretty good as it is. 100% recommend taking his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor, he really cares about his students and wants everyone to do well in his class.

Smit is a great professor! Lectures were very interesting and fun! Important to attend because not a lot of info online. This is a super easy gen ed. 2 tests for the 1st and 2nd half of content and some reflections. Tests are easy if u take good notes and look at the study guide. I didnt do any readings and the tests were still easy.

Overall an entertaining professor who is passionate about the topic he teaches. You will need to actually attend lecture and do the reading to do well or you wont do well (the average on the midterm was around a 70). He does curve and provide study guides though.

1/3 of the study guild wasn't on the midterm. 

midterm was written in a way to inflict maximum pain and frustration for students.
Pretty easy class for first years, great professor and very entertaining. One group project and a final paper.

Love Dr. Smit! He genuinely cares & wants his students to succeed. Canceled class a few times & went outside around campus. There are discussion posts for every reading (kinda long), but you can miss up to 12. Short artifact presentation, Midterm/Final, 2 papers. Honestly, I did badly on my midterm but he curved! Just DO the readings & youre good!

Best first-year seminar, Archeology and Pop Culture. Watch movies and read articles each week on which you write an easy 200-word discussion post; some are optional. There's a group project you will present and a final paper; with effort, you will likely receive an A. Participation is encouraged but not required. Extra credit possibilities.

Great prof., good at choosing really interesting readings and giving engaging lectures. Exams are pretty lax, but you do need to come to class to get all the info you're tested on. Very understanding and forgiving, but slightly unresponsive grader.

I highly recommend Dr. Smit he is an amazing professor. Class is easy, but there are pop quizzes. They are really easy if you do the readings. He is funny and appreciates when the class engages. He does take forever to grade things though.

Amazing professor. he had that cool professor vibe going for him, in a respectful manner. aside from that he was an awesome teacher and made the lectures very interesting. he was also a VERY fair grader and made learning what it should be. highly suggest.

This is not a difficult class but it can be very frustrating at times because of how slowly Dr. Smit grades. The papers aren't too bad and pretty quick to write. Some of the readings are more dense/boring than others but overall the course materials are fairly interesting and a lot of class is just discussion.

Professor Smit is my favorite professor at UNC. His lectures were always fun and engaging, and he often had some sort of activity to accompany them. He cares about attendance and has "Pop quizzes" on the readings from every class. They are straightforward and not difficult if you at least skim the reading. I highly recommend taking this class.

Prof Smit is amazing! Take this seminar if you can!! I learned something new and interesting every class. He's a great person and his lectures were always fun and engaging- he even brought his dog in once. No tests, just 5 pop quizzes that aren't worth much of the grade or too hard if you do the readings. Two group projects but they aren't hard.

great professor even if you do not care about anthropology! he cares about students and makes his class engaging. if you have him, participate in discussions. as long as you do the work and participate you will do well. I would 100% recommend, especially for first-year seminar; best class!!

This class was my favorite of the semester by far. I always looked forward to going to his class and he made it great by choosing important topics and describing them in an interesting ways. There's movies to watch every couple weeks but that's the majority of the homework so it's not that bad. The grading is fairly easy too. Overall great class!

As long as you show up to class, watch the posted movies, and contribute to the conversation a bit, you'll get an A. Professor Smit is a really easy grader, and most of the assignments in his freshman seminar are very straightforward. He's also a funny guy, so the lectures can be entertaining.

Great first year seminar. Material was interesting the workload was pretty light. If you show up a decent amount and do the work, you'll be just fine. Professor Smit is a really nice guy and an easy grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Respected

reviews.comment: Douglas is the man. Easily one of my favorite lecturers at UNC. Would take any class and make it easy to listen. Highly recommend taking this course.

Douggy Smit was fantastic. He wants you to succeed in this class. I currently have over a 100% in this class, I bet you didn't think that could happen at UNC, but alas. I am saying this before the final, so.... There are mini papers(750), case studies(500), and finals. If you like anthropology you will probs love it way more than me!

Dr. Smit's lectures are always entertaining, profound, and engaging. He assigns a very justified amount of reading for every lecture (20 pages max, normally around 10-15). Don't forget to do the (easy) journal post weekly. Super chill, rational, funny guy. Sign up if you're even remotely interested in archaeology, I promise you won't regret it.

I loved Economic Anthropology! There are daily readings/weekly journal entries. His lectures are super engaging and he clearly wants his students to succeed. 2 exams, both fair as long as you engage with the content and one final paper. Overall, a super interesting class with a great, funny, honest, and open professor. Highly recommend!!!

Sweet professor who cares about his students. Only a couple of homework assignments throughout the semester that you can do in groups. Exams are heavily weighted but he curves a ton. Manageable if you can do practice problems and in-lecture practice. Confused by low ratings, he is such a nice guy who wants everyone in his classes to do well!

He is a nice guy but has no backbone. He made the exams but didn't grade anything (all grading done by his poor TA), so it took forever to get stuff back. Cheating was rampant on the final exam. You can tell he wants his students to like him, but he is an inefficient lecturer and bad with technology. He does allow cheat sheets and curves heavily.

Professor Shin really cares about his students' education. 408 has difficult material, but he does a great job explaining concepts. If you pay attention during lectures, you will do well and have a strong understanding of corporate finance outside of just the exams.

The class is just hard but he's cool and loves FRED. I don't know what type of voodoo witchcraft insane formula he curved the final using, but I thought I would finish with maybe a C if I was lucky and I got a B+. I am not like that. He maybe just didn't want us to hate him. One day he will buy that house!

I loved Professor Shin. Busi 408 is a difficult class, but he made the information digestible and less intimidating. All homework is done in groups, and there are plenty of practice problems for the midterm and final. Overall such a nice guy who clearly cares deeply about his students and the course topics.

I loved Professor Shin. Busi 408 is a challenging class, especially for me with no prior finance knowledge, but he made information digestible and less intimidating. Homework is group-based and there's lots of practice for midterm and final. Such a nice guy who obviously cares so much about the subject and his students.

I LOVE Dongwha. I was scared for this class because I'm not a fan of finance, but he really wants you to do well. Lectures are a little hard to follow and he can sometimes go on tangents. However, the expectations are very clear and he gives you all the materials you need to succeed. I highly recommend.

Not hard to earn good grade but class is disorganized. Little practice for concepts that need more than 2 problems to understand. Professor is sweet but if you want to deeply learn the material consider other instructor. Class is focused on applying concepts instead of learning equations, but if you want to take more advanced courses you need both.

Very weird class. Prof is chill but disorganized and prone to digressing, esp when the fratty finance bros ask random questions to flex their niche finance knowledge. Very unclear class and you basically self-study the whole thing, because lectures are not super relevant to exams. Still, very accomodating prof and overall a neutral experience.

Prof. Shin is super chill, obviously super passionate about crypto. He can get off-topic sometimes and can go on tangents on complex concepts that lose a number of ppl in the class. Class was interesting though and I enjoyed the final research project.

Professor Shin is the best!! 408 is hard, but I would 1000% recommend taking it with him. The final is hard and weighted heavy, but he curves a lot. Few long homeworks done in groups, but it's not too hard to do well on them. Real world examples make the content relevant and I always looked forward to class. His energy makes lectures fun!

Professor Shim is such a sweet professor. Those who are giving him bad reviews didn't put in enough time for this class. He even prefaced that he will push you more than other sections, so you can gain practical skills, representing yourself and Kenan in the workplace. As someone not going into finance, I was excited every day to go to class.
Confusing and unnecessarily difficult class. 45% of grade is final and spends the lecture before the final teaching new material. Surprised his rating is 4.5.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Shin is a nice guy, BUT I wouldn't recommend! Although he assigns little homework, this means the class is EXTREMELY test-heavy. You also have to teach yourself everything because the lectures are so confusing. Also, from what I heard from other 408 students and tutors, he teaches different, more complex material than other classes.

He's a nice guy and in theory makes Corporate Finance interesting by bringing in current events. However, he puts practice problems on the board with the solutions on the same slide and many of his answer keys have basic arithmetic mistakes. Not the worst teacher by any means, but lacks basic diligence. Final average is 60 - would take someone else

408 is a hard class in general, but I recommend taking with Shin. He genuinely cares for students, is funny, and will help you out and provide additional resources if needed. Very test heavy but are graded or curved as needed. Not many HWs but they take a long time, but you can work with group. Most of work was studying before midterm and final
phenomenal prof, really vested in students. took him for two classes absolutely love the guy. if you have the opportunity to take a class with shin take him!!!!!
Excellent professor; goated

Prof Shin is the best 408 professor. He provides everyone with resources to succeed and is transparent about his expectations. He teaches challenging concepts in a way that everyone can understand. I highly recommend taking 408 with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is THE BEST for 408, hands down. The content is hard and there is nothing you can do to change that, but he really listens to students feedback and will slow down if you ask him. Literally only half of the class shows up, but going is so worth it because the lectures are easier to follow in person. I love him! Wish I could stay in this class tbh
Dongwha is the man and I really hope he can buy a house soon. 408 sucks tho and investment banking is for try-hards.

Professor Shin was one of the best professors I've had at unc. He explained often abstract topics beautifully and used plenty of examples to make sure that we all understood. Plenty of opportunities to ask questions. My favorite part of the course is his frequent inclusion of real world examples to show how what we are learning is actually useful.

Professor Shin was by far the best option for taking 408. He has 6 homeworks that are worked on in groups. Midterm is very easy. He said the final is really the only thing he cares about, so it is very hard but he curves. You wont get less than a B if you do basically anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved 408 with Professor Shin. He was very down-to-earth and incorporated current events into his teaching (Evergrande, cryptocurrency, etc.). Lectures were easy to follow. The final was particularly difficult, but it was curved.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely cool guy. Class is hard but not a lot of work. You'd have to be super lazy to get less than a B. Would recommend.

He said I knew my lecture is much harder than other professors', but you guys deserve harder courses. Spent a week preparing for the final and doesn't help at all. DON'T believe that he said two days for the final is enough! It is super difficult! Even though he curved, I still feel that there's no need to make simple things complicated.
Super cool professor and extremely nice guy. The final is super hard but he curves so definitely would recommend. Not much work at all

Professor Shin is an awesome professor- my favorite at UNC. He made a difficult concept like corporate finance fun to learn. The class is still challenging but he lets you use a cheat sheet on the midterm and final, which helps alot. If you work hard and show up, Professor Shin will take notice and help you out. He is also hilarious.

Professor Shin seriously cares about his students! He was so helpful during these crazy COVID times. He regularly checked in on us and modified the course to ensure that we could learn at a good, healthy pace. He is a great instructor and genuinely wants you to succeed! I could not recommend him enough.

Took Arab 407 with Prof. Doria and currently in Arab 408. The topics are interesting and the class is easy. She's very caring and lenient but gives a lot of work. The work amount is justified since the class is just a conversation. You must do the reading or watch the movie in order to participate. If you speak Arabic, give it a try.

Doria is very sweet and caring and is always willing to take additional time to explain the language and Arab history and culture; she also has easy tests. That being said, the class isn't too enjoyable because of the heaps of HW (1-2 hours/night) and unclear class calendar. Just make sure you show up and don't fall behind on HW or it'll be tough.

Doria means well, but it's hard to do well in her class. She constantly talks about how she's sad students are stressed, but grades on unclear guidelines & doesn't teach grammar. I did corrections AND extra credit, and she told me she wouldn't give me the points back because I already had a "good enough" grade. I wish someone else was teaching 204.

Professor Doria is the sweetest person. She gives a good amount of homework that is crucial to learning the material, so it is for good cause. She is very lenient with due dates if you speak with her about it and she is not at all a tough grader. If you want to learn Arabic and are excited about doing so, you should have no trouble in her class.

Ustaaza Doria really emphasizes language immersion and speaks only in Arabic for nearly the entire class period. She also has a lot of cultural knowledge and is eager to share it with students.
