The homework was excessive, usually amounting to 3-4 hours of homework a day, but she tried to be flexible with everyone and sometimes accepted late work.
Doria is very enthusiastic about Arabic which is wonderful to have in a teacher, however she gives heaping amounts of homework and does not always explain what is reviewed in the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Doria is very sweet, but homewrk load was awful, especially during a pandemic. There was some sort of a project due along w/ usual 2-3 wrth of homewrk every single weekend toward the end of this class, hw was worth more than tests and almost every hw was graded on accuracy. Too much work and disappointed that there was virtually no accomodation

Doria is tough, but also very caring. She wants you to do your best and puts in a lot of effort to give you helpful feedback. If you go in knowing its going to be a lot of work she will be your biggest cheerleader. I have had a friend who had a breakdown in her office and she made them tea. Make sure you stay up on hw and go to office hours!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed my time with Prof. El Kerdany. She is very patient with her students and gives a lot of feedback on hw assignments for you to improve on. Participation in class is rly important to understanding the language and the rules associated with it. She also introduces you to Arab culture around the middle east which is really interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Favorite class, and favorite professor - really cares for her students and wants you to do well. Makes language learning challenging, but I'm leaving this semester actually speaking/writing Arabic independently. If you want to learn the language, are happy to put some work in, and don't mind learning the Egyptian dialect, TAKE THIS CLASS.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is the kindest professor I have ever had. I struggled a lot in class, but she always took time to help me when I showed that I cared. She goes the extra mile to ensure students understand what is going on. The class is so much work, but I learned so much.

ARAB 101 is designed as a "weed-out" class for non-native speakers. If you have taken Arabic before or speak it at home, you will pass with flying colors. If you have never done anything with Arabic before, you will not pass. This class is HARD. This class is TIME-CONSUMING.

Professor El Kerdany is a very good Arabic teacher. She is deeply knowledgeable about Arabic, being a native speaker, and tries to help students, although she can be a bit confusing sometimes. I found her very nice, but I have heard she can be harsh if you're struggling in the class. Overall, ARAB 102 is a lot of work, but manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I was scared to take her at first but once I started going to office hours you get to know how sweet she is. Also, was willing to work with my schedule which I could not make most office hours. She makes you work for your grade. You will learn a lot about Arab culture from her and she will usually invite you to events on campus.

Professor Reid is very kind and encouraging. Although the class has a lot of reading (80-100 pages of reading due per class), I found the material fascinating. Classes are almost all discussion, so participation matters!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: If I have one piece of advice, take HIST398 with Dr. Reid. He's so awesome at giving feedback, always checking in on us as people, built good community in class, and easy to reach outside of class. He made the paper feel less daunting. 1000/10 recommend one of my favorite professors at UNC!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The lectures aren't very engaging and you really have to pay attention to what he is saying because not all the material is on the slides. That being said, there aren't too many assignments. As long as you read the assigned material and participate in recitation you will be fine. It does mainly depend on the TA that you get and how hard they grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Reid is very knowledgeable, and is passionate about teaching students. Which TA you get can heavily influence your grade. I got a hard one, but was fortunate enough because they liked me.

Lectures aren't too engaging, but some content (eg Israel/Palestine, the environment, Apartheid) is very relevant, & the readings/films are interesting. You need to love history to enjoy the class, though, and 3-page essay limits can make it tough to say everything I want to (one required us to use 4 sources!). Worthwhile class for some but not all

We have 4 papers to write. The recitation was required, but the lecture was not. It was easy to learn if you didn't go to the lecture. Participation in the recitation was also required to count as present. We had 3 books we had to read, and would strongly suggest actually reading because you will write a paper on it in the future.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved Professor Reid and his course!! The material was heavy but extremely engaging nonetheless. There were two 6 page papers and a 6-8 pages final, all which were graded and returned extremely quickly. Dr. Reid gave incredible feedback and was extremely encouraging! I highly reccomend going to his office hours/talking to him 1 on 1!

291H: To succeed in his class, talk to him, do your readings, and PROOFREAD EVERYTHING. No tests or exams, but he's very into class participation and writing compositions as an alternative. I really enjoyed this class, it felt like just the right amount of challenging without being totally overwhelming. Very flexible about accommodations.
Nice guy. Decent amount of reading and movies you have to look at for recitations. Overall, solid professor.

reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I liked Professor Reid but my TA was awful. The TAs grade everything and mine was way too tough and gave mostly Bs (only 3 As total) for participation in the lecture even if you attend all classes and participate every time. There were 4 essays and the prompts were unclear and incredibly long.

This was a relatively easy, interesting class. Be aware Reid is often challenging to hear and rambles some. Attending lectures isn't mandatory, but attending the weekly recitation section is. These are NOT study sessions but seminars you need to prep for. Four three-page papers, recitation attendance, and the final paper are the only grades.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: With one 2 1/2 hour class per week, you will be spending a lot of time reading novels for the class. In total we read 7 novels which sometimes necessitated us to read a full novel in one week. The assignments are not too bad, each week you'll submit a brief reflection on the assigned reading and there were 3 6-page essays (including the final.)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Unfortunately for me, attendance was not mandatory (so obviously I did not go). This led to me struggling immensely on the final because it was entirely based on lecture content. All papers/assignments are based on readings and films not covered in lecture so technically you could never go to class and do fine (until the final).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you are interested in history, you will love Dr. Reid! He assigns really interesting readings and films that deepen your understanding of world history. Theres only 4 papers but they allowed for a lot of creativity and intepretation. His lectures can be long and a little dull to those not into history.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Reid's lectures are boring, but the class isn't hard at all. Be prepared to read, write, and watch films often though. There is a recitation, but you just talk about what you read/watched. The final consists of writing an essay over a certain time period, but he doesn't tell you which time period you'll get before. TAs grade everything.

65% of his class are based on 4 essays. The essays are hard, boring, and they do not have a clear structure. The essays are graded by the TA's - they are graded very unfairly as they do not have a clear structure or requirements checklist and the grade only depends on the TA (better hope that u get a good one). Lot of reading and film watching.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Reid is absolutely amazing! He is extremely caring, compassionate, & kind. He really cares about his students and wants us to succeed. He was very understanding with some extenuating circumstances I was dealing with & showed me so much kindness throughout. Truly a gem. Hes also very accessible! Take this class you will learn so much!
Personally love Reid. Taken 2 classes with him because of how much I liked him. All paper-based but relatively easy and as long as you study the slightest bit, you'll pass. Would recommend! Love!

Really smart guy. He's understanding and accessible outside class. The lectures are a bit dry sometimes but the events he focuses on are interesting and he really gets you to think about history in new ways. I'm about 80% sure everyone complaining about how hard the class is didn't actually read the material, because it's not that bad if you do.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I was a little nervous going into my class based on the reviews on here, however, I absolutely adored Professor Reid. I really enjoyed his class and his discussion. I do not know if maybe it was just because it was a seminar class and he is different in other classes but he was not a harsh grader for us. Really recommend!

The workload at times was a lot with readings and lectures but the class overall was good. Professor Reid is willing to work with you if you simply ask. Our grades were based on papers and participation. We mostly interacted with TA, but he cares about his students and wants to get to know them. He also tweaked the final grading scale to help us.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor offers tons of lecture to watch and they can be long and boring. His voice can be tricky since it's too hoarse. Grades depends heavily on your TA (avoid tough grader!) Three papers per semester and each for 5 pages. A 9 pages essay for final. Books and films every week. Do not take this class if you only want GenEds. Heavy workload.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: In the online portion, lectures were asynchronous and often unrelated to recitations, which focused on readings and films. The 3 5-page papers and part of the final were all based on recitations, so make sure you prepare and participate for those. As far as I could tell, all grades (including the final) were done by the TA's.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You have to read a novel or watch a movie every week, and the recitation is on that work. The lectures are very boring and don't really tie into the novels or movies watched. You're graded on three 5 page papers and a final 2 part 9 page paper. This isn't the worst class I've taken, but I would probably choose a different class for the gen ed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--So many papers

reviews.comment: Took HIST140 as a Gen Ed and I think it was worth it. Lots of reading (read about 4 whole novels the whole semester) plus other assigned online readings. Lectures were pretty lengthy and not the most interesting. Total of three 5-page essays plus the final which was a 3 page essay and a 6 page essay.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I used rate my professor to decide if I was going to take this class and honestly the good reviews let me down, this class was my toughest and I seriously considered pass/fail. The TAs grade the essays harshly and the final was the most stressful thing I've done in awhile. I somehow did well, but the stress isn't worth the 3 gen eds I promise.

I really enjoyed Dr. Reid's first-year seminar. It was based around a TV show you had to watch, and where you'd a few episodes a week, write a weekly journal on it, and have occasional papers. If you come to class, participate enough, and show that you are actually interested then it's a pretty easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Reid was a good professor to work with but his grading does not make any sense. He does not give 100s and even if you do everything he asks you will probably not receive an A
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Reid's class is a bit of a hard one, there's a lot of reading and if you aren't the type to participate in lectures then be prepared to fail because he will try to get you to speak. The Professor is very knowledgeable about the topic, and has proven to be good at lectures although at times it is slow. Can be hard but it is manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Quizzes save your grade, he gives them about every other week with no warning and they are usually based on the book/film that was assigned that week. Everything else depends on the TA, Reid is obviously very smart but his lectures are dry as dirt.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Reid is very knowledgeable, however, when asked a question in lecture, he would usually never fully answer. Lectures were sometimes boring. There is sometimes a lot of reading and the pop quizzes are very in-depth. The three topics for the papers were very vague mostly because you had to write a paper about a single word.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Reid is very lecture heavy and the lectures can sometimes be boring, but this class is otherwise easy. The course does not require a textbook, but you are required to read 3 books over the semester and watch around 10 movies which will have pop quizzes. There are also 3 papers throughout the semester which are graded by TA's.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Beware of pop quizzes--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: hands down the WORST professor I have ever had. He cannot finish a single sentence! The only reason I took this was because of the three gen-eds but honestly not at all worth it. There's three papers with extremely vague topics and a final paper to be written in the final time. He has "pop" quizzes on the assigned texts and sometimes the readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Awful class. His lectures are incredibly boring. You have to watch movies every week to discuss in recitation. Would not recommend this class for gen ed.

Don Reid is not a good professor at all. He treats the class as if he is your only professor for the entire semester. You have to read and watch videos before sectionals on Thursdays and Fridays, but he will give a quiz on Wednesday. This becomes an issue for students like me who have a busy beginning to the week. Paper prompts are too vague.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took this class for a GenEd and I don't know how people can complain. His lectures are heavy but he posts the full powerpoints and does not take attendance. You have to read the books and go to recitation but there isn't any other homework. There are three papers and a final exam and your worst paper grade is worth a low percentage of your grade.

Professor Reid is an extremely nice guy, but the lectures were almost pointless. Attendance is not mandatory and attending lectures doesn't effect your grade much at all. TA's grade the 3 papers and reading quizzes, so be sure to attend recitations. Grade based on 3 papers, 5-6 quizzes on books and films, and the final exam.

Took for the gen eds and totally regret it. nice guy but horrible at lecturing - uses powerpoints with no clear points and raises questions about the subject of the lecture without answering them. quized on 5 or 6 obscure books and a few films. learned more studying for the final than all his lectures combined. graded on quizes, 3 papers, final
Nice guy but drones on in lectures, his mic doesn't work 75% of the time so beware of sitting in the back.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Reid is super passionate about his class and makes a lot of modern references, which is cool. The books he makes you read are actually kind of interesting - take the recitation with Donald Santacaterina!! But there is literally SO MUCH information because you learn about so many eras. Also the fact that our final exam is ONE ESSAY question.....
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: God bless him but well I learned nothing from the lectures. Didn't really need to come to class at all because Prof Reid posted the slides online. The papers were actually not that bad (usually based on movies) and a lot of people in my class didn't actually read the book. I skimmed it, so the class wasn't bad at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Reviews are accurate. Very tough grading; I only know of a couple As. Nice guy, I think he cares about his students, but teaching is not his gift. Prompts were very confusing. Lectures were unnecessary because they don't relate the assignments. Only really have to watch the films for grades because you can prepare for the final with good Googling.

I took this class because it fills 3 gen-eds, and I have regretted every minute of it. Professor Reid's lectures are incredibly boring, dense, and LONG. He makes minimalistic powerpoints for each lecture, and half of the time, I'm not sure how the lecture relates to anything we're reading about. Also, you watch a film every week. And write A LOT
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Horrible speaker. His lectures made little to no sense and he made the same hand motion for the entire lecture. He didn't teach chronologically and the "thematic" learning style didn't make sense. There is a reading every week and two extensive papers.

Don't take this class. Even though the content is interesting, many students often get more confused by going to the lectures than by researching the content themselves. You must read a novel every week and complete two 7 page papers. Guidelines and expectations for tests and papers are very vague yet they are graded very specifically.

Donald Reid is a very smart guy, but has trouble getting his points across. He will pose very dynamic questions at the beginning of class and seldom arrive on an answer. The T.A.'s are your best resource. They will explain anything that you are confused about because they understand how jumbled Prof. Reid's lectures really are.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr. Reid isn't very clear when he asks questions on exams and many times his lectures are both boring and confusing. He's very smart and sort of funny but he talks very fast and gets off track easily.
Draws the A line at 95, be very cautious about taking a class from him.

Reid is a nice guy in person but his class is pretty tough.  The paper assignments are difficult and expectations are a bit unclear.  The grading on papers is also tough but the tests aren't too bad and he gives the questions before hand.  You also have to read cause half the exams come from the textbook.  Also I had a bad TA so that made it worse.

Professor Reid is very enthusiastic and helpful in person. His lectures are convoluted, but he cracks jokes and they seem to go by pretty quickly. The recitations are *amazing*. Essays are tough but the tests are simple enough, and he gives a generous curve. I would recommend for anyone who wants a better understanding of current events.

Professor Reid is quirky person and is passionate about history. He may not be the best public speaker but he really tries to get students interested. He ended up being my favorite professor this semester. The content the class covers is eye opening and interesting. The class wasn't too hard but it also wasn't easy.

Super boring lectures, then the tests are hardly based on anything he talked about. Memorize a whole bunch of pointless facts (not from the book).  Tough paper assignment in the beginning. Harsh on grading - 5 assessments make up a total of 100 points, so every point missed is a point off your final grade.

EXTREMELY boring lecturer. Has the longest and most convoluted essay prompts I've ever seen. Hard class not because the material is difficult but because he is a bad lecturer and his tests are difficult.

I had Professor Reid for a upper level research and writing seminar and I wouldn't have wanted anyone else. He worked with me to explore a topic that was somewhat unusual, but he encouraged me to pursue it. He is very articulate and I found him very helpful and supportive whenever I asked him about something. Great professor!

His lectures weren't clearly organized and he isn't the best speaker on campus.  Overall, the class isn't that difficult and uses fairly interesting books and films to teach.  If you interested in history or are looking for a class to fill, this isn't a bad option
His lectures are nearly impossible to follow.
choose another professor if u want coherent lectures. If not youll get his stream of conscious which is filled with tangents that dont relate to the topic at hand. He is not a good speaker
A wonderful, helpful professor.
I like the guy a lot, but found his class to be mediocre. Teaches off of books and movies, but still lost my interest.
Awesome professor. There's a good amount of work, but the class is a real learning experience.

Worst lecturer i've ever had. His lectures are disjointed and it feels like you're in a different class every time you go. Weekly quizzes require attendance, often had to read a book  or see a 3 hour film every week. Too much work required for this class for the level it is and none of it is enjoyable. Grading was harsh, multiple long papers.

His fuzzy head (and chest mind you) can distract you from his digressions. He finds it impossible to focus on one topic and follow it through in a logical coherent manner. Instead he meanders through vague themes "stepping back" every other sentence to re-clarify an already simple topic. prepared to do a ton of reading and sleeping in this class.
The class is kinda hard, and a B is to be expected.

Professor Reid definately knows what he's talking about. His lectures are a little jumpy and you have to read and write alot, but you learn so much. The sections are great because of the engaged TA's.
No Comments

Brillant professor, finally a challenge after breezing through high school. Many of my friends in the class thought it was vague or difficult, but that's just because they failed the quizzes on the assigned readings. You have to read things a couple of times to actually absorb the information, not just once the morning of.
Would not recommend.

Lectures were boring and hard to follow.  The reading was interesting, and the TA section with a great TA made up for the short comings of the class.  The class was not hard, but that was mostly thanks to being a good writer and having a great TA.
rambling, ineffective lectures, LOTS of reading on a few specific questions on quizzes. 3 massive 10 page papers on obscure questions
To all future students, if you're planning to take STOR555, get out while you still can. Find another way to get credit for this class, because this is not the way you want to do it.
Nobel's lectures are clear and very concise. I compare to other lectures from the same classes of different schools, they are basically similar. He is very nice and approachable outside class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: It was the worst class I have ever taken. Long homework and harsh graded exams with no answer keys, no practice. BEYOND THAT, his lectures were awful, and he was too stubborn to listen to student feedback. He sees “poetry” and “story” in statistics problems and acts as if students are crazy for not seeing them.

cant find a 555 option, so im putting this under 565. its laughable how bad bro is at lecturing. tests are needlessly long. only thing that saved me from failing was decent hw grades. hard agree with the other person who said this dude says you tell me to every question.

I had him for STOR 555, not 565, but there is no 555 option (those two classes are completely different btw). I genuinely don't know how people ever succeed in that class. Any time someone asks a question, he will only, and I mean ONLY, respond with "you tell me." Like, dude, WE SHOULD BE TELLING YOU THAT. YOU'RE THE TEACHER, NOT US!

Nice person but he will make sure you suffer. Insane amounts of homework with intense deadlines (like 4 days). Lectures are very confusing. Exams aren't too bad but are graded harshly, and there will be no answer keys for anything. Good luck.

Strong knowledge of the material but not the greatest at teaching it to students. Only given difficult problem sets and computer assignments five days in advance. Two time-consuming projects that are worth a cumulative 8% of your grade and a midterm and final that are worth a cumulative 74%. Recommended for masochists and passionate statisticians.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Hardest class I've taken so far. If you just want to learn cool flashy machine learning stuff, this class is not for you. This class is about the mathematical foundations of ML (search "andrew nobel teaching" to get his website/notes). Nobel teaches and explains things very well. But you'll have to put effort into understanding the material.

Prof. Nobel's ML is the most valuable and the most difficult ug class I have at UNC. You ll learn how to think mathematically instead of do computational alchemy facing a ML algorithm. I have a solid background in ML after 565. Even hard, I would say that the Berkeley version of this course is much heavier. Nobel is approachable outside the classrm
Tons of homework, hard exams, and frivolous group projects. Would not take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Nobel designed the class to make it miserable for the students taking it -- a bunch of long homework problems, extremely hard exams, and silly group projects. DO NOT TAKE.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Nobel is passionate about the topic he teaches, but he often forgot how we actually care about the grades in this class. Extremely long exam, long computing and homework every week (and he expects us to finish both in 4 days), then he decides to give a final project that requires remote collaboration during COVID19. Just no

Professor Nobel is awful. He does not care about students at all. He enjoys making students embarrassed and in trouble in some sense. He is just a DEVIL. Never respectful. The worst professor I have ever seen in my life.

Professor Nobel is a very nice guy if you go to his office and chat, but his class is miserable. Very long, boring lectures where he reads right from his slides/notes and does not put much effort into making sure you get it. Very smart guy, but not very good at getting students to understand. Exams are tough because you have to teach yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: DO NOT RECOMMEND! He does not care about teaching and his lectures only leave me more confused. Very intelligent but does not know how to explain things. Homework are ridiculously time consuming and irrelevant to the tests.
Exams are extremely difficult and he doesn't know how to explain stuff. This class is a massive headache... I would not recommend him

Worst teacher at UNC. Doesn't listen to students, only worried about getting through his slideshow. Gives homework 10x harder than what is in class and then grades it tough and doesnt give feedback. Irresponsible adds homework to assignments throughout the week didn't give answers to practice tests because we should "know answers deep in our heart"

I took Nobels freshman seminar class, STOR 89. it was pretty easy especially because there are no exams! there was some homework, but overall the workload is very minimal. therefore even if you think it is difficult it doesnt really matter because you will never be tested on the material. Nobel is very quirky and loves what he does! nice guy.

He cares about his students and does not take any shortcuts in helping them succeed in the class. He adapted the pacing of the class based on student feedback and gave students sufficient opportunities to ask questions and connect in office hours. Pay attention to lectures and do the practice exams, and you will know everything you need.

Having had difficulty in math my entire college career, andrew was by far the most impactful professor I've had in this field. He cares a lot and provides plenty of outside help to allow his students to succeed. He's a lil goofy but a great explainer. DO THE HANDOUTS AND PRACTICE EXAMS FROM OFFICE HOURS!!!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: STOR 113.The class was fine. The content wasn't bad. The first midterm was kinda awful but the rest were fine. My main issue was how passive aggressive this dude is. Literally could not ask a question without getting a weird remark. Went to his office hours once and never again. He kinda chilled out after a while but yikes, did not wanna be there.

The first test was hard, but after we gave feedback he totally adapted his lectures for us. Even though this was a lecture based class he went above and beyond to make weekly lecture notes, problem sets, and practice exams. Overall, couldn't ask for a more dedicated and flexible teacher who wants students to succeed without handing it to them.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Stor 113. Class content itself is not terrible, but Andrew truly is not meant to be a teacher. Constanly getting annoyed and showing absolutely 0 will to teach. Gives practice material the day before exams and doesn't even announce it. Sometimes only gives practice papers to student who show up to office hours. Avoid if you can.

Pretty vague on what my grade was until it was finalized, but a chill dude who is clearly very passionate and respected in his field. Very niche topics but you don't have to memorize as much as other ARTH electives I've taken (only like 20-30 things per exam) and attendance didn't matter.

Prof Turner was a great, he was understanding and didn't mind absences (don't abuse this). He graded papers for completion and the 'term paper' on accuracy. His exams aren't bad but you must memorize a lot (took me 2-3 hr w/flashcards). I rec if you have a busy schedule bc he has no homework, but exams are weighed heavily but graded forgivingly.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures can be boring, but overall it is a chill class with interesting content and teacher. What started off as a filler class eventually became a fav. He doesn't grade harshly, and focuses more on conceptualization than gpa. He said before the final. “I'm not here to tank your gpa.” Not much work outside of the classroom, few assignments.

Prof Turner is very knowledgeable and passionate about his work and that shows in his lectures. The content is quite interesting, but the lectures themselves can drag on and feel boring at times. Final grade is determined by 3 assignments and 2 exams which kind of sucks, but he is a pretty forgiving grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: While some do say his voice is a little monotone, he's clearly passionate about the subject and really cares. He revamped the curriculum this semester a lot to make it more accessible and interesting to students, and his willingness to change and tinker stuff shows he's super caring of students. Exams are open note and online, albeit a little hard.

Prof. Boysen is clearly very knowledgable about the world of corporate strategy. I really enjoyed the assigned cases and the in-class exercises - they really helped me grasp the course concepts. Prof. Boysen was also always willing to meet with students (even outside of his scheduled office hours). He has been one of my favorite proffesors at KF!
Professor Boysen was one of the kindest professors ever. He makes the class super manageable and I would 100% take another class with him. Definitely take him for BUSI 412!

I think 412 is overall j a boring class in general. But prof boysen is very respectful and knowledgeable in this field of study. He is also SOOO kind and often would bring small treats and gifts to class (which honestly makes my day)! Overall, choose a good project group, and you'll be fine

Professor Boysen is a kind and caring person who repeatedly emphasizes we prioritize our mental health before all else. His attendance policy is relaxed, and he is encouraging of us to schedule office hours for extra help. Reading-heavy with lots of cases and a discussion-based class. I enjoy his sense of dry humor. He loves his daughter! )

Such a good guy and understanding but extremely boring. All the quizzes and exams are online. There's a group project that is relatively easy but a big portion of the grade so choose your group wisely.

Boysen is such a great guy and wants everyone to succeed. The lectures are extremely boring though which is a bummer because it makes it hard to pay attention and learn. Choose a good group for the group project, my group screwed me over :/
Not a good teacher and is in the wrong line of work. Not sure who gave him this job or how he passed an interview to teach at KF. Take 412 with someone else.

The content was difficult to understand, but Prof Boysen is accessible outside of class and wants you to succeed. The weekly quizzes are difficult, but if you go to office hours, he will help you out. If you put forth any effort in the class, you will do fine. He is also funny and breaks up lecture with group activities/Pollev's version of Kahoot.
insanely boring but not hard to get an A if you try

He's definitely passionate and very knowledgeable about corporate strategy but its extremely difficult to understand his course material. His teaching style incorporates a lot of in-class group discussion, but often times the other people in the class were just as lost so it made it harder to learn this way.

Prof. Boysen is very knowledgeable about corporate strategy. However, he has trouble explaining these concepts to undergraduate students, and it boils down to students using his buzzwords without knowing what they actually mean. I believe he is better suited for research as other ratings say, but maybe he will improve in future semesters.

Dr. Boysen is extremely knowledgeable and knows a ton about corporate strategy and management. Classes are reading and case-based and the format is straightforward. Lectures can be long, but breakout groups split up lecture time and he is very supportive. He is really accessible outside of class for office hours and overall is an awesome professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Boysen does a great job of making himself available outside of class. You can tell how much he cares about his students and spends a lot of time going over feedback to make his lectures better. He is a little bit shy at first, but is definitely one of my favorite UNC professors!

Professor Boysen really cares about his students and makes a deliberate effort to be available for office hours and take students' feedback to make his class better. He definitely is monotone/the material is somewhat boring, but he really does his best to make the class as engaging as possible (PollEv activities, group breakouts).

Horrible class. Its almost like he didnt even try to design it from the perspective of a student. Make him do research instead of teaching undergrads. Im sure hes probably brilliant at that, but he is very out of touch with the average college student. If everyone fails your exam, you are a bad teacheryour students are not bad

DUDE CANNOT TEACH FOR HIS LIFE, avoid at literally all costs. Take this class with Wilson and save yourself the agony. 5 minutes into your first class with him and you'll see what I'm talking about. he teaches in the same voice you'd expect to hear a lullaby, maybe softer. Showing any sort of enthusiasm might make this guy explode. U've been warned

The most boring and unhelpful professor at KF. Let's start with the fact that this guy never posts his deadlines for stuff until like a week before. The quizzes are actually challenging, especially once he found out the answers were online. WORST PART, THIS DUDE CANNOT TEACH. He thinks he's talking to PHDs and doesn't know how to teach undergrads.

Took him during Covid Pandemic. Quizzes after every class that are not too bad. One group project where you can choose groups and isn't too difficult at all. Final exam worth most of the grade. Class material is dry, but Boysen is super nice and accommodating. If class is hard he will give you a break or let you turn in stuff late, just talk to him
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. D is awesome! The class is easy if you do the readings and go to lecture. The essays/writing assignments are chill and have clear instructions. The TA's were very nice!

Very funny, respectful, and intelligent. His lectures were really interesting, engaging (many people participated), and he used a lot of cool media as examples (music videos, artifacts, literally like Little Women and SpongeBob too). Gives good feedback and grades well if you try. Class became kinda optional towards the end. Fav prof at unc so far

Dr. Dooling has been one of the best professors that I have had. The class has reading checks every week which were pretty easy and 3 papers. There were no tests and if you ask for feedback before assignments are due he will give you it.

Dr. Dooling is a wonderful professor that is truly passionate about his work and studies. His lectures are entertaining and fun. He is a tough grader, especially with the bigger papers, but not unreasonable and he is willing to talk about it. I would take his class again any day!

If you can take any insightful and phenomenal class at UNC, take Comm 224 with Dr. Dooling. He is amazing, hilarious, caring, etc! The class is genuinely enjoyable and incredibly thought-provoking. Dr. Dooling is a fair grader but expects passion and effort. Take this class or any of his classes!

Loved taking 325 with him! He is very down-to-earth and always makes the content fun/engaging. Lot's of group collaboration, so prepare to talk. Class is so much better when you do the readings, btw. They aren't just busy work. Exams are open-note/textbook, but not too easy. Very relevant content!

Dr. Dooling is my favorite professor I have had at UNC. His lectures are super engaging, he uses pop culture examples to help students understand concepts, and he truly cares about his students. He is also very helpful in office hours. I would recommend him and this course to anyone!

I love Dr. Dooling! He is super engaging and is very passionate about the course content. I would reccomend this class to anyone! Graded by a few essays and some reading responses; a great choice for those who do not love the typical exam format in most classes.

Dr. Dooling has been a great professor and has a clear passion for his area of work. The readings are relevant to the class, and his lecture style is engaging. Minimal busy work, reasonable grading, relevant insights- all of that. 10/10!

Difficult to get an A but not hard to get above a B. Lectures were not helpful in doing the homeworks, which ended up being 80% of the coursework (there is a homework question on both exams). Overall, just not a great course to learn in and had to teach myself how to work out most of the homeworks/exams. Very passable class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very lecture-heavy with no posted slides or notes, so attendance is important. Grading is based only on homework and exams. six homework assignments and two exams. The exams closely reflected the study guide, and one homework-style problem appeared on the exam. Grading is done in blocks, so small point differences can affect final letter grades.

Yates is a funny and straightforward guy, and lectures were enjoyable. Tests were similar to hw and practice ?s, and although grading scale made it very difficult to get an A, the tests were graded leniently enough for a B as long as you practiced. If you would like to learn, make sure to attend and pay attention in lecture.

Professor Yates is fantastic! Super funny and down to earth guy. Econ 410 is a hard class, and you WILL need to study for at least 20 hours before exams, but Yates has great lectures that really clarify the material. Although attendance isn't mandatory, if you want an A, you need to go to class. Overall, great class with a great prof.

Yates is passionate, but the class felt unfair at some points and did not feel like he wanted us to do well. His grading scale is super difficult because there's no room for mistakes. You need to do significantly well on both exams and perfect on homework if you want an A but a B is doable if you utilize econ aid.

Very caring and funny guy, but wow this class is hard. Not a lot of materials besides lectures, textbook is not really used outside of recitations. If you prefer a more structured class, take MSA. Hard to get A-/A, but also hard to fail with how tests are graded. Definitely use the ULAs/econaid, but expect to teach yourself a lot outside of class.

Loved his class. He knows what he's talking about and was very interesting lecturer. Made you pay attention which is great. Puts up with lots of ridiculous questions well. Only thing is I think the grading scheme based on basically 2 tests of 5 questions each is a little weird and I feel like I knew the content way better than my grade reflected.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Yates is a very different type of professor but it worked for me. I can see why people don't like it, but I enjoyed this class. His handwriting is hard to read for taking notes. Office hours with the ULA's will save your grade. Do the practice problems before exams and they won't be so bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Difficult to get above a B in my opinion. Only grades homework and exams. Drops one homework grade. One midterm exam on topics from the first half of the class. Final is content from the second. Used only one homework problem on the exams this semester. 5 questions on each exam with practice problems given about 2 weeks prior. Extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The test structure is fair, but exams are weighted too heavily. The class relies on upper-level math I never learned, so most problems felt overly math-heavy. I barely learned microeconomics, and the final tested random topics we hardly covered, so it didn't feel fair or representative.

Nice guy. Lectures consists of him completing practice problems on his iPad and attempting to explain along the way. May work for some but was extremely hard to follow or stay engaged for me. Not to mention his handwriting is hieroglyphic bordering on indecipherable. HW relates to class but you're on your own for most of your studying and learning
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Agree with a lot of the previous reviews, Professor doesn't teach he just writes solutions with little to explanation. Very hard to follow if you are not confident in the skill before class. Easy to pass if you are willing to spend 20 hours outside of class to teach yourself. Exams are homework with numbers switched.

He's a great guy but absolutely hate his grading scale which is non-negotiable. You need a 97 to get an A and a low 90 is considered a B+. He gives review problems for the midterm/final and 3 out of the 5 test questions will be from those but with different numbers. If you grind those and know all the hw questions too, you'll prob end with a B.

Weird grading system but not hard to get good grades. 7 HW (lowest grade dropped), he randomly chooses one question to grade from each homework. 1 midterm and one cumulative final, both five questions (one past homework question, three questions similar to HW but with different numbers, and one new question). Attendance not taken at my recitation
He is not that bad as the reviews claim him to be
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Be prepared to study hard for this class. It took me around 20 hours in total to study for the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While Yates was chill, energy economics wasn't a fulfilling class. He wrote a bunch of concepts & equations on the iPad, & we had no hw to reinforce what he was teaching us. He's funny & answers questions well, but it could be a bit more structured. I will say I did learn new things conceptually, but again, can't back it up with the econ side.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: easiest class i've taken at UNC. Concepts can be a little hard if you're actually trying to learn, but he does a good job teaching it (other than his handwriting). You're given a bank of questions for all the exams, so you just have to memorize it.

Gives you a 20-question bank w/ answers for the test, and expects you to get 116/120 between midterm and final for an A. This makes the tests a complete joke (tip: don't just memorize the answers), but also forces you to study for the specific questions instead of reviewing actual class content, leaving you poorly prepared for future ECON courses.
great professor. He is a bit more casual than other professors which is refreshing and has good sense of humor.

I really liked 410 with Yates. It was hard but I loved his applications to real life. His handwriting is horrible so you need to focus during lecture to know what he's writing. He does make it possible to succeed in this class and even become passionate about it. My TA, August, was incredible and reinforced a lot of what Yates taught in class.

Obviously a smart guy, but an absolutely horrible professor. Operates under the assumption that we can mentally do complicated algebra in seconds, which he may be able to do but I was not. This made his lectures useless. That being said, office hours saved my grade. They will help on the homework. The exams were wack but doable.

ECON 410 is going to be challenging, no matter who you take it with, but Prof. Yates made it manageable. The only complaint I have is that his handwriting is illegible, so you have to take notes based on what you hear. HWs are tough so I had to hire a TA. For the final exam, I studied roughly 15 hours a day for three days to feel prepared. 4/5
Don't even want to talk about it. GTHY
love the new grading i dont know a single thing and i got a hundred on every single assignment

Truly a fun professor. ECON-410 is notoriously a hard class so he's probably one of the best to take it with anyways. His lectures are really funny and aren't too bad to understand if you have any quantitative background because then it's just definitions and learning how to solve problems. He also goes over homeworks and a lot of examples in class
GOAT!!!!!!

A year later and he continues to be the laziest man in the department. This class is easy if you cheat since he doesn't care, his handwriting is terrible so be ready to record every lecture back and review things by yourself. PICKING THE RIGHT TA IS CRUCIAL. He's better at teaching than MSA and less confusing doesn't over work students.

Prof. Yates is a good man but his quality of teaching is not. He moves quickly and his notes follow no sort of rigid structure which makes transcribing them onto your own paper extremely difficult. Handwriting is atrocious. By the time you figure out that he was writing a 'q' for quantity instead of the number '9' he has moved on to the next topic.

Andy's teaching style is woeful. Lectures are him saying a problem verbally, then solving it with no explanation on concepts while skipping math steps. His handwriting is the worst I've ever seen, and you have to decipher his notes. The class is graded easier now than before, but seriously, you're going to have to teach yourself everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I hope he sees this. I am a transfer student and was excited to take his class, he does everything but help you. He goes so fast you can't keep up, no pre-class videos, doesn't tell you what chapter you're on. He is delusional and in his own world. Very nice man but not fit to help students as he makes no effort to explain, elaborate etc.

Amazing Professor. Very caring and patient. Answer all questions that students have in review sessions. Do the practice questions before the exam, and you will pass easily. The only problem is his writing in lecture notes(a little bit unclear), so go to classes and listen carefully. Overall, great Econ professor. I will definitely take it again.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Andy was a cool dude, really enjoyed his personality. His lectures could be a bit fast and disorganized. He does a lot of examples but doesn't always fully explain the concept before he does so, so it can be confusing. Lowest midterm and lowest homework dropped. Overall though it is what you would expect from a 400 level econ class.

The lectures were disorganized as Yates would go pretty fast and go through examples before explaining the concepts fully. All of the homework and midterms were very math and calculus based, all FRQ. The lowest midterm is dropped. Yates is a caring professor and will listen to feedback from students. Responds to emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Andy is a bit disorganized prof, but very knowledgeable and ultimately got info across pretty well. Not an easy class, but about what you'd expect from 400s econ class. Grading criteria is super clear, you'll know what you need to get a grade. Very exams/final heavy, but a good grade is doable. 8(?) hws, 3 midterms (one of each dropped) and final.
If you fall behind in lectures even a little bit it can be hard to catch up. Overall, he's a very nice guy and you can get a decent grade even if you don't do that well on exams.

He lectures for the full class and it can be very information heavy so be prepared to attend class especially since his notes can have some bad handwriting. This is a hard class to get an A/A- in but his grading system will help you pass with a pretty good grade.

I really enjoyed Professor Yates and his class. He is funny and helps students see how to apply the concepts learned in class to real-world problems through realistic test and practice problems. However, it's pretty easy to sometimes get lost in all the calculus notation. I came from doing calc and econ AP in high school and did well in this class.

Yates lectures from the start to the end of every class period, and you need to be writing notes. 70% of the grade is midterms+final but the lowest midterm is dropped. You need to study hard to do well in this class. Teaches different stuff from other 410 Professors. Doesn't give a lot of review material but is a nice and funny guy.

I loved Professor Yates as a person but his teaching style is definitely difficult. I enjoyed his lectures although he goes too fast at times and needs someone to ask him to slow down. The tests are quite difficult it came to the point that I felt like studying was a waste of time since it was dependent on just what he asked on the test.

His brand of Econ is a 180 from the way MSA teaches. She is math-heavy, here, the math is simple, but he uses a lot more variables so the algebra can get very chaotic. Tests are 3 questions only and a large part of the grade, so do well on them. Hard to hear him through the mask that he is still wearing so be locked in during lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Funny guy and def knows what he's talking about, took a decision making class with totally new concepts and think I can apply them in the real world no problem. Beware handwriting--you have to go to class bc you will NOT understand his notes. Also beware math, not always explained super clearly even when simple. Amazing professor, will take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Yates is a great guy. He tries to make the class fun and more entertaining. Graded on 6 homework assignments (drops the lowest one), two midterms (total is three but lowest is dropped), and the final. Almost no extra practice problems, but if you can do the homework well then you will be fine on the exams. Worked kinda hard and got a B+.

People will hate on Yates for his terrible handwriting and difficult testing style. However, once you understand how he tests his material, you can start to approach the exams in the right way and ace them. The handwriting argument is so weak, just go to class and write down what he says. Super caring guy, very willing to help students in need.

The class is impossible to follow along with. Barely any practice problems are utilized so studying for exams and completing homework is incredibly difficult. The exams are obscure and the only way kids do somewhat well is because the exams are graded incredibly lightly. Yates is a good guy but the class is just rough.

He talks so fast and never stops and will get mad if you ask him to slow down or tell him you can't read his handwriting (it is atrocious and worse than a five-year-old's). The exams are not based on anything you do in class. He refuses to record his lectures so you have to rely on the poorly written notes (Mandarin would be easier to understand).

He is the kind of professor you don't know how to rate. Very funny sometimes, and a good lecturer, but gives out tough homework. Really need to figure out lots on one's own. If you study hard and go to him with questions, even re-grade requests, he is very nice about that and you'd do well. TBH after all those ECON classes, he is my favorite.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Yates is a very nice and funny guy and definitely tries to make sure everyone understands the material. However, there are no outside of the classroom resources besides the homeworks. Overall if you do good on the homeworks and decent on the tests youll pass this class.

Lectures are very fast-paced and conceptual. Exams are v difficult-he wants you to apply the concepts. Take great notes-write everything he says and go over it after class. 10/10 rec doing the practice problems in the textbook for every chapter. He's a generous grader. Very funny and to the point. Ask questions in class if you don't understand.

I went in expecting a reasonably easy class, but NO. Must copy all his blackboard notes, because anything he talked about is fair game in exams, even those that were barely explained. Math part is way easier than MSA, but highly theoretical, almost doing calculations with no numbers. Get ready to spend hours pondering the material on your own.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Many people think he is hard but you should just read the text book and you will be ok. Try hard and will get a good grade. Will get a better grade than MSA but will have to teach yourself to really understand

If you want a clear pic, read all reviews from December 5th, they sum up everything as best as possible. Grading scale was terrible, literally no curve at all, which is extremely frustrating given how challenging Econ 410 is.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Yates' class. Bummed to see all of the negative reviews. I think 410 is difficult regardless of who you take it with. Prof. Yates treats students fairly and teaches the class with real examples (not apples and oranges). Still the best option for 410. It is hard to get an A but equally hard to get a C.

If this tells you anything, my entire notes summed up and the few examples we had were on the cheat sheet we get for the exam and it didn't even help. Nothing I studied for or what he taught on exam. Weird grading scale didn't help. Chalkboard notes, no ppts or other resources. No one in econ aid center can understand his problems take with MSA

Nice but DO NOT recommend. Test heavy and are not at all representative of any examples we did in class (which were highly limited). Very conceptual and variable heavy, vague, very little hw but that was why we didnt have any practice materials. Reviews before exams not helpful for what was actually on exam. The amount of effort I put in for a B-..
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor's final wasn't true to what he had told us in class, as truthfully, I studied all of the material. He never provided us with example exam problems or extra practice problems. Poor communication between professor and TA. Also, change the format of exams during semester. If you miss class he will not send you the notes.

Yates is a nice guy and seems very interested in the material, but he is not a good teacher. He does very vague (if any) examples in class that don't match up to the homework problems or exams. The exams are mostly hypothetical with no numbers and no one at the econ aid center knows how to do his problems so you can't get help.

Where to start... semi-nice guy and seems to genuinely care about students, exclusively uses chalkboard (no extra resources), was a bit of a jerk when a loved one almost died, has a weird grading scale that was implied to benefit students but A- started at 92%, he is not detailed in making sure concepts come across clearly, and hard to follow.

Attendance isn't mandatory but if you don't go to lecture you will not pass, recitation is not helpful either. Your only resource for learning is the textbook and his chalkboard lectures which aren't the easiest to follow. His grading scale is unique and based on grade distribution from the whole class which can be both helpful and harmful.

Yates is a really good 410 teacher! He doesn't assign much work outside of class and his tests are graded very leniently. His lectures are super accessible and as long as you ask questions when you're confused, you should be ok!

By the book professor who lectures only by writing on the chalkboard so if you are not taking good notes you're in trouble. Drops one exam and homework grade,. Very hard class in general and he does not go in depth but expects you to further apply concepts on exams. Very funny guy and always willing to answer questions.

I wasn't impressed with Yates given the reviews. His lectures are decent, but he does not post notes online and does not give practice resources. Preparing for exams seemed pretty useless considering 2/3 of it was stuff we discussed in class for 10 minutes. Reviews overrate him. Attend lectures and you'll be okay. Weird grading scale.

Man are his lectures disorganized. Class is super hard to follow, and if you don't ask questions to make sure you're staying engaged you're dead in the water. He doesn't do a ton of examples either. Expect concepts explained in class for 10 minutes to consist of 30% of your exam. I will say he is a super nice guy though. Exams 50% Final 30% HW 20%.

Yates is awesome! He's super sweet and knowledgable. The class is graded by a lot of things so there's a lot of opportunities to get feedback and check your understanding. I learned a lot from this class!

Dr. Yates is honestly the best choice for 410. He is the most standard, by-the-book professor I have ever had at UNC. He literally just writes on the chalk board and talks, no slides or anything. If you pay attention in class, it is easy to get an A. He is also really knowledgable and a kind person! I really enjoyed this class after 101 with Staub.
Professor Yates is very nice. Take Yates for a good grade, but youll learn way more with MSA. He kinda prioritizes environmental econ more than book content. I enjoyed his class though.

Yay Prof Yates! If you need to take 410 next semester, take him over MSA 100%. You won't learn as much but you'll do better in the class by a long shot. He grades VERY leniently and is a kind soul. Even though attendance isn't mandatory, go to class because his recordings are impossible to see or hear.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Andy was a joy to be taught ECON 410 by. While disorganized and confusing at times in his lecture, he really cares about this students. Make sure to show up to class because he has no PowerPoint slides and records on his MacBook while he writes in the faintest chalk known to man. He is also an extremely easy grader.

Professor Yates is the best Econ professor I've had to date. He genuinely wants you to succeed. He grades kindly. I don't have to reference the book at all. His lectures are really thorough and he's funny. I was intimidated at first, but I will take any class i can with him!

Professor Yates is the best professor I've had. After having a horrible experience in 101, he changed my opinion on ECON. You have to go to class and actually listen to lectures to succeed, but if you do, his tests are designed for you to do well if you pay attention. I don't read the textbook and I've gotten As on both exams. Absolutely adore him.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: This was a fascinating class, and Dr. Yates managed to make the most of the remote situation. His lecture style is extremely engaging and his sense of humor isn't lacking. Otherwise, he is a super lenient grade and is willing extend deadlines for reasonable excuses. Super enjoyable class with chill and knowledgeable professor.

Professor Yates gives engaging lectures and really tries to make it fun along the way. I hate ECON, yet I'm planning on taking another course with him next semester because he made the material genuinely understandable. Couldn't recommend him more!

Professor Yates is awesome. He is super passionate and knowledgable about the subject. He is approachable and enjoys teaching. The content itself can be confusing at times but if you ask questions, he is helpful and will make sure you understand. There wasn't a lot of work except the research paper at the end but you get to write about anything
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Yates truly invested a lot of time, effort, and money in ensuring his students received the best possible online instruction during the pandemic. Although this class was not very work- or test-heavy, attending lectures is very important, and do not procrastinate on the term paper!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Duan is very accessible but was not the most understanding. Assigns a LOT of work, one of my heaviest workloads I have ever had at UNC, and a lot of it is not productive work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Duan is amazing, I had no poetry experience before and she had such a welcoming class for all levels. You do have to go to class and attend all workshops, there is no test/exam and the final was reading our completed poems and she brought drinks and food. I recommend this class to everyone I know!

Incredible! absolutely amazing professor who cares about every individual student. I feel like my writing improved so much over the course of the semester. This class was never a source of stress, but you can get so much out of it because of the poetry workshops, and Carlina's constructive comments on every poem you write.
Professor Duan is an angel on earth, truly. She is incredible, caring, and kind, and fosters the safest space. Her knowledge is vast and her acceptance is unwavering.

Professor Duarte was an extremely caring and passionate professor. I found him funny and tried to make a boring class more interesting through real world examples. With that said, the class is very difficult. I could not follow along in lectures easily and it took me time outside of class to grasp the topics. Tests are very hard, but have big curve

Duarte is great. 445 is a math-heavy continuation of Micro with a lot of game theory involved. He keeps lectures interesting with real-life legal examples. Exams are hard but the curve is very generous. If you're decent at math, you'll be fine for an A-.

Class is insanely hard. That being said Marco works with you to ensure you don't fail. He has numerous extra credit opportunities, hw is graded for completion, and exams are curved extensively (30=C, 40=B, etc.). While this class is not by any means a guarranteed A I found it easy to obtain a B with pretty average effort. Just go to class.

Arbitrary grader. The topics are interesting, but he speedruns through them, and lectures have little to do with his horribly difficult math-heavy exams. Gets easily frustrated and mad when the class doesn't understand his teaching methods. I threw up one question into midterm 2, and he wouldn't let me retake it. Don't take this course, trust me!!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class will have super challenging midterms where you just speedrun solve everything you know, but the curve will SAVE YOU from getting below a B unless you skip class/put in 0 effort. Legit got a 14 on a midterm curved to C- LOL. Content is super interesting, pricing strategy/game theory, you actually learn something meaningful in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would avoid this at all costs unless you have to have it for credit. As far as a general 400 level econ elective this is a horrible choice. Class is ridiculously difficult, averages on exams are in the 40s. 80% of the class is graded on exams. There is curve on exams where a 30 is a C and 60 is an A. Overall just a miserable experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not take this class unless you need the credit. Exams are nearly impossible to finish, and lecture notes lack depth or relevance to the math-heavy tests. Lectures are dull and hard to follow. The professor is brilliant but assumes everyone can keep up, making this one of the toughest and least rewarding econ classes offered.

Material is challenging enough that going to lectures is important even if not required. Problem sets graded on completion, which offsets extremely difficult tests with averages below 50%. All exams are curved extensively. Marco knows his stuff and applies class topics to real world issues. A must-have class for those interested in consulting

His lectures are fun, tho sometimes a bit hard to follow. However, his lecture notes explain everything. He is very accessible for help, and responds to emails quickly. If you keep up with class, you should get an A- at least. I unfortunately missed the deadline of a problem set and fell behind in class after being sick for 3 weeks.

Overall Marco is a great guy and can be very personable. His information that he teaches you in class isn't too hard and pretty interesting but the test were quite intuitive and takes further knowledge from outside of what he teaches you. Everyone would fail the test but would curve a lot to match older section grading scales, a 30 would be a C.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Marco is a nice guy, but this class is just not worth it. The material presented should not have been that difficult to learn, but there was an utter lack of resources, and each homework and test question had layers of intuition stacked on it. Midterm averages were right around 50%. With 20's curving to C's. Homeworks are graded for completion.

Prof. Duvall was amazing! My favorite teacher during my first semester, definitely take ENG105 with her. Class was 3 projects, each with drafting assignments that prepare you fully for the final submission. She gave incredible feedback as well! Did not stress at all with this class.

super chill and easy class. Basically everything is completion if u put in a bit of effort. Attendance is not rly required either, she's pretty lenient with missing class as long as u email her beforehand, and it won't even affect ur grade. TAKE THIS PROF FOR ENGLISH
Easy course, but I don't feel like I actually learned anything.
If you can take a class with her next term you MUST.

Genuinely such an amazing professor and person. Class was not hard at all, and she made it clear she didn't want this class to be a stressor. Class consisted of some small assignments and 3 projects. Plenty of time was given, and she was very understanding on attendance (probably missed 5/6 classes from sickness). Great professor!

Emma made a class I thought I would hate one of my most enjoyable. She genuinely cares about all of the people in her classes. There are no exams, just 2-3 feeder assignments and a culminating project in each of the 3 units. She gives clear rubrics and feedback to help each student thrive in the course. If she teaches another section, take it.
Easy A for 105. Amazing professor who really cares and is invested in you. No tests just three projects for three units. No final as well. 10/10

Emma is an amazing professor! She is extremely caring and kind, and absolutely wants the best for her students. The assignments are very straightforward, and she is an understanding grader. I loved this class. If you are able take ENGL 105 with Emma, do it!

Emma was my TA for CMPL 120. Recitations were fun and really helpful for understanding the course, Emma was super knowledgeable on the course material. Emma was kind and caring, always super accommodating and willing to answer questions. Can't recommend her enough, she's awesome!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Lots and lots of readings in the semester, very fast paced. 3 essays that are all 1500+ words, plus a (really hard and strictly graded) midterm, with a final at the end. Tons of work for a class that's only a 100 level class, wouldn't take this at all if you're not a CMPL major or whatever.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Emma is an absolute sweetie. Most of her classes are discussion based, so it is easy to participate if you can get 1 comment in each class. There are 4 papers and she will review them before you turn them in as many times as you want. You can tell she wants you to succeed always. There isn't much prep that goes in and even if you don't it's fine.

Emma gave me a completely new understanding of poetry in the best way. Lectures were interesting and engaging, and she really made an effort to get to know each student. She is one of the most genuinely caring professors I've had so far. She was also very flexible with deadlines. The class workload was very manageable.
Emma is fantastic. Really interesting lectures and readings. Super accommodating and flexible when it comes to assignment due dates.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures and homework were directly geared towards assignments. She's very nice, meeting with her will help if you need it for papers. Not a lot of work though, just a few projects. Just do your work and you'll do well, it's an easy class.

Emma was a great TA for CMPL 120. She is genuinely one of the most caring instructors I have met at UNC. She is very accessible outside of class to answer questions about essays. Her recitations were a great addition to the main lecture, having us perform close readings of passages or art pieces.
Definitely should choose her as your 105 teacher if it's possible!

Quick chase for those of you who just want it: 100% awesome professor. Finished with a 99%. Super respected. Very nice. Kind.
I found this class to be one of the greatest introductory classes, especially online, though the units move quickly, the class goes by fast, despite being 90 minutes, 5 days a week. 
Grades "easy" but you have to try!

Take her for your 105!! I would've never expected to enjoy ENGL. I didn't even mind going at 8am. She is so kind and uplifting and gives you an A for just attempting to improve from your draft. The units are all different so it's not just paper writing. 1-2 assignments per week, most of which took me 10 minutes.

She is very kind and accomadating for circumstances! ENGL 105 coursework relatively easy and she gives great feedback for your rough drafts so that you can do well on final projects. No midterm or final. Very sweet and respected by all of the classmates. Love her!

Take eng105 with her if u can (even if its early its worth it)!! She is so nice and understanding. Very reachable outside of class. Give u extension if u ask. Easy grader as well. Some say lecture is boring but thats not on her all eng105 lecture r boring its an intro class what do u expect. She will make ur life easier trust me.

This was the easiest A I will get in college. Really, don't bother buying the book because you won't use it and probably already know the material. Emma is a sweet teacher and approachable but a boring lecturer and the class is such common sense but she taught it so in-depth. Just do the work and you get credit. I attended over zoom to save myself.
Emma is a wonderful teacher that is so flexible with everything in her class. Her class was very fun and nothing was particularly hard. She was one of the best teachers I had freshman year at UNC.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: If you're taking ENGL 105 I definitely recommend Emma. She was the kindest and most understanding professor I had this spring. She was very flexible on assignments and gave very useful templates for each. Her class was structured very well and I can tell that she genuinely cares about her students. It is not difficult at all to get a good grade.

YOU WANT HER FOR ENGL 105. Her class is the easiest I've ever taken bc she always pushes back deadlines and wants to help you. I still learned the material but was never stressed. She's sooo sweet and gives clear feedback and is a very lenient grader. And if you're shy she lets you do the one presentation for her individually.

Emma Duvall is truly a nice person. She is considerate and the perfect supporter in an otherwise very stressful college environment. I had her for English 105. The workload is extremely manageable, and she often gives time in class to work on assignments. She is an easy grader, but still gives great and helpful feedback for the assignments.

Lectures are in-depth and engaging. Homework is a huge portion of your grade, so do not procrastinate doing it. Paying attention in lecture is important because the posted slides do not have the same level of depth or insight that you will need to do well on the final. Group project is quite a bit of work too, just make sure to start on time.
Class wasn't too difficult, but it was hard to understand what we actually needed to know and what was just extra, which a lot of people ended up struggling with when came the final.

His rmp rating scared me before taking the class but as someone who doesn't go to UNC I thought he was a really good prof and gave all the resources to succeed compared to the profs I've had for my other pre-med classes. Just grind the practice exams and make sure you understand how to do the homework questions + studios and you're golden.

Dr. Drut was a fantastic professor. I've heard some people didn't enjoy his teaching style for PHYS 115, but for Numerical II I couldn't disagree more. He is genuinely the best physics professor I've had here at UNC by a wide margin. He's a clear lecturer and realistic about what we will and won't need in our careers, and encourages questions.

Terrible lecturer. Everything he tried to explain was explained in the worst way possible, where i thought it was hard until i watched youtube videos and realized it was pretty simple. Almost never finished all the slides from lecture as he went on lots of tangents. Tests problems were always confusingly worded or had things he didnt teach us.

SS2 didn't tell us hw due b4 class starting but graded it.talked about stuff not on exams for 20/50min class & leave 10+slides for you to learn on own, say "oops out of time" hold us over when we had studio after class! exams had material that we didn't learn bc he was too lazy to make a new exam based on course.didn't release final exam grades
