SS2, 2025: this prof. is one of a kind. he comes across as a friend, but acts as a foe. every single exam had questions from content he explicitly said would not be on the exam. its like he didnt check what the exam was before he gave it to us... assignments due b4 FDOC and after LDOC.

SS2. office hours were 20 min before our 9am class. lazy professor who didn't want to change the grading of a question because he messed it up. we had an assignment due the day before class started. changes exam questions mid exams. doesnt follow posted schedule/syllabus. confusing syllabus. said attendance isnt graded but syllabus said it is

Was able to effectively dumb down physics concepts for freshmen in a humanities class. Lectures were occasionally excellent, sometimes okay. Not his fault imo but overall the class is horrible. Think of a bad attribute a class could have and it probably has it. I would rather rip off each of my toe nails one by one than take this class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Drut was a good professor overall. I'm not a physics person and never will be, but I thought he explained the concepts well enough. I would not take IDST 122 again because we were graded on so few things that were each weighed heavily, but I did feel like I learned from the course. As long as you pay attention and take notes, you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Drut was really nice but his lectures were all over the place and a bit complex for a Triple-I. I wouldn't recommend taking IDST 122 for your Triple-I. It's an interesting enough course, but you're only graded on the midterms, paper, and final, and the expectations they have seem unrealistic for people fresh out of high school.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Decent professor. Not a physics guy, so by far the most confusing of the three for me, but by no means is he bad or trying to trip anyone up with his lecturing. I'm sure he's fine solo in an actual physics course. IDST122 is a useless course, however. Don't take it.

I thought Professor Drut was very kind and passionate about his subject. However, I found the concepts hard to grasp as someone who had never taken physics before, and I didn't feel like Drut explained things in a thorough way at times. Overall, IDSt 122 was a very interesting and engaging class but definitely one of the hardest triple-Is.
he explains topics of astrophysics pretty well and answers all questions as well as he can,

Prof.Drut is a kind man, but his classes are not the most clear, especially if you are not into physics. He wants you to succeed though, and if you go to oh he will explain things until you feel satisfied. Overall he is a good professor, but this format does not allow for him to be at his best, and reading material/ testings are heavy, so be ready.

Professor Drut is a funny guy who knows how to apply difficult topics to real life situations. If you're in HATC, you seriously don't need to know the formulas or the fine details of physics. Have fun, do the readings, ask questions in his office hours, let yourself be confused from time to time.

Professor Drut is an excellent professor! He's passionate about his content and very easy to talk to. One of the problems that you'll often find with highly intelligent professors is that they are somewhat incomprehensible: this is NOT the case with Dr. Drut. He's a genius in his fields and also very personable, especially in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Nice guy and passionate about his field, but HOC was a trainwreck. His lectures were disorganized, and he doesn't know how to explain physics to non-majors. His lectures were also painfully boring, and I gave up taking notes. You might survive in a class taught just by him if you're a physics major, but avoid Humans and the Cosmos at all costs.

Gave very engaging lectures, if sometimes difficult to follow. Very few grades overall so take the HW and project seriously. Was always friendly to the class, and cares about his students. Big ups as well to Tyler Britt if you can get him as your TA for anything, super cool guy and gave great explanations for the HW concepts.

I took this course over summer session 2 and can confidently say this was the WORST CLASS I have ever taken in college. Dr. Drut cares more about his ego than his students and can not teach for the life of him. His tests were far too difficult given the time constraint, and he did nothing about rampant cheating and incompetent TAs and assignments.

Took this class over SS2. Professor Drut knows his stuff and is very knowledgeable. However, this does not quite translate to being a good lecturer/teacher. Although this class is over the summer and the content is sped up, Professor Drut rarely slows down on the complex topics. The exams were fairly difficult and did not correlate with HW at all.
ABSOLUTELY AVOID FOR PHYS 114/115!!!!!! Drut does not care about students' feelings and his course structure was horrible. I hated every second of this class and Drut made it worse.

Dr. Drut is an awful professor. His lectures are barely understandable because he talks too fast and he gives you like 5 seconds to do the hardest problems. He is determined to weed you out and ruin your career.

Dr. Drut is probably the best professor I've had at UNC. Unlike many phys professors, he's able to read the room and tell when students are generally lost and makes changes to accommodate the students. He is respectful and his lectures are clear. He answers your questions very clearly. I had very little coding experience before this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Drut was attuned to students' feelings and very lenient with regrade requests. Additionally, he curved our first midterm despite the median not being that bad by UNC standards. Sadly, I had to watch COVID era videos on YouTube because his lectures were not great. The studios were tedious but exam questions may be drawn from them so beware.

Drut is a great professor in 331. He has clear and informative lectures (attendance is not required, but I encourage it), and the homework sets are long but legitimately helpful and interesting. The concepts in class are abstract, but he connects them with subjects you may see in other physics classes. Tests are very fair and he grades leniently.

Drut was my favorite out of the professors (Trop a close second) for Humans & Cosmos. Really interesting content and a great teacher of it. I had to go to him multiple times due to my TA for the class being an absolute hater towards me, and he really heard me out and attempted to help. This class was a waste of time overall, but he's a great prof.
Dr. Drut does a decent job of explaining complex physics topics to humans and the cosmos but ultimately it is a very difficult task. He is very nice prof though, Vamos Argentina

Dr. Drut teaches physics well but as someone who does not previous knowledge on physics it was hard to understand. This class was the worst class I've ever taken in terms of rigorousness and excessive reading. The professors expected a lot out of freshman students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Drut taught the complex physics concepts very well in this class, but it was still difficult to follow especially for it being a first year triple-i for any major. The lectures were very packed, and you have to pay close attention in order to grasp the full concepts.

He does an excellent job at teaching extremely complex physics concepts in a way that someone who doesn't have any prior physics knowledge (like myself) can understand. Gives detailed answers to questions and is very friendly.

Out of the three instructors, Professor Drut was my favorite even though I found it a bit hard to understand the physics section of the class. He explains physics at a high level, probably a little too advanced for first year students in a class mostly about philosophy. Don't take Humans and the Cosmos though, it's just not a good experience.

Professor Drut seems very nice and passionate about physics, but it is just difficult to follow. While I like Professor Drut, I do not recommend Humans and the Cosmos because it is just way too difficult for a first year course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Humans & The Cosmos is extremely interesting but prepare to READ. Too much reading for a first-year requirement in my opinion. Assignments were manageable: 1 weekly reading response, 2 papers, 1 midterm, and the final. Everything is graded by TAs.  Prof. Drut is passionate about the material and it translates through his lectures -- enthralling.

He seems to know his information and is very smart but when paired with humans and the cosmos it makes no sense. Trying to teach and dumb down heavy and strong ideas of physics is hard to do and it does not work out. Most of his lectures make no sense and there is no connection to the course. Outside in a physics class it might be interesting
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Drut is great. He really recognizes students who are putting in effort in the class and is very understanding about workload and the test are crafted very fairly.

As much as I enjoyed Professor Drut, I feel like he did not do a very good job explaining physics to a group of non-physics students. It was clear he knew what he was talking about, but I was frequently in the complicated lectures about particle physics or thermodynamics. However, I am sure that taking a pure physics class with him would be great!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Drut was very good at explaining very complex physics concepts in a way that non-physics students can understand. He is very nice and loves to take and answer questions from curious students. He is a great professor, very approachable, and very kind.

took the triple I class, didn't really understand any of the content he lectured about but I always felt smart after his class (you didn't really need to understand the specifics for that class). very interesting and i'd like to listen to his lectures again, but if I had to actually do the physics work it would probably be tough

I had Prof Drut as part of the triple I course, which was very interesting. Prof Drut's lectures were very dense and equation heavy, which made it hard to understand at first and would require extra work outside of class. Overall, the class was very interesting and I highly recommend Prof Drut for another class as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I didnt enjoy the Humans and the Cosmos class overall because subject matter between him and the other professors seemed disconnected, but Prof Drut is clearly a good teacher. He is very willing to help students understand, good at explaining, and attractive too

Drut is a literal genius. It seriously freaks me out. He is insanely good at explaining challenging concepts. I usually walk into his class completely lost from our readings but then somehow leave understanding everything. I would definitely recommend taking a class from him.

Drut is a very amazing professor. He is very interested in his topic and tries to answer every question people may ask. The attendance was not mandatory but they may change this. He is willing to help his students and can explain very complex subjects in simple, understandable ways. Reading heavy and complex.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Prof Drut is an amazing teacher. He taught alongside 2 other professors for this class but was easily the best one. He is so passionate about physics and it's clear from his lectures he is extremely intelligent. He cares about his students, is funny, and has engaging lectures where you learn a lot. Highly recommend!

Professor Drut is easily one of the best I've had in the physics department. Take a coding class and/or linear algebra before 331 if you want to do well otherwise the homework will be impossible, but Drut is always available to help and offers great solutions. Emails back very quickly and is overall just a kind and incredibly helpful professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Drut is a very caring and funny guy. He will go out of his way to help you and will work with you in any way you need. The linear algebra in this class is taught well enough that you don't have to take the math class prior to this course. Take a coding class before this one, bc the homework is insanely difficult if you don't have prior experience.

Dr Drut is a wonderful professor. Phys331 is VERY challenging, and if you have no prior experience with linear algebra or coding you will have to work even harder, but Dr Drut will do to ANYTHING to help you succeed. If you reach out, he will drop everything to help you. I learned a lot, and I owe it all to him. I wish more profs were like him.

I feel like my previous comment was unfair for Professor Drut. After I struggled a little more, I talked to Professor Drut and he really showed care for my situation. He expressed understanding and also encouraged me to not be held back by the difficulties in the course. I'll probably still get a B to B+ in the course, but I don't regret taking it.

I'm not a physics major and was taking this class for interest. Had all the prereqs but they are definitely not enough for the course. Dr. Drut is a really nice guy, hilarious too at times, but not the clearest in lectures. If you are a physics major I'd recommend you take it with him, but if you are like me then just stay away from the course!
What a guy. Has an espresso machine in his office. Great hair. Actually knows python. You can't beat em.
Very approachable and willing to talk to you about the class and your problems. If you have trouble understanding something he will be able to help you.

Great professor, really cares about his students and their learning. Willing to go the extra mile to make sure his students get the most out of his classes, and genuinely cares. Amazing professor, and would take again!
He was not the best of teachers. He did an OK job
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Really enjoyed this class, favorite of the semester. I found Prof. Sebell's discussions engaging, even if they often trailed off a bit or lagged behind the readings. Don't take if you don't want to read or don't like engaging in in-class discussions. I found what brought me success was just staying engaged in class & actively participating.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Really interesting class. Attendance is mandatory but as long as you show up and do the readings it's an easy A. Pop quizzes here and there but short and not difficult. Participation encouraged but not required. 1 midterm, 2 papers, 1 final. Nice professor and fun class as long as you complete the readings and put some effort into the essays!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He lectured the entire class and was extremely disorganized, making it difficult to study my (paper) notes— no devices allowed. Lots of pop quizzes that make up a good bit of your grade (and were often given a whileee after the reading it was based on). Not a great environment to ask questions during class or ask peers for help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Some of the topics were interesting but I feel like half the time the class was sidetracked so bad by some random kid saying something so irreverent. And then Sebell entertains it and before you know it the class is over and you're sitting there wondering what you even learned. The levels of disorganization in this class should be studied in a lab.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Tough class because it's the same thing every single day (reading books/writings and analyzing them). Gave pop quizzes so make sure you do the readings. He also gives extra credit opportunities by going to events, having perfect attendance, and participating class. Can be hard to participate and understand the key points sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not a bad professor, just a boring class. But I am also not interested in the class topic at all. Beware of pop quizzes because lots of reading, and class consist one 1 exam, 2 papers, and a final. A reasonable grader, and easy to reach out to. I would recommend this class if you are interested in philosophy, but if not, I wouldn't take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class wasn't awful but it was just so boring. Every day in class it was just us listening to him talk about the dense reading we were assigned. There are random pop quizzes throughout the semester. I just wish the class was more organized as the syllabus is a joke for staying on track. There were times Sebell didn't even know when break was
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really liked Professor Sebell - he brings up very interesting points about justice and how justice is defined (the class is listed as SCLL 103). I really don't understand the hate against him, especially considering how our class average is probably around the A/B range. Great lecturer, lots of discussions in class, and very quick with emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The worst professor experience I have had at UNC. Horrible, unorganized lectures and awful grading system. Absolutely no positives from taking his class, and I dreaded every day that I had his class. Painfully long and boring lectures. DO NOT take any of his classes by any means.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures the whole class, line by line through dense readings. No participation, just him talking. Pure suffering - everyone hated it and struggled to stay awake, except that one reviewer. You haven't seen lifeless students until you've watched Sebell's class walk out at 10:45, and he noticed and didn't care at all.

In class, Prof. Sebell delivered incredible lectures on the basics of modern political theory. He is very knowledgable on the topics he teaches on, however his fatal flaw, funny enough, is that his lectures are often very long, because of his love for the material, so we did not get through all the expected readings. Overall, phenomenal professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Duncan is a great professor. Just do the work (which is minimal and not difficult at all), participate, and you'll easily get an A. He does take attendance, but communicate with him and he's super understanding, and class was often asynchronous. I will say he is a tad bit strict, but overall, great instructor.

Professor Duncan was great! He gives great feedback and wants you to do well in the class. He is willing to work with you and is incredibly helpful, just make sure you actually go to class. I took this class as a major requirement but I really enjoyed it.

Minimal work outside of class and easy to get an A. He's also very caring for his students and offers lots of flexibility. English isn't always the most fun class, but he finds ways to make it engaging. He is very thorough with instruction and gives feeders leading up to the projects, which makes it so projects don't burden us with work to do.

Prof. Duncan makes taking eng 105 more bearable. He gives you time in class to work on assignments so that you do not have homework. He also is very understanding if you cannot make it to class or have a question about one of the assignments. Each assignment can be resubmitted to get back points. I recommend!!

While Prof. Duncan can be a little serious and the class isn't super exciting, it is exactly what I needed as a first-year requirement. We had no homework and time in class to work on assignments. You will get an automatic A if you show up to class and turn in your assignments on time. You get to do a mock interview, which is super helpful.

Professor Duncan is simply too serious about ENGL 105 which should be an easy pass first-year english class, but the assignments have to be submitted on time, he gets passive aggressive about attendance, and honestly expects too much out of us when we are just trying to do class to get the credit and get it over with.
Best Prof ever! Great person, great lecture, great project!

Professor Duncan was my favorite professor this year. If you do the work on time you get an automatic A. He did his best to do the HW in class so you didn't have to do it out of class. He was super understanding about physical and mental health if you missed the class and was good about responding to emails! I would 100% recommend taking his class.

Matthew was an amazing professor. All the assignments he gave during class were super useful and he gave extremely valuable feedback every time. He wants every student to succeed and understands that we're all first year students so most if not all assignments are relevant to each student and is super open to helping both inside and outside class.

Matt is a very easygoing professor. He likes to work with students to find solutions to issues. If you communicate your needs for an extension or anything else he is usually more than happy to work with you. He gives good feedback to improve our writing and presentation skills.
Professor Duncan was great for ENG-105. He took time to make sure how every student was doing, and assignments were not difficult as long as you complete them. I 10/10 recommend him!

Mr. Duncan made ENGL105 a lot more enjoyable then I was expecting. He is very clear about what he wants in every assignment and you will get an A if you put in the bare minimum. Grade is made up of 6 short assignments and 3 projects, but theyre not difficult. Highly recommend him for this class.

He does a really great job with understanding the stressors students have in school and how to get efficient work done while still making sure we are not overwhelmed or lost. His class schedules are always well laid out and he makes sure we are well aware of due dates but is willing to change them when he sees that the class needs it.

This was the second class I've taken with Professor Duncan and much like the first, I found it to be easy and pretty good. The entire class consists of three papers, which sounds daunting but he's an easy grader. He doesn't want any of his students doing poorly, and would be happy to see everyone get an A in the class.

Professor Duncan was a great professor and was so caring. He would sit with students after class and answer any questions they had no matter what. He truly wanted to make sure they had it down. 3 big projects: a paper, a zoom presentation, and a posterboard. Very lenient and understanding of situations regarding online school as well.

Professor Duncan is a pretty solid English professor. He gave lots of extra credit opportunities and graded fairly easily. At the beginning of each class, he would show us a meme that related to what we'd be working on. The last project was about memes, but I found it far more complicated than it needed to be, which really sucked the fun out of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Prof Duncan is amazing! He is so caring and is always available for his students. He did an amazing job teaching online and was always clear on rubrics and projects. He made ENGL105 fun and insightful at the same time, I learned so much! The projects do require a lot of work to be put in, but he is a fair grader. Overall the best!

Easiest english105 prof ever! You do an entire project on memes and spend time making them in class. He is super caring and willing to help students outside of class. His rubrics are clear and he grades fairly.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Matthew was always available outside of class for help. Grading was fair and even gave leeway through forum posts that were basically free points. He was good at introducing us to the three main schools of writing and this class was a fairly easy English 105 class.

Ended up with an A-, but don't take ENGL105 with Duncan if you want the easy A as ENGL105 usually is. He takes the class too seriously for English 105 and you will be more than annoyed when you are putting in loads of effort while your friends with other teachers don't do anything all year. Oh and they'll have better grades too.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Duxbury is incredibly kind and makes the homework very straightforward. I came in with no coding experience, and he makes everything doable. He's passionate, always willing to help, and his office hours are amazing. Plus, there's a ton of extra credit available.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Duxbury is such an amazing human being and lecturer. He's clearly knowledgeable and enjoys teaching. He introduced me to data science and motivated to pursue it as a major. Overall, take this class with him if you can! :)

i think you'd have to try to do bad in this class. Scott is a great prof - v caring, accessible, knowledgable, gives great feedback. i loved this class; it was genuinely interesting, and learned a lot w/out ever being stressed abt it. no exams, just reading quizzes (open note) and ~5 hw and a final project - all v doable w/out R/coding experience
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Scott was an amazing professor. If you had any problems he was always available and throughout the course of the semester we would slowly chip away at our final. He gives great feedback and makes all the hw/quizzes very manageable. If you show up and do the work you will do fantastic. Highly recommend

Dr. Duxbury was amazing. This class was super interesting and very manageable. He was very accommodating to those of us without any coding experience. He gave really good feedback and was available outside of class to get help. Can definitely get an A if you show up and do all the work. Highly recommend!

Scott is one of the best professors I've had at unc! He is so kind and is always available to answer your questions outside of class. Class went by so fast because the discussions were always really interesting and inspirational. He is such a smart and funny professor. Take this class if you can, you wont regret it!

I loved this class so much! It was super interesting and not too hard. We had weekly quizzes and biweekly writing assignments, but most of the grade was the midterm and final, which were both open note. I would definitely recommend this class!

I took SOCI 318 (not 123) with Professor Duxbury and it was my favorite class I have taken at UNC so far. Professor Duxbury is very understanding and makes content extremely interesting, 10/10 would recommend this class and Professor Duxbury for students within every major!

I had Scott in Fall 2021, and he's an excellent professor. He's a criminologist so he really knows the subject matter. He's always approachable and very flexible. It would be pretty difficult to get less than an A in his class; just pay attention, do the short assigned writing, and follow the study guide for the midterm/final. Great teacher!

Scott was the greatest Prof I had last semester. He really cared about his students and has a super simple grading scheme. If you show up to class and take the quizzes + exams which are open note then youll be fine. He assigns reading but you can get by without doing them. Definitely a GPA boosting class
Probably the best professor I've had at UNC. The class covers some difficult material, but Scott is great at making it easy to understand. As long as you show up and do your best, you'll get an A.
Scott made lectures interesting and always stopped to answer questions and have spontaneous class discussions. All assignments or quizzes/tests were simple and open-note. Class flew by.

Very clear expectations, good amount of graded items, no one type of assignment (quizzes, papers, participation, exams) was weighted too heavily. He's always willing to explain and discuss topics. Readings only mattered for the weekly quizzes, not exams. Midterm and finals were direct from study guide.

Professor Duxbury is one of the best professors I have ever had. He is so intelligent and explains concepts clearly. I've learned so much in his class. He is also caring and will work with you if things come up. He is clearly more interested that we learn in his class rather than being a tough grader. Highly recommend taking his classes!

Duxbury made this class very enjoyable. He is very transparent about caring for his students and wanting them to learn and does not intend to overload them with homework or give bad grades. The content covered in the course is interesting, and Duxbury does a good job of teaching some difficult machine learning processes. Highly recommend!

This man has my favorite type of teaching style -- informative but not bulky presentation slides, clear and concise when explaining the material, and encourages engagement from the class. Not to mention he's a very understanding professor. SOCI290 is not hard if you've done stats/R classes, the reading is cool and the HW/quiz aren't hard.
Loved this class! Super easy A--short & easy weekly quizzes, 1-page reflections every other week, an easy midterm & final. Classes were interesting, would definitely recommend.

Computational Sociology is a really interesting class. Although a very complex topic, Scott makes it seem clear through his lectures. The work is hard, but he walks you through the R and is very helpful if you need it. Definitely recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Duxbury gives great lectures that are easy to follow. His tests are very similar to his lectures and are very straightforward and simple. Duxbury is very understanding about late work and the workload is not too heavy. The main grades are from discussion posts, weekly quizzes, and small writing assignments.

Best professor I've had in the 4 years I've been at UNC! He provides the reading material, exams & quizzes were super reasonable, lecture slides are available on Sakai, he explains topics well, has optional zoom meetings during class time, and is super helpful! He's very accommodating to students' needs and is super chill/friendly!
Probably my favorite professor I've ever had at UNC. The class was a super easy A as well, definitely recommend!

Nothing but good things to say about Dwight, I learned so much from taking this class and if I had to opportunity to take another class from him I would. His assignments force you to learn the topics while actually being interesting. Without a doubt one of the best professors I've ever had.
Great guy
Very great teacher, easy to follow assignments, very flexible with due dates, gives a lot of good feedback every week, and he's really easy to talk to if you need help.
My favorite class, even if it was just a gen ed. He made it enjoyable and I got a lot out of it!

Tanners a great guy, and really cares about helping you learn how to be a better writer. By far my best class last semester, if you can take him you should. show up to class, and when he assigns a reading you do it, because he will talk about it in class and youll feel stupid. Gives great feedback on papers, just make sure you do them on time.

Prof Tanner is lovely! He chose interesting material for the course and he's extremely knowledgeable about all of it. Lectures are pretty interesting and the assignments/essays are actually fun. Do the readings, show up to class consistently, and you'll do great
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Great professor. Favorite of the semester.

reviews.comment: Absolutely my favorite professor at app so far. Takes the time to learn his students names and genuinely cares about improving your writing. He is respectful and creates a safe space in his classroom
Great professor and by far my favorite class. Very smart and opens your thinking into avenues you never thought about before. True gem. You get as much out of the class as you want to as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I have him at Appalachian State University, and he has been awesome! He is very hip and relatable unlike a lot of other professors, and he is very caring about his students and their capability. When I had COVID, he was the best at reaching out to me outside of class and I really appreciated it. He is very inspiring and makes writing interesting.

I took his class my first year at UNC as a transfer student and I don't think I ever thanked him for helping me with my writing. He really took the time to look at my papers and critique them. I took his class on a whim but I am so glad I did. He loves to 'unpack' the literature and relate it to current times. He's an amazing professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dwight is young and hip, and he is able to convey stuff in an exciting and engaging way. He is always funny and relaxed, totally approachable, and most importantly, he gave great feedback on writing assignments. There wasn't that much work and everything we did do was really interesting and allowed for a lot of creativity. 10/10 would recommend

Dwight is probably one of the best professors I'll ever have. He's awesome at lecturing, always willing to help (by email or office hours), and clearly cares about all of his students. Abide by his pet peeves, follow his super clear grading criteria, and you'll have a great semester with a great guy.
Taking ENGL 105 was relatively stress-free. There aren't too many assignments and gives good and fair feedback. If you are relatively good at writing, getting an A/A- isn't too hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This class is a lot easier when you read the required texts and participate somewhat in the group discussions. Two papers and a relatively easy final make this class an easy A as long as you're a decent writer. Read the books!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dwight is literally the coolest professor I've ever had. He's super chill, very caring, and all around a pretty cool guy. The class required a lot of books, but they all were pretty good, and as long as you didn't procrastinate till the last day it's really doable. Definitely my favorite professor, would highly recommend taking one of his courses!

Dwight is the coolest! This was my favorite class this semester. He's super passionate about the material, explains topics really well, and gives great feedback on assignments. There's a lot of reading but most of the books are pretty interesting and the rest of the class definitely isn't too heavy of a work load. 11/10, would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Younger professor but super interested about his subject. Always very invested in class discussion and always willing to talk about papers or in class assignments outside of class. Not too easy but definitely not too hard as long as you go to class

reviews.comment: Bo rules. That is all. I only feel bad for him having to guide recitations where no one did the reading.

Class consisted of discussions that he never offered feedback. Posts by students in the forum asking questions went unanswered, students also said emails went unanswered. Going into the final only the first discussion had been graded, nothing else.

Class consists of 1 weekly discussion post, a midterm, and a final paper. Super easy and he grades well, but hard to access outside of class especially since this class was asynchronous. Great TA though!

COMP550: Sridhar is a really great person who definitely cares about his students. However his lectures are pretty unorganized. Instead of slides, he projects his handwritten notes that are almost illegible. His exams are worded ambiguously and can be difficult, but his homeworks are perfect. Curve was generous and ensured no one got less than a C+

I'm not sure why the ratings are low. I found that he was a pretty good professor and was really kind. I think a lot of people rating low just didn't show up to classes regularly or office hours. Attendance isn't mandatory, but basically is if you want to do well, since it is a harder class. His handwriting can be difficult to understand at times.

Really cool dude, he's one of my favorite comp sci professors. I also thought he was a good teacher. It is tough material, probable should have went to office hours and would have probably done better.

Very knowledgeable, not mean, gives extensions, gives extra credit, but teaching was just not great. Difficult to follow handwriting and lectures. I don't think I really absorbed anything. Maybe the material is just extremely difficult, but the homework and exams felt impossible. You don't know your grade until the end, and it's too late by then.

reviews.comment: If you wanna take any class with this guy, think thrice. That's the worst professor I've ever had—unclear grading, low-quality teaching, and tough exams. It'd have been okay to make exams tough if his teaching were good. Please, for your own good, if it's your last semester, postpone graduation and take 455 with someone else.

OMG what an awful journey it was. I lost 10 pounds and some hair on my head bc of the stress in this class. His lectures were useless; hw are extremely difficult; horrible exams. I can go on with the negatives bc i don't have any positives to say about him. He's funny? Yeah, creepy funny.

His grading is very unclear and unfair. I don't know where he was educated but his style of teaching doesn't fit into the standards of American College Education. He is such a bad lecturer—his exams and hw were so difficult as if we're in India and we have to take JEE to get into the best college in India to survive. ZERO points to Duggi.
I have no idea where the los

I swear all the positive reviews are just Duggirala trying to save his average. no way anybody actually thinks he is a good professor. funnyish guy, which is why he gets a 2, but worst professor I think I've ever taken. yes, the curve is legendary, but the real challenge is surviving his incoherent lectures long enough to complete the course.

ok yeah he sucks at teaching and the hw is hard but if u put in the time (as u should for a class at this level), u will do well and pass. the curves are HUGE, and he has dumb extra credit like making memes. he also really does try to be funny/engaging, just kinda fails at it. but srsly if ur complaining, just take some time to like...practice?try?

reviews.comment: Homeworks were insanely difficult. Midterms were also very difficult (not as difficult as HW's but still absurdly more difficult than needed). Practice Exam answers were incomplete or hard to understand!

Sridhar is an amazing professor with clear grading who gives us more curve than we deserve. So curved that you could probably get a 70 and still finish with an A. Homeworks are very difficult, but relevant and helpful. His handwriting is truly scary, but otherwise lectures are fun and abstract. Taking 550 with him next semester, would recommend!

I've finally finished the course yesterday. This was a tough and awful journey. Hopefully no other CS professor would be that horrible in terms of exams, hw, grading, and relaying information during lectures. Didn't attend the class bc I thought his lectures were just useless. TAs helped a lot but the way they graded hw was vicious.

Class is not well-organized. We missed a few lectures bc of the weather and bc prof decided to cancel one of the lectures. He covers the material very quickly with his bad handwriting. He'll be teaching 550 next sem so expect not to understand anything from his lectures. It's unfortunate that Kevin didn't teach 455 this sem.
just very bad. have no clue how

OK prof but his exams and hw are extremely tough so don't take 455 with him if u can. Midterms were very difficult and long. Good thing is that he doesn't typically fail students because of the curving. I got 60%s on both midterms and it was curved up close to 70%s. Otherwise just a horrible teaching and extra credit is hard to get.

The assignments were challenging, requiring several hours to finish. Rather than focusing on basic understanding with simpler problems, all the homework questions were difficult. Exams were also challenging; the lectures didn't provide adequate support. While the course could be structured for better learning, the current design feels unmanageable.

Very knowledgeable guy who's not the best at teaching. Bad handwriting and lectures are difficult to follow, but maybe because the material is just difficult. Homework and exams are very challenging and time consuming. He's not mean or anything and I'm sure he's trying his best. Overall, lots of room for improvement and would recommend another prof

Homework was graded strictly, likely due to TAs, while exams were more lenient. Prof. Duggirala was very helpful during office hours. Many complaints stem from students avoiding responsibility. Go to an Ivy and you'll see teaching isn't perfect there either—welcome to academia.
Didn't show to class bc duggi was p useless, but the class content is not hard and midterms/hw were generally chill. idk why we take this class

The worst CS professor out there. Thanks God I'm taking COMP 550 with Kevin Sun next semester, not with Duggirala. This guy might be a good researcher, but he's a horrible prof. Hope he will stop teaching bc I don't want other students to go through this hell.
Avoid at all cost. His slides, homework, and exam grading are horrible. The whole semester was just full of stress.

While he is clearly very knowledgeable about the topics, he is not a good professor. Midterms and exams are more like IQ tests rather than testing to see if you actually learned something, and they are way too long. He has messy handwriting and lectures are completely useless. HW's take forever to complete and don't really help with understanding.

He's a nice person, but his teaching isn't effective, so think carefully before enrolling in COMP455 with him. The lectures aren't helpful, assignments take an excessive amount of time, and exams are so challenging they're hard to finish within the time limit. However, the TAs are excellent and do most of the actual teaching and explanation.

Just a bad professor. Not tough, not strict, just bad. He's clearly a genius in his field, but teaching is not his strong suit. Hardly elaborates on topics, interrupts students' questions, gives little to no explanation on practice midterm solutions (just writes "trivial" or tells us to read the textbook). Curve is legendary, but 455 is still hell.

This class is so tough -- I can't imagine how it's possible to succeed in his class. Not many people show up to his lectures because his slides are useless, so you should do a lot of self-studying. His exams are so tough that I can't even finish answering all questions on time. In general, I'm having horrible experience with this class.

reviews.comment: Don't take 455 with him. He makes the class unnecessarily difficult. Other sections with different profs had easier time with this course. Duggirala's 455 is illegally hard. One of friends even attempted s…. while taking this class.
horrible. avoid at all cost or burn. i hope one day karma will catch with Duggirala for making me depressed and mentally unstable for the whole semester.

reviews.comment: When the huge portion of the grade are exams, you know that Prof doesn't know how to design a class.

This class made me think of self-harm at least thrice. As a student with perfect attendance, the discrepancy in difficulty between his lectures and homework is genuinely unfathomable. Staring into his homework is like staring into the abyss - try to comprehend it and you'll go insane. Don't do this to yourself. Take this class with someone else.

The other reviews are accurate: this is probably one of the harder CS professors out there.  But he gives so many opportunities and resources to learn the material, and OH are invaluable.  If you put your nose to the grindstone he you will certainly do good

Professor Duggirala's class is extremely proof-heavy and harder than other sections, but he makes up for it with curves and plenty of extra credit. I received a 54, 67, and 62 on the midterms and final and still ended up with a B+ in the class. The material is VERY VERY hard but if you put the time in on your homework you will get an A or a B.

Oh boy this class was not it. He really cares about his students but the material was impossible to understand. You have to spend hours in OH to solve the HWs, and although he had extra credit on his exams they were impossible to finish. Never gave proper solutions to his practice problems - just wrote "TRIVIAL". How are we even supposed to learn?!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures were confusing so get ready to learn all the material outside of class. He is a funny guy though. Curve came in clutch. But take someone else for COMP 455 if you can.

Sridhar is nice but god this class was the worst. Tests are difficult and long. The final was 20 pages long. Homeworks were hard but exams were harder for the amount of time you had. Always wanted participation in class but spoke over people with the right answer and created never ending circular debates. Don't bother w/ this class or prof

Sridhar wants students to succeed, but he wasn't always timely or thorough in giving feedback (solutions for practice problems called "Trivial" with no more explanation).  Exams and HW were difficult.  Curved final, extra credit on HW and for improving test to test.  Decent lectures with bad handwriting.

I somewhat disagree with the ratings of previous students. The exams and homeworks were difficult and the professor took too long to grade, yes. However, it's evident to me that he only wishes to motivate and help students, and significantly curved the final exam. Plus he does his best to explain concepts in class and ensures understanding.

This class is insanely difficult for an introductory class to theoretical computer science. Exams are extremely difficult and make up a significant portion of your grade. His explanations aren't clear usually, slides aren't detailed at all and his handwriting is hard to follow. Be ready to spend hours outside of class trying to understand anything.

Could understand more from random YT channels than him, he refuses to upload key for the practice midterm the day before the midterm, exams were horribly hard and difficult, super PROOF HEAVY compared to other teachers, was thinking to drop out or withdraw after the first midterm, disturbs students during exam with changing seats w/o prior notice.

Dr. Duggirala is a passionate, caring, and funny teacher, and will take the time to help you understand on a deeper level if you ask, but he expects you to spend a LOT of time in office hours every week trying to get the homework done and understand it.

This professor refuses to release answer keys for the midterm. He's unclear during lecture. The class is all math proofs and the homeworks are incredibly difficult. The doesn't hold office hours and is unwilling to do the bare minimum to help students. It has been a horrifying experience. The concepts are beyond what should be reasonably expected.

WORST TEACHER EVER. Doesn't explain answers to any question or procedures for solving proofs. Completely illegible handwriting makes lectures impossible to follow. TAs can't understand his answer keys due to how poorly he writes them. Unfair, extremely difficult HW problems. Proof heavy (other 455 teacher has no proofs in the curriculum). AVOID HIM
Such an awesome teacher! Class is pretty easy as long as you study. One of my favorite classes I've ever taken.

The homework was so hard and the exams were extremely difficult. Although he's a nice professor, he really makes you work for the answers during office hours and does not give coherent lectures. The material was hard and confusing and I had to mostly learn the material myself. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's not for you if you just want to program video games, as his version of COMP455 is more difficult and more proof heavy, but don't let that fool you into thinking Prof. Duggirala isn't a good lecturer or doesn't care about his students. He may not have the best handwriting, but he's helpful, he'll make you laugh, and you'll learn a lot from him.

Encourages students to give wrong answers to encourage participation during lectures. Thinking through the problems during lectures (how to approach the proofs, how to design an automata) helped in solving the assignments and exams.

Course is difficult but would have been worse if the practice problems were given during the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class is made much more difficult than necessary with Professor Duggirala. The class is very lecture heavy and most of the time difficult to understand and review due to his poor slides and sloppy annotations. His HWs are very difficult and time-consuming and his tests are even more difficult with content that has not been thoroughly explained

Struggled to grasp the concepts from the very first class due to his unclear and fast paced teaching style. The homework assignements were often confusing and unrelated to lecture material and the tests and exams were even harder. Would strongly encourage people not to take this class.

Lots of difficult homework and difficult tests make this class pretty brutal. Duggirala isn't the greatest teacher and his slides are average at best. Very little, and not super helpful, office hours (3 hrs a week between him and a TA). If you take 455 with Duggirala I'd highly recommend supplementing his lessons with the textbook/online videos.

He's a nice guy and is very open for questions during lecture. Lectures were pretty confusing,and he didn't do the best job of conveying his expertise in the subject. Even if you understood the material in lecture, the homeworks were still pretty confusing, a lot of them I had absolutely no idea what to do. Would not take another elective with him
Great professor! Super willing to help out on homework (which you will probably need)
Very helpful teacher. Knows the material well and gives clear explanations. The difficulty in his class has more to do with the material than any deficiency in his teaching style.

Far and away my best professor. Really helpful whenever you ask. He really teaches the class well and his tests aren't too hard. He tells you that what is on the test is all in the homework. He's being completely honest. If you study the homework, you'll be all set for the test.

I loved having Professor Eberlein. His lectures are easy to follow, and he is so knowledgeable on the subject. I would highly, highly recommend him. Also had him for Math 233, which we was great for as well.

Wow you need to get this guy. He is fantastic. I really pity the other folks in the other classes because they do not get the opportunity to experience the greatness of Pat Eberlein. I have never been happier with a professor/ teacher in my life. Fair homework, fair tests, useful lectures. He also is a funny and kind character as well.

Not too hard a teacher for an honors-level course. Is pretty clear, although if you read the text, it's hard to not understand properly. His tests are fair and based on material already covered. He's also a friendly guy.
He's pretty funny.

Kind and approachable person who is accessible, definitely take advantage of that; class was WAY harder than it should have been. Lectures: extremely hard to follow, and it often felt like she didn't know how to teach the material. The content taught barely matched the midterms, if it weren't for the practice exams I would have failed the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ms. East was very sweet. She genuinely cares for the success of her students. However, I feel like her teaching style was not the best, as lessons were not always taught in a clear manner. I feel concepts could have been explained better in a simpler way; it sometimes would feel overly complicated. Her practice exams were very helpful!

She's very quirky and a fun professor, gives a lot of extra credit and is very understanding about test dates, and when to make things due. However, not the best teacher she writes how to do things, not why she's doing it. Overall, the lenience she had balances out the teaching

Felt significantly underprepared. She was accessible outside of class, but was always behind on lectures with rushed complex content! A nice person, but this class was extremely difficult. Still inexperienced. Appreciated how she supported the class. Caution taking this class though. Take the good and bad ratings with a grain of salt.

reviews.comment: She's genuinely one of the most loving people I've ever met. I would absolutely take the class again, but I just think she could benefit her lecture with a bit more structure, with clearer resources and more practice exercises.

Prof East is one of the most caring professors I've ever had, she teaches really well, she is mostly organised and super adaptable. If you're gonna take 110, take it with her, she actually understands what it's like to be a student and she's flexible, considerate and has the best dad jokes. She's such a sweetie

Extremely inexperienced when it comes to teaching. She grades very harsh and unfair, will take off multiple points for small mistakes. She does not allow you to discuss any exam grades with her. She has terrible handwriting, making lectures difficult to understand. Does not take anything serious, she found it funny that her class average was 70%.
I don't know guys. I wouldn't take a class with her again. I lowkey regret my decision taking this class.

Professor East is a very open minded and caring teacher who tries her best to make a fast paced summer course feel manageable.Very understanding of students' varying math backgrounds and acknowledges that even an "easy" class like Math 110 can be challenging due to outside circumstances.  The Dad jokes be hitting too sometimes lol.

Angela is clearly caring and wants us to do well, but is still a bit inexperienced with teaching. While she will help you outside of class hours, sometimes her lectures aren't super clear. She tells jokes and wants us to enjoy math but just needs to figure out some stuff. Also, for some reason math 110 seemed unnecessarily hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took this class before and hated it, but Angela genuinely made math class fun! She tells awful dad jokes and is charming. She really cares about your success and has so many office hours sessions available. She explains things in a way beginning math students can comprehend, so she's perfect to teach this course! 10/10 would take again.

Enjoyed taking this class and it was easy. Not too many assignments. not a very harsh grader. she is very nice and cares about what she teaches. Movies watched were interesting and we'd have to complete a discussion post/group discussion about 2 films and write 1 tv show review. Exams were multiple choice and one short answer question.

I loved this class and Elaina was a great instructor! She genuinely cares about her students and encourages prioritizing your health over class. That being said you have to at least act like you care and go sometimes to get participation credit. The class was super interesting and looked at gender and sexuality in the context of current events!

Honestly all of her ratings are hyping her up but I didn't like her that much. The papers and tests were annoying and kinda hard in my opinion. You definitely have to try if you want an A she doesn't just hand them out. And just in general her vibe is kinda strange, monotone voice, and just seems like she would much rather be doing anything else.

It's not letting me select the correct class, but I took Comm 325 with Elaina. She is so sweet and also an extremely lenient grader, gladly grants extensions, and will do everything in her power to accommodate your needs if you just communicate. Lectures and exams are straightforward.

Amazing instructor that really makes her lectures engaging. Assignments are fair and she's always available for questions and feedback. Very caring instructor, and would definitely take another course with her!

Elaina was awesome!! So nice and caring, easy grader and very communicative! Would take again 100 times over! One large group project over the course of the semester, an open book midterm and final taken online and the book is online! Definitely take her if possible, you wont regret it.

Elaina is amazing! For those taking her class virtually, she provides a textbook but her videos are great. Her tests are open note and easy A's (no time limit!). She gave me lots of feedback and met extra with me for our course paper (20%). She is super kind and really cares about her students. I would be ecstatic taking another course with her.

Professor Eakle is extremely kind, caring, empathetic, and engaging in her lectures. I can genuinely say that I enjoyed this class and learning from her this semester. Highly recommend taking COMM 120 or any other class with her.

Professor Eakle was a great teacher! I really enjoyed her lectures because she includes interesting class activities and videos. There is a large research paper at the end of the course but she was always happy to help and gave good and detailed feedbacks. Highly recommend taking COMM 120 with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Eble is a real 70-year-old gem. If I could, I would do it all over again. She will no be teaching. Farewell, Master Grammarian.

Prof. Eble is a nice woman, but it is most definitely her time to retire. Her lectures are long and boring, and she is utterly unable to help you with things you don't understand. Don't take this class. The history portion of the course is fine, but once it gets to grammar, the class stinks.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Eble is obviously very knowledgable, but she's entirely too old to still be teaching classes. Her lectures were boring, she wasn't very helpful in office hours, and she never gave constructive feedback on any of my work. Seriously, don't take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Eble was fine in the history portion of this class, but the difficulty of the class shot up when we reached old English. She expects you to know all about the grammar, but she doesn't explain it well at all. If you've had any old English before you'll probably be fine, if not, good luck. She's a tough grader, and not always clear in criteria.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This is a hard class if you know nothing about English grammar, but I absolutely loved this class, but a lot of people will not. There are a lot of small quizzes, one paper, two tests, a final, and a presentation. Go to her office hours, she is incredibly helpful if you need individual help. She is well-known and respected in her field.

Goes real fast, no PowerPoint, only lectures. Questions on quizzes and tests can be vague. Tests are hard enough that she lowers the grading scale for them. Prompts for essays can be misleading (we had an essay about headlines that she treated as if we were writing a scholarly article on particle physics). May blindside you with a pop quiz.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Very informative. Lectures only to the class; no powerpoints or any other type of aid for you to study later, so if you miss class, your only hope is to get notes from a friend. (also seems like she can get a little impatient if you don't understand something)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: ENG 314 is a history of the english language course, however you will be teaching yourself Old English (how to read and translate it). Class is 100% lecture, and she will go at her own (very fast) pace. Prepare to study your butt off outside of class, she expects you to teach yourself content that she will only gloss over in class. not good gen-ed
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I  missed a day of class due to mono and ended up getting a 44 on the first test because I missed the day we went over Grimm's law, but I stopped by her office hours after class one day and she helped me understand where I went wrong. She is very dedicated to helping students succeed if they put in the effort.

Dr. Eble is a great professor. She's a stickler on style. Can be harsh in grading, but she'll really work with you and give lots of good comments. English 315 is especially fun because she gets very passionate about the material. Plus she's been at UNC for a long time, so she has a lot of interesting stories about various colleagues.

I had Ms. Eble along with her colleague Ms. Brown for the freshman seminar "Interpreting the South from Manuscripts." Ms. Eble is a hard grader, but she will make your writing so much better. The class itself I found to be very interesting as it is completely discussion and raw-reading based.  My favorite class of the semester!

Do not take her class unless you want to go home every night and teach yourself the subject. And, even after that don't expect to get an A in her tests because what you answered was not what she expected. When you talk to her she doesn't really seem to want to help. Also, she is very "my way of the highway" kind of person if you try to correct her.

This is my second class with Eble and I'm enjoying it even more than the last. She's willing to work with you--if you have a problem, she'll show you grace! She's a lot of fun and extremely knowledgeable in her field. Plus, the classes she teaches are always very interesting.

Eble is so interesting and entertaining! She is extremely knowledgeable and when you ask a question (which you always should!), she gives you a great, informative answer. She reminds me of my grandma, if my grandma could speak Old English. I've enjoyed taking her History of English class and I look forward to another class with her next semester.

I would NOT recommend the  freshman seminar "Interpreting the south through manuscripts." This class was completely awful. All of the papers we turned in were supposed to be analysis, however all she really wanted was a summary of the documents. She's a very "my way or the highway" person. I found her paper comments very rude and unhelpful.

This grammar class was useful and informative.  The nature of the material makes details matter. This professor is extremely knowledgeable, and I found her helpful. Few of my classmates knew as much about grammar as they thought they did. Some were offended when they were corrected on things they should have learned in (or before) high school.

She was very boring.  One day it snowed and many students were missing.  She proceeded to take out the dictionary and for 1 1/2 hours, read words from the dictionary and talked about their origins.  A complete waste of my time!

she tends to over explain things, which makes her class pretty boring, but you hear the same thing so many times you won't need to study much at home. she is very knowledgeable and not strict with grades. she is very strict on attendance though
she is not mean she is just kind of awkward about personal interactions but what do you expect from an academic

Dr. Eble is a really good professor! All of you guys complaining about attendance umm.. welcome to college! She is very smart and very thorough but not unfair. A lot of people get the impression that her class will be easy and get upset when it isn't a walk in the park. You have to work because she wants you to learn!

She talks a mile/min, the class lectures were jumbled and difficult to make sense of & she's a very demanding professor. However, she's also sensitive, and once started crying in class because some students didn't turn a paper in.. she talked about how personally she took it. Bizarre.

I had Dr. Eble for graduate Old English 20 years ago and want to respond to a couple of raters: she is a linguist, and a well-regarded one at that and she does know what she's talking about.  She was tough, but quite helpful and sat in on my diss defense at the last minute with some great suggestions.

She reminds me of a high school teacher who has been teaching wayyyy too long! Class content can be interesting at times, but overall drab. She has no pity on missing class (especially daily quizzes).  Essays were difficult to write and she was picky on answers for exams.  Text and outside readings were boring and sometimes difficult
I took a first year seminar with Ms. Eble and LOVED it. The way she pays attention to details will help make your writing more clear and precise. She will make you a better writer.
Very interesting and engaging class, and she seemed to genuinely care about her students.
Eble can be tough and she grades quite strictly. Overall though I think she's a good teacher.

Do everything you can to avoid Eble's classes. She is so nit-picky about little details, can't look at the larger picture, and refuses to compliment any of her students. She'll make you feel stupid and waste 3 hours of your time every week. In now way will she nurture your interest in English.

About 18 years ago, I took Dr. Eble's Modern Grammar class, and I'm still smarting from it.  Once, I came to her office to ask about the term paper (topic:  "write 20 pgs. on anything that is grammatically interesting").  She was so cold and hostile. If you weren't familiar with 1960s songs that comprised her tests, you were sunk too. Be warned.

This class was extremely tedious.  She insists on going through every little point as if the entire class is incapable of understanding anything on our own.  I could have skipped about half the classes, but she's insane about attendance.

I took a freshman seminar with her and another professor, called interpreting the south through manuscripts.  The labs were difficult, but interesting.  The class however was not.  She is tedious when it comes to grammer, to a point where it's ridiculous.  She doesn't pay attention to content.

Did not like the class or the professor. She interrupted students while they were asking questions, was rude, clashed with many students. Completely unhelpful, boring class....NOT ENGLISH GRAMMAR! will NEVER take another class with her again! You've been warned!
personality clash with many students. boring...not very helpful...students mainly taught the class
Eh...
I've taken two classes with her - she's great!  Very demanding, but you learn a lot, and she has lots of great stories to illustrate the lessons.
ick. she thinks shes a linguistics teacher. she's mean, not helpful, confusing, yells in class, and a touch grader. I love grammar, but not what she teaches! not recommended at all.
She played favorites, gave out only 3 A's the entire semester.  Did not enjoy teaching style at all.

Very unhelpful. Avoid this class at all costs. Was mean, told students that they must do things her way and no other (on topics where this just doesn't make sense), and was extremely unhelpful outside of class. No interest in teaching at all.
This is a TOUGH professor.  I've taken her twice and loved both classes, but believe me, you have to work in her classes.
Sends great pics in his emails!!! super entertaining guy..... the D he gave me turned into an A by doing super easy extra credit! he's so understanding and not as hard as you would think
Can't recommend Earl enough. Show up to class and you won't only get a good grade, but you'll learn to love Sociology through the eyes of Teacher Earl.
Teacher Earl is aways there for you... ALWAYS. Even when you didn't even know you needed him. Even when you're not in his class. Even after you graduate...

Prof. Teacher Earl has a strange grading policy that saw me get a B- even tho I specifically requested a B+ at the beginning of the semester. I am not a smart boy, so the B- was fair. Great guy over all, and the only time I hated his class was when we had a substitute for the week
Teacher Earl loves to perform silly social experiments during class. Some of these include watching Hillybillies and the Crippled Camp. Interesting films with disturbing images.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Beware of pop quizzes--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: long live teacher earl! always the highlight of my week

in love with every cell of his being. i wish I could take every class of his. thinking about applying to grad school at unc just so I can continue to see him. cannot recommend him enough! take a class with him, you will not regret it!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Teacher Earl truly got me out of my depressive episode. He brought so much light to my life, changed my whole view on the world through sociology. He is a beautiful person, not just inside, but on the outside too. <3 ;)
I love his homework assignments.
Teacher Earl was a fantastic Teacher. He made me so happy to learn. If you ever have the opportunity, take one of his classes. I will say that he hates PollEverywhere, however.
I loved Tyler's class! He was the most engaging instructor/professor I had this semester tbh. The class was mostly project-based and he was very willing to work with us with deadlines.

Tough quizzes! BUT, he grades projects leniently. The projects are fun too; do well on them (and talk every now and then in class) to get at least an A-. Tyler himself is interesting and fun to talk to. He made it a point to meet w/ every student before every project, which ends up being really helpful and says a lot about him!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Easterbrook was a great teacher. Effort is a huge thing for him. If you work hard, you will get a good grade even if you didn't do everything perfect. His lectures were really interesting and applicable to life. There were only like 4 projects and some reading quizzes. Very chill.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Megan is a wonderful person. I had no experience or even much interest in Baroque Opera, but she made the topic and the class extremely interesting and engaging. She's extremely caring, and if she sees that you give a good effort, you will be rewarded. She helped me tremendously in office hours this semester and was really a fantastic professor.

One of the best professors I've had at UNC. Her passion and interest in the material is clear, and that translates to clear, engaging lectures that touch on really interesting material. Approachable, friendly, and fair, she really does care about helping you succeed no matter your circumstances. If you have the choice, definitely take 255 with her.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Easy class that's fairly interesting because she does a lot of activities. Really easy A with extra credit on tests. I think 95% of the class got an A. There is one 10 page paper but this is required for all World Before 1750 gen. ed. classes, and she makes it easier than the other classes by adding sections like lit review and stuff. EASY A!

Dr. Eagen is a very nice lady, but the class itself was pretty boring. The majority of the material you learn is from the early 1900s and you don't get into the fun stuff like MJ until the last week and a half of class. Very easy class, essays are graded very easily, exams aren't hard if you study. She focuses a lot on music theory too.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Megan Eagen is awesome, super nice and cares deeply about all of her students, even in a huge lecture hall like mine. according to the books i deserved an a- but she knew me and that i worked hard so she lifted me up to an A. knows a lot about music and will leave a good impression on you

Dr. Megan Eagen-Jones is an excellent professor. This was her first class in a large lecture hall, and she managed to keep things engaging. Her lectures are interesting, and she does a good job of highlighting the main points that she tests on. She genuinely cares about her students and offers really in depth feedback on the papers she grades.

Dr. Eagen-Jones was a wonderful teacher. She gave us the tools to succeed with ease and was passionate and knowledgable on the subject matter. I could totally nerd out with Dr. Eagen-Jones, and if you're into early music, I'm sure you could too. I organized a performance of a medieval mass movement outside of class for fun and she participated!

Dr. Eagen is very passionate about what she teaches and I would highly recommend. She is willing to help and answer questions and emails in a timely manner. Never played an instrument or been in a music class and loved it.

The lecture is boring and not mandatory, but it definitely helps because it highlights all of the important stuff form the textbook. The exams are super easy and Dr. Eagen-Jones intentionally makes it this way. Also, she is super helpful during her office hours and wants to give you the information you need to succeed on your papers.

I've never written one of these before but this teacher was so phenomenal I had to.  Megan is a fantastic proffesor who really knows her stuff.  She isn't out to trick you on the tests and gives very helpful quizzes.  If you give her a little effort anyone can get an easy A here.

Megan is the most enthusiastic teacher I've had here at UNC. Her class wasn't very difficult, and she showed a great desire for her students to learn the material. Very accessible outside of the classroom. 10/10 would reccomend

I absolutely adored this class! Megan is amazing. She is one of the best teachers I've ever had. I love the course content and she is so understanding and helpful. This class is done on the students' time and desires. She's also just a really great person outside of class!

There are pop quizzes, but they're not hard. Homework once a week. Best to do the readings (they're not long), but she goes over what you need to know in class. Really chill class, good pacing, ample opportunities for participation. She's really understanding. 10/10 recommend!
Megan is awesome!
